translation: If you disclose your charitable expenditures, they are good; but if you conceal them and give them to the poor, it is better for you, and He will remove from you some of your misdeeds [thereby]. And Allah, with what you do, is [fully] Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the virtue of giving charity, highlighting that while public charity is commendable, giving in secret is even more rewarding. The act of concealing one's charitable deeds not only purifies the intention behind the giving, focusing it solely on pleasing Allah rather than seeking praise from others, but also increases the spiritual reward. Additionally, the verse reassures that Allah is fully aware of all actions, encouraging believers to perform good deeds sincerely, knowing that their efforts are recognized and will be rewarded by Allah, who will also forgive some of their sins as a result of their charitable acts.
orig: إن تبدوا الصدقات فنعما هي وإن تخفوها وتؤتوها الفقراء فهو خير لكم ويكفر عنكم من سيئاتكم والله بما تعملون خبير

translation: It is not upon you [O Muhammad] to guide them, but Allah guides whom He wills. And whatever good you spend is for yourselves, and you should not spend except seeking the countenance of Allah. And whatever good you spend will be repaid to you in full, and you will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of guidance and charity in Islam. It relieves the Prophet Muhammad from the burden of ensuring others follow the right path, stating that guidance is ultimately in the hands of Allah. The verse encourages believers to engage in acts of charity, reminding them that such actions are for their own spiritual benefit and should be performed solely to please Allah. It reassures that any good deed done will be fully rewarded by Allah, and no one will be treated unjustly in this regard. This highlights the importance of intention in charitable acts and the divine justice in rewarding them.
orig: ليس عليك هداهم ولكن الله يهدي من يشاء وما تنفقوا من خير فلأنفسكم وما تنفقون إلا ابتغاء وجه الله وما تنفقوا من خير يوف إليكم وأنتم لا تظلمون

translation: For the poor who are restricted in the way of Allah, unable to travel in the land. The ignorant think them rich because of their restraint. You will know them by their appearance; they do not beg from people importunately. And whatever you spend of good, indeed, Allah is Knowing of it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of giving charity to those who are truly in need but maintain their dignity and do not beg. It highlights that such individuals, despite their poverty, are often mistaken as wealthy due to their modesty and restraint. The verse encourages believers to recognize these people by their demeanor and to give generously, assuring that Allah is fully aware of and rewards such charitable acts.
orig: للفقراء الذين أحصروا في سبيل الله لا يستطيعون ضربا في الأرض يحسبهم الجاهل أغنياء من التعفف تعرفهم بسيماهم لا يسألون الناس إلحافا وما تنفقوا من خير فإن الله به عليم

translation: Those who spend their wealth by night and by day, secretly and publicly, they will have their reward with their Lord, and no fear shall come upon them, nor shall they grieve.
interpretation: This verse highlights the virtue of charity, emphasizing that it should be performed consistently and in all conditions, whether in secrecy or openly. It reassures believers that such acts of kindness are recognized by Allah, and those who engage in them will be rewarded in the hereafter. The promise of no fear or grief further underscores the spiritual security and peace that comes from living a life of generosity and faith.
orig: الذين ينفقون أموالهم بالليل والنهار سرا وعلانية فلهم أجرهم عند ربهم ولا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: Those who consume usury will not stand except as stands one whom the devil has confounded with his touch. That is because they say, 'Trade is [just] like usury.' But Allah has permitted trade and has forbidden usury. So whoever has received an admonition from his Lord and desists may have what is past, and his affair rests with Allah. But whoever returns [to usury] - those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide eternally therein.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe consequences of engaging in usury, equating it to being under the influence of Satan, which leads to spiritual and moral confusion. It highlights the distinction between trade, which is permissible and blessed by Allah, and usury, which is strictly forbidden. The verse offers a chance for repentance to those who have engaged in usury; if they stop upon receiving divine guidance, their past actions can be forgiven, and their fate is left to Allah's judgment. However, persistent engagement in usury after receiving admonition results in eternal damnation, underscoring the gravity of this sin and the importance of adhering to divine commandments.
orig: الذين يأكلون الربا لا يقومون إلا كما يقوم الذي يتخبطه الشيطان من المس ذلك بأنهم قالوا إنما البيع مثل الربا وأحل الله البيع وحرم الربا فمن جاءه موعظة من ربه فانتهى فله ما سلف وأمره إلى الله ومن عاد فأولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون

translation: Allah destroys interest and increases charities, and Allah does not love every sinful disbeliever.
interpretation: This verse highlights the moral and spiritual consequences of different financial practices. It suggests that engaging in usury or interest (riba) leads to spiritual and material loss, as it is condemned by Allah. Conversely, giving in charity (sadaqat) is rewarded and blessed by Allah, leading to spiritual growth and material increase. The verse also connects the act of taking interest with disbelief and sinfulness, indicating a deep moral failing. It serves as a reminder to Muslims to avoid interest-based transactions and to engage in charitable acts, aligning their financial practices with divine approval and love.
orig: يمحق الله الربا ويربي الصدقات والله لا يحب كل كفار أثيم

translation: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds and established prayer and given zakah will have their reward with their Lord, and there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the rewards promised to the believers who not only have faith but also actively engage in righteous actions, maintain their prayers, and give to charity. It underscores that such individuals will receive their recompense from Allah, indicating divine approval and blessings. Furthermore, it reassures them of a state free from fear and sorrow in the hereafter, highlighting the spiritual security and peace that comes with true faith and good deeds.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات وأقاموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة لهم أجرهم عند ربهم ولا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: O you who have believed, fear Allah and give up what remains [due to you] of interest, if you should be believers.
interpretation: This verse addresses believers directly, urging them to maintain a consciousness of Allah by abandoning the practice of usury (riba). It emphasizes that true faith requires the relinquishment of any gains from interest, highlighting the incompatibility of usury with the principles of faith and justice in Islam. The verse serves as a call to purify one's economic dealings in accordance with divine guidance.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله وذروا ما بقي من الربا إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: But if you do not do so, then be informed of a war from Allah and His Messenger. And if you repent, you will have your principal - neither will you be harmed, nor will you harm.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fulfilling financial obligations, particularly in the context of debts and loans. It warns that failure to adhere to these obligations will result in severe consequences, described as a war from Allah and His Messenger, symbolizing divine displeasure and potential worldly repercussions. However, the verse also offers a path to redemption through repentance, promising that upon sincere repentance, individuals will be entitled to reclaim their principal amounts without incurring or causing any injustice. This reflects the Qur'an's emphasis on justice, fairness, and the moral responsibility to honor financial commitments.
orig: فإن لم تفعلوا فأذنوا بحرب من الله ورسوله وإن تبتم فلكم رءوس أموالكم لا تظلمون ولا تظلمون

translation: And if the debtor is in difficulty, then grant him time until it is easy for him to repay; but if you remit it by way of charity, that is better for you if you only knew.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of compassion and leniency in financial dealings. It instructs believers to extend the repayment period for those in financial hardship, reflecting the Islamic principle of easing burdens on others. Furthermore, it encourages the act of forgiving the debt entirely as an act of charity, which is considered even more virtuous. This teaching promotes a society where empathy and support are prioritized, suggesting that such acts of kindness not only benefit the recipient but also spiritually enrich the giver, aligning with the broader Islamic ethos of social justice and mutual aid.
orig: وإن كان ذو عسرة فنظرة إلى ميسرة وأن تصدقوا خير لكم إن كنتم تعلمون

translation: And fear a Day when you will be returned to Allah. Then every soul will be compensated for what it earned, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of being mindful of the Day of Judgment, when all individuals will return to Allah. It serves as a reminder that every action a person takes in their life will have consequences, as each soul will be fully recompensed for its deeds. The assurance that 'they will not be wronged' underscores the justice of Allah, indicating that the recompense will be fair and just, without any injustice or favoritism. This verse encourages believers to live righteously, with the awareness that their actions are accountable before Allah on the Day of Judgment.
orig: واتقوا يوما ترجعون فيه إلى الله ثم توفى كل نفس ما كسبت وهم لا يظلمون

translation: O you who have believed, when you contract a debt for a specified term, write it down. And let a scribe write [it] between you in justice. Let no scribe refuse to write as Allah has taught him. So let him write and let the one who has the obligation dictate, and let him fear Allah, his Lord, and not leave anything out of it. But if the one who has the obligation is of limited understanding or weak or unable to dictate himself, then let his guardian dictate in justice. And bring to witness two witnesses from among your men. And if there are not two men [available], then a man and two women from those whom you accept as witnesses - so that if one of the women errs, then the other can remind her. And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called upon. And do not be [too] weary to write it, whether it is small or large, for its [specified] term. That is more just in the sight of Allah and stronger as evidence and more likely to prevent doubt between you, except when it is an immediate transaction which you conduct among yourselves. For [then] there is no blame upon you if you do not write it. And take witnesses when you conclude a contract. Let no scribe be harmed or any witness. For if you do so, indeed, it is sinful of you. And fear Allah. And Allah teaches you. And Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of documenting financial transactions and contracts to ensure justice and clarity in dealings among Muslims. It mandates the use of written agreements for debts that have a specified term, highlighting the role of a scribe in recording these transactions accurately and fairly. The verse also addresses the procedure for those who might not be able to dictate their obligations due to mental or physical limitations, ensuring their rights are protected through a guardian's assistance. The requirement for witnesses, preferably two men or one man and two women, underscores the communal aspect of ensuring fairness and preventing disputes. The verse also allows for exceptions in immediate transactions, where writing might not be necessary, but still encourages the presence of witnesses. Overall, the verse promotes transparency, accountability, and the fear of Allah in financial dealings, aiming to prevent disputes and uphold justice within the community.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا تداينتم بدين إلى أجل مسمى فاكتبوه وليكتب بينكم كاتب بالعدل ولا يأب كاتب أن يكتب كما علمه الله فليكتب وليملل الذي عليه الحق وليتق الله ربه ولا يبخس منه شيئا فإن كان الذي عليه الحق سفيها أو ضعيفا أو لا يستطيع أن يمل هو فليملل وليه بالعدل واستشهدوا شهيدين من رجالكم فإن لم يكونا رجلين فرجل وامرأتان ممن ترضون من الشهداء أن تضل إحداهما فتذكر إحداهما الأخرى ولا يأب الشهداء إذا ما دعوا ولا تسأموا أن تكتبوه صغيرا أو كبيرا إلى أجله ذلكم أقسط عند الله وأقوم للشهادة وأدنى ألا ترتابوا إلا أن تكون تجارة حاضرة تديرونها بينكم فليس عليكم جناح ألا تكتبوها وأشهدوا إذا تبايعتم ولا يضار كاتب ولا شهيد وإن تفعلوا فإنه فسوق بكم واتقوا الله ويعلمكم الله والله بكل شيء عليم

translation: And if you are on a journey and cannot find a scribe, then a security deposit [should be] taken. And if one of you entrusts another, then let him who is entrusted discharge his trust and let him fear Allah, his Lord. And do not conceal testimony, for whoever conceals it - his heart is indeed sinful, and Allah is Knowing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fulfilling trusts and the moral obligation to be honest and transparent, even in situations where formal documentation is not available. It highlights that trust and fear of Allah should guide one's actions, particularly in financial dealings or when acting as a witness. The verse warns against concealing the truth, equating such an act with a sinful heart, and reminds believers that Allah is fully aware of all actions, reinforcing the concept of accountability to God.
orig: وإن كنتم على سفر ولم تجدوا كاتبا فرهان مقبوضة فإن أمن بعضكم بعضا فليؤد الذي اؤتمن أمانته وليتق الله ربه ولا تكتموا الشهادة ومن يكتمها فإنه آثم قلبه والله بما تعملون عليم

translation: To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And whether you reveal what is in yourselves or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it. Then He will forgive whom He wills and punish whom He wills, and Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse underscores the omnipotence and omniscience of Allah, emphasizing that everything in existence is under His dominion. It highlights the accountability of individuals for their innermost thoughts and intentions, whether expressed or hidden. The verse also reflects Allah's absolute authority in granting forgiveness or meting out punishment according to His divine will, reinforcing the concept that His power extends over all aspects of creation and He is fully capable of enacting His will.
orig: لله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وإن تبدوا ما في أنفسكم أو تخفوه يحاسبكم به الله فيغفر لمن يشاء ويعذب من يشاء والله على كل شيء قدير

translation: The Messenger has believed in what was revealed to him from his Lord, and [so have] the believers. All of them have believed in Allah and His angels and His books and His messengers, [saying], "We make no distinction between any of His messengers." And they say, "We hear and we obey. [We seek] Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the [final] destination."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity of faith among the Prophet Muhammad and all believers, highlighting their complete acceptance of the divine revelations, including belief in Allah, His angels, scriptures, and all His messengers without any discrimination. It also underscores the believers' submission to Allah's commands, their plea for forgiveness, and their acknowledgment of the ultimate return to Allah, reinforcing the importance of unity, obedience, and humility in faith.
orig: آمن الرسول بما أنزل إليه من ربه والمؤمنون كل آمن بالله وملائكته وكتبه ورسله لا نفرق بين أحد من رسله وقالوا سمعنا وأطعنا غفرانك ربنا وإليك المصير

translation: Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity. It will have [the consequence of] what it has earned, and it will be accountable for what it has acquired. Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we have forgotten or erred. Our Lord, and lay not upon us a burden like that which You laid upon those before us. Our Lord, and burden us not with that which we have no ability to bear. And pardon us; and forgive us; and have mercy upon us. You are our protector, so give us victory over the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of divine justice and mercy in Islam. It reassures believers that Allah does not test them beyond their capabilities, which reflects the fairness and compassion of God. The verse also includes a supplication that highlights human vulnerability and dependence on Allah's mercy, asking for forgiveness for unintentional mistakes and relief from overwhelming burdens. It encourages believers to seek Allah's help and protection against those who oppose faith, reinforcing the concept of reliance on divine support in the face of adversity.
orig: لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا وسعها لها ما كسبت وعليها ما اكتسبت ربنا لا تؤاخذنا إن نسينا أو أخطأنا ربنا ولا تحمل علينا إصرا كما حملته على الذين من قبلنا ربنا ولا تحملنا ما لا طاقة لنا به واعف عنا واغفر لنا وارحمنا أنت مولانا فانصرنا على القوم الكافرين

translation: Alif, Lam, Mim.
interpretation: These are among the mysterious letters (muqatta'at) at the beginning of some Qur'anic chapters. Their precise meanings are known only to Allah, but they are believed to hold deep spiritual significance and to signify the miraculous nature of the Qur'an.
orig: الم

translation: Allah - there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of [all] existence.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute oneness and uniqueness of Allah, declaring that He alone is worthy of worship. The attributes 'the Ever-Living' and 'the Sustainer of all existence' highlight His eternal nature and His role in maintaining and governing the universe, underscoring His self-sufficiency and omnipotence.
orig: الله لا إله إلا هو الحي القيوم

translation: The Book has been sent down to you in truth, confirming what was before it, and He revealed the Torah and the Gospel.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin and authenticity of the Qur'an, stating that it has been revealed as a continuation and confirmation of the previous scriptures, namely the Torah and the Gospel. It underscores the unity of the divine message across different revelations, affirming that the Qur'an is part of a consistent series of truths sent by God to guide humanity.
orig: نزل عليك الكتاب بالحق مصدقا لما بين يديه وأنزل التوراة والإنجيل

translation: Before this, as guidance for the people, and He revealed the Criterion. Indeed, those who disbelieve in the verses of Allah will have a severe punishment, and Allah is Exalted in Might, the Owner of Retribution.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin and purpose of the Qur'an as a guide for humanity and a means to distinguish between right and wrong (the Criterion). It serves as a warning to those who reject the signs and messages of Allah, indicating that disbelief leads to a severe punishment. The mention of Allah as 'Exalted in Might' and 'Owner of Retribution' underscores His power and authority to enforce justice and retribution against those who deny His revelations.
orig: من قبل هدى للناس وأنزل الفرقان إن الذين كفروا بآيات الله لهم عذاب شديد والله عزيز ذو انتقام

translation: Indeed, Allah - not hidden from Him is anything in the earth or in the heaven.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience of Allah, indicating that His knowledge encompasses everything in existence, both in the terrestrial and celestial realms. It reassures believers that Allah is aware of all things, seen and unseen, affirming His complete and perfect knowledge over all creation.
orig: إن الله لا يخفى عليه شيء في الأرض ولا في السماء

translation: He is the One Who shapes you in the wombs as He wills. There is no deity except Him, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and sovereignty of Allah over creation. It highlights His role as the sole creator who meticulously designs every human being in the womb according to His divine will. The mention of 'no deity except Him' reinforces the concept of Tawheed, the oneness of God, and His unique attributes of being 'the Exalted in Might' and 'the Wise' underscore His omnipotence and perfect wisdom in all His actions.
orig: هو الذي يصوركم في الأرحام كيف يشاء لا إله إلا هو العزيز الحكيم

translation: He it is Who has sent down to you the Book. In it are verses that are entirely clear, they are the foundations of the Book [and those are the Verses of Al-Ahkam, Al-Fara'id and Al-Hudud]; and others not entirely clear. So as for those in whose hearts there is a deviation [from truth] they follow that which is not entirely clear thereof, seeking Al-Fitnah, and seeking its Ta'wil, but none knows its Ta'wil except Allah. And those who are firmly grounded in knowledge say: "We believe in it; the whole of it is from our Lord." And none receive admonition except men of understanding.
interpretation: This verse highlights the distinction between the clear and the ambiguous verses in the Qur'an. The clear verses, described as the 'mother of the Book,' provide foundational guidance and are straightforward in their meaning. In contrast, the ambiguous verses can be interpreted in various ways. The verse warns that those with deviation in their hearts may exploit these ambiguous parts to cause discord or to seek interpretations that suit their desires, rather than seeking the true meaning intended by Allah. Only Allah fully understands the ultimate interpretation of these ambiguous verses. However, those deeply rooted in knowledge acknowledge the entire Qur'an as divine revelation from Allah and accept it wholly, without being swayed by personal biases. This acceptance and understanding are characteristics of those with true insight and wisdom.
orig: هو الذي أنزل عليك الكتاب منه آيات محكمات هن أم الكتاب وأخر متشابهات فأما الذين في قلوبهم زيغ فيتبعون ما تشابه منه ابتغاء الفتنة وابتغاء تأويله وما يعلم تأويله إلا الله والراسخون في العلم يقولون آمنا به كل من عند ربنا وما يذكر إلا أولو الألباب

translation: Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us, and grant us mercy from Yourself. Indeed, You are the Bestower.
interpretation: This verse is a supplication where believers ask Allah to keep their hearts firm on the path of guidance. It reflects a deep awareness of human vulnerability to stray from righteousness even after receiving guidance. The request for mercy from Allah underscores the believers' recognition of their continuous need for divine support and grace. The attribute of Allah as 'the Bestower' emphasizes His boundless generosity and ability to grant without limit, reinforcing the believers' trust in His providence.
orig: ربنا لا تزغ قلوبنا بعد إذ هديتنا وهب لنا من لدنك رحمة إنك أنت الوهاب

translation: Our Lord, indeed You are the Gatherer of mankind for a Day about which there is no doubt. Indeed, Allah does not fail in His promise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty of the Day of Judgment, affirming that Allah will gather all people on that day, which is inevitable and undeniable. It reassures believers of Allah's unwavering commitment to fulfill His promises, highlighting His attributes of justice and reliability.
orig: ربنا إنك جامع الناس ليوم لا ريب فيه إن الله لا يخلف الميعاد

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve, their wealth and their children will not avail them at all against Allah; and it is they who are the fuel of the Fire.
interpretation: This verse underscores the futility of worldly possessions and familial ties in providing protection or benefit in the eyes of Allah for those who reject faith. It emphasizes that true security and salvation come only through belief and righteousness, not through material wealth or human relationships. Those who disbelieve are warned that their ultimate fate is to serve as fuel for the Hellfire, illustrating the severe consequences of denying the truth.
orig: إن الذين كفروا لن تغني عنهم أموالهم ولا أولادهم من الله شيئا وأولئك هم وقود النار

translation: Like the way of the people of Pharaoh and those before them; they rejected Our signs, so Allah seized them for their sins. And Allah is severe in punishment.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder and warning to those who reject the signs and messages of Allah, drawing a parallel with historical examples like the people of Pharaoh. The rejection of divine guidance leads to divine retribution, emphasizing that Allah's punishment is severe for those who persistently deny His signs. It underscores the importance of heeding divine warnings and the consequences of arrogance and disbelief.
orig: كدأب آل فرعون والذين من قبلهم كذبوا بآياتنا فأخذهم الله بذنوبهم والله شديد العقاب

translation: Say to those who disbelieve, 'You will be overcome and gathered to Hell, and wretched is the resting place.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to those who reject faith, emphasizing the inevitable defeat and ultimate gathering of disbelievers into Hell. It underscores the notion of divine justice where disbelief leads to a miserable end, described here as a wretched resting place. The message is meant to provoke reflection and possibly repentance among the disbelievers by highlighting the dire consequences of their actions.
orig: قل للذين كفروا ستغلبون وتحشرون إلى جهنم وبئس المهاد

translation: There has certainly been for you in the two armies that met an example: one fighting in the cause of Allah and another of disbelievers. They saw them [to be] twice their [own] number by [their] eyesight. But Allah supports with His victory whom He wills. Indeed in that is a lesson for those of vision.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Battle of Badr, where the smaller Muslim army defeated a much larger Meccan force. The lesson here is that apparent numerical or physical strength is not the ultimate determinant of victory; rather, it is Allah's support and will that decides the outcome. This serves as a reminder to believers to trust in Allah's plan and not be disheartened by the apparent power of their adversaries. Those with insight will see this as a sign of divine intervention and a source of hope and perseverance in their faith.
orig: قد كان لكم آية في فئتين التقتا فئة تقاتل في سبيل الله وأخرى كافرة يرونهم مثليهم رأي العين والله يؤيد بنصره من يشاء إن في ذلك لعبرة لأولي الأبصار

translation: Beautified for people is the love of that which they desire - of women and sons, heaped-up sums of gold and silver, fine branded horses, and cattle and tilled land. That is the enjoyment of worldly life, but Allah has with Him the best return.
interpretation: This verse highlights the allure of worldly pleasures and possessions, which are temporary and limited to the life of this world. It serves as a reminder that while these things may be appealing and enjoyable, they should not distract believers from the ultimate goal of seeking the pleasure of Allah and the eternal rewards of the hereafter, which are far superior and everlasting.
orig: زين للناس حب الشهوات من النساء والبنين والقناطير المقنطرة من الذهب والفضة والخيل المسومة والأنعام والحرث ذلك متاع الحياة الدنيا والله عنده حسن المآب

translation: Say, "Shall I inform you of [something] better than that? For those who fear [Allah] will be gardens with their Lord, beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally, and purified spouses and approval from Allah. And Allah is Seeing of [His] servants."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the superiority of the rewards awaiting the pious in the hereafter. It describes Paradise as a place of eternal bliss with flowing rivers, everlasting stay, pure companionship, and divine approval. The mention of Allah's sight over His servants underscores His omniscience and the fairness of His judgment, encouraging believers to strive for righteousness with the assurance that their deeds are seen and will be justly rewarded.
orig: قل أؤنبئكم بخير من ذلكم للذين اتقوا عند ربهم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها وأزواج مطهرة ورضوان من الله والله بصير بالعباد

translation: Those who say, 'Our Lord, indeed we have believed, so forgive us our sins and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of sincere faith and the acknowledgment of one's sins, coupled with a plea for forgiveness and protection from Hell's punishment. It underscores the humility and dependence on God's mercy that believers should exhibit, emphasizing the need for a continuous relationship with God through prayer and repentance.
orig: الذين يقولون ربنا إننا آمنا فاغفر لنا ذنوبنا وقنا عذاب النار

translation: The patient, the true, the obedient, those who spend [in the way of Allah], and those who seek forgiveness before dawn
interpretation: This verse highlights five key virtues that are highly valued in Islam: patience, truthfulness, obedience to Allah, generosity in spending for the sake of Allah, and seeking forgiveness during the early hours of the morning. These qualities are essential for spiritual growth and earning Allah's pleasure. Patience helps believers endure hardships and remain steadfast in faith. Truthfulness fosters integrity and trust within the community. Obedience to Allah's commands demonstrates submission and devotion. Generosity in spending reflects a selfless attitude and support for those in need. Lastly, seeking forgiveness at dawn signifies a sincere repentance and a desire to start each day with a cleansed heart.
orig: الصابرين والصادقين والقانتين والمنفقين والمستغفرين بالأسحار

translation: Allah bears witness that there is no deity except Him, and so do the angels and those of knowledge, maintaining justice. There is no deity except Him, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute oneness of Allah, affirming that He alone is worthy of worship. It highlights that Allah Himself, along with the angels and those endowed with knowledge, testify to His unique divinity. The mention of 'maintaining justice' underscores that this testimony is not just a declaration but is upheld with fairness and equity. The attributes 'the Exalted in Might' and 'the Wise' further describe Allah's omnipotence and wisdom, reinforcing the idea that His sovereignty is both powerful and perfectly reasoned.
orig: شهد الله أنه لا إله إلا هو والملائكة وأولو العلم قائما بالقسط لا إله إلا هو العزيز الحكيم

translation: Indeed, the religion in the sight of Allah is Islam. And those who were given the Scripture did not differ except after knowledge had come to them - out of jealous animosity between themselves. And whoever disbelieves in the verses of Allah, then indeed, Allah is swift in account.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity of the divine message and the finality of Islam as the complete and perfected religion in the eyes of Allah. It suggests that the divergence among the People of the Scripture (Jews and Christians) occurred due to envy and rivalry after the truth was made clear to them. The verse also serves as a warning that disbelief in Allah's signs will be swiftly accounted for, underscoring the urgency and seriousness of adhering to the truth as revealed in Islam.
orig: إن الدين عند الله الإسلام وما اختلف الذين أوتوا الكتاب إلا من بعد ما جاءهم العلم بغيا بينهم ومن يكفر بآيات الله فإن الله سريع الحساب

translation: So if they argue with you, say, 'I have submitted my face to Allah, and those who follow me.' And say to those who were given the Scripture and the unlettered people, 'Have you submitted?' And if they submit, then they are guided; but if they turn away, then upon you is only the notification, and Allah is Seeing of [His] servants.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of submission to Allah as the core of Islamic faith. It instructs the Prophet Muhammad to declare his complete submission to Allah and invites others, both those who have received previous scriptures and those who have not, to do the same. The verse underscores that the role of the Prophet is merely to convey the message of Islam, and it is up to individuals to accept or reject it. Allah's omniscience is highlighted, indicating that He is fully aware of the choices and actions of all people.
orig: فإن حاجوك فقل أسلمت وجهي لله ومن اتبعن وقل للذين أوتوا الكتاب والأميين أأسلمتم فإن أسلموا فقد اهتدوا وإن تولوا فإنما عليك البلاغ والله بصير بالعباد

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve in the verses of Allah and kill the prophets without right and kill those who order justice from among the people - give them tidings of a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe consequences of three grave sins: rejecting the signs and revelations of Allah, unjustly killing prophets, and murdering those who advocate for justice. It serves as a stern warning that such actions will lead to a painful punishment in the hereafter, underscoring the importance of faith, respect for divine messengers, and the promotion of justice within society.
orig: إن الذين يكفرون بآيات الله ويقتلون النبيين بغير حق ويقتلون الذين يأمرون بالقسط من الناس فبشرهم بعذاب أليم

translation: Those are the ones whose deeds have become worthless in this world and in the Hereafter, and for them there will be no helpers.
interpretation: This verse refers to individuals whose actions, due to their lack of faith or sincerity, are rendered void and ineffective in both worldly life and the afterlife. It emphasizes the consequence of such a state where these individuals will find themselves without any supporters or allies, highlighting the isolation and helplessness that results from their invalidated efforts.
orig: أولئك الذين حبطت أعمالهم في الدنيا والآخرة وما لهم من ناصرين

translation: Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture? They are called to the Book of Allah to judge between them, then a group of them turns away and they are averse.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of some people who, despite being given knowledge of the Scripture, refuse to accept the judgment of Allah's Book when it goes against their desires. It points out their selective adherence to religious texts, showing a willingness to invoke the Scripture when it suits them but turning away from it when it challenges their interests or biases. This behavior is a form of rejection and aversion to the divine guidance, illustrating a deeper issue of faith and obedience.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين أوتوا نصيبا من الكتاب يدعون إلى كتاب الله ليحكم بينهم ثم يتولى فريق منهم وهم معرضون

translation: That is because they said, 'The Fire will not touch us except for a few days,' and they were deluded in their religion by what they were inventing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the self-deception and false beliefs of some people who wrongly assume that their punishment in the hereafter will be limited. It warns against the dangers of fabricating religious beliefs to suit one's desires, which leads to a false sense of security and ultimately misguides them in their faith.
orig: ذلك بأنهم قالوا لن تمسنا النار إلا أياما معدودات وغرهم في دينهم ما كانوا يفترون

translation: So how will it be when We gather them for a Day about which there is no doubt, and each soul will be compensated for what it earned, and they will not be wronged?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability and justice of the Day of Judgment. It serves as a reminder to believers that every individual will be held accountable for their actions without any injustice. The phrase 'a Day about which there is no doubt' underscores the certainty of this event, urging people to reflect on their deeds and prepare for the ultimate reckoning where fairness prevails.
orig: فكيف إذا جمعناهم ليوم لا ريب فيه ووفيت كل نفس ما كسبت وهم لا يظلمون

translation: Say, 'O Allah, Owner of Sovereignty, You give sovereignty to whom You will and You take sovereignty away from whom You will. You honor whom You will and You humble whom You will. In Your hand is all good. Indeed, You are over all things competent.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and power of Allah over all aspects of creation. It highlights that Allah alone has the authority to grant or remove power, to elevate or to humble individuals according to His divine wisdom. The phrase 'In Your hand is all good' signifies that all blessings and goodness originate from Allah, and the affirmation 'Indeed, You are over all things competent' underscores His omnipotence and complete control over every detail of the universe. This verse serves as a reminder for believers to trust in Allah's judgment and to recognize His ultimate authority in all matters.
orig: قل اللهم مالك الملك تؤتي الملك من تشاء وتنزع الملك ممن تشاء وتعز من تشاء وتذل من تشاء بيدك الخير إنك على كل شيء قدير

translation: You cause the night to enter into the day, and You cause the day to enter into the night; and You bring the living out of the dead, and You bring the dead out of the living; and You give sustenance to whom You will without limit.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's omnipotence and His control over the natural cycles and life itself. The alternation of night and day symbolizes the continuous cycle of life and death, illustrating Allah's power to transform and renew. The bringing of the living from the dead and vice versa signifies the resurrection and the cycle of life, emphasizing Allah's ability to give life and cause death. The provision of sustenance without measure underscores Allah's boundless generosity and His sovereignty in distributing resources as He sees fit, reminding believers of their dependence on Him and His limitless capacity to provide.
orig: تولج الليل في النهار وتولج النهار في الليل وتخرج الحي من الميت وتخرج الميت من الحي وترزق من تشاء بغير حساب

translation: The believers should not take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. And whoever does that has no connection with Allah, except when you fear from them a danger. And Allah warns you of Himself, and to Allah is the return.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of loyalty and allegiance among believers, cautioning against forming close alliances with those who reject faith, as such actions could compromise one's faith and disconnect them from Allah. However, it acknowledges the necessity of self-preservation in situations of genuine threat, allowing for cautious interactions with non-believers out of fear. The verse serves as a reminder of Allah's oversight and the ultimate accountability to Him, urging believers to maintain their faith and integrity despite external pressures.
orig: لا يتخذ المؤمنون الكافرين أولياء من دون المؤمنين ومن يفعل ذلك فليس من الله في شيء إلا أن تتقوا منهم تقاة ويحذركم الله نفسه وإلى الله المصير

translation: Say, 'Whether you conceal what is in your hearts or reveal it, Allah knows it. And He knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth. And Allah is over all things competent.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience of Allah, indicating that He is fully aware of the innermost thoughts and feelings of every individual, whether they are hidden or expressed. It serves as a reminder to believers to be mindful of their intentions and thoughts, as nothing is hidden from Allah. Additionally, it underscores Allah's complete knowledge of the universe and His supreme power over all creation, reinforcing the concept of His omnipotence and the need for humans to submit to His will.
orig: قل إن تخفوا ما في صدوركم أو تبدوه يعلمه الله ويعلم ما في السماوات وما في الأرض والله على كل شيء قدير

translation: The Day every soul will find what it has done of good present [before it] and what it has done of evil, it will wish that between itself and that [evil] was a great distance. And Allah warns you of Himself, and Allah is Kind to [His] servants.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Day of Judgment, where individuals will be confronted with the full record of their deeds. The good deeds will be readily apparent and welcomed, while the evil deeds will cause regret and a desire to distance oneself from them. The mention of Allah warning us of Himself serves as a reminder of His omnipotence and the seriousness of accountability. The verse concludes by highlighting Allah's kindness and mercy towards His creation, indicating that despite the stern warning, there is hope and compassion from Allah for those who seek His forgiveness and guidance.
orig: يوم تجد كل نفس ما عملت من خير محضرا وما عملت من سوء تود لو أن بينها وبينه أمدا بعيدا ويحذركم الله نفسه والله رءوف بالعباد

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], "If you should love Allah, then follow me, [so] Allah will love you and forgive your sins. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of following the Prophet Muhammad as a means to express one's love for Allah. It suggests that true love for Allah is demonstrated through obedience to the Prophet's guidance. By following him, believers can attain Allah's love and forgiveness, highlighting the merciful and forgiving nature of Allah.
orig: قل إن كنتم تحبون الله فاتبعوني يحببكم الله ويغفر لكم ذنوبكم والله غفور رحيم

translation: Say, 'Obey Allah and the Messenger.' But if they turn away, then indeed, Allah does not like the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to Allah and His Messenger as a fundamental aspect of faith. It instructs the Prophet Muhammad to convey this message clearly to the people. The latter part of the verse addresses the consequence of rejecting this call, indicating that turning away from the guidance of Allah and His Messenger leads to disbelief, which is displeasing to Allah. This highlights the seriousness of rejecting divine guidance and underscores the necessity of adherence to the teachings of Islam for spiritual well-being.
orig: قل أطيعوا الله والرسول فإن تولوا فإن الله لا يحب الكافرين

translation: Indeed, Allah chose Adam and Noah, and the family of Abraham and the family of 'Imran above the worlds.
interpretation: This verse highlights the special selection by Allah of these individuals and their families for their righteousness and devotion. It underscores the divine favor and the significant roles they played in guiding humanity towards the worship of one God, emphasizing their elevated status among all creation.
orig: إن الله اصطفى آدم ونوحا وآل إبراهيم وآل عمران على العالمين

translation: Offspring, some of them from others. And Allah is Hearing, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the interconnectedness of human generations, illustrating how each generation descends from the previous one, forming a continuous chain of lineage. The mention of Allah as 'Hearing' and 'Knowing' underscores His omniscience and awareness of all familial and generational relationships, indicating that He is fully aware of the lineage and the deeds of every individual.
orig: ذرية بعضها من بعض والله سميع عليم

translation: When the wife of 'Imran said, 'My Lord, I have vowed to You what is in my womb, to be dedicated [to Your service], so accept [this] from me. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the sincerity and devotion of the wife of 'Imran, who is dedicating her unborn child to the service of God. It reflects the importance of making sincere vows to God and trusting in His acceptance and omniscience. The attributes of God mentioned, 'the Hearing, the Knowing,' emphasize that God is fully aware of and responsive to the intentions and prayers of His servants.
orig: إذ قالت امرأت عمران رب إني نذرت لك ما في بطني محررا فتقبل مني إنك أنت السميع العليم

translation: So when she delivered her, she said, 'My Lord, I have delivered a female.' And Allah was most knowing of what she had delivered, 'And the male is not like the female. And I have named her Mary, and I seek refuge for her in You and [for] her descendants from Satan, the expelled [from the mercy of Allah].'
interpretation: This verse reflects the moment when Hannah, the mother of Mary, expressed her surprise and submission to God's will upon giving birth to a daughter instead of the son she had vowed to dedicate to the service of the temple. Her statement, 'the male is not like the female,' acknowledges the societal preference for males at the time, yet she accepts God's choice with faith and trust. By naming her daughter Mary and seeking refuge for her and her descendants from Satan, Hannah demonstrates her deep faith and protective love, entrusting Mary's spiritual safety to God. This act underscores the theme of divine wisdom surpassing human understanding and the importance of faith in God's plan.
orig: فلما وضعتها قالت رب إني وضعتها أنثى والله أعلم بما وضعت وليس الذكر كالأنثى وإني سميتها مريم وإني أعيذها بك وذريتها من الشيطان الرجيم

translation: So her Lord accepted her with good acceptance and caused her to grow in a good manner and put her in the care of Zechariah. Every time Zechariah entered upon her in the prayer chamber, he found with her provision. He said, 'O Mary, from where has this come to you?' She said, 'It is from Allah. Indeed, Allah provides for whom He wills without account.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the divine favor and miraculous provision bestowed upon Mary by Allah. It emphasizes Allah's boundless generosity and His ability to provide for His chosen servants in ways that surpass human understanding and expectation. The acceptance of Mary and her miraculous sustenance highlight her special status and the purity of her devotion, serving as a testament to the unseen support and blessings that Allah grants to those who are sincere in their faith and obedience.
orig: فتقبلها ربها بقبول حسن وأنبتها نباتا حسنا وكفلها زكريا كلما دخل عليها زكريا المحراب وجد عندها رزقا قال يا مريم أنى لك هذا قالت هو من عند الله إن الله يرزق من يشاء بغير حساب

translation: There Zechariah called upon his Lord, saying, 'My Lord, grant me from Yourself a good offspring. Indeed, You are the Hearer of supplication.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound faith and humility of Zechariah as he prays for a righteous child, acknowledging God's omnipotence and His attentiveness to the prayers of His servants. It underscores the theme of divine responsiveness to sincere supplications, emphasizing that God listens and can fulfill the deepest desires of the heart when they align with His will.
orig: هنالك دعا زكريا ربه قال رب هب لي من لدنك ذرية طيبة إنك سميع الدعاء

translation: Then the angels called him while he was standing in prayer in the chamber, 'Indeed, Allah gives you glad tidings of John, confirming a Word from Allah and [he will be] noble, chaste, and a prophet from among the righteous.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine announcement to Zechariah about the birth of his son, John (Yahya), during his prayer. It underscores the miraculous nature of this announcement, as John was to be a confirmation of God's word, a leader, pure, and a prophet among the righteous. This emphasizes God's power to bestow blessings and fulfill His promises, even when they seem impossible by human standards, and it serves as a reminder of the importance of faith and devotion in receiving divine favor.
orig: فنادته الملائكة وهو قائم يصلي في المحراب أن الله يبشرك بيحيى مصدقا بكلمة من الله وسيدا وحصورا ونبيا من الصالحين

translation: He said, 'My Lord, how will I have a boy when I have reached old age and my wife is barren?' He said, 'Thus Allah does what He wills.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of divine omnipotence and the miraculous nature of God's power. Zachariah, despite his old age and his wife's barrenness, is promised a son by God, illustrating that God's will transcends human limitations and natural laws. It serves as a reminder to believers of the boundless capabilities of Allah, encouraging faith and trust in His divine plan even when circumstances seem impossible.
orig: قال رب أنى يكون لي غلام وقد بلغني الكبر وامرأتي عاقر قال كذلك الله يفعل ما يشاء

translation: He said, 'My Lord, make for me a sign.' He said, 'Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three days except by gesture. And remember your Lord much and glorify [Him] in the evening and the morning.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of patience and reliance on God. When Zechariah asked for a sign from God, he was given a test of silence for three days, symbolizing a period of reflection and dependence on divine guidance. The instruction to remember and glorify God frequently underscores the necessity of maintaining a strong spiritual connection through constant remembrance and praise, especially during times of trial.
orig: قال رب اجعل لي آية قال آيتك ألا تكلم الناس ثلاثة أيام إلا رمزا واذكر ربك كثيرا وسبح بالعشي والإبكار

translation: And [mention] when the angels said, 'O Mary, indeed Allah has chosen you and purified you and chosen you above the women of the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the special status and honor bestowed upon Mary by Allah. It underscores her purity and divine selection, indicating that she was chosen for a significant role in the divine plan, surpassing all other women in her time and beyond. This emphasizes her exemplary faith and righteousness, serving as a model for believers.
orig: وإذ قالت الملائكة يا مريم إن الله اصطفاك وطهرك واصطفاك على نساء العالمين

translation: O Mary, be devoutly obedient to your Lord and prostrate and bow with those who bow [in prayer].
interpretation: This verse is a direct command to Mary, emphasizing the importance of devotion and submission to God. It instructs her to engage in physical acts of worship, such as prostration and bowing, alongside others who are performing these acts of prayer. The emphasis on joining others in worship highlights the communal aspect of faith and the importance of aligning oneself with the faithful in acts of submission to God.
orig: يا مريم اقنتي لربك واسجدي واركعي مع الراكعين

translation: That is from the news of the unseen which We reveal to you. And you were not with them when they cast their pens as to which of them should take charge of Mary, nor were you with them when they were disputing.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine origin of the Qur'anic revelations, emphasizing that the Prophet Muhammad was not present during historical events such as the casting of lots to determine who would guardianship over Mary. It highlights the miraculous nature of the Qur'an, as it contains knowledge of unseen events that could only have been revealed by God, thereby affirming the authenticity and trustworthiness of the Qur'anic narrative.
orig: ذلك من أنباء الغيب نوحيه إليك وما كنت لديهم إذ يلقون أقلامهم أيهم يكفل مريم وما كنت لديهم إذ يختصمون

translation: When the angels said, 'O Mary, indeed Allah gives you good tidings of a word from Him, whose name will be the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary - distinguished in this world and the Hereafter and among those brought near [to Allah].'
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine announcement to Mary about the birth of Jesus, emphasizing his miraculous nature as a 'word from Allah' and his esteemed status both in worldly life and in the hereafter. It underscores Jesus's role as the Messiah and his close relationship with Allah, indicating his significant spiritual position and mission.
orig: إذ قالت الملائكة يا مريم إن الله يبشرك بكلمة منه اسمه المسيح عيسى ابن مريم وجيها في الدنيا والآخرة ومن المقربين

translation: And he will speak to the people in the cradle and in maturity and will be of the righteous.
interpretation: This verse refers to Prophet Jesus (Isa), son of Mary, indicating his miraculous ability to speak as an infant in the cradle, as well as in his adulthood. This ability underscores his prophethood and divine mission. The verse also highlights that Jesus will be among the righteous, emphasizing his moral and spiritual excellence throughout his life.
orig: ويكلم الناس في المهد وكهلا ومن الصالحين

translation: She said, 'My Lord, how will I have a child when no man has touched me?' He said, 'Thus Allah creates what He wills. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, 'Be,' and it is.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the omnipotence of Allah, illustrating that His power transcends natural laws. Maryam's question about having a child without human intervention is answered by affirming that Allah's will is the ultimate cause of creation, needing only His command, 'Be,' to bring anything into existence. This emphasizes the concept of divine decree and the miraculous nature of Jesus's birth, reinforcing faith in Allah's boundless capabilities.
orig: قالت رب أنى يكون لي ولد ولم يمسسني بشر قال كذلك الله يخلق ما يشاء إذا قضى أمرا فإنما يقول له كن فيكون

translation: And He will teach him the Book and wisdom and the Torah and the Gospel
interpretation: This verse refers to the divine knowledge and guidance that God bestowed upon Jesus. The 'Book' symbolizes comprehensive divine knowledge, while 'wisdom' indicates the ability to apply this knowledge appropriately. The mention of the Torah and the Gospel specifically highlights that Jesus was given insight into these scriptures, affirming his role in continuing and fulfilling the prophetic tradition. This teaching underscores Jesus's mission to guide humanity with divine wisdom and scriptural knowledge.
orig: ويعلمه الكتاب والحكمة والتوراة والإنجيل

translation: And (make him) a messenger to the Children of Israel (saying), 'Indeed I have come to you with a sign from your Lord - that I design for you from clay (a figure) like the shape of a bird, then I breathe into it and it becomes a bird by permission of Allah. And I cure the blind and the leper, and I give life to the dead - by permission of Allah. And I inform you of what you eat and what you store in your houses. Indeed in that is a sign for you, if you are believers.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the miraculous signs that Prophet Jesus (Isa) was given as a messenger to the Children of Israel. These miracles, such as creating life from clay, healing the sick, reviving the dead, and knowing the unseen, were performed by the permission of Allah, emphasizing Jesus's role as a prophet and servant of God. The verse serves as a reminder to the believers of the power of Allah and the authenticity of Jesus's prophethood, urging them to recognize these signs as evidence of faith.
orig: ورسولا إلى بني إسرائيل أني قد جئتكم بآية من ربكم أني أخلق لكم من الطين كهيئة الطير فأنفخ فيه فيكون طيرا بإذن الله وأبرئ الأكمه والأبرص وأحيي الموتى بإذن الله وأنبئكم بما تأكلون وما تدخرون في بيوتكم إن في ذلك لآية لكم إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: And confirming what was before me of the Torah, and to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you. And I have come to you with a sign from your Lord, so fear Allah and obey me.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the continuity and confirmation of the divine message across different scriptures, specifically highlighting that the message brought by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) aligns with and validates the teachings of the Torah. It also indicates a change in some religious rulings, making previously forbidden things permissible, which reflects the adaptability of divine law to different times and contexts. The verse further underscores the importance of recognizing the signs of God through the Prophet, urging believers to fear God and follow the Prophet's guidance, which is essential for spiritual and moral rectitude.
orig: ومصدقا لما بين يدي من التوراة ولأحل لكم بعض الذي حرم عليكم وجئتكم بآية من ربكم فاتقوا الله وأطيعون

translation: Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity of God as the Lord of all, calling for the worship of Allah alone. It serves as a reminder that recognizing and submitting to the oneness of God is the fundamental principle of Islam, guiding believers on the straight path towards righteousness and away from idolatry and polytheism.
orig: إن الله ربي وربكم فاعبدوه هذا صراط مستقيم

translation: So when Jesus felt disbelief from them, he said, 'Who are my supporters for [the cause of] Allah?' The disciples said, 'We are supporters of Allah. We have believed in Allah and bear witness that we are Muslims [submitting to Him].'
interpretation: This verse highlights the moment when Jesus, recognizing the disbelief among the people, sought out those who would stand with him in devotion to Allah. It underscores the importance of faith and submission to God, illustrating that true support for a divine cause comes from those who sincerely believe and publicly affirm their submission to Allah's will. The disciples' response signifies their commitment to faith over societal disbelief, emphasizing the value of steadfastness in belief even in the face of opposition.
orig: فلما أحس عيسى منهم الكفر قال من أنصاري إلى الله قال الحواريون نحن أنصار الله آمنا بالله واشهد بأنا مسلمون

translation: Our Lord, we have believed in what You have sent down and have followed the messenger, so register us among the witnesses.
interpretation: This verse is a supplication where believers express their faith in the revelations sent by Allah and their commitment to follow the Prophet Muhammad. By asking to be registered among the witnesses, they are seeking to be counted among those who testify to the truth of Islam and who will bear witness on the Day of Judgment to their faith and actions. This reflects a deep desire for divine acceptance and recognition of their sincerity and obedience.
orig: ربنا آمنا بما أنزلت واتبعنا الرسول فاكتبنا مع الشاهدين

translation: And they plotted and Allah plotted, and Allah is the best of plotters.
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of divine providence and the ultimate futility of human schemes against God's will. It suggests that while humans may engage in deceitful planning, God's counter-planning is superior and always prevails, emphasizing His omnipotence and wisdom in guiding the course of events to His desired outcome.
orig: ومكروا ومكر الله والله خير الماكرين

translation: When Allah said, 'O Jesus, indeed I will take you and raise you to Myself and purify you from those who disbelieve and make those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection. Then to Me is your return, and I will judge between you concerning that in which you used to differ.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the event of Jesus's ascension, emphasizing that Allah will take Jesus's soul, elevate him to a higher spiritual realm, and cleanse him from the false accusations and disbelief of his detractors. It also highlights the divine promise to elevate the status of Jesus's followers above that of the disbelievers until the Day of Judgment. The verse concludes with a reminder of the ultimate return to Allah, who will adjudicate the disputes and differences that existed among people during their earthly lives, underscoring the themes of divine justice and accountability.
orig: إذ قال الله يا عيسى إني متوفيك ورافعك إلي ومطهرك من الذين كفروا وجاعل الذين اتبعوك فوق الذين كفروا إلى يوم القيامة ثم إلي مرجعكم فأحكم بينكم فيما كنتم فيه تختلفون

translation: As for those who disbelieve, I will punish them with a severe punishment in this world and the Hereafter, and they will have no helpers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequences of disbelief, indicating that those who reject faith will face severe punishment both in the worldly life and in the afterlife. The mention of 'no helpers' underscores the isolation and helplessness of disbelievers in facing divine judgment, highlighting the importance of faith and obedience to avoid such a fate.
orig: فأما الذين كفروا فأعذبهم عذابا شديدا في الدنيا والآخرة وما لهم من ناصرين

translation: And as for those who believed and did righteous deeds, He will give them their rewards, and Allah does not love the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine promise of reward for those who have faith and perform good deeds, highlighting the justice and fairness of Allah. It also serves as a reminder of Allah's disapproval of injustice, reinforcing the moral imperative for believers to act righteously and justly in all their actions.
orig: وأما الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات فيوفيهم أجورهم والله لا يحب الظالمين

translation: That is what We recite to you from the verses and the wise Reminder.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an, referred to as "the wise Reminder," is being revealed and recited to the Prophet Muhammad. It underscores the divine origin of the Qur'an, highlighting its role as a source of guidance and wisdom for humanity. The use of "We" signifies the majesty and authority of Allah in conveying these sacred verses.
orig: ذلك نتلوه عليك من الآيات والذكر الحكيم

translation: The example of Jesus with Allah is like the example of Adam. He created him from dust, then said to him, 'Be,' and he was.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the miraculous nature of Jesus's creation by drawing a parallel with Adam, highlighting that both were created by God's command without the need for a human father. It underscores the omnipotence of Allah, who can bring into existence whatever He wills, simply by decreeing it to be.
orig: إن مثل عيسى عند الله كمثل آدم خلقه من تراب ثم قال له كن فيكون

translation: The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty and authenticity of the revelation from Allah. It urges believers to have unwavering faith in the divine message and not to fall into skepticism or doubt about the truths conveyed by the Qur'an. The call to not be among the doubters is an encouragement to maintain strong conviction in the face of any challenges or contrary opinions.
orig: الحق من ربك فلا تكن من الممترين

translation: So whoever disputes with you concerning him, after the knowledge that has come to you, say: 'Come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves, then we pray and invoke the curse of Allah upon those who lie.'
interpretation: This verse refers to the event known as 'Mubahala,' where the Prophet Muhammad was challenged by the Christians of Najran regarding the nature of Jesus. The verse instructs the Prophet to propose a mutual curse (Mubahala) to settle the dispute. The inclusion of 'our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves' signifies the seriousness and the communal aspect of the challenge, emphasizing the willingness to bring the closest and most beloved to participate in this solemn act. The verse underscores the confidence in the truth of the Prophet's message and the readiness to invoke divine judgment to distinguish truth from falsehood.
orig: فمن حاجك فيه من بعد ما جاءك من العلم فقل تعالوا ندع أبناءنا وأبناءكم ونساءنا ونساءكم وأنفسنا وأنفسكم ثم نبتهل فنجعل لعنت الله على الكاذبين

translation: Indeed, this is the true account, and there is no deity except Allah, and indeed, Allah is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the authenticity and truthfulness of the narratives presented in the Qur'an, affirming that they are not mere stories but factual accounts. It also reinforces the central Islamic belief in the oneness of God, declaring that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah. The attributes of Allah as the Exalted in Might and the Wise underscore His supreme power and perfect wisdom in all His actions and decrees, encouraging believers to trust in His divine plan and governance.
orig: إن هذا لهو القصص الحق وما من إله إلا الله وإن الله لهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: But if they turn away, then indeed, Allah is Knowing of the corrupters.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that if people reject the message of Islam and turn away from the truth, Allah is fully aware of their corrupt intentions and actions. It underscores the notion that no one can escape the knowledge and judgment of Allah, who sees and understands the true nature of those who cause corruption and mischief.
orig: فإن تولوا فإن الله عليم بالمفسدين

translation: Say, 'O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable between us and you - that we will not worship except Allah and not associate anything with Him and not take one another as lords instead of Allah.' But if they turn away, then say, 'Bear witness that we are Muslims.'
interpretation: This verse is an invitation to the People of the Scripture (Jews and Christians) to unite on the fundamental belief in the oneness of God (Tawheed). It emphasizes the rejection of polytheism and the elevation of any human to a divine status. The verse suggests a common ground for dialogue and mutual understanding based on monotheism. If this invitation is rejected, Muslims are instructed to affirm their submission to God alone, highlighting the clarity and firmness of their faith.
orig: قل يا أهل الكتاب تعالوا إلى كلمة سواء بيننا وبينكم ألا نعبد إلا الله ولا نشرك به شيئا ولا يتخذ بعضنا بعضا أربابا من دون الله فإن تولوا فقولوا اشهدوا بأنا مسلمون

translation: O People of the Scripture, why do you argue about Abraham while the Torah and the Gospel were not revealed until after him? Have you then no sense?
interpretation: This verse addresses the Jews and Christians, collectively referred to as the People of the Scripture, and critiques their disputes over the religious significance of Abraham. It points out the chronological inconsistency in their arguments since both the Torah and the Gospel were revealed after Abraham's time. The rhetorical question at the end emphasizes the need for logical reasoning and reflection on their part, urging them to reconsider their claims in light of historical and scriptural facts.
orig: يا أهل الكتاب لم تحاجون في إبراهيم وما أنزلت التوراة والإنجيل إلا من بعده أفلا تعقلون

translation: Here you are - those who have argued about that of which you have [some] knowledge, but why do you argue about that of which you have no knowledge? And Allah knows, while you know not.
interpretation: This verse criticizes the human tendency to engage in debates and disputes over matters about which they possess only partial or superficial knowledge, while confidently avoiding discussion on topics where their ignorance is complete. It highlights the arrogance and folly of arguing without sufficient understanding, emphasizing that true knowledge belongs to Allah alone. The verse serves as a reminder for believers to be humble and cautious in their claims, recognizing the limits of their own knowledge and deferring ultimately to the omniscience of Allah.
orig: ها أنتم هؤلاء حاججتم فيما لكم به علم فلم تحاجون فيما ليس لكم به علم والله يعلم وأنتم لا تعلمون

translation: Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was a monotheist, a Muslim, and he was not of the polytheists.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Prophet Abraham adhered to the pure monotheistic faith, submitting to the will of God alone, which is the essence of Islam. It clarifies that the religious identities of Judaism and Christianity, which came after Abraham, do not define his faith. Instead, Abraham's faith is described as 'hanif', indicating his unwavering commitment to monotheism, and 'muslim', signifying his submission to God. The verse also distinguishes Abraham from polytheists, underlining his rejection of associating partners with God.
orig: ما كان إبراهيم يهوديا ولا نصرانيا ولكن كان حنيفا مسلما وما كان من المشركين

translation: Indeed, the people most worthy of Abraham are those who followed him and this prophet and those who believe. And Allah is the ally of the believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the spiritual lineage and connection to Prophet Abraham, indicating that those who truly follow his path are the believers in Islam, including the followers of Prophet Muhammad. It underscores the unity of faith across time and the special relationship believers have with Allah, who is described as their protector and ally.
orig: إن أولى الناس بإبراهيم للذين اتبعوه وهذا النبي والذين آمنوا والله ولي المؤمنين

translation: A faction of the People of the Scripture wish they could mislead you. But they do not mislead except themselves, and they perceive it not.
interpretation: This verse highlights the misguided intentions of some from the People of the Scripture who aim to lead Muslims astray from their faith. However, their efforts are futile and only result in their own spiritual loss, which they fail to recognize. It serves as a reminder to Muslims to remain steadfast in their faith and not be swayed by external influences, emphasizing the concept of personal accountability in one's spiritual journey.
orig: ودت طائفة من أهل الكتاب لو يضلونكم وما يضلون إلا أنفسهم وما يشعرون

translation: O People of the Scripture, why do you disbelieve in the verses of Allah while you witness [to their truth]?
interpretation: This verse addresses the Jews and Christians, referred to as the People of the Scripture, questioning their rejection of the signs and revelations of Allah despite their knowledge and recognition of these truths. It highlights the inconsistency and the moral responsibility they bear for denying what they know to be true, urging them to reflect on their actions and beliefs.
orig: يا أهل الكتاب لم تكفرون بآيات الله وأنتم تشهدون

translation: O People of the Scripture, why do you mix the truth with falsehood and conceal the truth while you know?
interpretation: This verse addresses the People of the Scripture, referring to Jews and Christians, admonishing them for deliberately distorting the truth by mixing it with falsehood and hiding the clear signs and prophecies about the Prophet Muhammad in their scriptures, despite their knowledge of the truth. It highlights the seriousness of such actions and calls for integrity and honesty in conveying religious truths.
orig: يا أهل الكتاب لم تلبسون الحق بالباطل وتكتمون الحق وأنتم تعلمون

translation: And a group from the People of the Book said, 'Believe in what has been revealed to those who believed at the beginning of the day, and disbelieve at its end, perhaps they will return [to our faith].'
interpretation: This verse highlights a strategic deception employed by some members of the People of the Book. They advised their followers to outwardly express belief in the revelations given to Muslims during the day, but to revert to disbelief by the end of the day. The intention behind this tactic was to test the Muslims' faith and potentially lure them back to their own religion. This reflects a deeper theme of the challenges faced by early Muslims and the importance of steadfastness in faith amidst external pressures and deceit.
orig: وقالت طائفة من أهل الكتاب آمنوا بالذي أنزل على الذين آمنوا وجه النهار واكفروا آخره لعلهم يرجعون

translation: And do not believe except those who follow your religion. Say, 'Indeed, the guidance is the guidance of Allah, lest someone be given the like of that which you have been given or they argue with you before your Lord.' Say, 'Indeed, the bounty is in the hand of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills. And Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of recognizing that true guidance comes solely from Allah, not from following a particular religious group or tradition. It warns against the arrogance of believing that one's own religious path is the only valid one, and instead encourages humility and openness to the possibility that Allah may guide others in ways that might differ from one's own experiences. The verse also underscores Allah's sovereignty and wisdom in distributing His blessings and guidance as He sees fit, reminding believers that His knowledge and generosity are boundless.
orig: ولا تؤمنوا إلا لمن تبع دينكم قل إن الهدى هدى الله أن يؤتى أحد مثل ما أوتيتم أو يحاجوكم عند ربكم قل إن الفضل بيد الله يؤتيه من يشاء والله واسع عليم

translation: He selects for His mercy whom He wills, and Allah is the Possessor of great bounty.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine prerogative of Allah to bestow His mercy upon whomever He chooses, emphasizing His absolute sovereignty and wisdom in His decisions. It serves as a reminder to believers of the boundless and selective nature of Allah's grace, encouraging them to remain hopeful and submissive to His will, knowing that His mercy and generosity are immense and beyond human comprehension.
orig: يختص برحمته من يشاء والله ذو الفضل العظيم

translation: And among the People of the Scripture is he who, if you entrust him with a great amount [of wealth], he will return it to you. And among them is he who, if you entrust him with a single coin, he will not return it to you unless you constantly stand over him [demanding it]. That is because they say, 'There is no blame upon us concerning the unlettered ones.' And they speak untruth about Allah while they know [it].
interpretation: This verse highlights the diversity in trustworthiness among the People of the Scripture. It points out that while some are honest and reliable, others are not, reflecting on their moral integrity. The verse also criticizes a specific justification used by some for their dishonest behavior towards non-Jews or non-Christians, claiming it is permissible based on a misinterpretation of religious texts. Furthermore, it condemns those who falsely attribute such permissibility to God, knowing well that it contradicts divine justice and morality.
orig: ومن أهل الكتاب من إن تأمنه بقنطار يؤده إليك ومنهم من إن تأمنه بدينار لا يؤده إليك إلا ما دمت عليه قائما ذلك بأنهم قالوا ليس علينا في الأميين سبيل ويقولون على الله الكذب وهم يعلمون

translation: Yes, whoever fulfills his pledge and fears Allah - then indeed, Allah loves the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of keeping one's promises and maintaining a state of piety. It suggests that fulfilling obligations and being conscious of Allah's commands are qualities that attract divine love. The verse encourages believers to be trustworthy and God-fearing, as these traits are highly valued by Allah.
orig: بلى من أوفى بعهده واتقى فإن الله يحب المتقين

translation: Indeed, those who purchase with the covenant of Allah and their oaths a small price, those - there is no share for them in the Hereafter, and Allah will not speak to them, nor will He look at them on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify them, and for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe consequences of betraying one's covenant with Allah and breaking oaths for worldly gains. It underscores the importance of integrity and faithfulness to one's commitments to Allah, warning that such betrayal leads to exclusion from divine favor and mercy in the afterlife, culminating in a painful punishment. The verse serves as a reminder of the gravity of one's spiritual obligations and the eternal ramifications of neglecting them.
orig: إن الذين يشترون بعهد الله وأيمانهم ثمنا قليلا أولئك لا خلاق لهم في الآخرة ولا يكلمهم الله ولا ينظر إليهم يوم القيامة ولا يزكيهم ولهم عذاب أليم

translation: And indeed, among them is a group that distorts the Scripture with their tongues so you may think it is from the Scripture, but it is not from the Scripture. And they say, 'This is from Allah,' but it is not from Allah. And they speak lies about Allah while they know.
interpretation: This verse addresses the issue of religious distortion and deceit by certain individuals who falsely claim that their statements or interpretations are part of the divine scripture. It highlights the deliberate manipulation of religious texts by a group who twist the meanings of the words to suit their own purposes, misleading others into believing these distortions are from God. This act is condemned as a grave sin, especially because these individuals are fully aware of their deceit, yet they continue to attribute falsehoods to Allah, thereby committing a serious transgression against the truth and integrity of divine revelation.
orig: وإن منهم لفريقا يلوون ألسنتهم بالكتاب لتحسبوه من الكتاب وما هو من الكتاب ويقولون هو من عند الله وما هو من عند الله ويقولون على الله الكذب وهم يعلمون

translation: It is not for a human being that Allah should give him the Scripture and authority and prophethood and then he would say to the people, "Be servants to me rather than Allah," but [instead, he would say], "Be pious scholars of the Lord, because of what you have been teaching of the Scripture and because of what you have been studying."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the responsibility of those who are given divine knowledge and authority, such as prophets and religious scholars. It highlights that such individuals should never use their position to elevate themselves to a status of worship or obedience above Allah. Instead, they are instructed to guide people towards becoming knowledgeable and pious servants of Allah, using the knowledge they have gained from the Scripture and their studies. The verse serves as a reminder and a warning against the misuse of religious authority for personal gain or veneration.
orig: ما كان لبشر أن يؤتيه الله الكتاب والحكم والنبوة ثم يقول للناس كونوا عبادا لي من دون الله ولكن كونوا ربانيين بما كنتم تعلمون الكتاب وبما كنتم تدرسون

translation: And He does not command you to take the angels and the prophets as lords. Would He command you to disbelieve after you have been Muslims?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness of God and warns against associating partners with Him, even if those partners are revered figures like angels and prophets. It underscores that such an action would be tantamount to disbelief, contradicting the fundamental principle of Islam which is submission to the one true God. The verse serves as a reminder to Muslims to maintain their faith purely and not to elevate any created being to the status of divinity.
orig: ولا يأمركم أن تتخذوا الملائكة والنبيين أربابا أيأمركم بالكفر بعد إذ أنتم مسلمون

translation: And [mention] when Allah took the covenant of the prophets, [saying], 'Whatever I have given you of the Scripture and wisdom, then there comes to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you must believe in him and support him.' [Allah] said, 'Have you acknowledged and taken upon that My covenant?' They said, 'We have acknowledged.' He said, 'Then bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the unity of divine revelation across different prophets and scriptures. It highlights that all prophets, regardless of their time or community, were bound by a covenant with Allah to believe in and support any future messenger who confirms the truth of their own scriptures. This emphasizes the continuity and consistency of the message of monotheism and submission to Allah's will, culminating in the prophethood of Muhammad, who is seen as the final messenger confirming the previous scriptures. The verse also establishes a collective testimony among the prophets and Allah Himself, reinforcing the solemnity and binding nature of this covenant.
