orig: وإذ أخذ الله ميثاق النبيين لما آتيتكم من كتاب وحكمة ثم جاءكم رسول مصدق لما معكم لتؤمنن به ولتنصرنه قال أأقررتم وأخذتم على ذلكم إصري قالوا أقررنا قال فاشهدوا وأنا معكم من الشاهدين

translation: So whoever turns away after that - those are the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequences of rejecting guidance after it has been clearly presented. It suggests that those who consciously choose to turn away from the truth, despite having knowledge of it, are categorized as 'fasiqoon' or the defiantly disobedient. This indicates a deliberate act of rebellion against divine guidance, highlighting the severity of such a choice in the eyes of Allah.
orig: فمن تولى بعد ذلك فأولئك هم الفاسقون

translation: Do they seek other than the religion of Allah, while to Him submitted all creatures in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly, and to Him they shall be returned?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universal submission to Allah's will, indicating that all creation, whether in the heavens or on earth, is inherently subject to His sovereignty. It challenges those who might seek an alternative to Islam, reminding them that ultimately, everything and everyone will return to Allah, reinforcing the concept of the oneness of God and the inevitability of returning to Him.
orig: أفغير دين الله يبغون وله أسلم من في السماوات والأرض طوعا وكرها وإليه يرجعون

translation: Say, 'We have believed in Allah and what has been revealed to us and what was revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the Descendants, and what was given to Moses and Jesus and the prophets from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them, and to Him we are Muslims.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity of faith across different prophets and scriptures, asserting that Muslims believe in all the revelations sent by Allah to various prophets from Adam to Muhammad, without differentiating between them. It underscores the concept of Islam as submission to the will of Allah, which is the essence of the message brought by all prophets. This declaration of faith serves as a fundamental statement of belief, promoting a universal message of monotheism and submission to God, transcending time and specific religious communities.
orig: قل آمنا بالله وما أنزل علينا وما أنزل على إبراهيم وإسماعيل وإسحاق ويعقوب والأسباط وما أوتي موسى وعيسى والنبيون من ربهم لا نفرق بين أحد منهم ونحن له مسلمون

translation: And whoever seeks a religion other than Islam, it will never be accepted from him, and in the Hereafter he will be among the losers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the finality and completeness of Islam as the religion chosen by Allah for humanity. It suggests that rejecting Islam in favor of another religion leads to a loss of divine acceptance and spiritual success in the afterlife, underscoring the importance of adhering to the path of Islam for ultimate salvation.
orig: ومن يبتغ غير الإسلام دينا فلن يقبل منه وهو في الآخرة من الخاسرين

translation: How shall Allah guide a people who disbelieved after their belief and had witnessed that the Messenger is true and clear signs had come to them? And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse questions the possibility of divine guidance for those who revert to disbelief after having faith. It emphasizes the severity of rejecting faith after having clear evidence and witnessing the truth of the Prophet. The rhetorical question suggests that such a reversal is a profound betrayal of the truth they once acknowledged. The verse concludes by stating that Allah does not guide those who are unjust, indicating that persistent injustice and rejection of clear signs lead to a state where divine guidance is no longer accessible.
orig: كيف يهدي الله قوما كفروا بعد إيمانهم وشهدوا أن الرسول حق وجاءهم البينات والله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: Those - their recompense is that upon them is the curse of Allah, and the angels, and all of mankind.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who have committed grave sins and injustices, indicating that their punishment is severe and universal. The curse from Allah, the angels, and all of mankind signifies complete rejection and isolation from divine and communal acceptance, emphasizing the gravity of their actions and the unanimous condemnation they face.
orig: أولئك جزاؤهم أن عليهم لعنة الله والملائكة والناس أجمعين

translation: Abiding therein, the punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be reprieved.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the permanence and severity of the punishment in Hell for those who are condemned to it. It underscores that there will be no relief or respite from the torment, highlighting the gravity of the consequences of one's actions in the afterlife. The eternal nature of the punishment serves as a stark warning and a call to righteousness and repentance in this life.
orig: خالدين فيها لا يخفف عنهم العذاب ولا هم ينظرون

translation: Except for those who repent thereafter and reform, for indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the mercy and forgiveness of Allah, emphasizing that even after committing sins, if a person sincerely repents and makes amends, they can still attain Allah's forgiveness. It underscores the importance of repentance and the continuous opportunity for spiritual renewal and moral improvement.
orig: إلا الذين تابوا من بعد ذلك وأصلحوا فإن الله غفور رحيم

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve after their belief and then increase in disbelief - never will their [claimed] repentance be accepted, and they are the ones astray.
interpretation: This verse addresses the severity of apostasy, emphasizing that those who revert to disbelief after having faith and further deepen their rejection of faith will not have their repentance accepted. It underscores the importance of steadfastness in faith, warning that increasing in disbelief after having believed leads one astray from the path of guidance, resulting in a state from which repentance is not accepted.
orig: إن الذين كفروا بعد إيمانهم ثم ازدادوا كفرا لن تقبل توبتهم وأولئك هم الضالون

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers - never would the (whole) earth full of gold be accepted from one of them if he offered it as a ransom. For them there will be a painful punishment, and they will have no helpers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the irrevocable nature of disbelief upon death. It teaches that once a person dies in a state of disbelief, no amount of worldly wealth or material offering can change their fate or buy their way into Paradise. The mention of 'the earth full of gold' emphasizes the futility of any attempt at redemption after death. The verse also highlights the severe consequence of disbelief - a painful punishment in the hereafter, and the complete isolation of the disbelievers, as they will have no helpers or intercessors to aid them.
orig: إن الذين كفروا وماتوا وهم كفار فلن يقبل من أحدهم ملء الأرض ذهبا ولو افتدى به أولئك لهم عذاب أليم وما لهم من ناصرين

translation: You will never attain righteousness until you spend from that which you love. And whatever you spend, indeed Allah is Knowing of it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true righteousness and piety are achieved not just through obligatory acts, but through the willingness to sacrifice what one cherishes most for the sake of others. It teaches that genuine generosity involves giving from one's beloved possessions, highlighting the importance of selflessness and the purity of intention in acts of charity. Allah's knowledge of all that is spent underscores the accountability and the spiritual reward associated with such acts.
orig: لن تنالوا البر حتى تنفقوا مما تحبون وما تنفقوا من شيء فإن الله به عليم

translation: All food was lawful to the Children of Israel except what Israel had made unlawful to himself before the Torah was revealed. Say, 'Bring the Torah and recite it, if you are truthful.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the original permissibility of all foods for the Children of Israel, with the exception of those self-imposed restrictions by Jacob (Israel) before the Torah was given. It challenges the Jews of the Prophet Muhammad's time to bring forth the Torah and verify their claims about dietary laws, emphasizing the importance of adhering to divine scripture over human traditions or interpretations. This underscores the Qur'anic theme of returning to the original, unaltered messages of the prophets.
orig: كل الطعام كان حلا لبني إسرائيل إلا ما حرم إسرائيل على نفسه من قبل أن تنزل التوراة قل فأتوا بالتوراة فاتلوها إن كنتم صادقين

translation: So whoever invents a lie against Allah after that - then those are [truly] the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity of attributing falsehood to Allah after the truth has been made clear. It underscores that such an action is not merely a mistake, but a grave injustice, categorizing those who do so as oppressors. This highlights the importance of honesty and integrity in matters of faith, warning believers against the dangers of fabricating lies about divine revelation.
orig: فمن افترى على الله الكذب من بعد ذلك فأولئك هم الظالمون

translation: Say, "Allah has spoken the truth, so follow the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth; and he was not of the polytheists."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of following the monotheistic path exemplified by Abraham, who is described as a 'hanif' or one who inclines towards the truth, rejecting polytheism. It underscores the Qur'anic affirmation of the truthfulness of God's message and encourages believers to adhere strictly to the pure monotheism that Abraham practiced, distancing themselves from any form of idolatry or association of partners with God.
orig: قل صدق الله فاتبعوا ملة إبراهيم حنيفا وما كان من المشركين

translation: Indeed, the first House [of worship] established for mankind was that at Bakkah, blessed and a guidance for the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the significance of the Ka'bah in Makkah, known as Bakkah in ancient times, as the first place of worship designated for all of humanity. It underscores the Ka'bah's sacredness and its role as a universal guide, highlighting its importance not just for Muslims but for all people across the world. The mention of it being 'blessed and a guidance' suggests that visiting or orienting oneself towards the Ka'bah can bring spiritual blessings and direction in life.
orig: إن أول بيت وضع للناس للذي ببكة مباركا وهدى للعالمين

translation: In it are clear signs, the standing place of Abraham. Whoever enters it is safe. And it is a duty to Allah upon the people to make the pilgrimage to the House for whoever is able to find a way. And whoever disbelieves, then indeed, Allah is free from need of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sanctity and significance of the Ka'bah in Mecca, highlighting its role as a place of safety and peace. The 'clear signs' refer to the evident miracles and the historical and spiritual importance of the site, including the Maqam Ibrahim, which is the stone on which Abraham stood while building the Ka'bah. The verse mandates the Hajj pilgrimage for those who are physically and financially able, underscoring the communal and individual obligation to worship Allah. The final part of the verse serves as a reminder of Allah's self-sufficiency and independence from the creation, reinforcing that faith and obedience are for the benefit of the believers themselves, not for Allah's need.
orig: فيه آيات بينات مقام إبراهيم ومن دخله كان آمنا ولله على الناس حج البيت من استطاع إليه سبيلا ومن كفر فإن الله غني عن العالمين

translation: Say, O People of the Scripture, why do you disbelieve in the verses of Allah while Allah is witness over what you do?
interpretation: This verse addresses the People of the Scripture (Jews and Christians) and challenges them on their rejection of the signs and revelations of Allah. It emphasizes the omnipresence and omniscience of Allah, who is fully aware of their actions and intentions. The verse serves as a reminder and a call to reflect on their disbelief, urging them to consider the consequences of their actions under the watchful eye of Allah.
orig: قل يا أهل الكتاب لم تكفرون بآيات الله والله شهيد على ما تعملون

translation: Say, O People of the Scripture, why do you turn away from the way of Allah those who believe, seeking to make it crooked, while you are witnesses? And Allah is not unaware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse addresses the People of the Scripture (Jews and Christians) and challenges their actions of obstructing believers from following the path of Allah. It criticizes their attempts to distort the truth and lead believers astray, despite knowing the truth themselves. The verse emphasizes that Allah is fully aware of their actions and their intentions, reinforcing the notion of divine justice and accountability.
orig: قل يا أهل الكتاب لم تصدون عن سبيل الله من آمن تبغونها عوجا وأنتم شهداء وما الله بغافل عما تعملون

translation: O you who have believed, if you obey a party of those who were given the Scripture, they would turn you back, after your belief, [to being] disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse warns believers against following certain groups among the People of the Scripture (Jews and Christians) who might mislead them away from Islam. It emphasizes the importance of maintaining steadfastness in faith and not allowing external influences to undermine one's belief in Islam, highlighting the potential risk of reverting to disbelief due to such influences.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إن تطيعوا فريقا من الذين أوتوا الكتاب يردوكم بعد إيمانكم كافرين

translation: And how can you disbelieve while the verses of Allah are being recited to you and among you is His Messenger? And whoever holds firmly to Allah has been guided to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the profound contradiction and irrationality of disbelief in the face of clear divine guidance. It highlights that the presence of the Qur'an being recited and the Prophet Muhammad among the people serves as undeniable evidence of Allah's existence and message. The verse also underscores the importance of clinging to Allah, suggesting that true guidance and the path to righteousness are found through a strong connection and reliance on Him.
orig: وكيف تكفرون وأنتم تتلى عليكم آيات الله وفيكم رسوله ومن يعتصم بالله فقد هدي إلى صراط مستقيم

translation: O you who have believed, fear Allah as He should be feared and do not die except as Muslims [in submission to Him].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining a deep and sincere fear of Allah throughout one's life, which is a fear rooted in awe and reverence rather than mere dread. It calls upon believers to ensure that their faith and submission to Allah remain intact until the moment of their death, highlighting that the ultimate goal of a believer's life should be to die in a state of complete submission to Allah's will, thereby ensuring a successful end in the hereafter.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله حق تقاته ولا تموتن إلا وأنتم مسلمون

translation: And hold fast, all of you together, to the rope of Allah, and be not divided among yourselves, and remember Allah's favor on you, for you were enemies one to another but He joined your hearts together, so that, by His Grace, you became brethren; and you were on the brink of a pit of Fire, and He saved you from it. Thus Allah makes His signs clear to you, that you may be guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of unity among Muslims, urging them to adhere collectively to the teachings and guidance of Allah, symbolized by 'the rope of Allah.' It serves as a reminder of the divine favor that transformed former enemies into brothers, highlighting the transformative power of faith and obedience to Allah. The verse also warns of the dangers of disunity and straying from the path, which could lead to spiritual ruin, but reassures that adherence to Allah's guidance leads to salvation and clear understanding of His signs.
orig: واعتصموا بحبل الله جميعا ولا تفرقوا واذكروا نعمت الله عليكم إذ كنتم أعداء فألف بين قلوبكم فأصبحتم بنعمته إخوانا وكنتم على شفا حفرة من النار فأنقذكم منها كذلك يبين الله لكم آياته لعلكم تهتدون

translation: And let there be from among you a group that calls to goodness, and commands what is right, and forbids what is wrong, and those are the ones who will be successful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of a community having a group of individuals dedicated to promoting righteousness and preventing wrongdoing. It suggests that the success and prosperity of a society are closely tied to the presence and active engagement of such a group, which works tirelessly to guide people towards good deeds and moral behavior, thereby fostering a just and thriving community.
orig: ولتكن منكم أمة يدعون إلى الخير ويأمرون بالمعروف وينهون عن المنكر وأولئك هم المفلحون

translation: And do not be like those who became divided and differed after clear proofs had come to them. And those will have a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns against the dangers of division and disagreement within the community after receiving clear guidance from Allah. It emphasizes the importance of unity and adherence to the truth that has been revealed, indicating that straying from this path and engaging in disputes leads to severe consequences. The 'great punishment' mentioned serves as a reminder of the seriousness of such actions and the accountability one faces in the hereafter.
orig: ولا تكونوا كالذين تفرقوا واختلفوا من بعد ما جاءهم البينات وأولئك لهم عذاب عظيم

translation: On the Day when faces will be whitened and faces will be blackened. As for those whose faces are blackened, [it will be said to them]: 'Did you disbelieve after your faith? Then taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve.'
interpretation: This verse speaks to the Day of Judgment, highlighting the stark contrast between the believers and the disbelievers through the metaphor of facial colors. The 'whitened faces' symbolize the purity, joy, and acceptance of the believers, reflecting their faith and good deeds. Conversely, the 'blackened faces' represent the shame, regret, and punishment of those who disbelieved or turned away from faith after initially believing. The rhetorical question posed to those with blackened faces underscores the gravity of their choice to disbelieve after having faith, emphasizing personal responsibility and the consequences of one's actions. The command to 'taste the punishment' serves as a reminder of the accountability for disbelief and the rejection of faith, illustrating the severe repercussions that await on the Day of Judgment.
orig: يوم تبيض وجوه وتسود وجوه فأما الذين اسودت وجوههم أكفرتم بعد إيمانكم فذوقوا العذاب بما كنتم تكفرون

translation: And as for those whose faces have been whitened, they are in the mercy of Allah, they will abide therein forever.
interpretation: This verse describes the blessed state of the righteous believers on the Day of Judgment. The whitening of their faces symbolizes their purity, joy, and acceptance by Allah. Being in the mercy of Allah signifies their entry into Paradise, where they will enjoy eternal bliss and happiness, as indicated by the phrase 'they will abide therein forever.' This reflects the ultimate reward and the everlasting nature of the hereafter for those who have lived a life of faith and righteousness.
orig: وأما الذين ابيضت وجوههم ففي رحمة الله هم فيها خالدون

translation: These are the verses of Allah which We recite to you in truth, and Allah does not intend injustice to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin and truthfulness of the Qur'anic revelations, asserting that they are conveyed accurately through the Prophet Muhammad. It also underscores the justice of Allah, indicating that His laws and decrees are not meant to oppress or cause harm to any of His creation, but rather to guide them towards righteousness and fairness.
orig: تلك آيات الله نتلوها عليك بالحق وما الله يريد ظلما للعالمين

translation: And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and to Allah return all matters.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and ownership of Allah over everything in existence, both in the heavens and on earth. It underscores the concept that all affairs and decisions ultimately return to Allah, reinforcing the belief in His ultimate authority and the interconnectedness of all creation under His divine will.
orig: ولله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وإلى الله ترجع الأمور

translation: You are the best nation produced for mankind. You enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong and believe in Allah. If only the People of the Scripture had believed, it would have been better for them. Among them are believers, but most of them are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse highlights the exemplary role of the Muslim community as a model for humanity, emphasizing their duty to promote good, prevent evil, and maintain faith in Allah. It also reflects on the potential for goodness among the People of the Scripture, noting that while some of them do believe, the majority are disobedient, underscoring the universal call to righteousness and the consequences of rejecting faith.
orig: كنتم خير أمة أخرجت للناس تأمرون بالمعروف وتنهون عن المنكر وتؤمنون بالله ولو آمن أهل الكتاب لكان خيرا لهم منهم المؤمنون وأكثرهم الفاسقون

translation: They will not harm you except for [some] annoyance. And if they fight you, they will show you their backs [in flight]; then they will not be aided.
interpretation: This verse reassures the believers that their enemies, despite their efforts, will only be able to cause minor harm or irritation. It emphasizes the ultimate weakness and cowardice of these adversaries, suggesting that in any real confrontation, they will flee and receive no support, highlighting the protection and victory that God promises to the faithful.
orig: لن يضروكم إلا أذى وإن يقاتلوكم يولوكم الأدبار ثم لا ينصرون

translation: Humiliation was imposed upon them wherever they were found, except by a rope from Allah and a rope from the people. They incurred the wrath of Allah, and poverty was imposed upon them. That was because they used to disbelieve in the signs of Allah and kill the prophets without right. That was because they disobeyed and used to transgress.
interpretation: This verse refers to the consequences faced by the Children of Israel due to their persistent disobedience and transgression against God's commandments. The 'humiliation' and 'poverty' mentioned symbolize the spiritual and material decline they experienced as a result of rejecting divine guidance and wrongfully killing prophets. The 'rope from Allah' signifies divine mercy and protection, while the 'rope from the people' indicates the support or treaties they might receive from others, offering them temporary relief from their plight. This verse serves as a reminder of the severe consequences of rejecting faith and the importance of adhering to God's laws.
orig: ضربت عليهم الذلة أين ما ثقفوا إلا بحبل من الله وحبل من الناس وباءوا بغضب من الله وضربت عليهم المسكنة ذلك بأنهم كانوا يكفرون بآيات الله ويقتلون الأنبياء بغير حق ذلك بما عصوا وكانوا يعتدون

translation: Not equal are the People of the Book; there is an upright community among them who recite the verses of Allah during the hours of the night while they prostrate.
interpretation: This verse highlights the diversity within the People of the Book, emphasizing that not all are the same. It specifically acknowledges a group among them who are distinguished by their piety and devotion. These individuals are described as spending their nights in worship, reciting the Qur'an and engaging in prostration, which signifies their deep commitment to their faith. The verse serves to encourage Muslims to recognize and appreciate the sincere believers among other religious communities, promoting a message of respect and understanding across different faiths.
orig: ليسوا سواء من أهل الكتاب أمة قائمة يتلون آيات الله آناء الليل وهم يسجدون

translation: They believe in Allah and the Last Day, and they enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and they hasten to do good deeds. And those are among the righteous.
interpretation: This verse describes the characteristics of the righteous believers. It emphasizes that true faith in Allah and the Last Day is manifested through actions: enjoining good, forbidding evil, and rushing to perform acts of kindness. The verse suggests that righteousness is not merely a state of belief but a dynamic engagement with the community, promoting moral values and actively contributing to the betterment of society.
orig: يؤمنون بالله واليوم الآخر ويأمرون بالمعروف وينهون عن المنكر ويسارعون في الخيرات وأولئك من الصالحين

translation: And whatever good they do, they will not be denied it. And Allah is All-Knowing of the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine promise that every good deed performed by individuals will be recognized and rewarded by Allah. It reassures believers that no act of kindness or righteousness goes unnoticed or unrewarded, reflecting Allah's attribute of being All-Knowing and particularly aware of those who are pious and God-fearing. This encourages continuous good actions with the assurance of divine acknowledgment.
orig: وما يفعلوا من خير فلن يكفروه والله عليم بالمتقين

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve, neither their wealth nor their children will avail them anything against Allah, and they are the inhabitants of the Fire, they will abide therein forever.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that material possessions and familial ties hold no value or protection in the eyes of Allah for those who reject faith. It underscores the ultimate futility of worldly achievements and relationships when it comes to salvation and the afterlife, highlighting that only faith and righteousness can save one from the eternal punishment of Hellfire.
orig: إن الذين كفروا لن تغني عنهم أموالهم ولا أولادهم من الله شيئا وأولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون

translation: The example of what they spend in this worldly life is like that of a wind containing frost which strikes the harvest of a people who have wronged themselves and destroys it. And Allah has not wronged them, but they wrong themselves.
interpretation: This verse uses the metaphor of a destructive wind to illustrate the futility and harmful consequences of spending wealth in ways that do not please Allah, often driven by greed or injustice. The 'wind containing frost' represents how such spending can ruin one's good deeds and spiritual harvest, just as frost can destroy crops. The verse emphasizes personal responsibility, indicating that any harm or loss experienced is a result of one's own actions ('they wrong themselves') rather than any injustice from Allah. It serves as a warning against misusing wealth and the importance of using it in ways that align with divine guidance.
orig: مثل ما ينفقون في هذه الحياة الدنيا كمثل ريح فيها صر أصابت حرث قوم ظلموا أنفسهم فأهلكته وما ظلمهم الله ولكن أنفسهم يظلمون

translation: O you who have believed, do not take as intimates those other than yourselves, for they will not spare you [any] ruin. They wish you would have hardship. Hatred has already appeared from their mouths, and what their breasts conceal is greater. We have certainly made clear to you the signs, if you will use reason.
interpretation: This verse advises believers to be cautious in forming close relationships with non-believers, as such relationships could potentially lead to harm or betrayal. The verse highlights that the outward expressions of hostility from non-believers are less severe than their hidden intentions, emphasizing the importance of discernment and awareness. It underscores the clarity of divine guidance provided in the Qur'an, urging believers to use their intellect to understand and heed these signs.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتخذوا بطانة من دونكم لا يألونكم خبالا ودوا ما عنتم قد بدت البغضاء من أفواههم وما تخفي صدورهم أكبر قد بينا لكم الآيات إن كنتم تعقلون

translation: Here you are loving them but they do not love you, while you believe in the whole Scripture. And when they meet you, they say, 'We believe'; but when they are alone, they bite their fingertips at you in rage. Say, 'Die in your rage. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of that within the breasts.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the believers' relationship with the hypocrites, who outwardly profess faith but inwardly harbor enmity and resentment. It highlights the believers' sincere love and faith contrasted with the hypocrites' deceit and hidden anger. The command to 'die in your rage' is a powerful assertion of the believers' confidence in Allah's knowledge of all hearts, emphasizing divine justice and the ultimate futility of the hypocrites' hostility.
orig: ها أنتم أولاء تحبونهم ولا يحبونكم وتؤمنون بالكتاب كله وإذا لقوكم قالوا آمنا وإذا خلوا عضوا عليكم الأنامل من الغيظ قل موتوا بغيظكم إن الله عليم بذات الصدور

translation: If a good thing comes to you, it grieves them; but if a bad thing happens to you, they rejoice at it. And if you are patient and fear Allah, their plot will not harm you at all. Indeed, Allah encompasses what they do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrasting reactions of the hypocrites and disbelievers towards the believers. It underscores the importance of patience and piety in the face of adversity. The verse reassures believers that no matter how much the enemies plot against them, their schemes will be futile if the believers remain steadfast and God-fearing. This is because Allah is fully aware of and in control of all actions, ensuring that the believers are ultimately protected and guided by His encompassing knowledge and power.
orig: إن تمسسكم حسنة تسؤهم وإن تصبكم سيئة يفرحوا بها وإن تصبروا وتتقوا لا يضركم كيدهم شيئا إن الله بما يعملون محيط

translation: And when you left your family early, assigning the believers their positions for the battle, and Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Prophet Muhammad's strategic leadership and dedication during the Battle of Uhud. It highlights his proactive approach in the early morning to organize the Muslim forces, demonstrating his commitment to the welfare and guidance of the believers. The mention of Allah being All-Hearing and All-Knowing emphasizes that God is fully aware of the Prophet's actions and intentions, underscoring divine approval and omniscience over the events.
orig: وإذ غدوت من أهلك تبوئ المؤمنين مقاعد للقتال والله سميع عليم

translation: When two parties from among you were about to lose heart, but Allah was their protector, and upon Allah let the believers rely.
interpretation: This verse reflects on a moment of weakness during a critical situation where two groups among the Muslim community were on the verge of despair. It serves as a reminder that even in moments of doubt or fear, Allah remains the ultimate protector and supporter of the believers. The verse encourages steadfastness and trust in Allah's plan, emphasizing that true faith involves relying on Allah's wisdom and protection, especially during times of trial.
orig: إذ همت طائفتان منكم أن تفشلا والله وليهما وعلى الله فليتوكل المؤمنون

translation: And Allah certainly helped you at Badr when you were weak. So fear Allah; perhaps you will be grateful.
interpretation: This verse reminds the believers of the victory at the Battle of Badr, where despite being outnumbered and less equipped, they triumphed with God's help. It serves as a reminder to remain humble and pious, acknowledging that all success comes from Allah. The verse encourages gratitude towards Allah, recognizing His aid and mercy in times of need.
orig: ولقد نصركم الله ببدر وأنتم أذلة فاتقوا الله لعلكم تشكرون

translation: When you said to the believers, 'Is it not enough for you that your Lord should reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down?'
interpretation: This verse refers to a moment during the Battle of Badr when the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) reassured the believers of divine support. The mention of three thousand angels being sent down symbolizes God's immense power and His readiness to aid the faithful in times of need. It serves as a reminder to the believers to trust in God's plan and His ability to provide assistance beyond human capabilities, reinforcing the concept of reliance on divine intervention and the importance of faith in overcoming adversity.
orig: إذ تقول للمؤمنين ألن يكفيكم أن يمدكم ربكم بثلاثة آلاف من الملائكة منزلين

translation: Yes, if you remain patient and mindful of God, and they come upon you suddenly, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels, specially marked.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of patience and piety in the face of adversity. It assures believers that if they maintain these qualities, even when suddenly attacked by their enemies, God will provide them with divine support in the form of five thousand specially marked angels. This promise serves as a source of comfort and encouragement, reinforcing the faith of believers in God's protection and assistance during times of trial.
orig: بلى إن تصبروا وتتقوا ويأتوكم من فورهم هذا يمددكم ربكم بخمسة آلاف من الملائكة مسومين

translation: And Allah made it not except as good tidings for you and to reassure your hearts thereby. And victory is not but from Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the events or signs mentioned are meant to bring comfort and reassurance to the believers, serving as glad tidings from Allah. It underscores the notion that true victory and success come solely from Allah, who is described as the Almighty and the Wise, reinforcing the dependence of believers on divine support and guidance.
orig: وما جعله الله إلا بشرى لكم ولتطمئن قلوبكم به وما النصر إلا من عند الله العزيز الحكيم

translation: So that He may cut off a section of those who disbelieved or suppress them so they turn back frustrated.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the purpose of divine intervention or military action by believers is to weaken or defeat a portion of the disbelievers, thereby causing them to retreat in disappointment and frustration. It emphasizes the strategic aspect of such actions, aiming not only at immediate victory but also at long-term demoralization of the enemy.
orig: ليقطع طرفا من الذين كفروا أو يكبتهم فينقلبوا خائبين

translation: You have no say in the matter, whether He forgives them or punishes them; for they are wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute authority of Allah in deciding the fate of wrongdoers. It emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) has no control over whether Allah chooses to forgive or punish those who have committed injustices. This serves to remind believers of the limits of human influence and the ultimate sovereignty of Allah in matters of divine judgment and mercy.
orig: ليس لك من الأمر شيء أو يتوب عليهم أو يعذبهم فإنهم ظالمون

translation: And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills, and Allah is Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty of Allah over all creation, indicating that everything in the universe is under His control. The mention of forgiveness and punishment highlights His divine authority to judge and His capacity for mercy and justice. The attributes of being 'Forgiving' and 'Most Merciful' serve as a reminder of His immense compassion, encouraging believers to seek His forgiveness while acknowledging His power to hold accountable.
orig: ولله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض يغفر لمن يشاء ويعذب من يشاء والله غفور رحيم

translation: O you who have believed, do not consume usury, doubled and multiplied, and fear Allah that you may be successful.
interpretation: This verse addresses the believers, urging them to abstain from engaging in usury, which is considered a grave sin in Islam. The prohibition is emphasized by describing usury as something that is doubled and multiplied, highlighting its exploitative nature. The verse connects the avoidance of usury with the fear of Allah, suggesting that righteousness and success in the eyes of Allah are tied to ethical financial practices. By fearing Allah and avoiding usury, believers are promised success, which can be understood as both worldly prosperity and spiritual salvation.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تأكلوا الربا أضعافا مضاعفة واتقوا الله لعلكم تفلحون

translation: And fear the Fire, which is prepared for the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder and a warning to believers to be mindful of their actions and to avoid disbelief, as the consequence of disbelief is severe punishment in the Hereafter. The Fire mentioned here symbolizes the Hellfire, which is a place of torment prepared specifically for those who reject faith. The emphasis on fearing the Fire underscores the importance of maintaining faith and righteousness to avoid such a fate.
orig: واتقوا النار التي أعدت للكافرين

translation: And obey Allah and the Messenger so that you may obtain mercy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to Allah and His Messenger as a means to attain divine mercy. It suggests that true guidance and blessings come through submission to the commandments and teachings revealed by Allah through His Prophet. Obedience here is not just about following rules, but about aligning one's will with the divine will, which is the path to spiritual growth and receiving Allah's compassion and forgiveness.
orig: وأطيعوا الله والرسول لعلكم ترحمون

translation: And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a garden as wide as the heavens and the earth, prepared for the righteous.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to actively seek Allah's forgiveness and strive for Paradise, which is described as vast as the heavens and earth. The emphasis on hastening suggests urgency and the importance of immediate action in one's spiritual journey. It highlights that Paradise is specifically prepared for those who are righteous, indicating that a life of piety and good deeds is the path to this ultimate reward.
orig: وسارعوا إلى مغفرة من ربكم وجنة عرضها السماوات والأرض أعدت للمتقين

translation: Those who spend [in the way of Allah] in ease and in hardship, and those who restrain their anger and pardon people - and Allah loves the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the virtues of generosity, patience, and forgiveness. It highlights that true believers are those who continue to give charitably regardless of their financial situation, whether in times of prosperity or adversity. Additionally, it praises those who control their anger and forgive others, indicating that these qualities are highly valued by Allah. The verse concludes by affirming that Allah loves those who perform good deeds, underscoring the importance of these moral actions in the eyes of God.
orig: الذين ينفقون في السراء والضراء والكاظمين الغيظ والعافين عن الناس والله يحب المحسنين

translation: And those who, when they commit an indecency or wrong themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins - and who can forgive sins except Allah? - and they do not persist in what they have done while they know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of immediate repentance and seeking forgiveness from Allah after committing a sin or wronging oneself. It emphasizes that true believers are those who, upon realizing their mistakes, turn to Allah with sincere remorse and seek His forgiveness, acknowledging that only Allah can absolve sins. The verse also stresses the necessity of not persisting in sinful behavior, indicating that genuine repentance involves a conscious decision to change one's actions, demonstrating an awareness and understanding of the wrong committed.
orig: والذين إذا فعلوا فاحشة أو ظلموا أنفسهم ذكروا الله فاستغفروا لذنوبهم ومن يغفر الذنوب إلا الله ولم يصروا على ما فعلوا وهم يعلمون

translation: Those, their reward is forgiveness from their Lord, and Gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they shall abide forever. Excellent is the reward of the workers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate reward awaiting those who faithfully follow God's path. The promise of forgiveness from the Lord signifies a complete cleansing of sins, offering believers a fresh start in the afterlife. The description of Gardens with flowing rivers symbolizes a paradise of abundance and eternal peace, reflecting the infinite mercy and generosity of Allah. The phrase 'wherein they shall abide forever' underscores the permanence of this reward, providing comfort and motivation for believers to persevere in their righteous deeds. The final statement, 'Excellent is the reward of the workers,' highlights the value and worth of diligent effort in faith and good deeds, affirming that such efforts are richly rewarded in the hereafter.
orig: أولئك جزاؤهم مغفرة من ربهم وجنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها ونعم أجر العاملين

translation: There have been examples before you, so travel in the land and see how was the end of those who denied.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to reflect on historical examples of past nations who rejected the truth. By traveling and observing, one can witness the consequences faced by those who denied the messages of the prophets. It serves as a reminder and a warning that disbelief leads to a negative outcome, urging current generations to heed the lessons from history and accept the divine message.
orig: قد خلت من قبلكم سنن فسيروا في الأرض فانظروا كيف كان عاقبة المكذبين

translation: This is a clear statement to the people and guidance and admonition for the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an serves multiple purposes: it is a clear communication meant for all people, providing guidance on how to live righteously, and it acts as a reminder and warning for those who are pious and God-fearing. It underscores the universal applicability of the Qur'an's message, while also highlighting its special significance for those who strive to live according to its teachings.
orig: هذا بيان للناس وهدى وموعظة للمتقين

translation: And do not weaken or grieve, and you will be superior if you are believers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a source of encouragement and reassurance for believers. It emphasizes the importance of maintaining steadfastness and resilience in the face of adversity. By not succumbing to weakness or sadness, believers are promised superiority and victory, contingent upon their faith. The verse suggests that true strength and ultimate success are derived from a deep and unwavering belief in God, which empowers them to overcome challenges and maintain hope.
orig: ولا تهنوا ولا تحزنوا وأنتم الأعلون إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: If a wound has touched you, be sure a similar wound has touched the others. Such days (of varying fortunes) We deal out to men and women, so that Allah may know those who believe, and that He may take martyrs from among you: and Allah loveth not those who do wrong.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder that the trials and tribulations faced by the believers are not unique to them; others have faced similar challenges. It underscores the concept of divine testing through the ups and downs of life, which are distributed among people to distinguish the true believers from others. The verse also highlights the honor of martyrdom as a potential outcome of such tests, emphasizing that enduring these trials with faith and patience is a way to demonstrate one's commitment to their beliefs. Furthermore, it warns against wrongdoing, as Allah does not favor those who engage in unjust actions.
orig: إن يمسسكم قرح فقد مس القوم قرح مثله وتلك الأيام نداولها بين الناس وليعلم الله الذين آمنوا ويتخذ منكم شهداء والله لا يحب الظالمين

translation: And Allah will test those who have believed and will destroy the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah will put the believers through trials to distinguish their faith and commitment, while He will ultimately bring about the downfall of those who reject faith, emphasizing the divine justice and the eventual triumph of belief over disbelief.
orig: وليمحص الله الذين آمنوا ويمحق الكافرين

translation: Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while Allah has not yet made evident those of you who strive [for His cause] and made evident those who are steadfast?
interpretation: This verse suggests that entry into Paradise is not automatic but is contingent upon demonstrating one's commitment and perseverance in the path of Allah. It emphasizes that Allah tests believers to distinguish those who genuinely strive in His cause and those who exhibit patience and endurance. The verse implies that these qualities must be proven through real-life challenges and trials, underscoring the importance of active effort and resilience in faith.
orig: أم حسبتم أن تدخلوا الجنة ولما يعلم الله الذين جاهدوا منكم ويعلم الصابرين

translation: And indeed you used to wish for death before you met it. Now you have seen it while you were looking on.
interpretation: This verse reflects on the state of the believers who, in their zeal and commitment to their faith, used to wish for martyrdom as a means to meet Allah and attain a high spiritual rank. However, when faced with the reality of death in battle, they experienced the true gravity and fear of it. The verse serves as a reminder of the difference between the idealization of a concept and its stark reality, urging believers to be prepared for the trials they may face and to maintain their faith steadfastly even in the face of death.
orig: ولقد كنتم تمنون الموت من قبل أن تلقوه فقد رأيتموه وأنتم تنظرون

translation: And Muhammad is not but a messenger; [other] messengers have passed on before him. So if he was to die or be killed, would you turn back on your heels [to unbelief]? And he who turns back on his heels will never harm Allah at all; but Allah will reward the grateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the mortality of Prophet Muhammad and reminds the believers that he is just one of many messengers sent by Allah. It serves as a test of faith, urging the believers not to abandon Islam if the Prophet were to die or be killed. The verse reassures that turning away from faith after the Prophet's death will not harm Allah in any way, as His plan and message will continue regardless. Instead, it encourages steadfastness and gratitude, promising that Allah will reward those who remain faithful and appreciative of His blessings.
orig: وما محمد إلا رسول قد خلت من قبله الرسل أفإن مات أو قتل انقلبتم على أعقابكم ومن ينقلب على عقبيه فلن يضر الله شيئا وسيجزي الله الشاكرين

translation: And no soul can die except by Allah's permission, a decree determined. And whoever desires the reward of this world, We give him thereof; and whoever desires the reward of the Hereafter, We give him thereof. And We will reward the grateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty of Allah over life and death, asserting that no one dies without His permission and according to a predetermined decree. It also highlights the divine justice in rewarding individuals based on their intentions and desires, whether they seek worldly gains or spiritual rewards in the Hereafter. The promise to reward the grateful underscores the importance of gratitude as a virtue that attracts divine favor.
orig: وما كان لنفس أن تموت إلا بإذن الله كتابا مؤجلا ومن يرد ثواب الدنيا نؤته منها ومن يرد ثواب الآخرة نؤته منها وسنجزي الشاكرين

translation: And how many a prophet has been killed with him many thousands, yet they did not waver due to what afflicted them in the cause of Allah, nor did they weaken, nor did they give in. And Allah loves the patient.
interpretation: This verse highlights the resilience and steadfastness of prophets and their followers in the face of adversity. It emphasizes that despite facing severe trials and even death, they remained firm in their faith and commitment to Allah's cause. The verse serves as an encouragement for believers to emulate this patience and perseverance, as Allah cherishes those who endure hardships with steadfastness.
orig: وكأين من نبي قاتل معه ربيون كثير فما وهنوا لما أصابهم في سبيل الله وما ضعفوا وما استكانوا والله يحب الصابرين

translation: And their words were only that they said: Our Lord, forgive us our sins and our transgressions in our affairs, and make our feet firm, and give us victory over the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse highlights the essence of a sincere prayer from believers, acknowledging their faults and seeking divine forgiveness and strength. It emphasizes the importance of asking for steadfastness in faith and seeking God's help in overcoming challenges posed by those who reject faith. The prayer reflects a deep reliance on God for moral and spiritual support, underscoring the believer's humility and trust in divine mercy and assistance.
orig: وما كان قولهم إلا أن قالوا ربنا اغفر لنا ذنوبنا وإسرافنا في أمرنا وثبت أقدامنا وانصرنا على القوم الكافرين

translation: So Allah gave them the reward of this world and the excellent reward of the Hereafter. And Allah loves those who do good.
interpretation: This verse highlights the dual rewards bestowed by Allah upon those who perform righteous deeds. The "reward of this world" refers to the blessings and benefits one may receive in their earthly life as a result of their good actions, while the "excellent reward of the Hereafter" points to the eternal bliss and salvation in the afterlife. The phrase "Allah loves those who do good" underscores that acts of kindness and righteousness are particularly cherished by Allah, encouraging believers to continuously engage in beneficial actions not only for the rewards but also to attain Allah's love and approval.
orig: فآتاهم الله ثواب الدنيا وحسن ثواب الآخرة والله يحب المحسنين

translation: O you who have believed, if you obey those who disbelieve, they will turn you back on your heels, and you will [then] become losers.
interpretation: This verse warns believers against following the guidance or influence of disbelievers, as doing so could lead them away from their faith and cause them to lose the spiritual and moral gains they have achieved. It emphasizes the importance of steadfastness in faith and the potential consequences of straying from the path of belief.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إن تطيعوا الذين كفروا يردوكم على أعقابكم فتنقلبوا خاسرين

translation: Rather, Allah is your Protector, and He is the best of helpers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that while believers may face opposition or feel alone, they should remember that Allah is their ultimate guardian and supporter. It reassures the faithful that no matter the challenges they face, Allah's support is the most effective and reliable, surpassing any human assistance.
orig: بل الله مولاكم وهو خير الناصرين

translation: We will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve because they associated with Allah that for which He had not sent down any authority. And their refuge will be the Fire, and wretched is the residence of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequences of disbelief and polytheism. It suggests that those who attribute partners to Allah without any divine authorization will experience fear and dread in their hearts as a direct result of their actions. The verse also underscores the ultimate fate of such individuals, indicating that their final abode will be Hell, which is described as a miserable dwelling for those who oppress and wrong others through their disbelief. This serves as a warning and a reminder of the severe repercussions of straying from monotheism and divine guidance.
orig: سنلقي في قلوب الذين كفروا الرعب بما أشركوا بالله ما لم ينزل به سلطانا ومأواهم النار وبئس مثوى الظالمين

translation: And Allah had certainly fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing the enemy by His permission until [the time] when you lost courage and fell to disputing about the order and disobeyed after He had shown you that which you love. Among you are some who desire this world, and among you are some who desire the Hereafter. Then he turned you away from them [defeated] that He might test you. And He has already forgiven you, and Allah is the possessor of bounty to the believers.
interpretation: This verse reflects on the Battle of Uhud, where the Muslims initially gained the upper hand due to their obedience to Allah's command. However, their victory turned into defeat when some of them disobeyed the Prophet's orders out of a desire for worldly gains, such as plundering the enemy's camp. This disobedience led to a reversal of fortunes, serving as a test from Allah to distinguish those who were steadfast in their faith and those who prioritized worldly desires over the Hereafter. The verse also highlights Allah's mercy, as He forgave the believers despite their faltering, underscoring His grace and favor towards those who believe.
orig: ولقد صدقكم الله وعده إذ تحسونهم بإذنه حتى إذا فشلتم وتنازعتم في الأمر وعصيتم من بعد ما أراكم ما تحبون منكم من يريد الدنيا ومنكم من يريد الآخرة ثم صرفكم عنهم ليبتليكم ولقد عفا عنكم والله ذو فضل على المؤمنين

translation: When you were climbing (the hill) without turning your attention to anyone, and the Messenger was calling you from behind. So He requited you with grief upon grief so that you would not grieve over what you missed, nor over what afflicted you. And Allah is All-Aware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse reflects on the Battle of Uhud, where the Muslims faced a setback due to disobedience to the Prophet's command. It highlights the moment when some Muslims were fleeing the battlefield, ascending a hill in panic without heeding the Prophet's calls for regrouping. The verse suggests that the subsequent sorrow and grief they experienced were a form of divine retribution intended to teach them a lesson, preventing them from being overly affected by their losses or the adversities they faced. It underscores the concept of divine wisdom in trials and the omniscience of Allah regarding human actions and their consequences.
orig: إذ تصعدون ولا تلوون على أحد والرسول يدعوكم في أخراكم فأثابكم غما بغم لكيلا تحزنوا على ما فاتكم ولا ما أصابكم والله خبير بما تعملون

translation: Then after the distress, He sent down upon you security [in the form of] a slumber, overcoming a group of you, while another group was concerned about themselves, thinking wrongly of Allah - the thought of ignorance, saying, 'Is there anything for us in the matter?' Say, 'Indeed, the matter belongs wholly to Allah.' They conceal within themselves what they will not reveal to you. They say, 'If there was anything for us in the matter, we would not have been killed here.' Say, 'Even if you had been in your houses, those for whom death was decreed would have come out to their death places.' And [this is] so that Allah might test what is in your breasts and purify what is in your hearts. And Allah is Knowing of that within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse reflects on the human response to adversity and divine providence, particularly during the Battle of Uhud. It highlights the emotional and psychological states of the believers, showing how some found peace through divine reassurance in the form of sleep, while others were consumed by fear and doubt. The verse emphasizes the importance of trusting in Allah's complete control over all affairs, challenging the believers to recognize that life and death are predetermined by Allah, not influenced by human actions or locations. It serves as a reminder that trials are a means for Allah to test and purify the faith and intentions of individuals, ultimately strengthening their reliance on and understanding of divine wisdom.
orig: ثم أنزل عليكم من بعد الغم أمنة نعاسا يغشى طائفة منكم وطائفة قد أهمتهم أنفسهم يظنون بالله غير الحق ظن الجاهلية يقولون هل لنا من الأمر من شيء قل إن الأمر كله لله يخفون في أنفسهم ما لا يبدون لك يقولون لو كان لنا من الأمر شيء ما قتلنا هاهنا قل لو كنتم في بيوتكم لبرز الذين كتب عليهم القتل إلى مضاجعهم وليبتلي الله ما في صدوركم وليمحص ما في قلوبكم والله عليم بذات الصدور

translation: Indeed, those who turned back on the day the two armies met, it was Satan who caused them to slip because of some of their deeds. And Allah has already forgiven them. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing.
interpretation: This verse refers to the incident during the Battle of Uhud where some Muslims turned away from the battle. It teaches that even when believers falter due to their own shortcomings, Satan can exploit these weaknesses to lead them astray. However, the verse also emphasizes Allah's mercy and forgiveness, highlighting that despite their lapse, Allah forgave them, showcasing His attributes of being Forgiving and Forbearing. This serves as a reminder to believers of the importance of steadfastness in faith and the boundless mercy of Allah.
orig: إن الذين تولوا منكم يوم التقى الجمعان إنما استزلهم الشيطان ببعض ما كسبوا ولقد عفا الله عنهم إن الله غفور حليم

translation: O you who have believed, do not be like those who disbelieved and said about their brothers when they traveled through the land or went out to fight, "If they had been with us, they would not have died or been killed," so Allah makes that [misconception] a regret within their hearts. And Allah gives life and causes death, and Allah is Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse cautions believers against falling into the same error as the disbelievers who wrongly believed that staying at home could have prevented the death or killing of their brothers. It highlights the misconception that one's fate is controlled by their location or actions, rather than by Allah's decree. The verse emphasizes that life and death are in Allah's hands, and He is fully aware of all actions. It serves as a reminder to trust in Allah's wisdom and plan, rather than harboring regrets or false beliefs about what could have been done differently.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تكونوا كالذين كفروا وقالوا لإخوانهم إذا ضربوا في الأرض أو كانوا غزى لو كانوا عندنا ما ماتوا وما قتلوا ليجعل الله ذلك حسرة في قلوبهم والله يحيي ويميت والله بما تعملون بصير

translation: And if you are killed in the cause of Allah or die - then forgiveness from Allah and mercy are better than what they accumulate.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the spiritual rewards and divine blessings that await those who sacrifice their lives or die in the path of serving Allah. It suggests that the eternal forgiveness and mercy granted by Allah surpass any worldly gains or possessions that others might amass. The verse encourages believers to prioritize their faith and the hereafter over material accumulations, highlighting the ultimate value of spiritual devotion and sacrifice.
orig: ولئن قتلتم في سبيل الله أو متم لمغفرة من الله ورحمة خير مما يجمعون

translation: And if you die or are killed, to Allah you will be gathered.
interpretation: This verse reassures believers that whether they die naturally or are killed, their ultimate destination is to be gathered before Allah. It emphasizes the certainty of the afterlife and the accountability of every soul to Allah, highlighting the transient nature of life and the importance of preparing for the Hereafter.
orig: ولئن متم أو قتلتم لإلى الله تحشرون

translation: So by mercy from Allah, [O Muhammad], you were lenient with them. And if you had been rude [in speech] and harsh in heart, they would have disbanded from about you. So pardon them and ask forgiveness for them and consult them in the matter. And when you have decided, then rely upon Allah. Indeed, Allah loves those who rely [upon Him].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of compassion and leniency in leadership, as exemplified by the Prophet Muhammad. It suggests that harshness and severity could lead to alienation and division. Instead, leaders should be forgiving, seek forgiveness for their followers, and involve them in decision-making processes. The verse also underscores the value of trust in Allah after making decisions, indicating that reliance on divine guidance is crucial for successful outcomes. This approach not only fosters unity and loyalty but also aligns with divine love for those who trust in Him.
orig: فبما رحمة من الله لنت لهم ولو كنت فظا غليظ القلب لانفضوا من حولك فاعف عنهم واستغفر لهم وشاورهم في الأمر فإذا عزمت فتوكل على الله إن الله يحب المتوكلين

translation: If Allah helps you, none can overcome you; and if He forsakes you, who is there that can help you after Him? And in Allah let the believers put their trust.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and sovereignty of Allah over all affairs. It teaches that victory and success come solely from Allah's support, and without His aid, no one can achieve true success or protection. The verse encourages believers to place their complete trust and reliance in Allah alone, highlighting the importance of faith and dependence on divine assistance in all circumstances.
orig: إن ينصركم الله فلا غالب لكم وإن يخذلكم فمن ذا الذي ينصركم من بعده وعلى الله فليتوكل المؤمنون

translation: It is not for a prophet to embezzle, and whoever embezzles will come with what he embezzled on the Day of Resurrection; then every soul will be recompensed for what it earned, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the moral accountability of prophets and all individuals. It asserts that prophets are inherently honest and would not engage in dishonest acts such as embezzlement. If anyone, including a prophet, were to commit such an act, they would be held accountable on the Day of Resurrection. The verse underlines the principle of divine justice, where every individual will face the consequences of their actions, ensuring fairness and no injustice on the Day of Judgment.
orig: وما كان لنبي أن يغل ومن يغلل يأت بما غل يوم القيامة ثم توفى كل نفس ما كسبت وهم لا يظلمون

translation: Is one who follows the pleasure of Allah like one who has incurred the wrath of Allah and whose abode is Hell? And what a wretched destination!
interpretation: This verse highlights the stark contrast between those who strive to please Allah and those who earn His displeasure. It emphasizes that the ultimate consequence of one's actions in this life is determined by their alignment with Allah's will. Those who follow what pleases Allah are promised a favorable outcome, while those who incur His wrath face the dire consequence of Hell, illustrating the severe dichotomy in the afterlife based on one's deeds and intentions.
orig: أفمن اتبع رضوان الله كمن باء بسخط من الله ومأواه جهنم وبئس المصير

translation: They are in varying degrees in the sight of Allah, and Allah is observant of what they do.
interpretation: This verse indicates that people are not equal in their status before Allah; their ranks differ based on their deeds and faith. Allah, being all-seeing, is fully aware of every action individuals perform, and He judges them accordingly. This emphasizes the importance of righteous actions and the accountability of each person for their deeds.
orig: هم درجات عند الله والله بصير بما يعملون

translation: Indeed, Allah conferred a great favor on the believers when He sent among them a Messenger (Muhammad) from among themselves, reciting to them His Verses, and purifying them, and teaching them the Book and wisdom, while before that they had been in manifest error.
interpretation: This verse highlights the immense blessing bestowed upon the believers through the Prophet Muhammad. It emphasizes the comprehensive role of the Prophet: not only does he convey the divine revelations, but he also purifies the believers spiritually and educates them in the Qur'an and wisdom. This holistic guidance is presented as a stark contrast to the believers' previous state of clear misguidance, underscoring the transformative impact of the Prophet's mission on their lives.
orig: لقد من الله على المؤمنين إذ بعث فيهم رسولا من أنفسهم يتلو عليهم آياته ويزكيهم ويعلمهم الكتاب والحكمة وإن كانوا من قبل لفي ضلال مبين

translation: Or do you think that you will enter Paradise without such (trials) as came to those who passed away before you? They were afflicted with severe poverty and ailments and were so shaken that even the Messenger and those who believed along with him said, 'When (will come) the Help of Allah?' Yes! Certainly, the Help of Allah is near.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the necessity of enduring hardships and trials as a means of spiritual purification and preparation for Paradise. It teaches that facing difficulties is an integral part of the believer's journey, mirroring the experiences of previous generations of faithful. The verse reassures believers that divine help is imminent, encouraging steadfastness and patience in the face of adversity.
orig: أولما أصابتكم مصيبة قد أصبتم مثليها قلتم أنى هذا قل هو من عند أنفسكم إن الله على كل شيء قدير

translation: And what struck you on the day the two armies met was by the permission of Allah, and so that He might know the believers.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the hardships and trials faced by the believers during the Battle of Uhud were part of Allah's divine plan. The phrase 'by the permission of Allah' suggests that nothing happens without His will, emphasizing the concept of divine decree. The purpose of these trials, as mentioned, is to test and reveal the true faith and steadfastness of the believers, allowing them to demonstrate their commitment and trust in Allah under difficult circumstances.
orig: وما أصابكم يوم التقى الجمعان فبإذن الله وليعلم المؤمنين

translation: And [He did this] so that Allah may make evident those who are hypocrites. And it was said to them, 'Come, fight in the way of Allah or [at least] defend.' They said, 'If we knew [how to] fight, we would have followed you.' They were nearer to disbelief that day than to faith, saying with their mouths what was not in their hearts. And Allah is most knowing of what they conceal.
interpretation: This verse highlights the exposure of hypocrisy among those who claim to be believers but fail to act when called upon to defend their faith. It underscores the importance of sincerity in faith, as the hypocrites outwardly profess belief but inwardly harbor disbelief. Their reluctance to participate in jihad or even to defend the community when called upon reveals their true nature. Allah's omniscience is emphasized, indicating that He is fully aware of the hidden intentions and the concealed disbelief within their hearts, despite their verbal claims of faith.
orig: وليعلم الذين نافقوا وقيل لهم تعالوا قاتلوا في سبيل الله أو ادفعوا قالوا لو نعلم قتالا لاتبعناكم هم للكفر يومئذ أقرب منهم للإيمان يقولون بأفواههم ما ليس في قلوبهم والله أعلم بما يكتمون

translation: Those who said to their brothers while they themselves stayed back, "If they had obeyed us, they would not have been killed." Say, "Then avert death from yourselves if you are truthful."
interpretation: This verse addresses those who discourage others from participating in jihad by claiming that obedience to their advice would have prevented deaths. The Qur'an challenges them to prove their claim by averting death from themselves, highlighting the inevitability of death and the fallacy of their argument. It emphasizes that one should not use fear of death as an excuse to avoid fulfilling religious duties.
orig: الذين قالوا لإخوانهم وقعدوا لو أطاعونا ما قتلوا قل فادرءوا عن أنفسكم الموت إن كنتم صادقين

translation: And never think of those who have been killed in the cause of Allah as dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision.
interpretation: This verse conveys the belief that martyrs who die in the path of Allah are not truly dead but are alive in a spiritual sense, enjoying the blessings and sustenance provided by their Lord. It emphasizes the eternal life and reward awaiting those who sacrifice their lives for the sake of their faith, offering comfort and encouragement to believers.
orig: ولا تحسبن الذين قتلوا في سبيل الله أمواتا بل أحياء عند ربهم يرزقون

translation: Rejoicing in what Allah has bestowed upon them of His bounty, and they receive good tidings about those who have not yet joined them but are left behind, that there is no fear upon them, nor shall they grieve.
interpretation: This verse highlights the joy and gratitude of the believers for the blessings they receive from Allah. It also emphasizes the concept of intergenerational solidarity among the faithful, as they take comfort and find happiness in the assurance that future generations of believers will also be safe from fear and sorrow. This reflects the communal aspect of faith and the continuous divine protection extended to all believers across time.
orig: فرحين بما آتاهم الله من فضله ويستبشرون بالذين لم يلحقوا بهم من خلفهم ألا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: They rejoice in a Grace and a Bounty from Allah, and that Allah will not waste the reward of the believers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the joy and gratitude felt by believers due to the blessings and favors bestowed upon them by Allah. It reassures them that their faith and good deeds will be rewarded, emphasizing Allah's justice and generosity. The promise that Allah does not let the reward of the believers go to waste serves as a source of comfort and motivation for them to continue on the path of righteousness.
orig: يستبشرون بنعمة من الله وفضل وأن الله لا يضيع أجر المؤمنين

translation: Those who responded to Allah and the Messenger after the injury had struck them - for those who did good among them and feared Allah is a great reward.
interpretation: This verse highlights the resilience and faith of believers who, despite facing hardships and injuries, continue to respond positively to the call of Allah and His Messenger. It emphasizes that those who maintain their righteousness and piety even in adversity are promised a significant reward from Allah, underscoring the value of steadfastness and moral integrity in the face of trials.
orig: الذين استجابوا لله والرسول من بعد ما أصابهم القرح للذين أحسنوا منهم واتقوا أجر عظيم

translation: Those to whom people said, 'Indeed, the people have gathered against you, so fear them.' But it [merely] increased them in faith, and they said, 'Sufficient for us is Allah, and [He is] the best Disposer of affairs.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the steadfast faith of the believers in the face of threats and adversity. When warned about the gathering of enemies against them, instead of succumbing to fear, their faith in Allah intensified. Their response, 'Sufficient for us is Allah, and [He is] the best Disposer of affairs,' reflects a profound trust in Allah's protection and wisdom, demonstrating that true believers find strength and reassurance in their faith, no matter the external pressures or dangers they face.
orig: الذين قال لهم الناس إن الناس قد جمعوا لكم فاخشوهم فزادهم إيمانا وقالوا حسبنا الله ونعم الوكيل

translation: So they returned with favor from Allah and bounty, no harm having touched them. And they pursued the pleasure of Allah, and Allah is the possessor of great bounty.
interpretation: This verse highlights the blessings and protection bestowed by Allah upon the believers who undertake a journey or mission in His path. It emphasizes that those who seek to please Allah and follow His guidance are rewarded with His favor and bounty, and are shielded from harm. The verse serves as a reminder of Allah's immense generosity and the importance of striving for His pleasure above all else.
orig: فانقلبوا بنعمة من الله وفضل لم يمسسهم سوء واتبعوا رضوان الله والله ذو فضل عظيم

translation: That is only Satan who frightens his allies, so do not fear them, but fear Me if you are believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the psychological tactics used by Satan to instill fear in his followers, suggesting that fear is a tool of manipulation. It instructs believers to redirect their fear from worldly threats, which are influenced by Satan, to the fear of God, which is a path to righteousness and faith. This redirection of fear is a test of true belief, encouraging believers to trust in God's protection and guidance over succumbing to the fears propagated by evil forces.
orig: إنما ذلكم الشيطان يخوف أولياءه فلا تخافوهم وخافون إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: And let not those who hasten to disbelief grieve you. Indeed, they will never harm Allah at all. Allah intends that He should give them no share in the Hereafter, and for them is a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reassurance to the Prophet Muhammad and by extension to all believers, emphasizing that the actions of those who rush into disbelief should not cause them sorrow or distress. It highlights the powerlessness of disbelievers against Allah, indicating that their disbelief does not affect Allah's sovereignty or plan. The verse also underscores divine justice, stating that Allah has decided not to grant disbelievers any portion in the Hereafter, and instead, they will face a severe punishment. This serves to strengthen the faith of believers by reminding them of the ultimate accountability and the consequences of disbelief.
orig: ولا يحزنك الذين يسارعون في الكفر إنهم لن يضروا الله شيئا يريد الله ألا يجعل لهم حظا في الآخرة ولهم عذاب عظيم

translation: Indeed, those who purchase disbelief at the price of faith - they will never harm Allah at all, and for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility and consequences of choosing disbelief over faith. It underscores that such a choice does not affect Allah's power or sovereignty in any way. Instead, those who make this choice will face severe punishment, emphasizing the gravity of rejecting faith after recognizing it. This serves as a warning and a reminder of the accountability one has for their choices regarding belief.
orig: إن الذين اشتروا الكفر بالإيمان لن يضروا الله شيئا ولهم عذاب أليم

translation: And let not those who disbelieve think that Our granting them respite is good for themselves. We grant them respite only that they may increase in sin, and for them is a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns that the temporary delay in punishment for disbelievers should not be misinterpreted as a sign of divine favor or leniency. Instead, this respite is a strategic delay by Allah, allowing disbelievers more time to accumulate sins, which will ultimately lead to a more severe and humiliating punishment. It emphasizes the inevitability of divine justice and the wisdom behind Allah's timing in meting out punishment.
orig: ولا يحسبن الذين كفروا أنما نملي لهم خير لأنفسهم إنما نملي لهم ليزدادوا إثما ولهم عذاب مهين

translation: It is not for Allah to leave the believers in the state you are in until He distinguishes the wicked from the good. Nor is it for Allah to inform you of the unseen, but Allah chooses from His messengers whom He wills. So believe in Allah and His messengers. And if you believe and fear Allah, then for you is a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine wisdom behind the trials and tests faced by believers, indicating that such challenges are necessary to separate the righteous from the corrupt. It underscores that Allah's knowledge of the unseen is not disclosed to everyone, but selectively revealed through chosen messengers. The verse calls for faith in Allah and His messengers, promising a significant reward for those who maintain their faith and piety, suggesting that enduring these trials with belief and righteousness leads to spiritual and possibly material rewards in the afterlife.
orig: ما كان الله ليذر المؤمنين على ما أنتم عليه حتى يميز الخبيث من الطيب وما كان الله ليطلعكم على الغيب ولكن الله يجتبي من رسله من يشاء فآمنوا بالله ورسله وإن تؤمنوا وتتقوا فلكم أجر عظيم

translation: And let not those who covetously withhold of the gifts which Allah hath given them of His Grace, think that it is good for them: Nay, it will be the worse for them: soon shall the things which they covetously withheld be tied to their necks like a collar on the Day of Resurrection. To Allah belongs the heritage of the heavens and the earth; and Allah is well-acquainted with all that you do.
interpretation: This verse warns against the dangers of stinginess and hoarding wealth, which is seen as a gift from Allah. The interpretation suggests that those who withhold their wealth out of greed mistakenly believe it benefits them, but in reality, it harms them spiritually. On the Day of Judgment, their hoarded wealth will become a burden around their necks, symbolizing the consequences of their actions. The verse emphasizes that all wealth ultimately belongs to Allah, reinforcing the Islamic principle of stewardship and the importance of using one's resources in ways that are pleasing to Allah, who is fully aware of all deeds.
orig: ولا يحسبن الذين يبخلون بما آتاهم الله من فضله هو خيرا لهم بل هو شر لهم سيطوقون ما بخلوا به يوم القيامة ولله ميراث السماوات والأرض والله بما تعملون خبير

translation: Indeed, Allah has heard the statement of those who said, 'Indeed, Allah is poor, and we are rich.' We will record what they said and their killing of the prophets without right and will say, 'Taste the punishment of the Burning Fire.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the arrogance and falsehood of those who claimed that Allah, the Almighty, is in need while boasting about their own wealth. Such a claim is a grave sin, reflecting a deep misunderstanding and disrespect towards the Divine. The verse also condemns the unjust killing of prophets, linking these two acts of defiance against God. The promise of recording their statements and actions signifies that no deed, especially those against divine figures and principles, goes unnoticed or unpunished. The mention of tasting the punishment of the Burning Fire serves as a stern warning of the severe consequences awaiting those who commit such blasphemies and injustices, emphasizing divine justice and retribution.
orig: لقد سمع الله قول الذين قالوا إن الله فقير ونحن أغنياء سنكتب ما قالوا وقتلهم الأنبياء بغير حق ونقول ذوقوا عذاب الحريق

translation: That is because of what your hands have put forth, and that Allah is not unjust to the servants.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of personal accountability in Islam. It suggests that the outcomes individuals face in life, whether positive or negative, are a direct result of their own actions ("what your hands have put forth"). The latter part of the verse reassures that Allah is always just and fair, never wronging His servants. This underlines the Islamic belief in divine justice, where every individual is responsible for their deeds, and Allah's judgment is always equitable.
orig: ذلك بما قدمت أيديكم وأن الله ليس بظلام للعبيد

translation: Those who said, 'Allah has taken a covenant with us that we shall not believe in a messenger until he brings us an offering that fire consumes.' Say, 'There have already come to you messengers before me with clear proofs and with that which you describe. So why did you kill them, if you are truthful?'
