orig: ومن يطع الله والرسول فأولئك مع الذين أنعم الله عليهم من النبيين والصديقين والشهداء والصالحين وحسن أولئك رفيقا

translation: That is the bounty from Allah, and sufficient is Allah as All-Knower.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all blessings and favors come from Allah alone, highlighting His generosity and sovereignty. The phrase 'sufficient is Allah as All-Knower' reassures believers that Allah's knowledge encompasses everything, and His wisdom in bestowing His bounty is perfect and complete. It encourages trust in Allah's omniscience and providence.
orig: ذلك الفضل من الله وكفى بالله عليما

translation: O you who have believed, take your precautions and either go forth in companies or go forth all together.
interpretation: This verse is a call to the believers to be vigilant and prepared for potential threats or battles. It emphasizes the importance of taking necessary precautions and organizing themselves either in smaller groups or as a whole unit to face challenges effectively. The underlying message is about unity, readiness, and strategic planning in the face of adversity.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا خذوا حذركم فانفروا ثبات أو انفروا جميعا

translation: And among you is he who lingers behind; and if a disaster strikes you, he says, 'Allah has favored me because I was not present with them as a witness.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy within the community, specifically addressing those who avoid participating in struggles or hardships, such as battles, out of fear or reluctance. When a calamity befalls the group, these individuals express relief and gratitude for not being involved, attributing their absence to a blessing from Allah. This behavior is criticized as it shows a lack of solidarity and genuine faith, revealing a self-centered attitude that contradicts the communal spirit and sacrifice encouraged in Islam.
orig: وإن منكم لمن ليبطئن فإن أصابتكم مصيبة قال قد أنعم الله علي إذ لم أكن معهم شهيدا

translation: And if a bounty comes to you from Allah, he would surely say - as if there had been no affection between you and him - 'Oh, I wish I had been with them so I could have attained a great triumph.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of those who distance themselves from believers during times of hardship but express regret and a desire to be with them when they see the believers receiving blessings or victories from Allah. It underscores the superficial nature of their supposed allegiance, which is driven by self-interest rather than genuine faith or loyalty.
orig: ولئن أصابكم فضل من الله ليقولن كأن لم تكن بينكم وبينه مودة يا ليتني كنت معهم فأفوز فوزا عظيما

translation: So let those fight in the cause of Allah who sell the life of this world for the Hereafter. And he who fights in the cause of Allah and is killed or achieves victory - We will bestow upon him a great reward.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to engage in jihad, not merely as physical combat but as a broader struggle in the path of Allah, prioritizing the eternal life over worldly existence. It promises a significant reward for those who participate in this struggle, whether they are martyred or victorious, emphasizing the spiritual value and divine appreciation of their sacrifice and effort.
orig: فليقاتل في سبيل الله الذين يشرون الحياة الدنيا بالآخرة ومن يقاتل في سبيل الله فيقتل أو يغلب فسوف نؤتيه أجرا عظيما

translation: And what is [the matter] with you that you do not fight in the cause of Allah and [for] the oppressed among men and women and children who say, 'Our Lord, take us out of this city of oppressive people and appoint for us from Yourself a protector and appoint for us from Yourself a helper?'
interpretation: This verse calls upon believers to engage in jihad, not only for the sake of Allah but also to protect and liberate the oppressed, including men, women, and children. It highlights the plight of those who are suffering under tyranny and their prayers for divine intervention and support. The verse emphasizes the moral obligation of the Muslim community to actively participate in alleviating the suffering of the oppressed, suggesting that fighting in such a cause is a fundamental aspect of faith and justice.
orig: وما لكم لا تقاتلون في سبيل الله والمستضعفين من الرجال والنساء والولدان الذين يقولون ربنا أخرجنا من هذه القرية الظالم أهلها واجعل لنا من لدنك وليا واجعل لنا من لدنك نصيرا

translation: Those who believe fight in the cause of Allah, and those who disbelieve fight in the cause of the taghut. So fight against the allies of Satan. Indeed, the plan of Satan is weak.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ideological and spiritual battle between believers and disbelievers, framing it as a struggle between divine guidance and the forces of misguidance. It calls upon believers to actively oppose those who support evil and falsehood, represented by Satan and his allies. The reassurance that Satan's schemes are weak serves to encourage believers, indicating that despite the apparent strength of evil forces, their foundation is frail and ultimately doomed to fail. This underscores the importance of steadfastness and faith in the face of opposition.
orig: الذين آمنوا يقاتلون في سبيل الله والذين كفروا يقاتلون في سبيل الطاغوت فقاتلوا أولياء الشيطان إن كيد الشيطان كان ضعيفا

translation: Have you not seen those who were told, 'Restrain your hands, establish prayer, and give zakah'? But when fighting was prescribed for them, a group of them feared people as they should fear Allah or even more so, and they said, 'Our Lord, why have You decreed fighting upon us? If only You had postponed it for us to a near term.' Say, 'The enjoyment of this world is little, and the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah. And you will not be wronged, even as much as a thread [inside a date seed].'
interpretation: This verse addresses the hypocrisy and fear of some believers when faced with the obligation of jihad. It highlights their preference for the comfort and safety of the worldly life over the spiritual and moral duties prescribed by Allah. The verse underscores the importance of prioritizing the eternal rewards of the Hereafter over the fleeting pleasures of this world, and reassures believers that they will not be wronged in the slightest by Allah, encouraging steadfastness and trust in divine justice.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين قيل لهم كفوا أيديكم وأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة فلما كتب عليهم القتال إذا فريق منهم يخشون الناس كخشية الله أو أشد خشية وقالوا ربنا لم كتبت علينا القتال لولا أخرتنا إلى أجل قريب قل متاع الدنيا قليل والآخرة خير لمن اتقى ولا تظلمون فتيلا

translation: Wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you are in lofty towers. And if a good thing comes to them, they say, 'This is from Allah,' but if an evil thing befalls them, they say, 'This is from you.' Say, 'All is from Allah.' So what is wrong with these people that they do not seem to understand any statement?
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of death and the human tendency to attribute good fortune to divine favor while blaming others for misfortune. It teaches that both good and bad come from Allah, emphasizing the need for acceptance and understanding of divine decree. The rhetorical question at the end highlights a common human failing to grasp the deeper meanings of life's events and divine messages, urging believers to reflect more deeply on their faith and the nature of existence.
orig: أينما تكونوا يدرككم الموت ولو كنتم في بروج مشيدة وإن تصبهم حسنة يقولوا هذه من عند الله وإن تصبهم سيئة يقولوا هذه من عندك قل كل من عند الله فمال هؤلاء القوم لا يكادون يفقهون حديثا

translation: Whatever good reaches you is from Allah, and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself. And We have sent you to mankind as a messenger, and Allah is sufficient as a witness.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine providence and human responsibility. It teaches that all blessings and good fortunes are bestowed by Allah, reflecting His mercy and grace. Conversely, any misfortune or evil that one experiences is a result of one's own actions, underscoring the importance of personal accountability. The verse also highlights the prophetic mission of Muhammad, sent as a messenger to all of humanity, with Allah serving as the ultimate witness to this mission and to the truth of the message conveyed.
orig: ما أصابك من حسنة فمن الله وما أصابك من سيئة فمن نفسك وأرسلناك للناس رسولا وكفى بالله شهيدا

translation: Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah; and whoever turns away - We have not sent you over them as a guardian.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of following the Prophet Muhammad's guidance, as obedience to him is equated with obedience to Allah. It also relieves the Prophet, and by extension all messengers, of the responsibility for those who choose to turn away from the message, indicating that their role is to convey the message, not to enforce compliance.
orig: من يطع الرسول فقد أطاع الله ومن تولى فما أرسلناك عليهم حفيظا

translation: And they say, 'Obedience,' but when they leave you, a group of them spends the night planning other than what you say. But Allah records what they plan by night. So turn away from them and put your trust in Allah, and sufficient is Allah as a Trustee.
interpretation: This verse addresses the hypocrisy within the community, highlighting the discrepancy between what some people profess publicly and their true intentions in private. It emphasizes the omniscience of Allah, who is aware of all secret plans and discussions. The instruction to the Prophet Muhammad to turn away from such individuals and to trust in Allah underscores the importance of reliance on divine guidance and protection over human assurances. It serves as a reminder that Allah is the ultimate guardian and protector, sufficient in His capacity to manage and oversee all affairs.
orig: ويقولون طاعة فإذا برزوا من عندك بيت طائفة منهم غير الذي تقول والله يكتب ما يبيتون فأعرض عنهم وتوكل على الله وكفى بالله وكيلا

translation: Do they not then ponder over the Qur'an? And if it had been from other than Allah, they would have found in it much discrepancy.
interpretation: This verse invites believers to reflect deeply on the Qur'an, emphasizing its divine origin. The absence of contradictions within the text is presented as evidence of its revelation from Allah, suggesting that human-authored works typically contain inconsistencies. This encourages a thoughtful engagement with the scripture to appreciate its coherence and divine nature.
orig: أفلا يتدبرون القرآن ولو كان من عند غير الله لوجدوا فيه اختلافا كثيرا

translation: And when there comes to them an affair of security or fear, they spread it. But if they had referred it to the Messenger or to those in authority among them, then the ones who can draw correct conclusions from it would have known about it. And if not for the favor of Allah upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan, except for a few.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of verifying information and consulting with knowledgeable and authoritative figures before spreading news, especially concerning matters of security or fear. It highlights a societal issue where people often react hastily and spread rumors without proper investigation, which can lead to chaos and misinformation. The verse suggests that by referring such matters to the Prophet Muhammad or the leaders within the community, those capable of understanding and analyzing the situation correctly would be able to guide the community appropriately. Furthermore, it underscores the protective grace and mercy of Allah, indicating that without divine guidance, people are prone to follow misleading paths influenced by Satan, except for a few who remain steadfast.
orig: وإذا جاءهم أمر من الأمن أو الخوف أذاعوا به ولو ردوه إلى الرسول وإلى أولي الأمر منهم لعلمه الذين يستنبطونه منهم ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته لاتبعتم الشيطان إلا قليلا

translation: So fight in the cause of Allah; you are not responsible except for yourself. And encourage the believers [to fight]. Perhaps Allah will restrain the [military] might of those who disbelieve. And Allah is greater in might and stronger in [exemplary] punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the personal responsibility of the Prophet Muhammad to engage in jihad for the sake of Allah, indicating that his duty is to exert himself fully in this cause without being accountable for the actions of others. It also instructs him to motivate the believers to participate in this struggle, with the hope that Allah will curb the power of the disbelievers. The verse underscores the belief in Allah's superior power and His ability to deliver a more severe punishment than any human force, serving as a reassurance to the believers of divine support and ultimate victory.
orig: فقاتل في سبيل الله لا تكلف إلا نفسك وحرض المؤمنين عسى الله أن يكف بأس الذين كفروا والله أشد بأسا وأشد تنكيلا

translation: Whoever intercedes for a good cause will have a share in it, and whoever intercedes for an evil cause will have a portion of its burden. And Allah is Ever a Careful Accountant over everything.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the moral responsibility of intercession. It teaches that when a person advocates or intercedes on behalf of others, whether for good or bad, they will bear a portion of the consequences of that action. If one intercedes for a righteous cause, they will be rewarded accordingly. Conversely, if one intercedes for a harmful or evil cause, they will be held accountable for contributing to that harm. The verse underscores the omnipresence and meticulousness of Allah in recording and judging every action, highlighting the importance of choosing one's actions and associations wisely.
orig: من يشفع شفاعة حسنة يكن له نصيب منها ومن يشفع شفاعة سيئة يكن له كفل منها وكان الله على كل شيء مقيتا

translation: And when you are greeted with a greeting, greet [in return] with one better than it or [at least] return it [in like]. Indeed, Allah is ever, over all things, an Accountant.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of responding to greetings with kindness and generosity. It teaches Muslims to either respond to a greeting with a better one, showcasing humility and respect, or at the very least, to return the greeting as it was given. The underlying message is about fostering positive social interactions and maintaining good relations with others. The mention of Allah as an Accountant over all things serves as a reminder that our actions, including how we greet and respond to others, are observed and will be accounted for in the hereafter, encouraging sincerity and mindfulness in our daily interactions.
orig: وإذا حييتم بتحية فحيوا بأحسن منها أو ردوها إن الله كان على كل شيء حسيبا

translation: Allah - there is no deity except Him. He will surely assemble you for [account on] the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt. And who is more truthful than Allah in statement?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness of Allah, affirming that He is the only deity worthy of worship. It underscores the certainty of the Day of Resurrection, where all people will be gathered for judgment. The rhetorical question at the end reinforces the absolute truthfulness of Allah's promises and statements, encouraging believers to have unwavering faith in His words about the hereafter.
orig: الله لا إله إلا هو ليجمعنكم إلى يوم القيامة لا ريب فيه ومن أصدق من الله حديثا

translation: So why, when the hypocrites have a faction among them, do you [Muslims] not fight them, while Allah will destroy them for what they earned? Do you wish to guide those whom Allah has sent astray? And he whom Allah sends astray - never will you find for him a way [to guidance].
interpretation: This verse addresses the Muslim community's interaction with hypocrites within their midst. It questions the hesitation of Muslims to confront these hypocrites, emphasizing that it is not their role to guide those whom Allah has chosen to lead astray due to their own actions. The verse underscores the divine justice where Allah will ultimately deal with the hypocrites according to their deeds, and it serves as a reminder to the believers not to take upon themselves the responsibility of correcting those who have been divinely misguided, as there is no path to guidance for them.
orig: فما لكم في المنافقين فئتين والله أركسهم بما كسبوا أتريدون أن تهدوا من أضل الله ومن يضلل الله فلن تجد له سبيلا

translation: They wish that you should disbelieve as they disbelieve, and thus you become alike. So do not take friends from among them until they emigrate in the way of Allah. But if they turn away, then seize them and kill them wherever you find them, and do not take from among them any friend or helper.
interpretation: This verse addresses the believers, warning them about the intentions of the disbelievers who wish for the believers to abandon their faith and join them in disbelief, thereby creating a false sense of equality. The verse instructs the believers not to form alliances or friendships with these disbelievers unless they demonstrate their commitment to Islam by emigrating in the path of Allah. If the disbelievers refuse to do so and continue to oppose the believers, the verse permits the believers to take action against them, emphasizing the importance of maintaining the purity and integrity of the Muslim community. This directive is specific to the context of hostility and persecution faced by the early Muslim community, highlighting the need for vigilance and separation from those who actively work against the faith.
orig: ودوا لو تكفرون كما كفروا فتكونون سواء فلا تتخذوا منهم أولياء حتى يهاجروا في سبيل الله فإن تولوا فخذوهم واقتلوهم حيث وجدتموهم ولا تتخذوا منهم وليا ولا نصيرا

translation: Except for those who take refuge with a people between yourselves and whom is a treaty or those who come to you, their hearts strained at [the prospect of] fighting you or fighting their own people. And if Allah had willed, He could have given them power over you, and they would have fought you. So if they remove themselves from you and do not fight you and offer you peace, then Allah has not made for you a cause [for fighting] against them.
interpretation: This verse provides guidance on the treatment of individuals who seek refuge among Muslims due to a treaty or due to internal conflict within their own group. It emphasizes the importance of granting safety to such individuals, reflecting Islamic principles of peace and protection. The verse suggests that if these individuals refrain from fighting and instead seek peace, Muslims are not permitted to engage them in combat. This highlights the Qur'anic emphasis on resolving conflicts peacefully and respecting treaties, showcasing the value placed on peace and security over warfare.
orig: إلا الذين يصلون إلى قوم بينكم وبينهم ميثاق أو جاءوكم حصرت صدورهم أن يقاتلوكم أو يقاتلوا قومهم ولو شاء الله لسلطهم عليكم فلقاتلوكم فإن اعتزلوكم فلم يقاتلوكم وألقوا إليكم السلم فما جعل الله لكم عليهم سبيلا

translation: You will find others who wish to have security from you and security for their own people. Every time they are sent back to temptation, they succumb to it. If they do not withdraw from you nor offer you peace, nor restrain their hands, then seize them and kill them wherever you find them. And those - We have given you a clear authority against them.
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad and the Muslim community about dealing with certain groups during conflicts. It highlights a category of people who outwardly express a desire for peace and security but are easily swayed back into hostility when faced with temptation or pressure. The verse instructs Muslims to be vigilant and take decisive action against such individuals if they do not genuinely seek peace, refrain from aggression, and stop their hostile actions. It underscores the principle of self-defense and the necessity of maintaining security, providing a clear mandate for action against those who pose a continuous threat despite opportunities for peace.
orig: ستجدون آخرين يريدون أن يأمنوكم ويأمنوا قومهم كل ما ردوا إلى الفتنة أركسوا فيها فإن لم يعتزلوكم ويلقوا إليكم السلم ويكفوا أيديهم فخذوهم واقتلوهم حيث ثقفتموهم وأولئكم جعلنا لكم عليهم سلطانا مبينا

translation: It is not for a believer to kill another believer except by mistake. And whoever kills a believer by mistake - then the freeing of a believing slave and a compensation payment presented to the deceased's family, unless they remit it as charity. But if the deceased was from a people at war with you and he was a believer - then [only] the freeing of a believing slave; and if he was from a people with whom you have a treaty - then a compensation payment presented to his family and the freeing of a believing slave. And whoever does not find [or afford that] - then [instead], a fast for two months consecutively, [seeking] acceptance of repentance from Allah. And Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse establishes the sanctity of a believer's life and outlines the consequences and atonements for unintentionally killing a fellow believer. It emphasizes the importance of reconciliation and compensation to the victim's family, while also considering the context of the deceased's affiliations. The verse provides a structured path for repentance and forgiveness, reflecting Allah's mercy and justice. It also highlights the value of human life and the need for believers to maintain peace and avoid harm within the community.
orig: وما كان لمؤمن أن يقتل مؤمنا إلا خطأ ومن قتل مؤمنا خطأ فتحرير رقبة مؤمنة ودية مسلمة إلى أهله إلا أن يصدقوا فإن كان من قوم عدو لكم وهو مؤمن فتحرير رقبة مؤمنة وإن كان من قوم بينكم وبينهم ميثاق فدية مسلمة إلى أهله وتحرير رقبة مؤمنة فمن لم يجد فصيام شهرين متتابعين توبة من الله وكان الله عليما حكيما

translation: And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, to abide therein forever, and the wrath of Allah will be upon him, and He will curse him and prepare for him a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse underscores the severity of the crime of intentionally killing a believer, emphasizing that such an act is not only a grave sin but also results in eternal damnation in Hell. The mention of Allah's wrath, curse, and the preparation of a great punishment highlights the profound spiritual and moral consequences of this act, serving as a strong deterrent against such a transgression and reflecting the sanctity of human life in Islam.
orig: ومن يقتل مؤمنا متعمدا فجزاؤه جهنم خالدا فيها وغضب الله عليه ولعنه وأعد له عذابا عظيما

translation: O you who have believed, when you go forth [to fight] in the cause of Allah, investigate; and do not say to one who gives you [a greeting of] peace, 'You are not a believer,' seeking the goods of worldly life; for with Allah are many gains. You were like that before; then Allah conferred His favor upon you, so investigate. Indeed, Allah is ever, with what you do, Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of discernment and fairness in interactions, particularly in times of conflict. It instructs believers not to hastily judge others' faith based on superficial interactions, such as a greeting of peace, especially when driven by materialistic motives. The verse reminds Muslims of their own past, where they were in a similar position of being judged, and urges them to learn from that experience. It encourages a thorough investigation before making judgments about someone's faith, highlighting Allah's omniscience and the moral accountability that comes with one's actions. The underlying message is a call for justice, humility, and awareness of Allah's greater rewards beyond worldly gains.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا ضربتم في سبيل الله فتبينوا ولا تقولوا لمن ألقى إليكم السلام لست مؤمنا تبتغون عرض الحياة الدنيا فعند الله مغانم كثيرة كذلك كنتم من قبل فمن الله عليكم فتبينوا إن الله كان بما تعملون خبيرا

translation: Not equal are those believers who sit (at home) except those who are disabled, and those who strive in the way of Allah with their wealth and their lives. Allah has preferred those who strive with their wealth and their lives over those who sit (at home) by a degree. And to all Allah has promised the best (reward), but Allah has preferred those who strive over those who sit (at home) with a great reward.
interpretation: This verse highlights the distinction in merit between two groups of believers: those who actively participate in jihad (struggle or striving) in the path of Allah with their wealth and lives, and those who remain at home without any valid excuse. The verse emphasizes that while both groups are promised goodness by Allah, those who engage in jihad are granted a higher status and a greater reward. This differentiation is not to demean the believers who stay behind but to encourage active participation in the defense and propagation of faith, recognizing the sacrifices made by those who strive. The mention of 'except those who are disabled' indicates that the verse does not apply to those who are physically unable to participate, acknowledging their intention and spirit.
orig: لا يستوي القاعدون من المؤمنين غير أولي الضرر والمجاهدون في سبيل الله بأموالهم وأنفسهم فضل الله المجاهدين بأموالهم وأنفسهم على القاعدين درجة وكلا وعد الله الحسنى وفضل الله المجاهدين على القاعدين أجرا عظيما

translation: Degrees from Him, and forgiveness and mercy. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the various levels of reward and spiritual elevation that Allah bestows upon believers, alongside His forgiveness and mercy. It emphasizes that Allah's nature is inherently forgiving and merciful, encouraging believers to seek closeness to Him through righteous deeds, knowing that His mercy encompasses all things and His forgiveness is always accessible.
orig: درجات منه ومغفرة ورحمة وكان الله غفورا رحيما

translation: Indeed, those whom the angels take [in death] while wronging themselves - [the angels] will say, 'In what [condition] were you [living]?' They will say, 'We were oppressed in the land.' [The angels] will say, 'Was not the earth of Allah spacious [enough] for you to emigrate therein?' For those, their refuge will be Hell - and evil it is as a destination.
interpretation: This verse addresses those who die in a state of wrongdoing because they did not emigrate from a land where they were oppressed and unable to practice their faith freely. The angels question them about their choice to remain in such conditions, highlighting that Allah's earth is vast and they had the option to migrate to a place where they could live righteously. The verse emphasizes personal responsibility and the importance of taking action to preserve one's faith, warning that failure to do so leads to Hell as a final abode, underscoring the gravity of neglecting this duty.
orig: إن الذين توفاهم الملائكة ظالمي أنفسهم قالوا فيم كنتم قالوا كنا مستضعفين في الأرض قالوا ألم تكن أرض الله واسعة فتهاجروا فيها فأولئك مأواهم جهنم وساءت مصيرا

translation: Except for the weak ones among men, women, and children who cannot devise a plan nor are they directed to a way.
interpretation: This verse provides an exception for those who are oppressed and lack the power or means to escape or resist the circumstances they are in. It highlights the mercy and understanding of Allah towards those who are truly helpless and unable to find a way out of their situation, indicating that they will not be held accountable in the same manner as those who have the ability to act but choose not to.
orig: إلا المستضعفين من الرجال والنساء والولدان لا يستطيعون حيلة ولا يهتدون سبيلا

translation: So perhaps Allah will pardon them, and Allah is Ever-Pardoning, All-Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse suggests that there is hope for Allah's forgiveness and mercy even for those who have committed sins, as long as they sincerely repent and seek His pardon. It emphasizes Allah's attributes of being Ever-Pardoning and All-Forgiving, highlighting the vastness of His mercy and the possibility of redemption for believers.
orig: فأولئك عسى الله أن يعفو عنهم وكان الله عفوا غفورا

translation: And whoever emigrates in the cause of Allah will find on the earth many places of refuge and abundance. And whoever leaves his home as an emigrant to Allah and His Messenger and then death overtakes him - his reward has already become incumbent upon Allah. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the spiritual and material support that Allah provides to those who migrate for His sake. It reassures believers that by undertaking hijra (migration) in pursuit of faith and righteousness, they will find ample resources and safe havens. Furthermore, it highlights the divine promise that if a person dies during this migration, their reward is guaranteed by Allah, underscoring His attributes of forgiveness and mercy. This serves as a profound encouragement for Muslims to prioritize their faith over worldly attachments, trusting in Allah's providence and ultimate justice.
orig: ومن يهاجر في سبيل الله يجد في الأرض مراغما كثيرا وسعة ومن يخرج من بيته مهاجرا إلى الله ورسوله ثم يدركه الموت فقد وقع أجره على الله وكان الله غفورا رحيما

translation: And when you travel throughout the land, there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer, [especially] if you fear that those who disbelieve may harm you. Indeed, the disbelievers are ever to you a clear enemy.
interpretation: This verse provides a practical concession for Muslims who are traveling, allowing them to shorten their prayers from the usual four rak'ahs to two. This ruling is not just a matter of convenience but is also linked to the potential danger posed by non-believers during travel. The verse underscores the perpetual state of enmity between believers and those who reject faith, highlighting the need for vigilance and adaptability in religious practice under such circumstances. It reflects the Qur'an's recognition of the challenges faced by the Muslim community and offers a solution that balances religious duty with personal safety.
orig: وإذا ضربتم في الأرض فليس عليكم جناح أن تقصروا من الصلاة إن خفتم أن يفتنكم الذين كفروا إن الكافرين كانوا لكم عدوا مبينا

translation: And when you are among them and lead them in prayer, let a group of them stand [in prayer] with you and let them carry their arms. And when they have prostrated, let them be [in position] behind you and have the other group that has not yet prayed come and pray with you, taking precaution and carrying their arms. Those who disbelieve wish that you would neglect your arms and your equipment so they could attack you in a single [rush]. And there is no blame upon you if you are troubled by rain or are ill for putting down your arms, but take precaution. Indeed, Allah has prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse was revealed during a time of military engagement, specifically during the Battle of Uhud. It provides practical guidance on how to maintain both spiritual and physical readiness in the face of potential attack. The instruction to pray in shifts while keeping arms at the ready underscores the necessity of vigilance and preparedness in times of danger. It reflects the broader Islamic principle of balancing religious duties with the practical needs of self-defense and community protection. The verse also warns against complacency, as the disbelievers are eager to exploit any moment of negligence. The allowance to lay down arms under certain conditions, like rain or illness, shows a pragmatic approach to religious rulings, emphasizing the importance of context in applying Islamic law. Ultimately, the verse reassures believers of divine support and warns the disbelievers of a forthcoming punishment, reinforcing the themes of trust in God and the consequences of disbelief.
orig: وإذا كنت فيهم فأقمت لهم الصلاة فلتقم طائفة منهم معك وليأخذوا أسلحتهم فإذا سجدوا فليكونوا من ورائكم ولتأت طائفة أخرى لم يصلوا فليصلوا معك وليأخذوا حذرهم وأسلحتهم ود الذين كفروا لو تغفلون عن أسلحتكم وأمتعتكم فيميلون عليكم ميلة واحدة ولا جناح عليكم إن كان بكم أذى من مطر أو كنتم مرضى أن تضعوا أسلحتكم وخذوا حذركم إن الله أعد للكافرين عذابا مهينا

translation: So when you have finished the prayer, remember Allah standing, sitting, and on your sides. But when you are secure, establish the prayer. Indeed, the prayer has been decreed upon the believers at specific times.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining a constant remembrance of Allah in all states and conditions, whether standing, sitting, or lying on one's side, reflecting a life permeated with mindfulness of God. It also highlights the necessity of performing the obligatory prayers at their designated times, underscoring that prayer is a fundamental duty for believers, structured and timed as a means of maintaining spiritual discipline and connection with the Divine.
orig: فإذا قضيتم الصلاة فاذكروا الله قياما وقعودا وعلى جنوبكم فإذا اطمأننتم فأقيموا الصلاة إن الصلاة كانت على المؤمنين كتابا موقوتا

translation: And do not weaken in pursuit of the enemy; if you are suffering, then indeed they are suffering as you suffer, but you hope from Allah that which they do not hope for, and Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse encourages steadfastness and perseverance in the face of adversity, particularly in the context of conflict. It reassures believers that their enemies suffer similarly, yet the believers have a unique hope in divine reward and support from Allah, which their adversaries lack. This hope should strengthen their resolve. The mention of Allah being Knowing and Wise underscores that this situation is under divine observation and wisdom, guiding believers to trust in the ultimate justice and plan of Allah.
orig: ولا تهنوا في ابتغاء القوم إن تكونوا تألمون فإنهم يألمون كما تألمون وترجون من الله ما لا يرجون وكان الله عليما حكيما

translation: Indeed, We have revealed to you the Book in truth so that you may judge between the people by that which Allah has shown you. And do not be an advocate for the deceitful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin and purpose of the Qur'an, which is to provide guidance for making just decisions among people. It instructs the Prophet Muhammad, and by extension all Muslims, to use the Qur'an as the criterion for judgment, ensuring decisions are aligned with divine wisdom rather than personal biases or societal pressures. Additionally, it warns against supporting or advocating for those who are dishonest or deceitful, reinforcing the importance of integrity and justice in Islamic governance and personal conduct.
orig: إنا أنزلنا إليك الكتاب بالحق لتحكم بين الناس بما أراك الله ولا تكن للخائنين خصيما

translation: And seek forgiveness from Allah. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to frequently seek forgiveness from Allah, emphasizing that no matter the magnitude of one's sins, Allah's attribute of being Forgiving and Merciful is always available to those who sincerely repent. It highlights the importance of repentance in maintaining a close relationship with Allah and assures believers of His readiness to forgive.
orig: واستغفر الله إن الله كان غفورا رحيما

translation: And do not argue on behalf of those who deceive themselves. Indeed, Allah does not like those who are deceitful and sinful.
interpretation: This verse warns against defending or making excuses for those who engage in self-deception and wrongdoing. It emphasizes that Allah disapproves of individuals who are dishonest and commit sins, highlighting the importance of integrity and righteousness in one's actions and associations.
orig: ولا تجادل عن الذين يختانون أنفسهم إن الله لا يحب من كان خوانا أثيما

translation: They seek to hide from the people, but they cannot hide from Allah, for He is with them when they plot by night with words that do not please Him. And Allah encompasses what they do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility and moral error of attempting to conceal one's misdeeds from Allah. It emphasizes Allah's omnipresence and omniscience, indicating that no matter how secretive or nocturnal one's actions may be, they are fully known to Him. The verse serves as a reminder of divine accountability, urging believers to be mindful of their actions and words, as Allah is fully aware and surrounds all that they do.
orig: يستخفون من الناس ولا يستخفون من الله وهو معهم إذ يبيتون ما لا يرضى من القول وكان الله بما يعملون محيطا

translation: Here you are, those who have argued on their behalf in worldly life, but who will argue with Allah on their behalf on the Day of Resurrection, or who will be their advocate?
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of human intercession and advocacy on the Day of Judgment. It points out that while people may argue and defend others in this worldly life, no one will be able to intercede or act as an advocate for anyone else before Allah on the Day of Resurrection. It emphasizes the direct accountability of every individual to Allah, underscoring the importance of personal responsibility and the ultimate sovereignty of Allah's judgment.
orig: ها أنتم هؤلاء جادلتم عنهم في الحياة الدنيا فمن يجادل الله عنهم يوم القيامة أم من يكون عليهم وكيلا

translation: And whoever does evil or wrongs himself but then seeks Allah's forgiveness, he will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the boundless mercy and forgiveness of Allah. It reassures believers that no matter the severity of their sins or the wrongs they commit against themselves, the door to repentance and forgiveness remains open. By seeking forgiveness sincerely, one can always turn back to Allah and find Him ready to forgive and show mercy, highlighting the importance of repentance and the ever-present opportunity for spiritual renewal and divine pardon.
orig: ومن يعمل سوءا أو يظلم نفسه ثم يستغفر الله يجد الله غفورا رحيما

translation: And whoever earns a sin, then he earns it only against himself, and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes personal accountability for one's actions. It teaches that the consequences of sinning affect the individual sinner alone, reinforcing the concept of individual responsibility in Islam. Additionally, it highlights the attributes of Allah as being fully aware and wise, indicating that His judgments are based on complete knowledge and perfect wisdom.
orig: ومن يكسب إثما فإنما يكسبه على نفسه وكان الله عليما حكيما

translation: And whoever earns a fault or a sin and then throws it on an innocent person, he has indeed borne false accusation and a clear sin.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity of falsely accusing someone of a wrongdoing or sin. It highlights that such an act not only constitutes a false accusation but also a manifest sin in itself. The verse serves as a warning against the injustice of shifting blame onto the innocent, underscoring the moral and ethical responsibility to bear the consequences of one's own actions.
orig: ومن يكسب خطيئة أو إثما ثم يرم به بريئا فقد احتمل بهتانا وإثما مبينا

translation: And if it were not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, a group of them would have intended to mislead you. But they do not mislead except themselves, and they will not harm you at all. And Allah has revealed to you the Book and wisdom and has taught you what you did not know. And the grace of Allah upon you has ever been great.
interpretation: This verse highlights the protective nature of Allah's grace and mercy towards the Prophet Muhammad. It suggests that despite the efforts of some individuals to lead the Prophet astray, their attempts are futile because Allah's guidance and protection are paramount. The verse reassures the Prophet that those who try to mislead him only harm themselves and cannot affect him adversely. Furthermore, it emphasizes that the revelation of the Qur'an and divine wisdom to the Prophet is a manifestation of Allah's immense favor, which not only guides him but also elevates his status, underscoring the continuous and significant blessings bestowed upon him by Allah.
orig: ولولا فضل الله عليك ورحمته لهمت طائفة منهم أن يضلوك وما يضلون إلا أنفسهم وما يضرونك من شيء وأنزل الله عليك الكتاب والحكمة وعلمك ما لم تكن تعلم وكان فضل الله عليك عظيما

translation: There is no good in much of their secret talks, except for the one who enjoins charity, or goodness, or reconciliation between people. And whoever does that, seeking the pleasure of Allah, We will give him a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of using speech for beneficial purposes. It criticizes idle or harmful secret conversations, suggesting that most private discussions lack moral value unless they are aimed at promoting charity, doing good deeds, or resolving conflicts among people. The verse encourages believers to use their words constructively and with the intention of pleasing Allah, promising a significant reward for such actions. This highlights the Islamic value placed on positive communication and the intention behind one's actions.
orig: لا خير في كثير من نجواهم إلا من أمر بصدقة أو معروف أو إصلاح بين الناس ومن يفعل ذلك ابتغاء مرضات الله فسوف نؤتيه أجرا عظيما

translation: And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows other than the way of the believers - We will give him what he has taken and drive him into Hell, and evil it is as a destination.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequences of rejecting the clear guidance provided by the Messenger of Allah after it has been made evident. It warns that choosing a path divergent from that of the faithful believers leads to a dire outcome. Specifically, it indicates that such a person will be burdened with the consequences of their choices and ultimately be consigned to Hell, illustrating the severe punishment awaiting those who deliberately stray from the right path after receiving clear guidance.
orig: ومن يشاقق الرسول من بعد ما تبين له الهدى ويتبع غير سبيل المؤمنين نوله ما تولى ونصله جهنم وساءت مصيرا

translation: Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. And whoever associates others with Allah has certainly gone far astray.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity of shirk, or associating partners with Allah, which is considered the gravest sin in Islam. It underscores that while Allah may forgive other sins at His discretion, shirk is unforgivable if one dies in that state without repentance. The verse also highlights the spiritual and moral consequences of shirk, describing it as a profound deviation from the right path, leading one far astray from the truth and guidance of Islam.
orig: إن الله لا يغفر أن يشرك به ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشاء ومن يشرك بالله فقد ضل ضلالا بعيدا

translation: They invoke none but female deities besides Him, and they invoke none but a rebellious Satan.
interpretation: This verse critiques the polytheistic practices of invoking female deities and associating them with Satan, emphasizing that such acts are misguided and lead to following a rebellious entity against God's will.
orig: إن يدعون من دونه إلا إناثا وإن يدعون إلا شيطانا مريدا

translation: May Allah curse him. And he said, 'I will surely take from among Your servants a specific portion.'
interpretation: This verse refers to Iblis (Satan) after he was cursed by Allah for refusing to prostrate to Adam. The curse signifies his eternal damnation and separation from divine mercy. Iblis's statement reflects his defiance and determination to mislead humanity, claiming a portion of Allah's servants as his followers. This highlights the ongoing spiritual battle between good and evil, where Iblis seeks to corrupt and lead astray as many of Allah's servants as possible.
orig: لعنه الله وقال لأتخذن من عبادك نصيبا مفروضا

translation: And I will mislead them, and I will create in them false desires, and I will order them to slit the ears of cattle, and to deface the (fair) nature created by Allah. Whoever, forsaking Allah, takes satan for a friend, hath surely suffered a loss that is manifest.
interpretation: This verse reveals the deceptive tactics of Satan, who promises to mislead humans by instilling false desires and encouraging them to commit acts that go against the natural order established by Allah, such as mutilating animals. The verse warns that choosing to follow Satan instead of Allah leads to a clear and evident loss, emphasizing the severe consequences of straying from divine guidance.
orig: ولأضلنهم ولأمنينهم ولآمرنهم فليبتكن آذان الأنعام ولآمرنهم فليغيرن خلق الله ومن يتخذ الشيطان وليا من دون الله فقد خسر خسرانا مبينا

translation: He promises them and arouses desire in them, but Satan does not promise them except delusion.
interpretation: This verse highlights the deceptive nature of Satan, who entices people with false promises and illusions of gain, leading them astray from the path of righteousness. It serves as a warning to believers to be wary of such temptations and to recognize that the promises made by Satan are ultimately empty and misleading, aimed at causing spiritual ruin.
orig: يعدهم ويمنيهم وما يعدهم الشيطان إلا غرورا

translation: Those - their abode is Hell, and they will find no escape from it.
interpretation: This verse indicates that those who are described in the preceding verses as disbelievers or wrongdoers will have Hell as their final destination. The use of "ma'wa" (abode) suggests a permanent residence, emphasizing the eternal nature of their punishment. The phrase "la yajiduna 'anha mahisa" (they will find no escape from it) underscores the inescapable and irreversible nature of their fate, highlighting the severity of divine judgment and the consequences of one's actions in the afterlife.
orig: أولئك مأواهم جهنم ولا يجدون عنها محيصا

translation: And those who believe and do righteous deeds, We will surely admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever. [This is] the promise of Allah, [which is] true. And who is more truthful than Allah in statement?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the reward awaiting those who have faith and perform good deeds. It assures believers of their entry into Paradise, described as gardens with flowing rivers, symbolizing eternal peace and abundance. The promise of eternal dwelling in this paradise underscores the certainty and permanence of the reward. By affirming that this is a promise from Allah and questioning who could be more truthful than Him, the verse reinforces the absolute trustworthiness of Allah's word, encouraging steadfastness in faith and righteousness.
orig: والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات سندخلهم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها أبدا وعد الله حقا ومن أصدق من الله قيلا

translation: It is not in accordance with your wishes, nor the wishes of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be requited for it, and will not find for themselves, besides Allah, any protector or helper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of divine justice and accountability. It underscores that human desires, whether from Muslims or the People of the Scripture, do not influence the outcome of one's actions in the eyes of Allah. The verse asserts that every individual is responsible for their deeds, and those who commit evil will face the consequences without any external support or intercession, as only Allah holds the ultimate authority and power to judge and assist.
orig: ليس بأمانيكم ولا أماني أهل الكتاب من يعمل سوءا يجز به ولا يجد له من دون الله وليا ولا نصيرا

translation: And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while being a believer - those will enter Paradise and will not be wronged, [even as much as] the speck on a date seed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the equality of all believers before God, regardless of gender. It highlights that righteous actions combined with faith are the criteria for entering Paradise. The mention of "not being wronged, [even as much as] the speck on a date seed" underscores God's justice and fairness, indicating that no one will be treated unjustly in the slightest measure. This reassures believers of the meticulous fairness in divine judgment.
orig: ومن يعمل من الصالحات من ذكر أو أنثى وهو مؤمن فأولئك يدخلون الجنة ولا يظلمون نقيرا

translation: And who is better in religion than one who submits his face [i.e., self] to Allah while being a doer of good and follows the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth? And Allah took Abraham as an intimate friend.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the superiority of Islam as a religion, highlighting the ideal of complete submission to Allah, coupled with righteous actions. It positions the religion of Abraham as a model of monotheism and sincerity, suggesting that true faith involves not only belief but also emulation of prophetic examples, such as Abraham, who was chosen by Allah as a close friend due to his unwavering faith and obedience. The verse encourages Muslims to follow this path of submission, goodness, and adherence to the pure monotheism exemplified by Abraham.
orig: ومن أحسن دينا ممن أسلم وجهه لله وهو محسن واتبع ملة إبراهيم حنيفا واتخذ الله إبراهيم خليلا

translation: And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, and Allah is, of all things, encompassing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and omnipresence of Allah. It asserts that everything in existence, both in the heavens and on earth, is under Allah's dominion and ownership. The phrase 'Allah is, of all things, encompassing' highlights Allah's complete knowledge and control over all aspects of creation, indicating that nothing is beyond His reach or understanding. This underscores the concept of Tawheed (the Oneness of Allah) and encourages believers to recognize and submit to Allah's all-encompassing power and presence in their lives.
orig: ولله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وكان الله بكل شيء محيطا

translation: And they seek your ruling concerning women. Say, 'Allah gives you His ruling about them, and what is recited to you in the Book concerning the orphan girls whom you do not give what is prescribed for them and yet you desire to marry them, and concerning the weak among children, and that you stand firm for justice to orphans. And whatever good you do, indeed, Allah is ever knowing of it.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad's role in providing guidance on matters related to women, specifically focusing on the treatment of orphan girls and vulnerable children. It emphasizes the importance of justice and fairness, particularly in ensuring that orphan girls receive their rightful inheritance and are not exploited through marriage for financial gain. The verse also underscores that any good deeds done in this regard are known to Allah, encouraging believers to act justly out of a sense of moral and religious duty.
orig: ويستفتونك في النساء قل الله يفتيكم فيهن وما يتلى عليكم في الكتاب في يتامى النساء اللاتي لا تؤتونهن ما كتب لهن وترغبون أن تنكحوهن والمستضعفين من الولدان وأن تقوموا لليتامى بالقسط وما تفعلوا من خير فإن الله كان به عليما

translation: And if a woman fears from her husband ill-conduct or desertion, there is no sin upon them if they make terms of peace between themselves - and peace is better. And present in [human] souls is stinginess. But if you do good and fear Allah - then indeed Allah is ever, with what you do, Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of reconciliation and peace in marital relationships. It suggests that if a wife senses neglect or aversion from her husband, both are encouraged to seek a mutual agreement to resolve their issues, highlighting that maintaining peace is preferable. The verse acknowledges the natural human tendency towards selfishness but encourages overcoming this through acts of kindness and piety. It reassures that Allah is fully aware of all actions, promoting a sense of accountability and encouraging moral behavior within the marriage.
orig: وإن امرأة خافت من بعلها نشوزا أو إعراضا فلا جناح عليهما أن يصلحا بينهما صلحا والصلح خير وأحضرت الأنفس الشح وإن تحسنوا وتتقوا فإن الله كان بما تعملون خبيرا

translation: And you will never be able to be equal [in feeling] between wives, even if you should strive [to do so]. So do not incline completely [toward one] and leave another hanging. And if you amend [your affairs] and fear Allah - then indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse addresses the challenge of maintaining fairness among multiple wives, acknowledging that complete emotional equality is unattainable due to human nature. It advises against favoring one wife to the extent of neglecting another, which could lead to her feeling abandoned or 'hanging'. The verse encourages men to strive for fairness and to be conscious of Allah, promising that if they do so, they can seek forgiveness and mercy from Allah, who is forgiving and merciful.
orig: ولن تستطيعوا أن تعدلوا بين النساء ولو حرصتم فلا تميلوا كل الميل فتذروها كالمعلقة وإن تصلحوا وتتقوا فإن الله كان غفورا رحيما

translation: And if they separate, Allah will enrich each of them from His abundance. And Allah is Ever All-Sufficient, All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse addresses the situation of divorce, reassuring that even if a couple separates, Allah will provide for each individual from His vast resources. It emphasizes God's boundless capacity to sustain His creation and His wisdom in managing affairs, encouraging trust in divine providence during times of personal upheaval.
orig: وإن يتفرقا يغن الله كلا من سعته وكان الله واسعا حكيما

translation: And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth. And indeed, We have instructed those who were given the Scripture before you and you to fear Allah. But if you disbelieve - then to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth. And Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty of Allah over all creation, both in the heavens and on earth. It serves as a reminder to all people, including those who received previous scriptures and the contemporaries of the Prophet Muhammad, to be mindful of Allah and to live in accordance with His guidance. The verse also underscores that Allah's dominion and sufficiency are not affected by human belief or disbelief; He remains independent and worthy of all praise regardless of human actions.
orig: ولله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض ولقد وصينا الذين أوتوا الكتاب من قبلكم وإياكم أن اتقوا الله وإن تكفروا فإن لله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وكان الله غنيا حميدا

translation: And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And sufficient is Allah as a Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and ownership of Allah over everything in existence, both in the heavens and on the earth. It reassures believers that Allah alone is sufficient to manage and take care of all matters, serving as a perfect and all-sufficient guardian and manager of the universe and the affairs of His creation.
orig: ولله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وكفى بالله وكيلا

translation: If He wills, He can do away with you, O people, and bring others [in your place]. And Allah is ever capable of that.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute power and authority of Allah over all creation. It serves as a reminder to humanity of their dependence on Allah's will and mercy. The mention of replacing one group of people with another illustrates the transient nature of human existence and the continuous cycle of life and divine decree. It encourages believers to remain humble and obedient, recognizing that their existence and roles are subject to Allah's supreme will.
orig: إن يشأ يذهبكم أيها الناس ويأت بآخرين وكان الله على ذلك قديرا

translation: Whoever desires the reward of this world - then with Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter. And ever is Allah Hearing and Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all rewards, whether in this worldly life or in the hereafter, ultimately come from Allah. It encourages believers to seek their rewards from Allah alone, as He is fully aware of their intentions and actions, being both All-Hearing and All-Seeing. This underscores the importance of sincerity in one's deeds and the trust in Allah's comprehensive knowledge and justice.
orig: من كان يريد ثواب الدنيا فعند الله ثواب الدنيا والآخرة وكان الله سميعا بصيرا

translation: O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for Allah, even if it be against yourselves or parents and relatives. Whether one is rich or poor, Allah is more worthy of both. So follow not [personal] inclination, lest you not be just. And if you distort [your testimony] or refuse [to give it], then indeed Allah is ever, with what you do, Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of upholding justice and truthfulness in all circumstances, even when it involves personal sacrifice or goes against the interests of oneself or close relatives. It teaches that justice should be administered impartially, without being swayed by the social or economic status of the individuals involved. The verse warns against allowing personal desires or biases to influence one's judgment, highlighting that Allah is fully aware of all actions and intentions. It serves as a reminder that true justice is a divine mandate, and adherence to it is a fundamental aspect of faith.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا كونوا قوامين بالقسط شهداء لله ولو على أنفسكم أو الوالدين والأقربين إن يكن غنيا أو فقيرا فالله أولى بهما فلا تتبعوا الهوى أن تعدلوا وإن تلووا أو تعرضوا فإن الله كان بما تعملون خبيرا

translation: O you who have believed, believe in Allah and His Messenger and the Book that He revealed to His Messenger and the Book which He revealed before. And whoever disbelieves in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day has certainly gone far astray.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of complete faith in the entirety of divine revelation. It calls upon believers to reaffirm their faith not only in Allah and His Messenger but also in all scriptures revealed to previous messengers. The verse warns that rejecting any part of this comprehensive belief system—including faith in Allah, His angels, His scriptures, His messengers, and the Last Day—leads to profound spiritual misguidance. It underscores the interconnectedness of these elements of faith and the necessity of accepting them wholly to remain on the right path.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا آمنوا بالله ورسوله والكتاب الذي نزل على رسوله والكتاب الذي أنزل من قبل ومن يكفر بالله وملائكته وكتبه ورسله واليوم الآخر فقد ضل ضلالا بعيدا

translation: Indeed, those who have believed then disbelieved, then believed, then disbelieved, and then increased in disbelief - never will Allah forgive them, nor will He guide them to a way.
interpretation: This verse addresses the individuals who repeatedly shift between faith and disbelief, ultimately deepening their rejection of faith. It underscores the severity of such fluctuating belief, indicating that such a pattern of behavior leads to a state where forgiveness and guidance from Allah become unattainable. The verse serves as a warning against the dangers of inconsistent faith and the importance of steadfastness in belief.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا ثم كفروا ثم آمنوا ثم كفروا ثم ازدادوا كفرا لم يكن الله ليغفر لهم ولا ليهديهم سبيلا

translation: Give tidings to the hypocrites that for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who outwardly profess faith but inwardly harbor disbelief or doubt. It underscores the concept of hypocrisy as a grave sin, emphasizing that such deception will not go unpunished. The 'painful punishment' mentioned here is a reminder of the accountability and justice in the hereafter, urging individuals to align their inner beliefs with their outward actions.
orig: بشر المنافقين بأن لهم عذابا أليما

translation: Those who take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers - do they seek honor with them? Indeed, all honor belongs to Allah.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual and moral error of prioritizing alliances with non-believers over the community of faith for the sake of worldly gain or prestige. It underscores that true honor and power are exclusively in the domain of Allah, suggesting that seeking status through such alliances is futile and misguided, as it diverts one from the path of divine approval and true empowerment which comes only through faith and adherence to Allah's guidance.
orig: الذين يتخذون الكافرين أولياء من دون المؤمنين أيبتغون عندهم العزة فإن العزة لله جميعا

translation: And it has been revealed to you in the Book that when you hear the verses of Allah being denied and ridiculed, do not sit with them until they engage in a different conversation. Indeed, you would then be like them. Indeed, Allah will gather the hypocrites and disbelievers in Hell altogether.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of distancing oneself from those who mock or reject the signs of Allah. It instructs believers to avoid participating in or even being present during such blasphemous discussions, as remaining in their company could be seen as tacit approval or association with their disbelief. The verse warns that those who do not heed this guidance risk being grouped with the hypocrites and disbelievers, who will ultimately be gathered together in Hell. This serves as a reminder of the seriousness of maintaining one's faith and the company one keeps, highlighting the collective accountability in the afterlife.
orig: وقد نزل عليكم في الكتاب أن إذا سمعتم آيات الله يكفر بها ويستهزأ بها فلا تقعدوا معهم حتى يخوضوا في حديث غيره إنكم إذا مثلهم إن الله جامع المنافقين والكافرين في جهنم جميعا

translation: Those who wait and watch you: if you gain a victory from Allah, they say, 'Were we not with you?' But if the disbelievers gain a share, they say [to them], 'Did we not gain mastery over you, and protect you from the believers?' Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection, and never will Allah give the disbelievers over the believers a way [to prevail].
interpretation: This verse addresses the hypocrisy of certain individuals who shift their allegiance based on the outcome of events. They claim to support the believers when they are successful, suggesting they were always on their side. Conversely, when the disbelievers have the upper hand, these same individuals claim to have protected the disbelievers from the believers. The verse emphasizes that such deceitful behavior will be judged by Allah on the Day of Resurrection, and it reassures believers that Allah will not allow disbelievers to ultimately triumph over them.
orig: الذين يتربصون بكم فإن كان لكم فتح من الله قالوا ألم نكن معكم وإن كان للكافرين نصيب قالوا ألم نستحوذ عليكم ونمنعكم من المؤمنين فالله يحكم بينكم يوم القيامة ولن يجعل الله للكافرين على المؤمنين سبيلا

translation: Indeed, the hypocrites [think to] deceive Allah, but He is deceiving them. And when they stand for prayer, they stand lazily, showing off to the people and not remembering Allah except a little.
interpretation: This verse highlights the deceitful nature of the hypocrites who attempt to fool Allah, yet they are the ones being outwitted by Him. Their insincerity is evident in their prayer, where they stand reluctantly, more concerned with being seen by others than with genuine devotion. Their minimal remembrance of Allah during prayer underscores their lack of true faith and spiritual connection, emphasizing the importance of sincerity and devotion in worship.
orig: إن المنافقين يخادعون الله وهو خادعهم وإذا قاموا إلى الصلاة قاموا كسالى يراءون الناس ولا يذكرون الله إلا قليلا

translation: wavering between that, neither to these nor to those; and whoever Allah leaves astray - never will you find for him a way.
interpretation: This verse describes a state of confusion and indecision among people who are not firmly committed to either faith or disbelief. They are described as being 'wavering between that,' indicating their lack of a clear path or conviction. The phrase 'neither to these nor to those' emphasizes their isolation from both the believers and the disbelievers. The latter part of the verse underscores the finality of divine guidance or misguidance; if Allah allows someone to go astray, no human effort can bring them back to the right path, highlighting the ultimate sovereignty of Allah in guiding or misguiding individuals.
orig: مذبذبين بين ذلك لا إلى هؤلاء ولا إلى هؤلاء ومن يضلل الله فلن تجد له سبيلا

translation: O you who have believed, do not take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Do you wish to give Allah a clear authority against yourselves?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of loyalty and solidarity among believers, warning against forming close alliances with those who reject faith. It suggests that aligning with disbelievers over believers can be seen as a betrayal of one's faith, potentially leading to divine disapproval or judgment. The rhetorical question at the end underscores the gravity of such actions, implying that they provide a clear justification for divine retribution.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتخذوا الكافرين أولياء من دون المؤمنين أتريدون أن تجعلوا لله عليكم سلطانا مبينا

translation: Indeed, the hypocrites are in the lowest depths of the fire, and you will not find for them any helper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe punishment awaiting hypocrites in the afterlife, indicating that their position will be at the very bottom of Hell due to the gravity of their deception and betrayal of faith. It also highlights their isolation and lack of support, underscoring that no one will come to their aid or intercede on their behalf, reflecting the ultimate consequence of their insincerity and duplicity.
orig: إن المنافقين في الدرك الأسفل من النار ولن تجد لهم نصيرا

translation: Except for those who repent and reform and hold fast to Allah and are sincere in their religion for Allah, then those are with the believers. And Allah is going to give the believers a great reward.
interpretation: This verse highlights the path to redemption and inclusion among the believers for those who have strayed. It emphasizes four key actions: repentance for past sins, reforming one's behavior, steadfastly clinging to faith in Allah, and dedicating one's worship purely to Him. Those who undertake these steps are promised to be counted among the believers and assured of a great reward from Allah, underscoring the mercy and inclusivity of Islam towards those who seek to correct their ways.
orig: إلا الذين تابوا وأصلحوا واعتصموا بالله وأخلصوا دينهم لله فأولئك مع المؤمنين وسوف يؤت الله المؤمنين أجرا عظيما

translation: What would Allah do with your punishment if you are grateful and believe? And Allah is Appreciative and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that if individuals express gratitude and maintain faith, Allah's nature is to respond with appreciation and understanding, rather than punishment. It highlights the merciful and just aspect of Allah, suggesting that sincere gratitude and faith can avert divine retribution, as Allah values and acknowledges these qualities in His servants.
orig: ما يفعل الله بعذابكم إن شكرتم وآمنتم وكان الله شاكرا عليما

translation: Allah does not like the public mention of evil except by one who has been wronged. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of discretion and avoiding publicizing negative speech or actions, except in cases where one has been wronged. It teaches that while Allah dislikes the spread of harmful or evil talk, an exception is made for those who have suffered injustice, allowing them to speak out to seek justice or protection. The attributes of Allah as Hearing and Knowing underscore His awareness of all situations and His understanding of the motives behind human actions, encouraging believers to trust in His justice and wisdom.
orig: لا يحب الله الجهر بالسوء من القول إلا من ظلم وكان الله سميعا عليما

translation: If you disclose a good deed or conceal it or pardon an evil, then indeed, Allah is ever Pardoning and Competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the moral virtues of performing good deeds, whether publicly or privately, and the importance of forgiveness. It reassures believers that Allah possesses the attributes of forgiveness and omnipotence, encouraging them to act righteously and forgive others, knowing that Allah will be forgiving and capable of rewarding their actions.
orig: إن تبدوا خيرا أو تخفوه أو تعفوا عن سوء فإن الله كان عفوا قديرا

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers and wish to separate between Allah and His messengers and say, 'We believe in some and disbelieve in others,' and wish to take a way in between -
interpretation: This verse addresses the hypocrisy and selective belief of those who claim to accept parts of the divine message while rejecting others. It warns against the dangerous practice of distinguishing between Allah and His messengers, suggesting that true faith requires acceptance of the entirety of the revelation and the messengers who convey it. The verse condemns the attempt to create a middle path or compromise in belief, emphasizing that such an approach is a form of disbelief and a deviation from the straight path of Islam.
orig: إن الذين يكفرون بالله ورسله ويريدون أن يفرقوا بين الله ورسله ويقولون نؤمن ببعض ونكفر ببعض ويريدون أن يتخذوا بين ذلك سبيلا

translation: Those are the disbelievers, truly. And We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty of disbelief among those who reject faith, labeling them as true disbelievers. It serves as a warning that disbelief is not merely a personal choice without consequences; rather, it leads to a severe and humiliating punishment in the hereafter, underscoring the gravity of rejecting the message of Islam and the accountability that follows in the afterlife.
orig: أولئك هم الكافرون حقا وأعتدنا للكافرين عذابا مهينا

translation: And those who believe in Allah and His messengers and do not differentiate between any of them, those - He will give them their rewards, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of having a unified belief in all of Allah's messengers without making distinctions between them. It teaches that true faith involves accepting the continuity and consistency of the divine message across different prophets. Those who adhere to this principle are promised their rewards by Allah, highlighting His attributes of forgiveness and mercy, which encourage believers to maintain a comprehensive and inclusive faith.
orig: والذين آمنوا بالله ورسله ولم يفرقوا بين أحد منهم أولئك سوف يؤتيهم أجورهم وكان الله غفورا رحيما

translation: The People of the Scripture ask you to bring down to them a book from the heaven. But they asked Moses for something even greater than that when they said, 'Show us Allah outright,' and the thunderbolt struck them for their wrongdoing. Then they took the calf [for worship] after clear proofs had come to them, yet We pardoned that and gave Moses a clear authority.
interpretation: This verse highlights the recurring theme of disbelief and the human tendency to demand extraordinary signs from God despite receiving clear evidence of His existence and guidance. The People of the Scripture, in this context, are shown to be demanding a book from heaven, similar to how they demanded to see God directly during the time of Moses. This demand for visible proof, despite the miracles and guidance already provided, reflects a deeper issue of faith and submission to God's will. The punishment they received, such as the thunderbolt, serves as a reminder of the consequences of such disbelief and arrogance. However, God's mercy is also evident as He forgave their subsequent idolatry with the calf and continued to support Moses with clear authority, emphasizing the balance between divine justice and mercy.
orig: يسألك أهل الكتاب أن تنزل عليهم كتابا من السماء فقد سألوا موسى أكبر من ذلك فقالوا أرنا الله جهرة فأخذتهم الصاعقة بظلمهم ثم اتخذوا العجل من بعد ما جاءتهم البينات فعفونا عن ذلك وآتينا موسى سلطانا مبينا

translation: And We raised above them the Mount (Sinai) for their covenant, and We said to them: 'Enter the gate prostrating,' and We said to them: 'Do not transgress on the Sabbath,' and We took from them a solemn covenant.
interpretation: This verse reflects on the covenant between God and the Children of Israel, emphasizing the seriousness and solemnity of their commitments. The raising of Mount Sinai over them symbolizes the gravity and the divine enforcement of the covenant, reminding them of the consequences of breaking it. The instructions to enter the gate in prostration and to observe the Sabbath are specific commandments that test their obedience and faith. The 'solemn covenant' underscores the binding nature of these obligations, highlighting the importance of adherence to divine laws and the consequences of disobedience.
orig: ورفعنا فوقهم الطور بميثاقهم وقلنا لهم ادخلوا الباب سجدا وقلنا لهم لا تعدوا في السبت وأخذنا منهم ميثاقا غليظا

translation: So because of their breaking of their covenant, and their disbelief in the signs of Allah, and their killing of the prophets without right, and their saying, 'Our hearts are uncircumcised,' rather, Allah has sealed them for their disbelief, so they do not believe except for a few.
interpretation: This verse explains the reasons behind the disbelief of a particular group, highlighting their violation of the covenant they had with Allah, their rejection of divine signs, and their unjust killing of prophets. The phrase 'Our hearts are uncircumcised' reflects their claim of being spiritually closed off, but the verse clarifies that it is Allah who has sealed their hearts due to their persistent disbelief. The mention that only a few will believe underscores the rarity of faith among them, emphasizing the consequences of their collective actions and attitudes.
orig: فبما نقضهم ميثاقهم وكفرهم بآيات الله وقتلهم الأنبياء بغير حق وقولهم قلوبنا غلف بل طبع الله عليها بكفرهم فلا يؤمنون إلا قليلا

translation: And because of their disbelief and their uttering against Mary a tremendous slander
interpretation: This verse highlights the gravity of the accusations made against Mary, the mother of Jesus, by some disbelievers. It underscores the moral and religious offense of slandering a righteous person, emphasizing that such false accusations are a form of disbelief and a serious transgression against the sanctity and honor upheld in Islamic teachings.
orig: وبكفرهم وقولهم على مريم بهتانا عظيما

translation: And [for] their saying, 'Indeed, we have killed the Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary, the messenger of Allah.' And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him; but it was made to appear so to them. And indeed, those who differ over it are in doubt about it. They have no knowledge of it except the following of assumption. And they did not kill him, for certain.
interpretation: This verse addresses the claim by some that they killed Jesus, the Messiah and messenger of Allah. It refutes this claim, stating that Jesus was neither killed nor crucified; rather, it was made to appear so to them. This suggests a divine intervention where the reality was altered in the perception of the observers. The verse further indicates that those who argue about this event are in doubt and lack true knowledge, relying only on conjecture. It emphasizes the certainty that Jesus was not killed, highlighting the theme of divine protection and the limits of human understanding and control over divine plans.
orig: وقولهم إنا قتلنا المسيح عيسى ابن مريم رسول الله وما قتلوه وما صلبوه ولكن شبه لهم وإن الذين اختلفوا فيه لفي شك منه ما لهم به من علم إلا اتباع الظن وما قتلوه يقينا

translation: Rather, Allah raised him to Himself. And ever is Allah Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah, in His infinite power and wisdom, chose to elevate Jesus (peace be upon him) to Himself, rather than allowing him to suffer death at the hands of his enemies. This act underscores Allah's supreme authority and His ability to protect His prophets, demonstrating His attributes of being Exalted in Might and Wise.
orig: بل رفعه الله إليه وكان الله عزيزا حكيما

translation: And there is none among the People of the Scripture but will surely believe in him before his death. And on the Day of Resurrection, he will be a witness against them.
interpretation: This verse suggests that every individual from the People of the Scripture (Jews and Christians) will come to recognize and believe in the truth of Prophet Muhammad before their death. This belief might occur at the moment of death or through a divine revelation at that time. Additionally, on the Day of Judgment, Prophet Muhammad will stand as a witness against them, testifying to the message he conveyed and their response to it.
orig: وإن من أهل الكتاب إلا ليؤمنن به قبل موته ويوم القيامة يكون عليهم شهيدا

translation: So because of the wrongdoing of those who were Jews, We prohibited to them [the consumption of] good things which had been lawful to them, and because of their averting many from the way of Allah,
interpretation: This verse highlights that due to the transgressions and injustices committed by some among the Jewish community, certain permissible foods were made forbidden to them as a form of divine punishment. Additionally, their actions led many people astray from the path of Allah, indicating a severe consequence of their misdeeds not only affecting themselves but also influencing others negatively in their spiritual journey.
orig: فبظلم من الذين هادوا حرمنا عليهم طيبات أحلت لهم وبصدهم عن سبيل الله كثيرا

translation: And their taking of usury while they were forbidden from it, and their consuming of people's wealth unjustly. And We have prepared for the disbelievers among them a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse addresses the serious moral and ethical violations of taking usury (riba) and unjustly consuming others' wealth, despite clear prohibitions against these actions. It emphasizes that such behaviors are not only sinful but also lead to disbelief (kufr), for which a severe punishment is promised in the hereafter. The verse serves as a stern warning against engaging in economic exploitation and injustice, highlighting the accountability and consequences for those who persist in these wrongs.
orig: وأخذهم الربا وقد نهوا عنه وأكلهم أموال الناس بالباطل وأعتدنا للكافرين منهم عذابا أليما

translation: But those firm in knowledge among them and the believers believe in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you, and the establishers of prayer and the givers of zakah and the believers in Allah and the Last Day - those We will give a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of deep understanding and faith among the knowledgeable and the believers. It highlights that true faith encompasses belief in the revelations given to the Prophet Muhammad as well as to previous prophets, and is demonstrated through the practice of prayer and charity.
