The verse also connects belief in Allah with belief in the Last Day, indicating a comprehensive faith system that is rewarded with a significant recompense from Allah. This suggests that intellectual conviction, when coupled with righteous actions and a holistic belief in divine principles, leads to divine favor and great reward.
orig: لكن الراسخون في العلم منهم والمؤمنون يؤمنون بما أنزل إليك وما أنزل من قبلك والمقيمين الصلاة والمؤتون الزكاة والمؤمنون بالله واليوم الآخر أولئك سنؤتيهم أجرا عظيما

translation: Indeed, We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him, and We revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, the Descendants, Jesus, Job, Jonah, Aaron, and Solomon, and to David We gave the Psalms.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the continuity and unity of divine revelation across different prophets and times. It reassures the Prophet Muhammad that his mission is part of a long chain of prophetic messages from Allah, starting with Noah and extending through a list of prominent prophets, each of whom received guidance tailored to their people. The mention of David receiving the Psalms specifically highlights the diversity of the forms of revelation, yet all are from the same source, Allah. This verse serves to validate the prophethood of Muhammad by connecting him to this revered lineage, reinforcing the concept of a single, unified message from God throughout history.
orig: إنا أوحينا إليك كما أوحينا إلى نوح والنبيين من بعده وأوحينا إلى إبراهيم وإسماعيل وإسحاق ويعقوب والأسباط وعيسى وأيوب ويونس وهارون وسليمان وآتينا داوود زبورا

translation: And [We sent] messengers about whom We have related [their stories] to you before, and messengers about whom We have not related to you. And Allah spoke directly to Moses.
interpretation: This verse underscores the diversity of divine communication through prophets and messengers. Some of their stories are detailed in the Qur'an to serve as lessons and guidance for believers, while others are not mentioned, indicating that Allah's interaction with humanity is vast and not fully disclosed. The special mention of Allah speaking directly to Moses highlights the unique nature of his prophethood and the intimate relationship he had with the Divine, emphasizing the significance of direct revelation and obedience to God's commands.
orig: ورسلا قد قصصناهم عليك من قبل ورسلا لم نقصصهم عليك وكلم الله موسى تكليما

translation: Messengers as bearers of good news and warners, so that people may have no argument against Allah after the messengers. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of prophets and messengers as both bearers of glad tidings and warnings from God. Their primary function is to convey God's message clearly to humanity, ensuring that no one can claim ignorance or lack of guidance as an excuse on the Day of Judgment. The mention of Allah being 'Exalted in Might and Wise' underscores His supreme power and wisdom in choosing this method of communication, ensuring fairness and justice in His divine plan.
orig: رسلا مبشرين ومنذرين لئلا يكون للناس على الله حجة بعد الرسل وكان الله عزيزا حكيما

translation: But Allah bears witness to that which He has revealed to you. He has revealed it with His knowledge, and the angels bear witness as well. And sufficient is Allah as a Witness.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin and authenticity of the Qur'an. It assures the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers that the revelation he received is from Allah, supported by His knowledge and affirmed by the angels. The phrase 'sufficient is Allah as a Witness' underscores the ultimate authority and reliability of Allah's testimony, reinforcing the believers' faith in the Qur'an as the true word of God.
orig: لكن الله يشهد بما أنزل إليك أنزله بعلمه والملائكة يشهدون وكفى بالله شهيدا

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert [people] from the way of Allah have certainly strayed far away.
interpretation: This verse highlights the severe spiritual misguidance of those who not only reject faith themselves but also actively prevent others from following the path of Allah. It underscores the notion that such actions lead to a profound deviation from the truth, emphasizing the gravity of their error and the distance it creates from divine guidance.
orig: إن الذين كفروا وصدوا عن سبيل الله قد ضلوا ضلالا بعيدا

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and do wrong, Allah will not forgive them, nor will He guide them to a way.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe consequences of disbelief and wrongdoing. It indicates that those who consciously reject faith and engage in injustice will not receive Allah's forgiveness or guidance. This underscores the importance of faith and righteousness, highlighting that persistent disbelief and oppression lead to a spiritual loss, where individuals are left without divine guidance or the possibility of redemption.
orig: إن الذين كفروا وظلموا لم يكن الله ليغفر لهم ولا ليهديهم طريقا

translation: Except the way of Hell, to dwell therein forever. And that was easy for Allah.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability and ease with which Allah can decree punishment for those who stray from His path. It emphasizes the concept of divine justice and the permanence of the consequences for those who choose a path leading to Hell. The phrase 'that was easy for Allah' highlights Allah's omnipotence and the effortless nature of His decrees, serving as a reminder of His absolute power and the seriousness of disobeying His commands.
orig: إلا طريق جهنم خالدين فيها أبدا وكان ذلك على الله يسيرا

translation: O mankind, the Messenger has come to you with the truth from your Lord, so believe; it is better for you. But if you disbelieve, then indeed, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. And Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universal message of Islam, calling all of humanity to believe in the Prophet Muhammad and the truth he brings from God. It highlights the choice given to people: faith leads to their own benefit, while disbelief does not diminish God's dominion over the universe. The verse reassures believers of God's omniscience and wisdom, suggesting that His plan encompasses all outcomes, whether people choose to believe or not.
orig: يا أيها الناس قد جاءكم الرسول بالحق من ربكم فآمنوا خيرا لكم وإن تكفروا فإن لله ما في السماوات والأرض وكان الله عليما حكيما

translation: O People of the Scripture, do not commit excess in your religion or say about Allah except the truth. The Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary, was but a messenger of Allah and His word which He directed to Mary and a soul from Him. So believe in Allah and His messengers, and do not say, 'Three'; desist - it is better for you. Indeed, Allah is but one God. Exalted is He above having a son. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And sufficient is Allah as a Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse addresses the People of the Scripture, specifically Christians, urging them not to exceed the bounds of their religion by attributing divinity to Jesus Christ, who is described as a messenger of God and a manifestation of His word and spirit. The verse emphasizes the oneness of God, rejecting the concept of the Trinity and affirming that God is above having a son. It calls for belief in the singular nature of God and His absolute sovereignty over the universe, reinforcing the sufficiency of God as the ultimate authority and manager of all affairs.
orig: يا أهل الكتاب لا تغلوا في دينكم ولا تقولوا على الله إلا الحق إنما المسيح عيسى ابن مريم رسول الله وكلمته ألقاها إلى مريم وروح منه فآمنوا بالله ورسله ولا تقولوا ثلاثة انتهوا خيرا لكم إنما الله إله واحد سبحانه أن يكون له ولد له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وكفى بالله وكيلا

translation: The Messiah will never disdain to be a servant of Allah, nor will the angels who are near [to Him]. And whoever disdains His worship and is arrogant - He will gather them to Himself, all of them.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the humility and submission of Jesus (the Messiah) and the angels closest to God, illustrating that even the most exalted beings do not consider themselves above serving God. It serves as a reminder to humans that arrogance and refusal to worship God are grave sins, and those who exhibit such behavior will be brought before God to account for their actions.
orig: لن يستنكف المسيح أن يكون عبدا لله ولا الملائكة المقربون ومن يستنكف عن عبادته ويستكبر فسيحشرهم إليه جميعا

translation: As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, He will give them their rewards in full and increase them from His bounty. But as for those who disdained and were arrogant, He will punish them with a painful punishment, and they will not find for themselves besides Allah any protector or helper.
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle of divine justice and the consequences of one's actions in the afterlife. It emphasizes that faith coupled with good deeds leads to divine rewards and additional blessings from Allah's grace. Conversely, arrogance and rejection of faith result in severe punishment, with no possibility of finding any support or intercession other than from Allah. This highlights the importance of humility, faith, and righteous living as key to spiritual success and protection.
orig: فأما الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات فيوفيهم أجورهم ويزيدهم من فضله وأما الذين استنكفوا واستكبروا فيعذبهم عذابا أليما ولا يجدون لهم من دون الله وليا ولا نصيرا

translation: O mankind, there has come to you a convincing proof from your Lord, and We have sent down to you a clear light.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the arrival of a definitive sign or proof from God, which is the Prophet Muhammad and the Qur'an itself, referred to as a 'clear light.' It suggests that this revelation is a guiding beacon for humanity, illuminating the path to righteousness and truth, and it serves as an invitation for all people to recognize and follow this divine guidance.
orig: يا أيها الناس قد جاءكم برهان من ربكم وأنزلنا إليكم نورا مبينا

translation: As for those who believe in Allah and hold fast to Him, He will admit them to His mercy and grace, and guide them to Himself on a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the rewards and guidance provided to those who have faith in Allah and maintain a strong connection with Him. It suggests that true believers who cling to their faith and rely on Allah will be enveloped in His mercy and favor. Additionally, it indicates that such devotion leads to divine guidance, directing them towards a righteous and clear path in life, ultimately bringing them closer to Allah.
orig: فأما الذين آمنوا بالله واعتصموا به فسيدخلهم في رحمة منه وفضل ويهديهم إليه صراطا مستقيما

translation: They ask you for a legal ruling. Say: "Allah gives you a ruling concerning the person who has neither descendants nor ascendants as heirs. If a man dies, leaving no child but only a sister, she will have half of what he left. And he inherits from her if she has no child. But if there are two sisters, they will have two-thirds of what he left. If the heirs are both brothers and sisters, the male will have twice the share of the female. Allah makes clear to you lest you go astray. And Allah is All-Knowing of all things."
interpretation: This verse addresses the rules of inheritance in cases where a person dies without direct descendants or ascendants. It specifies the shares of inheritance for siblings, particularly focusing on the scenario where a man dies leaving only a sister or sisters. The verse establishes that a single sister inherits half of the deceased's estate, and if there are two or more sisters, they collectively inherit two-thirds. It also sets the principle that a brother's share is double that of a sister's in the presence of both male and female siblings. This ruling aims to clarify inheritance laws to prevent disputes and confusion, reflecting Allah's comprehensive knowledge and guidance in all matters.
orig: يستفتونك قل الله يفتيكم في الكلالة إن امرؤ هلك ليس له ولد وله أخت فلها نصف ما ترك وهو يرثها إن لم يكن لها ولد فإن كانتا اثنتين فلهما الثلثان مما ترك وإن كانوا إخوة رجالا ونساء فللذكر مثل حظ الأنثيين يبين الله لكم أن تضلوا والله بكل شيء عليم

translation: O you who have believed, fulfill [all] contracts. Lawful to you is the game from the sea and its food as provision for you and the travelers, but forbidden to you is the game from the land as long as you are in the state of ihram. Indeed, Allah decrees what He intends.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fulfilling all contracts and agreements, reflecting the value of trustworthiness and integrity in Islam. It also addresses the dietary laws during the state of ihram, specifically allowing seafood while prohibiting land game, which serves to remind believers of the sanctity and discipline required during pilgrimage. The final part of the verse underscores Allah's sovereignty and His authority to legislate as He wills, reinforcing the concept of submission to divine law.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا أوفوا بالعقود أحلت لكم بهيمة الأنعام إلا ما يتلى عليكم غير محلي الصيد وأنتم حرم إن الله يحكم ما يريد

translation: O you who have believed, do not violate the rites of Allah or the sacred month or the sacrificial animals or the garlands [marking them] or those coming to the Sacred House seeking bounty from their Lord and [His] approval. But when you come out of ihram, then hunt. And do not let the hatred of a people who prevented you from al-Masjid al-Haram lead you to transgress. And cooperate in righteousness and piety, but do not cooperate in sin and aggression. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is severe in penalty.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sanctity of certain religious practices and symbols in Islam, such as the rites of pilgrimage, the sacred months, and the sacrificial animals marked with garlands. It instructs believers to respect these sanctities and not to desecrate them, even when faced with hostility from others who might prevent them from performing their religious duties, such as visiting the Sacred Mosque. The verse encourages cooperation in good deeds and piety, while explicitly forbidding collaboration in sinful or aggressive acts. It serves as a reminder of the importance of maintaining moral integrity and fear of Allah, highlighting that divine retribution is severe for those who transgress these boundaries.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تحلوا شعائر الله ولا الشهر الحرام ولا الهدي ولا القلائد ولا آمين البيت الحرام يبتغون فضلا من ربهم ورضوانا وإذا حللتم فاصطادوا ولا يجرمنكم شنآن قوم أن صدوكم عن المسجد الحرام أن تعتدوا وتعاونوا على البر والتقوى ولا تعاونوا على الإثم والعدوان واتقوا الله إن الله شديد العقاب

translation: Forbidden to you are carrion, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than Allah, and that which has been strangled, beaten to death, killed by a fall, gored to death, and that which has been partially eaten by a wild animal - unless you are able to slaughter it (before its death) - and that which has been sacrificed on stone altars, and to seek decisions through divining arrows. That is grave disobedience. This day those who disbelieve have despaired of [defeating] your religion; so fear them not, but fear Me. This day I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you and have approved for you Islam as religion. But whoever is forced by severe hunger with no inclination to sin - then indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse outlines the dietary laws and prohibitions in Islam, emphasizing the sanctity of life and the importance of dedicating acts of slaughter to Allah alone. It also marks the completion of the Islamic faith, signaling that the religion is now fully revealed and perfected. The mention of despair among disbelievers indicates a turning point where the Muslim community should feel confident in their faith and not be swayed by external threats. The allowance for those in extreme necessity to consume prohibited foods underscores the mercy and understanding of Allah, highlighting that His laws are meant to guide and protect, not to burden unduly.
orig: حرمت عليكم الميتة والدم ولحم الخنزير وما أهل لغير الله به والمنخنقة والموقوذة والمتردية والنطيحة وما أكل السبع إلا ما ذكيتم وما ذبح على النصب وأن تستقسموا بالأزلام ذلكم فسق اليوم يئس الذين كفروا من دينكم فلا تخشوهم واخشون اليوم أكملت لكم دينكم وأتممت عليكم نعمتي ورضيت لكم الإسلام دينا فمن اضطر في مخمصة غير متجانف لإثم فإن الله غفور رحيم

translation: They ask you what is lawful for them. Say: 'Lawful for you are all good things, and what you have taught the hunting animals, training them as Allah has taught you. So eat of what they catch for you, and mention the name of Allah over it, and fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is swift in account.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the permissibility of consuming all that is good and pure, extending this to include the meat caught by trained hunting animals, provided the name of Allah is mentioned at the time of hunting. It highlights the importance of gratitude and mindfulness of Allah in all aspects of life, including the consumption of food. The mention of Allah's swift accounting serves as a reminder of accountability for one's actions, encouraging believers to remain conscious of their deeds in light of the hereafter.
orig: يسألونك ماذا أحل لهم قل أحل لكم الطيبات وما علمتم من الجوارح مكلبين تعلمونهن مما علمكم الله فكلوا مما أمسكن عليكم واذكروا اسم الله عليه واتقوا الله إن الله سريع الحساب

translation: This day are (all) good things made lawful for you. The food of those who have received the Scripture is lawful for you, and your food is lawful for them. And so are the virtuous women of the believers and the virtuous women of those who received the Scripture before you (lawful for you) when you give them their due dowries, taking (them) in wedlock, not in debauchery, nor as secret lovers. And whoever denies the faith, his work is in vain, and he will be among the losers in the Hereafter.
interpretation: This verse signifies a shift from the restrictive dietary and marital laws of the early Muslim community to a broader acceptance, reflecting the completion of Islam's legislative framework. It emphasizes the permissibility of consuming food prepared by the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) and marrying their chaste women, provided that the marriage is conducted with proper Islamic rites and respect, not for illicit purposes. The verse underscores the importance of faith, warning that disbelief nullifies one's deeds and leads to loss in the afterlife, reinforcing the centrality of faith to the validity of one's actions.
orig: اليوم أحل لكم الطيبات وطعام الذين أوتوا الكتاب حل لكم وطعامكم حل لهم والمحصنات من المؤمنات والمحصنات من الذين أوتوا الكتاب من قبلكم إذا آتيتموهن أجورهن محصنين غير مسافحين ولا متخذي أخدان ومن يكفر بالإيمان فقد حبط عمله وهو في الآخرة من الخاسرين

translation: O you who have believed, when you rise to [perform] prayer, wash your faces and your forearms to the elbows and wipe over your heads and wash your feet to the ankles. And if you are in a state of janabah, then purify yourselves. But if you are ill or on a journey or one of you comes from the place of relieving himself or you have contacted women and do not find water, then seek clean earth and wipe over your faces and hands with it. Allah does not intend to make difficulty for you, but He intends to purify you and complete His favor upon you that you may be grateful.
interpretation: This verse outlines the ritual purification required before prayer, emphasizing both the physical and spiritual cleanliness necessary for worship. It provides specific instructions on ablution (wudu) and dry ablution (tayammum) as alternatives when water is unavailable, reflecting Islam's practical approach to religious duties. The verse reassures believers that these rituals are not meant to impose hardship but to facilitate spiritual purity and to fulfill God's blessings, encouraging gratitude towards divine guidance.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا قمتم إلى الصلاة فاغسلوا وجوهكم وأيديكم إلى المرافق وامسحوا برءوسكم وأرجلكم إلى الكعبين وإن كنتم جنبا فاطهروا وإن كنتم مرضى أو على سفر أو جاء أحد منكم من الغائط أو لامستم النساء فلم تجدوا ماء فتيمموا صعيدا طيبا فامسحوا بوجوهكم وأيديكم منه ما يريد الله ليجعل عليكم من حرج ولكن يريد ليطهركم وليتم نعمته عليكم لعلكم تشكرون

translation: And remember the favor of Allah upon you and His covenant with which He bound you when you said, 'We hear and we obey.' And fear Allah. Indeed, Allah knows what is in the breasts.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of gratitude towards Allah for His blessings and the necessity of upholding the covenant made with Him. The phrase 'We hear and we obey' reflects a commitment to follow Allah's commands. The reminder to fear Allah serves as a call to maintain piety and righteousness. The verse concludes by affirming Allah's omniscience, indicating that He is aware of the true intentions and feelings within people's hearts, encouraging sincerity in faith and actions.
orig: واذكروا نعمة الله عليكم وميثاقه الذي واثقكم به إذ قلتم سمعنا وأطعنا واتقوا الله إن الله عليم بذات الصدور

translation: O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for Allah, even if it be against yourselves or parents and relatives. Whether one is rich or poor, Allah is more worthy of both. So follow not [personal] inclination, lest you not be just. And if you distort [your testimony] or refuse [to give it], then indeed Allah is ever, with what you do, Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of upholding justice and fairness in all circumstances, even when it involves personal sacrifice or goes against one's own interests or those of close relatives. It instructs believers to act as witnesses for Allah, meaning they should embody and testify to the truth and justice that Allah commands. The verse warns against letting personal biases or hatreds influence one's judgment, as this can lead to injustice. It highlights that maintaining justice is a fundamental aspect of piety (taqwa), and reminds believers that Allah is fully aware of all actions, encouraging them to act justly out of a sense of accountability to Him.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا كونوا قوامين لله شهداء بالقسط ولا يجرمنكم شنآن قوم على ألا تعدلوا اعدلوا هو أقرب للتقوى واتقوا الله إن الله خبير بما تعملون

translation: Allah has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds that for them there is forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine promise from Allah to the believers who not only have faith but also actively engage in good deeds. The promise includes forgiveness for their sins, indicating a cleansing of their spiritual slate, and a great reward, which could be interpreted as entry into Paradise or other divine favors in the afterlife. This serves as a motivation for Muslims to maintain their faith and perform righteous actions, assuring them of Allah's mercy and generosity.
orig: وعد الله الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لهم مغفرة وأجر عظيم

translation: And those who disbelieved and denied Our signs, those are the companions of the Hellfire.
interpretation: This verse underscores the consequence of disbelief and rejection of the divine signs and revelations. It emphasizes that those who consciously choose to disbelieve and deny the truth presented through God's signs will ultimately be consigned to Hellfire, reflecting the severe punishment awaiting them in the afterlife for their rejection of faith.
orig: والذين كفروا وكذبوا بآياتنا أولئك أصحاب الجحيم

translation: O you who have believed, remember the favor of Allah upon you when a people determined to extend their hands [in violence] against you, but He restrained their hands from you; and fear Allah. And upon Allah let the believers rely.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of gratitude towards Allah for His protection and blessings. It serves as a reminder to the believers of a specific instance where Allah prevented an enemy from attacking them, highlighting His mercy and power. The verse encourages believers to maintain a constant awareness of Allah's favors, to fear Him, and to place their trust solely in Him, reinforcing the themes of reliance on Allah and the necessity of faith in His divine plan.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اذكروا نعمت الله عليكم إذ هم قوم أن يبسطوا إليكم أيديهم فكف أيديهم عنكم واتقوا الله وعلى الله فليتوكل المؤمنون

translation: And indeed Allah took the covenant from the Children of Israel (Jews), and We appointed from among them twelve leaders. And Allah said: 'I am with you if you establish prayer, give Zakat, believe in My Messengers, honor and assist them, and lend to Allah a goodly loan. I will surely remove from you your misdeeds and admit you into gardens beneath which rivers flow. But whoever of you disbelieves after that has certainly strayed from the right way.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the covenant that Allah made with the Children of Israel, highlighting the conditions they must fulfill to receive divine blessings and forgiveness. The conditions include performing regular prayers, giving charity, believing in and supporting the messengers of Allah, and engaging in acts of charity as a form of lending to Allah. The promise from Allah is clear: fulfillment of these obligations will lead to the expiation of sins and entry into Paradise. However, the verse also serves as a warning that disbelief after accepting this covenant leads to straying from the correct path, underscoring the importance of steadfastness in faith and obedience to divine commandments.
orig: ولقد أخذ الله ميثاق بني إسرائيل وبعثنا منهم اثني عشر نقيبا وقال الله إني معكم لئن أقمتم الصلاة وآتيتم الزكاة وآمنتم برسلي وعزرتموهم وأقرضتم الله قرضا حسنا لأكفرن عنكم سيئاتكم ولأدخلنكم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار فمن كفر بعد ذلك منكم فقد ضل سواء السبيل

translation: So for their breaking of the covenant We cursed them and made their hearts hard. They distort words from their [proper] usages and have forgotten a portion of that of which they were reminded. And you will still observe deceit among them, except a few of them. But pardon them and overlook [their misdeeds]. Indeed, Allah loves the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse addresses the consequences faced by the Children of Israel for repeatedly breaking their covenant with Allah. The 'curse' and 'hardening of hearts' symbolize a spiritual and moral decline, leading them to misinterpret and misuse divine revelations. The verse also highlights the prevalence of deceit among them, yet it commands the Prophet Muhammad to forgive and be lenient towards them, reflecting the Islamic value of mercy and goodness, as Allah favors those who do good deeds.
orig: فبما نقضهم ميثاقهم لعناهم وجعلنا قلوبهم قاسية يحرفون الكلم عن مواضعه ونسوا حظا مما ذكروا به ولا تزال تطلع على خائنة منهم إلا قليلا منهم فاعف عنهم واصفح إن الله يحب المحسنين

translation: And from those who say, 'We are Christians,' We took their covenant; but they forgot a portion of that of which they were reminded. So We caused among them animosity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection. And Allah will inform them of what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of neglecting the covenant with God, specifically among those who identify as Christians. The covenant mentioned refers to the divine guidance and commandments given to them, which they were supposed to uphold. By forgetting or neglecting these teachings, discord and enmity were sown among them, which will persist until the Day of Judgment. This serves as a reminder of the importance of adhering to divine guidance and the consequences of straying from it. Ultimately, God will hold them accountable for their actions, emphasizing divine justice and the inevitability of facing the outcomes of one's deeds.
orig: ومن الذين قالوا إنا نصارى أخذنا ميثاقهم فنسوا حظا مما ذكروا به فأغرينا بينهم العداوة والبغضاء إلى يوم القيامة وسوف ينبئهم الله بما كانوا يصنعون

translation: O People of the Scripture, there has come to you Our Messenger making clear to you much of what you used to conceal of the Scripture and overlooking much. There has come to you from Allah a light and a clear Book.
interpretation: This verse addresses the People of the Scripture, referring to Jews and Christians, indicating that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) has been sent to them to clarify many truths that were hidden or misinterpreted in their scriptures. The verse suggests that the Prophet's mission includes both revealing concealed truths and forgiving or overlooking certain errors or deviations. The 'light' and 'clear Book' refer to the Quran, which is described as a source of guidance and clarity, reinforcing the message that the Quran is a continuation and confirmation of the previous divine revelations, urging the People of the Scripture to recognize and accept this new guidance.
orig: يا أهل الكتاب قد جاءكم رسولنا يبين لكم كثيرا مما كنتم تخفون من الكتاب ويعفو عن كثير قد جاءكم من الله نور وكتاب مبين

translation: With it Allah guides those who follow His pleasure to the ways of peace and brings them out from darknesses into the light by His permission and guides them to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the transformative power of divine guidance through the Qur'an. It suggests that those who sincerely seek to please Allah are led towards a state of peace and security, both spiritually and potentially in their worldly lives. The transition from 'darknesses' to 'light' symbolizes a journey from ignorance, sin, and confusion to knowledge, righteousness, and clarity. This guidance is not arbitrary but comes by the permission of Allah, indicating His sovereignty and mercy. Finally, being guided to the 'straight path' refers to the clear and direct route to divine favor and ultimate salvation, as outlined in Islamic teachings.
orig: يهدي به الله من اتبع رضوانه سبل السلام ويخرجهم من الظلمات إلى النور بإذنه ويهديهم إلى صراط مستقيم

translation: Indeed, those who say, 'Allah is the Messiah, the son of Mary,' have disbelieved. Say, 'Then who could prevent Allah at all if He had intended to destroy the Messiah, the son of Mary, and his mother and everyone on the earth?' And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them. He creates what He wills, and Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental Islamic belief in the oneness of God (Tawhid) and refutes the Christian doctrine of the Trinity, specifically the belief that Jesus (the Messiah, son of Mary) is divine or part of God. It challenges the notion by posing a rhetorical question about God's absolute power and sovereignty, suggesting that if Jesus were truly divine, no one could stop God from destroying him if He so willed. The verse underscores that Allah has complete control over creation, capable of creating and destroying as He pleases, and is omnipotent over all things. This serves to reinforce the Islamic teaching that Jesus, while revered as a prophet, is not to be equated with God.
orig: لقد كفر الذين قالوا إن الله هو المسيح ابن مريم قل فمن يملك من الله شيئا إن أراد أن يهلك المسيح ابن مريم وأمه ومن في الأرض جميعا ولله ملك السماوات والأرض وما بينهما يخلق ما يشاء والله على كل شيء قدير

translation: And the Jews and the Christians say, 'We are the children of Allah and His beloved.' Say, 'Then why does He punish you for your sins? Rather, you are human beings from among those He has created. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, and to Him is the return.'
interpretation: This verse challenges the claims of exclusivity and divine favoritism by Jews and Christians, asserting that all humans are equal before God, subject to His judgment based on their actions. It emphasizes God's sovereignty and justice, reminding believers that divine forgiveness or punishment is at His discretion, and ultimately, all will return to Him.
orig: وقالت اليهود والنصارى نحن أبناء الله وأحباؤه قل فلم يعذبكم بذنوبكم بل أنتم بشر ممن خلق يغفر لمن يشاء ويعذب من يشاء ولله ملك السماوات والأرض وما بينهما وإليه المصير

translation: O People of the Scripture, there has come to you Our Messenger, making clear to you [Our message] after a period [of suspension] of messengers, lest you say, 'There did not come to us any bringer of good tidings or a warner.' But there has come to you a bringer of good tidings and a warner. And Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse addresses the People of the Scripture (Jews and Christians) and informs them of the arrival of Prophet Muhammad, who is described as a clear messenger from God. The phrase 'after a period [of suspension] of messengers' indicates that there had been a significant time gap since the last prophet was sent to them. This verse serves as a reminder and a warning to them not to claim ignorance of divine guidance, as they have now been given both a bringer of good news (about the mercy and forgiveness of God) and a warner (about the consequences of disobedience). The assertion that 'Allah is over all things competent' emphasizes God's omnipotence and His ability to send messengers and fulfill His promises.
orig: يا أهل الكتاب قد جاءكم رسولنا يبين لكم على فترة من الرسل أن تقولوا ما جاءنا من بشير ولا نذير فقد جاءكم بشير ونذير والله على كل شيء قدير

translation: And [mention] when Moses said to his people, 'O my people, remember the favor of Allah upon you when He appointed among you prophets and made you kings and gave you what He had not given anyone in the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of gratitude and remembrance of God's blessings. Moses reminds his people of the unique favors bestowed upon them by Allah, including the appointment of prophets from among them, the establishment of their rule as kings, and the granting of distinctive blessings not given to any other nation. The interpretation emphasizes that recognizing and appreciating these divine favors should inspire the community to remain faithful and obedient to Allah's commandments.
orig: وإذ قال موسى لقومه يا قوم اذكروا نعمة الله عليكم إذ جعل فيكم أنبياء وجعلكم ملوكا وآتاكم ما لم يؤت أحدا من العالمين

translation: O my people, enter the Holy Land which Allah has assigned to you and do not turn back [from fighting in Allah's cause] and [thus] become losers.
interpretation: This verse addresses the Children of Israel, urging them to enter the Holy Land that God has promised them. It emphasizes the importance of obedience to God's commands and the need to advance forward in faith, rather than retreating out of fear or doubt. The verse warns that turning away from this divine directive would lead to loss and failure, highlighting the consequences of disobedience and lack of trust in God's plan.
orig: يا قوم ادخلوا الأرض المقدسة التي كتب الله لكم ولا ترتدوا على أدباركم فتنقلبوا خاسرين

translation: They said, "O Moses, indeed there is a people of great might within it, and we will never enter it until they leave it; but if they leave it, then we will enter."
interpretation: This verse reflects the fear and hesitation of the Children of Israel when faced with the challenge of confronting the inhabitants of the Promised Land. It highlights their lack of faith and trust in God's promise and support, as they condition their entry into the land upon the departure of its current occupants, showing a reluctance to engage in the struggle required to claim what was promised to them by God.
orig: قالوا يا موسى إن فيها قوما جبارين وإنا لن ندخلها حتى يخرجوا منها فإن يخرجوا منها فإنا داخلون

translation: Two men from those who feared [Allah], upon whom Allah had bestowed favor, said, 'Enter upon them through the gate, for when you have entered it, you will be predominant. And upon Allah rely, if you should be believers.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of faith and trust in Allah during challenging times. The two men, who are described as fearing Allah and having been favored by Him, advise their companions to enter the city through the gate as a strategic move, assuring them that with this action and their faith, they will overcome their adversaries. The call to rely on Allah underscores the belief that true success and victory come from divine support, encouraging believers to maintain their trust in Allah's plan and guidance, even in the face of daunting situations.
orig: قال رجلان من الذين يخافون أنعم الله عليهما ادخلوا عليهم الباب فإذا دخلتموه فإنكم غالبون وعلى الله فتوكلوا إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: They said, 'O Moses, indeed we will not enter it, ever, as long as they are in it; so go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are remaining here.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the fear and lack of faith among the Children of Israel when Moses led them to the Promised Land. They were hesitant to enter and confront the inhabitants due to their perceived strength, showing a moment of weakness and reluctance to trust in God's plan. Their suggestion for Moses to go with his Lord to fight indicates a separation between their own efforts and divine support, highlighting their doubt and unwillingness to participate in the struggle for their promised destiny.
orig: قالوا يا موسى إنا لن ندخلها أبدا ما داموا فيها فاذهب أنت وربك فقاتلا إنا هاهنا قاعدون

translation: He said, 'My Lord, indeed I do not possess except myself and my brother, so separate between us and the defiantly disobedient people.'
interpretation: This verse reflects a plea for divine intervention and protection. The speaker acknowledges his limited control over external circumstances, emphasizing reliance solely on his own integrity and the bond with his brother. The request to be separated from the corrupt group signifies a desire for moral and physical distancing from those who engage in wrongdoing, seeking God's help to maintain righteousness and avoid the influence or consequences of others' sins.
orig: قال رب إني لا أملك إلا نفسي وأخي فافرق بيننا وبين القوم الفاسقين

translation: He said: "Then it is forbidden to them for forty years, while they wander in the land. So do not grieve over the defiantly disobedient people."
interpretation: This verse refers to the punishment given to the Children of Israel for their disobedience and lack of faith. After they refused to enter the Holy Land out of fear, despite Moses' encouragement, God decreed that they would wander in the wilderness for forty years. This period of wandering was a consequence of their rebellion and a time for them to reflect on their actions. The command to Moses not to grieve over the defiantly disobedient people emphasizes the importance of not being overly attached to those who choose to stray from the path of righteousness, as their fate is ultimately in God's hands.
orig: قال فإنها محرمة عليهم أربعين سنة يتيهون في الأرض فلا تأس على القوم الفاسقين

translation: And recite to them the story of the two sons of Adam in truth, when they both offered a sacrifice, and it was accepted from one of them but not accepted from the other. He said, 'I will surely kill you.' He said, 'Indeed, Allah only accepts from the righteous.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of sincerity and righteousness in worship and offerings to Allah. It teaches that acceptance by Allah is not based on the quantity or outward appearance of the offering but on the piety and God-consciousness of the person. The story of the two sons of Adam serves as a moral lesson on jealousy, the consequences of evil intentions, and the value of patience and righteousness in the face of adversity.
orig: واتل عليهم نبأ ابني آدم بالحق إذ قربا قربانا فتقبل من أحدهما ولم يتقبل من الآخر قال لأقتلنك قال إنما يتقبل الله من المتقين

translation: If you do indeed stretch out your hand against me to kill me, I shall not stretch out my hand against you to kill you, for I fear Allah, the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse reflects the moral and ethical stance of Prophet Ibrahim's son, who, despite being threatened with death by his brother, chooses not to retaliate. It underscores the importance of fearing Allah and adhering to moral principles even in the face of extreme adversity. The verse teaches patience, forgiveness, and the prioritization of spiritual values over immediate personal safety or revenge.
orig: لئن بسطت إلي يدك لتقتلني ما أنا بباسط يدي إليك لأقتلك إني أخاف الله رب العالمين

translation: Indeed, I wish that you bear my sin and your sin, so you will be among the dwellers of the Fire, and that is the recompense of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of personal accountability in Islam. It suggests that one should not attempt to shift their own sins or burdens onto others, as each individual will be held responsible for their own actions. The verse serves as a warning against injustice and the manipulation of others for personal gain, emphasizing that such actions lead to severe consequences in the afterlife, specifically being among those who suffer in the Fire. It underscores the importance of fairness and the moral consequences of one's deeds.
orig: إني أريد أن تبوء بإثمي وإثمك فتكون من أصحاب النار وذلك جزاء الظالمين

translation: And his soul permitted to him the murder of his brother, so he killed him and became one of the losers.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the internal struggle and moral decline that can lead to grave sins. The phrase 'his soul permitted to him' suggests that the individual's conscience, influenced by envy or other negative emotions, rationalized the act of murder. This internal justification led to the brother's killing, highlighting how unchecked desires can lead one to commit heinous acts and ultimately result in spiritual loss, as indicated by 'became one of the losers.' The verse serves as a warning about the consequences of allowing one's lower self to dominate over moral and ethical considerations.
orig: فطوعت له نفسه قتل أخيه فقتله فأصبح من الخاسرين

translation: So Allah sent a crow to scratch in the earth and show him how to hide his brother's nakedness. He said, 'Woe to me! Have I failed to be like this crow and hide my brother's nakedness?' And he became one of the remorseful.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the story of Cain and Abel, where Cain, after killing his brother Abel, is taught a lesson by a crow on how to bury his brother's body, symbolizing the importance of learning from nature and the consequences of one's actions. It highlights the theme of remorse and the human capacity for moral reflection and repentance after committing a grave sin.
orig: فبعث الله غرابا يبحث في الأرض ليريه كيف يواري سوءة أخيه قال يا ويلتا أعجزت أن أكون مثل هذا الغراب فأواري سوءة أخي فأصبح من النادمين

translation: Because of that, We decreed upon the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul unless for a soul or for corruption [done] in the land - it is as if he had killed all humankind. And whoever saves a life - it is as if he had saved all humankind. And Our messengers had certainly come to them with clear proofs. Then indeed many of them, [even] after that, throughout the land, were transgressors.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sanctity of human life, highlighting that the act of killing one person unjustly is tantamount to killing all of humanity, while saving one life is equivalent to saving all of humanity. It reflects the profound moral and ethical responsibility placed on individuals to protect life. The reference to the Children of Israel and the messengers with clear proofs indicates that this moral law was communicated to them, yet despite this guidance, many still chose to transgress, illustrating the ongoing human struggle between righteousness and wrongdoing.
orig: من أجل ذلك كتبنا على بني إسرائيل أنه من قتل نفسا بغير نفس أو فساد في الأرض فكأنما قتل الناس جميعا ومن أحياها فكأنما أحيا الناس جميعا ولقد جاءتهم رسلنا بالبينات ثم إن كثيرا منهم بعد ذلك في الأرض لمسرفون

translation: The recompense of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and strive to spread corruption in the land is that they should be killed or crucified or their hands and feet should be cut off from opposite sides or they should be exiled from the land. That is their disgrace in this world, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse outlines the severe consequences for those who actively oppose and fight against the principles of Islam, represented by Allah and His Messenger, and engage in activities that cause widespread corruption and disorder. It emphasizes the gravity of such actions by prescribing harsh punishments as deterrents, which are meant to maintain social order and protect the community. The mention of disgrace in this world and a great punishment in the hereafter underscores the moral and spiritual dimensions of these offenses, highlighting their seriousness both in earthly life and in the afterlife.
orig: إنما جزاء الذين يحاربون الله ورسوله ويسعون في الأرض فسادا أن يقتلوا أو يصلبوا أو تقطع أيديهم وأرجلهم من خلاف أو ينفوا من الأرض ذلك لهم خزي في الدنيا ولهم في الآخرة عذاب عظيم

translation: Except for those who repent before you overpower them; and know that Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the mercy and forgiveness of Allah, indicating that even those who have committed wrongdoings can be forgiven if they sincerely repent before being confronted or overpowered. It emphasizes the importance of timely repentance and the boundless nature of divine forgiveness and mercy.
orig: إلا الذين تابوا من قبل أن تقدروا عليهم فاعلموا أن الله غفور رحيم

translation: O you who have believed, fear Allah and seek the means [of nearness] to Him and strive in His cause that you may succeed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of three key actions for believers: fearing Allah, which means being conscious of Him and avoiding sin; seeking means to draw closer to Him, which can be through prayer, good deeds, and learning; and striving in His cause, which involves personal effort and sacrifice for the sake of righteousness and spreading the message of Islam. Success in this life and the hereafter is promised to those who adhere to these principles.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله وابتغوا إليه الوسيلة وجاهدوا في سبيله لعلكم تفلحون

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve, if they had all that is in the earth and the like of it with them, they would offer it to ransom themselves from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection. But it will not be accepted from them, and for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity and inevitability of divine judgment on the Day of Resurrection. It illustrates that no amount of worldly wealth or possessions can save disbelievers from the punishment they will face. The imagery of offering the entire earth and more as ransom emphasizes the desperation and futility of their situation when confronted with the reality of their disbelief. The verse serves as a stark reminder of the consequences of rejecting faith and the absolute nature of God's justice, where material wealth holds no sway.
orig: إن الذين كفروا لو أن لهم ما في الأرض جميعا ومثله معه ليفتدوا به من عذاب يوم القيامة ما تقبل منهم ولهم عذاب أليم

translation: They want to get out of the Fire, but never will they get out therefrom; and for them is a lasting punishment.
interpretation: This verse underscores the eternal nature of the punishment in Hell for those who are destined to remain there. It reflects the finality and inescapability of divine judgment, emphasizing that once a person is consigned to Hell due to their actions and disbelief, there is no escape from it. The desire to leave the Fire, mentioned here, highlights the torment and regret felt by its inhabitants, yet it also serves as a stark reminder of the consequences of one's choices in life.
orig: يريدون أن يخرجوا من النار وما هم بخارجين منها ولهم عذاب مقيم

translation: As for the thief, the male and the female, amputate their hands in recompense for what they committed as a deterrent [punishment] from Allah. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse establishes a specific punishment for theft, which is the amputation of the hands of both male and female thieves. The purpose of this punishment is twofold: it serves as a retribution for the crime committed and acts as a deterrent to prevent others from engaging in theft. The mention of Allah being 'Exalted in Might and Wise' emphasizes that this ruling comes from divine wisdom and authority, underscoring the seriousness with which theft is viewed in Islamic law. It reflects the balance between justice and mercy, aiming to protect society's rights while offering a chance for the offender to reflect on their actions.
orig: والسارق والسارقة فاقطعوا أيديهما جزاء بما كسبا نكالا من الله والله عزيز حكيم

translation: So whoever repents after his wrongdoing and reforms, indeed, Allah will turn to him in forgiveness. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the mercy and forgiveness of Allah, highlighting that no matter the severity of one's sins, sincere repentance and a commitment to reform can lead to Allah's forgiveness. It serves as a reminder of the boundless compassion of Allah, encouraging believers to never despair of His mercy and to always strive towards righteousness after acknowledging and correcting their wrongs.
orig: فمن تاب من بعد ظلمه وأصلح فإن الله يتوب عليه إن الله غفور رحيم

translation: Do you not know that to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth? He punishes whom He wills and forgives whom He wills, and Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute sovereignty and authority over the universe. It reminds believers that Allah has the ultimate power to decide the fate of individuals, choosing to either punish or forgive them according to His wisdom and justice. The verse also underscores Allah's omnipotence, indicating that His capability extends over all aspects of creation, reinforcing the concept of tawheed (the oneness of God) and the necessity of submitting to His will.
orig: ألم تعلم أن الله له ملك السماوات والأرض يعذب من يشاء ويغفر لمن يشاء والله على كل شيء قدير

translation: O Messenger, let not those who hasten to disbelief grieve you from among those who say, 'We believe' with their mouths, but their hearts believe not, and from among the Jews; [they are] listeners to falsehood, [and] listeners to other people who have not come to you. They distort words from their [proper] usages, saying, 'If you are given this, take it; but if you are not given it, then beware.' And he whom Allah wants to put to trial - never will you possess [power to do] anything for him against Allah. Those are the ones for whom Allah does not intend to purify their hearts. For them in this world is disgrace, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad, advising him not to be disheartened by the hypocrisy and deceit of certain individuals. It highlights the insincerity of those who verbally profess faith but harbor disbelief in their hearts, as well as some Jews who listen to falsehood and distort the meanings of words to serve their interests. The verse emphasizes that such people manipulate religious teachings to suit their desires, warning against following them. It also underscores the concept of divine trial, indicating that those whom Allah chooses to test, no one can intervene on their behalf. The verse concludes by stating that Allah will not purify the hearts of such individuals, leading to their disgrace in this life and severe punishment in the hereafter, reflecting the consequences of their actions and the importance of sincerity in faith.
orig: يا أيها الرسول لا يحزنك الذين يسارعون في الكفر من الذين قالوا آمنا بأفواههم ولم تؤمن قلوبهم ومن الذين هادوا سماعون للكذب سماعون لقوم آخرين لم يأتوك يحرفون الكلم من بعد مواضعه يقولون إن أوتيتم هذا فخذوه وإن لم تؤتوه فاحذروا ومن يرد الله فتنته فلن تملك له من الله شيئا أولئك الذين لم يرد الله أن يطهر قلوبهم لهم في الدنيا خزي ولهم في الآخرة عذاب عظيم

translation: Listeners to falsehood, devourers of what is unlawful. If they come to you, then judge between them or turn away from them. And if you turn away from them, they will not harm you at all. And if you judge, then judge between them with justice. Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly.
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad and instructs him on how to deal with people who are known for engaging in falsehood and consuming unlawful gains. It advises that when such individuals approach him for judgment, he has the option either to adjudicate their disputes or to ignore their requests. The verse emphasizes that choosing not to engage with them will not result in any harm to the Prophet. However, if he decides to intervene, he must do so with fairness and equity, reflecting the divine preference for justice. This guidance underscores the importance of maintaining integrity and justice in leadership, even when dealing with morally questionable individuals.
orig: سماعون للكذب أكالون للسحت فإن جاءوك فاحكم بينهم أو أعرض عنهم وإن تعرض عنهم فلن يضروك شيئا وإن حكمت فاحكم بينهم بالقسط إن الله يحب المقسطين

translation: And how do they appoint you as a judge while they have the Torah, in which is the judgement of Allah; then they turn away after that? And those are not believers.
interpretation: This verse critiques the inconsistency of those who possess the Torah, which contains God's laws, yet they turn away from its judgments and seek a different arbiter. It highlights a lack of faith and adherence to divine guidance, suggesting that true belief entails following the divine rulings as laid out in the scriptures.
orig: وكيف يحكمونك وعندهم التوراة فيها حكم الله ثم يتولون من بعد ذلك وما أولئك بالمؤمنين

translation: Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which was guidance and light. The prophets who submitted [to Allah] judged by it for the Jews, as did the rabbis and scholars by that with which they were entrusted of the Scripture of Allah, and they were witnesses thereto. So do not fear the people but fear Me, and do not exchange My verses for a small price. And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin of the Torah, highlighting its role as a source of guidance and light for the Jewish community. It underscores the responsibility of the prophets, rabbis, and scholars to adhere to and implement its teachings. The verse also serves as a reminder to all believers to prioritize the fear of God over the fear of human beings and to uphold divine laws without compromising them for worldly gains. It warns against the rejection of God's revelations, equating such rejection with disbelief.
orig: إنا أنزلنا التوراة فيها هدى ونور يحكم بها النبيون الذين أسلموا للذين هادوا والربانيون والأحبار بما استحفظوا من كتاب الله وكانوا عليه شهداء فلا تخشوا الناس واخشون ولا تشتروا بآياتي ثمنا قليلا ومن لم يحكم بما أنزل الله فأولئك هم الكافرون

translation: And We ordained for them therein that life is for life, and eye for eye, and nose for nose, and ear for ear, and tooth for tooth, and for wounds is legal retribution. But whoever forgoes it out of charity, it shall be an expiation for him. And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, then it is those who are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse outlines the principle of qisas (retribution) in Islamic law, emphasizing the concept of justice through equivalence in punishment for crimes like murder and bodily harm. It also encourages forgiveness and charity, suggesting that choosing to forgo retribution can serve as an expiation for one's sins. Moreover, the verse stresses the importance of adhering to divine law, warning that those who do not judge by what Allah has revealed are considered wrongdoers, highlighting the moral and legal obligation to follow God's commandments.
orig: وكتبنا عليهم فيها أن النفس بالنفس والعين بالعين والأنف بالأنف والأذن بالأذن والسن بالسن والجروح قصاص فمن تصدق به فهو كفارة له ومن لم يحكم بما أنزل الله فأولئك هم الظالمون

translation: And We sent following in their footsteps Jesus, the son of Mary, confirming what came before him of the Torah; and We gave him the Gospel, in which was guidance and light and confirming what was before it of the Torah as guidance and admonition for the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the continuity and confirmation of divine revelation across different scriptures. Jesus, as a prophet, is presented as a continuer of the prophetic tradition, specifically affirming the Torah that came before him. The Gospel given to Jesus is described as containing guidance and light, further reinforcing the message of the Torah. This underscores the unity of the message across different revelations, aimed at guiding the righteous. The mention of 'guidance and admonition for the righteous' highlights the purpose of these scriptures to lead believers towards righteousness and moral conduct.
orig: وقفينا على آثارهم بعيسى ابن مريم مصدقا لما بين يديه من التوراة وآتيناه الإنجيل فيه هدى ونور ومصدقا لما بين يديه من التوراة وهدى وموعظة للمتقين

translation: And let the People of the Gospel judge by what Allah has revealed therein. And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed - it is those who are the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the obligation of the People of the Gospel (Christians) to adhere to the divine laws revealed in their scripture. It underscores the importance of following God's commandments as they are revealed in the sacred texts. The term 'defiantly disobedient' (al-fasiqun) refers to those who knowingly reject or fail to implement these divine laws, indicating a severe moral and spiritual transgression. This highlights the universal principle in Islam that all people must abide by the guidance given to them through their respective scriptures.
orig: وليحكم أهل الإنجيل بما أنزل الله فيه ومن لم يحكم بما أنزل الله فأولئك هم الفاسقون

translation: And We have revealed to you the Book in truth, confirming that which preceded it of the Scripture and as a criterion over it. So judge between them by what Allah has revealed and do not follow their inclinations away from the truth that has come to you. To each of you We have given a law and a way. And if Allah had willed, He would have made you one nation [united in religion], but [He intended] to test you in what He has given you; so race to [all that is] good. To Allah is your return all together, and He will [then] inform you concerning that over which you used to differ.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin and authority of the Qur'an, which is described as a confirmation of previous scriptures and a criterion to judge them. It instructs the Prophet Muhammad to use the Qur'an as the basis for judgment among people, rather than following their desires, which might deviate from the truth. The verse acknowledges the diversity of laws and paths given to different communities, suggesting that this diversity is part of God's plan to test humanity. It encourages believers to strive towards good deeds, reminding them that ultimately, all will return to God, who will resolve all disputes and differences.
orig: وأنزلنا إليك الكتاب بالحق مصدقا لما بين يديه من الكتاب ومهيمنا عليه فاحكم بينهم بما أنزل الله ولا تتبع أهواءهم عما جاءك من الحق لكل جعلنا منكم شرعة ومنهاجا ولو شاء الله لجعلكم أمة واحدة ولكن ليبلوكم في ما آتاكم فاستبقوا الخيرات إلى الله مرجعكم جميعا فينبئكم بما كنتم فيه تختلفون

translation: And judge between them by what Allah has revealed and do not follow their desires, and beware of them lest they tempt you away from some of what Allah has revealed to you. And if they turn away, then know that Allah wants to afflict them with some of their sins. And indeed, many among the people are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of adhering strictly to the divine revelations when making judgments, rather than being swayed by the desires or pressures of others. It instructs the Prophet Muhammad, and by extension all leaders and judges, to remain steadfast in applying God's laws, even in the face of opposition or temptation to compromise. The verse also warns that if people reject the divine guidance, they will face consequences for their sins, highlighting the concept of divine justice and the prevalence of disobedience among mankind.
orig: وأن احكم بينهم بما أنزل الله ولا تتبع أهواءهم واحذرهم أن يفتنوك عن بعض ما أنزل الله إليك فإن تولوا فاعلم أنما يريد الله أن يصيبهم ببعض ذنوبهم وإن كثيرا من الناس لفاسقون

translation: Do they then seek the judgement of the Days of Ignorance? And who is better in judgement than Allah for a people who are certain [in faith]?
interpretation: This verse critiques those who prefer the customs and laws of the pre-Islamic period, known as the Days of Ignorance, over the divine laws revealed by Allah. It emphasizes that Allah's judgement is superior and more just, especially for those who have firm faith. The verse challenges believers to reflect on their sources of guidance and to trust in Allah's perfect judgement over human-made systems.
orig: أفحكم الجاهلية يبغون ومن أحسن من الله حكما لقوم يوقنون

translation: O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies. They are allies of one another. And whoever among you takes them as allies, then indeed, he is one of them. Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse advises believers to be cautious in forming alliances with Jews and Christians, emphasizing the importance of loyalty to the Muslim community. It suggests that aligning closely with these groups could lead to a compromise of one's faith and identity, as such alliances might pull a believer away from the principles of Islam. The verse stresses that those who choose such alliances are considered to have joined the other group in a way that distances them from the Muslim community. It underscores the guidance of Allah, indicating that those who wrongfully ally themselves in this manner are straying from the path of righteousness.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتخذوا اليهود والنصارى أولياء بعضهم أولياء بعض ومن يتولهم منكم فإنه منهم إن الله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: So you see those in whose hearts is a disease hastening into [association with] them, saying, 'We fear lest a misfortune befall us.' But perhaps Allah will bring about a victory or a decision from Him, so they would become, over what they had been concealing within themselves, regretful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inner conflict and hypocrisy of those who outwardly claim fear of misfortune as a reason to align with disbelievers, yet inwardly harbor doubts and fear. It suggests that such individuals are driven by a 'disease' in their hearts, symbolizing weakness of faith or hypocrisy. The verse warns that their actions may lead to regret if Allah grants victory or a divine decision to the believers, exposing their hidden intentions and leaving them remorseful for their lack of trust and faith.
orig: فترى الذين في قلوبهم مرض يسارعون فيهم يقولون نخشى أن تصيبنا دائرة فعسى الله أن يأتي بالفتح أو أمر من عنده فيصبحوا على ما أسروا في أنفسهم نادمين

translation: And those who believe say, 'Are these the ones who swore by Allah their strongest oaths that indeed they were with you?' Their deeds have become worthless, and they have become losers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the disillusionment felt by the believers towards those who falsely claimed allegiance to them through strong oaths in the name of Allah. It underscores the consequences of hypocrisy and betrayal, illustrating that such actions render one's deeds void and lead to ultimate loss in both worldly and spiritual terms. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of sincerity in faith and the severe repercussions of deceit.
orig: ويقول الذين آمنوا أهؤلاء الذين أقسموا بالله جهد أيمانهم إنهم لمعكم حبطت أعمالهم فأصبحوا خاسرين

translation: O you who have believed, whoever of you should revert from his religion - Allah will bring forth [in place of them] a people He will love and who will love Him [who are] humble toward the believers, powerful against the disbelievers; they strive in the cause of Allah and do not fear the blame of a critic. That is the favor of Allah; He bestows it upon whom He wills. And Allah is all-Encompassing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse addresses the believers, warning them about the consequences of apostasy and reassuring them of Allah's plan. It emphasizes that if some believers abandon their faith, Allah will replace them with a new group of people who are characterized by their love for Allah and His love for them. These individuals will be humble and gentle towards fellow believers but firm and strong against those who reject faith. They are dedicated to striving in Allah's path, undeterred by criticism or blame from detractors. The verse highlights that such qualities and the emergence of such a group are a manifestation of Allah's grace, which He bestows according to His wisdom. It underscores Allah's attributes of being all-Encompassing and all-Knowing, indicating His vast capacity and complete knowledge in managing the affairs of His creation.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا من يرتد منكم عن دينه فسوف يأتي الله بقوم يحبهم ويحبونه أذلة على المؤمنين أعزة على الكافرين يجاهدون في سبيل الله ولا يخافون لومة لائم ذلك فضل الله يؤتيه من يشاء والله واسع عليم

translation: Your ally is none but Allah and [therefore] His Messenger and those who have believed - those who establish prayer and give zakah, and they bow [in worship].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of allegiance and support in Islam. It clarifies that the true allies or protectors of the believers are Allah, His Messenger, and the believers themselves who actively practice their faith through regular prayer and giving zakah. The mention of bowing (raka') during prayer signifies humility and devotion. The verse serves as a reminder to Muslims to seek support and guidance from these sources, reinforcing the importance of community and collective worship in strengthening faith and unity.
orig: إنما وليكم الله ورسوله والذين آمنوا الذين يقيمون الصلاة ويؤتون الزكاة وهم راكعون

translation: And whoever allies themselves with Allah and His Messenger and those who believe - then the party of Allah are the ones who will be victorious.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of aligning oneself with Allah, His Messenger, and the community of believers. It suggests that true success and victory in life come from being part of the group that follows Allah's guidance and supports His cause. The term "party of Allah" refers to those who are committed to righteousness and faith, indicating that such a group will ultimately prevail over opposition and adversity due to their steadfastness and divine support.
orig: ومن يتول الله ورسوله والذين آمنوا فإن حزب الله هم الغالبون

translation: O you who have believed, do not take those who have taken your religion in ridicule and amusement from among the ones who were given the Scripture before you and the disbelievers as allies. And fear Allah, if you should be believers.
interpretation: This verse advises believers not to form close alliances with those who mock or belittle their faith, including those from among the People of the Scripture (Jews and Christians) and other disbelievers. The underlying message is to maintain the integrity and seriousness of one's faith by not associating closely with those who do not respect it. The call to fear Allah emphasizes the importance of prioritizing one's faith and spiritual well-being over worldly relationships that could compromise it.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتخذوا الذين اتخذوا دينكم هزوا ولعبا من الذين أوتوا الكتاب من قبلكم والكفار أولياء واتقوا الله إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: And when you called to prayer, they took it as mockery and play; that is because they are a people who do not understand.
interpretation: This verse highlights the attitude of those who treat the call to prayer with disdain and amusement, indicating a lack of seriousness and respect towards religious obligations. It suggests that such behavior stems from a deeper issue of not comprehending the significance and purpose of prayer, reflecting a broader spiritual and intellectual deficiency.
orig: وإذا ناديتم إلى الصلاة اتخذوها هزوا ولعبا ذلك بأنهم قوم لا يعقلون

translation: Say, O People of the Scripture, do you resent us except [for] that we have believed in Allah and what was revealed to us and what was revealed before, and [because] most of you are defiantly disobedient?
interpretation: This verse addresses the People of the Scripture (Jews and Christians) and challenges their resentment towards Muslims. The interpretation suggests that their opposition stems not from any genuine theological disagreement, but rather from the Muslims' belief in Allah and the revelations given to them, as well as the earlier scriptures. The verse implies that the root of their animosity is envy and their own disobedience to God, as it states that most of them are defiantly disobedient. It highlights a theme of moral and spiritual critique against those who should know better due to their access to earlier divine revelations.
orig: قل يا أهل الكتاب هل تنقمون منا إلا أن آمنا بالله وما أنزل إلينا وما أنزل من قبل وأن أكثركم فاسقون

translation: Say, "Shall I inform you of [something] worse than that as penalty from Allah? [It is that of] those whom Allah has cursed and with whom He became angry and made of them apes and pigs and slaves of Taghut. Those are worse in position and far astray from the sound way."
interpretation: This verse is a warning from Allah to the disbelievers, highlighting the severe consequences of rejecting faith and following false deities. It describes the ultimate punishment for those who have been cursed by Allah, His wrath upon them, and their transformation into apes and pigs as a metaphor for their degraded state. Additionally, it refers to those who worship Taghut (false gods or idols) as being in the lowest position and furthest from the straight path of righteousness. The verse emphasizes the gravity of disbelief and idolatry, urging people to heed the warning and turn towards the true path of Islam.
orig: قل هل أنبئكم بشر من ذلك مثوبة عند الله من لعنه الله وغضب عليه وجعل منهم القردة والخنازير وعبد الطاغوت أولئك شر مكانا وأضل عن سواء السبيل

translation: And when they come to you, they say, "We believe." But they have entered with disbelief, and they have left with it; and Allah knows best what they were concealing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of certain individuals who claim to embrace faith when in the presence of the Prophet Muhammad, yet their hearts remain entrenched in disbelief. They enter and leave the Prophet's company with the same hidden rejection of faith. Allah, being all-knowing, is fully aware of their concealed intentions and the true state of their hearts, underscoring the futility of their deception.
orig: وإذا جاءوكم قالوا آمنا وقد دخلوا بالكفر وهم قد خرجوا به والله أعلم بما كانوا يكتمون

translation: And you see many of them hastening into sin and transgression and their devouring of unlawful gain. Evil indeed is what they have been doing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the moral decay among some individuals, emphasizing their eagerness to engage in sinful acts, aggression, and the consumption of what is forbidden or impure. It serves as a critique of their actions, underscoring the gravity and wrongness of their deeds, suggesting that such behavior is deeply flawed and contrary to the ethical standards expected in Islam.
orig: وترى كثيرا منهم يسارعون في الإثم والعدوان وأكلهم السحت لبئس ما كانوا يعملون

translation: Why do not the rabbis and the scholars forbid them from saying sinful words and eating unlawful things? Evil indeed is what they have been doing.
interpretation: This verse criticizes the religious leaders, specifically the rabbis and scholars, for failing to guide their community away from sinful speech and the consumption of forbidden substances. It highlights their responsibility to prevent moral corruption and suggests that their inaction or negligence in fulfilling this duty is a grave error, contributing to the spread of evil within the society.
orig: لولا ينهاهم الربانيون والأحبار عن قولهم الإثم وأكلهم السحت لبئس ما كانوا يصنعون

translation: And the Jews say, "The hand of Allah is chained." Chained are their hands, and cursed are they for what they said. Rather, both His hands are outstretched; He spends however He wills. And that which has been revealed to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in transgression and disbelief. And We have cast among them animosity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection. Every time they kindled the fire of war, Allah extinguished it. And they strive throughout the land [causing] corruption, and Allah does not like corrupters.
interpretation: This verse addresses the false claim by some Jews that Allah's power or generosity is limited, symbolized by the metaphor of a 'chained hand'. The Qur'an refutes this by asserting that Allah's hands are 'outstretched', indicating His boundless generosity and power to provide as He wills. The verse also reflects on the spiritual consequences of such disbelief, noting that it leads to increased transgression and disbelief among them. Furthermore, it highlights the ongoing conflict and enmity among the Jews as a divine decree until the Day of Judgment, emphasizing that their attempts at war and corruption are ultimately futile as Allah extinguishes their efforts and disapproves of corruption.
orig: وقالت اليهود يد الله مغلولة غلت أيديهم ولعنوا بما قالوا بل يداه مبسوطتان ينفق كيف يشاء وليزيدن كثيرا منهم ما أنزل إليك من ربك طغيانا وكفرا وألقينا بينهم العداوة والبغضاء إلى يوم القيامة كلما أوقدوا نارا للحرب أطفأها الله ويسعون في الأرض فسادا والله لا يحب المفسدين

translation: And if the People of the Scripture had believed and feared Allah, We would have surely removed from them their misdeeds and admitted them into Gardens of Pleasure.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the conditional promise of divine forgiveness and reward. It suggests that faith and piety are key prerequisites for the expiation of sins and entry into Paradise. The verse specifically addresses the People of the Scripture, indicating that despite their possession of earlier revelations, their acceptance of the final message of Islam is crucial for attaining divine mercy and ultimate salvation.
orig: ولو أن أهل الكتاب آمنوا واتقوا لكفرنا عنهم سيئاتهم ولأدخلناهم جنات النعيم

translation: And if they had upheld the Torah and the Gospel and what was revealed to them from their Lord, they would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet. Among them is a moderate community, but many of them - evil is what they do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to the divine scriptures, specifically the Torah and the Gospel, as well as the revelations given to them. It suggests that had the people followed these scriptures faithfully, they would have enjoyed abundant blessings and prosperity, symbolized by eating 'from above them and from beneath their feet.' However, the verse also acknowledges the existence of a moderate group within the community who strive to follow the right path, in contrast to the majority who engage in evil actions, highlighting the moral and spiritual decline among many despite the guidance available to them.
orig: ولو أنهم أقاموا التوراة والإنجيل وما أنزل إليهم من ربهم لأكلوا من فوقهم ومن تحت أرجلهم منهم أمة مقتصدة وكثير منهم ساء ما يعملون

translation: O Messenger, convey what has been revealed to you from your Lord, and if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message. And Allah will protect you from the people. Indeed, Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of the Prophet Muhammad fulfilling his duty to convey the message of Islam as revealed to him by Allah, without any fear or hesitation. It reassures him that Allah will provide protection against any harm from people who might oppose the message. The verse also highlights that those who disbelieve and reject the message are not guided by Allah, underscoring the significance of accepting and following the divine guidance.
orig: يا أيها الرسول بلغ ما أنزل إليك من ربك وإن لم تفعل فما بلغت رسالته والله يعصمك من الناس إن الله لا يهدي القوم الكافرين

translation: Say, O People of the Scripture, you have no [valid] standing until you uphold the Torah and the Gospel, and what has been revealed to you from your Lord. And it increases many of them in rebellion and disbelief. So do not grieve over the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to the divine scriptures that were revealed before the Qur'an, specifically the Torah and the Gospel. It addresses the People of the Scripture (Jews and Christians) and instructs them to follow their own scriptures faithfully. The verse also acknowledges that despite the clear guidance provided in these scriptures, many among them choose to rebel and disbelieve, which leads to an increase in their transgression. The Prophet Muhammad is advised not to be distressed by the disbelief of these people, indicating that their rejection does not negate the truth of the message he brings. This serves as a reminder of the continuity of divine guidance across different revelations and the universal call to righteousness and faith.
orig: قل يا أهل الكتاب لستم على شيء حتى تقيموا التوراة والإنجيل وما أنزل إليكم من ربكم وليزيدن كثيرا منهم ما أنزل إليك من ربك طغيانا وكفرا فلا تأس على القوم الكافرين

translation: Indeed, those who believed and those who were Jews or Sabeans or Christians - all who believed in Allah and the Last Day and did righteous deeds - there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inclusivity of salvation in Islam, indicating that righteousness and belief in the fundamental principles of faith in God and the Hereafter are the key criteria for salvation, regardless of one's specific religious affiliation. It reassures that those who meet these criteria from various religious backgrounds will be free from fear and sorrow in the afterlife.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا والذين هادوا والصابئون والنصارى من آمن بالله واليوم الآخر وعمل صالحا فلا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: We took the covenant from the Children of Israel and sent to them messengers. Every time a messenger came to them with what their souls did not desire, a group of them they denied, and another group they killed.
interpretation: This verse reflects on the historical relationship between God and the Children of Israel, emphasizing their repeated rejection of divine guidance.
