It highlights a pattern of behavior where, whenever a messenger brought teachings or commandments that did not align with their desires or expectations, segments of the community either denied the messenger's authenticity or resorted to violence against them. This underscores the human tendency to resist messages that challenge personal or communal inclinations, illustrating a broader lesson on the importance of accepting divine guidance regardless of personal preference.
orig: لقد أخذنا ميثاق بني إسرائيل وأرسلنا إليهم رسلا كلما جاءهم رسول بما لا تهوى أنفسهم فريقا كذبوا وفريقا يقتلون

translation: And they thought that there would be no fitnah (trial), so they became blind and deaf; then Allah forgave them; then (again) many of them became blind and deaf. And Allah is Seeing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse reflects on the spiritual condition of a group of people who were initially heedless of the trials and tribulations that would test their faith. Their initial blindness and deafness symbolize their lack of understanding and awareness of the divine message. Allah's forgiveness indicates His mercy, giving them another chance to heed the message. However, the repetition of their becoming blind and deaf again shows their persistent refusal to accept guidance despite being given the opportunity to do so. The verse underscores Allah's omniscience, emphasizing that He is fully aware of all actions and intentions, and that individuals are accountable for their choices.
orig: وحسبوا ألا تكون فتنة فعموا وصموا ثم تاب الله عليهم ثم عموا وصموا كثير منهم والله بصير بما يعملون

translation: Indeed, those who say, 'Allah is the Messiah, the son of Mary,' have disbelieved. The Messiah himself said, 'O Children of Israel, worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord.' Indeed, whoever associates partners with Allah - Allah has forbidden him Paradise, and his refuge is the Fire. And there are not for the wrongdoers any helpers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Islamic belief in the oneness of God (Tawhid) and explicitly rejects the Christian doctrine of the Trinity, particularly the belief that Jesus (referred to as the Messiah, son of Mary) is divine or a part of God. It underscores that Jesus himself called for the worship of the one true God, Allah, and not himself. The verse warns that associating partners with Allah (shirk) is a grave sin that leads to exclusion from Paradise and consigns one to Hell, highlighting the severity of this theological error and the absence of any support for those who commit such injustice.
orig: لقد كفر الذين قالوا إن الله هو المسيح ابن مريم وقال المسيح يا بني إسرائيل اعبدوا الله ربي وربكم إنه من يشرك بالله فقد حرم الله عليه الجنة ومأواه النار وما للظالمين من أنصار

translation: Indeed, those who say, 'Allah is the third of three,' have disbelieved, and there is no deity except one God. And if they do not desist from what they are saying, there will surely afflict the disbelievers among them a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse addresses the concept of trinity, specifically rejecting the notion that Allah is one part of a triune God. It emphasizes the fundamental Islamic belief in the absolute oneness of God (Tawhid), asserting that there is no deity worthy of worship except the one God. The verse warns those who persist in such beliefs of a severe punishment, underlining the seriousness of associating partners with Allah, which is considered a grave sin in Islam.
orig: لقد كفر الذين قالوا إن الله ثالث ثلاثة وما من إله إلا إله واحد وإن لم ينتهوا عما يقولون ليمسن الذين كفروا منهم عذاب أليم

translation: Will they not repent to Allah and seek His forgiveness? And Allah is Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to turn back to Allah in repentance and seek His forgiveness, emphasizing that no matter the severity of their sins, Allah's mercy and forgiveness are vast and readily available to those who sincerely seek it.
orig: أفلا يتوبون إلى الله ويستغفرونه والله غفور رحيم

translation: The Messiah, son of Mary, was no more than a messenger; many were the messengers that passed away before him. His mother was a truthful woman. They both ate food. See how We make the signs clear to them; yet see how they are turned away!
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the humanity of Jesus (Isa) and his mother Mary (Maryam), highlighting that despite their revered status, they were still human beings who needed to eat, just like other prophets before them. The verse serves as a reminder to not elevate Jesus beyond his role as a messenger of God, and it critiques the tendency of some to deviate from this understanding, illustrating how clear signs are provided yet people still turn away from the truth.
orig: ما المسيح ابن مريم إلا رسول قد خلت من قبله الرسل وأمه صديقة كانا يأكلان الطعام انظر كيف نبين لهم الآيات ثم انظر أنى يؤفكون

translation: Say, 'Do you worship besides Allah that which has no power to harm or benefit you, while Allah is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing?'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility and error of worshipping anything other than Allah, as these entities possess no real power to affect one's life positively or negatively. It underscores the omnipotence and omniscience of Allah, encouraging believers to direct their worship solely to Him, who hears all and knows all, thereby reinforcing the concept of Tawheed (the oneness of God).
orig: قل أتعبدون من دون الله ما لا يملك لكم ضرا ولا نفعا والله هو السميع العليم

translation: Say, O People of the Scripture, do not exceed limits in your religion beyond the truth, and do not follow the desires of a people who went astray before and misled many and have strayed from the soundness of the way.
interpretation: This verse addresses the People of the Scripture, which includes Jews and Christians, urging them not to go beyond the bounds of truth in their religious practices and beliefs. It warns against following the misguided inclinations of previous generations who deviated from the right path, leading many astray. The verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to the true essence of faith as revealed by God, rather than being swayed by human desires or erroneous interpretations of scripture.
orig: قل يا أهل الكتاب لا تغلوا في دينكم غير الحق ولا تتبعوا أهواء قوم قد ضلوا من قبل وأضلوا كثيرا وضلوا عن سواء السبيل

translation: Cursed were those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel by the tongue of David and Jesus, the son of Mary. That was because they disobeyed and were transgressing.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the disbelief and disobedience of some among the Children of Israel led to their being cursed by two of God's prophets, David and Jesus. The curse is a consequence of their persistent transgression and disobedience against God's commandments. It underscores the gravity of rejecting faith and the resultant divine disapproval, serving as a warning to all believers about the consequences of straying from the path of righteousness.
orig: لعن الذين كفروا من بني إسرائيل على لسان داوود وعيسى ابن مريم ذلك بما عصوا وكانوا يعتدون

translation: They used to not forbid one another from the evil they committed. How wretched was what they used to do!
interpretation: This verse highlights the moral decay within a community where individuals fail to prevent wrongdoing among themselves. It underscores the importance of mutual accountability and the negative consequences of neglecting to enjoin good and forbid evil, leading to a society that perpetuates harmful actions.
orig: كانوا لا يتناهون عن منكر فعلوه لبئس ما كانوا يفعلون

translation: You see many of them turning to those who disbelieve. Wretched is that which their souls have sent forth for them, that Allah's wrath is upon them, and in the punishment they will abide forever.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual and moral consequences of aligning oneself with disbelievers, indicating a severe misjudgment and a betrayal of faith. It suggests that such actions lead to divine displeasure and eternal punishment, emphasizing the gravity of choosing worldly alliances over faith in Allah.
orig: ترى كثيرا منهم يتولون الذين كفروا لبئس ما قدمت لهم أنفسهم أن سخط الله عليهم وفي العذاب هم خالدون

translation: And if they had believed in Allah and the Prophet and what was revealed to him, they would not have taken them as allies; but many of them are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of true faith in Allah, the Prophet Muhammad, and the Qur'an. It suggests that genuine belief would lead to a clear distinction in alliances, preventing believers from aligning with those who oppose their faith. The verse highlights that the failure to make such distinctions often stems from a lack of true faith, as evidenced by the disobedience of many who claim to believe.
orig: ولو كانوا يؤمنون بالله والنبي وما أنزل إليه ما اتخذوهم أولياء ولكن كثيرا منهم فاسقون

translation: You will surely find the most intense of the people in animosity toward the believers to be the Jews and those who associate others with Allah; and you will find the nearest of them in affection to the believers to be those who say, 'We are Christians.' That is because among them are priests and monks and because they are not arrogant.
interpretation: This verse highlights the varying degrees of hostility and affinity towards Muslims from different religious groups at the time of the Prophet Muhammad. It specifically points out that the Jews and polytheists were the most antagonistic towards Muslims, likely due to theological and political conflicts. In contrast, Christians are noted as being more affectionate towards Muslims, attributed to the presence of humble and devoted religious figures among them, such as priests and monks, who did not exhibit arrogance. This suggests that humility and lack of arrogance can foster better interfaith relations.
orig: لتجدن أشد الناس عداوة للذين آمنوا اليهود والذين أشركوا ولتجدن أقربهم مودة للذين آمنوا الذين قالوا إنا نصارى ذلك بأن منهم قسيسين ورهبانا وأنهم لا يستكبرون

translation: And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of what they have recognized of the truth. They say, 'Our Lord, we have believed, so register us among the witnesses.'
interpretation: This verse describes the profound emotional response of the believers upon hearing the revelations of the Qur'an. Their tears are a manifestation of their deep recognition and acceptance of the truth contained within the message. The believers' immediate reaction is to affirm their faith and request to be recorded among those who bear witness to the truth, indicating their commitment to uphold and testify to the message of Islam. This highlights the transformative power of the Qur'an, which not only touches the hearts but also inspires a public declaration of faith and a desire to be counted among the righteous.
orig: وإذا سمعوا ما أنزل إلى الرسول ترى أعينهم تفيض من الدمع مما عرفوا من الحق يقولون ربنا آمنا فاكتبنا مع الشاهدين

translation: And what is there to prevent us from believing in Allah and in the truth that has come to us, while we hope that our Lord will admit us among the righteous people?
interpretation: This verse reflects a deep sense of faith and optimism among believers. It expresses their readiness to embrace the truth revealed by Allah and their hope for divine acceptance among the righteous. It underscores the importance of faith in Allah and the anticipation of being rewarded with the company of the virtuous in the hereafter, highlighting the believers' motivation and ultimate goal in their spiritual journey.
orig: وما لنا لا نؤمن بالله وما جاءنا من الحق ونطمع أن يدخلنا ربنا مع القوم الصالحين

translation: So Allah rewarded them for what they said with gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide eternally. And that is the reward of the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the divine promise of reward for those who exhibit faith and righteousness. The gardens with flowing rivers symbolize the eternal bliss and tranquility of Paradise, which is granted to those who speak and act with sincerity and goodness. The phrase 'for what they said' highlights the importance of truthful speech and the intention behind one's words, indicating that both actions and words are significant in earning Allah's reward. The eternal nature of the reward ('wherein they will abide eternally') emphasizes the everlasting nature of the afterlife, and 'the doers of good' underscores that consistent good deeds are essential for attaining this divine recompense.
orig: فأثابهم الله بما قالوا جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها وذلك جزاء المحسنين

translation: And those who disbelieve and deny Our signs, those are the companions of the Hellfire.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequence of disbelief and rejection of divine signs. It indicates that those who consciously choose to disbelieve and deny the truths revealed through the signs of Allah will ultimately find themselves in Hellfire. This serves as a warning and a reminder of the accountability that awaits individuals based on their faith and actions.
orig: والذين كفروا وكذبوا بآياتنا أولئك أصحاب الجحيم

translation: O you who have believed, do not prohibit the good things which Allah has made lawful to you and do not transgress. Indeed, Allah does not like transgressors.
interpretation: This verse encourages Muslims to enjoy the lawful pleasures and provisions that Allah has provided, emphasizing moderation and gratitude. It warns against self-imposed prohibitions that go beyond the limits set by Allah, which could lead to a form of extremism or unnecessary hardship. The verse also cautions against excess and transgression in any form, reminding believers that such behavior is displeasing to Allah. It promotes a balanced approach to life, where one enjoys Allah's blessings without overstepping moral and religious boundaries.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تحرموا طيبات ما أحل الله لكم ولا تعتدوا إن الله لا يحب المعتدين

translation: And eat of what Allah has provided for you, lawful and good, and fear Allah in whom you believe.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to consume food that is permissible and wholesome, emphasizing the importance of gratitude and mindfulness of God's provisions. It also serves as a reminder to maintain piety and fear of Allah, acknowledging His role as the sustainer and the object of their faith.
orig: وكلوا مما رزقكم الله حلالا طيبا واتقوا الله الذي أنتم به مؤمنون

translation: Allah will not call you to account for your unintentional oaths, but He will call you to account for what you have sworn with intention. Its expiation is the feeding of ten poor people from the average of what you feed your families, or clothing them, or freeing a slave. And whoever does not find [the means] - then a fast of three days. That is the expiation of your oaths when you have sworn. And protect your oaths. Thus does Allah make clear to you His verses that you may be grateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of intention in oaths and provides a clear guideline for expiation when an intentional oath is broken. It teaches that while unintentional oaths are not held against a person, intentional oaths carry a responsibility. The prescribed expiations - feeding the poor, clothing them, freeing a slave, or fasting - serve as acts of charity and atonement, reflecting the values of compassion and social justice in Islam. The verse also encourages believers to be mindful of their oaths, promoting integrity and reliability in one's word. Through these detailed instructions, Allah demonstrates His mercy and guidance, enabling believers to understand and fulfill their religious obligations, thereby fostering a sense of gratitude towards Him.
orig: لا يؤاخذكم الله باللغو في أيمانكم ولكن يؤاخذكم بما عقدتم الأيمان فكفارته إطعام عشرة مساكين من أوسط ما تطعمون أهليكم أو كسوتهم أو تحرير رقبة فمن لم يجد فصيام ثلاثة أيام ذلك كفارة أيمانكم إذا حلفتم واحفظوا أيمانكم كذلك يبين الله لكم آياته لعلكم تشكرون

translation: O you who have believed, indeed, intoxicants, gambling, [sacrificing on] stone alters [to other than Allah], and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it that you may be successful.
interpretation: This verse instructs believers to abstain from activities that are considered morally and spiritually corrupting, such as alcohol, gambling, and certain pagan practices. These are described as 'defilement' stemming from Satan's influence, suggesting that engaging in them can lead one away from the path of righteousness and success in the hereafter. The command to avoid these acts is framed as a means to achieve true success, emphasizing the importance of spiritual purity and obedience to divine guidance for a prosperous life.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إنما الخمر والميسر والأنصاب والأزلام رجس من عمل الشيطان فاجتنبوه لعلكم تفلحون

translation: Satan's plan is to incite enmity and hatred among you through intoxicants and gambling, and to hinder you from the remembrance of Allah and from prayer. Will you then desist?
interpretation: This verse highlights the dangers of intoxicants and gambling, illustrating how they are tools used by Satan to sow discord and distract believers from their spiritual obligations. It serves as a warning and a call to action for Muslims to avoid these vices in order to maintain unity and focus on worship and remembrance of Allah.
orig: إنما يريد الشيطان أن يوقع بينكم العداوة والبغضاء في الخمر والميسر ويصدكم عن ذكر الله وعن الصلاة فهل أنتم منتهون

translation: And obey Allah and obey the Messenger and beware. And if you turn away, then know that Our Messenger's duty is only to convey the clear message.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to Allah and His Messenger, Muhammad, as a fundamental aspect of faith. It warns believers to be cautious and mindful of their actions, indicating that turning away from this obedience has consequences. The phrase 'if you turn away' suggests a choice given to individuals, highlighting free will. However, it also clarifies the role of the Prophet, stating that his responsibility is solely to deliver the message clearly. This underscores the concept that after the message is conveyed, the responsibility for following it lies with the individual, not the Prophet. The 'clear message' refers to the unambiguous nature of the Qur'anic guidance, which leaves no excuse for those who choose to ignore it.
orig: وأطيعوا الله وأطيعوا الرسول واحذروا فإن توليتم فاعلموا أنما على رسولنا البلاغ المبين

translation: There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten [in the past], as long as they fear Allah and believe and do righteous deeds; then they fear Allah and believe; then they fear Allah and do good; and Allah loves the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of faith, righteousness, and continuous improvement in one's actions. It reassures believers that past dietary practices, which might have been questionable, are not held against them if they have since embraced faith, performed good deeds, and maintained a state of piety. The repetition of 'fear Allah and believe' underscores the necessity of ongoing spiritual vigilance and growth. The verse concludes by highlighting that Allah appreciates those who consistently strive to do good, encouraging a lifestyle of continuous moral and ethical enhancement.
orig: ليس على الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات جناح فيما طعموا إذا ما اتقوا وآمنوا وعملوا الصالحات ثم اتقوا وآمنوا ثم اتقوا وأحسنوا والله يحب المحسنين

translation: O you who have believed, Allah will surely test you with something of the game that your hands and spears can reach, so that Allah may know who fears Him in secret. And whoever transgresses after that - for him is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse addresses the believers, indicating that Allah will test their faith and obedience through the temptation of hunting, which is easily within their reach. The test is designed to reveal those who truly fear Allah even when they are alone and unseen by others. The emphasis on 'in secret' highlights the importance of internal piety and self-restraint. Those who fail this test by transgressing the divine command will face a severe punishment, underscoring the gravity of maintaining obedience to Allah's laws even in private moments.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا ليبلونكم الله بشيء من الصيد تناله أيديكم ورماحكم ليعلم الله من يخافه بالغيب فمن اعتدى بعد ذلك فله عذاب أليم

translation: O you who have believed, do not kill game while you are in the state of ihram. And whoever among you kills it intentionally - its penalty is an equivalent of what he killed from the cattle, as judged by two just men among you as an offering [to be brought] to the Ka'bah, or an expiation: the feeding of needy people or the equivalent of that in fasting, that he may taste the consequence of his deed. Allah has pardoned what has passed, but whoever returns [to violation], then Allah will take retribution from him. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Owner of Retribution.
interpretation: This verse addresses the sanctity of the state of ihram during pilgrimage, emphasizing the prohibition against hunting. It serves as a reminder of the spiritual discipline required during this sacred time, where one's focus should be on devotion and not on worldly pursuits like hunting. The prescribed penalties for breaking this rule—offering a sacrifice, feeding the poor, or fasting—underscore the themes of atonement and restitution. The verse also highlights Allah's mercy by forgiving past transgressions, while warning of His justice and power to punish repeated violations, reinforcing the importance of obedience and the consequences of one's actions.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تقتلوا الصيد وأنتم حرم ومن قتله منكم متعمدا فجزاء مثل ما قتل من النعم يحكم به ذوا عدل منكم هديا بالغ الكعبة أو كفارة طعام مساكين أو عدل ذلك صياما ليذوق وبال أمره عفا الله عما سلف ومن عاد فينتقم الله منه والله عزيز ذو انتقام

translation: Lawful to you is the game of the sea and its food as provision for you and for travelers, but forbidden to you is the game of the land as long as you are in the state of ihram. And fear Allah to whom you will be gathered.
interpretation: This verse addresses the regulations concerning hunting and consumption during the state of ihram, which is a sacred state entered into by Muslims performing Hajj or Umrah. It specifies that while in ihram, Muslims are permitted to benefit from the sea's resources, including fishing and consuming seafood, as these do not violate the sanctity of ihram. However, hunting land animals is strictly prohibited during this period, emphasizing the need for pilgrims to adhere to the rules of ihram, which are designed to foster a sense of humility, equality, and devotion to Allah. The verse concludes with a reminder to fear Allah, reinforcing the importance of obedience to His commands, as all will ultimately be accountable to Him on the Day of Judgment.
orig: أحل لكم صيد البحر وطعامه متاعا لكم وللسيارة وحرم عليكم صيد البر ما دمتم حرما واتقوا الله الذي إليه تحشرون

translation: Allah has made the Ka'bah, the Sacred House, an establishment for mankind, and [has sanctified] the sacred month, the sacrificial animals and the garlands [that mark them]. That is so you may know that Allah knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on earth, and that Allah is All-Knowing of everything.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sanctity and significance of the Ka'bah and related rituals as established by Allah for the guidance and unity of humanity. It underscores that these sacred elements are not only symbols of worship but also reminders of Allah's omniscience. The mention of Allah knowing what is in the heavens and the earth serves to remind believers of His all-encompassing knowledge and the importance of adhering to His commands with full awareness of His constant watchfulness over all affairs.
orig: جعل الله الكعبة البيت الحرام قياما للناس والشهر الحرام والهدي والقلائد ذلك لتعلموا أن الله يعلم ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وأن الله بكل شيء عليم

translation: Know that Allah is severe in punishment and that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the dual nature of Allah's attributes: His severity in punishment serves as a warning against disobedience and sin, while His forgiveness and mercy offer hope and encouragement for repentance and righteousness. It reminds believers of the balance between fear of Allah's wrath and hope in His mercy, motivating them to adhere to His commands and seek His forgiveness.
orig: اعلموا أن الله شديد العقاب وأن الله غفور رحيم

translation: There is no responsibility on the Messenger except to convey (the message), and Allah knows what you reveal and what you conceal.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of the Prophet Muhammad as a messenger whose duty is solely to deliver the message of Islam. It highlights that the Prophet is not responsible for forcing people to accept the message or for the outcomes of their choices. Additionally, it underscores the omniscience of Allah, indicating that He is fully aware of the intentions and actions of individuals, whether they are expressed openly or kept hidden. This serves as a reminder to believers of Allah's all-encompassing knowledge and the importance of sincerity in faith and actions.
orig: ما على الرسول إلا البلاغ والله يعلم ما تبدون وما تكتمون

translation: Say, 'The bad and the good are not equal, even if the abundance of the bad may please you.' So fear Allah, O you of understanding, that you may be successful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the moral distinction between good and evil, urging believers to recognize that the quantity or prevalence of something bad does not make it equal to what is good. It calls upon those with understanding to fear Allah and adhere to righteousness, as this is the path to true success and prosperity in both this life and the hereafter.
orig: قل لا يستوي الخبيث والطيب ولو أعجبك كثرة الخبيث فاتقوا الله يا أولي الألباب لعلكم تفلحون

translation: O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they are shown to you, will distress you. And if you ask about them while the Qur'an is being revealed, they will be shown to you. Allah has pardoned that, and Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing.
interpretation: This verse advises believers not to inquire about matters that could potentially cause them distress or discomfort if revealed. It suggests a trust in divine wisdom, indicating that some knowledge is better left undisclosed for the peace of mind of the believers. The verse also highlights Allah's attributes of forgiveness and patience, emphasizing that even if such inquiries are made, Allah is willing to overlook them out of His mercy.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تسألوا عن أشياء إن تبد لكم تسؤكم وإن تسألوا عنها حين ينزل القرآن تبد لكم عفا الله عنها والله غفور حليم

translation: People before you have asked about it, then they became disbelievers because of it.
interpretation: This verse suggests that previous communities inquired about the timing of the Day of Judgment or similar divine matters out of skepticism or impatience. Their disbelief intensified when their expectations were not met according to their desires, illustrating a warning against questioning divine wisdom with doubt.
orig: قد سألها قوم من قبلكم ثم أصبحوا بها كافرين

translation: Allah has not instituted things like Bahirah (a she-camel whose milk was spared for the idols and nobody was allowed to milk it), or Sa'ibah (a she-camel let loose for free pasture for their false gods, e.g. idols, etc., and nothing was allowed to be carried on it), or Wasilah (a she-camel set free for idols because it has given birth to a she-camel at its first delivery and then again gives birth to a she-camel at its second delivery), or Ham (a stallion-camel freed from work for their idols, after it had finished a number of copulations assigned for it, all these animals were liberated in honor of idols as practiced by pagan Arabs in the pre-Islamic period). But those who disbelieve invent lies against Allah, and most of them lack understanding.
interpretation: This verse criticizes the pre-Islamic pagan practices of dedicating certain animals to idols, which were considered sacred and were not to be used for normal purposes. The Qur'an rejects these customs as fabrications and falsehoods attributed to Allah by those who disbelieve. It emphasizes that such practices have no basis in divine law and are a result of human invention due to a lack of understanding and faith.
orig: ما جعل الله من بحيرة ولا سائبة ولا وصيلة ولا حام ولكن الذين كفروا يفترون على الله الكذب وأكثرهم لا يعقلون

translation: And when it is said to them, 'Come to what Allah has revealed and to the Messenger,' they say, 'Sufficient for us is that which we found our fathers following.' Even though their fathers knew nothing and were not guided?
interpretation: This verse highlights the resistance of some people to accept the divine message brought by the Prophet Muhammad. It points out their blind adherence to ancestral customs and traditions, even when those practices are devoid of knowledge and true guidance. The verse critiques the irrationality of following predecessors without critically evaluating the truth and wisdom of their ways, emphasizing the importance of seeking and adhering to the revelation from Allah and the guidance of His Messenger.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم تعالوا إلى ما أنزل الله وإلى الرسول قالوا حسبنا ما وجدنا عليه آباءنا أولو كان آباؤهم لا يعلمون شيئا ولا يهتدون

translation: O you who have believed, upon you is [responsibility for] yourselves. Those who have gone astray will not harm you when you have been guided. To Allah is your return, all together; then He will inform you of what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes personal responsibility in faith. It instructs believers to focus on their own spiritual journey and righteousness, assuring them that the misguidance of others will not affect their own standing with Allah as long as they remain on the right path. The verse also reminds believers of the ultimate accountability before Allah, where everyone will return and be judged based on their actions. This encourages a focus on individual moral conduct and reliance on divine guidance.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا عليكم أنفسكم لا يضركم من ضل إذا اهتديتم إلى الله مرجعكم جميعا فينبئكم بما كنتم تعملون

translation: O you who have believed, testimony among you when death approaches one of you at the time of bequest is that of two just men from among you or two others from outside if you are traveling through the land and the disaster of death befalls you. Detain them after the prayer and let them both swear by Allah if you doubt: 'We will not exchange it for a price, even if he should be a near relative, and we will not conceal the testimony of Allah. Indeed, we would then be of the sinful.'
interpretation: This verse establishes the importance of having witnesses during the time of making a will, particularly when death is near. It specifies that two just witnesses should be present, ideally from within the community, but if not possible, from outside. The requirement to detain the witnesses after prayer and have them swear an oath underscores the gravity and sanctity of their testimony. The oath they take emphasizes honesty and integrity, warning against any form of corruption or concealment of the truth, even for personal gain or familial loyalty. This reflects the Islamic principle of upholding justice and truthfulness, even in the face of death, and serves as a reminder of the accountability one has before Allah.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا شهادة بينكم إذا حضر أحدكم الموت حين الوصية اثنان ذوا عدل منكم أو آخران من غيركم إن أنتم ضربتم في الأرض فأصابتكم مصيبة الموت تحبسونهما من بعد الصلاة فيقسمان بالله إن ارتبتم لا نشتري به ثمنا ولو كان ذا قربى ولا نكتم شهادة الله إنا إذا لمن الآثمين

translation: Then if it is found that they have committed a sin, two others shall take their place from among those against whom the first two have committed the offense, and they shall swear by Allah, 'Our testimony is truer than their testimony, and we have not transgressed. Indeed, we would then be among the wrongdoers.'
interpretation: This verse outlines a procedure for replacing witnesses who are found to have committed a sin or offense in the context of giving testimony. It emphasizes the importance of integrity and truthfulness in legal proceedings. If the initial witnesses are found to be untruthful, they must be replaced by two others who have been wronged by the first witnesses. These new witnesses must then swear an oath by Allah, affirming that their testimony is more accurate and that they have not overstepped their bounds, acknowledging that doing so would place them among the wrongdoers. This mechanism serves to safeguard justice by ensuring that only truthful testimonies are considered, thereby maintaining the moral and ethical standards expected in Islamic jurisprudence.
orig: فإن عثر على أنهما استحقا إثما فآخران يقومان مقامهما من الذين استحق عليهم الأوليان فيقسمان بالله لشهادتنا أحق من شهادتهما وما اعتدينا إنا إذا لمن الظالمين

translation: That is more likely that they will give testimony according to its true nature, or else they will fear that oaths will be rebutted after their oaths. And fear Allah and listen; and Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of honesty and fear of God in the context of giving testimony. It suggests that by adhering to a strict protocol for witnesses, people are more likely to testify truthfully, knowing that false oaths could be challenged. The verse also serves as a reminder to maintain piety and attentiveness to God's guidance, warning that those who deliberately disobey will not receive divine guidance.
orig: ذلك أدنى أن يأتوا بالشهادة على وجهها أو يخافوا أن ترد أيمان بعد أيمانهم واتقوا الله واسمعوا والله لا يهدي القوم الفاسقين

translation: The Day when Allah will gather the messengers and say, 'What was the response to you?' They will say, 'We have no knowledge. Indeed, it is You who is the Knower of the unseen.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the ultimate accountability of the messengers to Allah. On the Day of Judgment, Allah will gather all the messengers and inquire about the responses they received from their peoples. The messengers' reply, 'We have no knowledge,' reflects their humility and acknowledgment that only Allah possesses complete knowledge of the unseen and the true nature of people's hearts and deeds. This emphasizes the omniscience of Allah and the limited perspective of even the most righteous humans, reinforcing the concept that all judgment and knowledge of the unseen belong solely to Allah.
orig: يوم يجمع الله الرسل فيقول ماذا أجبتم قالوا لا علم لنا إنك أنت علام الغيوب

translation: When Allah said, 'O Jesus, son of Mary, remember My favor upon you and upon your mother when I supported you with the Holy Spirit and you spoke to the people in the cradle and in maturity; and when I taught you the Scripture and wisdom, the Torah and the Gospel; and when you made from clay the likeness of a bird by My permission, then you breathed into it, and it became a bird by My permission; and you healed the blind and the leper by My permission; and when you brought forth the dead by My permission; and when I restrained the Children of Israel from [killing] you when you came to them with clear proofs and those who disbelieved among them said, 'This is not but obvious magic.''
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine support and miraculous abilities bestowed upon Jesus by Allah, emphasizing that these miracles were performed by the permission of Allah alone. It serves to affirm Jesus's prophethood and his role as a messenger, while also clarifying that the disbelief of some among the Children of Israel stemmed from their misinterpretation of these miracles as mere magic, rather than recognizing them as signs from Allah.
orig: إذ قال الله يا عيسى ابن مريم اذكر نعمتي عليك وعلى والدتك إذ أيدتك بروح القدس تكلم الناس في المهد وكهلا وإذ علمتك الكتاب والحكمة والتوراة والإنجيل وإذ تخلق من الطين كهيئة الطير بإذني فتنفخ فيها فتكون طيرا بإذني وتبرئ الأكمه والأبرص بإذني وإذ تخرج الموتى بإذني وإذ كففت بني إسرائيل عنك إذ جئتهم بالبينات فقال الذين كفروا منهم إن هذا إلا سحر مبين

translation: And [mention] when I inspired the disciples to believe in Me and in My messenger, they said, 'We have believed, and bear witness that we are Muslims.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the moment when Jesus (peace be upon him) inspired his disciples, known as the Hawariyyun, to affirm their faith in God and in Jesus as His messenger. Their response, 'We have believed, and bear witness that we are Muslims,' signifies their submission to the will of God, indicating that true faith involves both belief in the divine message and the messenger. This underscores the concept of Islam as submission to God, which is a universal message applicable to all prophets and their followers.
orig: وإذ أوحيت إلى الحواريين أن آمنوا بي وبرسولي قالوا آمنا واشهد بأننا مسلمون

translation: When the disciples said, 'O Jesus, son of Mary, can your Lord send down to us a table from heaven?' He said, 'Fear Allah, if you are believers.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of faith and the appropriate manner of requesting signs from God. The disciples, seeking reassurance, ask Jesus if God can provide a miraculous sign in the form of a heavenly table. Jesus's response, 'Fear Allah, if you are believers,' serves as a reminder that true faith does not necessitate constant signs or miracles. Instead, believers should trust in God's wisdom and power without demanding proofs, reflecting a deeper level of faith and submission to divine will.
orig: إذ قال الحواريون يا عيسى ابن مريم هل يستطيع ربك أن ينزل علينا مائدة من السماء قال اتقوا الله إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: They said, 'We wish to eat from it and to reassure our hearts and to know that you have told us the truth and to be among its witnesses.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the human need for tangible proof and reassurance in matters of faith. The request to eat from the food sent from heaven by the Israelites to Moses illustrates their desire for a direct, sensory experience to confirm the truth of the divine message and strengthen their belief. It underscores the importance of faith being supported by evidence that can be witnessed and experienced, thereby fostering a deeper conviction and communal affirmation of the divine promise.
orig: قالوا نريد أن نأكل منها وتطمئن قلوبنا ونعلم أن قد صدقتنا ونكون عليها من الشاهدين

translation: Jesus, son of Mary, said, 'O Allah, our Lord, send down to us a table from heaven to be a festival for us, for the first of us and the last of us, and a sign from You. And provide for us; You are the best of providers.'
interpretation: This verse highlights Jesus's supplication to Allah for a miraculous sign in the form of a heavenly feast, which would serve as a celebration and a testament to Allah's power and provision for all generations of believers. It underscores the theme of divine sustenance and the recognition of Allah as the ultimate provider.
orig: قال عيسى ابن مريم اللهم ربنا أنزل علينا مائدة من السماء تكون لنا عيدا لأولنا وآخرنا وآية منك وارزقنا وأنت خير الرازقين

translation: Allah said, 'Indeed, I will send it down to you, but whoever disbelieves afterwards from among you - then indeed I will punish him with a punishment by which I have not punished anyone among the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the seriousness of disbelief after receiving clear signs and guidance from Allah. It serves as a warning that rejecting faith after it has been clearly presented incurs a severe punishment, unique in its intensity, underscoring the gravity of such a choice and the divine justice that follows.
orig: قال الله إني منزلها عليكم فمن يكفر بعد منكم فإني أعذبه عذابا لا أعذبه أحدا من العالمين

translation: And [beware the Day] when Allah will say, 'O Jesus, Son of Mary, did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as deities besides Allah?'' He will say, 'Exalted are You! It was not for me to say that to which I have no right. If I had said it, You would have known it. You know what is within myself, and I do not know what is within Yourself. Indeed, it is You who is Knower of the unseen.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the theme of monotheism and the rejection of any form of association with Allah. It portrays a scene from the Day of Judgment where Allah directly questions Jesus about whether he instructed people to worship him and his mother as deities alongside Allah. Jesus's response emphasizes his absolute submission to Allah, denying any such claim and affirming Allah's omniscience. The verse serves as a clear refutation of the Christian doctrine of the Trinity, asserting that Jesus never claimed divinity for himself or his mother, and it highlights the Islamic principle that only Allah possesses complete knowledge of the unseen.
orig: وإذ قال الله يا عيسى ابن مريم أأنت قلت للناس اتخذوني وأمي إلهين من دون الله قال سبحانك ما يكون لي أن أقول ما ليس لي بحق إن كنت قلته فقد علمته تعلم ما في نفسي ولا أعلم ما في نفسك إنك أنت علام الغيوب

translation: I said to them nothing except what You commanded me - to worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord. And I was a witness over them while I was among them; but when You took me up, You were the Observer over them, and You are, over all things, Witness.
interpretation: This verse is a declaration by Jesus (Isa) in the Qur'an, affirming his role as a messenger of God. He states that he only conveyed the message he was commanded to deliver, which was to worship Allah, the Lord of all. This highlights the unity of the message across all prophets - the worship of one God. Jesus also acknowledges his temporary presence among his people as a witness to their actions, but emphasizes God's eternal and omnipresent watchfulness over humanity after his departure. This underscores the concept of Tawheed (the oneness of God) and divine omniscience, affirming that God is the ultimate witness to all deeds, reinforcing accountability and the continuity of divine oversight beyond the life of any prophet.
orig: ما قلت لهم إلا ما أمرتني به أن اعبدوا الله ربي وربكم وكنت عليهم شهيدا ما دمت فيهم فلما توفيتني كنت أنت الرقيب عليهم وأنت على كل شيء شهيد

translation: If You punish them, they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, You are the Almighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and wisdom of Allah. It acknowledges that whether Allah chooses to punish or forgive, both actions are within His divine right and reflect His attributes of omnipotence and supreme wisdom. The verse underscores the servitude of humans to Allah, indicating that their fate lies entirely in His hands, and it encourages a reliance on His mercy and forgiveness, while recognizing His capacity for justice.
orig: إن تعذبهم فإنهم عبادك وإن تغفر لهم فإنك أنت العزيز الحكيم

translation: Allah said, 'This is the Day when the truthful will benefit from their truthfulness.' For them are gardens [in Paradise] beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever, Allah being pleased with them and they with Him. That is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate reward for those who remain steadfast in truthfulness throughout their lives. On the Day of Judgment, their sincerity and honesty will be their greatest asset, granting them entry into Paradise. The gardens described symbolize the eternal bliss and tranquility that await the truthful, where they will enjoy everlasting life in the presence of Allah. The mutual pleasure between Allah and the believers signifies a profound spiritual connection and fulfillment, representing the highest level of success and achievement in the hereafter.
orig: قال الله هذا يوم ينفع الصادقين صدقهم لهم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها أبدا رضي الله عنهم ورضوا عنه ذلك الفوز العظيم

translation: To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them, and He is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and omnipotence of Allah. It asserts that everything in the universe, from the vastness of the heavens to the expanse of the earth, is under His control and ownership. The phrase 'and He is over all things competent' underscores Allah's unlimited power and ability to manage and govern all affairs, reinforcing the belief in His all-encompassing capability and authority.
orig: لله ملك السماوات والأرض وما فيهن وهو على كل شيء قدير

translation: Praise be to Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and made the darknesses and the light, then those who disbelieve in their Lord equate [others] with Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the greatness of Allah as the Creator of the universe, highlighting His power and sovereignty. It also critiques the disbelief of those who, despite the clear signs of Allah's creation, choose to associate partners with Him, equating others to His divine status. This act of equating or associating partners with Allah is a fundamental error in faith, as it undermines the unique oneness and supremacy of Allah.
orig: الحمد لله الذي خلق السماوات والأرض وجعل الظلمات والنور ثم الذين كفروا بربهم يعدلون

translation: He is the One who created you from clay, then decreed a term, and a specified term is with Him; yet you still doubt.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and authority of Allah as the Creator, who fashioned humanity from humble beginnings (clay) and has set a predetermined time for each individual's life and death. The mention of a 'specified term' underscores the divine knowledge and control over life's duration, which is known only to Allah. Despite this clear demonstration of divine power and planning, the verse points out human beings' tendency to doubt or question these truths, highlighting a common human flaw of uncertainty or disbelief in the face of clear signs of Allah's omnipotence and omniscience.
orig: هو الذي خلقكم من طين ثم قضى أجلا وأجل مسمى عنده ثم أنتم تمترون

translation: And He is Allah, [the only deity] in the heavens and the earth. He knows your secret and what you make public, and He knows what you earn.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipresence and omniscience of Allah. It asserts that Allah is the sole deity worshipped in both the heavens and the earth, highlighting His universal sovereignty. The mention of knowing secrets and public actions underscores that nothing is hidden from Allah; He is aware of all deeds, thoughts, and intentions. The phrase 'what you earn' refers to the consequences of one's actions, indicating that Allah is fully aware of the moral and spiritual outcomes of everything individuals do, and will judge them accordingly.
orig: وهو الله في السماوات وفي الأرض يعلم سركم وجهركم ويعلم ما تكسبون

translation: And no sign comes to them from among the signs of their Lord except that they turn away from it.
interpretation: This verse highlights the persistent rejection of divine signs by those who are averse to faith. It suggests that no matter how clear or compelling the evidence of God's existence and power is presented to them, they choose to ignore or dismiss it. This reflects a deep-seated resistance to accepting the truth, stemming from their own biases and desires.
orig: وما تأتيهم من آية من آيات ربهم إلا كانوا عنها معرضين

translation: They have indeed rejected the truth when it came to them, so soon will come to them the news of what they used to mock.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequence of rejecting divine truth. When individuals deny the truth revealed to them, they will eventually face the reality of the very things they mocked. It serves as a warning that disbelief and mockery of divine messages will lead to an inevitable confrontation with the truth, manifesting in a way that they can no longer deny or ridicule.
orig: فقد كذبوا بالحق لما جاءهم فسوف يأتيهم أنباء ما كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them? We had established them in the land in ways that We have not established for you, and We sent the sky upon them in abundant rain, and We made rivers flow beneath them; then We destroyed them for their sins and raised up after them other generations.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder and a warning to the current generation about the transient nature of worldly power and the consequences of sin. It highlights that previous nations were given even greater worldly prosperity and resources, yet they were ultimately destroyed due to their transgressions against God's commandments. The mention of abundant rain and flowing rivers symbolizes the blessings and opportunities these nations received, which they failed to appreciate and use righteously. The verse underscores the cycle of civilizations: those who misuse their blessings and commit sins will be replaced by others, illustrating the divine justice and the continuous renewal of human societies according to God's will.
orig: ألم يروا كم أهلكنا من قبلهم من قرن مكناهم في الأرض ما لم نمكن لكم وأرسلنا السماء عليهم مدرارا وجعلنا الأنهار تجري من تحتهم فأهلكناهم بذنوبهم وأنشأنا من بعدهم قرنا آخرين

translation: And if We had sent down to you a book on paper and they touched it with their hands, the disbelievers would have said, 'This is nothing but obvious magic.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the inherent skepticism and denial of the disbelievers. It suggests that even if God had provided a tangible, physical proof of the Qur'an, such as a written book on paper that they could touch, the disbelievers would still reject it, labeling it as mere magic. This underscores the idea that their disbelief stems not from a lack of evidence, but from a deeper resistance to accepting the truth.
orig: ولو نزلنا عليك كتابا في قرطاس فلمسوه بأيديهم لقال الذين كفروا إن هذا إلا سحر مبين

translation: And they said, 'Why has an angel not been sent down to him?' And if We had sent down an angel, the matter would have been settled, then they would not be given respite.
interpretation: This verse addresses the skepticism of those who demanded that an angel be sent to Prophet Muhammad as a sign of his prophethood. It highlights the human tendency to seek miraculous proofs, yet even if such a sign were given, like an angel descending, it would conclusively end the test of faith. The verse suggests that the purpose of life is to test faith and patience through belief without seeing, and if an angel were sent, it would remove the opportunity for people to exercise their free will in choosing faith, thus ending the trial prematurely.
orig: وقالوا لولا أنزل عليه ملك ولو أنزلنا ملكا لقضي الأمر ثم لا ينظرون

translation: And if We had made him an angel, We would have made him [appear as] a man, and We would have covered them in confusion as they are already confused.
interpretation: This verse suggests that if God had sent an angel as a messenger instead of a human, the angel would have been made to appear in human form. This would have further confused the disbelievers, who were already struggling to accept the human messenger. The verse underscores the wisdom in God's choice to send human messengers, as it aligns with the human experience and capacity for understanding, despite the disbelievers' rejection and confusion.
orig: ولو جعلناه ملكا لجعلناه رجلا وللبسنا عليهم ما يلبسون

translation: And indeed, [many] messengers were mocked before you, but those who mocked them were enveloped by what they used to ridicule.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the historical pattern of disbelief and mockery faced by prophets and messengers sent by Allah. It serves as a reminder and a warning to those who ridicule the truth and the messengers of Allah. The consequence of such mockery is that the very thing they mock will ultimately encompass them, illustrating the inevitability of divine justice and the futility of denying the truth. It encourages believers to remain steadfast in their faith despite opposition, knowing that the outcome for the mockers is predetermined by Allah's decree.
orig: ولقد استهزئ برسل من قبلك فحاق بالذين سخروا منهم ما كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: Say, "Travel through the land and observe how was the end of those who denied."
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to reflect on historical examples of civilizations that rejected the messages of their prophets. By traveling and observing, one can see the consequences faced by those who denied the truth, serving as a reminder and warning to heed the divine message and not follow in their footsteps.
orig: قل سيروا في الأرض ثم انظروا كيف كان عاقبة المكذبين

translation: Say, "To whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and earth?" Say, "To Allah." He has decreed upon Himself mercy. He will surely assemble you for the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt. Those who lost themselves [in sin] will not believe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty of Allah over all creation, both in the heavens and on earth. It underscores that everything belongs to Him, and He has chosen to bind Himself with mercy, which is a fundamental attribute of His nature. The promise of gathering all people on the Day of Resurrection is affirmed, highlighting the certainty of this event. The verse also points out a spiritual reality: those who have lost their own souls through disbelief and sin are unable to have faith, indicating a deep connection between one's actions and their capacity for belief.
orig: قل لمن ما في السماوات والأرض قل لله كتب على نفسه الرحمة ليجمعنكم إلى يوم القيامة لا ريب فيه الذين خسروا أنفسهم فهم لا يؤمنون

translation: And to Him belongs whatever dwells in the night and the day, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's sovereignty and omnipresence, indicating that everything that exists or occurs during the night and day is under His dominion. It also highlights His attributes of being All-Hearing and All-Knowing, which means He is fully aware of and attentive to all that happens in His creation, reinforcing the concept of His complete knowledge and surveillance over all affairs.
orig: وله ما سكن في الليل والنهار وهو السميع العليم

translation: Say, "Shall I take a protector other than Allah, the Creator of the heavens and the earth, who provides for you and is not fed?" Say, "I have been commanded to be the first of those who submit [to Allah] and [I have been commanded], 'Do not be of the polytheists.'"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the exclusive worship of Allah, highlighting His role as the sole Creator and Sustainer of the universe. It challenges the notion of associating partners with Allah by questioning the logic of taking anyone else as a protector when Allah is the one who provides for all without needing sustenance Himself. The command to be the first to submit to Allah and to avoid polytheism underscores the importance of monotheism and the personal responsibility of the Prophet Muhammad to lead by example in submitting to Allah's will.
orig: قل أغير الله أتخذ وليا فاطر السماوات والأرض وهو يطعم ولا يطعم قل إني أمرت أن أكون أول من أسلم ولا تكونن من المشركين

translation: Say, 'Indeed, I fear, if I should disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous Day.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to Allah, highlighting the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) awareness and fear of the severe consequences of disobedience. It serves as a reminder to all believers of the accountability on the Day of Judgment, urging them to adhere to divine commandments to avoid the punishment of that great Day.
orig: قل إني أخاف إن عصيت ربي عذاب يوم عظيم

translation: Whoever is spared from it that Day, He has had mercy on him. And that is the clear triumph.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate mercy of Allah on the Day of Judgment. Being spared from the punishment of Hellfire is described as a clear and evident success, highlighting the immense relief and joy of receiving Allah's mercy. It underscores the notion that the true victory for a believer is not worldly achievements but salvation in the hereafter.
orig: من يصرف عنه يومئذ فقد رحمه وذلك الفوز المبين

translation: And if Allah touches you with harm, none can remove it but He; and if He touches you with good, then He is Able to do all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and sovereignty of Allah over all aspects of life. It teaches that any adversity or hardship that befalls a person comes from Allah, and only He has the power to relieve it. Conversely, any good or blessing that one receives is also from Allah, demonstrating His complete control and ability over everything. This understanding encourages believers to turn to Allah in all circumstances, relying on Him alone for relief and gratitude.
orig: وإن يمسسك الله بضر فلا كاشف له إلا هو وإن يمسسك بخير فهو على كل شيء قدير

translation: And He is the Subduer, above His servants, and He is the All-Wise, the All-Aware.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and authority of Allah over all creation. The term 'Al-Qahhar' (the Subduer) signifies His irresistible power and control, indicating that nothing can oppose His will. The phrase 'above His servants' underscores His transcendence and sovereignty. Additionally, the attributes 'Al-Hakim' (the All-Wise) and 'Al-Khabir' (the All-Aware) highlight His perfect wisdom and comprehensive knowledge, suggesting that His dominion is exercised with complete understanding and purpose. This verse serves as a reminder of Allah's omnipotence and omniscience, encouraging believers to submit to His will and trust in His divine plan.
orig: وهو القاهر فوق عباده وهو الحكيم الخبير

translation: Say, "What thing is greatest in testimony?" Say, "Allah is witness between me and you, and this Quran has been revealed to me that I may warn you thereby and whomever it reaches. Do you truly testify that there are other deities besides Allah?" Say, "I will not testify." Say, "Indeed, He is but one God, and indeed, I am innocent of what you associate [with Him]."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness of Allah and the role of the Prophet Muhammad as a warner through the Quran. It challenges the polytheistic beliefs of the Quraysh by asking them to consider the greatest testimony, which is that of Allah Himself. The Prophet is instructed to firmly reject any notion of multiple deities, affirming that Allah is the sole deity and declaring his disassociation from idolatry. This verse serves as a clear declaration of monotheism and a rejection of polytheism, reinforcing the central message of Islam.
orig: قل أي شيء أكبر شهادة قل الله شهيد بيني وبينكم وأوحي إلي هذا القرآن لأنذركم به ومن بلغ أئنكم لتشهدون أن مع الله آلهة أخرى قل لا أشهد قل إنما هو إله واحد وإنني بريء مما تشركون

translation: Those to whom We have given the Book recognize it as they recognize their own sons. Those who have lost their own souls, they will not believe.
interpretation: This verse highlights the recognition of truth by those who have been given divine scripture, akin to the intimate knowledge one has of their own children. It suggests that the truth of the Qur'an is evident and undeniable to those familiar with earlier scriptures. However, it also points out that some individuals, referred to as those who have lost their own souls, are so entrenched in disbelief or denial that they refuse to accept this truth despite its clarity.
orig: الذين آتيناهم الكتاب يعرفونه كما يعرفون أبناءهم الذين خسروا أنفسهم فهم لا يؤمنون

translation: And who is more unjust than he who invents a lie against Allah or denies His verses? Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity of attributing falsehood to Allah or rejecting His revelations. It highlights that such actions are the epitome of injustice. The statement that wrongdoers will not succeed serves as a warning and a reminder of the consequences of such grave sins, reinforcing the belief in divine justice and the ultimate failure of those who engage in these acts.
orig: ومن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا أو كذب بآياته إنه لا يفلح الظالمون

translation: And the Day We will gather them all together; then We will say to those who associated others with Allah, 'Where are your partners that you used to claim?'
interpretation: This verse underscores the accountability and the ultimate realization of truth on the Day of Judgment. It highlights how those who ascribed partners to Allah will be confronted with the absence of these false deities, emphasizing the futility and falsehood of their beliefs. It serves as a reminder of the oneness of Allah and the consequences of associating others with Him.
orig: ويوم نحشرهم جميعا ثم نقول للذين أشركوا أين شركاؤكم الذين كنتم تزعمون

translation: Then their only plea, when Our punishment overtook them, was to say, 'By Allah, we were not polytheists.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the moment of realization and regret that comes too late for those who denied the truth. It underscores the human tendency to acknowledge the oneness of God and disavow polytheism only when faced with divine retribution, illustrating the futility of such last-minute declarations when one's life has been spent in denial and disobedience.
orig: ثم لم تكن فتنتهم إلا أن قالوا والله ربنا ما كنا مشركين

translation: See how they lied against themselves and how that which they used to invent has deserted them.
interpretation: This verse highlights the self-deception of those who deny the truth. It points out that their fabrications and false beliefs, which they clung to in life, ultimately abandon them, leaving them to face the reality of their actions and beliefs. It serves as a reminder of the consequences of straying from the truth and the importance of sincerity and honesty in one's faith.
orig: انظر كيف كذبوا على أنفسهم وضل عنهم ما كانوا يفترون

translation: And among them are those who listen to you, but We have placed veils over their hearts, lest they understand it, and in their ears is deafness. And if they see every sign, they will not believe in it, until when they come to you to argue with you, those who disbelieve say, 'This is nothing but tales of the ancients.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual and psychological barriers that prevent some people from accepting the message of Islam. It suggests that despite being exposed to the teachings and signs of the Prophet Muhammad, some individuals have been divinely allowed to remain in a state of disbelief due to their own choices and inclinations. The 'veils over their hearts' and 'deafness in their ears' symbolize an internal resistance to truth, indicating that their rejection is not merely intellectual but deeply rooted in their hearts. The mention of them calling the Qur'an 'tales of the ancients' reflects a common dismissal of divine revelation as mere folklore or myth, showcasing their unwillingness to engage with the message on a sincere level.
orig: ومنهم من يستمع إليك وجعلنا على قلوبهم أكنة أن يفقهوه وفي آذانهم وقرا وإن يروا كل آية لا يؤمنوا بها حتى إذا جاءوك يجادلونك يقول الذين كفروا إن هذا إلا أساطير الأولين

translation: And they forbid [others] from it and they turn away from it, and they destroy not but themselves, but they perceive [it] not.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy and self-destructive behavior of those who reject the message of the Qur'an. They not only turn away from the truth themselves but also actively prevent others from accessing it. Their actions lead to their own spiritual ruin, yet they remain unaware of the harm they are causing to themselves. This underscores the theme of accountability and the consequences of denying divine guidance.
orig: وهم ينهون عنه وينأون عنه وإن يهلكون إلا أنفسهم وما يشعرون

translation: And if you could see when they are stationed before the Fire and say, 'Oh, would that we were sent back and did not deny the signs of our Lord and were among the believers!'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the regret and remorse of the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment when they are confronted with the reality of Hellfire. It highlights their wish to be given another chance to return to the world, where they would not reject the signs of Allah and would instead embrace faith. The verse serves as a warning to the living about the consequences of disbelief and the importance of accepting and following the revelations of Allah while there is still time.
orig: ولو ترى إذ وقفوا على النار فقالوا يا ليتنا نرد ولا نكذب بآيات ربنا ونكون من المؤمنين

translation: Rather, what they used to conceal before has [now] appeared to them. And even if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden; and indeed, they are liars.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the hidden disbelief and sins of the hypocrites are now exposed to them in the Hereafter. It emphasizes that even if they were given another chance to live, they would revert to their forbidden actions, indicating the deep-rooted nature of their hypocrisy and deceit. The verse underscores the inevitability of their punishment due to their persistent lying and refusal to change.
orig: بل بدا لهم ما كانوا يخفون من قبل ولو ردوا لعادوا لما نهوا عنه وإنهم لكاذبون

translation: And they say, "There is nothing but our worldly life, and we will not be resurrected."
interpretation: This verse reflects the disbelief and denial of the afterlife by some people. They assert that life is limited to the material world and reject the concept of resurrection, which is a fundamental belief in Islam about the continuation of life after death and the accountability for one's actions.
orig: وقالوا إن هي إلا حياتنا الدنيا وما نحن بمبعوثين

translation: And if you could see when they are made to stand before their Lord, He will say, 'Is this not the truth?' They will say, 'Yes, by our Lord.' He will say, 'So taste the punishment for what you used to deny.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the moment of accountability before God, emphasizing the undeniable truth of His existence and the consequences of disbelief. It serves as a reminder of the certainty of the Day of Judgment, where individuals will confront the reality they denied in life, and subsequently face the appropriate recompense for their rejection of faith.
orig: ولو ترى إذ وقفوا على ربهم قال أليس هذا بالحق قالوا بلى وربنا قال فذوقوا العذاب بما كنتم تكفرون

translation: Those who deny the meeting with Allah have indeed lost, until when the Hour comes upon them suddenly, they will say, 'Oh, our regret over what we neglected in it,' while they bear their burdens on their backs. Indeed, evil is what they bear.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of disbelief and the denial of the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes that those who reject the concept of meeting Allah will ultimately face a sudden and regretful realization when the Hour arrives. The imagery of bearing burdens on their backs symbolizes the weight of their sins and the remorse they will feel for neglecting their spiritual duties. The verse serves as a warning about the severe outcome of disbelief and the importance of preparing for the afterlife.
orig: قد خسر الذين كذبوا بلقاء الله حتى إذا جاءتهم الساعة بغتة قالوا يا حسرتنا على ما فرطنا فيها وهم يحملون أوزارهم على ظهورهم ألا ساء ما يزرون

translation: And what is the life of this world except an amusement and diversion? And indeed, the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah. Then will you not use reason?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the transient and superficial nature of worldly life, likening it to mere play and amusement. It contrasts this with the eternal and superior nature of the Hereafter, which is promised to be better for those who are conscious of God and live righteously. The rhetorical question at the end challenges the reader to reflect deeply on these truths and to prioritize spiritual and moral values over temporary worldly gains.
orig: وما الحياة الدنيا إلا لعب ولهو وللدار الآخرة خير للذين يتقون أفلا تعقلون

translation: We know indeed that what they say grieves you; it is not you they deny, but it is the signs of Allah that the wrongdoers reject.
interpretation: This verse reassures the Prophet Muhammad that the rejection and hurtful words from the disbelievers are not a personal attack against him, but rather a rejection of the divine messages from Allah. It highlights that the wrongdoers are actually denying the truth of Allah's signs, not the Prophet himself. This serves to comfort the Prophet and emphasize the spiritual battle between truth and falsehood, where the disbelievers' denial is rooted in their rejection of divine guidance.
orig: قد نعلم إنه ليحزنك الذي يقولون فإنهم لا يكذبونك ولكن الظالمين بآيات الله يجحدون

translation: And indeed, messengers before you were denied, but they were patient in the face of denial and harm until Our help came to them. And there is no changer of the words of Allah. And there has certainly come to you news of the messengers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a source of comfort and encouragement for the Prophet Muhammad and by extension, all believers facing adversity. It reassures them that previous prophets also faced rejection and persecution but remained steadfast in their faith and mission. The promise of divine support and the unchangeable nature of God's decrees highlight the importance of patience and trust in Allah's timing and plan. The reference to the news of the messengers reminds believers of the historical continuity of their struggle and the ultimate triumph of truth, reinforcing their resolve and hope.
orig: ولقد كذبت رسل من قبلك فصبروا على ما كذبوا وأوذوا حتى أتاهم نصرنا ولا مبدل لكلمات الله ولقد جاءك من نبإ المرسلين

translation: And if their aversion is difficult for you, then if you can seek a tunnel in the earth or a ladder into the sky to bring them a sign, [do so]. But if Allah had willed, He could have gathered them upon guidance. So never be of the ignorant.
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad, reminding him that the disbelief and rejection of the message by some people should not cause him distress. It emphasizes that even if he were to go to great lengths to bring them a sign or miracle, their guidance ultimately depends on Allah's will. The verse encourages the Prophet not to be frustrated or to act ignorantly by trying to force guidance upon those who are unwilling to accept it, as true guidance comes from Allah alone.
orig: وإن كان كبر عليك إعراضهم فإن استطعت أن تبتغي نفقا في الأرض أو سلما في السماء فتأتيهم بآية ولو شاء الله لجمعهم على الهدى فلا تكونن من الجاهلين

translation: Only those who listen will respond, but the dead - Allah will raise them; then to Him they will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of spiritual responsiveness. Those who are spiritually 'alive' and attentive to the message of Allah will respond to His call. However, even those who are spiritually 'dead' or unresponsive in this life will be resurrected by Allah on the Day of Judgment, and ultimately, everyone will return to Him for accountability. This underscores the inevitability of facing Allah and the universal scope of His power and judgment.
orig: إنما يستجيب الذين يسمعون والموتى يبعثهم الله ثم إليه يرجعون

translation: And they say, "Why has a sign not been sent down to him from his Lord?" Say, "Indeed, Allah is able to send down a sign, but most of them do not know."
interpretation: This verse addresses the skepticism of those who demanded a miraculous sign from the Prophet Muhammad as proof of his prophethood. It highlights the divine capability of Allah to provide such signs, yet emphasizes that the majority of people are unaware or ignorant of this fact. The verse suggests that the demand for signs stems from a lack of faith and understanding, rather than a genuine need for proof, as faith should be based on the message and its coherence rather than solely on miracles.
orig: وقالوا لولا نزل عليه آية من ربه قل إن الله قادر على أن ينزل آية ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: And there is no creature on earth or bird that flies with its wings except that they are communities like you. We have not neglected anything in the record, and they will be gathered to their Lord.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity and equality of all creation before Allah. It suggests that every creature, whether on land or in the air, forms part of a community with its own societal structure, similar to human societies. The verse underscores the meticulousness of Allah's knowledge and record-keeping, indicating that nothing in creation is overlooked or forgotten. Ultimately, it points to the accountability of all beings, as they will be gathered before their Creator, highlighting the interconnectedness and purposefulness of all life under Allah's divine plan.
orig: وما من دابة في الأرض ولا طائر يطير بجناحيه إلا أمم أمثالكم ما فرطنا في الكتاب من شيء ثم إلى ربهم يحشرون

translation: And those who have denied Our signs are deaf and dumb in darknesses. Whomever Allah wills, He lets go astray, and whomever He wills, He places him on a straight path.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual condition of those who reject the signs of Allah, describing them as being in a state of sensory and intellectual deprivation, akin to being deaf and mute within layers of darkness. This metaphor suggests a profound disconnection from divine guidance. The latter part of the verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah over human guidance and misguidance. It implies that while human beings have free will, the ultimate direction of their path—whether towards misguidance or righteousness—is under Allah's control. This serves as a reminder of divine omnipotence and the importance of seeking Allah's guidance.
orig: والذين كذبوا بآياتنا صم وبكم في الظلمات من يشإ الله يضلله ومن يشأ يجعله على صراط مستقيم

translation: Say, "Have you considered: if the punishment of Allah should come to you or the Hour should come upon you, would you invoke other than Allah, if you should be truthful?"
interpretation: This verse challenges the polytheists to reflect on their beliefs by posing a hypothetical scenario where divine punishment or the Day of Judgment arrives. It questions whether, in such a critical moment, they would turn to their false deities or acknowledge the one true God, Allah. The verse underscores the inherent recognition of Allah's sovereignty and the futility of worshipping others beside Him, urging a return to monotheism and sincerity in faith.
orig: قل أرأيتكم إن أتاكم عذاب الله أو أتتكم الساعة أغير الله تدعون إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Nay, but Him you call upon, and He will remove that which you call upon Him for, if He wills, and you will forget that which you associate (with Him).
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the exclusive power and authority of Allah. It suggests that when people call upon Allah in times of need, He has the ability to relieve their distress if He so chooses. The verse also critiques the practice of associating partners with Allah (shirk), indicating that such beliefs are ultimately forgotten or proven futile when true reliance is placed on Allah alone. It underscores the importance of Tawheed (the oneness of Allah) and the futility of polytheism.
orig: بل إياه تدعون فيكشف ما تدعون إليه إن شاء وتنسون ما تشركون

translation: And We have certainly sent [messengers] to nations before you, [O Muhammad]; then We seized them with poverty and hardship that perhaps they might humble themselves.
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah sent messengers to previous nations as a mercy and guidance. When those nations rejected the messengers, Allah tested them with trials of poverty and hardship. The purpose of these trials was to bring the people to a state of humility and submission to Allah, encouraging them to turn back to Him in repentance and seek His mercy. It serves as a reminder that adversity can be a means of spiritual purification and a call to return to the path of righteousness.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا إلى أمم من قبلك فأخذناهم بالبأساء والضراء لعلهم يتضرعون

translation: So why, when Our punishment came to them, did they not humble themselves? But their hearts became hardened, and Satan made attractive to them what they were doing.
interpretation: This verse reflects on the human tendency to remain unrepentant and arrogant even when faced with divine punishment. It suggests that instead of turning to God in humility and seeking forgiveness, people's hearts can become hardened due to the influence of Satan, who makes their sinful actions appear appealing and justified. This highlights the importance of self-reflection and the need to resist evil influences, even in the face of adversity.
orig: فلولا إذ جاءهم بأسنا تضرعوا ولكن قست قلوبهم وزين لهم الشيطان ما كانوا يعملون

translation: So when they forgot that by which they had been reminded, We opened for them the doors of every [good] thing until, when they rejoiced in that which they were given, We seized them suddenly, and they were [then] in despair.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the cycle of divine favor and punishment. When a community forgets the lessons and reminders given to them by Allah, they are initially granted an abundance of worldly pleasures and resources. This prosperity leads them to become complacent and overly joyful in their material gains, causing them to further neglect their spiritual duties. As a result, Allah suddenly withdraws His blessings and punishes them, leaving them in a state of despair. The verse serves as a warning against the dangers of forgetting Allah's messages and becoming too attached to worldly life, emphasizing the importance of maintaining gratitude and obedience to Allah regardless of one's circumstances.
orig: فلما نسوا ما ذكروا به فتحنا عليهم أبواب كل شيء حتى إذا فرحوا بما أوتوا أخذناهم بغتة فإذا هم مبلسون

translation: And the fate of the people who wronged was cut off, and praise be to Allah, the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse signifies the ultimate end and destruction of those who commit injustice and wrongdoing. It emphasizes that despite the temporary power or success of the wrongdoers, their end is inevitable and decreed by Allah. The phrase 'and praise be to Allah, the Lord of the worlds' that follows, serves as a reminder to believers to always express gratitude to Allah, acknowledging His justice and sovereignty over all creation, regardless of the apparent triumph or downfall of any group.
orig: فقطع دابر القوم الذين ظلموا والحمد لله رب العالمين

translation: Say, "Have you considered: if Allah should take away your hearing and your sight and seal your hearts, which deity other than Allah could bring them [back] to you?" Look how We diversify the signs; yet they turn away.
interpretation: This verse challenges the disbelief of those who worship other deities besides Allah by posing a hypothetical scenario where Allah removes their faculties of hearing and sight and seals their hearts. It emphasizes Allah's omnipotence and the futility of turning to any other deity for help in such a situation.
