This is the she-camel of Allah [sent] to you as a sign. So leave her to eat within Allah's land and do not touch her with harm, lest there seize you a painful punishment.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the mission of the Prophet Salih, who was sent to the Thamud tribe to guide them back to the worship of the one true God, Allah. The she-camel mentioned is a miraculous sign from Allah, symbolizing a test of the tribe's obedience and faith. The command to allow the she-camel to graze freely and not harm it underscores the importance of respecting and following divine signs and commandments. The warning of a painful punishment serves as a reminder of the consequences of rejecting God's messengers and disobeying His directives.
orig: وإلى ثمود أخاهم صالحا قال يا قوم اعبدوا الله ما لكم من إله غيره قد جاءتكم بينة من ربكم هذه ناقة الله لكم آية فذروها تأكل في أرض الله ولا تمسوها بسوء فيأخذكم عذاب أليم

translation: And remember when He made you successors after 'Ad and settled you in the land, [and] you take from its plains palaces and carve out the mountains into homes. So remember the favors of Allah and do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder to the people of Thamud about the blessings bestowed upon them by Allah after the destruction of the 'Ad people. It highlights how Allah granted them authority and prosperity, enabling them to build sophisticated structures on the plains and within the mountains. The verse urges them to be grateful for these blessings and warns against using their power to spread corruption and cause mischief in the land. It emphasizes the importance of gratitude and the moral responsibility that comes with power and prosperity.
orig: واذكروا إذ جعلكم خلفاء من بعد عاد وبوأكم في الأرض تتخذون من سهولها قصورا وتنحتون الجبال بيوتا فاذكروا آلاء الله ولا تعثوا في الأرض مفسدين

translation: The leaders who were arrogant among his people said to those who were oppressed among them who believed, 'Do you know that Salih has been sent from his Lord?' They said, 'We believe in that with which he has been sent.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the social dynamics and power structures within the community of Prophet Salih. The arrogant leaders are challenging the faith of the weaker members of society who have embraced the message of Salih. Their question reflects an attempt to undermine the credibility of the prophet and to create doubt among the believers. The response of the believers, affirming their faith in the message of Salih, demonstrates their conviction and resistance against the societal pressure and manipulation by the elite. This interaction underscores the theme of steadfastness in faith despite opposition from those in power.
orig: قال الملأ الذين استكبروا من قومه للذين استضعفوا لمن آمن منهم أتعلمون أن صالحا مرسل من ربه قالوا إنا بما أرسل به مؤمنون

translation: Those who were arrogant said, 'We disbelieve in what you have believed.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the rejection by the arrogant and proud individuals of the faith and beliefs held by the believers. It underscores the theme of disbelief stemming from pride and arrogance, illustrating how such attitudes lead to the denial of truth and divine guidance.
orig: قال الذين استكبروا إنا بالذي آمنتم به كافرون

translation: So they hamstrung the she-camel and insolently defied the command of their Lord. And they said, 'O Salih, bring us what you threaten us with, if you are indeed of the messengers.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the defiance and disbelief of the people of Thamud towards the prophet Salih and the clear signs sent to them by Allah. By killing the miraculous she-camel, which was a test of their obedience, they not only rejected the message but also challenged Allah's authority. Their demand for Salih to bring upon them the punishment he warned about further demonstrates their arrogance and refusal to heed the divine warning, showcasing a critical moment of their sealing their own fate due to their disobedience and disbelief.
orig: فعقروا الناقة وعتوا عن أمر ربهم وقالوا يا صالح ائتنا بما تعدنا إن كنت من المرسلين

translation: So the earthquake seized them, and they became within their home, fallen prone.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the sudden and overwhelming nature of divine punishment that befell the people due to their disbelief and rejection of the message brought by the prophets. The use of 'earthquake' symbolizes a catastrophic event that is both unexpected and inescapable, emphasizing the power and decisiveness of God's judgment. The phrase 'within their home, fallen prone' suggests that the punishment was so immediate and severe that it struck them in the very place where they felt most secure, highlighting the inescapable nature of divine retribution when it is due.
orig: فأخذتهم الرجفة فأصبحوا في دارهم جاثمين

translation: So he turned away from them and said, 'O my people, I have indeed conveyed to you the message of my Lord and advised you, but you do not like those who advise.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the frustration and fulfillment of duty by a prophet or messenger who has diligently conveyed God's message and offered sincere advice to his people. Despite his efforts, the people reject him, illustrating a common theme in the Qur'an where messengers face resistance and hostility from their communities. The verse underscores the importance of delivering the message regardless of the reception, emphasizing the role of the messenger as a guide and advisor, and the human tendency to dislike or reject advice, even when it is beneficial.
orig: فتولى عنهم وقال يا قوم لقد أبلغتكم رسالة ربي ونصحت لكم ولكن لا تحبون الناصحين

translation: And [mention] Lot, when he said to his people, 'Do you commit such immorality as no one has preceded you with from among the worlds?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the Prophet Lot's confrontation with his people regarding their engagement in homosexual acts, which he describes as an unprecedented immorality among all nations. It underscores the severity of their sin and serves as a reminder of the moral boundaries set by divine guidance, emphasizing the uniqueness of their transgression in human history.
orig: ولوطا إذ قال لقومه أتأتون الفاحشة ما سبقكم بها من أحد من العالمين

translation: Indeed, you approach men with desire, instead of women. Rather, you are a transgressing people.
interpretation: This verse addresses the people of Lot, condemning their practice of engaging in homosexual acts, which is considered a deviation from the natural order established by God. The term 'transgressing' highlights that their actions are not only against the moral and ethical standards set by divine law but also an excessive indulgence in desires that leads them away from righteousness.
orig: إنكم لتأتون الرجال شهوة من دون النساء بل أنتم قوم مسرفون

translation: And the answer of his people was only that they said, 'Drive them out of your town; indeed, they are people who keep themselves pure.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the rejection faced by the messengers of God by their own people. The community's response to the call towards purity and righteousness was not only dismissive but also hostile, as they demanded the expulsion of the believers from their town. This reaction underscores a societal fear or disdain for those who strive to maintain moral and spiritual purity, illustrating the challenge and persecution that often accompanies the path of righteousness.
orig: وما كان جواب قومه إلا أن قالوا أخرجوهم من قريتكم إنهم أناس يتطهرون

translation: So We saved him and his family, except his wife; she was of those who remained behind.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine intervention in the life of Prophet Lut, where Allah saved him and his believing family members from the destruction that befell his community due to their immoral actions. The exception of his wife, who was left behind, underscores the principle that faith and righteousness are individual responsibilities; even close familial ties cannot save someone who does not adhere to the path of Allah. It serves as a reminder of the consequences of disbelief and the importance of personal accountability in one's faith.
orig: فأنجيناه وأهله إلا امرأته كانت من الغابرين

translation: And We rained upon them a rain, so see how was the end of the criminals.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of disobedience and sinfulness by describing a divine punishment in the form of a destructive rain, urging reflection on the fate of those who commit crimes against God's commands. It serves as a reminder of the inevitability of divine justice and the importance of heeding God's warnings.
orig: وأمطرنا عليهم مطرا فانظر كيف كان عاقبة المجرمين

translation: And to Madyan [We sent] their brother Shu'ayb. He said, 'O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. There has come to you clear evidence from your Lord, so give full measure and weight and do not deprive people of their due and do not commit abuse on the earth after it has been reformed. That is better for you, if you should be believers.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of monotheism and ethical conduct in business and societal interactions. Shu'ayb, as a prophet sent to the people of Madyan, calls them to worship Allah alone and warns them against idolatry. The 'clear evidence' refers to the undeniable signs and miracles that accompany the prophetic message, reinforcing its authenticity. He specifically addresses issues of honesty and fairness in trade, urging them to give full measure and weight, which symbolizes justice and integrity in transactions. The prohibition against depriving others of their rights and causing corruption in the land after it has been reformed highlights the broader ethical responsibility to maintain societal harmony and justice. Shu'ayb's message is that adherence to these principles is not only a religious duty but also leads to a better life, contingent upon their faith and obedience to Allah's commands.
orig: وإلى مدين أخاهم شعيبا قال يا قوم اعبدوا الله ما لكم من إله غيره قد جاءتكم بينة من ربكم فأوفوا الكيل والميزان ولا تبخسوا الناس أشياءهم ولا تفسدوا في الأرض بعد إصلاحها ذلكم خير لكم إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: And do not sit on every path, threatening and turning away from the way of Allah those who believe in Him, and seeking to make it crooked. And remember when you were few and He increased you. And see how was the end of the corrupters.
interpretation: This verse warns against obstructing the path of those seeking to follow Allah's guidance. It emphasizes the importance of not only avoiding actions that mislead believers or make the path to righteousness difficult, but also reflects on the historical growth of the Muslim community from a small group to a larger one, attributing this growth to divine support. The verse encourages believers to consider the fate of those who spread corruption, suggesting a reflection on historical and moral lessons to guide current and future actions.
orig: ولا تقعدوا بكل صراط توعدون وتصدون عن سبيل الله من آمن به وتبغونها عوجا واذكروا إذ كنتم قليلا فكثركم وانظروا كيف كان عاقبة المفسدين

translation: And if a group among you believes in that with which I have been sent and another group does not believe, then be patient until Allah judges between us. And He is the best of judges.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of patience and trust in Allah's judgment when faced with division and disbelief within the community. It encourages believers to remain steadfast in their faith and await Allah's decision, highlighting His supreme wisdom and justice in resolving disputes and guiding the community.
orig: وإن كان طائفة منكم آمنوا بالذي أرسلت به وطائفة لم يؤمنوا فاصبروا حتى يحكم الله بيننا وهو خير الحاكمين

translation: The leaders who were arrogant among his people said, 'We will surely expel you, O Shu'ayb, and those who have believed with you from our city, or you must return to our religion.' He said, 'Even if we were unwilling?'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the confrontation between Prophet Shu'ayb and the arrogant leaders of his community. It highlights the resistance and hostility faced by prophets when they challenge the status quo and call people towards monotheism and justice. The leaders' threat to expel Shu'ayb and his followers unless they conform to the prevailing religion underscores the theme of persecution faced by believers. Shu'ayb's response, questioning their demand even if it goes against their will, emphasizes the importance of steadfastness in faith and the moral courage required to stand against oppression and coercion.
orig: قال الملأ الذين استكبروا من قومه لنخرجنك يا شعيب والذين آمنوا معك من قريتنا أو لتعودن في ملتنا قال أولو كنا كارهين

translation: We would be inventing lies against Allah if we were to return to your religion after Allah has saved us from it. And it is not for us to return to it unless Allah, our Lord, should will. Our Lord has encompassed all things in knowledge. In Allah we put our trust. Our Lord, decide between us and our people in truth, and You are the best of those who decide.
interpretation: This verse reflects a strong affirmation of faith and trust in Allah's guidance and protection. The speakers are expressing that reverting to a false religion after being guided to the truth would be a grave sin, akin to lying about Allah's will. They acknowledge that any return to such a state would only be possible if willed by Allah, emphasizing His ultimate control and knowledge over all matters. The verse concludes with a plea for divine judgment and intervention, highlighting the believers' reliance on Allah's justice and wisdom to resolve their conflicts with those who oppose them. It underscores the themes of steadfastness in faith, divine omniscience, and the believers' complete trust in Allah's decision-making.
orig: قد افترينا على الله كذبا إن عدنا في ملتكم بعد إذ نجانا الله منها وما يكون لنا أن نعود فيها إلا أن يشاء الله ربنا وسع ربنا كل شيء علما على الله توكلنا ربنا افتح بيننا وبين قومنا بالحق وأنت خير الفاتحين

translation: And the chiefs of those who disbelieved among his people said, 'If you follow Shu'ayb, indeed, you will then be losers.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the opposition faced by the Prophet Shu'ayb from the elite of his community who rejected his message. It highlights the fear of economic and social loss that the disbelievers felt if they were to follow the guidance of a prophet, illustrating the common theme in the Qur'an of resistance to divine messages due to perceived worldly disadvantages.
orig: وقال الملأ الذين كفروا من قومه لئن اتبعتم شعيبا إنكم إذا لخاسرون

translation: So the earthquake seized them, and they became within their home, fallen prone.
interpretation: This verse describes the sudden and devastating punishment that befell the people of the Prophet Shu'ayb due to their persistent rejection of his message and their refusal to mend their corrupt ways. The 'earthquake' symbolizes the overwhelming and inescapable nature of divine retribution, which struck them in their very homes, leaving them lifeless and humbled. It serves as a powerful reminder of the consequences of ignoring divine warnings and the importance of heeding the call to righteousness.
orig: فأخذتهم الرجفة فأصبحوا في دارهم جاثمين

translation: Those who denied Shu'aib - it was as though they had never prospered therein. Those who denied Shu'aib - they were the losers.
interpretation: This verse reflects on the consequences faced by the people who rejected the message of the Prophet Shu'aib. It suggests that their apparent prosperity was illusory and temporary, as ultimately, their denial led to their downfall and loss. The verse underscores the theme that rejecting divine guidance leads to ruin, emphasizing that true success and prosperity are linked to faith and obedience to God's messengers.
orig: الذين كذبوا شعيبا كأن لم يغنوا فيها الذين كذبوا شعيبا كانوا هم الخاسرين

translation: So he turned away from them and said, 'O my people, I have indeed conveyed to you the messages of my Lord and advised you, so how can I grieve for a disbelieving people?'
interpretation: This verse reflects the Prophet's sense of duty fulfilled and his detachment from the outcome of his people's response. After diligently conveying God's messages and offering sincere advice, he recognizes that he has done all he could. His rhetorical question expresses a sense of resignation and acceptance that he cannot control their disbelief, highlighting the emotional and spiritual boundary he must maintain despite his deep concern for their fate.
orig: فتولى عنهم وقال يا قوم لقد أبلغتكم رسالات ربي ونصحت لكم فكيف آسى على قوم كافرين

translation: And We did not send a prophet to a town except that We seized its people with hardship and adversity so that they might humble themselves.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine method of testing communities through prophets. By sending prophets, God introduces trials in the form of hardship and adversity to the people of a town. The purpose of these trials is to encourage the inhabitants to turn to God in humility and supplication, seeking His mercy and guidance. It reflects the belief that adversity can serve as a means to spiritual awakening and repentance, prompting people to recognize their dependence on God and to seek a closer relationship with Him.
orig: وما أرسلنا في قرية من نبي إلا أخذنا أهلها بالبأساء والضراء لعلهم يضرعون

translation: Then We substituted in their place good [conditions] until they increased and said, 'Our fathers were touched by hardship and ease.' So We seized them suddenly while they did not perceive.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the cycle of divine test through varying conditions of life. Initially, God replaces hardship with ease to test the gratitude and faith of people. As they prosper and their population grows, they become heedless, attributing their past and present conditions to natural cycles experienced by their ancestors rather than recognizing divine intervention. Consequently, God punishes them unexpectedly for their ingratitude and lack of awareness, emphasizing the importance of recognizing and appreciating God's blessings and trials.
orig: ثم بدلنا مكان السيئة الحسنة حتى عفوا وقالوا قد مس آباءنا الضراء والسراء فأخذناهم بغتة وهم لا يشعرون

translation: And if the people of the towns had believed and feared Allah, We would have opened upon them blessings from the heaven and the earth. But they denied [the messengers], so We seized them for what they were earning.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the conditional nature of divine blessings, suggesting that faith and righteousness are prerequisites for receiving God's favors. It indicates that the rejection of divine guidance leads to consequences determined by one's actions, illustrating the principle of accountability in the Qur'an.
orig: ولو أن أهل القرى آمنوا واتقوا لفتحنا عليهم بركات من السماء والأرض ولكن كذبوا فأخذناهم بما كانوا يكسبون

translation: Do the people of the towns feel secure that Our punishment will not come upon them by night while they are asleep?
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder and a warning to the inhabitants of towns that they should not feel complacent or secure from God's punishment. It emphasizes the suddenness and unexpected nature of divine retribution, which can come at any moment, even when people are in their most vulnerable state, such as during sleep. The verse encourages vigilance, repentance, and a constant awareness of God's power and justice.
orig: أفأمن أهل القرى أن يأتيهم بأسنا بياتا وهم نائمون

translation: Or do the people of the villages feel secure that Our punishment will not come upon them in the morning while they are playing?
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder and warning to people not to be complacent or heedless of God's power and potential punishment. It suggests that divine retribution can come suddenly and unexpectedly, even during moments of leisure and play, emphasizing the need for constant awareness and adherence to righteous behavior.
orig: أوأمن أهل القرى أن يأتيهم بأسنا ضحى وهم يلعبون

translation: Do they feel secure from the plan of Allah? But no one feels secure from the plan of Allah except the losing people.
interpretation: This verse warns against the false sense of security some people might feel, thinking they are beyond the reach of divine retribution or planning. It emphasizes that only those who are heedless and ultimately at loss ("the losing people") would feel safe from Allah's plan, indicating that true believers remain conscious of Allah's power and justice, and do not take their safety or success for granted.
orig: أفأمنوا مكر الله فلا يأمن مكر الله إلا القوم الخاسرون

translation: Has it not become clear to those who inherit the earth after its [previous] people that if We willed, We could afflict them for their sins and seal their hearts so they would not hear?
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder and a warning to the successors of past nations that their current state of power and prosperity is not a sign of divine favor or immunity from punishment. It emphasizes that Allah has the power to punish them for their sins just as He punished those before them, by sealing their hearts and rendering them deaf to guidance. This should instill a sense of humility and urgency in them to seek forgiveness and righteousness, recognizing that their fate is contingent upon their actions and Allah's will.
orig: أولم يهد للذين يرثون الأرض من بعد أهلها أن لو نشاء أصبناهم بذنوبهم ونطبع على قلوبهم فهم لا يسمعون

translation: Those were the towns whose stories We relate to you. Their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they were not going to believe in what they had previously denied. Thus Allah seals the hearts of the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the recurring theme of divine messengers being sent to various communities with clear signs and proofs of their message. Despite the clarity and evidence provided, the people's refusal to believe stems from their prior rejection of truth. This persistent denial leads to a spiritual sealing of their hearts by Allah, indicating a point of no return in their disbelief, emphasizing the consequences of rejecting divine guidance repeatedly.
orig: تلك القرى نقص عليك من أنبائها ولقد جاءتهم رسلهم بالبينات فما كانوا ليؤمنوا بما كذبوا من قبل كذلك يطبع الله على قلوب الكافرين

translation: And We found that most of them do not fulfill their covenant; indeed, We found most of them to be defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse reflects on the general human tendency to break promises and covenants with God. It suggests that despite being given guidance and opportunities to adhere to divine commandments, the majority of people choose to act rebelliously and disobediently, highlighting a common moral failing among humanity.
orig: وما وجدنا لأكثرهم من عهد وإن وجدنا أكثرهم لفاسقين

translation: Then We sent Moses with Our signs to Pharaoh and his chiefs, but they wronged them. So see how was the end of the corrupters.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine mission of Moses, sent with clear signs from Allah to guide Pharaoh and his people. Despite the clarity and miracles presented, they chose to reject and oppress the message, illustrating their corruption and moral decay. The verse serves as a reminder and a warning to observe the ultimate fate of those who corrupt and reject divine guidance, emphasizing the consequences of such actions.
orig: ثم بعثنا من بعدهم موسى بآياتنا إلى فرعون وملئه فظلموا بها فانظر كيف كان عاقبة المفسدين

translation: And Moses said, 'O Pharaoh, indeed I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse highlights Moses's declaration of his prophetic mission to Pharaoh, emphasizing his divine authority and the universal scope of his message, which comes from the Lord of all creation. It underscores the confrontation between divine truth and worldly power, setting the stage for the subsequent narrative of liberation and divine intervention.
orig: وقال موسى يا فرعون إني رسول من رب العالمين

translation: It is only right that I should not say anything about Allah except the truth. I have come to you with clear evidence from your Lord, so let the Children of Israel go with me.
interpretation: In this verse, the speaker, who is Moses, emphasizes the importance of truthfulness when speaking about Allah, highlighting his own integrity and divine mission. He presents the miracles given to him by Allah as undeniable proof of his prophethood and demands the release of the Israelites from Pharaoh's oppression, underscoring the divine command to liberate them.
orig: حقيق على أن لا أقول على الله إلا الحق قد جئتكم ببينة من ربكم فأرسل معي بني إسرائيل

translation: He said, "If you have come with a sign, then bring it forth, if you are among the truthful."
interpretation: This verse reflects a challenge posed by Pharaoh to Moses, demanding proof of his claim to prophethood. It underscores the theme of skepticism and the demand for tangible evidence in the face of divine messages, illustrating the human tendency to question and test the authenticity of spiritual claims. It also highlights the courage required of prophets to confront disbelief and the importance of patience and faith in the face of such challenges.
orig: قال إن كنت جئت بآية فأت بها إن كنت من الصادقين

translation: So he threw down his staff, and behold, it was a serpent, plainly visible.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the miraculous power bestowed upon Moses by Allah, demonstrating divine support and the ability to transform ordinary objects into extraordinary signs. The transformation of the staff into a serpent serves as a clear and undeniable proof of Moses's prophethood and the truth of his message, intended to convince Pharaoh and his people of the might and reality of Allah.
orig: فألقى عصاه فإذا هي ثعبان مبين

translation: And he drew out his hand, and behold, it was white to the onlookers.
interpretation: This verse refers to the miracle given to Moses when he was commanded to place his hand inside his cloak and then draw it out. When he did so, his hand shone brightly, appearing white to those who saw it, symbolizing purity and divine power. This miracle was a sign to Pharaoh and the people of Egypt to believe in the message Moses brought from God.
orig: ونزع يده فإذا هي بيضاء للناظرين

translation: The chiefs from among the people of Pharaoh said, 'This is indeed a skilled magician.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the reaction of Pharaoh's elite to the miracles performed by Moses. They attribute his miraculous acts to magic rather than divine intervention, reflecting their denial and arrogance in the face of clear signs from God. This underscores the theme of resistance to truth by those in power, who are threatened by anything that challenges their authority and beliefs.
orig: قال الملأ من قوم فرعون إن هذا لساحر عليم

translation: He wants to drive you out of your land, so what do you command?
interpretation: This verse reflects a situation where a group is faced with a threat from an external force trying to displace them from their homeland. It poses a rhetorical question to the leaders or the community, urging them to decide on a course of action in response to this threat. The verse emphasizes the importance of strategic decision-making and unity in the face of adversity.
orig: يريد أن يخرجكم من أرضكم فماذا تأمرون

translation: They said: 'Delay him and his brother, and send heralds to the cities.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the Pharaoh's strategy to delay Moses and Aaron, giving him time to gather support and possibly suppress the growing influence of the two prophets. It highlights the tactics of those in power who feel threatened by the message of truth, using delay and distraction to maintain their control.
orig: قالوا أرجه وأخاه وأرسل في المدائن حاشرين

translation: They come to you with every skilled magician.
interpretation: This verse refers to the magicians who were brought before the Prophet Moses by Pharaoh to challenge his miracles. It highlights the lengths to which those in power will go to discredit the truth, using deception and false expertise. It underscores the theme of truth prevailing over falsehood, as ultimately, Moses's miracles, supported by divine power, proved superior to the magicians' tricks.
orig: يأتوك بكل ساحر عليم

translation: And the magicians came to Pharaoh. They said, 'Indeed, for us there will be a reward if we are the victors.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the materialistic and self-serving nature of the magicians who were willing to engage in a contest against Moses for personal gain. It reflects a broader theme in the Qur'an about how worldly incentives can lead individuals to oppose divine truth, illustrating the moral and spiritual challenges faced by those who prioritize earthly rewards over righteousness.
orig: وجاء السحرة فرعون قالوا إن لنا لأجرا إن كنا نحن الغالبين

translation: He said, 'Yes, and indeed you are among those brought near.'
interpretation: This verse indicates that the speaker, likely an angel or a divine messenger, is affirming the status of the individuals being addressed as being close to God, highlighting their elevated spiritual rank and the honor bestowed upon them due to their faith and righteousness.
orig: قال نعم وإنكم لمن المقربين

translation: They said, 'O Moses, either you throw or we will be the ones who throw.'
interpretation: This verse reflects a moment of confrontation and challenge between Moses and the magicians of Pharaoh. It underscores the theme of faith versus disbelief, where the magicians, representing the forces of disbelief, challenge Moses to a contest of miracles. This challenge is not just about physical power but symbolizes the deeper struggle between truth and falsehood. The magicians' readiness to throw first indicates their confidence in their magic, yet it also sets the stage for the demonstration of divine power through Moses, highlighting the ultimate victory of truth over deception.
orig: قالوا يا موسى إما أن تلقي وإما أن نكون نحن الملقين

translation: He said, 'Throw.' So when they threw, they bewitched the eyes of the people and struck them with awe, and they came with a great magic.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the power of illusion and deception, as the magicians were able to create a spectacle that not only visually deceived the onlookers but also instilled fear and awe in them. It highlights the theme of the struggle between truth and falsehood, where the magicians' magic, though impressive, is ultimately a form of deception that cannot stand against the truth represented by Moses' miracle.
orig: قال ألقوا فلما ألقوا سحروا أعين الناس واسترهبوهم وجاءوا بسحر عظيم

translation: And We inspired Moses: 'Throw your staff,' and behold, it swallowed up what they were falsifying.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the power of divine intervention and the triumph of truth over falsehood. When Moses, under God's command, throws his staff, it transforms into a serpent that consumes the magic of the sorcerers, symbolizing how divine truth can overcome deception and falsehood. This event not only serves as a sign of Moses' prophethood but also reassures believers of God's support in confronting challenges and adversaries.
orig: وأوحينا إلى موسى أن ألق عصاك فإذا هي تلقف ما يأفكون

translation: The truth has come, and falsehood has vanished.
interpretation: This verse signifies the ultimate triumph of truth over falsehood. It reflects the idea that when divine truth is revealed, all human-made falsehoods and deceptions are exposed and ultimately fail. It serves as a reminder of the power and inevitability of truth in the face of all opposition.
orig: فوقع الحق وبطل ما كانوا يعملون

translation: So they were defeated there and turned back, utterly humiliated.
interpretation: This verse describes a significant defeat of the disbelievers, illustrating the consequences of opposing God's will and the Prophet Muhammad. It serves as a reminder of the ultimate triumph of truth over falsehood, emphasizing that those who reject divine guidance will face humiliation and failure in their endeavors.
orig: فغلبوا هنالك وانقلبوا صاغرين

translation: And the magicians fell down prostrate.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the moment of truth and submission when the magicians, upon witnessing the undeniable miracle of Moses, recognized the superiority of his God-given power over their own magic. Their prostration signifies their acknowledgment of the truth of Moses' message and their immediate conversion to faith, highlighting the transformative power of divine signs and the humility required to accept them.
orig: وألقي السحرة ساجدين

translation: They said, 'We believe in the Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse reflects a declaration of faith by a group of people, acknowledging their belief in Allah, who is described as the Lord of all creation. This affirmation signifies a pivotal moment of acceptance and submission to the divine authority and unity of God, emphasizing the universal aspect of His lordship over all beings and realms.
orig: قالوا آمنا برب العالمين

translation: The Lord of Moses and Aaron
interpretation: This phrase emphasizes the shared belief in one God between the followers of Moses and Aaron, highlighting the continuity and unity of monotheistic faith across different prophets and communities. It serves as a reminder of the universal message of submission to the one true God, as conveyed through various messengers in Islamic theology.
orig: رب موسى وهارون

translation: Pharaoh said, "Have you believed in him before I gave you permission? Indeed, this is a conspiracy which you have plotted in the city to expel its people from it. But you will soon know [the consequences].
interpretation: Pharaoh's reaction to the faith of his people in Moses reveals his authoritarian control and paranoia. He perceives their belief as a threat to his power, accusing them of conspiring against him to overthrow his rule. This verse underscores the theme of resistance against tyranny and the inevitable downfall of oppressors who challenge divine truth.
orig: قال فرعون آمنتم به قبل أن آذن لكم إن هذا لمكر مكرتموه في المدينة لتخرجوا منها أهلها فسوف تعلمون

translation: I will certainly cut off your hands and feet on opposite sides, then I will crucify you all.
interpretation: This verse illustrates a severe punishment mentioned by Pharaoh as a threat to the magicians who believed in Moses. It underscores the extreme measures taken by oppressive rulers to maintain control and suppress dissent, highlighting the courage of those who stand firm in their faith despite facing such dire consequences.
orig: لأقطعن أيديكم وأرجلكم من خلاف ثم لأصلبنكم أجمعين

translation: They said, 'Indeed, to our Lord we will return.'
interpretation: This verse reflects a profound sense of faith and submission to God. It indicates that the speakers are aware of their ultimate return to their Creator, acknowledging that their life's journey will end with them facing God. This acknowledgment fosters a mindset of accountability and hope, reinforcing the belief in the afterlife and divine judgment.
orig: قالوا إنا إلى ربنا منقلبون

translation: And they do not resent us except because we believed in the signs of our Lord when they came to us. Our Lord, pour upon us patience and let us die as Muslims [in submission to You].
interpretation: This verse reflects the steadfastness and faith of believers in the face of opposition and persecution. It highlights that the animosity from others stems solely from the believers' acceptance of divine revelations. The prayer for patience and a peaceful end as Muslims underscores the importance of perseverance and submission to God's will, even in the midst of trials. It teaches believers to seek divine support to maintain their faith and integrity until the end of their lives.
orig: وما تنقم منا إلا أن آمنا بآيات ربنا لما جاءتنا ربنا أفرغ علينا صبرا وتوفنا مسلمين

translation: And the chiefs among the people of Pharaoh said: "Will you leave Moses and his people to cause corruption in the land and abandon you and your gods?" He said: "We will kill their sons and let their women live, and we will be dominant over them."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the reaction of the ruling elite of Pharaoh's society to the growing influence of Moses and his followers. It highlights their fear that Moses's message would undermine their authority and lead to the abandonment of their deities. Pharaoh's response to kill the sons of the Israelites while sparing their daughters is a strategic move to weaken the future generations of the Israelites, ensuring they remain subjugated. This decision reflects the oppressive nature of Pharaoh's regime and their determination to maintain power through violent means, showcasing a theme of tyranny versus the divine mission of Moses.
orig: وقال الملأ من قوم فرعون أتذر موسى وقومه ليفسدوا في الأرض ويذرك وآلهتك قال سنقتل أبناءهم ونستحيي نساءهم وإنا فوقهم قاهرون

translation: Moses said to his people, 'Seek help from Allah and be patient. Indeed, the earth belongs to Allah; He gives it as inheritance to whom He wills of His servants. And the [best] outcome is for the righteous.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of reliance on Allah and patience during times of hardship. Moses advises his people to turn to Allah for assistance and to remain steadfast, reminding them that Allah is the ultimate owner of the earth and has the power to grant it to whomever He chooses among His servants. This serves as a reassurance that divine justice will prevail, and the final outcome will favor those who are pious and God-fearing.
orig: قال موسى لقومه استعينوا بالله واصبروا إن الأرض لله يورثها من يشاء من عباده والعاقبة للمتقين

translation: They said, 'We were harmed before you came to us and after you have come to us.' He said, 'Perhaps your Lord will destroy your enemy and grant you succession in the land, and then He will see how you will do.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the dialogue between the oppressed people and their prophet, likely Moses, during their struggle against Pharaoh. The people express their ongoing suffering, both before and after the prophet's arrival, indicating their frustration and despair. The prophet responds with hope and faith, suggesting that God might eliminate their adversary, Pharaoh, and allow them to inherit the land. This promise is conditional, as it is followed by God observing their actions afterward, emphasizing the importance of righteousness and gratitude following divine intervention. The verse underscores themes of perseverance, divine justice, and the test of faith through trials and subsequent responsibilities.
orig: قالوا أوذينا من قبل أن تأتينا ومن بعد ما جئتنا قال عسى ربكم أن يهلك عدوكم ويستخلفكم في الأرض فينظر كيف تعملون

translation: And indeed We seized the people of Pharaoh with years of famine and a shortage of fruits, that they might take heed.
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's use of natural disasters and scarcity as a means to remind and warn people of their wrongdoings. Specifically, it refers to the trials inflicted upon the people of Pharaoh, suggesting that such hardships are intended to prompt reflection and a return to righteousness. The mention of Pharaoh's people underscores the theme of divine justice and the consequences of persistent disbelief and oppression.
orig: ولقد أخذنا آل فرعون بالسنين ونقص من الثمرات لعلهم يذكرون

translation: So when good comes to them, they say, 'This is due to us'; and if evil befalls them, they say, 'This is due to Moses and those with him.' Beware, their fate is only with Allah, but most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy and selective attribution of the Children of Israel. When they experience good fortune, they attribute it to their own merits, reflecting a sense of self-righteousness and denial of divine favor. Conversely, when faced with adversity, they blame Moses and his followers, showcasing their tendency to scapegoat others for their misfortunes. The verse underscores that ultimately, their destiny and judgment lie solely with Allah, emphasizing divine justice and omniscience. However, the verse also points out the ignorance prevalent among them, as most fail to recognize this truth, illustrating a broader theme of human nature's inclination towards misattribution and lack of understanding of divine will.
orig: فإذا جاءتهم الحسنة قالوا لنا هذه وإن تصبهم سيئة يطيروا بموسى ومن معه ألا إنما طائرهم عند الله ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: And they said, 'No matter what sign you bring to us, to work your magic on us, we will not believe in you.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the stubborn disbelief of the people who were confronted with the miracles of the Prophet. Despite witnessing clear signs, they attributed these to magic, showcasing their deep-seated denial and refusal to accept the truth. It underscores the challenge faced by prophets in convincing those whose hearts are hardened against faith.
orig: وقالوا مهما تأتنا به من آية لتسحرنا بها فما نحن لك بمؤمنين

translation: So We sent upon them the flood and locusts and lice and frogs and blood as distinct signs, but they were arrogant and were a criminal people.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the consequences of persistent disobedience and arrogance towards divine signs. The afflictions sent upon the people, such as the flood, locusts, lice, frogs, and blood, were clear and distinct signs from God intended to guide them back to the right path. However, their response of arrogance and continued criminal behavior underscores a deeper spiritual ailment, reflecting a rejection of divine guidance and a refusal to acknowledge the power and mercy of God. This serves as a reminder of the importance of humility and obedience to God's signs and warnings.
orig: فأرسلنا عليهم الطوفان والجراد والقمل والضفادع والدم آيات مفصلات فاستكبروا وكانوا قوما مجرمين

translation: And when the punishment descended upon them, they said, 'O Moses, call upon your Lord for us by what He has promised you. If you remove the punishment from us, we will surely believe in you, and we will send the Children of Israel with you.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the moment when the Egyptians, under the affliction of a divine punishment, acknowledged their vulnerability and sought Moses' intercession. It reflects a common human tendency to turn to faith and make promises in times of distress, yet their sincerity is questionable as their commitment to belief and action is conditional upon the removal of their immediate suffering. This illustrates the theme of faith tested by adversity and the challenge of maintaining true belief beyond immediate crises.
orig: ولما وقع عليهم الرجز قالوا يا موسى ادع لنا ربك بما عهد عندك لئن كشفت عنا الرجز لنؤمنن لك ولنرسلن معك بني إسرائيل

translation: So when We removed from them the affliction until a term which they were to reach, behold, they broke their word.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the human tendency to forget their promises and revert to disbelief or disobedience once relief comes after a period of hardship. It serves as a reminder of the importance of steadfastness in faith and gratitude, regardless of changing circumstances.
orig: فلما كشفنا عنهم الرجز إلى أجل هم بالغوه إذا هم ينكثون

translation: So We took vengeance on them and drowned them in the sea because they denied Our signs and were heedless of them.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the consequence of rejecting divine guidance. The drowning of the people in the sea is a direct result of their denial of God's signs and their negligence towards them. It serves as a warning that ignoring the messages and proofs of God's existence and authority can lead to severe punishment. The emphasis on their heedlessness suggests that their downfall was not only due to active disbelief but also due to a lack of attention and reflection on the divine messages they received.
orig: فانتقمنا منهم فأغرقناهم في اليم بأنهم كذبوا بآياتنا وكانوا عنها غافلين

translation: And We caused the people who were considered weak to inherit the eastern parts of the land and the western parts, which We had blessed. And the good word of your Lord was fulfilled for the Children of Israel, because of their patience. And We destroyed what Pharaoh and his people were producing and what they had been constructing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine justice and reward system where the oppressed, symbolized by the 'people who were considered weak', are given authority and prosperity over lands blessed by Allah. It specifically refers to the Children of Israel who, due to their steadfast patience, were rewarded with the fulfillment of God's promise. Conversely, the verse also serves as a reminder of the transient nature of power and wealth, exemplified by the destruction of the works of Pharaoh and his people, indicating that no matter how grand their constructions or achievements, they are ultimately futile against the will of Allah.
orig: وأورثنا القوم الذين كانوا يستضعفون مشارق الأرض ومغاربها التي باركنا فيها وتمت كلمت ربك الحسنى على بني إسرائيل بما صبروا ودمرنا ما كان يصنع فرعون وقومه وما كانوا يعرشون

translation: And We took the Children of Israel across the sea, and they came upon a people intent on their idols. They said, 'O Moses, make for us a god just as they have gods.' He said, 'Indeed, you are a people behaving ignorantly.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual weakness and lack of faith among the Children of Israel shortly after their miraculous crossing of the Red Sea. Despite witnessing God's power and deliverance, they quickly succumbed to the influence of idol-worshipping people they encountered, showing their susceptibility to idolatry and their failure to trust in the one true God. Moses' response underscores their ignorance and the folly of their request, emphasizing the need for steadfast faith in the face of external temptations.
orig: وجاوزنا ببني إسرائيل البحر فأتوا على قوم يعكفون على أصنام لهم قالوا يا موسى اجعل لنا إلها كما لهم آلهة قال إنكم قوم تجهلون

translation: Indeed, these [disbelievers] are in falsehood concerning that which they are in, and what they used to do is null and void.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate futility and falsehood of the beliefs and actions of those who reject faith. It suggests that their state of disbelief and the deeds they perform based on that disbelief will ultimately be revealed as meaningless and ineffective in the eyes of God. The verse serves as a reminder of the transient nature of worldly pursuits that are not aligned with divine truth, urging believers to focus on actions that have lasting value in the hereafter.
orig: إن هؤلاء متبر ما هم فيه وباطل ما كانوا يعملون

translation: He said, 'Should I seek a god other than Allah for you, while He has preferred you over all the worlds?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the Prophet Muhammad's rhetorical question to his people, emphasizing the absurdity of worshipping any deity other than Allah. It underscores the unique favor and superiority that Allah has bestowed upon the believers, distinguishing them from all other nations and peoples. The verse serves as a reminder of the gratitude and loyalty owed to Allah alone, reinforcing the monotheistic principle central to Islamic faith.
orig: قال أغير الله أبغيكم إلها وهو فضلكم على العالمين

translation: And [remember] when We saved you from the people of Pharaoh, who were afflicting you with the worst torment, killing your sons and sparing your women. And in that was a great trial from your Lord.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder to the Children of Israel of the divine intervention that saved them from the tyranny of Pharaoh. It highlights the severe oppression they faced, including the killing of their sons and the sparing of their daughters, which was a method used by Pharaoh to control their population. The verse emphasizes that this ordeal was not only a test of their faith and endurance but also a demonstration of God's power and mercy in delivering them from such extreme adversity. It underscores the theme of divine salvation and the trials that believers may face as part of their spiritual journey.
orig: وإذ أنجيناكم من آل فرعون يسومونكم سوء العذاب يقتلون أبناءكم ويستحيون نساءكم وفي ذلكم بلاء من ربكم عظيم

translation: And We appointed for Moses thirty nights and We completed them with ten, so the appointment of his Lord was completed in forty nights. And Moses said to his brother Aaron: 'Take my place among my people, and do right, and do not follow the way of the corrupt.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of divine appointment and obedience to God's commands. The forty nights signify a period of spiritual preparation and purification for Moses before receiving the Torah. Moses' instruction to Aaron to lead the people righteously in his absence underscores the responsibility of leaders to maintain moral integrity and guide their community away from corruption.
orig: وواعدنا موسى ثلاثين ليلة وأتممناها بعشر فتم ميقات ربه أربعين ليلة وقال موسى لأخيه هارون اخلفني في قومي وأصلح ولا تتبع سبيل المفسدين

translation: And when Moses came at Our appointed time and his Lord spoke to him, he said, 'My Lord, show me Yourself, that I may look upon You.' He said, 'You will not see Me, but look at the mountain; if it remains firm in its place, then you will see Me.' But when his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble to dust, and Moses fell unconscious. When he recovered, he said, 'Glory be to You! I repent to You, and I am the first of the believers.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the human limitation in comprehending the divine essence of God. Moses, a prophet close to God, requests to see Him directly, which reflects a deep yearning for a closer connection with the divine. However, God explains that direct vision of Him is beyond human capacity, using the mountain as a test to demonstrate this limitation. When the mountain crumbles upon God's manifestation, it symbolizes the overwhelming power and majesty of God that no physical entity can withstand. Moses's subsequent unconsciousness and repentance signify his acknowledgment of God's greatness and his own humility and submission, reinforcing the theme that true faith involves recognizing and accepting the limits of human perception and the boundless nature of God.
orig: ولما جاء موسى لميقاتنا وكلمه ربه قال رب أرني أنظر إليك قال لن تراني ولكن انظر إلى الجبل فإن استقر مكانه فسوف تراني فلما تجلى ربه للجبل جعله دكا وخر موسى صعقا فلما أفاق قال سبحانك تبت إليك وأنا أول المؤمنين

translation: He said, 'O Moses, indeed I have chosen you over the people with My messages and My words, so take what I have given you and be among the grateful.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the special selection of Moses by Allah, emphasizing the divine favor and responsibility bestowed upon him. It underscores the importance of gratitude and acceptance of divine gifts, urging believers to appreciate and utilize the blessings and guidance provided by Allah.
orig: قال يا موسى إني اصطفيتك على الناس برسالاتي وبكلامي فخذ ما آتيتك وكن من الشاكرين

translation: And We wrote for him on the tablets from everything an admonition and a detailed explanation of all things. So take them with strength and command your people to take the best of it. I will show you the home of the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse refers to the revelation given to Moses on the tablets, which contained comprehensive guidance and detailed laws for the Israelites. The command to 'take them with strength' suggests that Moses and his people should adhere firmly to these divine instructions. The phrase 'command your people to take the best of it' implies that while the laws are to be followed, the spirit of the law, which includes moral and ethical guidance, should be embraced foremost. The promise to 'show you the home of the defiantly disobedient' serves as a warning of the consequences of straying from God's path, illustrating the importance of obedience to divine commandments.
orig: وكتبنا له في الألواح من كل شيء موعظة وتفصيلا لكل شيء فخذها بقوة وأمر قومك يأخذوا بأحسنها سأريكم دار الفاسقين

translation: I will turn away from My signs those who are arrogant upon the earth without right; and if they should see every sign, they will not believe in it; and if they see the path of righteousness, they will not take it as a path; but if they see the path of error, they will take that as a path. That is because they denied Our signs and were heedless of them.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual consequence of arrogance and denial of divine signs. It suggests that those who are unjustly proud and reject the truth will be spiritually blinded, unable to recognize or accept clear signs of guidance. Their rejection stems from a deep-seated denial and negligence of divine messages, leading them to choose paths of error over righteousness. This serves as a warning about the dangers of pride and the importance of humility and attentiveness to divine guidance.
orig: سأصرف عن آياتي الذين يتكبرون في الأرض بغير الحق وإن يروا كل آية لا يؤمنوا بها وإن يروا سبيل الرشد لا يتخذوه سبيلا وإن يروا سبيل الغي يتخذوه سبيلا ذلك بأنهم كذبوا بآياتنا وكانوا عنها غافلين

translation: And those who denied Our signs and the meeting of the Hereafter - their deeds have become worthless; are they recompensed except for what they used to do?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequence of disbelief in the signs of Allah and the reality of the afterlife. It underscores that the actions of those who reject these fundamental truths become futile and devoid of any spiritual reward. The rhetorical question at the end serves to highlight the justice in divine retribution, indicating that individuals will be recompensed precisely according to their deeds, with no alteration or injustice. It serves as a reminder of personal accountability and the importance of faith in shaping the value of one's actions.
orig: والذين كذبوا بآياتنا ولقاء الآخرة حبطت أعمالهم هل يجزون إلا ما كانوا يعملون

translation: And the people of Moses made, after [he left them], from their ornaments a calf - an image having a lowing sound. Did they not see that it could neither speak to them nor guide them to a way? They took it [for worship], and they were wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the grave mistake of the Israelites who, in the absence of Moses, succumbed to idolatry by crafting and worshipping a golden calf. It underscores their failure to recognize the calf's inability to communicate or provide guidance, illustrating the folly and injustice of turning away from the true guidance of God towards false deities. This act of idolatry is portrayed as a clear injustice and deviation from the path of righteousness.
orig: واتخذ قوم موسى من بعده من حليهم عجلا جسدا له خوار ألم يروا أنه لا يكلمهم ولا يهديهم سبيلا اتخذوه وكانوا ظالمين

translation: And when they fell into their hands and saw that they had gone astray, they said, 'If our Lord does not have mercy on us and forgive us, we will surely be among the losers.'
interpretation: This verse reflects a moment of realization and repentance among a group of people who, after experiencing a downfall or failure ("fell into their hands"), acknowledge their error in straying from the right path. Their statement expresses a deep understanding that without God's mercy and forgiveness, they would be doomed to loss and ruin. It underscores the importance of divine mercy and forgiveness as the ultimate means of salvation and redemption, highlighting the human recognition of dependence on God's grace.
orig: ولما سقط في أيديهم ورأوا أنهم قد ضلوا قالوا لئن لم يرحمنا ربنا ويغفر لنا لنكونن من الخاسرين

translation: And when Moses returned to his people, angry and grieved, he said, 'How wretched is that which you have done in my absence. Did you hasten the matter of your Lord?' And he threw down the tablets and seized his brother by [the hair of] his head, pulling him toward him. [Aaron] said, 'O son of my mother, indeed the people oppressed me and were about to kill me, so let not the enemies rejoice over me and do not place me among the wrongdoing people.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of leadership and the challenges faced by prophets in guiding their communities. Moses' reaction of anger and grief upon seeing his people worshipping the golden calf after his absence underscores the disappointment and responsibility felt by leaders when their followers stray from the path of righteousness. Aaron's response to Moses' confrontation reveals the pressures and threats faced by those in secondary leadership roles, illustrating the need for compassion and understanding within the community. The verse also emphasizes the importance of not allowing personal grievances to lead to actions that could benefit the enemies of faith, promoting unity and forgiveness among believers.
orig: ولما رجع موسى إلى قومه غضبان أسفا قال بئسما خلفتموني من بعدي أعجلتم أمر ربكم وألقى الألواح وأخذ برأس أخيه يجره إليه قال ابن أم إن القوم استضعفوني وكادوا يقتلونني فلا تشمت بي الأعداء ولا تجعلني مع القوم الظالمين

translation: He said, "My Lord, forgive me and my brother and admit us into Your mercy, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful."
interpretation: In this verse, the speaker is Prophet Moses (Musa) who is asking for Allah's forgiveness not only for himself but also for his brother Aaron (Harun). This plea reflects the humility and compassion of Moses, demonstrating his concern for his brother's well-being as well as his own. By requesting to be admitted into Allah's mercy, Moses acknowledges the vastness of Allah's mercy and His attribute as the Most Merciful among those who show mercy. This verse underscores the importance of seeking forgiveness and mercy from Allah, and the value of interceding on behalf of others, highlighting the communal aspect of faith and the interconnectedness of believers.
orig: قال رب اغفر لي ولأخي وأدخلنا في رحمتك وأنت أرحم الراحمين

translation: Indeed, those who took the calf [for worship] will obtain anger from their Lord and humiliation in the worldly life, and thus do We recompense the inventors [of falsehood].
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning and a reminder of the consequences of idolatry and straying from the path of monotheism. It specifically refers to the incident where a group of Israelites, after being saved by Moses, worshipped a golden calf, an act of disbelief and disobedience. The verse emphasizes that such actions provoke divine anger and result in worldly humiliation. It also generalizes this punishment to all who invent falsehood or deviate from the truth, indicating that God's justice ensures that those who engage in such acts will face appropriate consequences both in this life and the hereafter.
orig: إن الذين اتخذوا العجل سينالهم غضب من ربهم وذلة في الحياة الدنيا وكذلك نجزي المفترين

translation: And those who have done evil deeds, then repented afterwards and believed, indeed, your Lord, after that, is Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the mercy and forgiveness of Allah. It teaches that even those who have committed sins have the opportunity to seek forgiveness through sincere repentance and faith. The verse reassures believers that no matter the gravity of their past actions, Allah's forgiveness and mercy are boundless, encouraging them to turn back to Him with genuine remorse and belief.
orig: والذين عملوا السيئات ثم تابوا من بعدها وآمنوا إن ربك من بعدها لغفور رحيم

translation: And when Moses' anger subsided, he took up the tablets; and in their inscription was guidance and mercy for those who fear their Lord.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of divine guidance and mercy as embodied in the tablets given to Moses. It suggests that true guidance and mercy are available to those who maintain a reverent fear of God, indicating that a deep respect and awe of the divine is essential for receiving and benefiting from God's teachings and compassion.
orig: ولما سكت عن موسى الغضب أخذ الألواح وفي نسختها هدى ورحمة للذين هم لربهم يرهبون

translation: And Moses chose from his people seventy men for Our appointed time. And when the earthquake seized them, he said, 'My Lord, if You had willed, You could have destroyed them before and me [as well]. Would You destroy us for what the foolish among us have done? This is not but Your trial by which You send astray whom You will and guide whom You will. You are our Protector, so forgive us and have mercy upon us; and You are the best of forgivers.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the concept of divine testing and the mercy of Allah. Moses, after witnessing the earthquake that struck his chosen group, acknowledges that such trials are part of Allah's plan to test and guide His servants. He recognizes that Allah's will is supreme and that He can guide or lead astray as He sees fit. Moses appeals to Allah's mercy, asking for forgiveness not just for himself but for his people, emphasizing the belief in Allah as the ultimate Protector and the most forgiving. This reflects the Islamic teaching that while humans are accountable for their actions, they can always turn to Allah in repentance, seeking His forgiveness and guidance.
orig: واختار موسى قومه سبعين رجلا لميقاتنا فلما أخذتهم الرجفة قال رب لو شئت أهلكتهم من قبل وإياي أتهلكنا بما فعل السفهاء منا إن هي إلا فتنتك تضل بها من تشاء وتهدي من تشاء أنت ولينا فاغفر لنا وارحمنا وأنت خير الغافرين

translation: And write for us in this world [that which is] good and in the Hereafter; indeed, we have turned to You. [Allah] said, 'My punishment - I afflict with it whom I will, but My mercy encompasses all things. So I will decree it for those who fear Allah and give zakah, and those who believe in Our verses.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the dual nature of divine justice and mercy. It reflects the human plea for goodness in both worldly life and the hereafter, acknowledging their submission to God. God's response underscores His absolute authority to punish, yet His mercy is all-encompassing. The promise of mercy is specifically directed towards those who exhibit piety, fulfill their obligation of zakah, and have faith in the divine signs, illustrating that these acts of righteousness are pathways to receiving God's mercy.
orig: واكتب لنا في هذه الدنيا حسنة وفي الآخرة إنا هدنا إليك قال عذابي أصيب به من أشاء ورحمتي وسعت كل شيء فسأكتبها للذين يتقون ويؤتون الزكاة والذين هم بآياتنا يؤمنون

translation: Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, whom they find written in what they have of the Torah and the Gospel, who enjoins upon them what is right and forbids them what is wrong and makes lawful for them the good things and prohibits for them the evil and relieves them of their burden and the shackles which were upon them. So those who have believed in him, honored him, helped him and followed the light which was sent down with him - it is those who will be successful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of following Prophet Muhammad, who is described as the unlettered Prophet foretold in the previous scriptures, the Torah and the Gospel. The verse highlights his role in guiding the community towards righteousness by commanding what is good and forbidding what is evil. It also signifies the liberation that comes with his message, as he relieves believers of unnecessary burdens and restrictions. The verse concludes by stating that those who believe in him, respect him, support him, and follow the divine guidance revealed through him will achieve success in both this world and the hereafter. This success is not merely material but encompasses spiritual fulfillment and salvation.
orig: الذين يتبعون الرسول النبي الأمي الذي يجدونه مكتوبا عندهم في التوراة والإنجيل يأمرهم بالمعروف وينهاهم عن المنكر ويحل لهم الطيبات ويحرم عليهم الخبائث ويضع عنهم إصرهم والأغلال التي كانت عليهم فالذين آمنوا به وعزروه ونصروه واتبعوا النور الذي أنزل معه أولئك هم المفلحون

translation: Say, 'O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of Allah to you all, [from Him] to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. There is no deity except Him; He gives life and causes death. So believe in Allah and His Messenger, the unlettered prophet, who believes in Allah and His words, and follow him that you may be guided.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universal message of Prophet Muhammad, sent by Allah, the sole creator and ruler of the universe, who has the power over life and death. It calls upon all of humanity to believe in the oneness of Allah and to accept Muhammad as His final messenger, who, despite being unlettered, fully believes in Allah and His revelations. The verse urges people to follow the Prophet's guidance to attain true righteousness and divine guidance.
orig: قل يا أيها الناس إني رسول الله إليكم جميعا الذي له ملك السماوات والأرض لا إله إلا هو يحيي ويميت فآمنوا بالله ورسوله النبي الأمي الذي يؤمن بالله وكلماته واتبعوه لعلكم تهتدون

translation: And among the people of Moses is a community which guides by truth and by it establishes justice.
interpretation: This verse highlights the existence of a righteous group within the followers of Moses who not only adhere to the truth but also use it as a guiding principle to establish justice in their community. It emphasizes the importance of truth as a tool for guidance and the establishment of a just society, reflecting the ideal that religious guidance should lead to equitable and fair treatment among people.
orig: ومن قوم موسى أمة يهدون بالحق وبه يعدلون

translation: And We divided them into twelve tribes as nations. And We inspired to Moses, when his people asked him for water, 'Strike the rock with your staff.' So there gushed forth from it twelve springs. Every people knew its watering place. And We shaded them with clouds and sent down upon them manna and quails. [We said], 'Eat of the good things with which We have provided you.' And they wronged Us not - but they were [only] wronging themselves.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine providence and guidance provided to the Israelites through Moses. The splitting into twelve tribes signifies organization and the establishment of a structured community under divine guidance. The miracle of water from the rock, with twelve springs, symbolizes God's ability to provide for the needs of His people in miraculous ways, tailored to each tribe's needs. The shading with clouds and the provision of manna and quails further illustrate God's continuous care and sustenance. The verse emphasizes that the Israelites' hardships were not due to God's injustice but rather a result of their own actions, underscoring the theme of personal responsibility and the consequences of one's choices.
orig: وقطعناهم اثنتي عشرة أسباطا أمما وأوحينا إلى موسى إذ استسقاه قومه أن اضرب بعصاك الحجر فانبجست منه اثنتا عشرة عينا قد علم كل أناس مشربهم وظللنا عليهم الغمام وأنزلنا عليهم المن والسلوى كلوا من طيبات ما رزقناكم وما ظلمونا ولكن كانوا أنفسهم يظلمون

translation: And [mention] when it was said to them, 'Dwell in this town and eat from it wherever you will and say, 'Relieve us of our burden,' and enter the gate bowing humbly; We will forgive you your sins. We will increase the doers of good.'
interpretation: This verse refers to the instructions given to the Children of Israel after their exodus from Egypt. It emphasizes the importance of obedience to divine commandments, humility, and the promise of forgiveness and reward for those who follow God's guidance. The specific acts of saying 'ḥiṭṭah' (a plea for forgiveness), entering the gate in a state of humility, and the general call to dwell and eat freely in the town, symbolize a covenant between God and the people, highlighting themes of repentance, submission, and divine mercy.
orig: وإذ قيل لهم اسكنوا هذه القرية وكلوا منها حيث شئتم وقولوا حطة وادخلوا الباب سجدا نغفر لكم خطيئاتكم سنزيد المحسنين

translation: So those who did wrong changed the word from that which had been told to them. So We sent upon them a punishment from the heaven because they were doing wrong.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the consequences of altering divine commandments or messages. It highlights that when individuals or groups deliberately change or disobey the instructions given by God, they invite divine retribution. The 'punishment from the heaven' symbolizes a direct and severe consequence from God, emphasizing the seriousness of their disobedience and the inevitable justice that follows wrongdoing.
orig: فبدل الذين ظلموا منهم قولا غير الذي قيل لهم فأرسلنا عليهم رجزا من السماء بما كانوا يظلمون

translation: And ask them about the town that was by the sea, when they transgressed in the matter of the Sabbath. When their fish came to them openly on their Sabbath day, and did not come to them on the day they had no Sabbath. Thus did We try them because they were defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of the People of the Sabbath, a community that was tested by God due to their disobedience. The test involved the miraculous appearance of fish on the Sabbath day, which was meant to be a day of rest and worship, not for worldly activities like fishing. The fish would come to them only on the Sabbath, tempting them to break the sacred day. This was a trial from God to see if they would adhere to His commandments or succumb to their desires. Their failure in this test led to their punishment, illustrating the consequences of defying God's laws and the importance of obedience and faith.
orig: واسألهم عن القرية التي كانت حاضرة البحر إذ يعدون في السبت إذ تأتيهم حيتانهم يوم سبتهم شرعا ويوم لا يسبتون لا تأتيهم كذلك نبلوهم بما كانوا يفسقون

translation: And [mention] when a faction of them said, 'Why do you advise a people whom Allah is [about] to destroy or to punish with a severe punishment?' They said, 'To be absolved before your Lord and perhaps they may fear Allah.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the internal dialogue among the Children of Israel regarding their duty to warn the people of impending divine punishment. It reflects a moral and ethical debate about the responsibility to guide others towards righteousness, even when it seems futile. The faction questioning the advisement suggests a resignation to fate, while the response emphasizes the importance of fulfilling one's duty to warn others as a means of seeking exoneration before God, and in hope that it might lead some to piety and fear of God.
orig: وإذ قالت أمة منهم لم تعظون قوما الله مهلكهم أو معذبهم عذابا شديدا قالوا معذرة إلى ربكم ولعلهم يتقون

translation: So when they forgot that by which they had been reminded, We saved those who forbade evil and seized those who wronged with a wretched punishment because they were defiantly disobeying.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequence of heedlessness after receiving divine guidance. It emphasizes that when a community neglects the reminders and warnings given to them, God intervenes by saving the righteous individuals who actively discouraged wrongdoing, while punishing those who persisted in their oppression and disobedience. The 'wretched punishment' serves as a manifestation of divine justice, underscoring the importance of adhering to moral and ethical standards as outlined in the reminders provided by God.
orig: فلما نسوا ما ذكروا به أنجينا الذين ينهون عن السوء وأخذنا الذين ظلموا بعذاب بئيس بما كانوا يفسقون

translation: So when they exceeded the limits of what they were forbidden from, We said to them, "Be apes, despised."
interpretation: This verse refers to a specific incident where a group of people transgressed the boundaries set by God, specifically by fishing on the Sabbath despite being forbidden to do so. As a consequence of their disobedience and arrogance, God transformed them into apes as a punishment and a sign of their degradation. This serves as a warning to all believers about the severe consequences of deliberately disobeying God's commands and the importance of adhering to divine prohibitions.
orig: فلما عتوا عن ما نهوا عنه قلنا لهم كونوا قردة خاسئين

translation: And [mention] when your Lord declared that He would surely send upon them, until the Day of Resurrection, those who would subject them to severe torment. Indeed, your Lord is swift in penalty, but indeed, He is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the dual nature of God's justice and mercy. It serves as a reminder that while God can impose severe punishment on those who deserve it, His swiftness in penalty is balanced by His forgiveness and mercy. This duality encourages believers to be mindful of their actions, knowing that while divine retribution is certain for wrongdoers, repentance and seeking forgiveness can lead to God's mercy, which is always available.
orig: وإذ تأذن ربك ليبعثن عليهم إلى يوم القيامة من يسومهم سوء العذاب إن ربك لسريع العقاب وإنه لغفور رحيم

translation: And We have dispersed them throughout the earth as nations. Among them are the righteous, and among them are otherwise. And We tested them with good and evil, so that they may return.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the diversity of human conditions and moral standings as a divine test. Allah has spread humanity across the earth in various groups, where individuals exhibit a range of behaviors from righteousness to less than that. The trials of life, both positive and negative, are designed by Allah to encourage people to reflect on their actions and potentially return to the right path. This testing is a manifestation of Allah's mercy, offering everyone an opportunity for spiritual growth and redemption.
orig: وقطعناهم في الأرض أمما منهم الصالحون ومنهم دون ذلك وبلوناهم بالحسنات والسيئات لعلهم يرجعون

translation: Then, after them, came successors who inherited the Scripture, taking the fleeting gains of this lower world and saying, 'We will be forgiven.' But if similar fleeting gains come to them, they take them. Was not the covenant of the Scripture taken from them that they would not say about Allah except the truth, while they studied what was in it? And the Home of the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah. Then will you not use reason?
interpretation: This verse critiques those who inherit religious texts but prioritize worldly gains over spiritual values. It highlights the hypocrisy of claiming forgiveness while continuously indulging in material pursuits. The verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to the truth as conveyed in the scripture, which they have studied, and reminds believers that the afterlife offers a superior reward for the pious. It challenges the reader to reflect on their actions and priorities, urging a deeper understanding and application of religious teachings.
orig: فخلف من بعدهم خلف ورثوا الكتاب يأخذون عرض هذا الأدنى ويقولون سيغفر لنا وإن يأتهم عرض مثله يأخذوه ألم يؤخذ عليهم ميثاق الكتاب أن لا يقولوا على الله إلا الحق ودرسوا ما فيه والدار الآخرة خير للذين يتقون أفلا تعقلون

translation: And those who hold fast to the Scripture and establish prayer - indeed, We will not let the reward of the reformers be lost.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to the divine guidance as revealed in the Scripture and maintaining regular prayer. It assures that those who engage in these acts of worship and strive to improve themselves and their society (the reformers) will be rewarded by Allah. The promise of not losing the reward of the reformers serves as a motivation for believers to persist in their efforts towards righteousness and societal betterment, highlighting Allah's justice and recognition of good deeds.
orig: والذين يمسكون بالكتاب وأقاموا الصلاة إنا لا نضيع أجر المصلحين

translation: And [mention] when We raised the mountain above them as if it were a canopy, and they thought it was going to fall upon them: 'Take what We have given you with determination and remember what is in it that you might become righteous.'
interpretation: This verse refers to a significant event in the history of the Children of Israel, where God raised Mount Sinai above them to emphasize the importance of the Torah and the covenant they were about to enter. The mountain being raised 'as if it were a canopy' symbolizes the protective and guiding nature of the divine law, while the fear that it might fall upon them represents the gravity and seriousness of adhering to God's commandments. The instruction to 'take what We have given you with determination' urges them to embrace the Torah with strength and commitment, and to 'remember what is in it' highlights the importance of continuous reflection on the teachings to foster righteousness and piety.
orig: وإذ نتقنا الجبل فوقهم كأنه ظلة وظنوا أنه واقع بهم خذوا ما آتيناكم بقوة واذكروا ما فيه لعلكم تتقون

translation: And [mention] when your Lord took from the children of Adam - from their loins - their descendants and made them testify of themselves, [saying to them], 'Am I not your Lord?' They said, 'Yes, we have testified.' [This] lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, 'Indeed, we were of this unaware.'
interpretation: This verse refers to the concept of the primordial covenant, where Allah took a covenant from all human souls before their earthly existence. This covenant is a testimony from every soul acknowledging Allah as their Lord, ensuring that no one can claim ignorance of this fundamental truth on the Day of Judgment. It underscores the innate recognition of Allah in every human being, highlighting the accountability and responsibility humans have towards their Creator from the very beginning of their existence.
orig: وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم من ظهورهم ذريتهم وأشهدهم على أنفسهم ألست بربكم قالوا بلى شهدنا أن تقولوا يوم القيامة إنا كنا عن هذا غافلين

translation: Or you say, 'It was only our forefathers who associated others with Allah before, and we were their descendants after them. So are You going to destroy us for what the falsifiers have done?'
interpretation: This verse addresses the argument some people might make on the Day of Judgment, claiming that they should not be punished for the idolatry of their ancestors. It reflects the human tendency to shift blame and avoid personal responsibility for one's actions. The verse emphasizes that each individual is accountable for their own deeds, regardless of the actions of their forebears. It serves as a reminder of the importance of personal faith and the rejection of idolatry, urging believers to not follow in the footsteps of those who strayed from the path of monotheism.
orig: أو تقولوا إنما أشرك آباؤنا من قبل وكنا ذرية من بعدهم أفتهلكنا بما فعل المبطلون

translation: And thus We explain the verses in detail, and so that they may return.
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah, in His mercy, provides detailed explanations of the Qur'anic verses to guide humanity. The purpose is to offer clear signs and guidance so that people might reflect on their actions and return to the right path, seeking forgiveness and rectifying their ways.
orig: وكذلك نفصل الآيات ولعلهم يرجعون

translation: And recite to them the news of him to whom We gave Our signs, but he detached himself from them; so Satan followed him, and he became of those who went astray.
