translation: And those who believed afterwards, and emigrated and strove hard along with you, they are of you. But kindred by blood are nearer to one another (regarding inheritance) in the decree of Allah. Verily, Allah is the All-Knower of everything.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity and brotherhood among Muslims, particularly those who have embraced Islam, migrated, and fought alongside the Prophet Muhammad. It highlights that these individuals are considered part of the Muslim community, reinforcing the concept of a unified ummah. However, it also acknowledges the natural and legal precedence of blood relatives in matters of inheritance, as decreed by Allah. This balance between communal solidarity and familial rights underscores Allah's comprehensive knowledge and wisdom in legislating for human affairs.
orig: والذين آمنوا من بعد وهاجروا وجاهدوا معكم فأولئك منكم وأولو الأرحام بعضهم أولى ببعض في كتاب الله إن الله بكل شيء عليم

translation: A declaration of immunity from Allah and His Messenger to those of the pagans with whom you have made a treaty.
interpretation: This verse signifies a formal announcement of disengagement and release from obligations towards the polytheists who had previously made treaties with the Muslims. It reflects a pivotal moment where the Muslims, under divine guidance, are instructed to no longer honor agreements with those who have persistently violated their pacts and shown hostility towards Islam. This declaration emphasizes the importance of upholding justice and integrity in treaties, while also highlighting the necessity of taking decisive action against persistent breaches of trust.
orig: براءة من الله ورسوله إلى الذين عاهدتم من المشركين

translation: So travel freely, [O disbelievers], throughout the land [during] four months but know that you cannot escape [the punishment of] Allah and that Allah will disgrace the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse addresses the disbelievers who had violated their treaty with the Prophet Muhammad. It grants them a period of four months to move freely in the land, which serves as a grace period for them to reconsider their stance and possibly embrace Islam. However, the verse also emphasizes the inevitability of divine judgment, indicating that no matter where they go, they cannot avoid Allah's decree. The mention of Allah disgracing the disbelievers serves as a warning of the consequences of persisting in disbelief and opposition to the message of Islam.
orig: فسيحوا في الأرض أربعة أشهر واعلموا أنكم غير معجزي الله وأن الله مخزي الكافرين

translation: And a declaration from Allah and His Messenger to mankind on the day of the greater pilgrimage that Allah is free from (all) obligations to the polytheists, and so is His Messenger. So if you repent, it is better for you, but if you turn away, then know that you cannot escape Allah. And give tidings to those who disbelieve of a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse signifies a pivotal moment in Islamic history, marking the end of any treaty or obligation between the Muslim community and the polytheists. It was proclaimed during the Farewell Pilgrimage, emphasizing that Allah and His Messenger are no longer bound by previous agreements with those who associate partners with Allah. The verse offers a clear ultimatum: repentance is encouraged and beneficial, but continued disbelief will lead to inescapable divine retribution. It underscores the themes of divine justice, the finality of the prophetic message, and the consequences of rejecting faith, serving as a warning and a call to embrace Islam before it is too late.
orig: وأذان من الله ورسوله إلى الناس يوم الحج الأكبر أن الله بريء من المشركين ورسوله فإن تبتم فهو خير لكم وإن توليتم فاعلموا أنكم غير معجزي الله وبشر الذين كفروا بعذاب أليم

translation: Except for those with whom you made a treaty among the polytheists and then they have not been deficient toward you in anything or supported anyone against you; so complete for them their treaty until their term. Indeed, Allah loves the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of honoring treaties and agreements, even with those who are not of the same faith, as long as they uphold their end of the agreement. It highlights the value of integrity and righteousness in dealings with others, reflecting Allah's love for those who maintain such qualities. The verse serves as a directive for Muslims to fulfill their obligations and commitments, promoting peace and trust in interfaith relations.
orig: إلا الذين عاهدتم من المشركين ثم لم ينقصوكم شيئا ولم يظاهروا عليكم أحدا فأتموا إليهم عهدهم إلى مدتهم إن الله يحب المتقين

translation: So when the sacred months have passed, then kill the polytheists wherever you find them and capture them and besiege them and sit in wait for them at every place of ambush. But if they should repent, establish prayer, and give zakah, let them [go] on their way. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse is situated in the context of a specific historical event, the annulment of the treaty of Hudaybiyah, which was violated by the polytheists. It instructs the Muslims to engage in combat against those who broke the treaty and continued to oppose Islam after the sacred months, a period during which fighting was prohibited, had ended. However, the verse also emphasizes the mercy and forgiveness of Allah, offering the polytheists a chance to repent and join the Muslim community by adhering to its fundamental practices of prayer and charity. This reflects the Qur'an's broader theme of combining justice with mercy, providing an opportunity for reconciliation and peace even amidst conflict.
orig: فإذا انسلخ الأشهر الحرم فاقتلوا المشركين حيث وجدتموهم وخذوهم واحصروهم واقعدوا لهم كل مرصد فإن تابوا وأقاموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة فخلوا سبيلهم إن الله غفور رحيم

translation: And if any one of the polytheists seeks your protection, then grant him protection so that he may hear the words of Allah. Then deliver him to his place of safety. That is because they are a people who do not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of extending protection and safety to those who seek it, even if they are from opposing groups like the polytheists. It reflects the Islamic principle of offering refuge and the opportunity for dialogue and understanding, allowing them to hear the message of Islam. The verse also acknowledges the ignorance of those who oppose Islam, suggesting that their hostility stems from a lack of knowledge, thereby advocating for patience and education rather than immediate condemnation or conflict.
orig: وإن أحد من المشركين استجارك فأجره حتى يسمع كلام الله ثم أبلغه مأمنه ذلك بأنهم قوم لا يعلمون

translation: How can there be a treaty with Allah and His Messenger for the polytheists, except for those with whom you made a treaty near the Sacred Mosque? As long as they are upright toward you, be upright toward them. Indeed, Allah loves the righteous.
interpretation: This verse addresses the issue of treaties between Muslims and polytheists, emphasizing that generally, such treaties are not valid or acceptable to Allah and His Messenger due to the inherent conflict between the two groups' beliefs and objectives. However, an exception is made for those polytheists who had entered into a treaty near the Sacred Mosque in Mecca. The verse instructs Muslims to uphold their part of the treaty as long as the polytheists remain faithful to it, reflecting the Islamic principle of honoring agreements. This directive is grounded in the broader Islamic value of righteousness, as Allah's love for the righteous is highlighted, suggesting that maintaining justice and integrity in dealings, even with those of differing faiths, is a path to divine favor.
orig: كيف يكون للمشركين عهد عند الله وعند رسوله إلا الذين عاهدتم عند المسجد الحرام فما استقاموا لكم فاستقيموا لهم إن الله يحب المتقين

translation: How [can there be a treaty] while, if they gain dominance over you, they do not observe concerning you any pact of kinship or covenant of protection? They satisfy you with their mouths, but their hearts refuse [compliance], and most of them are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy and unreliability of those who outwardly profess peace and alliance but inwardly harbor enmity and deceit. It warns believers to be cautious of those who may appear friendly but are not bound by moral or religious obligations, as their true intentions are contrary to their words. The verse underscores the importance of discerning the sincerity of others, especially in matters of treaties and agreements, and recognizing that many among the adversaries are morally corrupt and likely to break their promises.
orig: كيف وإن يظهروا عليكم لا يرقبوا فيكم إلا ولا ذمة يرضونكم بأفواههم وتأبى قلوبهم وأكثرهم فاسقون

translation: They have purchased with the verses of Allah a small price, so they hinder (people) from His path. Indeed, evil is what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse criticizes those who trade the divine guidance and revelations from Allah for worldly gains, which are insignificant in comparison to the spiritual rewards. By doing so, they obstruct others from following the path of righteousness, leading them astray. The verse emphasizes the moral corruption and the severe consequences of such actions, highlighting that their deeds are fundamentally wrong and harmful.
orig: اشتروا بآيات الله ثمنا قليلا فصدوا عن سبيله إنهم ساء ما كانوا يعملون

translation: They do not respect in a believer either kinship or covenant. And it is they who are the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse highlights the moral and ethical bankruptcy of those who disregard the bonds of kinship and the sanctity of covenants when dealing with believers. It underscores that such actions are not only violations of social norms but also transgressions against divine principles, labeling those who commit such acts as oppressors and wrongdoers in the eyes of God.
orig: لا يرقبون في مؤمن إلا ولا ذمة وأولئك هم المعتدون

translation: But if they repent and establish prayer and give zakah, then they are your brothers in religion; and We detail the verses for a people who know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of repentance, prayer, and charity as fundamental aspects of faith. It suggests that through these actions, individuals can be considered part of the Muslim community, highlighting the inclusivity and brotherhood within Islam. The verse also indicates that the Qur'an provides clear guidance for those who seek understanding, reinforcing the idea that knowledge and practice of the religion go hand in hand.
orig: فإن تابوا وأقاموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة فإخوانكم في الدين ونفصل الآيات لقوم يعلمون

translation: And if they break their oaths after their treaty and defame your religion, then fight the leaders of disbelief - indeed, they have no [binding] oaths - so that they might cease.
interpretation: This verse instructs Muslims to engage in combat against the leaders of disbelief if they violate their treaties and insult Islam. The focus on leaders suggests a strategic approach to warfare, targeting those who guide and influence disbelief rather than the general populace. The phrase 'they have no [binding] oaths' indicates that such leaders cannot be trusted to honor their agreements, justifying the defensive action. The ultimate goal of this fighting is not destruction but to bring about a cessation of hostility and aggression against Muslims, aiming for peace and security.
orig: وإن نكثوا أيمانهم من بعد عهدهم وطعنوا في دينكم فقاتلوا أئمة الكفر إنهم لا أيمان لهم لعلهم ينتهون

translation: Will you not fight a people who broke their oaths and determined to expel the Messenger, and they attacked you first? Do you fear them? But Allah has more right that you should fear Him, if you are believers.
interpretation: This verse encourages the believers to engage in defensive combat against those who have violated their treaties, plotted to expel the Prophet Muhammad, and initiated aggression. It emphasizes that fear of Allah should outweigh any fear of the enemy, highlighting the importance of faith and trust in Allah over worldly fears when defending the community and its values.
orig: ألا تقاتلون قوما نكثوا أيمانهم وهموا بإخراج الرسول وهم بدءوكم أول مرة أتخشونهم فالله أحق أن تخشوه إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: Fight them; Allah will punish them by your hands and will disgrace them and give you victory over them, and He will heal the breasts of a believing people.
interpretation: This verse instructs believers to engage in combat against those who oppose them, emphasizing that such action is a means through which Allah will exact punishment on the adversaries through the believers' efforts. It highlights the divine support and victory that believers will receive, as well as the emotional and spiritual relief that will come to the faithful as a result of their perseverance and trust in Allah's plan.
orig: قاتلوهم يعذبهم الله بأيديكم ويخزهم وينصركم عليهم ويشف صدور قوم مؤمنين

translation: And He removes the rage from their hearts, and Allah forgives whom He wills. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's mercy and wisdom in dealing with human emotions and forgiveness. The removal of rage from the hearts signifies the spiritual healing and peace that Allah can grant to believers, transforming their inner states from anger to tranquility. The phrase 'Allah forgives whom He wills' underscores the divine prerogative in granting forgiveness, emphasizing that it is not an automatic right but a gift from Allah, based on His knowledge and wisdom. The attributes 'Knowing and Wise' affirm that Allah's decisions are perfectly informed and judicious, reflecting His complete understanding of each individual's circumstances and intentions.
orig: ويذهب غيظ قلوبهم ويتوب الله على من يشاء والله عليم حكيم

translation: Or do you think that you will be left [as you are] while Allah has not yet made evident those who strive among you and do not take other than Allah, His Messenger, and the believers as intimate associates? And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.
interpretation: This verse challenges the believers not to assume they will be left unexamined or untested. It emphasizes that Allah will distinguish those who truly strive in His cause, demonstrating their faith not only through words but through actions. The verse highlights the importance of loyalty and allegiance solely to Allah, His Messenger, and the community of believers, rather than forming alliances or seeking support from other sources. It serves as a reminder that Allah is fully aware of all deeds, and the trials believers face are a means for Allah to manifest their sincerity and commitment.
orig: أم حسبتم أن تتركوا ولما يعلم الله الذين جاهدوا منكم ولم يتخذوا من دون الله ولا رسوله ولا المؤمنين وليجة والله خبير بما تعملون

translation: It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of Allah while they witness against themselves with disbelief. Those - their deeds have become worthless, and in the Fire they will abide eternally.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the spiritual and moral disqualification of polytheists from maintaining or overseeing the mosques of Allah. It highlights that their open acknowledgment of disbelief nullifies any religious acts they might perform, rendering their deeds void in the eyes of Allah. The verse serves as a warning about the consequences of associating partners with Allah, underscoring that such actions lead to eternal damnation in the hereafter.
orig: ما كان للمشركين أن يعمروا مساجد الله شاهدين على أنفسهم بالكفر أولئك حبطت أعمالهم وفي النار هم خالدون

translation: The mosques of Allah are only maintained by those who believe in Allah and the Last Day, and establish prayer and give zakah, and do not fear except Allah. It is expected that those will be of the guided ones.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the true caretakers and maintainers of the mosques are those who possess a deep faith in Allah and the Hereafter, consistently perform their prayers, and fulfill their obligation of zakah. These individuals are characterized by their fear of Allah alone, not being swayed by worldly fears or pressures. The verse suggests that such people are likely to be among those who are rightly guided, indicating that their actions and dedication to these pillars of faith are signs of true guidance and righteousness.
orig: إنما يعمر مساجد الله من آمن بالله واليوم الآخر وأقام الصلاة وآتى الزكاة ولم يخش إلا الله فعسى أولئك أن يكونوا من المهتدين

translation: Do you consider the providing of drinking water to the pilgrims and the maintenance of the Sacred Mosque to be equal to the one who believes in Allah and the Last Day and strives in the way of Allah? They are not equal in the sight of Allah. And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that while acts of charity and service, such as providing water to pilgrims and maintaining the Sacred Mosque, are commendable, they do not equate to the spiritual and moral value of faith in Allah, belief in the Last Day, and striving in Allah's path. The verse highlights a hierarchy of deeds in the eyes of Allah, where sincere faith and active struggle in His cause hold a higher status than purely physical acts of service. It also serves as a reminder that Allah's guidance is not extended to those who engage in wrongdoing, indicating that the quality and intention behind one's actions are crucial in determining their value and acceptance by Allah.
orig: أجعلتم سقاية الحاج وعمارة المسجد الحرام كمن آمن بالله واليوم الآخر وجاهد في سبيل الله لا يستوون عند الله والله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: Those who believed and emigrated and strove in the way of Allah with their wealth and their lives are of greater rank with Allah, and it is they who are the successful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the high status and ultimate success granted by Allah to those who have faith, migrated from their homes for the sake of their faith, and exerted their efforts, both financially and personally, in striving for Allah's cause. It highlights that such comprehensive dedication and sacrifice in the path of righteousness elevates one's standing in the eyes of Allah, leading to true success in both this life and the hereafter.
orig: الذين آمنوا وهاجروا وجاهدوا في سبيل الله بأموالهم وأنفسهم أعظم درجة عند الله وأولئك هم الفائزون

translation: Their Lord gives them glad tidings of mercy from Him and good pleasure and Gardens wherein is lasting bliss.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the believers about the rewards awaiting them in the Hereafter. The "mercy" and "good pleasure" from Allah signify His acceptance and love for those who have lived righteously. The "Gardens wherein is lasting bliss" represent Paradise, a place of eternal joy and happiness, which is promised to the faithful as a reward for their faith and good deeds. This promise serves as a motivation for believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to strive for righteousness in their lives.
orig: يبشرهم ربهم برحمة منه ورضوان وجنات لهم فيها نعيم مقيم

translation: Abiding therein forever. Indeed, with Allah is a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the eternal nature of the reward in the hereafter for those who are righteous. It reassures believers that the ultimate recompense for their faith and good deeds lies with Allah, and it is immense and everlasting. The phrase 'with Allah' highlights that this reward is divinely ordained and beyond human measure, encouraging steadfastness and hope in divine justice and mercy.
orig: خالدين فيها أبدا إن الله عنده أجر عظيم

translation: O you who have believed, do not take your fathers and your brothers as allies if they prefer disbelief over belief. And whoever among you takes them as allies, then it is those who are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of prioritizing faith over familial ties. It instructs believers not to align themselves with their family members if those relatives choose disbelief over faith. The verse highlights that choosing to support or ally with disbelieving family members, despite their stance against faith, constitutes wrongdoing. It underscores the principle that loyalty to God and His teachings should supersede even the closest of human relationships, reflecting the ultimate allegiance a believer must have to their faith.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتخذوا آباءكم وإخوانكم أولياء إن استحبوا الكفر على الإيمان ومن يتولهم منكم فأولئك هم الظالمون

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], 'If your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your wives, your clan, the wealth that you have gained, the commerce wherein you fear a decline, and the dwellings with which you are pleased are more beloved to you than Allah and His Messenger and striving in His cause, then wait until Allah executes His command. And Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.'
interpretation: This verse challenges believers to reflect on their priorities and loyalties. It suggests that if one values worldly relationships and possessions more than their devotion to Allah, His Messenger, and the struggle in His path, they are misguided. The verse warns that such misplaced priorities indicate a deviation from the path of righteousness, and those who persist in this state should await the consequences of Allah's decree, as He does not guide those who are defiantly disobedient.
orig: قل إن كان آباؤكم وأبناؤكم وإخوانكم وأزواجكم وعشيرتكم وأموال اقترفتموها وتجارة تخشون كسادها ومساكن ترضونها أحب إليكم من الله ورسوله وجهاد في سبيله فتربصوا حتى يأتي الله بأمره والله لا يهدي القوم الفاسقين

translation: Indeed, Allah has helped you in many places, and [remember] the Day of Hunayn when your great number pleased you, but it did not avail you at all, and the earth, vast as it is, was straitened for you, then you turned back in retreat.
interpretation: This verse reflects on the Battle of Hunayn, where the Muslims, despite their large numbers, initially faced defeat due to overconfidence. It teaches that numerical strength or material advantage does not guarantee success; rather, reliance on Allah and humility are crucial. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of spiritual strength and trust in Allah over worldly means, illustrating how the vastness of the earth felt constricting due to their fear and lack of faith, leading to their retreat.
orig: لقد نصركم الله في مواطن كثيرة ويوم حنين إذ أعجبتكم كثرتكم فلم تغن عنكم شيئا وضاقت عليكم الأرض بما رحبت ثم وليتم مدبرين

translation: Then Allah sent down His tranquillity upon His Messenger and upon the believers, and He sent down forces which you did not see, and He punished those who disbelieved. And that is the recompense of the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine support and protection provided by Allah to His Messenger and the believers during times of trial or battle. The 'tranquillity' mentioned refers to a sense of peace and calmness that Allah bestows, which helps in maintaining steadfastness and courage. The 'forces which you did not see' indicate the unseen help from Allah, possibly through angels or other unseen means, which played a crucial role in the outcome of the event. The punishment of the disbelievers serves as a reminder of the consequences of rejecting faith, emphasizing that disbelief leads to a just retribution from Allah.
orig: ثم أنزل الله سكينته على رسوله وعلى المؤمنين وأنزل جنودا لم تروها وعذب الذين كفروا وذلك جزاء الكافرين

translation: Then Allah, after that, accepts the repentance of whom He wills. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's attribute of forgiveness and mercy, indicating that even after a person has committed a sin, Allah may still accept their repentance if He wills. It highlights the hope that sinners can have in Allah's boundless mercy, encouraging them to turn back to Him in sincere repentance. The phrase 'whom He wills' underscores that Allah's forgiveness is a divine prerogative, bestowed according to His wisdom and knowledge of the hearts of His servants.
orig: ثم يتوب الله من بعد ذلك على من يشاء والله غفور رحيم

translation: O you who have believed, indeed the polytheists are unclean, so let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram after this year of theirs. And if you fear poverty, Allah will enrich you from His bounty if He wills. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse addresses the believers, emphasizing the prohibition of polytheists entering the Sacred Mosque in Mecca after a specified year, highlighting the sanctity and purity required for such a holy place. It reassures the believers that if they fear economic loss due to this prohibition, Allah promises to provide for them from His bounty, indicating that trust in Allah's provision should supersede material concerns. The verse underscores Allah's attributes of being All-Knowing and Wise, affirming that His commands and promises are based on complete knowledge and wisdom.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إنما المشركون نجس فلا يقربوا المسجد الحرام بعد عامهم هذا وإن خفتم عيلة فسوف يغنيكم الله من فضله إن شاء إن الله عليم حكيم

translation: Fight those who do not believe in Allah nor in the Last Day, nor forbid what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, nor follow the religion of truth, from among those who were given the Scripture, until they pay the jizyah willingly while they are humbled.
interpretation: This verse is often cited in discussions about jihad and the treatment of non-Muslims in Islamic law. It specifically addresses the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) who have not accepted Islam. The verse mandates fighting against them if they do not pay the jizyah, a tax levied on non-Muslims in lieu of military service and as a sign of their submission to Islamic rule. The underlying principle is the establishment of Islamic governance and the propagation of Islamic values, with the jizyah serving as a means to integrate non-Muslims into the Islamic state under certain conditions of humility and acknowledgment of Muslim authority. This verse reflects the historical context of early Islamic expansion and the need to consolidate power and ensure the security and order of the nascent Muslim community.
orig: قاتلوا الذين لا يؤمنون بالله ولا باليوم الآخر ولا يحرمون ما حرم الله ورسوله ولا يدينون دين الحق من الذين أوتوا الكتاب حتى يعطوا الجزية عن يد وهم صاغرون

translation: And the Jews say, "Ezra is the son of Allah," and the Christians say, "The Messiah is the son of Allah." That is their statement from their mouths; they imitate the saying of those who disbelieved before. May Allah destroy them; how are they deluded?
interpretation: This verse critiques the theological assertions made by some Jews and Christians regarding the divinity of human figures, specifically Ezra and Jesus, respectively. It suggests that such claims are not only false but also echo the disbelief of earlier communities who similarly attributed divine status to human beings. The verse expresses a strong condemnation of these beliefs, emphasizing the gravity of attributing divinity to anyone other than Allah, and prays for divine retribution against those who perpetuate such falsehoods, highlighting the severity of their misguidance.
orig: وقالت اليهود عزير ابن الله وقالت النصارى المسيح ابن الله ذلك قولهم بأفواههم يضاهئون قول الذين كفروا من قبل قاتلهم الله أنى يؤفكون

translation: They have taken their scholars and monks as lords besides Allah, and [also] the Messiah, the son of Mary. And they were not commanded except to worship one God; there is no deity except Him. Exalted is He above whatever they associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse critiques the practice of elevating religious figures and human leaders to a divine status, which is a form of shirk (associating partners with Allah). It specifically addresses Christians who venerate Jesus and religious leaders excessively, suggesting that such actions deviate from the core monotheistic principle of worshipping only Allah. The verse emphasizes the purity and singularity of Allah, asserting His transcendence over any false associations or idolatry.
orig: اتخذوا أحبارهم ورهبانهم أربابا من دون الله والمسيح ابن مريم وما أمروا إلا ليعبدوا إلها واحدا لا إله إلا هو سبحانه عما يشركون

translation: They want to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah refuses except to perfect His light, even though the disbelievers dislike it.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futile efforts of those who oppose the divine message and guidance of Allah. Despite their attempts to suppress or undermine the truth through their words and actions, Allah's guidance and light will inevitably prevail and reach its completion. The term 'light of Allah' symbolizes the truth, guidance, and the message of Islam, which cannot be extinguished by the disbelief or opposition of the disbelievers. This verse reassures believers of the ultimate triumph of Allah's plan and the spread of His message, regardless of the resistance it faces.
orig: يريدون أن يطفئوا نور الله بأفواههم ويأبى الله إلا أن يتم نوره ولو كره الكافرون

translation: He is the One who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to make it prevail over all religions, even if the polytheists dislike it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine mission of Prophet Muhammad to establish Islam as the true religion, destined to prevail over all other religions. It underscores the inevitability of Islam's triumph, regardless of opposition from those who associate partners with Allah (polytheists). The verse conveys a message of perseverance and faith in the ultimate victory of truth and monotheism.
orig: هو الذي أرسل رسوله بالهدى ودين الحق ليظهره على الدين كله ولو كره المشركون

translation: O you who have believed, indeed, many of the scholars and the monks devour the wealth of people unjustly and avert [them] from the way of Allah. And those who hoard gold and silver and spend it not in the way of Allah - give them tidings of a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning against religious leaders who exploit their positions for personal gain, misguiding people away from the path of righteousness. It also criticizes the hoarding of wealth, emphasizing that resources should be used to support the community and further the cause of Allah, rather than being amassed selfishly. The promise of a painful punishment underscores the severity of these actions in the eyes of Allah.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إن كثيرا من الأحبار والرهبان ليأكلون أموال الناس بالباطل ويصدون عن سبيل الله والذين يكنزون الذهب والفضة ولا ينفقونها في سبيل الله فبشرهم بعذاب أليم

translation: The Day when they will be heated in the fire of Hell, and their foreheads, sides, and backs will be branded with it: 'This is what you hoarded for yourselves, so taste what you used to hoard.'
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Judgment, emphasizing the consequences of one's actions in the material world. The imagery of being branded by the fire of Hell on the foreheads, sides, and backs symbolizes the inescapable and all-encompassing nature of divine justice. The hoarding mentioned here refers to the accumulation of wealth and resources without sharing or using them for good, which leads to a painful punishment. The command to 'taste what you used to hoard' serves as a stark reminder that the fruits of selfish actions will be experienced in the afterlife, urging believers to use their worldly possessions in a manner that aligns with divine guidance and benefits others.
orig: يوم يحمى عليها في نار جهنم فتكوى بها جباههم وجنوبهم وظهورهم هذا ما كنزتم لأنفسكم فذوقوا ما كنتم تكنزون

translation: The number of months with Allah is twelve months in the Book of Allah, the day He created the heavens and the earth; of them, four are sacred. That is the right religion, so wrong not yourselves therein. And fight the polytheists all together as they fight you all together. And know that Allah is with the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sanctity of time as ordained by Allah, highlighting the twelve months of the Islamic lunar calendar, of which four are designated as sacred months (Dhu al-Qi'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah, Muharram, and Rajab). These sacred months are periods during which fighting is prohibited, reflecting the importance of peace and the sanctity of certain times in Islamic law. The verse also calls for justice and self-restraint during these months, urging believers not to wrong themselves by engaging in prohibited actions. Additionally, it addresses the context of conflict, instructing Muslims to fight against polytheists collectively, mirroring their collective aggression, while reminding them that Allah supports those who are pious and God-fearing. This underscores the balance between defending the faith and community and maintaining personal righteousness and adherence to divine commandments.
orig: إن عدة الشهور عند الله اثنا عشر شهرا في كتاب الله يوم خلق السماوات والأرض منها أربعة حرم ذلك الدين القيم فلا تظلموا فيهن أنفسكم وقاتلوا المشركين كافة كما يقاتلونكم كافة واعلموا أن الله مع المتقين

translation: The postponing (of a sacred month) is only an addition in disbelief, by which those who disbelieve are led astray; they make it lawful one year and they make it unlawful another year, to adjust the number of months which Allah has made sacred, so that they may make lawful what Allah has made unlawful. The evil of their deeds is made fair-seeming to them. And Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse addresses the pre-Islamic practice of 'al-nasi', where the sanctity of certain months was manipulated to suit personal or tribal interests. It criticizes the practice as an increase in disbelief because it involves altering God's commandments regarding the sanctity of specific times, which is a form of rebellion against divine law. The verse highlights how such actions lead people astray by making them believe they can change what God has ordained, ultimately leading to a justification of their wrongdoings. It underscores the theme that God does not guide those who knowingly reject His laws, emphasizing the importance of adhering to divine commandments without alteration.
orig: إنما النسيء زيادة في الكفر يضل به الذين كفروا يحلونه عاما ويحرمونه عاما ليواطئوا عدة ما حرم الله فيحلوا ما حرم الله زين لهم سوء أعمالهم والله لا يهدي القوم الكافرين

translation: O you who have believed, what is [the matter] with you that, when you are told to go forth in the cause of Allah, you adhere heavily to the earth? Are you satisfied with the life of this world rather than the Hereafter? But what is the enjoyment of worldly life compared to the Hereafter except a [very] little.
interpretation: This verse addresses the believers, questioning their reluctance to participate in jihad (striving in the way of Allah) when called upon. It highlights a spiritual ailment where worldly attachments cause believers to cling to earthly life, preferring it over the eternal life of the Hereafter. The verse critiques this preference, emphasizing that the pleasures and comforts of this world are insignificant and fleeting when compared to the everlasting rewards of the Hereafter. It serves as a reminder and a call to reorient one's priorities towards spiritual and eternal values over temporary material gains.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا ما لكم إذا قيل لكم انفروا في سبيل الله اثاقلتم إلى الأرض أرضيتم بالحياة الدنيا من الآخرة فما متاع الحياة الدنيا في الآخرة إلا قليل

translation: Unless you go forth [in the cause of Allah], He will punish you with a painful punishment and will replace you with another people. And you will not harm Him at all. And Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of actively participating in the cause of Allah, which includes striving for justice and defending the oppressed. It warns that neglecting this duty can lead to severe consequences, including divine punishment and being replaced by others who are willing to fulfill this role. The verse also underscores Allah's omnipotence and independence, indicating that human actions do not affect His power or plans. It serves as a reminder of the responsibility believers have to engage in righteous actions and the potential consequences of failing to do so.
orig: إلا تنفروا يعذبكم عذابا أليما ويستبدل قوما غيركم ولا تضروه شيئا والله على كل شيء قدير

translation: If you do not aid the Prophet - Allah has already aided him when those who disbelieved had driven him out [of Makkah] as one of two, when they were in the cave and he said to his companion, "Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us." And Allah sent down his tranquillity upon him and supported him with angels you did not see and made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest, while the word of Allah - that is the highest. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine support and protection that Allah provides to His messengers, exemplified by the incident of Prophet Muhammad and his companion Abu Bakr in the cave during their migration from Makkah to Medina. It reassures believers that even in the face of overwhelming odds and danger, faith in Allah's plan and presence brings peace and ultimate victory. The verse also emphasizes the superiority of Allah's decree over the plans of the disbelievers, reinforcing the themes of divine omnipotence and wisdom.
orig: إلا تنصروه فقد نصره الله إذ أخرجه الذين كفروا ثاني اثنين إذ هما في الغار إذ يقول لصاحبه لا تحزن إن الله معنا فأنزل الله سكينته عليه وأيده بجنود لم تروها وجعل كلمة الذين كفروا السفلى وكلمة الله هي العليا والله عزيز حكيم

translation: Go forth, whether light or heavy, and strive with your wealth and your lives in the cause of Allah. That is better for you, if you only knew.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to participate in jihad, which can include both physical and financial efforts, regardless of their personal circumstances. It emphasizes that engaging in such efforts for the sake of Allah is ultimately beneficial for the individual, highlighting the importance of understanding the deeper value and reward of such actions.
orig: انفروا خفافا وثقالا وجاهدوا بأموالكم وأنفسكم في سبيل الله ذلكم خير لكم إن كنتم تعلمون

translation: If it had been a near gain and a short journey, they would have followed you, but the distance seemed too great for them. And they will swear by Allah, 'If we could, we would have gone forth with you,' destroying themselves [through false oaths], and Allah knows that indeed they are liars.
interpretation: This verse addresses the hypocrisy of some individuals who claim to support the Prophet Muhammad but are unwilling to make sacrifices for the cause of Islam. It highlights their reluctance to participate in a long and arduous journey for a distant gain, contrasting it with their willingness to engage in activities that promise immediate benefits. Their excuses and oaths are false, as Allah knows their true intentions and recognizes their deceit. The verse underscores the theme of sincerity in faith and the importance of actions over mere words.
orig: لو كان عرضا قريبا وسفرا قاصدا لاتبعوك ولكن بعدت عليهم الشقة وسيحلفون بالله لو استطعنا لخرجنا معكم يهلكون أنفسهم والله يعلم إنهم لكاذبون

translation: May Allah forgive you. Why did you give them permission [to stay behind] until it became clear to you who were telling the truth and you knew the liars?
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad, indicating a moment of divine guidance where he is reminded of the importance of discernment. It suggests that the Prophet should have waited to see who genuinely intended to participate in a mission (likely a military expedition) and who was making excuses out of falsehood. The verse underscores the themes of accountability and the need for clear judgment in leadership, particularly in distinguishing between sincerity and deceit among followers.
orig: عفا الله عنك لم أذنت لهم حتى يتبين لك الذين صدقوا وتعلم الكاذبين

translation: Those who believe in Allah and the Last Day would not seek exemption from striving with their wealth and their lives. And Allah is Knowing of the righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights the commitment and sincerity of true believers who do not seek to avoid their duty to engage in jihad, which in this context refers to striving in the path of Allah with their wealth and their lives. It underscores that genuine faith in Allah and the Day of Judgment naturally leads to active participation in such efforts. The verse also reassures that Allah is fully aware of those who are pious and sincere in their actions, emphasizing divine knowledge and justice in recognizing and rewarding the righteous.
orig: لا يستأذنك الذين يؤمنون بالله واليوم الآخر أن يجاهدوا بأموالهم وأنفسهم والله عليم بالمتقين

translation: Only those ask your permission who do not believe in Allah and the Last Day and whose hearts are in doubt, so they are in their doubt wavering.
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who seek to be excused from participating in the efforts of the Muslim community, particularly in times of need or jihad, are typically those who lack faith in Allah and the Hereafter. Their hesitation stems from a heart filled with doubt and uncertainty about their beliefs, causing them to waver and be indecisive in their commitment to the faith and its obligations.
orig: إنما يستأذنك الذين لا يؤمنون بالله واليوم الآخر وارتابت قلوبهم فهم في ريبهم يترددون

translation: And if they had intended to go forth, they would have prepared for it [some] preparation. But Allah disliked their being sent forth, so He kept them back, and they were told, 'Remain [behind] with those who remain.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom behind the decision to keep certain individuals from participating in a battle or a significant event. It suggests that their absence was not due to a lack of logistical preparation but rather a divine decree, reflecting Allah's knowledge of their true intentions or readiness. The verse underscores the idea that sometimes, what appears as a personal choice or inability might actually be part of a larger divine plan, emphasizing the importance of accepting Allah's will over one's own desires or plans.
orig: ولو أرادوا الخروج لأعدوا له عدة ولكن كره الله انبعاثهم فثبطهم وقيل اقعدوا مع القاعدين

translation: If they had gone forth with you, they would have added nothing to you except confusion, and they would have hurried about in your midst, seeking to cause you dissension. And among you are some who would have listened to them. And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the potential negative impact of hypocrites on the Muslim community. It suggests that their presence during critical times, such as battles, would have led to increased confusion and internal discord. The verse warns believers about the dangers of being influenced by such individuals, emphasizing that Allah is fully aware of those who cause mischief and injustice. It serves as a reminder for Muslims to be cautious and maintain unity, trusting in Allah's knowledge and justice.
orig: لو خرجوا فيكم ما زادوكم إلا خبالا ولأوضعوا خلالكم يبغونكم الفتنة وفيكم سماعون لهم والله عليم بالظالمين

translation: They had already sought to cause sedition before and had upset matters for you until the truth came and the decree of Allah prevailed, while they were hating it.
interpretation: This verse reflects on the persistent efforts of some individuals to create discord and confusion, challenging the Prophet Muhammad and the early Muslim community. Despite their attempts to distort the truth and disrupt the divine plan, the ultimate reality and command of Allah became manifest, overpowering their schemes. This highlights the inevitability of divine truth prevailing over falsehood, no matter the resistance from those who oppose it.
orig: لقد ابتغوا الفتنة من قبل وقلبوا لك الأمور حتى جاء الحق وظهر أمر الله وهم كارهون

translation: And among them are some who say, 'Grant me permission and do not put me to trial.' Unquestionably, into trial they have fallen. And indeed, Hell will encompass the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse addresses the hypocrites who, during the time of the Prophet Muhammad, sought excuses to avoid participating in jihad, claiming they feared being tempted or tested in their faith. By asking to be excused, they reveal their lack of trust in Allah's protection and their own weakness in faith, which ironically is the very trial they sought to avoid. The verse indicates that by making such requests, they have already failed the test of their faith. Furthermore, it serves as a warning that those who disbelieve and shirk their responsibilities will ultimately find themselves surrounded by the punishment of Hell, emphasizing the consequences of hypocrisy and lack of faith.
orig: ومنهم من يقول ائذن لي ولا تفتني ألا في الفتنة سقطوا وإن جهنم لمحيطة بالكافرين

translation: If good befalls you, it grieves them; but if a calamity befalls you, they say, 'We took our precautions beforehand,' and turn away, rejoicing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy and insincerity of certain individuals who are distressed by the good fortune of the believers and pleased by their misfortunes. It suggests that such people falsely claim to have anticipated and prepared for the believers' downfall, using it as an excuse to distance themselves and express joy at the believers' hardships. This behavior underscores their lack of genuine concern or support, revealing their true nature and intentions.
orig: إن تصبك حسنة تسؤهم وإن تصبك مصيبة يقولوا قد أخذنا أمرنا من قبل ويتولوا وهم فرحون

translation: Say, 'Never will afflict us except what Allah has decreed for us; He is our protector.' And upon Allah let the believers rely.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Islamic belief in predestination and divine decree, asserting that believers should trust that only what Allah has written for them will occur. It encourages a deep sense of reliance on Allah, fostering resilience and faith in His plan, and reminding believers that their ultimate protector and sustainer is Allah, thus they should place their complete trust in Him.
orig: قل لن يصيبنا إلا ما كتب الله لنا هو مولانا وعلى الله فليتوكل المؤمنون

translation: Say, 'Do you await for us except one of the two best outcomes while we await for you that Allah strikes you with a punishment from Himself or by our hands? So wait; indeed, we are with you waiting.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the confidence and steadfastness of the believers in the face of their adversaries. It highlights that the believers are only expecting one of two positive outcomes for themselves: victory or martyrdom, both of which are considered favorable in the eyes of Allah. Conversely, they warn their enemies that they should be wary of divine retribution, which could come directly from Allah or through the actions of the believers themselves. The verse encourages patience and vigilance among the believers, assuring them that they are not alone in their waiting and readiness for whatever may come.
orig: قل هل تربصون بنا إلا إحدى الحسنيين ونحن نتربص بكم أن يصيبكم الله بعذاب من عنده أو بأيدينا فتربصوا إنا معكم متربصون

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], "Spend, willingly or unwillingly; never will it be accepted from you. Indeed, you have been a defiantly disobedient people."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sincerity in acts of charity. It indicates that spending or giving in charity is not merely about the act itself but about the intention behind it. If the giving is done unwillingly or without genuine faith, it will not be accepted by Allah. The verse addresses those who might perform good deeds out of obligation or for show, highlighting that such actions are void of true righteousness. It serves as a reminder that one's spiritual state and obedience to Allah are crucial for the acceptance of their deeds.
orig: قل أنفقوا طوعا أو كرها لن يتقبل منكم إنكم كنتم قوما فاسقين

translation: And nothing prevents their contributions from being accepted from them except that they have disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger, and they do not come to prayer except while they are lazy, and they do not spend except while they are unwilling.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the sincerity and faith of an individual are crucial in the acceptance of their charitable acts. It indicates that for acts of charity to be truly accepted by Allah, they must be accompanied by genuine belief in Allah and His Messenger, and performed with a willing and eager heart, not out of reluctance or as a mere obligation. The verse emphasizes that without true faith and a positive attitude towards worship and giving, the spiritual value of these actions is diminished.
orig: وما منعهم أن تقبل منهم نفقاتهم إلا أنهم كفروا بالله وبرسوله ولا يأتون الصلاة إلا وهم كسالى ولا ينفقون إلا وهم كارهون

translation: So let not their wealth and their children impress you. Allah only intends to punish them through them in the worldly life and that their souls should depart [at death] while they are disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder not to be envious or impressed by the apparent worldly success of those who disbelieve. It underscores the notion that the wealth and progeny of the disbelievers might seem like blessings, but in reality, they are a means of their own punishment in this life. The verse suggests that such worldly possessions can lead them further astray, increasing their attachment to the material world and thus, their ultimate punishment is that they die in a state of disbelief, missing out on the eternal rewards of the hereafter.
orig: فلا تعجبك أموالهم ولا أولادهم إنما يريد الله ليعذبهم بها في الحياة الدنيا وتزهق أنفسهم وهم كافرون

translation: And they swear by Allah that they are from among you while they are not from among you, but they are a people who cause division.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of certain individuals who falsely claim to be part of the Muslim community. They swear oaths to gain trust and appear as allies, but their true intent is to sow discord and division within the community. The verse serves as a warning to believers to be vigilant and discerning, recognizing that not all who profess faith are sincere, and some may actively work against the unity and well-being of the community.
orig: ويحلفون بالله إنهم لمنكم وما هم منكم ولكنهم قوم يفرقون

translation: If they could find a refuge or caves or a place to enter, they would turn to it, rushing headlong.
interpretation: This verse highlights the intense fear and desperation of the hypocrites, illustrating their readiness to flee and seek any possible escape from the consequences of their actions. It underscores their lack of faith and commitment, showing how they would abandon the community in times of difficulty, driven by their own self-interest and cowardice.
orig: لو يجدون ملجأ أو مغارات أو مدخلا لولوا إليه وهم يجمحون

translation: And among them are those who criticize you concerning the charities. If they are given from them, they are pleased; but if they are not given from them, at once they become angry.
interpretation: This verse addresses the issue of hypocrisy within the community. It points out that some individuals criticize the distribution of charitable funds not out of concern for fairness or justice, but rather out of personal interest. Their satisfaction or dissatisfaction is directly tied to whether they personally receive from these charities. This behavior reflects a lack of sincerity and a selfish motive, highlighting the importance of giving charity with a pure intention and not being driven by personal gain or loss.
orig: ومنهم من يلمزك في الصدقات فإن أعطوا منها رضوا وإن لم يعطوا منها إذا هم يسخطون

translation: And if only they had been content with what Allah and His Messenger gave them and said, 'Sufficient for us is Allah; Allah will give us of His bounty, and [so will] His Messenger; indeed, we are desirous toward Allah.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of contentment and trust in Allah's provision. It suggests that believers should be satisfied with what Allah and His Messenger have provided, and express their reliance solely on Allah's bounty. The phrase 'Sufficient for us is Allah' reflects a deep faith and submission to Allah's will, indicating that true fulfillment comes from spiritual rather than material wealth. The verse also highlights the need for a sincere orientation towards Allah, indicating that one's ultimate desire and hope should be directed towards Him.
orig: ولو أنهم رضوا ما آتاهم الله ورسوله وقالوا حسبنا الله سيؤتينا الله من فضله ورسوله إنا إلى الله راغبون

translation: Alms are for the poor and the needy, and those employed to administer them, and for those whose hearts are to be reconciled, and to free the captives, and for those in debt, and in the way of Allah, and for the wayfarer; a duty imposed by Allah. Allah is Knowing, Wise.
interpretation: This verse outlines the specific categories of people who are entitled to receive zakat (alms), emphasizing that zakat is not a general charity but a structured obligation with designated recipients. It highlights Allah's wisdom and knowledge in legislating this system, ensuring that the distribution of zakat addresses various social and economic needs within the community, thereby fostering social justice and support for the vulnerable.
orig: إنما الصدقات للفقراء والمساكين والعاملين عليها والمؤلفة قلوبهم وفي الرقاب والغارمين وفي سبيل الله وابن السبيل فريضة من الله والله عليم حكيم

translation: And among them are those who hurt the Prophet and say, 'He is all ear.' Say, '[He is] an ear of goodness for you; he believes in Allah and trusts the believers and is a mercy to those who believe among you.' And those who hurt the Messenger of Allah - for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse addresses the issue of disrespect and harm directed towards the Prophet Muhammad. It highlights the inappropriate behavior of some individuals who mock the Prophet by saying he is merely 'all ear,' implying he is gullible or easily influenced. The response given in the verse defends the Prophet, emphasizing his role as a beneficial listener who not only believes in Allah but also trusts and shows mercy to the believers. The verse also serves as a stern warning, indicating that those who cause harm or disrespect to the Prophet will face severe consequences, underscoring the sanctity and high regard of the prophetic office in Islam.
orig: ومنهم الذين يؤذون النبي ويقولون هو أذن قل أذن خير لكم يؤمن بالله ويؤمن للمؤمنين ورحمة للذين آمنوا منكم والذين يؤذون رسول الله لهم عذاب أليم

translation: They swear by Allah to you to please you, but Allah and His Messenger are more worthy that they should please Him, if they are believers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of sincerity in faith and actions. It critiques those who make oaths to gain favor with people, suggesting that true believers should prioritize pleasing Allah and His Messenger over seeking human approval. The verse emphasizes that genuine faith is demonstrated by aligning one's actions with the pleasure of Allah, rather than using religious oaths as a means to manipulate or appease others.
orig: يحلفون بالله لكم ليرضوكم والله ورسوله أحق أن يرضوه إن كانوا مؤمنين

translation: Do they not know that whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger, then for him is the Fire of Hell, wherein he will abide eternally? That is the great disgrace.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe consequences of opposing or going against the commandments of Allah and His Messenger. It serves as a warning to believers about the eternal punishment in Hellfire that awaits those who choose to defy divine guidance. The mention of "the great disgrace" underscores the ultimate humiliation and loss that such opposition entails, highlighting the importance of obedience and submission to Allah's will.
orig: ألم يعلموا أنه من يحادد الله ورسوله فأن له نار جهنم خالدا فيها ذلك الخزي العظيم

translation: The hypocrites fear lest a surah be revealed about them, informing them of what is in their hearts. Say, 'Mock [as you wish]; indeed, Allah will expose what you fear.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the inner anxiety of the hypocrites who are concerned that their hidden thoughts and doubts might be exposed through a revelation. The command to 'say, 'Mock [as you wish]'' indicates a dismissal of their mockery, emphasizing that their derision does not affect the truth. The promise that 'Allah will expose what you fear' serves as a reminder of divine omniscience and justice, suggesting that no secret will remain hidden and that Allah will ultimately reveal the truth about their hypocrisy.
orig: يحذر المنافقون أن تنزل عليهم سورة تنبئهم بما في قلوبهم قل استهزئوا إن الله مخرج ما تحذرون

translation: And if you ask them, they will surely say, 'We were only conversing and playing.' Say, 'Is it Allah and His verses and His Messenger that you were mocking?'
interpretation: This verse addresses the hypocrisy of those who mock the revelations and the Prophet. It highlights their attempt to downplay their mockery by claiming it was mere jest, yet it challenges them directly by questioning whether they would dare to mock something as sacred as Allah, His verses, and His Messenger. The verse underscores the seriousness of such actions and the accountability for disrespecting divine matters.
orig: ولئن سألتهم ليقولن إنما كنا نخوض ونلعب قل أبالله وآياته ورسوله كنتم تستهزئون

translation: Make no excuse; you have disbelieved after your belief. If We pardon one group of you, We will punish another group because they were criminals.
interpretation: This verse addresses those who have reverted from faith to disbelief, emphasizing that their excuses for such apostasy are invalid. It underscores the gravity of abandoning faith after having accepted it, indicating that such an action is a form of disbelief. The verse also highlights divine justice, suggesting that while some may be forgiven, others will face punishment due to their criminal actions, reflecting the accountability for one's deeds in the eyes of God.
orig: لا تعتذروا قد كفرتم بعد إيمانكم إن نعف عن طائفة منكم نعذب طائفة بأنهم كانوا مجرمين

translation: The hypocrites, men and women, are from one another. They enjoin evil and forbid good, and withhold their hands. They have forgotten Allah, so He has forgotten them. Indeed, the hypocrites are the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse highlights the interconnected nature of hypocrites, both men and women, suggesting a mutual influence that leads them away from righteousness. Their collective behavior is characterized by promoting wrongdoing and discouraging virtuous acts, which is a direct reflection of their neglect of God's commandments. The phrase 'withhold their hands' can be interpreted as their reluctance to engage in acts of charity or support for the community, further illustrating their disconnection from divine guidance. The consequence of forgetting Allah is that they are, in turn, forgotten by Him, indicating a spiritual abandonment. This verse serves as a warning that hypocrisy leads to a state of being among the defiantly disobedient, those who knowingly rebel against God's path.
orig: المنافقون والمنافقات بعضهم من بعض يأمرون بالمنكر وينهون عن المعروف ويقبضون أيديهم نسوا الله فنسيهم إن المنافقين هم الفاسقون

translation: Allah has promised the hypocrite men and hypocrite women and the disbelievers the fire of Hell, wherein they will abide eternally. It is sufficient for them; and Allah has cursed them, and for them is an enduring punishment.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning from Allah to those who engage in hypocrisy and disbelief. It underscores the severe consequences of such actions, emphasizing that the punishment in the Hereafter is not only eternal but also fitting for their deeds. The mention of Allah's curse further highlights the gravity of their spiritual state, indicating a complete severance from divine mercy. This enduring punishment is described as 'muqeem', suggesting a punishment that is firmly established and unending, reinforcing the notion that the choices made in this life have profound implications in the afterlife.
orig: وعد الله المنافقين والمنافقات والكفار نار جهنم خالدين فيها هي حسبهم ولعنهم الله ولهم عذاب مقيم

translation: Like those before you; they were mightier than you in power, and more abundant in wealth and children. They enjoyed their portion [in worldly life]; so enjoy your portion as those before you enjoyed their portion, and you indulged [in worldly matters] as they indulged. Those - their deeds became worthless in this world and in the Hereafter, and those are the losers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder and a warning to the believers about the fleeting nature of worldly pleasures and the ultimate futility of focusing solely on material gains. It draws a parallel between the current generation and those who came before them, highlighting that despite their greater strength, wealth, and progeny, the previous generations were led astray by their indulgence in worldly life. The verse emphasizes that such indulgence leads to the nullification of one's deeds both in this life and the hereafter, categorizing those who follow this path as the ultimate losers. It encourages a shift in focus towards spiritual and moral values, urging believers to not let the temporary enjoyment of worldly life distract them from their ultimate goal of achieving success in the hereafter.
orig: كالذين من قبلكم كانوا أشد منكم قوة وأكثر أموالا وأولادا فاستمتعوا بخلاقهم فاستمتعتم بخلاقكم كما استمتع الذين من قبلكم بخلاقهم وخضتم كالذي خاضوا أولئك حبطت أعمالهم في الدنيا والآخرة وأولئك هم الخاسرون

translation: Has there not come to them the news of those before them - the people of Noah, 'Ad, Thamud, the people of Abraham, the companions of Madyan, and the overturned cities? Their messengers came to them with clear proofs. So it was not Allah who wronged them, but they wronged themselves.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder and a warning to the disbelievers that the fate of previous nations who rejected their prophets is a lesson for them. It emphasizes that Allah does not wrong anyone; rather, people wrong themselves by rejecting the clear signs and guidance provided by their messengers. The mention of specific nations like the people of Noah, 'Ad, Thamud, and others, underscores the recurring pattern of divine justice where disbelief leads to self-inflicted ruin.
orig: ألم يأتهم نبأ الذين من قبلهم قوم نوح وعاد وثمود وقوم إبراهيم وأصحاب مدين والمؤتفكات أتتهم رسلهم بالبينات فما كان الله ليظلمهم ولكن كانوا أنفسهم يظلمون

translation: And the believing men and believing women are allies of one another. They enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong and establish prayer and give zakah and obey Allah and His Messenger. Those - Allah will have mercy upon them. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity and mutual support among believers, highlighting that both men and women who believe are protectors and helpers of each other. Their collective actions include promoting good, preventing evil, maintaining regular prayers, giving to charity, and obeying Allah and His Messenger. These actions are not only individual responsibilities but communal duties that strengthen the bonds within the Muslim community. The promise of Allah's mercy to those who fulfill these duties underscores the importance of these acts in earning divine favor. The attributes of Allah mentioned at the end, 'Exalted in Might and Wise,' remind believers of His power and wisdom in guiding and rewarding them according to His perfect plan.
orig: والمؤمنون والمؤمنات بعضهم أولياء بعض يأمرون بالمعروف وينهون عن المنكر ويقيمون الصلاة ويؤتون الزكاة ويطيعون الله ورسوله أولئك سيرحمهم الله إن الله عزيز حكيم

translation: Allah has promised the believing men and believing women gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever, and pleasant dwellings in gardens of perpetual residence; and approval from Allah is greater. That is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the rewards awaiting believers in the afterlife. It highlights that both men and women who have faith and adhere to the teachings of Islam will be granted entry into Paradise, described as gardens with flowing rivers, eternal dwellings, and the ultimate blessing of Allah's approval. The mention of 'gardens of perpetual residence' (Jannat 'Adn) signifies the everlasting nature of this reward. The verse underscores that the greatest achievement for a believer is not just the material comforts of Paradise but the spiritual satisfaction and honor of receiving Allah's pleasure, which is described as the 'great attainment' or the ultimate success.
orig: وعد الله المؤمنين والمؤمنات جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها ومساكن طيبة في جنات عدن ورضوان من الله أكبر ذلك هو الفوز العظيم

translation: O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites and be harsh with them. And their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad to exert effort in opposing those who reject faith and those who are hypocrites, indicating a need for firmness and resolve in dealing with opposition to the message of Islam. The mention of Hell as their destination underscores the severity of their rejection and the consequences of their actions, emphasizing the importance of steadfastness in faith and the seriousness of disbelief and hypocrisy.
orig: يا أيها النبي جاهد الكفار والمنافقين واغلظ عليهم ومأواهم جهنم وبئس المصير

translation: They swear by Allah that they did not say it, but they certainly did utter the word of disbelief and disbelieved after their Islam, and they intended what they did not achieve. And they were not resentful except because Allah and His Messenger enriched them of His bounty. So if they repent, it is better for them; but if they turn away, Allah will punish them with a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter. And there will be for them on earth no protector or helper.
interpretation: This verse addresses the hypocrisy of some individuals who, after converting to Islam, revert to disbelief and even deny their own words of disbelief. It highlights their ingratitude towards the blessings bestowed upon them by Allah and His Messenger. The verse emphasizes the importance of repentance for those who stray, offering them a chance to return to the right path. However, it also warns of severe consequences in both this life and the hereafter for those who persist in their disbelief and hypocrisy, underscoring the isolation and lack of support they will face without Allah's guidance and protection.
orig: يحلفون بالله ما قالوا ولقد قالوا كلمة الكفر وكفروا بعد إسلامهم وهموا بما لم ينالوا وما نقموا إلا أن أغناهم الله ورسوله من فضله فإن يتوبوا يك خيرا لهم وإن يتولوا يعذبهم الله عذابا أليما في الدنيا والآخرة وما لهم في الأرض من ولي ولا نصير

translation: And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah, [saying], 'If He gives us from His bounty, we will surely give charity and be among the righteous.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of some individuals who make promises to Allah, vowing to be charitable and righteous if blessed with His bounty. However, their sincerity is questionable, as their commitment is conditional upon receiving material wealth, suggesting that their faith and good deeds are motivated by self-interest rather than genuine devotion to Allah.
orig: ومنهم من عاهد الله لئن آتانا من فضله لنصدقن ولنكونن من الصالحين

translation: So when He gave them from His bounty, they were stingy with it and turned away while they refused.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ingratitude and selfishness of people who, upon receiving blessings and favors from Allah, hoard them instead of sharing or using them in ways that please Him. It points to a spiritual ailment where individuals become so attached to worldly gains that they turn away from Allah, showing a lack of faith and a refusal to acknowledge His generosity. This behavior is a form of rejection of Allah's guidance and a sign of spiritual deviation.
orig: فلما آتاهم من فضله بخلوا به وتولوا وهم معرضون

translation: So He caused hypocrisy to follow as a result in their hearts until the Day they meet Him because they broke what they had promised Allah and because they used to lie.
interpretation: This verse indicates that hypocrisy was a consequence of their actions, specifically their failure to fulfill their promises to Allah and their habit of lying. It suggests that such behavior leads to a spiritual ailment that persists until the Day of Judgment, emphasizing the severe consequences of breaking one's covenant with Allah and engaging in deceit.
orig: فأعقبهم نفاقا في قلوبهم إلى يوم يلقونه بما أخلفوا الله ما وعدوه وبما كانوا يكذبون

translation: Do they not know that Allah knows their secret and their private conversations, and that Allah is the Knower of the unseen?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience of Allah, highlighting that He is fully aware of all that is hidden and all that is whispered in secret. It serves as a reminder to believers that nothing is concealed from Allah, urging them to be mindful of their thoughts and actions, even in private, as they are always under divine observation.
orig: ألم يعلموا أن الله يعلم سرهم ونجواهم وأن الله علام الغيوب

translation: Those who find fault with the believers who give charity voluntarily, and those who find nothing but their own efforts to give, and they mock them - Allah mocks them, and for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse addresses the issue of hypocrisy and mockery within the community of believers. It specifically criticizes those who deride others for their charitable contributions, whether those contributions are substantial or merely the best one can offer given their circumstances. The act of mocking others for their charitable efforts is seen as a serious moral failing, reflecting a lack of empathy and understanding. Allah's response to such behavior is to mock those who mock, indicating divine disapproval and a promise of a painful punishment in the hereafter. This serves as a reminder to believers to be sincere in their faith and charitable actions, and to refrain from judging or belittling the efforts of others.
orig: الذين يلمزون المطوعين من المؤمنين في الصدقات والذين لا يجدون إلا جهدهم فيسخرون منهم سخر الله منهم ولهم عذاب أليم

translation: Ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them. If you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, Allah will not forgive them. That is because they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger, and Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.
interpretation: This verse indicates that intercession or seeking forgiveness on behalf of those who have willfully rejected faith in Allah and His Messenger is futile. It underscores the severity of disbelief and disobedience, suggesting that such actions place individuals beyond the reach of forgiveness, no matter how much it is sought on their behalf. The mention of 'seventy times' emphasizes the pointlessness of repeatedly seeking forgiveness for them, as their rejection of faith is a barrier to divine forgiveness. This serves as a reminder of the importance of faith and obedience to Allah's guidance.
orig: استغفر لهم أو لا تستغفر لهم إن تستغفر لهم سبعين مرة فلن يغفر الله لهم ذلك بأنهم كفروا بالله ورسوله والله لا يهدي القوم الفاسقين

translation: Those who remained behind rejoiced in their staying [at home] against the Messenger of Allah and disliked to strive with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah and said, 'Do not go forth in the heat.' Say, 'The fire of Hell is more intense in heat - if they could only understand.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the hypocrisy of those who chose to stay behind and not participate in the battle, using the excuse of the heat. It critiques their lack of commitment to the cause of Allah, prioritizing their comfort over the greater good. The verse uses the metaphor of the heat of Hell to emphasize the severity of their spiritual negligence and lack of understanding of the true stakes involved in their actions.
orig: فرح المخلفون بمقعدهم خلاف رسول الله وكرهوا أن يجاهدوا بأموالهم وأنفسهم في سبيل الله وقالوا لا تنفروا في الحر قل نار جهنم أشد حرا لو كانوا يفقهون

translation: So let them laugh a little and weep much, as a recompense for what they used to earn.
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who engage in mockery and disbelief will experience fleeting moments of joy in this life, but will face significant sorrow and regret in the hereafter. The 'little laughter' represents the temporary pleasures they enjoy, while the 'much weeping' symbolizes the prolonged suffering they will endure as a consequence of their deeds. This serves as a reminder of the divine justice where actions in this life directly influence one's state in the afterlife.
orig: فليضحكوا قليلا وليبكوا كثيرا جزاء بما كانوا يكسبون

translation: If Allah brings you back to a group of them and they ask your permission to go out (to fight), say, 'You will never go out with me, nor will you fight an enemy with me. You were content with sitting (at home) the first time, so sit with those who stay behind.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the issue of hypocrisy and commitment in the context of jihad. It instructs the Prophet Muhammad to firmly reject the participation of those who previously chose to stay behind during a military expedition, indicating their lack of sincerity and commitment. The verse emphasizes the importance of genuine faith and readiness to sacrifice for the cause of Islam, distinguishing true believers from those who are hesitant or insincere in their faith.
orig: فإن رجعك الله إلى طائفة منهم فاستأذنوك للخروج فقل لن تخرجوا معي أبدا ولن تقاتلوا معي عدوا إنكم رضيتم بالقعود أول مرة فاقعدوا مع الخالفين

translation: And never pray [the funeral prayer] for any of them who has died - ever - and do not stand by his grave. Indeed, they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger and died while they were defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse instructs Muslims not to perform the funeral prayer for those who died in a state of disbelief and defiance against Allah and His Messenger. It emphasizes the severity of dying in a state of disbelief and disobedience, highlighting that such individuals are not to be honored with Islamic funeral rites. This serves as a reminder of the importance of faith and obedience to Allah throughout one's life.
orig: ولا تصل على أحد منهم مات أبدا ولا تقم على قبره إنهم كفروا بالله ورسوله وماتوا وهم فاسقون

translation: And let not their wealth and their children impress you. Allah only intends to punish them through these in the worldly life and that their souls should depart [at death] while they are disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder not to be deceived by the apparent worldly success of disbelievers. It suggests that the wealth and progeny of those who reject faith may actually be a means of their punishment in this life, leading them to a state of heedlessness and ultimately causing their souls to leave this world in a state of disbelief. It underscores the transient nature of worldly possessions and the importance of faith over material success.
orig: ولا تعجبك أموالهم وأولادهم إنما يريد الله أن يعذبهم بها في الدنيا وتزهق أنفسهم وهم كافرون

translation: And when a surah is revealed [enjoining]: 'Believe in Allah and strive with His Messenger,' those of wealth among them ask your permission [to stay back] and say, 'Let us be with those who remain behind.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the reluctance of some wealthy individuals to participate in jihad when it is commanded by Allah through the revelation of a new surah. It points to a deeper issue of faith and commitment, where material comfort and personal safety are prioritized over the collective duty and spiritual obligation to support the Prophet's mission. The verse serves as a critique of those who seek excuses to avoid contributing to the community's efforts, revealing their lack of true belief and dedication to the cause of Islam.
orig: وإذا أنزلت سورة أن آمنوا بالله وجاهدوا مع رسوله استأذنك أولو الطول منهم وقالوا ذرنا نكن مع القاعدين

translation: They are content to be with those who stay behind, and their hearts have been sealed, so they do not understand.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who choose to remain with the hypocrites or those who do not participate in the efforts for the cause of Islam. Their decision to stay behind is not merely physical but reflects a deeper spiritual malaise. The sealing of their hearts symbolizes a divine act where their ability to perceive and understand the truth is blocked due to their persistent rejection and lack of sincerity. This condition prevents them from gaining true insight and understanding of the faith, leading them further away from the path of righteousness.
orig: رضوا بأن يكونوا مع الخوالف وطبع على قلوبهم فهم لا يفقهون

translation: But the Messenger and those who believed with him strove with their wealth and their lives. And those - for them are the good things, and it is those who are the successful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of striving (jihad) in the path of Allah, not only with one's wealth but also with one's life. It highlights that the Prophet Muhammad and his companions exemplified this commitment, dedicating themselves fully to the cause of Islam. The verse promises that those who engage in such efforts will be rewarded with the best of outcomes in the Hereafter, indicating that true success and prosperity are reserved for those who sacrifice for their faith.
orig: لكن الرسول والذين آمنوا معه جاهدوا بأموالهم وأنفسهم وأولئك لهم الخيرات وأولئك هم المفلحون

translation: Allah will admit them to Gardens underneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever. That is the great triumph.
interpretation: This verse promises believers a reward in the afterlife, symbolized by the Gardens of Paradise with flowing rivers, indicating eternal peace, abundance, and joy. The phrase "that is the great triumph" emphasizes that this eternal abode represents the ultimate success and fulfillment of one's spiritual journey, highlighting the significance of faith and righteous deeds in achieving this divine reward.
orig: أعد الله لهم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها ذلك الفوز العظيم

translation: And those who made excuses from among the Bedouins came to be given leave, and those who denied Allah and His Messenger sat [at home]. There will afflict those who disbelieved among them a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse addresses the situation during a military expedition where some Bedouins sought excuses to avoid participation, while others outright rejected the call of Allah and His Messenger, choosing to stay behind. The verse warns that those who disbelieved and did not join the expedition out of denial will face a severe punishment. It underscores the importance of sincerity and obedience in faith, highlighting the consequences of hypocrisy and disbelief.
