orig: وجاء المعذرون من الأعراب ليؤذن لهم وقعد الذين كذبوا الله ورسوله سيصيب الذين كفروا منهم عذاب أليم

translation: There is no blame upon the weak, nor upon the sick, nor upon those who find nothing to spend, if they are sincere to Allah and His Messenger. There is no way (of blame) against the good-doers; and Allah is Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who are unable to participate in jihad due to physical weakness, illness, or financial constraints are not to be blamed as long as their intentions and sincerity towards Allah and His Messenger remain pure. It highlights Allah's mercy and forgiveness, indicating that He values the sincerity of the heart over physical or material contributions. The verse reassures believers that as long as they strive to do good according to their capacities, they are on the right path, and Allah will not hold them accountable for what they cannot do.
orig: ليس على الضعفاء ولا على المرضى ولا على الذين لا يجدون ما ينفقون حرج إذا نصحوا لله ورسوله ما على المحسنين من سبيل والله غفور رحيم

translation: And not upon those who, when they came to you to carry them, you said, 'I cannot find anything to carry you on,' turned away while their eyes overflowed with tears of grief that they could not find anything to spend.
interpretation: This verse highlights the sincerity and emotional depth of the believers who wished to participate in a military expedition but were unable to do so due to lack of resources. It emphasizes that their genuine desire to contribute, evidenced by their tears of sorrow, absolves them from blame or criticism. The verse underscores the importance of intention and the emotional commitment to the cause, even when material support is unavailable.
orig: ولا على الذين إذا ما أتوك لتحملهم قلت لا أجد ما أحملكم عليه تولوا وأعينهم تفيض من الدمع حزنا ألا يجدوا ما ينفقون

translation: The way (of blame) is only against those who ask your permission while they are rich. They are content to be with those who remain behind, and Allah has sealed their hearts, so they do not know.
interpretation: This verse addresses the issue of hypocrisy within the Muslim community during the time of the Prophet Muhammad. It specifically criticizes those who were financially capable but still sought excuses to avoid participating in military expeditions or other communal obligations. Their reluctance stems from a lack of true faith and commitment, as indicated by the sealing of their hearts by Allah. This sealing suggests a spiritual blindness that prevents them from recognizing the importance of their duties and the consequences of their inaction. The verse underscores the gravity of such behavior, highlighting it as a path leading to blame and spiritual loss.
orig: إنما السبيل على الذين يستأذنونك وهم أغنياء رضوا بأن يكونوا مع الخوالف وطبع الله على قلوبهم فهم لا يعلمون

translation: They will make excuses to you when you return to them. Say, 'Do not make excuses; we will not believe you. Allah has already informed us of your news. And Allah will observe your deeds, and [so will] His Messenger. Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of what you used to do.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the hypocrites who will offer excuses for their absence or lack of participation in a battle or mission, upon the return of the believers. The command to not accept their excuses signifies a divine knowledge and judgment that transcends human justifications. It emphasizes that Allah and His Messenger are fully aware of the true intentions and actions of individuals. The verse underscores the concept of accountability before Allah, who knows all things, both hidden and apparent. It serves as a reminder that all deeds will be scrutinized in the hereafter, where no excuses will be accepted, and every individual will be held accountable for their actions.
orig: يعتذرون إليكم إذا رجعتم إليهم قل لا تعتذروا لن نؤمن لكم قد نبأنا الله من أخباركم وسيرى الله عملكم ورسوله ثم تردون إلى عالم الغيب والشهادة فينبئكم بما كنتم تعملون

translation: They will swear by Allah to you when you return to them, so that you may leave them alone. So leave them alone; indeed, they are filth, and their refuge will be Hell as recompense for what they used to earn.
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad and the believers, warning them about hypocrites who will make false oaths to gain favor and avoid scrutiny upon the believers' return from a journey or battle. The verse advises the believers to disregard these oaths and to distance themselves from the hypocrites, labeling them as 'filth' due to their insincere and harmful actions. The ultimate consequence for the hypocrites is stated to be Hell, which serves as a divine retribution for their deeds. This underscores the importance of sincerity in faith and the severe consequences of hypocrisy.
orig: سيحلفون بالله لكم إذا انقلبتم إليهم لتعرضوا عنهم فأعرضوا عنهم إنهم رجس ومأواهم جهنم جزاء بما كانوا يكسبون

translation: They swear to you to please you, but if you are pleased with them, indeed, Allah is not pleased with a people who are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse highlights the distinction between human satisfaction and divine approval. It suggests that while people might try to appease others with oaths and promises, true righteousness is determined by Allah's standards. The verse warns against being swayed by superficial assurances from those who are disobedient to Allah, emphasizing that divine displeasure towards the defiantly disobedient is more significant than any temporary human satisfaction.
orig: يحلفون لكم لترضوا عنهم فإن ترضوا عنهم فإن الله لا يرضى عن القوم الفاسقين

translation: The Bedouins are the worst in disbelief and hypocrisy, and most likely to be unaware of the limits of what Allah has revealed to His Messenger. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual and moral challenges faced by the Bedouins, indicating that their isolation and lifestyle may lead them to be more prone to disbelief and hypocrisy. It also emphasizes that ignorance of divine laws and boundaries set by Allah through His Messenger is more prevalent among them. The mention of Allah as All-Knowing and All-Wise serves as a reminder that these observations are based on divine knowledge and wisdom, underscoring the importance of adhering to the teachings revealed by Allah.
orig: الأعراب أشد كفرا ونفاقا وأجدر ألا يعلموا حدود ما أنزل الله على رسوله والله عليم حكيم

translation: And among the Bedouins are those who take what they spend as a fine, and they await for you turns of misfortune. Upon them is a turn of evil. And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the attitude of some Bedouins who reluctantly give charity, considering it a loss or a fine imposed upon them rather than an act of worship. Their hearts are not in their giving, and they even hope for misfortune to befall the Muslim community, perhaps so they might be relieved of such obligations. The verse warns that such negative attitudes and intentions will bring about evil consequences for them. It also reassures believers that Allah is fully aware of their inner thoughts and actions, emphasizing His attributes of being All-Hearing and All-Knowing.
orig: ومن الأعراب من يتخذ ما ينفق مغرما ويتربص بكم الدوائر عليهم دائرة السوء والله سميع عليم

translation: And among the Bedouins are those who believe in Allah and the Last Day and consider what they spend as a means of nearness to Allah and of [receiving] the prayers of the Messenger. Unquestionably, it is a means of nearness for them; Allah will admit them to His mercy. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the sincerity and faith of some Bedouins who, despite their simple lifestyle, hold strong beliefs in Allah and the Hereafter. Their charitable acts are not just social obligations but are performed with the intention of drawing closer to Allah and earning the Prophet's prayers. The verse reassures that such acts of devotion are indeed recognized by Allah as means of spiritual proximity, promising them entry into divine mercy. It underscores the themes of divine forgiveness and mercy, emphasizing that Allah's forgiveness and compassion are accessible to all who approach Him with genuine faith and good deeds.
orig: ومن الأعراب من يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر ويتخذ ما ينفق قربات عند الله وصلوات الرسول ألا إنها قربة لهم سيدخلهم الله في رحمته إن الله غفور رحيم

translation: And the first forerunners [in the faith] among the Muhajireen and the Ansar and those who followed them with excellence - Allah is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him, and He has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever. That is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the honor and reward bestowed upon the early Muslims who migrated from Mecca to Medina (Muhajireen) and those who welcomed and supported them in Medina (Ansar), along with those who followed their exemplary conduct. It emphasizes divine satisfaction with these individuals and their contentment with Allah, promising them eternal paradise as a reward for their faith and good deeds. The 'great attainment' refers to the ultimate success and fulfillment found in the afterlife, underscoring the significance of their efforts and sacrifices in the path of Islam.
orig: والسابقون الأولون من المهاجرين والأنصار والذين اتبعوهم بإحسان رضي الله عنهم ورضوا عنه وأعد لهم جنات تجري تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها أبدا ذلك الفوز العظيم

translation: And among the Bedouins around you are hypocrites, and among the people of Medina are those who have become accustomed to hypocrisy. You do not know them; We know them. We will punish them twice; then they will be returned to a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse reveals the presence of hypocrites within the Muslim community, both among the Bedouins and the residents of Medina. It emphasizes that while these hypocrites may not be identifiable to the Prophet Muhammad and the believers, Allah is fully aware of their true nature and intentions. The verse serves as a warning that these individuals will face divine retribution not once, but twice in this life, followed by a severe punishment in the hereafter. This underscores the gravity of hypocrisy and the certainty of divine justice, highlighting that no deceit can escape Allah's knowledge and judgment.
orig: وممن حولكم من الأعراب منافقون ومن أهل المدينة مردوا على النفاق لا تعلمهم نحن نعلمهم سنعذبهم مرتين ثم يردون إلى عذاب عظيم

translation: And others have acknowledged their sins, having mixed a righteous deed with another that was evil. Perhaps Allah will turn to them in forgiveness. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the human condition where individuals often engage in both good and bad actions. It offers hope to those who have sinned but also done good, suggesting that sincere acknowledgment of one's sins, coupled with repentance, can lead to Allah's forgiveness. The verse underscores Allah's attributes of being Forgiving and Merciful, encouraging believers to seek forgiveness and not despair, as Allah's mercy encompasses all and is always available to those who turn back to Him.
orig: وآخرون اعترفوا بذنوبهم خلطوا عملا صالحا وآخر سيئا عسى الله أن يتوب عليهم إن الله غفور رحيم

translation: Take from their wealth a charity that will purify them and cause them to grow, and pray for them; indeed your prayer is a source of comfort for them. And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad to collect zakat (charity) from the believers' wealth, which serves not only as a means of purifying their souls and increasing their spiritual growth but also as a mechanism for social welfare. The act of giving zakat is transformative, both for the giver, who is cleansed of greed and attachment to material wealth, and for the community, which benefits from the redistribution of resources. Additionally, the Prophet is directed to pray for those who give, as his prayers provide them with spiritual comfort and reassurance. The mention of Allah being All-Hearing and All-Knowing emphasizes that these actions are performed under divine observation and guidance, reinforcing the significance and sincerity required in fulfilling these obligations.
orig: خذ من أموالهم صدقة تطهرهم وتزكيهم بها وصل عليهم إن صلاتك سكن لهم والله سميع عليم

translation: Do they not know that it is Allah who accepts repentance from His servants and takes charities, and that Allah is the Accepter of Repentance, the Most Merciful?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine attributes of Allah as the one who accepts repentance and receives charitable acts from His servants. It serves as a reminder to believers of Allah's mercy and readiness to forgive, encouraging them to turn back to Him in repentance and to engage in acts of charity. The verse underscores the importance of recognizing Allah's role in these acts, fostering a deeper connection and reliance on His mercy and compassion.
orig: ألم يعلموا أن الله هو يقبل التوبة عن عباده ويأخذ الصدقات وأن الله هو التواب الرحيم

translation: And say: 'Work, for Allah will see your work, and (so will) His Messenger and the believers. And you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of what you used to do.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes accountability and transparency in one's actions. It instructs believers to perform their deeds sincerely, knowing that their actions are observed not only by Allah, who is omniscient and aware of both the hidden and the apparent, but also by the Prophet Muhammad and the community of believers. This awareness should motivate individuals to act righteously, as they will ultimately be brought before Allah, who will judge them based on their deeds. The verse underscores the importance of living a life of integrity, as all actions will be accounted for in the hereafter.
orig: وقل اعملوا فسيرى الله عملكم ورسوله والمؤمنون وستردون إلى عالم الغيب والشهادة فينبئكم بما كنتم تعملون

translation: And others are deferred to the command of Allah, either He will punish them or He will forgive them, and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse refers to a group of people whose final judgment is postponed by Allah. It highlights Allah's absolute authority and wisdom in deciding their fate, indicating that He may choose to punish them for their deeds or show mercy and forgive them. The mention of Allah being 'All-Knowing, All-Wise' emphasizes that His decision will be based on complete knowledge and perfect wisdom, reflecting the fairness and justice of His judgment.
orig: وآخرون مرجون لأمر الله إما يعذبهم وإما يتوب عليهم والله عليم حكيم

translation: And those who took a mosque for causing harm and disbelief, and to disunite the believers, and as an outpost for those who warred against Allah and His Messenger before; and they will certainly swear: 'We intended nothing but good.' And Allah bears witness that they are certainly liars.
interpretation: This verse refers to the incident of the Mosque of Dhirar, built by hypocrites in Medina with the intention to harm the Muslim community and divide them. It highlights the deceptive nature of hypocrites who claim their actions are for good, while Allah exposes their true intentions as false. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to be wary of those who might use religious pretexts to sow discord and to trust in Allah's knowledge of the truth.
orig: والذين اتخذوا مسجدا ضرارا وكفرا وتفريقا بين المؤمنين وإرصادا لمن حارب الله ورسوله من قبل وليحلفن إن أردنا إلا الحسنى والله يشهد إنهم لكاذبون

translation: Never stand in it. A mosque founded on righteousness from the first day is more worthy for you to stand in. In it are men who love to purify themselves, and Allah loves those who purify themselves.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sincerity and purity in worship. It instructs the Prophet Muhammad not to pray in the mosque built by hypocrites, known as the Mosque of Dissension (Masjid al-Dirar), which was established with ill intentions. Instead, the verse directs believers to worship in a mosque that was built with piety and righteousness from its inception, highlighting the Quba Mosque as an example. The mention of men who love to purify themselves underscores the value of spiritual and physical cleanliness in Islam, reflecting Allah's love for those who strive for purity in their devotion and actions.
orig: لا تقم فيه أبدا لمسجد أسس على التقوى من أول يوم أحق أن تقوم فيه فيه رجال يحبون أن يتطهروا والله يحب المطهرين

translation: Is he who founded his building on piety to Allah and His good pleasure better, or he who founded his building on the brink of a crumbling precipice so that it crumbled with him into the fire of Hell? And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse uses the metaphor of building foundations to illustrate the difference between a life built on faith and righteousness versus one built on shaky, worldly foundations. The person who builds their life on piety and seeking Allah's pleasure is likened to constructing a stable, enduring structure. In contrast, building on the edge of a crumbling cliff represents a life based on transient, unstable values that ultimately leads to ruin and damnation. The verse emphasizes the importance of a solid spiritual foundation for a successful and guided life, warning that those who choose otherwise will not receive Allah's guidance.
orig: أفمن أسس بنيانه على تقوى من الله ورضوان خير أم من أسس بنيانه على شفا جرف هار فانهار به في نار جهنم والله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: Their building which they built will continue to be a source of doubt in their hearts unless their hearts are cut. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the efforts and structures built by some people, possibly referring to their religious or ideological constructs, will perpetually cause uncertainty and doubt within them. The only way to resolve this internal conflict is through a complete transformation or 'cutting' of their hearts, symbolizing a profound change in their beliefs or convictions. This transformation is necessary for true faith and certainty. The verse concludes by affirming that Allah is fully aware of their states and wise in His decrees, emphasizing divine knowledge and wisdom in guiding human hearts.
orig: لا يزال بنيانهم الذي بنوا ريبة في قلوبهم إلا أن تقطع قلوبهم والله عليم حكيم

translation: Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their wealth [in exchange] for Paradise. They fight in the cause of Allah, so they kill and are killed. [It is] a true promise [binding] upon Him in the Torah and the Gospel and the Qur'an. And who is truer to his covenant than Allah? So rejoice in your transaction which you have contracted. And it is that which is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of martyrdom and the ultimate sacrifice believers are willing to make for their faith. It portrays the idea that believers have made a covenant with Allah, trading their lives and wealth for the promise of Paradise. This transaction is not only mentioned in the Qur'an but is also affirmed in the Torah and the Gospel, underscoring its universal significance across Abrahamic faiths. The verse highlights the reliability of Allah's promise, encouraging believers to find joy and satisfaction in this divine contract, as it leads to the greatest success and achievement in the hereafter.
orig: إن الله اشترى من المؤمنين أنفسهم وأموالهم بأن لهم الجنة يقاتلون في سبيل الله فيقتلون ويقتلون وعدا عليه حقا في التوراة والإنجيل والقرآن ومن أوفى بعهده من الله فاستبشروا ببيعكم الذي بايعتم به وذلك هو الفوز العظيم

translation: Those who repent, those who worship, those who praise, those who journey, those who bow down, those who prostrate, those who enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and those who observe the limits set by Allah - and give good tidings to the believers.
interpretation: This verse describes the qualities of true believers, highlighting their repentance, devotion through worship and praise, commitment to spiritual journeys, physical acts of worship like bowing and prostrating, their role in promoting good and preventing evil, and their adherence to Allah's commandments. It serves as an encouragement for believers to embody these characteristics, promising them good tidings as a reward for their faith and actions.
orig: التائبون العابدون الحامدون السائحون الراكعون الساجدون الآمرون بالمعروف والناهون عن المنكر والحافظون لحدود الله وبشر المؤمنين

translation: It is not for the Prophet and those who have believed to ask forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they were relatives, after it has become clear to them that they are companions of the Hellfire.
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle that intercession or seeking forgiveness for those who have died in a state of disbelief, even if they are close relatives, is not permissible once their fate as dwellers of Hell has been made clear. It emphasizes the importance of not compromising one's faith by seeking forgiveness for those who have clearly rejected the message of Islam, highlighting the seriousness of associating partners with Allah and the finality of one's stance on faith at the time of death.
orig: ما كان للنبي والذين آمنوا أن يستغفروا للمشركين ولو كانوا أولي قربى من بعد ما تبين لهم أنهم أصحاب الجحيم

translation: And the request for forgiveness by Abraham for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him. But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy to Allah, he disassociated himself from him. Indeed, Abraham was compassionate and forbearing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the moral and spiritual integrity of Prophet Abraham. It shows that his initial plea for forgiveness for his father was out of a personal promise, reflecting his compassionate nature. However, upon realizing his father's enmity towards Allah, Abraham chose to uphold his faith and loyalty to God over familial ties, demonstrating his forbearance and commitment to righteousness. This teaches believers the importance of prioritizing divine principles over personal relationships when they conflict.
orig: وما كان استغفار إبراهيم لأبيه إلا عن موعدة وعدها إياه فلما تبين له أنه عدو لله تبرأ منه إن إبراهيم لأواه حليم

translation: And Allah would not let a people go astray after He has guided them until He makes clear to them what they should fear. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah does not leave people misguided after having guided them without first making clear to them what they should be cautious about. It highlights the divine justice and wisdom in guidance, indicating that Allah ensures that individuals are fully aware of the consequences of their actions before they go astray. This underscores the comprehensive knowledge of Allah over all matters, reinforcing the belief in His omniscience and fairness in dealing with His creation.
orig: وما كان الله ليضل قوما بعد إذ هداهم حتى يبين لهم ما يتقون إن الله بكل شيء عليم

translation: Indeed, Allah has the dominion of the heavens and the earth; He gives life and causes death, and you have, besides Allah, no protector or helper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and power of Allah over all creation. It underscores that Allah alone controls life and death, highlighting His omnipotence. The verse also serves as a reminder to believers of their complete dependence on Allah, as they have no other true protector or helper besides Him. This reinforces the concept of Tawheed (the oneness of God) and encourages reliance on Allah alone in all aspects of life.
orig: إن الله له ملك السماوات والأرض يحيي ويميت وما لكم من دون الله من ولي ولا نصير

translation: Indeed, Allah has forgiven the Prophet, the Muhajirun, and the Ansar who followed him in the hour of hardship after the hearts of a group of them had almost faltered. Then He forgave them. Indeed, He is to them Kind and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse reflects on the human nature of experiencing doubt and faltering faith during times of severe trial, as seen during a critical moment in the Prophet Muhammad's life. It underscores the divine compassion and forgiveness extended by Allah to the Prophet, the Muhajirun (emigrants from Mecca), and the Ansar (helpers in Medina) who remained steadfast despite their initial wavering. The verse emphasizes Allah's attributes of kindness and mercy, reassuring believers that even in moments of weakness, repentance and steadfastness are met with divine forgiveness and compassion.
orig: لقد تاب الله على النبي والمهاجرين والأنصار الذين اتبعوه في ساعة العسرة من بعد ما كاد يزيغ قلوب فريق منهم ثم تاب عليهم إنه بهم رءوف رحيم

translation: And [He also forgave] the three who were left behind [and regretted their failure to join the expedition] until the earth, vast as it is, became [too] narrow for them and their souls became [too] constricted for them, and they realized that there was no refuge from Allah except to Him. Then He turned to them in mercy that they might repent. Indeed, Allah is the Accepting of Repentance, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound spiritual journey of the three individuals who were left behind during a military expedition due to their initial reluctance or inability to join. Their experience of feeling the earth closing in on them, despite its vastness, symbolizes the intense psychological and spiritual distress they felt due to their separation from the community and from God's grace. This distress led them to a deep realization of their total dependence on Allah, understanding that there is no escape or refuge from His judgment except through turning back to Him in sincere repentance. The verse underscores the themes of divine mercy and forgiveness, illustrating that Allah is always ready to accept repentance, no matter how dire the situation, emphasizing His attributes of being the Most Merciful and the Acceptor of Repentance.
orig: وعلى الثلاثة الذين خلفوا حتى إذا ضاقت عليهم الأرض بما رحبت وضاقت عليهم أنفسهم وظنوا أن لا ملجأ من الله إلا إليه ثم تاب عليهم ليتوبوا إن الله هو التواب الرحيم

translation: O you who have believed, fear Allah and be with those who are true.
interpretation: This verse calls upon the believers to maintain a deep reverence and consciousness of Allah, which should manifest in their actions and decisions. Additionally, it encourages them to align themselves with individuals known for their truthfulness and integrity. By associating with the truthful, believers are guided towards righteousness and are supported in maintaining their own integrity and faith.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله وكونوا مع الصادقين

translation: It is not for the people of Medina and the Bedouins around them to remain behind the Messenger of Allah, nor should they prefer themselves to him. That is because they do not suffer any thirst or fatigue or hunger in the cause of Allah, nor do they tread any path that angers the disbelievers, nor do they inflict any injury upon an enemy, but it is recorded for them as a righteous deed. Indeed, Allah does not allow the reward of the doers of good to be lost.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of supporting the Prophet Muhammad in his mission, highlighting that it is obligatory for the people of Medina and the surrounding Bedouins to join him in his efforts. The verse underscores that any hardship or action taken in the path of Allah, including enduring thirst, fatigue, hunger, or engaging in actions that frustrate the disbelievers and harm the enemy, is considered a righteous deed. This reflects the value of collective effort and sacrifice in the cause of Islam, assuring believers that Allah recognizes and rewards every small act of goodness and dedication to the faith.
orig: ما كان لأهل المدينة ومن حولهم من الأعراب أن يتخلفوا عن رسول الله ولا يرغبوا بأنفسهم عن نفسه ذلك بأنهم لا يصيبهم ظمأ ولا نصب ولا مخمصة في سبيل الله ولا يطئون موطئا يغيظ الكفار ولا ينالون من عدو نيلا إلا كتب لهم به عمل صالح إن الله لا يضيع أجر المحسنين

translation: And they do not spend any small or large amount, nor do they traverse a valley, except that it is recorded for them, so that Allah may reward them for the best of what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the meticulous recording of every action by Allah, emphasizing that no deed, regardless of its size or the effort involved, goes unnoticed. It underscores the divine promise of reward for the believers' good deeds, encouraging them to continue their acts of charity and perseverance in faith, knowing that Allah will compensate them with the best possible recompense for their actions.
orig: ولا ينفقون نفقة صغيرة ولا كبيرة ولا يقطعون واديا إلا كتب لهم ليجزيهم الله أحسن ما كانوا يعملون

translation: And it is not for the believers to go forth [to battle] all at once. For there should separate from every division of them a group to [stay back to] obtain understanding in the religion and warn their people when they return to them that they might be cautious.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of balancing participation in jihad with the need for some members of the Muslim community to stay behind and deepen their understanding of Islam. It suggests that not all believers should engage in military efforts simultaneously; rather, a portion should remain to study and learn the religion thoroughly. This group's role is crucial as they are to educate and warn others upon their return, fostering a community that is both knowledgeable and cautious in its actions. The verse underscores the value of religious education and the dissemination of knowledge as integral to the strength and guidance of the Muslim ummah.
orig: وما كان المؤمنون لينفروا كافة فلولا نفر من كل فرقة منهم طائفة ليتفقهوا في الدين ولينذروا قومهم إذا رجعوا إليهم لعلهم يحذرون

translation: O you who have believed, fight those adjacent to you of the disbelievers and let them find in you harshness. And know that Allah is with the righteous.
interpretation: This verse is a directive to the believers to engage in combat against the disbelievers who are near them, emphasizing the importance of demonstrating strength and firmness in such encounters. It serves as a reminder that while engaging in this struggle, believers should remain conscious of their moral and ethical conduct, as Allah supports those who are pious and God-fearing. The verse underscores the balance between necessary defensive actions and maintaining righteousness.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا قاتلوا الذين يلونكم من الكفار وليجدوا فيكم غلظة واعلموا أن الله مع المتقين

translation: And whenever We send down a surah, there are some among them who say, 'Which of you has this increased in faith?' As for those who believed, it has increased them in faith, and they rejoice.
interpretation: This verse highlights the different reactions of people to the revelation of the Qur'an. It points out that while some may question or challenge the impact of the Qur'an on faith, those who are true believers find that their faith is strengthened and they feel joy upon receiving new revelations. This underscores the idea that the Qur'an serves as a source of guidance and reassurance for the faithful, enhancing their belief and spiritual well-being.
orig: وإذا ما أنزلت سورة فمنهم من يقول أيكم زادته هذه إيمانا فأما الذين آمنوا فزادتهم إيمانا وهم يستبشرون

translation: As for those in whose hearts is disease, it has increased them in filth to their filth, and they will die while they are disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse addresses individuals whose hearts are afflicted with doubt and hypocrisy. The term 'disease' metaphorically refers to their spiritual ailment, which is exacerbated by the revelation of truth. Instead of purifying their hearts, the truth only adds to their impurity, leading them further away from faith. Ultimately, they die in a state of disbelief, unable to overcome their internal corruption.
orig: وأما الذين في قلوبهم مرض فزادتهم رجسا إلى رجسهم وماتوا وهم كافرون

translation: Do they not see that they are tried every year once or twice? Yet, they neither repent nor do they remember.
interpretation: This verse highlights the recurring nature of trials and tribulations that humans face annually, suggesting that these events are meant to serve as reminders and opportunities for spiritual reflection and repentance. The verse criticizes the lack of response from people who fail to recognize these trials as divine tests, and thus, do not turn back to God in repentance or even remember the lessons these trials are meant to teach. It underscores the importance of being mindful and responsive to life's challenges as a means of spiritual growth and alignment with divine will.
orig: أولا يرون أنهم يفتنون في كل عام مرة أو مرتين ثم لا يتوبون ولا هم يذكرون

translation: And whenever We send down a sūrah, some of them say to others, 'Does anyone see you?' Then they turn away. Allāh has turned their hearts away because they are a people who do not understand.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy and lack of faith among some individuals who, upon the revelation of a new chapter of the Qur'an, conspire secretly to check if they are being observed, indicating their fear of being exposed. Their subsequent turning away from the message signifies their rejection and unwillingness to accept the truth. The verse suggests that their hearts have been sealed by Allah as a consequence of their persistent refusal to understand and embrace the guidance, illustrating the concept of divine justice where those who deliberately choose ignorance are left to their own devices.
orig: وإذا ما أنزلت سورة نظر بعضهم إلى بعض هل يراكم من أحد ثم انصرفوا صرف الله قلوبهم بأنهم قوم لا يفقهون

translation: There has come to you a Messenger from among yourselves, it grieves him that you should suffer, he is eager for your welfare, and he is compassionate and merciful to the believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unique relationship between the Prophet Muhammad and the believers. It highlights his human nature, being 'from among yourselves', which makes him relatable and accessible. The verse also underscores his deep emotional connection with the community; he feels their pain and is genuinely concerned for their well-being. The terms 'compassionate' and 'merciful' further illustrate his loving and caring nature towards the believers, portraying him as a leader who not only guides but also nurtures and supports his followers with kindness and empathy.
orig: لقد جاءكم رسول من أنفسكم عزيز عليه ما عنتم حريص عليكم بالمؤمنين رءوف رحيم

translation: But if they turn away, then say, 'Sufficient for me is Allah; there is no deity except Him. On Him I have relied, and He is the Lord of the Great Throne.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of complete reliance on Allah alone, especially in times of rejection or opposition from others. It teaches believers to maintain their faith and trust in Allah's sufficiency and sovereignty, regardless of external circumstances. The affirmation of 'there is no deity except Him' reinforces the concept of Tawheed (oneness of God), and the mention of 'the Lord of the Great Throne' highlights Allah's supreme power and authority over all creation.
orig: فإن تولوا فقل حسبي الله لا إله إلا هو عليه توكلت وهو رب العرش العظيم

translation: Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the Wise Book.
interpretation: The opening letters 'Alif, Lam, Ra' are among the mysterious letters (muqatta'at) whose meanings are known only to Allah, serving as a divine signature to the Qur'an. The phrase 'These are the verses of the Wise Book' emphasizes that the Qur'an is a source of profound wisdom and guidance, indicating its divine origin and comprehensive nature.
orig: الر تلك آيات الكتاب الحكيم

translation: Is it a wonder to people that We revealed Our message to a man from among them, saying, 'Warn mankind and give good news to those who believe that they will have a true position of honor with their Lord'? The disbelievers say, 'This is indeed an evident sorcerer.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the disbelief and astonishment of some people towards the divine revelation being given to a human messenger, specifically Prophet Muhammad. It highlights the dual role of the messenger to warn those who reject faith and to give glad tidings to the believers of a high rank with God. The reaction of the disbelievers, labeling the Prophet as a sorcerer, reflects their rejection of the message due to their inability to accept that God would choose a man from among them as His messenger.
orig: أكان للناس عجبا أن أوحينا إلى رجل منهم أن أنذر الناس وبشر الذين آمنوا أن لهم قدم صدق عند ربهم قال الكافرون إن هذا لساحر مبين

translation: Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days and then established Himself above the Throne. He directs the affairs. There is no intercessor except by His permission. That is Allah, your Lord, so worship Him. Then will you not remember?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness and sovereignty of Allah, highlighting His role as the Creator of the universe in a structured period of six days, and His ultimate authority seated upon the Throne. It underscores that all affairs are managed by Him alone, and that intercession is only possible with His permission, reinforcing the concept of tawhid (the oneness of God). The verse calls for worship of Allah alone, urging believers to reflect upon and remember these fundamental truths of their faith.
orig: إن ربكم الله الذي خلق السماوات والأرض في ستة أيام ثم استوى على العرش يدبر الأمر ما من شفيع إلا من بعد إذنه ذلكم الله ربكم فاعبدوه أفلا تذكرون

translation: To Him is your return all together. [It is] the promise of Allah [which is] truth. Indeed, He begins the [process of] creation and then repeats it, that He may reward those who have believed and done righteous deeds, in justice. But those who disbelieved will have a drink of scalding water and a painful punishment for what they used to deny.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability of returning to Allah, underscoring the concept of accountability in the afterlife. It reassures believers of the truthfulness of Allah's promise, highlighting His power over creation and its recreation. The verse serves as a reminder of divine justice, where believers who perform good deeds will be rewarded fairly, while those who reject faith will face severe punishment. This dichotomy serves to motivate individuals towards faith and righteous actions, illustrating the consequences of one's choices in the hereafter.
orig: إليه مرجعكم جميعا وعد الله حقا إنه يبدأ الخلق ثم يعيده ليجزي الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات بالقسط والذين كفروا لهم شراب من حميم وعذاب أليم بما كانوا يكفرون

translation: He is the One Who made the sun a radiant light and the moon a reflected light, and determined for it phases, so that you may know the number of years and calculation. Allah did not create this except in truth. He details the signs for a people who know.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's meticulous design in the creation of the sun and moon, serving specific functions beyond mere illumination. The sun provides direct light, while the moon reflects light and goes through phases, which are essential for humans to measure time, specifically years and months. This precise arrangement is presented as evidence of Allah's purposeful creation, intended to facilitate human life and understanding. The verse emphasizes that these natural phenomena are not random but are signs (ayat) from Allah, meant to be recognized and understood by those who seek knowledge, reinforcing the importance of reflection and learning in Islam.
orig: هو الذي جعل الشمس ضياء والقمر نورا وقدره منازل لتعلموا عدد السنين والحساب ما خلق الله ذلك إلا بالحق يفصل الآيات لقوم يعلمون

translation: Indeed, in the alternation of night and day and what Allah has created in the heavens and the earth are signs for a people who fear Him.
interpretation: This verse highlights the natural phenomena of the changing cycles of night and day, along with the vast creation in the heavens and the earth, as clear signs of Allah's power and wisdom. It suggests that those who are mindful of Allah and live in piety will recognize these signs as evidence of His existence and omnipotence, prompting them to reflect on their own lives and their relationship with the Creator.
orig: إن في اختلاف الليل والنهار وما خلق الله في السماوات والأرض لآيات لقوم يتقون

translation: Indeed, those who do not expect the meeting with Us and are pleased with the life of this world and feel secure in it, and those who are heedless of Our signs -
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual condition of individuals who are disconnected from the divine reality. They are characterized by a lack of anticipation for the afterlife and a contentment with worldly life, leading them to a false sense of security. Their heedlessness towards the signs of God further entrenches their spiritual negligence, illustrating a state of spiritual blindness and attachment to transient pleasures over eternal truths.
orig: إن الذين لا يرجون لقاءنا ورضوا بالحياة الدنيا واطمأنوا بها والذين هم عن آياتنا غافلون

translation: Those, their abode is the Fire, because of what they used to earn.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the individuals described will end up in Hell due to the consequences of their actions and deeds during their lifetime. It emphasizes the concept of accountability in the afterlife, where one's destination is determined by their moral and ethical choices.
orig: أولئك مأواهم النار بما كانوا يكسبون

translation: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds, their Lord will guide them because of their faith. Rivers will flow beneath them in the Gardens of Delight.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that faith combined with righteous actions leads to divine guidance and ultimate reward. The promise of rivers flowing beneath the believers in the Gardens of Delight symbolizes the abundance and joy of Paradise, illustrating the profound blessings awaiting those who maintain their faith and perform good deeds.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات يهديهم ربهم بإيمانهم تجري من تحتهم الأنهار في جنات النعيم

translation: Their call therein will be, 'Glory to You, O Allah,' and their greeting therein will be, 'Peace.' And the last of their call will be, 'Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse describes the state of the inhabitants of Paradise, where their constant expressions reflect their spiritual state and gratitude. The phrase 'Glory to You, O Allah' signifies their awe and recognition of God's majesty. Their greeting of 'Peace' indicates the harmony and tranquility of Paradise. The final praise, 'Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds,' underscores their eternal gratitude and acknowledgment of God's sovereignty over all creation, encapsulating their perpetual state of worship and thankfulness.
orig: دعواهم فيها سبحانك اللهم وتحيتهم فيها سلام وآخر دعواهم أن الحمد لله رب العالمين

translation: And if Allah were to hasten for the people the evil as they would hasten the good, their term would have been decreed for them. But We leave those who do not expect the meeting with Us, in their transgression, wandering blindly.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom in delaying the punishment for the wrongdoers. If Allah were to immediately bring upon people the evil consequences of their actions as quickly as they desire good outcomes, it would lead to their immediate destruction. Instead, Allah, out of His mercy, gives them time, which serves as a test and an opportunity for them to repent and correct their ways. Those who do not believe in the hereafter and continue in their sinful ways are left to wander in their transgressions, blinded by their own disbelief and arrogance.
orig: ولو يعجل الله للناس الشر استعجالهم بالخير لقضي إليهم أجلهم فنذر الذين لا يرجون لقاءنا في طغيانهم يعمهون

translation: And when affliction touches man, he calls upon Us, whether lying on his side, or sitting, or standing; but when We remove his affliction from him, he passes on as if he had never called upon Us to [remove] the affliction that touched him. Thus is made fair-seeming to the transgressors that which they have been doing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to turn to God in times of distress and then to forget or neglect Him once the hardship is alleviated. It serves as a reminder of the importance of maintaining a consistent relationship with God, not just in times of need. The verse critiques the behavior of those who only remember God when they are in trouble, suggesting that such inconsistency is a characteristic of those who exceed the bounds of righteousness. It underscores the allure of worldly distractions that can lead individuals away from a path of continuous devotion and gratitude towards God.
orig: وإذا مس الإنسان الضر دعانا لجنبه أو قاعدا أو قائما فلما كشفنا عنه ضره مر كأن لم يدعنا إلى ضر مسه كذلك زين للمسرفين ما كانوا يعملون

translation: And We have certainly destroyed the generations before you when they wronged, and their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they were not to believe. Thus do We recompense the criminal people.
interpretation: This verse underscores the historical pattern of divine justice where previous nations were destroyed due to their persistent injustice and rejection of the clear signs brought by their prophets. It serves as a warning to the current generation that similar consequences await those who continue to commit crimes and disbelieve, emphasizing that God's retribution is a consistent response to such behavior.
orig: ولقد أهلكنا القرون من قبلكم لما ظلموا وجاءتهم رسلهم بالبينات وما كانوا ليؤمنوا كذلك نجزي القوم المجرمين

translation: Then We made you successors in the land after them, so that We may see how you will act.
interpretation: This verse indicates that after the previous nations, God has appointed humans as successors on Earth, giving them the responsibility to manage and utilize its resources. The purpose behind this is a test from God, to observe and evaluate the actions and behaviors of humans, assessing their obedience, justice, and righteousness in fulfilling their role as stewards of the Earth.
orig: ثم جعلناكم خلائف في الأرض من بعدهم لننظر كيف تعملون

translation: And when Our clear verses are recited to them, those who do not expect to meet Us say, 'Bring a Qur'an other than this or change it.' Say, 'It is not for me to change it on my own accord. I only follow what is revealed to me. Indeed, I fear, if I were to disobey my Lord, the punishment of a Great Day.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the disbelief and arrogance of those who reject the Qur'an. When faced with the clear signs and verses of God, they demand a different scripture or alterations to the existing one, showing their unwillingness to accept divine guidance. The Prophet Muhammad is instructed to firmly declare that he has no authority to alter the Qur'an, emphasizing his role as a messenger who strictly adheres to divine revelation. This underscores the integrity and unchangeable nature of the Qur'an as a divine text. The verse also highlights the Prophet's fear of divine retribution should he disobey God, reflecting the seriousness of his mission and the consequences of straying from the path set by God.
orig: وإذا تتلى عليهم آياتنا بينات قال الذين لا يرجون لقاءنا ائت بقرآن غير هذا أو بدله قل ما يكون لي أن أبدله من تلقاء نفسي إن أتبع إلا ما يوحى إلي إني أخاف إن عصيت ربي عذاب يوم عظيم

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], 'If Allah had willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made it known to you. I have certainly lived among you a lifetime before this. Then will you not use reason?'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of divine will in the revelation of the Qur'an. It suggests that the Prophet Muhammad's recitation of the Qur'an and the people's knowledge of it are contingent upon Allah's will. The verse also highlights the Prophet's long-standing presence among his people before the revelation, which serves as a testament to his integrity and humanity. The rhetorical question at the end challenges the listeners to reflect on these facts and use their reason to recognize the truth of the message.
orig: قل لو شاء الله ما تلوته عليكم ولا أدراكم به فقد لبثت فيكم عمرا من قبله أفلا تعقلون

translation: So who is more unjust than one who invents a lie about Allah or denies His verses? Indeed, the criminals will not succeed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity of two major sins: attributing falsehood to Allah and rejecting His signs. It underscores that those who engage in such acts are considered the most unjust, as they not only mislead themselves but also others. The verse serves as a warning that those who commit these crimes, referred to as 'the criminals,' will ultimately fail in achieving true success or salvation, highlighting the moral and spiritual consequences of such actions.
orig: فمن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا أو كذب بآياته إنه لا يفلح المجرمون

translation: And they worship besides Allah that which neither harms them nor benefits them, and they say, 'These are our intercessors with Allah.' Say, 'Do you inform Allah of something He does not know in the heavens or on the earth?' Exalted is He and high above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse critiques the practice of idolatry and the belief in intercessors other than Allah. It emphasizes the futility of worshipping entities that have no power to harm or benefit, highlighting the absurdity of attributing intercessory roles to them. The rhetorical question posed in the verse challenges the notion that humans could inform Allah of something unknown to Him, underscoring Allah's omniscience and the blasphemy of associating partners with Him. The declaration of Allah's transcendence ('Exalted is He and high above') serves to reaffirm His unique status and the purity of monotheism, rejecting any form of polytheism or idolatry.
orig: ويعبدون من دون الله ما لا يضرهم ولا ينفعهم ويقولون هؤلاء شفعاؤنا عند الله قل أتنبئون الله بما لا يعلم في السماوات ولا في الأرض سبحانه وتعالى عما يشركون

translation: And mankind was not but one community [united in religion], but then they differed. And if not for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been judged between them in what they differ.
interpretation: This verse reflects on the unity of humanity in its origin, both in terms of creation and in the initial monotheistic belief system. It suggests that all people were once united under one religion or belief, but over time, differences emerged leading to various religious and ideological divisions. The 'word that preceded from your Lord' refers to God's decree or promise, which delays the final judgment on these differences until the appointed time. This indicates God's patience and mercy, allowing time for people to reflect, repent, and return to the truth before the final judgment is made on their disputes.
orig: وما كان الناس إلا أمة واحدة فاختلفوا ولولا كلمة سبقت من ربك لقضي بينهم فيما فيه يختلفون

translation: And they say, "Why has no sign been sent down to him from his Lord?" Say, "The unseen belongs to Allah alone. So wait; indeed, I am with you among those who wait."
interpretation: This verse addresses the skeptics who demanded miraculous signs from the Prophet Muhammad to validate his prophethood. It emphasizes the concept of the unseen (al-ghayb), which is exclusively within Allah's knowledge. The Prophet is instructed to respond to these demands by affirming that only Allah knows the unseen and that all should wait patiently for divine wisdom to unfold. This response not only underscores the limitations of human understanding but also encourages patience and trust in Allah's timing and plan.
orig: ويقولون لولا أنزل عليه آية من ربه فقل إنما الغيب لله فانتظروا إني معكم من المنتظرين

translation: And when We let the people taste mercy after adversity has touched them, at once they conspire against Our verses. Say, "Allah is swifter in strategy." Indeed, Our messengers record what you conspire.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to forget or even oppose divine guidance when experiencing relief after hardship. It suggests that people often attribute their relief to their own efforts or luck, rather than recognizing it as a mercy from Allah. The verse warns that such ingratitude and plotting against divine signs will be noted by Allah's messengers, emphasizing that no scheme against the truth can outpace Allah's wisdom and justice.
orig: وإذا أذقنا الناس رحمة من بعد ضراء مستهم إذا لهم مكر في آياتنا قل الله أسرع مكرا إن رسلنا يكتبون ما تمكرون

translation: He it is Who enables you to travel on land and sea until, when you are in ships and they sail with them by a goodly wind and they rejoice therein, there comes to them a stormy wind and waves come to them from all directions, and they think that they are surrounded by them; they call upon Allah, making their faith pure for Him alone, [saying], 'If You deliver us from this, we will surely be among the thankful.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the human tendency to turn to God in times of distress and the promise of gratitude if saved. It emphasizes the power of Allah over nature and the fleeting nature of human faith, which often becomes sincere only when faced with life-threatening situations. The verse serves as a reminder to maintain a constant state of gratitude and faith, not just in moments of desperation.
orig: هو الذي يسيركم في البر والبحر حتى إذا كنتم في الفلك وجرين بهم بريح طيبة وفرحوا بها جاءتها ريح عاصف وجاءهم الموج من كل مكان وظنوا أنهم أحيط بهم دعوا الله مخلصين له الدين لئن أنجيتنا من هذه لنكونن من الشاكرين

translation: So when We delivered them, at once they committed oppression in the land without right. O mankind, your oppression is only against yourselves. [It is but] the enjoyment of worldly life. Then to Us is your return, and We will inform you of what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to revert to wrongdoing even after being saved from adversity, emphasizing that such actions are ultimately self-destructive. The temporary pleasures of this worldly life should not distract from the ultimate accountability before God, where all deeds will be judged and consequences faced.
orig: فلما أنجاهم إذا هم يبغون في الأرض بغير الحق يا أيها الناس إنما بغيكم على أنفسكم متاع الحياة الدنيا ثم إلينا مرجعكم فننبئكم بما كنتم تعملون

translation: The example of the worldly life is like water that We sent down from the sky, and it mixed with the plants of the earth from which people and cattle eat, until when the earth takes on its adornment and is beautified and its people think that they have control over it, Our command comes to it by night or by day, and We make it like a reaped field, as if it had not flourished yesterday. Thus do We explain the signs for a people who reflect.
interpretation: This verse uses the metaphor of rain and plant growth to illustrate the transient and deceptive nature of worldly life. Just as rain causes plants to grow and the earth to become lush, leading people to believe they have control over it, worldly life can seem prosperous and under human control. However, just as suddenly as the rain can turn the earth into a barren field, God's command can strip away the illusions of control and permanence in life. This serves as a reminder of the impermanence of worldly affairs and the importance of reflecting on the deeper meanings and signs provided by God, encouraging believers to focus on the eternal rather than the temporary.
orig: إنما مثل الحياة الدنيا كماء أنزلناه من السماء فاختلط به نبات الأرض مما يأكل الناس والأنعام حتى إذا أخذت الأرض زخرفها وازينت وظن أهلها أنهم قادرون عليها أتاها أمرنا ليلا أو نهارا فجعلناها حصيدا كأن لم تغن بالأمس كذلك نفصل الآيات لقوم يتفكرون

translation: And Allah invites to the Home of Peace and guides whom He wills to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's invitation to all of humanity towards the ultimate abode of peace, which is Paradise. It highlights that Allah guides those He chooses to the straight path, indicating His mercy and sovereignty in guiding individuals towards righteousness and salvation. The 'straight path' refers to the path of Islam, which leads to divine peace and fulfillment.
orig: والله يدعو إلى دار السلام ويهدي من يشاء إلى صراط مستقيم

translation: For those who have done good is the best [reward] and an increase. And no darkness or humiliation will cover their faces. Those are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine promise of reward for those who perform righteous deeds. The "best [reward]" refers to the ultimate reward of Paradise, while the "increase" suggests additional blessings or honors beyond the basic reward. The assurance that their faces will not be covered with "darkness or humiliation" emphasizes the purity and honor they will experience in the afterlife, free from any form of disgrace. The verse concludes by affirming their eternal residence in Paradise, underscoring the permanence of their reward and the enduring nature of their joy and peace.
orig: للذين أحسنوا الحسنى وزيادة ولا يرهق وجوههم قتر ولا ذلة أولئك أصحاب الجنة هم فيها خالدون

translation: And those who have earned evil deeds, the recompense of an evil deed is the like thereof; and humiliation will cover them - they will have no protector from Allah - as if their faces are covered with pieces of the dark night. Those are the people of the Fire; they will abide therein forever.
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle of divine justice, where the consequences of one's actions are meted out with an equivalent measure. It emphasizes that those who engage in wrongdoing will face a corresponding punishment, not only in the form of tangible retribution but also through spiritual and emotional degradation, symbolized by the covering of their faces with darkness. This imagery of darkness signifies a separation from divine light and guidance, indicating a state of spiritual blindness and despair. The verse further solidifies the concept of eternal damnation for those who persist in evil, reinforcing the Qur'anic theme of accountability and the afterlife, where the 'people of the Fire' are those eternally committed to their misdeeds, thus remaining in Hell indefinitely.
orig: والذين كسبوا السيئات جزاء سيئة بمثلها وترهقهم ذلة ما لهم من الله من عاصم كأنما أغشيت وجوههم قطعا من الليل مظلما أولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون

translation: And the Day We will gather them all together - then We will say to those who associated others with Allah, "To your place, you and your 'partners." Then We will separate them, and their 'partners' will say, "You did not used to worship us."
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate accountability on the Day of Judgment. It underscores the futility and falsehood of polytheism, where those who worshipped false deities will be confronted with the reality that these deities deny any worship or association with them. This separation and denial serve as a profound lesson on the oneness of God and the rejection of any partners ascribed to Him, emphasizing that only Allah is worthy of worship and that all other supposed deities will disavow any connection to the acts of worship directed towards them.
orig: ويوم نحشرهم جميعا ثم نقول للذين أشركوا مكانكم أنتم وشركاؤكم فزيلنا بينهم وقال شركاؤهم ما كنتم إيانا تعبدون

translation: So sufficient is Allah as a witness between us and you, if we should be heedless of your worship.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sufficiency of Allah as the ultimate witness in disputes or differences between believers and non-believers. It suggests that even if believers are accused of neglecting the worship practices of others, Allah's knowledge and judgment are enough to vindicate them. The verse reassures believers that their focus on true worship and their disregard for idolatrous practices are justified and witnessed by Allah, who will ultimately judge between all parties.
orig: فكفى بالله شهيدا بيننا وبينكم إن كنا عن عبادتكم لغافلين

translation: There, every soul will be put to the test for what it did previously, and they will be brought back to Allah, their true Lord, and what they used to fabricate will vanish from them.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Day of Judgment where every individual will be held accountable for their actions. The 'test' refers to the scrutiny of one's deeds, where nothing will be hidden. The return to Allah, described as the 'true Lord,' underscores the ultimate reality and authority of Allah over all creation. The phrase 'what they used to fabricate' refers to false beliefs, lies, and idolatry that people clung to in life, which will be exposed as falsehood and will no longer provide any support or refuge on that day. This verse serves as a reminder of the importance of living a life aligned with truth and righteousness, as all falsehoods will be stripped away in the hereafter.
orig: هنالك تبلو كل نفس ما أسلفت وردوا إلى الله مولاهم الحق وضل عنهم ما كانوا يفترون

translation: Say, 'Who provides for you from the heaven and the earth? Or who controls hearing and sight? And who brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living? And who manages all affairs?' They will say, 'Allah.' Say, 'Then will you not fear Him?'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness and omnipotence of Allah by highlighting His role in providing sustenance, controlling human faculties, and managing the cycle of life and death. It challenges the listeners to acknowledge Allah as the sole provider and manager of all affairs, and then urges them to fear Him and be conscious of their actions, questioning their lack of piety despite this recognition.
orig: قل من يرزقكم من السماء والأرض أمن يملك السمع والأبصار ومن يخرج الحي من الميت ويخرج الميت من الحي ومن يدبر الأمر فسيقولون الله فقل أفلا تتقون

translation: So that is Allah, your true Lord. What then, after the truth, is there except error? How then are you turned away?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute truth of Allah as the sole Lord and Creator. It questions the logic of turning away from this undeniable truth, suggesting that any deviation from acknowledging Allah as the true Lord leads only to error and misguidance. The rhetorical question at the end challenges the reader to reflect on their actions and choices, urging a return to the straight path of truth.
orig: فذلكم الله ربكم الحق فماذا بعد الحق إلا الضلال فأنى تصرفون

translation: Thus the word of your Lord has been justified against those who defiantly disobeyed; that they will not believe.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine decree that those who persistently rebel against God's commands will ultimately be unable to embrace faith. It reflects the consequence of their ongoing defiance and moral corruption, which hardens their hearts against belief. The verse serves as a reminder of the seriousness of disobedience and the spiritual consequences it entails, emphasizing that such a state of disbelief is a fulfillment of God's word.
orig: كذلك حقت كلمت ربك على الذين فسقوا أنهم لا يؤمنون

translation: Say, 'Is there among your partners any who can begin creation and then repeat it?' Say, 'Allah begins creation and then repeats it. So how are you deluded?'
interpretation: This verse challenges the polytheists by questioning the capabilities of their false deities or partners they ascribe to Allah. It emphasizes the exclusive power of Allah as the sole Creator who initiates the creation and has the ability to resurrect it. The rhetorical question at the end, 'So how are you deluded?', serves to highlight the absurdity and error in their beliefs, urging them to reflect on the undeniable signs of Allah's omnipotence and to abandon their false gods.
orig: قل هل من شركائكم من يبدأ الخلق ثم يعيده قل الله يبدأ الخلق ثم يعيده فأنى تؤفكون

translation: Say, 'Is there any of your partners who guides to the truth?' Say, 'Allah guides to the truth. Is He who guides to the truth more worthy to be followed, or he who guides not unless he is guided?' Then what is [wrong] with you - how do you judge?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the exclusive ability of Allah to guide to the truth, challenging the notion that any partners or deities associated with Him can do the same. It poses a rhetorical question to the believers, urging them to reflect on whom they should follow: Allah, who inherently guides to the truth, or those who can only guide if they themselves are guided by Allah. The verse critiques the judgment of those who follow false deities, questioning the rationality and logic behind such choices, and implicitly calls for a return to the worship and following of the one true God, Allah.
orig: قل هل من شركائكم من يهدي إلى الحق قل الله يهدي للحق أفمن يهدي إلى الحق أحق أن يتبع أمن لا يهدي إلا أن يهدى فما لكم كيف تحكمون

translation: And most of them follow nothing but conjecture. Indeed, conjecture avails nothing against the truth. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the human tendency to rely on assumptions and speculation rather than seeking out and adhering to the truth. It highlights that such conjecture is ultimately futile and ineffective when compared to the absolute truth, which is known and upheld by Allah. The verse serves as a reminder that Allah is fully aware of all actions and intentions, reinforcing the importance of seeking and following the truth as opposed to baseless assumptions.
orig: وما يتبع أكثرهم إلا ظنا إن الظن لا يغني من الحق شيئا إن الله عليم بما يفعلون

translation: And this Qur'an is not such as could ever be invented in despite of Allah; but it is a confirmation of that which was before it and an exposition of the Book - wherein there is no doubt - from the Lord of the Worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin of the Qur'an, asserting that it could not have been fabricated by anyone other than Allah. It serves as a confirmation of the previous scriptures, thereby validating their messages, and it provides a detailed explanation of the divine guidance. The verse underscores the certainty and truthfulness of the Qur'an, attributing its revelation to the Lord of all creation, thus establishing its authority and authenticity.
orig: وما كان هذا القرآن أن يفترى من دون الله ولكن تصديق الذي بين يديه وتفصيل الكتاب لا ريب فيه من رب العالمين

translation: Or do they say, 'He has invented it'? Say, 'Then bring forth a surah like it and call upon [for assistance] whomever you can besides Allah, if you should be truthful.'
interpretation: This verse challenges the disbelievers who claim that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) fabricated the Qur'an. It invites them to produce a chapter (surah) similar to the Qur'an if they believe it to be a human creation, emphasizing the Qur'an's divine origin and inimitable nature. The verse also underscores the futility of seeking help from anyone other than Allah in this challenge, highlighting the absolute dependence on God and the truthfulness of the Prophet's message.
orig: أم يقولون افتراه قل فأتوا بسورة مثله وادعوا من استطعتم من دون الله إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Nay, they have denied that which they could not compass the knowledge of, and whose final explanation has not yet come to them. Thus did those before them deny. Then see what was the end of the wrong-doers!
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to reject what they do not understand or cannot fully grasp. It points out that people often deny divine truths and revelations because they lack the knowledge to comprehend them fully, and because the complete realization or interpretation of these truths has not yet been revealed to them. The verse draws a parallel between the current deniers and those of the past, urging reflection on the ultimate fate of those who wrongfully reject divine guidance. It serves as a reminder of the consequences of disbelief and the importance of faith in the unseen and the yet-to-be-understood aspects of divine wisdom.
orig: بل كذبوا بما لم يحيطوا بعلمه ولما يأتهم تأويله كذلك كذب الذين من قبلهم فانظر كيف كان عاقبة الظالمين

translation: And among them are some who believe in it, and among them are some who do not believe in it. And your Lord knows best the corruptors.
interpretation: This verse highlights the diversity of responses to the message of the Qur'an among people. It acknowledges that while some will accept and believe in its truth, others will reject it. The phrase 'your Lord knows best the corruptors' suggests that God is fully aware of those who reject the message out of corrupt intentions or mischief, emphasizing divine knowledge and justice in distinguishing between believers and disbelievers.
orig: ومنهم من يؤمن به ومنهم من لا يؤمن به وربك أعلم بالمفسدين

translation: And if they deny you, then say: For me are my deeds and for you are your deeds. You are innocent of what I do, and I am innocent of what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes personal accountability and the separation of individual actions in matters of faith. It instructs the Prophet Muhammad, and by extension all believers, to focus on their own deeds and not be swayed or disheartened by the disbelief or opposition of others. It underscores the principle that each person is responsible for their own actions and will be judged accordingly, promoting a sense of independence and moral integrity in one's religious practice.
orig: وإن كذبوك فقل لي عملي ولكم عملكم أنتم بريئون مما أعمل وأنا بريء مما تعملون

translation: And among them are some who listen to you. But can you make the deaf hear, even though they do not understand?
interpretation: This verse highlights the challenge of communicating with those who are spiritually deaf and lack understanding. It suggests that the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) is tasked with conveying the message of Islam, but he cannot force comprehension or acceptance upon those who are unwilling or unable to grasp it due to their own spiritual or intellectual barriers.
orig: ومنهم من يستمعون إليك أفأنت تسمع الصم ولو كانوا لا يعقلون

translation: And among them are those who look at you, but can you guide the blind even though they do not see?
interpretation: This verse highlights the challenge of guiding those who are spiritually blind, indicating that some people may appear to be paying attention but are actually incapable of understanding or accepting the truth due to their own internal barriers. It emphasizes the limitation of the Prophet's role in guiding such individuals, suggesting that true guidance ultimately comes from Allah.
orig: ومنهم من ينظر إليك أفأنت تهدي العمي ولو كانوا لا يبصرون

translation: Indeed, Allah does not wrong the people at all, but it is the people who wrong themselves.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the justice of Allah, indicating that any hardship or misfortune experienced by individuals is not due to injustice from Allah, but rather a result of their own actions and choices. It underscores personal responsibility and the concept that humans are often the architects of their own suffering through their own wrongdoing.
orig: إن الله لا يظلم الناس شيئا ولكن الناس أنفسهم يظلمون

translation: And the Day He will gather them, [it will be] as if they had not remained [in the world] but an hour of the day, [and] they will know each other. Those will have lost who denied the meeting with Allah, and were not guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fleeting nature of worldly life in comparison to the Hereafter. On the Day of Judgment, it will seem to those gathered as if their entire earthly existence lasted only an hour. This realization will come too late for those who denied the reality of meeting Allah, highlighting their ultimate loss and lack of guidance. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of faith and preparation for the afterlife, urging believers to recognize the temporary nature of this world and the eternal significance of the next.
orig: ويوم يحشرهم كأن لم يلبثوا إلا ساعة من النهار يتعارفون بينهم قد خسر الذين كذبوا بلقاء الله وما كانوا مهتدين

translation: And whether We show you some of what We promise them or take you [in death], to Us is their return; then Allah is a Witness over what they do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability of divine judgment and the omniscience of Allah. It reassures the Prophet Muhammad that whether he witnesses the fulfillment of God's promises to the disbelievers or passes away before seeing it, the ultimate return of all people is to Allah. Here, Allah asserts His role as the ultimate witness to all actions, underscoring that no deed, hidden or apparent, escapes His knowledge. This serves as a reminder of accountability and the certainty of divine justice.
orig: وإما نرينك بعض الذي نعدهم أو نتوفينك فإلينا مرجعهم ثم الله شهيد على ما يفعلون

translation: And for every nation is a messenger. So when their messenger comes, it will be judged between them in justice, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universality of divine guidance and justice. It indicates that every community or nation is provided with a messenger from God, ensuring that no group is left without guidance. When the appointed messenger arrives and delivers the message, God will judge the people of that nation with fairness and equity. The assurance that 'they will not be wronged' underscores the divine commitment to justice, highlighting that each individual will be judged based on their actions and the guidance they received, without any injustice or oppression.
orig: ولكل أمة رسول فإذا جاء رسولهم قضي بينهم بالقسط وهم لا يظلمون

translation: And they say, "When is this promise, if you are truthful?"
interpretation: This verse reflects the skepticism and impatience of the disbelievers towards the Prophet Muhammad's warnings about the Day of Judgment. They are challenging the believers to prove the truth of their claims by demanding a specific time for the promised events, indicating their doubt in the prophecy and the message of Islam.
orig: ويقولون متى هذا الوعد إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Say, 'I have no power to cause harm or bring benefit to myself, except as Allah wills. For every nation there is an appointed term. When their time arrives, they can neither delay it nor advance it by a moment.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the complete dependence of humans on Allah's will, highlighting the Prophet Muhammad's humility and submission to divine decree. It underscores the concept of predestination (qadar) in Islam, where every event, including the lifespan of nations, is predetermined by Allah. The verse reassures believers of the inevitability and precision of divine timing, encouraging patience and trust in Allah's plan.
orig: قل لا أملك لنفسي ضرا ولا نفعا إلا ما شاء الله لكل أمة أجل إذا جاء أجلهم فلا يستأخرون ساعة ولا يستقدمون

translation: Say, 'Have you considered: if His punishment should come to you by night or by day, what portion of it would the criminals wish to hasten?'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability and suddenness of divine punishment, urging the disbelievers to reflect on their readiness for such an event. It challenges them to consider whether they would still be eager for the punishment they mockingly demand, highlighting their lack of understanding and the gravity of their situation.
orig: قل أرأيتم إن أتاكم عذابه بياتا أو نهارا ماذا يستعجل منه المجرمون

translation: Then, when it befalls, you believe in it? And now, when [you had been] impatient for it?
interpretation: This verse highlights the irony and hypocrisy of those who doubted the divine warnings and impatiently demanded the punishment, only to believe in them when the punishment actually occurs. It serves as a critique of their lack of faith and understanding until faced with the consequences, emphasizing the importance of belief and patience in the unseen and the promises of God.
orig: أثم إذا ما وقع آمنتم به آلآن وقد كنتم به تستعجلون

translation: Then it will be said to those who wronged, "Taste the punishment of eternity! Are you recompensed except for what you used to earn?"
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle of divine justice, emphasizing that the punishment in the hereafter is a direct consequence of one's actions in this life. It serves as a reminder that individuals will be held accountable for their deeds, and the eternal nature of the punishment reflects the gravity of their wrongdoings. The rhetorical question at the end reinforces the idea that there is no injustice in the divine retribution; it is solely based on what individuals have earned through their actions.
orig: ثم قيل للذين ظلموا ذوقوا عذاب الخلد هل تجزون إلا بما كنتم تكسبون

translation: And they ask you, [O Muhammad], "Is it true?" Say, "Yes, by my Lord. It is the truth, and you will not cause failure [to Allah]."
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad's response to those who question the truth of the Qur'an and the Day of Judgment. The affirmation "Yes, by my Lord" underscores the certainty and divine origin of the message. The phrase "and you will not cause failure [to Allah]" reassures believers that no matter how much the disbelievers may try to oppose or deny the truth, they cannot thwart Allah's plan or the ultimate fulfillment of His promises.
orig: ويستنبئونك أحق هو قل إي وربي إنه لحق وما أنتم بمعجزين

translation: And if every soul that wronged itself had all that is on earth, it would offer it in ransom, and they would feel remorse when they see the punishment. And it will be judged between them with justice, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of wrongdoing and the futility of seeking redemption through material wealth when faced with divine judgment. It illustrates that at the moment of reckoning, the realization of the impending punishment will evoke deep regret in wrongdoers, yet no amount of earthly possessions can avert the consequences of their actions. The verse reassures that the judgment will be conducted with absolute justice, emphasizing that no one will be treated unfairly, highlighting the fairness and inevitability of divine justice.
orig: ولو أن لكل نفس ظلمت ما في الأرض لافتدت به وأسروا الندامة لما رأوا العذاب وقضي بينهم بالقسط وهم لا يظلمون

translation: Beware, to Allah belongs all that is in the heavens and the earth. Beware, the promise of Allah is true, but most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty of Allah over everything in existence, encompassing both the heavens and the earth. It serves as a reminder to believers of the omnipotence and ownership of Allah over all creation. The second part of the verse reaffirms the certainty and truthfulness of Allah's promises, which are often related to divine rewards and punishments. However, the verse also points out a common human failing: the lack of knowledge or understanding among most people about these fundamental truths.
