This ignorance leads to disbelief or neglect of Allah's promises, underscoring the need for increased awareness and faith in the divine assurances.
orig: ألا إن لله ما في السماوات والأرض ألا إن وعد الله حق ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: He gives life and causes death, and to Him you will return.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and authority of Allah over life and death, underscoring that all creation is ultimately accountable to Him and will return to Him for judgment.
orig: هو يحيي ويميت وإليه ترجعون

translation: O mankind, there has come to you a warning from your Lord, and a healing for what is in the breasts, and guidance and mercy for the believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the comprehensive nature of the Qur'an as a divine message sent to all of humanity. It serves multiple purposes: it acts as a warning to heed the guidance of God, offers healing for spiritual and emotional ailments, provides clear guidance on how to live righteously, and extends mercy specifically to those who believe. The mention of 'healing for what is in the breasts' suggests that the Qur'an addresses the inner struggles and diseases of the heart, offering solace and a path to spiritual recovery.
orig: يا أيها الناس قد جاءتكم موعظة من ربكم وشفاء لما في الصدور وهدى ورحمة للمؤمنين

translation: Say, 'By the grace of Allah and His mercy- in that let them rejoice; it is better than what they accumulate.'
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to find true joy and satisfaction in the blessings and mercy bestowed by Allah, rather than in material possessions. It emphasizes that spiritual contentment derived from divine favor is far superior to any worldly gains or accumulations.
orig: قل بفضل الله وبرحمته فبذلك فليفرحوا هو خير مما يجمعون

translation: Say, "Have you considered what Allah has sent down to you of provision of which you have made some lawful and some unlawful?" Say, "Has Allah permitted you [to do so], or do you invent [something] about Allah?"
interpretation: This verse challenges the human tendency to arbitrarily categorize certain provisions as lawful or unlawful without divine sanction. It emphasizes that only Allah has the authority to declare what is permissible or forbidden. The verse critiques the practice of attributing human-made rules to divine will, urging believers to adhere strictly to Allah's commandments rather than fabricating religious laws.
orig: قل أرأيتم ما أنزل الله لكم من رزق فجعلتم منه حراما وحلالا قل آلله أذن لكم أم على الله تفترون

translation: And what will be the thought of those who invent lies against Allah on the Day of Resurrection? Indeed, Allah is full of bounty to mankind, but most of them are not thankful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the grave consequences faced by those who falsely attribute statements to Allah. On the Day of Resurrection, their realization of the severity of their actions will be profound. The verse also emphasizes Allah's abundant grace and blessings upon humanity, yet it points out the ingratitude of most people, which is a significant spiritual failing.
orig: وما ظن الذين يفترون على الله الكذب يوم القيامة إن الله لذو فضل على الناس ولكن أكثرهم لا يشكرون

translation: And whatever matter you are engaged in, and whatever portion of the Qur'an you recite, and whatever deed you do - We are Witnesses over you when you are engaged therein. And not [even] the weight of an atom on the earth or in the heaven escapes your Lord; nor [anything] smaller than that or greater but is [written] in a clear Record.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipresence and omniscience of Allah, indicating that He is fully aware of every action, word, and even the smallest details of existence. It serves as a reminder to believers that they are constantly under divine observation, encouraging mindfulness and accountability in all aspects of life, as everything is recorded in the divine ledger.
orig: وما تكون في شأن وما تتلو منه من قرآن ولا تعملون من عمل إلا كنا عليكم شهودا إذ تفيضون فيه وما يعزب عن ربك من مثقال ذرة في الأرض ولا في السماء ولا أصغر من ذلك ولا أكبر إلا في كتاب مبين

translation: Behold! Verily on the friends of Allah there is no fear, nor shall they grieve.
interpretation: This verse highlights the special status of those who are close to Allah, known as the 'awliya'. It assures that these individuals, due to their deep faith and righteous actions, are protected from fear and sorrow. The absence of fear relates to their trust in Allah's plan, while the absence of grief stems from their contentment with divine decree. This promise serves as a motivation for believers to strive to be among Allah's friends by adhering closely to His guidance.
orig: ألا إن أولياء الله لا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: Those who believed and were pious
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of faith (iman) coupled with righteousness (taqwa). It suggests that true belief in Allah must be accompanied by a conscious effort to avoid sin and to live a life of moral and ethical integrity. The combination of faith and piety is essential for spiritual success and closeness to Allah.
orig: الذين آمنوا وكانوا يتقون

translation: For them there is good news in the life of this world and in the Hereafter. There is no change in the words of Allah; that is the great triumph.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the assurance and certainty of divine promises for the believers. The 'good news' refers to the blessings and guidance they receive in their earthly life, as well as the eternal reward in the Hereafter. The phrase 'no change in the words of Allah' underscores the immutable nature of God's decrees and promises, providing comfort and confidence to the faithful. The 'great triumph' signifies the ultimate success and salvation that believers achieve through their faith and adherence to God's guidance, culminating in the eternal bliss of the Hereafter.
orig: لهم البشرى في الحياة الدنيا وفي الآخرة لا تبديل لكلمات الله ذلك هو الفوز العظيم

translation: And let not their speech grieve you. Indeed, all might belongs to Allah. He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse reassures the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) not to be disheartened by the derogatory remarks and opposition from disbelievers. It emphasizes that ultimate power and authority rest solely with Allah, who is fully aware of all things and hears all that is said. The verse serves as a reminder that despite the apparent strength or influence of the opponents, their power is insignificant compared to Allah's, and He is cognizant of the Prophet's situation and the challenges he faces.
orig: ولا يحزنك قولهم إن العزة لله جميعا هو السميع العليم

translation: Beware! To Allah belong all those who are in the heavens and all those who are on the earth. And those whom they invoke besides Allah do not follow them as partners; they follow nothing but conjecture, and they do nothing but lie.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty of Allah over all creation, both in the heavens and on earth. It critiques the practice of shirk, or associating partners with Allah, by highlighting that the deities or idols worshipped by polytheists have no real power or influence. Instead, those who engage in such worship are merely following baseless assumptions and fabrications, as these false deities cannot respond or aid them in any way. The verse serves as a reminder of the futility and falsehood of idolatry, urging believers to recognize and worship only Allah, the true and sole deity.
orig: ألا إن لله من في السماوات ومن في الأرض وما يتبع الذين يدعون من دون الله شركاء إن يتبعون إلا الظن وإن هم إلا يخرصون

translation: He is the One Who made the night for you to rest in and the day to see. Indeed, in that are signs for a people who listen.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's mercy and wisdom in creating the cycle of night and day, which serves as a natural system for rest and activity. The night is designed for humans to rest and rejuvenate, while the day provides light for them to work and engage in their daily tasks. The verse suggests that this natural phenomenon is a sign of God's thoughtful creation, and it calls upon people to reflect on these signs and listen to the message they convey about the Creator's care and planning.
orig: هو الذي جعل لكم الليل لتسكنوا فيه والنهار مبصرا إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يسمعون

translation: They say, 'Allah has taken a son.' Exalted is He; He is the [one who is] free of need. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. You have no authority for this. Do you say about Allah that which you do not know?
interpretation: This verse addresses the claim made by some that Allah has a son, which is a direct challenge to the fundamental Islamic belief in the oneness and uniqueness of Allah. The verse emphasizes Allah's self-sufficiency and sovereignty over all creation, indicating that He has no need for offspring. It also criticizes the baselessness of such claims, highlighting that those who make them lack any scriptural or rational evidence. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to be cautious and truthful in their statements about Allah, avoiding unfounded assertions.
orig: قالوا اتخذ الله ولدا سبحانه هو الغني له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض إن عندكم من سلطان بهذا أتقولون على الله ما لا تعلمون

translation: Say, 'Indeed, those who invent falsehood about Allah will not succeed.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe consequences of attributing false statements or lies to Allah. It serves as a warning that such actions lead to failure and ruin, both in this life and the hereafter. The use of "Say" at the beginning instructs the Prophet Muhammad to convey this message clearly to the people, highlighting the importance of truthfulness and the gravity of fabricating lies about the divine.
orig: قل إن الذين يفترون على الله الكذب لا يفلحون

translation: A provision in the world, then to Us is their return; then We will make them taste the severe punishment because of what they used to disbelieve.
interpretation: This verse suggests that worldly possessions and enjoyments are temporary and are given as a test. Ultimately, all individuals will return to Allah, where they will be judged based on their faith and actions. Those who disbelieved and rejected the truth during their life will face a severe punishment as a consequence of their disbelief. The verse emphasizes the transient nature of worldly life and the eternal significance of the hereafter, urging believers to prioritize their faith and moral conduct.
orig: متاع في الدنيا ثم إلينا مرجعهم ثم نذيقهم العذاب الشديد بما كانوا يكفرون

translation: And recite to them the news of Noah, when he said to his people, 'O my people, if my stay (with you) and my reminding you of the signs of Allah has become burdensome upon you, then I put my trust in Allah. So decide upon your plan and (call upon) your partners. Then let not your plan be doubtful to you. Then pass your judgment on me and give me no respite.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of steadfastness in faith and trust in Allah, even in the face of opposition. Noah, as a prophet, faced rejection from his people but remained resolute, trusting completely in Allah's plan. The verse encourages believers to remain firm in their faith and to rely on Allah, even when their efforts to guide others are met with resistance or hostility. It also highlights the futility of opposing Allah's will, as Noah challenges his people to proceed with their plans without hesitation, underscoring the inevitability of divine judgment.
orig: واتل عليهم نبأ نوح إذ قال لقومه يا قوم إن كان كبر عليكم مقامي وتذكيري بآيات الله فعلى الله توكلت فأجمعوا أمركم وشركاءكم ثم لا يكن أمركم عليكم غمة ثم اقضوا إلي ولا تنظرون

translation: But if you turn away, [O people], I have not asked you for any reward. My reward is only from Allah, and I have been commanded to be of the Muslims.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophet Muhammad's role as a messenger who does not seek personal gain from his mission. His sustenance and reward come solely from Allah, reinforcing the purity of his message and his reliance on divine support. The command to be among the Muslims underscores the importance of submission to God's will and unity with the community of believers.
orig: فإن توليتم فما سألتكم من أجر إن أجري إلا على الله وأمرت أن أكون من المسلمين

translation: So they rejected him, and We saved him and those with him in the ship, and We made them successors, and We drowned those who rejected Our signs. So see how was the end of those who were warned.
interpretation: This verse reflects the story of Prophet Nuh (Noah) and his people. It underscores the theme of divine justice where those who reject the truth and the messengers of God face consequences, while the believers are saved and granted a new beginning. The verse serves as a reminder and a warning to all people about the outcomes of disbelief and obedience to God's commands.
orig: فكذبوه فنجيناه ومن معه في الفلك وجعلناهم خلائف وأغرقنا الذين كذبوا بآياتنا فانظر كيف كان عاقبة المنذرين

translation: Then We sent after him messengers to their peoples, and they came to them with clear proofs, but they were not going to believe in what they had previously denied. Thus We seal the hearts of the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse highlights the continuity of divine guidance through prophets and messengers sent to various nations after the time of a previous prophet. Despite the messengers bringing clear signs and evidence of the truth, the people's rejection of the message is attributed to their prior disbelief and denial of the truth. The sealing of the hearts of the transgressors signifies a spiritual consequence of persistent rejection of divine guidance, where their hearts become hardened and unresponsive to further calls to faith. This serves as a reminder of the importance of heeding the message of God's messengers and the potential spiritual peril of continued disbelief.
orig: ثم بعثنا من بعده رسلا إلى قومهم فجاءوهم بالبينات فما كانوا ليؤمنوا بما كذبوا به من قبل كذلك نطبع على قلوب المعتدين

translation: Then We sent after them Moses and Aaron to Pharaoh and his chiefs with Our signs, but they behaved arrogantly and they were a criminal people.
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of divine guidance and human response to it. After the earlier prophets, Moses and Aaron were sent to Pharaoh and his people as a continuation of God's message to humanity. The 'signs' refer to the miracles and clear proofs of God's power and authority that were presented to them. Despite these clear demonstrations, Pharaoh and his chiefs chose arrogance and rejection, illustrating a deliberate choice to persist in wrongdoing and disbelief. This underscores the moral responsibility of individuals and communities to heed divine guidance, and the consequences of choosing pride and criminality over submission to God's will.
orig: ثم بعثنا من بعدهم موسى وهارون إلى فرعون وملئه بآياتنا فاستكبروا وكانوا قوما مجرمين

translation: So when the truth came to them from Us, they said, 'Indeed, this is obvious magic.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to reject divine truth when it conflicts with their preconceived notions or desires. When faced with clear evidence of the truth from God, some people label it as mere magic or deception, as a means to dismiss it without engaging with its implications. This reaction stems from a reluctance to accept change or to acknowledge truths that challenge their current beliefs or lifestyles.
orig: فلما جاءهم الحق من عندنا قالوا إن هذا لسحر مبين

translation: Moses said, "Do you say about the truth when it has come to you, 'This is magic?' And magicians will not succeed."
interpretation: Moses is confronting the disbelief of his people who, despite witnessing clear signs and miracles, still deny the truth and label it as magic. This verse emphasizes the theme of rejecting truth due to stubbornness or fear, and it highlights the ultimate failure of those who resort to falsehood and deception, as represented by the magicians.
orig: قال موسى أتقولون للحق لما جاءكم أسحر هذا ولا يفلح الساحرون

translation: They said, 'Have you come to us to turn us away from what we found our fathers following, and to have greatness in the land? We are not believers in you.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the resistance of a community to the message of the prophets, highlighting their attachment to ancestral traditions and their rejection of new guidance. It underscores the challenge prophets face in convincing people to abandon familiar customs in favor of divine truth, and also touches on the theme of pride and power, as the people accuse the prophets of seeking dominance over them.
orig: قالوا أجئتنا لتلفتنا عما وجدنا عليه آباءنا وتكون لكما الكبرياء في الأرض وما نحن لكما بمؤمنين

translation: And Pharaoh said, 'Bring me every skilled magician.'
interpretation: Pharaoh's command to gather all the skilled magicians reflects his arrogance and desperation to challenge the miracles of Moses. It underscores his refusal to accept the divine signs and his reliance on human power and trickery to maintain his authority, illustrating the theme of disbelief and the human tendency to oppose truth with falsehood.
orig: وقال فرعون ائتوني بكل ساحر عليم

translation: So when the magicians came, Moses said to them, "Throw what you are going to throw."
interpretation: This verse illustrates Moses's confidence and trust in God's power. By challenging the magicians to perform their magic first, Moses demonstrates his faith that the truth of God's miracles will prevail over any deception, highlighting the theme of divine support against false powers.
orig: فلما جاء السحرة قال لهم موسى ألقوا ما أنتم ملقون

translation: So when they threw, Moses said, "What you have brought is magic. Indeed, Allah will nullify it. Indeed, Allah does not amend the work of corrupters."
interpretation: This verse highlights the confrontation between Moses and the magicians of Pharaoh. When the magicians cast their staffs and ropes, turning them into serpents through magic, Moses declares that their act is mere sorcery. He asserts that Allah will ultimately nullify their magic, emphasizing the superiority of divine power over human trickery. The statement that Allah does not amend the work of corrupters serves as a reminder that the actions of those who spread corruption and falsehood will not be sustained or validated by God, reinforcing the theme of divine justice and the ultimate triumph of truth over deception.
orig: فلما ألقوا قال موسى ما جئتم به السحر إن الله سيبطله إن الله لا يصلح عمل المفسدين

translation: And Allah will establish the truth by His words, even if the criminals dislike it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability and supremacy of Allah's truth. It assures believers that no matter how much the wrongdoers or those who oppose the truth may dislike or resist it, Allah's words and His truth will ultimately prevail and be established. This serves as a reminder of the power and justice of Allah, encouraging steadfastness and faith among the believers in the face of opposition.
orig: ويحق الله الحق بكلماته ولو كره المجرمون

translation: So none believed in Moses, except some of his people, for fear of Pharaoh and their chiefs, lest they should persecute them; and indeed Pharaoh was arrogant in the land, and indeed he was of the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of faith amidst oppression. It illustrates that only a small group from Moses' people believed in his message due to the overwhelming fear of persecution by Pharaoh and his regime. The verse underscores the courage required to embrace faith under tyranny, and it also serves as a critique of Pharaoh's character, portraying him as not only a political oppressor but also a moral transgressor who exceeded all bounds in his arrogance and tyranny. This serves to emphasize the moral and spiritual dimensions of the struggle against oppression.
orig: فما آمن لموسى إلا ذرية من قومه على خوف من فرعون وملئهم أن يفتنهم وإن فرعون لعال في الأرض وإنه لمن المسرفين

translation: And Moses said, 'O my people, if you have believed in Allah, then rely upon Him, if you should be Muslims.'
interpretation: Moses is urging his people to place their complete trust and reliance on Allah, emphasizing that true faith (iman) in Allah necessitates total dependence on Him. This reliance is a fundamental aspect of being a Muslim, indicating submission to Allah's will and confidence in His plan.
orig: وقال موسى يا قوم إن كنتم آمنتم بالله فعليه توكلوا إن كنتم مسلمين

translation: So they said, "In Allah we have put our trust. Our Lord, do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people."
interpretation: This verse reflects a deep trust in Allah and a plea for divine protection. The believers express their reliance on Allah's guidance and support, acknowledging that their faith and actions should not be used as a means to test or persecute them by the oppressive people. It highlights the importance of seeking Allah's help to maintain steadfastness and integrity in the face of adversity.
orig: فقالوا على الله توكلنا ربنا لا تجعلنا فتنة للقوم الظالمين

translation: And save us by Your mercy from the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse is a supplication for divine protection and deliverance from the harm and influence of those who reject faith. It reflects a deep reliance on God's mercy to provide safety and guidance away from the negative impacts of disbelief and towards a path of righteousness and salvation.
orig: ونجنا برحمتك من القوم الكافرين

translation: And We inspired Moses and his brother: 'Settle your people in Egypt in houses, and make your houses places of worship, and establish prayer, and give glad tidings to the believers.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine guidance given to Moses and Aaron to establish a strong community foundation in Egypt. By instructing them to settle their people in houses, it emphasizes the importance of creating a stable and secure environment for the community. The command to make their houses places of worship suggests transforming personal spaces into sanctuaries of faith, where worship and devotion to God are central. The establishment of prayer is emphasized as a crucial pillar of faith, reinforcing the spiritual discipline and connection to God. Finally, the instruction to give glad tidings to the believers reflects the role of leaders in uplifting and encouraging their community, fostering hope and resilience amidst challenges.
orig: وأوحينا إلى موسى وأخيه أن تبوآ لقومكما بمصر بيوتا واجعلوا بيوتكم قبلة وأقيموا الصلاة وبشر المؤمنين

translation: And Moses said, 'Our Lord, indeed You have given Pharaoh and his establishment splendor and wealth in the worldly life, our Lord, that they may lead [others] astray from Your way. Our Lord, obliterate their wealth and harden their hearts so that they will not believe until they see the painful punishment.'
interpretation: In this verse, Moses is making a supplication to Allah against Pharaoh and his people, who were using their wealth and power to mislead others from the path of God. Moses asks Allah to destroy their wealth and to harden their hearts as a form of punishment, so that they would not believe until they face the severe consequences of their actions. This reflects the theme of divine justice and the consequences of using one's resources to lead others astray from the truth.
orig: وقال موسى ربنا إنك آتيت فرعون وملأه زينة وأموالا في الحياة الدنيا ربنا ليضلوا عن سبيلك ربنا اطمس على أموالهم واشدد على قلوبهم فلا يؤمنوا حتى يروا العذاب الأليم

translation: He said, "Your supplication has been answered, so remain steadfast and do not follow the way of those who do not know."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of steadfastness and guidance after receiving divine response to one's prayers. It instructs believers to adhere to the straight path and avoid the misguided ways of those who lack knowledge, highlighting the necessity of following divine guidance over human ignorance.
orig: قال قد أجيبت دعوتكما فاستقيما ولا تتبعان سبيل الذين لا يعلمون

translation: And We took the Children of Israel across the sea, and Pharaoh and his soldiers pursued them in tyranny and enmity until, when drowning overtook him, he said, 'I believe that there is no deity except that in whom the Children of Israel believe, and I am of the Muslims.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of divine justice and the consequences of arrogance and disbelief. Pharaoh, who had relentlessly oppressed the Israelites and denied the signs of God, only professed faith when he was on the brink of death. His last-minute declaration of faith is not accepted because it is driven by desperation rather than genuine belief. This serves as a lesson that true faith cannot be a reaction to imminent punishment but must be a sincere conviction in the heart. It underscores the importance of timely repentance and the futility of seeking God's mercy out of fear of immediate peril.
orig: وجاوزنا ببني إسرائيل البحر فأتبعهم فرعون وجنوده بغيا وعدوا حتى إذا أدركه الغرق قال آمنت أنه لا إله إلا الذي آمنت به بنو إسرائيل وأنا من المسلمين

translation: Now you have disobeyed before and you were among the corruptors.
interpretation: This verse reflects on the past actions of an individual, indicating that they have previously disobeyed divine commands and engaged in actions that cause corruption or mischief. It serves as a reminder of one's history of moral failings and the need for repentance and change.
orig: آلآن وقد عصيت قبل وكنت من المفسدين

translation: So today We will save you in body, that you may be a sign to those who succeed you. And indeed, many among the people, of Our signs, are heedless.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Pharaoh, where Allah preserved his body as a sign for future generations. The interpretation highlights that even though Pharaoh's body was preserved as a lesson and a reminder of Allah's power and the consequences of disbelief, many people still remain heedless and indifferent to the signs and messages from Allah. It serves as a reminder for believers to reflect on these signs and not to be among those who ignore the lessons from history and the teachings of the Qur'an.
orig: فاليوم ننجيك ببدنك لتكون لمن خلفك آية وإن كثيرا من الناس عن آياتنا لغافلون

translation: And We settled the Children of Israel in a secure settlement and provided them with good things, and they did not differ until knowledge came to them. Indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ.
interpretation: This verse reflects on the historical journey of the Children of Israel, highlighting how they were initially granted a secure and prosperous dwelling by God. The 'secure settlement' refers to the land of Canaan, which was given to them as a divine promise. The 'good things' symbolize the blessings and sustenance provided to them. The verse then points out that despite these blessings, the Children of Israel began to differ among themselves only after receiving knowledge, possibly referring to the Torah and subsequent interpretations and disputes over religious and legal matters. The mention of God's judgment on the Day of Resurrection emphasizes the ultimate accountability for these differences, underscoring the theme of divine justice and the resolution of earthly disputes in the hereafter.
orig: ولقد بوأنا بني إسرائيل مبوأ صدق ورزقناهم من الطيبات فما اختلفوا حتى جاءهم العلم إن ربك يقضي بينهم يوم القيامة فيما كانوا فيه يختلفون

translation: And if you are in doubt about what We have revealed to you, then ask those who read the Scripture before you. The truth has come to you from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters.
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad, and by extension all believers, to seek confirmation of the Qur'an's truth from the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) who possess earlier scriptures. It emphasizes the continuity of divine revelation and encourages believers to dispel any doubts about the Qur'an's authenticity by consulting those who have knowledge of previous scriptures. The verse underscores the certainty of the Qur'an as a divine revelation and urges steadfastness in faith, warning against lingering in doubt.
orig: فإن كنت في شك مما أنزلنا إليك فاسأل الذين يقرءون الكتاب من قبلك لقد جاءك الحق من ربك فلا تكونن من الممترين

translation: And do not be among those who have denied the signs of Allah, lest you be among the losers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to believers to accept and believe in the signs and revelations of Allah. It emphasizes the importance of faith and the consequences of disbelief, indicating that those who reject Allah's signs will ultimately be among the losers in the Hereafter. The term 'losers' here refers to those who will miss out on the rewards and blessings of the afterlife due to their denial of divine truths.
orig: ولا تكونن من الذين كذبوا بآيات الله فتكون من الخاسرين

translation: Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has come into effect will not believe.
interpretation: This verse indicates that there are certain individuals who, due to their persistent rejection and disbelief, have reached a point where faith is no longer possible for them. The 'word of your Lord' refers to a divine decree that has been finalized regarding their disbelief, suggesting that their hearts have become sealed against faith. This serves as a reminder of the consequences of continuous rejection of the truth and the importance of accepting guidance when it is offered.
orig: إن الذين حقت عليهم كلمت ربك لا يؤمنون

translation: And even if every sign came to them, until they see the painful punishment
interpretation: This verse suggests that some people will remain in denial of the truth and the signs of God, no matter how clear and numerous they are, until they are confronted with the severe consequences of their disbelief.
orig: ولو جاءتهم كل آية حتى يروا العذاب الأليم

translation: So why was there not a town that believed and its faith benefited it except the people of Jonah? When they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the worldly life and gave them enjoyment for a time.
interpretation: This verse highlights the rarity of a community's collective faith leading to their salvation, with the notable exception being the people of Jonah. Their sincere repentance and belief after initially rejecting Jonah's message led to the divine mercy that averted the impending punishment and granted them a period of prosperity. It underscores the transformative power of genuine faith and repentance, illustrating that God's mercy can manifest in tangible relief from worldly afflictions when a community turns back to Him wholeheartedly.
orig: فلولا كانت قرية آمنت فنفعها إيمانها إلا قوم يونس لما آمنوا كشفنا عنهم عذاب الخزي في الحياة الدنيا ومتعناهم إلى حين

translation: And had your Lord willed, those on earth would have believed - all of them entirely. Then, would you compel the people until they become believers?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of free will in Islam. It indicates that faith cannot be forced upon people; it must be a personal choice. The verse rhetorically questions the Prophet Muhammad about compelling others to believe, underscoring that even though Allah could make everyone believe if He wished, He has chosen to allow humans the freedom to choose their path. This highlights the importance of da'wah (invitation to Islam) being conducted with wisdom and patience, rather than coercion.
orig: ولو شاء ربك لآمن من في الأرض كلهم جميعا أفأنت تكره الناس حتى يكونوا مؤمنين

translation: And it was not for a soul to believe except by the permission of Allah, and He places filth upon those who do not use reason.
interpretation: This verse underscores the concept that faith is a divine gift bestowed by Allah's will. It emphasizes that while human effort and reasoning are involved in the journey towards faith, ultimately, belief is enabled by Allah's permission. The latter part of the verse serves as a warning, indicating that those who fail to engage their intellect and reasoning faculties are susceptible to spiritual and moral corruption, symbolized by 'filth'. This suggests a responsibility on the individual to actively use their capacity for understanding and reflection in their pursuit of faith and moral integrity.
orig: وما كان لنفس أن تؤمن إلا بإذن الله ويجعل الرجس على الذين لا يعقلون

translation: Say, 'Observe what is in the heavens and the earth.' But of no avail will be signs and warnings to a people who do not believe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of observing and reflecting upon the natural world as a means to recognize the existence and majesty of God. However, it also highlights a critical point that for those who are determined not to believe, no amount of signs or warnings will change their hearts. This underscores the notion that faith is not solely an intellectual exercise but also involves a willingness to accept and submit to the truth.
orig: قل انظروا ماذا في السماوات والأرض وما تغني الآيات والنذر عن قوم لا يؤمنون

translation: Are they waiting for anything except the fate of those who passed away before them? Say, 'Then wait; indeed, I am with you among those who wait.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability of divine judgment and the futility of delaying repentance or acceptance of faith. It challenges those who are hesitant or skeptical about the message of Islam to reflect on the historical precedent of previous nations that were destroyed due to their disbelief and disobedience. The Prophet Muhammad is instructed to join them in waiting, not out of doubt, but to affirm his certainty in the coming judgment, thereby highlighting his confidence in the truth of his message and the eventual manifestation of God's promise.
orig: فهل ينتظرون إلا مثل أيام الذين خلوا من قبلهم قل فانتظروا إني معكم من المنتظرين

translation: Then We will save Our messengers and those who have believed. Thus, it is an obligation upon Us to save the believers.
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah's promise to protect and save His messengers and the believers who follow them. It reflects the divine commitment to the safety and salvation of those who remain steadfast in their faith, emphasizing that such protection is a fundamental aspect of Allah's justice and mercy. This assurance serves to strengthen the faith of believers, reminding them that their trust in Allah will ultimately lead to their deliverance.
orig: ثم ننجي رسلنا والذين آمنوا كذلك حقا علينا ننج المؤمنين

translation: Say, 'O people, if you are in doubt about my religion, then I do not worship those whom you worship besides Allah, but I worship Allah, Who causes you to die, and I have been commanded to be among the believers.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophet Muhammad's unwavering commitment to monotheism, rejecting the worship of any deities other than Allah. It serves as a clear declaration of faith, asserting that the Prophet's religion is based solely on the worship of the One God who has power over life and death. The verse also highlights the Prophet's role as a messenger, commanded to adhere to and promote belief in Allah, encouraging others to join the community of believers.
orig: قل يا أيها الناس إن كنتم في شك من ديني فلا أعبد الذين تعبدون من دون الله ولكن أعبد الله الذي يتوفاكم وأمرت أن أكون من المؤمنين

translation: And direct your face toward the religion, inclining to truth, and never be among the polytheists
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sincere devotion to the monotheistic faith of Islam, urging the believer to fully commit to the religion with a pure heart and to avoid any form of idolatry or association of partners with God. It calls for a steadfast adherence to the path of truth and righteousness, distancing oneself from the practices and beliefs of those who attribute divinity to entities other than Allah.
orig: وأن أقم وجهك للدين حنيفا ولا تكونن من المشركين

translation: And do not invoke, besides Allah, that which neither benefits you nor harms you, for if you did, then indeed you would be of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of monotheism and warns against the futility and sin of worshipping or seeking help from anything other than Allah. It teaches that turning to idols or other deities, which have no power to benefit or harm, is not only ineffective but also places one in the category of wrongdoers, as it constitutes a form of injustice to oneself and a deviation from the path of righteousness.
orig: ولا تدع من دون الله ما لا ينفعك ولا يضرك فإن فعلت فإنك إذا من الظالمين

translation: And if Allah touches you with harm, none can remove it but He, and if He intends for you good, none can repel His Favor. He causes it to reach whom He wills of His slaves. And He is the Oft-Forgiving, the Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and sovereignty of Allah over all aspects of life. It teaches that any affliction or hardship that befalls a person is under Allah's control, and only He can relieve it. Conversely, any good or blessing that comes to a person is also from Allah, and no one can prevent His blessings from reaching those He chooses. The verse also highlights Allah's attributes of forgiveness and mercy, indicating that despite His immense power, He is also compassionate and forgiving towards His servants. This understanding encourages believers to turn to Allah in times of difficulty and to be grateful for His blessings, recognizing that all comes from Him.
orig: وإن يمسسك الله بضر فلا كاشف له إلا هو وإن يردك بخير فلا راد لفضله يصيب به من يشاء من عباده وهو الغفور الرحيم

translation: Say, 'O mankind, the truth has come to you from your Lord, so whoever is guided is only guided for [the benefit of] his soul, and whoever goes astray only goes astray [to its detriment]. And I am not a guardian over you.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the individual responsibility for seeking and following guidance. It conveys that the truth has been clearly presented to all people, and now it is up to each individual to choose whether to follow it or not. The guidance or misguidance affects one's own soul, highlighting personal accountability. The Prophet Muhammad is instructed to convey the message but is not responsible for ensuring people follow it, underscoring the limits of his role as a messenger.
orig: قل يا أيها الناس قد جاءكم الحق من ربكم فمن اهتدى فإنما يهتدي لنفسه ومن ضل فإنما يضل عليها وما أنا عليكم بوكيل

translation: And follow what is revealed to you, and be patient until Allah judges, and He is the best of judges.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to divine guidance received through revelation and maintaining patience in the face of adversity. It instructs the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to follow the revelations he receives and to remain steadfast, trusting in Allah's ultimate judgment. The verse reassures believers that Allah's judgment is the most just and wise, encouraging them to rely on His timing and decision-making, which is superior to any human judgment.
orig: واتبع ما يوحى إليك واصبر حتى يحكم الله وهو خير الحاكمين

translation: Alif, Lam, Ra. [This is] a Book whose verses are perfected and then presented in detail from [one who is] Wise and Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse introduces the Qur'an as a divine scripture that is meticulously detailed and organized, originating from Allah, who is described as both Wise and fully Aware. The use of 'Alif, Lam, Ra' at the beginning is one of the mysterious letter combinations known as 'Muqatta'at', which are believed to emphasize the miraculous nature of the Qur'an. The perfection and detailed explanation of the verses suggest that the Qur'an is clear and comprehensive in its guidance, reflecting the wisdom and omniscience of its divine source.
orig: الر كتاب أحكمت آياته ثم فصلت من لدن حكيم خبير

translation: Do not worship except Allah; indeed, I am to you from Him a warner and a bringer of good news.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental principle of Islam, which is the worship of Allah alone, rejecting all forms of idolatry and polytheism. The speaker, likely a prophet or messenger, is declaring their role as both a warner against the consequences of disbelief and a bearer of good news about the rewards of faith and obedience to Allah. This dual role underscores the comprehensive nature of divine guidance, which includes both admonition and promise, urging people to heed the message and align their lives accordingly.
orig: ألا تعبدوا إلا الله إنني لكم منه نذير وبشير

translation: And that you should seek forgiveness from your Lord, then turn to Him in repentance, He will let you enjoy a good provision for a specified term and give every one of possessor of merit his merit. And if they turn away, then indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a great Day.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking forgiveness from Allah and repenting sincerely. By doing so, Allah promises to provide believers with good provisions until a designated time, rewarding each person according to their merit. However, the verse also warns of the severe consequences of turning away from this guidance, expressing concern about facing the punishment on the Day of Judgment, which is described as great and significant. The message underscores the balance between divine mercy and justice, encouraging a path of righteousness while cautioning against neglect and disobedience.
orig: وأن استغفروا ربكم ثم توبوا إليه يمتعكم متاعا حسنا إلى أجل مسمى ويؤت كل ذي فضل فضله وإن تولوا فإني أخاف عليكم عذاب يوم كبير

translation: To Allah is your return, and He is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse reminds believers that ultimately, they will return to Allah after their life on earth, emphasizing the concept of accountability in the hereafter. It also reassures them of Allah's omnipotence, indicating that He has complete power and control over everything, which can provide comfort and trust in His divine plan and justice.
orig: إلى الله مرجعكم وهو على كل شيء قدير

translation: Do they not see that We have created for them of what Our hands have made, grazing livestock, so they are their owners?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine knowledge and awareness of God. It suggests that people may try to hide their true feelings or intentions, but God is fully aware of what is concealed in their hearts and what they openly express. The imagery of turning away and covering with garments symbolizes attempts to hide from God, yet it underscores the futility of such actions because God knows all, even the innermost secrets of the heart.
orig: ألا إنهم يثنون صدورهم ليستخفوا منه ألا حين يستغشون ثيابهم يعلم ما يسرون وما يعلنون إنه عليم بذات الصدور

translation: And there is no creature on earth but that upon Allah is its provision, and He knows its place of dwelling and place of storage; all is in a clear record.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's omniscience and providence. It reassures believers that every living creature's sustenance is provided by Allah, indicating His care and responsibility for all creation. The mention of knowing each creature's dwelling and storage place underscores Allah's complete knowledge of every detail of existence. The phrase 'all is in a clear record' suggests that everything is predetermined and recorded by Allah, reflecting the belief in divine decree and the meticulous order of the universe.
orig: وما من دابة في الأرض إلا على الله رزقها ويعلم مستقرها ومستودعها كل في كتاب مبين

translation: And He it is Who created the heavens and the earth in six days, and His Throne was upon the water, that He might try you, which of you is best in conduct. And if you were to say, 'Indeed, you will be resurrected after death,' those who disbelieve would surely say, 'This is nothing but clear magic.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's creative power and His sovereignty over the universe, highlighting that He created the heavens and the earth in six days, and His Throne was upon water, symbolizing His dominion over all creation. The mention of the trial through deeds suggests that the purpose of creation is to test humanity's moral and ethical conduct. The latter part of the verse addresses the disbelief and denial of resurrection by some, illustrating the challenge prophets face in conveying divine truths to those who reject them, often labeling such truths as mere magic or deception.
orig: وهو الذي خلق السماوات والأرض في ستة أيام وكان عرشه على الماء ليبلوكم أيكم أحسن عملا ولئن قلت إنكم مبعوثون من بعد الموت ليقولن الذين كفروا إن هذا إلا سحر مبين

translation: And if We delay the punishment from them until a determined time, they will surely say, 'What is holding it back?' Indeed, on the Day it comes to them, it will not be averted from them, and they will be enveloped by what they used to mock.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to question and doubt the timing of divine retribution. It suggests that even if God delays punishment to give people more time to repent, they often fail to recognize this mercy and instead mock the idea of divine justice. The verse warns that when the appointed time arrives, the punishment will be inevitable and inescapable, serving as a reminder of the consequences of disbelief and mockery.
orig: ولئن أخرنا عنهم العذاب إلى أمة معدودة ليقولن ما يحبسه ألا يوم يأتيهم ليس مصروفا عنهم وحاق بهم ما كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: And if We let man taste mercy from Us, then We withdraw it from him, indeed, he is despairing, ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency towards ingratitude and despair when faced with the withdrawal of blessings. It suggests that when people are given ease and comfort, they often take it for granted, and when these are taken away, they lose hope and fail to recognize the initial blessing as a mercy from God. This serves as a reminder for believers to maintain gratitude and patience in all circumstances, recognizing that all conditions are tests from God.
orig: ولئن أذقنا الإنسان منا رحمة ثم نزعناها منه إنه ليئوس كفور

translation: And if We let him taste mercy from Us after adversity has touched him, he will surely say, 'Harm has left me.' Indeed, he is exultant and boastful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to quickly forget past hardships and attribute subsequent relief or blessings solely to one's own merit or luck, rather than acknowledging divine providence. It critiques the arrogance and ingratitude that can arise from such a mindset, reminding believers to remain humble and thankful to Allah in all circumstances.
orig: ولئن أذقناه نعماء بعد ضراء مسته ليقولن ذهب السيئات عني إنه لفرح فخور

translation: Except for those who are patient and do righteous deeds; those will have forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the virtues of patience and righteous actions as key qualities that lead to divine forgiveness and a significant reward in the hereafter. It suggests that enduring hardships with patience, while consistently performing good deeds, is a path to spiritual purification and ultimate salvation. The promise of forgiveness and a great reward serves as an encouragement for believers to persevere in their faith and moral conduct despite challenges.
orig: إلا الذين صبروا وعملوا الصالحات أولئك لهم مغفرة وأجر كبير

translation: So perhaps you would omit some of what is revealed to you, and your chest becomes tight from it because they say, 'Why has a treasure not been sent down to him, or an angel come with him?' You are only a warner, and Allah is in charge of all things.
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad, indicating that he might feel inclined to withhold some of the revelations due to the criticism and doubts expressed by the disbelievers. They questioned why he was not given a treasure or accompanied by an angel as proof of his prophethood. The verse reassures the Prophet that his role is merely to warn people, and he should not be distressed by their demands. It emphasizes that Allah is the ultimate overseer and manager of all affairs, reinforcing the Prophet's trust in divine wisdom and providence.
orig: فلعلك تارك بعض ما يوحى إليك وضائق به صدرك أن يقولوا لولا أنزل عليه كنز أو جاء معه ملك إنما أنت نذير والله على كل شيء وكيل

translation: Or do they say, 'He has invented it'? Say, 'Then bring ten invented chapters like it and call upon whoever you can besides Allah, if you are truthful.'
interpretation: This verse challenges those who doubt the divine origin of the Qur'an by asserting its inimitable nature. It invites skeptics to produce even ten chapters similar to those of the Qur'an if they claim it is fabricated by a human. The challenge extends to invoking any help they can muster other than from Allah, emphasizing the impossibility of replicating the Qur'an's style, content, and miraculous nature without divine assistance, thus affirming its authenticity and divine source.
orig: أم يقولون افتراه قل فأتوا بعشر سور مثله مفتريات وادعوا من استطعتم من دون الله إن كنتم صادقين

translation: If they do not respond to you, then know that it has been revealed with the knowledge of Allah, and that there is no deity except Him. So will you submit?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin of the Qur'an and the oneness of God. It challenges the believers to recognize the truth of the message and to submit to it wholeheartedly, reinforcing the call to faith and submission to Allah alone.
orig: فإلم يستجيبوا لكم فاعلموا أنما أنزل بعلم الله وأن لا إله إلا هو فهل أنتم مسلمون

translation: Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornments - We will fully compensate them for their deeds therein, and they will not be deprived therein.
interpretation: This verse addresses those whose primary focus and desire is the material and transient pleasures of this worldly life. It indicates that God will give them what they seek in this life as a consequence of their actions, ensuring they receive the full recompense for their worldly pursuits. However, the underlying message is a reminder of the temporary nature of these rewards, suggesting that while they will not be shortchanged in worldly terms, their focus on the ephemeral may lead them away from the eternal rewards of the hereafter.
orig: من كان يريد الحياة الدنيا وزينتها نوف إليهم أعمالهم فيها وهم فيها لا يبخسون

translation: Those are the ones for whom there is nothing in the Hereafter except the Fire. And lost is what they did therein, and worthless is what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse describes the fate of those who reject faith and engage in sinful actions. It emphasizes that their efforts in this life will be in vain because they will lead to nothing but punishment in the Hereafter. The phrase 'lost is what they did therein' suggests that any good deeds they might have performed will be nullified due to their disbelief or hypocrisy. The term 'worthless is what they used to do' further reinforces the idea that their worldly pursuits and actions, driven by incorrect intentions or beliefs, will hold no value in the eyes of God on the Day of Judgment.
orig: أولئك الذين ليس لهم في الآخرة إلا النار وحبط ما صنعوا فيها وباطل ما كانوا يعملون

translation: Is he who has a clear proof from his Lord, and a witness from Him recites it, and before it was the Book of Moses, a guide and mercy; those believe in it. But whoever disbelieves in it from the factions - the Fire is his promised destination. So be not in doubt about it. Indeed, it is the truth from your Lord, but most of the people do not believe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the continuity and divine origin of the revelation given to Prophet Muhammad, connecting it directly with the earlier revelation to Moses. It suggests that those who have clear evidence and witnesses of the truth of the Qur'an, and who recognize the continuity of divine guidance from the Torah to the Qur'an, are the ones who will believe. Conversely, those who reject this message, categorized as different factions or groups, are warned of the severe consequence of disbelief, which is the Fire. The verse reassures the Prophet and believers not to be in doubt about the truth of the Qur'an, affirming its authenticity as a divine message from God, despite the widespread disbelief among people.
orig: أفمن كان على بينة من ربه ويتلوه شاهد منه ومن قبله كتاب موسى إماما ورحمة أولئك يؤمنون به ومن يكفر به من الأحزاب فالنار موعده فلا تك في مرية منه إنه الحق من ربك ولكن أكثر الناس لا يؤمنون

translation: And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie about Allah? Those will be presented before their Lord, and the witnesses will say, 'These are the ones who lied about their Lord.' Unquestionably, the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity of attributing falsehood to Allah, which is considered the utmost form of injustice. It warns that those who engage in such acts will be brought before Allah on the Day of Judgment, where witnesses will testify against them, confirming their deceit. The verse underscores that such individuals are cursed by Allah, highlighting the grave consequences of fabricating lies about the divine, which not only misleads others but also incurs divine wrath.
orig: ومن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا أولئك يعرضون على ربهم ويقول الأشهاد هؤلاء الذين كذبوا على ربهم ألا لعنة الله على الظالمين

translation: Those who hinder from the way of Allah and seek to make it crooked, and they, in the Hereafter, are disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse refers to individuals who obstruct others from following the path of Allah, whether through direct opposition or by distorting the teachings of Islam. Their actions not only lead them astray but also prevent others from achieving spiritual guidance. The mention of their disbelief in the Hereafter underscores their rejection of accountability and divine judgment, highlighting a deep-seated denial of fundamental Islamic principles.
orig: الذين يصدون عن سبيل الله ويبغونها عوجا وهم بالآخرة هم كافرون

translation: Those were not ones who could cause corruption on the earth, and they had no protectors besides Allah. Their punishment will be doubled. They were not able to hear, nor were they able to see.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fate of those who reject faith and engage in corruption, emphasizing their isolation and helplessness without divine support. The doubling of their punishment underscores the severity of their misdeeds and their spiritual blindness and deafness to truth, illustrating their complete disconnection from guidance and righteousness.
orig: أولئك لم يكونوا معجزين في الأرض وما كان لهم من دون الله من أولياء يضاعف لهم العذاب ما كانوا يستطيعون السمع وما كانوا يبصرون

translation: Those are the ones who have lost their own souls, and lost from them is what they used to invent.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who have rejected faith and followed false beliefs or idolatry. They have not only lost their chance at spiritual salvation but also the falsehoods they created and believed in will be of no avail to them in the Hereafter. It underscores the ultimate futility and loss associated with straying from the truth.
orig: أولئك الذين خسروا أنفسهم وضل عنهم ما كانوا يفترون

translation: Indeed, they will be the greatest losers in the Hereafter.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe consequence of disbelief and rejection of faith. Those who deny the truth and lead a life contrary to God's guidance will ultimately face the greatest loss in the afterlife, as they will be deprived of the eternal bliss and rewards promised to the righteous. It serves as a stark warning about the importance of faith and righteous deeds in securing a favorable outcome in the Hereafter.
orig: لا جرم أنهم في الآخرة هم الأخسرون

translation: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds and humbled themselves to their Lord - those are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein forever.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the qualities required for entry into Paradise: faith in Allah, performing good deeds, and humility towards the Creator. It underscores that those who embody these characteristics will be rewarded with eternal residence in Paradise, highlighting the importance of a balanced life of belief, action, and spiritual humility.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات وأخبتوا إلى ربهم أولئك أصحاب الجنة هم فيها خالدون

translation: The example of the two parties is like the blind and the deaf, and the seeing and the hearing. Are they equal in comparison? Will you not then take heed?
interpretation: This verse uses the metaphor of sensory abilities to illustrate the difference between those who are guided (believers) and those who are not (disbelievers). The 'blind and deaf' represent those who are unable to perceive the truth and guidance of Islam, while the 'seeing and hearing' symbolize those who can understand and follow the divine message. The rhetorical question challenges the audience to reflect on the obvious disparity between these two groups, urging them to consider their own spiritual state and to heed the call to guidance.
orig: مثل الفريقين كالأعمى والأصم والبصير والسميع هل يستويان مثلا أفلا تذكرون

translation: And We certainly sent Noah to his people, [saying], 'Indeed, I am to you a clear warner'
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine mission of Prophet Noah, who was sent to guide his people away from idolatry and towards the worship of the one true God. The term 'clear warner' emphasizes the clarity and urgency of Noah's message, indicating that his warnings were unmistakable and his role was to alert his people of the impending consequences of their actions if they did not repent and follow the path of righteousness.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا نوحا إلى قومه إني لكم نذير مبين

translation: That you worship none but Allah. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a painful Day.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental principle of monotheism in Islam, urging believers to worship only Allah. The speaker, likely a prophet or messenger, expresses a deep concern for the people, warning them about the severe consequences of associating partners with Allah. The mention of a 'painful Day' refers to the Day of Judgment, highlighting the urgency and importance of adhering to this command to avoid divine retribution.
orig: أن لا تعبدوا إلا الله إني أخاف عليكم عذاب يوم أليم

translation: So the chiefs of those who disbelieved among his people said, 'We see you but as a man like ourselves, and we do not see anyone following you except those who are the lowest of us and immature in opinion. And we do not see in you any merit over us; rather, we think you are liars.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the arrogance and denial of the disbelievers who reject the prophet's message. They dismiss him as merely a human like themselves, and belittle his followers as being of low status and lacking wisdom. This attitude underscores their refusal to acknowledge any divine authority or merit in the prophet, revealing their deep-seated disbelief and their attempt to discredit the message by attacking the messenger and his supporters.
orig: فقال الملأ الذين كفروا من قومه ما نراك إلا بشرا مثلنا وما نراك اتبعك إلا الذين هم أراذلنا بادي الرأي وما نرى لكم علينا من فضل بل نظنكم كاذبين

translation: He said, 'O my people, have you considered: if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord and He has given me mercy from Himself but it has been made unapparent to you, should I force it upon you while you are averse to it?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the dilemma of a prophet who has received clear guidance and mercy from God, yet faces the challenge of his people's unwillingness to accept it. The prophet questions whether he should impose this divine gift upon his people against their will, emphasizing the ethical consideration of not forcing faith or belief onto others. It underscores the principle of free will in religious matters and the prophet's role as a guide rather than a coercer.
orig: قال يا قوم أرأيتم إن كنت على بينة من ربي وآتاني رحمة من عنده فعميت عليكم أنلزمكموها وأنتم لها كارهون

translation: And O my people, I ask you not for wealth in return for it. My reward is only from Allah, and I am not going to drive away those who have believed. Indeed, they will meet their Lord, but I see that you are a people behaving ignorantly.
interpretation: In this verse, the Prophet is addressing his people, emphasizing his sincerity and disinterest in material gain from his prophetic mission. He clarifies that his reward comes solely from Allah, reinforcing the purity of his intentions. Furthermore, he expresses his commitment to not alienating believers, acknowledging their faith and their ultimate meeting with Allah. The verse also highlights the ignorance of his people, who fail to recognize the truth of his message and the righteousness of the believers, indicating a call for them to reflect and change their ways.
orig: ويا قوم لا أسألكم عليه مالا إن أجري إلا على الله وما أنا بطارد الذين آمنوا إنهم ملاقو ربهم ولكني أراكم قوما تجهلون

translation: And O my people, who would support me against Allah if I drove them away? Will you not then give a thought?
interpretation: This verse reflects Prophet Hud's plea to his people, emphasizing the futility of opposing Allah's will. Hud questions the wisdom of his people in rejecting the divine message, highlighting that no one can protect him from Allah's wrath if he were to unjustly drive away the believers. It serves as a reminder of the importance of heeding divine guidance and the consequences of ignoring it, urging introspection and a return to righteousness.
orig: ويا قوم من ينصرني من الله إن طردتهم أفلا تذكرون

translation: And I do not say to you that I possess the treasures of Allah, nor do I know the unseen, nor do I say that I am an angel, nor do I say to those whom your eyes despise that Allah will not give them any good. Allah knows best what is in their souls. Indeed, I would then be among the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the humility and truthfulness of Prophet Muhammad. He explicitly denies having divine powers or knowledge of the unseen, and refutes any claim to angelic status. Furthermore, he acknowledges that it is not for him to judge who is worthy of Allah's blessings, as only Allah truly knows the hearts and intentions of people. By making these statements, the Prophet distances himself from any form of arrogance or injustice, which would place him among the wrongdoers.
orig: ولا أقول لكم عندي خزائن الله ولا أعلم الغيب ولا أقول إني ملك ولا أقول للذين تزدري أعينكم لن يؤتيهم الله خيرا الله أعلم بما في أنفسهم إني إذا لمن الظالمين

translation: They said, 'O Noah, you have disputed with us and prolonged the dispute, so bring us what you promise us, if you are of the truthful.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the impatience and disbelief of Noah's people. They challenge Noah to bring the promised punishment immediately, indicating their doubt in his prophethood and the divine message he conveys. It highlights their demand for immediate proof, showcasing their rejection of faith and the process of divine timing.
orig: قالوا يا نوح قد جادلتنا فأكثرت جدالنا فأتنا بما تعدنا إن كنت من الصادقين

translation: He said: 'Only Allah will bring it to you if He wills, and you will not be able to escape (from the decree of Allah).'
interpretation: This verse underscores the belief in divine omnipotence and predestination. It suggests that all outcomes are ultimately in the hands of Allah, and human beings cannot alter or escape what Allah has decreed. It serves as a reminder of human limitations and the necessity of submitting to God's will.
orig: قال إنما يأتيكم به الله إن شاء وما أنتم بمعجزين

translation: And my advice will not benefit you, even if I wish to advise you, if Allah intends to let you go astray; He is your Lord, and to Him you will return.
interpretation: This verse underscores the concept of divine will and human agency. It suggests that while human efforts to guide or advise others are valuable, they are ultimately subject to God's overarching plan. If God decides to lead someone astray as a test or consequence of their actions, no amount of human advice can alter that divine decree. This highlights the importance of recognizing God's sovereignty and the ultimate return to Him for judgment, emphasizing both humility in human endeavors and the acceptance of divine will.
orig: ولا ينفعكم نصحي إن أردت أن أنصح لكم إن كان الله يريد أن يغويكم هو ربكم وإليه ترجعون

translation: Or do they say, 'He has invented it'? Say, 'If I have invented it, then upon me is [the consequence of] my crime; but I am innocent of what [crimes] you commit.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the accusations against the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that he fabricated the Qur'an. It emphasizes personal accountability for one's actions. The Prophet is instructed to assert that if he were to invent the Qur'an, he would bear the full responsibility for such a sin. However, he declares his innocence and distances himself from the wrongdoings of those who accuse him, highlighting the moral integrity and truthfulness of his mission.
orig: أم يقولون افتراه قل إن افتريته فعلي إجرامي وأنا بريء مما تجرمون

translation: And it was revealed to Noah that none of your people will believe except those who have already believed, so do not be distressed by what they have been doing.
interpretation: This verse indicates that God informed Noah that the faith of his people was predetermined and only a specific group among them would accept the message of Islam. It serves as a reminder to Noah, and by extension to all prophets and believers, not to be disheartened by the rejection of their message by the majority. The focus should remain on fulfilling their duty of conveying the message, rather than being overly concerned with the outcome, which is in God's hands.
orig: وأوحي إلى نوح أنه لن يؤمن من قومك إلا من قد آمن فلا تبتئس بما كانوا يفعلون

translation: And construct the ship under Our watch and Our inspiration, and do not address Me concerning those who have wronged; indeed, they are to be drowned.
interpretation: This verse refers to the command given to Prophet Noah by Allah to build the ark under divine supervision and guidance. The instruction to not plead on behalf of the wrongdoers signifies a point of no return for them, emphasizing divine justice and the inevitability of their punishment due to their persistent rejection of the truth and their corrupt actions. It underscores the theme of obedience to God's commands and the consequences of persistent wrongdoing.
orig: واصنع الفلك بأعيننا ووحينا ولا تخاطبني في الذين ظلموا إنهم مغرقون

translation: And he constructs the ship, and every time a group from his people passed by him, they mocked him. He said, 'If you mock us, then we mock you just as you mock.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the perseverance and faith of Prophet Noah in the face of ridicule from his people. Despite their mockery as he built the ark, Noah remained steadfast, responding to their derision with a statement that reflects both his resilience and a subtle warning of the impending divine judgment. It underscores the theme of steadfastness in faith and the eventual triumph of truth over mockery and disbelief.
orig: ويصنع الفلك وكلما مر عليه ملأ من قومه سخروا منه قال إن تسخروا منا فإنا نسخر منكم كما تسخرون

translation: So you will come to know who will be visited by a punishment that will disgrace him and upon whom will descend an enduring punishment.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning and a promise from Allah to those who deny the truth and engage in wrongdoing. It emphasizes that there will be a clear distinction and revelation in the Hereafter about who will face a humiliating and everlasting punishment. The 'punishment that will disgrace him' refers to the immediate shame and exposure of one's sins, while the 'enduring punishment' signifies the eternal nature of the torment in the afterlife. This verse reassures believers of divine justice and serves as a reminder for individuals to reflect on their actions and their consequences in the eternal realm.
orig: فسوف تعلمون من يأتيه عذاب يخزيه ويحل عليه عذاب مقيم

translation: Until, when Our command came and the oven boiled, We said, 'Load into it of each kind two, and your family, except those against whom the word has preceded, and whoever has believed.' And none had believed with him, except a few.
interpretation: This verse describes the moment when the divine command for the flood came to Prophet Noah, symbolized by the boiling of the oven, indicating the start of the deluge. The instruction to take aboard the ark two of each kind reflects the preservation of species for the continuation of life post-flood. The mention of Noah's family, with the exception of those already condemned, and the believers, highlights the themes of divine justice and salvation based on faith. The small number of believers with Noah underscores the rarity of true faith in the face of widespread disbelief and corruption.
orig: حتى إذا جاء أمرنا وفار التنور قلنا احمل فيها من كل زوجين اثنين وأهلك إلا من سبق عليه القول ومن آمن وما آمن معه إلا قليل

translation: And he said: "Embark therein! In the name of Allah be its course and its mooring. Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful."
interpretation: This verse reflects the moment when Prophet Nuh (Noah) instructed his followers to board the ark, invoking Allah's name for protection and guidance throughout their journey. The mention of Allah as Forgiving and Merciful underscores the hope and trust in divine mercy, even amidst a trial as severe as the flood. It highlights the themes of obedience to God's commands, reliance on His mercy, and the assurance of safety and forgiveness for those who follow His guidance.
orig: وقال اركبوا فيها بسم الله مجراها ومرساها إن ربي لغفور رحيم

translation: And it sailed with them through waves like mountains, and Noah called out to his son, who had separated himself, 'O my son, come aboard with us and be not with the disbelievers.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the moment of the flood when Noah's Ark was navigating through massive waves. It highlights Noah's concern for his son, urging him to join the believers on the Ark and warning him against staying with the disbelievers. The verse underscores themes of family, faith, and the consequences of one's choices in the face of divine judgment.
orig: وهي تجري بهم في موج كالجبال ونادى نوح ابنه وكان في معزل يا بني اركب معنا ولا تكن مع الكافرين

translation: He said, 'I will take refuge on a mountain to protect me from the water.' He said, 'There is no protector today from the decree of Allah except for whom He has mercy.' And the waves came between them, and he was among those who were drowned.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the futility of relying on worldly means for safety when faced with divine decree. The individual's attempt to seek refuge on a mountain during the flood signifies human efforts to escape inevitable divine punishment. However, the response from the other party emphasizes that no earthly refuge can shield one from Allah's will, except through His mercy. The separation by waves and the subsequent drowning serve as a stark reminder of the powerlessness of human plans against the overwhelming force of divine judgment, highlighting the importance of seeking Allah's mercy and submitting to His will.
orig: قال سآوي إلى جبل يعصمني من الماء قال لا عاصم اليوم من أمر الله إلا من رحم وحال بينهما الموج فكان من المغرقين

translation: And it was said, 'O earth, swallow your water, and O sky, withhold [your rain].' And the water subsided, and the matter was accomplished, and the ship came to rest on the [mountain of] Judi. And it was said, 'Away with the wrongdoing people.'
interpretation: This verse describes the conclusion of the flood of Prophet Noah, where divine command is given to the earth to absorb the floodwaters and the sky to stop raining, signaling the end of the deluge. The subsiding of the water and the Ark's safe landing on Mount Judi symbolize the fulfillment of God's promise to save the believers and punish the wrongdoers. The final proclamation of 'Away with the wrongdoing people' underscores the moral lesson that divine justice ultimately prevails, serving as a warning to future generations about the consequences of persistent disobedience and injustice.
orig: وقيل يا أرض ابلعي ماءك ويا سماء أقلعي وغيض الماء وقضي الأمر واستوت على الجودي وقيل بعدا للقوم الظالمين

translation: And Noah called upon his Lord and said, 'My Lord, indeed my son is of my family; and indeed, Your promise is true; and You are the most just of judges.'
interpretation: Noah's plea to Allah reflects his deep faith and trust in God's promise and justice. Despite the dire situation, Noah appeals to Allah's mercy for his son, acknowledging Allah's supreme judgment and the truthfulness of His word. This verse underscores the theme of divine justice and the importance of faith in God's promises, even in the face of personal loss.
orig: ونادى نوح ربه فقال رب إن ابني من أهلي وإن وعدك الحق وأنت أحكم الحاكمين

translation: He said, 'O Noah, indeed he is not of your family; indeed, he is [one whose] work was other than righteous, so ask Me not for that about which you have no knowledge. Indeed, I admonish you, lest you be among the ignorant.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the limits of intercession and the importance of knowledge in making requests. Noah's plea for his son is denied because his son's actions were not righteous, illustrating that familial ties do not supersede divine justice. God reminds Noah not to ask for things about which he has no knowledge, emphasizing the need for humans to recognize the boundaries of their understanding and submit to divine wisdom. The admonition serves as a warning against ignorance, encouraging believers to seek knowledge and align their requests with divine will.
orig: قال يا نوح إنه ليس من أهلك إنه عمل غير صالح فلا تسألن ما ليس لك به علم إني أعظك أن تكون من الجاهلين

translation: He said, 'My Lord, I seek refuge in You from asking You that of which I have no knowledge. And unless You forgive me and have mercy upon me, I will be among the losers.'
interpretation: This verse reflects a deep sense of humility and dependence on God. The speaker acknowledges the limitations of their own knowledge and expresses a fear of making requests that may be misguided or harmful. By seeking refuge in God from such unknowing requests, the speaker demonstrates a profound trust in divine wisdom over personal desires. Furthermore, the plea for forgiveness and mercy underscores the belief that without God's grace, one's spiritual and moral standing is at risk, highlighting the necessity of divine intervention to avoid being counted among those who ultimately fail in their spiritual journey.
orig: قال رب إني أعوذ بك أن أسألك ما ليس لي به علم وإلا تغفر لي وترحمني أكن من الخاسرين

translation: It was said, 'O Noah, disembark in peace from Us and blessings upon you and upon nations from those with you. And [there will be] nations We will grant enjoyment; then there will touch them from Us a painful punishment.'
interpretation: This verse signifies God's promise of peace and blessings to Prophet Noah and his followers after the flood, symbolizing a new beginning and covenant with God. It also serves as a reminder that while some nations will be granted temporary enjoyment in this life, they will eventually face divine retribution if they stray from the path of righteousness, emphasizing the themes of divine justice and the consequences of moral actions.
orig: قيل يا نوح اهبط بسلام منا وبركات عليك وعلى أمم ممن معك وأمم سنمتعهم ثم يمسهم منا عذاب أليم

translation: These are among the news of the unseen, which We reveal to you. You were not aware of them, neither you nor your people, before this. So be patient; indeed, the outcome is for the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin of the Qur'anic revelations, highlighting that the knowledge imparted to Prophet Muhammad about past events and unseen matters was not known to him or his community prior to the revelation. It serves as a reminder for the Prophet to remain patient in the face of adversity and opposition, reinforcing the promise that ultimate success and a favorable outcome are assured for those who remain steadfast in their faith and righteousness.
orig: تلك من أنباء الغيب نوحيها إليك ما كنت تعلمها أنت ولا قومك من قبل هذا فاصبر إن العاقبة للمتقين

translation: And to 'Ad [We sent] their brother Hud. He said, 'O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. You are not but inventors [of falsehood].'
interpretation: This verse highlights the mission of the Prophet Hud, who was sent to the people of 'Ad to guide them back to the worship of the one true God, Allah. Hud's message emphasizes monotheism, urging his people to abandon the false gods they had fabricated and to recognize that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah. The term 'inventors' refers to the people's creation of false deities, indicating their deviation from the truth and their engagement in idolatry. This verse serves as a reminder of the fundamental Islamic principle of Tawhid (the oneness of God) and the rejection of polytheism.
orig: وإلى عاد أخاهم هودا قال يا قوم اعبدوا الله ما لكم من إله غيره إن أنتم إلا مفترون

translation: O my people, I ask you not for any reward for it. My reward is only from the One who created me. Will you not then understand?
interpretation: In this verse, the prophet is emphasizing that his message is purely for the guidance of his people and not for personal gain. He is reminding them that his sustenance and reward come solely from God, the Creator, which underscores his sincerity and dedication to his prophetic mission. The rhetorical question at the end challenges the people to reflect on their understanding and acceptance of this truth, urging them towards a deeper contemplation of the divine message.
orig: يا قوم لا أسألكم عليه أجرا إن أجري إلا على الذي فطرني أفلا تعقلون

translation: And O my people, ask forgiveness of your Lord and then repent to Him. He will send [rain from] the sky upon you in showers and increase you in strength [added] to your strength. And do not turn away, [being] criminals.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking forgiveness from Allah and repenting sincerely. It suggests that through repentance, not only will individuals receive spiritual purification, but they will also be blessed with material benefits such as rain, which is vital for agriculture and sustenance, and an increase in physical strength. The verse warns against persisting in sinful behavior, indicating that turning away from repentance leads to a life of crime and spiritual loss.
orig: ويا قوم استغفروا ربكم ثم توبوا إليه يرسل السماء عليكم مدرارا ويزدكم قوة إلى قوتكم ولا تتولوا مجرمين

translation: They said, 'O Hud, you have not brought us clear evidence, and we will not abandon our gods on your say-so, and we are not believers in you.'
