interpretation: This verse reflects the skepticism and resistance of Hud's people towards his message. They demand clear, undeniable proof of his prophethood and are unwilling to forsake their traditional deities based solely on Hud's words. Their statement underscores a common theme in the Qur'an of disbelief and the human tendency to cling to familiar beliefs despite prophetic warnings.
orig: قالوا يا هود ما جئتنا ببينة وما نحن بتاركي آلهتنا عن قولك وما نحن لك بمؤمنين

translation: They said, 'We only say that some of our gods have afflicted you with evil.' He said, 'I call Allah to witness, and bear witness yourselves, that I am innocent of what you associate [with Allah].'
interpretation: This verse highlights the Prophet Abraham's firm rejection of idolatry and his declaration of monotheism. When accused by his people that their gods had afflicted him with madness, Abraham responds by invoking Allah as a witness to his innocence and disavowal of their polytheistic practices. This demonstrates his unwavering faith and commitment to the oneness of God, setting a powerful example for believers to stand firm in their faith against societal pressures and false accusations.
orig: إن نقول إلا اعتراك بعض آلهتنا بسوء قال إني أشهد الله واشهدوا أني بريء مما تشركون

translation: Apart from Him, so plot against me all together; then give me no respite
interpretation: This verse reflects the steadfastness and unwavering faith of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in the face of opposition from his enemies. He challenges them to do their worst, knowing that their plots are futile because his trust is solely in Allah, who is above all and beyond their reach. The Prophet's confidence in divine protection and his readiness to face any adversity for the sake of his mission exemplify the ultimate submission to God's will and the strength derived from such faith.
orig: من دونه فكيدوني جميعا ثم لا تنظرون

translation: Indeed, I have relied upon Allah, my Lord and your Lord. There is no creature except that He holds its forelock. Indeed, my Lord is on a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of complete trust and reliance on Allah, acknowledging His sovereignty over all creation. The metaphor of holding the forelock signifies absolute control and power over every living being. The affirmation that Allah is on a straight path underscores His justice and guidance, reinforcing the believer's confidence in divine wisdom and righteousness.
orig: إني توكلت على الله ربي وربكم ما من دابة إلا هو آخذ بناصيتها إن ربي على صراط مستقيم

translation: But if they turn away, then I have conveyed to you what I was sent with, and my Lord will appoint a people other than you, and you will not harm Him at all. Indeed, my Lord is Guardian over all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophet Muhammad's duty to convey the message of Islam, regardless of the response of his audience. It reassures him that if the people reject his message, it is not a failure on his part, as his responsibility is only to deliver the message. The verse also highlights God's omnipotence and His ability to replace one community with another if they do not heed His call. It underscores the concept that God is not affected by human actions and remains the ultimate Guardian and Protector of everything.
orig: فإن تولوا فقد أبلغتكم ما أرسلت به إليكم ويستخلف ربي قوما غيركم ولا تضرونه شيئا إن ربي على كل شيء حفيظ

translation: And when Our command came, We saved Hud and those who believed with him by Our mercy, and We saved them from a severe punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine mercy and justice of Allah. When the time for divine judgment arrived, Allah saved the prophet Hud and his followers, who had adhered to faith and righteousness, from the destruction that befell their disbelieving community. It underscores the theme that faith and obedience to Allah's messengers can lead to salvation from worldly and spiritual punishments, emphasizing the protective aspect of divine mercy towards the faithful.
orig: ولما جاء أمرنا نجينا هودا والذين آمنوا معه برحمة منا ونجيناهم من عذاب غليظ

translation: And that was 'Ad, who rejected the Signs of their Lord and disobeyed His messengers and followed the command of every obstinate tyrant.
interpretation: This verse highlights the downfall of the 'Ad people due to their rejection of divine guidance and their submission to tyrannical leaders. It serves as a warning to all societies about the consequences of ignoring God's signs and messages, and instead following the dictates of arrogant and stubborn rulers. The verse underscores the importance of adhering to divine guidance and the dangers of allowing oppressive leadership to steer a community away from righteousness.
orig: وتلك عاد جحدوا بآيات ربهم وعصوا رسله واتبعوا أمر كل جبار عنيد

translation: And they were pursued in this world by a curse, and on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, 'Aad disbelieved in their Lord; then, away with 'Aad, the people of Hud.
interpretation: This verse reflects on the fate of the tribe of 'Aad, who were cursed in this life and will face further consequences on the Day of Resurrection due to their disbelief in their Lord. The mention of 'Aad as the people of Hud underscores their historical and prophetic context, emphasizing the severe repercussions of rejecting divine guidance. The phrase 'away with 'Aad' signifies a complete rejection and abandonment by God, serving as a warning to others about the consequences of persistent disbelief.
orig: وأتبعوا في هذه الدنيا لعنة ويوم القيامة ألا إن عادا كفروا ربهم ألا بعدا لعاد قوم هود

translation: And to Thamud [We sent] their brother Salih. He said, 'O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. He has produced you from the earth and settled you in it, so ask forgiveness of Him and then repent to Him. Indeed, my Lord is near and responsive.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the monotheistic message delivered by the prophet Salih to his people, Thamud. It underscores the fundamental Islamic belief in the oneness of God, urging the people to worship only Allah, who is the Creator and Sustainer of life. The call to seek forgiveness and repent reflects the merciful nature of God, who is described as being close to His servants and responsive to their prayers. This message serves as a reminder of the importance of humility, repentance, and the direct relationship between the individual and God.
orig: وإلى ثمود أخاهم صالحا قال يا قوم اعبدوا الله ما لكم من إله غيره هو أنشأكم من الأرض واستعمركم فيها فاستغفروه ثم توبوا إليه إن ربي قريب مجيب

translation: They said, 'O Saleh, you were among us as one in whom we had hope before this. Do you forbid us to worship what our fathers worshipped? Indeed, we are in disquieting doubt about that to which you invite us.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the reaction of Saleh's people to his call towards monotheism. It shows their initial respect for him, yet their reluctance to abandon the traditional polytheistic practices of their ancestors. Their statement reveals a psychological and cultural resistance to change, highlighting the challenge prophets face in reforming societal norms. The phrase 'disquieting doubt' indicates their internal conflict and uncertainty about the new faith Saleh is preaching, which underscores the difficulty in shifting long-held beliefs and the human tendency to cling to familiar customs despite recognizing the messenger's credibility.
orig: قالوا يا صالح قد كنت فينا مرجوا قبل هذا أتنهانا أن نعبد ما يعبد آباؤنا وإننا لفي شك مما تدعونا إليه مريب

translation: He said, 'O my people, have you considered: if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord and He has given me mercy from Himself, who would support me against Allah if I disobeyed Him? You would not increase me except in loss.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the prophet's plea to his people to reflect on the consequences of rejecting his message. It highlights the prophet's reliance on divine guidance and mercy, underscoring that disobedience to Allah would lead to personal loss and no one could protect him from divine retribution. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of obedience to God and the futility of seeking support against His will.
orig: قال يا قوم أرأيتم إن كنت على بينة من ربي وآتاني منه رحمة فمن ينصرني من الله إن عصيته فما تزيدونني غير تخسير

translation: And O my people, this is the she-camel of Allah - a sign for you. So leave her to graze in Allah's land and do not touch her with harm, lest a near punishment should seize you.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of respecting and acknowledging the signs and miracles sent by Allah. The she-camel mentioned here is a specific sign given to the people of Thamud as a test of their obedience and faith. The command to let the she-camel graze freely and not harm her serves as a reminder that Allah's commands must be followed without question or harm. Disobedience to such clear signs leads to swift divine retribution, highlighting the consequences of rejecting Allah's guidance and mercy.
orig: ويا قوم هذه ناقة الله لكم آية فذروها تأكل في أرض الله ولا تمسوها بسوء فيأخذكم عذاب قريب

translation: So they hamstrung her, and he said, 'Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days. That is a promise not to be belied.'
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of the Prophet Salih and the people of Thamud. After the people of Thamud defiantly killed the she-camel that was sent as a sign from God, Prophet Salih warned them of impending punishment. The three days given to them to enjoy their homes symbolize a brief period of respite before divine retribution. The promise mentioned is a stern reminder of the inevitability and truthfulness of God's judgment, emphasizing that His warnings are never false.
orig: فعقروها فقال تمتعوا في داركم ثلاثة أيام ذلك وعد غير مكذوب

translation: So when Our command came, We saved Salih and those who believed with him, by a mercy from Us, and from the disgrace of that day. Indeed, your Lord - He is the Powerful, the Exalted in Might.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine protection and mercy extended to the Prophet Salih and his followers when the punishment was decreed upon the disbelieving community. It highlights that God's mercy is selective, based on faith and obedience, and serves as a reminder of His supreme power and authority to save or punish as He wills. The mention of God as 'the Powerful, the Exalted in Might' emphasizes His absolute control over events and His ability to enforce His decrees, reinforcing the lesson that faith in God can lead to salvation from worldly and spiritual disgrace.
orig: فلما جاء أمرنا نجينا صالحا والذين آمنوا معه برحمة منا ومن خزي يومئذ إن ربك هو القوي العزيز

translation: And the cry seized those who had wronged, and they became lifeless bodies in their homes.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the sudden and complete destruction of the wrongdoers by a divine punishment, emphasizing the inevitability and the overwhelming power of Allah's retribution. The use of "the cry" as the instrument of punishment symbolizes a swift and inescapable divine intervention that leaves the wrongdoers dead in their own homes, highlighting the futility of their previous actions against the will of Allah.
orig: وأخذ الذين ظلموا الصيحة فأصبحوا في ديارهم جاثمين

translation: As if they had never prospered therein. Indeed, Thamud disbelieved in their Lord; so away with Thamud!
interpretation: This verse reflects on the fate of the Thamud people, who were once prosperous but were ultimately destroyed due to their disbelief and rejection of their Lord's messages. The phrase 'as if they had never prospered therein' emphasizes the complete erasure of their civilization, serving as a warning about the consequences of denying divine guidance. The declaration 'so away with Thamud!' underscores the finality and severity of their punishment, highlighting the importance of faith and obedience to God.
orig: كأن لم يغنوا فيها ألا إن ثمود كفروا ربهم ألا بعدا لثمود

translation: And certainly Our messengers came to Abraham with good tidings. They said, 'Peace.' He said, 'Peace,' and he was not long in bringing a roasted calf.
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of hospitality and the readiness to serve guests, as exemplified by Abraham. When the angels came to him with the good news, his immediate response was to offer them food, demonstrating his generous nature and the importance of welcoming guests warmly, which is a valued virtue in Islamic teachings.
orig: ولقد جاءت رسلنا إبراهيم بالبشرى قالوا سلاما قال سلام فما لبث أن جاء بعجل حنيذ

translation: So when he saw their hands not reaching for it, he distrusted them and felt apprehension from them. They said, 'Fear not. We have been sent to the people of Lot.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the moment of Abraham's initial fear and suspicion when he noticed that his guests did not eat, which was unusual and caused him to question their intentions. The reassurance from the angels that they were sent on a mission to the people of Lot underscores the divine purpose behind their visit, illustrating themes of trust in divine messengers and the execution of God's will.
orig: فلما رأى أيديهم لا تصل إليه نكرهم وأوجس منهم خيفة قالوا لا تخف إنا أرسلنا إلى قوم لوط

translation: And his wife was standing, and she laughed. Then We gave her glad tidings of Isaac, and after Isaac, Jacob.
interpretation: This verse highlights the miraculous nature of divine promise and the human reaction to it. Sarah, the wife of Abraham, laughs in astonishment and perhaps disbelief upon hearing the news of her impending pregnancy at an old age. This laughter is a natural human response to what seems impossible, yet it underscores the theme of God's omnipotence and ability to fulfill His promises beyond human expectations. The mention of Isaac and Jacob further emphasizes the continuity and fulfillment of God's covenant through generations.
orig: وامرأته قائمة فضحكت فبشرناها بإسحاق ومن وراء إسحاق يعقوب

translation: She said, 'Woe to me! Shall I bear a child while I am an old woman and this, my husband, is an elderly man? Indeed, this is a strange thing!'
interpretation: This verse reflects Sarah's astonishment and disbelief upon hearing the news of her impending pregnancy at an old age. It highlights the human reaction of doubt when faced with seemingly impossible miracles, yet it also sets the stage for demonstrating God's omnipotence and ability to transcend natural laws.
orig: قالت يا ويلتى أألد وأنا عجوز وهذا بعلي شيخا إن هذا لشيء عجيب

translation: They said, 'Do you wonder at the command of Allah? The mercy of Allah and His blessings be upon you, O people of the house. Indeed, He is Praiseworthy and Glorious.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the awe and reverence towards the divine command and the special status of the Prophet Muhammad's family, known as the Ahl al-Bayt. It emphasizes that Allah's mercy and blessings are bestowed upon them, highlighting their esteemed position in Islam. The phrase 'He is Praiseworthy and Glorious' underscores Allah's supreme attributes, reinforcing the belief in His perfection and the legitimacy of His decrees.
orig: قالوا أتعجبين من أمر الله رحمت الله وبركاته عليكم أهل البيت إنه حميد مجيد

translation: So when the fear had gone away from Ibrahim (Abraham) and the glad tidings had reached him, he began to plead with Us for the people of Lut (Lot).
interpretation: This verse illustrates the compassionate nature of Prophet Ibrahim. After receiving the good news of the birth of his son and overcoming his initial fear, Ibrahim immediately turns his attention to interceding for the people of Lut, demonstrating his deep concern for others and his willingness to advocate for mercy on behalf of a community facing divine punishment. This reflects the prophetic trait of intercession and the importance of praying for the well-being of others.
orig: فلما ذهب عن إبراهيم الروع وجاءته البشرى يجادلنا في قوم لوط

translation: Indeed, Abraham was forbearing, compassionate, and penitent.
interpretation: This verse highlights the exemplary character of Prophet Abraham, emphasizing his patience and forbearance in the face of trials, his compassion towards others, and his constant return to God in repentance and devotion. It serves as a model for believers to emulate these qualities in their own lives.
orig: إن إبراهيم لحليم أواه منيب

translation: O Ibrahim, turn away from this. Indeed, the command of your Lord has come, and indeed, there will come to them a punishment that cannot be repelled.
interpretation: This verse addresses Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) and instructs him to disengage from the situation involving his people who rejected his message. It emphasizes the inevitability of divine decree, indicating that God's command for the punishment of those who disbelieve is set and will be executed without fail. The verse underscores the theme of divine justice and the certainty of consequences for those who reject the truth, reinforcing the importance of obedience to God's commands and the reality of accountability in the hereafter.
orig: يا إبراهيم أعرض عن هذا إنه قد جاء أمر ربك وإنهم آتيهم عذاب غير مردود

translation: And when Our messengers came to Lot, he was distressed for them and felt straitened on their account and said, 'This is a distressful day.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates Lot's emotional state upon the arrival of the angels, who appeared as young men, to his town. His distress and anxiety stem from his fear for their safety, knowing the corrupt nature of his people who were known for their immoral behavior towards strangers. Lot's declaration of the day being 'distressful' reflects his deep concern and the tension he felt, anticipating the potential harm that could come to the messengers.
orig: ولما جاءت رسلنا لوطا سيء بهم وضاق بهم ذرعا وقال هذا يوم عصيب

translation: And his people came rushing towards him, and they had been doing evil deeds before. He said, 'O my people, these are my daughters; they are purer for you. So fear Allah and do not disgrace me concerning my guests. Is there not among you a man of reason?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the Prophet Lut's confrontation with his people, who were engaging in immoral acts. His offer of his daughters as a means to divert their attention from his guests underscores his desperate attempt to protect the divine messengers from harm. The call to fear Allah and not to dishonor guests emphasizes the importance of hospitality and moral integrity in Islamic teachings. The rhetorical question at the end challenges the community's lack of righteous individuals, urging them to reflect on their actions and societal values.
orig: وجاءه قومه يهرعون إليه ومن قبل كانوا يعملون السيئات قال يا قوم هؤلاء بناتي هن أطهر لكم فاتقوا الله ولا تخزون في ضيفي أليس منكم رجل رشيد

translation: They said, 'Indeed, you know that we have no right to your daughters, and indeed, you know what we want.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the audacity and moral corruption of the people of Lot, as they openly acknowledge that they have no legitimate claim over Lot's daughters, yet they persist in their sinful demand, indicating their blatant disregard for moral and divine laws.
orig: قالوا لقد علمت ما لنا في بناتك من حق وإنك لتعلم ما نريد

translation: He said, 'If only I had power over you or could resort to a strong support.'
interpretation: This verse reflects a moment of helplessness and frustration from the speaker, who wishes for the ability to exert control or find refuge in a powerful ally. It underscores the human condition of seeking strength or protection when faced with adversity, highlighting the importance of reliance on a higher power or community for support.
orig: قال لو أن لي بكم قوة أو آوي إلى ركن شديد

translation: They said, 'O Lot, indeed we are messengers of your Lord; they will never reach you. So set out with your family during a portion of the night and let not any among you look back - except your wife; indeed, she will be struck by what strikes them. Indeed, their appointed time is the morning. Is not the morning near?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine intervention and protection extended to Prophet Lot and his family, with the exception of his wife, who was to face the same fate as the people of Sodom due to her disbelief. It underscores the themes of obedience to divine commands and the consequences of aligning oneself with evil. The urgency of the departure at night and the prohibition against looking back symbolize the need for immediate and complete separation from corrupt environments. The mention of the morning as their appointed time emphasizes the inevitability and closeness of divine judgment.
orig: قالوا يا لوط إنا رسل ربك لن يصلوا إليك فأسر بأهلك بقطع من الليل ولا يلتفت منكم أحد إلا امرأتك إنه مصيبها ما أصابهم إن موعدهم الصبح أليس الصبح بقريب

translation: So when Our command came, We made the highest part [of the city] its lowest and rained upon them stones of layered hard clay,
interpretation: This verse describes the divine punishment that befell the people of Lot, illustrating God's power to completely overturn and destroy a society that persists in sin and disobedience. The transformation of the highest part of the city to its lowest signifies a complete reversal of their status and a manifestation of God's justice. The raining of stones made of layered hard clay symbolizes the precise and overwhelming nature of the punishment, emphasizing that it was a deliberate act of God to eradicate the corruption and immorality that had taken root in the community.
orig: فلما جاء أمرنا جعلنا عاليها سافلها وأمطرنا عليها حجارة من سجيل منضود

translation: Marked in the sight of your Lord, and it is not far from the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the punishment or decree mentioned is clearly recorded and known by Allah, and it is imminent for the wrongdoers, emphasizing the inevitability and closeness of divine justice.
orig: مسومة عند ربك وما هي من الظالمين ببعيد

translation: And to Madyan [We sent] their brother Shu'ayb. He said, 'O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. And do not decrease from the measure and the scale. Indeed, I see you in prosperity, and indeed, I fear for you the punishment of an all-encompassing Day.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the prophetic mission of Shu'ayb to the people of Madyan, emphasizing monotheism and ethical conduct in trade. Shu'ayb calls his people to worship Allah alone, rejecting any form of idolatry, and warns them against dishonest practices in measuring and weighing goods. His observation of their current prosperity serves as a reminder of their vulnerability to divine punishment if they continue in their unjust ways. The 'all-encompassing Day' refers to the Day of Judgment, underscoring the severity and inevitability of divine retribution for those who fail to heed the prophetic guidance.
orig: وإلى مدين أخاهم شعيبا قال يا قوم اعبدوا الله ما لكم من إله غيره ولا تنقصوا المكيال والميزان إني أراكم بخير وإني أخاف عليكم عذاب يوم محيط

translation: And O my people, give full measure and weight in justice and do not defraud the people of their due and do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of honesty and fairness in transactions and dealings with others. It calls for giving full and accurate measures in trade, which is a manifestation of justice. The prohibition against defrauding people of their rights extends beyond mere transactions to encompass all forms of social and economic interactions. Additionally, the verse warns against causing corruption and disorder in society, highlighting the broader ethical responsibility to maintain peace and integrity in all actions. It reflects the Qur'anic principle of promoting a just and harmonious community.
orig: ويا قوم أوفوا المكيال والميزان بالقسط ولا تبخسوا الناس أشياءهم ولا تعثوا في الأرض مفسدين

translation: Remain conscious of Allah; it is better for you if you are believers. And I am not a guardian over you.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining a constant awareness and fear of Allah, which is described as beneficial for the believers. It serves as a reminder and encouragement for the faithful to stay on the path of righteousness. The latter part of the verse, where the speaker (often interpreted as a prophet or messenger) disclaims guardianship over the people, underscores the individual responsibility of each person towards their faith and actions, highlighting that ultimate guidance and accountability lie with Allah alone.
orig: بقيت الله خير لكم إن كنتم مؤمنين وما أنا عليكم بحفيظ

translation: They said, 'O Shu'ayb, does your prayer command you that we should leave what our fathers worshipped or that we should do with our wealth as we please? Indeed, you are the forbearing, the rightly guided.'
interpretation: In this verse, the people of Shu'ayb are challenging his call to monotheism and ethical conduct by sarcastically questioning if his religious practices compel him to demand that they abandon their ancestral worship and restrict their financial freedom. They acknowledge Shu'ayb's qualities of forbearance and wisdom, yet use these traits to imply that he is overly tolerant and perhaps misguided in his approach, highlighting their resistance to change and reform.
orig: قالوا يا شعيب أصلاتك تأمرك أن نترك ما يعبد آباؤنا أو أن نفعل في أموالنا ما نشاء إنك لأنت الحليم الرشيد

translation: He said: 'O my people! Do you see if I am on clear evidence from my Lord and He has provided me with a good provision from Himself, and I do not want to oppose you to what I forbid you from. I only want to reform as much as I can. My success is only with Allah; upon Him I rely and to Him I return.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sincerity and humility of a prophet or messenger addressing his people. He is asserting that his guidance and sustenance come directly from God, and his intention is not to oppose them out of personal gain but to guide them towards righteousness. His ultimate goal is reform and improvement within the community, acknowledging that his ability to succeed in this mission depends entirely on God's will. This reflects a deep trust in divine support and a commitment to return to God, underscoring the importance of reliance on divine guidance and the pursuit of communal betterment.
orig: قال يا قوم أرأيتم إن كنت على بينة من ربي ورزقني منه رزقا حسنا وما أريد أن أخالفكم إلى ما أنهاكم عنه إن أريد إلا الإصلاح ما استطعت وما توفيقي إلا بالله عليه توكلت وإليه أنيب

translation: And O my people, let not your dissension from me cause you to be struck by that which struck the people of Noah or the people of Hud or the people of Salih. And the people of Lot are not far off from you.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning from a prophet to his people, emphasizing the consequences of rejecting divine guidance. The prophet reminds them of the fates of previous nations who were destroyed for their disbelief and disobedience. By mentioning the peoples of Noah, Hud, Salih, and Lot, the verse underscores the recurring pattern of divine retribution against those who oppose God's messengers. The reference to Lot's people being 'not far off' suggests that the consequences of such actions are imminent and should serve as a stark reminder to heed the prophet's call to righteousness.
orig: ويا قوم لا يجرمنكم شقاقي أن يصيبكم مثل ما أصاب قوم نوح أو قوم هود أو قوم صالح وما قوم لوط منكم ببعيد

translation: And seek forgiveness from your Lord, then turn to Him in repentance. Indeed, my Lord is Most Merciful, Loving.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking forgiveness from Allah and repenting sincerely. It reassures believers that Allah's mercy and love are vast, encouraging them to turn back to Him with hope and trust in His compassion. The mention of Allah as 'Most Merciful' and 'Loving' highlights His readiness to forgive and His affection towards those who seek His forgiveness.
orig: واستغفروا ربكم ثم توبوا إليه إن ربي رحيم ودود

translation: They said, 'O Shu'ayb, we do not understand much of what you say, and indeed, we see you as weak among us. And if it were not for your clan, we would have stoned you; and you are not mighty against us.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the rejection and hostility faced by Prophet Shu'ayb from his people. It reflects a common theme in the Qur'an where prophets are often met with disbelief and opposition from their communities. The people's claim of not understanding Shu'ayb's message is a pretext for their refusal to accept his call to monotheism and righteousness. Their mention of his perceived weakness and their threat to stone him if not for his clan's protection underscores the societal pressure and personal danger prophets endure. The verse also illustrates the importance of community support for prophets and the moral courage required to stand against societal norms and injustices.
orig: قالوا يا شعيب ما نفقه كثيرا مما تقول وإنا لنراك فينا ضعيفا ولولا رهطك لرجمناك وما أنت علينا بعزيز

translation: He said, 'O my people, is my family more important to you than Allah? And you have taken Him as something to be disregarded behind your backs. Indeed, my Lord is encompassing of what you do.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the Prophet's frustration with his people's misplaced priorities, where they value their social and familial ties over their devotion to Allah. It underscores the theme of divine awareness, emphasizing that Allah is fully aware of all actions, and no deed, whether hidden or public, escapes His knowledge. The Prophet is reminding his people of the ultimate accountability to Allah, urging them to reconsider their values and actions in light of divine judgment.
orig: قال يا قوم أرهطي أعز عليكم من الله واتخذتموه وراءكم ظهريا إن ربي بما تعملون محيط

translation: And O my people, work according to your position; indeed, I am working. You are going to know to whom will come a punishment that will disgrace him and who is a liar. So watch; indeed, I am with you a watcher.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of accountability and the inevitability of divine justice. It encourages steadfastness in faith and righteousness, even in the face of opposition. The speaker, likely a prophet, is asserting that both he and his people will continue their respective actions, but ultimately, the truth will be revealed, and divine judgment will distinguish between the truthful and the liar. The mutual watching signifies a challenge to observe the outcomes of their deeds, reinforcing the belief in an ultimate accountability before God.
orig: ويا قوم اعملوا على مكانتكم إني عامل سوف تعلمون من يأتيه عذاب يخزيه ومن هو كاذب وارتقبوا إني معكم رقيب

translation: And when Our command came, We saved Shu'ayb and those who believed with him by Our mercy, and the blast seized those who wronged, and they became lifeless in their homes.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the divine justice and mercy of Allah. It shows that when the appointed time for divine intervention arrives, Allah rescues the righteous, exemplified by Prophet Shu'ayb and his followers, through His mercy. Conversely, those who persist in wrongdoing are punished, as symbolized by the destructive blast that leaves them dead in their dwellings. This serves as a reminder of the consequences of rejecting the message of the prophets and the ultimate accountability before Allah.
orig: ولما جاء أمرنا نجينا شعيبا والذين آمنوا معه برحمة منا وأخذت الذين ظلموا الصيحة فأصبحوا في ديارهم جاثمين

translation: As if they had never prospered therein. So away with Madyan, just as Thamud was taken away.
interpretation: This verse reflects on the destruction of the people of Madyan, likening their fate to that of Thamud. It serves as a reminder of the consequences of rejecting the messengers of God and indulging in corruption and disbelief. The phrase 'as if they had never prospered therein' emphasizes the complete erasure of their civilization, underscoring the transient nature of worldly success when it is not aligned with divine guidance. The mention of both Madyan and Thamud together highlights a recurring theme in the Qur'an of divine retribution against communities that stray from the path of righteousness.
orig: كأن لم يغنوا فيها ألا بعدا لمدين كما بعدت ثمود

translation: And indeed We sent Moses with Our signs and a clear authority.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine mission of Moses, highlighting that he was sent by Allah with clear miracles and undeniable proof of his prophethood. It underscores the legitimacy and authority of Moses' message, serving as a reminder to believers of the continuity of divine guidance through prophets.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا موسى بآياتنا وسلطان مبين

translation: To Pharaoh and his chiefs, but they followed the command of Pharaoh, and the command of Pharaoh was not rightly guided.
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of following misguided leadership. It specifically refers to the people of Pharaoh who, despite the clear signs and warnings from Moses, chose to adhere to Pharaoh's directives. The verse underscores the consequences of blindly following a leader who is not guided by righteousness or divine wisdom, leading to their ultimate downfall. It serves as a warning to all societies about the dangers of submitting to authority that deviates from the path of truth and justice.
orig: إلى فرعون وملئه فاتبعوا أمر فرعون وما أمر فرعون برشيد

translation: He will lead his people on the Day of Resurrection and bring them into the Fire. And wretched is the destination reached.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the consequence of following a misguided leader. It emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, such a leader will not only face punishment but will also lead his followers into Hellfire. The phrase 'wretched is the destination reached' underscores the severity and finality of their fate, serving as a warning about the importance of choosing righteous leadership and the accountability one has for leading others astray.
orig: يقدم قومه يوم القيامة فأوردهم النار وبئس الورد المورود

translation: And they were followed in this [life] by a curse, and on the Day of Resurrection, wretched is the gift to be given.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of disbelief and rejection of divine guidance. The 'curse' mentioned refers to the spiritual and worldly disgrace that follows those who stray from the path of righteousness. On the Day of Resurrection, the 'wretched gift' symbolizes the ultimate failure and loss that awaits them, underscoring the severity of their punishment and the finality of their rejection by God.
orig: وأتبعوا في هذه لعنة ويوم القيامة بئس الرفد المرفود

translation: That is from the news of the cities, which We relate to you; of them, some are standing and some are reaped.
interpretation: This verse highlights the transient nature of civilizations. It suggests that God narrates the stories of various cities to the Prophet Muhammad as lessons or warnings. Some of these cities still exist ("standing"), serving as ongoing examples, while others have been destroyed or "reaped," indicating their end due to their actions. This serves as a reminder of the consequences of moral and ethical conduct, urging reflection on one's own society and actions.
orig: ذلك من أنباء القرى نقصه عليك منها قائم وحصيد

translation: And We did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves. So their gods, which they called upon besides Allah, did not avail them at all when the command of your Lord came. And they did not increase them in anything except ruin.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of personal responsibility and the futility of idolatry. It suggests that humans are accountable for their own actions, and when they choose to worship entities other than Allah, they are essentially harming themselves. The verse indicates that these false deities offer no protection or benefit when divine judgment arrives, highlighting the ultimate powerlessness of idols and the self-destructive nature of such worship, which only leads to further ruin.
orig: وما ظلمناهم ولكن ظلموا أنفسهم فما أغنت عنهم آلهتهم التي يدعون من دون الله من شيء لما جاء أمر ربك وما زادوهم غير تتبيب

translation: And thus is the seizure of your Lord when He seizes the towns while they are committing wrong. Indeed, His seizure is painful and severe.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the consequence of persistent wrongdoing and oppression by communities. It emphasizes that when Allah decides to punish such communities, His punishment is intense and agonizing. The verse serves as a warning to societies to adhere to justice and righteousness, highlighting the inevitability and severity of divine retribution when it is unleashed.
orig: وكذلك أخذ ربك إذا أخذ القرى وهي ظالمة إن أخذه أليم شديد

translation: Indeed, in that is a sign for whoever fears the punishment of the Hereafter. That is a Day for which humankind will be gathered, and that is a Day witnessed.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder and a warning to those who are conscious of the consequences of their actions in the afterlife. It emphasizes the inevitability of the Day of Judgment, where all people will be assembled and held accountable for their deeds. The phrase 'a Day witnessed' underscores the public nature of this event, where nothing will be hidden, and all actions will be exposed and judged. This should instill a sense of urgency and mindfulness in believers to live righteously, as the reality of this day is a significant sign for those who fear divine retribution.
orig: إن في ذلك لآية لمن خاف عذاب الآخرة ذلك يوم مجموع له الناس وذلك يوم مشهود

translation: And We delay it only for a limited term.
interpretation: This verse suggests that God's actions, including the delay of certain events or punishments, are purposeful and timed according to a divine schedule that is predetermined and finite. It emphasizes the concept of divine timing and patience, indicating that there is wisdom and a specific reason behind the postponement of events, which are part of God's overall plan.
orig: وما نؤخره إلا لأجل معدود

translation: The Day it comes, no soul will speak except by His permission. And among them will be the wretched and the prosperous.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, emphasizing the absolute authority of Allah. On that day, no one will be able to speak without Allah's permission, highlighting the complete submission and accountability of every soul. The mention of 'the wretched and the prosperous' indicates the stark division among people based on their deeds; some will be in a state of misery due to their sins, while others will be in a state of happiness due to their righteousness. This underscores the importance of living a life in accordance with Allah's guidance to be among the prosperous on that day.
orig: يوم يأت لا تكلم نفس إلا بإذنه فمنهم شقي وسعيد

translation: As for those who were wretched, they will be in the Fire, wherein there will be for them [only] the exhaling and inhaling of sighs.
interpretation: This verse describes the fate of those who have led a life of disobedience and sin, referred to as 'those who were wretched.' Their ultimate destination is Hell, symbolized by 'the Fire.' The mention of 'exhaling and inhaling of sighs' illustrates the intense suffering and despair they will experience in the afterlife, emphasizing the eternal nature of their punishment and the absence of any relief or comfort.
orig: فأما الذين شقوا ففي النار لهم فيها زفير وشهيق

translation: Abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills. Indeed, your Lord is the Doer of what He intends.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the eternal nature of the punishment in Hell for those who are condemned to it, lasting as long as the heavens and the earth exist. However, it also underscores the absolute power and sovereignty of Allah, indicating that He can alter this duration if He so wills, reflecting His complete control over creation and His ability to do whatever He intends.
orig: خالدين فيها ما دامت السماوات والأرض إلا ما شاء ربك إن ربك فعال لما يريد

translation: And as for those who were fortunate, they will be in Paradise, abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills - a gift without end.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the eternal nature of the reward for the righteous in the afterlife. The phrase 'as long as the heavens and the earth endure' emphasizes the permanence of their stay in Paradise, suggesting that it is tied to the existence of the universe itself. However, the exception 'except what your Lord wills' indicates that Allah's will is supreme and can alter even what seems eternal. The 'gift without end' reinforces the idea of an everlasting reward, highlighting Allah's boundless generosity and the unending nature of the blessings in Paradise. This interpretation underscores the concept of divine mercy and the ultimate hope for believers in achieving a perpetual state of bliss.
orig: وأما الذين سعدوا ففي الجنة خالدين فيها ما دامت السماوات والأرض إلا ما شاء ربك عطاء غير مجذوذ

translation: So be not in doubt about what these people worship. They worship nothing but what their fathers worshipped before. And indeed, We will give them their share without decrease.
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad, reassuring him not to be in doubt or confused about the idolatry of the polytheists. It explains that their worship is merely a continuation of ancestral traditions without any rational basis. The verse also promises that despite their misguided worship, God will still provide them with their due sustenance and worldly provisions, emphasizing His justice and mercy that extends even to those who are astray.
orig: فلا تك في مرية مما يعبد هؤلاء ما يعبدون إلا كما يعبد آباؤهم من قبل وإنا لموفوهم نصيبهم غير منقوص

translation: And We certainly gave Moses the Scripture, but disputes arose about it. And if it had not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been concluded between them. And indeed they are, concerning it, in disquieting doubt.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine bestowal of the Torah to Moses, yet it underscores the human tendency towards disagreement and doubt even in the face of clear divine guidance. The 'word that preceded from your Lord' refers to God's decree to delay the final judgment, allowing time for people to reflect and choose their path. The ongoing disputes and doubts about the Scripture reflect the broader theme of human uncertainty and the challenge of maintaining faith amidst differing interpretations and beliefs.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى الكتاب فاختلف فيه ولولا كلمة سبقت من ربك لقضي بينهم وإنهم لفي شك منه مريب

translation: And indeed, each [of them] - your Lord will fully compensate them for their deeds. Indeed, He is Acquainted with what they do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine justice and accountability in Islam. It reassures believers that Allah, who is described as the Lord, will ensure that every individual receives a just recompense for their actions. The use of "fully compensate" suggests that the reward or punishment will be precisely measured according to one's deeds. The affirmation that Allah is "Acquainted with what they do" underscores His omniscience, indicating that nothing escapes His knowledge, and thus, His judgment will be perfectly fair and informed.
orig: وإن كلا لما ليوفينهم ربك أعمالهم إنه بما يعملون خبير

translation: So stand firm as you have been commanded, and those who have turned [to Allah] with you, and do not transgress. Indeed, He is Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of steadfastness in faith and obedience to Allah's commands. It is a call to the Prophet Muhammad and his followers to remain resolute in their commitment to Islam, not allowing external pressures or internal desires to lead them astray. The instruction to 'not transgress' serves as a reminder to maintain balance and justice in all actions, avoiding excess or oppression. The assurance that Allah sees all deeds underscores the accountability of every individual, encouraging a constant awareness of divine observation and the moral implications of one's actions.
orig: فاستقم كما أمرت ومن تاب معك ولا تطغوا إنه بما تعملون بصير

translation: And do not incline toward those who do wrong, lest the Fire touch you, and you have no protectors other than Allah, nor will you be helped.
interpretation: This verse warns believers against associating with or supporting oppressors and wrongdoers, as such actions can lead them astray and expose them to divine punishment. It emphasizes the importance of maintaining moral integrity and reliance solely on Allah, highlighting that aligning with the unjust will leave one without divine support or protection.
orig: ولا تركنوا إلى الذين ظلموا فتمسكم النار وما لكم من دون الله من أولياء ثم لا تنصرون

translation: And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night. Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds. That is a reminder for those who remember.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of performing the five daily prayers, which are distributed throughout the day and night. The 'two ends of the day' refer to the morning (Fajr) and afternoon (Asr) prayers, while 'the approach of the night' includes the evening (Maghrib) and night (Isha) prayers, along with the noon (Dhuhr) prayer. The verse also highlights the concept of redemption through good deeds, suggesting that engaging in acts of worship and righteousness can erase previous sins. This serves as a motivational reminder for believers to maintain their prayers and other good actions, as a means of spiritual purification and closeness to God.
orig: وأقم الصلاة طرفي النهار وزلفا من الليل إن الحسنات يذهبن السيئات ذلك ذكرى للذاكرين

translation: And be patient, for indeed, Allah does not let the reward of the good-doers go to waste.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of patience in the face of adversity. It reassures believers that their perseverance and good deeds will be rewarded by Allah, who is just and never overlooks the efforts of those who do good. It serves as a reminder to maintain steadfastness and continue performing righteous acts, trusting in Allah's promise of recompense.
orig: واصبر فإن الله لا يضيع أجر المحسنين

translation: So why were there not among the generations before you those endowed with a remnant who would forbid corruption on the earth, except for a few of those whom We saved from among them? But those who did wrong pursued what luxury they were given therein, and they were criminals.
interpretation: This verse reflects on the moral responsibility of communities to have righteous individuals who actively work to prevent corruption and evil. It suggests that the lack of such individuals in past generations contributed to their downfall, except for a few who were saved due to their righteousness. The verse also critiques the behavior of the wrongdoers who, instead of using their resources for good, indulged in luxury and persisted in their sinful ways, ultimately leading to their ruin.
orig: فلولا كان من القرون من قبلكم أولو بقية ينهون عن الفساد في الأرض إلا قليلا ممن أنجينا منهم واتبع الذين ظلموا ما أترفوا فيه وكانوا مجرمين

translation: And your Lord would not destroy the cities unjustly while their people were reformers
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the justice of Allah, indicating that He does not unjustly destroy communities whose inhabitants are actively engaged in righteous deeds and efforts to reform society. It highlights the importance of individual and collective righteousness in averting divine punishment.
orig: وما كان ربك ليهلك القرى بظلم وأهلها مصلحون

translation: And if your Lord had willed, He could have made mankind one community; but they will not cease to differ.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom behind human diversity and differences in belief. It suggests that God intentionally allows for a variety of perspectives and communities among people, rather than forcing uniformity. This diversity serves as a test and a means for individuals to exercise their free will, demonstrating that unity in faith or understanding is not predestined but depends on human choice and effort.
orig: ولو شاء ربك لجعل الناس أمة واحدة ولا يزالون مختلفين

translation: Except those on whom your Lord has bestowed His Mercy, and for that did He create them. And the Word of your Lord has been fulfilled (His saying): "Surely, I will fill Hell with jinns and men all together."
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of divine mercy and predestination. It suggests that while God's mercy is available to all, it is specifically bestowed upon those He chooses, indicating a divine selection process. The purpose of creation, as mentioned, is linked to this mercy, implying that the ultimate goal of creation is to manifest God's mercy. Additionally, the verse underscores the inevitability of God's decree, stating that Hell will be filled with both jinn and humans, which serves as a reminder of the consequences of straying from the path of righteousness. This dual message of hope through mercy and warning through predestined judgment encourages believers to seek God's mercy actively while being mindful of their actions.
orig: إلا من رحم ربك ولذلك خلقهم وتمت كلمة ربك لأملأن جهنم من الجنة والناس أجمعين

translation: And We have related to you from the news of the messengers what We strengthen your heart with, and there has come to you in this the truth and an admonition and a reminder for the believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the stories of the messengers are not merely historical accounts but are divinely chosen to fortify the Prophet Muhammad's heart and resolve. These narratives serve multiple purposes: they affirm the truth of the Qur'an, provide moral guidance, and serve as a reminder for believers to remain steadfast in their faith. The verse underscores the supportive and instructive nature of these stories, highlighting their relevance and importance to the spiritual and moral development of the faithful.
orig: وكلا نقص عليك من أنباء الرسل ما نثبت به فؤادك وجاءك في هذه الحق وموعظة وذكرى للمؤمنين

translation: And say to those who do not believe, 'Do your worst, we are doing our best.'
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to remain steadfast in their faith and actions, even in the face of opposition from non-believers. It suggests a message of resilience and confidence, urging Muslims to continue their efforts in righteousness and good deeds, regardless of the challenges posed by those who do not share their faith. The verse implies a sense of competition or challenge, where believers are called to outdo the non-believers in moral and ethical conduct.
orig: وقل للذين لا يؤمنون اعملوا على مكانتكم إنا عاملون

translation: And wait, indeed we are waiting.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes patience and steadfastness in faith. It suggests that believers should remain patient and trust in God's timing, just as they are assured that God is also waiting to see the outcome of their actions and faith. It serves as a reminder of the mutual waiting between humans and the divine, encouraging believers to persevere in their spiritual journey.
orig: وانتظروا إنا منتظرون

translation: And to Allah belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and to Him all matters are returned. So worship Him and put your trust in Him, and your Lord is not unaware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence and omniscience of Allah, indicating that all hidden matters and future events are under His control, and ultimately, everything will return to Him for judgment. It encourages believers to worship Allah exclusively and to place their complete trust in Him, reinforcing the notion that Allah is fully aware of all actions, thereby urging mindfulness and accountability in one's deeds.
orig: ولله غيب السماوات والأرض وإليه يرجع الأمر كله فاعبده وتوكل عليه وما ربك بغافل عما تعملون

translation: Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the clear Book.
interpretation: The opening letters 'Alif, Lam, Ra' are among the mysterious letters (muqatta'at) whose meanings are known only to Allah, serving as a divine signature on the Quran. The phrase 'These are the verses of the clear Book' emphasizes that the Quran is a book of guidance that is clear and unambiguous, providing clarity and understanding to those who seek it.
orig: الر تلك آيات الكتاب المبين

translation: Indeed, We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an that you might understand.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an was revealed in the Arabic language to facilitate understanding among its primary audience, the Arabs, and by extension, to all humanity. The choice of Arabic underscores the importance of clear communication of divine guidance, encouraging reflection and comprehension of its messages.
orig: إنا أنزلناه قرآنا عربيا لعلكم تعقلون

translation: We narrate to you the best of stories in what We have revealed to you of this Qur'an, though you were, before it, among those who were unaware.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin and superiority of the stories within the Qur'an, which are presented as the best and most exemplary narratives. It also acknowledges the Prophet Muhammad's state of unawareness before the revelation, highlighting the transformative power of the Qur'an in enlightening and guiding him, and by extension, all believers.
orig: نحن نقص عليك أحسن القصص بما أوحينا إليك هذا القرآن وإن كنت من قبله لمن الغافلين

translation: When Joseph said to his father, 'O my father, indeed I saw [in a dream] eleven stars, and the sun and the moon; I saw them prostrating to me.'
interpretation: This verse recounts a dream that Prophet Joseph had, symbolizing his future greatness and authority. The eleven stars represent his brothers, while the sun and moon symbolize his parents. The act of prostration in the dream signifies that they will eventually recognize and submit to his leadership and prophetic status, as ordained by God.
orig: إذ قال يوسف لأبيه يا أبت إني رأيت أحد عشر كوكبا والشمس والقمر رأيتهم لي ساجدين

translation: He said, 'O my son, do not relate your vision to your brothers lest they plot against you a plot. Indeed, Satan is to man a clear enemy.'
interpretation: This verse advises caution in sharing personal revelations or dreams with others, as it may provoke jealousy or harmful actions from them. It highlights the ever-present danger of Satan's influence, which can turn people against one another, emphasizing the need for discretion and awareness of human vulnerabilities to envy and deceit.
orig: قال يا بني لا تقصص رؤياك على إخوتك فيكيدوا لك كيدا إن الشيطان للإنسان عدو مبين

translation: And thus will your Lord choose you and teach you the interpretation of narratives and complete His favor upon you and upon the family of Jacob, as He completed it upon your fathers before - Abraham and Isaac. Indeed, your Lord is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine selection and guidance bestowed upon Prophet Muhammad, similar to the blessings given to previous prophets like Jacob, Abraham, and Isaac. It emphasizes that Allah's favor is not limited to one prophet but is a continuous thread through the lineage of chosen messengers, demonstrating His knowledge and wisdom in guiding humanity through different eras.
orig: وكذلك يجتبيك ربك ويعلمك من تأويل الأحاديث ويتم نعمته عليك وعلى آل يعقوب كما أتمها على أبويك من قبل إبراهيم وإسحاق إن ربك عليم حكيم

translation: Indeed, in Joseph and his brothers there were signs for those who ask.
interpretation: This verse highlights that the story of Joseph and his brothers contains profound lessons and signs that serve as guidance and answers for those who seek understanding and wisdom from the Quran. It emphasizes the importance of reflecting on the narratives within the Quran to gain insights into life's challenges and moral teachings.
orig: لقد كان في يوسف وإخوته آيات للسائلين

translation: When they said, 'Joseph and his brother are more beloved to our father than us, while we are a group. Indeed, our father is in clear error.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the jealousy and resentment felt by Joseph's brothers towards him and his younger brother Benjamin. They perceive their father Jacob's preferential treatment of Joseph and Benjamin as an injustice, leading them to wrongly conclude that their father is misguided. This highlights the theme of envy leading to false judgments and moral errors, illustrating how personal biases can cloud one's perception of truth and fairness.
orig: إذ قالوا ليوسف وأخوه أحب إلى أبينا منا ونحن عصبة إن أبانا لفي ضلال مبين

translation: Kill Yusuf or cast him out to some land, so that your father's attention will be focused on you alone, and after that you will be a righteous people.
interpretation: This verse reflects the jealousy and moral corruption of Yusuf's brothers, who plot to eliminate him in order to gain their father's undivided attention. Their suggestion to kill him or abandon him shows their willingness to commit grave sins for personal gain. The phrase 'you will be a righteous people' is ironic, as it highlights their self-deception and false justification of their evil actions, believing that removing Yusuf would somehow make them virtuous.
orig: اقتلوا يوسف أو اطرحوه أرضا يخل لكم وجه أبيكم وتكونوا من بعده قوما صالحين

translation: A speaker from among them said: Do not kill Yusuf, but throw him into the bottom of the well; some caravan will pick him up, if you will do (this).
interpretation: This verse highlights the cunning and deceitful nature of Yusuf's brothers, who were plotting against him. The suggestion to throw Yusuf into a well instead of killing him directly shows their attempt to mitigate their guilt while still achieving their goal of removing him from their lives. It also reflects a moment of hesitation or moral conflict among them, as one brother proposes a less violent solution, yet still harmful, indicating the complexity of human morality and the lengths to which jealousy can drive people.
orig: قال قائل منهم لا تقتلوا يوسف وألقوه في غيابت الجب يلتقطه بعض السيارة إن كنتم فاعلين

translation: They said, 'O our father, why do you not trust us with Joseph while indeed we are to him sincere advisers?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the brothers' attempt to manipulate their father, Jacob, by questioning his trust in them regarding Joseph. It reflects their insincere intentions masked under the guise of concern and advice, showcasing a theme of deceit and family dynamics in the story of Joseph.
orig: قالوا يا أبانا ما لك لا تأمنا على يوسف وإنا له لناصحون

translation: Send him with us tomorrow so he may enjoy himself and play, and indeed, we will be his guardians.
interpretation: This verse highlights the request made by Yusuf's brothers to their father, Ya'qub, to allow Yusuf to accompany them. It reflects themes of deception and the false sense of security they promised, as they intended harm rather than guardianship. It underscores the importance of trust and the potential for betrayal within familial relationships.
orig: أرسله معنا غدا يرتع ويلعب وإنا له لحافظون

translation: He said: Indeed, it grieves me that you should take him away, and I fear that the wolf may eat him while you are heedless of him.
interpretation: This verse reflects the deep concern and protective nature of a parent, specifically Jacob's worry about his son Benjamin. It underscores the theme of trust in divine protection versus human fears and the challenges of balancing faith with natural parental instincts. Jacob's fear of losing another son to a wolf illustrates his emotional turmoil and the human tendency to worry despite faith in God's plan.
orig: قال إني ليحزنني أن تذهبوا به وأخاف أن يأكله الذئب وأنتم عنه غافلون

translation: They said: 'If the wolf should eat him while we are a group, then indeed, we would be losers.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the brothers' false sense of security and their underestimation of the potential dangers to Yusuf (Joseph). They believed that their presence as a group would be sufficient to protect him, highlighting their negligence and lack of genuine care for his safety. This statement also underscores their attempt to rationalize their actions and shift blame, illustrating human tendencies towards denial and self-justification when faced with moral failings.
orig: قالوا لئن أكله الذئب ونحن عصبة إنا إذا لخاسرون

translation: So when they took him away and agreed to throw him into the bottom of the well, We revealed to him: 'You will surely inform them of this affair of theirs while they are unaware.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine intervention and foreknowledge bestowed upon Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) by Allah. Even as he was being betrayed and cast into the well by his brothers, Allah communicated to him that he would eventually reveal their actions to them, unbeknownst to them at the time. This underscores the theme of divine providence and the ultimate triumph of truth, showing that Allah's plan for Yusuf included his eventual rise to a position where he could confront his brothers about their deed, demonstrating the power of patience and faith in Allah's wisdom.
orig: فلما ذهبوا به وأجمعوا أن يجعلوه في غيابت الجب وأوحينا إليه لتنبئنهم بأمرهم هذا وهم لا يشعرون

translation: And they came to their father in the evening, weeping
interpretation: This verse illustrates the emotional state of Prophet Ya'qub's sons as they return to him after their deceitful act against Yusuf. Their weeping is a manifestation of their guilt and fear of being discovered, highlighting the psychological impact of their actions. It underscores the theme of the consequences of sin and deception, showing how wrongdoing can lead to inner turmoil and distress.
orig: وجاءوا أباهم عشاء يبكون

translation: They said: 'O our father! We went racing and left Yusuf with our belongings, and a wolf devoured him. But you will not believe us even if we were telling the truth.'
interpretation: This verse reveals the deception of Yusuf's brothers as they attempt to convince their father, Ya'qub, of Yusuf's death by a wolf. Their statement reflects a lack of trust from Ya'qub towards them, hinting at previous dishonest behaviors. The brothers' manipulation of the truth underscores themes of jealousy, betrayal, and the consequences of deceit within family dynamics.
orig: قالوا يا أبانا إنا ذهبنا نستبق وتركنا يوسف عند متاعنا فأكله الذئب وما أنت بمؤمن لنا ولو كنا صادقين

translation: And they came with false blood on his shirt. He said, 'Rather, your souls have enticed you to do something. So patience is most fitting. And Allah is the one sought for help against that which you describe.'
interpretation: In this verse, Prophet Ya'qub (Jacob) demonstrates his unwavering faith and patience when faced with the deception of his sons. Despite the false evidence of blood on Yusuf's (Joseph's) shirt, Ya'qub immediately senses the deceit and attributes it to the evil inclinations of his sons' souls. His response, 'So patience is most fitting,' reflects his acceptance of the trial as a test from Allah and his commitment to enduring it with dignity and trust in divine wisdom. By saying, 'And Allah is the one sought for help against that which you describe,' Ya'qub acknowledges that only Allah can provide true assistance and relief from the falsehood and accusations leveled against him and his beloved son. This verse underscores the themes of patience, trust in Allah, and the recognition of human weaknesses and deceit.
orig: وجاءوا على قميصه بدم كذب قال بل سولت لكم أنفسكم أمرا فصبر جميل والله المستعان على ما تصفون

translation: And [it so happened that] a caravan came, and they sent their water-drawer, and he let down his bucket. He said, 'Good news! Here is a boy.' And they concealed him as merchandise, and Allah is Knowing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the moment when Yusuf (Joseph) was discovered by a caravan after being thrown into the well by his brothers. The water-drawer's exclamation of 'Good news!' upon finding Yusuf signifies the unexpected turn of events that led to Yusuf's journey to Egypt. The phrase 'they concealed him as merchandise' reflects the moral and ethical decline of those who treated a human being as a commodity, highlighting the theme of divine justice and knowledge, as Allah is fully aware of their actions and intentions.
orig: وجاءت سيارة فأرسلوا واردهم فأدلى دلوه قال يا بشرى هذا غلام وأسروه بضاعة والله عليم بما يعملون

translation: And they sold him for a low price - a few dirhams - and they were, concerning him, of those content with little.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) when his brothers sold him into slavery for a meager sum. The phrase 'of those content with little' indicates that his brothers were willing to settle for a small amount, reflecting their lack of value for Yusuf and their hasty decision to get rid of him. This highlights themes of betrayal, the underestimation of true worth, and the consequences of short-sighted actions.
orig: وشروه بثمن بخس دراهم معدودة وكانوا فيه من الزاهدين

translation: And the one who bought him from Egypt said to his wife, 'Make his stay honorable; perhaps he will benefit us or we will adopt him as a son.' And thus We established Joseph in the land, and to teach him the interpretation of events. And Allah is predominant over His affair, but most of the people do not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine plan and providence in the life of Prophet Joseph. Despite being sold into slavery, Allah had a greater purpose for him, as demonstrated by the Egyptian's intention to honor him, which unknowingly aligns with Allah's plan to elevate Joseph's status and grant him wisdom in interpreting dreams. The verse underscores the theme that Allah's will prevails, often in ways that are not immediately apparent to most people, illustrating the importance of faith and patience in understanding and accepting divine decrees.
orig: وقال الذي اشتراه من مصر لامرأته أكرمي مثواه عسى أن ينفعنا أو نتخذه ولدا وكذلك مكنا ليوسف في الأرض ولنعلمه من تأويل الأحاديث والله غالب على أمره ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: And when he reached his full strength, We gave him wisdom and knowledge. And thus do We reward the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine reward of wisdom and knowledge bestowed upon Prophet Joseph when he reached maturity. It underscores the Islamic principle that those who are patient and righteous will be granted blessings and guidance from Allah, reflecting the broader theme of divine justice and the rewarding of good deeds.
orig: ولما بلغ أشده آتيناه حكما وعلما وكذلك نجزي المحسنين

translation: And she, in whose house he was, sought to seduce him from himself; she closed the doors and said: "Come, you." He said: "I seek refuge with Allah! Indeed, He is my Lord, who has made my stay [here] excellent. Indeed, wrongdoers will not succeed."
interpretation: This verse highlights the story of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) and the wife of the Aziz of Egypt, illustrating a test of moral integrity and faith. When faced with temptation, Yusuf's immediate response is to seek refuge in Allah, acknowledging God's blessings upon him and affirming his belief that those who engage in wrongdoing will not ultimately succeed. This response underscores the importance of maintaining one's moral and spiritual values even in the face of significant temptation, emphasizing reliance on divine guidance and the conviction that righteousness leads to true success.
orig: وراودته التي هو في بيتها عن نفسه وغلقت الأبواب وقالت هيت لك قال معاذ الله إنه ربي أحسن مثواي إنه لا يفلح الظالمون

translation: And indeed he had almost led him astray. And had We not caused him to see the proof of his Lord, he would have surely succumbed to it. And thus We turn away from him evil and immorality. Indeed, he was among Our chosen servants.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine intervention that protected Prophet Ibrahim from falling into temptation and sin. It underscores the concept of God's guidance and protection over His sincere servants, showing that divine support can prevent believers from moral corruption. The 'proof' or evidence from God serves as a critical moment of clarity and strength, enabling the believer to resist temptation and remain steadfast in faith.
orig: ولقد همت به وهم بها لولا أن رأى برهان ربه كذلك لنصرف عنه السوء والفحشاء إنه من عبادنا المخلصين

translation: And they raced to the door, and she tore his shirt from behind, and they found her master at the door. She said, 'What is the recompense of one who intended evil to your family except imprisonment or a painful punishment?'
interpretation: This verse illustrates a critical moment in the story of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) where Zuleikha falsely accuses him of attempting to seduce her, as they rush towards the door and her husband finds them. Her immediate accusation and demand for severe punishment reflect the societal norms and the power dynamics at play, highlighting themes of false accusation, the vulnerability of the innocent, and the potential for justice to be miscarried based on deceit and power. It underscores the challenges faced by Yusuf due to his integrity and righteousness in a corrupt environment.
orig: واستبقا الباب وقدت قميصه من دبر وألفيا سيدها لدى الباب قالت ما جزاء من أراد بأهلك سوءا إلا أن يسجن أو عذاب أليم

translation: He said, 'She sought to seduce me.' And a witness from her family testified, 'If his shirt is torn from the front, then she has told the truth, and he is of the liars.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of truth and falsehood, and the importance of evidence in resolving disputes. It illustrates how Yusuf (Joseph) was falsely accused by the wife of the Aziz, and how the evidence of his torn shirt from the back would later exonerate him, demonstrating that the truth will eventually come to light despite initial appearances and accusations.
orig: قال هي راودتني عن نفسي وشهد شاهد من أهلها إن كان قميصه قد من قبل فصدقت وهو من الكاذبين

translation: And if his shirt is torn from behind, then she has lied, and he is of the truthful ones.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of evidence in resolving disputes. It suggests that physical evidence, like the condition of Joseph's shirt, can serve as a means to uncover the truth and vindicate the innocent. The verse underscores the theme of justice and the divine support for those who are truthful.
orig: وإن كان قميصه قد من دبر فكذبت وهو من الصادقين

translation: So when he saw his shirt torn from behind, he said: "This is of your guile, your guile is great."
interpretation: This verse highlights the moment when Yusuf's master recognizes the falsehood of the accusations against Yusuf due to the physical evidence of the torn shirt. It underscores the theme of deceit and the power of truth to eventually surface, illustrating how cunning and manipulation, though potent, are ultimately exposed. The master's acknowledgment of the women's 'guile' reflects a broader commentary on the moral and ethical challenges faced by individuals, emphasizing the need for discernment and justice in societal interactions.
orig: فلما رأى قميصه قد من دبر قال إنه من كيدكن إن كيدكن عظيم

translation: O Yusuf, turn away from this. And ask forgiveness for your sin; indeed, you were of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse addresses Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) and advises him to avoid the temptation presented by Zuleikha, the wife of the Egyptian minister. It emphasizes the importance of turning away from sinful actions and seeking forgiveness from Allah, acknowledging human fallibility and the need for repentance. The verse underscores the moral strength required to resist temptation and maintain righteousness, even when faced with significant personal challenges.
orig: يوسف أعرض عن هذا واستغفري لذنبك إنك كنت من الخاطئين

translation: And women in the city said, "The wife of Al-'Aziz is seeking to seduce her slave boy; he has impassioned her with love. Indeed, we see her [to be] in clear error."
interpretation: This verse highlights the societal gossip and judgment that can arise from personal matters. It reflects how the community perceived Zulaikha's actions towards Yusuf as morally wrong, indicating a broader theme of how public opinion can often misjudge or oversimplify complex personal situations. It serves as a reminder of the need for compassion and understanding rather than hasty judgments based on rumors.
orig: وقال نسوة في المدينة امرأت العزيز تراود فتاها عن نفسه قد شغفها حبا إنا لنراها في ضلال مبين

translation: So when she heard of their scheming, she sent for them and prepared for them a banquet, and she gave each one of them a knife and said [to Joseph], 'Come out to them.' And when they saw him, they greatly admired him and cut their hands and said, 'Perfect is Allah! This is not a man; this is none but a noble angel.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of human weakness and the overpowering nature of beauty and virtue, as embodied by Prophet Joseph. The women, upon seeing Joseph, were so struck by his beauty that they inadvertently cut their hands, mistaking him for an angel. This reaction underscores the moral and spiritual test that beauty can pose, challenging one's self-control and perception. It also serves as a testament to Joseph's exceptional character and divine favor, illustrating how his presence could evoke a recognition of the divine in human form.
orig: فلما سمعت بمكرهن أرسلت إليهن وأعتدت لهن متكأ وآتت كل واحدة منهن سكينا وقالت اخرج عليهن فلما رأينه أكبرنه وقطعن أيديهن وقلن حاش لله ما هذا بشرا إن هذا إلا ملك كريم

translation: She said, 'That is the one about whom you blamed me. And I certainly sought to seduce him, but he firmly refused; and if he does not do what I order him, he will surely be imprisoned and will be of those debased.'
interpretation: In this verse, Zulaikha, the wife of Al-Aziz, confesses her attempt to seduce Prophet Yusuf (Joseph). Her statement reveals her persistence in her wrongful desire despite Yusuf's steadfast refusal. It highlights the moral strength and integrity of Yusuf, who chose imprisonment over compromising his values. The verse also underscores the theme of resisting temptation and the consequences of failing to uphold one's principles, as Zulaikha threatens Yusuf with imprisonment and disgrace if he does not comply with her demands.
orig: قالت فذلكن الذي لمتنني فيه ولقد راودته عن نفسه فاستعصم ولئن لم يفعل ما آمره ليسجنن وليكونا من الصاغرين

translation: He said, 'My Lord, prison is more beloved to me than what they invite me to. And if You do not turn away their plan from me, I might incline towards them and become of the ignorant.'
interpretation: In this verse, Yusuf (Joseph) demonstrates his strong faith and moral integrity by choosing imprisonment over succumbing to the temptations presented by the women who were trying to seduce him. He acknowledges his human vulnerability and seeks Allah's protection to maintain his righteousness, showing that even prophets need divine assistance to resist sin. This highlights the importance of relying on Allah's guidance and strength to overcome personal trials and maintain one's moral compass.
orig: قال رب السجن أحب إلي مما يدعونني إليه وإلا تصرف عني كيدهن أصب إليهن وأكن من الجاهلين

translation: So his Lord responded to him and averted their plan from him. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the power and responsiveness of Allah to the prayers of His servants. When Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) sought refuge in Allah from the deceit of the women, Allah answered his prayer by turning away their plot. This demonstrates that Allah hears all supplications and is fully aware of every situation, emphasizing His attributes of being All-Hearing (As-Samee') and All-Knowing (Al-Aleem). It reassures believers that Allah's knowledge and intervention can protect them from harm and deceit.
orig: فاستجاب له ربه فصرف عنه كيدهن إنه هو السميع العليم

translation: Then it appeared to them, after they had seen the proofs, to imprison him until a time.
interpretation: This verse reflects the moment when, despite witnessing clear signs and evidence of Yusuf's innocence and righteousness, the people around him still chose to imprison him. It underscores the theme of human denial and injustice, even in the face of undeniable truth. The decision to imprison Yusuf 'until a time' indicates a temporary measure, suggesting that divine wisdom often allows for trials and tribulations as part of a larger plan, which ultimately leads to Yusuf's vindication and rise to power.
orig: ثم بدا لهم من بعد ما رأوا الآيات ليسجننه حتى حين

translation: And with him entered the prison two young men. One of them said, 'Indeed, I see myself [in a dream] pressing wine.' The other said, 'Indeed, I see myself carrying upon my head [some] bread, from which the birds were eating. Inform us of its interpretation; indeed, we see you as one of the righteous.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of divine knowledge and interpretation. The two young men, who were imprisoned with Yusuf (Joseph), recognized his righteousness and sought his help in interpreting their dreams. This reflects the belief that righteous individuals are often endowed with wisdom and insight from God, which can guide others in understanding divine messages and navigating their life's challenges.
orig: ودخل معه السجن فتيان قال أحدهما إني أراني أعصر خمرا وقال الآخر إني أراني أحمل فوق رأسي خبزا تأكل الطير منه نبئنا بتأويله إنا نراك من المحسنين

translation: He said, 'You will not receive any food with which you are provided but that I will inform you of its interpretation before it comes to you. That is from what my Lord has taught me. Indeed, I have left the religion of a people who do not believe in Allah, and they, in the Hereafter, are disbelievers.'
interpretation: In this verse, Yusuf (Joseph) is expressing his God-given ability to interpret dreams and visions, which extends to foretelling the nature of the food they will receive. This showcases his prophetic gift and reliance on divine knowledge. Additionally, Yusuf distances himself from the disbelief of his people, emphasizing his monotheistic faith and belief in the afterlife, which contrasts with their rejection of these truths.
orig: قال لا يأتيكما طعام ترزقانه إلا نبأتكما بتأويله قبل أن يأتيكما ذلكما مما علمني ربي إني تركت ملة قوم لا يؤمنون بالله وهم بالآخرة هم كافرون

translation: And I have followed the religion of my fathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. It was never for us to associate anything with Allah. That is from the grace of Allah to us and to the people, but most of the people do not give thanks.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the steadfastness in monotheism of the prophets Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and their descendants, including the speaker, who is traditionally understood to be Joseph. It highlights that associating partners with Allah (shirk) is strictly prohibited and contrary to the pure monotheism they upheld.
