The verse also acknowledges that maintaining this purity of faith is a blessing and favor from Allah, not only to these prophets and their lineage but to all of humanity. However, it laments that most people fail to recognize and appreciate this divine favor, indicating a widespread ingratitude among mankind.
orig: واتبعت ملة آبائي إبراهيم وإسحاق ويعقوب ما كان لنا أن نشرك بالله من شيء ذلك من فضل الله علينا وعلى الناس ولكن أكثر الناس لا يشكرون

translation: O my fellow prisoners, are separate lords better or Allah, the One, the Subduer?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of monotheism, highlighting the superiority and uniqueness of Allah over multiple deities. It invites reflection on the logical fallacy of polytheism by contrasting it with the belief in one all-powerful God, who is described as 'the One, the Subduer,' indicating His absolute sovereignty and overwhelming power over all creation.
orig: يا صاحبي السجن أأرباب متفرقون خير أم الله الواحد القهار

translation: What you worship besides Him are nothing but names which you have named, you and your fathers, for which Allah has sent down no authority. The command is for none but Allah. He has commanded that you worship none but Him. That is the right religion, but most men know not.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of Tawhid, the oneness of God, by asserting that all other deities or objects of worship are merely human constructs without divine sanction. It critiques idolatry and polytheism as baseless, originating from human and ancestral naming without any revelation from Allah. The verse reaffirms that true authority and command belong solely to Allah, who has ordained the worship of Him alone as the correct and upright religion. However, it acknowledges that despite this clear directive, the majority of people remain ignorant of this truth, highlighting a widespread human failing to recognize and adhere to the monotheistic principle.
orig: ما تعبدون من دونه إلا أسماء سميتموها أنتم وآباؤكم ما أنزل الله بها من سلطان إن الحكم إلا لله أمر ألا تعبدوا إلا إياه ذلك الدين القيم ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: O my two companions of the prison, one of you will serve his lord wine, while the other will be crucified, and the birds will eat from his head. The matter has been decreed about which you both inquire.
interpretation: This verse from the story of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) illustrates the divine knowledge and prophetic ability bestowed upon him by Allah. Yusuf interprets the dreams of his fellow prisoners, predicting their futures with certainty. The interpretation underscores the theme of predestination and the power of divine decree, showing that Allah's will is inevitable and that Yusuf's role as a prophet is to convey this truth. The contrasting fates of the two prisoners serve as a reminder of the diverse outcomes in life, all of which are under Allah's control.
orig: يا صاحبي السجن أما أحدكما فيسقي ربه خمرا وأما الآخر فيصلب فتأكل الطير من رأسه قضي الأمر الذي فيه تستفتيان

translation: And he said to the one whom he knew would be saved of the two, "Mention me before your lord." But Satan made him forget the mention of his Lord, and he remained in prison several years.
interpretation: This verse highlights the influence of Satan in causing forgetfulness and delay in fulfilling one's obligations. It teaches that even a righteous person like Yusuf (Joseph) can be affected by Satan's whispers, leading to prolonged hardship. The verse underscores the importance of relying on Allah and being vigilant against Satan's attempts to distract us from our duties and remembrance of Allah.
orig: وقال للذي ظن أنه ناج منهما اذكرني عند ربك فأنساه الشيطان ذكر ربه فلبث في السجن بضع سنين

translation: And the king said, 'Indeed, I see [in a dream] seven fat cows being eaten by seven lean ones, and seven green spikes [of grain] and others [that were] dry. O eminent ones, explain to me my vision, if you should be able to interpret visions.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of divine knowledge and human reliance on it for understanding complex matters. The king's dream about the cows and spikes symbolizes periods of prosperity and hardship, respectively. By seeking interpretation from his advisors, the king acknowledges the limitations of human understanding and the necessity of divine guidance, which ultimately leads to the involvement of Prophet Yusuf, who interprets the dream correctly through divine inspiration. This narrative underscores the Qur'anic principle that true wisdom and insight come from Allah, and humans must seek His guidance to navigate life's challenges.
orig: وقال الملك إني أرى سبع بقرات سمان يأكلهن سبع عجاف وسبع سنبلات خضر وأخر يابسات يا أيها الملأ أفتوني في رؤياي إن كنتم للرؤيا تعبرون

translation: They said, 'These are confused dreams, and we are not skilled in the interpretation of dreams.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the disbelief and dismissal by Yusuf's brothers of his dream, indicating their lack of understanding and their attempt to belittle the significance of his visions, which were actually prophetic.
orig: قالوا أضغاث أحلام وما نحن بتأويل الأحلام بعالمين

translation: And he who was saved from them both said, after some time had passed, 'I will inform you of its interpretation, so send me forth.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of patience and the eventual revelation of truth. The one who was saved, Yusuf (Joseph), waited until the appropriate time to reveal the interpretation of the king's dream, demonstrating wisdom and strategic timing. It underscores the theme that divine knowledge and guidance will be disclosed at the right moment, encouraging believers to trust in God's timing and to use their knowledge for the greater good.
orig: وقال الذي نجا منهما وادكر بعد أمة أنا أنبئكم بتأويله فأرسلون

translation: Joseph, O truthful one, explain to us about seven fat cows that seven lean ones eat, and seven green ears of corn and others dry, that I may return to the people, perhaps they may know.
interpretation: This verse is a plea from the king's messenger to Prophet Joseph to interpret a dream that the king had. The dream symbolizes a period of abundance followed by a period of scarcity. The seven fat cows represent seven years of prosperity, while the seven lean cows signify seven years of drought and famine that will follow. Similarly, the seven green ears of corn indicate years of plenty, and the dry ears represent years of hardship. The request to interpret this dream reflects a broader theme in the Qur'an about divine knowledge and guidance being sought through prophets, emphasizing the importance of understanding and preparing for future events as ordained by God. The ultimate goal is to share this knowledge with the people so they can prepare and learn from it.
orig: يوسف أيها الصديق أفتنا في سبع بقرات سمان يأكلهن سبع عجاف وسبع سنبلات خضر وأخر يابسات لعلي أرجع إلى الناس لعلهم يعلمون

translation: He said: 'You will cultivate for seven years consecutively, except for a little of what you harvest, leave it in its ear.'
interpretation: This verse refers to the dream interpretation given by Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) to the King of Egypt. The instruction to cultivate for seven years and leave most of the harvest in its ear symbolizes a period of abundance and the need to store surplus grain for future use, reflecting the importance of planning and foresight in times of plenty to prepare for potential scarcity.
orig: قال تزرعون سبع سنين دأبا فما حصدتم فذروه في سنبله إلا قليلا مما تأكلون

translation: Then will come after that seven severe (years) which will eat what you have advanced for them, except a little of what you have preserved.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) and his interpretation of the dream of the King of Egypt. The seven severe years symbolize a period of drought and famine that will follow the seven years of abundance. During this time, the resources stored during the plentiful years will be consumed, with only a small portion remaining for those who have taken measures to protect their provisions. The verse highlights the importance of planning and preparation for future hardships, as well as the inevitability of divine decree in the cycles of abundance and scarcity.
orig: ثم يأتي من بعد ذلك سبع شداد يأكلن ما قدمتم لهن إلا قليلا مما تحصنون

translation: Then comes a year in which people are given abundant rain, and in it they press [olives and grapes].
interpretation: This verse highlights the cycle of divine providence, illustrating how after periods of hardship or scarcity, Allah provides relief and abundance. The mention of rain and the pressing of olives and grapes symbolizes not only physical sustenance but also the renewal of life and prosperity. It serves as a reminder of Allah's mercy and the importance of patience and gratitude during times of both scarcity and abundance.
orig: ثم يأتي من بعد ذلك عام فيه يغاث الناس وفيه يعصرون

translation: And the king said, 'Bring him to me.' But when the messenger came to him, [Joseph] said, 'Go back to your lord and ask him what is the case of the women who cut their hands. Indeed, my Lord is Knowing of their cunning plan.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of divine knowledge and justice. Joseph, despite being summoned by the king, requests that the king first investigate the incident involving the women who cut their hands. This action demonstrates Joseph's trust in God's omniscience and his belief that the truth will be revealed through divine intervention. It underscores the idea that God is fully aware of the deceitful plans of individuals and that justice will ultimately prevail through His wisdom.
orig: وقال الملك ائتوني به فلما جاءه الرسول قال ارجع إلى ربك فاسأله ما بال النسوة اللاتي قطعن أيديهن إن ربي بكيدهن عليم

translation: He said, 'What was your condition when you sought to seduce Joseph away from himself?' They said, 'God forbid! We know no evil of him.' The wife of al-'Aziz said, 'Now the truth has come to light. It was I who sought to seduce him, and indeed, he is of the truthful.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of truth and falsehood. When confronted by the truth, the wife of al-'Aziz admits her attempt to seduce Joseph, acknowledging his integrity and truthfulness. It underscores the importance of honesty and the eventual revelation of truth, even when initially concealed by lies or denial.
orig: قال ما خطبكن إذ راودتن يوسف عن نفسه قلن حاش لله ما علمنا عليه من سوء قالت امرأت العزيز الآن حصحص الحق أنا راودته عن نفسه وإنه لمن الصادقين

translation: That was so that he would know that I did not betray him in his absence, and that Allah does not guide the plot of the betrayers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of trust and integrity in relationships, emphasizing that Allah is aware of all actions, even those done in secret. It serves as a reminder that deceitful actions, particularly betrayal, will not be supported or guided by Allah, reinforcing the moral accountability of individuals.
orig: ذلك ليعلم أني لم أخنه بالغيب وأن الله لا يهدي كيد الخائنين

translation: And I do not acquit myself. Indeed, the soul is a persistent enjoiner of evil, except those upon which my Lord has mercy. Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse reflects the humility and self-awareness of the Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) when he acknowledges that even he, a prophet, is not free from the influence of the self's inclination towards evil. It underscores the universal human struggle against one's own desires and the necessity of divine mercy and guidance to overcome these inclinations. The verse emphasizes the importance of seeking God's forgiveness and mercy, as it is through His compassion that one can hope to prevail over the soul's evil promptings.
orig: وما أبرئ نفسي إن النفس لأمارة بالسوء إلا ما رحم ربي إن ربي غفور رحيم

translation: And the king said, 'Bring him to me; I will attach him to my service.' Then when he spoke to him, he said, 'Indeed, you are today, with us, [someone] established and trusted.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the transformation of Prophet Yusuf from a prisoner to a high-ranking official due to his integrity and wisdom. It underscores the theme of divine providence and how patience and faith can lead to unexpected elevations in status. The king's recognition of Yusuf as 'established and trusted' reflects the fulfillment of Yusuf's dream and God's plan for him, emphasizing that true honor and trust come from righteousness and divine favor.
orig: وقال الملك ائتوني به أستخلصه لنفسي فلما كلمه قال إنك اليوم لدينا مكين أمين

translation: He said, 'Appoint me over the treasuries of the land; indeed, I am a knowledgeable guardian.'
interpretation: In this verse, the speaker, often identified as Qarun in Islamic tradition, is requesting to be put in charge of the earth's treasures. He claims to possess the qualities of being both knowledgeable and trustworthy, suggesting that he believes himself capable of managing such responsibilities effectively. This verse highlights themes of ambition, self-perception, and the dangers of arrogance, as Qarun's request is later shown to be motivated by greed and a desire for power, leading to his downfall.
orig: قال اجعلني على خزائن الأرض إني حفيظ عليم

translation: And thus We established Joseph in the land, to settle therein wherever he willed. We bestow Our mercy on whom We will, and We do not let the reward of the righteous be lost.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine favor and authority bestowed upon Prophet Joseph, illustrating how God granted him power and influence in Egypt. It underscores the theme of divine providence and mercy, showing that God's blessings and rewards are bestowed according to His will, particularly on those who are righteous and do good deeds. The verse reassures believers that their good actions will not go unrewarded by God, emphasizing the importance of faith and moral conduct.
orig: وكذلك مكنا ليوسف في الأرض يتبوأ منها حيث يشاء نصيب برحمتنا من نشاء ولا نضيع أجر المحسنين

translation: And the reward of the Hereafter is better for those who have believed and used to fear Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the superiority of the rewards in the afterlife for those who have faith and maintain a state of piety. It encourages believers to prioritize their actions and intentions towards earning the eternal rewards of the Hereafter, rather than being solely focused on the temporary gains of this world. The verse underscores the importance of faith and righteousness as the keys to achieving a better outcome in the afterlife.
orig: ولأجر الآخرة خير للذين آمنوا وكانوا يتقون

translation: And the brothers of Yusuf came and they entered upon him; he recognized them, but they did not recognize him.
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of recognition and concealment in the story of Yusuf. Yusuf, now in a position of power in Egypt, recognizes his brothers who sold him into slavery, but they do not recognize him. This moment underscores the divine plan and Yusuf's journey from betrayal to a position where he can test his brothers' repentance and moral growth, illustrating the Qur'anic teaching on patience, forgiveness, and the unfolding of God's wisdom in human affairs.
orig: وجاء إخوة يوسف فدخلوا عليه فعرفهم وهم له منكرون

translation: And when he had furnished them with their provisions, he said: 'Bring me a brother of yours from your father. Do you not see that I give full measure and that I am the best of hosts?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the strategic cunning of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) as he sets the stage for the eventual reunion with his younger brother, Benjamin. By requesting them to bring their brother, Yusuf is subtly testing the integrity and truthfulness of his brothers, who had previously betrayed him. Additionally, this request serves as a means to further assess their character and to see if they have changed since their past actions. Yusuf's mention of his generosity and hospitality underscores his position of power and authority in Egypt, yet it also reflects his underlying kindness and fairness, which are hallmarks of his prophetic character.
orig: ولما جهزهم بجهازهم قال ائتوني بأخ لكم من أبيكم ألا ترون أني أوفي الكيل وأنا خير المنزلين

translation: If you do not bring it to me, then there will be no measure for you from me, and do not come near.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fulfilling obligations and responsibilities. It indicates that if someone fails to deliver what is promised or expected, they will not receive their due share or benefit. Additionally, it serves as a warning to maintain distance if duties are not met, highlighting the consequences of negligence and the importance of trust and reliability in transactions and relationships.
orig: فإن لم تأتوني به فلا كيل لكم عندي ولا تقربون

translation: They said, "We will try to get his father to agree, and we will surely do it."
interpretation: This verse reflects the determination and deceitful planning of Yusuf's brothers to manipulate their father, Yaqub, into allowing them to take Yusuf away from him. It highlights their intention to execute their plan, showcasing their resolve to achieve their goal despite the moral implications of their actions.
orig: قالوا سنراود عنه أباه وإنا لفاعلون

translation: And he said to his young men, "Place their merchandise in their saddlebags, so that they may recognize it when they return to their people, and perhaps they will come back."
interpretation: This verse highlights the strategic kindness of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) towards his brothers. By secretly returning their merchandise, Yusuf not only ensures their safe return home but also plants a seed of curiosity and gratitude that might encourage them to return. This act reflects themes of forgiveness, strategic planning, and the hope of reconciliation, illustrating how Yusuf uses his position to foster a potential reunion with his family, despite past grievances.
orig: وقال لفتيانه اجعلوا بضاعتهم في رحالهم لعلهم يعرفونها إذا انقلبوا إلى أهلهم لعلهم يرجعون

translation: So when they returned to their father, they said, 'O our father, we have been denied [our] measure, so send with us our brother [that] we will get a measure. And indeed, we will be his guardians.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the brothers' manipulation and deceit towards their father, Jacob. They falsely claim that they were denied their full measure of grain in Egypt, suggesting that sending their younger brother, Benjamin, with them would ensure they receive the full amount. This request is part of their ongoing scheme to separate Joseph from his family, showing their lack of repentance and continued envy. The verse underscores themes of family dynamics, deceit, and the trials faced by prophets and their families.
orig: فلما رجعوا إلى أبيهم قالوا يا أبانا منع منا الكيل فأرسل معنا أخانا نكتل وإنا له لحافظون

translation: He said, 'Do you entrust him to me except as you entrusted his brother to me before? But Allah is the best guardian, and He is the most merciful of the merciful.'
interpretation: In this verse, Yusuf's (Joseph's) brother expresses his concern and doubt about being entrusted with Binyamin (Benjamin), recalling the previous incident with Yusuf himself. This highlights human mistrust and fear of repeating past mistakes. However, the verse reassures that despite human failings, Allah is the ultimate protector and guardian, emphasizing His mercy and compassion as the most merciful of those who show mercy. It teaches believers to trust in Allah's plan and protection over human judgments and fears.
orig: قال هل آمنكم عليه إلا كما أمنتكم على أخيه من قبل فالله خير حافظا وهو أرحم الراحمين

translation: And when they opened their baggage, they found their merchandise returned to them. They said, 'O our father, what more could we desire? This is our merchandise returned to us, and we will get provisions for our family and protect our brother and obtain an increase of a camel's load; this is a small quantity.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of divine providence and the unexpected blessings that can come from God. The brothers of Yusuf, upon discovering their money returned to them, recognize it as a sign of God's favor. They see it as an opportunity not only to provide for their family but also to safeguard their younger brother, Benjamin, and to increase their resources. The verse illustrates how God can turn situations around, providing more than what is hoped for, and encourages believers to trust in divine wisdom and planning, even in seemingly challenging circumstances.
orig: ولما فتحوا متاعهم وجدوا بضاعتهم ردت إليهم قالوا يا أبانا ما نبغي هذه بضاعتنا ردت إلينا ونمير أهلنا ونحفظ أخانا ونزداد كيل بعير ذلك كيل يسير

translation: He said, 'I will not send him with you until you give me a solemn oath by Allah that you will surely bring him back to me, unless you are surrounded [by enemies].' And when they had given him their solemn oath, he said, 'Allah is Witness over what we say.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of trust and divine oversight in human affairs. Ya'qub (Jacob) insists on a solemn oath from his sons before allowing Benjamin to travel with them, indicating the gravity of the promise and his reliance on their integrity. The condition 'unless you are surrounded [by enemies]' shows a realistic understanding of potential dangers but also an expectation of effort to fulfill the oath. The affirmation 'Allah is Witness over what we say' underscores the belief that God is aware of all promises and will hold individuals accountable, emphasizing the sanctity of oaths and the role of divine justice in human interactions.
orig: قال لن أرسله معكم حتى تؤتون موثقا من الله لتأتنني به إلا أن يحاط بكم فلما آتوه موثقهم قال الله على ما نقول وكيل

translation: And he said, 'O my sons, do not enter from one gate but enter from different gates. And I cannot avail you against [the decree of] Allah at all. The decision is only for Allah; upon Him I have relied, and upon Him let those who would rely [indeed] rely.'
interpretation: In this verse, Ya'qub (Jacob) advises his sons to enter the city from different gates as a strategy to avoid potential harm, reflecting a practical approach to dealing with worldly affairs. However, he immediately emphasizes the limits of human planning by stating that no precaution can alter what Allah has decreed. This underscores the Islamic principle of tawakkul (reliance on Allah), where believers are encouraged to take necessary actions but ultimately trust in Allah's will and wisdom. Ya'qub's statement serves as a reminder that while we should make efforts in our lives, our ultimate reliance should be on Allah, acknowledging His sovereignty and the belief that all outcomes are in His hands.
orig: وقال يا بني لا تدخلوا من باب واحد وادخلوا من أبواب متفرقة وما أغني عنكم من الله من شيء إن الحكم إلا لله عليه توكلت وعليه فليتوكل المتوكلون

translation: And when they entered from where their father had commanded them, it availed them nothing against Allah except a need in the soul of Yaqub, which he fulfilled. And indeed, he was a possessor of knowledge because of what We had taught him, but most of the people do not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of divine decree and the limitations of human efforts when they are not aligned with God's will. Despite the sons of Yaqub following their father's instructions meticulously, their actions did not change the outcome predestined by Allah. The 'need in the soul of Yaqub' refers to his intuitive understanding and trust in Allah's plan, which was fulfilled despite apparent setbacks. Yaqub's knowledge, granted by Allah, allowed him to see beyond the immediate events and trust in the divine wisdom, a level of understanding that most people do not possess due to their limited perspective and faith.
orig: ولما دخلوا من حيث أمرهم أبوهم ما كان يغني عنهم من الله من شيء إلا حاجة في نفس يعقوب قضاها وإنه لذو علم لما علمناه ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: And when they entered upon Joseph, he took his brother aside to himself and said, "Indeed, I am your brother, so do not despair over what they used to do."
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of reassurance and familial bonds. When Joseph's brothers came to Egypt, unaware of his true identity, Joseph privately revealed himself to his younger brother Benjamin. This act of disclosure was not only a moment of emotional reunion but also a strategic move to comfort Benjamin, who might have been distressed by the actions of their other brothers. Joseph's words, "so do not despair over what they used to do," serve as a reminder that past wrongs should not overshadow the present and future possibilities of reconciliation and hope. It underscores the Qur'anic message of forgiveness and the importance of maintaining hope and trust in divine providence despite adversity.
orig: ولما دخلوا على يوسف آوى إليه أخاه قال إني أنا أخوك فلا تبتئس بما كانوا يعملون

translation: So when he had furnished them with their provisions, he put the drinking cup in his brother's saddlebag. Then a crier proclaimed: 'O you (in) the caravan, surely you are thieves!'
interpretation: This verse highlights the strategic move by Prophet Yusuf to keep his brother Binyamin in Egypt by placing the king's cup in his bag, thereby setting the stage for the accusation of theft. It reflects the theme of divine planning and wisdom, where seemingly negative events are part of a larger, positive divine scheme to reunite Yusuf with his family. The proclamation of theft by the crier serves as a pivotal moment that tests the integrity and reactions of Yusuf's brothers, furthering the narrative of moral and spiritual growth.
orig: فلما جهزهم بجهازهم جعل السقاية في رحل أخيه ثم أذن مؤذن أيتها العير إنكم لسارقون

translation: They said, and they turned to them, 'What are you seeking?'
interpretation: This verse illustrates a moment of inquiry and engagement between two groups, where one group turns their attention towards the other to ask about their purpose or what they are looking for. It highlights the importance of communication and seeking clarity in interactions, reflecting a theme of openness and directness in addressing others.
orig: قالوا وأقبلوا عليهم ماذا تفقدون

translation: They said: We have lost the king's goblet, and he who brings it shall have a camel-load, and I am responsible for it.
interpretation: This verse reflects the cunning plan of the brothers to frame Benjamin for theft, as they had previously conspired against Joseph. The goblet mentioned is a pretext to search the brothers' belongings, knowing that it would be found in Benjamin's bag, thus giving them a reason to detain him. The promise of a camel-load as a reward is an enticement to encourage others to search diligently, while the statement of responsibility underscores the seriousness of the situation and the authority behind the search.
orig: قالوا نفقد صواع الملك ولمن جاء به حمل بعير وأنا به زعيم

translation: They said, 'By Allah, you have indeed known that we did not come to cause corruption in the land, nor were we thieves.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the defense of the brothers of Yusuf (Joseph) against the accusations made against them. They are swearing by Allah to emphasize the truthfulness of their statement, asserting that their intentions were not to cause harm or to steal. This highlights the theme of false accusations and the importance of defending one's integrity and innocence in the face of wrongful charges.
orig: قالوا تالله لقد علمتم ما جئنا لنفسد في الأرض وما كنا سارقين

translation: They said: "Then what is the recompense for him if you are liars?"
interpretation: This verse reflects the challenge posed by the disbelievers to the Prophet Muhammad, demanding proof of his claims. It highlights their skepticism and the demand for tangible evidence or consequences if the Prophet's message were proven false. This interaction underscores the theme of faith versus doubt, illustrating the disbelievers' reluctance to accept the divine message without empirical proof.
orig: قالوا فما جزاؤه إن كنتم كاذبين

translation: They said, 'The penalty for this is that the one in whose bag it is found, he will be its penalty. Thus do we penalize the wrongdoers.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the brothers of Yusuf (Joseph) unknowingly setting the stage for the fulfillment of Yusuf's dream and God's plan. By agreeing to this penalty, they inadvertently facilitate the separation of Binyamin (Benjamin) from them, which is a crucial step in the larger narrative of Yusuf's story. It underscores the theme of divine justice and how human actions, even when intended to be just or punitive, can serve a greater divine purpose.
orig: قالوا جزاؤه من وجد في رحله فهو جزاؤه كذلك نجزي الظالمين

translation: So he began (the search) with their bags before the bag of his brother; then he brought it out of his brother's bag. Thus did We plan for Joseph. He could not have taken his brother according to the law of the king except that Allah willed. We raise in degrees whom We will, and above every possessor of knowledge is (one more) knowing.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the divine plan and intervention in the life of Prophet Joseph (Yusuf). It shows how Allah orchestrated events so that Joseph's brother Benjamin's bag was searched last, leading to the discovery of the king's cup, which was part of a larger plan to reunite Joseph with his family. The verse emphasizes that what happened was not merely by human design or legal right but was a manifestation of Allah's will. It underscores the concept of divine elevation, where Allah raises the status of whom He wills, and it also highlights the hierarchy of knowledge, suggesting that no matter how knowledgeable someone is, there is always a higher knowledge possessed by Allah.
orig: فبدأ بأوعيتهم قبل وعاء أخيه ثم استخرجها من وعاء أخيه كذلك كدنا ليوسف ما كان ليأخذ أخاه في دين الملك إلا أن يشاء الله نرفع درجات من نشاء وفوق كل ذي علم عليم

translation: They said, 'If he steals - indeed, his brother [Joseph] stole before.' But Joseph kept it within himself and did not reveal it to them. He said, 'You are worse in position, and Allah knows best what you describe.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of false accusations and the importance of patience and restraint in the face of injustice. When Joseph's brothers falsely accuse Benjamin of theft, citing a supposed previous theft by Joseph himself, Joseph chooses not to reveal his true identity or defend himself aggressively. Instead, he internalizes his feelings and responds with a measured statement, indicating that their moral standing is worse than his. This reflects Joseph's trust in God's justice and his ability to maintain dignity and composure under false accusations, teaching believers the value of patience and reliance on divine wisdom over immediate retaliation or self-justification.
orig: قالوا إن يسرق فقد سرق أخ له من قبل فأسرها يوسف في نفسه ولم يبدها لهم قال أنتم شر مكانا والله أعلم بما تصفون

translation: They said, "O Aziz, indeed he has a father, an old man, so take one of us in his place. Indeed, we see you as one of the doers of good."
interpretation: This verse reflects the brothers' plea to the Aziz (governor) of Egypt, highlighting their recognition of his potential for mercy and kindness. They appeal to his sense of justice and compassion by noting the old age and vulnerability of their father, suggesting that taking one of them instead of Benjamin would be a more merciful act. This demonstrates their understanding of the Aziz's character as someone capable of good deeds, and they leverage this perception in hopes of swaying his decision.
orig: قالوا يا أيها العزيز إن له أبا شيخا كبيرا فخذ أحدنا مكانه إنا نراك من المحسنين

translation: Ma'ad said, 'May Allah be far removed from such a thing! We would only take what we found with them of our property. Indeed, we would then be wrongdoers.'
interpretation: In this verse, Ma'ad expresses a strong moral stance against taking anything beyond what rightfully belongs to them, emphasizing the importance of justice and fairness in dealings. He invokes a sense of divine disapproval to highlight the severity of unjust actions, indicating that to take more than what is rightfully theirs would be an act of zulm (oppression or wrongdoing), which is condemned in Islamic ethics.
orig: قال معاذ الله أن نأخذ إلا من وجدنا متاعنا عنده إنا إذا لظالمون

translation: So when they despaired of him, they secluded themselves and privately said, 'The eldest among them said, 'Do you not know that your father has taken from you a solemn oath by Allah, and before this you failed in the matter of Yusuf? So I will not leave this land until my father permits me or Allah decides for me, and He is the best of judges.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of loyalty and obedience to parental authority and divine will. The eldest brother's refusal to leave the land without his father's permission or a divine decree underscores the importance of upholding promises and maintaining integrity, even in challenging situations. It reflects the Islamic values of honoring one's commitments and trusting in Allah's judgment as the ultimate arbiter of justice.
orig: فلما استيأسوا منه خلصوا نجيا قال كبيرهم ألم تعلموا أن أباكم قد أخذ عليكم موثقا من الله ومن قبل ما فرطتم في يوسف فلن أبرح الأرض حتى يأذن لي أبي أو يحكم الله لي وهو خير الحاكمين

translation: Return to your father and say, 'O our father, indeed your son has stolen. And we testify only to what we know, and we were not guardians of the unseen.'
interpretation: This verse from the story of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) highlights the brothers' attempt to deceive their father, Ya'qub (Jacob), about Yusuf's fate. It underscores the theme of honesty and the consequences of falsehood. The brothers' claim of Yusuf stealing and their assertion of only testifying to what they know, while denying knowledge of the unseen, reveals their manipulation and lack of integrity. This narrative serves as a moral lesson on the importance of truthfulness and the dangers of deceit, emphasizing that one cannot hide the truth from Allah, who is aware of all secrets and intentions.
orig: ارجعوا إلى أبيكم فقولوا يا أبانا إن ابنك سرق وما شهدنا إلا بما علمنا وما كنا للغيب حافظين

translation: And ask the town where we were and the caravan with which we came, and indeed we are truthful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of verifying information through multiple sources, as the speakers urge others to inquire about their truthfulness from the people of the town and the caravan. It highlights the value of honesty and the confidence of the speakers in their truthfulness, encouraging a community standard of integrity and trustworthiness.
orig: واسأل القرية التي كنا فيها والعير التي أقبلنا فيها وإنا لصادقون

translation: He said, "Rather, your souls have enticed you to something, so patience is most fitting. Perhaps Allah will bring them to me all together. Indeed, He is the Knowing, the Wise."
interpretation: In this verse, Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) is addressing his brothers who had wronged him. He suggests that their actions were driven by their own desires and temptations, not by any fault of his. He expresses his intention to remain patient and hopeful, trusting that Allah, who is all-knowing and wise, might reunite him with his family. This reflects the Islamic values of patience, forgiveness, and trust in Allah's wisdom and plan.
orig: قال بل سولت لكم أنفسكم أمرا فصبر جميل عسى الله أن يأتيني بهم جميعا إنه هو العليم الحكيم

translation: And he turned away from them and said, 'Oh, my grief over Joseph!' And his eyes became white from grief, for he was [of that] a suppressor.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound emotional distress of Prophet Jacob when he learned about the presumed death of his son Joseph. The phrase 'his eyes became white' symbolizes that his grief was so intense that it affected his physical health, causing his eyes to lose their color. The term 'suppressor' indicates that Jacob internalized his sorrow, choosing not to openly express his overwhelming sadness, which reflects his patience and strength in the face of immense personal tragedy.
orig: وتولى عنهم وقال يا أسفى على يوسف وابيضت عيناه من الحزن فهو كظيم

translation: They said, "By Allah, you will not cease to remember Joseph until you become weak or until you are among the perishing."
interpretation: This verse reflects the exasperation of Joseph's brothers towards their father, Jacob, who continuously mourns and remembers Joseph. The brothers are suggesting that Jacob's persistent grief over Joseph, who they believe is dead, is causing him physical and emotional harm, to the point where he might become extremely weak or even die. This highlights the theme of the emotional toll of loss and the impatience or insensitivity of others towards prolonged mourning.
orig: قالوا تالله تفتأ تذكر يوسف حتى تكون حرضا أو تكون من الهالكين

translation: He said: "I only complain of my grief and sorrow to Allah, and I know from Allah what you do not know."
interpretation: This verse reflects the Prophet Yaqub's (Jacob) deep faith and trust in Allah during times of distress. Despite his sons' disbelief and the loss of his son Yusuf (Joseph), Yaqub expresses that he turns to Allah alone with his complaints and sorrows, indicating a profound reliance on divine wisdom and support. He also subtly asserts his knowledge of divine secrets and plans, which others around him are unaware of, showcasing his patience and certainty in Allah's ultimate justice and mercy.
orig: قال إنما أشكو بثي وحزني إلى الله وأعلم من الله ما لا تعلمون

translation: O my sons, go and search for Joseph and his brother, and do not despair of the mercy of Allah; indeed, no one despairs of the mercy of Allah except the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining hope and faith in Allah's mercy, even in dire situations. It teaches that despairing of Allah's mercy is a characteristic of disbelief, encouraging believers to remain steadfast and hopeful, as exemplified by the father's guidance to his sons in their search for Joseph and his brother.
orig: يا بني اذهبوا فتحسسوا من يوسف وأخيه ولا تيأسوا من روح الله إنه لا ييأس من روح الله إلا القوم الكافرون

translation: So when they entered upon him, they said, 'O Aziz, adversity has touched us and our family, and we have come with meager merchandise, so give us full measure and be charitable to us. Indeed, Allah rewards the charitable.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of seeking help from those in positions of power or influence, like the Aziz, while maintaining humility and acknowledging one's dire circumstances. It also emphasizes the value of charity, as the brothers of Yusuf ask for charity and remind the Aziz that Allah rewards those who give charity, suggesting a moral and spiritual incentive for acts of kindness and generosity.
orig: فلما دخلوا عليه قالوا يا أيها العزيز مسنا وأهلنا الضر وجئنا ببضاعة مزجاة فأوف لنا الكيل وتصدق علينا إن الله يجزي المتصدقين

translation: He said, 'Do you know what you did with Yusuf and his brother when you were ignorant?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of accountability and the consequences of actions taken out of ignorance. It serves as a reminder that even actions committed without full understanding or knowledge are not excused from scrutiny and judgment. The question posed by Yaqub (Jacob) to his sons about their treatment of Yusuf (Joseph) and Benjamin underscores the need for reflection on past deeds and the importance of seeking forgiveness and making amends.
orig: قال هل علمتم ما فعلتم بيوسف وأخيه إذ أنتم جاهلون

translation: They said, 'Are you indeed Joseph?' He said, 'I am Joseph, and this is my brother. Allah has indeed been gracious to us. Indeed, whoever fears Allah and is patient, then indeed, Allah does not let the reward of the good-doers go to waste.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of divine favor and reward for righteousness. Joseph's revelation of his identity to his brothers serves as a moment of reconciliation and divine providence. His statement emphasizes that those who maintain piety and patience, like Joseph did throughout his trials, will be rewarded by Allah. It underscores the Islamic teaching that perseverance in faith and good deeds, despite hardships, is recognized and compensated by Allah, reinforcing the moral that steadfastness in faith leads to divine blessings and rewards.
orig: قالوا أإنك لأنت يوسف قال أنا يوسف وهذا أخي قد من الله علينا إنه من يتق ويصبر فإن الله لا يضيع أجر المحسنين

translation: They said, "By Allah, Allah has preferred you over us, and indeed, we have been sinners."
interpretation: This verse reflects the acknowledgment by the brothers of Prophet Yusuf of their past mistakes and the recognition of Allah's favor upon Yusuf. It signifies a moment of humility and repentance, highlighting the theme of divine preference and the importance of admitting one's faults.
orig: قالوا تالله لقد آثرك الله علينا وإن كنا لخاطئين

translation: He will say, "There is no blame upon you today. May Allah forgive you, and He is the most merciful of the merciful."
interpretation: This verse reflects the ultimate mercy and forgiveness of Allah on the Day of Judgment. It suggests that despite the sins and shortcomings of individuals, Allah's mercy prevails, offering forgiveness and absolution. The phrase 'no blame upon you today' indicates a complete erasure of past faults, emphasizing the boundless compassion of Allah, who is described as 'the most merciful of the merciful.' This underscores the hope and reassurance that believers can have in Allah's infinite mercy and forgiveness.
orig: قال لا تثريب عليكم اليوم يغفر الله لكم وهو أرحم الراحمين

translation: Go with this shirt of mine and cast it over my father's face, and he will regain his sight. And bring me all your family.
interpretation: This verse from the story of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) illustrates the miraculous power bestowed upon him by Allah. The shirt symbolizes Yusuf's innocence and divine favor, and its ability to restore his father Ya'qub's (Jacob) eyesight signifies the restoration of truth and justice. It also emphasizes the theme of family reunion and reconciliation after years of separation and hardship, highlighting the importance of faith and patience in overcoming trials.
orig: اذهبوا بقميصي هذا فألقوه على وجه أبي يأت بصيرا وأتوني بأهلكم أجمعين

translation: And when the caravan departed, their father said, 'Indeed, I find the smell of Joseph, if you do not think me senile.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the prophetic intuition and strong emotional connection of Jacob to his son Joseph. Despite the physical distance and the passage of time, Jacob senses that something significant related to Joseph is happening, illustrating the theme of parental love and spiritual insight transcending physical barriers.
orig: ولما فصلت العير قال أبوهم إني لأجد ريح يوسف لولا أن تفندون

translation: They said, 'By Allah, you are surely in your old error.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the disbelief and denial of the truth by the people to whom the Prophet was sent. They are accusing him of being misguided in the same way he was before, refusing to accept the new message he brings as divine revelation. It highlights their stubbornness and rejection of the prophetic message, attributing it to his personal error rather than acknowledging it as guidance from Allah.
orig: قالوا تالله إنك لفي ضلالك القديم

translation: So when the bearer of good news came, he cast it on his face, and he regained his sight. He said, 'Did I not tell you that I know from Allah what you do not know?'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the fulfillment of a divine promise and the power of faith. When the good news of the return of Prophet Ya'qub's son, Yusuf, was brought by his other sons, Ya'qub, who had been blind from grief, was miraculously restored to sight upon receiving the good news. This event reaffirms Ya'qub's earlier assertion of his knowledge of unseen matters granted by Allah, emphasizing that true knowledge and miracles come from divine sources and are beyond human comprehension.
orig: فلما أن جاء البشير ألقاه على وجهه فارتد بصيرا قال ألم أقل لكم إني أعلم من الله ما لا تعلمون

translation: They said, 'O our father, ask forgiveness for our sins; indeed, we have been sinners.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the repentance of Yusuf's brothers after realizing their mistakes. It underscores the Islamic principle of seeking forgiveness from Allah through intermediaries, in this case, their father Yaqub, who is a prophet. It highlights the importance of acknowledging one's sins and the humility required in seeking forgiveness, illustrating a model for repentance and the hope for divine mercy.
orig: قالوا يا أبانا استغفر لنا ذنوبنا إنا كنا خاطئين

translation: He said, 'I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord. Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the Prophet Noah's compassionate nature as he expresses his intention to seek forgiveness from Allah for his people, despite their disbelief and rejection of his message. It highlights the attributes of Allah as being Forgiving and Merciful, emphasizing the possibility of repentance and divine pardon.
orig: قال سوف أستغفر لكم ربي إنه هو الغفور الرحيم

translation: So when they entered upon Joseph, he took his parents to himself and said, "Enter Egypt, if Allah wills, in safety."
interpretation: This verse highlights the culmination of Prophet Joseph's journey from hardship to a position of power and reunification with his family. When his parents and brothers entered Egypt, Joseph embraced his parents, symbolizing the restoration of family ties and the fulfillment of divine promise. His invitation to enter Egypt safely, contingent on Allah's will, underscores the themes of divine protection, trust in God's plan, and the ultimate triumph of patience and faith over adversity.
orig: فلما دخلوا على يوسف آوى إليه أبويه وقال ادخلوا مصر إن شاء الله آمنين

translation: And he raised his parents upon the throne, and they fell down in prostration before him. And he said, 'O my father, this is the interpretation of my dream of old. My Lord has made it reality. And He was good to me when He took me out of prison and brought you [here] from bedouin life, after Satan had induced [estrangement] between me and my brothers. Indeed, my Lord is Subtle in what He wills. Indeed, He is the Knowing, the Wise.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the fulfillment of Yusuf's dream where he saw the sun, the moon, and eleven stars prostrating to him, symbolizing his family's eventual submission and recognition of his status. It underscores the themes of divine providence and patience, illustrating how Allah's plan unfolds over time, turning hardships into blessings. Yusuf acknowledges Allah's subtle planning and wisdom in orchestrating events that led to his rise from a prisoner to a ruler, and the reconciliation with his family, emphasizing trust in Allah's knowledge and wisdom.
orig: ورفع أبويه على العرش وخروا له سجدا وقال يا أبت هذا تأويل رؤياي من قبل قد جعلها ربي حقا وقد أحسن بي إذ أخرجني من السجن وجاء بكم من البدو من بعد أن نزغ الشيطان بيني وبين إخوتي إن ربي لطيف لما يشاء إنه هو العليم الحكيم

translation: My Lord, You have given me [something] of sovereignty and taught me of the interpretation of events. Originator of the heavens and earth, You are my protector in this world and in the Hereafter. Cause me to die a Muslim and join me with the righteous.
interpretation: In this verse, the speaker, traditionally understood to be Prophet Yusuf (Joseph), expresses gratitude to Allah for the blessings of authority and the ability to interpret dreams and events. He acknowledges Allah as the Creator of the universe and seeks His protection in both this life and the hereafter. The request to die as a Muslim and to be joined with the righteous reflects a deep desire for a life and death aligned with submission to Allah's will, and a hope for eternal companionship with the virtuous. This verse underscores themes of gratitude, acknowledgment of divine sovereignty, and the aspiration for a righteous end.
orig: رب قد آتيتني من الملك وعلمتني من تأويل الأحاديث فاطر السماوات والأرض أنت وليي في الدنيا والآخرة توفني مسلما وألحقني بالصالحين

translation: That is from the news of the unseen which We reveal to you. You were not with them when they cast their lots and conspired.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine origin of the Qur'an, emphasizing that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was not present during the historical events described, yet he received this knowledge through revelation from Allah. It underscores the miraculous nature of the Qur'an, as it contains information about past events that could not have been known through ordinary means, thereby affirming its authenticity and the prophethood of Muhammad.
orig: ذلك من أنباء الغيب نوحيه إليك وما كنت لديهم إذ أجمعوا أمرهم وهم يمكرون

translation: And most of the people, even if you are eager, are not believers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the reality that despite the Prophet Muhammad's earnest efforts and desire for people to embrace Islam, the majority of humanity will not become believers. It serves as a reminder to the Prophet and the believers not to be disheartened by the lack of widespread acceptance of the faith, as this is part of the divine plan and human nature.
orig: وما أكثر الناس ولو حرصت بمؤمنين

translation: And you do not ask them for it any payment. It is not but a reminder to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the selfless nature of the Prophet Muhammad's mission. He did not seek any worldly compensation for conveying the message of Islam, highlighting that the Qur'an is a divine reminder and guidance meant for all humanity, not a source of personal gain.
orig: وما تسألهم عليه من أجر إن هو إلا ذكر للعالمين

translation: And how many a sign in the heavens and the earth they pass by, while they are turning away from them.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to overlook the numerous signs of God's existence and power that are evident in the universe. It suggests that people often go about their lives, indifferent to the wonders and miracles around them, which serve as reminders of the Creator's presence and majesty. The verse calls attention to the spiritual negligence and the need for greater awareness and reflection on these divine signs.
orig: وكأين من آية في السماوات والأرض يمرون عليها وهم عنها معرضون

translation: And most of them believe not in Allah except [while they are] associating others with Him.
interpretation: This verse highlights the prevalent issue of polytheism among people, indicating that even when they profess belief in Allah, their faith is often tainted by the association of partners with Him, which fundamentally contradicts the principle of Tawheed (the oneness of God). It serves as a reminder of the importance of pure monotheism in Islam.
orig: وما يؤمن أكثرهم بالله إلا وهم مشركون

translation: Do they feel secure that there will come to them an overwhelming punishment from Allah, or that the Hour will come upon them suddenly while they do not perceive?
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who are heedless of God's signs and the impending Day of Judgment. It questions the false sense of security that some people might feel, thinking they are safe from God's punishment or the sudden arrival of the Hour. The verse emphasizes the unpredictability and inevitability of divine retribution and the end of times, urging believers to remain vigilant and conscious of their actions and faith.
orig: أفأمنوا أن تأتيهم غاشية من عذاب الله أو تأتيهم الساعة بغتة وهم لا يشعرون

translation: Say, 'This is my way; I invite to Allah with insight, I and those who follow me. And exalted is Allah; and I am not of those who associate others with Him.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophet Muhammad's clear and deliberate path of inviting people to the worship of Allah alone, guided by divine insight and certainty. It underscores the purity of his mission, free from any association with idolatry or polytheism, and highlights the importance of monotheism in Islam. The phrase 'and exalted is Allah' serves as a declaration of Allah's transcendence and majesty, reinforcing the monotheistic message.
orig: قل هذه سبيلي أدعو إلى الله على بصيرة أنا ومن اتبعني وسبحان الله وما أنا من المشركين

translation: And We sent not before you except men to whom We revealed from among the people of the towns. So have they not traveled through the earth and observed how was the end of those before them? And the home of the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah, so will you not use reason?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the continuity of divine revelation through human messengers who were chosen from among the common people of various towns. It serves as a reminder and a challenge to the current generation to reflect on the historical evidence of the consequences faced by previous nations who rejected their prophets. The verse encourages believers to consider the transient nature of worldly life and the superior reward awaiting those who live righteously in the afterlife. It calls for introspection and the use of intellect to understand the deeper truths of faith and morality.
orig: وما أرسلنا من قبلك إلا رجالا نوحي إليهم من أهل القرى أفلم يسيروا في الأرض فينظروا كيف كان عاقبة الذين من قبلهم ولدار الآخرة خير للذين اتقوا أفلا تعقلون

translation: Until, when the messengers despaired and thought that they were denied, then came to them Our help, and whoever We willed was saved. And Our punishment cannot be repelled from the people who are criminals.
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of divine support and justice. It illustrates that even when the messengers of God reach a point of despair and believe that their message has been rejected, God's help arrives unexpectedly. This signifies that divine assistance is not bound by human timelines or expectations. The verse also emphasizes God's sovereignty in choosing whom to save, indicating that salvation is a divine prerogative. Furthermore, it underscores the inevitability of God's punishment for those who persist in wrongdoing, reinforcing the concept that divine justice will ultimately prevail, regardless of any temporary delays or apparent setbacks.
orig: حتى إذا استيأس الرسل وظنوا أنهم قد كذبوا جاءهم نصرنا فنجي من نشاء ولا يرد بأسنا عن القوم المجرمين

translation: Indeed, in their stories is a lesson for those of understanding. It is not a fabricated account, but a confirmation of what was before it and a detailed explanation of all things, and guidance and mercy for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the narratives of the prophets and their communities, as recounted in the Qur'an, serve as profound lessons and moral guidance for those endowed with insight and wisdom. These stories are not mere fables or invented tales but are authenticated by their consistency with previous scriptures. They provide a comprehensive exposition of various aspects of life and faith, offering both guidance and mercy specifically to those who embrace faith. The verse underscores the Qur'an's role as a source of divine wisdom and compassion, reinforcing its authenticity and its purpose in aiding believers in their spiritual journey.
orig: لقد كان في قصصهم عبرة لأولي الألباب ما كان حديثا يفترى ولكن تصديق الذي بين يديه وتفصيل كل شيء وهدى ورحمة لقوم يؤمنون

translation: Those are the verses of the Book, and that which has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth, but most people do not believe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin and truthfulness of the Qur'an, which is described as part of the 'Book' - a reference to the eternal knowledge of God. It acknowledges that despite the clarity and truth of the revelation sent to the Prophet Muhammad, the majority of people choose not to believe, highlighting a common human tendency towards disbelief or denial of divine messages.
orig: المر تلك آيات الكتاب والذي أنزل إليك من ربك الحق ولكن أكثر الناس لا يؤمنون

translation: Allah is He Who raised the heavens without any pillars that you can see; then He established Himself above the Throne; He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running its course for a term appointed; He regulates the affair, explaining the signs, that you may believe in the meeting with your Lord.
interpretation: This verse highlights the omnipotence and meticulous planning of Allah. By describing the creation of the heavens without visible support, it emphasizes Allah's ability to sustain the universe through unseen means. The mention of the Throne signifies His supreme authority and governance over all creation. The regulation of celestial bodies like the sun and moon for specific periods underscores the divine order and purpose in the cosmos. The verse concludes by urging believers to recognize these signs as evidence of Allah's power and wisdom, fostering a firm belief in the eventual meeting with Him.
orig: الله الذي رفع السماوات بغير عمد ترونها ثم استوى على العرش وسخر الشمس والقمر كل يجري لأجل مسمى يدبر الأمر يفصل الآيات لعلكم بلقاء ربكم توقنون

translation: And it is He who spread the earth and placed therein firmly set mountains and rivers, and from all the fruits He made therein two mates; He causes the night to cover the day. Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's creative power and the intricate design of the earth. By mentioning the spreading of the earth, the establishment of mountains and rivers, and the creation of paired fruits, it highlights the balance and diversity in nature. The alternation of night and day serves as a reminder of the continuous cycle of life and the passage of time. These signs are presented as evidence of Allah's existence and wisdom, encouraging reflection and contemplation among those who ponder over the creation.
orig: وهو الذي مد الأرض وجعل فيها رواسي وأنهارا ومن كل الثمرات جعل فيها زوجين اثنين يغشي الليل النهار إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يتفكرون

translation: And on the earth are neighboring tracts, and gardens of grapes, and fields, and palm trees, some sharing one root and others not, watered with one water; and We make some of them taste better than others. Indeed, in that are signs for a people who understand.
interpretation: This verse highlights the diversity and unity in creation as a sign of God's wisdom and power. The variety of plants, all nourished by the same water yet differing in taste and quality, illustrates that God can create diversity from the same source. This serves as a reminder for humans to reflect on these natural phenomena and recognize the underlying divine order and the purposeful variation in creation, encouraging a deeper understanding and appreciation of God's signs in the world.
orig: وفي الأرض قطع متجاورات وجنات من أعناب وزرع ونخيل صنوان وغير صنوان يسقى بماء واحد ونفضل بعضها على بعض في الأكل إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يعقلون

translation: And if you are amazed, then amazing is their saying: "When we are dust, shall we indeed be created anew?" Those are the ones who have disbelieved in their Lord, and those will have shackles around their necks, and those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever.
interpretation: This verse highlights the disbelief and astonishment of those who reject the concept of resurrection after death. Their incredulity at the idea of being recreated from dust underscores their lack of faith in the power and promise of Allah. The verse serves as a warning that such disbelief leads to severe consequences in the hereafter, symbolized by the shackles and eternal damnation in the Fire, emphasizing the importance of faith and the reality of the afterlife.
orig: وإن تعجب فعجب قولهم أإذا كنا ترابا أإنا لفي خلق جديد أولئك الذين كفروا بربهم وأولئك الأغلال في أعناقهم وأولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون

translation: And they urge you to hasten the evil before the good while there have certainly been exemplary punishments before them. And indeed, your Lord is full of forgiveness for mankind despite their wrongdoing, and indeed, your Lord is severe in penalty.
interpretation: This verse addresses the impatience and disbelief of those who demand that the Prophet Muhammad hasten the punishment they believe they deserve, rather than waiting for the good that Allah promises. It reminds them of past nations that faced divine punishment as a warning. The verse emphasizes Allah's attributes of forgiveness and mercy, which are vast and encompass even those who wrong themselves, yet it also underscores His severe punishment for those who persist in disbelief and transgression. This dual aspect of Allah's nature - mercy and justice - serves as a reminder to humanity of the consequences of their actions and the importance of seeking forgiveness and righteousness.
orig: ويستعجلونك بالسيئة قبل الحسنة وقد خلت من قبلهم المثلات وإن ربك لذو مغفرة للناس على ظلمهم وإن ربك لشديد العقاب

translation: And those who disbelieve say, 'Why has a sign not been sent down to him from his Lord?' You are only a warner, and for every people there is a guide.
interpretation: This verse addresses the skepticism of the disbelievers who demanded a miraculous sign from the Prophet Muhammad to prove his prophethood. It emphasizes that the Prophet's role is not to perform miracles on demand but to warn people of the consequences of their actions. The verse also highlights the universal aspect of guidance, indicating that every community has been provided with a guide or a prophet to lead them to the right path. This underscores the fairness and completeness of God's plan for guidance across different peoples and times.
orig: ويقول الذين كفروا لولا أنزل عليه آية من ربه إنما أنت منذر ولكل قوم هاد

translation: Allah knows what every female carries and what the wombs decrease or increase, and with Him everything is by measure.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's complete knowledge and control over all aspects of creation, particularly highlighting His awareness of the development within the wombs. It underscores the notion that every detail, from conception to the growth of the fetus, is precisely measured and known to Allah, reflecting His omnipotence and meticulous oversight of all life processes.
orig: الله يعلم ما تحمل كل أنثى وما تغيض الأرحام وما تزداد وكل شيء عنده بمقدار

translation: Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Great, the Exalted
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience of Allah, highlighting His complete knowledge of both the hidden and the apparent aspects of existence. It underscores His supreme greatness and exalted status above all creation, affirming His unique attributes that distinguish Him from all else.
orig: عالم الغيب والشهادة الكبير المتعال

translation: It is the same [to Him] whether any of you conceal his speech or publicize it, and whether he is hidden by night or conspicuous by day.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience of Allah, indicating that He is fully aware of all actions and thoughts of individuals, regardless of whether they are expressed openly or kept secret. It serves as a reminder to believers that they cannot hide anything from Allah, encouraging them to be mindful of their actions and intentions at all times, as they are always under divine observation.
orig: سواء منكم من أسر القول ومن جهر به ومن هو مستخف بالليل وسارب بالنهار

translation: He has guardian angels, before him and behind him, who protect him by Allah's command. Indeed, Allah will not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves. And when Allah intends ill for a people, there is no turning it back, and there is no protector for them besides Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipresence of divine protection and guidance through angels, highlighting that individuals are constantly watched over by Allah's command. It also underscores the principle of personal responsibility and collective change, suggesting that societal transformation begins with individual self-reformation. The verse further conveys the notion of divine decree, indicating that when Allah decides a fate for a people, it is inevitable and they have no recourse or protector other than Him, reinforcing the concept of ultimate divine authority and the limits of human control over destiny.
orig: له معقبات من بين يديه ومن خلفه يحفظونه من أمر الله إن الله لا يغير ما بقوم حتى يغيروا ما بأنفسهم وإذا أراد الله بقوم سوءا فلا مرد له وما لهم من دونه من وال

translation: He is the One who shows you the lightning, causing fear and hope, and He produces the heavy clouds.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's control over natural phenomena, specifically mentioning lightning and clouds. The lightning is described as instilling both fear and hope in people; fear due to its potential danger and hope because it often precedes rain, which is vital for life. The heavy clouds are a sign of God's power to bring forth rain, essential for the sustenance of life on earth. This verse serves as a reminder of God's omnipotence and His ability to evoke a range of human emotions through natural events, urging believers to reflect on His signs in the universe.
orig: هو الذي يريكم البرق خوفا وطمعا وينشئ السحاب الثقال

translation: And the thunder exalts His praise, and the angels [as well] from fear of Him. And He sends the thunderbolts and strikes therewith whom He wills. Yet they dispute about Allah while He is severe in assault.
interpretation: This verse highlights the omnipotence and majesty of Allah, as even natural phenomena like thunder glorify Him, and the angels do so out of awe and reverence. The sending of thunderbolts serves as a reminder of Allah's power to enforce His will. Meanwhile, the reference to people disputing about Allah despite these clear signs underscores human stubbornness and the futility of arguing against the evident might and authority of the Creator, who is described as severe in His ability to retaliate against disbelief and transgression.
orig: ويسبح الرعد بحمده والملائكة من خيفته ويرسل الصواعق فيصيب بها من يشاء وهم يجادلون في الله وهو شديد المحال

translation: To Him belongs the call of truth. And those whom they invoke besides Him do not respond to them with anything, except like one who stretches his hands towards water to reach his mouth, but it does not reach it. And the call of the disbelievers is nothing but in error.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the exclusive right of Allah to be called upon in truth and sincerity. It illustrates the futility of calling upon false deities or idols, likening it to a person desperately trying to drink water but unable to reach it, symbolizing the emptiness and ineffectiveness of such calls. The verse underscores that only Allah can truly respond to the needs and prayers of His creation, and any other form of worship or supplication is misguided and leads to nothing but error.
orig: له دعوة الحق والذين يدعون من دونه لا يستجيبون لهم بشيء إلا كباسط كفيه إلى الماء ليبلغ فاه وما هو ببالغه وما دعاء الكافرين إلا في ضلال

translation: And to Allah prostrates whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly, and their shadows too, in the morning and in the afternoon.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universal submission to Allah's sovereignty. It indicates that everything in creation, from the celestial bodies to the beings on earth, and even their shadows, are in a state of prostration to Allah. This prostration occurs continuously, symbolizing the constant and inescapable nature of Allah's dominion. The mention of 'willingly or unwillingly' highlights that this submission is inherent to the nature of creation, whether acknowledged and accepted by the creatures or not. The timing 'in the morning and in the afternoon' suggests the perpetual and ongoing nature of this submission throughout the day, reinforcing the idea of Allah's unceasing control over all aspects of existence.
orig: ولله يسجد من في السماوات والأرض طوعا وكرها وظلالهم بالغدو والآصال

translation: Say, 'Who is the Lord of the heavens and the earth?' Say, 'Allah.' Say, 'Have you then taken besides Him allies who do not possess [even] for themselves any benefit or any harm?' Say, 'Is the blind equivalent to the seeing? Or is darkness equivalent to light? Or have they attributed to Allah partners who created like His creation, so that the creation [of those others] seemed similar to them?' Say, 'Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is the One, the Prevailing.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness and supremacy of Allah as the sole Creator and Lord of the universe. It challenges the belief in multiple deities or partners alongside Allah, questioning the rationality of such beliefs by comparing them to clear distinctions like blindness versus sight, and darkness versus light. The verse underscores that any supposed partners to Allah cannot even control their own benefit or harm, let alone create anything comparable to Allah's creation. It reaffirms that Allah alone is the Creator of everything, and His unique attributes of being the One and the Prevailing further highlight His incomparable nature and absolute authority over all existence.
orig: قل من رب السماوات والأرض قل الله قل أفاتخذتم من دونه أولياء لا يملكون لأنفسهم نفعا ولا ضرا قل هل يستوي الأعمى والبصير أم هل تستوي الظلمات والنور أم جعلوا لله شركاء خلقوا كخلقه فتشابه الخلق عليهم قل الله خالق كل شيء وهو الواحد القهار

translation: He sends down water from the sky, and valleys flow according to their measure, and the flood carries a swelling foam. And from what they heat in the fire, desiring ornaments or utensils, comes a foam like it. Thus does Allah present truth and falsehood. As for the foam, it vanishes, being nothing, while that which benefits people remains in the earth. Thus does Allah present examples.
interpretation: This verse uses the metaphor of water and foam to illustrate the difference between truth and falsehood. The water, which flows and benefits the earth, represents the truth that remains and is useful to people. In contrast, the foam, which is produced by the flood and by the heating of metals, represents falsehood that is transient and ultimately vanishes. Allah uses these natural phenomena to draw a parallel between enduring truth and fleeting falsehood, emphasizing that while falsehood may appear significant, it is ultimately inconsequential and disappears, whereas truth has lasting value and utility.
orig: أنزل من السماء ماء فسالت أودية بقدرها فاحتمل السيل زبدا رابيا ومما يوقدون عليه في النار ابتغاء حلية أو متاع زبد مثله كذلك يضرب الله الحق والباطل فأما الزبد فيذهب جفاء وأما ما ينفع الناس فيمكث في الأرض كذلك يضرب الله الأمثال

translation: For those who have responded to their Lord is the best [reward], but those who did not respond to Him - if they had all that is in the earth entirely and the like of it with it, they would [attempt to] ransom themselves thereby. Those will have the worst account, and their refuge will be Hell, and wretched is the resting place.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequences of one's response to God's call. It highlights that those who heed and respond positively to their Lord will be rewarded with the ultimate goodness. Conversely, those who ignore or reject God's call will face severe consequences. Even if they were to offer everything on earth and more as a ransom, it would not suffice to save them from the accountability they will face. The verse underscores the gravity of their situation by describing their fate as having the worst account, with Hell as their abode, which is described as a wretched resting place. This serves as a stark reminder of the importance of responding to God's guidance and the dire consequences of neglecting it.
orig: للذين استجابوا لربهم الحسنى والذين لم يستجيبوا له لو أن لهم ما في الأرض جميعا ومثله معه لافتدوا به أولئك لهم سوء الحساب ومأواهم جهنم وبئس المهاد

translation: Is then he who knows that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth like him who is blind? Only those who have understanding will take heed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the distinction between those who recognize and accept the truth of the Qur'an as divine revelation and those who are spiritually blind to its message. It suggests that true insight and understanding (those who have understanding) are necessary to appreciate and heed the divine guidance, highlighting the importance of intellectual and spiritual discernment in faith.
orig: أفمن يعلم أنما أنزل إليك من ربك الحق كمن هو أعمى إنما يتذكر أولو الألباب

translation: Those who fulfill the covenant of Allah and do not break the promise
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of integrity and faithfulness in one's commitment to Allah. It highlights that true believers are those who adhere steadfastly to their religious obligations and promises made to Allah, demonstrating their trustworthiness and dedication to their faith.
orig: الذين يوفون بعهد الله ولا ينقضون الميثاق

translation: And those who keep the ties which Allah has commanded to be kept, and fear their Lord, and dread the evil reckoning.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining family and social ties as ordained by Allah, highlighting that those who do so are characterized by their piety and fear of Allah. It also underscores the accountability in the hereafter, where individuals will face a reckoning for their actions, encouraging believers to be mindful of their deeds and to uphold their responsibilities towards others out of reverence for Allah and fear of divine judgment.
orig: والذين يصلون ما أمر الله به أن يوصل ويخشون ربهم ويخافون سوء الحساب

translation: And those who are patient, seeking the countenance of their Lord, and establish prayer and spend out of what We have provided for them, secretly and publicly, and repel evil with good - those will have the good consequence of [life in] the Home.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the qualities of patience, devotion to God, regular prayer, and charitable giving in secret and openly, as well as responding to evil with goodness. These actions are presented as pathways to achieving a favorable outcome in the afterlife, illustrating that true success lies in the Hereafter for those who embody these virtues.
orig: والذين صبروا ابتغاء وجه ربهم وأقاموا الصلاة وأنفقوا مما رزقناهم سرا وعلانية ويدرءون بالحسنة السيئة أولئك لهم عقبى الدار

translation: Gardens of Eden which they will enter, and whoever was righteous among their fathers, their spouses, and their offspring. And the angels will enter upon them from every gate.
interpretation: This verse describes the reward of Paradise for the believers, emphasizing that not only will they enter it, but also their righteous family members. The inclusion of 'from every gate' signifies the honor and abundance of blessings bestowed upon them, highlighting the comprehensive and welcoming nature of divine mercy and the communal aspect of salvation in Islam.
orig: جنات عدن يدخلونها ومن صلح من آبائهم وأزواجهم وذرياتهم والملائكة يدخلون عليهم من كل باب

translation: Peace be upon you for your patience. How excellent is the final home!
interpretation: This verse is a greeting and promise from Allah to the believers who have shown patience in their trials and tribulations. It emphasizes that the reward for their steadfastness will be peace and an excellent abode in the hereafter, highlighting the ultimate success and tranquility awaiting them in Paradise.
orig: سلام عليكم بما صبرتم فنعم عقبى الدار

translation: And those who break the covenant of Allah after its ratification, and sever that which Allah has commanded to be joined, and cause corruption on the earth, for them is the curse, and for them is the evil abode.
interpretation: This verse highlights the severe consequences for those who violate their commitments to Allah, specifically by breaking their covenant with Him, failing to maintain familial and social ties as commanded, and causing disorder and corruption in society. Such actions are not only morally reprehensible but also incur divine wrath, leading to a cursed existence and an unfavorable outcome in the hereafter. It emphasizes the importance of upholding one's promises, preserving relationships, and contributing positively to the world.
orig: والذين ينقضون عهد الله من بعد ميثاقه ويقطعون ما أمر الله به أن يوصل ويفسدون في الأرض أولئك لهم اللعنة ولهم سوء الدار

translation: Allah extends provision for whom He wills and restricts [it]. And they rejoice in the worldly life, while the worldly life is not, compared to the Hereafter, except [brief] enjoyment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine control over sustenance and the transient nature of worldly life. It serves as a reminder that while people may find joy in material possessions and worldly achievements, these are fleeting and insignificant when compared to the eternal life of the Hereafter. The verse encourages believers to focus on spiritual growth and preparation for the afterlife, rather than becoming overly attached to the temporary pleasures of this world.
orig: الله يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء ويقدر وفرحوا بالحياة الدنيا وما الحياة الدنيا في الآخرة إلا متاع

translation: And those who disbelieve say, 'Why has a sign not been sent down to him from his Lord?' Say, 'Indeed, Allah lets go astray whom He wills and guides to Himself whoever turns back [to Him].'
interpretation: This verse addresses the skepticism of disbelievers who demand a miraculous sign from the Prophet Muhammad to validate his prophethood. The response given in the verse emphasizes the divine prerogative of Allah, indicating that guidance and misguidance are under His control. It suggests that the purpose of signs is not merely to convince the skeptics but is part of a broader divine plan where true guidance is granted to those who sincerely turn towards Allah. This underscores the importance of personal faith and repentance over external proofs.
orig: ويقول الذين كفروا لولا أنزل عليه آية من ربه قل إن الله يضل من يشاء ويهدي إليه من أناب

translation: Those who believe and whose hearts find rest in the remembrance of Allah. Indeed, in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual tranquility and peace that believers experience through the remembrance of Allah. It emphasizes that true contentment and serenity of the heart are achieved by maintaining a constant connection with Allah through acts like prayer, recitation of the Qur'an, and supplication. The verse reassures believers that engaging in the remembrance of Allah is a source of inner peace and stability, reinforcing the importance of spiritual practices in achieving emotional and psychological well-being.
orig: الذين آمنوا وتطمئن قلوبهم بذكر الله ألا بذكر الله تطمئن القلوب

translation: Those who have believed and done righteous deeds, for them is blessedness and a goodly return.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the reward awaiting those who combine faith with righteous actions.
