It suggests that true success and ultimate happiness in the hereafter are promised to those who not only believe in God but also actively engage in good deeds. The term 'طوبى' (blessedness) signifies a state of ultimate joy and peace, while 'حسن مآب' (a goodly return) points to the favorable destination in the afterlife, reinforcing the Islamic belief in the importance of both faith and deeds for achieving salvation.
orig: الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات طوبى لهم وحسن مآب

translation: Thus have We sent you to a community before whom other communities have passed away, in order that you may recite to them what We have revealed to you, while they disbelieve in the Most Merciful. Say, "He is my Lord; there is no deity except Him. Upon Him I rely, and to Him is my return."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the prophetic mission of Muhammad, indicating that he was sent to a people who had predecessors, highlighting the continuity of divine messages across different nations. The verse underscores the challenge Muhammad faced, as his people disbelieved in Allah, referred to here as 'the Most Merciful.' In response to their disbelief, Muhammad is instructed to affirm his unwavering faith in Allah as the sole deity, expressing his complete dependence and trust in Him, and his ultimate return to Him. This declaration serves as a model of faith and submission for believers, illustrating the importance of steadfastness in faith amidst opposition.
orig: كذلك أرسلناك في أمة قد خلت من قبلها أمم لتتلو عليهم الذي أوحينا إليك وهم يكفرون بالرحمن قل هو ربي لا إله إلا هو عليه توكلت وإليه متاب

translation: And if there were a Qur'an by which the mountains could be moved, or the earth could be split, or the dead could be made to speak, [it would be this one]. But to Allah belongs the entire affair. Then, have those who believed not despaired that if Allah willed, He could guide all of mankind? And those who disbelieved will not cease to be struck by a calamity for what they have done, or it will settle close to their homes until the promise of Allah comes. Indeed, Allah does not fail in His promise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence and sovereignty of Allah over all matters, including the guidance of humanity. It suggests that the Qur'an itself is a powerful testament to Allah's authority, capable of influencing even the most inanimate or lifeless elements if He so willed. However, the verse also conveys that the ultimate decision to guide or not guide people lies with Allah alone, and not even the Qur'an can force this guidance upon those who reject it. It further warns that those who disbelieve will face continuous trials and calamities as a consequence of their actions, serving as a reminder of Allah's promise and the inevitability of His judgment.
orig: ولو أن قرآنا سيرت به الجبال أو قطعت به الأرض أو كلم به الموتى بل لله الأمر جميعا أفلم ييأس الذين آمنوا أن لو يشاء الله لهدى الناس جميعا ولا يزال الذين كفروا تصيبهم بما صنعوا قارعة أو تحل قريبا من دارهم حتى يأتي وعد الله إن الله لا يخلف الميعاد

translation: And indeed, [many] messengers were ridiculed before you, but I granted respite to those who disbelieved; then I seized them, and how [terrible] was My penalty.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder and warning to the Prophet Muhammad and the believers that the mockery and disbelief faced by him were not unique. It reassures that Allah has a pattern of giving disbelievers time to reflect and possibly repent, but ultimately, He punishes them severely. The phrase 'how [terrible] was My penalty' emphasizes the intensity and inevitability of divine retribution, urging believers to remain steadfast and not be disheartened by the temporary success or mockery of the disbelievers.
orig: ولقد استهزئ برسل من قبلك فأمليت للذين كفروا ثم أخذتهم فكيف كان عقاب

translation: Is He then Who is the Maintainer of every soul for what it has earned, and yet they have made partners with Allah? Say, 'Name them. Or do you inform Him of what He does not know on the earth, or is it just a show of words?' Nay, their plot has been made attractive to those who disbelieve, and they have been turned away from the Path. And whomsoever Allah sends astray, for him there is no guide.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness and omniscience of Allah, challenging the polytheistic beliefs by questioning the logic of attributing partners to Him. It critiques the absurdity of informing Allah of what He already knows or using mere rhetoric to justify false beliefs. The verse also warns that those who disbelieve are deceived by their own schemes, which lead them astray from the right path, and without Allah's guidance, they remain lost.
orig: أفمن هو قائم على كل نفس بما كسبت وجعلوا لله شركاء قل سموهم أم تنبئونه بما لا يعلم في الأرض أم بظاهر من القول بل زين للذين كفروا مكرهم وصدوا عن السبيل ومن يضلل الله فما له من هاد

translation: For them there is punishment in the life of this world, and the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe; and they will have no defender against Allah.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences faced by those who reject faith or commit wrongdoings. It emphasizes that such individuals will experience punishment not only in the worldly life but also in the afterlife, where the punishment is described as more severe. The phrase 'no defender against Allah' underscores the absolute justice of Allah, indicating that no one can intercede or protect them from the divine judgment. This serves as a reminder of the accountability one has for their actions and the importance of seeking righteousness to avoid such outcomes.
orig: لهم عذاب في الحياة الدنيا ولعذاب الآخرة أشق وما لهم من الله من واق

translation: The likeness of the Paradise which the righteous are promised - beneath it rivers flow - its food is everlasting and so is its shade. That is the reward of those who are righteous, and the reward of the disbelievers is the Fire.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the contrast between the rewards of the righteous and the punishment of the disbelievers. The Paradise promised to the righteous is described with flowing rivers, eternal food, and perpetual shade, symbolizing a state of perpetual peace, abundance, and comfort. This imagery serves to motivate believers to adhere to righteousness and piety, as these qualities lead to such a blissful afterlife. Conversely, the mention of the Fire as the outcome for disbelievers underscores the severe consequences of disbelief and sin, urging individuals to reflect on their actions and their eternal consequences.
orig: مثل الجنة التي وعد المتقون تجري من تحتها الأنهار أكلها دائم وظلها تلك عقبى الذين اتقوا وعقبى الكافرين النار

translation: And those to whom We have given the Book rejoice in what has been revealed to you, but among the factions are those who deny part of it. Say, [O Muhammad], "I have only been commanded to worship Allah and not to associate anything with Him. To Him I call, and to Him is my return."
interpretation: This verse highlights the diversity of responses to the revelation of the Qur'an. It points out that while some people of the scripture (Jews and Christians) recognize and rejoice in the truth of the Qur'an, others from various groups reject parts of it due to their biases or disbelief. The verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad to focus on the core message of monotheism, emphasizing that his primary duty is to worship Allah alone and invite others to do the same, without associating partners with Him. This underscores the universal call to monotheism and the ultimate return to Allah, reinforcing the centrality of Tawheed (the oneness of God) in Islam.
orig: والذين آتيناهم الكتاب يفرحون بما أنزل إليك ومن الأحزاب من ينكر بعضه قل إنما أمرت أن أعبد الله ولا أشرك به إليه أدعو وإليه مآب

translation: And thus We have sent it down as an Arabic judgment. And if you were to follow their desires after what has come to you of knowledge, you will have from Allah neither a protector nor a defender.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin and authority of the Qur'an, revealed in Arabic as a clear and final judgment. It warns the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and by extension all believers, against compromising the message of Islam by following the desires or whims of others. Doing so, especially after receiving clear knowledge from Allah, would result in losing Allah's protection and support. The verse underscores the importance of adhering steadfastly to divine guidance over human inclinations.
orig: وكذلك أنزلناه حكما عربيا ولئن اتبعت أهواءهم بعدما جاءك من العلم ما لك من الله من ولي ولا واق

translation: And We have certainly sent messengers before you and made for them wives and descendants. And it was not for a messenger to come with a sign except by permission of Allah. For every term there is a decree.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the continuity of divine guidance through the succession of prophets sent by Allah, each with their own families, underscoring their human nature and the personal sacrifices they made. It also highlights the sovereignty of Allah over the revelation of signs and miracles, which are granted only according to His will and wisdom. The final part of the verse reminds us of the predetermined nature of all events, reinforcing the concept of divine decree and the ultimate control Allah has over the timing and outcome of all matters.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا رسلا من قبلك وجعلنا لهم أزواجا وذرية وما كان لرسول أن يأتي بآية إلا بإذن الله لكل أجل كتاب

translation: Allah erases what He wills and confirms [what He wills], and with Him is the Mother of the Book.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's absolute authority over all things, including the divine decrees and the records of events. The phrase 'Allah erases what He wills and confirms [what He wills]' indicates that Allah has the power to change or maintain the course of events as He sees fit. The 'Mother of the Book' refers to the preserved tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz) where all decrees are recorded, signifying that the ultimate knowledge and control of all affairs rest with Allah alone.
orig: يمحو الله ما يشاء ويثبت وعنده أم الكتاب

translation: And whether We show you some of what We promise them or take you [in death], upon you is only the [duty of] notification, and upon Us is the account.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of the Prophet Muhammad as a messenger whose primary responsibility is to convey the message of God. It reassures him that whether he sees the fulfillment of God's promises in his lifetime or not, his duty is solely to deliver the message. The outcome and judgment of the people's response to the message are in God's hands alone, relieving the Prophet of any burden beyond his task of communication.
orig: وإن ما نرينك بعض الذي نعدهم أو نتوفينك فإنما عليك البلاغ وعلينا الحساب

translation: Do they not see that We come to the land and reduce it from its borders? And Allah judges; there is no repeller of His judgment. And He is swift in account.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inevitability and the power of Allah's decree. It points out that just as the earth's borders diminish over time, symbolizing the transient nature of worldly existence, so too does Allah's judgment come without fail. The verse serves as a reminder of the Day of Judgment, where Allah's decisions are final and swiftly executed, emphasizing the urgency for humans to reflect on their actions and prepare for accountability.
orig: أولم يروا أنا نأتي الأرض ننقصها من أطرافها والله يحكم لا معقب لحكمه وهو سريع الحساب

translation: And those before them did plot, but to Allah belongs the plotting, all of it. He knows what every soul earns, and the disbelievers will know to whom the final home belongs.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate sovereignty and omniscience of Allah. It highlights that while disbelievers and previous nations may have devised schemes against the truth, Allah's plan encompasses all and surpasses any human plotting. The verse reassures believers that Allah is fully aware of the deeds of every individual, and it serves as a warning to the disbelievers that they will eventually realize the true outcome and consequences of their actions in the hereafter, affirming that the final abode belongs to the righteous under Allah's judgment.
orig: وقد مكر الذين من قبلهم فلله المكر جميعا يعلم ما تكسب كل نفس وسيعلم الكفار لمن عقبى الدار

translation: And those who disbelieve say, 'You are not a messenger.' Say, 'Sufficient is Allah as a Witness between me and you, and [the witness of] whoever has knowledge of the Scripture.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad's response to the accusations of the disbelievers who denied his prophethood. The verse emphasizes that Allah's testimony and the testimony of those who are well-versed in the scriptures are sufficient to affirm the truth of Muhammad's mission. It underscores the reliance on divine and scholarly validation over the rejection by those who refuse to believe, highlighting the confidence and assurance that comes from divine support and knowledge.
orig: ويقول الذين كفروا لست مرسلا قل كفى بالله شهيدا بيني وبينكم ومن عنده علم الكتاب

translation: Alif, Lam, Ra. [This is] a Book which We have revealed to you, that you might bring mankind out of darknesses into the light by permission of their Lord - to the path of the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the purpose of the Qur'an as a divine guidance sent to Prophet Muhammad. It is meant to lead people from the ignorance and confusion (darknesses) of disbelief and sin to the clarity and righteousness (light) of faith and obedience to God. This transformation is enabled by God's permission, guiding individuals to follow the path that leads to Him, characterized by His attributes of might and praise. The use of 'Alif, Lam, Ra' at the beginning is one of the mysterious letters (Muqatta'at) whose meanings are known only to God, serving to draw attention to the divine origin of the message.
orig: الر كتاب أنزلناه إليك لتخرج الناس من الظلمات إلى النور بإذن ربهم إلى صراط العزيز الحميد

translation: Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth. And woe to the disbelievers from a severe punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty of Allah over all creation, encompassing everything in the heavens and the earth. It serves as a reminder of His omnipotence and ownership. The latter part of the verse warns those who disbelieve in Allah of the severe consequences they will face due to their rejection of faith. It underscores the gravity of disbelief and the inevitable punishment that awaits the disbelievers, highlighting the urgency of embracing faith and righteousness.
orig: الله الذي له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وويل للكافرين من عذاب شديد

translation: Those who prefer the life of this world to the Hereafter and avert [people] from the way of Allah, seeking to make it crooked - those are in extreme error.
interpretation: This verse criticizes those who prioritize worldly gains and pleasures over spiritual and eternal rewards, and who actively obstruct others from following the path of righteousness and truth as prescribed by Allah. Such individuals not only mislead themselves but also corrupt the path for others, leading them astray from divine guidance. Their actions are described as severely misguided, indicating a deep moral and spiritual deviation.
orig: الذين يستحبون الحياة الدنيا على الآخرة ويصدون عن سبيل الله ويبغونها عوجا أولئك في ضلال بعيد

translation: And We sent not a Messenger except with the language of his people, to make (things) clear for them. Then Allah misleads whom He wills and guides whom He wills. And He is the All-Mighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine wisdom in sending messengers who speak the same language as their people, ensuring clear communication of the divine message. It reflects Allah's sovereignty in guiding or misleading individuals according to His will, emphasizing His attributes of power and wisdom in managing the affairs of creation.
orig: وما أرسلنا من رسول إلا بلسان قومه ليبين لهم فيضل الله من يشاء ويهدي من يشاء وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: And indeed, We sent Moses with Our signs, [saying], 'Bring out your people from darknesses into the light and remind them of the days of Allah.' Indeed, in that are signs for everyone patient and grateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the mission of Prophet Moses, which was to guide his people from ignorance and oppression (darkness) to knowledge and righteousness (light). The 'days of Allah' refer to significant historical events that demonstrate God's power and mercy, serving as reminders for the people. The verse highlights that such divine messages and historical lessons are particularly meaningful for those who exhibit patience and gratitude, qualities that enable them to appreciate and benefit from these signs.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا موسى بآياتنا أن أخرج قومك من الظلمات إلى النور وذكرهم بأيام الله إن في ذلك لآيات لكل صبار شكور

translation: And [remember] when Moses said to his people, 'Remember the favor of Allah upon you when He saved you from the people of Pharaoh, who were afflicting you with the worst torment and were slaughtering your sons and keeping your women alive. And in that was a great trial from your Lord.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder to the Israelites of the immense favor and deliverance granted to them by Allah through the leadership of Moses. It highlights the severe oppression they endured under Pharaoh's rule, characterized by brutal torture, the killing of their sons, and the sparing of their daughters for exploitation. The mention of this historical event as a 'great trial' underscores that their suffering was not without purpose; it was a test of their faith and patience, designed to strengthen their reliance on Allah and to prepare them for future challenges. This narrative encourages believers to reflect on past trials as lessons in gratitude and steadfastness, recognizing divine intervention and mercy in their deliverance.
orig: وإذ قال موسى لقومه اذكروا نعمة الله عليكم إذ أنجاكم من آل فرعون يسومونكم سوء العذاب ويذبحون أبناءكم ويستحيون نساءكم وفي ذلكم بلاء من ربكم عظيم

translation: And [remember] when your Lord proclaimed, 'If you are grateful, I will surely increase you [in favor]; but if you deny, indeed, My punishment is severe.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of gratitude towards Allah. It suggests that expressing thankfulness for the blessings bestowed by Allah will lead to an increase in those blessings. Conversely, ingratitude or denial of these blessings will result in severe punishment. The verse serves as a reminder of the reciprocal relationship between the Creator and the creation, highlighting the moral and spiritual consequences of one's actions.
orig: وإذ تأذن ربكم لئن شكرتم لأزيدنكم ولئن كفرتم إن عذابي لشديد

translation: And Moses said, 'If you should disbelieve, you and whoever is on the earth - then indeed, Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the self-sufficiency and independence of Allah from the belief or disbelief of His creation. Moses is conveying that even if all the people on earth were to reject faith, it would not diminish Allah's greatness or His attributes of being free from all needs and worthy of all praise. It underscores the idea that human acceptance or rejection of faith does not affect Allah's sovereignty or His inherent qualities.
orig: وقال موسى إن تكفروا أنتم ومن في الأرض جميعا فإن الله لغني حميد

translation: Has there not come to you the news of those before you - the people of Noah, 'Ad, and Thamud, and those after them? None knows them but Allah. Their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they put their hands in their mouths and said, 'Indeed, we disbelieve in that with which you have been sent, and indeed we are, about that to which you invite us, in disquieting doubt.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder and a warning to the contemporaries of the Prophet Muhammad about the fate of previous nations who rejected their prophets. The mention of the people of Noah, 'Ad, and Thamud, along with others unknown except to Allah, underscores the universality of divine messages and the recurring pattern of disbelief. The action of putting their hands in their mouths symbolizes their rejection and refusal to accept the truth, despite the clear signs and proofs presented by their messengers. The verse highlights the stubbornness and doubt of these nations, which ultimately led to their destruction, serving as a lesson for those who hear the Qur'an to heed its message and avoid a similar fate.
orig: ألم يأتكم نبأ الذين من قبلكم قوم نوح وعاد وثمود والذين من بعدهم لا يعلمهم إلا الله جاءتهم رسلهم بالبينات فردوا أيديهم في أفواههم وقالوا إنا كفرنا بما أرسلتم به وإنا لفي شك مما تدعوننا إليه مريب

translation: Their messengers said, 'Is there doubt about Allah, the Creator of the heavens and the earth? He calls you to forgive your sins and to delay you for a specified term.' They said, 'You are but humans like us, wanting to turn us away from what our forefathers worshipped. So bring us a clear authority.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the dialogue between the messengers of God and their people, emphasizing the disbelief and skepticism of the people towards the message of monotheism. The messengers assert the undeniable existence and power of Allah as the Creator, urging the people to repent and believe in order to attain forgiveness and a prolonged life. In response, the people's rejection is rooted in their attachment to ancestral traditions and their demand for a tangible proof or miracle, reflecting a deeper resistance to change and acceptance of divine guidance. This interaction underscores the challenge faced by prophets in conveying the message of God against entrenched societal norms and beliefs.
orig: قالت رسلهم أفي الله شك فاطر السماوات والأرض يدعوكم ليغفر لكم من ذنوبكم ويؤخركم إلى أجل مسمى قالوا إن أنتم إلا بشر مثلنا تريدون أن تصدونا عما كان يعبد آباؤنا فأتونا بسلطان مبين

translation: Their messengers said to them, 'We are only human beings like you, but Allah bestows His favor upon whom He wills of His servants. It is not for us to bring you any authority except by the permission of Allah. And upon Allah let the believers rely.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the humility and humanity of the prophets, emphasizing that they are ordinary humans chosen by Allah to convey His message. It highlights the divine authority behind their mission, as they can only act with Allah's permission. The verse also encourages believers to place their trust in Allah alone, reinforcing the theme of reliance on divine will and guidance.
orig: قالت لهم رسلهم إن نحن إلا بشر مثلكم ولكن الله يمن على من يشاء من عباده وما كان لنا أن نأتيكم بسلطان إلا بإذن الله وعلى الله فليتوكل المؤمنون

translation: And what is there to prevent us from putting our trust in Allah, when He has guided us to our ways? And we will surely endure patiently whatever harm you may cause us. And upon Allah let those who would rely put their trust.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unwavering faith and patience of believers in the face of adversity. It highlights that trust in Allah is justified because He provides guidance and support. The verse encourages steadfastness and reliance on Allah alone, especially when facing persecution or hardship, as a demonstration of true faith and submission to divine will.
orig: وما لنا ألا نتوكل على الله وقد هدانا سبلنا ولنصبرن على ما آذيتمونا وعلى الله فليتوكل المتوكلون

translation: And those who disbelieved said to their messengers, 'We will surely drive you out of our land, or you must return to our religion.' So their Lord inspired to them, 'We will surely destroy the wrongdoers.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the resistance faced by the prophets and messengers from the disbelievers, who threatened to expel them unless they conformed to their idolatrous practices. It underscores the unwavering support and divine promise of protection and justice from Allah to His messengers, assuring them that the oppressors and wrongdoers will ultimately face destruction. This serves as a reassurance to believers facing persecution and a reminder of the ultimate triumph of truth over falsehood.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا لرسلهم لنخرجنكم من أرضنا أو لتعودن في ملتنا فأوحى إليهم ربهم لنهلكن الظالمين

translation: And We will surely settle you in the land after them. That is for him who fears My position and fears My threat.
interpretation: This verse promises the believers that they will inherit the land from those who disbelieved before them, as a reward for their piety and fear of Allah's punishment. It emphasizes the importance of fearing Allah's position and His warnings, indicating that such fear is a key to receiving divine favor and blessings.
orig: ولنسكننكم الأرض من بعدهم ذلك لمن خاف مقامي وخاف وعيد

translation: And they sought a judgment, and every tyrant obstinate was disappointed.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate failure of those who arrogantly oppose divine will. It emphasizes that no matter how powerful or stubborn a tyrant may be, their efforts to challenge or undermine God's decree will inevitably lead to their disappointment and defeat. The verse serves as a reminder of the futility of resisting divine justice and the certainty of divine retribution against oppressors.
orig: واستفتحوا وخاب كل جبار عنيد

translation: Behind him is Hell, and he will be given to drink from a boiling spring.
interpretation: This verse describes the punishment awaiting the disbelievers in the Hereafter. The imagery of Hell being behind them signifies that it is their ultimate destination, inescapable and ever-present. The mention of being given to drink from a boiling spring, or 'maa' sadiid', emphasizes the torment and suffering they will endure, as this water is not for refreshment but for punishment, intensifying their agony.
orig: من ورائه جهنم ويسقى من ماء صديد

translation: He will gulp it but will hardly be able to swallow it, and death will come to him from every direction, yet he will not die, and before him is a harsh torment.
interpretation: This verse describes the torment of the disbeliever in the Hereafter. The imagery of struggling to drink a scalding liquid symbolizes the intense suffering and the inability to escape the punishment. The mention of death approaching from all sides yet not being able to die illustrates the eternal nature of the punishment, emphasizing the severity and the hopelessness of the situation. The 'harsh torment' that follows indicates that the suffering will intensify, serving as a warning of the consequences of disbelief and sin.
orig: يتجرعه ولا يكاد يسيغه ويأتيه الموت من كل مكان وما هو بميت ومن ورائه عذاب غليظ

translation: The example of those who disbelieve in their Lord is that their deeds are like ashes which the wind blows forcefully on a stormy day; they are unable to gain anything from what they have earned. That is the extreme error.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the futility and ultimate worthlessness of the actions of those who reject faith in Allah. Just as ashes are scattered and lost in a storm, the efforts and deeds of disbelievers are rendered meaningless and unbeneficial in the Hereafter. The metaphor emphasizes the transient nature of worldly achievements when they are not aligned with divine guidance, leading to a state of profound misguidance described as 'the extreme error.'
orig: مثل الذين كفروا بربهم أعمالهم كرماد اشتدت به الريح في يوم عاصف لا يقدرون مما كسبوا على شيء ذلك هو الضلال البعيد

translation: Have you not seen that Allah created the heavens and the earth with truth? If He wills, He can remove you and bring forth a new creation.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute power and sovereignty over creation. It reminds us that the creation of the heavens and the earth is not arbitrary but based on truth and purpose. The possibility of Allah replacing humanity with a new creation serves as a reminder of our accountability and the transient nature of our existence, urging us to reflect on our actions and live in accordance with His will.
orig: ألم تر أن الله خلق السماوات والأرض بالحق إن يشأ يذهبكم ويأت بخلق جديد

translation: And that is not difficult for Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence of Allah, indicating that nothing is too hard or burdensome for Him to accomplish. It reassures believers of Allah's infinite power and capability to manage all affairs, no matter how complex or challenging they may seem.
orig: وما ذلك على الله بعزيز

translation: And they will be brought forth before Allah, all together. Then the weak will say to those who were arrogant, 'Indeed, we were your followers, so can you avail us anything against the punishment of Allah?' They will say, 'If Allah had guided us, we would have guided you. It is all the same for us whether we show impatience or are patient, there is no escape for us.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the Day of Judgment when all people are presented before Allah. It highlights the realization and regret of the weak who followed the arrogant leaders. The weak, upon seeing the consequences of their actions, seek help from their former leaders, only to be told that guidance comes from Allah alone, and now, in the face of divine judgment, neither group can escape their fate. This underscores the theme of personal accountability and the futility of seeking intercession from others when facing Allah's judgment.
orig: وبرزوا لله جميعا فقال الضعفاء للذين استكبروا إنا كنا لكم تبعا فهل أنتم مغنون عنا من عذاب الله من شيء قالوا لو هدانا الله لهديناكم سواء علينا أجزعنا أم صبرنا ما لنا من محيص

translation: And Satan will say when the matter has been concluded, 'Indeed, Allah had promised you the promise of truth. And I promised you, but I betrayed you. I had no authority over you except that I invited you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me; blame yourselves. I cannot be called to your aid, nor can you be called to my aid. Indeed, I deny your association of me [with Allah] before. Indeed, the wrongdoers will have a painful punishment.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate accountability of individuals for their actions. Satan admits that he had no real power over humans except through deception and temptation. He reminds them that Allah's promise was true, while his own promises were false. This serves as a warning that humans must take responsibility for their choices, as they cannot blame Satan for their misdeeds on the Day of Judgment. The verse underscores the themes of personal accountability, the futility of seeking help from false deities, and the severe consequences awaiting those who engage in wrongdoing and idolatry.
orig: وقال الشيطان لما قضي الأمر إن الله وعدكم وعد الحق ووعدتكم فأخلفتكم وما كان لي عليكم من سلطان إلا أن دعوتكم فاستجبتم لي فلا تلوموني ولوموا أنفسكم ما أنا بمصرخكم وما أنتم بمصرخي إني كفرت بما أشركتمون من قبل إن الظالمين لهم عذاب أليم

translation: And admit those who believe and do righteous deeds to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever by permission of their Lord. Their greeting therein will be, 'Peace.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the reward awaiting believers who perform good deeds: eternal residence in Paradise. The gardens with flowing rivers symbolize the abundance and everlasting nature of the blessings in the afterlife. The greeting of 'Peace' signifies the state of harmony, safety, and tranquility that believers will experience in Paradise, granted by the permission of Allah, highlighting His mercy and sovereignty over the ultimate reward.
orig: وأدخل الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها بإذن ربهم تحيتهم فيها سلام

translation: Have you not seen how Allah presents an example, [comparing] a good word to a good tree, whose root is firm and whose branches are in the sky?
interpretation: This verse illustrates the power and growth of a righteous statement or belief, likened to a strong tree. The 'good word' represents faith or a beneficial utterance that, like a tree with deep roots and high-reaching branches, is firmly established in the heart and extends its positive influence widely, reaching towards the heavens in spiritual growth and connection with the divine.
orig: ألم تر كيف ضرب الله مثلا كلمة طيبة كشجرة طيبة أصلها ثابت وفرعها في السماء

translation: It brings forth its fruit at all times, by the leave of its Lord. And Allah sets forth parables for mankind that they may remember.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the concept of divine providence and the continuous provision from Allah, symbolized by a tree that bears fruit consistently by Allah's permission. The use of the tree as a metaphor emphasizes the idea that sustenance and blessings are always available to those who seek them, reflecting Allah's mercy and care. Additionally, the verse highlights the educational purpose of parables in the Qur'an, intended to remind and guide people towards mindfulness and gratitude.
orig: تؤتي أكلها كل حين بإذن ربها ويضرب الله الأمثال للناس لعلهم يتذكرون

translation: And the example of an evil word is like an evil tree, uprooted from the surface of the earth, having no stability.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the transient and unstable nature of falsehood or evil speech. Just as an evil tree is uprooted and has no firm foundation, evil words or ideas lack substance and permanence, quickly being exposed and discarded. This serves as a reminder of the inherent weakness and eventual downfall of evil, encouraging believers to shun such words and adhere to truth and righteousness.
orig: ومثل كلمة خبيثة كشجرة خبيثة اجتثت من فوق الأرض ما لها من قرار

translation: Allah will keep firm those who believe, with the word that stands firm in this world and in the Hereafter. And Allah will cause to go astray those who are wrongdoers, and Allah does what He wills.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine support and stability granted to believers through their faith, which remains steadfast both in the temporal world and the eternal afterlife. Conversely, it highlights the divine justice where those who engage in wrongdoing are led astray as a consequence of their actions. The verse concludes by affirming Allah's absolute sovereignty and will, indicating that all outcomes are ultimately under His control.
orig: يثبت الله الذين آمنوا بالقول الثابت في الحياة الدنيا وفي الآخرة ويضل الله الظالمين ويفعل الله ما يشاء

translation: Have you not seen those who exchanged the favor of Allah for disbelief and caused their people to descend into the house of ruin?
interpretation: This verse criticizes those who, despite receiving blessings and guidance from Allah, choose to reject faith and lead their community astray into destruction. It highlights the grave consequences of ingratitude and misguidance, emphasizing the moral and spiritual downfall that results from turning away from Allah's favors.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين بدلوا نعمت الله كفرا وأحلوا قومهم دار البوار

translation: Hell, they will roast in it, and what a miserable abode!
interpretation: This verse describes the severe punishment of Hell, emphasizing the torment and suffering that the inhabitants will endure. It serves as a warning to believers about the consequences of disbelief and sinful actions, highlighting the importance of righteousness and obedience to God's commands to avoid such a dreadful fate.
orig: جهنم يصلونها وبئس القرار

translation: And they have taken for Allah rivals, to lead away from His Path. Say: Enjoy yourselves, for indeed, your destination is the Fire.
interpretation: This verse highlights the grave error of those who attribute partners to Allah, leading people astray from the true path of Islam. It serves as a warning and a reminder of the consequences of such actions, indicating that temporary worldly enjoyment will ultimately lead to eternal damnation in the Fire. The command to 'say' emphasizes the role of the Prophet Muhammad in conveying this message, urging believers to remain steadfast on the right path and to warn others of the dangers of shirk (polytheism).
orig: وجعلوا لله أندادا ليضلوا عن سبيله قل تمتعوا فإن مصيركم إلى النار

translation: Say to My servants who have believed to establish prayer and spend from what We have provided them, secretly and publicly, before a Day comes in which there will be no trade or friendship.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of regular prayer and charitable giving as acts of worship and gratitude towards Allah. It instructs believers to perform these acts consistently, both in private and in public, as a means of spiritual growth and preparation for the Day of Judgment. The mention of a day with no trade or friendship underscores the urgency and inevitability of this day, urging believers to prioritize their spiritual duties over worldly transactions and relationships.
orig: قل لعبادي الذين آمنوا يقيموا الصلاة وينفقوا مما رزقناهم سرا وعلانية من قبل أن يأتي يوم لا بيع فيه ولا خلال

translation: Allah is He Who created the heavens and the earth and sends down water from the sky, and by it brings forth fruits as provision for you; and He has made the ships subservient to you, that they may sail through the sea by His command; and He has made the rivers subservient to you.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's omnipotence and His role as the sole Creator and Sustainer of the universe. It highlights His provision for humanity through natural phenomena like rain, which nurtures the earth to produce fruits for sustenance. Additionally, the verse points out Allah's favor towards humans by making elements of nature, such as ships and rivers, serve them, illustrating His command over all aspects of creation and His benevolence in facilitating human life and movement.
orig: الله الذي خلق السماوات والأرض وأنزل من السماء ماء فأخرج به من الثمرات رزقا لكم وسخر لكم الفلك لتجري في البحر بأمره وسخر لكم الأنهار

translation: And He has subjected for you the sun and the moon, constant [in their courses], and He has subjected for you the night and the day.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine power and mercy of Allah, illustrating how He has made the celestial bodies and the cycle of day and night serve humanity. It emphasizes the purposeful design of the universe to benefit mankind, encouraging gratitude and recognition of Allah's omnipotence and benevolence in sustaining life and providing guidance through the natural order.
orig: وسخر لكم الشمس والقمر دائبين وسخر لكم الليل والنهار

translation: And He gave you of all that you asked of Him. And if you count the favors of Allah, you will not be able to number them. Indeed, mankind is unjust and ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the boundless generosity of Allah, indicating that He provides for humanity beyond their requests. It highlights human nature's tendency towards ingratitude and injustice, as despite the innumerable blessings from Allah, people often fail to recognize or appreciate them, leading to a sense of entitlement and forgetfulness of Allah's continuous favors.
orig: وآتاكم من كل ما سألتموه وإن تعدوا نعمت الله لا تحصوها إن الإنسان لظلوم كفار

translation: And [mention] when Abraham said, 'My Lord, make this city [Mecca] secure and keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols.'
interpretation: Abraham's prayer highlights his deep concern for the spiritual well-being of his descendants, emphasizing the importance of monotheism and the rejection of idolatry. His request for the city of Mecca to be made secure reflects a desire for a safe environment that supports the practice of true faith, free from the corruption of idol worship.
orig: وإذ قال إبراهيم رب اجعل هذا البلد آمنا واجنبني وبني أن نعبد الأصنام

translation: My Lord, indeed they have led astray many among mankind. So whoever follows me - then he is of me; and whoever disobeys me - indeed, You are Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: In this verse, Prophet Adam (peace be upon him) is acknowledging the misguidance caused by Iblis and his followers among humanity. He is expressing his submission to God, recognizing that those who follow his guidance are part of his community, while those who disobey him are still under God's mercy and forgiveness. This reflects the dual aspects of divine justice and mercy, emphasizing that even those who stray can seek forgiveness from the All-Forgiving and Merciful God.
orig: رب إنهن أضللن كثيرا من الناس فمن تبعني فإنه مني ومن عصاني فإنك غفور رحيم

translation: Our Lord, I have settled some of my descendants in an uncultivated valley near Your Sacred House, our Lord, that they may establish prayer. So make hearts among the people incline toward them and provide them with fruits that they might be grateful.
interpretation: This verse reflects the prayer of Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) when he left his family in the barren valley of Mecca. It signifies a profound act of faith and submission to God's will, trusting that God will provide for them despite the inhospitable environment. The request for hearts to incline towards them indicates a hope for the establishment of a community that would be supported and visited by others, ultimately leading to the development of Mecca as a center of pilgrimage. The mention of fruits symbolizes God's provision and sustenance, emphasizing the importance of gratitude for divine blessings.
orig: ربنا إني أسكنت من ذريتي بواد غير ذي زرع عند بيتك المحرم ربنا ليقيموا الصلاة فاجعل أفئدة من الناس تهوي إليهم وارزقهم من الثمرات لعلهم يشكرون

translation: Our Lord, indeed You know what we conceal and what we declare, and nothing is hidden from Allah on the earth or in the heaven.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience of Allah, highlighting that He is fully aware of all things, whether they are hidden or revealed. It serves as a reminder to believers of the importance of sincerity in their actions and thoughts, knowing that Allah sees and knows everything, encouraging them to be mindful of their deeds in both private and public spheres.
orig: ربنا إنك تعلم ما نخفي وما نعلن وما يخفى على الله من شيء في الأرض ولا في السماء

translation: Praise be to Allah, Who has granted me in old age Ishmael and Isaac. Indeed, my Lord is the Hearer of supplication.
interpretation: This verse expresses gratitude to Allah for the blessing of children in old age, emphasizing the belief in Allah's responsiveness to prayers. It highlights the theme of divine favor and the importance of recognizing and appreciating Allah's blessings, no matter the timing or circumstances. The mention of Ishmael and Isaac also underscores the continuity of prophethood and the fulfillment of divine promises.
orig: الحمد لله الذي وهب لي على الكبر إسماعيل وإسحاق إن ربي لسميع الدعاء

translation: My Lord, make me an establisher of prayer, and from my descendants. Our Lord, and accept my supplication.
interpretation: This verse is a prayer from Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) asking Allah to enable him and his descendants to be steadfast in performing the prayers. It reflects a deep desire for spiritual consistency and a legacy of devotion. The request for Allah to accept his supplication underscores the importance of divine acceptance in one's worship and life, highlighting the humility and dependence on Allah's mercy and guidance.
orig: رب اجعلني مقيم الصلاة ومن ذريتي ربنا وتقبل دعاء

translation: Our Lord, forgive me and my parents and the believers on the Day of Reckoning.
interpretation: This verse is a supplication asking for God's forgiveness not only for oneself but also for one's parents and all believers. It emphasizes the importance of intercessory prayer and communal solidarity in seeking divine mercy, especially on the Day of Judgment when accountability for one's actions is paramount. It reflects a deep sense of humility and recognition of the interconnectedness of the faithful in their spiritual journey.
orig: ربنا اغفر لي ولوالدي وللمؤمنين يوم يقوم الحساب

translation: And never think that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do. He only delays them for a Day when eyes will stare [in horror].
interpretation: This verse reassures believers that Allah is fully aware of the actions of the wrongdoers, even if it seems that they are not immediately punished. The delay in their punishment is not due to Allah's unawareness or negligence, but rather a strategic postponement until the Day of Judgment. On that day, the severity of the situation will be so intense that people's eyes will be wide open in shock and horror, emphasizing the gravity and inevitability of divine justice.
orig: ولا تحسبن الله غافلا عما يعمل الظالمون إنما يؤخرهم ليوم تشخص فيه الأبصار

translation: Reclining on couches, their heads not drooping, their eyes not lowered, and their hearts void of emptiness.
interpretation: This verse describes the state of the righteous in Paradise, emphasizing their comfort and contentment. The reclining on couches signifies ultimate relaxation and luxury. The mention of their heads not drooping and eyes not lowered indicates a state of alertness and joy, free from any worry or shame. The phrase 'their hearts void of emptiness' suggests that their hearts are filled with satisfaction and fulfillment, devoid of any worldly concerns or spiritual emptiness, reflecting the complete peace and happiness they experience in the afterlife.
orig: مهطعين مقنعي رءوسهم لا يرتد إليهم طرفهم وأفئدتهم هواء

translation: And warn the people of a Day when the punishment will come upon them, and those who have wronged will say, 'Our Lord, delay us for a short term; we will answer Your call and follow the messengers.' Had you not sworn before that there would be no departure for you?
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder and warning to all people about the inevitability of the Day of Judgment, when the consequences of one's actions will be fully realized. It highlights the desperation and regret of those who have committed wrongdoings, as they plead for a brief delay to amend their ways and follow the guidance of the messengers. However, this plea comes too late, as they had previously sworn confidently that they would never face such an end, reflecting their denial and underestimation of divine justice. The verse underscores the themes of accountability, the futility of last-minute repentance when one's fate is sealed, and the importance of heeding divine warnings and guidance in one's lifetime.
orig: وأنذر الناس يوم يأتيهم العذاب فيقول الذين ظلموا ربنا أخرنا إلى أجل قريب نجب دعوتك ونتبع الرسل أولم تكونوا أقسمتم من قبل ما لكم من زوال

translation: And you dwelt in the dwellings of those who wronged themselves, and it became clear to you how We dealt with them, and We presented for you examples.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder and a warning to the believers about the consequences of following in the footsteps of those who have gone astray. By living in the homes and lands of previous nations who were destroyed due to their transgressions, the believers are given a tangible example of God's justice and power. The verse emphasizes that God has clearly shown through historical examples how He punishes those who wrong themselves by disobeying His commands. These examples are meant to serve as lessons and deterrents, urging the believers to adhere to righteousness and avoid the sins that led to the downfall of past communities.
orig: وسكنتم في مساكن الذين ظلموا أنفسهم وتبين لكم كيف فعلنا بهم وضربنا لكم الأمثال

translation: And they plotted their plot, and their plot is with Allah, even if their plot were such that the mountains could be moved by it.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility and ultimate failure of the schemes devised by those who oppose God's will. It emphasizes that no matter how cunning or powerful the plots of the adversaries might seem, they are ultimately under God's control and oversight. The reference to mountains being moved signifies the perceived strength and impact of their plans, yet it underscores that even such formidable schemes are insignificant before God's power and wisdom.
orig: وقد مكروا مكرهم وعند الله مكرهم وإن كان مكرهم لتزول منه الجبال

translation: So never think that Allah will fail in His promise to His messengers. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Owner of Retribution.
interpretation: This verse reassures believers not to doubt the fulfillment of Allah's promises to His messengers. It emphasizes Allah's attributes of strength and justice, indicating that His power is unmatched and His retribution is certain. This serves to strengthen the faith of believers, reminding them that Allah's promises are guaranteed and His justice will prevail, no matter the circumstances.
orig: فلا تحسبن الله مخلف وعده رسله إن الله عزيز ذو انتقام

translation: The Day when the earth will be changed to other than the earth, and the heavens as well, and they will come forth before Allah, the One, the Irresistible.
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Judgment, when the fundamental nature of the earth and the heavens will be transformed into something entirely different from their current state. This transformation signifies the end of the world as we know it and the beginning of a new reality. On this day, all beings will be presented before Allah, who is described as 'the One, the Irresistible,' emphasizing His absolute unity and overwhelming power over all creation. The verse underscores the inevitability of facing Allah and the complete submission to His will that will characterize that day.
orig: يوم تبدل الأرض غير الأرض والسماوات وبرزوا لله الواحد القهار

translation: And you will see the criminals on that Day chained together in shackles.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the Day of Judgment, emphasizing the fate of those who have committed crimes or sins during their lifetime. The imagery of the criminals being chained together in shackles serves as a powerful metaphor for the consequences of their actions, highlighting the inescapable nature of divine justice and accountability. It underscores the theme of retribution and the ultimate manifestation of God's justice, where no wrongdoer can escape the consequences of their deeds.
orig: وترى المجرمين يومئذ مقرنين في الأصفاد

translation: Their garments will be of pitch, and fire will cover their faces.
interpretation: This verse describes the punishment of the disbelievers in Hell, where their clothing is made from a tar-like substance, symbolizing their impurity and the unbearable nature of their punishment. The fire covering their faces signifies the intense and inescapable torment they will endure, emphasizing the severity of their fate as a consequence of their rejection of faith.
orig: سرابيلهم من قطران وتغشى وجوههم النار

translation: So that Allah may reward every soul for what it has earned. Indeed, Allah is swift in account.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of individual accountability in Islam. It underscores that every person will be recompensed by Allah based on their deeds, highlighting the justice and fairness of divine judgment. The phrase "Allah is swift in account" reassures believers of the efficiency and promptness with which Allah will evaluate and reward or punish actions, reinforcing the importance of living a righteous life with the certainty of an impending and just reckoning.
orig: ليجزي الله كل نفس ما كسبت إن الله سريع الحساب

translation: This is a proclamation for the people, and to warn them thereby, and to inform them that He is the one and only God, and that those endowed with understanding may take heed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universal message of the Qur'an, which serves as a warning and a reminder to all of humanity about the oneness of God. It highlights the responsibility of believers to convey this message, and stresses that the Qur'an is a source of guidance particularly for those who possess wisdom and understanding, urging them to reflect deeply on its teachings.
orig: هذا بلاغ للناس ولينذروا به وليعلموا أنما هو إله واحد وليذكر أولو الألباب

translation: Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the Book and a clear Qur'an.
interpretation: The opening letters 'Alif, Lam, Ra' are among the mysterious letters (muqatta'at) whose meanings are known only to Allah, serving as a divine signature to the Qur'an. The verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is a clear and manifest scripture, indicating its clarity in guidance and its role as a comprehensive book of divine wisdom and law.
orig: الر تلك آيات الكتاب وقرآن مبين

translation: Perhaps those who disbelieve wish that they were Muslims.
interpretation: This verse suggests that deep down, even those who reject faith might harbor a desire to embrace Islam, indicating an internal recognition of the truth of the religion despite their outward denial.
orig: ربما يود الذين كفروا لو كانوا مسلمين

translation: Leave them to eat and enjoy themselves and be diverted by [false] hope; for they will come to know.
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who are heedless of God's signs and indulge in worldly pleasures should be left to their devices for now. It emphasizes a temporary allowance for them to continue in their ways, driven by false hopes, but warns that eventually, they will face the consequences of their actions and realize the truth.
orig: ذرهم يأكلوا ويتمتعوا ويلههم الأمل فسوف يعلمون

translation: And We did not destroy any town except that it had a known decree.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine justice and order in the world. It indicates that every community or civilization has a predetermined time and reason for its destruction, known to Allah. This serves as a reminder that the rise and fall of nations are not random but are part of a divine plan, where each community is given the opportunity to heed warnings and change its ways before facing the consequences of its actions.
orig: وما أهلكنا من قرية إلا ولها كتاب معلوم

translation: No nation can anticipate its term, nor delay it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine decree and the predetermined timing of events for each nation or community. It underscores that no matter how powerful or influential a group may be, they cannot hasten or postpone the fate that Allah has set for them. This serves as a reminder of the ultimate control and authority of Allah over the affairs of the world, encouraging believers to trust in divine wisdom and timing.
orig: ما تسبق من أمة أجلها وما يستأخرون

translation: And they said, 'O you upon whom the Reminder has been bestowed, indeed you are mad.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the rejection and mockery faced by Prophet Muhammad by his contemporaries who accused him of being insane because of the divine revelations he received. It reflects the common human tendency to dismiss or ridicule what is not understood or what challenges the status quo, illustrating the resistance faced by messengers of truth throughout history.
orig: وقالوا يا أيها الذي نزل عليه الذكر إنك لمجنون

translation: If you do not bring the angels to us, if you are of the truthful ones.
interpretation: This verse challenges the Prophet Muhammad to produce a miracle by summoning angels as proof of his truthfulness. It reflects the skepticism and demand for tangible evidence from those who doubted his prophethood, illustrating the human tendency to seek visible signs despite the presence of other forms of divine guidance.
orig: لو ما تأتينا بالملائكة إن كنت من الصادقين

translation: We send not the angels down except with the truth; and then they would not be respited.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that angels are sent by Allah only for just and true purposes, such as delivering messages or executing divine commands. It also indicates that once angels are sent, there is no delay or respite in their mission, underscoring the immediate and certain nature of divine intervention when it occurs.
orig: ما ننزل الملائكة إلا بالحق وما كانوا إذا منظرين

translation: Indeed, it is We who sent down the Qur'an and indeed, We will be its guardians.
interpretation: This verse asserts the divine origin of the Qur'an, emphasizing that Allah Himself revealed it. It also provides reassurance to believers that the Qur'an's purity and integrity will be preserved by Allah against any corruption or alteration, reflecting the belief in its miraculous inimitability and eternal relevance.
orig: إنا نحن نزلنا الذكر وإنا له لحافظون

translation: And We have certainly sent [messengers] before you among the sects of the former peoples.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the continuity of divine guidance throughout history. It reassures the Prophet Muhammad that he is part of a long line of messengers sent by Allah to guide different nations and communities. This connection to previous prophets serves to validate his mission and to remind believers that Allah's message has been consistent across time, tailored to the needs of various groups.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا من قبلك في شيع الأولين

translation: And no messenger came to them except that they mocked him.
interpretation: This verse highlights the recurring pattern of disbelief and mockery faced by prophets and messengers sent by Allah. It reflects the human tendency to reject divine guidance out of arrogance, ignorance, or a refusal to change their ways, emphasizing the challenge messengers face in conveying the truth to a resistant audience.
orig: وما يأتيهم من رسول إلا كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: Thus do We let it enter the hearts of the criminals.
interpretation: This verse illustrates how Allah allows disbelief and corruption to permeate the hearts of those who persistently engage in sinful acts. It suggests a divine process where the more one indulges in wrongdoing, the more their heart becomes hardened and distant from the truth, ultimately leading them deeper into their criminal state.
orig: كذلك نسلكه في قلوب المجرمين

translation: They do not believe in it, while the practice of the ancients has already passed.
interpretation: This verse highlights the disbelief of certain people in the message of the Qur'an, despite the fact that the fate of previous nations who rejected their prophets is well-known. It serves as a reminder that the consequences of disbelief are not new; they have been witnessed throughout history. The verse urges reflection on past examples to encourage faith and warns against following in the footsteps of those who were punished for their rejection of divine guidance.
orig: لا يؤمنون به وقد خلت سنة الأولين

translation: And if We opened upon them a gate from the heaven, and they continued to ascend therein,
interpretation: This verse suggests that even if God were to perform a miraculous sign like opening a gate to heaven, the disbelievers would still not believe. It highlights the stubbornness and denial of those who reject faith, indicating that their disbelief is not due to a lack of evidence but rather a refusal to accept the truth despite clear signs.
orig: ولو فتحنا عليهم بابا من السماء فظلوا فيه يعرجون

translation: They said, "Our eyes have only been dazzled. Rather, we are a people affected by magic."
interpretation: This verse reflects the denial and rationalization of the people who were confronted with a clear sign or miracle. Instead of accepting the truth, they attributed their perception of the event to being temporarily blinded or dazzled, suggesting a natural explanation for a supernatural occurrence. They further claimed to be under the influence of magic, indicating their refusal to acknowledge the divine nature of what they witnessed. This highlights human tendencies to reject or misinterpret divine signs due to preconceived notions or fear of the implications of accepting the truth.
orig: لقالوا إنما سكرت أبصارنا بل نحن قوم مسحورون

translation: And We have placed within the heaven great stars and have beautified it for the observers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine craftsmanship in the creation of the universe, specifically pointing to the stars as both functional and decorative elements. The 'great stars' or constellations serve as navigational aids, guiding travelers, while also enhancing the aesthetic appeal of the night sky for those who observe it. This reflects the idea that the universe is not only created with purpose but also with beauty, inviting humans to reflect on the majesty and artistry of the Creator.
orig: ولقد جعلنا في السماء بروجا وزيناها للناظرين

translation: And We have protected it from every accursed devil.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the Qur'an is safeguarded by Allah from any interference or corruption by devils or evil forces, emphasizing its purity and divine protection.
orig: وحفظناها من كل شيطان رجيم

translation: Except him who snatches a hearing, and then a clear flaming fire pursues him.
interpretation: This verse refers to the jinn who attempt to eavesdrop on the conversations of the angels in the heavens. When they try to steal information, they are chased away by a bright, flaming fire, symbolizing divine protection of the celestial realm and the punishment for unauthorized intrusion.
orig: إلا من استرق السمع فأتبعه شهاب مبين

translation: And the earth We have spread out, and We have cast therein firm mountains, and We have caused to grow therein every kind of balanced plant.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's power and wisdom in the creation of the earth. The spreading out of the earth signifies its vastness and the suitability for life. The mountains are described as firm, indicating their role in stabilizing the earth's surface. The mention of plants being balanced suggests a divine order and harmony in the ecosystem, where every element is created in precise measure to sustain life. This reflects the meticulous care and planning in Allah's creation, encouraging reflection on the balance and purpose in the natural world.
orig: والأرض مددناها وألقينا فيها رواسي وأنبتنا فيها من كل شيء موزون

translation: And We have made for you therein means of living and [for] those for whom you are not providers.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's provision and sustenance for all creatures. It emphasizes that Allah has created the earth with resources that not only sustain humans but also other beings for whom humans are not responsible. This underscores the concept of divine providence and the interconnectedness of all life, reminding believers of their dependence on Allah's mercy and the need to be grateful and responsible stewards of the earth's resources.
orig: وجعلنا لكم فيها معايش ومن لستم له برازقين

translation: And there is no thing except that with Us are its treasuries, and We do not send it down except in a known measure.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and meticulous control of Allah over all aspects of creation. It indicates that every resource and provision in the universe is stored in divine treasuries under Allah's command, and He dispenses these resources in precise and predetermined amounts according to His wisdom and plan. This highlights the concept of divine providence and the belief that nothing in the universe occurs randomly or without purpose.
orig: وإن من شيء إلا عندنا خزائنه وما ننزله إلا بقدر معلوم

translation: And We send the winds as pollinators, and We send down from the sky water, then We give it to you to drink, and you are not the ones to store it.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine system of providence and sustenance. The winds are described as pollinators, illustrating their role in the natural cycle that leads to the growth of plants, which is essential for life. The subsequent sending of rain from the sky further emphasizes God's control over the elements that sustain life. The verse concludes by reminding humans that they have no control over these natural resources; they are merely recipients of God's mercy and provision. This serves to foster a sense of humility and gratitude towards the Creator, acknowledging His omnipotence and benevolence in providing for all living beings.
orig: وأرسلنا الرياح لواقح فأنزلنا من السماء ماء فأسقيناكموه وما أنتم له بخازنين

translation: And indeed, it is We who give life and cause death, and We are the Inheritors.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and sovereignty of Allah over life and death. It reminds believers that Allah alone has the authority to grant life, to take it away, and ultimately, to inherit everything after the demise of all creation. This underscores the transient nature of worldly life and the eternal dominion of Allah, encouraging a focus on the hereafter and submission to His will.
orig: وإنا لنحن نحيي ونميت ونحن الوارثون

translation: And We have certainly given knowledge to those before you from among you, and We have certainly given knowledge to those after you.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the continuity and universality of divine guidance across different generations and communities. It reassures believers that God has bestowed knowledge and wisdom upon people in the past, present, and future, ensuring that guidance is always available to those who seek it. This reflects the Qur'anic principle that God's message is timeless and inclusive, reaching all humanity throughout history.
orig: ولقد علمنا المستقدمين منكم ولقد علمنا المستأخرين

translation: And indeed, your Lord will gather them. Indeed, He is Wise, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty of the Day of Resurrection where Allah will gather all people. It reassures believers of Allah's ultimate authority and wisdom in managing the affairs of the universe, and His complete knowledge of all things, which ensures that the gathering and judgment will be just and fair.
orig: وإن ربك هو يحشرهم إنه حكيم عليم

translation: And indeed, We created man from sounding clay from altered black mud.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the humble and earthly origin of human beings, reminding us that despite our potential for greatness, we are fundamentally created from the same material as the earth, which should instill in us a sense of humility and gratitude towards our Creator.
orig: ولقد خلقنا الإنسان من صلصال من حمإ مسنون

translation: And the jinn, We created them before from scorching fire.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the jinn were created from a different elemental substance than humans, specifically from a fire that is intensely hot and fierce. This highlights the unique nature of jinn as beings distinct from humans, emphasizing their origin and composition as part of the diverse creation of Allah.
orig: والجان خلقناه من قبل من نار السموم

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when your Lord said to the angels, 'Indeed, I am going to create a human being from clay from an altered black mud.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine announcement of the creation of Adam, emphasizing God's power and sovereignty over creation. The use of 'clay from an altered black mud' underscores the humble origins of humanity, reminding us of our earthly beginnings and the miraculous nature of our creation from simple, base materials. This serves to instill a sense of humility and gratitude towards God for the gift of life.
orig: وإذ قال ربك للملائكة إني خالق بشرا من صلصال من حمإ مسنون

translation: So when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My spirit, then fall down to him in prostration.
interpretation: This verse highlights the moment of the creation of Adam, where Allah shapes him and then instills in him a part of His spirit, signifying the honor and unique status of humans among creation. The command for the angels to prostrate to Adam underscores the respect and submission owed to humans as bearers of divine spirit, emphasizing human dignity and the responsibility that comes with it.
orig: فإذا سويته ونفخت فيه من روحي فقعوا له ساجدين

translation: So the angels prostrated, all of them together
interpretation: This verse illustrates the obedience and submission of the angels to Allah's command. When Allah ordered the angels to prostrate to Adam, they complied without hesitation, demonstrating their complete submission to Allah's will. This act of prostration signifies the respect and honor given to Adam as the first human and as a creation favored by Allah.
orig: فسجد الملائكة كلهم أجمعون

translation: Except Iblis, he refused to be with those who prostrated.
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and disobedience of Iblis, who, out of pride, refused to prostrate to Adam as commanded by Allah. It underscores the theme of free will and the consequences of choosing to disobey divine commands, illustrating Iblis's fall from grace due to his refusal to submit to Allah's will.
orig: إلا إبليس أبى أن يكون مع الساجدين

translation: He said, 'O Iblis, what is [the matter] with you that you are not with those who prostrate?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the moment when Allah questions Iblis about his refusal to prostrate to Adam, emphasizing Iblis's disobedience and setting the stage for his eventual fall from grace. It underscores the theme of obedience to divine command and the consequences of arrogance and rebellion.
orig: قال يا إبليس ما لك ألا تكون مع الساجدين

translation: He said, 'I will not prostrate to a human whom You created from sounding clay, from altered black mud.'
interpretation: This verse reflects Iblis's (Satan's) arrogance and refusal to obey Allah's command to prostrate to Adam. It highlights his pride in his own creation from fire, as opposed to Adam's creation from clay, showing his disobedience and the beginning of his enmity towards humanity.
orig: قال لم أكن لأسجد لبشر خلقته من صلصال من حمإ مسنون

translation: He said, "Then get out of it, for indeed, you are stoned."
interpretation: This verse signifies the expulsion of Iblis (Satan) from Paradise after he refused to prostrate to Adam. The term "stoned" (rajim) here symbolizes being cursed and driven away, reflecting the severe consequence of disobedience and arrogance against God's command. It underscores the theme of accountability for one's actions and the consequences of defying divine orders.
orig: قال فاخرج منها فإنك رجيم

translation: And indeed, upon you is the curse until the Day of Judgment.
interpretation: This verse indicates a perpetual state of condemnation and divine disapproval directed towards the individual or entity it addresses, lasting until the final day of reckoning. It underscores the severity and the enduring nature of the consequence for the actions or state of being of the cursed, emphasizing accountability and the long-term impact of one's deeds in the eyes of God.
orig: وإن عليك اللعنة إلى يوم الدين

translation: He said, 'My Lord, then defer me until the Day they are resurrected.'
interpretation: In this verse, Satan pleads with Allah to grant him respite until the Day of Resurrection. This request reflects Satan's acknowledgment of his impending doom but also his determination to continue misleading humanity until the very end. It underscores the theme of free will and the ongoing battle between good and evil, illustrating Satan's role as a persistent adversary to mankind's spiritual journey.
orig: قال رب فأنظرني إلى يوم يبعثون

translation: He said, 'Then you are of those who are respited.'
interpretation: This verse indicates that the speaker, likely referring to Allah, is granting a temporary delay or respite to the individual being addressed. This respite is not a forgiveness or absolution, but rather a postponement of the consequences or punishment that the individual is due to face. It suggests a period of time given for the person to reflect on their actions or possibly to repent, yet with the understanding that the eventual accountability remains inevitable.
orig: قال فإنك من المنظرين

translation: Until the Day of the appointed time
interpretation: This verse refers to the predetermined time set by Allah for the Day of Judgment, emphasizing that all events and lifespans are measured until this inevitable and known time to Allah alone.
orig: إلى يوم الوقت المعلوم

translation: He said, 'My Lord, because You have led me astray, I will surely make [sin] attractive to them on the earth, and I will mislead them all.'
interpretation: This verse reflects Iblis's (Satan's) declaration of defiance and his intention to lead humans astray after being expelled from Paradise. It highlights the theme of free will and the ongoing spiritual battle between good and evil, emphasizing Iblis's role as a tempter who seeks to corrupt human beings by making sin appear appealing.
orig: قال رب بما أغويتني لأزينن لهم في الأرض ولأغوينهم أجمعين

translation: Except Your servants among them who are sincere.
interpretation: This verse highlights that while many may be led astray, those who remain sincere in their devotion and faith to Allah are protected from misguidance. It emphasizes the importance of sincerity in faith and obedience to Allah, suggesting that true believers, who are pure in their intentions and actions, will be safeguarded by Allah from the influences of evil.
orig: إلا عبادك منهم المخلصين

translation: He said, 'This is my straight path.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the declaration of a clear and direct path set by a prophet or messenger, indicating guidance that is straightforward and true, leading to righteousness and divine favor.
orig: قال هذا صراط علي مستقيم

translation: Indeed, over My servants you have no authority, except those who follow you among the deviators.
interpretation: This verse asserts the limited power of Satan over the believers. It emphasizes that Satan has no control over those who are truly devoted to God, indicating the protective nature of faith. However, it also warns that Satan can influence those who stray from the right path, highlighting the importance of vigilance and adherence to divine guidance to avoid falling into misguidance.
orig: إن عبادي ليس لك عليهم سلطان إلا من اتبعك من الغاوين

translation: And indeed, Hell is the promised place for them all.
interpretation: This verse underscores the certainty and inevitability of Hell as the final destination for those who reject faith and righteousness. It serves as a stark reminder of the consequences of one's actions and the ultimate accountability before God.
orig: وإن جهنم لموعدهم أجمعين

translation: It has seven gates; for each gate there is a designated portion.
interpretation: This verse describes the structure of Hell, indicating that it is divided into seven levels or gates, each reserved for a specific group of sinners based on the severity of their deeds. This illustrates the justice and order in the punishment, where individuals are assigned to different sections according to their actions in life.
orig: لها سبعة أبواب لكل باب منهم جزء مقسوم

translation: Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and springs.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the reward awaiting the righteous in the afterlife. The "gardens and springs" symbolize a state of eternal peace, abundance, and joy, reflecting the ultimate fulfillment and satisfaction that comes from living a life of piety and righteousness according to Islamic teachings.
orig: إن المتقين في جنات وعيون

translation: Enter it in peace, safe [and secure].
interpretation: This verse signifies the ultimate reward for the righteous, where they are welcomed into Paradise with peace and security. It emphasizes the state of tranquility and safety that believers will experience upon entering the hereafter, reflecting the culmination of their faith and good deeds in a serene and protected environment.
orig: ادخلوها بسلام آمنين

translation: And We will remove whatever is in their hearts of resentment, [so they will be] brothers, on thrones facing each other.
interpretation: This verse describes the state of the believers in Paradise, where Allah will purify their hearts from any feelings of resentment or ill will towards one another. This purification will enable them to enjoy a state of brotherhood and harmony, sitting together on thrones arranged in a way that they can face each other, fostering an atmosphere of closeness and mutual respect.
orig: ونزعنا ما في صدورهم من غل إخوانا على سرر متقابلين

translation: No fatigue will touch them therein, nor will they be removed from it.
interpretation: This verse describes the state of the righteous in Paradise, emphasizing that they will experience no hardship or exhaustion. It also assures that their stay in Paradise is permanent, indicating the eternal nature of their reward and the absence of any possibility of being expelled from this blissful state.
orig: لا يمسهم فيها نصب وما هم منها بمخرجين

translation: Inform My servants that I am the Forgiving, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's attributes of forgiveness and mercy, encouraging believers to seek repentance and trust in His boundless compassion. It serves as a reminder of the divine promise of forgiveness for those who turn to Him sincerely, fostering a relationship based on hope and divine love.
orig: نبئ عبادي أني أنا الغفور الرحيم

translation: And that My punishment - it is the painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity and intensity of the punishment that Allah warns about. It serves as a reminder of the consequences of disobeying Allah's commands, highlighting that His punishment is not only inevitable but also extremely painful and distressing. This is intended to instill a sense of fear and urgency in believers to adhere to the right path and avoid actions that would incur such a severe retribution.
orig: وأن عذابي هو العذاب الأليم

translation: And inform them about the guest of Ibrahim
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of the angels who visited Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) as guests. The mention of this event serves to remind believers of the miraculous nature of these visitors, who were angels sent by Allah to deliver the news of the birth of Ibrahim's son, Ishaq (Isaac), and to warn of the impending destruction of the people of Lut (Lot). The narrative underscores themes of divine hospitality, the power of Allah to bring about the extraordinary, and the importance of obedience to divine commands.
orig: ونبئهم عن ضيف إبراهيم

translation: When they entered upon him and said, 'Peace,' he said, 'Indeed, we are afraid of you.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the natural human reaction of fear or apprehension when confronted with the unknown or unexpected. It highlights the importance of maintaining peace and good intentions, as the greeting of peace from the visitors should ideally alleviate fears, yet Abraham's initial response reflects a common human emotion of caution towards strangers.
orig: إذ دخلوا عليه فقالوا سلاما قال إنا منكم وجلون

translation: They said, 'Do not be anxious; we give you glad tidings of a boy possessing knowledge.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the angels' reassurance to Abraham, promising him the birth of his son Isaac, who would be endowed with wisdom and knowledge. It underscores the divine promise and the prophetic lineage, highlighting the importance of knowledge and its transmission through generations.
orig: قالوا لا توجل إنا نبشرك بغلام عليم

translation: He said: "Do you give me glad tidings even though old age has come upon me? Of what, then, are you giving me glad tidings?"
