interpretation: This verse reflects the initial disbelief and astonishment of Prophet Ibrahim when angels informed him of the forthcoming birth of his son, Isaac, despite his old age. It highlights the human reaction to divine promises that seem impossible by worldly standards, emphasizing the theme of faith in God's omnipotence and His ability to transcend natural laws.
orig: قال أبشرتموني على أن مسني الكبر فبم تبشرون

translation: They said, 'You have given us good news, so do not be of those who despair.'
interpretation: This verse reflects a moment of encouragement and optimism from the people towards a prophet or messenger, urging him not to lose hope despite the challenges he faces. It emphasizes the importance of maintaining faith and perseverance in the face of adversity, as the good news they received signifies divine support and promise.
orig: قالوا بشرناك بالحق فلا تكن من القانطين

translation: He said, "And who despairs of the mercy of his Lord except those who are astray?"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining hope in God's mercy. It suggests that only those who are misguided and have lost their way would give up on the possibility of receiving God's forgiveness and compassion. It serves as a reminder to believers to never lose faith in God's boundless mercy, no matter the circumstances.
orig: قال ومن يقنط من رحمة ربه إلا الضالون

translation: He said: "What is your errand, O messengers?"
interpretation: This verse reflects Pharaoh's initial reaction to the messengers sent by Allah, showcasing his arrogance and curiosity about their purpose. It highlights the moment of confrontation where Pharaoh, feeling his authority challenged, seeks to understand the mission of the prophets, thereby setting the stage for the ensuing dialogue and conflict.
orig: قال فما خطبكم أيها المرسلون

translation: They said, 'We have been sent to a people of criminals.'
interpretation: This verse indicates the purpose of the angels' mission, which was to deliver a divine message or enact punishment upon a community known for their persistent wrongdoing and transgression against God's laws. It underscores the theme of divine justice and the consequences of moral corruption.
orig: قالوا إنا أرسلنا إلى قوم مجرمين

translation: Except the family of Lot; indeed, we will save them all,
interpretation: This verse indicates that despite the impending destruction of the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah due to their immoral actions, God's mercy extends to the family of Lot. It underscores the theme of divine protection and salvation for the righteous amidst widespread corruption, emphasizing that God's judgment can differentiate between the guilty and the innocent, even within the same community or family.
orig: إلا آل لوط إنا لمنجوهم أجمعين

translation: Except his wife, We have decreed that she is of those who will stay behind.
interpretation: This verse indicates that while Lot's family was to be saved from the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah, his wife was an exception. She was not to be saved because she was aligned with the corrupt ways of the people and did not believe in the message of Lot. This serves as a reminder that familial ties do not guarantee salvation; it is one's faith and actions that determine their fate.
orig: إلا امرأته قدرنا إنها لمن الغابرين

translation: So when the messengers came to the family of Lut
interpretation: This verse indicates the arrival of divine messengers to the Prophet Lut, signaling the commencement of a critical event in the narrative of Lut's people. It underscores the moment when divine intervention becomes imminent, highlighting the gravity of the situation and the impending judgment upon the community due to their persistent rejection of divine guidance.
orig: فلما جاء آل لوط المرسلون

translation: He said, "Indeed, you are a people who are ungrateful."
interpretation: This verse highlights the Prophet's frustration and disappointment with his people for their persistent denial and rejection of the divine message. It underscores the theme of ingratitude towards the blessings and guidance provided by Allah, reflecting a broader commentary on human nature's tendency to overlook or reject truth and favor.
orig: قال إنكم قوم منكرون

translation: They said, "Rather, we have come to you with that about which they were disputing."
interpretation: This verse indicates that the speakers are presenting themselves as bearers of truth or clarification regarding a matter that was previously under contention or dispute among others. It suggests a resolution or a decisive statement intended to settle the ongoing debates or disagreements.
orig: قالوا بل جئناك بما كانوا فيه يمترون

translation: And We have brought you the truth, and indeed We are truthful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin and truthfulness of the Qur'an. It asserts that the message delivered to the Prophet Muhammad is from Allah, and thus, it is the absolute truth. The phrase 'and indeed We are truthful' reinforces the credibility and reliability of the divine message, assuring believers of its authenticity and urging them to trust and follow its guidance.
orig: وأتيناك بالحق وإنا لصادقون

translation: So set out with your family in a portion of the night, and follow behind them, and let not any among you look back, and proceed to where you are commanded.
interpretation: This verse is a divine command to Prophet Lot to leave the sinful city of Sodom with his family during the night, ensuring they do not look back, symbolizing a complete departure from sin and corruption. It emphasizes obedience to God's command and the urgency of escaping from environments of moral decay.
orig: فأسر بأهلك بقطع من الليل واتبع أدبارهم ولا يلتفت منكم أحد وامضوا حيث تؤمرون

translation: And We decreed for him that command, that the last of these will be cut off in the morning.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Musa (Moses) and his encounter with the magicians of Pharaoh. The "command" mentioned is the divine instruction given to Musa, assuring him that the power and influence of Pharaoh and his magicians would be severed by the morning. This signifies the ultimate triumph of truth over falsehood, as the magicians, upon witnessing the miracles of Musa, acknowledged the truth of his message and were subsequently defeated. The phrase "cut off in the morning" symbolizes the swift and decisive nature of this victory, emphasizing the inevitability of divine justice and the downfall of oppressors.
orig: وقضينا إليه ذلك الأمر أن دابر هؤلاء مقطوع مصبحين

translation: And the people of the city came, rejoicing.
interpretation: This verse describes the arrival of the people of the city in a state of joy and happiness, likely in anticipation of good news or a celebration. It reflects the human emotion of hope and eagerness for positive outcomes.
orig: وجاء أهل المدينة يستبشرون

translation: He said: 'These are my guests, so do not disgrace me.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the importance of hospitality and protection of guests, as Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) is asking his people not to shame him by mistreating his guests, the angels, who came to him in the guise of men. It underscores the moral duty to honor and safeguard those who seek refuge and hospitality in one's home.
orig: قال إن هؤلاء ضيفي فلا تفضحون

translation: And fear Allah and do not be ashamed
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining a reverent fear of Allah, which should guide one's actions and decisions. It warns against allowing shame or embarrassment to deter one from fulfilling religious obligations or doing what is right in the eyes of Allah. The message is to prioritize divine approval over societal judgment.
orig: واتقوا الله ولا تخزون

translation: They said, "Did we not forbid you from [associating with] the world?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the reaction of the disbelievers to the Prophet Muhammad's message. They are reminding him that they had previously warned him against interfering with their societal norms and traditions, which they considered as their 'world'. This reflects their resistance to change and their rejection of the new message of Islam, illustrating the challenge faced by the Prophet in conveying the divine message to a society deeply entrenched in its ways.
orig: قالوا أولم ننهك عن العالمين

translation: He said, 'These are my daughters, if you are to do anything.'
interpretation: In this verse, Lot offers his daughters to the people of Sodom as a means to divert them from their immoral intentions towards his guests. This act underscores Lot's desperation and his attempt to protect the angels, who were disguised as men, from the townspeople's homosexual desires. It reflects the societal values and the extreme measures taken to uphold hospitality and protect guests, which are highly valued in Islamic ethics.
orig: قال هؤلاء بناتي إن كنتم فاعلين

translation: By your life, they wander blindly in their intoxication.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the spiritual blindness and confusion of those who are heedless of God's guidance, metaphorically described as being intoxicated. It suggests that their state of ignorance and misguidance is so profound that they are unaware of their own condition, wandering aimlessly without true purpose or direction.
orig: لعمرك إنهم لفي سكرتهم يعمهون

translation: So the shriek seized them at sunrise.
interpretation: This verse describes the sudden and complete destruction of a community by a divine punishment, referred to as 'the shriek,' which came upon them unexpectedly at the break of dawn. The timing at sunrise emphasizes the abruptness and the inescapable nature of God's judgment, serving as a reminder of the consequences of disbelief and disobedience.
orig: فأخذتهم الصيحة مشرقين

translation: So We made the highest part [of the city] its lowest and rained upon them stones of hard clay.
interpretation: This verse describes the divine punishment inflicted upon the people of Lot, where God overturned their city, causing the highest parts to become the lowest, symbolizing a complete reversal of their societal order. The raining of stones of hard clay signifies a targeted and severe destruction, emphasizing the consequence of their rejection of divine guidance and moral corruption.
orig: فجعلنا عاليها سافلها وأمطرنا عليهم حجارة من سجيل

translation: Indeed, in that are signs for those who discern.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the phenomena or events being referred to contain clear indications and lessons that can be understood and appreciated by individuals who possess insight and the ability to reflect deeply on the signs of God in the universe.
orig: إن في ذلك لآيات للمتوسمين

translation: And indeed, it is a path of ascent.
interpretation: This verse refers to the path of righteousness and spiritual ascent that believers must follow. It signifies the continuous journey towards moral and spiritual elevation, which is stable and enduring, guiding individuals towards closeness to Allah.
orig: وإنها لبسبيل مقيم

translation: Indeed, in that is a sign for the believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the events or phenomena described in the preceding context serve as a clear indication or proof of God's power and wisdom, which should be recognized and reflected upon by those who have faith. It encourages believers to see the deeper meanings and lessons in the world around them as signs of divine guidance and truth.
orig: إن في ذلك لآية للمؤمنين

translation: And indeed, the people of the Wood were wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse refers to the people of the Wood (Aṣḥāb al-Aykah), who were a community that rejected the message of their prophet, Shu'aib. The term 'wrongdoers' (ẓālimīn) here indicates that they were unjust in their actions, particularly in their rejection of divine guidance and their oppression of others. This serves as a reminder of the consequences of denying the truth and the importance of following the messengers of God.
orig: وإن كان أصحاب الأيكة لظالمين

translation: So We took vengeance on them, and indeed, both were upon a clear highway.
interpretation: This verse reflects the divine justice of Allah, where punishment is meted out to those who transgressed. The 'clear highway' symbolizes the straightforward path of righteousness that the two individuals (likely referring to the prophets or righteous figures mentioned in the context) were following, highlighting their moral clarity and guidance in contrast to the wrongdoing of those punished.
orig: فانتقمنا منهم وإنهما لبإمام مبين

translation: And the people of Al-Hijr denied the messengers
interpretation: This verse refers to the people of Thamud, who lived in the region of Al-Hijr and rejected the message brought by the Prophet Salih. It highlights a recurring theme in the Qur'an about the consequences of denying divine messengers and the importance of heeding their warnings.
orig: ولقد كذب أصحاب الحجر المرسلين

translation: And We gave them Our signs, but they were turning away from them.
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of divine guidance and human response. It suggests that Allah provided clear signs and evidence of His existence and guidance to a people, yet they consciously chose to ignore or reject these signs. This turning away reflects a deliberate act of disbelief or negligence, emphasizing human free will and the consequences of rejecting divine guidance.
orig: وآتيناهم آياتنا فكانوا عنها معرضين

translation: And they used to carve from the mountains houses, feeling secure.
interpretation: This verse refers to the people of Thamud, who were known for their advanced skills in carving homes out of the mountains. The phrase 'feeling secure' highlights their false sense of security and arrogance, as they believed their impressive constructions made them invulnerable, yet they were ultimately punished for their disbelief and disobedience to Allah.
orig: وكانوا ينحتون من الجبال بيوتا آمنين

translation: So the blast seized them at sunrise.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the sudden and complete destruction of a community as a consequence of divine retribution. The use of 'the blast' symbolizes a powerful and immediate punishment from Allah, emphasizing the inevitability and swiftness of divine justice. The timing 'at sunrise' adds a layer of irony, as it contrasts the beginning of a new day, typically associated with hope and renewal, with the abrupt end of the people's lives due to their disobedience.
orig: فأخذتهم الصيحة مصبحين

translation: So their earnings did not avail them.
interpretation: This verse underscores the futility of worldly gains in the face of divine judgment. It suggests that the material wealth and achievements accumulated by individuals are of no benefit when it comes to their spiritual salvation or standing before God. The verse serves as a reminder of the transient nature of worldly possessions and the importance of focusing on righteous deeds and faith, which are the true measures of value in the hereafter.
orig: فما أغنى عنهم ما كانوا يكسبون

translation: And We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except in truth, and indeed, the Hour is coming; so forgive with gracious forgiveness.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the purposeful creation of the universe by Allah, indicating that everything was created with a specific reason and not in vain. The mention of the Hour (the Day of Judgment) being imminent serves as a reminder of the accountability that follows this life. The command to forgive with gracious forgiveness suggests that, in light of the ultimate truth and the coming judgment, believers should practice forgiveness generously, reflecting the mercy and justice of Allah in their interactions.
orig: وما خلقنا السماوات والأرض وما بينهما إلا بالحق وإن الساعة لآتية فاصفح الصفح الجميل

translation: Indeed, your Lord is the Creator, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the dual attributes of Allah as both the Creator of all existence and the possessor of complete knowledge. It reassures believers of Allah's omnipotence and omniscience, highlighting that He not only brings everything into being but also understands every aspect of His creation in its entirety.
orig: إن ربك هو الخلاق العليم

translation: And indeed, We have given you seven of the often-repeated [verses] and the great Qur'an.
interpretation: This verse refers to the granting of the seven verses of Surah Al-Fatihah, known as 'Al-Mathani' (the oft-repeated), and the entirety of the Qur'an, described as 'Al-Qur'an Al-'Azim' (the Great Qur'an). The significance lies in the divine bestowal of these essential components of Islamic scripture, highlighting their importance and the completeness of the guidance provided to the Prophet Muhammad and, by extension, to all believers.
orig: ولقد آتيناك سبعا من المثاني والقرآن العظيم

translation: Do not extend your eyes towards that with which We have provided some of them, and do not grieve over them, and lower your wing for the believers.
interpretation: This verse advises the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to maintain humility and not to covet the worldly possessions that God has given to others. It emphasizes the importance of not being envious and instead focusing on compassion and humility towards believers, symbolized by lowering one's wing, which suggests a nurturing and protective attitude towards the faithful.
orig: لا تمدن عينيك إلى ما متعنا به أزواجا منهم ولا تحزن عليهم واخفض جناحك للمؤمنين

translation: And say, "Indeed, I am the clear warner."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of Prophet Muhammad as a clear and unambiguous messenger, warning people about the consequences of their actions and the impending judgment. It highlights the clarity and transparency of the message he was sent to deliver, urging people to heed the warning and mend their ways before it is too late.
orig: وقل إني أنا النذير المبين

translation: Just as We sent down upon those who divided
interpretation: This verse refers to the divine revelation that was sent to previous nations who divided themselves into factions, emphasizing that the Qur'an, like previous scriptures, is a guidance sent by Allah to unify and guide people. It serves as a reminder that division and sectarianism are contrary to the purpose of divine revelation, which aims to bring people together under the worship of one God.
orig: كما أنزلنا على المقتسمين

translation: Those who have made the Qur'an into portions
interpretation: This verse refers to those who have divided the Qur'an into segments, taking some parts and rejecting others, thereby distorting its holistic message and guidance. It criticizes the selective adherence to the Qur'an, where individuals or groups choose to follow certain verses that align with their desires while ignoring or dismissing others that challenge their beliefs or practices.
orig: الذين جعلوا القرآن عضين

translation: And by your Lord, We will surely question them all.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty and comprehensiveness of the Day of Judgment, where every individual will be held accountable for their actions. It underscores God's promise and oath by His Lordship that no one will escape being questioned about their deeds, reinforcing the concept of divine justice and individual responsibility.
orig: فوربك لنسألنهم أجمعين

translation: from what they used to do
interpretation: This phrase emphasizes that the consequences individuals face in the afterlife are directly linked to their actions during their earthly life. It underscores the Islamic principle of accountability, where every deed, good or bad, is recorded and will be judged by Allah. The use of 'used to do' indicates a reflection on past actions, suggesting that one's consistent behavior and choices shape their ultimate fate.
orig: عما كانوا يعملون

translation: So declare what you are commanded and turn away from the polytheists.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad to openly proclaim the message of Islam as he has been commanded by Allah, without fear or hesitation. It also advises him to disregard the opposition and rejection from those who associate partners with Allah, emphasizing the importance of steadfastness in conveying the divine message despite resistance from polytheists.
orig: فاصدع بما تؤمر وأعرض عن المشركين

translation: Indeed, We are sufficient for you against the mockers.
interpretation: This verse reassures the Prophet Muhammad that God will protect him from those who mock and ridicule him. It emphasizes divine support and sufficiency, indicating that no matter how intense the opposition or mockery from disbelievers, God's protection and aid are more than enough for the Prophet to continue his mission with confidence and resilience.
orig: إنا كفيناك المستهزئين

translation: Those who set up another deity alongside Allah will soon come to know.
interpretation: This verse warns those who associate partners with Allah, indicating that they will eventually realize the gravity of their error and face the consequences of their actions in the hereafter. It emphasizes the certainty of divine justice and the ultimate truth of monotheism.
orig: الذين يجعلون مع الله إلها آخر فسوف يعلمون

translation: And indeed We know that your heart is constricted by what they say.
interpretation: This verse acknowledges the emotional distress that Prophet Muhammad felt due to the rejection and mockery from his people. It highlights the human aspect of the Prophet, showing that even he, as a chosen messenger, experienced feelings of sadness and frustration when faced with opposition. This serves to comfort believers, indicating that feeling distressed by opposition to one's faith is a natural response, yet it is recognized and understood by Allah.
orig: ولقد نعلم أنك يضيق صدرك بما يقولون

translation: So glorify the praises of your Lord and be of those who prostrate themselves.
interpretation: This verse encourages the believer to engage in the act of glorifying Allah through praise and to actively participate in the physical act of prostration during prayer. It emphasizes the importance of both verbal and physical expressions of worship, highlighting a complete submission to God. By doing so, one aligns themselves with the community of worshippers who demonstrate their humility and devotion to the Creator.
orig: فسبح بحمد ربك وكن من الساجدين

translation: And worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of steadfastness in worship and devotion to Allah throughout one's life, until the moment of death, which is referred to as 'the certainty.' It encourages believers to remain committed to their faith and religious duties without wavering, highlighting the lifelong nature of submission to God.
orig: واعبد ربك حتى يأتيك اليقين

translation: The command of Allah has come, so do not hasten it. Glory be to Him and exalted is He above what they associate [with Him].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes patience and trust in the divine timing of Allah's decree. It instructs believers not to rush or seek to hasten the fulfillment of Allah's command, as His plan unfolds in its perfect time. The phrase 'Glory be to Him and exalted is He above what they associate [with Him]' serves as a reminder of Allah's transcendence and purity, rejecting any form of polytheism or association of partners with Him. This call to patience and affirmation of monotheism is meant to strengthen the faith of the believers and encourage them to maintain steadfastness in their belief and worship of the one true God.
orig: أتى أمر الله فلا تستعجلوه سبحانه وتعالى عما يشركون

translation: The angels descend with the Spirit by the command of their Lord upon whom He wills of His servants, [saying], 'Warn that there is no deity except Me; so fear Me.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine mechanism of revelation where angels, along with the Spirit (often interpreted as Gabriel), are sent by Allah's command to specific chosen servants. The purpose of this divine intervention is to convey the fundamental message of Tawheed (the oneness of God), urging people to worship only Allah and to be conscious of Him through fear and reverence. It emphasizes the exclusivity of Allah's divinity and the importance of monotheism in Islamic theology.
orig: ينزل الملائكة بالروح من أمره على من يشاء من عباده أن أنذروا أنه لا إله إلا أنا فاتقون

translation: He created the heavens and the earth with truth. He is exalted above what they associate [with Him].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the monotheistic principle of Islam, asserting that God alone created the universe with purpose and truth. The phrase 'with truth' suggests that the creation is not random or meaningless but is imbued with divine wisdom and order. The latter part of the verse serves as a refutation of polytheism, elevating God above any false associations or partners that humans might attribute to Him, reinforcing the purity and singularity of His divine nature.
orig: خلق السماوات والأرض بالحق تعالى عما يشركون

translation: He created man from a sperm-drop; then at once, he is a clear adversary.
interpretation: This verse highlights the paradox of human creation and behavior. Despite being created from something as humble and insignificant as a sperm-drop, humans often exhibit a sense of entitlement and opposition to divine guidance. The term 'clear adversary' suggests that humans, upon gaining consciousness and capability, frequently challenge or dispute the truth and the commands of their Creator, showcasing an inherent tendency towards contention and ingratitude.
orig: خلق الإنسان من نطفة فإذا هو خصيم مبين

translation: And the livestock - He created them for you; in them is warmth and benefits, and from them you eat.
interpretation: This verse highlights the multifaceted utility of livestock as a divine provision for humanity. It emphasizes that these animals are not only a source of food but also provide warmth and other benefits, illustrating the comprehensive nature of God's creation designed to meet various human needs. This underscores the importance of recognizing and appreciating the multiple ways in which Allah supports human life through His creation.
orig: والأنعام خلقها لكم فيها دفء ومنافع ومنها تأكلون

translation: And there is beauty in them for you when you bring them home and when you lead them to pasture.
interpretation: This verse highlights the aesthetic and functional value of livestock to humans. It points out the beauty found in the natural cycle of animal husbandry, from the moment the animals are brought back to their shelters to when they are allowed to graze freely. This reflects the broader theme in the Qur'an of appreciating the blessings and provisions provided by Allah, emphasizing the harmony between human life and the natural world.
orig: ولكم فيها جمال حين تريحون وحين تسرحون

translation: And they carry your loads to a land that you could not have reached except with great difficulty. Indeed, your Lord is Kind and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the blessings and mercy of Allah, who has provided humans with the means to travel and transport goods over long distances, which would otherwise be extremely challenging. The reference to camels or ships (implied by the context) as carriers of loads underscores the divine provision and ease granted to mankind. The mention of Allah as 'Kind and Merciful' emphasizes that these provisions are a manifestation of His compassion and care for His creation, encouraging gratitude and recognition of His benevolence.
orig: وتحمل أثقالكم إلى بلد لم تكونوا بالغيه إلا بشق الأنفس إن ربكم لرءوف رحيم

translation: And the horses, mules and donkeys, for you to ride and as an adornment; and He creates what you do not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the blessings of Allah in providing various animals for human use, such as horses, mules, and donkeys, which serve both practical purposes like transportation and aesthetic purposes as adornments. Additionally, it points to the vastness of Allah's creative power, indicating that He continues to create things beyond human knowledge, encouraging a sense of awe and humility in recognizing the limits of human understanding compared to the infinite creativity of the Creator.
orig: والخيل والبغال والحمير لتركبوها وزينة ويخلق ما لا تعلمون

translation: And upon Allah is the direction of the way, and among them are those who deviate; and if He willed, He could have guided you all.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the ultimate guidance and the correct path are determined by Allah alone. It acknowledges that while Allah has provided the way, some people will still choose to deviate from it due to their free will. The verse also highlights Allah's omnipotence by stating that if He so willed, He could guide everyone, underscoring the divine power and the mystery of why some are guided while others are not, which is part of the divine wisdom and plan.
orig: وعلى الله قصد السبيل ومنها جائر ولو شاء لهداكم أجمعين

translation: He it is Who sends down water from the sky, from which you have drink and from which are trees on which you pasture your herds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's role as the provider of sustenance through the natural cycle of rain. The water from the sky not only quenches human thirst but also nourishes the earth, leading to the growth of trees that serve as fodder for livestock. It highlights the interconnectedness of creation and the divine provision that sustains life, encouraging gratitude and recognition of Allah's mercy and power in the natural world.
orig: هو الذي أنزل من السماء ماء لكم منه شراب ومنه شجر فيه تسيمون

translation: He causes to grow for you thereby grain and olives and palm trees and grapes and from all [other] fruits. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who give thought.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's provision and sustenance for humanity through the growth of various crops and fruits, emphasizing the diversity and abundance of His blessings. It serves as a reminder and a sign for those who reflect deeply on the creation and order of the world, encouraging gratitude and contemplation of God's omnipotence and care.
orig: ينبت لكم به الزرع والزيتون والنخيل والأعناب ومن كل الثمرات إن في ذلك لآية لقوم يتفكرون

translation: And He has subjected for you the night and the day, and the sun and the moon, and the stars are subjected by His command. Indeed, in that are signs for a people who use reason.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine order and control over the natural phenomena, emphasizing that the alternation of night and day, and the movements of celestial bodies like the sun, moon, and stars, are all under Allah's command. These natural cycles are presented as signs of Allah's power and wisdom, intended to provoke thought and reflection among those who are inclined to reason and understand the deeper meanings behind creation.
orig: وسخر لكم الليل والنهار والشمس والقمر والنجوم مسخرات بأمره إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يعقلون

translation: And the things He has spread out for you on the earth, of varying colors; surely in this there is a sign for people who remember.
interpretation: This verse highlights the diversity and beauty of the earth's resources as a manifestation of God's creative power. It serves as a reminder for those who are mindful and reflective to recognize the signs of God's existence and benevolence in the natural world around them.
orig: وما ذرأ لكم في الأرض مختلفا ألوانه إن في ذلك لآية لقوم يذكرون

translation: And it is He who has subjected the sea for you, so that you may eat from it tender meat and extract from it ornaments that you wear. And you see the ships plowing through it, and [He subjected it] that you may seek of His bounty and perhaps you will be grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the blessings and provisions provided by Allah through the sea. It emphasizes the multifaceted utility of the sea, from providing food in the form of fresh meat, to resources for adornment, and as a means of transportation and trade. The mention of ships plowing through the sea symbolizes human ingenuity and the divine permission to harness natural elements for sustenance and prosperity. The verse calls upon believers to recognize and be thankful for these blessings, reminding them that all these benefits are a manifestation of Allah's grace and favor.
orig: وهو الذي سخر البحر لتأكلوا منه لحما طريا وتستخرجوا منه حلية تلبسونها وترى الفلك مواخر فيه ولتبتغوا من فضله ولعلكم تشكرون

translation: And He has cast into the earth firm mountains lest it should shake with you, and rivers and roads, that you may be guided.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's meticulous design of the earth to ensure stability and guidance for humanity. The mountains are described as anchors that prevent the earth from trembling, symbolizing the physical stability provided by Allah. The rivers and roads serve as means of guidance, both literally for navigation and metaphorically as paths towards righteousness and understanding. This verse encourages believers to recognize and appreciate the purposeful creation around them, which aids in their journey through life.
orig: وألقى في الأرض رواسي أن تميد بكم وأنهارا وسبلا لعلكم تهتدون

translation: And landmarks (signs) and by the stars they are guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine signs and guidance provided by Allah through natural phenomena. The 'landmarks' refer to the visible signs on Earth that help people navigate, while the 'stars' symbolize the celestial guidance that has been used for navigation throughout human history. Together, these elements illustrate how Allah has placed various forms of guidance in the universe to assist humanity in finding their way, both literally and metaphorically, reinforcing the concept of divine assistance and direction in life's journey.
orig: وعلامات وبالنجم هم يهتدون

translation: Is He who creates like one who does not create? Will you not then remember?
interpretation: This verse challenges the reader to reflect on the fundamental difference between the Creator, Allah, who has the power to bring things into existence, and those who cannot create anything. It urges believers to use their reason and memory to recognize the clear signs of Allah's creative power, prompting a deeper contemplation of His uniqueness and omnipotence.
orig: أفمن يخلق كمن لا يخلق أفلا تذكرون

translation: And if you should count the favors of Allah, you could not enumerate them. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the boundless nature of Allah's blessings upon humanity, suggesting that no matter how much one tries to count or recognize these blessings, they are beyond human capacity to fully comprehend or list. It serves as a reminder of Allah's infinite generosity and kindness. The mention of Allah being Forgiving and Merciful at the end of the verse underscores that despite our inability to fully appreciate His favors, Allah's forgiveness and mercy remain ever-present, encouraging a continuous state of gratitude and repentance.
orig: وإن تعدوا نعمة الله لا تحصوها إن الله لغفور رحيم

translation: And Allah knows what you conceal and what you reveal.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience of Allah, indicating that He is fully aware of the innermost secrets and thoughts of individuals, as well as their outward actions and declarations. It serves as a reminder to believers to be mindful of their intentions and deeds, both hidden and apparent, as nothing is hidden from Allah's knowledge.
orig: والله يعلم ما تسرون وما تعلنون

translation: And those they invoke besides Allah create nothing, and they [themselves] are created.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the powerlessness of idols and false deities. It underscores that these entities, which people might mistakenly worship or call upon, have no creative power whatsoever. They are themselves creations, fashioned by the true Creator, Allah. This highlights the fundamental error in polytheism and directs believers to recognize and worship only Allah, the sole Creator of all things.
orig: والذين يدعون من دون الله لا يخلقون شيئا وهم يخلقون

translation: Dead, not alive, and they do not perceive when they will be resurrected.
interpretation: This verse describes the state of those who are spiritually dead due to their disbelief or heedlessness. They are likened to the physically dead because they are unaware of the spiritual realities and the impending resurrection. The verse emphasizes their complete lack of awareness about when they will be brought back to life, highlighting the suddenness and unexpected nature of the resurrection for those who do not believe.
orig: أموات غير أحياء وما يشعرون أيان يبعثون

translation: Your god is one God. So those who do not believe in the Hereafter - their hearts are in denial, and they are arrogant.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness of God, a fundamental belief in Islam. It then addresses the spiritual condition of those who reject the concept of the Hereafter, suggesting that their disbelief stems from a heart that denies the truth and an attitude of arrogance. This denial and arrogance prevent them from accepting the reality of God's unity and the accountability in the afterlife.
orig: إلهكم إله واحد فالذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة قلوبهم منكرة وهم مستكبرون

translation: Indeed, Allah knows what they conceal and what they declare. Indeed, He does not love the arrogant.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's omniscience, highlighting that He is fully aware of the hidden intentions and actions of individuals, as well as those that are openly expressed. It serves as a reminder to believers to be sincere in their faith and actions, knowing that nothing is hidden from Allah. Additionally, the verse warns against arrogance, indicating that such a trait is detestable to Allah, encouraging humility and submission to His will.
orig: لا جرم أن الله يعلم ما يسرون وما يعلنون إنه لا يحب المستكبرين

translation: And when it is said to them, 'What has your Lord sent down?' They say, 'Legends of the former peoples.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the dismissive attitude of the disbelievers towards the revelations of the Quran. When confronted with the divine message, they reject it outright, labeling it as mere myths or legends from ancient times. This response reflects their unwillingness to engage with the truth and their preference for clinging to familiar falsehoods, illustrating a common human tendency to deny new revelations that challenge their existing beliefs.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم ماذا أنزل ربكم قالوا أساطير الأولين

translation: They will bear their own burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection, and also of the burdens of those whom they misled without knowledge. Evil indeed is that which they bear!
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the accountability and consequences of leading others astray. On the Day of Judgment, not only will individuals be responsible for their own sins, but they will also carry the weight of the sins of those they misguided. This highlights the severe repercussions of spreading falsehood or misguiding others, as it increases one's burden of sin. The verse serves as a warning against the grave mistake of misleading others, underscoring the moral and spiritual responsibility each person holds towards others in the community.
orig: ليحملوا أوزارهم كاملة يوم القيامة ومن أوزار الذين يضلونهم بغير علم ألا ساء ما يزرون

translation: Those before them also plotted, but Allah struck at the foundations of their building, and the roof collapsed upon them from above them, and the punishment came upon them from where they did not perceive.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the futility and ultimate failure of the schemes devised by those who oppose God's will. It serves as a reminder that no matter how well-planned or seemingly secure the endeavors of the disbelievers may be, God has the power to undermine and destroy them completely and unexpectedly. The imagery of the collapsing building symbolizes the sudden and total destruction of their plans, emphasizing that divine retribution can come from unforeseen directions, highlighting the omnipotence and omniscience of Allah.
orig: قد مكر الذين من قبلهم فأتى الله بنيانهم من القواعد فخر عليهم السقف من فوقهم وأتاهم العذاب من حيث لا يشعرون

translation: Then on the Day of Resurrection He will disgrace them and say, 'Where are My partners for whom you used to oppose [My guidance]?' Those who were given knowledge will say, 'Indeed, disgrace, this Day, and evil are upon the disbelievers,'
interpretation: This verse underscores the accountability and the ultimate realization of truth on the Day of Judgment. It illustrates how those who associated partners with Allah will be publicly shamed and questioned about their false deities. The response from those endowed with knowledge signifies a clear acknowledgment that the disgrace and misfortune on that day will befall only the disbelievers, emphasizing the consequences of disbelief and the vindication of monotheism.
orig: ثم يوم القيامة يخزيهم ويقول أين شركائي الذين كنتم تشاقون فيهم قال الذين أوتوا العلم إن الخزي اليوم والسوء على الكافرين

translation: Those whose souls are taken by the angels while they wrong themselves, they will say, 'We were not doing any evil.' Yes, indeed! Allah knows well what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse addresses individuals who die in a state of wrongdoing, yet attempt to deny their actions at the moment of death. It highlights the human tendency to rationalize or deny one's sins, even in the face of divine judgment. The verse underscores the omniscience of Allah, emphasizing that no one can deceive Him about their deeds. It serves as a reminder of personal accountability and the futility of denying one's actions before Allah, who is fully aware of all that we do.
orig: الذين تتوفاهم الملائكة ظالمي أنفسهم فألقوا السلم ما كنا نعمل من سوء بلى إن الله عليم بما كنتم تعملون

translation: So enter the gates of Hell, to abide therein forever. Indeed, wretched is the abode of the arrogant.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequence of arrogance and disobedience to God. It serves as a warning that those who exhibit pride and haughtiness, rejecting humility and submission to God's will, will be condemned to eternal punishment in Hell. The phrase 'wretched is the abode of the arrogant' underscores the miserable fate awaiting those who prioritize their own perceived greatness over the worship and obedience to their Creator.
orig: فادخلوا أبواب جهنم خالدين فيها فلبئس مثوى المتكبرين

translation: And it is said to those who feared Allah, 'What has your Lord sent down?' They say, 'Good.' For those who do good in this world is good, and the home of the Hereafter is better. And excellent indeed is the home of the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the positive outcomes for those who live in piety and righteousness. It suggests that when the pious are questioned about what their Lord has revealed, they confidently respond with 'Good,' indicating that the divine message brings goodness. The verse further explains that those who perform good deeds will experience goodness in this worldly life, but the ultimate reward lies in the Hereafter, where the abode of the righteous is described as exceptionally superior. This interpretation underscores the Qur'anic theme of the continuity of divine reward from this life to the next, encouraging believers to maintain righteousness for both immediate and eternal benefits.
orig: وقيل للذين اتقوا ماذا أنزل ربكم قالوا خيرا للذين أحسنوا في هذه الدنيا حسنة ولدار الآخرة خير ولنعم دار المتقين

translation: Gardens of Eden which they will enter, beneath which rivers flow; they will have therein whatever they desire. Thus Allah rewards the righteous.
interpretation: This verse describes the reward awaiting the righteous in the afterlife, symbolized by the Gardens of Eden. The imagery of rivers flowing beneath the gardens signifies abundance and purity. The promise that they will have whatever they desire reflects the ultimate fulfillment and satisfaction in Paradise. This reward is a manifestation of Allah's justice and mercy, specifically designated for those who have lived a life of piety and righteousness, illustrating that divine recompense is perfectly tailored to the deeds of the believers.
orig: جنات عدن يدخلونها تجري من تحتها الأنهار لهم فيها ما يشاءون كذلك يجزي الله المتقين

translation: Those whom the angels take [in death] while they are pure, [the angels] will say, 'Peace be upon you; enter Paradise for what you used to do.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine reward for those who lead a life of purity and righteousness. It emphasizes that at the moment of death, such individuals are greeted by angels with peace and are directly invited into Paradise as a result of their good deeds. The mention of angels saying 'Peace be upon you' signifies the acceptance and honor bestowed upon these souls, affirming their righteous conduct during their earthly life.
orig: الذين تتوفاهم الملائكة طيبين يقولون سلام عليكم ادخلوا الجنة بما كنتم تعملون

translation: Are they waiting for anything except that the angels should come to them or that the command of your Lord should come? Thus did those before them. And Allah did not wrong them, but they used to wrong themselves.
interpretation: This verse highlights the impatience and denial of those who await clear signs or divine intervention before believing. It suggests that people often seek extraordinary events like the arrival of angels or a direct command from God as a condition for faith, yet history shows that such signs did not benefit previous nations who were destroyed for their disbelief. The verse emphasizes personal accountability, indicating that God does not wrong anyone; rather, individuals wrong themselves through their choices and disbelief.
orig: هل ينظرون إلا أن تأتيهم الملائكة أو يأتي أمر ربك كذلك فعل الذين من قبلهم وما ظلمهم الله ولكن كانوا أنفسهم يظلمون

translation: So the evil (consequences) of what they did smote them, and that which they used to mock at surrounded them.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the principle of divine justice where the negative outcomes of one's actions eventually catch up with them. It emphasizes that those who mock or deny the truth will ultimately face the very realities they scoffed at, serving as a reminder of the inevitability of facing the consequences of one's deeds in this life or the hereafter.
orig: فأصابهم سيئات ما عملوا وحاق بهم ما كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: And those who associate partners with Allah say, 'If Allah had willed, we would not have worshipped anything besides Him, neither we nor our fathers, nor would we have prohibited anything besides Him.' Thus did those before them. But is there upon the messengers except the clear conveyance?
interpretation: This verse addresses the argument of polytheists who claim that their idolatry and the practices of their ancestors were part of Allah's will. They suggest that if Allah truly disapproved, He would have prevented such worship. The verse refutes this by indicating that this excuse was also used by previous generations who strayed from the truth. It emphasizes that the role of prophets and messengers is solely to deliver the clear message of monotheism and guidance, not to enforce belief. The responsibility for accepting or rejecting this message lies with the individuals themselves.
orig: وقال الذين أشركوا لو شاء الله ما عبدنا من دونه من شيء نحن ولا آباؤنا ولا حرمنا من دونه من شيء كذلك فعل الذين من قبلهم فهل على الرسل إلا البلاغ المبين

translation: And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, [saying], 'Worship Allah and avoid Taghut.' And among them were those whom Allah guided, and among them were those upon whom misguidance was [deservedly] decreed. So proceed through the earth and observe how was the end of the deniers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universal message of monotheism that Allah has sent through messengers to every nation, urging people to worship Him alone and to shun false deities or Taghut. It highlights the divergent outcomes for individuals based on their response to this message: some are guided by Allah towards the right path, while others, due to their rejection, are left in misguidance. The verse then encourages reflection on historical examples of those who denied the messengers, suggesting that observing their ultimate fate can serve as a lesson and a warning for current and future generations about the consequences of rejecting divine guidance.
orig: ولقد بعثنا في كل أمة رسولا أن اعبدوا الله واجتنبوا الطاغوت فمنهم من هدى الله ومنهم من حقت عليه الضلالة فسيروا في الأرض فانظروا كيف كان عاقبة المكذبين

translation: If you are eager for their guidance, then indeed, Allah does not guide those whom He lets go astray, and they will have no helpers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the limits of human influence on others' faith. It suggests that while one may earnestly desire to guide others towards the right path, ultimately, the guidance of individuals is in the hands of Allah alone. If Allah chooses not to guide someone, no human effort can change that, and such individuals will find no one to assist them in their misguidance. This serves as a reminder to believers to focus on their own faith and actions, rather than becoming overly concerned or frustrated with the lack of response from others to their efforts at guidance.
orig: إن تحرص على هداهم فإن الله لا يهدي من يضل وما لهم من ناصرين

translation: And they swore by Allah their strongest oaths that Allah would not resurrect the one who dies. But it is a promise upon Him [which is] true, but most of the people do not know.
interpretation: This verse addresses the disbelief of some people in the resurrection after death, which they vehemently deny by swearing oaths. The Qur'an asserts that resurrection is a true promise from Allah, highlighting the ignorance of most people about this fundamental aspect of faith. It underscores the certainty of the afterlife and critiques the lack of knowledge among the majority regarding divine promises.
orig: وأقسموا بالله جهد أيمانهم لا يبعث الله من يموت بلى وعدا عليه حقا ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: To make clear to them what they differ about and to let those who disbelieve know that they were liars.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of divine revelation in clarifying disputes among people, particularly in matters of faith. It suggests that the Qur'an serves as a means to resolve differences by providing clear guidance. Additionally, it warns those who reject this guidance that their disbelief will ultimately be exposed as falsehood, reinforcing the accountability of individuals for their choices in faith.
orig: ليبين لهم الذي يختلفون فيه وليعلم الذين كفروا أنهم كانوا كاذبين

translation: Our command to a thing, when We intend it, is only that We say to it, 'Be,' and it is.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and sovereignty of Allah. It illustrates that Allah's will is executed instantly and effortlessly through His command 'Be,' highlighting the simplicity and immediacy of divine creation and action. This underscores the concept of Allah's omnipotence and the effortless nature of His command over all existence.
orig: إنما قولنا لشيء إذا أردناه أن نقول له كن فيكون

translation: And those who emigrated for the cause of Allah after they had been wronged - We will surely settle them in this world in a good place; but indeed, the reward of the Hereafter is greater, if only they knew.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine promise to those who migrate in the path of Allah due to persecution or oppression. It reassures them that their sacrifice will be rewarded not only in this worldly life with a good settlement, but more importantly, their reward in the hereafter will be far greater. The phrase 'if only they knew' emphasizes the profound nature of the reward in the afterlife, which surpasses human comprehension, encouraging steadfastness and faith in Allah's promise despite the hardships faced during migration.
orig: والذين هاجروا في الله من بعد ما ظلموا لنبوئنهم في الدنيا حسنة ولأجر الآخرة أكبر لو كانوا يعلمون

translation: Those who are patient and put their trust in their Lord.
interpretation: This verse highlights the virtues of patience and trust in God. It emphasizes that true believers exhibit steadfastness in the face of trials and challenges, relying completely on Allah's wisdom and timing. This patience is not passive but an active trust in God's plan, demonstrating a deep faith and submission to His will.
orig: الذين صبروا وعلى ربهم يتوكلون

translation: And We sent not before you except men to whom We revealed. So ask the people of the message if you do not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the human nature of the prophets, indicating that all messengers sent by Allah were men chosen to receive divine revelation. It encourages those who are uncertain or seeking further knowledge to consult with the scholars or those knowledgeable in religious texts, referred to as 'the people of the message', to gain a deeper understanding of the prophetic tradition and divine guidance.
orig: وما أرسلنا من قبلك إلا رجالا نوحي إليهم فاسألوا أهل الذكر إن كنتم لا تعلمون

translation: With clear proofs and the scriptures (Zubur), and We have sent down to you the Reminder (Qur'an) that you may explain to the people what has been sent down to them, and that they may reflect.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin and clarity of the messages given to the Prophet Muhammad, including the Qur'an, which is described as a reminder. The purpose of the revelation to the Prophet is twofold: firstly, to clearly explain to humanity the divine guidance that has been sent down, ensuring that the message is accessible and understandable. Secondly, it is hoped that through this clear explanation, people will engage in deep reflection and contemplation about their lives and the divine guidance, leading to a better understanding and implementation of the teachings in their lives.
orig: بالبينات والزبر وأنزلنا إليك الذكر لتبين للناس ما نزل إليهم ولعلهم يتفكرون

translation: Do those who devise evil feel secure that Allah will not cause the earth to swallow them or that the punishment will not come upon them from where they do not perceive?
interpretation: This verse warns those who engage in evil plots and schemes that they should not feel safe from Allah's punishment. It emphasizes the omnipotence of Allah, who can punish the wrongdoers in unexpected ways, such as causing the earth to swallow them or bringing a punishment from an unforeseen direction. The verse serves as a reminder of the suddenness and inevitability of divine retribution for those who persist in their evil ways.
orig: أفأمن الذين مكروا السيئات أن يخسف الله بهم الأرض أو يأتيهم العذاب من حيث لا يشعرون

translation: Or He may take them in their going to and fro, and they will not be able to escape.
interpretation: This verse highlights the omnipotence of Allah, indicating that He has the power to seize people at any moment during their daily activities. It serves as a reminder of the unpredictability of life and the inevitability of divine decree, urging believers to remain conscious of Allah and prepared for the hereafter, as no one can escape His will.
orig: أو يأخذهم في تقلبهم فما هم بمعجزين

translation: Or He may seize them with gradual calamity: for, verily, your Lord is full of kindness and mercy.
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah has the power to punish people gradually, reflecting His justice, but He chooses to be merciful and kind, indicating His compassion and patience towards His creation, giving them time to repent and improve their ways.
orig: أو يأخذهم على تخوف فإن ربكم لرءوف رحيم

translation: Have they not seen how Allah creates a thing and then its shadow inclines to the right and to the left, prostrating to Allah while they are humble?
interpretation: This verse invites reflection on the natural phenomena created by Allah, specifically the movement of shadows, as a sign of His omnipotence and the inherent submission of all creation to Him. The verse encourages believers to observe and contemplate these signs, which should lead to a deeper appreciation and humility before Allah, recognizing that even the shadows, which are mere reflections, submit to Him in a state of humility and prostration.
orig: أولم يروا إلى ما خلق الله من شيء يتفيأ ظلاله عن اليمين والشمائل سجدا لله وهم داخرون

translation: And to Allah prostrates whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth of creatures, and the angels [as well], and they are not arrogant.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universal submission to Allah, indicating that all creatures in the heavens and on earth, including the angels, willingly prostrate to Him without any arrogance. It highlights the humility and obedience that should be emulated by humans, recognizing Allah's supreme authority and power over all creation.
orig: ولله يسجد ما في السماوات وما في الأرض من دابة والملائكة وهم لا يستكبرون

translation: They fear their Lord above them, and they do what they are commanded.
interpretation: This verse describes the characteristics of the righteous believers who are constantly aware of Allah's presence and oversight. Their fear of Allah is not out of dread but out of deep reverence and consciousness of His majesty and authority. This fear motivates them to obey His commands diligently, reflecting their submission and commitment to live according to His will. It highlights the importance of taqwa (God-consciousness) and obedience as integral parts of a believer's life.
orig: يخافون ربهم من فوقهم ويفعلون ما يؤمرون

translation: And Allah said: 'Do not take two gods. Indeed, He is but one God, so fear Me alone.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental Islamic belief in the oneness of God (Tawhid). It directly addresses the prohibition of polytheism, urging believers to worship and fear only Allah, reinforcing the concept that there is no deity worthy of worship except Him. The command to fear Allah alone serves as a reminder of His supreme authority and the importance of submitting to His will exclusively.
orig: وقال الله لا تتخذوا إلهين اثنين إنما هو إله واحد فإياي فارهبون

translation: And to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, and to Him is due the religion perpetually. Then will you fear other than Allah?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and ownership of Allah over everything in existence, both in the heavens and the earth. It underscores that all forms of worship and religious devotion are rightfully due to Him alone, continuously and without interruption. The rhetorical question at the end challenges the reader to reflect on the folly of fearing or revering anyone or anything other than Allah, reinforcing the concept of tawhid (the oneness of God) and the exclusive right of Allah to be worshipped and feared.
orig: وله ما في السماوات والأرض وله الدين واصبا أفغير الله تتقون

translation: And whatever blessings you have, it is from Allah. Then, when harm touches you, to Him you cry aloud for help.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the dependency of humans on Allah for all blessings and goodness in their lives. It highlights that while people may forget or overlook Allah's continuous favors during times of ease, they instinctively turn to Him in desperation when faced with adversity. The verse serves as a reminder of the need for constant gratitude and recognition of Allah's sovereignty and mercy, urging believers to maintain a strong connection with Him in all circumstances, not just during times of distress.
orig: وما بكم من نعمة فمن الله ثم إذا مسكم الضر فإليه تجأرون

translation: Then, when He has removed the harm from you, behold! some of you associate others with their Lord,
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to turn away from pure monotheism and gratitude towards God after experiencing relief from hardship. It points out that some people, upon being relieved of their distress, forget the favor of Allah and start attributing partners to Him, either through direct idolatry or by giving undue importance to other entities or beings. This behavior reflects a lack of steadfastness in faith and a failure to recognize Allah's sole authority and power over all circumstances.
orig: ثم إذا كشف الضر عنكم إذا فريق منكم بربهم يشركون

translation: So they deny what We have given them. Then enjoy yourselves, for you will soon know.
interpretation: This verse addresses those who deny the blessings and signs from Allah, warning them that they should enjoy their worldly pleasures temporarily, as they will soon face the consequences of their disbelief and ingratitude. It underscores the transient nature of worldly enjoyment in contrast to the eternal reality of the hereafter.
orig: ليكفروا بما آتيناهم فتمتعوا فسوف تعلمون

translation: And they assign to what they do not know a portion of that which We have provided them. By Allah, you will surely be questioned about what you used to invent.
interpretation: This verse critiques the practice of attributing partners to Allah and dedicating portions of their sustenance to idols or false deities, which they themselves do not fully understand or know. It emphasizes the accountability humans will face for such fabrications and false claims on the Day of Judgment, underscoring the seriousness of associating partners with Allah and the inevitable questioning about these actions.
orig: ويجعلون لما لا يعلمون نصيبا مما رزقناهم تالله لتسألن عما كنتم تفترون

translation: And they assign to Allah daughters - exalted is He - and for themselves what they desire.
interpretation: This verse critiques the pre-Islamic Arabian practice of attributing female offspring to Allah while preferring sons for themselves, highlighting the hypocrisy and the degradation of their understanding of divinity. It emphasizes the sanctity and transcendence of Allah, who is above such human biases and preferences.
orig: ويجعلون لله البنات سبحانه ولهم ما يشتهون

translation: And when one of them is given news of [the birth of] a female, his face becomes dark, and he is filled with grief.
interpretation: This verse highlights the pre-Islamic societal attitude towards the birth of a daughter, reflecting a deep-seated gender bias where the birth of a girl was considered undesirable and shameful. It critiques the emotional response of gloom and suppressed anger, indicating the moral and ethical shortcomings of such a reaction, which is contrary to the values of equality and respect for all human life that Islam promotes.
orig: وإذا بشر أحدهم بالأنثى ظل وجهه مسودا وهو كظيم

translation: He hides himself from the people because of the evil of what he has been informed. Should he keep it in spite of disgrace or bury it in the dust? Unquestionably, evil is what they decide.
interpretation: This verse addresses the practice of female infanticide that was prevalent among the pre-Islamic Arabs. It highlights the moral dilemma and shame a father feels upon learning that his newborn is a girl, to the extent that he considers hiding from society or even contemplating whether to keep the child despite the social disgrace or to bury her alive. The verse condemns this decision-making process as morally reprehensible, emphasizing the gravity of such a choice and the inherent evil in the societal norms that lead to it.
orig: يتوارى من القوم من سوء ما بشر به أيمسكه على هون أم يدسه في التراب ألا ساء ما يحكمون

translation: For those who do not believe in the Hereafter, there is an evil example, and to Allah belongs the highest example. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between the outcomes for those who reject the concept of the Hereafter and the supreme nature of Allah. The 'evil example' refers to the consequences and moral degradation that disbelief in the afterlife brings upon individuals, leading them astray from righteousness. Conversely, 'the highest example' signifies Allah's perfection and the ultimate goodness and wisdom exemplified in His creation and commandments. The attributes 'the Exalted in Might, the Wise' emphasize Allah's omnipotence and perfect wisdom, reinforcing the idea that His example is the pinnacle of excellence and should be the standard for believers to follow.
orig: للذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة مثل السوء ولله المثل الأعلى وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: And if Allah were to punish people for their wrongdoing, He would not leave upon the earth any creature, but He delays them for a specified term. Then when their time arrives, they will not remain behind an hour, nor will they precede [it].
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's mercy and patience towards humanity despite their transgressions. It suggests that if Allah were to immediately punish people for their sins, no living creature would survive on earth. However, out of His mercy, He gives people a chance to repent and reform by delaying their punishment until a predetermined time. This emphasizes the concept of divine justice being intertwined with mercy, allowing time for repentance. When the appointed time comes, the punishment or reckoning is inevitable and precisely timed, underscoring the certainty and fairness of divine judgment.
orig: ولو يؤاخذ الله الناس بظلمهم ما ترك عليها من دابة ولكن يؤخرهم إلى أجل مسمى فإذا جاء أجلهم لا يستأخرون ساعة ولا يستقدمون

translation: And they assign to Allah what they dislike, and their tongues assert the lie that they will have the best. Without doubt, for them is the Fire, and they will be abandoned.
interpretation: This verse critiques the hypocrisy of those who attribute to Allah things they themselves dislike, while falsely claiming through their speech that they deserve the best in the hereafter. It underscores the certainty of their punishment in the Fire, emphasizing that such deceitful behavior leads to their ultimate abandonment and loss.
orig: ويجعلون لله ما يكرهون وتصف ألسنتهم الكذب أن لهم الحسنى لا جرم أن لهم النار وأنهم مفرطون

translation: By Allah, We have sent (messengers) to nations before you, but Satan made their deeds seem fair to them. So he is their ally today, and for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the historical pattern of divine guidance being sent to various nations through messengers. Despite this guidance, Satan's influence led these nations astray by beautifying their sinful actions, making them appear righteous or harmless. As a result, on the Day of Judgment, Satan will be their only ally, and they will face severe punishment for following his misguidance instead of the divine message. This serves as a warning to believers to be vigilant against Satan's deceptions and to adhere strictly to the path shown by the messengers of Allah.
orig: تالله لقد أرسلنا إلى أمم من قبلك فزين لهم الشيطان أعمالهم فهو وليهم اليوم ولهم عذاب أليم

translation: And We have not sent down to you the Book except that you make clear to them that wherein they differ and [as] guidance and mercy for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the purpose of the Qur'an's revelation, which is to clarify disputes among people regarding religious matters, and to serve as a source of guidance and mercy specifically for those who believe. It underscores the Qur'an's role in resolving theological disagreements and providing believers with a clear path towards righteousness and divine compassion.
orig: وما أنزلنا عليك الكتاب إلا لتبين لهم الذي اختلفوا فيه وهدى ورحمة لقوم يؤمنون

translation: And Allah sends down rain from the sky and gives life thereby to the earth after its death. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who listen.
interpretation: This verse highlights the miraculous power of Allah in reviving the earth through rainfall after it has become barren and lifeless. It serves as a reminder and a sign of Allah's ability to bring life from death, symbolizing resurrection and renewal. The verse encourages believers to reflect on this natural phenomenon and recognize the deeper spiritual lessons it imparts, urging those who are willing to listen to heed this sign of Allah's omnipotence and mercy.
orig: والله أنزل من السماء ماء فأحيا به الأرض بعد موتها إن في ذلك لآية لقوم يسمعون

translation: And indeed, for you in the livestock there is a lesson. We give you drink from what is in their bellies, between excrement and blood, pure milk, palatable to the drinkers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the miraculous nature of the creation of milk within the bodies of livestock. It emphasizes the purity and palatability of milk, which is produced in close proximity to impurities like excrement and blood, yet emerges as a wholesome and nourishing drink. This serves as a reminder of God's intricate design and provision, illustrating how He can bring forth purity and sustenance from seemingly unlikely sources.
orig: وإن لكم في الأنعام لعبرة نسقيكم مما في بطونه من بين فرث ودم لبنا خالصا سائغا للشاربين

translation: And from the fruits of the date-palm and the grapevine, you derive intoxicants and goodly provision. Indeed, in that is a sign for a people who reason.
interpretation: This verse highlights the dual nature of the blessings provided by Allah through the fruits of the date-palm and grapevine. It points out that these fruits can be used to produce both intoxicants, which can lead to harm, and goodly provision, which benefits mankind. The verse serves as a reminder of the responsibility humans have in using the blessings of Allah wisely. It encourages reflection on the signs of Allah's creation and the wisdom in using natural resources in a way that promotes well-being and avoids harm, urging those who are capable of reasoning to ponder upon this divine sign.
orig: ومن ثمرات النخيل والأعناب تتخذون منه سكرا ورزقا حسنا إن في ذلك لآية لقوم يعقلون

translation: And your Lord inspired the bee, saying: 'Take for yourself homes in the mountains, and in the trees, and in what they construct.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine guidance and wisdom imparted by Allah to even the smallest of creatures, like the bee, illustrating the intricate balance and order in creation. It underscores the concept of tawheed (oneness of God) by showing that all aspects of nature are under Allah's command and serve a purpose in His plan. The bee's instruction to build homes in various places also symbolizes the importance of utilizing the resources provided by Allah wisely and living in harmony with the environment.
orig: وأوحى ربك إلى النحل أن اتخذي من الجبال بيوتا ومن الشجر ومما يعرشون

translation: Then eat from all the fruits and follow the ways of your Lord made easy for you." There emerges from their bellies a drink, varying in colors, in which there is healing for people. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who give thought.
interpretation: This verse from Surah An-Nahl (16:69) uses the example of the bee to illustrate the concept of divine guidance and provision. The bee is instructed to eat from various fruits, symbolizing the diversity of sustenance provided by Allah, and to follow the paths made easy by Him, indicating the ease with which one can follow divine guidance. The production of honey, described as a drink of varying colors with healing properties, serves as a metaphor for the beneficial outcomes of adhering to Allah's commands. The verse emphasizes the signs of Allah's wisdom and benevolence in nature, encouraging believers to reflect on these signs and recognize the purposeful design in creation.
orig: ثم كلي من كل الثمرات فاسلكي سبل ربك ذللا يخرج من بطونها شراب مختلف ألوانه فيه شفاء للناس إن في ذلك لآية لقوم يتفكرون

translation: And Allah created you, then He will cause you to die. And among you is he who is returned to the most abject stage of life so that he will not know, after having knowledge, anything. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the cycle of life and death that Allah has ordained for humans. It highlights the power of Allah over life, death, and the stages in between, including the possibility of returning to a state of senility where one loses previously acquired knowledge. This serves as a reminder of human vulnerability and the ultimate knowledge and ability of Allah, who is fully aware of all stages of human life and capable of managing them as He sees fit.
orig: والله خلقكم ثم يتوفاكم ومنكم من يرد إلى أرذل العمر لكي لا يعلم بعد علم شيئا إن الله عليم قدير

translation: And Allah has favored some of you over others in provision. But those who were favored would not hand over their provision to those whom their right hands possess so they would be equal therein. Then is it the favor of Allah they reject?
interpretation: This verse highlights the natural disparity in wealth and provision that Allah has ordained among people. It serves as a reminder that those who have been given more should not be expected to redistribute their wealth to make everyone equal, as this goes against the divine order of provision. The rhetorical question at the end challenges those who might complain about this inequality, suggesting that to deny or reject the blessings they have received is to reject Allah's favor. It encourages gratitude and acceptance of the divine wisdom in the distribution of wealth.
orig: والله فضل بعضكم على بعض في الرزق فما الذين فضلوا برادي رزقهم على ما ملكت أيمانهم فهم فيه سواء أفبنعمة الله يجحدون

translation: And Allah has made for you from yourselves mates and has made for you from your mates sons and grandchildren and has provided for you from the good things. Then do they believe in falsehood and deny the favor of Allah?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the blessings and provisions that Allah has bestowed upon humanity, specifically highlighting the creation of spouses and the continuation of lineage through children and grandchildren. It underscores the divine origin of these relationships and the sustenance provided, which are considered among the 'good things'. The rhetorical question at the end challenges the disbelief in these blessings, suggesting that rejecting these favors is akin to embracing falsehood and ingratitude towards Allah's benevolence.
orig: والله جعل لكم من أنفسكم أزواجا وجعل لكم من أزواجكم بنين وحفدة ورزقكم من الطيبات أفبالباطل يؤمنون وبنعمت الله هم يكفرون

translation: And they worship besides Allah that which has no power to provide them with provision from the heavens and the earth, nor can they (the worshipped ones) do so.
interpretation: This verse critiques the act of worshipping idols or deities other than Allah, emphasizing their inability to provide sustenance or any benefit to their worshippers. It underscores the futility and irrationality of such worship, as these entities are powerless and incapable of influencing or controlling anything in the heavens or on earth. The verse serves as a reminder of Allah's sole authority and capability to provide for His creation, reinforcing the monotheistic principle central to Islamic belief.
orig: ويعبدون من دون الله ما لا يملك لهم رزقا من السماوات والأرض شيئا ولا يستطيعون

translation: So do not set up rivals to Allah while you know [the truth]. Indeed, Allah knows and you do not know.
interpretation: This verse warns against associating partners with Allah, an act known as shirk, which is considered the gravest sin in Islam. It emphasizes that such actions are futile because Allah possesses complete knowledge, whereas human understanding is limited. The verse encourages believers to rely on Allah's omniscience and to avoid creating false equivalences or idols, as doing so contradicts the truth and knowledge that Allah alone is the all-knowing.
orig: فلا تضربوا لله الأمثال إن الله يعلم وأنتم لا تعلمون

translation: Allah presents an example: a slave owned by another, unable to do anything, and a man to whom We have given a good provision from Us, and he spends from it secretly and publicly. Are they equal? Praise be to Allah. But most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between two types of people: one who is enslaved and powerless, unable to act independently, and another who has been blessed with ample provisions from Allah and uses these blessings to benefit others both privately and publicly. The rhetorical question posed in the verse, 'Are they equal?', underscores the vast difference in their states and actions. The verse emphasizes gratitude and the responsible use of wealth, suggesting that those who are given more should use their resources to help others, reflecting a higher moral and spiritual standing. The closing statement, 'But most of them do not know,' indicates that many people fail to recognize or appreciate this distinction and the importance of using one's blessings wisely.
orig: ضرب الله مثلا عبدا مملوكا لا يقدر على شيء ومن رزقناه منا رزقا حسنا فهو ينفق منه سرا وجهرا هل يستوون الحمد لله بل أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: And Allah presents an example: two men, one of them is dumb and unable to do anything, and he is a burden on his master. Wherever he directs him, he brings no good. Is he equal to one who commands justice and is on a straight path?
interpretation: This verse uses the metaphor of two men to illustrate the difference between a person who is guided by Allah and one who is not. The 'dumb' man represents someone who lacks understanding and guidance, unable to contribute positively and dependent on others. In contrast, the man who commands justice and follows the straight path symbolizes a believer who is guided by divine wisdom, actively contributing to society with righteousness. The verse emphasizes the vast difference in value and impact between a person living in ignorance and one living according to divine guidance.
orig: وضرب الله مثلا رجلين أحدهما أبكم لا يقدر على شيء وهو كل على مولاه أينما يوجهه لا يأت بخير هل يستوي هو ومن يأمر بالعدل وهو على صراط مستقيم

translation: And to Allah belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and the matter of the Hour is not but as a twinkling of the eye, or even nearer. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's complete sovereignty and knowledge over all hidden and unseen matters in the universe, including the timing and occurrence of the Day of Judgment. The comparison of the Hour to the blink of an eye or even quicker illustrates how swiftly and unexpectedly it can come upon us, urging believers to be ever-prepared and mindful of their actions. The affirmation of Allah's omnipotence reassures that He has the power to bring about the Hour and manage all affairs with absolute control.
orig: ولله غيب السماوات والأرض وما أمر الساعة إلا كلمح البصر أو هو أقرب إن الله على كل شيء قدير

translation: And Allah brought you forth from the wombs of your mothers while you knew nothing, and He gave you hearing and sight and hearts that you may give thanks.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the dependency of humans on Allah from the very beginning of their existence. It highlights that humans are born without knowledge, and it is Allah who endows them with the faculties of hearing, sight, and understanding.
