These gifts are bestowed upon us so that we might recognize and appreciate Allah's blessings, prompting us to express gratitude towards Him. The verse serves as a reminder of our innate obligation to be thankful to Allah for the basic yet profound capabilities that enable us to navigate and understand the world around us.
orig: والله أخرجكم من بطون أمهاتكم لا تعلمون شيئا وجعل لكم السمع والأبصار والأفئدة لعلكم تشكرون

translation: Do they not see the birds controlled in the expanse of the sky? None holds them up except Allah. Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse invites believers to reflect on the natural world as a manifestation of God's power and wisdom. The example of birds flying effortlessly in the sky is used to illustrate that their ability to remain aloft is solely due to God's will. This phenomenon serves as a sign for those who have faith, encouraging them to recognize and appreciate the intricate design and control that God exerts over creation, thereby strengthening their belief in His omnipotence and care.
orig: ألم يروا إلى الطير مسخرات في جو السماء ما يمسكهن إلا الله إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يؤمنون

translation: And Allah has made for you from your homes a place of rest, and made for you from the hides of cattle tents which you find light on the day of your travel and on the day of your stay; and from their wool, fur, and hair, furnishings and articles of convenience for a while.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's provision and care for humanity by providing homes as places of rest and security. It also acknowledges the utility of animal products, specifically from cattle, in creating portable shelters like tents, which are essential for travel and temporary stays. Additionally, the verse points out the use of wool, fur, and hair for making household items, emphasizing the temporary nature of worldly possessions ("for a while"), reminding believers of the transient nature of life and the importance of gratitude for Allah's provisions.
orig: والله جعل لكم من بيوتكم سكنا وجعل لكم من جلود الأنعام بيوتا تستخفونها يوم ظعنكم ويوم إقامتكم ومن أصوافها وأوبارها وأشعارها أثاثا ومتاعا إلى حين

translation: And Allah has made for you, from that which He has created, shades, and He has made for you from the mountains, shelters, and He has made for you garments that protect you from the heat and garments that protect you from your own violence. Thus does He complete His favor upon you that you might submit [to Him].
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's benevolence and care for humanity by providing natural and man-made means of protection and comfort. The mention of shades, shelters in mountains, and garments that protect from heat and harm illustrates how Allah has created an environment that supports human life and well-being. The phrase 'Thus does He complete His favor upon you' emphasizes that these provisions are part of a comprehensive system of divine favor, intended to lead humans towards submission and gratitude to Allah, as indicated by 'that you might submit [to Him].' This submission is not just an act of obedience but a recognition of and response to the continuous blessings and care from Allah.
orig: والله جعل لكم مما خلق ظلالا وجعل لكم من الجبال أكنانا وجعل لكم سرابيل تقيكم الحر وسرابيل تقيكم بأسكم كذلك يتم نعمته عليكم لعلكم تسلمون

translation: But if they turn away, then your duty is only to convey the clear message.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophet Muhammad's role as a messenger whose primary responsibility is to clearly communicate the message of Islam. It highlights that the acceptance or rejection of the message by others is not within his control, and thus, he should not be distressed or feel responsible for their choices. The focus is on the importance of fulfilling one's duty in conveying the truth, regardless of the outcome.
orig: فإن تولوا فإنما عليك البلاغ المبين

translation: They recognize the favor of Allah; then they deny it. And most of them are disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ingratitude and denial of Allah's blessings by a majority of people, despite their awareness of these favors. It points to a common human tendency to acknowledge divine blessings in times of need or reflection but to deny or forget them in times of prosperity or when following personal desires, leading to disbelief.
orig: يعرفون نعمت الله ثم ينكرونها وأكثرهم الكافرون

translation: And the Day when We will resurrect from every nation a witness, then those who disbelieved will not be permitted [to speak], nor will they be allowed to make excuses.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the Day of Judgment when representatives from every community will be raised as witnesses to testify about their people's deeds. On this day, those who rejected faith will find themselves unable to speak or offer any excuses for their disbelief, highlighting the finality and justice of the divine judgment where no false justifications will be accepted.
orig: ويوم نبعث من كل أمة شهيدا ثم لا يؤذن للذين كفروا ولا هم يستعتبون

translation: And when those who wronged see the punishment, it will not be lightened for them, nor will they be reprieved.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability and severity of divine justice. It suggests that once the wrongdoers witness the punishment on the Day of Judgment, there will be no reduction in its intensity or delay in its execution. This serves as a warning to believers to avoid wrongdoing, emphasizing the accountability and the finality of the consequences of one's actions in the afterlife.
orig: وإذا رأى الذين ظلموا العذاب فلا يخفف عنهم ولا هم ينظرون

translation: And when those who associated partners with Allah see their partners, they will say, 'Our Lord, these are our partners [whom] we used to invoke besides You.' But they will throw the word back at them, 'Indeed, you are liars.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the moment of realization and regret for those who committed shirk (associating partners with Allah). When they see the false deities they worshipped alongside Allah, they attempt to shift the blame by addressing these idols as their partners in worship. However, these false deities will reject any association with them, declaring the polytheists as liars. This scene underscores the futility and falsehood of shirk, emphasizing that on the Day of Judgment, the truth will be evident, and no false deity will come to the aid of those who worshipped them.
orig: وإذا رأى الذين أشركوا شركاءهم قالوا ربنا هؤلاء شركاؤنا الذين كنا ندعو من دونك فألقوا إليهم القول إنكم لكاذبون

translation: And they will offer submission to Allah on that Day, and what they used to invent will depart from them.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, those who were previously arrogant or disbelieving will finally submit to Allah, recognizing His sovereignty and power. At that moment, all the false claims and inventions they had propagated in their earthly lives will vanish, leaving them with no false gods or ideologies to cling to, exposing the truth of their situation and the futility of their previous deceptions.
orig: وألقوا إلى الله يومئذ السلم وضل عنهم ما كانوا يفترون

translation: Those who disbelieved and hindered others from the path of Allah, We increased them in punishment above the punishment for what they used to corrupt.
interpretation: This verse indicates that those who not only reject faith but also actively prevent others from following the path of Allah will face an intensified punishment. The additional punishment is a consequence of their actions that contribute to corruption and moral decay in society. It underscores the severity of obstructing others from righteousness and the accountability for such deeds in the hereafter.
orig: الذين كفروا وصدوا عن سبيل الله زدناهم عذابا فوق العذاب بما كانوا يفسدون

translation: And the Day We will resurrect from every nation a witness over them from among themselves. And We will bring you, [O Muhammad], as a witness over these. And We have sent down to you the Book as clarification for all things and as guidance and mercy and good tidings for the Muslims.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Day of Judgment when Allah will raise a witness from every nation to testify about their deeds, highlighting the accountability of all people. The Prophet Muhammad is specifically mentioned as a witness over his community, underscoring his role in conveying the message of Islam. The Qur'an is described as a comprehensive guide that clarifies all matters, providing guidance, mercy, and good news for Muslims, reinforcing its role as a complete source of divine wisdom and direction.
orig: ويوم نبعث في كل أمة شهيدا عليهم من أنفسهم وجئنا بك شهيدا على هؤلاء ونزلنا عليك الكتاب تبيانا لكل شيء وهدى ورحمة وبشرى للمسلمين

translation: Indeed, Allah orders justice and good conduct and giving to relatives and forbids immorality and bad conduct and oppression. He admonishes you that perhaps you will be reminded.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the core ethical principles that Muslims are expected to follow. It highlights Allah's command to uphold justice in all dealings, to engage in acts of kindness and generosity, particularly towards family members. Conversely, it explicitly prohibits behaviors that are considered immoral, harmful, or oppressive. The verse serves as a reminder and a call to mindfulness, urging believers to reflect on their actions and align them with these divine directives, fostering a society based on righteousness and moral integrity.
orig: إن الله يأمر بالعدل والإحسان وإيتاء ذي القربى وينهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر والبغي يعظكم لعلكم تذكرون

translation: And fulfill the covenant of Allah when you have taken it, and do not break oaths after their confirmation while you have made Allah a witness over you. Indeed, Allah knows what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of upholding one's promises and oaths, especially those made in the name of Allah. It serves as a reminder that Allah is aware of all actions and that breaking a solemn oath after it has been confirmed is a serious transgression. The verse encourages believers to be mindful of their commitments and to honor them as a reflection of their faith and integrity.
orig: وأوفوا بعهد الله إذا عاهدتم ولا تنقضوا الأيمان بعد توكيدها وقد جعلتم الله عليكم كفيلا إن الله يعلم ما تفعلون

translation: And do not be like the one who unraveled her yarn after it was firmly spun, taking your oaths as a means of deception among yourselves because one group is more numerous than another. Allah only tests you by it, and He will surely make clear to you on the Day of Resurrection that over which you used to differ.
interpretation: This verse uses the metaphor of a woman unraveling her yarn to illustrate the futility and harm of breaking oaths and using them deceitfully. Just as unraveling yarn undoes the hard work put into spinning it, breaking oaths undermines trust and integrity. The verse warns against using oaths to gain advantage over others, especially when motivated by numerical superiority. It emphasizes that such actions are merely a test from Allah, and the true judgment of these actions will be revealed on the Day of Resurrection, highlighting the temporary nature of worldly gains and the ultimate accountability to Allah.
orig: ولا تكونوا كالتي نقضت غزلها من بعد قوة أنكاثا تتخذون أيمانكم دخلا بينكم أن تكون أمة هي أربى من أمة إنما يبلوكم الله به وليبينن لكم يوم القيامة ما كنتم فيه تختلفون

translation: And if Allah had willed, He could have made you one nation [united in religion], but He causes to stray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. And you will surely be questioned about what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom in the diversity of human beliefs and actions. It underscores that Allah's will allows for different paths among people, not because He desires their misguidance, but to test and manifest their choices and efforts. The verse also serves as a reminder of personal accountability, emphasizing that everyone will be held responsible for their deeds, reinforcing the importance of conscious decision-making in one's spiritual journey.
orig: ولو شاء الله لجعلكم أمة واحدة ولكن يضل من يشاء ويهدي من يشاء ولتسألن عما كنتم تعملون

translation: And do not take your oaths as a means of deception between yourselves, lest a foot slip after being firmly planted and you taste the evil consequences of having turned away from the path of Allah, and for you there will be a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns against using oaths deceitfully among yourselves, which can lead to moral and spiritual downfall. It emphasizes the importance of integrity and honesty in one's commitments. The 'foot slipping' metaphorically represents a loss of moral grounding and stability, leading to negative consequences both in this life and the hereafter. The 'great punishment' refers to the severe repercussions of straying from the righteous path set by Allah, highlighting the gravity of such actions.
orig: ولا تتخذوا أيمانكم دخلا بينكم فتزل قدم بعد ثبوتها وتذوقوا السوء بما صددتم عن سبيل الله ولكم عذاب عظيم

translation: And do not exchange the covenant of Allah for a small price. Indeed, what is with Allah is better for you, if you only knew.
interpretation: This verse warns against betraying the trust and commitments made to Allah for worldly gains, which are insignificant compared to the eternal rewards promised by Allah. It emphasizes the importance of prioritizing spiritual values and divine promises over material temptations, highlighting that true knowledge and understanding would lead one to recognize the superiority of Allah's rewards.
orig: ولا تشتروا بعهد الله ثمنا قليلا إنما عند الله هو خير لكم إن كنتم تعلمون

translation: What is with you will be exhausted, and what is with Allah will remain. And We will surely give those who were patient their reward according to the best of what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the transient nature of worldly possessions and the eternal nature of divine rewards. It teaches that material things will eventually run out, but the blessings and rewards from Allah are everlasting. The promise to reward those who patiently endure hardships with the best of their deeds highlights the importance of patience and good actions in achieving a lasting reward from Allah.
orig: ما عندكم ينفد وما عند الله باق ولنجزين الذين صبروا أجرهم بأحسن ما كانوا يعملون

translation: Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer - We will surely cause him to live a good life, and We will surely give them their reward [in the Hereafter] according to the best of what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the equality of reward for righteous actions between men and women, provided they are believers. It highlights that faith combined with good deeds leads to a rewarding life in this world and an even greater reward in the hereafter, based on the excellence of their actions. This underscores the Islamic principle that spiritual and moral merit is not determined by gender but by one's faith and deeds.
orig: من عمل صالحا من ذكر أو أنثى وهو مؤمن فلنحيينه حياة طيبة ولنجزينهم أجرهم بأحسن ما كانوا يعملون

translation: So when you recite the Qur'an, seek refuge with Allah from the accursed Satan.
interpretation: This verse instructs believers to seek Allah's protection from Satan's influence before reciting the Qur'an. It emphasizes the importance of spiritual purity and the acknowledgment of Satan's potential to mislead, even during the sacred act of Qur'an recitation. By invoking Allah's name, the reciter is reminded of their dependence on divine guidance and protection against evil.
orig: فإذا قرأت القرآن فاستعذ بالله من الشيطان الرجيم

translation: Indeed, he has no power over those who believe and in their Lord they put their trust.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the protection and security that faith in Allah provides to believers. It asserts that Shaytan (Satan) has no authority or influence over those who have true faith and who rely completely on Allah. The act of trusting in Allah is highlighted as a shield against the deceptions and temptations of Shaytan, reinforcing the importance of faith and reliance on the Divine as a means of spiritual safety.
orig: إنه ليس له سلطان على الذين آمنوا وعلى ربهم يتوكلون

translation: His authority is only over those who take him as an ally and those who associate others with Allah.
interpretation: This verse indicates that Satan's power is limited to those who willingly follow him and those who commit the sin of shirk, or associating partners with Allah. It emphasizes the importance of monotheism and warns believers against aligning themselves with evil influences, highlighting that one's choices in faith and allegiance determine the extent to which they are susceptible to negative spiritual forces.
orig: إنما سلطانه على الذين يتولونه والذين هم به مشركون

translation: And when We replace a verse with another verse - and Allah is most knowing of what He reveals - they say, 'You are but an inventor [of lies].' Rather, most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse addresses the disbelief and accusations of fabrication by some people when changes or replacements occur in the Qur'anic revelation. It highlights the omniscience of Allah regarding what He reveals, emphasizing that such changes are part of divine wisdom. The verse critiques the ignorance of those who hastily label the Prophet Muhammad as a fabricator, suggesting that their rejection stems from a lack of understanding and knowledge about the nature of divine revelation.
orig: وإذا بدلنا آية مكان آية والله أعلم بما ينزل قالوا إنما أنت مفتر بل أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], 'The Holy Spirit has brought it down from your Lord in truth to make firm those who believe and as guidance and good tidings to the Muslims.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin of the Qur'an, stating that it was revealed by the Holy Spirit (often interpreted as the Angel Gabriel) from God to Prophet Muhammad. The purpose of this revelation is to strengthen the faith of believers, provide them with guidance, and offer good news to those who submit to God (Muslims). The verse underscores the Qur'an's role as a source of spiritual fortitude, direction, and hope for the Muslim community.
orig: قل نزله روح القدس من ربك بالحق ليثبت الذين آمنوا وهدى وبشرى للمسلمين

translation: And indeed, We know that they say, 'It is only a human being who teaches him.' The tongue of the one they refer to is foreign, while this is a clear Arabic tongue.
interpretation: This verse addresses the accusations made by the disbelievers against the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), claiming that he was taught the Qur'an by a non-Arab, specifically hinting at a foreign slave who was known to be around him. The Qur'an refutes this claim by pointing out the linguistic difference; the alleged teacher spoke a foreign language, whereas the Qur'an is in clear, eloquent Arabic, which could not have been produced by someone whose native tongue is not Arabic. This highlights the miraculous nature of the Qur'an and its divine origin, as it challenges the disbelievers to produce something similar if they believe it to be the work of a human.
orig: ولقد نعلم أنهم يقولون إنما يعلمه بشر لسان الذي يلحدون إليه أعجمي وهذا لسان عربي مبين

translation: Indeed, those who do not believe in the verses of Allah, Allah will not guide them, and for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequence of disbelief in the signs and revelations of Allah. It suggests that rejecting these divine messages leads to a lack of guidance from Allah, resulting in spiritual loss and a painful punishment in the hereafter. The verse underscores the importance of faith in Allah's revelations for achieving divine guidance and avoiding punishment.
orig: إن الذين لا يؤمنون بآيات الله لا يهديهم الله ولهم عذاب أليم

translation: Only those who do not believe in the verses of Allah invent falsehood, and it is those who are the liars.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the act of fabricating lies and falsehood is attributed specifically to those who reject the signs and revelations of Allah. It underscores the moral and spiritual consequence of disbelief, indicating that denial of divine truth leads to dishonesty and deceit. The verse serves as a warning that those who engage in such behavior are truly the ones who are false in their essence.
orig: إنما يفتري الكذب الذين لا يؤمنون بآيات الله وأولئك هم الكاذبون

translation: Whoever disbelieves in Allah after his belief, except for one who is forced [to renounce his religion] while his heart is secure in faith. But those who [willingly] open their breasts to disbelief, upon them is wrath from Allah, and for them is a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse addresses the gravity of apostasy and the conditions under which it may be forgiven. It highlights that if someone is forced to verbally renounce their faith but internally remains steadfast in belief, they are not considered to have truly disbelieved. However, those who willingly and openly embrace disbelief after having faith are subject to Allah's wrath and a severe punishment. This underscores the importance of sincerity in faith and the severe consequences of deliberately turning away from it.
orig: من كفر بالله من بعد إيمانه إلا من أكره وقلبه مطمئن بالإيمان ولكن من شرح بالكفر صدرا فعليهم غضب من الله ولهم عذاب عظيم

translation: That is because they preferred the life of this world over the Hereafter and because Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse explains that the reason some people go astray is due to their preference for the temporary pleasures and material gains of worldly life over the eternal rewards of the Hereafter. It underscores the consequence of such a choice, indicating that Allah does not guide those who consciously choose disbelief and reject faith, highlighting the importance of prioritizing spiritual values and the afterlife over transient worldly desires.
orig: ذلك بأنهم استحبوا الحياة الدنيا على الآخرة وأن الله لا يهدي القوم الكافرين

translation: Those are the ones upon whose hearts, hearing, and sight Allah has set a seal. And those are the heedless.
interpretation: This verse describes individuals who have become spiritually and morally unresponsive due to their own actions and choices. Allah has placed a metaphorical seal on their hearts, hearing, and sight, symbolizing their inability to perceive and understand divine guidance. This sealing is a consequence of their persistent rejection of truth and righteousness, leading them to a state of heedlessness where they are unaware of their spiritual condition and the consequences of their actions.
orig: أولئك الذين طبع الله على قلوبهم وسمعهم وأبصارهم وأولئك هم الغافلون

translation: Indeed, they will be the losers in the Hereafter.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate consequence of disbelief and wrongdoing. Those who reject faith and indulge in sinful actions may appear successful in worldly terms, but in the Hereafter, they will face the reality of their loss. The term "losers" (الخاسرون) signifies a profound spiritual and eternal defeat, highlighting the gravity of their misguidance and the irreversible nature of their fate in the afterlife.
orig: لا جرم أنهم في الآخرة هم الخاسرون

translation: Then, indeed, your Lord, to those who emigrated after they had been persecuted and then strove and were patient - indeed, your Lord, after that, is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine promise of forgiveness and mercy from Allah to those who have faced persecution for their faith, yet chose to emigrate in search of a place where they can practice their religion freely. It emphasizes the virtues of perseverance and striving in the path of righteousness despite hardships. The verse reassures believers that their efforts and patience in the face of adversity are recognized by Allah, who will ultimately reward them with His forgiveness and mercy.
orig: ثم إن ربك للذين هاجروا من بعد ما فتنوا ثم جاهدوا وصبروا إن ربك من بعدها لغفور رحيم

translation: The Day when every soul will come pleading for itself, and every soul will be paid in full for what it did, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Day of Judgment, where each individual will be solely accountable for their actions. It highlights the personal responsibility and the fairness of divine justice, where no soul will be wronged or treated unjustly. The verse underscores the concept that one's deeds in life will directly determine their fate, reinforcing the importance of righteous living and moral accountability.
orig: يوم تأتي كل نفس تجادل عن نفسها وتوفى كل نفس ما عملت وهم لا يظلمون

translation: And Allah presents an example of a village that was secure and content, its provision coming to it in abundance from every location, but it denied the favors of Allah. So Allah made it taste the envelopment of hunger and fear for what they had been doing.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder and warning about the consequences of ingratitude towards Allah's blessings. The village described was once prosperous and safe, receiving ample sustenance from all directions, symbolizing the abundance of Allah's provision. However, when the inhabitants rejected and were ungrateful for these blessings, Allah replaced their state of security and abundance with hunger and fear. This change was a direct result of their actions, illustrating that ingratitude can lead to the withdrawal of divine favors and the onset of hardship. It emphasizes the importance of recognizing and appreciating Allah's gifts, and maintaining faith and righteousness to sustain divine blessings.
orig: وضرب الله مثلا قرية كانت آمنة مطمئنة يأتيها رزقها رغدا من كل مكان فكفرت بأنعم الله فأذاقها الله لباس الجوع والخوف بما كانوا يصنعون

translation: And indeed, there came to them a messenger from among themselves, but they denied him; so the punishment seized them while they were wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequence of rejecting a messenger sent by Allah. It emphasizes that when a community denies the truth brought by a prophet from their own people, they invite divine punishment upon themselves due to their injustice and wrongdoing. The verse serves as a reminder of the accountability for one's actions and the importance of heeding divine guidance.
orig: ولقد جاءهم رسول منهم فكذبوه فأخذهم العذاب وهم ظالمون

translation: So eat of what Allah has provided for you, lawful and good, and be grateful for the blessings of Allah if it is Him that you worship.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of consuming food that is permissible and pure, reflecting the broader Islamic principle of halal consumption. It also underscores the necessity of gratitude towards Allah for His provisions, linking the act of eating to worship and spiritual mindfulness. By eating what is lawful and good, and expressing gratitude, believers demonstrate their devotion and obedience to Allah, integrating their daily sustenance with their religious practice.
orig: فكلوا مما رزقكم الله حلالا طيبا واشكروا نعمت الله إن كنتم إياه تعبدون

translation: He has only forbidden to you dead meat, and blood, and the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than Allah. But if one is forced by necessity, without willful disobedience, nor transgressing due limits, then indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse outlines the dietary prohibitions in Islam, specifying that Muslims are forbidden from consuming carrion, blood, pork, and food dedicated to idols or other deities. However, it also provides a concession for those in extreme necessity, allowing them to consume these forbidden items if they are compelled by hunger and not out of defiance or excess. This exception highlights the merciful nature of Allah, who understands human needs and forgives those who are forced into such situations without deliberate transgression.
orig: إنما حرم عليكم الميتة والدم ولحم الخنزير وما أهل لغير الله به فمن اضطر غير باغ ولا عاد فإن الله غفور رحيم

translation: And do not say about what your tongues assert of falsehood, 'This is lawful and this is unlawful,' to invent lies about Allah. Indeed, those who invent lies about Allah will not succeed.
interpretation: This verse warns against the grave sin of attributing false statements to Allah, particularly in the context of declaring things as lawful or unlawful without divine authority. It emphasizes the importance of adhering strictly to the revealed laws and not innovating in religion, as such actions not only mislead others but also incur divine displeasure and lead to failure in both worldly and spiritual terms.
orig: ولا تقولوا لما تصف ألسنتكم الكذب هذا حلال وهذا حرام لتفتروا على الله الكذب إن الذين يفترون على الله الكذب لا يفلحون

translation: A little enjoyment, and they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the worldly pleasures and material gains that some people pursue are fleeting and insignificant when compared to the eternal consequences of their actions. It serves as a reminder that those who indulge in such temporary enjoyments at the expense of their moral and spiritual duties will face a severe punishment in the hereafter. The phrase emphasizes the contrast between the brief nature of worldly life and the enduring reality of the afterlife, urging believers to prioritize their actions with the long-term perspective in mind.
orig: متاع قليل ولهم عذاب أليم

translation: And upon those who are Jews, We forbade what We have related to you before; and We did not wrong them, but they were wronging themselves.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the prohibitions placed upon the Jews were not an act of injustice from Allah, but rather a consequence of their own actions. It suggests that the Jews, through their own choices and behaviors, brought upon themselves the restrictions mentioned in previous verses. The emphasis here is on personal responsibility and the idea that divine decrees often reflect the moral state of the people they affect.
orig: وعلى الذين هادوا حرمنا ما قصصنا عليك من قبل وما ظلمناهم ولكن كانوا أنفسهم يظلمون

translation: Then, indeed your Lord, to those who have done wrong out of ignorance and then repent after that and correct themselves - indeed, your Lord, thereafter, is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the mercy and forgiveness of Allah. It highlights that even those who commit sins due to ignorance can be forgiven if they sincerely repent and make amends. The verse reassures believers that Allah's mercy is vast and that He is always ready to forgive those who turn back to Him with genuine repentance and effort to improve their actions.
orig: ثم إن ربك للذين عملوا السوء بجهالة ثم تابوا من بعد ذلك وأصلحوا إن ربك من بعدها لغفور رحيم

translation: Indeed, Abraham was a nation, obedient to Allah, inclining toward truth, and he was not of those who associate others with Allah.
interpretation: This verse highlights the exemplary status of Prophet Abraham, describing him as a 'nation' due to his profound influence and righteousness. His unwavering obedience to Allah and his monotheistic stance set him apart from idolaters, emphasizing his role as a model of devotion and purity in faith for all believers.
orig: إن إبراهيم كان أمة قانتا لله حنيفا ولم يك من المشركين

translation: Grateful for His blessings, He chose him and guided him to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of gratitude towards Allah's blessings. It emphasizes that being thankful leads to divine selection and guidance towards the righteous path. The chosen individual is not only favored by Allah but also directed towards a life of moral and spiritual integrity.
orig: شاكرا لأنعمه اجتباه وهداه إلى صراط مستقيم

translation: And We gave him good in this world, and indeed, in the Hereafter he will be among the righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights the dual blessings bestowed upon a person by Allah; not only does he receive goodness and prosperity in his earthly life, but he is also promised a place among the righteous in the Hereafter. It underscores the concept of divine favor that extends beyond the temporal world into eternal life, emphasizing that true success is measured by one's standing in the afterlife.
orig: وآتيناه في الدنيا حسنة وإنه في الآخرة لمن الصالحين

translation: Then We revealed to you, [O Muhammad], to follow the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth; and he was not of the polytheists.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad to adhere to the monotheistic faith of Abraham, who is described as a 'ḥanīf' - someone who turns away from polytheism and inclines towards the pure, unadulterated worship of one God. The emphasis on Abraham not being among the polytheists underscores the rejection of idolatry and the affirmation of pure monotheism as the core of the prophetic message.
orig: ثم أوحينا إليك أن اتبع ملة إبراهيم حنيفا وما كان من المشركين

translation: The Sabbath was only appointed for those who differed about it. And indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the institution of the Sabbath was specifically legislated for the Jewish people as a test and a matter of differentiation among them. It underscores the idea that religious obligations can serve as trials to distinguish between those who adhere faithfully and those who deviate. The verse also reassures believers that all disputes and differences regarding religious practices will ultimately be resolved by God on the Day of Judgment, emphasizing divine justice and the accountability of all actions and beliefs.
orig: إنما جعل السبت على الذين اختلفوا فيه وإن ربك ليحكم بينهم يوم القيامة فيما كانوا فيه يختلفون

translation: Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good instruction, and argue with them in a way that is best. Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of who is guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of using wisdom, kindness, and the best form of argumentation when inviting others to Islam. It teaches that the approach to da'wah (invitation to Islam) should be gentle and respectful, reflecting the attributes of wisdom and good advice. The verse also reassures the believer that the ultimate knowledge of who is misguided or rightly guided belongs to Allah alone, encouraging patience and trust in divine wisdom rather than being overly concerned with the immediate outcomes of one's efforts.
orig: ادع إلى سبيل ربك بالحكمة والموعظة الحسنة وجادلهم بالتي هي أحسن إن ربك هو أعلم بمن ضل عن سبيله وهو أعلم بالمهتدين

translation: And if you punish, then punish with the like of that with which you were afflicted. But if you endure patiently, indeed, that is better for the patient.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of proportionality in retaliation, suggesting that any punishment should not exceed the harm inflicted. However, it elevates patience and endurance above retaliation, indicating that choosing to bear the harm patiently is more virtuous and spiritually rewarding. This reflects the Islamic value of patience (sabr) as a means to achieve higher moral ground and spiritual growth.
orig: وإن عاقبتم فعاقبوا بمثل ما عوقبتم به ولئن صبرتم لهو خير للصابرين

translation: And be patient, and your patience is only with the help of Allah. And do not grieve over them, and do not be in distress over what they plot.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of patience in the face of adversity, reminding believers that true patience comes from reliance on Allah. It encourages steadfastness and discourages being overwhelmed or saddened by the actions and plots of others, promoting a trust in divine wisdom and timing.
orig: واصبر وما صبرك إلا بالله ولا تحزن عليهم ولا تك في ضيق مما يمكرون

translation: Indeed, Allah is with those who fear Him and those who are doers of good.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah's presence and support are with those who exhibit taqwa (fear of Allah and consciousness of Him) and those who actively engage in acts of goodness and righteousness. It serves as a reassurance and encouragement for believers to maintain piety and perform good deeds, knowing that they are never alone in their efforts as Allah is with them, guiding and supporting them.
orig: إن الله مع الذين اتقوا والذين هم محسنون

translation: Glory be to Him Who took His servant by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque, whose surroundings We have blessed, to show him some of Our signs. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.
interpretation: This verse refers to the miraculous journey of Prophet Muhammad, known as the Night Journey (Isra) and Ascension (Mi'raj). It highlights God's omnipotence and His ability to transport His servant across vast distances in a single night, from Mecca to Jerusalem. The journey serves as a demonstration of divine signs to the Prophet, affirming his status and mission. The mention of God being All-Hearing and All-Seeing emphasizes His complete awareness and oversight of all events, reinforcing the believers' trust in His divine plan.
orig: سبحان الذي أسرى بعبده ليلا من المسجد الحرام إلى المسجد الأقصى الذي باركنا حوله لنريه من آياتنا إنه هو السميع البصير

translation: And We gave Moses the Scripture and made it a guidance for the Children of Israel, [saying]: 'Take not other than Me as a disposer of affairs.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin and purpose of the Torah given to Moses, which was intended as a guide specifically for the Children of Israel. The command not to take anyone other than God as a disposer of affairs underscores the importance of monotheism and direct reliance on God, rejecting any intermediaries or false deities in matters of faith and governance.
orig: وآتينا موسى الكتاب وجعلناه هدى لبني إسرائيل ألا تتخذوا من دوني وكيلا

translation: Offspring of those We carried [in the ship] with Noah. Indeed, he was a grateful servant.
interpretation: This verse highlights the lineage of those who were saved with Noah on the ark, emphasizing their connection to a righteous ancestor. It underscores the importance of gratitude and obedience to God, as exemplified by Noah, who is described as a grateful servant. The mention of Noah's gratitude serves as a reminder for believers to cultivate a similar attitude of thankfulness towards God's blessings and guidance.
orig: ذرية من حملنا مع نوح إنه كان عبدا شكورا

translation: And We decreed for the Children of Israel in the Book: 'You will surely cause corruption on the earth twice, and you will surely reach [a degree of] great haughtiness.'
interpretation: This verse indicates a divine decree that the Children of Israel will experience two periods of corruption and moral decline. This is not a predestination of their actions but a forewarning of the consequences of straying from the path of righteousness. The 'great haughtiness' refers to their potential for arrogance and pride, which historically has led to their downfall. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of humility and adherence to divine guidance.
orig: وقضينا إلى بني إسرائيل في الكتاب لتفسدن في الأرض مرتين ولتعلن علوا كبيرا

translation: So when the promise of the first of the two came, We sent against you servants of Ours, possessing severe might, and they ransacked the houses; and it was a promise fulfilled.
interpretation: This verse refers to the historical event where the Children of Israel were punished for their disobedience and corruption. The "promise of the first of the two" alludes to the first of two punishments mentioned in the Qur'an. God sent a powerful army, described as "servants of Ours, possessing severe might," which could be interpreted as the Babylonian forces led by Nebuchadnezzar. These forces devastated the land, ransacking homes, which symbolizes the complete destruction and the fulfillment of God's warning. This serves as a reminder of the consequences of straying from God's path and the certainty of divine promises.
orig: فإذا جاء وعد أولاهما بعثنا عليكم عبادا لنا أولي بأس شديد فجاسوا خلال الديار وكان وعدا مفعولا

translation: Then We gave you once again your turn against them, and We aided you with wealth and children and made you more numerous in manpower.
interpretation: This verse highlights the cyclical nature of power and divine favor, illustrating how God can shift dominance from one group to another as a test or a lesson. Here, it specifically refers to the restoration of power to the Israelites after a period of subjugation, emphasizing God's role in providing them with resources and increasing their numbers as a means of empowerment and as a sign of His support. This reflects the broader theme in the Qur'an of God's sovereignty over human affairs and His ability to change the fortunes of nations according to His wisdom and plan.
orig: ثم رددنا لكم الكرة عليهم وأمددناكم بأموال وبنين وجعلناكم أكثر نفيرا

translation: If you do good, you do good for yourselves; and if you do evil, [you do it] to yourselves. Then when the promise of the Hereafter comes, they will be made to suffer - so that they will enter the mosque as they entered it the first time, and they will destroy all that they conquered, completely destroying it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes personal responsibility for one's actions, highlighting that the consequences of good or evil deeds directly affect the individual. It also serves as a warning about the transient nature of worldly gains and power, illustrated by the historical example of the destruction of the Temple in Jerusalem by the Babylonians, and later events. The verse suggests that just as previous nations faced divine retribution for their actions, those who follow similar paths of corruption and oppression will face a similar fate in the Hereafter, where their achievements will be utterly destroyed, symbolizing the ultimate futility of evil.
orig: إن أحسنتم أحسنتم لأنفسكم وإن أسأتم فلها فإذا جاء وعد الآخرة ليسوءوا وجوهكم وليدخلوا المسجد كما دخلوه أول مرة وليتبروا ما علوا تتبيرا

translation: Perhaps your Lord will have mercy on you, but if you return (to sin), We will return (to punishment). And We have made Hell a prison for the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse conveys a message of hope and warning. It suggests that Allah's mercy is always available and He may forgive the sins of those who repent. However, it also serves as a stern warning that if people revert to their sinful ways after receiving guidance, they will face the consequences of their actions. The mention of Hell as a prison for disbelievers emphasizes the severity of the punishment awaiting those who persistently reject faith and continue in disbelief.
orig: عسى ربكم أن يرحمكم وإن عدتم عدنا وجعلنا جهنم للكافرين حصيرا

translation: Indeed, this Qur'an guides to that which is most suitable and gives good tidings to the believers who do righteous deeds that they will have a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Qur'an's role as a guide towards the most upright and beneficial path in life. It also serves as a source of hope and encouragement for believers, assuring them that their righteous actions will be rewarded significantly in the hereafter. The promise of a 'great reward' motivates believers to persist in their good deeds, reinforcing the importance of faith combined with virtuous actions.
orig: إن هذا القرآن يهدي للتي هي أقوم ويبشر المؤمنين الذين يعملون الصالحات أن لهم أجرا كبيرا

translation: And that those who do not believe in the Hereafter - We have prepared for them a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse underscores the consequence of disbelief in the Hereafter, emphasizing that such a fundamental rejection of faith leads to a severe punishment prepared by God. It serves as a warning to those who deny the existence of life after death, highlighting the importance of faith in the divine scheme of accountability and justice.
orig: وأن الذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة أعتدنا لهم عذابا أليما

translation: And man supplicates for evil as he supplicates for good, and man is ever hasty.
interpretation: This verse highlights a fundamental aspect of human nature where individuals often pray or wish for things that may ultimately be harmful to them, just as they do for things that are beneficial. It points out the human tendency to be impatient and hasty in desires and decisions, often not considering the long-term consequences of what they are asking for. This impatience and lack of foresight can lead to supplicating for outcomes that might seem good in the short term but are detrimental in the long run.
orig: ويدع الإنسان بالشر دعاءه بالخير وكان الإنسان عجولا

translation: And We have made the night and the day two signs. Then We effaced the sign of the night and made the sign of the day visible that you may seek bounty from your Lord and that you may know the number of years and the calculation. And We have explained everything in detail.
interpretation: This verse highlights the purposeful design of day and night by Allah, illustrating His power and wisdom. The alternation of day and night serves multiple functions: it enables humans to seek sustenance and blessings from Allah, and it provides a means to measure time, which is essential for organizing life and understanding the passage of years. The verse emphasizes Allah's meticulous planning and His provision of clear signs and detailed explanations for human guidance and benefit.
orig: وجعلنا الليل والنهار آيتين فمحونا آية الليل وجعلنا آية النهار مبصرة لتبتغوا فضلا من ربكم ولتعلموا عدد السنين والحساب وكل شيء فصلناه تفصيلا

translation: And every soul We have fastened to it its fate upon its neck, and We will bring forth for it on the Day of Resurrection a record which it will find spread out.
interpretation: This verse signifies that every individual is responsible for their actions, as symbolized by the fate or record tied to their neck. On the Day of Resurrection, this record of their deeds will be presented to them in a clear and open manner, indicating that no one can escape accountability for their actions in this life.
orig: وكل إنسان ألزمناه طائره في عنقه ونخرج له يوم القيامة كتابا يلقاه منشورا

translation: Read your book. Your own self is sufficient as a reckoner against you this day.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes personal accountability on the Day of Judgment. It suggests that an individual's own deeds, recorded in their life's book, will serve as undeniable evidence against them. The soul itself will bear witness to its actions, indicating that no external accuser is needed; one's conscience and record of deeds are enough to hold them accountable.
orig: اقرأ كتابك كفى بنفسك اليوم عليك حسيبا

translation: Whoever is guided is only guided for [the benefit of] his soul, and whoever errs only errs against it. And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. And never would We punish until We have sent a messenger.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes personal responsibility and accountability in matters of guidance and misguidance. It teaches that the path one chooses to follow, whether it leads to guidance or astray, directly impacts their own soul and no one else's. The mention of not bearing another's burden underscores the individual nature of spiritual accountability. Furthermore, the verse asserts the divine justice in not punishing people until they have been warned through the sending of a messenger, highlighting the importance of divine guidance and the opportunity for repentance before judgment.
orig: من اهتدى فإنما يهتدي لنفسه ومن ضل فإنما يضل عليها ولا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى وما كنا معذبين حتى نبعث رسولا

translation: And when We intend to destroy a town, We command its affluent ones, but they defiantly disobey therein; so the word comes into effect upon it, and We destroy it with utter destruction.
interpretation: This verse underscores the concept of divine justice and the consequences of moral corruption. It illustrates that when a community is marked for destruction due to its moral decay, Allah first commands its affluent and influential members to reform, giving them a chance to change their ways. However, if they persist in their disobedience and immorality, their fate is sealed, and the divine decree of destruction is carried out. This serves as a reminder of the responsibility of the privileged in society to lead with righteousness and the severe consequences of failing to do so.
orig: وإذا أردنا أن نهلك قرية أمرنا مترفيها ففسقوا فيها فحق عليها القول فدمرناها تدميرا

translation: And how many generations have We destroyed after Noah! And sufficient is your Lord as All-Aware and All-Seeing of the sins of His servants.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's omnipotence and omniscience, reminding believers that He has the power to destroy entire civilizations due to their transgressions, as He did with numerous generations after Noah. It serves as a warning that Allah is fully aware of and sees all the sins committed by His servants, underscoring the importance of righteousness and obedience to His commands.
orig: وكم أهلكنا من القرون من بعد نوح وكفى بربك بذنوب عباده خبيرا بصيرا

translation: Whoever desires the immediate, We hasten for him therein what We will to whom We intend. Then We have made for him Hell, which he will enter, blamed and banished.
interpretation: This verse addresses the consequences of prioritizing worldly gains over spiritual and moral values. It suggests that those who seek only the immediate pleasures and benefits of this life will be granted them by Allah as a test or a temporary provision. However, this focus on the ephemeral leads to a spiritual downfall, ultimately resulting in their entry into Hell. The terms 'blamed' and 'banished' indicate the disgrace and isolation they will experience in the afterlife due to their short-sightedness and neglect of the hereafter.
orig: من كان يريد العاجلة عجلنا له فيها ما نشاء لمن نريد ثم جعلنا له جهنم يصلاها مذموما مدحورا

translation: And whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it with the effort it deserves, while he is a believer, then indeed, their striving will be appreciated.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sincere effort towards achieving the rewards of the Hereafter. It highlights that a believer's dedication and hard work towards spiritual goals, when driven by true faith, will be recognized and rewarded by Allah. The verse encourages Muslims to focus on their ultimate goal of pleasing Allah and attaining Paradise, assuring them that their efforts in this regard are not in vain but will be met with gratitude and appreciation from the Almighty.
orig: ومن أراد الآخرة وسعى لها سعيها وهو مؤمن فأولئك كان سعيهم مشكورا

translation: Nay, We shall provide for these and those from the bounty of your Lord, and the bounty of your Lord is not restricted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the boundless generosity and provision of Allah. It indicates that Allah provides for all people, regardless of their faith or status, illustrating His universal mercy and the non-restrictive nature of His bounty. This reassures believers that divine provision is available to everyone, and it encourages a sense of gratitude and trust in Allah's endless capacity to provide.
orig: كلا نمد هؤلاء وهؤلاء من عطاء ربك وما كان عطاء ربك محظورا

translation: Look how We have favored some of them over others, and the Hereafter is greater in degrees and greater in preference.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of divine favor and the varying degrees of provision and status that Allah bestows upon individuals in this worldly life. It serves as a reminder that while some may be granted more worldly advantages, the true and ultimate distinction lies in the Hereafter. The verse encourages believers to focus on achieving higher spiritual ranks and divine favor in the afterlife, which surpasses any temporal benefits or distinctions in this world.
orig: انظر كيف فضلنا بعضهم على بعض وللآخرة أكبر درجات وأكبر تفضيلا

translation: Do not set up with Allah another god, lest you sit disgraced and forsaken.
interpretation: This verse warns against the grave sin of associating partners with Allah (shirk), which is considered the most severe transgression in Islam. By engaging in shirk, one risks being left in a state of disgrace and abandonment, both in this life and the hereafter. The verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining the purity of faith in the oneness of Allah, as deviation from this fundamental principle leads to spiritual ruin and divine rejection.
orig: لا تجعل مع الله إلها آخر فتقعد مذموما مخذولا

translation: And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him, and that you be dutiful to your parents. If one of them or both of them attain old age in your life, say not to them a word of disrespect, nor shout at them, but address them in terms of honor.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental Islamic principle of monotheism, requiring believers to worship only Allah. Additionally, it highlights the importance of treating parents with utmost respect and kindness, especially in their old age. The command to not utter any word of disrespect or raise one's voice against them, and instead to speak to them with honor, underscores the high moral and ethical standards expected in familial relationships. This directive reflects the balance between devotion to God and the responsibilities towards family, illustrating that spiritual obligations and social duties are interconnected in Islam.
orig: وقضى ربك ألا تعبدوا إلا إياه وبالوالدين إحسانا إما يبلغن عندك الكبر أحدهما أو كلاهما فلا تقل لهما أف ولا تنهرهما وقل لهما قولا كريما

translation: And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy and say, 'My Lord, have mercy upon them as they brought me up [when I was] small.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of showing utmost respect, humility, and kindness to one's parents. It instructs believers to approach their parents with gentleness and compassion, symbolized by lowering the 'wing of humility.' Additionally, it encourages supplicating to Allah for the parents' well-being and mercy, acknowledging the care and nurturing they provided during one's childhood. This reflects the deep gratitude and continuous duty towards parents, highlighting the moral and spiritual values of respect and mercy in Islam.
orig: واخفض لهما جناح الذل من الرحمة وقل رب ارحمهما كما ربياني صغيرا

translation: Your Lord knows best what is in your souls. If you are righteous, then He is Most Forgiving to those who turn to Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience of Allah, indicating that He has complete knowledge of the innermost thoughts and intentions of individuals. It reassures believers that if they strive to be righteous and maintain good intentions, Allah, in His infinite mercy, is ready to forgive those who sincerely repent and turn back to Him. This serves as an encouragement for believers to continuously seek righteousness and repentance, knowing that Allah's forgiveness is always accessible to the penitent.
orig: ربكم أعلم بما في نفوسكم إن تكونوا صالحين فإنه كان للأوابين غفورا

translation: And give the relative his right, and the needy, and the traveler, and do not spend wastefully.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fulfilling one's financial obligations to close relatives, the poor, and travelers in need. It instructs believers to be charitable and to share their wealth with those who are entitled to it, such as family members and those in need. However, it also warns against extravagance and wasteful spending, encouraging a balanced approach to giving that is neither miserly nor excessive.
orig: وآت ذا القربى حقه والمسكين وابن السبيل ولا تبذر تبذيرا

translation: Indeed, the wasteful are brothers of the devils, and ever has Satan been to his Lord ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the moral and spiritual kinship between those who wastefully spend their resources and the devils, suggesting that such behavior aligns with satanic influence. It emphasizes that ingratitude and excess are traits of Satan, who is characterized as ungrateful to his Lord. Thus, the verse serves as a warning against extravagance and a reminder to be mindful and grateful for the blessings bestowed by Allah.
orig: إن المبذرين كانوا إخوان الشياطين وكان الشيطان لربه كفورا

translation: And if you [O Muhammad] turn away from them, seeking mercy from your Lord which you hope for, then speak to them a gentle word.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad to maintain a gentle and kind demeanor towards his followers, even if he chooses to distance himself from them temporarily in pursuit of divine mercy. It emphasizes the importance of compassion and gentle communication in leadership and interpersonal relations, reflecting the broader Islamic values of mercy and understanding.
orig: وإما تعرضن عنهم ابتغاء رحمة من ربك ترجوها فقل لهم قولا ميسورا

translation: And do not make your hand tied to your neck, nor extend it fully, lest you sit blamed and impoverished.
interpretation: This verse advises moderation in spending. It warns against being overly stingy, symbolized by keeping one's hand tied to the neck, as well as against being excessively generous to the point of recklessness, symbolized by extending the hand fully. The middle path is recommended to avoid the consequences of being criticized and ending up in a state of deprivation.
orig: ولا تجعل يدك مغلولة إلى عنقك ولا تبسطها كل البسط فتقعد ملوما محسورا

translation: Indeed, your Lord extends provision for whom He wills and restricts [it]. Indeed He is ever, concerning His servants, Acquainted and Seeing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine attribute of Allah as the sole provider, emphasizing His complete control over sustenance. It reassures believers that Allah's distribution of provision, whether abundant or limited, is based on His wisdom and knowledge. The verse underscores that Allah is fully aware of and observant over the conditions and needs of His servants, encouraging trust in His providence and fairness.
orig: إن ربك يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء ويقدر إنه كان بعباده خبيرا بصيرا

translation: And do not kill your children out of fear of poverty; We provide for them and for you. Indeed, their killing is a great sin.
interpretation: This verse addresses the prohibition of infanticide, a practice that was prevalent in pre-Islamic Arabia, often motivated by economic hardship or fear of not being able to provide for additional children. The verse reassures believers that sustenance is provided by Allah for all, thus alleviating the fear of poverty as a justification for such an act. It emphasizes the sanctity of life and classifies the killing of one's children as a grave sin, highlighting the moral and ethical responsibilities towards offspring.
orig: ولا تقتلوا أولادكم خشية إملاق نحن نرزقهم وإياكم إن قتلهم كان خطئا كبيرا

translation: And do not approach adultery; indeed, it is an immorality and an evil way.
interpretation: This verse serves as a strong prohibition against adultery, emphasizing not only the act itself but also any actions that lead towards it. It highlights the moral and ethical degradation associated with such behavior, labeling it as a shameful and harmful path that leads individuals away from righteousness and towards corruption.
orig: ولا تقربوا الزنا إنه كان فاحشة وساء سبيلا

translation: And do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right. And whoever is killed unjustly - We have given his heir authority, but let him not exceed limits in [the matter of] taking life. Indeed, he has been supported [by the law].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sanctity of human life, prohibiting murder except in cases where it is justified by Islamic law, such as in cases of legal retribution or self-defense. It also provides a mechanism for justice by granting the heir of the unjustly killed person the authority to seek retribution, but it cautions against excessive retaliation, indicating that the legal and moral support provided by Allah's law should guide the heir's actions.
orig: ولا تقتلوا النفس التي حرم الله إلا بالحق ومن قتل مظلوما فقد جعلنا لوليه سلطانا فلا يسرف في القتل إنه كان منصورا

translation: And do not approach the property of the orphan, except in the best possible way, until he reaches maturity. And fulfill every covenant; indeed, the covenant will be questioned about.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of safeguarding the rights and property of orphans, urging believers to manage their assets with utmost integrity and fairness until they are old enough to handle their affairs. Additionally, it underscores the significance of fulfilling all commitments and contracts, reminding us that we will be held accountable for our promises in the hereafter.
orig: ولا تقربوا مال اليتيم إلا بالتي هي أحسن حتى يبلغ أشده وأوفوا بالعهد إن العهد كان مسئولا

translation: And give full measure when you measure, and weigh with a balance that is straight. That is good and better in the end.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of honesty and fairness in transactions. It instructs believers to ensure they give full measure and use accurate scales when dealing in trade, reflecting the broader Islamic principle of justice in all dealings. The phrase 'that is good and better in the end' suggests that adhering to these ethical standards not only fulfills religious obligations but also leads to better outcomes in worldly and spiritual terms.
orig: وأوفوا الكيل إذا كلتم وزنوا بالقسطاس المستقيم ذلك خير وأحسن تأويلا

translation: And do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge. Indeed, the hearing, the sight and the heart - about all those [one] will be questioned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of not engaging in or spreading information without proper knowledge. It serves as a reminder that individuals are accountable for what they hear, see, and feel in their hearts. The verse underscores the concept of personal responsibility in Islam, urging believers to be mindful of their actions and the information they consume and disseminate, as they will be held accountable for these on the Day of Judgment.
orig: ولا تقف ما ليس لك به علم إن السمع والبصر والفؤاد كل أولئك كان عنه مسئولا

translation: And do not walk upon the earth exultantly. Indeed, you will never tear the earth [apart], and you will never reach the mountains in height.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder to maintain humility and not to behave arrogantly or with excessive pride. It emphasizes that no matter how powerful or important one may feel, they cannot alter the fundamental nature of the earth or surpass the height of mountains. This is a metaphor for the limits of human power and the importance of recognizing one's place in the grand scheme of creation, encouraging believers to walk humbly and with respect for the natural order established by Allah.
orig: ولا تمش في الأرض مرحا إنك لن تخرق الأرض ولن تبلغ الجبال طولا

translation: All that was evil in the sight of your Lord, detested.
interpretation: This verse indicates that actions or behaviors considered sinful or morally wrong are not only disliked but are deeply abhorrent to Allah. It emphasizes the severity of such actions in the eyes of the Divine, urging believers to avoid them due to their grave nature and the strong disapproval they incur from Allah.
orig: كل ذلك كان سيئه عند ربك مكروها

translation: That is from what your Lord has revealed to you of wisdom. And do not make another god with Allah, or you will be thrown into Hell, blameworthy and rejected.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin of the wisdom imparted to the Prophet Muhammad, indicating that it comes directly from Allah. It serves as a reminder to maintain the purity of monotheism (Tawheed) and warns against the grave sin of associating partners with Allah (Shirk). The consequence of such an act is severe punishment in Hell, where one will be both blameworthy for their actions and rejected by Allah. This underscores the importance of steadfastness in faith and the dire consequences of straying from the path of monotheism.
orig: ذلك مما أوحى إليك ربك من الحكمة ولا تجعل مع الله إلها آخر فتلقى في جهنم ملوما مدحورا

translation: Has your Lord then preferred for you sons, and taken for Himself from among the angels females? Indeed, you say a tremendous saying!
interpretation: This verse critiques the pre-Islamic Arab belief that God had daughters among the angels, while they preferred sons for themselves. It highlights the absurdity and blasphemy of attributing human-like gender preferences to God, emphasizing the gravity of such a claim against the divine nature of Allah, who is beyond human concepts of gender and familial roles.
orig: أفأصفاكم ربكم بالبنين واتخذ من الملائكة إناثا إنكم لتقولون قولا عظيما

translation: And indeed We have explained in this Qur'an that they may be reminded, but it only increases them in aversion.
interpretation: This verse suggests that despite the clarity and detailed explanations provided in the Qur'an, intended to guide and remind people of the truth, some individuals react with increased rejection and aversion. It highlights the human tendency to resist guidance due to various internal and external factors, emphasizing the challenge of overcoming personal biases and the importance of an open heart in receiving divine messages.
orig: ولقد صرفنا في هذا القرآن ليذكروا وما يزيدهم إلا نفورا

translation: Say, If there had been with Him other gods, as they say, then they would have sought a way to the Owner of the Throne.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the uniqueness and oneness of God (Tawheed). It suggests that if there were multiple gods, as claimed by polytheists, these gods would have competed for power and sought to overthrow the supreme God, the Owner of the Throne. The absence of such conflict and the orderly nature of the universe serve as evidence of the existence of only one God, who is unrivaled and sovereign.
orig: قل لو كان معه آلهة كما يقولون إذا لابتغوا إلى ذي العرش سبيلا

translation: Glory be to Him, and high be He above what they say, a great highness.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the transcendence and majesty of Allah, declaring His absolute purity and greatness far beyond any false claims or descriptions attributed to Him by others. It serves as a reminder of Allah's supreme nature, encouraging believers to recognize and revere His exalted status.
orig: سبحانه وتعالى عما يقولون علوا كبيرا

translation: The seven heavens and the earth and all that is in them glorify Him. And there is not a thing but glorifies His praise, but you understand not their glorification. Indeed, He is Ever Forbearing, Oft-Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universal nature of glorification of Allah, extending beyond human comprehension. It suggests that every element of creation, from the vast heavens to the smallest particle on earth, inherently praises Allah in ways that humans cannot fully understand. This highlights the omnipresence and greatness of Allah, as well as His attributes of patience and forgiveness, encouraging believers to recognize and appreciate the unseen aspects of divine worship and to trust in Allah's merciful nature.
orig: تسبح له السماوات السبع والأرض ومن فيهن وإن من شيء إلا يسبح بحمده ولكن لا تفقهون تسبيحهم إنه كان حليما غفورا

translation: And when you recite the Qur'an, We place between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter a hidden barrier.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual and psychological divide that occurs when the Qur'an is recited. It suggests that the recitation of the Qur'an creates a barrier, not just a physical or visible one, but a profound, hidden separation between believers and non-believers, particularly those who deny the Hereafter. This barrier is indicative of the different ways in which the message of the Qur'an is received and understood by different groups of people, emphasizing the deep impact of faith and the Qur'an's role in distinguishing between those who accept its message and those who reject it.
orig: وإذا قرأت القرآن جعلنا بينك وبين الذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة حجابا مستورا

translation: And We have placed over their hearts coverings, lest they understand it, and in their ears deafness. And when you mention your Lord alone in the Qur'an, they turn their backs in aversion.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual and psychological barriers that prevent some individuals from understanding and accepting the message of the Qur'an. The 'coverings over their hearts' and 'deafness in their ears' symbolize the internal resistance and unwillingness to engage with the truth. When the oneness of God is emphasized, their aversion becomes evident as they physically and metaphorically turn away, indicating a deep-seated rejection of monotheism.
orig: وجعلنا على قلوبهم أكنة أن يفقهوه وفي آذانهم وقرا وإذا ذكرت ربك في القرآن وحده ولوا على أدبارهم نفورا

translation: We know best what they listen to when they listen to you, and when they are in secret talk, when the wrong-doers say, 'You follow none other than a man bewitched.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the omniscience of Allah, emphasizing that He is fully aware of the intentions and discussions of the disbelievers when they listen to the Prophet Muhammad. It points out their secretive and dismissive attitude towards the Prophet, labeling him as bewitched, which reflects their denial and resistance to the divine message. The verse serves as a reassurance to the Prophet and believers that Allah is cognizant of the disbelievers' mockery and their attempts to undermine the message of Islam.
orig: نحن أعلم بما يستمعون به إذ يستمعون إليك وإذ هم نجوى إذ يقول الظالمون إن تتبعون إلا رجلا مسحورا

translation: Look how they strike for you comparisons; but they have strayed, so they cannot [find] a way.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futile attempts of those who oppose the Prophet Muhammad to discredit him by drawing false analogies. Their efforts are misguided and lead them astray from the truth, rendering them unable to find the right path. It emphasizes the importance of adhering to divine guidance rather than being swayed by misleading arguments.
orig: انظر كيف ضربوا لك الأمثال فضلوا فلا يستطيعون سبيلا

translation: And they say, "When we are bones and crumbled dust, will we [truly] be resurrected as a new creation?"
interpretation: This verse reflects the skepticism and disbelief of some people regarding the resurrection after death. They question how it is possible for them to be brought back to life as a new creation when their bodies have decayed into bones and dust. This highlights a common human doubt about the power of Allah to revive and recreate, emphasizing the miraculous nature of resurrection and the need for faith in Allah's omnipotence.
orig: وقالوا أإذا كنا عظاما ورفاتا أإنا لمبعوثون خلقا جديدا

translation: Say, 'Be stones or iron'
interpretation: This verse is a command to the Prophet Muhammad to challenge the disbelievers by saying that even if they were to become as hard and unyielding as stones or iron, the message of Islam would still reach them. It emphasizes the unstoppable nature of divine truth and the futility of resistance against it.
orig: قل كونوا حجارة أو حديدا

translation: Or were they created from nothing, or are they the creators? Or did they create the heavens and the earth? Rather, they are not certain. Or do they possess the treasures of your Lord, or are they the controllers? Or have they a ladder by which they listen? Then let their listener bring a clear authority. Or has He taken daughters while you have sons? Or do you ask them for a payment, so they are weighed down by debt? Or do they have knowledge of the unseen, so they write it down? Or do they intend a plot? But those who disbelieve are the ones who are plotted against. Or do they have a god other than Allah? Exalted is Allah above what they associate with Him. Or were they created from nothing, or are they the creators? Or did they create the heavens and the earth? Rather, they are not certain. Or do they possess the treasures of your Lord, or are they the controllers? Or have they a ladder by which they listen? Then let their listener bring a clear authority. Or has He taken daughters while you have sons? Or do you ask them for a payment, so they are weighed down by debt? Or do they have knowledge of the unseen, so they write it down? Or do they intend a plot? But those who disbelieve are the ones who are plotted against. Or do they have a god other than Allah? Exalted is Allah above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse challenges the disbelievers by presenting a series of rhetorical questions that highlight the absurdity of their disbelief in the resurrection and the power of Allah. It underscores the logical inconsistencies in their arguments against the possibility of being brought back to life after death. The verse suggests that their skepticism stems from a lack of faith and understanding of Allah's omnipotence, as they cannot fathom how He could recreate them after death. The response to their question about who will bring them back to life, "Say, [He is] the one who brought you into being the first time," reaffirms Allah's role as the Creator and Sustainer of life, capable of resurrecting them just as He initially created them. The verse concludes with the disbelievers' reaction of disbelief and their inquiry about when this resurrection will occur, to which the response, "Perhaps it will be soon," serves as a reminder of the imminence and inevitability of the Day of Judgment, urging them to reflect on their beliefs and actions.
orig: أو خلقا مما يكبر في صدوركم فسيقولون من يعيدنا قل الذي فطركم أول مرة فسينغضون إليك رءوسهم ويقولون متى هو قل عسى أن يكون قريبا

translation: The Day He will call you and you will respond with His praise, and you will think that you stayed only a short while.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when Allah will call all people to account. On that day, people will respond to His call with praise and gratitude, acknowledging His power and mercy. Despite the long duration they spent in the worldly life and the hereafter, they will feel as though their time was very brief, highlighting the relativity and insignificance of worldly life in comparison to the eternal life to come.
orig: يوم يدعوكم فتستجيبون بحمده وتظنون إن لبثتم إلا قليلا

translation: And say to My servants that they should say that which is best. Indeed, Satan sows discord among them. Indeed, Satan is to man a clear enemy.
interpretation: This verse instructs believers to always speak in the best possible manner, promoting harmony and good relations. It warns that Satan actively tries to create discord and enmity among people, emphasizing that Satan is an obvious and declared enemy to humanity. The verse serves as a reminder to be vigilant against Satan's influence and to counteract it by choosing words and actions that foster positivity and unity.
orig: وقل لعبادي يقولوا التي هي أحسن إن الشيطان ينزغ بينهم إن الشيطان كان للإنسان عدوا مبينا

translation: Your Lord is most knowing of you. If He wills, He will have mercy upon you, and if He wills, He will punish you. And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], over them as a manager.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience and absolute authority of Allah over all creation. It reminds believers that Allah's knowledge encompasses everything about them, and His mercy or punishment is entirely at His discretion. The verse also clarifies the role of the Prophet Muhammad; he is not a guardian or controller over people, but a messenger conveying Allah's message. This underscores the individual responsibility of each person to heed the message and act accordingly, as they will be accountable directly to Allah.
orig: ربكم أعلم بكم إن يشأ يرحمكم أو إن يشأ يعذبكم وما أرسلناك عليهم وكيلا

translation: And your Lord is most knowing of whoever is in the heavens and the earth. And We have certainly preferred some of the prophets over others, and We gave David the Zabur.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience of Allah, indicating that He has complete knowledge of all beings in the universe. The preference of some prophets over others highlights the varying roles and responsibilities assigned by Allah to His messengers, reflecting divine wisdom in the distribution of prophetic missions. The mention of David receiving the Zabur (Psalms) underscores the special status and unique contributions of certain prophets, illustrating how Allah bestows specific scriptures and abilities tailored to the needs of different communities and times.
orig: وربك أعلم بمن في السماوات والأرض ولقد فضلنا بعض النبيين على بعض وآتينا داوود زبورا

translation: Say, 'Call upon those you have claimed [as deities] besides Him, for they do not possess the ability to remove affliction from you, nor [can they effect] any change.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the exclusive power and authority of Allah over all other entities. It instructs the Prophet Muhammad to challenge those who worship other deities to call upon them for help, highlighting that these false deities are powerless to relieve any hardship or alter any situation. The verse underscores the futility of polytheism and reinforces the concept of Tawhid, the oneness of Allah, urging believers to rely solely on Allah for protection and change.
orig: قل ادعوا الذين زعمتم من دونه فلا يملكون كشف الضر عنكم ولا تحويلا

translation: Those whom they invoke seek means of access to their Lord, [striving as to] which of them would be nearest, and they hope for His mercy and fear His punishment. Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is ever feared.
interpretation: This verse highlights the humility and devotion of the angels and other beings close to God. They are constantly seeking to draw nearer to Him, not out of a sense of competition, but out of a deep desire for closeness to their Creator. Their actions are driven by a hope for God's mercy and a fear of His punishment, underscoring the seriousness with which they approach their relationship with God. The verse also serves as a reminder to humans of the gravity of God's punishment, encouraging a similar reverence and mindfulness in our own spiritual lives.
orig: أولئك الذين يدعون يبتغون إلى ربهم الوسيلة أيهم أقرب ويرجون رحمته ويخافون عذابه إن عذاب ربك كان محذورا

translation: And there is no town but We will destroy it before the Day of Resurrection, or punish it with a severe punishment. That is inscribed in the Book.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability of divine judgment and accountability for all communities. It serves as a reminder that no town or civilization is exempt from facing the consequences of their actions, either through destruction or severe punishment before the Day of Judgment. The reference to it being 'inscribed in the Book' underscores the predetermination and certainty of these events, highlighting the omniscience and justice of Allah.
