orig: وإن من قرية إلا نحن مهلكوها قبل يوم القيامة أو معذبوها عذابا شديدا كان ذلك في الكتاب مسطورا

translation: And We did not send the signs except that the former peoples denied them. And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a clear sign, but they wronged it. And We do not send the signs except as a warning.
interpretation: This verse explains that Allah did not continuously send miraculous signs because the earlier nations rejected them, demonstrating their disbelief and ingratitude. The example of Thamud, who were given the she-camel as a clear sign of Allah's power and mercy, yet they transgressed by harming it, underscores human tendencies towards disbelief and injustice despite clear evidence. The verse emphasizes that the purpose of sending such signs is not for entertainment or to force belief, but as a means of warning and a call to heed the lessons from past nations, encouraging repentance and righteousness.
orig: وما منعنا أن نرسل بالآيات إلا أن كذب بها الأولون وآتينا ثمود الناقة مبصرة فظلموا بها وما نرسل بالآيات إلا تخويفا

translation: And [remember] when We said to you, 'Indeed, your Lord has encompassed the people.' And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people, and [also] the accursed tree in the Qur'an. And We threaten them, but it increases them not except in great transgression.
interpretation: This verse reflects on the divine knowledge and omnipresence of Allah, reminding the Prophet Muhammad that Allah is fully aware of all human actions. The vision granted to the Prophet serves as a test for humanity, assessing their faith and obedience. Similarly, the mention of the accursed tree in the Qur'an is another test, symbolizing the consequences of disobedience. Despite these warnings and threats, the verse suggests that some people only increase in their rebellion and transgression, highlighting the challenge of guiding those who are determined to stray from the path of righteousness.
orig: وإذ قلنا لك إن ربك أحاط بالناس وما جعلنا الرؤيا التي أريناك إلا فتنة للناس والشجرة الملعونة في القرآن ونخوفهم فما يزيدهم إلا طغيانا كبيرا

translation: And [mention] when We said to the angels, 'Prostrate to Adam,' and they prostrated, except for Iblees. He said, 'Should I prostrate to one You created from clay?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the moment of creation and the test of obedience among the angels. It underscores the theme of submission to God's command, as all angels complied except Iblees, who questioned God's directive due to his arrogance and pride. This refusal marks the beginning of Iblees's transformation into Satan, illustrating the consequences of disobedience and pride against divine will.
orig: وإذ قلنا للملائكة اسجدوا لآدم فسجدوا إلا إبليس قال أأسجد لمن خلقت طينا

translation: He said, 'Do you see this whom You have honored above me? If You delay me until the Day of Resurrection, I will surely destroy his descendants, except for a few.'
interpretation: This verse reveals Iblis's (Satan's) arrogance and envy towards Adam, whom God honored. Iblis expresses his intent to mislead and corrupt Adam's descendants until the Day of Judgment, except for those whom God protects. It underscores the ongoing spiritual battle between good and evil, highlighting Iblis's determination to lead humanity astray, yet acknowledging God's ultimate power to save a chosen few.
orig: قال أرأيتك هذا الذي كرمت علي لئن أخرتن إلى يوم القيامة لأحتنكن ذريته إلا قليلا

translation: He said, 'Go forth, and whoever follows you from among them, then indeed, Hell will be the recompense for you - an ample recompense.'
interpretation: This verse is directed towards Iblis (Satan) after he refused to prostrate to Adam, as commanded by Allah. It signifies the consequence of disobedience and rebellion against Allah's command. The verse emphasizes that those who follow Iblis in his path of defiance will share his fate in Hell, illustrating the severity and sufficiency of the punishment awaiting them. It serves as a warning to humanity about the dangers of following Satan and the ultimate accountability for one's choices.
orig: قال اذهب فمن تبعك منهم فإن جهنم جزاؤكم جزاء موفورا

translation: And incite [to senselessness] whoever you can among them with your voice and assault them with your cavalry and infantry and be a partner in their wealth and their children and promise them - but Satan does not promise them except delusion.
interpretation: This verse is directed towards Iblis (Satan), instructing him on how to mislead humanity. It suggests that Satan uses various methods to corrupt humans, including using persuasive speech to incite them towards sin, employing forces to intimidate them, and tempting them with worldly possessions and offspring. The verse also highlights the deceptive nature of Satan's promises, which ultimately lead to nothing but illusion and misguidance, emphasizing the importance of resisting these temptations and staying on the path of righteousness.
orig: واستفزز من استطعت منهم بصوتك وأجلب عليهم بخيلك ورجلك وشاركهم في الأموال والأولاد وعدهم وما يعدهم الشيطان إلا غرورا

translation: Indeed, My servants - you have no authority over them, and sufficient is your Lord as a Guardian.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the protection and sovereignty of Allah over His servants. It asserts that despite the temptations and influence of evil forces, represented here by Iblis (Satan), they have no real power over the believers who remain faithful to Allah. The phrase 'sufficient is your Lord as a Guardian' reassures believers of Allah's omnipotence and His role as the ultimate protector and guide, instilling a sense of security and trust in divine providence.
orig: إن عبادي ليس لك عليهم سلطان وكفى بربك وكيلا

translation: Your Lord is He Who drives the ships for you in the sea, that you may seek of His bounty; verily, He is Ever-Merciful towards you.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine providence and mercy of Allah, illustrating how He facilitates means of sustenance and travel through the sea. The ships, driven by the winds and currents which are under Allah's control, symbolize the blessings and opportunities provided by Him for humans to seek their livelihood and explore the world. The mention of Allah's mercy emphasizes that these provisions are not just acts of creation but are imbued with His compassion and care for humanity, encouraging gratitude and recognition of His benevolence.
orig: ربكم الذي يزجي لكم الفلك في البحر لتبتغوا من فضله إنه كان بكم رحيما

translation: And when distress afflicts you at sea, those you call upon vanish except for Him. But when He delivers you to the land, you turn away [from Him]. And ever is man ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to turn to God in times of desperation and distress, such as when facing peril at sea, only to forget and turn away from Him once safety is restored. It underscores the theme of ingratitude and forgetfulness that is common in human nature, reminding believers to maintain their faith and gratitude consistently, not just in times of need.
orig: وإذا مسكم الضر في البحر ضل من تدعون إلا إياه فلما نجاكم إلى البر أعرضتم وكان الإنسان كفورا

translation: Do you feel secure that He Who is in heaven will not cause the earth to swallow you up when it quakes? Or do you feel secure that He will not send against you a violent sandstorm? Then you will know the truth of My warning.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of Allah's omnipotence and the fragility of human security. It urges believers to remain conscious of Allah's power to alter their circumstances abruptly, such as through natural disasters like earthquakes or sandstorms, which can strike without warning. The verse emphasizes the importance of humility and constant awareness of Allah's might, encouraging a deeper faith and reliance on Him rather than feeling overly secure in worldly conditions.
orig: أفأمنتم أن يخسف بكم جانب البر أو يرسل عليكم حاصبا ثم لا تجدوا لكم وكيلا

translation: Or do you feel secure that He will not send you back to it another time and send upon you a hurricane of wind and drown you for your disbelief? Then you will not find for yourselves against Us an avenger.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of God's power and the consequences of disbelief. It warns that just as God can provide safety and prosperity, He can also bring about destruction and punishment if people turn away from faith. The mention of being sent back to the sea and facing a hurricane emphasizes the unpredictability and might of divine retribution. The verse underscores the idea that there is no one to appeal to or seek justice from against God's decisions, highlighting the absolute authority and justice of God.
orig: أم أمنتم أن يعيدكم فيه تارة أخرى فيرسل عليكم قاصفا من الريح فيغرقكم بما كفرتم ثم لا تجدوا لكم علينا به تبيعا

translation: And We have certainly honored the children of Adam and carried them on the land and sea and provided for them of the good things and preferred them greatly over many of those We have created, with [definite] preference.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the special status and honor bestowed upon humanity by Allah. It highlights that humans are distinguished among creation through the blessings of transportation across land and sea, provision of wholesome sustenance, and a general preference over many other creatures. This honor comes with the responsibility to recognize and appreciate Allah's favors, and to live in a manner that reflects gratitude and humility.
orig: ولقد كرمنا بني آدم وحملناهم في البر والبحر ورزقناهم من الطيبات وفضلناهم على كثير ممن خلقنا تفضيلا

translation: The Day when We will call every people with their leader; so whoever is given his record in his right hand - those will read their records, and injustice will not be done to them, even as much as a thread [inside the date seed].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Day of Judgment when individuals will be grouped according to their leaders or guides, reflecting their worldly affiliations and beliefs. The imagery of receiving the record in the right hand symbolizes success and divine approval. Those who receive their records in this manner are assured of fairness and justice, indicating that they will be rewarded without any injustice, no matter how small. This underscores the Qur'anic theme of divine justice and accountability, where every individual's deeds are meticulously recorded and justly evaluated.
orig: يوم ندعو كل أناس بإمامهم فمن أوتي كتابه بيمينه فأولئك يقرءون كتابهم ولا يظلمون فتيلا

translation: And whoever is blind in this [life] will be blind in the Hereafter and more astray in way.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the spiritual blindness or ignorance a person has in this worldly life will carry over into the afterlife, exacerbating their state of being lost and misguided. It emphasizes the importance of gaining spiritual insight and guidance in this life, as the consequences of remaining spiritually blind will be magnified in the Hereafter.
orig: ومن كان في هذه أعمى فهو في الآخرة أعمى وأضل سبيلا

translation: And indeed, they were about to tempt you away from that which We revealed to you, so that you would fabricate something else in Our name; and then they would have taken you as a close friend.
interpretation: This verse highlights the challenge faced by the Prophet Muhammad when his adversaries tried to mislead him from the divine message. It underscores the importance of steadfastness in conveying the truth as revealed by Allah, without alteration or fabrication. The verse also warns about the deceptive nature of those who might pretend to be allies but have ulterior motives to corrupt the divine message.
orig: وإن كادوا ليفتنونك عن الذي أوحينا إليك لتفتري علينا غيره وإذا لاتخذوك خليلا

translation: And if We had not made you stand firm, you would have almost inclined towards them a little.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine support and strength provided to the Prophet Muhammad by Allah, which prevented him from yielding to the pressures and temptations of his opponents. It underscores the importance of steadfastness in faith and the role of divine assistance in maintaining one's commitment to the truth.
orig: ولولا أن ثبتناك لقد كدت تركن إليهم شيئا قليلا

translation: Then will We certainly cause you to taste of the double of life and the double of death; then you shall not find for yourself against Us any helper.
interpretation: This verse warns of a severe punishment in the afterlife for those who reject faith. The "double of life and the double of death" refers to an intensified experience of suffering, suggesting that the punishment will be so severe it feels like living and dying twice. The phrase "then you shall not find for yourself against Us any helper" emphasizes the isolation and helplessness one will feel, indicating that no one will be able to intercede or assist against God's judgment. This underscores the importance of heeding God's warnings and living a righteous life to avoid such a fate.
orig: إذا لأذقناك ضعف الحياة وضعف الممات ثم لا تجد لك علينا نصيرا

translation: And they were about to tempt you away from the land [of Mecca] to expel you from it. And then they would not have remained after you except a little.
interpretation: This verse highlights the opposition faced by the Prophet Muhammad from the disbelievers in Mecca, who were plotting to drive him out of the city. It underscores the precarious situation of the early Muslim community and the hostility they encountered. The phrase 'they would not have remained after you except a little' suggests that the disbelievers' power and presence would have been short-lived had they succeeded in expelling the Prophet, indicating the ultimate triumph of the Islamic message despite the immediate threats.
orig: وإن كادوا ليستفزونك من الأرض ليخرجوك منها وإذا لا يلبثون خلافك إلا قليلا

translation: A way of life of those whom We sent before you of Our messengers, and you will not find any change in Our way of life.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consistency and unchangeable nature of the divine message and methodology across all prophets and messengers sent by Allah. It reassures the Prophet Muhammad that the challenges and opposition he faces are not unique but part of a recurring pattern experienced by all previous messengers. The verse underscores the importance of steadfastness and adherence to the divine path, as it has been established and will not be altered.
orig: سنة من قد أرسلنا قبلك من رسلنا ولا تجد لسنتنا تحويلا

translation: Establish prayer at the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night and the recitation of the dawn. Indeed, the recitation of the dawn is witnessed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of performing the five daily prayers at their designated times, specifically highlighting the times from the decline of the sun (Dhuhr prayer) until the darkness of the night (Isha prayer), and the dawn prayer (Fajr). The mention of the dawn prayer being 'witnessed' suggests that it is a particularly significant prayer, possibly attended by angels or other spiritual beings, underscoring its importance and the need for Muslims to be diligent in performing it.
orig: أقم الصلاة لدلوك الشمس إلى غسق الليل وقرآن الفجر إن قرآن الفجر كان مشهودا

translation: And from the night, keep vigil with it as an additional [prayer] for you; perhaps your Lord will raise you to a praised station.
interpretation: This verse encourages the Prophet Muhammad to perform additional prayers during the night, specifically referring to the Tahajjud prayer. The act of waking up in the night to pray is seen as a form of devotion and sacrifice, which is believed to bring the worshipper closer to Allah. The promise of being raised to a 'praised station' (Maqam Mahmud) suggests that such devotion could lead to a high spiritual rank, possibly referring to the Prophet's intercession on behalf of his followers on the Day of Judgment. This verse underscores the importance of voluntary worship and its potential rewards.
orig: ومن الليل فتهجد به نافلة لك عسى أن يبعثك ربك مقاما محمودا

translation: And say: My Lord, cause me to enter a truthful entrance and cause me to exit a truthful exit, and grant me from Yourself a supporting authority.
interpretation: This verse is a supplication taught by Allah to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to be recited for seeking divine guidance and support in all aspects of life. The "truthful entrance" and "truthful exit" symbolize a life lived in accordance with truth and righteousness from beginning to end. The request for a "supporting authority" from Allah signifies a plea for strength and assistance that comes directly from God, enabling the believer to uphold truth and justice. This prayer reflects a deep reliance on Allah for guidance and empowerment in navigating life's challenges with integrity.
orig: وقل رب أدخلني مدخل صدق وأخرجني مخرج صدق واجعل لي من لدنك سلطانا نصيرا

translation: And say, 'Truth has come, and falsehood has departed. Indeed is falsehood, [by nature], ever bound to depart.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate triumph of truth over falsehood. It instructs believers to proclaim the arrival of truth, which is eternal and unchanging, and the inevitable disappearance of falsehood, which is transient and doomed to vanish. The verse reassures believers that no matter how pervasive or powerful falsehood may seem, it is inherently weak and destined to be eradicated by the truth.
orig: وقل جاء الحق وزهق الباطل إن الباطل كان زهوقا

translation: And We send down from the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy to the believers, but it does not increase the wrongdoers except in loss.
interpretation: This verse highlights the dual impact of the Qur'an on different groups of people. For believers, the Qur'an serves as a source of spiritual healing and mercy, guiding them towards righteousness and inner peace. Conversely, for those who persist in wrongdoing and reject its message, the Qur'an does not benefit them; instead, their rejection leads to further spiritual and moral loss, emphasizing the accountability and consequences of one's actions in relation to divine guidance.
orig: وننزل من القرآن ما هو شفاء ورحمة للمؤمنين ولا يزيد الظالمين إلا خسارا

translation: And when We bestow favor upon man, he turns away and distances himself; but when evil touches him, then he is in despair.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fluctuating nature of human gratitude and faith. When God blesses a person with prosperity and ease, that person often becomes arrogant and neglects their spiritual duties, turning away from God. Conversely, when faced with hardship or adversity, the same person falls into despair, forgetting that God's mercy and wisdom are at play even in difficult times. The verse serves as a reminder to maintain a balanced perspective and consistent faith, regardless of life's ups and downs.
orig: وإذا أنعمنا على الإنسان أعرض ونأى بجانبه وإذا مسه الشر كان يئوسا

translation: Say, 'Everyone acts according to his disposition. Your Lord knows best who is most guided in way.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the diversity in human actions and beliefs, suggesting that each person follows a path shaped by their own nature and understanding. However, it asserts that ultimate knowledge and judgment of who is on the most righteous path belongs to Allah alone, encouraging humility and trust in divine wisdom over human judgment.
orig: قل كل يعمل على شاكلته فربكم أعلم بمن هو أهدى سبيلا

translation: And they ask you about the soul. Say, 'The soul is of the affair of my Lord. And you have not been given of knowledge except a little.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad when he was questioned about the nature of the soul. It instructs him to respond by affirming that the soul is part of the divine mysteries known only to Allah. The verse emphasizes human limitation in understanding the full scope of divine knowledge, reminding believers that our knowledge is minimal compared to Allah's infinite wisdom. It encourages humility and acceptance of the boundaries of human understanding in spiritual matters.
orig: ويسألونك عن الروح قل الروح من أمر ربي وما أوتيتم من العلم إلا قليلا

translation: And if We willed, We could take away that which We have revealed to you. Then you would not find for yourself any protector against Us.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute authority and power of Allah over His revelations. It serves as a reminder to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and to all believers that the Qur'an is a gift from Allah, and He has the power to withhold it if He so chooses. This highlights the importance of gratitude and humility in receiving divine guidance, and it also emphasizes that no one can intercede or protect against Allah's will.
orig: ولئن شئنا لنذهبن بالذي أوحينا إليك ثم لا تجد لك به علينا وكيلا

translation: Except for mercy from your Lord; indeed, His favor upon you has ever been great.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that any good that comes to the Prophet Muhammad is solely due to the mercy and favor of Allah. It highlights the immense grace and kindness that Allah has bestowed upon him, indicating that without Allah's mercy, nothing would be possible. This serves as a reminder of the Prophet's dependence on Allah and the boundless nature of divine favor.
orig: إلا رحمة من ربك إن فضله كان عليك كبيرا

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], 'If mankind and the jinn gathered in order to produce the like of this Qur'an, they could not produce the like of it, even if they were to each other assistants.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unique and inimitable nature of the Qur'an, asserting that it is beyond human and jinn capabilities to replicate its divine eloquence and profound message, even if they collaborated and supported each other fully. It underscores the miraculous aspect of the Qur'an as a sign of its divine origin.
orig: قل لئن اجتمعت الإنس والجن على أن يأتوا بمثل هذا القرآن لا يأتون بمثله ولو كان بعضهم لبعض ظهيرا

translation: And We have certainly presented for the people in this Qur'an from every [kind of] example; but most of the people refused except disbelief.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an contains a diverse range of examples and parables intended to guide and enlighten humanity. Despite this comprehensive approach to teaching, the verse laments that the majority of people choose to reject the message and persist in disbelief, highlighting the challenge of conveying divine guidance to those who are unwilling to accept it.
orig: ولقد صرفنا للناس في هذا القرآن من كل مثل فأبى أكثر الناس إلا كفورا

translation: And they said, 'We will not believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth from the earth for us.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the skepticism and demands for miracles from those who opposed the Prophet Muhammad. It reflects their disbelief and the unreasonable conditions they set for faith, illustrating the challenge faced by prophets in convincing people of divine truth through extraordinary signs.
orig: وقالوا لن نؤمن لك حتى تفجر لنا من الأرض ينبوعا

translation: Or do you have a garden of date-palms and grapes, from which you cause rivers to gush forth abundantly?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question posed to the disbelievers, challenging them to produce something miraculous like the garden described, which would be a sign of their truthfulness. It underscores the inability of humans to create such wonders on their own, emphasizing the divine origin and power behind the creation of the universe and the miracles mentioned in the Qur'an.
orig: أو تكون لك جنة من نخيل وعنب فتفجر الأنهار خلالها تفجيرا

translation: Or the sky fall upon us in pieces, as you have claimed, or you bring Allah and the angels before us face to face.
interpretation: This verse challenges the Prophet Muhammad to perform a miracle that would validate his claims of prophethood. It reflects the skepticism and demand for tangible proof from the disbelievers, who were asking for extraordinary signs such as the sky falling apart or the direct appearance of Allah and the angels. The verse underscores the theme of faith versus the demand for visible miracles, highlighting the nature of belief that does not rely solely on empirical evidence.
orig: أو تسقط السماء كما زعمت علينا كسفا أو تأتي بالله والملائكة قبيلا

translation: Or you have a house of gold or you ascend into the sky. And we will not believe in your ascension until you bring down to us a book that we can read. Say, 'Glory be to my Lord! Am I anything but a human, a messenger?'
interpretation: This verse addresses the skepticism and demands of the disbelievers towards Prophet Muhammad. They challenged him to perform miraculous feats, like owning a house made of gold or ascending to the sky, as a proof of his prophethood. They further demanded a tangible, readable book directly from the heavens. The Prophet's response, 'Glory be to my Lord! Am I anything but a human, a messenger?', emphasizes his humility and the nature of his mission. It underscores that the essence of prophethood lies not in performing miracles or possessing material wealth, but in conveying the divine message as a human messenger. This highlights the Qur'anic theme that faith should be based on the message itself, rather than on miraculous signs or material proofs.
orig: أو يكون لك بيت من زخرف أو ترقى في السماء ولن نؤمن لرقيك حتى تنزل علينا كتابا نقرؤه قل سبحان ربي هل كنت إلا بشرا رسولا

translation: And nothing prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them except that they said, 'Has Allah sent a human as a messenger?'
interpretation: This verse highlights a common human reaction to divine guidance, where people's disbelief stems from their expectation of a non-human messenger. It critiques the arrogance and disbelief of those who reject the prophethood of Muhammad because he was human, emphasizing that Allah's choice of a human messenger should not be a barrier to faith. The verse underscores the theme of human messengers being a test of faith and acceptance of divine wisdom.
orig: وما منع الناس أن يؤمنوا إذ جاءهم الهدى إلا أن قالوا أبعث الله بشرا رسولا

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], 'If there were angels walking securely on the earth, We would have sent down to them from the heaven an angel as a messenger.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the appropriateness of the messenger to the nature of the beings being addressed. It suggests that if the earth were populated by angels, then an angelic messenger would have been sent to them, indicating that the human prophet Muhammad was sent because the earth is populated by humans. This underscores the wisdom and suitability of divine communication tailored to the recipients' nature.
orig: قل لو كان في الأرض ملائكة يمشون مطمئنين لنزلنا عليهم من السماء ملكا رسولا

translation: Say, "Sufficient is Allah as a witness between me and you. Indeed, He is ever, concerning His servants, Knowing and Seeing."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sufficiency of Allah as the ultimate witness in disputes or disagreements, particularly between the Prophet Muhammad and his opponents. It reassures believers that Allah's knowledge and observation of all actions and intentions are complete and unerring, highlighting His attributes of being All-Knowing and All-Seeing. This serves as a reminder of divine accountability and the importance of sincerity in one's actions and faith.
orig: قل كفى بالله شهيدا بيني وبينكم إنه كان بعباده خبيرا بصيرا

translation: And whoever Allah guides - he is the [rightly] guided; and whoever He sends astray - you will never find for them protectors besides Him. And We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection [fallen] on their faces - blind, dumb and deaf. Their refuge is Hell; every time it subsides We increase them in blazing fire.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty of Allah in guiding or leading astray. It suggests that human beings are entirely dependent on divine guidance for true righteousness. Those whom Allah guides are truly guided, and those He allows to go astray will find no help from any other source. The verse also vividly describes the state of the misguided on the Day of Judgment, highlighting their helplessness and the severe punishment awaiting them in Hell, which intensifies without respite, underscoring the eternal nature of divine justice and the consequences of straying from Allah's path.
orig: ومن يهد الله فهو المهتد ومن يضلل فلن تجد لهم أولياء من دونه ونحشرهم يوم القيامة على وجوههم عميا وبكما وصما مأواهم جهنم كلما خبت زدناهم سعيرا

translation: That is their recompense because they disbelieved in Our signs and said, 'When we are bones and crumbled dust, will we [truly] be resurrected as a new creation?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the disbelief and skepticism of those who reject the resurrection after death. They question the possibility of being brought back to life as a new creation when their bodies have decayed into bones and dust. The verse underscores the consequence of such disbelief, indicating that their denial of the signs of Allah leads to a specific recompense, which is a form of punishment or loss in the afterlife. It emphasizes the power of Allah to resurrect and recreate, challenging the limited human understanding and faith in the divine capabilities.
orig: ذلك جزاؤهم بأنهم كفروا بآياتنا وقالوا أإذا كنا عظاما ورفاتا أإنا لمبعوثون خلقا جديدا

translation: Have they not seen that Allah, who created the heavens and the earth, is able to create the likes of them and has appointed for them a term, about which there is no doubt? But the wrongdoers refuse [anything] except disbelief.
interpretation: This verse challenges the disbelief of those who deny Allah's power, emphasizing His capability to create beings similar to humans, given His creation of the vast universe. It also highlights the certainty of an appointed time for all, underscoring the inevitability of divine judgment. The refusal of the wrongdoers to accept these truths is portrayed as a stubborn rejection of faith, illustrating the deep-seated nature of disbelief among those who choose to deny Allah's signs and power.
orig: أولم يروا أن الله الذي خلق السماوات والأرض قادر على أن يخلق مثلهم وجعل لهم أجلا لا ريب فيه فأبى الظالمون إلا كفورا

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], "If you possessed the depositories of the mercy of my Lord, then you would withhold out of fear of spending." And ever has man been stingy.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency towards stinginess and fear of loss, even when it comes to the boundless mercy of Allah. It suggests that if humans were given control over Allah's mercy, they would hoard it due to their inherent nature of being miserly, fearing that sharing it would deplete their resources. This reflects a deeper lesson on trust in Allah's endless provision and the importance of generosity, contrasting human limitations with divine abundance.
orig: قل لو أنتم تملكون خزائن رحمة ربي إذا لأمسكتم خشية الإنفاق وكان الإنسان قتورا

translation: And certainly We gave Moses nine clear signs, so ask the Children of Israel when he came to them, then Pharaoh said to him, 'Indeed, I think you, O Moses, are bewitched.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine support given to Moses in the form of nine clear miracles, which were meant to establish his prophethood and aid him in his mission against Pharaoh. The mention of asking the Children of Israel about these events serves to affirm the truth of the narrative from historical witnesses. Pharaoh's accusation that Moses was bewitched reflects his denial and arrogance in the face of clear evidence, illustrating the theme of disbelief and the human tendency to reject truth when it challenges one's power or beliefs.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى تسع آيات بينات فاسأل بني إسرائيل إذ جاءهم فقال له فرعون إني لأظنك يا موسى مسحورا

translation: He said: You know that these have been sent down only by the Lord of the heavens and the earth as insights, and I truly think, O Pharaoh, that you are doomed.
interpretation: In this verse, Moses is confronting Pharaoh, asserting that the miracles and signs he has shown are clear evidence from God, the Creator of the heavens and the earth. Moses is not only affirming the divine origin of his message but also warning Pharaoh of his impending doom due to his persistent rejection of the truth. This highlights the theme of divine justice and the consequences of denying God's signs.
orig: قال لقد علمت ما أنزل هؤلاء إلا رب السماوات والأرض بصائر وإني لأظنك يا فرعون مثبورا

translation: So he intended to drive them out of the land, but We drowned him and those with him, all together.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the consequences of arrogance and oppression, as it refers to Pharaoh's attempt to expel Moses and the believers from Egypt. Despite his power, Pharaoh's defiance against God's will led to his ultimate downfall, drowning in the Red Sea along with his army. This serves as a reminder that no matter how powerful one may seem, challenging God's commands and oppressing the righteous will lead to ruin.
orig: فأراد أن يستفزهم من الأرض فأغرقناه ومن معه جميعا

translation: And We said after him to the Children of Israel, 'Dwell in the land, and when the promise of the Hereafter comes, We will bring you forth in a mixed crowd.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the Children of Israel after the time of Moses, instructing them to inhabit the land that was promised to them. The phrase 'when the promise of the Hereafter comes' refers to the Day of Resurrection. On that day, God promises to gather the Children of Israel, along with others, in a diverse assembly, symbolizing the universal judgment where all people will be resurrected and brought together irrespective of their backgrounds. This underscores the themes of divine promise, resurrection, and the ultimate gathering of all humanity for judgment.
orig: وقلنا من بعده لبني إسرائيل اسكنوا الأرض فإذا جاء وعد الآخرة جئنا بكم لفيفا

translation: And with the truth We have sent it down, and with the truth it has descended. And We have not sent you except as a bearer of good tidings and a warner.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin and truthfulness of the Qur'an, asserting that it was revealed from Allah with absolute truth. It also highlights the dual role of Prophet Muhammad as both a messenger of glad tidings for those who follow the right path and a warner of the consequences for those who stray, underscoring the comprehensive nature of his mission to guide humanity.
orig: وبالحق أنزلناه وبالحق نزل وما أرسلناك إلا مبشرا ونذيرا

translation: And [We have revealed] a Quran which We have divided [into parts], so that you may recite it to the people at intervals. And We have sent it down progressively.
interpretation: This verse highlights the methodical revelation of the Quran, which was not sent down all at once but in segments over time. This gradual revelation allowed the Prophet Muhammad to recite and teach the Quran to the people in a manageable way, facilitating their understanding and application of its teachings in their daily lives. The verse underscores the divine wisdom in the Quran's revelation, ensuring that it could be effectively communicated and integrated into the community's life.
orig: وقرآنا فرقناه لتقرأه على الناس على مكث ونزلناه تنزيلا

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], 'Believe in it or do not believe. Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it - when it is recited to them, they fall upon their faces in prostration.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the humility and reverence of those who possess prior knowledge and wisdom. When they hear the Qur'an being recited, their immediate response is to prostrate in submission and acknowledgment of the truth it contains, reflecting their deep understanding and recognition of its divine origin.
orig: قل آمنوا به أو لا تؤمنوا إن الذين أوتوا العلم من قبله إذا يتلى عليهم يخرون للأذقان سجدا

translation: And they say, 'Glory be to our Lord! Indeed, the promise of our Lord is surely to be fulfilled.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the believers' affirmation and glorification of God, expressing their unwavering faith in the certainty of God's promises. It underscores the theme of trust in divine decree and the inevitability of God's word coming to pass, encouraging steadfastness and patience among the faithful.
orig: ويقولون سبحان ربنا إن كان وعد ربنا لمفعولا

translation: And they fall upon their faces weeping, and it increases them in humility.
interpretation: This verse describes the profound emotional and spiritual response of believers to the revelations of God. The act of falling upon their faces and weeping signifies an overwhelming sense of awe, gratitude, and repentance. The increase in humility indicates that such experiences deepen their submission and devotion to God, reinforcing their faith and moral character.
orig: ويخرون للأذقان يبكون ويزيدهم خشوعا

translation: Say, "Call upon Allah or call upon the Most Merciful. Whichever [name] you call - to Him belong the best names." And do not be too loud in your prayer nor speak it in a low voice, but seek a way in between.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness of God and the acceptability of using different names to refer to Him, such as Allah or Ar-Rahman (The Most Merciful), as all beautiful names belong to Him. It also provides guidance on the manner of prayer, advocating for a moderate tone - neither too loud nor too soft - suggesting a balanced approach in worship that reflects humility and sincerity.
orig: قل ادعوا الله أو ادعوا الرحمن أيا ما تدعوا فله الأسماء الحسنى ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها وابتغ بين ذلك سبيلا

translation: And say, "Praise be to Allah, who has not taken a son and has had no partner in [His] dominion and has no [need of a] protector out of weakness; and [who is] great beyond any greatness."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the uniqueness and absolute sovereignty of Allah. It refutes the notion of Allah having any offspring or partners in His dominion, which is a direct rejection of polytheistic beliefs. The mention of Allah not needing a protector due to weakness underscores His self-sufficiency and omnipotence. The final phrase, "and [who is] great beyond any greatness," highlights Allah's incomparable greatness, reinforcing the concept of Tawheed (the oneness of God) and His supreme nature above all creation.
orig: وقل الحمد لله الذي لم يتخذ ولدا ولم يكن له شريك في الملك ولم يكن له ولي من الذل وكبره تكبيرا

translation: Praise be to Allah, who has sent down the Book to His servant, and has not placed therein any crookedness.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the perfection and clarity of the Qur'an, which was revealed to Prophet Muhammad. It highlights that the Qur'an is free from any deviation or distortion, indicating its divine origin and the straightforward guidance it provides to humanity.
orig: الحمد لله الذي أنزل على عبده الكتاب ولم يجعل له عوجا

translation: So that he may warn of a severe punishment from Him and give good tidings to the believers who do righteous deeds that they will have a good reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the dual role of the Prophet Muhammad as both a warner and a bearer of good news. It highlights the severity of divine punishment for those who reject faith, serving as a deterrent and a call to heed the warnings. Conversely, it offers hope and encouragement to those who believe and perform good deeds, promising them a rewarding outcome in the hereafter. This dual message underscores the comprehensive nature of the Prophet's mission, addressing both the consequences of disbelief and the benefits of faith and righteousness.
orig: قيما لينذر بأسا شديدا من لدنه ويبشر المؤمنين الذين يعملون الصالحات أن لهم أجرا حسنا

translation: remaining in it eternally
interpretation: This phrase emphasizes the eternal nature of the punishment or reward described in the context of the verse. It suggests that the state being referred to, whether it be Hell or Paradise, is unending and permanent, underscoring the gravity and finality of one's actions in this life.
orig: ماكثين فيه أبدا

translation: And it warns those who said, 'Allah has taken a son.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who attribute human characteristics, such as having offspring, to Allah. It emphasizes the fundamental Islamic belief in the oneness and uniqueness of Allah, rejecting any form of anthropomorphism or association of partners with Him. The verse underscores the severity of such a claim, highlighting its blasphemous nature in the eyes of Islamic theology.
orig: وينذر الذين قالوا اتخذ الله ولدا

translation: They have no knowledge of it, nor did their fathers. Grave is the word that comes out of their mouths; they speak nothing but lies.
interpretation: This verse criticizes those who make unfounded claims about Allah without any knowledge or evidence, a practice that was also done by their forefathers. It emphasizes the seriousness of such false statements, labeling them as grave sins because they not only misrepresent the truth but also lead others astray. The verse underscores the importance of speaking with knowledge and truth, warning against the propagation of lies, especially in matters related to faith and divine attributes.
orig: ما لهم به من علم ولا لآبائهم كبرت كلمة تخرج من أفواههم إن يقولون إلا كذبا

translation: Perhaps you would kill yourself in grief over them, if they do not believe in this discourse, out of sorrow.
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad, indicating that he should not be overly distressed or grieve to the point of harming himself because some people reject the message of Islam. It highlights the emotional toll that the Prophet felt due to his deep concern for his people's guidance, but also serves as a reminder that his role is to convey the message, not to ensure its acceptance. The verse reassures him that he should not despair over the disbelief of others, as their faith is ultimately their own responsibility.
orig: فلعلك باخع نفسك على آثارهم إن لم يؤمنوا بهذا الحديث أسفا

translation: Indeed, We have made that which is on the earth an adornment for it, that We may test them [as to] which of them is best in deed.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the material attractions and beauties of the world are created by Allah as a means of trial for humanity. The purpose is to assess who among us will use these worldly resources and opportunities in the best possible way, focusing on righteous and beneficial actions rather than being distracted or misled by the allure of material possessions.
orig: إنا جعلنا ما على الأرض زينة لها لنبلوهم أيهم أحسن عملا

translation: And indeed, We will make what is upon it a barren ground.
interpretation: This verse signifies a divine promise of transformation, where the earth, currently teeming with life and resources, will be turned into a desolate and barren land. This transformation serves as a reminder of the temporary nature of worldly possessions and the ultimate power of Allah to alter the state of creation as He wills, emphasizing the transient nature of life and the importance of focusing on the hereafter.
orig: وإنا لجاعلون ما عليها صعيدا جرزا

translation: Or do you think that the companions of the cave and the inscription were among Our signs a wonder?
interpretation: This verse invites reflection on the story of the People of the Cave (Ahl al-Kahf) and the Inscription, emphasizing that their tale is one of the miraculous signs of Allah. It challenges the reader to consider the extraordinary nature of their experience as a demonstration of divine power and wisdom, urging believers to ponder over the deeper meanings and lessons contained within this narrative.
orig: أم حسبت أن أصحاب الكهف والرقيم كانوا من آياتنا عجبا

translation: When the youths took refuge in the cave and said, 'Our Lord, grant us mercy from Yourself and provide for us right guidance in our affair.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of turning to Allah in times of distress and seeking His guidance and mercy. The youths, faced with persecution for their faith, sought refuge in the cave and prayed for divine assistance, demonstrating their trust in Allah's providence and their desire for righteous guidance in their situation. This act of seeking refuge and guidance from Allah serves as a model for believers to rely on divine support and wisdom in all circumstances.
orig: إذ أوى الفتية إلى الكهف فقالوا ربنا آتنا من لدنك رحمة وهيئ لنا من أمرنا رشدا

translation: So We cast [a veil] over their ears in the cave for a number of years.
interpretation: This verse describes how Allah protected the sleepers in the cave by causing them to be deaf to the outside world, symbolizing a state of spiritual and physical isolation. This isolation allowed them to remain safe and undisturbed for many years, illustrating divine protection and the power of Allah to preserve His servants in extraordinary ways.
orig: فضربنا على آذانهم في الكهف سنين عددا

translation: Then We raised them up that We might know which of the two groups would best calculate the time they had tarried.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of the People of the Cave (Ashab al-Kahf), where God tested the two groups - the youths who slept in the cave and the people outside - to see which group could better estimate the duration of their stay. The test was not just about calculating time but also about the faith and patience of the believers, highlighting the importance of trust in God's plan and the mysteries of divine timing.
orig: ثم بعثناهم لنعلم أي الحزبين أحصى لما لبثوا أمدا

translation: We relate to you their story in truth. Indeed, they were young men who believed in their Lord, and We increased them in guidance.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine guidance and support given to the believers, specifically referring to the Companions of the Cave. It emphasizes that their faith in Allah was rewarded with increased guidance, illustrating the principle that faith is met with further enlightenment and divine assistance. This serves as an encouragement for believers to strengthen their faith, trusting that Allah will guide them further on the right path.
orig: نحن نقص عليك نبأهم بالحق إنهم فتية آمنوا بربهم وزدناهم هدى

translation: And We strengthened their hearts when they stood up and said, 'Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth. We will never call upon any god other than Him. If we did, we would indeed have uttered an enormity!'
interpretation: This verse highlights the unwavering faith and conviction of the believers, specifically the Companions of the Cave, as they publicly declared their monotheistic belief in the face of potential persecution. Their statement reflects a profound understanding and acceptance of God's sovereignty over all creation, and their resolve to worship none but Him, acknowledging that to do otherwise would be a grave sin. This serves as a model for all believers to remain steadfast in their faith, even in the face of adversity.
orig: وربطنا على قلوبهم إذ قاموا فقالوا ربنا رب السماوات والأرض لن ندعو من دونه إلها لقد قلنا إذا شططا

translation: These are our people who have taken gods besides Him. Why do they not bring a clear authority for them? So who is more unjust than he who invents a lie against Allah?
interpretation: This verse critiques the practice of idolatry among the people, highlighting their lack of evidence or authority for worshipping deities other than Allah. It emphasizes the injustice and falsehood of attributing partners to Allah, suggesting that such actions are a severe form of misguidance and dishonesty towards the truth of monotheism.
orig: هؤلاء قومنا اتخذوا من دونه آلهة لولا يأتون عليهم بسلطان بين فمن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا

translation: And when you have withdrawn from them and what they worship other than Allah, then take refuge in the cave. Your Lord will spread forth for you of His mercy and will prepare for you a provision in your affair.
interpretation: This verse from Surah Al-Kahf (18:16) speaks to the importance of disassociating oneself from idolatry and false worship. It instructs believers to seek refuge in a place of safety and seclusion, symbolized by the cave, where they can focus on their faith and devotion to Allah alone. The promise here is that Allah will provide His mercy and ease their circumstances, indicating that true reliance on Allah and separation from corrupting influences will lead to divine support and comfort.
orig: وإذ اعتزلتموهم وما يعبدون إلا الله فأووا إلى الكهف ينشر لكم ربكم من رحمته ويهيئ لكم من أمركم مرفقا

translation: And you would see the sun when it rose, inclining away from their cave to the right, and when it set, passing them by on the left, while they were in an open space thereof. That is from the signs of Allah. He whom Allah guides is the [rightly] guided, but he whom He leaves astray - never will you find for him a protecting guide.
interpretation: This verse describes the miraculous protection of the sleepers in the cave, where the sun's movement around their cave symbolizes divine protection and guidance. The sun's path ensures that the cave remains in a state of twilight, neither fully illuminated nor completely dark, which can be seen as a metaphor for the balance between guidance and misguidance. The verse emphasizes that true guidance comes from Allah alone, and those whom He guides are on the right path, while those He leaves astray will find no one to guide them correctly, highlighting the importance of divine guidance in one's life.
orig: وترى الشمس إذا طلعت تزاور عن كهفهم ذات اليمين وإذا غربت تقرضهم ذات الشمال وهم في فجوة منه ذلك من آيات الله من يهد الله فهو المهتد ومن يضلل فلن تجد له وليا مرشدا

translation: And you would have thought them awake, while they were asleep. And We turned them to the right and to the left, and their dog stretched his forelegs at the entrance. If you had looked at them, you would have turned from them in flight and would have been filled with terror of them.
interpretation: This verse describes the state of the Companions of the Cave (Ashab al-Kahf), illustrating a miraculous aspect of their sleep. The verse suggests that their sleep was so profound yet appeared so natural that one might mistake them for being awake. The turning of their bodies from side to side and the positioning of their dog at the entrance symbolizes divine protection and care over them during their long slumber. The mention of the potential fear and flight upon seeing them underscores the extraordinary nature of their situation, highlighting the awe-inspiring power of Allah's miracles and the sanctity of those chosen by Him.
orig: وتحسبهم أيقاظا وهم رقود ونقلبهم ذات اليمين وذات الشمال وكلبهم باسط ذراعيه بالوصيد لو اطلعت عليهم لوليت منهم فرارا ولملئت منهم رعبا

translation: And thus We raised them up that they might question one another. Said a speaker among them, 'How long have you remained?' They said, 'We have remained a day or a part of a day.' They said, 'Your Lord knows best how long you have remained. So send one of you with this silver coin of yours to the city, and let him see which is the best food, and let him bring you provision from it, and let him be cautious, and let no one be aware of you.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the story of the People of the Cave (Ashab al-Kahf), highlighting themes of divine protection and guidance. When the youths awoke after a long sleep, they were unaware of the time that had passed, emphasizing human limitations in understanding divine timing. Their decision to send one of their own to the city with caution reflects a reliance on God's wisdom and protection, as well as the importance of maintaining faith and secrecy in a potentially hostile environment. The verse underscores the necessity of trust in God's plan and the practical steps believers should take while maintaining their faith.
orig: وكذلك بعثناهم ليتساءلوا بينهم قال قائل منهم كم لبثتم قالوا لبثنا يوما أو بعض يوم قالوا ربكم أعلم بما لبثتم فابعثوا أحدكم بورقكم هذه إلى المدينة فلينظر أيها أزكى طعاما فليأتكم برزق منه وليتلطف ولا يشعرن بكم أحدا

translation: Indeed, if they gain dominance over you, they would stone you or force you back to their religion, and never would you succeed, ever.
interpretation: This verse highlights the severe persecution faced by early Muslims from the disbelievers. It underscores the potential consequences of the disbelievers gaining power over the believers, which include violent acts like stoning and coercive attempts to revert Muslims to their former faith. The verse also emphasizes the impossibility of true success or salvation for the believers if they were to succumb to such pressures and abandon their faith, indicating the importance of steadfastness in belief despite adversity.
orig: إنهم إن يظهروا عليكم يرجموكم أو يعيدوكم في ملتهم ولن تفلحوا إذا أبدا

translation: And thus We made their case known, that they might know that the promise of Allah is true, and that there is no doubt about the Hour. When they were disputing among themselves about their affair, they said, 'Construct a building over them. Their Lord knows best about them.' Those who prevailed in their matter said, 'We will surely take a mosque over them.'
interpretation: This verse reflects on the story of the People of the Cave (Ashab al-Kahf), illustrating divine wisdom in revealing their story to the public. The verse underscores the certainty of Allah's promises and the inevitability of the Day of Judgment. It also critiques human tendencies to venerate or build structures over sacred sites, which can lead to misguidance, as seen when some suggested building a mosque over the cave, potentially turning a sign of Allah into an object of worship or a place of superstition.
orig: وكذلك أعثرنا عليهم ليعلموا أن وعد الله حق وأن الساعة لا ريب فيها إذ يتنازعون بينهم أمرهم فقالوا ابنوا عليهم بنيانا ربهم أعلم بهم قال الذين غلبوا على أمرهم لنتخذن عليهم مسجدا

translation: They will say there were three, the fourth of them being their dog; and they will say there were five, the sixth of them being their dog - guessing at the unseen; and they will say there were seven, and the eighth of them was their dog. Say, [O Muhammad], 'My Lord is most knowing of their number. None knows them except a few.' So do not argue about them except with an obvious argument, nor consult about them any of them.
interpretation: This verse addresses the speculative debates about the number of the People of the Cave (Ahl al-Kahf) and their dog. It highlights human tendency to conjecture about matters beyond their knowledge, specifically the unseen (al-ghayb). The Qur'an discourages such speculative debates, emphasizing that only Allah has complete knowledge of such details. The verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad to not engage in fruitless arguments about these details, but if discussion is necessary, it should be based on clear and evident arguments. It also advises against seeking opinions from those who are likely to speculate without knowledge, reinforcing the importance of relying on divine revelation rather than human conjecture.
orig: سيقولون ثلاثة رابعهم كلبهم ويقولون خمسة سادسهم كلبهم رجما بالغيب ويقولون سبعة وثامنهم كلبهم قل ربي أعلم بعدتهم ما يعلمهم إلا قليل فلا تمار فيهم إلا مراء ظاهرا ولا تستفت فيهم منهم أحدا

translation: And never say of anything, 'Indeed, I will do that tomorrow'
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to avoid making definitive statements about future actions without acknowledging the will of Allah. It teaches humility and the recognition that only Allah knows what the future holds, promoting a mindset of reliance on divine will rather than personal certainty.
orig: ولا تقولن لشيء إني فاعل ذلك غدا

translation: Except if Allah wills. And remember your Lord when you forget and say, 'Perhaps my Lord will guide me to what is nearer than this to right conduct.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of relying on Allah's will and guidance in all matters. It teaches that even when one forgets or makes a mistake, they should turn back to Allah, seeking His guidance and hoping that He will lead them to a path that is even more righteous than the one they were on. It highlights the concept of tawakkul (trust in Allah) and the continuous need for remembrance of Allah and seeking His direction in life.
orig: إلا أن يشاء الله واذكر ربك إذا نسيت وقل عسى أن يهدين ربي لأقرب من هذا رشدا

translation: And they remained in their cave for three hundred years and added nine.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of the People of the Cave (Ashab al-Kahf), who were granted a long sleep by Allah as a means of protection from persecution. The duration mentioned, three hundred years plus nine, highlights the miraculous nature of their preservation and serves as a reminder of Allah's power over time and life. It also underscores the theme of patience and trust in divine providence.
orig: ولبثوا في كهفهم ثلاث مائة سنين وازدادوا تسعا

translation: Say, 'Allah knows best how long they stayed. With Him is [the knowledge of] the unseen of the heavens and the earth. How clearly He sees and hears! They have no protector other than Him; and He shares His command with none.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience and omnipotence of Allah, highlighting that He alone possesses the knowledge of the unseen aspects of the universe. It underscores the exclusivity of Allah's knowledge and authority, indicating that no other being shares in His governance or has the ability to protect as He does. The verse serves as a reminder of the absolute dependence of all creation on Allah, reinforcing the concept of Tawhid (the oneness of God) and the futility of associating partners with Him in any form.
orig: قل الله أعلم بما لبثوا له غيب السماوات والأرض أبصر به وأسمع ما لهم من دونه من ولي ولا يشرك في حكمه أحدا

translation: And recite what has been revealed to you of the Book of your Lord. None can alter His words, and you will not find a refuge other than Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to the Qur'an as revealed to Prophet Muhammad. It underscores the immutable nature of God's words, suggesting that the Qur'an's message is eternal and unchangeable. Additionally, it conveys a message of reliance solely on God, indicating that true security and guidance can only be found through Him and His revelations.
orig: واتل ما أوحي إليك من كتاب ربك لا مبدل لكلماته ولن تجد من دونه ملتحدا

translation: And keep yourself patient with those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening, seeking His face. And let not your eyes pass beyond them, desiring the adornment of the worldly life, and do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance and who follows his desire and whose affair is ever in neglect.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of patience and steadfastness in the company of the righteous. It instructs the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to remain patient and to associate closely with those who sincerely worship Allah, focusing on their devotion rather than being distracted by the fleeting attractions of worldly life. The verse also warns against following those who are neglectful of Allah's remembrance and are driven by their desires, indicating that such individuals lead to ruin. The underlying message is to prioritize spiritual growth and the hereafter over materialistic pursuits and to choose companions who reinforce one's faith and commitment to Allah.
orig: واصبر نفسك مع الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي يريدون وجهه ولا تعد عيناك عنهم تريد زينة الحياة الدنيا ولا تطع من أغفلنا قلبه عن ذكرنا واتبع هواه وكان أمره فرطا

translation: And say, "The truth is from your Lord, so whoever wills - let him believe; and whoever wills - let him disbelieve." Indeed, We have prepared for the wrongdoers a Fire whose walls will surround them. And if they call for relief, they will be relieved with water like molten brass that scalds their faces. Wretched is the drink, and evil is the resting place.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the freedom of choice given to humans regarding faith, underscoring that belief or disbelief is a personal decision influenced by the truth revealed by God. However, it also serves as a stern warning about the consequences of wrong actions, illustrating the severe punishment awaiting those who oppress and commit injustices. The imagery of the Fire and the scalding water symbolizes the intense suffering and the inescapable nature of divine retribution for the wrongdoers, highlighting the importance of moral accountability and the ultimate justice of God.
orig: وقل الحق من ربكم فمن شاء فليؤمن ومن شاء فليكفر إنا أعتدنا للظالمين نارا أحاط بهم سرادقها وإن يستغيثوا يغاثوا بماء كالمهل يشوي الوجوه بئس الشراب وساءت مرتفقا

translation: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds - We will not waste the reward of those who do good work.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine assurance that faith combined with righteous actions will be rewarded by Allah. It reassures believers that their efforts in performing good deeds are recognized and will not be in vain. The promise of not wasting the reward highlights the justice and generosity of Allah towards those who strive to do good, encouraging continuous effort in faith and morality.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات إنا لا نضيع أجر من أحسن عملا

translation: Those are the ones for whom there are Gardens of Eden, beneath which rivers flow; they will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold, and they will wear green garments of fine silk and brocade, reclining therein on adorned couches. Excellent is the reward, and beautiful is the resting place.
interpretation: This verse describes the rewards awaiting the righteous in Paradise. The imagery of Gardens of Eden with flowing rivers symbolizes the abundance and purity of the afterlife. The adornments of gold bracelets and green garments of silk and brocade signify the honor and beauty bestowed upon the inhabitants. Reclining on adorned couches reflects a state of ultimate relaxation and comfort. The phrase 'Excellent is the reward, and beautiful is the resting place' emphasizes the supreme value and desirability of this divine abode, highlighting that the ultimate reward for faith and good deeds is a blissful and eternal life in Paradise.
orig: أولئك لهم جنات عدن تجري من تحتهم الأنهار يحلون فيها من أساور من ذهب ويلبسون ثيابا خضرا من سندس وإستبرق متكئين فيها على الأرائك نعم الثواب وحسنت مرتفقا

translation: And present to them an example of two men: We provided one of them with two gardens of grapevines and surrounded them with palm trees and placed crops between them.
interpretation: This verse uses the allegory of two men to illustrate the differences in worldly possessions and the test of gratitude and faith. The man with the two gardens represents someone blessed with abundant worldly provisions, symbolized by the grapevines, palm trees, and crops. This abundance is a test from Allah to see if the individual will be thankful and use these blessings in a manner pleasing to Him, or if they will become arrogant and neglectful of their spiritual duties.
orig: واضرب لهم مثلا رجلين جعلنا لأحدهما جنتين من أعناب وحففناهما بنخل وجعلنا بينهما زرعا

translation: Both gardens yielded their fruits and did not fail in the least, and We caused a river to flow through them.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the abundance and perfection of the blessings in Paradise. The gardens symbolize the rewards that await the righteous, where the fruits are always available and never diminish, signifying eternal provision. The river flowing through them represents the continuous flow of divine favor and sustenance, emphasizing the completeness and sufficiency of Paradise's blessings.
orig: كلتا الجنتين آتت أكلها ولم تظلم منه شيئا وفجرنا خلالهما نهرا

translation: And it had fruit, so he said to his companion while he was conversing with him, 'I am greater than you in wealth and mightier in men.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and pride of the man who owned the garden. His statement to his companion reflects a materialistic worldview where he equates his worth and superiority to his wealth and the number of people he can command. It serves as a reminder of the dangers of pride and the false sense of security that material possessions can bring, illustrating how such attitudes can lead one away from gratitude and humility towards God.
orig: وكان له ثمر فقال لصاحبه وهو يحاوره أنا أكثر منك مالا وأعز نفرا

translation: And he entered his garden while he was unjust to himself. He said, 'I do not think that this will ever perish.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the arrogance and self-deception of a man who, upon entering his lush garden, wrongly attributes its permanence to his own doing, ignoring the transient nature of worldly possessions and the ultimate power of Allah over all creation. His statement reflects a deep spiritual injustice to himself, as he fails to acknowledge Allah's sovereignty and the reality of the hereafter.
orig: ودخل جنته وهو ظالم لنفسه قال ما أظن أن تبيد هذه أبدا

translation: And I do not think the Hour will occur, and even if I am brought back to my Lord, I will surely find better than this as a return.
interpretation: This verse expresses the disbelief and arrogance of a person who denies the Day of Judgment. The speaker dismisses the concept of the Hour, showing a lack of faith in the hereafter. Furthermore, the statement reflects a false sense of security and pride, suggesting that if there were an afterlife, the speaker believes they would be rewarded better than their current state, indicating a lack of understanding or acceptance of divine justice and accountability.
orig: وما أظن الساعة قائمة ولئن رددت إلى ربي لأجدن خيرا منها منقلبا

translation: His companion said to him while he was conversing with him, 'Do you disbelieve in He who created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then fashioned you into a man?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of disbelief and the reminder of human creation as a means to reflect on the power and existence of God. The companion's rhetorical question challenges the disbelief by tracing the human origin from dust to a sperm-drop and then to a fully formed man, emphasizing the miraculous process of creation that should lead one to acknowledge and believe in the Creator.
orig: قال له صاحبه وهو يحاوره أكفرت بالذي خلقك من تراب ثم من نطفة ثم سواك رجلا

translation: But He is Allah, my Lord, and I do not associate anyone with my Lord.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unwavering faith and monotheism of the speaker, declaring that Allah is their Lord and they refuse to associate any partners with Him. It reflects a strong commitment to the principle of Tawheed (the oneness of God), rejecting any form of idolatry or polytheism.
orig: لكنا هو الله ربي ولا أشرك بربي أحدا

translation: And why did you not, when you entered your garden, say, 'What Allah willed [has occurred]; there is no power except in Allah'? If you see me less than you in wealth and children,
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of acknowledging Allah's will and power in all aspects of life. It serves as a reminder to express gratitude and humility by attributing all successes and possessions to Allah's will, rather than taking personal pride or feeling superior to others. The verse critiques the arrogance of the person who did not say 'Masha'Allah, La Quwwata Illa Billah' upon entering his garden, indicating that true wealth and blessings come from Allah alone, and one should not compare themselves boastfully with others.
orig: ولولا إذ دخلت جنتك قلت ما شاء الله لا قوة إلا بالله إن ترن أنا أقل منك مالا وولدا

translation: Perhaps my Lord will give me something better than your garden and send upon it a calamity from the sky, and it will become a slippery slope.
interpretation: This verse reflects the concept of divine providence and the transient nature of worldly possessions. It suggests that reliance on God can lead to outcomes that surpass material gains, and it serves as a reminder that God has the power to alter circumstances, reducing what seems valuable to nothing. The verse encourages trust in God's plan over human achievements.
orig: فعسى ربي أن يؤتين خيرا من جنتك ويرسل عليها حسبانا من السماء فتصبح صعيدا زلقا

translation: Or its water becomes sunken, so you would never be able to find it.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the transient nature of worldly provisions and the potential for sudden loss. It serves as a reminder of the fragility of our material dependencies and encourages believers to place their trust in Allah rather than in the fleeting resources of this world.
orig: أو يصبح ماؤها غورا فلن تستطيع له طلبا

translation: And he is surrounded by its fruit, so he turns his hands in regret over what he spent on it, while it is ruined on its trellises, and he says, 'Oh, I wish I had not associated anyone with my Lord!'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the regret of a person who, after witnessing the destruction of his worldly investments, realizes the futility of his actions and his idolatry. It underscores the theme of the transient nature of worldly possessions and the ultimate realization of the importance of monotheism. The regret expressed here serves as a warning to believers about the consequences of associating partners with Allah and the importance of maintaining faith in the face of worldly temptations.
orig: وأحيط بثمره فأصبح يقلب كفيه على ما أنفق فيها وهي خاوية على عروشها ويقول يا ليتني لم أشرك بربي أحدا

translation: And he had no group of men to help him against Allah, nor could he defend himself.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and authority of Allah, illustrating that no human alliances or personal strength can provide protection or victory against His will. It serves as a reminder of human vulnerability and the futility of relying on anything other than submission to Allah's decree.
orig: ولم تكن له فئة ينصرونه من دون الله وما كان منتصرا

translation: There the authority is for Allah, the True. He is the best to reward and the best to end.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate sovereignty and authority of Allah in the hereafter. It reassures believers that in the afterlife, all power and decision-making belong to Allah alone, who is described as 'the True'. This highlights His absolute truthfulness and reliability. The verse further comforts believers by stating that Allah is the best in rewarding good deeds and in determining the final outcomes of all matters. It encourages steadfastness in faith and righteousness, knowing that the ultimate judgment and recompense will be just and favorable from the Most Merciful.
orig: هنالك الولاية لله الحق هو خير ثوابا وخير عقبا

translation: And present to them the example of the life of this world, [it is] like water which We send down from the sky, then the vegetation of the earth mingles with it, and it becomes dry stalks which the winds scatter. And Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse uses the metaphor of rain and vegetation to illustrate the transient nature of worldly life. Just as rain causes plants to grow but eventually they wither and are scattered by the wind, the pleasures and achievements of this world are temporary and fleeting. The verse reminds believers of the impermanence of material life and encourages them to focus on the eternal life hereafter, while also affirming Allah's complete power and control over all aspects of creation.
orig: واضرب لهم مثل الحياة الدنيا كماء أنزلناه من السماء فاختلط به نبات الأرض فأصبح هشيما تذروه الرياح وكان الله على كل شيء مقتدرا

translation: Wealth and children are the adornment of the worldly life, but the enduring good deeds are better in the sight of your Lord for reward and better for hope.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the transient nature of material possessions and familial ties, which, while beautiful and desirable in this life, are temporary. In contrast, the verse highlights the superior value of righteous deeds that have lasting impact and are more rewarding in the eyes of Allah. It encourages believers to focus on actions that contribute to their spiritual growth and eternal reward, rather than being overly attached to worldly gains.
orig: المال والبنون زينة الحياة الدنيا والباقيات الصالحات خير عند ربك ثوابا وخير أملا

translation: And the Day We will set the mountains in motion, and you will see the earth laid bare, and We will gather them, and We will not leave out any of them.
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Judgment, emphasizing the transformation of the physical world where mountains, symbols of stability, will be moved, revealing the earth's true state. It underscores the inevitability and completeness of the resurrection, where every individual will be gathered without exception, highlighting the all-encompassing justice and power of Allah.
orig: ويوم نسير الجبال وترى الأرض بارزة وحشرناهم فلم نغادر منهم أحدا

translation: And they will be presented before your Lord in rows (and He will say): "You have certainly come to Us as We created you the first time. Nay, you claimed that We would not make an appointment for you."
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of the Day of Judgment, where all individuals will be brought forth to stand before Allah in their original created state, stripped of worldly possessions and status. It highlights the accountability of humans for their deeds, as they had previously doubted or denied the reality of this appointed meeting with their Creator. The verse serves as a reminder of the certainty of resurrection and the importance of preparing for it by living a righteous life.
orig: وعرضوا على ربك صفا لقد جئتمونا كما خلقناكم أول مرة بل زعمتم ألن نجعل لكم موعدا

translation: And the record [of deeds] will be placed [open], and you will see the criminals fearful of that which is in it, and they will say, 'Oh, woe to us! What is this book that leaves nothing small or great except that it has enumerated it?' And they will find what they did present [before them], and your Lord does injustice to no one.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of accountability in the afterlife. It describes the moment when individuals are confronted with their life's record, which meticulously documents every action, no matter how minor or significant. The criminals' reaction of fear and despair underscores the realization of their accountability for their deeds. The verse reassures that divine justice is perfect and impartial, emphasizing that no one will be wronged by God, reinforcing the belief in a fair judgment based on one's actions.
orig: ووضع الكتاب فترى المجرمين مشفقين مما فيه ويقولون يا ويلتنا مال هذا الكتاب لا يغادر صغيرة ولا كبيرة إلا أحصاها ووجدوا ما عملوا حاضرا ولا يظلم ربك أحدا

translation: And [mention] when We said to the angels, 'Prostrate to Adam,' and they prostrated, except Iblees. He was of the jinn and departed from the command of his Lord. Then will you take him and his descendants as allies other than Me while they are enemies to you? Wretched it is for the wrongdoers as an exchange.
interpretation: This verse highlights the origin of Iblees's disobedience when he refused to prostrate to Adam, showcasing his arrogance and deviation from God's command due to his jinn nature. It serves as a warning against following Iblees and his progeny, who are adversaries to humanity, emphasizing the folly and danger of choosing such entities as protectors over God, which leads to a detrimental outcome for the wrongdoers.
orig: وإذ قلنا للملائكة اسجدوا لآدم فسجدوا إلا إبليس كان من الجن ففسق عن أمر ربه أفتتخذونه وذريته أولياء من دوني وهم لكم عدو بئس للظالمين بدلا

translation: I did not make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor the creation of themselves, and I would not take the misguided as helpers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's sovereignty and independence in the act of creation. It underscores that the creation of the universe and human beings was solely God's doing, without the involvement or witnessing of any other beings. Furthermore, it highlights God's disdain for associating with those who are misguided, reinforcing the purity and exclusivity of divine assistance and guidance.
orig: ما أشهدتهم خلق السماوات والأرض ولا خلق أنفسهم وما كنت متخذ المضلين عضدا

translation: And the Day He will say, 'Call My partners whom you claimed,' then they will call them, but they will not respond to them. And We will put between them a barrier.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of associating partners with Allah. On the Day of Judgment, those who worshipped false deities will be commanded to call upon them for help, but they will receive no response. This scenario underscores the isolation and despair of the disbelievers, as a barrier will be placed between them and their false gods, emphasizing the absolute power and uniqueness of Allah.
orig: ويوم يقول نادوا شركائي الذين زعمتم فدعوهم فلم يستجيبوا لهم وجعلنا بينهم موبقا

translation: And the criminals will see the Fire and will be certain that they are to fall into it. And they will not find from it a way out.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the moment of realization for the disbelievers and wrongdoers when they see Hellfire. It emphasizes their despair and certainty of punishment, highlighting that there will be no escape or diversion from the consequences of their actions. This serves as a stark reminder of the accountability and justice in the hereafter.
orig: ورأى المجرمون النار فظنوا أنهم مواقعوها ولم يجدوا عنها مصرفا

translation: And We have certainly presented for the people in this Qur'an from every example; and man has always been, of all things, most disputatious.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the comprehensive nature of the Qur'an, illustrating that it contains examples and guidance relevant to all aspects of human life. It also highlights a characteristic of human nature, pointing out that despite the clarity and completeness of the Qur'an's guidance, humans tend to engage in excessive argumentation and dispute, often rejecting or questioning the divine message out of their inherent contentiousness.
orig: ولقد صرفنا في هذا القرآن للناس من كل مثل وكان الإنسان أكثر شيء جدلا

translation: And nothing prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them and from seeking forgiveness from their Lord, except that the tradition of the former peoples should come upon them or that the punishment should come upon them before.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the reason people do not embrace faith and seek forgiveness despite receiving clear guidance is their fear of facing the same fate as previous nations who were punished for their disbelief. It indicates a psychological barrier where individuals hesitate to change their ways due to the dread of divine retribution, either in the form of historical precedents or imminent punishment.
orig: وما منع الناس أن يؤمنوا إذ جاءهم الهدى ويستغفروا ربهم إلا أن تأتيهم سنة الأولين أو يأتيهم العذاب قبلا
