translation: And We do not send the messengers except as bringers of good tidings and warners. But those who disbelieve argue by falsehood to refute thereby the truth. And they take My verses and that of which they are warned in jest.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the dual role of prophets and messengers as bearers of good news and warnings to humanity. It highlights the resistance they face from disbelievers who use false arguments to deny the truth, and who mock the divine signs and warnings. The interpretation suggests that the rejection of divine messages is not just a dismissal of the messengers, but a deeper refusal to accept the truth, often through deliberate distortion and ridicule of sacred teachings.
orig: وما نرسل المرسلين إلا مبشرين ومنذرين ويجادل الذين كفروا بالباطل ليدحضوا به الحق واتخذوا آياتي وما أنذروا هزوا

translation: And who is more unjust than one who is reminded of the verses of his Lord but turns away from them and forgets what his hands have put forth? Indeed, We have placed over their hearts coverings, lest they understand it, and in their ears deafness. And if you invite them to guidance - they will never be guided, then - ever.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual and moral consequences of rejecting divine guidance. It suggests that those who are reminded of God's signs but deliberately turn away and forget their past actions are committing a grave injustice against themselves. The verse uses the metaphor of coverings over the hearts and deafness in the ears to illustrate how persistent rejection of truth can lead to a state where one becomes incapable of understanding or accepting guidance. This condition is portrayed as a self-inflicted spiritual blindness and deafness, which ultimately makes it impossible for such individuals to find the right path, no matter how much they are called towards it.
orig: ومن أظلم ممن ذكر بآيات ربه فأعرض عنها ونسي ما قدمت يداه إنا جعلنا على قلوبهم أكنة أن يفقهوه وفي آذانهم وقرا وإن تدعهم إلى الهدى فلن يهتدوا إذا أبدا

translation: And your Lord is the Most Forgiving, full of mercy. If He were to seize them for what they have earned, He would hasten the punishment for them. But for them is an appointed term, beyond which they will find no refuge.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the immense mercy and patience of Allah. Despite the sins and wrongdoings of people, Allah does not immediately punish them but gives them time to repent and reform. The 'appointed term' refers to the Day of Judgment, indicating that while divine retribution is certain, it is delayed out of Allah's mercy, providing humans with a chance to seek forgiveness and change their ways. This underscores the concept of divine justice balanced with mercy, encouraging believers to take advantage of this period of respite to turn back to Allah.
orig: وربك الغفور ذو الرحمة لو يؤاخذهم بما كسبوا لعجل لهم العذاب بل لهم موعد لن يجدوا من دونه موئلا

translation: And those cities - We destroyed them when they wronged, and We made for their destruction an appointed time.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine justice of Allah, illustrating that the destruction of past communities was a direct consequence of their own wrongdoing and oppression. It serves as a reminder that Allah has set a predetermined time for the punishment of those who transgress, emphasizing the inevitability and fairness of divine retribution.
orig: وتلك القرى أهلكناهم لما ظلموا وجعلنا لمهلكهم موعدا

translation: And [mention] when Moses said to his servant, "I will not give up until I reach the junction of the two seas, even if it takes me years."
interpretation: This verse highlights Moses' determination and perseverance in seeking knowledge and guidance. His commitment to reach the junction of the two seas, where he will meet Al-Khidr, symbolizes the spiritual journey towards divine wisdom, even if it requires enduring hardships and a prolonged period of time.
orig: وإذ قال موسى لفتاه لا أبرح حتى أبلغ مجمع البحرين أو أمضي حقبا

translation: So when they had reached the junction between the two, they forgot their fish, and it took its way into the sea, swimming away.
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of divine intervention and guidance. The forgetting of the fish by Moses and Al-Khidr at the junction of the two seas symbolizes a moment where human oversight is corrected by divine plan. The fish's miraculous return to life and its path into the sea signify that God's guidance and miracles can occur in ways that are beyond human planning or expectation, guiding individuals towards their destined paths.
orig: فلما بلغا مجمع بينهما نسيا حوتهما فاتخذ سبيله في البحر سربا

translation: So when they had passed beyond it, he said to his young companion, "Bring us our meal; we have certainly suffered weariness in this journey of ours."
interpretation: This verse highlights the human aspect of the Prophet Moses, showing that even prophets can experience physical exhaustion and hunger. It underscores the importance of acknowledging and addressing one's physical needs, even during a journey of spiritual or moral significance. The request for a meal from his companion also reflects a moment of trust and reliance on others, which is a key aspect of human relationships and community.
orig: فلما جاوزا قال لفتاه آتنا غداءنا لقد لقينا من سفرنا هذا نصبا

translation: He said, 'Did you see when we retired to the rock? Indeed, I forgot the fish, and none made me forget it except Satan, that I should mention it. And it took its course into the sea amazingly.'
interpretation: In this verse, the servant of Moses narrates an incident where he forgot to remind Moses about the fish they had caught, which miraculously escaped back into the sea. The servant attributes his forgetfulness to the influence of Satan, suggesting that distractions or forgetfulness can be a result of satanic whispers. This highlights the human susceptibility to forgetfulness and the need for vigilance against such influences, emphasizing the miraculous nature of the event as a sign from God.
orig: قال أرأيت إذ أوينا إلى الصخرة فإني نسيت الحوت وما أنسانيه إلا الشيطان أن أذكره واتخذ سبيله في البحر عجبا

translation: He said, "This is what we were seeking." So they returned, retracing their footsteps.
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of divine guidance and the importance of patience and perseverance in the pursuit of spiritual goals. When Musa and his companion, upon losing their fish, realize that this was the sign they were seeking, they immediately retrace their steps to find the point where the divine plan intersected with their journey. It teaches believers to be attentive to the signs from Allah and to be willing to backtrack or change course when necessary to align with divine will.
orig: قال ذلك ما كنا نبغ فارتدا على آثارهما قصصا

translation: And they found a servant from among Our servants to whom We had given mercy from Us and had taught him knowledge from Us.
interpretation: This verse refers to the encounter of Moses and his servant with Al-Khidr, a figure endowed with divine wisdom and mercy. The interpretation highlights that true knowledge and mercy are bestowed by God, and Al-Khidr's role exemplifies the guidance and deeper understanding that comes from divine sources, beyond conventional human learning.
orig: فوجدا عبدا من عبادنا آتيناه رحمة من عندنا وعلمناه من لدنا علما

translation: Moses said to him, "May I follow you on the condition that you teach me from what you have been taught of guidance?"
interpretation: This verse highlights Moses' humility and eagerness to learn. Despite his own prophethood, Moses recognizes the knowledge and wisdom of the man he addresses, traditionally identified as Al-Khidr, and seeks to learn from him. It underscores the Islamic value of seeking knowledge and guidance, even from those who might not hold formal positions of authority, emphasizing that true wisdom can come from unexpected sources.
orig: قال له موسى هل أتبعك على أن تعلمن مما علمت رشدا

translation: He said, 'You will never be able to have patience with me.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the challenge of maintaining patience and perseverance in the face of trials and difficulties, as expressed by Khidr to Moses, indicating that true patience is a rare and difficult virtue to uphold consistently.
orig: قال إنك لن تستطيع معي صبرا

translation: And how can you be patient with that of which you have no knowledge?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the challenge of maintaining patience in situations where one lacks understanding or experience. It suggests that patience is closely linked to knowledge; without knowing the full context or details of a situation, it becomes much harder to remain patient and steadfast. The verse encourages seeking knowledge and understanding as a means to cultivate patience in difficult circumstances.
orig: وكيف تصبر على ما لم تحط به خبرا

translation: He said: "You will find me, if Allah wills, patient, and I will not disobey you in any order."
interpretation: This verse reflects the Prophet Musa's (Moses) response to Khidr, showcasing his commitment to patience and obedience to divine guidance. It emphasizes the importance of patience and submission to Allah's will, even in challenging situations, as a means to spiritual growth and understanding.
orig: قال ستجدني إن شاء الله صابرا ولا أعصي لك أمرا

translation: He said, "If you follow me, then do not ask me about anything until I mention it to you."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience and patience in the path of spiritual guidance. It suggests that true learning and understanding often require one to follow a teacher or guide without questioning their methods until they choose to explain, indicating a test of faith and trust in the wisdom of the guide.
orig: قال فإن اتبعتني فلا تسألني عن شيء حتى أحدث لك منه ذكرا

translation: So they set out, until when they had embarked on the ship, he tore it open. [Moses] said, 'Have you torn it open to drown its people? You have certainly done a grave thing.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the test of faith and understanding between Moses and Al-Khidr. When Al-Khidr damages the ship, Moses reacts with disbelief and questions the morality of the action, not understanding the wisdom behind it. This moment underscores the theme of trusting in divine wisdom even when actions seem unjust or harmful on the surface. It teaches that there may be deeper reasons for events that are beyond human comprehension at the time they occur.
orig: فانطلقا حتى إذا ركبا في السفينة خرقها قال أخرقتها لتغرق أهلها لقد جئت شيئا إمرا

translation: He said, "Did I not tell you that you will not be able to have patience with me?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of patience and human limitation in understanding divine wisdom. Moses, in his journey with Khidr, is reminded of his inability to remain patient when faced with actions that seem unjust or incomprehensible from a human perspective. It underscores the importance of trust in divine wisdom even when it contradicts our immediate understanding or expectations.
orig: قال ألم أقل إنك لن تستطيع معي صبرا

translation: He said, "Do not take me to account for what I have forgotten, and do not impose upon me a difficult task in my affairs."
interpretation: This verse reflects a prayer or plea for leniency and ease. It suggests that humans are prone to forgetfulness and mistakes, and thus, they seek God's mercy not to be held strictly accountable for unintentional errors. Additionally, it expresses a request for relief from overwhelming burdens in one's responsibilities, highlighting the human need for divine support and understanding in managing life's challenges.
orig: قال لا تؤاخذني بما نسيت ولا ترهقني من أمري عسرا

translation: So they set out, until when they met a boy, he killed him. [Moses] said, 'Have you killed a pure soul for other than [having killed] a soul? You have certainly done a grave thing!'
interpretation: This verse highlights the moral and ethical dilemma faced by Moses when he witnesses Al-Khidr killing a boy without apparent justification. It underscores the theme of divine wisdom versus human understanding, illustrating that actions which seem unjust or cruel on the surface may have a deeper, unseen purpose known only to Allah. Moses' reaction reflects the human tendency to judge based on immediate appearances, while Al-Khidr's actions are guided by a higher, divine knowledge.
orig: فانطلقا حتى إذا لقيا غلاما فقتله قال أقتلت نفسا زكية بغير نفس لقد جئت شيئا نكرا

translation: He said, "Did I not tell you that you will not be able to have patience with me?"
interpretation: This verse reflects the moment when Khidr reminds Moses of the limitations of human patience and understanding in the face of divine wisdom. It underscores the theme that some divine actions and decrees may be beyond human comprehension and require a level of patience and trust in God that not everyone can achieve.
orig: قال ألم أقل لك إنك لن تستطيع معي صبرا

translation: He said, "If you ask me about anything after this, do not keep company with me. You have received from me an excuse."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of obedience and trust in divine guidance. Moses' companion sets a clear boundary, emphasizing that further questioning after being given clear instructions shows a lack of trust and could disrupt their mission. It teaches that once guidance is received, one should adhere to it without unnecessary inquiry, as this demonstrates faith and commitment to the path set by divine wisdom.
orig: قال إن سألتك عن شيء بعدها فلا تصاحبني قد بلغت من لدني عذرا

translation: So they set out, until when they came to the people of a town, they asked its people for food, but they refused to host them. Then they found therein a wall about to collapse, and he set it up. [Moses] said, 'If you wished, you could have taken a payment for it.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates a test of patience and the value of selfless service. When the two travelers, believed to be Moses and Al-Khidr, find themselves in a town where they are refused hospitality, Al-Khidr proceeds to repair a wall that is about to fall without expecting any reward. This action symbolizes the importance of doing good deeds purely for the sake of Allah, without seeking worldly compensation. Moses' comment reflects his lack of understanding of this higher moral principle at that moment, highlighting the contrast between immediate worldly concerns and the deeper wisdom of acting for divine pleasure.
orig: فانطلقا حتى إذا أتيا أهل قرية استطعما أهلها فأبوا أن يضيفوهما فوجدا فيها جدارا يريد أن ينقض فأقامه قال لو شئت لاتخذت عليه أجرا

translation: He said, 'This is the separation between me and you. I will inform you of the interpretation of that which you could not have patience for.'
interpretation: In this verse, the Prophet Khidr informs Moses that their journey together has come to an end, marking a point of separation due to Moses' inability to remain patient with the mysterious actions Khidr took. The verse underscores the theme of patience and the limits of human understanding when faced with divine wisdom. Khidr's promise to explain the reasons behind his actions highlights the educational aspect of their journey, where the ultimate lesson is about trusting in the wisdom of Allah, even when the immediate actions seem inexplicable or harsh.
orig: قال هذا فراق بيني وبينك سأنبئك بتأويل ما لم تستطع عليه صبرا

translation: As for the ship, it belonged to poor people working at sea, so I intended to damage it, and there was behind them a king who seized every ship by force.
interpretation: This verse from the story of Moses and Al-Khidr illustrates the wisdom behind seemingly destructive actions. Al-Khidr damaged the ship to prevent it from being unjustly seized by a tyrannical king, thereby protecting the livelihood of the poor people who owned it. It teaches that divine wisdom may allow for actions that appear harmful on the surface but are intended to avert greater harm or injustice.
orig: أما السفينة فكانت لمساكين يعملون في البحر فأردت أن أعيبها وكان وراءهم ملك يأخذ كل سفينة غصبا

translation: And as for the boy, his parents were believers, and we feared that he would overburden them with transgression and disbelief.
interpretation: This verse explains the reason behind the seemingly harsh action taken by Al-Khidr, where he killed a young boy. The interpretation here is that sometimes, divine wisdom may necessitate actions that appear cruel or unjust to us, but they are ultimately for a greater good. In this case, the boy was destined to lead his believing parents into transgression and disbelief, causing them immense spiritual harm. By removing him, Al-Khidr prevented this future calamity, thus preserving the faith and well-being of the parents. This teaches us about the limits of human understanding and the necessity of trusting in divine wisdom, even when we cannot fully comprehend it.
orig: وأما الغلام فكان أبواه مؤمنين فخشينا أن يرهقهما طغيانا وكفرا

translation: So We intended that their Lord should substitute for them a better son than him in purity and closer in affection.
interpretation: This verse suggests that divine intervention can replace what is lost or taken away with something better and more cherished. It reflects the belief in God's ability to transform negative situations into positive outcomes, emphasizing His mercy and wisdom in providing what is ultimately more beneficial and loving for His servants.
orig: فأردنا أن يبدلهما ربهما خيرا منه زكاة وأقرب رحما

translation: And as for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the town, and there was beneath it a treasure that belonged to them. And their father had been righteous, so your Lord intended that they reach maturity and extract their treasure, as a mercy from your Lord. And I did not do it on my own accord. That is the interpretation of that about which you could not have patience.
interpretation: This verse explains the wisdom behind the seemingly inexplicable actions of Prophet Khidr, as narrated in the story of Moses and Khidr. The wall that Khidr repaired was not just a random act of kindness but was done to protect the treasure beneath it, which belonged to two orphan boys. This act was a manifestation of divine mercy, ensuring that the boys, upon reaching maturity, could benefit from their inheritance. The righteousness of their father played a role in this divine plan, highlighting that good deeds can have lasting effects that benefit future generations. Khidr's actions, though not immediately understandable to Moses, were part of a larger divine plan, emphasizing the theme of patience and trust in God's wisdom and mercy.
orig: وأما الجدار فكان لغلامين يتيمين في المدينة وكان تحته كنز لهما وكان أبوهما صالحا فأراد ربك أن يبلغا أشدهما ويستخرجا كنزهما رحمة من ربك وما فعلته عن أمري ذلك تأويل ما لم تسطع عليه صبرا

translation: And they ask you about Dhul-Qarnayn. Say, 'I will recite to you a mention of him.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad's companions who inquired about the historical figure Dhul-Qarnayn. The response given to the Prophet to recite a mention of him indicates that the Qur'an will provide a narrative or account about Dhul-Qarnayn, highlighting his story as an example of divine guidance and justice. This suggests that the Qur'an aims to educate believers about significant figures who exemplify moral and ethical conduct, thereby reinforcing the teachings and values it promotes.
orig: ويسألونك عن ذي القرنين قل سأتلو عليكم منه ذكرا

translation: Indeed, We had established him in the land and given him of everything a means.
interpretation: This verse refers to the empowerment and provision given to a person by Allah, indicating that this individual was granted authority and resources in the world as a means to fulfill a divine purpose or test. It underscores the concept of stewardship and responsibility that comes with such blessings.
orig: إنا مكنا له في الأرض وآتيناه من كل شيء سببا

translation: So he followed a way
interpretation: This verse refers to the journey of Dhul-Qarnayn, a righteous king mentioned in the Qur'an. The phrase 'So he followed a way' indicates that Dhul-Qarnayn embarked on a path or route in his travels, symbolizing his pursuit of justice and exploration of the world to spread goodness and combat evil. It underscores the importance of taking action and following a righteous path in life.
orig: فأتبع سببا

translation: Until, when he reached the setting of the sun, he found it [as if] setting in a spring of dark mud, and he found near it a people. We said, 'O Dhul-Qarnayn, either you punish [them], or else adopt among them [a way of] goodness.'
interpretation: This verse describes the journey of Dhul-Qarnayn to the westernmost part of the world, symbolizing his extensive travels and the exploration of different civilizations. The 'setting of the sun in a spring of dark mud' is a metaphorical expression used to describe the appearance of the sunset from Dhul-Qarnayn's perspective at that location. The verse then presents a moral choice to Dhul-Qarnayn, reflecting the Qur'anic theme of justice and mercy, where he is given the option to either punish the people he encounters or to treat them with kindness, highlighting the importance of ethical decision-making in leadership.
orig: حتى إذا بلغ مغرب الشمس وجدها تغرب في عين حمئة ووجد عندها قوما قلنا يا ذا القرنين إما أن تعذب وإما أن تتخذ فيهم حسنا

translation: He will say, "As for the one who wronged, we will surely punish him; then he will be returned to his Lord, and He will punish him with a tremendous punishment."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty and severity of divine retribution for those who commit wrongdoing. It indicates that the punishment begins in this life and is compounded in the hereafter, where the wrongdoer faces an even greater punishment from Allah. This serves as a warning and a reminder of the accountability one has for their actions, both in the temporal world and the eternal one.
orig: قال أما من ظلم فسوف نعذبه ثم يرد إلى ربه فيعذبه عذابا نكرا

translation: And as for him who believes and does righteous deeds, for him is a goodly reward, and we will speak to him from Our command with ease.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the reward for those who have faith and perform good deeds. The "goodly reward" refers to the blessings and Paradise promised in the afterlife. The phrase "we will speak to him from Our command with ease" suggests that God will guide and facilitate matters for the believer, making their path towards righteousness and eventual reward smoother and more manageable. This reflects the divine support and ease provided to those who are steadfast in their faith and actions.
orig: وأما من آمن وعمل صالحا فله جزاء الحسنى وسنقول له من أمرنا يسرا

translation: Then We made the sperm into a clinging clot
interpretation: This verse describes the miraculous process of human creation, emphasizing the stages from a mere sperm to a clinging clot, highlighting Allah's power and precision in the formation of life.
orig: ثم أتبع سببا

translation: Until, when he reached the rising place of the sun, he found it rising on a people for whom We had not made any shelter against it.
interpretation: This verse describes the journey of Dhul-Qarnayn to the easternmost part of the world, symbolizing his extensive travels and the exploration of different civilizations. The imagery of the sun rising on a people without any shelter signifies their vulnerability and exposure, possibly indicating a community living in a harsh environment or in a state of simplicity and directness in their relationship with nature and the divine. It reflects themes of justice, exploration, and the universal reach of God's creation and care.
orig: حتى إذا بلغ مطلع الشمس وجدها تطلع على قوم لم نجعل لهم من دونها سترا

translation: Thus, and We have encompassed what he has of information.
interpretation: This verse suggests that God has complete knowledge and awareness of all things, including the thoughts, actions, and circumstances of every individual. It emphasizes the concept of divine omniscience, indicating that nothing is hidden from God and He is fully aware of everything that pertains to His creation.
orig: كذلك وقد أحطنا بما لديه خبرا

translation: Then We sent down a rope
interpretation: This verse refers to the sending down of the Qur'an as a means of guidance and a lifeline for humanity, helping them to ascend from the depths of ignorance and sin towards the heights of knowledge and righteousness.
orig: ثم أتبع سببا

translation: Until, when he reached [a pass] between two mountains, he found, before them, a people who scarcely understood a word.
interpretation: This verse describes the journey of Dhul-Qarnayn, a figure mentioned in the Qur'an, who travels to the ends of the earth. Upon reaching a passage between two mountains, he encounters a community that struggles to communicate, indicating their isolation and perhaps their need for guidance or protection. This highlights themes of exploration, leadership, and the responsibility to help those in need, even in remote or challenging areas.
orig: حتى إذا بلغ بين السدين وجد من دونهما قوما لا يكادون يفقهون قولا

translation: They said, 'O Dhul-Qarnayn, indeed Gog and Magog are spreading corruption in the land. So may we assign for you an expenditure that you might make between us and them a barrier?'
interpretation: This verse reflects the plea of a community to Dhul-Qarnayn for protection against the chaos and corruption caused by Gog and Magog. It highlights the theme of seeking divine or righteous intervention to establish peace and security, suggesting that leaders with power and wisdom have a responsibility to protect their people from harm and to use their resources to foster safety and stability.
orig: قالوا يا ذا القرنين إن يأجوج ومأجوج مفسدون في الأرض فهل نجعل لك خرجا على أن تجعل بيننا وبينهم سدا

translation: He said: "The favor my Lord has bestowed upon me is better, so help me with strength, I will make between you and them a barrier."
interpretation: In this verse, the speaker acknowledges the blessings and support he has received from God, indicating a sense of gratitude and reliance on divine favor. He then requests assistance from others to construct a barrier, symbolizing a protective measure against external threats or evil forces. This reflects a theme of community cooperation and the use of divine gifts for the greater good and protection of society.
orig: قال ما مكني فيه ربي خير فأعينوني بقوة أجعل بينكم وبينهم ردما

translation: Bring me ingots of iron until, when he has leveled [them] between the two mountain walls, he said, "Blow," until when he has made it [like] fire, he said, "Bring me, that I may pour over it molten copper."
interpretation: This verse describes the construction of a barrier by Dhul-Qarnayn to block the passage of Gog and Magog. The use of iron and molten copper symbolizes the strength and permanence of the barrier, reflecting the divine assistance and wisdom granted to Dhul-Qarnayn in fulfilling his mission to protect the people from these destructive forces. The verse underscores the theme of divine intervention and the use of material means to achieve spiritual and societal goals.
orig: آتوني زبر الحديد حتى إذا ساوى بين الصدفين قال انفخوا حتى إذا جعله نارا قال آتوني أفرغ عليه قطرا

translation: So they were unable to scale it, nor were they able to penetrate it.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the inability of the people of Hell to overcome or escape their punishment. It emphasizes the absolute security and inescapability of Hell, highlighting that no matter how much they try, they cannot surmount its walls or find any way to break through it, reflecting the finality and severity of divine judgment.
orig: فما اسطاعوا أن يظهروه وما استطاعوا له نقبا

translation: He said, 'This is a mercy from my Lord. But when the promise of my Lord comes to pass, He will make it into ruins. And the promise of my Lord is true.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the story of Prophet Salih and the people of Thamud. The 'mercy' refers to the she-camel that was sent as a sign from Allah. The statement underscores the dual nature of divine intervention: mercy and punishment. The she-camel was a test of obedience and faith, and its presence was a mercy. However, the verse also warns that if the people fail to heed the warning and the promise of Allah's judgment comes to pass, the mercy will be withdrawn, and the area will be reduced to ruins. This emphasizes the certainty and inevitability of Allah's promises, whether they are of mercy or of punishment.
orig: قال هذا رحمة من ربي فإذا جاء وعد ربي جعله دكاء وكان وعد ربي حقا

translation: And We left some of them to surge like waves over others on that Day, and We blew in the Trumpet, so We gathered them all together.
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Judgment, where the chaotic state of humanity is depicted as some people surging over others, symbolizing the overwhelming fear and confusion. The blowing of the Trumpet signifies the moment of resurrection, when all people are gathered for accountability. It emphasizes the power of Allah to bring all creation together for judgment, highlighting the inevitability and universality of this event.
orig: وتركنا بعضهم يومئذ يموج في بعض ونفخ في الصور فجمعناهم جمعا

translation: And We will present Hell that Day to the disbelievers, a presentation.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the Day of Judgment where Hell will be vividly displayed to the disbelievers, emphasizing the stark reality and inevitability of their punishment. It serves as a warning to those who reject faith, highlighting the consequences of their disbelief.
orig: وعرضنا جهنم يومئذ للكافرين عرضا

translation: Those whose eyes were in a veil from My remembrance and were unable to hear.
interpretation: This verse describes individuals who are spiritually blind and deaf to the messages and reminders from Allah. The "veil" over their eyes symbolizes their inability to perceive or understand the divine guidance, while their inability to hear signifies their disconnection from the spiritual truths being communicated. This state reflects a deeper spiritual ailment where one is cut off from the awareness and consciousness of Allah's presence and teachings.
orig: الذين كانت أعينهم في غطاء عن ذكري وكانوا لا يستطيعون سمعا

translation: Do those who disbelieve think that they can take My servants as allies besides Me? Indeed, We have prepared Hell for the disbelievers as a dwelling.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility and error of the disbelievers who seek protection and support from other beings or deities instead of Allah. It underscores the concept of Tawheed (the oneness of God), warning that such actions lead to severe consequences, as Hell is prepared specifically for those who reject faith and associate partners with Allah.
orig: أفحسب الذين كفروا أن يتخذوا عبادي من دوني أولياء إنا أعتدنا جهنم للكافرين نزلا

translation: Say, "Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in respect to their deeds?"
interpretation: This verse serves as a rhetorical question posed by God to the Prophet Muhammad, inviting the audience to reflect on the futility of actions performed without sincerity or faith. It underscores the concept that deeds, no matter how great they may seem outwardly, are worthless if they are not done for the sake of God. This emphasizes the importance of intention (niyyah) in Islam, where the moral and spiritual value of an action is determined by the purity of one's intent.
orig: قل هل ننبئكم بالأخسرين أعمالا

translation: Those whose efforts have gone astray in the life of this world, while they think that they are doing well in their actions.
interpretation: This verse highlights the delusion of individuals who believe their worldly pursuits are righteous and beneficial, yet in reality, these efforts lead them astray from the true path of spiritual and moral righteousness. It serves as a reminder of the importance of aligning one's actions with divine guidance rather than being misled by apparent worldly success.
orig: الذين ضل سعيهم في الحياة الدنيا وهم يحسبون أنهم يحسنون صنعا

translation: Those are the ones who disbelieved in the signs of their Lord and in meeting Him, so their deeds have become worthless, and We will not assign to them any weight on the Day of Resurrection.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of disbelief in the divine signs and the Day of Judgment. It underscores that rejecting faith nullifies one's good deeds, rendering them devoid of any value or merit in the eyes of God. On the Day of Resurrection, such individuals will find that their actions carry no weight, symbolizing their complete lack of spiritual worth and the futility of their efforts in the hereafter. This serves as a stern warning about the importance of faith and the severe repercussions of its absence.
orig: أولئك الذين كفروا بآيات ربهم ولقائه فحبطت أعمالهم فلا نقيم لهم يوم القيامة وزنا

translation: That is their recompense - Hell - for what they disbelieved and took My signs and My messengers in mockery.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequence of disbelief and mocking the divine signs and messengers, indicating that such actions lead to the punishment of Hell. It underscores the seriousness of rejecting faith and ridiculing sacred messages and their bearers, highlighting the accountability for one's actions and attitudes towards divine guidance.
orig: ذلك جزاؤهم جهنم بما كفروا واتخذوا آياتي ورسلي هزوا

translation: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - for them will be the Gardens of Paradise as a dwelling.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the promise of Paradise for those who combine faith with righteous actions. It underscores the importance of not only believing in Islam but also actively engaging in good deeds. The mention of 'Gardens of Paradise' as a 'dwelling' suggests a permanent abode, indicating the eternal reward for those who live a life aligned with Islamic principles. This serves as a motivational reminder for believers to strive in their faith and actions, assuring them of a blissful afterlife.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات كانت لهم جنات الفردوس نزلا

translation: Abiding therein; they will not desire any change from it.
interpretation: This verse describes the eternal nature of the dwellers in Paradise, indicating that they will be content and satisfied with their state, never wishing to leave or alter their condition. It emphasizes the perfection and completeness of the bliss they experience, which fulfills all their desires and needs.
orig: خالدين فيها لا يبغون عنها حولا

translation: Say, If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would be exhausted before the words of my Lord are exhausted, even if We brought the like of it as a supplement.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the infinite nature of God's knowledge and wisdom. It suggests that no matter how vast the resources one might use to try to encapsulate or express the entirety of God's words or knowledge, such as the sea being used as ink, those resources would be depleted long before one could fully convey or exhaust the depth and breadth of divine revelation and wisdom. This highlights the boundless and inexhaustible nature of God's teachings and the impossibility of fully grasping or documenting them with human means.
orig: قل لو كان البحر مدادا لكلمات ربي لنفد البحر قبل أن تنفد كلمات ربي ولو جئنا بمثله مددا

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], "I am only a human being like you to whom it has been revealed that your god is one God. So whoever would hope for the meeting with his Lord - let him do righteous work and not associate in the worship of his Lord anyone."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the humanity of the Prophet Muhammad, reminding us that he, like all prophets, was a human messenger chosen by God to convey His message. The core message here is the oneness of God, a fundamental principle in Islam known as Tawhid. The verse also serves as a call to action for believers, urging them to perform righteous deeds and maintain pure devotion to God alone, without associating any partners with Him in worship. This is crucial for those who aspire to meet their Lord, highlighting the importance of faith and good actions in achieving spiritual success.
orig: قل إنما أنا بشر مثلكم يوحى إلي أنما إلهكم إله واحد فمن كان يرجو لقاء ربه فليعمل عملا صالحا ولا يشرك بعبادة ربه أحدا

translation: Kaf, Ha, Ya, 'Ayn, Sad
interpretation: These are among the mysterious letters (muqatta'at) that appear at the beginning of some Qur'anic chapters. Their exact meaning is known only to Allah, but they are believed to carry deep spiritual significance and to serve as a reminder of the Quran's divine origin and the limitations of human understanding.
orig: كهيعص

translation: Mention the mercy of your Lord to His servant Zachariah.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of remembering and reflecting upon the blessings and mercies that Allah bestows upon His servants, using the example of Zachariah. It serves as a reminder for believers to be grateful and to recognize Allah's continuous grace and kindness, which can manifest in various forms, such as granting offspring to those who are childless, as in the case of Zachariah.
orig: ذكر رحمت ربك عبده زكريا

translation: When he called to his Lord a secret call
interpretation: This verse refers to the intimate and sincere supplication of Prophet Zakariya to Allah, seeking a child in his old age. It highlights the personal and private nature of his prayer, emphasizing the deep faith and trust he placed in God, away from public display. This act of secret calling signifies the purity and earnestness of his request, showing that true devotion and connection with the Divine can be deeply personal and hidden from others.
orig: إذ نادى ربه نداء خفيا

translation: He said, 'My Lord, indeed my bones have weakened, and my head has filled with white hair, and never have I been in my supplication to You, my Lord, unfortunate.'
interpretation: This verse reflects a moment of humility and acknowledgment of human frailty before God. The speaker, traditionally understood to be Prophet Zakariya, is expressing his physical decline due to old age, yet he also affirms his unwavering faith and trust in God's response to his prayers. It highlights the theme of steadfastness in faith despite personal hardships and the recognition that true misfortune would be a lack of connection with the Divine.
orig: قال رب إني وهن العظم مني واشتعل الرأس شيبا ولم أكن بدعائك رب شقيا

translation: And indeed, I fear the allies against me after me, and my wife has been barren, so grant me from Yourself a successor
interpretation: In this verse, the Prophet Zakariya (Zachariah) expresses his fear of what will happen to his community after his death, as he has no children to carry on his legacy and guide the people. He also mentions his wife's infertility, emphasizing his desperate situation. He then turns to Allah, asking for a successor, not just for personal reasons but as a means to continue the prophetic mission and maintain the spiritual guidance of his people. This shows a deep trust in Allah's power and a recognition of divine intervention in human affairs.
orig: وإني خفت الموالي من ورائي وكانت امرأتي عاقرا فهب لي من لدنك وليا

translation: He will inherit me and inherit from the family of Jacob, and make him, my Lord, pleasing.
interpretation: This verse is a prayer from Prophet Zakariya, asking God to bless his potential offspring to be his heir and also an heir in the prophetic lineage of Jacob. The request to make the child 'pleasing' reflects a desire for the child to be righteous and accepted by God, indicating the importance of spiritual legacy and moral upbringing in Islamic teachings.
orig: يرثني ويرث من آل يعقوب واجعله رب رضيا

translation: O Zechariah, indeed We give you good tidings of a boy whose name will be John. We have not assigned to him before this name.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine intervention and blessing bestowed upon Zechariah, announcing the birth of his son, John (Yahya), who would be a unique and significant prophet. The naming of John before his birth emphasizes his predestined role and the special favor of God, indicating that John's mission was planned and ordained by God, distinct from any previous prophet.
orig: يا زكريا إنا نبشرك بغلام اسمه يحيى لم نجعل له من قبل سميا

translation: He said, 'My Lord, how will I have a boy when my wife is barren and I have reached extreme old age?'
interpretation: This verse reflects the human condition of doubt and questioning in the face of divine promise. Zachariah, despite his faith, expresses his astonishment and seeks clarification on how such a miracle could occur given his and his wife's physical conditions. It underscores the theme that divine power transcends human limitations and natural laws, encouraging believers to trust in God's omnipotence even when circumstances seem impossible.
orig: قال رب أنى يكون لي غلام وكانت امرأتي عاقرا وقد بلغت من الكبر عتيا

translation: He said: So (it will be). Your Lord says, 'It is easy for Me, and I have created you before, when you were nothing.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the omnipotence and creative power of Allah. It reassures that just as Allah created humans from nothing initially, bringing them into existence is a simple matter for Him. This underscores the theme of divine ease in creation and resurrection, emphasizing trust in Allah's ability to perform miracles and fulfill His promises.
orig: قال كذلك قال ربك هو علي هين وقد خلقتك من قبل ولم تك شيئا

translation: He said, 'My Lord, make for me a sign.' He said, 'Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three nights, [being] sound.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the moment when Zechariah, after praying for a son, asks for a sign from Allah to confirm that his prayer will be answered. Allah's response is to grant him the sign of temporary muteness, which serves as a personal test of faith and patience for Zechariah. This sign also acts as a divine assurance and a prelude to the miraculous birth of his son, John (Yahya), emphasizing the power and mercy of Allah in responding to the sincere prayers of His servants.
orig: قال رب اجعل لي آية قال آيتك ألا تكلم الناس ثلاث ليال سويا

translation: So he came out to his people from the prayer chamber and signaled to them to exalt [ Allah ] in the morning and afternoon.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of regular devotion and worship to Allah. It suggests that even in moments of personal spiritual experience, like that of Zakariya in the prayer chamber, there is a duty to guide and remind the community to engage in praise and glorification of Allah consistently, specifically in the morning and evening. This practice helps maintain a continuous connection with the divine and fosters a community centered on worship and remembrance of Allah.
orig: فخرج على قومه من المحراب فأوحى إليهم أن سبحوا بكرة وعشيا

translation: O John, take hold of the Book with strength, and We gave him wisdom while yet a boy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of adhering firmly to divine revelation, as exemplified by Prophet John (Yahya). The command to 'take hold of the Book with strength' suggests a deep commitment to the teachings of the scripture, not just in belief but in practice. The mention of wisdom being granted to him as a boy highlights that divine guidance and understanding can be bestowed at a young age, underscoring the potential for spiritual maturity and leadership regardless of one's age.
orig: يا يحيى خذ الكتاب بقوة وآتيناه الحكم صبيا

translation: And affection from Us and purity, and he was righteous
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine favor bestowed upon Prophet Yahya (John the Baptist), characterized by affection and purity directly from Allah, underscoring his inherent righteousness and moral integrity. It emphasizes that his virtuous qualities were a gift from God, reflecting his chosen status and the high esteem in which he was held.
orig: وحنانا من لدنا وزكاة وكان تقيا

translation: And dutiful to his parents, and he was not arrogant or disobedient.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of humility and obedience, particularly towards one's parents. It emphasizes that true righteousness includes not only fulfilling one's duties towards God but also maintaining a respectful and submissive attitude towards parents, avoiding arrogance and disobedience.
orig: وبرا بوالديه ولم يكن جبارا عصيا

translation: And peace be upon him the day he was born and the day he dies and the day he is raised alive.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the special honor and peace bestowed upon Prophet Jesus (Isa) by Allah. It emphasizes the divine protection and blessing that envelops Jesus from his birth, through his death, and into his resurrection. The mention of these three key moments in Jesus's life underscores the continuity of divine favor and the exceptional status of Jesus in Islam, affirming his miraculous nature and his role in the divine plan.
orig: وسلام عليه يوم ولد ويوم يموت ويوم يبعث حيا

translation: And mention in the Book, Mary, when she withdrew from her family to a place in the east.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual retreat of Mary, symbolizing her devotion and preparation for the divine miracle of giving birth to Jesus. It underscores the importance of solitude and reflection in one's spiritual journey, as Mary's seclusion in the east represents a turning towards divine guidance and away from worldly distractions.
orig: واذكر في الكتاب مريم إذ انتبذت من أهلها مكانا شرقيا

translation: So We placed between them a barrier, and We sent to her Our spirit, and he assumed for her the form of a perfect man.
interpretation: This verse describes the miraculous event of the annunciation to Mary, where God placed a barrier between her and others, ensuring her privacy and sanctity. The phrase "Our spirit" refers to the Angel Gabriel, who appeared to Mary in the form of a perfect human being. This event signifies the divine intervention and the beginning of the miraculous birth of Jesus, emphasizing the purity and chosen status of Mary in the Islamic tradition.
orig: فاتخذت من دونهم حجابا فأرسلنا إليها روحنا فتمثل لها بشرا سويا

translation: She said: "I seek refuge with the Most Merciful from you, [so leave me], if you fear Allah."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of seeking protection in Allah, specifically through His attribute of mercy (Ar-Rahman), when faced with potential harm or temptation. It underscores the empowerment and agency given to individuals to assert their boundaries and seek divine protection, emphasizing that fear of Allah should guide one's actions and interactions.
orig: قالت إني أعوذ بالرحمن منك إن كنت تقيا

translation: He said: "I am only a messenger of your Lord, to grant you a pure boy."
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine intervention and promise through the angel's announcement to Maryam (Mary) about the birth of a son, Isa (Jesus), who will be pure and righteous. It underscores the theme of divine miracles and the special status of prophets, as Isa's birth is a sign of God's power and mercy.
orig: قال إنما أنا رسول ربك لأهب لك غلاما زكيا

translation: She said: 'How can I have a son when no man has touched me, nor am I unchaste?'
interpretation: This verse reflects Maryam's (Mary's) astonishment and questioning of the possibility of having a child without any human intervention, emphasizing her purity and the miraculous nature of the impending birth of Prophet Isa (Jesus). It highlights the theme of divine intervention and the power of Allah to create beyond the norms of human understanding.
orig: قالت أنى يكون لي غلام ولم يمسسني بشر ولم أك بغيا

translation: He said: So (it will be). Your Lord says, 'It is easy for Me, and indeed We will make him a sign for the people and a mercy from Us. And it is a matter already decreed.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence and mercy of Allah. When Maryam (Mary) was informed of the birth of Prophet Isa (Jesus), despite her questioning how it could happen, Allah's response through the angel reassures her that such a miraculous birth is within His power and is part of His divine plan. The verse highlights that Prophet Isa would serve as a sign of Allah's power and a source of mercy for humanity, underscoring the predetermined nature of divine decrees.
orig: قال كذلك قال ربك هو علي هين ولنجعله آية للناس ورحمة منا وكان أمرا مقضيا

translation: So she conceived him, and she withdrew with him to a remote place.
interpretation: This verse illustrates Maryam's (Mary's) journey of solitude and seclusion after conceiving 'Isa (Jesus). It highlights her strength and faith as she chose a distant place to give birth, away from societal judgment and to focus on her spiritual connection with Allah. This act of withdrawal symbolizes the importance of turning to Allah in times of trial and the divine support provided to those who trust in Him.
orig: فحملته فانتبذت به مكانا قصيا

translation: So the pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of a palm tree. She said, 'Oh, I wish I had died before this and was long forgotten.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates Maryam's (Mary's) intense emotional and physical distress during the birth of 'Isa (Jesus). Her wish to have died and been forgotten reflects her feeling overwhelmed and isolated, highlighting the severity of her trial and her human vulnerability, which contrasts with the divine support she soon receives.
orig: فأجاءها المخاض إلى جذع النخلة قالت يا ليتني مت قبل هذا وكنت نسيا منسيا

translation: So he called to her from below her, 'Do not grieve; indeed, your Lord has made beneath you a stream.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates divine intervention and comfort provided by Allah to Maryam (Mary) during her time of distress after giving birth to Isa (Jesus). The voice from below, often interpreted as that of Jibril (Gabriel), reassures her not to be sorrowful because Allah has provided for her needs by placing a stream beneath her, symbolizing sustenance and support from Allah in times of hardship.
orig: فناداها من تحتها ألا تحزني قد جعل ربك تحتك سريا

translation: And shake toward you the trunk of the palm tree; it will drop upon you fresh dates.
interpretation: This verse is a directive from Allah to Maryam (Mary), instructing her to shake the trunk of the date palm tree to receive sustenance in the form of fresh dates. This act symbolizes divine provision and support during a time of need, illustrating that Allah provides for His servants in miraculous ways, even in seemingly impossible situations.
orig: وهزي إليك بجذع النخلة تساقط عليك رطبا جنيا

translation: So eat and drink and be glad. And if you see any human, say, 'Indeed, I have vowed a fast to the Most Merciful, so I will not speak to any person today.'
interpretation: This verse is directed to Maryam (Mary) after she gave birth to 'Isa (Jesus) under a palm tree. It instructs her to nourish herself and find solace in her situation. The command to eat, drink, and be glad emphasizes the divine support and reassurance provided to her in a moment of potential distress. Furthermore, the directive to remain silent if she encounters anyone, using the excuse of a vow of silence, serves as a protective measure. It allows her to avoid immediate confrontation and judgment from her community, thereby safeguarding her and the newborn 'Isa from potential harm or misunderstanding until the appropriate time for revelation arrives.
orig: فكلي واشربي وقري عينا فإما ترين من البشر أحدا فقولي إني نذرت للرحمن صوما فلن أكلم اليوم إنسيا

translation: So she brought him to her people, carrying him. They said, 'O Mary, indeed you have brought something unprecedented.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the moment when Mary, after giving birth to Jesus, presents him to her community. The reaction of her people underscores their astonishment and disbelief at the miraculous nature of her pregnancy and childbirth, as they were unaware of the divine intervention. It reflects the theme of the unexpected and miraculous in the narrative of Jesus's birth, emphasizing the challenge of faith in the face of the extraordinary.
orig: فأتت به قومها تحمله قالوا يا مريم لقد جئت شيئا فريا

translation: O sister of Aaron, your father was not a man of evil, nor was your mother unchaste.
interpretation: This verse is addressed to Maryam (Mary) by the people who were astonished to see her with a baby (Isa/Jesus). They call her 'sister of Aaron' as a way of connecting her to the noble lineage of Aaron, the brother of Moses, to emphasize her respected family background. The statement challenges her by implying that her current situation (being with a newborn) contradicts the honorable character of her parents, suggesting disbelief in her claim of a miraculous birth. It highlights the societal expectations and the immediate judgment faced by Maryam, reflecting on themes of faith, purity, and divine intervention.
orig: يا أخت هارون ما كان أبوك امرأ سوء وما كانت أمك بغيا

translation: So she pointed to him. They said, 'How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the miraculous nature of Prophet Jesus (Isa) as a newborn who could communicate. When Mary (Maryam) was questioned by her people about the child she had, she gestured towards the infant Jesus, indicating that he would answer their queries. The people's response reflects their astonishment and skepticism about a baby in a cradle being able to speak, emphasizing the extraordinary event about to unfold, which would serve as a sign of Jesus's prophethood and divine mission.
orig: فأشارت إليه قالوا كيف نكلم من كان في المهد صبيا

translation: He said, 'Indeed, I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Book and made me a prophet.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the humility and servitude of the Prophet, acknowledging his role as a messenger chosen by Allah. It highlights the divine origin of his mission and the scripture he received, emphasizing his status as a prophet appointed by God to guide people.
orig: قال إني عبد الله آتاني الكتاب وجعلني نبيا

translation: And He has made me blessed wherever I am, and has commanded me to establish prayer and give charity as long as I am alive.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine favor bestowed upon the Prophet, indicating that his presence brings blessings to any place he is in. It also emphasizes the importance of continuous engagement in prayer and charity, underscoring these acts as fundamental duties throughout one's life, reflecting a life of devotion and generosity.
orig: وجعلني مباركا أين ما كنت وأوصاني بالصلاة والزكاة ما دمت حيا

translation: And He has been gracious to me in my old age, and He has not made me arrogant and wretched.
interpretation: This verse reflects gratitude towards Allah for His continuous blessings and mercy, specifically highlighting the preservation of humility and contentment in old age. It underscores the value of maintaining a humble and grateful disposition despite the challenges and potential arrogance that can come with age and experience.
orig: وبرا بوالدتي ولم يجعلني جبارا شقيا

translation: And peace be upon me the day I was born, the day I die, and the day I am raised alive.
interpretation: This verse is a declaration by Jesus (Isa in Arabic) in the Qur'an, emphasizing his special status as a prophet. It highlights the divine protection and peace bestowed upon him from his birth, through his death, and into the afterlife when he is resurrected. This underscores the Islamic belief in the continuity of divine favor and the honor given to prophets throughout their existence, affirming their role in guiding humanity.
orig: والسلام علي يوم ولدت ويوم أموت ويوم أبعث حيا

translation: That is Jesus, the son of Mary - the word of truth about which they are in dispute.
interpretation: This verse affirms the true identity of Jesus as the son of Mary, emphasizing that he is a subject of divine truth. It highlights the ongoing debates and disputes among people regarding his nature and role, underscoring the importance of adhering to the Qur'anic truth about him.
orig: ذلك عيسى ابن مريم قول الحق الذي فيه يمترون

translation: It is not for Allah to take a son; exalted is He! When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, 'Be,' and it is.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute uniqueness and oneness of Allah, rejecting the concept of Him having offspring, which is a fundamental aspect of monotheism in Islam. It highlights Allah's omnipotence, illustrating that His will is executed instantly through His command 'Be,' underscoring His power to bring things into existence without any intermediaries.
orig: ما كان لله أن يتخذ من ولد سبحانه إذا قضى أمرا فإنما يقول له كن فيكون

translation: And indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity of God as the Lord of all, calling for the worship of Allah alone. It underscores that recognizing Allah as the sole deity and worshipping Him is the essence of the straight path, guiding believers towards righteousness and away from idolatry or polytheism.
orig: وإن الله ربي وربكم فاعبدوه هذا صراط مستقيم

translation: So the factions differed among themselves, and woe to those who disbelieved from the scene of a great Day.
interpretation: This verse highlights the division and disagreement among different groups regarding the truth of Islam. It serves as a warning to those who reject faith, indicating that they will face severe consequences on the Day of Judgment, a day of immense significance and terror for the disbelievers.
orig: فاختلف الأحزاب من بينهم فويل للذين كفروا من مشهد يوم عظيم

translation: Hear them and see on the Day they come to Us, but today the wrongdoers are in clear error.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience of Allah, who will hear and see the wrongdoers on the Day of Judgment. It serves as a reminder that while the wrongdoers may seem to prosper in this world, their true state is one of clear error, and they will be held accountable for their actions when they come before Allah.
orig: أسمع بهم وأبصر يوم يأتوننا لكن الظالمون اليوم في ضلال مبين

translation: And warn them of the Day of Regret, when the matter will be decided while they are heedless and they do not believe.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder and a warning to those who are heedless and do not believe in the message of Islam. The "Day of Regret" refers to the Day of Judgment, when individuals will deeply regret their disbelief and negligence in worldly life. The verse emphasizes the urgency of heeding the warning now, as once the matter is decided on that day, there will be no opportunity for repentance or change. It underscores the importance of faith and mindfulness in the present life to avoid eternal regret.
orig: وأنذرهم يوم الحسرة إذ قضي الأمر وهم في غفلة وهم لا يؤمنون

translation: Indeed, it is We who give inheritance of the earth and whoever is on it, and to Us they will be returned.
interpretation: This verse underscores the concept of divine sovereignty and the transient nature of worldly possessions. It reminds believers that ultimate ownership and control over the earth and its inhabitants belong to Allah alone. Humans are merely temporary stewards of the earth, and after their time, they will return to Allah, emphasizing accountability in the hereafter.
orig: إنا نحن نرث الأرض ومن عليها وإلينا يرجعون

translation: And mention in the Book, Abraham. Indeed, he was a man of truth, a prophet.
interpretation: This verse highlights the exemplary character of Prophet Abraham, emphasizing his truthfulness and prophetic role. It serves as a reminder for believers to reflect on his life and emulate his qualities of integrity and devotion to God.
orig: واذكر في الكتاب إبراهيم إنه كان صديقا نبيا

translation: When he said to his father, 'O my father, why do you worship that which does not hear and does not see and cannot avail you in anything?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of monotheism and the rejection of idolatry. It reflects the moment when a prophet, likely Ibrahim (Abraham), confronts his father about the futility of worshipping idols that are incapable of any sensory perception or providing any benefit. The verse underscores the importance of worshipping the one true God who is all-hearing, all-seeing, and capable of aiding His servants, thereby urging believers to abandon false deities and turn to the worship of Allah alone.
orig: إذ قال لأبيه يا أبت لم تعبد ما لا يسمع ولا يبصر ولا يغني عنك شيئا

translation: O my father, indeed there has come to me of knowledge that which has not come to you, so follow me; I will guide you to an even path.
interpretation: This verse is spoken by Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) to his father, Prophet Ya'qub (Jacob), emphasizing the divine knowledge and guidance he has received. Yusuf is urging his father to follow him, not out of arrogance, but with the intention of leading him to the straight and righteous path, which signifies the importance of following divine guidance over traditional or familial practices when they conflict with the truth revealed by God.
orig: يا أبت إني قد جاءني من العلم ما لم يأتك فاتبعني أهدك صراطا سويا

translation: O my father, do not worship Satan. Indeed, Satan has ever been, to the Most Merciful, disobedient.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of monotheism and obedience to God. It is a plea from a son to his father to reject the worship of false deities, represented here by Satan, who is characterized as being in constant rebellion against God's mercy and commands. The verse underscores the moral duty to guide family members towards the worship of the one true God and away from any form of idolatry or disobedience.
orig: يا أبت لا تعبد الشيطان إن الشيطان كان للرحمن عصيا

translation: O my father, indeed I fear that a punishment from the Most Merciful will touch you, so you would be to Satan a companion.
interpretation: This verse reflects the concern and sincerity of Prophet Ibrahim towards his father, warning him about the consequences of idolatry. It highlights the theme of monotheism and the fear of divine punishment for associating partners with Allah, emphasizing the importance of guidance and the struggle against misguidance. Ibrahim's plea also showcases the duty of a believer to advise and warn their loved ones about the path of righteousness, even in the face of potential rejection or hardship.
orig: يا أبت إني أخاف أن يمسك عذاب من الرحمن فتكون للشيطان وليا

translation: He (Nimrod) said, 'Do you turn away from my gods, O Abraham? If you do not stop, I will stone you, so leave me for a long time.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the confrontation between Prophet Abraham and the tyrant Nimrod, illustrating the theme of standing firm in faith against oppression. Abraham's refusal to worship idols and his unwavering commitment to monotheism provoke a direct threat from Nimrod, showcasing the challenges faced by those who uphold the truth in the face of powerful adversaries. The verse underscores the importance of patience and perseverance in faith, even when faced with severe persecution.
orig: قال أراغب أنت عن آلهتي يا إبراهيم لئن لم تنته لأرجمنك واهجرني مليا

translation: He said, 'Peace be upon you; I will pray to my Lord for your forgiveness. Indeed, He has been most kind to me.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the compassion and forgiveness that are central to Islamic teachings. Here, the speaker expresses a desire to seek forgiveness for another from Allah, acknowledging Allah's kindness towards him. It underscores the importance of interceding for others in prayer, showing mercy, and recognizing Allah's benevolence, which encourages believers to be forgiving and kind towards others.
orig: قال سلام عليك سأستغفر لك ربي إنه كان بي حفيا

translation: And I will turn away from you and from whatever you invoke besides Allah, and I will call upon my Lord. Perhaps I will not be in calling upon my Lord, wretched.
interpretation: This verse reflects a declaration of faith and reliance solely on Allah, indicating a conscious decision to reject idolatry and false deities. It expresses hope and trust in Allah's mercy and guidance, suggesting that true fulfillment and avoidance of misery come through sincere devotion and prayer to Allah alone.
orig: وأعتزلكم وما تدعون من دون الله وأدعو ربي عسى ألا أكون بدعاء ربي شقيا

translation: So when he had separated himself from them and from those they worshipped besides Allah, We bestowed upon him Isaac and Jacob, and each one We made a prophet.
interpretation: This verse highlights the reward of steadfastness in faith. After Abraham distanced himself from idolatry and those who practiced it, Allah blessed him with progeny, Isaac and Jacob, who were both made prophets. This signifies that true devotion to Allah, even in the face of opposition, leads to divine favor and the continuation of prophetic guidance through one's lineage.
orig: فلما اعتزلهم وما يعبدون من دون الله وهبنا له إسحاق ويعقوب وكلا جعلنا نبيا

translation: And We bestowed upon them Our mercy, and We granted them a high and truthful tongue.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine favor bestowed upon certain prophets or righteous individuals, emphasizing two aspects of this blessing: the mercy of Allah, which encompasses guidance and support, and the gift of eloquent and truthful speech. This 'high and truthful tongue' refers to their ability to convey the message of God with clarity, sincerity, and authority, thereby effectively guiding others towards the path of righteousness.
orig: ووهبنا لهم من رحمتنا وجعلنا لهم لسان صدق عليا

translation: And mention in the Book, Moses. Indeed, he was chosen, and he was a messenger and a prophet.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the high status of Moses as a chosen servant of God, highlighting his roles as both a messenger and a prophet. It underscores the importance of remembering and reflecting on the stories of significant figures in religious texts, as their lives provide guidance and lessons for believers. Moses' selection by God signifies his trustworthiness and the divine mission he was tasked with, which involved conveying God's messages and leading his people.
orig: واذكر في الكتاب موسى إنه كان مخلصا وكان رسولا نبيا

translation: And We called him from the right side of the Mount, and We brought him near for a confidential talk.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Prophet Moses (Musa) when Allah called him from the right side of Mount Sinai (Tūr), signifying a place of honor and divine favor. The 'confidential talk' (najwa) indicates a special, intimate communication between Allah and Moses, highlighting the closeness and trust bestowed upon him. This event underscores Moses' unique status as a prophet chosen for direct divine interaction and guidance.
orig: وناديناه من جانب الطور الأيمن وقربناه نجيا

translation: And We bestowed upon him from Our mercy his brother Aaron as a prophet.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine favor and support given to Moses by granting him his brother Aaron as a prophet. It signifies the importance of companionship and assistance in carrying out God's mission, emphasizing that divine mercy often manifests through the provision of supportive relationships and shared responsibilities in prophetic duties.
orig: ووهبنا له من رحمتنا أخاه هارون نبيا

translation: And mention in the Book, Ishmael. Indeed, he was true to his promise, and he was a messenger and a prophet.
interpretation: This verse highlights the exemplary character of Ishmael, emphasizing his integrity and reliability in fulfilling his commitments. It also acknowledges his significant role as both a messenger and a prophet, indicating his importance in conveying divine messages and guiding people. This recognition serves to honor Ishmael's legacy and underscores the values of truthfulness and dedication to one's divine mission.
orig: واذكر في الكتاب إسماعيل إنه كان صادق الوعد وكان رسولا نبيا

translation: And he used to enjoin on his family prayer and almsgiving, and he was pleasing to his Lord.
interpretation: This verse highlights the exemplary character of a righteous individual who not only practiced prayer and charity himself but also encouraged his family to do the same. His commitment to these pillars of faith made him beloved and accepted by Allah, indicating that consistent devotion and guidance towards righteousness are highly valued by the Creator.
orig: وكان يأمر أهله بالصلاة والزكاة وكان عند ربه مرضيا

translation: And mention in the Book, Idris. Indeed, he was a man of truth and a prophet.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of remembering and honoring Idris, a prophet known for his truthfulness and righteousness. The mention of Idris in the Qur'an serves as a reminder to believers to emulate his qualities of integrity and devotion to God, emphasizing the value of these traits in the eyes of Allah.
orig: واذكر في الكتاب إدريس إنه كان صديقا نبيا

translation: And We raised him to a high station.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Prophet Idris (Enoch), whom Allah elevated to a distinguished position in the spiritual and moral hierarchy, signifying his high rank among the prophets and his closeness to Allah due to his righteousness and piety.
orig: ورفعناه مكانا عليا

translation: Those are the ones upon whom Allah bestowed favor from among the prophets of the descendants of Adam and of those We carried [in the ship] with Noah, and of the descendants of Abraham and Israel, and of those whom We guided and chose. When the verses of the Most Merciful were recited to them, they fell in prostration and weeping.
interpretation: This verse highlights the exemplary behavior of the favored individuals from the lineage of prophets such as Adam, Noah, Abraham, and Israel, as well as others whom Allah guided and selected. Their response to the recitation of the verses of the Most Merciful (Allah) is one of deep humility and emotional connection, manifesting in prostration and tears. This reaction signifies their recognition of the divine message and their sincere submission to Allah, serving as a model for believers on how to respond to the revelation with reverence and heartfelt devotion.
orig: أولئك الذين أنعم الله عليهم من النبيين من ذرية آدم وممن حملنا مع نوح ومن ذرية إبراهيم وإسرائيل وممن هدينا واجتبينا إذا تتلى عليهم آيات الرحمن خروا سجدا وبكيا

translation: So there came after them generations who neglected prayer and pursued desires, so they are going to meet evil,
interpretation: This verse warns about the consequences of neglecting the obligatory prayers and following one's desires instead of God's guidance. It suggests that such behavior leads to spiritual and moral ruin, indicating that the abandonment of prayer is not just a personal failing but a societal one that leads to widespread corruption and eventual downfall.
orig: فخلف من بعدهم خلف أضاعوا الصلاة واتبعوا الشهوات فسوف يلقون غيا

translation: Except for those who repent, believe, and do righteous deeds; for those, they will enter Paradise and will not be wronged at all.
interpretation: This verse highlights the mercy and justice of Allah. It indicates that even those who have previously committed sins can still attain Paradise if they sincerely repent, embrace faith, and perform good deeds. The phrase "will not be wronged at all" emphasizes that Allah's judgment is fair and that those who meet these criteria will receive their full reward without any injustice.
orig: إلا من تاب وآمن وعمل صالحا فأولئك يدخلون الجنة ولا يظلمون شيئا

translation: Gardens of Eden which the Most Merciful has promised His servants in the unseen. Indeed, His promise has ever been coming to pass.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the promise of Paradise, described as Gardens of Eden, which Allah, the Most Merciful, has assured to His servants. The promise is made 'in the unseen,' indicating that it is a matter of faith and belief in the unseen realities promised by Allah. The verse emphasizes the certainty and reliability of Allah's promises, stating that His promise is always fulfilled. This reassures believers of the ultimate reward awaiting them, encouraging steadfastness and trust in Allah's word.
orig: جنات عدن التي وعد الرحمن عباده بالغيب إنه كان وعده مأتيا

translation: They will not hear therein any vain discourse, but only peace, and they will have their provision therein, morning and evening.
interpretation: This verse describes the serene and peaceful environment of Paradise, where believers are shielded from any form of idle or harmful talk. The emphasis on hearing only peace underscores the purity and tranquility of the afterlife. The mention of provision morning and evening signifies the continuous and abundant sustenance provided to the inhabitants of Paradise, reflecting God's endless generosity and care.
orig: لا يسمعون فيها لغوا إلا سلاما ولهم رزقهم فيها بكرة وعشيا

translation: That is the Paradise which We shall cause the righteous among Our servants to inherit.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Paradise is a reward specifically designated for those servants of Allah who have lived a life of piety and righteousness. It underscores the concept of inheritance, suggesting that entry into Paradise is a bestowed right for those who have adhered to God's commands and lived in fear of Him. The term 'inherit' also implies a sense of legacy and continuity, indicating that the righteous are part of a spiritual lineage that is promised eternal bliss.
orig: تلك الجنة التي نورث من عبادنا من كان تقيا

translation: And We do not descend except by the command of your Lord. To Him belongs what is before us and what is behind us and what is between that. And your Lord is never forgetful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine authority and omnipresence of Allah. It indicates that the angels or revelations do not come down to earth except by Allah's explicit command, underscoring His control over all aspects of creation. The mention of what is before, behind, and between signifies Allah's complete knowledge and dominion over all time and space. The affirmation that Allah is never forgetful reassures believers of His constant awareness and care over all affairs, reinforcing trust in His perfect plan and timing.
orig: وما نتنزل إلا بأمر ربك له ما بين أيدينا وما خلفنا وما بين ذلك وما كان ربك نسيا

translation: Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, so worship Him and be steadfast in His worship. Do you know of any similarity to Him?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness and uniqueness of Allah, who is the Creator and Sustainer of the entire universe. It commands the believer to worship Him alone and to remain patient and steadfast in this worship, acknowledging that there is no one or nothing comparable to Allah. The rhetorical question at the end reinforces the concept of tawhid (the oneness of God), challenging the reader to consider if there could possibly be any entity that rivals or resembles Allah in any way.
orig: رب السماوات والأرض وما بينهما فاعبده واصطبر لعبادته هل تعلم له سميا

translation: And man says, "When I am dead, will I be brought forth alive?"
interpretation: This verse reflects the skepticism and doubt that some individuals have about the concept of resurrection after death. It highlights a common human question regarding the afterlife, challenging the belief in life after death and the power of God to revive the dead. The verse underscores the theme of disbelief and the need for faith in the unseen aspects of God's creation and power.
orig: ويقول الإنسان أإذا ما مت لسوف أخرج حيا

translation: Does man not remember that We created him before, when he was nothing?
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder to humans of their origin and the power of Allah. It emphasizes the humble beginnings of mankind, created from nothing, to instill a sense of gratitude and humility. It prompts reflection on the miraculous nature of creation and encourages recognition of Allah's omnipotence and the insignificance of human existence without His will.
orig: أولا يذكر الإنسان أنا خلقناه من قبل ولم يك شيئا

translation: And by your Lord, We will surely gather them and the devils; then We will bring them to be present around Hell upon their knees.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability and certainty of the Day of Judgment, where all beings, including humans and devils, will be gathered and brought before Hell in a state of submission and humility, symbolized by being on their knees. It underscores God's absolute power and the ultimate accountability of all creation.
orig: فوربك لنحشرنهم والشياطين ثم لنحضرنهم حول جهنم جثيا

translation: Then We will surely extract from every sect those of them who were worst in enmity toward the Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse suggests that on the Day of Judgment, God will identify and separate from each group or sect those individuals who were most rebellious and antagonistic towards Him. It emphasizes the accountability of individuals for their actions and attitudes towards God, highlighting that no one will escape divine scrutiny based on their affiliations or groups.
orig: ثم لننزعن من كل شيعة أيهم أشد على الرحمن عتيا

translation: Then We are most knowing of those who are most worthy of being in it.
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah has complete knowledge and understanding of who deserves to be in Paradise. It emphasizes divine justice and wisdom in determining the rightful inhabitants of Paradise based on their deeds and faith, underscoring that human judgments or perceptions cannot compare to Allah's perfect knowledge.
orig: ثم لنحن أعلم بالذين هم أولى بها صليا

translation: And there is not one of you but will enter it (Hell); this was a thing decreed by your Lord, a thing determined.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of facing the consequences of one's actions, symbolized by entering Hell. It emphasizes that this is a divine decree, highlighting the accountability of every individual before God. The verse serves as a reminder of the seriousness of life's choices and the ultimate judgment that awaits everyone, urging believers to live righteously and seek forgiveness.
orig: وإن منكم إلا واردها كان على ربك حتما مقضيا

translation: Then We will save those who feared Allah and leave the wrongdoers therein, humbled to their knees.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the divine justice and mercy of Allah. It reassures believers that those who have lived in piety and righteousness, fearing Allah and adhering to His commands, will be saved from the punishment and trials of the hereafter. Conversely, those who have wronged others and lived unjustly will be left to face the consequences of their actions, humbled and defeated. This serves as a reminder of the ultimate accountability before Allah, encouraging believers to maintain righteousness and warning against oppression and wrongdoing.
orig: ثم ننجي الذين اتقوا ونذر الظالمين فيها جثيا
