translation: And when Our clear verses are recited to them, those who disbelieve say to those who believe, 'Which of the two groups is better in position and more excellent in assembly?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and denial of truth by those who disbelieve. When confronted with clear signs of God's existence and guidance, instead of reflecting on the message, they mock the believers by questioning which group is better off in terms of worldly status and social standing. This reflects their focus on material and superficial aspects of life, ignoring the spiritual and moral dimensions that the Qur'an emphasizes. It serves as a reminder to believers to remain steadfast in their faith despite such taunts, understanding that true success lies in the hereafter, not in worldly appearances.
orig: وإذا تتلى عليهم آياتنا بينات قال الذين كفروا للذين آمنوا أي الفريقين خير مقاما وأحسن نديا

translation: And how many a generation before them have We destroyed! They were mightier than these in power and more abundant in wealth.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of the transient nature of worldly power and wealth. It highlights that civilizations, no matter how advanced or prosperous, can be destroyed if they deviate from the path of righteousness. The mention of past nations that were destroyed despite their superior resources and strength underscores the importance of moral and spiritual values over material success. It encourages believers to reflect on their own actions and to prioritize their spiritual well-being, understanding that ultimate power and permanence belong to Allah alone.
orig: وكم أهلكنا قبلهم من قرن هم أحسن أثاثا ورئيا

translation: Say, 'Whoever is in error, let the Most Merciful extend for him an extension until, when they see that which they were promised, either the punishment or the Hour, then they will know who is worst in position and weaker in soldiers.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the patience and mercy of Allah, as He gives those who are astray ample time to realize their errors. It serves as a reminder that the delay in punishment is not a sign of Allah's inability to act, but rather an extension of His mercy, allowing more time for repentance. When the promised event, whether it be the punishment or the Day of Judgment, finally arrives, it will become evident to all who truly holds the weakest position and the least powerful support, highlighting the ultimate futility of opposing Allah's will.
orig: قل من كان في الضلالة فليمدد له الرحمن مدا حتى إذا رأوا ما يوعدون إما العذاب وإما الساعة فسيعلمون من هو شر مكانا وأضعف جندا

translation: And Allah increases in guidance those who are rightly guided, and the enduring good deeds are better in the sight of your Lord for reward and better for return.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine guidance and the importance of righteous actions. It suggests that those who are already on the path of guidance will receive further enlightenment from Allah, indicating a continuous process of spiritual growth and understanding. The 'enduring good deeds' refer to actions that have lasting positive impacts, which are highly valued by Allah. These deeds not only yield a greater reward but also lead to a better outcome in the hereafter, underscoring the significance of performing acts that benefit beyond one's lifetime.
orig: ويزيد الله الذين اهتدوا هدى والباقيات الصالحات خير عند ربك ثوابا وخير مردا

translation: Have you seen the one who denies Our verses and says, 'I will surely be given wealth and children'?
interpretation: This verse critiques the arrogance and false sense of security of those who reject the signs of God. It points out the mindset of someone who believes that their worldly possessions and progeny guarantee them a secure future, thereby dismissing the need for faith or accountability to a higher power. The verse serves as a reminder that material wealth and family are not indicators of divine favor or protection against the consequences of disbelief.
orig: أفرأيت الذي كفر بآياتنا وقال لأوتين مالا وولدا

translation: Has he knowledge of the unseen, or has he taken a covenant with the Most Merciful?
interpretation: This verse questions the claims of those who pretend to have knowledge of the unseen or to have a special pact with Allah. It challenges the legitimacy of such claims, emphasizing that true knowledge of the unseen belongs only to Allah, and no one can have a covenant with Him that would grant them such knowledge or authority.
orig: أطلع الغيب أم اتخذ عند الرحمن عهدا

translation: Nay, We will record what he says, and We will prolong for him from the punishment an extension.
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah is fully aware of the words and actions of every individual, and He records them meticulously. The promise to extend the punishment suggests that there is a deliberate and measured response to the deeds of the wrongdoer, emphasizing the justice and inevitability of divine retribution. It serves as a warning to those who might think they can escape accountability for their actions.
orig: كلا سنكتب ما يقول ونمد له من العذاب مدا

translation: And We will inherit from him what he says, and he will come to Us alone.
interpretation: This verse underscores the transient nature of worldly possessions and relationships. It reminds us that upon death, all that a person claims or possesses will be left behind, and they will face God alone, accountable for their deeds. It serves as a call to focus on the eternal rather than the temporary, emphasizing personal responsibility and the inevitability of divine judgment.
orig: ونرثه ما يقول ويأتينا فردا

translation: And they have taken gods besides Allah, that they might be for them a source of honor.
interpretation: This verse critiques the practice of idolatry, where people worship other deities alongside or instead of Allah. It suggests that the reason behind this misguided worship is the human desire for honor or strength, which they mistakenly believe can be derived from these false gods. The verse emphasizes the futility and error in seeking honor from anything other than Allah, the sole creator and sustainer of the universe.
orig: واتخذوا من دون الله آلهة ليكونوا لهم عزا

translation: Nay, they will deny their worship and will be against them.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate futility and betrayal in worshipping false deities or idols. On the Day of Judgment, these false gods will disavow any connection or allegiance to their worshippers, refusing to intercede on their behalf. Not only will they deny the worship offered to them, but they will also turn hostile, standing in opposition to those who once venerated them. This serves as a stark warning against associating partners with Allah and the dire consequences of such actions in the hereafter.
orig: كلا سيكفرون بعبادتهم ويكونون عليهم ضدا

translation: Have you not seen that We have sent the devils upon the disbelievers, inciting them to sin?
interpretation: This verse illustrates the concept of divine justice and the consequences of disbelief. It suggests that those who reject faith are influenced by malevolent forces, which lead them further astray. This is not merely a punishment but a natural consequence of their choice to disbelieve, highlighting the spiritual and moral decline that follows rejection of God's guidance.
orig: ألم تر أنا أرسلنا الشياطين على الكافرين تؤزهم أزا

translation: So do not be impatient with them; We are only counting for them a number.
interpretation: This verse advises the Prophet Muhammad not to be hasty in expecting the punishment of the disbelievers. It emphasizes patience and trust in Allah's timing, indicating that Allah is keeping an account of their deeds and will deal with them at the appropriate time. This teaches believers to remain steadfast and patient, trusting in divine justice.
orig: فلا تعجل عليهم إنما نعد لهم عدا

translation: The Day We will gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation
interpretation: This verse speaks to the ultimate gathering of the pious and righteous individuals on the Day of Judgment. They will be brought before Allah, referred to here as 'the Most Merciful,' not as individuals facing judgment, but as honored guests or a delegation. This imagery suggests a special status and treatment for the righteous, emphasizing the mercy and honor they will receive from Allah on that day. It highlights the concept of divine mercy and the reward awaiting those who have lived a life of piety and righteousness.
orig: يوم نحشر المتقين إلى الرحمن وفدا

translation: And We will drive the criminals to Hell in a thirsty state.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the consequence of disbelief and sinful behavior, where the criminals, due to their actions, are led to Hell in a state of thirst, symbolizing their spiritual and physical deprivation. It emphasizes the justice of the afterlife, where each person faces the repercussions of their deeds.
orig: ونسوق المجرمين إلى جهنم وردا

translation: They have no power of intercession, except for those who have taken a covenant with the Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that intercession on the Day of Judgment is not a right that can be claimed by anyone, except for those who have a special agreement or covenant with Allah, referred to here as the Most Merciful. This covenant is understood to be a promise or commitment made by Allah to certain individuals, such as prophets or righteous believers, allowing them to intercede on behalf of others. The verse underscores the exclusivity and divine nature of intercession, highlighting that it is not something that can be assumed or demanded by anyone without Allah's specific permission and covenant.
orig: لا يملكون الشفاعة إلا من اتخذ عند الرحمن عهدا

translation: And they said, "The Most Merciful has taken a son."
interpretation: This verse addresses the misconception held by some people that Allah, referred to here as "The Most Merciful," has offspring. The statement reflects a fundamental misunderstanding and a grave theological error, as Islamic doctrine firmly asserts the absolute oneness and uniqueness of Allah, who is beyond human attributes such as having children. This verse serves to refute and condemn such claims, emphasizing the purity and transcendence of Allah's nature.
orig: وقالوا اتخذ الرحمن ولدا

translation: You have indeed come with something monstrous!
interpretation: This verse highlights the disbelief and shock of the people when confronted with a message or event that challenges their existing beliefs or norms. It reflects the human tendency to reject or be astonished by what is radically new or different, especially when it contradicts established traditions or personal convictions.
orig: لقد جئتم شيئا إدا

translation: The heavens are almost rent asunder from above them, and the earth is split asunder, and the mountains fall down in utter ruin.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the immense power and majesty of Allah, suggesting that His presence or the revelation of His signs is so overwhelming that it could cause the very fabric of the universe to disintegrate. It emphasizes the awe-inspiring nature of divine revelation and the potential impact of Allah's judgment on creation.
orig: تكاد السماوات يتفطرن منه وتنشق الأرض وتخر الجبال هدا

translation: That they attribute to the Most Merciful a son
interpretation: This verse critiques the notion held by some that God, referred to here as 'the Most Merciful,' has offspring. It challenges the anthropomorphic views that assign human characteristics or familial relationships to the divine, emphasizing the transcendence and uniqueness of God in Islamic theology.
orig: أن دعوا للرحمن ولدا

translation: It is not befitting for the Most Merciful to take a son.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the uniqueness and oneness of God, highlighting that the concept of God having a son contradicts the fundamental Islamic belief in the absolute unity and transcendence of Allah. It refutes the notion of divine progeny, underscoring that such ideas are incompatible with the nature of the Most Merciful, who is beyond human attributes and familial relationships.
orig: وما ينبغي للرحمن أن يتخذ ولدا

translation: Indeed, all that is in the heavens and the earth will come to the Most Merciful as a servant.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate submission of all creation to Allah, the Most Merciful. It underscores the notion that every entity, whether in the heavens or on earth, will ultimately be in a state of servitude to Allah. This highlights the omnipotence and sovereignty of Allah over all existence, reminding believers of the inevitable return to Him and the importance of living in accordance with His will.
orig: إن كل من في السماوات والأرض إلا آتي الرحمن عبدا

translation: Indeed, He has enumerated them and counted them exactly.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's complete and precise knowledge of all things. It highlights His omniscience, indicating that He has a detailed account of every individual, leaving nothing unrecorded or uncounted. This serves as a reminder of divine accountability and the meticulous nature of God's awareness over His creation.
orig: لقد أحصاهم وعدهم عدا

translation: And all of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection, alone.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the individual accountability on the Day of Judgment. It highlights that every person will stand before Allah alone, without any companions or helpers, to account for their deeds. This solitude underscores the personal nature of one's relationship with Allah and the responsibility each individual bears for their actions.
orig: وكلهم آتيه يوم القيامة فردا

translation: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection.
interpretation: This verse highlights the promise of divine favor for believers who consistently perform good deeds. It suggests that faith combined with righteous actions leads to a special kind of love or affection from Allah, known as 'wudd'. This affection is a manifestation of Allah's mercy and can be understood as a spiritual bond or closeness to the divine, which also fosters love and harmony among the believers themselves.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات سيجعل لهم الرحمن ودا

translation: And indeed, We have made the Qur'an easy in your tongue so that you may give good news with it to the righteous and warn with it a contentious people.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine facilitation of the Qur'an's language to Prophet Muhammad, making it accessible and clear in his native tongue. This ease of language serves a dual purpose: to deliver glad tidings to those who are pious and fear Allah, encouraging them in their faith, and to warn those who are contentious and argumentative, urging them to heed the message and mend their ways. The verse highlights the Qur'an's role as both a source of guidance and a means of admonition, tailored to the Prophet's mission of spreading the message effectively to diverse audiences.
orig: فإنما يسرناه بلسانك لتبشر به المتقين وتنذر به قوما لدا

translation: And how many a generation have We destroyed before them! Do you perceive of them any one or hear from them the slightest sound?
interpretation: This verse reflects on the transient nature of human civilizations and serves as a reminder of the ultimate power of Allah. It underscores that many nations before the current ones were destroyed due to their disbelief and disobedience. The rhetorical question emphasizes the complete annihilation of these past generations, suggesting that they have left no trace or sound behind, which serves as a warning to contemporary societies about the consequences of straying from the path of righteousness.
orig: وكم أهلكنا قبلهم من قرن هل تحس منهم من أحد أو تسمع لهم ركزا

translation: Ta-Ha
interpretation: The letters "Ta-Ha" are among the mysterious letters (muqatta'at) that appear at the beginning of some chapters of the Qur'an. Their exact meaning is known only to Allah, but they are believed to carry deep spiritual significance and to serve as a reminder of the Qur'an's divine origin.
orig: طه

translation: We have not sent down the Qur'an to you to cause you hardship.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the purpose of the Qur'an is not to burden or cause distress to the Prophet Muhammad. Instead, it is a source of guidance and mercy, meant to ease and facilitate the path towards righteousness and understanding of God's will.
orig: ما أنزلنا عليك القرآن لتشقى

translation: Except as a reminder to those who fear.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an serves as a reminder and guidance specifically for those who possess a sense of fear and reverence towards Allah. It suggests that the message of the Qur'an is particularly effective for individuals who are conscious of their accountability to God and are thus more inclined to heed its warnings and follow its guidance.
orig: إلا تذكرة لمن يخشى

translation: A revelation from Him who created the earth and the highest heavens.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin of the Qur'an, attributing its revelation to the same Creator who fashioned the earth and the celestial realms. It underscores the authority and majesty of the Qur'anic message, linking the act of revelation to the omnipotent power of God, who is capable of creating vast and complex universes. This connection serves to validate the Qur'an as a sacred text worthy of reverence and obedience.
orig: تنزيلا ممن خلق الأرض والسماوات العلى

translation: The Most Merciful [who is] above the Throne established
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the transcendence and sovereignty of Allah, indicating that He is above and in complete control of all creation. The term 'established' (استوى) does not imply a physical positioning but rather signifies Allah's supreme authority and dominion over the universe.
orig: الرحمن على العرش استوى

translation: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth and whatever is between them and whatever is under the soil.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and ownership of Allah over all creation. It encompasses everything from the vastness of the heavens to the depths of the earth, including all that lies between and beneath, underscoring that nothing exists outside of His dominion and control.
orig: له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وما بينهما وما تحت الثرى

translation: And if you speak aloud - indeed, He knows the secret and what is even more hidden.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience of Allah, indicating that He is aware of everything, from the spoken word to the innermost secrets and thoughts that are concealed within a person's heart. It serves as a reminder to believers to be mindful of their intentions and thoughts, as nothing is hidden from Allah.
orig: وإن تجهر بالقول فإنه يعلم السر وأخفى

translation: Allah - there is no deity except Him. To Him belong the most beautiful names.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness of Allah, affirming that there is no other deity worthy of worship besides Him. It also highlights His majesty and perfection by attributing to Him the most beautiful and excellent names, which reflect His attributes and qualities. This serves as a reminder for believers to recognize and reverence Allah's unique and supreme nature.
orig: الله لا إله إلا هو له الأسماء الحسنى

translation: And has the story of Moses come to you?
interpretation: This verse serves as an introduction to the narrative of Moses, emphasizing the importance of his story as a lesson and guidance for the Prophet Muhammad and the believers. It implies that the story of Moses is significant and relevant, urging the audience to reflect on the trials, faith, and divine support that characterized Moses's life.
orig: وهل أتاك حديث موسى

translation: When he saw a fire, he said to his family, 'Stay here; indeed, I have perceived a fire; perhaps I can bring you a torch from it or find at the fire some guidance.'
interpretation: This verse refers to the moment when Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) saw a fire in the distance while traveling with his family. He decided to investigate it, hoping to bring back a flame to provide warmth and light for his family, or possibly find guidance or direction from someone at the fire. This incident marks the beginning of Moses' divine encounter with God, as it was at this fire that God spoke to him from the burning bush, commissioning him to lead the Israelites out of Egypt. The verse highlights Moses' proactive nature and his role as a caretaker for his family, as well as setting the stage for his prophetic mission.
orig: إذ رأى نارا فقال لأهله امكثوا إني آنست نارا لعلي آتيكم منها بقبس أو أجد على النار هدى

translation: So when he came to it, he was called, 'O Moses!'
interpretation: This verse describes the moment when Moses approached the burning bush and was directly addressed by God, marking the beginning of his divine mission. It signifies the personal and direct communication between God and His chosen prophet, emphasizing the importance of Moses' role in the narrative of the Qur'an.
orig: فلما أتاها نودي يا موسى

translation: Indeed, I am your Lord, so remove your sandals. Indeed, you are in the sacred valley of Tuwa.
interpretation: This verse signifies a moment of divine revelation and purification. When God commands Moses to remove his sandals, it symbolizes the need to shed worldly attachments and purify oneself before entering into a sacred communion with the Divine. The 'sacred valley of Tuwa' represents a state of spiritual readiness and closeness to God, where one can receive divine guidance and revelation.
orig: إني أنا ربك فاخلع نعليك إنك بالواد المقدس طوى

translation: And I have chosen you, so listen to what is revealed.
interpretation: This verse signifies a divine selection and a call to attentiveness. It underscores the importance of the recipient, in this context Moses, being chosen by God for a special mission. The command to 'listen to what is revealed' emphasizes the necessity of obedience and receptivity to divine guidance, highlighting that the chosen individual must be fully attentive and responsive to the messages and instructions conveyed through revelation.
orig: وأنا اخترتك فاستمع لما يوحى

translation: Indeed, I am Allah. There is no deity except Me, so worship Me and establish prayer for My remembrance.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness of Allah, declaring His unique divinity and calling for the exclusive worship of Him alone. It also highlights the importance of prayer as a means of remembering and maintaining a connection with Allah, underscoring the fundamental practices of monotheism and regular devotion in Islam.
orig: إنني أنا الله لا إله إلا أنا فاعبدني وأقم الصلاة لذكري

translation: Indeed, the Hour is coming - I almost conceal it - so that every soul may be recompensed for what it strives.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability of the Day of Judgment, referred to as 'the Hour.' It suggests that while the exact timing of this event is known only to Allah and is nearly kept hidden, its arrival is certain. The purpose of this concealment is to ensure that every individual is rewarded or punished based on their own efforts and actions, highlighting the importance of personal accountability and the fairness of divine justice.
orig: إن الساعة آتية أكاد أخفيها لتجزى كل نفس بما تسعى

translation: So let not those who do not believe in it and follow their desires turn you away from it, lest you should perish.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of steadfastness in faith and adherence to the divine guidance of the Qur'an. It warns the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) not to be swayed by those who reject the message of Islam and instead follow their own whims and desires. The verse serves as a reminder that deviating from the path of truth due to external pressures can lead to spiritual ruin. It encourages believers to remain firm in their convictions and to prioritize divine guidance over the fleeting opinions and influences of others.
orig: فلا يصدنك عنها من لا يؤمن بها واتبع هواه فتردى

translation: And what is that in your right hand, O Moses?
interpretation: This verse highlights the moment when God questions Moses about the staff in his hand, which is a test of Moses' faith and readiness to perform miracles. It signifies the beginning of Moses' prophetic mission, where ordinary objects like a staff can be transformed into symbols of divine power and authority when used in the path of God.
orig: وما تلك بيمينك يا موسى

translation: He said: 'This is my staff; I lean on it, and with it I beat down leaves for my sheep, and in it I have other uses.'
interpretation: This verse reflects Moses's humility and simplicity, showing that he uses his staff for everyday practical purposes like leaning on it for support and gathering food for his livestock. The mention of 'other uses' hints at the staff's future miraculous role, symbolizing that ordinary objects can be imbued with divine power and purpose.
orig: قال هي عصاي أتوكأ عليها وأهش بها على غنمي ولي فيها مآرب أخرى

translation: He said, 'Throw it down, O Moses'
interpretation: This verse illustrates a moment of divine command and trust between God and Moses. When God instructs Moses to throw down his staff, it is a test of faith and obedience. The act of throwing down the staff, which later turns into a serpent, symbolizes the transformation and empowerment that comes from submitting to God's will. It highlights the theme of divine intervention and the miraculous nature of God's support for His prophets.
orig: قال ألقها يا موسى

translation: So he threw it down, and behold, it was a snake, moving quickly.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the miraculous nature of the staff of Moses, which transformed into a serpent when thrown down. It signifies divine power and serves as a sign to Pharaoh and his people, demonstrating that Moses' mission was supported by God. The transformation of the staff into a living creature underscores the theme of divine intervention and the authority granted to prophets to perform miracles as proof of their prophethood.
orig: فألقاها فإذا هي حية تسعى

translation: He said, 'Take it and do not fear. We will return it to its former state.'
interpretation: This verse reassures that divine intervention can restore things to their original, perfect state, emphasizing God's power and mercy in alleviating fear and providing comfort and restoration.
orig: قال خذها ولا تخف سنعيدها سيرتها الأولى

translation: And draw your hand close to your side; it will come out white without any harm-another sign-
interpretation: This verse refers to a miracle given to Moses as a sign of his prophethood. When Moses drew his hand to his side and then brought it out, it would appear radiantly white, yet unharmed. This miracle was meant to convince Pharaoh and the people of Moses' divine mission. The instruction to Moses to perform this act 'another sign' indicates it was one among multiple miracles, emphasizing the continuity and reinforcement of divine proof.
orig: واضمم يدك إلى جناحك تخرج بيضاء من غير سوء آية أخرى

translation: That We may show you some of Our greatest signs.
interpretation: This verse suggests that God intends to reveal to the Prophet Muhammad some of the most significant miracles or signs, which serve to strengthen his faith and confirm his prophethood. These signs are meant to be clear manifestations of God's power and mercy, providing undeniable proof of the divine message.
orig: لنريك من آياتنا الكبرى

translation: Go to Pharaoh, for he has transgressed.
interpretation: This verse is a divine command to Moses to confront Pharaoh due to his tyranny and oppression. It highlights the theme of standing against injustice and the responsibility of prophets to guide even the most wayward of rulers back to the path of righteousness.
orig: اذهب إلى فرعون إنه طغى

translation: He said, 'My Lord, expand my chest [with assurance].'
interpretation: This verse is a supplication from Moses to Allah, asking for inner strength and confidence to face the challenges ahead, particularly in his mission to confront Pharaoh. It reflects a deep reliance on divine support to overcome personal fears and to carry out the responsibilities entrusted to him.
orig: قال رب اشرح لي صدري

translation: And make my task easy for me
interpretation: This verse is a supplication where the speaker asks Allah to facilitate and simplify their endeavors. It reflects a deep reliance on divine assistance to overcome challenges and accomplish tasks with ease. The request underscores the belief in Allah's power to alter difficulties into ease, emphasizing humility and trust in God's mercy and support.
orig: ويسر لي أمري

translation: And loosen the knot from my tongue
interpretation: This verse is a prayer from Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) asking Allah to improve his speech, indicating a request for eloquence and clarity in communication. It reflects the human need for divine assistance in overcoming personal limitations and challenges.
orig: واحلل عقدة من لساني

translation: they understand my words
interpretation: This phrase emphasizes the importance of comprehending the divine message. It suggests that true faith involves not just hearing the words of God, but deeply understanding and internalizing their meaning, which leads to a more profound connection with the divine guidance.
orig: يفقهوا قولي

translation: And grant me a minister from my family
interpretation: This verse is a prayer from Prophet Moses (Musa) to Allah, asking for support and assistance in his mission. Specifically, he requests a helper from his own family, indicating the importance of familial support and trust in carrying out divine tasks. It reflects the human need for companionship and assistance in fulfilling responsibilities, especially those of a prophetic nature.
orig: واجعل لي وزيرا من أهلي

translation: Aaron, my brother
interpretation: This phrase, "Aaron, my brother," refers to the Prophet Moses addressing his brother Aaron. It highlights the familial bond and the close relationship between the two prophets, emphasizing the support and partnership Aaron provided to Moses in his mission. This mention underscores the importance of family and collaboration in fulfilling divine duties.
orig: هارون أخي

translation: Strengthen my back with him
interpretation: This verse is a metaphorical request for support and assistance. The phrase "strengthen my back" implies seeking help to bear the burdens or responsibilities, indicating a need for reliable and strong support from someone trustworthy.
orig: اشدد به أزري

translation: And associate him in my affair
interpretation: This verse suggests the importance of consultation and partnership in decision-making. It implies that involving others, particularly those who are wise or have relevant experience, can lead to better outcomes and reflects a humble approach to leadership and governance.
orig: وأشركه في أمري

translation: so that we may glorify You much
interpretation: This phrase expresses the intention of the speaker to engage in frequent and abundant glorification of Allah, reflecting a deep desire to maintain a constant state of worship and remembrance of God. It underscores the importance of praising Allah regularly as a means to strengthen one's faith and connection with the Divine.
orig: كي نسبحك كثيرا

translation: And we mention you frequently
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of frequent remembrance and invocation of Allah in one's daily life, highlighting the spiritual practice of dhikr, which serves to strengthen the believer's connection with the Divine and maintain a constant awareness of Allah's presence.
orig: ونذكرك كثيرا

translation: Indeed, You are, over us, Ever-Watchful.
interpretation: This verse acknowledges Allah's attribute of being all-seeing and fully aware of the actions and states of His creation. It emphasizes the belief in divine omniscience, reminding believers that Allah is constantly observing and knows everything about them, which should encourage mindfulness and righteousness in their actions.
orig: إنك كنت بنا بصيرا

translation: He said, "You have been granted your request, O Moses."
interpretation: This verse signifies the acceptance of Moses' prayer by God, illustrating the importance of sincere supplication and God's responsiveness to the needs of His prophets. It highlights the theme of divine favor and the special relationship between God and His chosen messengers.
orig: قال قد أوتيت سؤلك يا موسى

translation: And indeed, We have bestowed upon you a second time.
interpretation: This verse refers to the resurrection and the second life granted to humans after death, emphasizing God's power and mercy in granting another chance at life in the hereafter.
orig: ولقد مننا عليك مرة أخرى

translation: When We inspired to your mother what was inspired
interpretation: This verse refers to the divine revelation given to Moses' mother, instructing her on how to protect her son from Pharaoh's decree to kill newborn boys. It highlights the theme of divine intervention and protection, showing how God communicates guidance and support to His chosen ones even in the most perilous situations.
orig: إذ أوحينا إلى أمك ما يوحى

translation: That cast him into the chest, then cast it into the river, and let the river cast him onto the bank, and an enemy to Me and an enemy to him will take him. And I cast upon you love from Me, and that you may be brought up under My eye.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Moses, where his mother is instructed by God to place him in a chest and set it afloat on the river. This act of faith and obedience to God's command is a test of her trust in divine protection. The river, symbolizing the flow of life and divine will, will guide the chest to the shore where it will be found by Pharaoh's family, who are enemies to God and to Moses. Despite this, God assures Moses' mother that He has instilled love in her heart, which is a divine gift meant to comfort her during this separation. The phrase 'under My eye' signifies that Moses will be under God's constant watch and protection, illustrating the theme of divine providence and care over the chosen ones, even in the midst of danger and among enemies.
orig: أن اقذفيه في التابوت فاقذفيه في اليم فليلقه اليم بالساحل يأخذه عدو لي وعدو له وألقيت عليك محبة مني ولتصنع على عيني

translation: When your sister went and said, 'Shall I show you someone who will nurse him?' So We returned you to your mother that her eye might be comforted and not grieve. And you had killed a person, but We saved you from distress and tried you with trials. And you stayed years among the people of Madyan. Then you came here at the destined time, O Moses.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine protection and guidance provided to Moses throughout his life. It emphasizes how God orchestrated events to ensure Moses' safety and development, from reuniting him with his mother to saving him after he killed a man, and guiding him through various trials to prepare him for his prophetic mission. The mention of Moses' time in Madyan and his arrival at the destined time underscores the idea that every step in Moses' journey was part of a divine plan, illustrating the concept of predestination and God's continuous care for His chosen servants.
orig: إذ تمشي أختك فتقول هل أدلكم على من يكفله فرجعناك إلى أمك كي تقر عينها ولا تحزن وقتلت نفسا فنجيناك من الغم وفتناك فتونا فلبثت سنين في أهل مدين ثم جئت على قدر يا موسى

translation: And I have created you for Myself.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the creation of human beings is for a divine purpose, emphasizing a special relationship between the Creator and humanity. It suggests that humans are meant to serve and worship Allah, aligning their lives with His will and guidance, ultimately finding their true purpose and fulfillment in this connection.
orig: واصطنعتك لنفسي

translation: Go, you and your brother, with My signs and do not slacken in My remembrance.
interpretation: This verse is a directive from Allah to Prophet Moses, instructing him to embark on his mission to Pharaoh alongside his brother Aaron. The emphasis on 'My signs' highlights the divine authority and miracles that Moses was to present as proof of his prophethood. The command 'do not slacken in My remembrance' serves as a reminder for Moses to maintain constant awareness and connection with Allah, underscoring the importance of steadfastness in faith and reliance on divine guidance throughout his challenging mission.
orig: اذهب أنت وأخوك بآياتي ولا تنيا في ذكري

translation: Go to Pharaoh, indeed he has transgressed.
interpretation: This verse instructs Moses and Aaron to confront Pharaoh due to his oppression and tyranny. It highlights the divine mission to challenge injustice and the responsibility of prophets to guide those who have strayed from the path of righteousness.
orig: اذهبا إلى فرعون إنه طغى

translation: So speak to him a gentle word; perhaps he will be reminded or fear [Allah].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of using gentle and kind speech when communicating, especially in situations where one might need to correct or guide another person. The use of soft words is suggested as a means to encourage reflection and instill a sense of fear or reverence towards Allah in the listener, rather than using harshness which might lead to resistance or further misunderstanding.
orig: فقولا له قولا لينا لعله يتذكر أو يخشى

translation: They said, 'Our Lord, indeed we fear that he will hasten [punishment] against us or that he will transgress.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the fear and humility of the two men, possibly referring to the prophets Moses and Aaron, as they approach Pharaoh. Their plea to God highlights their awareness of Pharaoh's potential to act oppressively or to exceed bounds in his reaction to their message. It underscores the theme of seeking divine protection and guidance when confronting powerful adversaries, emphasizing reliance on God in moments of vulnerability and potential danger.
orig: قالا ربنا إننا نخاف أن يفرط علينا أو أن يطغى

translation: He said, 'Do not fear; indeed, I am with you; I hear and see.'
interpretation: This verse reassures the prophets Moses and Aaron that they are under divine protection and guidance as they confront Pharaoh. It emphasizes God's omnipresence and omniscience, providing comfort and strength to believers in times of fear or challenge, reminding them that they are never alone in their struggles.
orig: قال لا تخافا إنني معكما أسمع وأرى

translation: So go to him and say, 'Indeed, we are messengers of your Lord, so send with us the Children of Israel and do not torment them. We have come to you with a sign from your Lord. And peace will be upon the one who follows the guidance.'
interpretation: This verse instructs Moses and Aaron to approach Pharaoh with a clear message of divine authority and mission. It emphasizes the importance of delivering the oppressed Children of Israel from Pharaoh's tyranny, underscoring the divine sign as proof of their legitimacy. The promise of peace to those who follow guidance highlights the universal message of submission to God's will, encouraging moral and spiritual alignment with divine directives.
orig: فأتياه فقولا إنا رسولا ربك فأرسل معنا بني إسرائيل ولا تعذبهم قد جئناك بآية من ربك والسلام على من اتبع الهدى

translation: Indeed, We have been inspired that the punishment is upon those who deny and turn away.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine revelation received by the Prophet Muhammad, indicating that severe consequences await those who reject the message of Islam and deliberately turn away from the truth. It serves as a warning to individuals about the accountability they will face for their disbelief and refusal to accept guidance.
orig: إنا قد أوحي إلينا أن العذاب على من كذب وتولى

translation: He said, 'Who is your Lord, O Moses?'
interpretation: This verse captures a moment of inquiry and challenge from Pharaoh to Moses, highlighting Pharaoh's disbelief and his demand for proof of Moses's claims about God. It underscores the theme of divine authority versus human arrogance, illustrating the confrontation between faith and skepticism.
orig: قال فمن ربكما يا موسى

translation: He said, 'Our Lord is He who gave everything its form and then guided [it].'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the belief in the comprehensive power and wisdom of Allah. It highlights that Allah not only creates every aspect of existence but also provides guidance to each creation, enabling them to fulfill their purpose. This underscores the notion that the entire universe operates under divine guidance, reflecting Allah's meticulous care and planning in creation.
orig: قال ربنا الذي أعطى كل شيء خلقه ثم هدى

translation: He said, 'Then what about the former generations?'
interpretation: This verse reflects a question posed by a disbeliever challenging the Prophet Muhammad about the fate of previous generations who did not receive the message of Islam. It underscores the human tendency to question divine justice and the accountability of those who lived before the revelation of the Qur'an. The question implies a concern about fairness and the criteria by which people from different eras are judged.
orig: قال فما بال القرون الأولى

translation: He said, "The knowledge of it is with my Lord in a record. My Lord neither errs nor forgets."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience and infallibility of Allah. It reassures believers that all knowledge, including the timing of events and the unseen, is perfectly recorded and managed by Allah. The verse instills trust in Allah's flawless memory and guidance, indicating that nothing is overlooked or forgotten by Him.
orig: قال علمها عند ربي في كتاب لا يضل ربي ولا ينسى

translation: Who made the earth a bed for you, and threaded paths for you therein, and sent down water from the sky, and with it We brought forth diverse pairs of plants.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's provision and care for humanity by illustrating how He has designed the earth to be a comfortable and navigable place, complete with natural pathways. The mention of water from the sky and the subsequent growth of various plants emphasizes the cycle of life and sustenance that Allah has put in place, showcasing His power and mercy in providing for all living beings through the diversity and abundance of vegetation.
orig: الذي جعل لكم الأرض مهدا وسلك لكم فيها سبلا وأنزل من السماء ماء فأخرجنا به أزواجا من نبات شتى

translation: Eat and pasture your cattle. Indeed, in that are signs for those of understanding.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the blessings and provisions that Allah has provided for humanity, such as food and livestock. It encourages people to utilize these resources, while also reflecting on the deeper signs and wisdom behind these provisions, which can be understood by those who possess insight and contemplation.
orig: كلوا وارعوا أنعامكم إن في ذلك لآيات لأولي النهى

translation: From it We created you, and into it We will return you, and from it We will bring you forth once again.
interpretation: This verse refers to the cycle of life, death, and resurrection as described in Islamic theology. The 'it' in the verse refers to the earth. The verse indicates that humans are created from the earth, will return to it upon death, and will be resurrected from it on the Day of Judgment. This emphasizes the temporary nature of worldly life and the inevitability of the afterlife, reinforcing the belief in resurrection and the continuity of existence beyond physical death.
orig: منها خلقناكم وفيها نعيدكم ومنها نخرجكم تارة أخرى

translation: And We certainly showed him Our signs, all of them, but he denied and refused.
interpretation: This verse refers to Pharaoh, illustrating how despite being presented with clear and comprehensive signs from Allah, he chose to deny them and stubbornly refused to believe. It highlights the theme of human arrogance and the consequences of rejecting divine guidance, emphasizing the importance of humility and acceptance of truth when it is presented.
orig: ولقد أريناه آياتنا كلها فكذب وأبى

translation: He said, 'Have you come to us to drive us out of our land with your magic, O Moses?'
interpretation: This verse reflects Pharaoh's reaction to Moses's demand to let the Israelites go, showcasing Pharaoh's fear and insecurity. Pharaoh accuses Moses of using magic as a means to overthrow him, revealing his perception of Moses's miracles as mere illusions intended to usurp his power and authority. This highlights the theme of the struggle between truth and falsehood, where the oppressor (Pharaoh) clings to power by denying the divine signs and accusing the messenger of deceit.
orig: قال أجئتنا لتخرجنا من أرضنا بسحرك يا موسى

translation: So we will bring you magic like it, so make between us and you an appointment that neither we nor you will fail to keep, at a place equally convenient.
interpretation: This verse reflects the challenge posed by the magicians of Pharaoh to Moses, asserting their confidence in their magical abilities to produce something similar to the miracles Moses performed. They propose a public contest to demonstrate their skills, suggesting a fair and neutral location for the event. This challenge underscores the theme of truth versus falsehood, where the magicians, representing the established power and false beliefs, confront Moses, the bearer of divine truth. The verse highlights the boldness of those who oppose divine signs, yet it also sets the stage for the ultimate demonstration of God's power over human deceit and illusion.
orig: فلنأتينك بسحر مثله فاجعل بيننا وبينك موعدا لا نخلفه نحن ولا أنت مكانا سوى

translation: He said, "Your appointment is for the Day of Adornment, and that the people will be gathered in the forenoon."
interpretation: This verse refers to a specific day known as the Day of Adornment, which is interpreted by many scholars to be the Day of Judgment. The mention of this day as a time of 'adornment' suggests that it will be a day of great significance and splendor, where the true nature of all things will be revealed. The gathering of people in the forenoon emphasizes the clarity and visibility of the events that will transpire, symbolizing that nothing will be hidden on this day. The forenoon also signifies a time when the sun is high, indicating the full illumination of truth and justice.
orig: قال موعدكم يوم الزينة وأن يحشر الناس ضحى

translation: So Pharaoh turned away and planned his scheme; then he came.
interpretation: This verse illustrates Pharaoh's reaction to the divine message brought by Moses. It highlights his arrogance and refusal to accept the truth, leading him to devise a plan against Moses and the believers. The phrase 'then he came' signifies Pharaoh's active engagement in executing his deceitful plot, emphasizing his determination to oppose the divine will.
orig: فتولى فرعون فجمع كيده ثم أتى

translation: Musa said to them, "Woe to you! Do not invent a lie against Allah, lest He destroy you with a punishment. And indeed, he has failed who invents [such falsehood]."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe consequences of attributing false statements to Allah. Musa warns the people against fabricating lies about Allah, highlighting that such actions could lead to divine punishment. The phrase "and indeed, he has failed who invents [such falsehood]" underscores the ultimate failure and moral bankruptcy of those who engage in such deceit, serving as a stern reminder of the importance of truthfulness and the gravity of false claims in the context of divine revelation.
orig: قال لهم موسى ويلكم لا تفتروا على الله كذبا فيسحتكم بعذاب وقد خاب من افترى

translation: So they disputed their affair among themselves and they kept their talk secret.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency towards disagreement and secrecy, even in matters that should be straightforward. It suggests that when people are faced with decisions or revelations, they often engage in internal conflicts and secretive discussions, which can lead to division and misunderstanding. This behavior is portrayed as a natural but flawed response, indicating the need for clarity, openness, and unity in addressing important issues.
orig: فتنازعوا أمرهم بينهم وأسروا النجوى

translation: They said: "These two are magicians who wish to drive you out of your land with their magic and to put an end to your exemplary way of life."
interpretation: This verse reflects the accusations made by the magicians of Pharaoh against Moses and Aaron, portraying them as threats to the social and political order of Egypt. The magicians claim that Moses and Aaron's intention is to use their perceived magical powers to destabilize the existing regime and disrupt the traditional way of life, which they describe as exemplary. This accusation is a tactic to discredit Moses and Aaron by instilling fear among the people, suggesting that their actions are not divinely inspired but are instead a form of sorcery aimed at overthrowing the established authority and altering the cultural norms.
orig: قالوا إن هذان لساحران يريدان أن يخرجاكم من أرضكم بسحرهما ويذهبا بطريقتكم المثلى

translation: So gather your plan, then come forth in a line; and whoever gains the upper hand today will indeed succeed.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inevitability of divine decree and the futility of human schemes against it. It encourages believers to trust in God's plan, as true success is determined by divine will, not by human strategies or power.
orig: فأجمعوا كيدكم ثم ائتوا صفا وقد أفلح اليوم من استعلى

translation: They said, 'O Moses, either you throw [your staff] or we will be the first to throw.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the challenge and confrontation between Moses and the magicians of Pharaoh. It reflects the magicians' confidence in their abilities and their attempt to assert dominance in the situation. The demand for Moses to throw his staff first or allow them to do so signifies a critical moment of spiritual and physical contest, where faith and divine power are put to the test against human skill and deception.
orig: قالوا يا موسى إما أن تلقي وإما أن نكون أول من ألقى

translation: He said, 'No, you throw.' And behold, their ropes and their staffs seemed to him, due to their magic, as though they were moving.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the power of illusion and deception, as the magicians' staffs and ropes appeared to move through their magic, emphasizing the theme of distinguishing between reality and deception. It highlights the challenge Moses faced in demonstrating the truth against false appearances.
orig: قال بل ألقوا فإذا حبالهم وعصيهم يخيل إليه من سحرهم أنها تسعى

translation: So he conceived in his mind a fear of Moses
interpretation: This verse indicates the psychological state of Pharaoh when he felt intimidated by Moses' growing influence and power. It highlights the fear and anxiety that Moses' presence and miracles instilled in Pharaoh, reflecting the internal conflict and doubt that began to undermine Pharaoh's confidence and control.
orig: فأوجس في نفسه خيفة موسى

translation: We said, 'Do not fear; indeed, you are the superior.'
interpretation: This verse reassures the Prophet Muhammad that he should not be afraid because he is supported and elevated by Allah above his adversaries. It emphasizes divine protection and the elevated status granted to the Prophet, encouraging steadfastness and courage in the face of opposition.
orig: قلنا لا تخف إنك أنت الأعلى

translation: And throw what is in your right hand; it will swallow up what they have crafted. What they have crafted is but the trick of a magician, and the magician will not succeed wherever he goes.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and truth of divine miracles over human-made deceptions. When Moses is instructed to throw down his staff, which turns into a serpent and consumes the magicians' serpents, it symbolizes the victory of God's truth over falsehood. The verse underscores that no matter how skilled or deceptive the efforts of those who oppose the truth (represented by the magicians), they are ultimately futile against the divine will and truth. It serves as a reminder of the ultimate failure of those who rely on deceit and manipulation, reinforcing the theme of God's omnipotence and the eventual triumph of righteousness.
orig: وألق ما في يمينك تلقف ما صنعوا إنما صنعوا كيد ساحر ولا يفلح الساحر حيث أتى

translation: So the magicians fell down in prostration. They said, "We believe in the Lord of Aaron and Moses."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the moment of transformation and enlightenment for the magicians who were initially in opposition to Moses. Their prostration and declaration of faith signify a profound recognition of the truth and power of God, as demonstrated through Moses and Aaron. It highlights the theme of divine guidance leading to the acceptance of monotheism, even among those who were previously adversaries, showing that faith can overcome doubt and opposition when confronted with clear signs of God's truth.
orig: فألقي السحرة سجدا قالوا آمنا برب هارون وموسى

translation: He said, 'Have you believed in him before I gave you permission? Indeed, he is your master who has taught you magic. So I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides, and I will surely crucify you on the trunks of palm trees, and you will surely know which of us is more severe in punishment and more enduring.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the Pharaoh's reaction to the magicians' belief in Moses, showcasing his authoritarian control and his use of severe punishment to maintain power. It reflects the theme of resistance against tyranny and the ultimate futility of oppressive measures against faith and truth.
orig: قال آمنتم له قبل أن آذن لكم إنه لكبيركم الذي علمكم السحر فلأقطعن أيديكم وأرجلكم من خلاف ولأصلبنكم في جذوع النخل ولتعلمن أينا أشد عذابا وأبقى

translation: They said, 'We will not prefer you over what has come to us of clear proofs and the One who created us. So decree whatever you are to decree. You can only decree for this worldly life.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the steadfastness and faith of the believers who were confronted by a tyrant. They assert that they will not abandon the clear signs and revelations from God, nor their faith in their Creator, despite the threats of punishment. They acknowledge the tyrant's power to harm them in this life but emphasize that such power is limited to the temporal world and does not extend to the afterlife, underscoring their belief in the eternal nature of the hereafter over the fleeting nature of worldly life.
orig: قالوا لن نؤثرك على ما جاءنا من البينات والذي فطرنا فاقض ما أنت قاض إنما تقضي هذه الحياة الدنيا

translation: Indeed, we have believed in our Lord, that He may forgive us our sins and what magic you compelled us to practice. And Allah is better and more enduring.
interpretation: This verse reflects a declaration of faith and repentance by those who were previously involved in magical practices under duress. It signifies a turning point where they acknowledge their belief in Allah and seek His forgiveness for their past actions, affirming that reliance on Allah is superior and everlasting compared to any worldly or magical pursuits.
orig: إنا آمنا بربنا ليغفر لنا خطايانا وما أكرهتنا عليه من السحر والله خير وأبقى

translation: Indeed, whoever comes to his Lord as a criminal - indeed, for him is Hell; he will neither die therein nor live.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe consequences of approaching Allah with sin and disobedience. It describes the state of the sinner in Hell as being in a perpetual condition between life and death, enduring endless torment without the relief of death. This serves as a stark warning about the importance of righteousness and the dire outcomes of a life spent in crime and moral corruption.
orig: إنه من يأت ربه مجرما فإن له جهنم لا يموت فيها ولا يحيى

translation: And whoever comes to Him as a believer and has done righteous deeds, for those will be the highest degrees.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who approach Allah with faith and a record of good deeds will be rewarded with the highest ranks in the hereafter. It underscores the importance of both faith and righteous actions in achieving elevated status in Paradise, suggesting that spiritual and moral excellence are key to attaining Allah's ultimate favor and proximity.
orig: ومن يأته مؤمنا قد عمل الصالحات فأولئك لهم الدرجات العلى

translation: Gardens of Eden beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever, and that is the reward for those who purify themselves.
interpretation: This verse describes the ultimate reward in the afterlife for those who strive to purify their souls and lead a righteous life. The 'Gardens of Eden' symbolize a state of eternal bliss and peace, where the believers are rewarded with everlasting life in a paradise where rivers flow, signifying abundance and purity. The emphasis on 'abiding therein forever' highlights the permanence of this reward, contrasting with the temporary nature of worldly life. The phrase 'those who purify themselves' refers to individuals who engage in spiritual and moral cleansing, striving to rid themselves of sin and to enhance their piety and devotion to God. This purification is not only about ritual cleanliness but also about moral integrity and the constant effort to improve one's character and actions in accordance with divine guidance.
orig: جنات عدن تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها وذلك جزاء من تزكى

translation: And We inspired Moses, 'Travel by night with My servants and strike for them a dry path in the sea; you will not fear being overtaken, nor be afraid.'
interpretation: This verse refers to the miraculous event of the parting of the Red Sea, where God commanded Moses to lead the Israelites out of Egypt. The instruction to 'strike a dry path' symbolizes God's power to alter the natural order for the salvation of His chosen people. The reassurance that Moses should not fear being overtaken or be afraid underscores the theme of divine protection and trust in God's plan, even in the face of seemingly insurmountable obstacles.
orig: ولقد أوحينا إلى موسى أن أسر بعبادي فاضرب لهم طريقا في البحر يبسا لا تخاف دركا ولا تخشى

translation: So Pharaoh pursued them with his soldiers, and there covered them from the sea that which covered them.
interpretation: This verse describes the moment when Pharaoh and his army chased after the Israelites, only to be overwhelmed and drowned by the sea. It symbolizes the ultimate downfall of tyranny and oppression when it pursues the path of injustice. The sea, which parted for the believers, becomes a means of destruction for the oppressors, illustrating divine justice and the protection of the faithful.
orig: فأتبعهم فرعون بجنوده فغشيهم من اليم ما غشيهم

translation: And Pharaoh led his people astray, and he did not guide [them].
interpretation: This verse highlights the moral and spiritual corruption of Pharaoh, who, instead of leading his people towards righteousness and truth, misguided them due to his arrogance and denial of God's signs. It serves as a reminder of the consequences of following leaders who deviate from the path of guidance.
orig: وأضل فرعون قومه وما هدى

translation: O Children of Israel, We delivered you from your enemy, and We made an appointment with you on the right side of Mount Sinai, and We sent down to you manna and quails.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder to the Children of Israel of the divine favors bestowed upon them by Allah. It emphasizes the miraculous deliverance from their enemies, symbolizing God's protection and guidance. The mention of the appointment at Mount Sinai highlights the covenant between Allah and the Israelites, underscoring the importance of obedience and faithfulness to divine commandments. The provision of manna and quails in the wilderness illustrates Allah's sustenance and care, reinforcing the theme of reliance on God's providence during times of need.
orig: يا بني إسرائيل قد أنجيناكم من عدوكم وواعدناكم جانب الطور الأيمن ونزلنا عليكم المن والسلوى

translation: Eat of the good things which We have provided for you, and do not transgress therein, lest My wrath should descend upon you; and he upon whom My wrath descends, he is lost indeed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of moderation and gratitude in enjoying the blessings provided by Allah. It warns against excess and transgression, which can lead to divine displeasure and ultimately, spiritual ruin. The message is clear: while it is permissible to enjoy the lawful provisions, one must remain within the bounds set by Allah, recognizing that overindulgence can lead to the loss of divine favor and guidance.
orig: كلوا من طيبات ما رزقناكم ولا تطغوا فيه فيحل عليكم غضبي ومن يحلل عليه غضبي فقد هوى

translation: And indeed, I am the Most Forgiving to whoever repents and believes and does righteous deeds, then remains guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's attribute of forgiveness, which is accessible to those who sincerely repent from their sins, embrace faith, engage in good deeds, and continue to follow the path of righteousness. It highlights the importance of a continuous journey towards guidance after initial repentance and faith, suggesting that true forgiveness is contingent upon an ongoing commitment to a righteous life.
orig: وإني لغفار لمن تاب وآمن وعمل صالحا ثم اهتدى

translation: And what has hastened you away from your people, O Moses?
interpretation: This verse questions Moses' urgency to leave his people, suggesting a divine test of his patience and commitment to his prophetic mission. It highlights the importance of steadfastness and trust in God's timing, even when faced with personal desires or concerns.
orig: وما أعجلك عن قومك يا موسى

translation: He said, 'They are my followers and I hastened to You, my Lord, so that You may be pleased.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the plea of a person on the Day of Judgment who claims to have followed the path of righteousness and hurried towards God's mercy, hoping to gain His satisfaction. It underscores the importance of sincerity in one's actions and the ultimate goal of pleasing Allah, highlighting the individual's accountability and the desire for divine acceptance.
orig: قال هم أولاء على أثري وعجلت إليك رب لترضى

translation: He said, 'Indeed, We have tested your people after you [left], and the Samiri has led them astray.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of trial and misguidance. After Moses left to receive the commandments from God, his people were put to the test in his absence. The Samiri, a figure who crafted the golden calf, symbolizes temptation and misguidance, leading the people astray from the path of righteousness. This serves as a reminder of the constant challenge believers face in maintaining faith and obedience to God, especially in the absence of their leaders.
orig: قال فإنا قد فتنا قومك من بعدك وأضلهم السامري

translation: So Moses returned to his people, angry and grieved. He said, 'O my people, did not your Lord promise you a good promise? Was the time of my absence too long for you? Or did you want that wrath should descend upon you from your Lord, so you broke your promise to me?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the themes of leadership, accountability, and the consequences of disobedience. Moses, upon returning to his people, expresses his anger and sorrow at their failure to uphold the covenant in his absence. His questioning reflects a leader's frustration and disappointment when his followers do not adhere to divine promises and instructions. The verse underscores the importance of patience and faith in God's promises, warning against the severe repercussions of breaking divine commandments out of impatience or doubt.
orig: فرجع موسى إلى قومه غضبان أسفا قال يا قوم ألم يعدكم ربكم وعدا حسنا أفطال عليكم العهد أم أردتم أن يحل عليكم غضب من ربكم فأخلفتم موعدي

translation: They said, 'We did not break our appointment with you by our own will, but we were made to carry burdens of the people's ornaments, so we threw them [into the fire], and thus did the Samiri throw.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the Israelites' attempt to justify their actions in the absence of Moses. They claim that they were compelled to carry the burdens of the people's ornaments, which led them to throw these into the fire, resulting in the creation of the golden calf by the Samiri. The interpretation suggests a human tendency to rationalize disobedience or sin by attributing it to external pressures or circumstances, rather than taking personal responsibility for one's actions.
orig: قالوا ما أخلفنا موعدك بملكنا ولكنا حملنا أوزارا من زينة القوم فقذفناها فكذلك ألقى السامري

translation: So he brought forth for them a calf, a body which had a lowing sound, and they said, 'This is your god and the god of Moses, but he forgot.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the idolatry committed by the Children of Israel during Moses' absence. The calf, crafted by the Samaritan, was given a semblance of life through its lowing sound, which deceived the people into worshipping it as a deity. Their statement reflects their deep misunderstanding and misguidance, attributing divinity to a created object and wrongly assuming that Moses himself worshipped it, indicating their forgetfulness of the true monotheistic teachings they had received.
orig: فأخرج لهم عجلا جسدا له خوار فقالوا هذا إلهكم وإله موسى فنسي

translation: Do they not see that they will not be able to respond to them with a word, nor will they have any power to harm or benefit them?
interpretation: This verse highlights the powerlessness of false deities or idols that people might worship. It emphasizes that these entities cannot respond to their worshippers, nor can they cause any harm or provide any benefit. The verse serves as a reminder of the futility of worshipping anything other than the one true God, who alone possesses the power to affect change in the world and in the lives of His creation.
orig: أفلا يرون ألا يرجع إليهم قولا ولا يملك لهم ضرا ولا نفعا

translation: And Aaron had already said to them before, "O my people, you have only been tested by it, and indeed, your Lord is the Most Merciful, so follow me and obey my order."
interpretation: This verse highlights Aaron's role as a guide and leader to the Israelites, urging them to recognize the trial they were facing with the golden calf as a test of their faith. He reminds them of God's mercy and calls them to follow his guidance and obey his commands, emphasizing the importance of steadfastness and obedience to God's chosen leaders in times of temptation and trial.
orig: ولقد قال لهم هارون من قبل يا قوم إنما فتنتم به وإن ربكم الرحمن فاتبعوني وأطيعوا أمري

translation: They said, 'We will not cease to be devoted to it until Moses returns to us.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the steadfastness and commitment of the Israelites to the worship of the golden calf, illustrating their impatience and lack of faith during Moses' absence. It underscores the human tendency to revert to idolatry and material worship when spiritual guidance is not immediately present.
orig: قالوا لن نبرح عليه عاكفين حتى يرجع إلينا موسى

translation: He said, 'O Aaron, what prevented you, when you saw them going astray,'
interpretation: This verse reflects Moses' inquiry to Aaron about why he did not intervene to guide the people back to the right path when he witnessed their deviation into idolatry. It underscores the responsibility of leaders to actively correct and guide their followers, highlighting the importance of proactive leadership in maintaining the community's faith and moral direction.
orig: قال يا هارون ما منعك إذ رأيتهم ضلوا

translation: Will you not then obey My command?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question from Allah to the Prophet Muhammad, emphasizing the importance of obedience to divine commands. It serves as a reminder to all believers of the necessity to follow Allah's directives without hesitation, highlighting the consequences of disobedience and the rewards of compliance.
orig: ألا تتبعن أفعصيت أمري

translation: He said, 'O son of my mother, do not seize me by my beard or my head. Indeed, I fear that you will say, 'You caused division among the Children of Israel and did not respect my word.''
interpretation: This verse highlights the tension and fear of causing division among the community, as expressed by Moses' brother, Aaron, who is concerned about the potential accusations of splitting the Children of Israel and not adhering to Moses' instructions. It reflects the importance of unity and the fear of being blamed for discord within the religious community.
orig: قال يا ابن أم لا تأخذ بلحيتي ولا برأسي إني خشيت أن تقول فرقت بين بني إسرائيل ولم ترقب قولي

translation: He said: 'What is the matter with you, O Samiri?'
interpretation: This verse reflects Moses' inquiry to Samiri, seeking an explanation for his actions in creating the golden calf, which led the Israelites astray. It highlights the importance of accountability and the need for leaders to confront and address wrongdoing within their community.
orig: قال فما خطبك يا سامري

translation: He said, 'I saw what they did not see, so I took a handful from the footprint of the messenger and threw it, and thus my soul prompted me.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the story of the golden calf, where Samiri claims to have seen something others did not, leading him to take dust from the hoofprint of the angel Gabriel's horse and throw it into the calf, animating it. His action was driven by his own soul's prompting, illustrating the human tendency towards temptation and the consequences of following personal desires over divine guidance.
orig: قال بصرت بما لم يبصروا به فقبضت قبضة من أثر الرسول فنبذتها وكذلك سولت لي نفسي

translation: He said: "Then go forth, for verily, it is granted to you in life that you say, 'Do not touch,' and indeed, you have an appointment that you will not fail to keep. And look at your god to which you have been devoted; we will surely burn it and scatter it into the sea, a total scattering."
interpretation: This verse is part of the narrative where Moses addresses the people who worshipped the golden calf. The command to "go forth" signifies a dismissal and a punishment for their idolatry. The phrase 'Do not touch' refers to the temporary power given to the calf to speak, which was a test and a sign of their misguidance. The 'appointment' alludes to the inevitable Day of Judgment where all will be held accountable. The destruction of the idol by burning and scattering it into the sea symbolizes the complete eradication of false worship and the return to true monotheism. This act serves as a powerful reminder of the consequences of idolatry and the ultimate triumph of divine truth.
orig: قال فاذهب فإن لك في الحياة أن تقول لا مساس وإن لك موعدا لن تخلفه وانظر إلى إلهك الذي ظلت عليه عاكفا لنحرقنه ثم لننسفنه في اليم نسفا

translation: Your god is only Allah, there is no god but He. He encompasses all things in knowledge.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness of Allah, asserting that He alone is worthy of worship and that there is no other deity besides Him. It also highlights His attribute of omniscience, indicating that Allah's knowledge is all-encompassing and extends to every aspect of existence, reinforcing the belief in His absolute power and awareness.
orig: إنما إلهكم الله الذي لا إله إلا هو وسع كل شيء علما

translation: Thus We relate to you from the news of what has preceded, and We have given you from Us a reminder.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the continuity of divine guidance through the stories of past nations and prophets, which are recounted to the Prophet Muhammad as lessons and warnings. The 'reminder' given to him is the Qur'an itself, a source of guidance and a means to reflect on the fate of those who came before, encouraging adherence to the path of righteousness.
orig: كذلك نقص عليك من أنباء ما قد سبق وقد آتيناك من لدنا ذكرا

translation: Whoever turns away from it - indeed, he will bear a burden on the Day of Resurrection.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequence of neglecting the guidance provided by the Qur'an. It suggests that those who deliberately turn away from its teachings will be held accountable and will carry the weight of their rejection as a burden on the Day of Judgment. This burden symbolizes the spiritual and moral responsibility one has towards following divine guidance, and the failure to do so results in a heavy accountability in the afterlife.
orig: من أعرض عنه فإنه يحمل يوم القيامة وزرا

translation: Abiding therein, and evil is the burden on them on the Day of Resurrection.
interpretation: This verse describes the state of those who will reside in Hell, emphasizing the permanence of their punishment. The phrase 'evil is the burden on them' suggests that the weight of their sins and the consequences they face will be overwhelmingly heavy and distressing on the Day of Resurrection, underscoring the severity and the inescapable nature of divine judgment.
orig: خالدين فيه وساء لهم يوم القيامة حملا

translation: The Day when the Trumpet is blown and We gather the criminals, that Day, blue-eyed.
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Judgment, emphasizing the moment when the trumpet is blown, signaling the resurrection of all beings. The criminals, referred to as those who have committed sins, are gathered with eyes described as 'zurq', which can be interpreted as blue or darkened, possibly indicating their fear, shock, or the physical manifestation of their inner state due to the overwhelming nature of the event. This imagery underscores the severity and the transformative impact of the Day of Judgment on the wrongdoers.
orig: يوم ينفخ في الصور ونحشر المجرمين يومئذ زرقا

translation: They whisper among themselves, 'You have not stayed except for ten [days].'
interpretation: This verse highlights the disbelief and confusion of the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment. They are shocked to find that the time they spent in the worldly life, which they thought was long, is perceived as merely ten days in the hereafter. It underscores the relativity of time between this world and the next, and serves as a reminder of how short and insignificant worldly life is in comparison to the eternal life to come.
orig: يتخافتون بينهم إن لبثتم إلا عشرا

translation: We know best what they say, when the best of them in conduct says, 'You have tarried only a day.'
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah is fully aware of the thoughts and statements of people, even when they are discussing the duration of their stay in the worldly life. The phrase 'the best of them in conduct' refers to the most righteous among them, who might perceive their life as fleeting, akin to a single day, when compared to the eternity of the hereafter. This highlights the relativity of time and the insignificance of worldly life in the grand scheme of existence, urging believers to focus on the hereafter.
orig: نحن أعلم بما يقولون إذ يقول أمثلهم طريقة إن لبثتم إلا يوما

translation: And they ask you about the mountains, so say, 'My Lord will blow them away, dispersing them completely.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the inquiry about the fate of mountains on the Day of Judgment. The response given to the Prophet Muhammad indicates that God will completely obliterate the mountains, reducing them to dust. This imagery serves to illustrate the immense power of God and the transformative nature of the Day of Judgment, where even the most stable and enduring elements of the earth will be utterly changed.
orig: ويسألونك عن الجبال فقل ينسفها ربي نسفا

translation: Then He makes it level, bare,
interpretation: This verse describes the process of Allah causing the earth to become a flat, barren expanse after it has been covered with vegetation. It symbolizes the cycle of life and death, and the power of Allah to transform the state of creation as He wills. The imagery of the earth being reduced to a 'qاع صفصف' or a leveled, bare plain, serves as a reminder of the transient nature of worldly life and the ultimate return to Allah.
orig: فيذرها قاعا صفصفا

translation: You will not see in it any crookedness or curvature.
interpretation: This verse describes the perfection and harmony of the Hereafter, where everything is in its rightful place without any deviation or imperfection, symbolizing the ultimate state of peace and order in Paradise.
orig: لا ترى فيها عوجا ولا أمتا

translation: On that Day, they will follow the caller, with no deviation therein, and [all] voices will be humbled for the Most Merciful, so you will not hear except a whisper.
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Judgment, emphasizing the absolute submission and obedience of all beings to God's command. The 'caller' represents the divine summons to which everyone will respond without any deviation, symbolizing the unity and inevitability of divine judgment. The humbling of voices to mere whispers signifies the awe and reverence all will feel in the presence of the Most Merciful, highlighting the overwhelming power and majesty of God on that day.
orig: يومئذ يتبعون الداعي لا عوج له وخشعت الأصوات للرحمن فلا تسمع إلا همسا

translation: On that Day, intercession will not benefit except for those to whom the Most Merciful has given permission and whose word He has accepted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the exclusivity and divine authority of Allah in granting intercession on the Day of Judgment. It underscores that no intercession will be effective unless it is sanctioned by Allah, the Most Merciful. This highlights the importance of divine approval and acceptance, reinforcing the belief that ultimate salvation and forgiveness are in the hands of Allah alone, based on His mercy and satisfaction with the individual's deeds and words.
orig: يومئذ لا تنفع الشفاعة إلا من أذن له الرحمن ورضي له قولا

translation: He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they do not encompass it with knowledge.
interpretation: This verse highlights the omniscience of Allah, indicating that He has complete knowledge of all that has happened and all that will happen, which is beyond the comprehension of human beings. It emphasizes the limitation of human knowledge in contrast to the all-encompassing knowledge of Allah.
orig: يعلم ما بين أيديهم وما خلفهم ولا يحيطون به علما

translation: And faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting, and he will be disappointed who carries injustice.
interpretation: This verse underscores the ultimate reality of facing Allah, the Ever-Living and Self-Subsisting, on the Day of Judgment. It highlights the humility and submission that all will experience in His presence. The phrase 'he will be disappointed who carries injustice' serves as a warning that those who have wronged others or committed sins without seeking forgiveness will face disappointment and loss.
