translation: They will not hear the slightest sound of it [Hell], while they are in what their souls desire, abiding eternally.
interpretation: This verse describes the state of the righteous in Paradise, emphasizing their complete protection from any disturbance or reminder of Hell. It signifies the ultimate peace and fulfillment they experience, as they are immersed in eternal bliss, enjoying everything their hearts desire without any fear or distress.
orig: لا يسمعون حسيسها وهم في ما اشتهت أنفسهم خالدون

translation: They will not be grieved by the greatest terror, and the angels will meet them, [saying], 'This is your day which you were promised.'
interpretation: This verse speaks to the believers who will experience a state of peace and joy on the Day of Judgment. The "greatest terror" refers to the overwhelming fear and dread that will be felt by many on that day, but the righteous will be protected from this feeling. Instead, they will be greeted by angels, who will affirm that this is the day they were promised, a day of reward and fulfillment of divine promises. This reassurance from the angels signifies the ultimate validation of their faith and the beginning of their eternal bliss.
orig: لا يحزنهم الفزع الأكبر وتتلقاهم الملائكة هذا يومكم الذي كنتم توعدون

translation: The Day that We roll up the heavens like a scroll rolled up for the writings: as We began the first creation, so shall We repeat it: a promise binding upon Us; truly We shall fulfill it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and capability of Allah to end the world as He began it, using the metaphor of rolling up the heavens like a scroll to illustrate the ease and control with which He will bring about the Day of Judgment. It reassures believers of the certainty of resurrection and the fulfillment of Allah's promises, reinforcing the concept of divine omnipotence and the inevitability of the hereafter.
orig: يوم نطوي السماء كطي السجل للكتب كما بدأنا أول خلق نعيده وعدا علينا إنا كنا فاعلين

translation: And We have already written in the Psalms after the reminder that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine promise that ultimately, the earth and its resources will be inherited by those who are righteous and obedient to Allah. It reassures believers that despite the temporary power of the unrighteous, the ultimate ownership and benefit of the earth belong to those who live according to Allah's guidance, as was foretold in earlier scriptures like the Psalms.
orig: ولقد كتبنا في الزبور من بعد الذكر أن الأرض يرثها عبادي الصالحون

translation: Indeed, in this is a message for a people who worship.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an contains guidance and lessons specifically for those who are devoted to worship and obedience to Allah. It suggests that the true believers, who actively engage in worship, will find profound meaning and direction in the messages conveyed through the Qur'an.
orig: إن في هذا لبلاغا لقوم عابدين

translation: And We have not sent you except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was sent by Allah as a manifestation of divine mercy, not just for the believers or a specific group, but for all of creation. His mission encompasses guidance, compassion, and salvation, extending to all humanity and beyond, emphasizing the universal nature of his prophethood.
orig: وما أرسلناك إلا رحمة للعالمين

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], "It has been revealed to me that your god is one God; so will you be Muslims [in submission to Him]?"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the core message of monotheism in Islam, instructing the Prophet Muhammad to convey that there is only one God worthy of worship. It challenges the listeners to accept this truth and submit to it by becoming Muslims, highlighting the universal call to faith and submission to the one true God.
orig: قل إنما يوحى إلي أنما إلهكم إله واحد فهل أنتم مسلمون

translation: So if they turn away, say: "I have warned you equally; and I know not whether that which you are warned is near or far."
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad to convey the message of warning to all people equally, regardless of their response. It emphasizes the role of the Prophet as a messenger who delivers the divine warning without knowing the exact timing of the events foretold, thus highlighting the urgency and seriousness of the message while acknowledging the uncertainty of when the warned events will occur.
orig: فإن تولوا فقل آذنتكم على سواء وإن أدري أقريب أم بعيد ما توعدون

translation: Indeed, He knows what is said aloud and what you conceal.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's omniscience, highlighting that He is fully aware of both the words that are openly expressed and the thoughts and intentions that are kept hidden within the hearts of individuals. It serves as a reminder to believers to be mindful of their speech and inner thoughts, as nothing is hidden from Allah.
orig: إنه يعلم الجهر من القول ويعلم ما تكتمون

translation: And I do not know; perhaps it is a trial for you and an enjoyment for a time.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the worldly life and its pleasures could be a test from Allah to see how people respond to them. It implies that the material world should not be the ultimate goal, as it is temporary and may serve as a means to test one's faith and patience.
orig: وإن أدري لعله فتنة لكم ومتاع إلى حين

translation: He said, 'My Lord, judge [between us] in truth. And our Lord is the Most Merciful, whose help is sought against what you ascribe.'
interpretation: This verse reflects a plea for divine justice and assistance. The speaker is asking Allah to adjudicate with fairness and truth, acknowledging Allah's attribute of mercy and seeking His help against the false accusations or descriptions made by others. It underscores a reliance on God's judgment and mercy in the face of adversity and false claims.
orig: قال رب احكم بالحق وربنا الرحمن المستعان على ما تصفون

translation: O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the earthquake of the Hour is a tremendous thing.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder and a warning to all of humanity to be conscious of and reverent towards Allah, emphasizing the severity and magnitude of the Day of Judgment. The 'earthquake of the Hour' symbolizes the cataclysmic events that will occur, urging believers to live righteously and prepare for the accountability that awaits them.
orig: يا أيها الناس اتقوا ربكم إن زلزلة الساعة شيء عظيم

translation: The Day you shall see it, every nursing mother will forget her nursing infant, and every pregnant female will drop her load. You shall see mankind as drunken, yet they will not be drunken, but severe will be the Torment of Allah.
interpretation: This verse describes the overwhelming nature of the Day of Judgment, where the terror and shock of the event will be so intense that it causes even the most nurturing and protective instincts, like those of a nursing mother or a pregnant woman, to be overridden. The comparison to drunkenness illustrates the disorientation and loss of control people will experience, not from intoxication, but from the severity of Allah's punishment, emphasizing the profound impact and fear that will grip humanity on that day.
orig: يوم ترونها تذهل كل مرضعة عما أرضعت وتضع كل ذات حمل حملها وترى الناس سكارى وما هم بسكارى ولكن عذاب الله شديد

translation: And among the people is he who disputes about Allah without knowledge and follows every rebellious devil.
interpretation: This verse highlights the behavior of individuals who engage in arguments about Allah and His nature without possessing any true knowledge or understanding. Instead of seeking guidance from divine revelation, they are swayed by their whims and follow misleading influences, symbolized here as 'every rebellious devil'. This reflects a warning against baseless speculation and the dangers of being led astray by one's desires or external corrupting forces.
orig: ومن الناس من يجادل في الله بغير علم ويتبع كل شيطان مريد

translation: It is written about him that whoever takes him as a friend, he will lead him astray and guide him to the torment of the Blaze.
interpretation: This verse warns against following Satan, indicating that those who ally themselves with him will be misled from the right path and ultimately led to the punishment of Hellfire. It emphasizes the severe consequences of choosing evil companionship and the importance of staying away from influences that lead one away from God's guidance.
orig: كتب عليه أنه من تولاه فأنه يضله ويهديه إلى عذاب السعير

translation: O mankind, if you are in doubt about the Resurrection, then indeed, We created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then from a clinging clot, and then from a lump of flesh, formed and unformed - that We may show you. And We settle in the wombs whom We will for a specified term; then We bring you out as a child, and then [We develop you] that you may reach your [time of] maturity. And among you is he who is taken in [early] death, and among you is he who is returned to the most decrepit [old] age so that he knows, after [once having] knowledge, nothing. And you see the earth barren, but when We send down upon it rain, it quivers and swells and grows [something] of every splendid kind.
interpretation: This verse addresses the skepticism about the concept of resurrection by illustrating the miraculous process of human creation and development, from the initial stages in the womb to the various stages of life and death. It emphasizes God's power over life cycles, using the analogy of the earth's transformation from barrenness to fertility with rain to affirm the possibility of resurrection. The verse suggests that just as God can bring life from seemingly lifeless earth, He can also resurrect humans after death, reinforcing the belief in the afterlife and God's omnipotence over creation and its renewal.
orig: يا أيها الناس إن كنتم في ريب من البعث فإنا خلقناكم من تراب ثم من نطفة ثم من علقة ثم من مضغة مخلقة وغير مخلقة لنبين لكم ونقر في الأرحام ما نشاء إلى أجل مسمى ثم نخرجكم طفلا ثم لتبلغوا أشدكم ومنكم من يتوفى ومنكم من يرد إلى أرذل العمر لكيلا يعلم من بعد علم شيئا وترى الأرض هامدة فإذا أنزلنا عليها الماء اهتزت وربت وأنبتت من كل زوج بهيج

translation: That is because Allah is the Truth, and it is He Who gives life to the dead, and He has power over all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence and truth of Allah. It asserts that Allah's existence and power are undeniable truths, as He has the ability to resurrect the dead, which is a demonstration of His supreme power over life and death. Furthermore, the verse underscores that Allah's authority extends over all aspects of existence, reinforcing the belief in His absolute control and capability to manage every detail of the universe.
orig: ذلك بأن الله هو الحق وأنه يحيي الموتى وأنه على كل شيء قدير

translation: And that the Hour is coming, there is no doubt about it, and that Allah will resurrect those who are in the graves.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty of the Day of Judgment, known as the Hour, which is an inevitable event in Islamic belief. It underscores the power of Allah to bring the dead back to life, highlighting the resurrection as a fundamental aspect of faith, where all individuals will be accountable for their deeds. This belief serves as a reminder of the afterlife and encourages believers to live righteously in preparation for that day.
orig: وأن الساعة آتية لا ريب فيها وأن الله يبعث من في القبور

translation: And among the people is he who disputes about Allah without knowledge or guidance or an enlightening book.
interpretation: This verse highlights the existence of individuals who engage in debates or arguments about Allah and His nature without possessing proper knowledge, divine guidance, or reference to a clear and enlightening scripture. It serves as a critique of baseless arguments and emphasizes the importance of relying on informed and guided discourse when discussing matters related to faith and theology.
orig: ومن الناس من يجادل في الله بغير علم ولا هدى ولا كتاب منير

translation: The second type, he turns away to lead astray from the path of Allah; for him is disgrace in the world, and We will make him taste the punishment of the Fire on the Day of Resurrection.
interpretation: This verse describes a person who deliberately misleads others from the path of Allah, characterized by arrogance and a desire to corrupt others' faith. Such an individual will face disgrace and humiliation in this worldly life as a consequence of their actions. Furthermore, on the Day of Judgment, they will experience the severe punishment of the Fire, emphasizing the grave consequences of leading others astray from the truth and righteousness.
orig: ثاني عطفه ليضل عن سبيل الله له في الدنيا خزي ونذيقه يوم القيامة عذاب الحريق

translation: That is because of what your hands have put forth, and that Allah is not unjust to the servants.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of personal accountability in Islam. It indicates that the consequences one faces are a direct result of their own actions ("what your hands have put forth"). Additionally, it reassures that Allah is never unjust to His servants, implying that any hardship or punishment is deserved and fair, based on one's deeds. This serves as a reminder for individuals to be mindful of their actions, as they will be held accountable for them.
orig: ذلك بما قدمت يداك وأن الله ليس بظلام للعبيد

translation: And among the people is he who worships Allah on an edge. If he is touched by good, he is content with it; but if he is struck by trial, he turns on his face. He has lost [both] this world and the Hereafter. That is the manifest loss.
interpretation: This verse describes a type of person who practices their faith superficially or conditionally. Such an individual worships Allah only when things are going well, feeling content and secure in times of prosperity. However, when faced with adversity or trials, their faith wavers, and they turn away from their religious commitments. This behavior demonstrates a lack of true faith and steadfastness, leading to a loss in both worldly life and the hereafter. The verse emphasizes that such a conditional approach to faith results in a clear and evident loss, highlighting the importance of consistent and sincere devotion to Allah regardless of circumstances.
orig: ومن الناس من يعبد الله على حرف فإن أصابه خير اطمأن به وإن أصابته فتنة انقلب على وجهه خسر الدنيا والآخرة ذلك هو الخسران المبين

translation: He invokes, instead of Allah, that which neither harms him nor benefits him. That is straying far away.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility and misguidance of worshipping or seeking help from anything other than Allah. It emphasizes that such actions lead one astray from the right path because they involve turning to entities that have no real power to affect one's life positively or negatively. The phrase "straying far away" underscores the severity of this deviation from true faith and submission to Allah alone.
orig: يدعو من دون الله ما لا يضره وما لا ينفعه ذلك هو الضلال البعيد

translation: He invokes, instead of Allah, that which neither harms him nor benefits him. That is a far straying.
interpretation: This verse criticizes the act of calling upon or worshipping entities other than Allah, which have no power to cause harm or bring benefit. It highlights the folly and misguidance of such actions, emphasizing that reliance on anything other than Allah is a severe form of deviation from the right path.
orig: يدعو لمن ضره أقرب من نفعه لبئس المولى ولبئس العشير

translation: Indeed, Allah will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds into Gardens beneath which rivers flow. Indeed, Allah does what He wills.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the promise of Paradise for those who have faith and perform good deeds, highlighting the divine reward for righteous living. It also underscores Allah's omnipotence, affirming that His will is absolute and He can fulfill His promises as He sees fit.
orig: إن الله يدخل الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار إن الله يفعل ما يريد

translation: Whoever thinks that Allah will not help him in this world and the Hereafter, let him stretch out a rope to the sky, then let him cut it off and see whether his plan can remove that which enrages him.
interpretation: This verse challenges the disbelief and despair of those who doubt Allah's support and assistance in both worldly and spiritual matters. It uses a powerful metaphor of someone trying to physically reach the sky with a rope, only to cut it off, illustrating the futility and absurdity of such actions. The verse emphasizes that no human scheme or effort can alleviate the frustration or anger caused by opposing Allah's will. It serves as a reminder of the omnipotence and ultimate control of Allah over all affairs, urging believers to trust in His divine plan and support.
orig: من كان يظن أن لن ينصره الله في الدنيا والآخرة فليمدد بسبب إلى السماء ثم ليقطع فلينظر هل يذهبن كيده ما يغيظ

translation: And thus We have sent it down as clear verses, and that Allah guides whom He wills.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the clarity and guidance provided by the Qur'an. It suggests that the revelation of the Qur'an in clear verses is a deliberate act by Allah to guide those whom He chooses. The phrase "whom He wills" indicates that divine guidance is bestowed according to Allah's wisdom and plan, not necessarily based on human merit or desire. This underscores the concept of divine sovereignty in guiding humanity towards the right path.
orig: وكذلك أنزلناه آيات بينات وأن الله يهدي من يريد

translation: Indeed, those who have believed and those who were Jews and the Sabeans and the Christians and the Magians and those who associated others with Allah - Allah will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed Allah is, over all things, a Witness.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate justice and omniscience of Allah. It states that on the Day of Resurrection, Allah will make a clear distinction and judgment among all people, regardless of their faith - whether they are Muslims, Jews, Sabeans, Christians, Magians, or polytheists. The mention of these diverse groups underscores the inclusivity of divine judgment, indicating that no one will be exempt from Allah's evaluation. The assertion that 'Allah is, over all things, a Witness' reinforces the belief in Allah's complete awareness and knowledge of every individual's actions and intentions, ensuring a fair and just judgment.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا والذين هادوا والصابئين والنصارى والمجوس والذين أشركوا إن الله يفصل بينهم يوم القيامة إن الله على كل شيء شهيد

translation: Have you not seen that to Allah prostrates whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, and the sun, the moon, the stars, the mountains, the trees, the moving creatures and many among mankind, but many are due for the punishment. And he whom Allah humiliates - for him there is no bestower of honor. Indeed, Allah does what He wills.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universal submission to Allah, highlighting that everything in creation, from celestial bodies to earthly beings, naturally prostrates to Him. It underscores the concept of Tawheed (the oneness of God) and the inherent recognition of Allah's sovereignty by all of creation. The mention of 'many among mankind' who prostrate willingly contrasts with those who do not, indicating that while submission is natural and expected, human free will allows for deviation, leading to potential punishment. The verse also conveys the absolute power of Allah, stating that whom He humiliates cannot find honor elsewhere, reinforcing the idea that all honor and power belong to Allah alone, and He acts according to His divine will.
orig: ألم تر أن الله يسجد له من في السماوات ومن في الأرض والشمس والقمر والنجوم والجبال والشجر والدواب وكثير من الناس وكثير حق عليه العذاب ومن يهن الله فما له من مكرم إن الله يفعل ما يشاء

translation: These two adversaries dispute about their Lord: But those who disbelieve, garments of fire will be cut out for them, and boiling water will be poured over their heads.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the stark contrast between believers and disbelievers in their disputes about the nature of God. The imagery of garments of fire and boiling water being poured over the heads of disbelievers serves as a powerful metaphor for the severe consequences and torment that await those who reject faith. It underscores the Qur'an's emphasis on the gravity of disbelief and the resultant punishment in the afterlife, urging individuals to reflect deeply on their beliefs and the ultimate accountability before God.
orig: هذان خصمان اختصموا في ربهم فالذين كفروا قطعت لهم ثياب من نار يصب من فوق رءوسهم الحميم

translation: It will melt what is in their bellies and their skins.
interpretation: This verse describes the intense heat of the Hellfire, which is so severe that it will cause the internal organs and the skin of the people in Hell to melt. This imagery serves as a warning of the severe punishment awaiting those who reject faith and commit evil deeds, emphasizing the physical torment that awaits them in the afterlife.
orig: يصهر به ما في بطونهم والجلود

translation: And for them are maces of iron
interpretation: This verse refers to the weapons that the disbelievers will have in Hell, symbolizing the severity of their punishment. The mention of iron maces underscores the strength and brutality of the torment they will endure, reflecting the consequences of their actions in the worldly life.
orig: ولهم مقامع من حديد

translation: Every time they want to get out of it [the Fire] from anguish, they will be returned to it, and [it will be said], 'Taste the punishment of the Blaze!'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the inescapable nature of Hell for those who are condemned to it. It emphasizes the continuous cycle of attempting to escape the torment only to be forced back into it, highlighting the severity and eternal aspect of the punishment. The phrase 'Taste the punishment of the Blaze' serves as a reminder of divine justice and the consequences of one's actions, reinforcing the idea that the suffering in Hell is a direct result of one's deeds in life.
orig: كلما أرادوا أن يخرجوا منها من غم أعيدوا فيها وذوقوا عذاب الحريق

translation: Indeed, Allah will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will be adorned with bracelets of gold and pearls, and their garments therein will be of silk.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the rewards awaiting believers in the afterlife. It highlights that faith combined with good deeds leads to entry into Paradise, described as gardens with flowing rivers, symbolizing abundance and eternal life. The adornments of gold bracelets and pearls, along with silk garments, signify the honor, purity, and luxury that the righteous will enjoy in the hereafter, reflecting their elevated status and the fulfillment of divine promise.
orig: إن الله يدخل الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار يحلون فيها من أساور من ذهب ولؤلؤا ولباسهم فيها حرير

translation: And they are guided to the good of speech, and they are guided to the path of the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse indicates that those who follow the guidance of Allah are led to speak in a manner that is beneficial and righteous, and are directed towards the path that leads to Allah, who is described as Al-Hamid, the Praiseworthy. It emphasizes the dual guidance in both speech and action towards what is pleasing to Allah.
orig: وهدوا إلى الطيب من القول وهدوا إلى صراط الحميد

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and obstruct the path of Allah and the Sacred Mosque, which We have designated for all people equally, whether they reside there or are visitors, and whoever seeks to deviate in it with injustice, We will make them taste a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sanctity of the Sacred Mosque and the severe consequences for those who hinder access to it or engage in wrongful acts within its premises. It underscores the universal right of all people to access the mosque, highlighting equality in worship regardless of one's status as a resident or a visitor. The mention of a painful punishment serves as a deterrent against disbelief and injustice, reinforcing the importance of maintaining the mosque's sanctity and the broader path of Allah.
orig: إن الذين كفروا ويصدون عن سبيل الله والمسجد الحرام الذي جعلناه للناس سواء العاكف فيه والباد ومن يرد فيه بإلحاد بظلم نذقه من عذاب أليم

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when We designated for Abraham the site of the House, [saying], 'Do not associate anything with Me and purify My House for those who circumambulate it and those who stand [in prayer] and those who bow and prostrate.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine command given to Abraham to establish the sanctity of the Ka'bah, emphasizing monotheism and the purification of the sacred space for worship. It underscores the importance of Tawhid (the oneness of God) and the Ka'bah's role as a focal point for various acts of worship, symbolizing unity and submission to God among Muslims.
orig: وإذ بوأنا لإبراهيم مكان البيت أن لا تشرك بي شيئا وطهر بيتي للطائفين والقائمين والركع السجود

translation: And proclaim to the people the pilgrimage; they will come to you on foot and on every lean camel; they will come from every distant pass.
interpretation: This verse instructs Prophet Muhammad to announce the Hajj pilgrimage to all people, emphasizing the universal call to Muslims to perform this sacred duty. The imagery of people arriving on foot and on camels from every distant path illustrates the diversity and unity of the Muslim ummah, coming together in devotion despite their varied origins and means of travel.
orig: وأذن في الناس بالحج يأتوك رجالا وعلى كل ضامر يأتين من كل فج عميق

translation: That they may witness benefits for themselves and mention the name of Allah on known days over what He has provided for them of [sacrificial] animals. So eat of them and feed the miserable and poor.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the communal and spiritual aspects of the Hajj pilgrimage. It highlights that the pilgrimage is not only for personal spiritual growth but also for the collective benefit of the community. The act of mentioning Allah's name during the sacrifice of animals signifies gratitude and acknowledgment of God's provisions. The instruction to eat from the sacrificial animals and to feed the poor underscores the values of sharing and charity, reinforcing the social responsibility of the pilgrims to care for the less fortunate within their community.
orig: ليشهدوا منافع لهم ويذكروا اسم الله في أيام معلومات على ما رزقهم من بهيمة الأنعام فكلوا منها وأطعموا البائس الفقير

translation: Then let them complete their rites and fulfill their vows and circumambulate the Ancient House.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of completing the Hajj rituals in their entirety, including the final act of circumambulating the Ka'bah, known as Tawaf al-Ifadah. It underscores the significance of fulfilling one's vows and obligations during the pilgrimage, highlighting the spiritual and communal aspects of Hajj. The 'Ancient House' refers to the Ka'bah, symbolizing the continuity and centrality of monotheistic worship from the time of Abraham.
orig: ثم ليقضوا تفثهم وليوفوا نذورهم وليطوفوا بالبيت العتيق

translation: That [has been commanded], and whoever honors the sacred ordinances of Allah - it is best for him in the sight of his Lord. And permitted to you are the grazing livestock, except what is recited to you. So avoid the uncleanliness of idols and avoid false statement,
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of respecting and upholding the sanctities and commandments set by Allah, which is considered highly beneficial for one's spiritual standing with their Creator. It also outlines the permissibility of consuming certain types of livestock, while prohibiting others as specified in divine revelations. Additionally, it instructs believers to steer clear of idolatry and falsehood, promoting a lifestyle of purity and truthfulness in devotion to Allah.
orig: ذلك ومن يعظم حرمات الله فهو خير له عند ربه وأحلت لكم الأنعام إلا ما يتلى عليكم فاجتنبوا الرجس من الأوثان واجتنبوا قول الزور

translation: Haneefs, devoted to Allah, not associating anything with Him. And whoever associates anything with Allah - it is as if he had fallen from the sky and was snatched by the birds, or the wind threw him to a distant place.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of pure monotheism, urging believers to be devoted solely to Allah without associating partners with Him. The imagery of falling from the sky and being snatched by birds or blown away by the wind illustrates the severe spiritual and existential downfall of those who commit shirk (polytheism or associating partners with Allah). It serves as a stark warning about the consequences of deviating from the path of Tawheed (the oneness of Allah).
orig: حنفاء لله غير مشركين به ومن يشرك بالله فكأنما خر من السماء فتخطفه الطير أو تهوي به الريح في مكان سحيق

translation: That is, and whoever honors the rituals of Allah, it is from the piety of the hearts.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that showing respect and reverence to the symbols and rituals ordained by Allah is a manifestation of true piety and fear of Allah in one's heart. It suggests that the outward act of honoring these rituals is deeply connected to an inner state of god-consciousness and devotion.
orig: ذلك ومن يعظم شعائر الله فإنها من تقوى القلوب

translation: Therein are benefits for you to an appointed term; then its proper place is the Ancient House.
interpretation: This verse highlights the temporary benefits humans derive from the sacrificial animals during Hajj, which are permissible until a specified time. After this period, the ultimate destination and sanctity of these offerings are directed towards the Ka'bah, symbolizing the return to the pure worship of God and the spiritual essence of the pilgrimage.
orig: لكم فيها منافع إلى أجل مسمى ثم محلها إلى البيت العتيق

translation: And for every nation We have appointed a rite that they may mention the name of Allah over what He has provided for them of quadruped of the flocks. So your god is one God, so to Him surrender, and give good tidings to the humble.
interpretation: This verse highlights the diversity of religious practices among different nations, each given specific rites by Allah to honor Him through the sustenance He provides, specifically mentioning the sacrifice of livestock. It underscores the unity of worship, emphasizing that despite these varied practices, there is only one God to whom all should submit. The verse also encourages the Prophet Muhammad to give good tidings to those who are humble and submissive to Allah, reinforcing the message of monotheism and humility in worship.
orig: ولكل أمة جعلنا منسكا ليذكروا اسم الله على ما رزقهم من بهيمة الأنعام فإلهكم إله واحد فله أسلموا وبشر المخبتين

translation: Those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts are filled with awe, and the patient ones upon what has befallen them, and those who establish prayer and spend out of what We have provided them.
interpretation: This verse describes the characteristics of true believers. It emphasizes that when reminded of Allah, their hearts are filled with reverence and fear, indicating a deep connection and consciousness of God. The mention of patience in the face of adversity highlights their resilience and trust in Allah's plan. Establishing prayer regularly shows their commitment to worship and maintaining a spiritual connection with Allah. Finally, spending from what they have been given reflects their generosity and recognition that their provisions are from Allah, encouraging them to share with others. This verse collectively paints a picture of a believer's life centered around faith, patience, worship, and charity.
orig: الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم والصابرين على ما أصابهم والمقيمي الصلاة ومما رزقناهم ينفقون

translation: And the camels and cattle We have appointed for you as among the symbols of Allah; you have therein much good. So mention the name of Allah over them when they are drawn up in lines. Then, when they have fallen down, eat thereof and feed the contented one and the beggar. Thus have We subjected them to you that you may be grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ritual of animal sacrifice during Hajj, emphasizing that these animals are designated by Allah as symbols of His worship. The act of sacrificing these animals is not just a ritual but a means of spiritual and communal benefit, as it involves remembering Allah's name during the process and sharing the meat with others, including those in need. This practice is meant to foster a sense of gratitude towards Allah for the provision and the opportunity to perform such acts of worship and charity.
orig: والبدن جعلناها لكم من شعائر الله لكم فيها خير فاذكروا اسم الله عليها صواف فإذا وجبت جنوبها فكلوا منها وأطعموا القانع والمعتر كذلك سخرناها لكم لعلكم تشكرون

translation: Allah will not be reached by their flesh nor their blood, but it is the piety from you that reaches Him. Thus, He has subjected them to you that you may glorify Allah for that which He has guided you; and give good tidings to the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the essence of religious rituals, such as sacrifice, is not in the physical act itself but in the spiritual intention and piety behind it. It teaches that what truly matters to Allah is the devotion and righteousness of the worshipper, not the material offerings. The verse also highlights the purpose of such rituals as a means to express gratitude and glorify Allah for His guidance. Additionally, it serves as a message of encouragement and hope, promising good tidings to those who perform good deeds.
orig: لن ينال الله لحومها ولا دماؤها ولكن يناله التقوى منكم كذلك سخرها لكم لتكبروا الله على ما هداكم وبشر المحسنين

translation: Indeed, Allah defends those who have believed. Indeed, Allah does not like any ungrateful traitor.
interpretation: This verse underscores the protective nature of Allah towards believers, emphasizing His role as a guardian and supporter of faith. It also highlights a moral stance against betrayal and ingratitude, suggesting that such traits are contrary to the values Allah cherishes, thereby encouraging believers to embody loyalty and gratitude in their conduct.
orig: إن الله يدافع عن الذين آمنوا إن الله لا يحب كل خوان كفور

translation: Permission [to fight] has been given to those who are being fought, because they were wronged. And indeed, Allah is Able to give them victory.
interpretation: This verse grants permission to Muslims to engage in defensive warfare when they are subjected to oppression and injustice. It emphasizes that the right to fight back is a response to being wronged, and it reassures believers that Allah has the power to support and grant them victory in their struggle against oppression.
orig: أذن للذين يقاتلون بأنهم ظلموا وإن الله على نصرهم لقدير

translation: Those who were expelled from their homes without right - except that they say, 'Our Lord is Allah.' And if Allah did not check one set of people by means of another, monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques, wherein the name of Allah is mentioned much, would surely have been pulled down. And Allah will surely support those who support Him. Indeed, Allah is All-Strong, All-Mighty.
interpretation: This verse underscores the protection and support that Allah provides to those who are persecuted for their faith. It highlights the divine intervention that prevents the destruction of places of worship where Allah's name is frequently invoked, emphasizing the importance of interfaith solidarity and the strength derived from faith. The verse reassures believers that Allah's support is assured for those who stand firm in their faith and support His cause, reflecting His attributes of strength and might.
orig: الذين أخرجوا من ديارهم بغير حق إلا أن يقولوا ربنا الله ولولا دفع الله الناس بعضهم ببعض لهدمت صوامع وبيع وصلوات ومساجد يذكر فيها اسم الله كثيرا ولينصرن الله من ينصره إن الله لقوي عزيز

translation: Those who, if We establish them in the land, establish prayer and give zakah and enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong. And to Allah belongs the outcome of [all] matters.
interpretation: This verse highlights the characteristics of righteous leaders or communities empowered by Allah. It emphasizes that when given authority or resources, they prioritize the establishment of regular prayers and the giving of zakah, which are foundational acts of worship and social welfare in Islam. Additionally, they actively promote good (ma'ruf) and prevent evil (munkar), reflecting a commitment to moral and social reform. The verse concludes by reminding that ultimate control and the final outcome of all affairs rest with Allah, underscoring the importance of humility and reliance on divine guidance in leadership and governance.
orig: الذين إن مكناهم في الأرض أقاموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة وأمروا بالمعروف ونهوا عن المنكر ولله عاقبة الأمور

translation: And if they deny you, then the people of Noah, and 'Ad, and Thamud denied before them.
interpretation: This verse reassures the Prophet Muhammad that he should not feel disheartened by the rejection of his message by his contemporaries, as previous prophets like Noah, 'Ad, and Thamud faced similar disbelief. It emphasizes the continuity of the prophetic mission across different times and peoples, highlighting that opposition to divine messages is not unique to his situation but a recurring theme in the history of prophethood.
orig: وإن يكذبوك فقد كذبت قبلهم قوم نوح وعاد وثمود

translation: And the people of Abraham and the people of Lot
interpretation: This verse refers to the communities associated with the prophets Abraham and Lot, highlighting their historical and spiritual significance in the narrative of divine guidance and moral lessons. It underscores the continuity of prophetic messages and the consequences faced by their respective peoples due to their responses to these messages.
orig: وقوم إبراهيم وقوم لوط

translation: And the companions of Madyan [denied]. So Moses was denied, so I gave the disbelievers respite; then I seized them, and how [terrible] was My denial.
interpretation: This verse reflects on the consequences of disbelief and rejection of divine messages, using the example of the people of Madyan and their denial of Moses. It underscores the patience of God, who grants a period of respite to disbelievers, allowing them time to possibly repent. However, when the time for judgment comes, the punishment is severe and inevitable, illustrating the ultimate power and justice of God. The rhetorical question at the end emphasizes the intensity and finality of divine retribution, serving as a warning to others.
orig: وأصحاب مدين وكذب موسى فأمليت للكافرين ثم أخذتهم فكيف كان نكير

translation: So how many a town have We destroyed while it was unjust, so it is lying fallen on its roofs, and (there is) a deserted well and an abandoned palace.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of injustice and disobedience to God's commands. It illustrates the fate of communities that were destroyed due to their wrongdoing, leaving behind only ruins as a testament to their downfall. The mention of a deserted well and an abandoned palace emphasizes the complete desolation and the loss of what was once considered valuable or central to the community's life. This serves as a warning to other societies to heed the lessons from the past and to live righteously, or face a similar fate.
orig: فكأين من قرية أهلكناها وهي ظالمة فهي خاوية على عروشها وبئر معطلة وقصر مشيد

translation: Have they not traveled through the land, so that they may have hearts by which to understand or ears by which to hear? For indeed, it is not the eyes that go blind, but it is the hearts within the chests that go blind.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of reflective thinking and understanding. It suggests that true insight and comprehension come from the heart, not merely from physical senses like sight. The heart, symbolizing the center of understanding and faith, can become blind due to negligence or refusal to reflect on the signs of God in the world. Traveling through the land and observing its diverse aspects should lead one to recognize God's creation and wisdom, yet many fail to do so because their hearts are not open to receiving this truth.
orig: أفلم يسيروا في الأرض فتكون لهم قلوب يعقلون بها أو آذان يسمعون بها فإنها لا تعمى الأبصار ولكن تعمى القلوب التي في الصدور

translation: And they urge you to hasten the punishment. And Allah will never fail in His promise. And indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count.
interpretation: This verse addresses the impatience of disbelievers who demand immediate punishment for their disbelief, reflecting their doubt in the Day of Judgment. It reassures believers that God's promise of judgment and reward is certain and will come to pass, emphasizing the divine perspective of time, where a single day with God equates to a thousand years in human reckoning. This highlights the vast difference between divine and human time scales, underscoring the patience and long-term planning of God's justice.
orig: ويستعجلونك بالعذاب ولن يخلف الله وعده وإن يوما عند ربك كألف سنة مما تعدون

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed while it was wrongdoing, so it is fallen into ruin; and [there are] to Us [many] ways.
interpretation: This verse reflects on the fate of numerous communities that were destroyed due to their unjust actions. It serves as a reminder of the transient nature of worldly power and the ultimate accountability before God. The phrase "to Us [many] ways" indicates that God's methods of dealing with such communities are manifold and beyond human comprehension, emphasizing divine wisdom and justice.
orig: وكأين من قرية أمليت لها وهي ظالمة ثم أخذتها وإلي المصير

translation: Say, 'O mankind, indeed I am to you a clear warner.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophet Muhammad's role as a messenger whose primary function is to warn people clearly and explicitly about the consequences of their actions in the sight of God. It underscores the universal message of Islam, addressing all of humanity, and highlights the clarity and transparency of the warning given through the Prophet.
orig: قل يا أيها الناس إنما أنا لكم نذير مبين

translation: So those who have believed and done righteous deeds - for them will be forgiveness and noble provision.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the reward for those who have faith in Allah and perform good deeds. The promise of forgiveness indicates that their sins will be pardoned, reflecting Allah's mercy. The 'noble provision' refers to the blessings and sustenance they will receive in the hereafter, which is described as noble due to its purity and excellence. This interpretation encourages believers to maintain their faith and continue performing righteous acts, with the assurance of divine reward.
orig: فالذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لهم مغفرة ورزق كريم

translation: And those who strove against Our signs, seeking to frustrate them, those are the companions of the Hellfire.
interpretation: This verse warns against those who actively oppose or try to undermine the divine signs and messages of Allah. It highlights that such individuals, who deliberately work against the truth and guidance provided by Allah, will ultimately be consigned to Hellfire. The term 'strived against' indicates a conscious and persistent effort to reject or distort the divine revelations, emphasizing the severity of their actions and the consequent punishment.
orig: والذين سعوا في آياتنا معاجزين أولئك أصحاب الجحيم

translation: And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet except that when he wished, Satan threw into his wish. But Allah abolishes that which Satan throws in, then Allah makes precise His verses. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine protection of the prophetic message against Satanic interference. It suggests that whenever a prophet or messenger has a wish or desire, Satan attempts to corrupt it by inserting false suggestions or desires. However, Allah, in His infinite wisdom and knowledge, nullifies these satanic insertions and ensures the purity and clarity of His revelations. This reassures believers of the integrity of the Qur'anic message, highlighting Allah's role as the ultimate guardian of truth, who uses His omniscience and wisdom to maintain the authenticity of His guidance.
orig: وما أرسلنا من قبلك من رسول ولا نبي إلا إذا تمنى ألقى الشيطان في أمنيته فينسخ الله ما يلقي الشيطان ثم يحكم الله آياته والله عليم حكيم

translation: So that He may make what Satan throws a trial for those in whose hearts is a disease and those whose hearts are hardened. And indeed, the wrongdoers are in extreme dissension.
interpretation: This verse explains that Allah allows Satan to cast doubts and temptations as a test for those who have weak faith or hardened hearts. This trial serves to distinguish the believers from the hypocrites and the disbelievers. Those with spiritual ailments or stubbornness in their hearts are more susceptible to Satan's whispers, leading them further astray. The verse also emphasizes that the wrongdoers, due to their rejection of truth, are deeply divided and in a state of severe opposition to the right path.
orig: ليجعل ما يلقي الشيطان فتنة للذين في قلوبهم مرض والقاسية قلوبهم وإن الظالمين لفي شقاق بعيد

translation: And let those who have been given knowledge see that it is the truth from your Lord, and let them believe in it, so their hearts may humbly submit to it. And indeed, Allah guides the believers to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of knowledge in recognizing the truth of the Qur'an, which is described as coming directly from God. It suggests that those endowed with knowledge should be able to discern the divine origin of the Qur'an, leading them to faith. This faith, in turn, should bring about a state of humility and submission in their hearts. The verse also underscores God's guidance, indicating that true believers are led by God towards a righteous and straightforward path in life.
orig: وليعلم الذين أوتوا العلم أنه الحق من ربك فيؤمنوا به فتخبت له قلوبهم وإن الله لهاد الذين آمنوا إلى صراط مستقيم

translation: And those who disbelieve will not cease to be in doubt about it until the Hour comes upon them suddenly or there comes to them the punishment of a barren day.
interpretation: This verse highlights the persistent skepticism and doubt of the disbelievers regarding the truth of Islam and the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes that their doubt will continue until they are suddenly confronted with the reality of the Hour, or they experience a severe punishment on a day devoid of any benefit or productivity, underscoring the inevitability and suddenness of divine judgment.
orig: ولا يزال الذين كفروا في مرية منه حتى تأتيهم الساعة بغتة أو يأتيهم عذاب يوم عقيم

translation: Sovereignty on that Day will be for Allah; He will judge between them. And those who believed and did righteous deeds will be in Gardens of Delight.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate authority and sovereignty of Allah on the Day of Judgment. It underscores that all judgment and decision-making power will belong to Allah alone, highlighting the insignificance of worldly power and status. The promise of Gardens of Delight for those who have faith and performed good deeds serves as a motivation for believers to remain steadfast in their faith and actions, knowing that their efforts will be rewarded in the hereafter.
orig: الملك يومئذ لله يحكم بينهم فالذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات في جنات النعيم

translation: And those who disbelieve and deny Our signs, for them there will be a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequence of disbelief and rejection of the divine signs. It serves as a warning that those who consciously choose to disbelieve and reject the truths presented in the Qur'an will face a punishment that is not only severe but also humiliating, underscoring the gravity of their denial.
orig: والذين كفروا وكذبوا بآياتنا فأولئك لهم عذاب مهين

translation: And those who emigrated in the way of Allah and then were killed or died - Allah will surely provide them a goodly provision. And indeed, Allah is the best of providers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the promise of Allah to those who sacrifice their lives or die in the path of migration for His sake. It underscores the divine assurance of a reward in the hereafter, emphasizing that such individuals will be granted a 'goodly provision' by Allah, which signifies not only sustenance but also spiritual rewards and blessings in Paradise. The verse also reaffirms Allah's attribute as the ultimate and most generous provider, instilling trust and hope in believers that their sacrifices are recognized and will be compensated generously in the afterlife.
orig: والذين هاجروا في سبيل الله ثم قتلوا أو ماتوا ليرزقنهم الله رزقا حسنا وإن الله لهو خير الرازقين

translation: Let them enter the place of entry that they will be pleased with, and indeed Allah is All-Knowing, Most Forbearing.
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah will grant the believers entry into Paradise, a place that will fulfill their utmost satisfaction and joy. The mention of Allah being All-Knowing and Most Forbearing emphasizes His complete awareness of the believers' deeds and His patience in dealing with them, ensuring that their reward is just and perfectly suited to their desires.
orig: ليدخلنهم مدخلا يرضونه وإن الله لعليم حليم

translation: That is so, and whoever retaliates with the like of that with which he was afflicted and then is oppressed again, Allah will surely help him. Indeed, Allah is Pardoning and Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of justice and the right to self-defense within the bounds of proportionality. It reassures believers that if they are wronged and respond appropriately, yet face further oppression, Allah will come to their aid. The mention of Allah as 'Pardoning and Forgiving' highlights that even in the context of seeking justice, one should not harbor grudges or seek vengeance beyond what is fair, as divine support and forgiveness are promised to those who maintain righteousness.
orig: ذلك ومن عاقب بمثل ما عوقب به ثم بغي عليه لينصرنه الله إن الله لعفو غفور

translation: That is because Allah causes the night to enter the day and causes the day to enter the night and because Allah is Hearing and Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence and omniscience of Allah. The metaphor of night entering day and vice versa illustrates the seamless transitions and balance in the universe, which are under Allah's control. The mention of Allah being Hearing and Seeing underscores His awareness and attentiveness to all that occurs, reinforcing the belief in His complete knowledge and surveillance over creation.
orig: ذلك بأن الله يولج الليل في النهار ويولج النهار في الليل وأن الله سميع بصير

translation: That is because Allah is the Truth, and what they call upon besides Him is falsehood, and because Allah is the Most High, the Great.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental Islamic belief in the oneness of God (Tawhid). It asserts that Allah is the ultimate reality and truth, while all other deities or objects of worship are false and devoid of any divine essence. The verse also highlights Allah's attributes of being exalted and great, reinforcing His supreme status and authority over all creation. This declaration serves to remind believers of the importance of directing their worship solely to Allah and to reject any form of idolatry or polytheism.
orig: ذلك بأن الله هو الحق وأن ما يدعون من دونه هو الباطل وأن الله هو العلي الكبير

translation: Have you not seen that Allah sends down water from the sky, and the earth becomes green? Indeed, Allah is Subtle and Well-Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse highlights the miraculous nature of rain and its effect on the earth, illustrating Allah's subtle control over natural phenomena and His deep knowledge of all things. It serves as a reminder of Allah's omnipotence and His ability to bring life and growth, symbolizing His mercy and provision for all creation.
orig: ألم تر أن الله أنزل من السماء ماء فتصبح الأرض مخضرة إن الله لطيف خبير

translation: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And indeed, Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and ownership of Allah over all creation, both in the heavens and on the earth. It underscores that everything belongs to Him and is under His control. The attributes of Allah mentioned, 'the Free of need' and 'the Praiseworthy', highlight His self-sufficiency and the fact that He is worthy of all praise despite not needing anything from His creation. This serves as a reminder to believers of their dependence on Allah and the importance of recognizing and praising Him for His boundless generosity and perfection.
orig: له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وإن الله لهو الغني الحميد

translation: Do you not see that Allah has subjected to you whatever is in the earth and the ships which run upon the sea by His command? And He restrains the sky from falling upon the earth, unless by His permission. Indeed, Allah is, to the people, Kind and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the omnipotence and mercy of Allah. It emphasizes how Allah has made the resources of the earth and the movement of ships on the sea available for human benefit, illustrating His control over the natural world. The mention of restraining the sky from falling upon the earth underscores Allah's power to maintain the cosmic order. The verse concludes by affirming Allah's attributes of kindness and mercy towards humanity, suggesting that these divine gifts and protections are manifestations of His compassion.
orig: ألم تر أن الله سخر لكم ما في الأرض والفلك تجري في البحر بأمره ويمسك السماء أن تقع على الأرض إلا بإذنه إن الله بالناس لرءوف رحيم

translation: And He is the One who gives you life, then causes you to die, then will bring you to life again. Indeed, mankind is ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse underscores the cycle of life, death, and resurrection controlled solely by Allah, emphasizing His power over all existence. It also highlights a critical aspect of human nature: ingratitude. Despite the evident signs of Allah's power and mercy in granting life and the promise of resurrection, humans often fail to acknowledge or appreciate these divine acts, reflecting a deep-seated tendency towards disbelief and thanklessness.
orig: وهو الذي أحياكم ثم يميتكم ثم يحييكم إن الإنسان لكفور

translation: For every nation We have appointed rites which they observe, so let them not dispute with you about the matter, and call to your Lord. Indeed, you are on a straight guidance.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the diversity of religious practices among different nations, acknowledging that each has its own set of rituals and customs ordained by Allah. It instructs the Prophet Muhammad not to engage in disputes with others over these differences, but instead to focus on inviting people to the worship of Allah. The verse reassures the Prophet that he is on the right path, reinforcing his mission to guide others towards the straight path of Islam without being distracted by arguments over ritual variances.
orig: لكل أمة جعلنا منسكا هم ناسكوه فلا ينازعنك في الأمر وادع إلى ربك إنك لعلى هدى مستقيم

translation: And if they argue with you, say, 'Allah knows best what you do.'
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to respond to those who dispute with him by affirming that ultimate knowledge of their actions and intentions lies with Allah alone. It emphasizes the principle of divine omniscience and encourages reliance on Allah's judgment rather than engaging in fruitless debates.
orig: وإن جادلوك فقل الله أعلم بما تعملون

translation: Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection concerning that wherein you used to differ.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate authority of Allah as the final arbiter on the Day of Judgment. It underscores that all disputes and differences among people, whether theological, moral, or otherwise, will be resolved by Allah's judgment. This serves as a reminder to believers to be mindful of their actions and beliefs, knowing that they will be accountable for them on that day.
orig: الله يحكم بينكم يوم القيامة فيما كنتم فيه تختلفون

translation: Do you not know that Allah knows what is in the heavens and the earth? Indeed, that is in a Record. Indeed, that is easy for Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience of Allah, indicating that He is fully aware of everything that exists in the universe. The mention of the 'Record' (Kitab) suggests that all knowledge and events are documented and known to Allah. The ease with which Allah manages this vast knowledge underscores His omnipotence and the effortless nature of His control over all creation.
orig: ألم تعلم أن الله يعلم ما في السماء والأرض إن ذلك في كتاب إن ذلك على الله يسير

translation: And they worship besides Allah that for which He has sent down no authority, and of which they have no knowledge, and for the wrongdoers there is no helper.
interpretation: This verse criticizes the practice of idolatry and the worship of deities other than Allah, emphasizing that such acts are baseless and unauthorized by divine revelation. It highlights the ignorance of those who engage in such worship, as they lack true knowledge about what they venerate. Furthermore, it serves as a warning that those who perpetrate such injustices will find no support or assistance, underscoring the ultimate futility and spiritual danger of their actions.
orig: ويعبدون من دون الله ما لم ينزل به سلطانا وما ليس لهم به علم وما للظالمين من نصير

translation: And when Our clear verses are recited to them, you see denial on the faces of those who disbelieve; they almost attack those who recite Our verses to them. Say, 'Shall I inform you of something worse than that? It is the Fire, which Allah has promised to those who disbelieve, and what a wretched destination.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the reaction of disbelievers when confronted with the clear signs and verses of Allah. Their immediate response is one of denial and hostility, to the extent that they nearly assault those who are reciting the verses. The verse then shifts to a warning, where the Prophet Muhammad is instructed to inform them of a fate worse than their current reaction - the Hellfire. This serves as a reminder of the severe consequences of disbelief and rejection of divine guidance, emphasizing the importance of faith and acceptance of Allah's messages.
orig: وإذا تتلى عليهم آياتنا بينات تعرف في وجوه الذين كفروا المنكر يكادون يسطون بالذين يتلون عليهم آياتنا قل أفأنبئكم بشر من ذلكم النار وعدها الله الذين كفروا وبئس المصير

translation: O mankind, an example has been made, so listen to it. Indeed, those you call upon besides Allah will never create [as much as] a fly, even if they gathered together for that purpose. And if the fly should steal from them a [tiny] thing, they could not recover it from the fly. Weak are the seeker and the sought.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the powerlessness of idols and false deities compared to Allah. It uses the metaphor of a fly to illustrate that these entities cannot even create something as insignificant as a fly, nor can they retrieve anything taken by a fly, highlighting their utter helplessness and dependence. The verse serves as a reminder to humans of the futility of worshipping anything other than the all-powerful Allah, underscoring the weakness of both the false deities and those who seek them.
orig: يا أيها الناس ضرب مثل فاستمعوا له إن الذين تدعون من دون الله لن يخلقوا ذبابا ولو اجتمعوا له وإن يسلبهم الذباب شيئا لا يستنقذوه منه ضعف الطالب والمطلوب

translation: They have not appraised Allah with true appraisal. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the human failure to fully comprehend and appreciate the greatness and omnipotence of Allah. It serves as a reminder that Allah's power and might are beyond human understanding, and that underestimating Him is a common human error. The attributes of being 'Powerful' and 'Exalted in Might' highlight Allah's supreme authority and strength, urging believers to recognize and respect His infinite capabilities.
orig: ما قدروا الله حق قدره إن الله لقوي عزيز

translation: Allah chooses from the angels messengers and from the people. Indeed, Allah is Hearing, Seeing.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's sovereign authority to select messengers from both the angelic and human realms, emphasizing His deliberate choice in divine communication. The attributes of Allah being Hearing and Seeing underscore His omniscience and omnipresence, indicating that He is fully aware of all affairs and capable of making the best selections for His divine mission.
orig: الله يصطفي من الملائكة رسلا ومن الناس إن الله سميع بصير

translation: He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and to Allah all matters return.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's omniscience and sovereignty. It indicates that Allah is fully aware of everything that happens to humans, both in their past and future. The phrase "to Allah all matters return" underscores the belief that ultimately, all decisions, judgments, and outcomes are in the hands of Allah, reinforcing the concept of divine decree and the accountability of all beings to Him.
orig: يعلم ما بين أيديهم وما خلفهم وإلى الله ترجع الأمور

translation: O you who have believed, bow down and prostrate yourselves and worship your Lord and do good - that you may succeed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of both the physical acts of worship, such as bowing and prostrating, and the moral actions of doing good. It suggests that success in both this life and the hereafter is contingent upon a combination of sincere devotion to God and righteous conduct towards others. The verse serves as a reminder that faith must be accompanied by action to achieve true success.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اركعوا واسجدوا واعبدوا ربكم وافعلوا الخير لعلكم تفلحون

translation: And strive for Allah with the striving due to Him. He has chosen you and has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty. [It is] the religion of your father, Abraham. He named you Muslims before and in this [revelation] that the Messenger may be a witness over you and you may be witnesses over the people. So establish prayer and give zakah and hold fast to Allah. He is your protector; and excellent is the protector, and excellent is the helper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of striving in the path of Allah with full dedication and sincerity. It reassures believers that Islam, the religion of Abraham, is designed to be free from unnecessary hardships, indicating that the obligations placed upon Muslims are meant to be manageable and beneficial. The verse also highlights the communal responsibility within Islam, where the Prophet Muhammad serves as a witness over the believers, and the believers, in turn, are witnesses to the rest of humanity about the truth of the message. The call to establish prayer and give zakah underscores the foundational acts of worship that strengthen the community and individual faith. Finally, the verse encourages Muslims to rely on Allah as their ultimate protector and helper, reinforcing the notion of divine support and guidance in all endeavors.
orig: وجاهدوا في الله حق جهاده هو اجتباكم وما جعل عليكم في الدين من حرج ملة أبيكم إبراهيم هو سماكم المسلمين من قبل وفي هذا ليكون الرسول شهيدا عليكم وتكونوا شهداء على الناس فأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة واعتصموا بالله هو مولاكم فنعم المولى ونعم النصير

translation: Indeed, the believers have succeeded.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate success and salvation of those who have true faith in Allah. It suggests that success in the eyes of Allah is not measured by worldly achievements but by the strength and sincerity of one's belief. The believers are promised a prosperous outcome in the hereafter, indicating that their faith will be rewarded with eternal bliss and divine favor.
orig: قد أفلح المؤمنون

translation: Those who are humble in their prayers
interpretation: This verse describes the quality of true believers who exhibit humility and reverence during their prayers. The term 'khāshiʿūn' indicates a deep sense of submission and awe before God, reflecting an inner state of heart that is focused solely on worship and devotion, free from worldly distractions.
orig: الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون

translation: And those who are from the vain talk, they turn away
interpretation: This verse highlights the virtue of avoiding idle and meaningless talk. It praises those who consciously choose to steer clear of conversations or activities that do not contribute to their spiritual or moral growth, emphasizing the importance of maintaining focus on what is beneficial and righteous.
orig: والذين هم عن اللغو معرضون

translation: And those who are performers of Zakah
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of Zakah, one of the five pillars of Islam, as a fundamental act of worship and social responsibility. It emphasizes that true believers are those who actively engage in giving Zakah, demonstrating their commitment to purifying their wealth and helping those in need, thereby fostering a sense of community and equity.
orig: والذين هم للزكاة فاعلون

translation: And those who guard their chastity
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of self-control and moral discipline in preserving one's chastity. It highlights the virtue of those who protect themselves from sexual misconduct and maintain purity in their actions and thoughts, which is a fundamental aspect of righteousness in Islam.
orig: والذين هم لفروجهم حافظون

translation: Except from their wives or those their right hands possess, for indeed, they will not be blamed
interpretation: This verse specifies exceptions to the general rule about lowering the gaze and guarding modesty. It indicates that within the bounds of marriage or with those whom one legally owns (in the context of the time, this refers to slaves), there is no blame for looking or interacting, as these relationships are sanctioned by Islamic law. This highlights the importance of lawful relationships and the boundaries set by Allah for maintaining moral conduct.
orig: إلا على أزواجهم أو ما ملكت أيمانهم فإنهم غير ملومين

translation: So whoever seeks beyond that, then those are the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the boundaries set by Allah in matters of sexual conduct. It specifically refers to those who seek relationships or desires beyond what is permissible (i.e., marriage). Such individuals are labeled as transgressors because they violate the divine limits established for human interactions, which are meant to protect the sanctity of family and societal order.
orig: فمن ابتغى وراء ذلك فأولئك هم العادون

translation: And those who are observant of their trusts and their covenants
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of integrity and responsibility in fulfilling one's obligations. It highlights that true believers are those who diligently honor their commitments, whether these are formal trusts or personal promises. This adherence to trust and covenant is a fundamental aspect of moral conduct in Islam, reflecting a person's reliability and righteousness.
orig: والذين هم لأماناتهم وعهدهم راعون

translation: And those who are observant of their prayers
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of steadfastness in performing the five daily prayers, highlighting that true believers are those who consistently maintain their prayers with punctuality and devotion, reflecting their commitment to their faith and obedience to Allah's commandments.
orig: والذين هم على صلواتهم يحافظون

translation: Those are the inheritors
interpretation: This verse refers to the believers who will inherit Paradise and the blessings therein due to their faith and righteous deeds. It emphasizes the promise of God to reward those who follow His path with eternal inheritance in the hereafter.
orig: أولئك هم الوارثون

translation: Those who inherit Paradise, they will abide therein forever.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the believers who will be granted entry into Paradise as an inheritance due to their faith and righteous deeds. The promise of eternity in Paradise underscores the ultimate reward and the everlasting nature of the bliss that awaits them, emphasizing the permanence of their reward and the fulfillment of God's promise to the faithful.
orig: الذين يرثون الفردوس هم فيها خالدون

translation: And indeed We created man from an extract of clay
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the humble origin of humanity, reminding us that despite our achievements and advancements, our fundamental creation is from the earth, specifically from clay. This serves as a reminder of our mortality and the need for humility and gratitude towards our Creator, who fashioned us from such simple beginnings.
orig: ولقد خلقنا الإنسان من سلالة من طين

translation: Then We made the sperm-drop into a clinging clot, placed in a firm resting-place.
interpretation: This verse describes the miraculous process of human creation, emphasizing the stages from a sperm-drop to a clinging clot, and highlights the secure and stable environment provided for the fetus in the womb. It reflects on the divine wisdom and care in the development of human life.
orig: ثم جعلناه نطفة في قرار مكين

translation: Then We made the sperm into a clot of congealed blood; then of that clot We made a (foetus) lump; then we made out of that lump bones and clothed the bones with flesh; then we developed out of it another creature. So blessed be Allah, the best to create!
interpretation: This verse describes the stages of human embryonic development, illustrating the miraculous process of creation from a mere sperm to a fully formed human being. It emphasizes Allah's power and perfection in creation, highlighting the intricate and sequential development as evidence of His supreme ability as the Creator. The phrase 'So blessed be Allah, the best to create!' serves as a declaration of praise and awe for Allah's unmatched creative abilities.
orig: ثم خلقنا النطفة علقة فخلقنا العلقة مضغة فخلقنا المضغة عظاما فكسونا العظام لحما ثم أنشأناه خلقا آخر فتبارك الله أحسن الخالقين

translation: Then, after that, you will surely die.
interpretation: This verse reminds us of the inevitable reality of death that follows life, emphasizing the transient nature of our worldly existence and urging believers to prepare for the afterlife by living righteously.
orig: ثم إنكم بعد ذلك لميتون

translation: Then on the Day of Resurrection you will be resurrected.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty and inevitability of the Day of Resurrection, reminding believers that after death, they will be brought back to life to face judgment based on their deeds in this world. It serves as a call to mindfulness and preparation for the afterlife.
orig: ثم إنكم يوم القيامة تبعثون

translation: And We have created above you seven paths, and We were never unmindful of the creation.
interpretation: This verse refers to the creation of the seven heavens or celestial layers above the earth, emphasizing Allah's meticulous attention and care in the act of creation. It reassures believers of Allah's omnipresence and omniscience, indicating that nothing in the creation is overlooked or forgotten by Him.
orig: ولقد خلقنا فوقكم سبع طرائق وما كنا عن الخلق غافلين

translation: And We sent down from the sky water in measure, and We caused it to settle in the earth, and indeed We are able to take it away.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's precise control over the natural world, specifically the water cycle. It emphasizes that the rain sent down from the sky is measured and purposeful, indicating divine wisdom in the distribution of water. The settling of water in the earth points to the role of water in sustaining life and agriculture. The assertion of Allah's ability to take away the water serves as a reminder of His power and the temporary nature of worldly provisions, encouraging gratitude and humility among believers.
orig: وأنزلنا من السماء ماء بقدر فأسكناه في الأرض وإنا على ذهاب به لقادرون

translation: So We brought forth for you thereby gardens of palm trees and grapevines in which for you are abundant fruits and from which you eat.
interpretation: This verse highlights the blessings and provisions that Allah has provided for humanity through water, which is essential for the growth of gardens filled with palm trees and grapevines. These gardens are not just sources of food but also symbolize the abundance and variety of sustenance that Allah has made available. The mention of eating from these fruits emphasizes the direct benefit and enjoyment humans derive from these divine provisions, reminding believers to be grateful and recognize Allah's role in sustaining life.
orig: فأنشأنا لكم به جنات من نخيل وأعناب لكم فيها فواكه كثيرة ومنها تأكلون

translation: And [We brought forth] a tree issuing from Mount Sinai which produces oil and food for those who eat.
interpretation: This verse refers to the olive tree, which is symbolic of blessings and peace in Islamic tradition. The mention of Mount Sinai connects it to divine revelation, suggesting that the sustenance and benefits derived from the olive tree are blessings from God. The oil and food it provides are not just physical nourishment but also represent spiritual enlightenment and sustenance for the believers.
orig: وشجرة تخرج من طور سيناء تنبت بالدهن وصبغ للآكلين

translation: And indeed, for you in the livestock there is a lesson. We give you drink from what is in their bellies, and for you in them are numerous benefits, and from them you eat.
interpretation: This verse highlights the blessings and lessons that can be derived from livestock, emphasizing their utility in providing sustenance and other benefits. It serves as a reminder of God's provision and the interconnectedness of creation, urging gratitude and reflection on the multifaceted uses of animals, such as milk for drinking and meat for eating, which are essential for human survival and well-being.
orig: وإن لكم في الأنعام لعبرة نسقيكم مما في بطونها ولكم فيها منافع كثيرة ومنها تأكلون

translation: And upon them and upon ships you are carried.
interpretation: This verse highlights the dependency of humans on various means of transportation provided by Allah, such as animals and ships, to travel across land and sea. It underscores the blessings and provisions from Allah that facilitate human movement and exploration.
orig: وعليها وعلى الفلك تحملون

translation: And We certainly sent Noah to his people, and he said, 'O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him; then will you not fear Him?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the mission of Prophet Noah, who was sent to guide his people towards the worship of the one true God, Allah. The rhetorical question at the end emphasizes the urgency and importance of fearing Allah and adhering to monotheism, urging the people to reflect on their actions and beliefs.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا نوحا إلى قومه فقال يا قوم اعبدوا الله ما لكم من إله غيره أفلا تتقون

translation: So the chiefs who disbelieved among his people said, 'This is nothing but a man like yourselves who wishes to assert his superiority over you. If Allah had willed, He would have sent down angels. We have not heard of this among our forefathers.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the disbelief and arrogance of the leaders of the community towards the prophet sent to them. They dismiss the prophet as merely a human trying to gain power over them, showing their resistance to change and their adherence to ancestral traditions. Their mention of angels reflects a common expectation of divine intervention in a form they deem more authoritative, revealing their misunderstanding of how divine guidance is delivered.
orig: فقال الملأ الذين كفروا من قومه ما هذا إلا بشر مثلكم يريد أن يتفضل عليكم ولو شاء الله لأنزل ملائكة ما سمعنا بهذا في آبائنا الأولين

translation: He is but a man possessed by jinn, so wait concerning him until a time.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the disbelievers dismissed the Prophet Muhammad as merely a man influenced by jinn, implying he was insane or possessed. They advised patience, expecting that his influence or condition would eventually wane or be exposed as false over time.
orig: إن هو إلا رجل به جنة فتربصوا به حتى حين

translation: He said, 'My Lord, support me because they have denied [the truth].'
interpretation: This verse reflects a plea for divine assistance in the face of opposition and disbelief. It underscores the reliance on God's support when one's message or truth is rejected by others, highlighting the theme of steadfastness in faith despite adversity.
orig: قال رب انصرني بما كذبون

translation: So We inspired him (saying): "Construct the ship under Our Eyes and Our Inspiration, and when Our Command comes, and the oven gushes forth water, then take on board of each kind two (male and female), and your family, except those thereof against whom the Word has already gone forth. And address Me not in favour of those who have done wrong; verily, they are to be drowned."
interpretation: This verse illustrates God's direct communication with Prophet Noah, instructing him to build the ark under divine supervision and guidance. It emphasizes obedience to God's commands and the importance of following divine instructions precisely. The verse also highlights the inevitability of divine judgment, as it specifies that only those chosen by God will be saved from the impending flood, excluding those who have been condemned. Additionally, it underscores the concept of justice, indicating that intercession for the wrongdoers is not permissible, reinforcing the notion that divine decrees are final and must be accepted.
orig: فأوحينا إليه أن اصنع الفلك بأعيننا ووحينا فإذا جاء أمرنا وفار التنور فاسلك فيها من كل زوجين اثنين وأهلك إلا من سبق عليه القول منهم ولا تخاطبني في الذين ظلموا إنهم مغرقون

translation: So when you have boarded the ship, you and those with you, then say, 'Praise be to Allah, who has saved us from the wrongdoing people.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of expressing gratitude to Allah upon achieving safety or deliverance from a harmful situation. It specifically refers to the moment when Prophet Nuh (Noah) and his followers were safe on the ark, away from the oppressive and disbelieving people.
