interpretation: This verse emphasizes the accountability of individuals for their actions and the consequences of leading others astray. On the Day of Judgment, those who have misled others will not only carry the weight of their own sins but also the sins of those they misguided. This highlights the severe responsibility of influencing others and the importance of ensuring that one's guidance is based on true knowledge, as they will be questioned about the falsehoods they propagated.
orig: وليحملن أثقالهم وأثقالا مع أثقالهم وليسألن يوم القيامة عما كانوا يفترون

translation: And We certainly sent Noah to his people, and he remained among them a thousand years minus fifty years; then the flood seized them while they were wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the patience and perseverance of Prophet Noah in conveying the message of God to his people over a long period, nearly a thousand years. It highlights the theme of divine justice, as despite the prolonged opportunity for repentance, the people's persistent wrongdoing led to their destruction by the flood. This serves as a reminder of the consequences of rejecting God's guidance and the inevitability of divine retribution for persistent injustice and oppression.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا نوحا إلى قومه فلبث فيهم ألف سنة إلا خمسين عاما فأخذهم الطوفان وهم ظالمون

translation: So We saved him and the companions of the ship, and made it a sign for the worlds.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Nuh (Noah) and the Ark. The deliverance of Nuh and those who believed in him aboard the ship is highlighted as a divine miracle, serving as a lesson and a sign for all humanity about the consequences of faith and obedience to God's commands, as well as the outcomes of disbelief and disobedience.
orig: فأنجيناه وأصحاب السفينة وجعلناها آية للعالمين

translation: And [mention] Abraham, when he said to his people, 'Worship Allah and fear Him. That is best for you, if you should know.'
interpretation: In this verse, Abraham is calling his people to the worship of the one true God, Allah, and to be conscious of Him in all their actions. The emphasis on 'if you should know' suggests that the knowledge of this truth is inherent or accessible to them, yet they need to be reminded and encouraged to act upon it. The verse underscores the fundamental Islamic principle that true benefit and goodness in life come from the worship and fear of Allah.
orig: وإبراهيم إذ قال لقومه اعبدوا الله واتقوه ذلكم خير لكم إن كنتم تعلمون

translation: You worship none but idols besides Allah, and you invent falsehood. Indeed, those you worship besides Allah do not possess for you any provision. So seek provision from Allah and worship Him and be grateful to Him. To Him you will return.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility and falsehood of idol worship, highlighting that idols have no power to provide sustenance or any real benefit. It urges believers to turn to Allah alone for their needs, as He is the true provider. The call to worship and thank Allah underscores the importance of gratitude and devotion to the one true God, reminding us that ultimately, we will return to Him. This serves as a reminder of our dependence on Allah and the necessity of aligning our lives with His worship and gratitude.
orig: إنما تعبدون من دون الله أوثانا وتخلقون إفكا إن الذين تعبدون من دون الله لا يملكون لكم رزقا فابتغوا عند الله الرزق واعبدوه واشكروا له إليه ترجعون

translation: And if you deny, then nations before you have denied. And the duty of the Messenger is only to convey the clear message.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability of disbelief among some people, as previous nations also rejected the messages of their prophets. It underscores that the responsibility of the Prophet Muhammad is solely to deliver the message of Islam clearly and effectively, without being accountable for the acceptance or rejection of the message by others. This highlights the concept of free will in choosing to believe or disbelieve, and the Prophet's role as a conveyer of divine guidance rather than a guarantor of its acceptance.
orig: وإن تكذبوا فقد كذب أمم من قبلكم وما على الرسول إلا البلاغ المبين

translation: Have they not seen how Allah originates creation, then repeats it? Indeed, that is easy for Allah.
interpretation: This verse invites reflection on the power and ease with which Allah creates life and then brings it back into existence. It emphasizes the miraculous nature of creation and resurrection, highlighting that such acts are effortless for Allah. This serves to strengthen faith in Allah's omnipotence and the reality of the hereafter.
orig: أولم يروا كيف يبدئ الله الخلق ثم يعيده إن ذلك على الله يسير

translation: Say, 'Travel through the land and observe how He began creation. Then Allah will produce the final creation. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.'
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to explore the world and reflect on the initial stages of creation as evidence of God's power and creativity. It reassures that just as Allah initiated the first creation, He will also bring about the resurrection and the final creation, emphasizing His omnipotence and control over all aspects of existence.
orig: قل سيروا في الأرض فانظروا كيف بدأ الخلق ثم الله ينشئ النشأة الآخرة إن الله على كل شيء قدير

translation: He punishes whom He wills and He grants mercy to whom He wills, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah over all creation. It highlights His authority to dispense both punishment and mercy according to His wisdom and will. The phrase 'and to Him you will be returned' serves as a reminder of the ultimate accountability before Allah, emphasizing that all beings will return to Him for judgment. This reinforces the concept of divine justice and the importance of living a life in accordance with His guidance, knowing that our final destination is back to Allah.
orig: يعذب من يشاء ويرحم من يشاء وإليه تقلبون

translation: And you are not able to escape (from Allah) in the earth nor in the heaven. And besides Allah you have neither any protector nor any helper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipresence and omnipotence of Allah, highlighting that no one can evade His reach or authority, whether on earth or in the heavens. It also underscores the complete dependence of humans on Allah, as there is no other entity that can offer protection or assistance outside of His will. This serves as a reminder of the absolute sovereignty of Allah and the futility of seeking refuge or support from any other source.
orig: وما أنتم بمعجزين في الأرض ولا في السماء وما لكم من دون الله من ولي ولا نصير

translation: And those who disbelieve in the verses of Allah and His meeting, those despair of My mercy, and for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of disbelief in Allah's signs and the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes that rejecting these fundamental aspects of faith leads to despair from Allah's mercy, indicating a complete spiritual loss. The mention of a painful punishment serves as a stern warning about the severe repercussions of such disbelief, underscoring the importance of faith and obedience to Allah's revelations.
orig: والذين كفروا بآيات الله ولقائه أولئك يئسوا من رحمتي وأولئك لهم عذاب أليم

translation: So the only answer of his people was that they said: "Kill him or burn him." But Allah saved him from the fire. Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse highlights the rejection and hostility faced by Prophet Ibrahim from his people when he called them to monotheism. Their extreme reaction to attempt to kill or burn him underscores the severity of their opposition to the truth. However, Allah's intervention to save Ibrahim from the fire demonstrates divine protection and support for His messengers, serving as a powerful sign of God's omnipotence and care for the faithful. This event is a testament to the believers, reinforcing their faith in Allah's ability to protect and deliver justice.
orig: فما كان جواب قومه إلا أن قالوا اقتلوه أو حرقوه فأنجاه الله من النار إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يؤمنون

translation: And he said, "You have taken idols besides Allah out of mutual affection in the life of this world. Then on the Day of Resurrection, some of you will deny others, and some of you will curse others. And your refuge will be the Fire, and you will have no helpers."
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility and falsehood of idolatry. It warns that the bonds formed through idolatry are superficial and will disintegrate on the Day of Judgment. On that day, the mutual affection that led people to idolatry will turn into denial and cursing among themselves, exposing the true nature of their relationships. The verse emphasizes that the ultimate consequence of such actions is damnation in the Fire, with no one to assist or save them, underscoring the importance of worshipping Allah alone.
orig: وقال إنما اتخذتم من دون الله أوثانا مودة بينكم في الحياة الدنيا ثم يوم القيامة يكفر بعضكم ببعض ويلعن بعضكم بعضا ومأواكم النار وما لكم من ناصرين

translation: So Lot believed in him, and he said, 'Indeed, I am emigrating to my Lord. Indeed, He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the faith and determination of Prophet Lot, who chose to leave his homeland due to the corruption and immorality prevalent there. His declaration of migration to his Lord signifies a complete trust in God's power and wisdom, emphasizing that true refuge and guidance come from Allah alone. It serves as an example for believers to seek righteousness and divine support even in the face of adversity.
orig: فآمن له لوط وقال إني مهاجر إلى ربي إنه هو العزيز الحكيم

translation: And We bestowed upon him Isaac and Jacob, and We placed in his progeny prophethood and the Book, and We granted him his reward in this world; and indeed, in the Hereafter he is among the righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights the blessings bestowed upon Abraham, emphasizing the continuity of divine favor through his lineage. The mention of Isaac and Jacob signifies the establishment of a prophetic lineage, while the reference to prophethood and the Book underscores the spiritual and scriptural legacy that would follow. The reward in the worldly life and the promise of being among the righteous in the Hereafter reflect the comprehensive nature of divine recompense, illustrating that Abraham's faithfulness was rewarded both in this life and the next, serving as a model for believers.
orig: ووهبنا له إسحاق ويعقوب وجعلنا في ذريته النبوة والكتاب وآتيناه أجره في الدنيا وإنه في الآخرة لمن الصالحين

translation: And [mention] Lot, when he said to his people, 'Indeed, you commit such immorality as no one has preceded you with from among the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the severity of the sin committed by the people of Lot, indicating that their act of homosexuality was unprecedented among all nations before them, emphasizing the gravity and uniqueness of their moral corruption.
orig: ولوطا إذ قال لقومه إنكم لتأتون الفاحشة ما سبقكم بها من أحد من العالمين

translation: Do you approach men and cut off the road and commit evil in your gatherings?" But the answer of his people was only that they said, "Bring us the punishment of Allah, if you are of the truthful."
interpretation: This verse highlights the moral corruption and defiance of the people of Lot. They were engaging in homosexual acts, highway robbery, and openly committing sins in their assemblies, showing a complete disregard for divine law. When confronted by Lot, instead of repenting, they challenged him to bring upon them the punishment of Allah, indicating their disbelief and arrogance. This response underscores their rejection of the prophet's warning and their demand for a sign, which reflects a deeper spiritual ailment and denial of truth.
orig: أئنكم لتأتون الرجال وتقطعون السبيل وتأتون في ناديكم المنكر فما كان جواب قومه إلا أن قالوا ائتنا بعذاب الله إن كنت من الصادقين

translation: He said, "My Lord, support me against the corrupting people."
interpretation: This verse reflects a plea for divine assistance against those who cause corruption and disorder. It underscores the reliance on God's help in confronting and overcoming evil and injustice, highlighting the importance of seeking divine support in struggles against moral and societal decay.
orig: قال رب انصرني على القوم المفسدين

translation: And when Our messengers came to Abraham with the good news, they said, 'We are going to destroy the people of this town; indeed, its people have been wrongdoers.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine justice and the consequences of persistent wrongdoing. The messengers' announcement to Abraham about the impending destruction of the town underscores that God's patience has limits, and when a community continuously engages in oppression and injustice, divine retribution becomes inevitable. It serves as a reminder of the importance of righteousness and the potential outcomes of moral decay within a society.
orig: ولما جاءت رسلنا إبراهيم بالبشرى قالوا إنا مهلكو أهل هذه القرية إن أهلها كانوا ظالمين

translation: He said, 'Indeed, within it is Lot.' They said, 'We know better who is within it. We will surely save him and his family, except his wife; she is to be of those who remain behind.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine knowledge and plan of Allah. When the angels inform Abraham about their mission to destroy the people of Lot due to their corruption, Abraham expresses concern for Lot, who resides among them. The angels reassure Abraham that they are fully aware of who is in the city and that they will save Lot and his family, with the exception of his wife, who will be left behind because of her complicity with the corrupt. This demonstrates that Allah's knowledge encompasses all details and His justice ensures that the righteous are saved while the corrupt face the consequences of their actions.
orig: قال إن فيها لوطا قالوا نحن أعلم بمن فيها لننجينه وأهله إلا امرأته كانت من الغابرين

translation: And when Our messengers came to Lut, he was distressed for them and felt straitened on their account. They said: "Fear not, nor grieve! We are going to save you and your family, except your wife; she is of those who lag behind."
interpretation: This verse highlights the emotional turmoil of Prophet Lut when he received the angels who appeared to him as guests. His distress stemmed from his fear for their safety in a society known for its immorality. The reassurance from the angels signifies divine protection and intervention, emphasizing that despite the surrounding corruption, Lut and his family (except his wife, who was influenced by the corrupt society) would be saved. This underscores the theme of divine justice and the protection of the righteous amidst widespread evil.
orig: ولما أن جاءت رسلنا لوطا سيء بهم وضاق بهم ذرعا وقالوا لا تخف ولا تحزن إنا منجوك وأهلك إلا امرأتك كانت من الغابرين

translation: Indeed, We will send down upon the people of this town a punishment from the sky because of their rebellious deeds.
interpretation: This verse signifies a divine warning and the consequence of persistent disobedience and moral corruption. It underscores the concept of divine retribution where communities that engage in sinful and rebellious behavior against God's commands may face severe punishment. The mention of the punishment coming from the sky emphasizes the overwhelming and inescapable nature of divine justice, serving as a reminder of the importance of adhering to righteousness and the potential consequences of collective societal sin.
orig: إنا منزلون على أهل هذه القرية رجزا من السماء بما كانوا يفسقون

translation: And indeed We have left thereof a clear sign for a people who use reason.
interpretation: This verse suggests that God has provided clear evidence and signs within the remnants or stories of past nations, which serve as lessons and warnings for those who are capable of understanding and reflecting upon them. It emphasizes the importance of using intellect and reason to comprehend the divine messages and historical examples provided in the Qur'an.
orig: ولقد تركنا منها آية بينة لقوم يعقلون

translation: And to Madyan [We sent] their brother Shu'ayb. He said, 'O my people, worship Allah and expect the Last Day and do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the mission of Prophet Shu'ayb, sent to the people of Madyan, emphasizing monotheism and the anticipation of the Hereafter. It also underscores the ethical responsibility to avoid corruption and maintain justice on earth, reflecting a core Islamic principle of balancing spiritual devotion with moral conduct in societal interactions.
orig: وإلى مدين أخاهم شعيبا فقال يا قوم اعبدوا الله وارجوا اليوم الآخر ولا تعثوا في الأرض مفسدين

translation: So they rejected him, and the earthquake seized them, and they became in their homes, lying prone.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the consequence of rejecting the truth and the divine message brought by the prophets. The people's denial of the prophet's warning led to their immediate punishment through a catastrophic earthquake, symbolizing the swift and inevitable retribution from Allah for disbelief and disobedience. The imagery of them lying prone in their homes emphasizes the total and humiliating defeat of those who oppose God's will.
orig: فكذبوه فأخذتهم الرجفة فأصبحوا في دارهم جاثمين

translation: And [the tribes of] 'Aad and Thamud - and it has become clear to you from their [ruined] dwellings. And Satan had made their deeds pleasing to them and averted them from the path, and they were endowed with perception.
interpretation: This verse reflects on the historical examples of the tribes of 'Aad and Thamud, whose fates serve as a warning. Their ruined dwellings are a testament to the consequences of straying from the right path. The verse highlights how Satan can deceive individuals by making sinful actions appear attractive, leading them away from righteousness despite their ability to discern right from wrong. It underscores the importance of vigilance against such deceptions and the need to adhere to divine guidance to avoid a similar fate.
orig: وعادا وثمود وقد تبين لكم من مساكنهم وزين لهم الشيطان أعمالهم فصدهم عن السبيل وكانوا مستبصرين

translation: And [mention] Korah and Pharaoh and Haman: indeed, Moses came to them with clear evidences, but they were arrogant upon the earth, and they were not outrunners [of Our punishment].
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of arrogance and rejection of divine guidance. Korah, Pharaoh, and Haman, despite receiving clear signs and proofs from Moses, chose to remain haughty and did not heed the warnings. Their refusal to accept the truth and their persistent arrogance ultimately led to their downfall, illustrating that no one can escape God's justice. The verse emphasizes the importance of humility and submission to God's messengers and the inevitability of divine retribution for those who persist in their pride and disbelief.
orig: وقارون وفرعون وهامان ولقد جاءهم موسى بالبينات فاستكبروا في الأرض وما كانوا سابقين

translation: So We seized each one for his sin; of them were some on whom We sent a storm of stones; some of them were overtaken by the Blast; some of them We caused the earth to swallow; and some of them We drowned. And Allah would not wrong them, but they wronged themselves.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the concept of divine justice and accountability. It emphasizes that each of the nations mentioned was punished specifically for their own sins, highlighting that the consequences they faced were a direct result of their actions. The variety of punishments mentioned - stones, the Blast, being swallowed by the earth, and drowning - underscores the power and diverse methods of Allah's retribution. The verse also clarifies that Allah's actions are just and fair, and it is the people who wronged themselves through their disobedience and sinfulness, thus bearing full responsibility for their fate.
orig: فكلا أخذنا بذنبه فمنهم من أرسلنا عليه حاصبا ومنهم من أخذته الصيحة ومنهم من خسفنا به الأرض ومنهم من أغرقنا وما كان الله ليظلمهم ولكن كانوا أنفسهم يظلمون

translation: The example of those who take allies other than Allah is like the example of the spider who takes a house. And indeed, the weakest of houses is the house of the spider, if they only knew.
interpretation: This verse uses the metaphor of a spider's web to illustrate the fragility and instability of relying on anything other than Allah for support and guidance. Just as a spider's web is delicate and easily destroyed, so too are the false securities and alliances that people create when they turn away from Allah. The verse emphasizes the importance of recognizing the ultimate strength and reliability of Allah alone, urging believers to place their trust and faith in Him rather than in fleeting worldly attachments.
orig: مثل الذين اتخذوا من دون الله أولياء كمثل العنكبوت اتخذت بيتا وإن أوهن البيوت لبيت العنكبوت لو كانوا يعلمون

translation: Indeed, Allah knows what they invoke besides Him of anything, and He is the Almighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's complete knowledge and awareness of the false deities and idols that people worship instead of Him. It serves as a reminder of His supreme power and wisdom, indicating that despite people's actions, Allah's sovereignty and insight remain unchallenged. The attributes of 'Almighty' and 'All-Wise' highlight His ability to judge and govern the universe with perfect justice and wisdom.
orig: إن الله يعلم ما يدعون من دونه من شيء وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: And these examples We present to the people, but none will understand them except those of knowledge.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of knowledge and understanding in grasping the deeper meanings of the Qur'anic parables and teachings. It suggests that while the verses are available to all, only those who possess true knowledge and insight can fully comprehend and appreciate their significance. This underscores the value of seeking knowledge and the role of scholars in guiding the community towards a deeper understanding of divine messages.
orig: وتلك الأمثال نضربها للناس وما يعقلها إلا العالمون

translation: Allah created the heavens and the earth in truth. Indeed, in that is a sign for the believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the purposeful creation of the universe by Allah, indicating that everything in existence has been created with a specific reason and wisdom. It serves as a reminder and a sign for believers to reflect on the order and precision in creation, reinforcing their faith in the divine plan and encouraging them to trust in Allah's wisdom and justice.
orig: خلق الله السماوات والأرض بالحق إن في ذلك لآية للمؤمنين

translation: Recite what has been revealed to you of the Book and establish prayer. Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing, and the remembrance of Allah is greater. And Allah knows what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of reciting the Qur'an as it has been revealed and performing the prayers regularly. The act of prayer is highlighted as a means to prevent one from engaging in sinful and evil acts. The verse suggests that while prayer is crucial, the remembrance of Allah holds even greater significance, indicating that constant awareness and mindfulness of Allah should permeate all aspects of a believer's life. The concluding statement that Allah knows all actions serves as a reminder of divine omniscience, encouraging believers to be conscious of their deeds, knowing they are always under Allah's watchful eye.
orig: اتل ما أوحي إليك من الكتاب وأقم الصلاة إن الصلاة تنهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر ولذكر الله أكبر والله يعلم ما تصنعون

translation: And do not argue with the People of the Scripture except in a way that is best, except for those who commit injustice among them, and say, 'We believe in that which has been revealed to us and revealed to you. Our God and your God is one, and we are Muslims [in submission] to Him.'
interpretation: This verse instructs Muslims to engage with Jews and Christians, referred to as the People of the Scripture, in a manner that is respectful and constructive, promoting understanding and dialogue. The exception is made for those among them who act unjustly, where a different approach might be necessary. The verse emphasizes the shared belief in the oneness of God and encourages Muslims to affirm their faith in the revelations given to both communities, thereby fostering a sense of unity and submission to the same God.
orig: ولا تجادلوا أهل الكتاب إلا بالتي هي أحسن إلا الذين ظلموا منهم وقولوا آمنا بالذي أنزل إلينا وأنزل إليكم وإلهنا وإلهكم واحد ونحن له مسلمون

translation: And thus We have revealed to you the Book. So those to whom We have given the Book believe in it. And among these are those who believe in it. And none reject Our verses except the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin of the Qur'an, revealed to Prophet Muhammad, and highlights the acceptance of this revelation by those who were previously given scriptures, such as Jews and Christians, indicating a continuity and confirmation of earlier messages. It also underscores that disbelief in the Qur'anic verses is a characteristic of those who reject faith, suggesting that rejection stems from a refusal to accept the truth rather than from any deficiency in the message itself.
orig: وكذلك أنزلنا إليك الكتاب فالذين آتيناهم الكتاب يؤمنون به ومن هؤلاء من يؤمن به وما يجحد بآياتنا إلا الكافرون

translation: And you were not reciting any book before it, nor did you write it with your right hand; otherwise, the falsifiers would have had doubts.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophet Muhammad's illiteracy and lack of prior scriptural knowledge, underscoring the miraculous nature of the Qur'an. It suggests that if Muhammad had been known to read or write, skeptics might have doubted the divine origin of the Qur'an, claiming he could have authored it himself. By highlighting his inability to read or write, the verse reinforces the belief that the Qur'an is a divine revelation, not a human composition.
orig: وما كنت تتلو من قبله من كتاب ولا تخطه بيمينك إذا لارتاب المبطلون

translation: Nay, but it is clear verses in the hearts of those who have been given knowledge. And none reject Our verses except the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an contains clear and evident signs that are deeply understood and appreciated by those endowed with knowledge. It suggests that true understanding and acceptance of the Qur'anic message is a characteristic of the learned and wise. Conversely, it points out that only those who are unjust and oppressive would deny these clear signs, indicating a moral failing rather than an intellectual one.
orig: بل هو آيات بينات في صدور الذين أوتوا العلم وما يجحد بآياتنا إلا الظالمون

translation: And they said, 'Why has he not been sent down with signs from his Lord?' Say, 'The signs are only with Allah, and I am only a clear warner.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the skepticism of those who demanded miraculous signs from the Prophet Muhammad as proof of his prophethood. It emphasizes that the ultimate authority and control over signs and miracles belong to Allah alone. The Prophet's role is clearly defined as a warner, whose duty is to convey the message of God clearly and truthfully, rather than to perform miracles on demand. This underscores the importance of faith based on the message itself, rather than on the expectation of supernatural displays.
orig: وقالوا لولا أنزل عليه آيات من ربه قل إنما الآيات عند الله وإنما أنا نذير مبين

translation: Is it not enough for them that We have sent down to you the Book which is recited to them? Indeed, in that is a mercy and a reminder for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sufficiency and the divine origin of the Qur'an as a source of guidance. It suggests that the mere revelation of the Qur'an to the Prophet Muhammad, and its recitation among the people, should be a compelling proof of its truth and a source of mercy and reminder for those who have faith. The verse challenges the disbelievers by questioning why they do not accept the Qur'an as a clear sign from God, indicating that belief in the Qur'an is integral to faith.
orig: أولم يكفهم أنا أنزلنا عليك الكتاب يتلى عليهم إن في ذلك لرحمة وذكرى لقوم يؤمنون

translation: Say, 'Sufficient is Allah as a witness between me and you. He knows what is in the heavens and the earth. And those who believe in falsehood and disbelieve in Allah, it is they who are the losers.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sufficiency of Allah as the ultimate witness and knower of all things, reinforcing the concept of Tawhid (the oneness of God). It serves as a reminder to the Prophet Muhammad and believers that Allah is fully aware of the truth and falsehood, and those who reject the truth of Allah in favor of falsehood are ultimately the ones who will suffer loss in the hereafter. The verse underscores the importance of faith in Allah and the consequences of disbelief.
orig: قل كفى بالله بيني وبينكم شهيدا يعلم ما في السماوات والأرض والذين آمنوا بالباطل وكفروا بالله أولئك هم الخاسرون

translation: And they urge you to hasten the punishment. And if it were not for a specified term, the punishment would have come upon them. And it will surely come upon them suddenly while they do not perceive.
interpretation: This verse highlights the impatience of the disbelievers who challenge the Prophet Muhammad to bring the punishment they are warned about, doubting its reality. It underscores the divine wisdom in delaying the punishment, indicating that there is a predetermined time set by Allah for its occurrence. The suddenness of the punishment, when it does come, serves as a reminder of the unexpected nature of divine retribution, emphasizing the need for constant vigilance and faith in the unseen.
orig: ويستعجلونك بالعذاب ولولا أجل مسمى لجاءهم العذاب وليأتينهم بغتة وهم لا يشعرون

translation: They ask you to hasten the punishment, and indeed, Hell will encompass the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse addresses the impatience of the disbelievers who mockingly ask the Prophet Muhammad to bring the punishment they are warned about. It serves as a reminder that divine retribution is certain and inescapable for those who reject faith. Hell is described as surrounding the disbelievers, indicating that no matter how they try to avoid or deny it, they will ultimately be enveloped by its consequences.
orig: يستعجلونك بالعذاب وإن جهنم لمحيطة بالكافرين

translation: The Day when the punishment will cover them from above them and from beneath their feet, and it will be said, 'Taste what you used to do.'
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Judgment, emphasizing the inescapable nature of divine punishment. The punishment enveloping from above and below signifies its all-encompassing and overwhelming presence, leaving no escape. The command to 'taste what you used to do' underscores the direct consequence of one's actions, highlighting the principle of accountability and the justice of divine retribution.
orig: يوم يغشاهم العذاب من فوقهم ومن تحت أرجلهم ويقول ذوقوا ما كنتم تعملون

translation: O My servants who have believed, indeed My earth is spacious, so worship Me alone.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of Tawheed (the oneness of God) and encourages believers to worship Allah alone, no matter where they are. It reassures them that Allah's earth is vast and there is always a place where they can practice their faith freely. This is particularly comforting for those who may face persecution or difficulty in their current location, reminding them that they can seek out other places where they can worship Allah without hindrance.
orig: يا عبادي الذين آمنوا إن أرضي واسعة فإياي فاعبدون

translation: Every soul shall taste death, then to Us you shall be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability of death for all beings, underscoring that it is a universal experience that no one can escape. It also highlights the concept of accountability after death, as all souls will return to Allah for judgment, reinforcing the belief in the afterlife and the continuity of existence beyond physical death.
orig: كل نفس ذائقة الموت ثم إلينا ترجعون

translation: And those who believed and did righteous deeds, We will surely settle them in chambers of Paradise, beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. Excellent is the reward of the workers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the promise of God to those who have faith and perform good deeds. It highlights the ultimate reward of dwelling in Paradise, described as having luxurious chambers with rivers flowing beneath, symbolizing the abundance and eternal nature of the blessings. The phrase 'Excellent is the reward of the workers' underscores the value and merit of one's efforts in this life, affirming that such endeavors are recognized and generously compensated in the hereafter.
orig: والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لنبوئنهم من الجنة غرفا تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها نعم أجر العاملين

translation: Those who are patient and put their trust in their Lord.
interpretation: This verse highlights the virtues of patience and trust in God. It emphasizes that true believers exhibit steadfastness in the face of trials and challenges, and they rely completely on Allah's wisdom and timing. This reliance on God fosters a deep sense of peace and resilience, enabling them to navigate life's difficulties with grace and faith.
orig: الذين صبروا وعلى ربهم يتوكلون

translation: And how many a creature that does not carry its own provision, yet Allah provides for it and for you. And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's role as the ultimate provider for all creatures, including those that cannot fend for themselves. It serves as a reminder of His omnipotence and benevolence, encouraging believers to trust in His provision and to recognize that just as He sustains other creatures, He will also sustain them. The attributes of Allah being All-Hearing and All-Knowing further reinforce the idea that He is fully aware of the needs of all His creation and is responsive to them.
orig: وكأين من دابة لا تحمل رزقها الله يرزقها وإياكم وهو السميع العليم

translation: And if you ask them who created the heavens and the earth and subjected the sun and the moon, they will surely say, 'Allah.' So how are they deluded?
interpretation: This verse highlights the inherent knowledge of the truth within people, as they acknowledge Allah as the Creator of the universe and the controller of celestial bodies. However, it also points out the contradiction in their belief, as despite this acknowledgment, they are still led astray by false beliefs and practices. The verse questions how they can be so misguided when they clearly recognize the truth.
orig: ولئن سألتهم من خلق السماوات والأرض وسخر الشمس والقمر ليقولن الله فأنى يؤفكون

translation: Allah extends provision for whom He wills of His servants and restricts it for him. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's sovereignty over the distribution of sustenance. It teaches that the provision given to each individual is a direct result of Allah's will, emphasizing that He may increase or decrease it according to His wisdom. The phrase "Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things" reassures believers that Allah's decisions are based on His complete knowledge, encouraging trust in His divine plan and acceptance of whatever provision one receives.
orig: الله يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء من عباده ويقدر له إن الله بكل شيء عليم

translation: And if you ask them, 'Who sends down rain from the sky and with it revives the earth after its death?' they will surely say, 'Allah.' Say, 'Praise be to Allah.' But most of them do not understand.
interpretation: This verse highlights the recognition of Allah's power and mercy in nature, specifically through the cycle of rain and the revival of the earth. It points out that while people may acknowledge Allah as the creator and sustainer when directly questioned, many fail to truly comprehend or internalize this knowledge in their daily lives and spiritual understanding. The phrase 'Praise be to Allah' serves as a reminder to the believers to constantly acknowledge and be grateful for Allah's signs and blessings, even if others do not fully grasp their significance.
orig: ولئن سألتهم من نزل من السماء ماء فأحيا به الأرض من بعد موتها ليقولن الله قل الحمد لله بل أكثرهم لا يعقلون

translation: And what is the life of this world except amusement and play? And indeed, the home of the Hereafter is the true life, if only they knew.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fleeting and superficial nature of worldly life, likening it to mere amusement and play. It contrasts this with the eternal and meaningful reality of the Hereafter, which is described as the true life. The verse suggests that if people truly understood this distinction, they would prioritize their actions and focus more on preparing for the everlasting life rather than being engrossed in the temporary pleasures of this world.
orig: وما هذه الحياة الدنيا إلا لهو ولعب وإن الدار الآخرة لهي الحيوان لو كانوا يعلمون

translation: And when they embark on a ship, they call upon Allah, being sincerely devoted to Him in religion. But when He delivers them safely to the land, behold, they associate others with Him.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to turn to God in times of distress and need, such as during a perilous journey at sea, and to promise sincere devotion to Him. However, once the danger has passed and they are safe on land, they revert to their old ways of associating partners with Allah, indicating a lack of true faith and gratitude. It serves as a reminder of the importance of maintaining steadfastness in faith and not forgetting God's mercy and help in times of ease.
orig: فإذا ركبوا في الفلك دعوا الله مخلصين له الدين فلما نجاهم إلى البر إذا هم يشركون

translation: So that they may deny what We have given them, and that they may enjoy themselves; but soon they will know.
interpretation: This verse suggests that some people will reject the blessings and guidance provided by Allah, choosing instead to indulge in worldly pleasures. However, it warns that their eventual realization of the consequences of their actions will come, indicating a future reckoning or divine justice.
orig: ليكفروا بما آتيناهم وليتمتعوا فسوف يعلمون

translation: Do they not see that We have made Mecca a safe sanctuary, while people are being snatched away from all around them? Then do they believe in falsehood and deny the favor of Allah?
interpretation: This verse highlights the ingratitude and disbelief of the Quraysh, who, despite living in the secure sanctuary of Mecca—a blessing from Allah—still reject the truth and cling to false beliefs. It serves as a reminder of the consequences of denying Allah's favors and the importance of recognizing and appreciating the blessings bestowed upon us.
orig: أولم يروا أنا جعلنا حرما آمنا ويتخطف الناس من حولهم أفبالباطل يؤمنون وبنعمة الله يكفرون

translation: And who is more unjust than he who invents a lie about Allah or denies the truth when it has come to him? Is there not in Hell a residence for the disbelievers?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity of two major sins: fabricating lies about Allah and rejecting the truth after it has been clearly presented. It underscores that such actions stem from a deep level of injustice and disbelief, warranting the severe punishment of Hell as the ultimate abode for those who persist in such disbelief. The rhetorical question at the end serves to affirm the inevitability and appropriateness of this punishment, highlighting the moral and spiritual consequences of denying divine truth.
orig: ومن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا أو كذب بالحق لما جاءه أليس في جهنم مثوى للكافرين

translation: And those who strive in Our (cause), We will certainly guide them to Our paths. And indeed, Allah is with those who do good.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of striving or exerting effort in the path of Allah. It promises divine guidance to those who sincerely struggle and work hard in their faith and actions for the sake of Allah. The guidance mentioned here is not just spiritual but also practical, leading individuals towards righteousness and success in their endeavors. The assurance that "Allah is with those who do good" provides comfort and motivation, indicating that divine support and companionship are with those who consistently perform good deeds and maintain virtuous conduct.
orig: والذين جاهدوا فينا لنهدينهم سبلنا وإن الله لمع المحسنين

translation: Alif, Lam, Meem
interpretation: These are among the disjointed letters (muqatta'at) at the beginning of some Qur'anic chapters. Their precise meaning is known only to Allah, but they are believed to signify the miraculous nature of the Qur'an and its divine origin, serving as a challenge to those who doubt its authenticity.
orig: الم

translation: The Romans have been defeated
interpretation: This verse refers to a historical event where the Byzantine Empire, known as the Romans in the Qur'an, suffered a defeat. The mention of this event serves to illustrate the transient nature of worldly power and to provide a context for the subsequent verses which predict the Romans' victory, showcasing God's knowledge of future events and His control over the affairs of nations.
orig: غلبت الروم

translation: In the lowest part of the earth, and they, after their defeat, will be victorious.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the resilience and ultimate triumph of the believers. Despite being in a position of apparent weakness and defeat, as symbolized by being in the lowest part of the earth, the believers are promised victory. This reflects the Qur'anic theme of patience and trust in God's plan, assuring the faithful that perseverance in the face of adversity will lead to success and dominance over their adversaries.
orig: في أدنى الأرض وهم من بعد غلبهم سيغلبون

translation: In a few years, the matter is for Allah, before and after, and on that day the believers will rejoice.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sovereignty of Allah over all affairs, indicating that within a short period, divine decree will manifest clearly. The phrase 'before and after' underscores that Allah's control is timeless, encompassing all moments. The mention of the believers' rejoicing suggests that this manifestation of Allah's decree will be a source of joy and relief for the faithful, likely referring to a significant event or victory that aligns with their faith and patience.
orig: في بضع سنين لله الأمر من قبل ومن بعد ويومئذ يفرح المؤمنون

translation: With the help of Allah, He helps whom He wills, and He is the Almighty, the Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that divine assistance and victory come from Allah alone, and He bestows this help upon whomever He chooses according to His wisdom. It underscores the attributes of Allah as being both powerful (Almighty) and compassionate (Most Merciful), indicating that His decisions are rooted in both strength and mercy.
orig: بنصر الله ينصر من يشاء وهو العزيز الرحيم

translation: The promise of Allah - never does Allah fail in His promise, but most people do not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty and reliability of Allah's promises. It reassures believers that whatever Allah has promised will undoubtedly come to pass, highlighting His unwavering commitment to His word. The latter part of the verse points out a common human failing: many people are unaware of this divine attribute due to their lack of knowledge or faith, which underscores the importance of understanding and trusting in Allah's promises.
orig: وعد الله لا يخلف الله وعده ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: They know what is apparent of the worldly life, but they, of the Hereafter, are unaware.
interpretation: This verse highlights the preoccupation of some individuals with the superficial aspects of worldly life, leading them to neglect the deeper realities and preparations necessary for the Hereafter. It serves as a reminder to balance worldly pursuits with spiritual awareness and readiness for the life to come.
orig: يعلمون ظاهرا من الحياة الدنيا وهم عن الآخرة هم غافلون

translation: Do they not reflect upon themselves? Allah created the heavens and the earth and everything between them in truth and for a specified term. Yet many people, in the meeting with their Lord, are disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse urges individuals to engage in introspection and consider the purpose and truth behind the creation of the universe by Allah. It emphasizes that the creation is not random but has a purpose and a defined duration. The verse also highlights the disbelief of many people in the reality of meeting their Lord, suggesting a call to faith and awareness of the afterlife.
orig: أولم يتفكروا في أنفسهم ما خلق الله السماوات والأرض وما بينهما إلا بالحق وأجل مسمى وإن كثيرا من الناس بلقاء ربهم لكافرون

translation: Have they not traveled through the land and observed how was the end of those before them? They were greater than them in power, and they plowed the earth and developed it more than they have developed it, and their messengers came to them with clear evidences. And Allah would not have wronged them, but they were wronging themselves.
interpretation: This verse encourages reflection on the historical consequences faced by past nations who were more powerful and had developed their lands extensively. Despite receiving clear messages from their prophets, these nations perished due to their own injustices and moral failings, not because of any injustice from Allah. It serves as a reminder that the downfall of civilizations is often self-inflicted, urging current societies to heed divine guidance and act justly to avoid a similar fate.
orig: أولم يسيروا في الأرض فينظروا كيف كان عاقبة الذين من قبلهم كانوا أشد منهم قوة وأثاروا الأرض وعمروها أكثر مما عمروها وجاءتهم رسلهم بالبينات فما كان الله ليظلمهم ولكن كانوا أنفسهم يظلمون

translation: Then the outcome for those who did evil was the worst [consequence] because they denied the signs of Allah and they used to ridicule them.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate consequence faced by those who engage in wrongdoing, specifically those who reject the divine revelations and mock them. It emphasizes that disbelief and mockery of Allah's signs lead to a severe and negative outcome in the hereafter, underscoring the importance of faith and reverence towards divine guidance.
orig: ثم كان عاقبة الذين أساءوا السوأى أن كذبوا بآيات الله وكانوا بها يستهزئون

translation: Allah begins the creation, then He repeats it, then to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and sovereignty of Allah over creation. It highlights the cycle of life and resurrection, indicating that Allah not only initiates the creation of all beings but also has the ability to bring them back to life after death. The final return to Allah underscores the accountability of all creation to Him, reinforcing the belief in the Day of Judgment where all will return to their Creator for reckoning.
orig: الله يبدأ الخلق ثم يعيده ثم إليه ترجعون

translation: And the Day the Hour appears, the criminals will despair.
interpretation: This verse highlights the moment of the Day of Judgment when the reality of the Hour becomes manifest. The term 'yablis' indicates a state of utter despair and hopelessness that will overcome the criminals, those who have committed sins and rejected faith. It underscores the finality and inevitability of divine judgment, where the consequences of one's actions become inescapable, leading to a profound realization of their doomed fate.
orig: ويوم تقوم الساعة يبلس المجرمون

translation: And they will have no intercessors from among their partners, and they will be disbelievers in their partners.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of polytheism on the Day of Judgment. It underscores that the false deities or partners that people associated with Allah will not be able to intercede on their behalf. Moreover, those who worshipped these partners will ultimately disbelieve in them when they see the truth, realizing that their faith in these entities was baseless. This serves as a warning against idolatry and a reminder of the exclusive oneness of Allah.
orig: ولم يكن لهم من شركائهم شفعاء وكانوا بشركائهم كافرين

translation: And the Day the Hour appears - that Day they will become separated.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, people will be divided into different groups based on their deeds and faith. This verse emphasizes the inevitability of accountability and the separation that will occur, highlighting the importance of one's actions in this life determining their position in the hereafter.
orig: ويوم تقوم الساعة يومئذ يتفرقون

translation: As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, they will be in a Garden, rejoicing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate reward for believers who perform good deeds. It emphasizes that faith must be accompanied by righteous actions to attain Paradise. The term 'Garden' symbolizes a place of eternal bliss and joy, where the faithful will experience continuous happiness and contentment as a result of their devotion and good conduct in the worldly life.
orig: فأما الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات فهم في روضة يحبرون

translation: As for those who disbelieved and denied Our signs and the meeting of the Hereafter, they will be brought to the punishment.
interpretation: This verse underscores the consequences of disbelief and rejection of divine signs and the reality of the afterlife. It serves as a warning that those who consciously choose to deny the existence of God and the Hereafter will face punishment in the hereafter. The term 'brought to the punishment' suggests an inevitable and direct confrontation with the consequences of their disbelief, emphasizing the certainty and severity of the divine judgment.
orig: وأما الذين كفروا وكذبوا بآياتنا ولقاء الآخرة فأولئك في العذاب محضرون

translation: So glorify Allah when you reach the evening and when you reach the morning.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of remembering and glorifying Allah consistently throughout the day, specifically at the times of evening and morning. It serves as a reminder for believers to maintain a continuous connection with Allah, acknowledging His greatness and expressing gratitude at the start and end of each day.
orig: فسبحان الله حين تمسون وحين تصبحون

translation: And to Him belongs all praise in the heavens and the earth, and [in the] evening and when you are at noon.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipresence and omnipotence of Allah, indicating that praise and gratitude are due to Him at all times and in all places, whether in the heavens, on earth, during the evening, or at noon. It underscores the continuous nature of worship and the recognition of Allah's sovereignty throughout the day and across the universe.
orig: وله الحمد في السماوات والأرض وعشيا وحين تظهرون

translation: He brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living, and He revives the earth after its death. And thus you will be brought forth.
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's power over life and death, emphasizing His ability to create and recreate life in various forms. The cycle of life and death is used as a metaphor for the resurrection, where Allah will bring forth humans from their graves just as He brings life to the earth after it appears dead. This serves as a reminder of the inevitable resurrection and the power of Allah to transform and renew, instilling hope and faith in the believers about their own revival on the Day of Judgment.
orig: يخرج الحي من الميت ويخرج الميت من الحي ويحيي الأرض بعد موتها وكذلك تخرجون

translation: And among His signs is that He created you from dust; then, behold, you are human beings dispersing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the miraculous nature of human creation as one of the signs of Allah's power and wisdom. It emphasizes the humble origin of humans from dust, illustrating the contrast between our initial state and our current existence as diverse and widespread beings. This serves as a reminder of our dependence on Allah and His ability to transform and spread life from the most basic elements.
orig: ومن آياته أن خلقكم من تراب ثم إذا أنتم بشر تنتشرون

translation: And of His signs is that He created for you from yourselves mates that you may find tranquility in them; and He placed between you affection and mercy. Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom in the creation of spouses from among humans, emphasizing that marriage is not just a social contract but a sign of Allah's mercy and care. The tranquility, affection, and mercy found in marital relationships are presented as clear signs of God's existence and benevolence, encouraging believers to reflect deeply on these blessings and recognize the purposeful design behind human relationships.
orig: ومن آياته أن خلق لكم من أنفسكم أزواجا لتسكنوا إليها وجعل بينكم مودة ورحمة إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يتفكرون

translation: And of His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth and the diversity of your languages and your colors. Indeed in that are signs for those who know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the diversity in creation as a sign of God's power and wisdom. The mention of the heavens and the earth, along with the variety in human languages and colors, serves as evidence of divine creativity and the purposeful design of the universe. It encourages believers to reflect on these aspects of creation to deepen their understanding and appreciation of God's majesty.
orig: ومن آياته خلق السماوات والأرض واختلاف ألسنتكم وألوانكم إن في ذلك لآيات للعالمين

translation: And among His signs is your sleep by night and by day and your seeking of His bounty. Indeed in that are signs for a people who listen.
interpretation: This verse highlights the miraculous nature of sleep, which rejuvenates us, and our pursuit of sustenance and blessings from Allah, as signs of His mercy and power. It emphasizes that these everyday phenomena are profound indicators of divine wisdom and care, urging those who are attentive and reflective to recognize and appreciate Allah's presence and generosity in their lives.
orig: ومن آياته منامكم بالليل والنهار وابتغاؤكم من فضله إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يسمعون

translation: And among His signs is that He shows you lightning, causing fear and hope, and He sends down water from the sky, reviving the earth with it after its death. Indeed, in that are signs for a people who understand.
interpretation: This verse highlights the dual nature of natural phenomena as both a source of fear and hope, exemplified by lightning, which can be terrifying yet signals the coming of rain. The rain itself is a profound sign of God's power and mercy, as it brings life to the dead earth, symbolizing resurrection and renewal. This cycle of nature is presented as a clear sign for those who reflect and understand, encouraging believers to recognize God's omnipotence and the lessons embedded in His creation.
orig: ومن آياته يريكم البرق خوفا وطمعا وينزل من السماء ماء فيحيي به الأرض بعد موتها إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يعقلون

translation: And among His signs is that the heaven and the earth stand firm by His command. Then when He calls you with a call from the earth, behold, you will come forth.
interpretation: This verse highlights the omnipotence and authority of Allah, illustrating His control over the universe. The stability of the heavens and the earth is maintained solely by His command, showcasing His power and the precision of His creation. The latter part of the verse refers to the resurrection, where Allah will call forth all beings from the earth on the Day of Judgment. This serves as a reminder of the inevitability of the afterlife and the accountability of all souls before Allah, emphasizing the transient nature of worldly life and the eternal reality of the hereafter.
orig: ومن آياته أن تقوم السماء والأرض بأمره ثم إذا دعاكم دعوة من الأرض إذا أنتم تخرجون

translation: And to Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth. All are devoutly obedient to Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty of Allah over all creation. It highlights that every being in the heavens and the earth is under His control and willingly submits to His will, underscoring the unity and obedience of all creation to the divine command.
orig: وله من في السماوات والأرض كل له قانتون

translation: And He it is who begins creation; then He repeats it, and that is easier for Him. And to Him belongs the highest attribute in the heavens and earth. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's supreme power and wisdom in the cycle of creation and resurrection. The ease with which Allah initiates life and then brings it back underscores His omnipotence. The reference to the highest attribute signifies that all perfection and excellence in the universe are attributed to Him alone. The titles 'Exalted in Might' and 'Wise' further affirm His unmatched strength and profound wisdom in managing the affairs of the universe.
orig: وهو الذي يبدأ الخلق ثم يعيده وهو أهون عليه وله المثل الأعلى في السماوات والأرض وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: An example has been set forth for you from yourselves: Do you have among those whom your right hands possess any partners in what We have provided for you, so that you are equal therein, fearing them as you fear yourselves? Thus We explain the signs for a people who understand.
interpretation: This verse uses the analogy of slaves or servants to illustrate the absurdity of associating partners with Allah. Just as it would be illogical for a person to share their wealth equally with their slaves and fear them as they fear themselves, it is equally illogical to attribute divine powers to anyone or anything other than Allah. The verse emphasizes the clarity and rationality of the Qur'anic message, intended for those who are willing to use their intellect to understand and reflect upon it.
orig: ضرب لكم مثلا من أنفسكم هل لكم من ما ملكت أيمانكم من شركاء في ما رزقناكم فأنتم فيه سواء تخافونهم كخيفتكم أنفسكم كذلك نفصل الآيات لقوم يعقلون

translation: Nay, but they follow the desires of those who have wronged, without knowledge. So who can guide those whom Allah has sent astray? And for them there are no helpers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequences of following the whims and desires of oppressors without any basis in knowledge or truth. It suggests that those who choose to follow such misguided paths are essentially led astray by Allah as a result of their own choices. The rhetorical question posed in the verse underscores the futility of seeking guidance once one has willingly embraced misguidance. Furthermore, it highlights the isolation of those who follow falsehood, as they will find no true supporters or helpers in their deviation from the right path.
orig: بل اتبع الذين ظلموا أهواءهم بغير علم فمن يهدي من أضل الله وما لهم من ناصرين

translation: So direct your face toward the religion, inclining to truth. [Adhere to] the fitrah of Allah upon which He has created [all] people. No change should there be in the creation of Allah. That is the correct religion, but most of the people do not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to the natural disposition (fitrah) that Allah has instilled in every human being, which inclines them towards monotheism and submission to God. It instructs believers to steadfastly follow the true religion, Islam, as it aligns with this innate nature. The verse asserts that this religion is unchangeable and perfect as created by Allah, yet it acknowledges that most people are unaware of this truth due to various influences and distractions in life.
orig: فأقم وجهك للدين حنيفا فطرت الله التي فطر الناس عليها لا تبديل لخلق الله ذلك الدين القيم ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: Turning to Him, and fear Him and establish the prayer and do not be of those who associate others with Allah
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sincere repentance and devotion to Allah alone. It calls believers to turn back to Allah in repentance (Muneebeen), to fear Him, which implies being conscious of His presence and commandments, and to regularly perform the prayer, which is a fundamental pillar of Islam. The verse also warns against associating partners with Allah (shirk), which is considered the gravest sin in Islam. The overall message is a call to spiritual purity, obedience to Allah's commands, and maintaining the purity of faith by avoiding idolatry.
orig: منيبين إليه واتقوه وأقيموا الصلاة ولا تكونوا من المشركين

translation: Of those who have divided their religion and become sects, each group rejoicing in what they have.
interpretation: This verse critiques the division within the Muslim community into various sects, each claiming to possess the truth and feeling content with their own interpretations and practices. It highlights the danger of fragmentation and the importance of unity in faith, suggesting that such divisions deviate from the intended oneness of the religion.
orig: من الذين فرقوا دينهم وكانوا شيعا كل حزب بما لديهم فرحون

translation: And when the people are touched by harm, they call upon their Lord, turning to Him in repentance. But when He gives them a taste of His mercy, behold, a group of them ascribe partners to their Lord.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fluctuating nature of human faith and gratitude. It illustrates how people often turn to God in times of distress, showing repentance and seeking His help. However, once their situation improves and they experience God's mercy, some of them revert to polytheism or associating partners with God, forgetting the sincerity of their prayers during hardship. This behavior reflects a lack of consistent faith and gratitude, emphasizing the human tendency to be forgetful of God's favors when life becomes comfortable.
orig: وإذا مس الناس ضر دعوا ربهم منيبين إليه ثم إذا أذاقهم منه رحمة إذا فريق منهم بربهم يشركون

translation: So that they may deny what We have given them, so enjoy yourselves, for you will soon know.
interpretation: This verse addresses those who deny the blessings and signs from Allah, warning them that their temporary enjoyment of worldly pleasures will soon be contrasted with the realization of the consequences of their disbelief. It emphasizes the fleeting nature of worldly life and the certainty of divine justice.
orig: ليكفروا بما آتيناهم فتمتعوا فسوف تعلمون

translation: Or have We sent down to them an authority, which speaks of what they were associating with Him?
interpretation: This verse challenges the polytheists by questioning whether they have received any divine scripture or authority that justifies their practice of associating partners with Allah. It emphasizes that their idolatrous beliefs lack any legitimate basis in revelation, highlighting the absence of any scriptural evidence supporting their shirk (polytheism).
orig: أم أنزلنا عليهم سلطانا فهو يتكلم بما كانوا به يشركون

translation: And when We let the people taste mercy, they rejoice in it, but if an evil afflicts them because of what their hands have put forth, then they despair.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to react differently to good and bad circumstances. When people experience blessings or mercy from Allah, they are quick to feel joy and happiness. However, when they face hardships or calamities, which are often a result of their own actions or sins, they fall into despair and lose hope. The verse serves as a reminder to maintain a balanced perspective, recognizing that both good and bad times are tests from Allah, and one should remain steadfast and hopeful in all situations, trusting in Allah's wisdom and mercy.
orig: وإذا أذقنا الناس رحمة فرحوا بها وإن تصبهم سيئة بما قدمت أيديهم إذا هم يقنطون

translation: Have they not seen that Allah extends provision for whom He wills and restricts [it]? Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine authority of Allah over the distribution of sustenance. It serves as a reminder to believers that the varying levels of wealth and provision among people are not random but are controlled by Allah's will. This understanding should lead believers to trust in Allah's wisdom and justice, recognizing these variations as signs of His power and a test of faith, encouraging gratitude and patience among them.
orig: أولم يروا أن الله يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء ويقدر إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يؤمنون

translation: So give the relative his right, as well as the needy and the traveler. That is best for those who desire the countenance of Allah, and it is they who will be successful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fulfilling the rights of close relatives, the poor, and travelers by giving them their due share. It suggests that performing these acts of charity and kindness is not only a moral obligation but also a means to seek the pleasure and approval of Allah. Those who engage in such righteous deeds with the intention of pleasing Allah are promised success and prosperity in the hereafter, highlighting the spiritual and moral rewards of altruism and compassion.
orig: فآت ذا القربى حقه والمسكين وابن السبيل ذلك خير للذين يريدون وجه الله وأولئك هم المفلحون

translation: And whatever you give in usury (riba) to increase in the wealth of people, it does not increase with Allah. And whatever you give in charity (zakah), desiring the countenance of Allah - those are the ones who will have their rewards multiplied.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the spiritual and moral superiority of giving charity (zakah) over engaging in usury (riba). It teaches that while usury might seem to increase wealth among people, it holds no value in the sight of Allah and does not contribute to spiritual growth or divine reward. In contrast, giving charity with the intention of pleasing Allah is highly valued and results in multiplied rewards in the hereafter. This underscores the Islamic principle that true wealth and growth come from acts of righteousness and generosity, not from exploitative financial practices.
orig: وما آتيتم من ربا ليربو في أموال الناس فلا يربو عند الله وما آتيتم من زكاة تريدون وجه الله فأولئك هم المضعفون

translation: Allah is He Who created you, then provided for you, then will cause you to die, and then will give you life. Are any of your partners (whom you ascribe to Allah) capable of doing any of that? Glory be to Him and Exalted is He above all that they associate (with Him).
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and uniqueness of Allah in the cycle of life, sustenance, death, and resurrection. It challenges the belief in any partners or deities alongside Allah by questioning their ability to perform even a single aspect of these divine acts. The rhetorical question serves to highlight the absurdity of polytheism, asserting that no other being can claim such authority or capability. The verse concludes with a declaration of Allah's transcendence and purity from any form of association or partnership, reinforcing monotheism and the rejection of idolatry.
orig: الله الذي خلقكم ثم رزقكم ثم يميتكم ثم يحييكم هل من شركائكم من يفعل من ذلكم من شيء سبحانه وتعالى عما يشركون

translation: Corruption has appeared throughout the land and sea by [reason of] what the hands of people have earned so He may let them taste part of [the consequence of] what they have done that perhaps they will return [to righteousness].
interpretation: This verse indicates that the environmental and societal corruption observed is a direct result of human actions and sins. It serves as a divine warning and a test from Allah, intended to make people experience the consequences of their deeds. The ultimate purpose is to encourage repentance and a return to righteous living, highlighting Allah's mercy and justice.
orig: ظهر الفساد في البر والبحر بما كسبت أيدي الناس ليذيقهم بعض الذي عملوا لعلهم يرجعون

translation: Say, "Travel through the land and observe how was the end of those before. Most of them were polytheists."
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to reflect on the historical outcomes of past civilizations, particularly those who practiced polytheism. It suggests that by examining the ruins and histories of these societies, one can see the consequences of straying from monotheism. The verse serves as a reminder and a warning that deviation from the worship of one God leads to downfall, urging contemporary believers to adhere to the path of monotheism to avoid a similar fate.
orig: قل سيروا في الأرض فانظروا كيف كان عاقبة الذين من قبل كان أكثرهم مشركين

translation: So direct your face toward the religion, inclining to truth. [Adhere to it] before there comes a Day from Allah which there is no repelling. On that Day they will be divided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the urgency of steadfastly adhering to the true religion (Islam) before the arrival of the Day of Judgment, which is inevitable and cannot be delayed or avoided. The phrase 'direct your face toward the religion' signifies complete devotion and sincerity in faith. The mention of the Day when people will be divided underscores the consequence of one's actions and beliefs, highlighting the importance of preparing for the afterlife by following the righteous path.
orig: فأقم وجهك للدين القيم من قبل أن يأتي يوم لا مرد له من الله يومئذ يصدعون

translation: Whoever disbelieves, upon him is [the consequence of] his disbelief, and whoever does righteous deeds - for themselves they are preparing [goodness].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes personal responsibility and the consequences of one's actions. It highlights that disbelief leads to negative outcomes borne by the individual themselves, while performing righteous deeds results in positive outcomes that benefit the doer. The verse underscores the idea that our actions pave the way for our own future, either towards spiritual loss or gain, depending on whether we choose disbelief or righteousness.
orig: من كفر فعليه كفره ومن عمل صالحا فلأنفسهم يمهدون

translation: That He may reward those who have believed and done righteous deeds out of His bounty. Indeed, He does not like the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's promise to reward the believers who perform good deeds with His grace and favor. It highlights the divine attribute of generosity towards those who have faith and act righteously. Conversely, it also underscores God's disapproval of disbelief, indicating a clear distinction between the treatment of believers and disbelievers in the divine scheme.
orig: ليجزي الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات من فضله إنه لا يحب الكافرين

translation: And among His signs is that He sends the winds as bearers of good tidings, and to make you taste of His mercy, and that the ships may sail by His command, and that you may seek of His bounty, and that you may be grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the interconnectedness of natural phenomena and human life as signs of God's mercy and providence. The winds, which are a natural occurrence, are described as bringing good news and enabling rainfall, which is essential for life. This rain also allows ships to sail, facilitating trade and travel, which are means for humans to seek God's bounty. The verse encourages gratitude towards God for these provisions, emphasizing that recognizing and appreciating these signs should lead to a deeper faith and thankfulness.
orig: ومن آياته أن يرسل الرياح مبشرات وليذيقكم من رحمته ولتجري الفلك بأمره ولتبتغوا من فضله ولعلكم تشكرون

translation: And We have certainly sent messengers before you to their peoples, and they came to them with clear proofs; then We took vengeance upon those who committed crimes, and it was incumbent upon Us to aid the believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the historical continuity of divine revelation and the mission of prophets. It highlights that prophets were sent with clear signs and evidence to guide their communities. The verse also underscores the principle of divine justice, where those who reject the message and persist in wrongdoing face consequences, while it is a duty of God to support and aid the believers. This reflects the balance between divine mercy and justice, encouraging faith and righteousness among people.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا من قبلك رسلا إلى قومهم فجاءوهم بالبينات فانتقمنا من الذين أجرموا وكان حقا علينا نصر المؤمنين

translation: Allah is He Who sends the winds, and they raise a cloud, then He spreads it in the sky as He wills, and breaks it into fragments, so you see the rain drops coming forth from its midst. Then when He causes it to fall upon whom He wills of His slaves, behold! they rejoice;
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's control over natural phenomena, specifically the process of rainfall. It emphasizes His omnipotence and meticulous management of the weather cycle, from the stirring of winds to the formation and dispersion of clouds, culminating in the provision of rain. The verse highlights the joy and gratitude of people when rain comes, underscoring the theme of divine providence and the blessings that Allah bestows upon His creation.
orig: الله الذي يرسل الرياح فتثير سحابا فيبسطه في السماء كيف يشاء ويجعله كسفا فترى الودق يخرج من خلاله فإذا أصاب به من يشاء من عباده إذا هم يستبشرون

translation: And indeed, before it was revealed to them, they were in a state of doubt.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the people mentioned were previously in a state of uncertainty and confusion about the truth before the revelation of the Qur'an. It highlights their initial skepticism and lack of clear guidance, which was later addressed by the divine message.
orig: وإن كانوا من قبل أن ينزل عليهم من قبله لمبلسين

translation: So observe the effects of Allah's mercy - how He revives the earth after its death. Indeed, He is the Reviver of the dead, and He is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse invites believers to reflect on the natural phenomenon of the earth's revival after a period of dryness and death, as a manifestation of Allah's mercy and power. The revival of the earth serves as a metaphor and a reminder of Allah's ability to resurrect the dead on the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes the omnipotence of Allah, who has control over all aspects of creation and can bring life to what was once dead, reinforcing the belief in the afterlife and the power of Allah over all things.
orig: فانظر إلى آثار رحمت الله كيف يحيي الأرض بعد موتها إن ذلك لمحيي الموتى وهو على كل شيء قدير

translation: And if We send a wind and they see it turning yellow, they will certainly continue to disbelieve after it.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubbornness and denial of people even when faced with clear signs from Allah. The 'wind' mentioned here could symbolize a trial or a natural phenomenon that changes the environment, such as causing plants to turn yellow. Despite witnessing such a sign, which should serve as a reminder of Allah's power and a call to faith, people persist in their disbelief. This reflects a deeper spiritual ailment where external evidence fails to penetrate the heart's denial.
orig: ولئن أرسلنا ريحا فرأوه مصفرا لظلوا من بعده يكفرون

translation: Indeed, you will not make the dead hear, nor will you make the deaf hear the call when they turn away, turning their backs.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the limitation of human influence over those who are spiritually or metaphorically 'dead' or 'deaf' to the message of Islam. It suggests that the Prophet Muhammad, and by extension all believers, cannot force understanding or acceptance upon those who deliberately turn away from the truth. The focus here is on the futility of trying to convince those who have consciously chosen to reject the message, highlighting the importance of patience and perseverance in conveying the message, while leaving the ultimate guidance to Allah.
orig: فإنك لا تسمع الموتى ولا تسمع الصم الدعاء إذا ولوا مدبرين

translation: And you are not one to guide the blind from their straying. You can only make those who believe in Our verses hear, and they are the ones who submit.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of the Prophet Muhammad as a messenger whose responsibility is limited to conveying the message of God. It highlights that he cannot force guidance upon those who are spiritually blind or unwilling to see the truth. The term 'blind' metaphorically refers to those who are unable or unwilling to perceive the truth due to their own biases or disbelief. The verse reassures the Prophet that his duty is only to communicate the divine message to those who are receptive, i.e., those who believe in the verses of God and submit to His will, becoming Muslims. This underscores the principle of free will in Islam, where acceptance of faith is an individual's choice.
orig: وما أنت بهاد العمي عن ضلالتهم إن تسمع إلا من يؤمن بآياتنا فهم مسلمون

translation: Allah is He Who created you from weakness, then made after weakness strength, then made after strength weakness and gray hair. He creates what He wills, and He is the All-Knowing, the All-Powerful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the cycle of human life as designed by Allah, illustrating His complete control over creation. It begins with human vulnerability at birth, progresses to strength in adulthood, and returns to weakness in old age, symbolized by gray hair. This cycle underscores the transient nature of human life and our dependence on Allah at every stage. The verse also emphasizes Allah's omnipotence and omniscience, affirming that He creates according to His will, with full knowledge and power over all things.
orig: الله الذي خلقكم من ضعف ثم جعل من بعد ضعف قوة ثم جعل من بعد قوة ضعفا وشيبة يخلق ما يشاء وهو العليم القدير

translation: And the Day the Hour appears the criminals will swear they remained but an hour. Thus they were deluded.
interpretation: This verse highlights the perception of time by the wrongdoers on the Day of Judgment. They will feel as though their time in the world was extremely brief, akin to just an hour, due to their shock and realization of the consequences of their actions. This feeling of time being short reflects their delusion and false sense of security in worldly life, where they believed they had ample time to repent or continue their misdeeds without consequence. The verse serves as a reminder of how deceptive worldly life can be and underscores the suddenness and inevitability of the Day of Judgment.
orig: ويوم تقوم الساعة يقسم المجرمون ما لبثوا غير ساعة كذلك كانوا يؤفكون

translation: And those who were given knowledge and faith will say: 'Indeed, you remained in the Book of Allah until the Day of Resurrection. So this is the Day of Resurrection, but you were unaware.'
