The verse underscores the importance of fearing Allah over societal norms and demonstrates that divine commands will ultimately be fulfilled, serving as a lesson in obedience and the execution of Allah's will.
orig: وإذ تقول للذي أنعم الله عليه وأنعمت عليه أمسك عليك زوجك واتق الله وتخفي في نفسك ما الله مبديه وتخشى الناس والله أحق أن تخشاه فلما قضى زيد منها وطرا زوجناكها لكي لا يكون على المؤمنين حرج في أزواج أدعيائهم إذا قضوا منهن وطرا وكان أمر الله مفعولا

translation: There is no difficulty for the Prophet in what Allah has ordained for him. That was the way of Allah with those who have passed away before. And the command of Allah is a decree determined.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, should not feel burdened or constrained by the divine decrees set by Allah. It reassures him that the obligations and permissions given to him by Allah are part of a consistent pattern that Allah has established with previous prophets. The verse underscores the concept of divine predestination and the unchangeable nature of Allah's decrees, indicating that whatever Allah has ordained for the Prophet is part of a larger, purposeful divine plan that has been set in motion and will be fulfilled.
orig: ما كان على النبي من حرج فيما فرض الله له سنة الله في الذين خلوا من قبل وكان أمر الله قدرا مقدورا

translation: Those who convey the messages of Allah and fear Him, and do not fear anyone except Allah. And sufficient is Allah as a Reckoner.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of courage and faith in conveying the divine messages. It speaks to the messengers and believers who are tasked with spreading the word of Allah, highlighting that their primary fear should be of Allah alone, not of any human repercussions or societal pressures. The phrase 'sufficient is Allah as a Reckoner' reassures that Allah's judgment is the only one that ultimately matters, encouraging steadfastness and integrity in fulfilling one's religious duties.
orig: الذين يبلغون رسالات الله ويخشونه ولا يخشون أحدا إلا الله وكفى بالله حسيبا

translation: Muhammad is not the father of any of your men, but he is the Messenger of Allah and the seal of the prophets. And Allah has full knowledge of all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unique status of Prophet Muhammad as the final prophet sent by Allah, indicating that no prophet will come after him. It clarifies that his role transcends typical familial relationships, focusing instead on his divine mission as a messenger. The mention of Allah's omniscience underscores the divine wisdom and planning behind this designation, affirming the completeness and finality of the prophetic message delivered through Muhammad.
orig: ما كان محمد أبا أحد من رجالكم ولكن رسول الله وخاتم النبيين وكان الله بكل شيء عليما

translation: O you who have believed, remember Allah with much remembrance.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to engage in frequent and continuous remembrance of Allah, emphasizing the importance of maintaining a strong connection with the Divine through regular acts of worship and mindfulness. It suggests that constant remembrance helps to strengthen faith, increase spiritual awareness, and bring one closer to Allah.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اذكروا الله ذكرا كثيرا

translation: And glorify Him morning and evening.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of consistently remembering and praising Allah throughout the day. By specifying 'morning and evening,' it suggests a routine of devotion that frames one's daily activities with spiritual mindfulness, encouraging believers to start and end their day with the remembrance of Allah, thereby maintaining a continuous connection with the Divine.
orig: وسبحوه بكرة وأصيلا

translation: He it is who sends blessings upon you, and His angels, that He may bring you out from the darknesses into the light. And He is ever Merciful to the believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine mercy and guidance provided by Allah and His angels to believers. The 'blessings' (salah) from Allah and the angels are a means of spiritual purification and enlightenment, helping believers to move from the state of ignorance and sin (darkness) to knowledge and righteousness (light). This process reflects Allah's continuous compassion and mercy towards those who have faith, indicating that divine support and guidance are always available to the believers, aiding them in their spiritual journey.
orig: هو الذي يصلي عليكم وملائكته ليخرجكم من الظلمات إلى النور وكان بالمؤمنين رحيما

translation: Their greeting on the Day they meet Him will be, 'Peace,' and He has prepared for them a noble reward.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the believers' experience on the Day of Judgment, emphasizing the serene and honorable reception they will receive from Allah. The greeting of 'Peace' signifies the ultimate state of tranquility and safety that the righteous will enjoy in the presence of their Lord. The 'noble reward' mentioned indicates that Allah has prepared a distinguished and generous recompense for those who have lived righteously, reflecting His immense generosity and the value He places on their faith and good deeds.
orig: تحيتهم يوم يلقونه سلام وأعد لهم أجرا كريما

translation: O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness and a bringer of good tidings and a warner.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the multifaceted role of Prophet Muhammad as assigned by Allah. As a 'witness', he testifies to the truth of Islam and the actions of his followers. As a 'bringer of good tidings', he delivers the message of hope and reward for those who follow the path of righteousness. As a 'warner', he alerts people to the consequences of straying from the right path. This verse underscores the comprehensive nature of his mission to guide humanity towards salvation.
orig: يا أيها النبي إنا أرسلناك شاهدا ومبشرا ونذيرا

translation: And calling to Allah by His permission, and an illuminating lamp.
interpretation: This verse describes the Prophet Muhammad as someone who invites people to the worship and recognition of Allah, with divine permission, emphasizing his role as a guide towards faith. The metaphor of an 'illuminating lamp' further signifies that the Prophet brings clarity and light to the darkness of ignorance, guiding people towards the truth and righteousness.
orig: وداعيا إلى الله بإذنه وسراجا منيرا

translation: And give glad tidings to the believers that they will have from Allah a great bounty.
interpretation: This verse serves as a message of hope and encouragement for believers, assuring them that their faith and good deeds will be rewarded by Allah with immense grace and favor. It emphasizes the concept of divine generosity and the promise of a significant reward in the hereafter, motivating believers to remain steadfast in their faith.
orig: وبشر المؤمنين بأن لهم من الله فضلا كبيرا

translation: And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and disregard their harm, and put your trust in Allah, and sufficient is Allah as a disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse encourages steadfastness and reliance on Allah in the face of opposition from disbelievers and hypocrites. It advises the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and by extension all believers, not to be swayed or influenced by the negativity and harm caused by these groups. Instead, one should place complete trust in Allah, recognizing that He alone is sufficient to manage and take care of all affairs. This reflects a deep theme of tawakkul (trust in Allah) and resilience in faith, emphasizing that divine support is more than enough to overcome any adversity.
orig: ولا تطع الكافرين والمنافقين ودع أذاهم وتوكل على الله وكفى بالله وكيلا

translation: O you who have believed, when you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them, then there is no waiting period for you to count concerning them. So provide for them and release them in a gracious manner.
interpretation: This verse addresses the situation where a marriage is dissolved before consummation. It emphasizes the principle of fairness and kindness in Islamic law, indicating that even in the absence of a physical relationship, the husband is still obligated to provide for the wife and to end the marriage respectfully. This reflects the broader Islamic ethos of treating others with dignity and generosity, particularly in sensitive situations like divorce.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا نكحتم المؤمنات ثم طلقتموهن من قبل أن تمسوهن فما لكم عليهن من عدة تعتدونها فمتعوهن وسرحوهن سراحا جميلا

translation: O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful to you your wives to whom you have given their due compensation and those your right hand possesses from what Allah has returned to you [of captives] and the daughters of your paternal uncles and the daughters of your paternal aunts and the daughters of your maternal uncles and the daughters of your maternal aunts who emigrated with you and a believing woman if she gives herself to the Prophet [and] if the Prophet wishes to marry her, [this is] only for you, excluding the [other] believers. We certainly know what We have made obligatory upon them concerning their wives and those their right hands possess, [but this is] for you that there would be no discomfort upon you. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad specifically, granting him permission to marry certain categories of women, which includes his wives to whom he has paid their dowries, women who were taken as captives and then freed, close female relatives who migrated with him, and any believing woman who offers herself to him without a dowry, provided he wishes to marry her. This permission is exclusive to the Prophet and not applicable to other believers. The verse emphasizes that this ruling was given to ease any hardship on the Prophet, acknowledging that Allah is aware of the obligations placed on other believers regarding their marriages and slaves. The underlying interpretation suggests a divine acknowledgment of the Prophet's unique role and responsibilities, ensuring that his personal life does not hinder his mission, while also highlighting Allah's attributes of forgiveness and mercy.
orig: يا أيها النبي إنا أحللنا لك أزواجك اللاتي آتيت أجورهن وما ملكت يمينك مما أفاء الله عليك وبنات عمك وبنات عماتك وبنات خالك وبنات خالاتك اللاتي هاجرن معك وامرأة مؤمنة إن وهبت نفسها للنبي إن أراد النبي أن يستنكحها خالصة لك من دون المؤمنين قد علمنا ما فرضنا عليهم في أزواجهم وما ملكت أيمانهم لكيلا يكون عليك حرج وكان الله غفورا رحيما

translation: You may defer [your turn with] any of them you please, and you may receive any you please. And whomsoever you desire of those you had set aside - there is no blame upon you. That is more suitable that they may be comforted and not grieve, and may all be pleased with what you have given them. And Allah knows what is in your hearts. And Allah is Knowing and Forbearing.
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad's unique situation regarding his marriages, allowing him flexibility in managing his relationships with his wives. It emphasizes that such arrangements are meant to ensure the emotional well-being of his wives, preventing them from feeling neglected or distressed. The verse also underscores that Allah is fully aware of the Prophet's intentions and feelings, and reassures that Allah's knowledge and forbearance encompass all such personal matters.
orig: ترجي من تشاء منهن وتؤوي إليك من تشاء ومن ابتغيت ممن عزلت فلا جناح عليك ذلك أدنى أن تقر أعينهن ولا يحزن ويرضين بما آتيتهن كلهن والله يعلم ما في قلوبكم وكان الله عليما حليما

translation: It is not lawful for you (O Muhammad) to marry more women after this, nor to exchange them for other wives, even though their beauty may attract you, except those whom your right hand possesses. And Allah is Ever a Watcher over all things.
interpretation: This verse is specifically addressed to the Prophet Muhammad, indicating that after the revelation of this verse, he was not permitted to marry additional women or to divorce his existing wives to marry others, regardless of their beauty. The exception mentioned, "those whom your right hand possesses," refers to the captives or slaves that were lawfully under his possession. This ruling underscores the unique position of the Prophet and the finality of his marital status as per divine decree. The mention of Allah being a Watcher over all things serves as a reminder of divine oversight and accountability in all actions, including personal and marital decisions.
orig: لا يحل لك النساء من بعد ولا أن تبدل بهن من أزواج ولو أعجبك حسنهن إلا ما ملكت يمينك وكان الله على كل شيء رقيبا

translation: O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet except when you are permitted for a meal, without awaiting its readiness. But when you are invited, then enter; and when you have eaten, disperse without seeking to remain for conversation. Indeed, that [behavior] was troubling the Prophet, and he is shy of [dismissing] you. But Allah is not shy of the truth. And when you ask [his wives] for something, ask them from behind a partition. That is purer for your hearts and their hearts. And it is not for you to harm the Messenger of Allah or to marry his wives after him, ever. Indeed, that would be in the sight of Allah an enormity.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of respecting the privacy and personal space of the Prophet Muhammad. It instructs believers to not enter his home without permission, particularly for meals, and to leave promptly after eating without lingering for unnecessary conversation. This guidance was given because such behavior was causing discomfort to the Prophet, who was too shy to express his feelings directly. The verse also introduces the practice of speaking to the Prophet's wives from behind a screen, which serves to maintain modesty and purity in interactions. Additionally, it firmly prohibits any harm to the Prophet and marrying his widows after his death, highlighting the sanctity and high regard for the Prophet's family in Islam.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تدخلوا بيوت النبي إلا أن يؤذن لكم إلى طعام غير ناظرين إناه ولكن إذا دعيتم فادخلوا فإذا طعمتم فانتشروا ولا مستأنسين لحديث إن ذلكم كان يؤذي النبي فيستحيي منكم والله لا يستحيي من الحق وإذا سألتموهن متاعا فاسألوهن من وراء حجاب ذلكم أطهر لقلوبكم وقلوبهن وما كان لكم أن تؤذوا رسول الله ولا أن تنكحوا أزواجه من بعده أبدا إن ذلكم كان عند الله عظيما

translation: Whether you reveal anything or conceal it, indeed Allah is All-Knowing of everything.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience of Allah, indicating that He is fully aware of all actions, thoughts, and intentions, whether they are openly expressed or kept hidden. It serves as a reminder to believers to be mindful of their actions at all times, as nothing escapes Allah's knowledge.
orig: إن تبدوا شيئا أو تخفوه فإن الله كان بكل شيء عليما

translation: There is no blame upon them concerning their fathers or their sons or their brothers or their brothers' sons or their sisters' sons or their women or those their right hands possess. And fear Allah. Indeed Allah is ever, over all things, a Witness.
interpretation: This verse from Surah Al-Ahzab (33:55) addresses the wives of the Prophet Muhammad, indicating that they are allowed to interact freely with specified male relatives and other women without any blame or sin. The verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining modesty and piety in these interactions, as Allah is a witness to all actions. It underscores the balance between permissible social interactions and the overarching need to remain conscious of Allah's presence and judgment.
orig: لا جناح عليهن في آبائهن ولا أبنائهن ولا إخوانهن ولا أبناء إخوانهن ولا أبناء أخواتهن ولا نسائهن ولا ما ملكت أيمانهن واتقين الله إن الله كان على كل شيء شهيدا

translation: Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who have believed, send blessings upon him and submit a salutation [of peace].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the high status of the Prophet Muhammad by indicating that Allah and His angels send blessings upon him, which is a form of divine honor and respect. It instructs believers to follow this example by sending blessings upon the Prophet and greeting him with peace, thereby fostering a deep spiritual connection and showing reverence. This act of sending blessings is not only a form of worship but also a means of drawing closer to Allah through the love and respect for His Messenger.
orig: إن الله وملائكته يصلون على النبي يا أيها الذين آمنوا صلوا عليه وسلموا تسليما

translation: Indeed, those who annoy Allah and His Messenger - Allah has cursed them in this world and in the Hereafter and has prepared for them a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe consequences for those who disrespect or harm Allah and His Messenger. It underscores the sanctity of Allah and His Prophet, indicating that such actions are not only morally wrong but also incur divine wrath both in this life and the hereafter. The 'humiliating punishment' serves as a deterrent, highlighting the gravity of the offense and the importance of reverence and respect towards divine figures.
orig: إن الذين يؤذون الله ورسوله لعنهم الله في الدنيا والآخرة وأعد لهم عذابا مهينا

translation: And those who harm believing men and believing women without them having earned it, they have indeed borne the guilt of slander and clear sin.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity of wrongfully harming believers, highlighting that such actions are not only morally reprehensible but also result in the perpetrator bearing the heavy burden of slander and evident sin. It underscores the importance of justice and fairness in interactions within the community, warning against the severe spiritual consequences of baseless harm.
orig: والذين يؤذون المؤمنين والمؤمنات بغير ما اكتسبوا فقد احتملوا بهتانا وإثما مبينا

translation: O Prophet, tell your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers to bring down over themselves [part] of their outer garments. That is more suitable that they will be known and not be abused. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse instructs Muslim women to cover themselves with their outer garments in a way that distinguishes them as believers, thereby protecting them from harassment. The emphasis on modesty is not only a means of personal protection but also a reflection of a broader societal ethic that values respect and dignity. The mention of Allah's attributes as Forgiving and Merciful at the end suggests that adherence to these guidelines is part of a broader spiritual and moral framework that seeks to foster a compassionate and understanding community.
orig: يا أيها النبي قل لأزواجك وبناتك ونساء المؤمنين يدنين عليهن من جلابيبهن ذلك أدنى أن يعرفن فلا يؤذين وكان الله غفورا رحيما

translation: If the hypocrites, and those in whose hearts is a disease, and the alarmists in the city do not desist, We will certainly urge you against them; then they will not be your neighbors therein except for a little while.
interpretation: This verse warns that if the hypocrites, those with doubts and weak faith, and those who spread fear and unrest in the community do not stop their harmful actions, divine intervention will support the Prophet Muhammad in taking action against them. This action will lead to their temporary presence in the community, implying eventual removal or isolation, emphasizing the need for a peaceful and stable society.
orig: لئن لم ينته المنافقون والذين في قلوبهم مرض والمرجفون في المدينة لنغرينك بهم ثم لا يجاورونك فيها إلا قليلا

translation: Cursed wherever they are found, they are seized and killed with slaughter.
interpretation: This verse describes the severe consequences faced by those who have been cursed due to their persistent disbelief and opposition to the truth. It highlights the inevitability of divine retribution, emphasizing that no matter where these individuals are located, they will be overtaken and dealt with decisively. The phrase "killed with slaughter" underscores the intensity and totality of the punishment, serving as a warning about the outcomes of rejecting divine guidance and engaging in enmity against the believers.
orig: ملعونين أينما ثقفوا أخذوا وقتلوا تقتيلا

translation: The way of Allah in those who have passed before, and you will not find any change in the way of Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consistency and unchangeability of Allah's divine laws and patterns throughout history. It suggests that the principles and decrees set by Allah for previous nations are the same that apply to all subsequent generations, indicating a universal and timeless application of divine justice and guidance.
orig: سنة الله في الذين خلوا من قبل ولن تجد لسنة الله تبديلا

translation: People ask you about the Hour. Say, 'Its knowledge is only with Allah. And what will make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the limitation of human knowledge regarding the timing of the Day of Judgment, known as the Hour. It instructs the Prophet Muhammad to respond to inquiries about when the Hour will occur by affirming that only Allah possesses this knowledge. The verse also introduces an element of urgency and unpredictability by suggesting that the Hour could be imminent, encouraging believers to remain vigilant and prepared for its arrival at any moment.
orig: يسألك الناس عن الساعة قل إنما علمها عند الله وما يدريك لعل الساعة تكون قريبا

translation: Indeed, Allah has cursed the disbelievers and prepared for them a Blaze.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe consequences of disbelief in Allah. The term "curse" here signifies Allah's rejection and distancing from those who deny His existence and message. The preparation of the "Blaze" or Hellfire for the disbelievers underscores the ultimate accountability and the punishment awaiting those who choose to reject faith. It serves as a stark reminder of the importance of belief and the dire outcomes of disbelief.
orig: إن الله لعن الكافرين وأعد لهم سعيرا

translation: Abiding therein forever, they will not find any protector or helper.
interpretation: This verse describes the eternal nature of the punishment in Hell for those who are condemned there. It emphasizes the isolation and helplessness of the damned, as they will have no one to turn to for protection or assistance, highlighting the severity and finality of their fate.
orig: خالدين فيها أبدا لا يجدون وليا ولا نصيرا

translation: The Day their faces will be turned about in the Fire, they will say, 'Oh, if only we had obeyed Allah and obeyed the Messenger.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the regret and realization that will come upon the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment. As they suffer in the Fire, they will wish they had followed the guidance of Allah and His Messenger during their earthly lives. It serves as a warning to heed the divine commands and the prophetic teachings, underscoring the consequences of disobedience and the importance of obedience in achieving salvation.
orig: يوم تقلب وجوههم في النار يقولون يا ليتنا أطعنا الله وأطعنا الرسولا

translation: And they will say, 'Our Lord, indeed we obeyed our leaders and our great ones, and they led us astray from the path.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to follow leaders and influential figures without questioning their guidance. It serves as a reminder of the personal responsibility each individual has in seeking the truth and not blindly following others, even if they hold positions of power or respect. The verse underscores the accountability one faces on the Day of Judgment for one's choices, emphasizing that following misguided leaders does not absolve one of the consequences of straying from the right path.
orig: وقالوا ربنا إنا أطعنا سادتنا وكبراءنا فأضلونا السبيلا

translation: Our Lord, give them double punishment and curse them with a great curse.
interpretation: This verse is a supplication for divine retribution against those who have wronged the believers. It reflects the intensity of the plea for justice and the severity of the punishment sought, emphasizing the gravity of the offenses committed by the adversaries. The request for a "double punishment" and a "great curse" underscores the depth of the transgression and the desire for a commensurate response from Allah.
orig: ربنا آتهم ضعفين من العذاب والعنهم لعنا كبيرا

translation: O you who have believed, be not like those who abused Moses; so Allah cleared him of what they said. And he was, in the sight of Allah, distinguished.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder to believers to avoid the behavior of those who wronged Prophet Moses by speaking ill of him. It emphasizes the importance of respecting prophets and not engaging in slander or false accusations against them. The verse highlights that Allah protected Moses's honor and reputation from the false claims made against him, indicating divine support and vindication for the righteous. Furthermore, it underscores Moses's esteemed status in the eyes of Allah, encouraging believers to recognize and honor the dignity of prophets.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تكونوا كالذين آذوا موسى فبرأه الله مما قالوا وكان عند الله وجيها

translation: O you who have believed, fear Allah and speak words of appropriate justice.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of mindfulness of Allah in all aspects of life, particularly in speech. It encourages believers to always speak truthfully and justly, reflecting the moral and ethical standards set by their faith. The term 'قولا سديدا' or 'words of appropriate justice' suggests that one's speech should be not only truthful but also fair and considerate, aligning with divine guidance and righteousness.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله وقولوا قولا سديدا

translation: He will amend for you your deeds and forgive you your sins. And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly attained a great attainment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the mercy and forgiveness of Allah, indicating that following His guidance and the teachings of His Messenger leads to the rectification of one's actions and the forgiveness of sins. Obedience to Allah and His Messenger is portrayed as the path to achieving a profound and ultimate success, which is the success in the Hereafter.
orig: يصلح لكم أعمالكم ويغفر لكم ذنوبكم ومن يطع الله ورسوله فقد فاز فوزا عظيما

translation: Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, and they declined to bear it and feared it; but man [undertook to] bear it. Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant.
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound responsibility given to humanity, symbolized as the 'Trust' (amānah), which even the inanimate and celestial elements of creation were unwilling to accept due to its weighty nature. The acceptance of this Trust by humans signifies our unique capacity for moral agency and free will. However, the verse also acknowledges human fallibility, describing us as 'unjust and ignorant', indicating that despite being entrusted with this significant responsibility, humans often fail to uphold justice and wisdom due to our inherent weaknesses.
orig: إنا عرضنا الأمانة على السماوات والأرض والجبال فأبين أن يحملنها وأشفقن منها وحملها الإنسان إنه كان ظلوما جهولا

translation: So that Allah may punish the hypocrite men and hypocrite women and the polytheist men and polytheist women, and Allah may accept the repentance of the believing men and believing women. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine justice and mercy of Allah. It underscores the consequence of hypocrisy and polytheism, indicating that such actions lead to punishment, reflecting the accountability of individuals for their beliefs and actions. Conversely, it emphasizes Allah's readiness to accept repentance from those who believe, showcasing His attributes of forgiveness and mercy. This duality serves as a reminder of the importance of faith and the potential for redemption, encouraging believers to maintain their faith and seek forgiveness when they err.
orig: ليعذب الله المنافقين والمنافقات والمشركين والمشركات ويتوب الله على المؤمنين والمؤمنات وكان الله غفورا رحيما

translation: Praise be to Allah, to Whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And to Him belongs all praise in the Hereafter. And He is the All-Wise, the All-Aware.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and omnipotence of Allah, highlighting that all praise and gratitude are due to Him alone, both in this world and the hereafter. It underscores the attributes of Allah as being All-Wise and All-Aware, indicating His perfect knowledge and wisdom in managing the affairs of the universe. This serves as a reminder for believers to acknowledge and appreciate Allah's greatness and to maintain a constant state of gratitude and submission to His will.
orig: الحمد لله الذي له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وله الحمد في الآخرة وهو الحكيم الخبير

translation: He knows what enters the earth and what comes out of it, and what descends from the sky and what ascends to it. And He is the Most Merciful, the Most Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's omniscience and His complete awareness of all natural processes and movements within His creation. It highlights His knowledge of the intricate details of the earth and the sky, symbolizing His control over the entire universe. The mention of His attributes as the Most Merciful and the Most Forgiving at the end of the verse serves to remind believers of His compassion and readiness to forgive, despite His all-encompassing knowledge of their actions.
orig: يعلم ما يلج في الأرض وما يخرج منها وما ينزل من السماء وما يعرج فيها وهو الرحيم الغفور

translation: And those who disbelieve say, 'The Hour will not come to us.' Say, 'Yes, by my Lord, it will surely come to you. [Allah] knows the unseen; not even the weight of an atom escapes Him in the heavens or on the earth, nor anything smaller or larger than that, except that it is in a clear record.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty of the Day of Judgment and the omniscience of Allah. It addresses the disbelief of those who deny the coming of the Hour, asserting that it is an undeniable truth. The verse highlights Allah's complete knowledge of all things, visible and invisible, down to the minutest detail, which is meticulously recorded. This underscores the accountability of every action and the inevitability of facing the consequences on the Day of Judgment.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا لا تأتينا الساعة قل بلى وربي لتأتينكم عالم الغيب لا يعزب عنه مثقال ذرة في السماوات ولا في الأرض ولا أصغر من ذلك ولا أكبر إلا في كتاب مبين

translation: That He may reward those who have believed and done righteous deeds. Those - for them is forgiveness and noble provision.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's promise to recompense those who have faith and perform good deeds. It highlights the dual aspects of spiritual reward - forgiveness of sins and the provision of noble sustenance in the hereafter. The mention of 'noble provision' suggests not only material sufficiency but also spiritual and moral elevation, indicating a comprehensive reward that encompasses all aspects of well-being in the afterlife.
orig: ليجزي الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات أولئك لهم مغفرة ورزق كريم

translation: And those who strive against Our signs, seeking to defeat them - for them there will be a torment of a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns against those who actively oppose or try to undermine the divine revelations and signs of Allah. It highlights the severe consequences, indicating that such actions are not only futile but will lead to a painful punishment. The emphasis on 'striving against' suggests a deliberate and persistent effort to challenge or disprove the truth of the Qur'an, which is seen as a grave sin leading to divine retribution.
orig: والذين سعوا في آياتنا معاجزين أولئك لهم عذاب من رجز أليم

translation: And those who have been given knowledge see that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth, and it guides to the path of the Almighty, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the recognition by knowledgeable individuals of the divine origin and truth of the Qur'an, which serves as a guide to the path of God, characterized by His attributes of might and praiseworthiness. It underscores the role of divine revelation in providing clear guidance and the importance of knowledge in affirming the authenticity of the message.
orig: ويرى الذين أوتوا العلم الذي أنزل إليك من ربك هو الحق ويهدي إلى صراط العزيز الحميد

translation: And those who disbelieved said, "Shall we direct you to a man who will inform you that when you have disintegrated into complete disintegration, you will indeed be in a new creation?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the skepticism and mockery of the disbelievers towards the concept of resurrection. They sarcastically question whether they should introduce others to a man (referring to Prophet Muhammad) who claims that after complete disintegration of the body, individuals will be brought back to life in a new creation. This reflects their disbelief in the afterlife and the power of Allah to resurrect the dead, showcasing their rejection of a fundamental tenet of faith.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا هل ندلكم على رجل ينبئكم إذا مزقتم كل ممزق إنكم لفي خلق جديد

translation: Has he invented a lie against Allah, or is there madness in him? Nay, but those who believe not in the Hereafter are in torment and far error.
interpretation: This verse addresses the accusations made against the Prophet Muhammad, questioning whether he was fabricating lies about Allah or if he was insane. The Qur'an refutes these claims by asserting that the real issue lies with those who reject the concept of the Hereafter. Such individuals are described as being in a state of punishment and profound misguidance, indicating that their disbelief leads them away from the truth and into a state of spiritual suffering and confusion.
orig: أفترى على الله كذبا أم به جنة بل الذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة في العذاب والضلال البعيد

translation: Do they not see what is before them and behind them of the sky and the earth? If We will, We can cause the earth to swallow them or cause fragments from the sky to fall upon them. Indeed, in that is a sign for every servant who turns back [to Allah].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence of Allah and the constant signs of His power that surround us. It serves as a reminder to humans of their vulnerability and the need for humility and repentance. The mention of the earth swallowing them or fragments from the sky falling upon them illustrates the potential for divine intervention at any moment, urging believers to reflect on their actions and turn towards Allah in sincere repentance.
orig: أفلم يروا إلى ما بين أيديهم وما خلفهم من السماء والأرض إن نشأ نخسف بهم الأرض أو نسقط عليهم كسفا من السماء إن في ذلك لآية لكل عبد منيب

translation: And We certainly gave David from Us bounty. [We said], 'O mountains, repeat [Our] praises with him, and the birds [as well].' And We made iron pliable for him.
interpretation: This verse highlights the special favor and blessings bestowed upon Prophet David by Allah. The mountains and birds echoing David's praises signify the harmony and submission of nature to divine will, reflecting the deep spiritual connection David had with his Creator. The softening of iron for him symbolizes the empowerment and authority granted to him, enabling him to fulfill his divine mission with ease and effectiveness.
orig: ولقد آتينا داوود منا فضلا يا جبال أوبي معه والطير وألنا له الحديد

translation: That you work in abundance and measure in the narration, and do good deeds, indeed I am All-Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of performing good deeds abundantly and with precision, as if narrating or accounting for them meticulously. It serves as a reminder that Allah is fully aware and observant of all actions, encouraging believers to be diligent and sincere in their efforts to do good, knowing that their deeds are seen and valued by the All-Seeing.
orig: أن اعمل سابغات وقدر في السرد واعملوا صالحا إني بما تعملون بصير

translation: And to Solomon [We subjected] the wind - its morning [journey was that of] a month, and its evening [journey was that of] a month, and We made flow for him a spring of [liquid] copper. And among the jinn were those who worked for him by the permission of his Lord. And whoever among them deviated from Our command - We will make him taste of the punishment of the Blaze.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine favor bestowed upon Prophet Solomon, illustrating his control over natural elements like the wind, which facilitated swift travel, and the spring of copper, symbolizing wealth and resources. It also underscores the obedience of the jinn to Solomon, working under God's permission, which reflects the broader theme of divine authority and the consequences of disobedience. The mention of punishment for those jinn who deviate from God's command serves as a reminder of accountability and the inevitability of divine justice.
orig: ولسليمان الريح غدوها شهر ورواحها شهر وأسلنا له عين القطر ومن الجن من يعمل بين يديه بإذن ربه ومن يزغ منهم عن أمرنا نذقه من عذاب السعير

translation: They work for him as he desires, making arches, statues, basins as large as reservoirs, and cooking-pots fixed in place. 'Work, O family of David, in gratitude.' And few of My servants are grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the obedience and craftsmanship of the jinn working under Solomon, creating various objects as he commanded. It emphasizes the importance of gratitude towards God, as Solomon's command to his family to work in gratitude reflects a deeper spiritual lesson. The mention of 'few of My servants are grateful' underscores the rarity of true gratitude among people, serving as a reminder to the believers to always be thankful for God's blessings.
orig: يعملون له ما يشاء من محاريب وتماثيل وجفان كالجواب وقدور راسيات اعملوا آل داوود شكرا وقليل من عبادي الشكور

translation: So when We decreed death for him, nothing showed them his death except a creature of the earth that ate away at his staff. And when he fell down, the jinn realized that if they had known the unseen, they would not have remained in the humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the limitations of knowledge and power among beings other than Allah. It recounts the story of Prophet Solomon (Sulaiman), where his death was concealed from the jinn who were working under his command. Only after a worm had eaten through his staff, causing it to collapse and reveal his death, did the jinn realize their inability to foresee the future or know the unseen. This realization underscores the theme that only Allah possesses complete knowledge of the unseen, and it serves as a reminder to humans and jinn alike of their dependence on divine guidance and the futility of arrogance or claims to omniscience.
orig: فلما قضينا عليه الموت ما دلهم على موته إلا دابة الأرض تأكل منسأته فلما خر تبينت الجن أن لو كانوا يعلمون الغيب ما لبثوا في العذاب المهين

translation: Indeed, there was for Sheba in their dwelling place a sign: two gardens, on the right and on the left. 'Eat from the provision of your Lord and be grateful to Him. A good land [have you], and a forgiving Lord.'
interpretation: This verse reflects on the blessings bestowed upon the people of Sheba, symbolized by the two gardens on either side of their settlement. It serves as a reminder of the abundance provided by Allah and the importance of gratitude. The verse emphasizes that acknowledging and appreciating these blessings is crucial, as it leads to a prosperous life in a good land under the care of a forgiving Lord. The message is a call to recognize divine favors and respond with thankfulness, which in turn fosters a harmonious relationship with the Creator.
orig: لقد كان لسبإ في مسكنهم آية جنتان عن يمين وشمال كلوا من رزق ربكم واشكروا له بلدة طيبة ورب غفور

translation: So they turned away [from the truth], so We sent upon them the flood of the dam, and We replaced their two gardens with two gardens bearing bitter fruit, tamarisks, and something of lote-trees few.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the consequences of rejecting divine guidance and the subsequent punishment that follows. The 'flood of the dam' refers to a historical event where a dam broke, leading to the destruction of the fertile lands of the people of 'Ād. The transformation of their lush gardens into ones with bitter fruit and sparse vegetation symbolizes the loss of blessings and prosperity due to their disobedience. It serves as a reminder of the transient nature of worldly pleasures and the importance of adhering to God's commands to maintain spiritual and material well-being.
orig: فأعرضوا فأرسلنا عليهم سيل العرم وبدلناهم بجنتيهم جنتين ذواتي أكل خمط وأثل وشيء من سدر قليل

translation: That is how We recompense them for their disbelief; and do We recompense except the ungrateful?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of divine justice, illustrating that disbelief and ingratitude towards God's blessings and signs lead to a corresponding recompense. It underscores that God's retribution is specifically directed towards those who reject faith, highlighting the fairness and precision of divine judgment.
orig: ذلك جزيناهم بما كفروا وهل نجازي إلا الكفور

translation: And We placed between them and the cities which We had blessed [many] visible cities. And We determined between them the [distances of] travel, [saying], 'Travel between them by night or by day in safety.'
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's provision and planning for the ease and safety of travel between blessed cities. It underscores the divine facilitation of journeys, ensuring that travelers can move securely during both day and night, reflecting Allah's care and the interconnectedness of human settlements for the benefit of mankind.
orig: وجعلنا بينهم وبين القرى التي باركنا فيها قرى ظاهرة وقدرنا فيها السير سيروا فيها ليالي وأياما آمنين

translation: So they said, 'Our Lord, make [the distance] between our journeys longer,' and they wronged themselves; so We made them narrations and dispersed them in every way. Indeed in that are signs for everyone patient and grateful.
interpretation: This verse reflects on the consequences of the Children of Israel's ingratitude and impatience during their journey from Egypt. They requested longer journeys, which symbolically represents their desire for a more challenging path, possibly out of a lack of trust in God's plan. As a result of their self-inflicted hardship and disobedience, God scattered them and turned their story into a lesson for others. The verse serves as a reminder that patience and gratitude are essential virtues, as exemplified by the signs left for those who embody these qualities.
orig: فقالوا ربنا باعد بين أسفارنا وظلموا أنفسهم فجعلناهم أحاديث ومزقناهم كل ممزق إن في ذلك لآيات لكل صبار شكور

translation: And indeed, Iblees had proven true his assumption about them, so they followed him, except for a group of the believers.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the influence of Iblees (Satan) on humanity, highlighting how he successfully misled a large portion of people due to their susceptibility to his temptations and doubts. However, it also emphasizes the resilience of faith among a group of believers who resisted his deception, showcasing the importance of steadfastness in faith amidst widespread corruption and misguidance.
orig: ولقد صدق عليهم إبليس ظنه فاتبعوه إلا فريقا من المؤمنين

translation: And he had no authority over them, except that We might know who believes in the Hereafter from him who is in doubt about it. And your Lord is a Guardian over all things.
interpretation: This verse highlights the test of faith that humans undergo in this life. It suggests that the existence of evil or temptation, represented by Iblis (Satan), serves a divine purpose. It is not that Iblis has any real power over humans, but rather, his role is to distinguish those who truly believe in the Hereafter and remain steadfast in their faith from those who are uncertain or doubtful about it. This trial is part of God's plan, and He watches over everything, ensuring that the test is fair and that every action is accounted for.
orig: وما كان له عليهم من سلطان إلا لنعلم من يؤمن بالآخرة ممن هو منها في شك وربك على كل شيء حفيظ

translation: Say, 'Invoke those you have claimed [as gods] besides Allah.' They do not possess an atom's weight in the heavens or on the earth, and they do not have any share in either of them, nor is there for Him any assistant from among them.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and sovereignty of Allah over all creation, asserting that no other beings or deities possess any real power or influence in the universe. It challenges the polytheistic beliefs by highlighting that these claimed deities cannot even control the smallest particle, symbolized by an atom's weight, and have no partnership or support in the governance of the heavens and the earth. The verse serves as a call to monotheism, urging believers to recognize and worship only Allah, who alone has the power and authority over all things.
orig: قل ادعوا الذين زعمتم من دون الله لا يملكون مثقال ذرة في السماوات ولا في الأرض وما لهم فيهما من شرك وما له منهم من ظهير

translation: And intercession with Him will not benefit except for him whom He permits. [And this is] until, when fear is removed from their hearts, they will say [to one another], "What has your Lord said?" They will say, "The truth. And He is the Most High, the Grand."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the exclusivity and sovereignty of Allah in granting intercession. It underscores that no one can intercede with Allah on behalf of anyone else unless He specifically allows it, highlighting His ultimate authority and control over all matters. The verse also illustrates a scene in the hereafter where, after the initial fear subsides, the believers inquire about the divine decree, and the response affirms the truth of Allah's judgment, reinforcing His supreme status as the Most High and the Grand. This serves to remind believers of the importance of submitting to Allah's will and the certainty of His just and truthful rulings.
orig: ولا تنفع الشفاعة عنده إلا لمن أذن له حتى إذا فزع عن قلوبهم قالوا ماذا قال ربكم قالوا الحق وهو العلي الكبير

translation: Say, 'Who provides for you from the heavens and the earth?' Say, 'Allah.' And indeed, we or you are either on guidance or in clear error.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the dependency of all creation on Allah for sustenance, highlighting His role as the sole provider. It challenges the listener to reflect on the source of their provisions, leading to the acknowledgment of Allah's omnipotence. The latter part of the verse introduces a dichotomy between guidance and error, suggesting that while both parties (believers and non-believers) claim to be on the right path, only one group is truly guided, urging a deeper introspection into one's beliefs and actions.
orig: قل من يرزقكم من السماوات والأرض قل الله وإنا أو إياكم لعلى هدى أو في ضلال مبين

translation: Say, "You will not be asked about what we committed, nor will we be asked about what you did."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes individual accountability in the eyes of God. It suggests that on the Day of Judgment, each person will be responsible for their own actions and will not be questioned about the deeds of others. This underscores the principle of personal responsibility and the direct relationship between an individual and God, highlighting that one's salvation or condemnation is based solely on their own conduct.
orig: قل لا تسألون عما أجرمنا ولا نسأل عما تعملون

translation: Say, 'Our Lord will bring us together, then He will judge between us in truth. And He is the Judge, the All-Knowing.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the belief in the ultimate justice of Allah. It reassures believers that on the Day of Judgment, Allah will gather all people and will adjudicate between them with absolute fairness and knowledge. The titles 'the Judge' and 'the All-Knowing' highlight Allah's authority and omniscience, reinforcing the trust that Muslims should have in His divine judgment.
orig: قل يجمع بيننا ربنا ثم يفتح بيننا بالحق وهو الفتاح العليم

translation: Say, 'Show me those whom you have attached as partners with Him.' No! Rather, He is Allah, the Almighty, the All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse challenges the polytheists to present evidence for their belief in associating partners with Allah. It emphasizes the oneness of Allah, asserting that He alone possesses the attributes of being Almighty and All-Wise, thereby refuting the concept of polytheism and affirming the fundamental Islamic belief in the absolute uniqueness and supremacy of Allah.
orig: قل أروني الذين ألحقتم به شركاء كلا بل هو الله العزيز الحكيم

translation: And We have not sent you except as a mercy to all people, as a bearer of glad tidings and a warner, but most people do not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universal mission of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), indicating that his message of guidance, hope, and warning is meant for all of humanity. The phrase "but most people do not know" highlights the widespread ignorance or denial of this universal message, underscoring the challenge faced by the Prophet in conveying the divine message to a largely unreceptive audience.
orig: وما أرسلناك إلا كافة للناس بشيرا ونذيرا ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: And they say, 'When is this promise, if you are truthful?'
interpretation: This verse reflects the skepticism and impatience of those who doubt the prophecies and promises mentioned in the Qur'an. It highlights a common human reaction to divine promises, where people demand immediate proof or a specific timeline, challenging the truthfulness of the messengers. This questioning underscores the need for faith and patience in the unseen and the timing of divine events.
orig: ويقولون متى هذا الوعد إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Say, 'For you is an appointment for a Day which you cannot postpone for an hour nor advance.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability and precision of the Day of Judgment. It underscores that this appointed time is fixed by Allah and cannot be altered by human actions or desires, highlighting the absolute control Allah has over time and events. It serves as a reminder to believers of the certainty of the afterlife and the importance of preparing for it, as no one can delay or hasten this critical moment.
orig: قل لكم ميعاد يوم لا تستأخرون عنه ساعة ولا تستقدمون

translation: And those who disbelieved said, 'We will never believe in this Qur'an nor in that which was before it.' And if you could see when the wrongdoers are made to stand before their Lord, some of them will say to others, 'If it were not for you, we would have been believers.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the denial and arrogance of the disbelievers who reject the Qur'an and previous scriptures. It also illustrates the accountability and blame-shifting that occurs among them in the Hereafter. When faced with the consequences of their disbelief, the weaker ones among the disbelievers will blame the more arrogant ones for leading them astray, suggesting that without their influence, they might have believed. This underscores the theme of individual responsibility and the impact of negative influences on one's faith.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا لن نؤمن بهذا القرآن ولا بالذي بين يديه ولو ترى إذ الظالمون موقوفون عند ربهم يرجع بعضهم إلى بعض القول يقول الذين استضعفوا للذين استكبروا لولا أنتم لكنا مؤمنين

translation: Those who were arrogant said to those who were oppressed, 'Did we prevent you from guidance after it had come to you? No, you were criminals.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the denial of responsibility by the arrogant ones towards the oppressed. It suggests that when faced with accountability, the arrogant will attempt to shift blame onto the oppressed, claiming that the oppressed were inherently criminal and not guided, rather than acknowledging their own role in obstructing the path to guidance. This reflects a common human tendency to avoid self-blame and to project one's faults onto others, especially those in weaker positions.
orig: قال الذين استكبروا للذين استضعفوا أنحن صددناكم عن الهدى بعد إذ جاءكم بل كنتم مجرمين

translation: And those who were oppressed will say to those who were arrogant, "Rather, [it was your] conspiracy by night and day when you were ordering us to disbelieve in Allah and to attribute to Him equals." But they will [come to] conceal regret when they see the punishment; and We will put shackles on the necks of those who disbelieved. Will they be recompensed except for what they used to do?
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of accountability and the consequences of leading others astray. Those who were oppressed and followed the misguided leadership of the arrogant will, on the Day of Judgment, confront their leaders, attributing their disbelief to the deceitful plotting of these leaders. The verse underscores the regret that will be felt by the disbelievers upon witnessing the punishment, emphasizing that divine justice will be served through the symbolic act of placing shackles on the necks of the disbelievers. This imagery serves as a reminder that individuals will ultimately be recompensed based on their actions, reinforcing the Islamic principle of personal responsibility and the consequences of misguiding others.
orig: وقال الذين استضعفوا للذين استكبروا بل مكر الليل والنهار إذ تأمروننا أن نكفر بالله ونجعل له أندادا وأسروا الندامة لما رأوا العذاب وجعلنا الأغلال في أعناق الذين كفروا هل يجزون إلا ما كانوا يعملون

translation: And We sent to no town a warner but that its wealthy ones said: "We disbelieve in that with which you have been sent."
interpretation: This verse highlights the common reaction of the affluent and influential members of society to divine messages. It suggests that those who are comfortable and prosperous often reject the warnings and guidance brought by prophets because the messages challenge their status quo and materialistic values. The verse underscores the difficulty of changing the hearts and minds of those who are deeply entrenched in worldly pleasures and power, illustrating a recurring theme in the Qur'an about the resistance of the elite to spiritual reform.
orig: وما أرسلنا في قرية من نذير إلا قال مترفوها إنا بما أرسلتم به كافرون

translation: And they said, "We are more in wealth and children, and we will not be punished."
interpretation: This verse reflects the arrogance and false sense of security of those who believe that their material wealth and large families will protect them from divine punishment. It highlights a common human error of equating worldly success with divine favor, ignoring the spiritual and moral accountability that comes with such blessings.
orig: وقالوا نحن أكثر أموالا وأولادا وما نحن بمعذبين

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], "Indeed, my Lord extends provision for whom He wills and restricts [it]. But most of the people do not know."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine control over sustenance and provision, highlighting that Allah has the absolute power to increase or decrease the provision for anyone He chooses. It serves as a reminder to believers to trust in Allah's wisdom and not to be overly concerned with material wealth, as the distribution of provision is part of His greater plan. The phrase 'but most of the people do not know' underscores the common human tendency to overlook or misunderstand this aspect of divine governance, often leading to discontent or envy.
orig: قل إن ربي يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء ويقدر ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: And your wealth and your children are not that which bring you near to Us in position, except for him who believes and does righteousness - for them there will be the double reward for what they did, and they will be secure in the high dwellings.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that material possessions and familial ties do not inherently elevate one's status in the sight of Allah. Instead, true proximity to Allah and spiritual elevation are achieved through faith and righteous actions. Those who combine belief with good deeds are promised a multiplied reward and a secure place in the hereafter, symbolized by the 'high dwellings', indicating a state of peace and safety in the afterlife.
orig: وما أموالكم ولا أولادكم بالتي تقربكم عندنا زلفى إلا من آمن وعمل صالحا فأولئك لهم جزاء الضعف بما عملوا وهم في الغرفات آمنون

translation: And those who strive against Our signs, seeking to defeat them - those will be brought into the punishment.
interpretation: This verse addresses individuals who actively oppose and attempt to undermine the divine signs and revelations of Allah. It emphasizes that such actions are not only futile but also lead to severe consequences. The term 'strive against' suggests a deliberate and persistent effort to challenge or disprove the authenticity and truth of Allah's signs. The promise of being 'brought into the punishment' serves as a stern warning that such opposition will result in their inevitable facing of divine retribution, highlighting the seriousness with which Allah views attempts to subvert His messages.
orig: والذين يسعون في آياتنا معاجزين أولئك في العذاب محضرون

translation: Say, 'Indeed, my Lord extends provision for whom He wills of His servants and restricts [it] for him, and whatever thing you spend [in His cause] - He will replace it; and He is the best of providers.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sovereignty of Allah over the distribution of sustenance. It reassures believers that Allah has the power to increase or decrease provision according to His wisdom and will. Furthermore, it encourages generosity by promising that any expenditure made in the path of Allah will be replenished by Him, highlighting His role as the ultimate and most generous provider.
orig: قل إن ربي يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء من عباده ويقدر له وما أنفقتم من شيء فهو يخلفه وهو خير الرازقين

translation: And the Day He will gather them all together, then He will say to the angels, 'Was it you that these people used to worship?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the Day of Judgment when all beings will be gathered before Allah. It underscores the futility of idolatry by illustrating a scenario where Allah questions the angels about being worshipped by humans, emphasizing that the angels themselves will deny any association with such worship. This serves as a reminder of the oneness of Allah and the error of directing worship to anyone or anything other than Him.
orig: ويوم يحشرهم جميعا ثم يقول للملائكة أهؤلاء إياكم كانوا يعبدون

translation: They said, 'Glory be to You! You are our protector, not them. Rather, they used to worship the jinn; most of them were believers in them.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the acknowledgment by the inhabitants of Paradise that all glory belongs to Allah alone, and they recognize Him as their true protector and sustainer, not the false deities that others worshipped. It underscores the error of those who, in their ignorance, worshipped jinn, mistakenly believing in their power and divinity. The verse emphasizes the clarity and truth that comes with divine guidance, contrasting it with the misguided beliefs of the majority who followed such practices.
orig: قالوا سبحانك أنت ولينا من دونهم بل كانوا يعبدون الجن أكثرهم بهم مؤمنون

translation: So today no soul will have power (to do) any good or harm to another; and We will say to those who wronged, "Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny."
interpretation: This verse underscores the individual accountability on the Day of Judgment, where no one can benefit or harm another. It emphasizes that each person will face the consequences of their actions alone. The command to the wrongdoers to taste the punishment of the Fire, which they denied, serves as a stark reminder of the reality of divine retribution and the futility of denying the truth in this life.
orig: فاليوم لا يملك بعضكم لبعض نفعا ولا ضرا ونقول للذين ظلموا ذوقوا عذاب النار التي كنتم بها تكذبون

translation: And when Our clear verses are recited to them, they say, 'This is nothing but a man who wishes to divert you from what your forefathers were worshipping.' And they say, 'This is nothing but a fabricated lie.' And those who disbelieved said about the truth when it came to them, 'This is nothing but clear magic.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the reactions of the disbelievers to the Qur'anic revelations. It shows their denial and resistance to the truth by labeling the Prophet Muhammad as a mere man trying to mislead them from their ancestral traditions. Their accusations of the Qur'an being a fabricated lie and mere magic reflect their deep-seated rejection of divine guidance, illustrating the psychological and societal barriers to accepting new religious truths.
orig: وإذا تتلى عليهم آياتنا بينات قالوا ما هذا إلا رجل يريد أن يصدكم عما كان يعبد آباؤكم وقالوا ما هذا إلا إفك مفترى وقال الذين كفروا للحق لما جاءهم إن هذا إلا سحر مبين

translation: And We did not give them any scriptures which they were studying, nor did We send to them before you any warner.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the people being addressed had no prior divine scriptures or warnings before the arrival of the Prophet Muhammad. It highlights the unique role of the Prophet as the first messenger sent to them, indicating that they had no excuse for their disbelief since they were not previously given guidance or warned about the consequences of their actions.
orig: وما آتيناهم من كتب يدرسونها وما أرسلنا إليهم قبلك من نذير

translation: And those before them denied, yet they did not reach a tenth of what We had given them. So they denied My messengers; then how [terrible] was My denial.
interpretation: This verse reflects on the disbelief of past nations who rejected the messengers sent by Allah, despite being granted significant blessings and signs. The verse emphasizes that these nations did not even achieve a fraction of the favors bestowed upon them compared to what was given to others, yet they still chose disbelief. The rhetorical question at the end underscores the severe consequences of their rejection, highlighting the inevitability and intensity of divine retribution against those who deny the truth after clear evidence has been presented to them.
orig: وكذب الذين من قبلهم وما بلغوا معشار ما آتيناهم فكذبوا رسلي فكيف كان نكير

translation: Say, "I only advise you of one thing - that you stand up for Allah, in pairs and individually, then reflect: there is no madness in your companion; he is only a warner to you before a severe punishment."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of personal and communal reflection on the message of the Prophet Muhammad. It encourages Muslims to stand up for the worship and obedience of Allah, both in private and in groups, and to seriously consider the rationality and sincerity of the Prophet's warnings. The verse reassures believers that the Prophet is not insane but a clear warner of the impending severe punishment if they do not heed his message. It calls for a thoughtful examination of faith and a collective and individual commitment to righteousness.
orig: قل إنما أعظكم بواحدة أن تقوموا لله مثنى وفرادى ثم تتفكروا ما بصاحبكم من جنة إن هو إلا نذير لكم بين يدي عذاب شديد

translation: Say, "I do not ask of you for it any reward. It is yours. My reward is only from Allah, and He is witness over all things."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophet Muhammad's sincerity and selflessness in his mission. He declares that he seeks no worldly compensation for conveying the message of Islam, as his reward is solely from Allah. This highlights the purity of his intentions and the divine nature of his mission, reinforcing the idea that his role is to deliver the message, while the responsibility for guidance lies with Allah. The mention of Allah being a witness over all things serves to affirm the truthfulness of the Prophet's claim and the omnipresence of Allah's knowledge and justice.
orig: قل ما سألتكم من أجر فهو لكم إن أجري إلا على الله وهو على كل شيء شهيد

translation: Say, 'My Lord hurls the truth, [He is] the Knower of the unseen.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine authority and omniscience of Allah. By stating that Allah 'hurls the truth,' it signifies that truth originates from and is upheld by Allah alone. The phrase 'Knower of the unseen' underscores Allah's complete knowledge of all things, visible and invisible, reinforcing the belief that nothing is hidden from Him. This verse can be seen as a reassurance to believers of the ultimate triumph of truth over falsehood, guided by the all-knowing and all-powerful Creator.
orig: قل إن ربي يقذف بالحق علام الغيوب

translation: Say, 'The truth has come, and falsehood can neither initiate anything nor can it restore anything.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate triumph and permanence of truth over falsehood. It asserts that truth, once established, cannot be overturned or replaced by falsehood, which lacks the power to either begin or sustain anything meaningful or lasting. This serves as a reassurance to believers that the message of Islam, being the truth, will prevail despite any attempts by falsehood to challenge or undermine it.
orig: قل جاء الحق وما يبدئ الباطل وما يعيد

translation: Say, 'If I should err, I would err only against myself. But if I am guided, it is by what my Lord reveals to me. Indeed, He is Hearing and near.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes personal responsibility and divine guidance. It suggests that if the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) were to stray from the right path, the consequences would be borne by himself alone, highlighting individual accountability for one's actions. Conversely, his guidance comes directly from Allah, indicating that true guidance is a divine gift received through revelation. The attributes of Allah mentioned, 'Hearing and near,' reassure believers that Allah is always attentive to their prayers and close to them, ready to guide and support them.
orig: قل إن ضللت فإنما أضل على نفسي وإن اهتديت فبما يوحي إلي ربي إنه سميع قريب

translation: And if you could see when they will be terrified with no escape, and they will be seized from a near place.
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Judgment, emphasizing the sudden and inescapable nature of the event. The terror experienced by the disbelievers is highlighted, as they realize there is no way to flee from the consequences of their actions. The phrase 'seized from a near place' suggests that the punishment or reckoning will come unexpectedly and swiftly, underscoring the proximity and inevitability of divine justice.
orig: ولو ترى إذ فزعوا فلا فوت وأخذوا من مكان قريب

translation: And they said, 'We have believed in it,' and how will they receive admonition from a place far away?
interpretation: This verse highlights the insincerity of those who claim to believe in the message of the Qur'an but fail to truly internalize its teachings. Their claim of faith is superficial because they are not willing to be influenced or admonished by the divine message, which they perceive as distant and irrelevant to their lives. The verse critiques the hypocrisy of such individuals who verbally profess faith but do not allow the Qur'an to affect their hearts and actions.
orig: وقالوا آمنا به وأنى لهم التناوش من مكان بعيد

translation: And they have denied it before, and they cast from a distant place at the unseen.
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who reject the message of the Qur'an have historically denied the truth of previous revelations as well. The phrase 'they cast from a distant place at the unseen' metaphorically indicates that they make unfounded judgments and speculations about matters beyond their knowledge, particularly about the divine and the hereafter, from a position of ignorance and distance from the truth.
orig: وقد كفروا به من قبل ويقذفون بالغيب من مكان بعيد

translation: And a barrier will be set between them and that which they desire, as was done with their kind before. Indeed, they were in disquieting doubt.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual and psychological state of those who reject faith, indicating that their doubts and uncertainties create a barrier between them and the fulfillment of their desires, similar to what happened to previous disbelievers. It underscores the consequences of doubt and disbelief, suggesting that such a state not only distances one from divine guidance but also from achieving true satisfaction and peace in life.
orig: وحيل بينهم وبين ما يشتهون كما فعل بأشياعهم من قبل إنهم كانوا في شك مريب

translation: Praise be to Allah, the Originator of the heavens and the earth, Who made the angels messengers with wings, two, three, and four. He increases in creation what He wills. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence and creative power of Allah. By describing Him as the 'Originator of the heavens and the earth,' it highlights His role as the sole creator of the universe. The mention of angels with varying numbers of wings illustrates the diversity and complexity of Allah's creation, underscoring that He can create as He wills. The statement 'Allah is over all things competent' reaffirms His absolute ability to manage and control all aspects of creation, reinforcing the concept of His unlimited power and authority.
orig: الحمد لله فاطر السماوات والأرض جاعل الملائكة رسلا أولي أجنحة مثنى وثلاث ورباع يزيد في الخلق ما يشاء إن الله على كل شيء قدير

translation: What Allah opens to people of mercy, there is no one to withhold it; and what He withholds, there is no one to release it thereafter. And He is the Almighty, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and wisdom of Allah in distributing His mercy. It teaches that Allah's decisions regarding the bestowal or withholding of His mercy are final and cannot be altered by any other power. This underscores the concept of Tawheed (the Oneness of God) and His ultimate control over all affairs. The attributes of 'Almighty' and 'Wise' highlight that His actions are not only powerful but also perfectly reasoned, encouraging believers to trust in His divine plan and timing.
orig: ما يفتح الله للناس من رحمة فلا ممسك لها وما يمسك فلا مرسل له من بعده وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: O mankind, remember the favor of Allah upon you. Is there any creator other than Allah who provides for you from the heaven and earth? There is no deity except Him. So how are you deluded?
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder to all people of the blessings and provisions bestowed by Allah, emphasizing His role as the sole creator and sustainer. It challenges the belief in any other deity or source of sustenance, reinforcing the concept of Tawheed (the oneness of God). The rhetorical question about another creator underscores the absurdity of polytheism and idolatry, urging believers to reflect on their faith and recognize the undeniable signs of Allah's providence in the heavens and the earth. The verse concludes with a call to introspection, questioning how one can be misled or deluded away from this clear truth.
orig: يا أيها الناس اذكروا نعمت الله عليكم هل من خالق غير الله يرزقكم من السماء والأرض لا إله إلا هو فأنى تؤفكون

translation: And if they deny you, then indeed, messengers before you were denied; and to Allah return all matters.
interpretation: This verse reassures the Prophet Muhammad that if people reject his message, he should not feel disheartened, as previous prophets also faced denial. It emphasizes the ultimate sovereignty of Allah, reminding that all affairs and outcomes are in His hands, encouraging steadfastness and trust in divine wisdom.
orig: وإن يكذبوك فقد كذبت رسل من قبلك وإلى الله ترجع الأمور

translation: O mankind, indeed the promise of Allah is truth, so let not the worldly life delude you and let not the Deceiver deceive you about Allah.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder to all people that the promises made by Allah, including those about the Hereafter, are undoubtedly true and will come to pass. It warns believers not to be distracted or misled by the temporary attractions and pleasures of worldly life, which can divert one's focus from the eternal life to come. Additionally, it cautions against being deceived by Satan, who may attempt to mislead people about Allah's truth and promises, thus leading them astray from the path of righteousness and faith.
orig: يا أيها الناس إن وعد الله حق فلا تغرنكم الحياة الدنيا ولا يغرنكم بالله الغرور

translation: Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you; so take him as an enemy. He only invites his party to be among the companions of the Blaze.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the adversarial nature of Satan towards humanity, urging believers to recognize and actively oppose him. It highlights that Satan's ultimate goal is to mislead people into joining him in Hell, thereby stressing the importance of vigilance and resistance against his temptations.
orig: إن الشيطان لكم عدو فاتخذوه عدوا إنما يدعو حزبه ليكونوا من أصحاب السعير

translation: Those who disbelieve will have a severe punishment, and those who believe and do righteous deeds will have forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: This verse highlights the dichotomy between the outcomes for disbelievers and believers. It emphasizes that disbelief leads to a severe punishment, reflecting the gravity of rejecting faith. Conversely, for those who embrace faith and complement it with righteous actions, the promise is twofold: forgiveness for their sins and a significant reward in the hereafter. This underscores the importance of both faith and good deeds in achieving divine mercy and reward.
orig: الذين كفروا لهم عذاب شديد والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لهم مغفرة وأجر كبير

translation: Is one whom We have beautified his evil deeds so it seems pleasing to him, (like one who is rightly guided)? For Allah leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. So do not let yourself waste away in regret over them. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of divine guidance and misguidance. It suggests that some individuals may perceive their wrongful actions as good due to a deception or 'beautification' of those deeds in their eyes, which is a form of misguidance from Allah. This misguidance is contrasted with divine guidance, indicating that Allah has the ultimate authority over whom He guides to the right path and whom He allows to stray. The verse advises the Prophet Muhammad (and by extension, believers) not to grieve excessively over those who are misguided, as their actions and the consequences thereof are fully known to Allah. The underlying message is one of trust in Allah's wisdom and justice, encouraging patience and perseverance in the face of others' misguidance.
orig: أفمن زين له سوء عمله فرآه حسنا فإن الله يضل من يشاء ويهدي من يشاء فلا تذهب نفسك عليهم حسرات إن الله عليم بما يصنعون

translation: And Allah is He Who sends the winds, so they raise clouds, then We drive them to a dead land, and We revive therewith the earth after its death. Thus will be the resurrection.
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's power and ability to bring life from death, using the metaphor of rain reviving a barren land. Just as the rain brings life to the earth, Allah will resurrect the dead on the Day of Judgment, demonstrating His omnipotence and the certainty of the afterlife.
orig: والله الذي أرسل الرياح فتثير سحابا فسقناه إلى بلد ميت فأحيينا به الأرض بعد موتها كذلك النشور

translation: Whoever desires honor [through power] - then to Allah belongs all honor. To Him ascends good speech, and righteous work raises it. But those who plot evil deeds will have a severe punishment, and the plotting of those - it will perish.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sovereignty and ultimate power of Allah, stating that true honor and glory belong to Him alone. It teaches that the path to real honor is through righteous speech and deeds, which are pleasing to Allah and elevate one's status in His eyes. Conversely, those who engage in deceitful and evil actions will face severe consequences, and their schemes will ultimately fail. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to seek honor through piety and good actions, rather than through worldly power or manipulation, as all such efforts are futile in the face of divine judgment.
orig: من كان يريد العزة فلله العزة جميعا إليه يصعد الكلم الطيب والعمل الصالح يرفعه والذين يمكرون السيئات لهم عذاب شديد ومكر أولئك هو يبور

translation: And Allah created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop; then He made you pairs. And no female conceives or gives birth except with His knowledge. And no aged person is granted [additional] life nor is his lifespan curtailed except that it is in a register. Indeed, that is easy for Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's complete control and knowledge over the creation and lifecycle of human beings. It highlights the stages of human creation from dust to a sperm-drop, illustrating the miraculous nature of life's origin. The mention of pairs signifies the complementary nature of human relationships. Furthermore, the verse underscores that every aspect of life, from conception to the extension or reduction of one's lifespan, is predetermined and recorded by Allah. This serves to remind believers of Allah's omnipotence and the ease with which He manages all affairs, reinforcing the concept of divine decree and the submission to Allah's will.
orig: والله خلقكم من تراب ثم من نطفة ثم جعلكم أزواجا وما تحمل من أنثى ولا تضع إلا بعلمه وما يعمر من معمر ولا ينقص من عمره إلا في كتاب إن ذلك على الله يسير

translation: And not equal are the two seas: this one is fresh, sweet, and palatable to drink, and that one is salty and bitter. And from each you eat fresh meat and extract ornaments that you wear, and you see the ships sailing through them, so that you may seek of His bounty, and perhaps you will be grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the diversity and utility of the seas, which are a sign of God's creation and provision. The contrast between the fresh and salty seas underscores the variety in nature, each type serving different purposes. The fresh sea provides drinkable water, while the salty sea supports life that humans can use for food and adornment. The mention of ships navigating the seas emphasizes human ability to harness these natural resources for travel and trade, illustrating God's bounty. The verse encourages gratitude towards God for these blessings, reminding believers to appreciate and be thankful for the diverse provisions made available to them.
orig: وما يستوي البحران هذا عذب فرات سائغ شرابه وهذا ملح أجاج ومن كل تأكلون لحما طريا وتستخرجون حلية تلبسونها وترى الفلك فيه مواخر لتبتغوا من فضله ولعلكم تشكرون
