translation: He causes the night to enter into the day and the day to enter into the night, and He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running its course for an appointed term. That is Allah, your Lord; to Him belongs the dominion. And those you invoke besides Him do not possess even the skin of a date seed.
interpretation: This verse highlights the omnipotence and sovereignty of Allah, illustrating His control over the natural cycles of day and night, as well as the celestial bodies like the sun and the moon. Each of these elements follows a precise and predetermined course set by Allah, underscoring the order and purpose in His creation. The verse then contrasts this with the powerlessness of any other beings or deities that people might worship, emphasizing that only Allah has true dominion and authority. The mention of 'the skin of a date seed' serves as a metaphor for the utter insignificance of the power of any other entity compared to Allah's supreme power.
orig: يولج الليل في النهار ويولج النهار في الليل وسخر الشمس والقمر كل يجري لأجل مسمى ذلكم الله ربكم له الملك والذين تدعون من دونه ما يملكون من قطمير

translation: If you invoke them, they do not hear your invocation; and if they were to hear, they could not respond to you. And on the Day of Resurrection, they will disown your associating them [with Allah]. And none can inform you like [One] Acquainted [with all matters].
interpretation: This verse underscores the futility and error of idol worship. It explains that idols or false deities are incapable of hearing or responding to the pleas of their worshippers, highlighting their complete lack of power and divinity. On the Day of Judgment, these false deities will reject any association with those who worshipped them, leaving their followers without support. The verse concludes by affirming that only Allah, who is all-knowing, can provide true guidance and knowledge, emphasizing the importance of seeking truth from the one true God.
orig: إن تدعوهم لا يسمعوا دعاءكم ولو سمعوا ما استجابوا لكم ويوم القيامة يكفرون بشرككم ولا ينبئك مثل خبير

translation: O mankind, you are the ones who stand in need of Allah, while Allah is the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the total dependence of humanity on Allah for all their needs, highlighting the inherent weakness and neediness of humans in contrast to Allah's absolute self-sufficiency and perfection. It serves as a reminder for people to recognize their position of humility and gratitude towards Allah, who is not only independent of all needs but also worthy of all praise due to His sublime attributes.
orig: يا أيها الناس أنتم الفقراء إلى الله والله هو الغني الحميد

translation: If He wills, He can do away with you and bring forth a new creation.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute power and sovereignty over creation. It reminds believers that Allah has the capability to remove the current creation, including humanity, and replace it with an entirely new creation if He so chooses. This serves as a reminder of the transient nature of our existence and the importance of humility and obedience to Allah, acknowledging that our existence is contingent upon His will.
orig: إن يشأ يذهبكم ويأت بخلق جديد

translation: And that is not difficult for Allah.
interpretation: This verse underscores the omnipotence of Allah, indicating that nothing is beyond His capability or power. It serves as a reminder to believers of Allah's infinite ability to manage and control all aspects of creation, no matter how complex or challenging they may seem to humans.
orig: وما ذلك على الله بعزيز

translation: And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. And if a heavily laden soul calls [another] to [carry some of] its load, nothing of it will be carried, even if he should be a close relative. You can only warn those who fear their Lord unseen and establish prayer. And whoever purifies himself only purifies himself for his own soul; and to Allah is the [final] destination.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes individual accountability before God, highlighting that each person is responsible for their own actions and cannot be burdened by the sins or responsibilities of others, even if they are close relatives. It serves as a reminder that spiritual purification and righteousness are personal endeavors, undertaken for one's own benefit and ultimate return to Allah. The verse also underscores the importance of fearing God in secret and maintaining regular prayer as key aspects of a believer's life.
orig: ولا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى وإن تدع مثقلة إلى حملها لا يحمل منه شيء ولو كان ذا قربى إنما تنذر الذين يخشون ربهم بالغيب وأقاموا الصلاة ومن تزكى فإنما يتزكى لنفسه وإلى الله المصير

translation: And not equal are the blind and the seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the distinction between those who are spiritually blind and those who possess spiritual insight. It highlights that individuals who are unaware of or indifferent to divine guidance (the blind) are not on the same level as those who perceive and follow the truth (the seeing). This serves as a metaphor for the difference in spiritual states and the importance of seeking and attaining true understanding and enlightenment.
orig: وما يستوي الأعمى والبصير

translation: Nor the darknesses nor the light
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine transcendence, indicating that Allah is beyond the comprehension of human concepts such as darkness and light. It underscores the idea that God's nature is not bound by the limitations of the physical world or human understanding, highlighting His absolute uniqueness and incomparability.
orig: ولا الظلمات ولا النور

translation: Neither shade nor heat.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability and inescapability of the Day of Judgment, where neither the comfort of shade nor the harshness of heat will be of any avail or significance to the individuals facing their reckoning.
orig: ولا الظل ولا الحرور

translation: And not equal are the living and the dead. Indeed, Allah causes to hear whom He wills, but you cannot make hear those who are in the graves.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the distinction between the living and the dead, not only in a physical sense but also spiritually. The living are those who are responsive to Allah's message and guidance, while the dead are those who are unresponsive and heedless. The verse also highlights Allah's omnipotence in choosing who will be receptive to His message. The Prophet Muhammad cannot bring the dead back to life or make them hear, symbolizing that he cannot force faith upon those who are spiritually dead. This underscores the importance of personal choice and responsibility in accepting or rejecting divine guidance.
orig: وما يستوي الأحياء ولا الأموات إن الله يسمع من يشاء وما أنت بمسمع من في القبور

translation: You are only a warner
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of the Prophet Muhammad as a messenger whose primary duty is to warn people about the consequences of their actions in the hereafter. It underscores the limitation of his responsibility to conveying the message, rather than enforcing it, highlighting the concept of free will and individual accountability in Islam.
orig: إن أنت إلا نذير

translation: Indeed, We have sent you with the truth as a bringer of good tidings and a warner. And there was no nation that had not been warned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universal mission of the Prophet Muhammad, indicating that he was sent with the truth to deliver messages of hope and warning to all people. It also underscores the divine justice, as every community throughout history has been given a warner, ensuring that no nation can claim ignorance of the message of God.
orig: إنا أرسلناك بالحق بشيرا ونذيرا وإن من أمة إلا خلا فيها نذير

translation: And if they deny you, then those before them have denied. Their messengers came to them with clear proofs and with the Scriptures and with the enlightening Book.
interpretation: This verse reassures the Prophet Muhammad that he should not be disheartened by the rejection of his message by his contemporaries, as previous prophets faced similar disbelief. The mention of 'clear proofs,' 'Scriptures,' and 'the enlightening Book' emphasizes that despite the undeniable evidence and divine guidance provided to past nations, they still rejected their prophets. This highlights the recurring theme of human resistance to divine messages and the importance of steadfastness in faith.
orig: وإن يكذبوك فقد كذب الذين من قبلهم جاءتهم رسلهم بالبينات وبالزبر وبالكتاب المنير

translation: Then the disbelievers were taken; so how was My rejection!
interpretation: This verse reflects on the fate of those who disbelieved after the truth was made clear to them. It emphasizes the severe consequences they faced due to their rejection of faith. The rhetorical question 'how was My rejection!' underscores the intensity and inevitability of divine retribution, serving as a warning to others about the outcomes of disbelief.
orig: ثم أخذت الذين كفروا فكيف كان نكير

translation: Have you not seen that Allah sends down water from the sky, and We bring forth with it fruits of varying colors? And from the mountains are tracts, white and red of varying shades and [some] extremely black.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's creative power and the diversity in His creation. The mention of water from the sky leading to fruits of different colors symbolizes how divine provision can lead to a variety of outcomes and beauty in life. Similarly, the varied colors of the mountains, including white, red, and black, reflect the diversity and complexity of the natural world, reminding believers of the vastness and intricacy of Allah's creation, encouraging appreciation and reflection on His omnipotence and artistry.
orig: ألم تر أن الله أنزل من السماء ماء فأخرجنا به ثمرات مختلفا ألوانها ومن الجبال جدد بيض وحمر مختلف ألوانها وغرابيب سود

translation: And among people, beasts, and livestock are various colors. Similarly, only those of His servants who possess knowledge fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse highlights the diversity in creation, using the variety of colors in people, beasts, and livestock as an example. It then draws a parallel to the spiritual realm, indicating that true fear and reverence of Allah comes from knowledge. Those who are knowledgeable are more aware of Allah's greatness and thus have a deeper fear and respect for Him. The verse concludes by affirming Allah's attributes of being Exalted in Might and Forgiving, emphasizing His power and mercy.
orig: ومن الناس والدواب والأنعام مختلف ألوانه كذلك إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء إن الله عزيز غفور

translation: Indeed, those who recite the Book of Allah, establish prayer, and spend out of what We have provided for them, secretly and publicly, can expect a trade that will never fail.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of engaging with the Qur'an through recitation, maintaining regular prayers, and being charitable with one's wealth, whether in private or public. These acts are likened to a 'trade' that will never fail, suggesting that the rewards for such deeds in the hereafter are guaranteed and everlasting. The verse encourages believers to invest in their spiritual growth and good deeds, promising that such investments will yield eternal benefits.
orig: إن الذين يتلون كتاب الله وأقاموا الصلاة وأنفقوا مما رزقناهم سرا وعلانية يرجون تجارة لن تبور

translation: That He may give them their rewards and increase them from His bounty. Indeed, He is Forgiving and Appreciative.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's promise to reward the believers not only with what they have earned through their deeds but also to grant them additional favors out of His immense generosity. It emphasizes the divine attributes of forgiveness and appreciation, indicating that God values and acknowledges the efforts and intentions of His servants, rewarding them beyond their expectations. This serves as an encouragement for believers to continue their good deeds, knowing that God's mercy and appreciation are boundless.
orig: ليوفيهم أجورهم ويزيدهم من فضله إنه غفور شكور

translation: And that which We have revealed to you from the Book is the truth, confirming what was before it. Indeed, Allah, of His servants, is All-Aware, All-Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the authenticity and continuity of divine revelation. The Qur'an is described as the truth that corroborates previous scriptures, affirming its role as the final revelation. The mention of Allah being 'All-Aware' and 'All-Seeing' underscores His omniscience and vigilance over humanity, indicating that He is fully cognizant of the actions and needs of His servants. This reassures believers of the divine guidance's relevance and the accountability inherent in their actions under Allah's watchful eye.
orig: والذي أوحينا إليك من الكتاب هو الحق مصدقا لما بين يديه إن الله بعباده لخبير بصير

translation: Then We caused to inherit the Book to those whom We have chosen from among Our servants. And among them is he who wrongs himself, and among them is he who is moderate, and among them is he who is foremost in good deeds by Allah's permission. That is the great bounty.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine selection of certain individuals to be the bearers and inheritors of the divine message, emphasizing the diversity in their adherence to the guidance provided. It suggests that even among those chosen, there exists a spectrum of behavior: some may fall short and wrong themselves, others maintain a balanced approach, and some excel in righteousness. This diversity is permitted by Allah, illustrating that the opportunity to follow the divine path is a significant grace from Allah, and how one utilizes this opportunity varies, reflecting personal responsibility and the varying levels of faith and action among believers.
orig: ثم أورثنا الكتاب الذين اصطفينا من عبادنا فمنهم ظالم لنفسه ومنهم مقتصد ومنهم سابق بالخيرات بإذن الله ذلك هو الفضل الكبير

translation: Gardens of Eden which they will enter, adorned therein with bracelets of gold and pearls, and their garments therein will be of silk.
interpretation: This verse describes the rewards awaiting the righteous in the afterlife, symbolizing purity, beauty, and honor. The mention of gardens, gold, pearls, and silk underscores the luxurious and eternal nature of Paradise, reflecting the ultimate fulfillment and joy that believers will experience in the presence of Allah.
orig: جنات عدن يدخلونها يحلون فيها من أساور من ذهب ولؤلؤا ولباسهم فيها حرير

translation: And they will say, "Praise be to Allah, who has removed from us [all] sorrow. Indeed, our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative."
interpretation: This verse reflects the gratitude of the believers in the Hereafter, acknowledging Allah's mercy in relieving them of all forms of grief and hardship. It underscores the divine attributes of forgiveness and appreciation, emphasizing that Allah not only forgives sins but also appreciates and rewards the good deeds of His servants. This expression of praise serves as a reminder of the ultimate relief and joy awaiting the righteous in the afterlife.
orig: وقالوا الحمد لله الذي أذهب عنا الحزن إن ربنا لغفور شكور

translation: The One Who has settled us in the Home of Permanence out of His bounty. No toil will touch us therein, nor will fatigue touch us therein.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the ultimate reward of the believers in the afterlife, where they will reside in a state of eternal peace and comfort in Paradise. It emphasizes that this settlement is a gift from Allah's grace, and in this divine abode, the believers will be free from any form of hardship or exhaustion, highlighting the perfection and bliss of the Hereafter.
orig: الذي أحلنا دار المقامة من فضله لا يمسنا فيها نصب ولا يمسنا فيها لغوب

translation: And those who disbelieve will have the Fire of Hell, where they will neither be finished off so that they die, nor will its torment be lightened for them. Thus do We recompense every disbeliever.
interpretation: This verse underscores the severe consequences of disbelief in the Hereafter. It emphasizes that those who reject faith will face eternal punishment in Hell, where death offers no escape and no relief from the torment is granted. This is portrayed as a just recompense for their disbelief, highlighting the gravity of rejecting the divine message and the accountability in the afterlife.
orig: والذين كفروا لهم نار جهنم لا يقضى عليهم فيموتوا ولا يخفف عنهم من عذابها كذلك نجزي كل كفور

translation: And they will cry out therein, 'Our Lord, bring us out; we will do righteous deeds other than what we used to do.' Did We not grant you long enough life that whoever would be reminded therein could be reminded? And the warner had come to you. So taste [the punishment], for there is no helper for the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the regret and desperation of the disbelievers in the Hereafter, as they plead for another chance to perform good deeds, having realized the gravity of their past actions. It underscores the concept of accountability and the finality of the afterlife, where pleas for a second chance are futile. The rhetorical question about the length of life given and the presence of a warner emphasizes that they had ample opportunity to reflect and amend their ways during their lifetime, highlighting themes of divine justice and the consequences of ignoring guidance.
orig: وهم يصطرخون فيها ربنا أخرجنا نعمل صالحا غير الذي كنا نعمل أولم نعمركم ما يتذكر فيه من تذكر وجاءكم النذير فذوقوا فما للظالمين من نصير

translation: Indeed, Allah is Knower of the unseen of the heavens and the earth. Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's omniscience, highlighting that He has complete knowledge of all hidden and unseen matters in the universe, as well as the innermost thoughts and feelings of every individual. It serves as a reminder to believers of the importance of sincerity and purity of heart, knowing that nothing is hidden from Allah.
orig: إن الله عالم غيب السماوات والأرض إنه عليم بذات الصدور

translation: He is the One Who has made you successors on the earth. So whoever disbelieves, his disbelief will be against himself. And the disbelief of the disbelievers does not increase their Lord in anything except in hatred. And the disbelief of the disbelievers does not increase them except in loss.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of human beings as vicegerents or successors on earth, entrusted with the responsibility of managing and developing the world in accordance with divine guidance. The disbelief mentioned here is not just a rejection of faith but a failure to fulfill this entrusted role. Such disbelief harms the disbeliever himself, as it leads to divine displeasure and increases his own loss, both in this world and the hereafter. The verse underscores the severe consequences of disbelief, highlighting that it only results in further estrangement from God and personal detriment, reinforcing the importance of faith and righteous action.
orig: هو الذي جعلكم خلائف في الأرض فمن كفر فعليه كفره ولا يزيد الكافرين كفرهم عند ربهم إلا مقتا ولا يزيد الكافرين كفرهم إلا خسارا

translation: Say, "Have you considered your 'partners' that you call upon besides Allah? Show me what they have created from the earth, or do they have a share in the heavens? Or have We given them a scripture so they are supported by clear evidence from it?" Rather, the wrongdoers promise each other nothing but delusion.
interpretation: This verse challenges the polytheists to present evidence of their deities' creative powers or divine authority. It emphasizes the exclusivity of Allah's creation and sovereignty, questioning the legitimacy of associating partners with Him. The verse suggests that the claims of polytheists are baseless and that they mislead each other with false promises, highlighting the deceptive nature of idolatry and the importance of relying solely on the truth revealed in the Qur'an.
orig: قل أرأيتم شركاءكم الذين تدعون من دون الله أروني ماذا خلقوا من الأرض أم لهم شرك في السماوات أم آتيناهم كتابا فهم على بينت منه بل إن يعد الظالمون بعضهم بعضا إلا غرورا

translation: Indeed, Allah holds the heavens and the earth, lest they cease [to exist]. And if they were to cease, no one could hold them [in place] after Him. Indeed, He is Forbearing and Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's omnipotence and His role as the sustainer of the universe. It highlights that the existence and stability of the heavens and the earth are solely dependent on Allah's will. The verse also underscores His attributes of forbearance and forgiveness, indicating that despite His power to let the universe collapse, He chooses to maintain it out of His mercy and patience towards His creation.
orig: إن الله يمسك السماوات والأرض أن تزولا ولئن زالتا إن أمسكهما من أحد من بعده إنه كان حليما غفورا

translation: And they swore by Allah their strongest oaths that if a warner came to them, they would be more guided than any of the nations. But when a warner came to them, it increased them in nothing but aversion.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy and denial of those who claimed they would follow guidance if it were presented to them. When the Prophet Muhammad, the warner, came with the message of Islam, instead of accepting the guidance, they rejected it out of aversion and pride. This shows how human nature can lead to the rejection of truth despite prior claims of openness to it, emphasizing the importance of sincerity in faith.
orig: وأقسموا بالله جهد أيمانهم لئن جاءهم نذير ليكونن أهدى من إحدى الأمم فلما جاءهم نذير ما زادهم إلا نفورا

translation: Out of arrogance in the land and plotting of evil; and the plotting of evil will not encompass except its own people. So do they await except the way of the former peoples? For you will never find any change in the way of Allah, and you will never find any alteration in the way of Allah.
interpretation: This verse warns against the dangers of arrogance and evil plotting, emphasizing that such actions ultimately harm those who engage in them. It reminds believers that historical patterns show that those who oppose divine guidance face inevitable consequences, as exemplified by previous nations. The verse underscores the immutable nature of Allah's laws and the certainty of divine justice, encouraging adherence to righteousness and warning against the futility of trying to circumvent Allah's decrees.
orig: استكبارا في الأرض ومكر السيئ ولا يحيق المكر السيئ إلا بأهله فهل ينظرون إلا سنت الأولين فلن تجد لسنت الله تبديلا ولن تجد لسنت الله تحويلا

translation: Have they not traveled through the earth and observed how was the end of those before them? They were greater than them in power, and Allah is not to be frustrated by anything in the heavens or on the earth. Indeed, He is Knowing and Competent.
interpretation: This verse encourages reflection on the historical consequences faced by past civilizations that were once powerful but ultimately declined. It serves as a reminder of the omnipotence and omniscience of Allah, suggesting that no matter how strong a nation or individual may be, they are still subject to the divine will and knowledge of Allah. The verse underscores the importance of humility and recognition of Allah's ultimate power and wisdom in guiding human affairs.
orig: أولم يسيروا في الأرض فينظروا كيف كان عاقبة الذين من قبلهم وكانوا أشد منهم قوة وما كان الله ليعجزه من شيء في السماوات ولا في الأرض إنه كان عليما قديرا

translation: And if Allah were to punish people for what they earned, He would not leave on the earth any creature, but He defers them for a specified term. Then when their time arrives, then indeed, Allah is ever, of His servants, Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's mercy and patience towards humanity. Despite the sins and wrongdoings that people commit, Allah chooses not to immediately punish them, which would otherwise lead to the destruction of all life on earth. Instead, He grants them a respite until a predetermined time, allowing them the opportunity to repent and reform. This delay is a manifestation of His attribute of forbearance. However, the verse also serves as a reminder that Allah is fully aware of all actions and will ultimately hold everyone accountable when their appointed time comes.
orig: ولو يؤاخذ الله الناس بما كسبوا ما ترك على ظهرها من دابة ولكن يؤخرهم إلى أجل مسمى فإذا جاء أجلهم فإن الله كان بعباده بصيرا

translation: Ya Seen
interpretation: This chapter, known as Ya Seen, is often referred to as the heart of the Qur'an. It serves as a reminder and a call to reflection for believers, emphasizing the themes of resurrection, the mercy of Allah, and the importance of following the messengers. The opening letters, 'Ya Seen,' are among the mysterious letters (muqatta'at) whose meanings are known only to Allah, but they are believed to signify the miraculous nature of the Qur'an itself.
orig: يس

translation: And the Qur'an, the Wise
interpretation: This phrase emphasizes the Qur'an's attribute of wisdom, indicating that it contains profound guidance and knowledge that is beneficial for all aspects of life. It underscores the Qur'an's role as a source of wise counsel and divine insight for believers.
orig: والقرآن الحكيم

translation: Indeed, you are among the messengers.
interpretation: This verse affirms the prophethood of Muhammad, peace be upon him, indicating that he is part of the esteemed lineage of messengers sent by Allah to guide humanity. It underscores his role and authority as a divinely appointed messenger, connecting him to the tradition of prophets who came before him.
orig: إنك لمن المرسلين

translation: On a straight path
interpretation: This phrase refers to the path of righteousness and guidance that Muslims are encouraged to follow, which leads to the pleasure of Allah and ultimately to Paradise. It symbolizes the clear, direct, and unwavering way of life prescribed by Islam, free from deviations and distractions.
orig: على صراط مستقيم

translation: A revelation from the Almighty, the Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is a divine revelation sent down by Allah, who is described with the attributes of being Almighty (Al-Aziz) and Most Merciful (Al-Rahim). The term 'Almighty' highlights Allah's power and authority over all creation, while 'Most Merciful' underscores His compassion and kindness towards His creation. This dual emphasis serves to remind believers of the balance between divine power and mercy in the revelation of the Qur'an, encouraging a response of awe, reverence, and gratitude.
orig: تنزيل العزيز الرحيم

translation: So that you may warn a people whose fathers were not warned, so they are heedless.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the mission of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to warn a new generation whose ancestors did not receive the message of previous prophets. It highlights the state of unawareness and negligence among these people, indicating the urgency and importance of the prophetic message to guide them back to the path of righteousness.
orig: لتنذر قوما ما أنذر آباؤهم فهم غافلون

translation: Indeed, the word has come into effect upon most of them, so they do not believe.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the majority of people have been affected by a divine decree or prophecy which results in their disbelief. It implies a predestined outcome where most individuals are unable to embrace faith due to the fulfillment of God's word.
orig: لقد حق القول على أكثرهم فهم لا يؤمنون

translation: Indeed, We have put shackles on their necks, and they are up to their chins, so they are with their heads raised up.
interpretation: This verse metaphorically describes the state of those who are spiritually and intellectually constrained by their own disbelief and arrogance. The 'shackles on their necks' symbolize the limitations and burdens they impose upon themselves through their rejection of divine guidance. The phrase 'up to their chins' indicates that these constraints are severe and pervasive, affecting their ability to see and understand the truth. 'With their heads raised up' suggests a state of stubbornness and pride, where they are unwilling to lower their gaze in humility or submission to God's will. This imagery serves as a warning about the consequences of persistent denial and the importance of humility and openness to divine guidance.
orig: إنا جعلنا في أعناقهم أغلالا فهي إلى الأذقان فهم مقمحون

translation: And We have put before them a barrier and behind them a barrier and We have covered them, so they do not see.
interpretation: This verse metaphorically describes how Allah has placed obstacles or veils around those who are heedless or disbelieving, preventing them from perceiving the truth. The 'barriers' symbolize the spiritual and intellectual impediments that keep them from understanding and accepting the message of Islam. The covering over them signifies a state of being engulfed in ignorance or denial, which blinds them to the reality and guidance of Allah.
orig: وجعلنا من بين أيديهم سدا ومن خلفهم سدا فأغشيناهم فهم لا يبصرون

translation: It is the same to them whether you warn them or do not warn them, they will not believe.
interpretation: This verse indicates that there are individuals who are so entrenched in their disbelief that no amount of warning or guidance will change their hearts. It reflects the reality that some people have hardened their hearts against faith, and thus, the Prophet's mission to warn them will not affect their disbelief. This serves as a reminder to the Prophet and believers not to despair over those who choose to reject faith, as their disbelief is a result of their own choices and not a reflection of the effectiveness of the message.
orig: وسواء عليهم أأنذرتهم أم لم تنذرهم لا يؤمنون

translation: You warn only those who follow the Reminder and fear the Most Merciful unseen. So give them good tidings of forgiveness and a noble reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the specific audience of the Prophet Muhammad's message: those who adhere to divine guidance (the Reminder) and have a deep, unseen fear of Allah (the Most Merciful). It highlights the importance of internalizing faith and living according to divine principles out of genuine reverence for Allah, rather than for worldly gain. The promise of forgiveness and a noble reward serves as an encouragement for believers to maintain steadfastness in their faith and righteousness, reinforcing the ultimate goal of divine mercy and reward in the hereafter.
orig: إنما تنذر من اتبع الذكر وخشي الرحمن بالغيب فبشره بمغفرة وأجر كريم

translation: Indeed, it is We who give life to the dead and record what they have put forth and their traces, and all things We have enumerated in a clear register.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's omnipotence and meticulous record-keeping. It reassures believers that Allah has the power to resurrect the dead, and that every action and its consequences are meticulously recorded. The "clear register" refers to the preserved tablet where all deeds are documented, underscoring the accountability of every individual for their actions in this life.
orig: إنا نحن نحيي الموتى ونكتب ما قدموا وآثارهم وكل شيء أحصيناه في إمام مبين

translation: And present to them an example: the people of the town, when there came to them the messengers.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad to use the story of the people of the town as a parable or lesson for his community. The story of the town's people and their reaction to the messengers serves as a warning and a reminder of the consequences of rejecting divine guidance. It emphasizes the importance of heeding the messages brought by prophets and the potential outcomes of disbelief and disobedience.
orig: واضرب لهم مثلا أصحاب القرية إذ جاءها المرسلون

translation: When We sent to them two but they denied them, so We strengthened them with a third and they said, 'Indeed, we are messengers to you.'
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of the messengers sent to the people of Thamud. Initially, two messengers were sent, but they were rejected by the people. Subsequently, a third messenger, Saleh, was sent to reinforce the message. The verse highlights the persistence of divine guidance and the clear declaration of the messengers' mission, emphasizing the importance of heeding the warnings sent by God.
orig: إذ أرسلنا إليهم اثنين فكذبوهما فعززنا بثالث فقالوا إنا إليكم مرسلون

translation: They said, 'You are but humans like us, and the Most Merciful has not revealed anything. You are only telling lies.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the disbelief and denial of the Quraysh towards the Prophet Muhammad and his message. They rejected the divine origin of the Qur'an, asserting that Muhammad and his followers were merely human beings like themselves, and thus incapable of receiving revelation from God. This highlights a common theme in the Qur'an where those who oppose the prophets often challenge their human nature as a means to discredit their message, revealing their refusal to accept the truth out of arrogance and ignorance.
orig: قالوا ما أنتم إلا بشر مثلنا وما أنزل الرحمن من شيء إن أنتم إلا تكذبون

translation: They said, "Our Lord knows that we have been sent to you."
interpretation: This verse reflects the confidence and certainty of the messengers in their divine mission. They assert that their Lord is fully aware of their truthful purpose and divine appointment to convey the message to the people they are addressing. It underscores the theme of divine knowledge and the messengers' reliance on God's awareness of their sincerity and mission.
orig: قالوا ربنا يعلم إنا إليكم لمرسلون

translation: And Our duty is only to convey the clear message.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the responsibility of the Prophet Muhammad and the believers to clearly communicate the message of Islam. It highlights that their role is solely to deliver the message in a straightforward and unambiguous manner, without being responsible for how others choose to accept or reject it.
orig: وما علينا إلا البلاغ المبين

translation: They said, 'We consider you a bad omen. If you do not stop, we will surely stone you, and a painful punishment will surely touch you from us.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the reaction of the people of Prophet Hud to his warnings. Their statement, 'We consider you a bad omen,' indicates their superstition and their refusal to accept responsibility for their own actions, instead blaming the prophet for their misfortunes. The threat to stone him and inflict a painful punishment shows their hostility and readiness to use violence to suppress the truth. This illustrates the common challenge faced by prophets, where their message is met with denial and aggression from those who are unwilling to change their ways.
orig: قالوا إنا تطيرنا بكم لئن لم تنتهوا لنرجمنكم وليمسنكم منا عذاب أليم

translation: They said, "Your omen is with you. Is it because you were reminded? Rather, you are a transgressing people."
interpretation: This verse suggests that the people are attributing their misfortune to the prophet's reminders, but the response indicates that their bad omens are a result of their own actions and transgressions. It highlights the human tendency to blame external factors or divine messages for personal failures, instead of acknowledging their own excesses and wrongdoing.
orig: قالوا طائركم معكم أئن ذكرتم بل أنتم قوم مسرفون

translation: And there came from the farthest part of the city a man, hurrying, he said, 'O my people, follow the messengers.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of individual responsibility and the potential for personal transformation within a community. The man from the outskirts of the city represents an ordinary individual who, despite not being part of the established leadership or elite, recognizes the truth of the message brought by the messengers. His urgency and call to his people to follow the messengers illustrate the importance of personal initiative in guiding others towards righteousness. It underscores that divine guidance can inspire anyone to take a stand for truth, regardless of their social standing, and encourages believers to actively participate in spreading and upholding the message of God.
orig: وجاء من أقصى المدينة رجل يسعى قال يا قوم اتبعوا المرسلين

translation: Follow those who do not ask you for any reward and who are rightly guided.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to follow the guidance of those who are sincerely committed to the path of righteousness, without any ulterior motives or personal gain. It emphasizes the importance of seeking guidance from those whose intentions are pure and whose actions reflect true adherence to divine guidance.
orig: اتبعوا من لا يسألكم أجرا وهم مهتدون

translation: And what is [the matter] with me that I should not worship the One who created me and to Him you will be returned?
interpretation: This verse expresses a rhetorical question posed by Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) in the Qur'an, highlighting his unwavering faith and logical reasoning for worshipping Allah alone. It underscores the natural inclination of humans to worship their Creator, emphasizing that Allah is the originator of life and the ultimate destination to whom all will return. The verse serves as a reminder of the fundamental duty of humans to worship Allah, reinforcing the concept of Tawheed (the oneness of God) and the accountability of all beings on the Day of Judgment.
orig: وما لي لا أعبد الذي فطرني وإليه ترجعون

translation: Shall I take besides Him other gods? If the Most Merciful intends for me some adversity, their intercession would not avail me at all, nor could they save me.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility of worshipping any deity other than Allah. It highlights that no other gods or intercessors can protect or save a person from the harm or adversity that Allah might decree. The verse serves as a reminder of the absolute power and sovereignty of Allah, urging believers to rely solely on Him and to reject polytheism.
orig: أأتخذ من دونه آلهة إن يردن الرحمن بضر لا تغن عني شفاعتهم شيئا ولا ينقذون

translation: Indeed, I would then be in manifest error.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the speaker's acknowledgment that without guidance, they would be in a clear state of misguidance. It highlights the importance of divine guidance in avoiding evident falsehood and maintaining the right path.
orig: إني إذا لفي ضلال مبين

translation: Indeed, I have believed in your Lord, so listen to me.
interpretation: This verse expresses a declaration of faith by a speaker, likely a prophet or a messenger, affirming belief in the Lord of the people being addressed. The call to 'listen' emphasizes the importance of heeding the message being conveyed, suggesting a plea for the audience to pay attention to the divine guidance being offered through the speaker's faith and subsequent actions or teachings.
orig: إني آمنت بربكم فاسمعون

translation: It was said, 'Enter Paradise.' He said, 'Oh, I wish my people knew.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the moment of a believer's entry into Paradise, highlighting a profound sense of gratitude and a wish to share this joy with others. It underscores the importance of da'wah (invitation to Islam) and the believer's ongoing concern for the guidance of their community, even after achieving personal salvation. The believer's statement expresses a longing for his people to understand the truth and attain the same bliss, emphasizing themes of communal responsibility and the desire for collective salvation.
orig: قيل ادخل الجنة قال يا ليت قومي يعلمون

translation: My Lord has forgiven me and placed me among the honored ones.
interpretation: This verse reflects a profound sense of gratitude and humility, expressing the speaker's acknowledgment of divine forgiveness and the subsequent elevation to a position of honor. It underscores the belief in God's mercy and the transformative power of repentance, leading to spiritual elevation and honor in the sight of God.
orig: بما غفر لي ربي وجعلني من المكرمين

translation: And We did not send down against his people, after him, any hosts from the heaven, nor was it Our way to send down.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that after the destruction of the people of Lot, God did not send additional forces from the heavens to punish them further. It highlights God's justice and mercy, indicating that once a punishment is decreed and executed, it is not repeated or compounded. This reflects the principle that God's actions are measured and purposeful, not excessive or arbitrary.
orig: وما أنزلنا على قومه من بعده من جند من السماء وما كنا منزلين

translation: It was but one mighty blast, and behold! They were all silenced.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the instantaneous and overwhelming power of Allah's command. The 'mighty blast' refers to the moment of divine intervention that can extinguish life or bring about a significant change in an instant, emphasizing the fragility and temporality of human existence in the face of divine will. The sudden silencing of the people signifies the abrupt end that can come upon any community or individual when Allah decrees it, serving as a reminder of the ultimate power and authority of the Creator over all creation.
orig: إن كانت إلا صيحة واحدة فإذا هم خامدون

translation: O the regret for the servants! No messenger comes to them except that they mock him.
interpretation: This verse expresses deep sorrow and regret over the persistent rejection and mockery by people towards the messengers sent by Allah. It highlights a recurring human flaw where divine guidance is met with ridicule and disbelief, emphasizing the gravity of such a response and the missed opportunity for guidance and salvation.
orig: يا حسرة على العباد ما يأتيهم من رسول إلا كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them, which will never return to them?
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder to the disbelievers of the transient nature of worldly life and the certainty of divine judgment. It highlights Allah's power to destroy nations that go astray, urging people to reflect on the fate of past civilizations as a warning. The phrase 'which will never return to them' emphasizes the finality of divine punishment and the impossibility of reversing one's fate after death, encouraging a return to righteousness before it is too late.
orig: ألم يروا كم أهلكنا قبلهم من القرون أنهم إليهم لا يرجعون

translation: And indeed, all of them, every one, will be brought before Us.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of accountability in the hereafter. It assures that every individual, without exception, will be presented before Allah for judgment. This underscores the Islamic belief in the Day of Judgment where all souls will be gathered to account for their deeds, reinforcing the notion of divine justice and the ultimate gathering of all creation before their Creator.
orig: وإن كل لما جميع لدينا محضرون

translation: And a sign for them is the dead earth: We give it life and bring forth from it grain, from which they eat.
interpretation: This verse highlights the power and mercy of Allah, illustrating His ability to revive and sustain life. The transformation of dead earth into a fertile land that produces grain is presented as a clear sign of Allah's omnipotence and His role as the ultimate provider. It serves as a reminder for humans to recognize and appreciate the continuous cycle of life and sustenance that Allah facilitates, urging gratitude and faith in His divine capabilities.
orig: وآية لهم الأرض الميتة أحييناها وأخرجنا منها حبا فمنه يأكلون

translation: And We placed within it gardens of palm trees and grapevines, and We caused to gush forth within it springs.
interpretation: This verse highlights the blessings and provisions that Allah has bestowed upon the earth, specifically mentioning the cultivation of gardens with palm trees and grapevines, and the emergence of springs. It underscores the idea that the earth's fertility and resources are a divine gift, intended to sustain and benefit humanity. The mention of specific plants and water sources emphasizes the diversity and abundance of these blessings, reflecting Allah's generosity and care for His creation.
orig: وجعلنا فيها جنات من نخيل وأعناب وفجرنا فيها من العيون

translation: That they may eat of its fruit and from what their hands have worked. Will they not then be grateful?
interpretation: This verse highlights the blessings bestowed upon humanity, specifically the provision of sustenance from the earth's fruits and the results of their own labor. It serves as a reminder and a call to gratitude towards Allah for these provisions. The rhetorical question at the end emphasizes the expectation of thankfulness, urging believers to reflect on their blessings and respond with appreciation and worship.
orig: ليأكلوا من ثمره وما عملته أيديهم أفلا يشكرون

translation: Glory be to Him Who created all the pairs of what the earth grows, and of themselves, and of what they do not know.
interpretation: This verse praises Allah for His creation of diversity and pairs in all aspects of existence. It highlights the divine wisdom behind the creation of pairs not only in the plant life ("what the earth grows") but also in humans ("of themselves") and in things beyond human understanding ("what they do not know"). This emphasizes the vastness and complexity of Allah's creation, encouraging contemplation and appreciation of the unseen aspects of the universe and the interconnectedness of all things.
orig: سبحان الذي خلق الأزواج كلها مما تنبت الأرض ومن أنفسهم ومما لا يعلمون

translation: And a sign for them is the night: We strip from it the day, and behold, they are in darkness.
interpretation: This verse highlights the natural cycle of day and night as a sign of God's power and control over the universe. The transition from day to night, where the light is gradually 'stripped away', leaving people in darkness, serves as a reminder of the temporary nature of worldly conditions and the omnipotence of the Creator. It encourages reflection on the divine signs that are evident in the natural world, urging believers to recognize and appreciate God's majesty and to prepare for the spiritual darkness that can envelop those who ignore these signs.
orig: وآية لهم الليل نسلخ منه النهار فإذا هم مظلمون

translation: And the sun runs [on course] toward its stopping point. That is the decree of the Exalted in Might, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the precise and purposeful movement of the sun, which follows a predetermined path set by Allah. It underscores the divine wisdom and power behind the celestial order, emphasizing that all natural phenomena are under the control and knowledge of Allah, who is described as the Exalted in Might and the Knowing. The verse serves as a reminder of the meticulous planning and sovereignty of Allah over the universe.
orig: والشمس تجري لمستقر لها ذلك تقدير العزيز العليم

translation: And the moon, We have measured for it mansions (to traverse) till it returns like the old (and withered) palm-stalk.
interpretation: This verse reflects the divine order and precision in the universe, illustrating how the moon follows a meticulously ordained path through its phases, symbolizing the cyclical nature of life and the inevitability of return to a state of origin or decay, akin to the life cycle of a palm stalk.
orig: والقمر قدرناه منازل حتى عاد كالعرجون القديم

translation: It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night outstrip the day. They all float, each in an orbit.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the precise order and harmony in the universe established by Allah. It highlights that each celestial body follows its own designated path without deviation, symbolizing the flawless design and control of the Creator over all creation. This order serves as a reminder of the need for humans to adhere to the divine laws set by Allah, reflecting the same precision and obedience in their lives.
orig: لا الشمس ينبغي لها أن تدرك القمر ولا الليل سابق النهار وكل في فلك يسبحون

translation: And a sign for them is that We carried their offspring in the laden ship.
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Noah's Ark, highlighting it as a sign of God's power and mercy. The 'laden ship' symbolizes the Ark, which carried the believers and representatives of all living creatures, demonstrating God's ability to save and sustain life amidst destruction. It serves as a reminder of divine intervention and the importance of faith and obedience to God's commands.
orig: وآية لهم أنا حملنا ذريتهم في الفلك المشحون

translation: And We created for them from the like of it what they ride.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's provision and creativity in providing means of transportation for humans, crafted from materials similar to those used in other creations. It underscores the divine wisdom in designing the world to facilitate human life and movement, reflecting on the interconnectedness of creation and human utility.
orig: وخلقنا لهم من مثله ما يركبون

translation: And if We will, We could drown them, so there would be no crying out for them, nor would they be saved.
interpretation: This verse underscores the omnipotence of Allah, emphasizing His ability to enact His will at any moment. It serves as a reminder of the vulnerability of human beings to divine decree, highlighting that no one can escape or alter Allah's decisions. The mention of drowning specifically might relate to historical events or serve as a metaphor for sudden, overwhelming divine action, illustrating that when Allah decides to act, human efforts to resist or seek help are futile.
orig: وإن نشأ نغرقهم فلا صريخ لهم ولا هم ينقذون

translation: Except for mercy from Us and provision until a time
interpretation: This verse suggests that the blessings and provisions granted to humans are ultimately from God's mercy, and they are temporary, lasting only until a designated time. It reminds believers to be grateful for what they have and to recognize that all good things come from God's grace, which should not be taken for granted.
orig: إلا رحمة منا ومتاعا إلى حين

translation: And when it is said to them, "Fear what is before you and what is behind you; perhaps you may receive mercy."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of being mindful and cautious of both the consequences of one's past actions and the potential outcomes of future deeds. It serves as a reminder to constantly be aware of one's moral and ethical responsibilities in all aspects of life, suggesting that such awareness and adherence to righteousness could lead to divine mercy and forgiveness.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم اتقوا ما بين أيديكم وما خلفكم لعلكم ترحمون

translation: And no sign comes to them from among the signs of their Lord except that they turn away from it.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubbornness and denial of those who reject faith. Despite being presented with clear signs and evidence from Allah, they consistently choose to ignore or dismiss these signs, indicating a deliberate turning away from the truth out of arrogance or disbelief.
orig: وما تأتيهم من آية من آيات ربهم إلا كانوا عنها معرضين

translation: And when it is said to them, 'Spend from what Allah has provided you,' those who disbelieve say to those who believe, 'Should we feed one whom, if Allah had willed, He would have fed? You are not but in clear error.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the attitude of disbelief and arrogance among those who reject faith. When encouraged to give charity from their provisions, which are seen as blessings from Allah, the disbelievers mock the believers, questioning the logic of feeding those whom they believe Allah should have fed if He willed. This response not only shows their lack of compassion but also their misunderstanding of human responsibility and divine will, suggesting that they view the believers' acts of charity as futile and misguided, thereby accusing them of being in clear error.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم أنفقوا مما رزقكم الله قال الذين كفروا للذين آمنوا أنطعم من لو يشاء الله أطعمه إن أنتم إلا في ضلال مبين

translation: And they say, 'When will this promise be fulfilled, if you are truthful?'
interpretation: This verse reflects the skepticism and impatience of the disbelievers towards the prophetic warnings about the Day of Judgment. It highlights their challenge to the Prophet Muhammad, demanding proof of the promised events to test the truthfulness of his message. This questioning underscores a deeper theme of faith versus doubt, illustrating how disbelief can lead to a demand for immediate signs rather than acceptance of divine timing and wisdom.
orig: ويقولون متى هذا الوعد إن كنتم صادقين

translation: They await only one blast which will seize them while they are disputing.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the disbelievers are heedless of the impending divine punishment, engrossed in their worldly disputes and arguments. The 'one blast' refers to the sudden and inevitable event of the Day of Judgment, which will come unexpectedly and catch them in the midst of their mundane concerns, emphasizing the urgency of preparing for the hereafter rather than being distracted by temporal matters.
orig: ما ينظرون إلا صيحة واحدة تأخذهم وهم يخصمون

translation: So they will not be able to make bequests, nor will they return to their families.
interpretation: This verse highlights the finality and isolation of death, emphasizing that once a person dies, they cannot influence worldly affairs or return to their loved ones. It serves as a reminder of the importance of preparing for the afterlife, as worldly connections and possessions become irrelevant after death.
orig: فلا يستطيعون توصية ولا إلى أهلهم يرجعون

translation: And the Trumpet will be blown, and at once from the graves they will hasten to their Lord.
interpretation: This verse describes the event of the Day of Resurrection when the Trumpet is blown, signaling the end of the world and the beginning of the afterlife. The blowing of the Trumpet causes the dead to rise from their graves and rush towards their Lord for judgment. It emphasizes the suddenness and inevitability of this event, highlighting the power of Allah to resurrect and gather all souls.
orig: ونفخ في الصور فإذا هم من الأجداث إلى ربهم ينسلون

translation: They will say, 'Woe to us! Who has raised us up from our sleeping place? This is what the Most Merciful had promised, and the messengers spoke the truth.'
interpretation: This verse depicts the moment of resurrection when the disbelievers are awakened from their graves. Their exclamation of 'Woe to us!' reflects their regret and realization of the truth of the Hereafter, which they had previously denied. The acknowledgment that this event was promised by Allah, the Most Merciful, and that the messengers had indeed spoken the truth, underscores the theme of divine justice and the fulfillment of God's promises. It serves as a reminder to believers of the inevitability of the Day of Judgment and the importance of heeding the warnings of the prophets.
orig: قالوا يا ويلنا من بعثنا من مرقدنا هذا ما وعد الرحمن وصدق المرسلون

translation: It was but one shout, and behold, they were all brought before Us.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the power and immediacy of Allah's command. The "one shout" symbolizes the finality and swiftness of divine judgment, where all souls are gathered before Allah without delay. It underscores the notion that the transition from life to the afterlife can be sudden, emphasizing the importance of readiness for the Day of Judgment.
orig: إن كانت إلا صيحة واحدة فإذا هم جميع لدينا محضرون

translation: So today no soul will be wronged in anything, nor will you be recompensed except for what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the justice of the Day of Judgment, where every individual will be treated fairly and will only receive the consequences of their own actions. It underscores the principle of personal accountability in Islam, where no one will be wronged or rewarded unjustly; each person's fate will be determined solely by their deeds.
orig: فاليوم لا تظلم نفس شيئا ولا تجزون إلا ما كنتم تعملون

translation: Indeed, the companions of Paradise, today, are busy in amusement.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the state of joy and contentment experienced by the inhabitants of Paradise. The term 'busy in amusement' suggests that they are fully engaged in delightful and pleasurable activities, reflecting the ultimate reward and happiness promised to the righteous. It emphasizes the contrast between the worldly life's struggles and the eternal bliss of the afterlife.
orig: إن أصحاب الجنة اليوم في شغل فاكهون

translation: They and their spouses are in shades, reclining on couches.
interpretation: This verse describes the blissful state of the righteous in Paradise, where they enjoy the comfort and tranquility of being shaded and reclining on luxurious couches alongside their spouses, symbolizing the ultimate reward and peace after a life of faith and good deeds.
orig: هم وأزواجهم في ظلال على الأرائك متكئون

translation: For them therein are fruits, and they will have whatever they call for.
interpretation: This verse describes the bountiful rewards awaiting the righteous in Paradise. The mention of 'fruits' symbolizes the abundance and variety of pleasures and delights available to them. The phrase 'whatever they call for' indicates that their desires will be instantly fulfilled, reflecting the ultimate satisfaction and contentment in the afterlife. This underscores the concept of divine generosity and the fulfillment of all wishes in the Hereafter.
orig: لهم فيها فاكهة ولهم ما يدعون

translation: Peace, a word from a Merciful Lord.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of peace as a divine message from Allah, who is described as the Most Merciful. It suggests that peace is not just a human aspiration but a blessing and a directive from God, reflecting His mercy and compassion towards His creation. The use of 'word' here signifies the power and sanctity of peace in the divine order.
orig: سلام قولا من رب رحيم

translation: And be separated today, O criminals!
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Day of Judgment when sinners will be distinctly separated from the righteous. It highlights the inevitability of accountability and the clear distinction that will be made between those who have committed crimes and those who have lived righteously. The command to 'be separated' underscores the finality and the immediate nature of this separation on that day.
orig: وامتازوا اليوم أيها المجرمون

translation: Did I not enjoin upon you, O children of Adam, that you not worship Satan - indeed, he is to you a clear enemy?
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder from Allah to all of humanity, represented by the children of Adam, about the fundamental prohibition against worshipping Satan. It emphasizes the clear enmity of Satan towards humans, highlighting that following him leads to spiritual ruin. The verse underscores the importance of obedience to Allah's commands and the recognition of Satan's deceptive nature, urging believers to stay vigilant against his influence.
orig: ألم أعهد إليكم يا بني آدم أن لا تعبدوا الشيطان إنه لكم عدو مبين

translation: And that you should worship Me. This is the straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the centrality of worshipping Allah alone as the core of the straight path in Islam. It suggests that true guidance and righteousness are achieved through the devotion and submission to Allah, indicating that all other forms of worship or deviation from this path lead away from the straight and correct way of life.
orig: وأن اعبدوني هذا صراط مستقيم

translation: And certainly, We have destroyed many generations before you. Did they not come to you or did they not perceive?
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of ignoring divine guidance. It points out that many past nations were destroyed due to their disbelief and failure to heed the warnings of their prophets. The rhetorical question at the end emphasizes the importance of reflection and understanding, urging the current generation to learn from the mistakes of those who came before them and to recognize the signs of God's power and mercy.
orig: ولقد أضل منكم جبلا كثيرا أفلم تكونوا تعقلون

translation: This is Hell, which you were promised.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder and a warning to the disbelievers about the reality of Hell, which was foretold to them. It emphasizes the certainty and inevitability of the punishment that awaits those who reject faith, underscoring the importance of heeding the warnings given in the Qur'an.
orig: هذه جهنم التي كنتم توعدون

translation: Taste it today for what you used to deny.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequence of disbelief and rejection of faith. It suggests that on the Day of Judgment, those who denied the truth will experience the punishment they were warned about, as a direct result of their denial. The use of "taste" implies a direct and personal experience of the repercussions of their actions, underscoring the accountability for one's choices in the afterlife.
orig: اصلوها اليوم بما كنتم تكفرون

translation: Today We will seal their mouths, and their hands will speak to Us, and their feet will bear witness to what they used to earn.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the Day of Judgment, where the truth will be inescapable. The sealing of the mouths signifies that individuals will be unable to lie or make excuses for their actions. Instead, their own body parts, metaphorically speaking, will testify against them, indicating the undeniable evidence of their deeds. This emphasizes the concept of accountability and the detailed recording of one's actions in the afterlife.
orig: اليوم نختم على أفواههم وتكلمنا أيديهم وتشهد أرجلهم بما كانوا يكسبون

translation: And if We willed, We could have wiped out their eyes, so they would race to the path, but how would they see?
interpretation: This verse highlights the absolute power of Allah over human perception and guidance. It suggests that if Allah chose to, He could remove the ability to see from people, rendering them unable to follow the right path despite their efforts. The rhetorical question at the end emphasizes the futility of human endeavor without divine guidance, underscoring the dependence of humans on Allah's mercy and direction for true vision and understanding.
orig: ولو نشاء لطمسنا على أعينهم فاستبقوا الصراط فأنى يبصرون

translation: And if We willed, We could have immobilized them in their places; then they would not be able to proceed, nor could they return.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's absolute power over creation. It suggests that if God chose to, He could render humans completely immobile, unable to move forward or backward, illustrating His control over human actions and the universe. This serves as a reminder of human dependence on God's will and mercy for their every movement and action.
orig: ولو نشاء لمسخناهم على مكانتهم فما استطاعوا مضيا ولا يرجعون

translation: And whom We grant long life, We reverse him in creation. Will they not then understand?
interpretation: This verse highlights the natural process of aging as a sign of God's power and a reminder of human vulnerability. It suggests that as people grow older, their physical and mental faculties decline, reversing the development they experienced in youth. The rhetorical question at the end urges people to reflect on this phenomenon and recognize the wisdom and inevitability of God's decree, encouraging a deeper understanding and appreciation of life's transient nature.
orig: ومن نعمره ننكسه في الخلق أفلا يعقلون

translation: And We did not teach him poetry, nor is it befitting for him. It is not but a reminder and a clear Qur'an.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is not a work of poetry, which was a common form of expression among the Arabs at the time of its revelation. Instead, it asserts that the Qur'an's purpose is to serve as a reminder and a clear message from God, focusing on guidance and truth rather than literary embellishment. This highlights the divine origin and the serious nature of the Qur'an, distinguishing it from human compositions.
orig: وما علمناه الشعر وما ينبغي له إن هو إلا ذكر وقرآن مبين

translation: That he may warn those who are alive and that the word may be proved true against the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the dual purpose of divine revelation: to serve as a warning to those who are spiritually alive and receptive, urging them towards righteousness and faith, and to confirm the inevitability of divine judgment upon those who reject the message, thereby fulfilling the prophecy concerning the disbelievers.
orig: لينذر من كان حيا ويحق القول على الكافرين

translation: Have they not seen that We have created for them from what Our hands have made, livestock, and they are their owners?
interpretation: This verse highlights the blessings and provisions that Allah has bestowed upon humanity. It specifically points out the creation of livestock, which humans have been given dominion over. The verse invites reflection on the divine origin of these provisions and the responsibility that comes with ownership, urging gratitude and proper stewardship of the resources provided by Allah.
orig: أولم يروا أنا خلقنا لهم مما عملت أيدينا أنعاما فهم لها مالكون

translation: And We have subjected them to them, so some of them they ride, and some of them they eat.
interpretation: This verse highlights the blessings and provisions that Allah has bestowed upon humanity. It specifically refers to the animals that have been made subservient to humans, allowing them to use these creatures for transportation and as a source of food. This demonstrates Allah's mercy and the interconnectedness of creation, where certain elements of nature are designed to support human life and facilitate their activities.
orig: وذللناها لهم فمنها ركوبهم ومنها يأكلون

translation: And for them therein are fruits, and they have whatever they desire. Will they not then give thanks?
interpretation: This verse highlights the blessings and provisions that Allah has bestowed upon humanity, emphasizing the abundance of fruits and desires fulfilled in the Hereafter. It poses a rhetorical question to provoke reflection on gratitude, urging believers to recognize and appreciate these divine gifts and to express thankfulness to Allah for His generosity and mercy.
orig: ولهم فيها منافع ومشارب أفلا يشكرون

translation: And they have taken gods besides Allah, hoping that they might be helped.
interpretation: This verse critiques the practice of polytheism, where individuals worship multiple deities in addition to or instead of Allah. It suggests that people turn to these false gods with the mistaken belief that they will provide support or assistance. The verse highlights the futility and error of such beliefs, emphasizing that true help and support can only come from Allah alone.
orig: واتخذوا من دون الله آلهة لعلهم ينصرون

translation: They will not be able to help them, and they themselves will be brought as a defeated army.
interpretation: This verse highlights the powerlessness of false deities or idols that people might worship. It suggests that these entities are incapable of providing any real assistance or protection to their followers. Instead, on the Day of Judgment, these false deities will be presented as a defeated army, unable to defend themselves, let alone their worshippers. This underscores the futility of relying on anything other than the one true God, Allah, for support and salvation.
orig: لا يستطيعون نصرهم وهم لهم جند محضرون

translation: So let not their speech grieve you. Indeed, We know what they conceal and what they declare.
interpretation: This verse is a reassurance to the Prophet Muhammad from Allah, indicating that he should not be distressed by the words or actions of those who oppose him. The comfort lies in the divine knowledge that Allah is fully aware of the hidden intentions and public declarations of the adversaries. This awareness underscores the omnipotence and omniscience of Allah, suggesting that justice and truth will ultimately prevail, and thus, there is no need for the Prophet to be disheartened by the current opposition.
orig: فلا يحزنك قولهم إنا نعلم ما يسرون وما يعلنون

translation: Has not man seen that We created him from a drop of sperm? Yet behold! He is an open disputant.
interpretation: This verse highlights the irony and ingratitude of human beings. Despite being created from something as insignificant as a drop of sperm, humans often engage in disputes and arguments against the truth and the signs of God, showing a lack of appreciation for their own creation and existence. It serves as a reminder of human vulnerability and the need for humility before the Creator.
orig: أولم ير الإنسان أنا خلقناه من نطفة فإذا هو خصيم مبين

translation: And he has set forth for us an example, and forgotten his own creation. He says, 'Who can give life to bones when they are decayed?'
interpretation: This verse critiques the disbelief of those who question the power of Allah to resurrect the dead. It highlights the irony and forgetfulness of such individuals who marvel at the possibility of reviving decayed bones, yet fail to reflect on their own creation by Allah. The verse underscores the theme of resurrection and the omnipotence of Allah, emphasizing that the same power that created humans from nothing can certainly bring them back to life after death.
orig: وضرب لنا مثلا ونسي خلقه قال من يحيي العظام وهي رميم

translation: Say, 'He will give it life who produced it the first time; and He is, of all creation, Knowing.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and knowledge of Allah, affirming that the same God who created life initially has the ability to revive it. It reassures believers of the resurrection and underscores Allah's complete understanding and control over all aspects of creation, reinforcing the concept of tawhid (the oneness of God) and His omnipotence.
orig: قل يحييها الذي أنشأها أول مرة وهو بكل خلق عليم

translation: He who made for you from the green tree fire, and behold, you kindle from it.
interpretation: This verse highlights the miraculous nature of fire, which can be derived from the seemingly opposite element of a green tree, symbolizing the hidden potential and blessings that Allah has placed in creation. It serves as a reminder of Allah's power to transform and provide for humanity in ways that might seem unexpected or paradoxical.
orig: الذي جعل لكم من الشجر الأخضر نارا فإذا أنتم منه توقدون

translation: Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the like of them? Yes, indeed! He is the Creator, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence and omniscience of Allah. It challenges the disbelief of those who doubt Allah's ability to resurrect humans by drawing a parallel between the creation of the vast universe and the creation of human beings. The verse affirms that just as Allah has the power to create the heavens and the earth, He is fully capable of recreating humans after their death. The attributes of being the 'Creator' and 'All-Knowing' highlight His absolute power and complete knowledge, reinforcing the belief in the Day of Resurrection and the continuity of His creative power.
orig: أوليس الذي خلق السماوات والأرض بقادر على أن يخلق مثلهم بلى وهو الخلاق العليم

translation: His command is only when He intends a thing that He says to it, "Be," and it is.
interpretation: This verse highlights the absolute power and omnipotence of Allah. It illustrates that Allah's will is immediate and effective; He needs only to command something to exist, and it comes into being instantly. This underscores the concept of Allah's sovereignty over creation, where His mere utterance brings things into existence, reflecting His unlimited power and the simplicity of His divine command.
orig: إنما أمره إذا أراد شيئا أن يقول له كن فيكون

translation: So exalted is He in whose hand is the dominion of all things, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and majesty of Allah, indicating that He has complete control over everything in existence. The phrase 'in whose hand is the dominion of all things' signifies Allah's omnipotence and the fact that nothing occurs without His will. The latter part, 'and to Him you will be returned,' serves as a reminder of the ultimate return to Allah for judgment, underscoring the accountability of all beings for their actions in this life.
orig: فسبحان الذي بيده ملكوت كل شيء وإليه ترجعون

translation: And the arrangers [of ranks] arrange.
interpretation: This verse refers to the angels who are organized in ranks and carry out their duties in a disciplined manner. It highlights the order and precision in the celestial realm, emphasizing the structured nature of divine command and the obedience of these celestial beings.
orig: والصافات صفا

translation: Then the ones who cause to quake, a quaking.
interpretation: This verse refers to the angels who will sound the Trumpet on the Day of Judgment, causing a tremendous quaking that will shake the earth and the heavens, signaling the end of the world and the beginning of the resurrection.
orig: فالزاجرات زجرا

translation: So the latter generations
interpretation: This verse refers to the generations that come after the initial group of believers or a particular event, emphasizing the continuity and succession of faith and responsibility across time. It highlights the importance of later generations in maintaining and propagating the message and values established by their predecessors.
orig: فالتاليات ذكرا

translation: Indeed, your god is One
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental Islamic belief in the oneness of God (Tawhid). It asserts that there is only one deity worthy of worship, reinforcing the concept that all forms of polytheism or associating partners with God are false. This declaration serves as a reminder to believers to maintain purity in their faith and devotion to the singular, unique God.
orig: إن إلهكم لواحد

translation: Lord of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them, and Lord of the Easts.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and omnipresence of Allah. By mentioning His lordship over the heavens, the earth, and everything in between, it underscores His complete control and authority over the entire universe. The reference to 'the Easts' (plural in Arabic) suggests the multiplicity of directions from which the sun rises throughout the year, symbolizing Allah's dominion over all aspects of creation and the passage of time. This verse serves to remind believers of Allah's all-encompassing power and the necessity of submitting to His will.
orig: رب السماوات والأرض وما بينهما ورب المشارق

translation: Indeed, We have adorned the nearest heaven with an adornment of stars
interpretation: This verse highlights the beauty and order of the universe, reflecting the divine wisdom and power of Allah. The adornment of the sky with stars serves as a reminder of Allah's creative majesty and the intricate design of creation, inspiring awe and contemplation among observers.
orig: إنا زينا السماء الدنيا بزينة الكواكب

translation: And protected from every rebellious devil
interpretation: This verse highlights the sanctity and purity of the Qur'an's revelation, emphasizing that it was safeguarded from any interference by malevolent forces, specifically devils who might seek to corrupt or distort the divine message. It underscores the divine protection over the prophetic mission and the integrity of the scripture.
orig: وحفظا من كل شيطان مارد

translation: They will not listen to the exalted assembly, and they will be pelted from every side.
interpretation: This verse describes the fate of the jinn who tried to eavesdrop on the heavenly discussions. They are prevented from hearing the secrets of the higher assembly of angels, and as a punishment, they are attacked and driven away from all directions, symbolizing their complete exclusion and the protection of divine secrets.
orig: لا يسمعون إلى الملإ الأعلى ويقذفون من كل جانب

translation: Driven on to a burning fire, and they will be given a boiling water to drink.
interpretation: This verse describes the punishment awaiting those who reject faith, illustrating the severity and inevitability of their torment in the hereafter. The imagery of being driven to a burning fire and given boiling water to drink serves as a vivid warning of the consequences of disbelief and sin, urging believers to adhere to the path of righteousness.
orig: دحورا ولهم عذاب واصب

translation: Except him who snatches a fragment, and he is pursued by a piercing flame.
interpretation: This verse refers to the jinn who attempt to eavesdrop on the heavenly discussions. If a jinn manages to snatch a fragment of the divine conversation, it is immediately pursued by a shooting star, which is described as a piercing flame, to prevent the spread of unauthorized information. This illustrates the strict protection of divine secrets and the consequences for those who try to breach this security.
orig: إلا من خطف الخطفة فأتبعه شهاب ثاقب

translation: So ask them, are they more difficult to create, or those whom We have created? Indeed, We created them from sticky clay.
interpretation: This verse prompts the Prophet Muhammad to challenge the disbelievers by questioning whether they believe they are more complex to create than other creatures. It emphasizes the simplicity of human creation from clay, highlighting God's power and the ease with which He can create and recreate, thereby urging reflection on the arrogance of those who deny the resurrection and the power of God.
orig: فاستفتهم أهم أشد خلقا أم من خلقنا إنا خلقناهم من طين لازب

translation: Nay, they wonder that a warner has come to them from among themselves. So the disbelievers say: 'This is a strange thing!'
interpretation: This verse highlights the disbelief and mockery of the Quraysh towards Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) when he was sent as a warner from among their own people. It reflects their astonishment and ridicule, indicating their rejection of the message due to its unexpected source, which challenges their societal norms and expectations.
orig: بل عجبت ويسخرون

translation: And when they are reminded, they do not remember
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual negligence of certain individuals who, despite being reminded of Allah's signs and messages, fail to reflect upon them or take heed. It points to a deeper issue of heedlessness and a lack of mindfulness towards divine guidance, suggesting that such people are so engrossed in worldly distractions that they remain unaffected by reminders meant to guide them towards righteousness.
orig: وإذا ذكروا لا يذكرون

translation: And when they see a sign, they mock it.
