translation: Or do they have the treasures of the mercy of your Lord, the Exalted in Might, the Bestower?
interpretation: This verse challenges the disbelievers who might think they have control over or can dictate the distribution of God's mercy and blessings. It emphasizes that only Allah, described here as the Exalted in Might and the Bestower, has the authority and power over His mercy and the right to bestow it as He wills. It serves as a reminder of human limitations and the boundless generosity and sovereignty of God.
orig: أم عندهم خزائن رحمة ربك العزيز الوهاب

translation: Or do they possess the dominion of the heavens and the earth and what is between them? Then let them ascend through the means.
interpretation: This verse challenges those who reject the message of the Qur'an by questioning their authority. It suggests that if the disbelievers truly had control over the universe, they should be able to ascend to the heavens through any means they choose, thereby proving their power. The verse underscores the omnipotence of Allah and the futility of human claims to divine authority or knowledge.
orig: أم لهم ملك السماوات والأرض وما بينهما فليرتقوا في الأسباب

translation: Indeed, there the confederates will be defeated.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate victory of the believers over their enemies. It reassures the faithful that despite the apparent strength and unity of the opposing forces, referred to as 'the confederates,' their defeat is certain and predetermined by God. This serves as a source of comfort and encouragement for Muslims facing adversity, reminding them of the divine support and the eventual triumph of truth over falsehood.
orig: جند ما هنالك مهزوم من الأحزاب

translation: The people of Noah, 'Ad, and Pharaoh, the owner of the stakes, denied before them.
interpretation: This verse highlights the historical pattern of disbelief among previous nations, specifically mentioning the people of Noah, the 'Ad tribe, and Pharaoh, who is described as 'the owner of the stakes,' indicating his power and tyranny. The verse serves as a reminder to the current audience of the Qur'an that their disbelief is not a new phenomenon but part of a recurring cycle of denial among communities who were ultimately punished for their rejection of divine messages. It underscores the importance of heeding the warnings given in the Qur'an to avoid a similar fate.
orig: كذبت قبلهم قوم نوح وعاد وفرعون ذو الأوتاد

translation: And [the tribes of] Thamud and the people of Lot and the companions of the Wood - those were the factions.
interpretation: This verse lists several communities - Thamud, the people of Lot, and the companions of the Wood - who were known for their disbelief and subsequent punishment by Allah. The mention of these groups as 'factions' highlights their collective rejection of the divine messages sent to them through their respective prophets. It serves as a reminder of the consequences of denying the truth and the unity of purpose among disbelieving groups across history.
orig: وثمود وقوم لوط وأصحاب الأيكة أولئك الأحزاب

translation: Indeed, all but the messengers were liars, so the punishment is justified.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the integrity and truthfulness of the prophets and messengers sent by Allah. It suggests that while many people throughout history have denied or lied about the messages brought by these messengers, the messengers themselves remained steadfast in conveying the truth. Consequently, the punishment that befell those who rejected the messengers is seen as a just consequence of their refusal to accept the truth. This underscores the gravity of rejecting divine guidance and the importance of heeding the warnings and teachings of the prophets.
orig: إن كل إلا كذب الرسل فحق عقاب

translation: And these [people] await nothing but a single blast [of the trumpet], which will not be delayed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the suddenness and inevitability of the Day of Judgment. The 'single blast' refers to the trumpet blast that will signal the end of the world and the beginning of the resurrection. The phrase 'which will not be delayed' underscores that this event will occur at its appointed time, without any possibility of postponement, urging believers to be ever-prepared for this momentous event.
orig: وما ينظر هؤلاء إلا صيحة واحدة ما لها من فواق

translation: And they said, "Our Lord, hasten for us our share before the Day of Account."
interpretation: This verse reflects the impatience and shortsightedness of those who seek immediate worldly gains without considering the consequences in the hereafter. It highlights a materialistic mindset that prioritizes temporal pleasures over spiritual accountability, illustrating a lack of faith in the divine timing and wisdom of God's plan.
orig: وقالوا ربنا عجل لنا قطنا قبل يوم الحساب

translation: Be patient with what they say, and remember Our servant David, the man of strength; indeed, he was one who repeatedly turned back [to Allah].
interpretation: This verse encourages the Prophet Muhammad to endure the mockery and opposition from disbelievers with patience, drawing inspiration from the example of Prophet David. David is described as 'ذا الأيد' (possessor of strength), indicating his physical and spiritual fortitude, and 'أواب' (one who repeatedly turns back to Allah), highlighting his constant repentance and devotion. The verse underscores the importance of patience and steadfastness in faith, using David's life as a model for perseverance and spiritual return to God.
orig: اصبر على ما يقولون واذكر عبدنا داوود ذا الأيد إنه أواب

translation: Verily, We have subjected the mountains to glorify (Us) with him in the evening and at sunrise.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine power and control over nature, illustrating that even the mountains, which are inanimate and massive, are made to join in the glorification of God alongside Prophet David. It underscores the concept of universal submission to God, where all creation, whether animate or inanimate, participates in the praise of the Creator at designated times, reflecting the harmony and order in the universe.
orig: إنا سخرنا الجبال معه يسبحن بالعشي والإشراق

translation: And the birds assembled, all with him turning.
interpretation: This verse highlights the obedience and submission of all creatures, symbolized by the birds, to the will of God. It illustrates the unity and harmony in creation, where everything, including the natural world, is oriented towards and returns to the Creator, emphasizing the concept of tawhid (the oneness of God).
orig: والطير محشورة كل له أواب

translation: And We strengthened his kingdom and gave him wisdom and decisive speech.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine favor bestowed upon Prophet Solomon, emphasizing how Allah not only enhanced his political power but also endowed him with profound wisdom and the ability to articulate clearly and decisively. This combination of attributes enabled Solomon to govern justly and effectively, illustrating that true leadership is a gift from Allah, encompassing both authority and the wisdom to use it rightly.
orig: وشددنا ملكه وآتيناه الحكمة وفصل الخطاب

translation: Has the story of the adversaries reached you, when they scaled the wall?
interpretation: This verse refers to a historical event where a group of people, known as the adversaries or disputants, climbed over a wall to enter a sacred or restricted area. The Qur'an uses this incident to illustrate a lesson about the consequences of trespassing and disrespecting boundaries set by divine command. It serves as a reminder of the importance of adhering to moral and religious guidelines.
orig: وهل أتاك نبأ الخصم إذ تسوروا المحراب

translation: When they entered upon David and were afraid of him, they said, 'Fear not. [We are] two adversaries, one of whom has wronged the other, so judge between us with truth and do not be unjust, and guide us to the straight path.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the principle of seeking justice through a divinely appointed leader, as the two adversaries approach Prophet David, seeking a fair judgment. It emphasizes the importance of resolving disputes with truth and justice, and the guidance towards the straight path, symbolizing the moral and ethical conduct expected in Islamic jurisprudence. The fear of David by the adversaries also reflects the awe and respect for a just ruler, highlighting the need for leaders to uphold justice fearlessly.
orig: إذ دخلوا على داوود ففزع منهم قالوا لا تخف خصمان بغى بعضنا على بعض فاحكم بيننا بالحق ولا تشطط واهدنا إلى سواء الصراط

translation: Indeed, this is my brother, he has ninety-nine sheep and I have one sheep, so he said, 'Entrust it to me,' and he overpowered me in speech.
interpretation: This verse from Surah Sad (38:23) illustrates the story of Prophet Dawud (David) and the two brothers who came to him for judgment. The brother with one sheep represents the oppressed, while the one with ninety-nine sheep symbolizes the oppressor. The verse highlights the theme of justice and the misuse of power in disputes. It shows how the brother with more sheep tried to manipulate and overpower the other in speech to take his only sheep, reflecting on the broader moral lesson of not exploiting the weak and the importance of fair judgment.
orig: إن هذا أخي له تسع وتسعون نعجة ولي نعجة واحدة فقال أكفلنيها وعزني في الخطاب

translation: He said, 'He has wronged you by demanding your ewe to add to his ewes. And indeed, many partners oppress one another, except for those who believe and do righteous deeds - and few are they.' And David assumed that We had only tried him, so he sought forgiveness of his Lord and fell down bowing [in prostration] and turned in repentance [to Allah].
interpretation: This verse reflects on the story of Prophet David and the lesson he learned from his mistake. It underscores the importance of justice and fairness, even among partners or those in close relationships. The verse highlights that oppression and injustice are common among people, but those who have faith and perform good deeds are exceptions to this rule, though they are few in number. David's realization that his trial was from God led him to immediate repentance, demonstrating the value of self-awareness, humility, and turning back to God in sincere repentance when one errs.
orig: قال لقد ظلمك بسؤال نعجتك إلى نعاجه وإن كثيرا من الخلطاء ليبغي بعضهم على بعض إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات وقليل ما هم وظن داوود أنما فتناه فاستغفر ربه وخر راكعا وأناب

translation: So We forgave him that, and indeed, he has nearness to Us and a good place of return.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the concept of divine forgiveness and the rewards of sincere repentance. It specifically refers to Prophet Yunus (Jonah), who, after his ordeal with the whale, was forgiven by Allah. The 'nearness to Us' signifies a special status granted to him, indicating closeness to Allah and a high spiritual rank. The 'good place of return' refers to the ultimate reward of Paradise, promised to those who seek forgiveness and remain steadfast in faith. This verse serves as a reminder of Allah's mercy and the importance of turning back to Him in repentance.
orig: فغفرنا له ذلك وإن له عندنا لزلفى وحسن مآب

translation: O David, indeed We have made you a successor upon the earth, so judge between the people in truth and do not follow [your own] desire, as it will lead you astray from the way of Allah. Indeed, those who go astray from the way of Allah will have a severe punishment because they forgot the Day of Account.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the responsibility of leadership and the importance of justice. It instructs Prophet David, and by extension all leaders, to govern with fairness and truth, rather than being swayed by personal desires. The warning against following one's whims underscores the potential for self-interest to lead one away from divine guidance. The mention of a severe punishment for those who stray from Allah's path serves as a reminder of the accountability on the Day of Judgment, highlighting the need for leaders to remain conscious of their actions and their impact on others.
orig: يا داوود إنا جعلناك خليفة في الأرض فاحكم بين الناس بالحق ولا تتبع الهوى فيضلك عن سبيل الله إن الذين يضلون عن سبيل الله لهم عذاب شديد بما نسوا يوم الحساب

translation: And We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them in vain. That is the assumption of those who disbelieve. So woe to those who disbelieve from the Fire.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the purposeful creation of the universe by Allah, refuting the notion held by disbelievers that the creation is without purpose. It warns of the severe consequences, specifically the punishment of Hellfire, awaiting those who reject this truth, highlighting the gravity of disbelief and its impact on one's hereafter.
orig: وما خلقنا السماء والأرض وما بينهما باطلا ذلك ظن الذين كفروا فويل للذين كفروا من النار

translation: Or do We treat the believers who do righteous deeds like the corrupters in the land? Or do We treat the pious like the wicked?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of divine justice, highlighting that God does not equate those who believe and perform good deeds with those who cause corruption and mischief. It underscores the distinction between the righteous and the wicked, affirming that the outcomes and treatments of these groups in the hereafter will be fundamentally different based on their actions and faith. This serves as a reassurance to believers that their efforts in righteousness are recognized and valued by God, and as a warning to those who engage in corruption that their actions have consequences.
orig: أم نجعل الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات كالمفسدين في الأرض أم نجعل المتقين كالفجار

translation: A Book which We have revealed to you, full of blessing, that they may ponder over its verses, and that those of understanding may remember.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin and the blessed nature of the Qur'an, revealed to Prophet Muhammad. It highlights the purpose of the Qur'an as a means for reflection and contemplation on its verses, encouraging those endowed with understanding and intellect to derive lessons and reminders from it, thereby fostering spiritual growth and awareness.
orig: كتاب أنزلناه إليك مبارك ليدبروا آياته وليتذكر أولو الألباب

translation: And We bestowed upon David, Solomon. How excellent a servant! Indeed, he was one who repeatedly turned back [to Allah].
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine favor bestowed upon David in the form of his son Solomon, emphasizing Solomon's exceptional servitude to Allah. The term 'awwab' indicates Solomon's continuous repentance and return to Allah, showcasing his deep spirituality and commitment to his faith. This serves as an example for believers to constantly turn back to Allah in repentance and devotion.
orig: ووهبنا لداوود سليمان نعم العبد إنه أواب

translation: When the sleek, fleet-footed steeds were displayed to him at eventide
interpretation: This verse refers to a moment when Prophet Solomon was presented with magnificent horses, highlighting his wealth and power. The presentation of these horses at evening time symbolizes the peak of his worldly achievements, reminding believers of the transient nature of material possessions and the importance of focusing on spiritual growth and devotion to God.
orig: إذ عرض عليه بالعشي الصافنات الجياد

translation: So he said, 'I have preferred the love of good over the remembrance of my Lord until it was hidden behind the veil.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the human tendency to become distracted by worldly desires and material possessions, which can lead to neglecting one's spiritual duties and connection with Allah. The 'love of good' symbolizes the allure of temporal pleasures and achievements that can veil the heart from the remembrance of God, causing a spiritual disconnect until it is concealed 'behind the veil.' It serves as a reminder for believers to prioritize their spiritual well-being and maintain a constant awareness of Allah amidst the distractions of life.
orig: فقال إني أحببت حب الخير عن ذكر ربي حتى توارت بالحجاب

translation: Return it to me. So he began to wipe over the foreheads and the necks.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the act of humility and obedience. When the command to return something is given, the response is immediate and thorough, symbolizing the importance of following divine instructions with diligence and care. The wiping over the foreheads and necks could be seen as a gesture of seeking forgiveness or purification, emphasizing the spiritual aspect of obedience.
orig: ردوها علي فطفق مسحا بالسوق والأعناق

translation: And We certainly tested Solomon and We placed on his throne a body; then he turned to Us.
interpretation: This verse highlights the trials faced by Prophet Solomon, where God tested his wisdom and faith by placing a lifeless body on his throne, symbolizing a challenge to his authority and leadership. Solomon's response to this test was to turn back to God in repentance and submission, demonstrating his humility and reliance on divine guidance rather than worldly power.
orig: ولقد فتنا سليمان وألقينا على كرسيه جسدا ثم أناب

translation: He said, 'My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom such as will not belong to anyone after me. Indeed, You are the Bestower.'
interpretation: In this verse, Solomon (peace be upon him) is expressing his humility and dependence on God by asking for forgiveness and a unique kingdom. His request for a kingdom "such as will not belong to anyone after me" reflects his desire for a divine endowment that would serve as a testament to God's unparalleled generosity and power. By acknowledging God as "the Bestower," Solomon recognizes that all blessings and authority come solely from God, emphasizing the importance of seeking divine favor through sincere supplication and gratitude.
orig: قال رب اغفر لي وهب لي ملكا لا ينبغي لأحد من بعدي إنك أنت الوهاب

translation: So We subjected the wind to him; it blew gently by his command wherever he directed.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine favor bestowed upon Prophet Solomon, illustrating his authority over natural elements as a sign of his prophethood and the obedience of creation to God's will. The wind, a powerful force of nature, was made subservient to Solomon, symbolizing how God can empower His chosen servants to achieve His purposes, guiding them gently towards their divine missions.
orig: فسخرنا له الريح تجري بأمره رخاء حيث أصاب

translation: And the devils, every builder and diver
interpretation: This verse refers to the jinn, specifically those who were subjugated by Prophet Solomon. The term 'builder' indicates those jinn who were skilled in construction, helping Solomon in building structures, while 'diver' refers to those who could dive into the sea to retrieve pearls and other treasures. This showcases the diverse abilities of the jinn and how they were employed in various tasks under Solomon's command, illustrating his authority and the miraculous nature of his reign.
orig: والشياطين كل بناء وغواص

translation: And others bound together in chains
interpretation: This verse refers to the disbelievers who will be gathered on the Day of Judgment, shackled and chained together as a symbol of their punishment and the consequence of their rejection of faith. It underscores the theme of accountability and the inevitability of facing the consequences of one's actions in the hereafter.
orig: وآخرين مقرنين في الأصفاد

translation: This is Our gift, so grant or withhold without account.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the blessings bestowed by Allah are given freely and generously, without any obligation for the recipient to account for them. It emphasizes the concept of divine generosity and the freedom that comes with it, suggesting that humans should also be generous in their giving, without expecting anything in return or keeping a record of their benevolence.
orig: هذا عطاؤنا فامنن أو أمسك بغير حساب

translation: And indeed, for him with Us is nearness and a good place of return.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the individual being referred to has a special status in the Hereafter, enjoying proximity to Allah and a favorable abode. This suggests a high level of spiritual reward and divine favor granted to him due to his righteous deeds and faith.
orig: وإن له عندنا لزلفى وحسن مآب

translation: And remember Our servant Job, when he called to his Lord, 'Indeed, Satan has touched me with hardship and torment.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the patience and faith of Prophet Job (Ayyub) during his trials. When afflicted by severe hardship and torment instigated by Satan, Job turned to Allah in sincere supplication, acknowledging the source of his suffering while maintaining his faith and reliance on God. This teaches believers the importance of turning to Allah in times of distress, recognizing that all trials are tests of faith and patience, and that true relief and support come from God alone.
orig: واذكر عبدنا أيوب إذ نادى ربه أني مسني الشيطان بنصب وعذاب

translation: Strike the ground with your foot; this is a cool spring and a drink.
interpretation: This verse demonstrates Allah's power to provide for His prophets in miraculous ways, showcasing the story of Musa (Moses) when he was in need of water. By commanding Musa to strike the ground, a spring of water emerged, symbolizing divine intervention and sustenance in times of need. It emphasizes trust in Allah's provision and the miraculous nature of His support for His chosen servants.
orig: اركض برجلك هذا مغتسل بارد وشراب

translation: And We bestowed upon him his family, and the like of them with them, as a mercy from Us and a reminder for those of understanding.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's mercy and generosity towards Prophet Abraham by not only restoring his family but also granting him an additional family of the same number, symbolizing divine favor and abundance. It serves as a reminder for those with insight to recognize and appreciate God's blessings and to understand the deeper spiritual lessons embedded in such divine acts.
orig: ووهبنا له أهله ومثلهم معهم رحمة منا وذكرى لأولي الألباب

translation: And take in your hand a bunch [of grass] and strike with it and do not break your oath. Indeed, We found him patient, an excellent servant. Indeed, he was one who turned back [to Allah].
interpretation: This verse refers to the story of Prophet Ayyub (Job) and highlights his patience and devotion to Allah. After enduring severe trials, Ayyub was instructed to strike the ground with a bunch of grass, which miraculously healed him. The verse emphasizes Ayyub's steadfastness in faith and his consistent repentance, showcasing his exemplary character as a servant of Allah.
orig: وخذ بيدك ضغثا فاضرب به ولا تحنث إنا وجدناه صابرا نعم العبد إنه أواب

translation: And remember Our servants, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, those of strength and vision.
interpretation: This verse highlights the exemplary qualities of the prophets Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, emphasizing their physical and spiritual strength ("أولي الأيدي") and their insight and foresight ("الأبصار"). It serves as a reminder to believers of the importance of emulating these qualities in their own lives, striving for both physical and moral fortitude, as well as clear vision in understanding and following the path of righteousness.
orig: واذكر عبادنا إبراهيم وإسحاق ويعقوب أولي الأيدي والأبصار

translation: Indeed, We have purified them with a pure quality, the remembrance of the Home.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the individuals mentioned have been spiritually purified through their constant remembrance and focus on the Hereafter, which is referred to as 'the Home'. This purification is a result of their dedication to maintaining a connection with the ultimate reality and purpose beyond this worldly life, thereby elevating their spiritual state.
orig: إنا أخلصناهم بخالصة ذكرى الدار

translation: And indeed, they are with Us among the chosen, the best.
interpretation: This verse indicates that those who are mentioned are not only selected by Allah but are also among the elite in terms of their righteousness and closeness to Him. It emphasizes their special status and honor in the sight of Allah, highlighting that their selection is a divine favor and a testament to their exemplary faith and conduct.
orig: وإنهم عندنا لمن المصطفين الأخيار

translation: And remember Ishmael, Elisha, and Dhul-Kifl, and all are among the chosen.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of the exemplary figures Ishmael, Elisha, and Dhul-Kifl, who are highlighted for their righteousness and closeness to God. By mentioning these prophets, the verse encourages believers to remember and emulate the virtues and steadfast faith of these chosen individuals, reinforcing the importance of following the guidance of prophets in one's spiritual journey.
orig: واذكر إسماعيل واليسع وذا الكفل وكل من الأخيار

translation: This is a reminder, and indeed, for the righteous is a goodly home.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder to all believers about the importance of righteousness and piety. It emphasizes that those who live their lives with taqwa (God-consciousness) will be rewarded with a beautiful and eternal abode in the Hereafter. The 'goodly home' refers to Paradise, which is described in the Qur'an as a place of ultimate peace, joy, and fulfillment for those who have strived to follow God's path.
orig: هذا ذكر وإن للمتقين لحسن مآب

translation: Gardens of Eden, with their gates opened for them
interpretation: This verse describes the reward awaiting the righteous in the afterlife, symbolizing ultimate peace and access to divine blessings. The 'Gardens of Eden' represent a state of eternal bliss and proximity to God, where the gates being open signifies that the believers are welcomed and have unhindered access to this paradise.
orig: جنات عدن مفتحة لهم الأبواب

translation: Reclining therein, they will call for abundant fruit and drink.
interpretation: This verse describes the blissful state of the righteous in Paradise, where they are comfortably reclining and have the luxury of calling for plentiful fruits and drinks, symbolizing the fulfillment of all desires and the abundance of blessings in the hereafter.
orig: متكئين فيها يدعون فيها بفاكهة كثيرة وشراب

translation: And with them will be chaste mates of modest gaze.
interpretation: This verse describes the companions of the righteous in Paradise, emphasizing the purity and modesty of their mates. The phrase "qasirat at-tarf" highlights the virtue of these companions, indicating that they are chaste and lower their gaze out of modesty, which is a quality highly valued in Islamic teachings. This reflects the serene and morally upright environment of Paradise.
orig: وعندهم قاصرات الطرف أتراب

translation: This is what you were promised for the Day of Account.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder to believers that the promises and warnings mentioned throughout the Qur'an about the Day of Judgment are real and will come to pass. It emphasizes the certainty of accountability for one's actions in the afterlife, urging individuals to prepare for that day by living righteously according to the teachings of Islam.
orig: هذا ما توعدون ليوم الحساب

translation: Indeed, this is Our provision, which will never be exhausted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the boundless and eternal nature of the sustenance provided by Allah. It reassures believers that the provisions granted by Allah, whether spiritual or material, are inexhaustible and will never run out, reflecting His infinite generosity and self-sufficiency.
orig: إن هذا لرزقنا ما له من نفاد

translation: This, and indeed for the transgressors is an evil abode.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequence of transgression and disobedience to God's commands. It serves as a warning that those who persist in wrongdoing and tyranny will ultimately find themselves in a terrible and painful situation in the hereafter, highlighting the justice and inevitability of divine retribution.
orig: هذا وإن للطاغين لشر مآب

translation: Hell, they will enter it, and how evil the resting place!
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the dire consequences of disbelief and sin, portraying Hell as the ultimate undesirable destination. It serves as a warning to believers about the importance of righteousness and obedience to Allah's commands, highlighting that Hell is not just a place of punishment but a profoundly uncomfortable and wretched abode.
orig: جهنم يصلونها فبئس المهاد

translation: So let them taste it - scalding water and purulence.
interpretation: This verse describes the punishment in the hereafter for those who disbelieve and reject the message of Islam. The 'scalding water' and 'purulence' symbolize the intense suffering and disgust that awaits them, serving as a deterrent and a reminder of the consequences of their actions in this life.
orig: هذا فليذوقوه حميم وغساق

translation: And others of their kind, in pairs
interpretation: This verse refers to the creation of other beings similar to humans, specifically indicating that they are created in pairs, highlighting the divine order and balance in creation. It suggests a reflection on the diversity and yet the unity in the creation of life forms, emphasizing the concept of companionship and duality in nature.
orig: وآخر من شكله أزواج

translation: This is a group rushing headlong with you; no welcome for them; indeed, they are bound for the Fire.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of accountability and the consequences of one's actions in the afterlife. It suggests that those who follow others blindly into wrongdoing will not be welcomed in the hereafter and are destined for punishment in the Fire. It serves as a warning against being part of a group that engages in sinful behavior, emphasizing individual responsibility for one's choices and the ultimate judgment that awaits everyone.
orig: هذا فوج مقتحم معكم لا مرحبا بهم إنهم صالو النار

translation: They said, "Rather, you are not welcome. You have brought it upon us, so wretched is the settlement."
interpretation: This verse reflects the blame and resentment of the people towards the magicians who, after their conversion to the message of Moses, are accused of bringing about the calamities that befell the community. It highlights the human tendency to scapegoat others for collective misfortunes, illustrating a deeper theme of accountability and the consequences of rejecting divine guidance.
orig: قالوا بل أنتم لا مرحبا بكم أنتم قدمتموه لنا فبئس القرار

translation: They will say, 'Our Lord, whoever brought this upon us - increase him in punishment, twofold in the Fire.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the intense frustration and anger of the people in Hell towards those who led them astray or influenced them negatively, leading to their damnation. It underscores the theme of accountability and the severe consequences of misguiding others, as those in Hell seek retribution against those who were instrumental in their downfall, highlighting the gravity of one's actions and their impact on others.
orig: قالوا ربنا من قدم لنا هذا فزده عذابا ضعفا في النار

translation: And they said, 'Why do we not see men whom we used to count among the wicked?'
interpretation: This verse reflects the surprise and questioning of the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment when they do not see certain individuals they considered morally corrupt in their worldly life. It highlights their expectation that these individuals would be punished alongside them, revealing their misunderstanding of divine justice and the criteria by which Allah judges individuals. The verse underscores the theme that human perceptions of morality and divine judgment can be vastly different, emphasizing the importance of not judging others based on one's own limited understanding.
orig: وقالوا ما لنا لا نرى رجالا كنا نعدهم من الأشرار

translation: Did we take them in jest, or have their eyes swerved away from them?
interpretation: This verse reflects on the disbelief of those who mock the signs of Allah or fail to see the truth due to their own negligence or arrogance. It questions whether the disbelievers considered the divine messages as mere jest, or if their perception has been distorted, causing them to overlook the clear signs of Allah's existence and power.
orig: أتخذناهم سخريا أم زاغت عنهم الأبصار

translation: Indeed, that is the truth: the people of the Fire will be disputing.
interpretation: This verse underscores the reality of the disputes and arguments that will occur among the inhabitants of Hell. It suggests that even in their punishment, the people of the Fire will not find unity or peace, but will continue to engage in contentious disagreements, reflecting their ongoing state of discord and misery.
orig: إن ذلك لحق تخاصم أهل النار

translation: Say, "I am only a warner, and there is no deity except Allah, the One, the Subduer."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of the Prophet Muhammad as a warner to humanity about the consequences of their actions and the oneness of God. It underscores the fundamental Islamic belief in the absolute unity and sovereignty of Allah, who is described as Al-Wahid (The One) and Al-Qahhar (The Subduer), highlighting His unique power and authority over all creation.
orig: قل إنما أنا منذر وما من إله إلا الله الواحد القهار

translation: Lord of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them, the Almighty, the All-Forgiving
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and omnipotence of Allah, who is described as the Lord of the entire universe, encompassing everything from the heavens to the earth. The attributes 'Almighty' (Al-Aziz) and 'All-Forgiving' (Al-Ghafur) highlight His supreme power and His mercy, indicating that while He has the power to enforce His will, He also forgives those who seek His forgiveness, showcasing a balance between His might and His compassion.
orig: رب السماوات والأرض وما بينهما العزيز الغفار

translation: Say, it is a great news
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance and magnitude of the message of Islam. It instructs the Prophet Muhammad to declare that the revelation he has received is not just ordinary news, but a monumental and extraordinary announcement from God, which carries profound implications for humanity's guidance and salvation.
orig: قل هو نبأ عظيم

translation: You are heedless of it.
interpretation: This verse suggests that people are often distracted or inattentive to the signs and messages of Allah, indicating a state of spiritual negligence or unawareness.
orig: أنتم عنه معرضون

translation: I had no knowledge of the Exalted Assembly when they were disputing.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was not privy to the discussions and disputes among the angels in the highest assembly before the revelation of the Qur'an. It underscores the human nature of the Prophet and the divine origin of the Qur'anic knowledge, emphasizing that his knowledge came solely from divine revelation.
orig: ما كان لي من علم بالملإ الأعلى إذ يختصمون

translation: It is revealed to me that I am only a clear warner
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of the Prophet Muhammad as a messenger whose primary duty is to warn people clearly about the consequences of their actions in the eyes of God. It underscores the clarity and transparency of the message he is tasked to deliver, focusing on his function as a guide rather than a enforcer of faith.
orig: إن يوحى إلي إلا أنما أنا نذير مبين

translation: When your Lord said to the angels, 'Indeed, I am going to create a human being from clay.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine announcement of the creation of humanity, emphasizing God's power and intentionality in creating humans from humble origins like clay, which signifies the beginning of human life and the special relationship between the Creator and His creation.
orig: إذ قال ربك للملائكة إني خالق بشرا من طين

translation: So when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My spirit, then fall down to him in prostration.
interpretation: This verse describes the creation of Adam by Allah, emphasizing the divine act of breathing His spirit into Adam, which signifies the unique honor and status bestowed upon him. The command for the angels to prostrate to Adam further underscores his elevated position in creation, symbolizing submission to Allah's will and the respect due to Adam as the first human and vicegerent on earth.
orig: فإذا سويته ونفخت فيه من روحي فقعوا له ساجدين

translation: So the angels prostrated, all of them together.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the obedience and submission of the angels to Allah's command. When Allah ordered the angels to prostrate before Adam, they all complied without hesitation, demonstrating their complete submission to Allah's will and their recognition of Adam's honored status as decreed by Allah.
orig: فسجد الملائكة كلهم أجمعون

translation: Except Iblis, he was arrogant and became one of the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance of Iblis, who refused to prostrate to Adam out of pride, leading to his fall from grace and his classification among the disbelievers. It serves as a warning against the dangers of arrogance and the importance of humility and obedience to God's commands.
orig: إلا إبليس استكبر وكان من الكافرين

translation: He said, 'O Iblis, what prevented you from prostrating to what I created with My own hands? Did you become arrogant, or were you among the haughty?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the moment when Allah questions Iblis about his refusal to prostrate to Adam, whom Allah created with His own hands. The question posed by Allah emphasizes the gravity of Iblis's disobedience and arrogance. It suggests that Iblis's refusal stems from either pride or a sense of superiority, illustrating the dangers of arrogance and the importance of humility and obedience to Allah's commands.
orig: قال يا إبليس ما منعك أن تسجد لما خلقت بيدي أستكبرت أم كنت من العالين

translation: He said, 'I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the arrogance and pride of Iblis (Satan) when he refused to prostrate to Adam. Iblis considered himself superior because he was created from fire, which he perceived as a nobler element than the clay from which Adam was made. This highlights the theme of humility and obedience to God's commands over self-perceived superiority based on material origins.
orig: قال أنا خير منه خلقتني من نار وخلقته من طين

translation: He said, 'Then get out of it, for indeed, you are stoned.'
interpretation: This verse signifies the expulsion of Satan from Paradise after his refusal to prostrate to Adam, as commanded by Allah. The term 'stoned' (rajim) here symbolizes being cursed or damned, indicating Satan's permanent rejection and his status as an outcast from divine favor due to his disobedience and arrogance.
orig: قال فاخرج منها فإنك رجيم

translation: And indeed, upon you is My curse until the Day of Judgment.
interpretation: This verse signifies a severe and continuous punishment from Allah upon the one being addressed, lasting until the Day of Judgment. It underscores the gravity of the transgression committed by the individual, indicating that their actions have led to a state of divine disapproval and separation from Allah's mercy. The mention of the curse extending 'until the Day of Judgment' emphasizes the eternal nature of the consequence, serving as a stark warning about the repercussions of defying Allah's commands.
orig: وإن عليك لعنتي إلى يوم الدين

translation: He said, 'My Lord, then respite me until the Day they are resurrected.'
interpretation: In this verse, Iblis (Satan) is pleading with Allah for a delay in his punishment until the Day of Resurrection. This request reflects Iblis's acknowledgment of his impending doom but also his desire to continue misleading humanity until the very end, showcasing his persistent defiance and enmity towards Allah's plan.
orig: قال رب فأنظرني إلى يوم يبعثون

translation: He said: "Then indeed, you are of those who are given respite."
interpretation: This verse indicates that the speaker, likely referring to Allah, is granting a temporary delay or respite to the one being addressed. It suggests a period of leniency or postponement of judgment, allowing the individual time to reflect on their actions or possibly to repent before the final decision is made. This reflects the divine attribute of patience and mercy, giving individuals a chance to change their course before facing the consequences.
orig: قال فإنك من المنظرين

translation: Until the Day of the appointed time
interpretation: This verse refers to a specific, predetermined day known only to Allah, which marks the end of a certain period or event. It emphasizes the certainty and inevitability of divine timing in the unfolding of cosmic and personal destinies.
orig: إلى يوم الوقت المعلوم

translation: He said, "By Your might, I will surely mislead them all."
interpretation: This verse reflects Iblis's (Satan's) declaration of his intention to lead humanity astray as an act of defiance against God. It underscores the theme of free will and the ongoing spiritual battle between good and evil, highlighting Iblis's arrogance and his use of God's might as a challenge to corrupt human beings.
orig: قال فبعزتك لأغوينهم أجمعين

translation: Except Your servants among them who are sincere.
interpretation: This verse indicates that while many may be led astray, there are exceptions among those who remain steadfast in their faith and sincerity towards Allah. It highlights the importance of genuine devotion and purity of intention in the face of widespread corruption or disbelief. The sincere servants of Allah are protected from the misguidance that affects others, underscoring the value of true faith and righteousness.
orig: إلا عبادك منهم المخلصين

translation: He said, "Then the truth, and I speak the truth."
interpretation: This verse reflects the affirmation of truthfulness and integrity in speech. When someone asserts "the truth," it signifies a commitment to honesty and sincerity, emphasizing the importance of truth in communication and dealings. The speaker is not only claiming to tell the truth but also reinforcing the value of truth itself, aligning with Islamic principles that highly regard truthfulness as a moral virtue.
orig: قال فالحق والحق أقول

translation: I will fill Hell with you and those of them who follow you, all together.
interpretation: This verse indicates God's promise to fill Hell with Satan and all those who follow him, emphasizing the ultimate consequence of following evil paths. It serves as a warning to believers about the dangers of straying from the righteous path and the inevitability of divine justice.
orig: لأملأن جهنم منك وممن تبعك منهم أجمعين

translation: Say, "I do not ask you for any reward for it, nor am I one of those who pretend."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sincerity and purity of the Prophet Muhammad's mission. He is instructed to declare that he seeks no material compensation for conveying God's message, highlighting that his motivation is solely to fulfill his divine duty. Furthermore, by stating he is not among the pretenders, it underscores his truthfulness and distinguishes his message from those who might seek personal gain or fabricate claims. This reinforces the authenticity and divine origin of the Qur'anic message.
orig: قل ما أسألكم عليه من أجر وما أنا من المتكلفين

translation: It is but a reminder to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is not just a message for a specific group, but a universal reminder and guidance for all of humanity and beyond, urging everyone to reflect on its teachings and apply them in their lives.
orig: إن هو إلا ذكر للعالمين

translation: And you will surely know its news after a time.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the truth or the outcome of a matter will become clear and known to the person after some time has passed. It emphasizes patience and the inevitability of revelation in due time.
orig: ولتعلمن نبأه بعد حين

translation: The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Almighty, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin of the Qur'an, attributing its revelation to Allah, who is described with the attributes of 'Almighty' (Al-'Aziz) and 'Wise' (Al-Hakim). The attribute 'Almighty' signifies Allah's supreme power and authority over all creation, while 'Wise' highlights His perfect wisdom in all His actions and decrees. This underscores the authority and perfection of the Qur'an as a divine text, meant to guide humanity with wisdom and strength.
orig: تنزيل الكتاب من الله العزيز الحكيم

translation: Indeed, We have revealed to you the Book in truth, so worship Allah, making your religion pure for Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin and truthfulness of the Qur'an, urging the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and by extension all believers to worship Allah alone. The call to make one's religion pure for Allah highlights the importance of sincerity and devotion in worship, rejecting any form of idolatry or polytheism. It serves as a reminder to Muslims to maintain the purity of their faith and to direct all acts of worship solely to Allah.
orig: إنا أنزلنا إليك الكتاب بالحق فاعبد الله مخلصا له الدين

translation: Beware, sincere religion is for Allah alone. And those who take protectors besides Him (say), 'We worship them only that they may bring us nearer to Allah.' Indeed, Allah will judge between them concerning that over which they differ. Indeed, Allah does not guide one who is a liar and a disbeliever.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of monotheism, asserting that true worship and devotion should be directed solely to Allah. It critiques the practice of associating partners with Allah, where people might venerate saints or other figures hoping these will intercede on their behalf to bring them closer to Allah. The verse warns that such actions are misguided and that Allah will ultimately judge these differing beliefs and practices. It further highlights that those who deliberately lie and reject the truth of monotheism will not be guided by Allah, underlining the importance of sincerity and truth in faith.
orig: ألا لله الدين الخالص والذين اتخذوا من دونه أولياء ما نعبدهم إلا ليقربونا إلى الله زلفى إن الله يحكم بينهم في ما هم فيه يختلفون إن الله لا يهدي من هو كاذب كفار

translation: If Allah had intended to take a son, He could have chosen from what He creates whatever He willed. Exalted is He; He is Allah, the One, the Prevailing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness and self-sufficiency of Allah, rejecting the notion of Him having a son or any partner. It underscores His absolute power and sovereignty, indicating that if He willed to have a son, He could do so from His creation, but He chooses not to, affirming His unique nature as the sole deity and the irresistible in power.
orig: لو أراد الله أن يتخذ ولدا لاصطفى مما يخلق ما يشاء سبحانه هو الله الواحد القهار

translation: He created the heavens and the earth in truth. He rolls the night over the day and rolls the day over the night. And He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running [its course] for a specified term. Unquestionably, He is the Exalted in Might, the Perpetual Forgiver.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's sovereignty and power over the universe. The creation of the heavens and the earth 'in truth' signifies that there is purpose and order in the cosmos, reflecting Allah's wisdom and justice. The rolling of night over day and vice versa illustrates the continuous cycle of time that Allah has ordained, symbolizing the constant change and renewal in life. The subjugation of the sun and the moon to their appointed courses underscores the precision and reliability of celestial movements, which serve as signs for humanity. The verse concludes by affirming Allah's attributes of might and forgiveness, indicating that despite His immense power, He is also merciful and forgiving, encouraging believers to turn to Him in repentance and trust.
orig: خلق السماوات والأرض بالحق يكور الليل على النهار ويكور النهار على الليل وسخر الشمس والقمر كل يجري لأجل مسمى ألا هو العزيز الغفار

translation: He created you from one soul, then made from it its mate, and He sent down for you from the livestock eight pairs. He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation, in three darknesses. That is Allah, your Lord; to Him belongs dominion. There is no deity except Him, so how are you turned away?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity and oneness of Allah, highlighting His role as the sole Creator of all life. It begins by describing the creation of humankind from a single soul, which underscores the fundamental unity of all humans and their shared origin. The mention of the mate being created from the same soul points to the complementary nature of human relationships and the divine design in human companionship. The reference to livestock and the process of human development in the womb further illustrates Allah's meticulous care and power in creation, occurring in stages and in a protected environment described as 'three darknesses'. The verse concludes by affirming Allah's sovereignty and the exclusivity of His divinity, challenging the reader to reflect on their deviation from this truth and to realign their faith and actions accordingly.
orig: خلقكم من نفس واحدة ثم جعل منها زوجها وأنزل لكم من الأنعام ثمانية أزواج يخلقكم في بطون أمهاتكم خلقا من بعد خلق في ظلمات ثلاث ذلكم الله ربكم له الملك لا إله إلا هو فأنى تصرفون

translation: If you disbelieve, indeed, Allah is not in need of you, and He does not approve disbelief for His servants. And if you are grateful, He approves it for you. And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you about what you used to do. Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the independence of Allah from human belief or disbelief, highlighting that faith or gratitude is for the benefit of the believers themselves, not Allah. It underscores personal accountability, as each individual is responsible for their own actions and will be judged accordingly by Allah, who has complete knowledge of their inner thoughts and intentions.
orig: إن تكفروا فإن الله غني عنكم ولا يرضى لعباده الكفر وإن تشكروا يرضه لكم ولا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى ثم إلى ربكم مرجعكم فينبئكم بما كنتم تعملون إنه عليم بذات الصدور

translation: And when affliction touches man, he calls upon his Lord, turning to Him [alone]; then when He bestows on him a favor from Himself, he forgets what he was calling for before, and he attributes equals to Allah to mislead [people] from His way. Say, 'Enjoy your disbelief for a little while; indeed, you are of the companions of the Fire.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to turn to God in times of distress but to forget and even associate partners with Him once relief is granted. It serves as a reminder of the fleeting nature of worldly pleasures and the consequences of disbelief, urging believers to maintain their faith consistently, not just in times of need. The promise of temporary enjoyment followed by eternal punishment underscores the importance of steadfastness in faith.
orig: وإذا مس الإنسان ضر دعا ربه منيبا إليه ثم إذا خوله نعمة منه نسي ما كان يدعو إليه من قبل وجعل لله أندادا ليضل عن سبيله قل تمتع بكفرك قليلا إنك من أصحاب النار

translation: Is one who is devoutly obedient during periods of the night, prostrating and standing [in prayer], fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord [like one who does not]? Say, "Are those who know equal to those who do not know?" Only they will remember [who are] people of understanding.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the value of spiritual devotion and knowledge in Islam. It contrasts the person who spends part of the night in prayer, demonstrating humility and fear of the Hereafter, with someone who does not engage in such practices. The rhetorical question about the equality of those who know and those who do not know underscores the importance of knowledge in distinguishing between right and wrong, guiding one's actions towards righteousness. The verse suggests that only those endowed with understanding will heed this message and benefit from it, highlighting the Qur'an's role as a guide for the thoughtful and reflective.
orig: أمن هو قانت آناء الليل ساجدا وقائما يحذر الآخرة ويرجو رحمة ربه قل هل يستوي الذين يعلمون والذين لا يعلمون إنما يتذكر أولو الألباب

translation: Say, O My servants who have believed, fear your Lord. For those who do good in this world is good, and the earth of Allah is spacious. Indeed, the patient will be given their reward without account.
interpretation: This verse is an encouragement from Allah to the believers to remain conscious of Him and to perform righteous deeds. It emphasizes that those who do good will be rewarded in this life with goodness, and it reassures believers that the earth is vast enough for them to find places where they can practice their faith freely. The promise at the end of the verse highlights the special reward for those who exhibit patience in their faith and actions; their reward will be immense and without any limit, reflecting Allah's boundless generosity and justice.
orig: قل يا عباد الذين آمنوا اتقوا ربكم للذين أحسنوا في هذه الدنيا حسنة وأرض الله واسعة إنما يوفى الصابرون أجرهم بغير حساب

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], "Indeed, I have been commanded to worship Allah, [being] sincere to Him in religion."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the core Islamic principle of monotheism, instructing the Prophet Muhammad, and by extension all Muslims, to worship Allah alone with complete sincerity and devotion. It underscores the importance of purity of intention in religious practices, highlighting that worship should be directed solely to Allah without any partners or intermediaries.
orig: قل إني أمرت أن أعبد الله مخلصا له الدين

translation: And I have been commanded to be the first of those who submit [to Allah].
interpretation: This verse underscores the Prophet Muhammad's role as the leader and exemplar in submitting to the will of Allah, emphasizing his position as the foremost in faith and obedience among Muslims.
orig: وأمرت لأن أكون أول المسلمين

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], "Indeed, I fear, if I should disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous Day."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophet Muhammad's deep awareness and fear of divine retribution for disobedience. It underscores the importance of obedience to God and the severe consequences of neglecting His commands, highlighting the concept of accountability on the Day of Judgment.
orig: قل إني أخاف إن عصيت ربي عذاب يوم عظيم

translation: Say, 'I worship Allah, sincere in my faith to Him.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sincerity in worship and devotion to Allah alone. It instructs the Prophet Muhammad, and by extension all Muslims, to declare their pure and exclusive worship to Allah, highlighting the core principle of Tawheed (the oneness of God) in Islam. This declaration serves as a reminder to maintain a genuine and undivided faith, free from any form of idolatry or association with other beings or entities.
orig: قل الله أعبد مخلصا له ديني

translation: So worship whatever you will besides Him. Say, 'Indeed, the losers are those who will lose themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Unquestionably, that is the clear loss.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility of worshipping anything other than Allah. It serves as a warning that those who choose to follow false deities or idols will ultimately face a profound loss on the Day of Judgment. The term 'losers' refers specifically to those who have not only failed to save themselves from Hellfire but have also led their families astray, resulting in their collective damnation. The phrase 'clear loss' underscores the undeniable and evident nature of this failure, highlighting the severe consequences of straying from the path of monotheism.
orig: فاعبدوا ما شئتم من دونه قل إن الخاسرين الذين خسروا أنفسهم وأهليهم يوم القيامة ألا ذلك هو الخسران المبين

translation: They will have canopies of fire above them and canopies [of fire] below them. With this Allah threatens His servants: O My servants, then fear Me.
interpretation: This verse describes the severe punishment awaiting those who disobey Allah, emphasizing the terrifying nature of Hell with fire surrounding them from above and below. It serves as a stark warning to believers to fear Allah and adhere to His commandments, highlighting the importance of taqwa (God-consciousness) as a means to avoid such a fate.
orig: لهم من فوقهم ظلل من النار ومن تحتهم ظلل ذلك يخوف الله به عباده يا عباد فاتقون

translation: And those who avoid the false deities, lest they worship them, and turn to Allah, for them are glad tidings. So give glad tidings to My servants.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of monotheism and the rejection of any form of idolatry or false worship. It highlights that those who consciously avoid worshipping anything other than Allah and turn towards Him in devotion will receive good news and blessings. The instruction to 'give glad tidings to My servants' serves as a directive to the Prophet Muhammad to convey this message of hope and reassurance to all believers, encouraging them to maintain their faith and devotion to Allah alone.
orig: والذين اجتنبوا الطاغوت أن يعبدوها وأنابوا إلى الله لهم البشرى فبشر عباد

translation: Those who listen to the speech and follow the best of it - those are the ones Allah has guided, and those are the people of understanding.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of discernment and wisdom in processing information. It suggests that true guidance from Allah is manifested in individuals who carefully listen to various opinions and choose to follow the most righteous and beneficial guidance. Such people are described as 'people of understanding' or 'those endowed with intellect,' indicating that wisdom and guidance are intertwined with the ability to critically evaluate and select the best course of action based on moral and ethical standards.
orig: الذين يستمعون القول فيتبعون أحسنه أولئك الذين هداهم الله وأولئك هم أولو الألباب

translation: Is then he who is consigned to the Fire better, or he who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection? Do what you will, for He sees all that you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the stark contrast between those destined for punishment and those who will be safe on the Day of Judgment. It serves as a reminder of personal accountability and the divine observation of all actions, urging believers to reflect on their deeds and the ultimate consequences thereof.
orig: أفمن حق عليه كلمة العذاب أفأنت تنقذ من في النار

translation: But those who fear their Lord, for them are chambers, above them chambers built, beneath which rivers flow. (This is) the promise of Allah. Allah does not fail in His promise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the reward for those who are mindful of Allah and live in fear of His displeasure. It describes their reward in the afterlife as luxurious chambers stacked upon each other, with rivers flowing beneath them, symbolizing abundance and eternal bliss. The repetition of 'chambers' and the flowing rivers underlines the grandeur and continuous nature of the reward. The verse reassures believers of the certainty of this promise, as Allah is described as never breaking His promises, instilling a sense of trust and hope in the divine commitment to reward righteousness.
orig: لكن الذين اتقوا ربهم لهم غرف من فوقها غرف مبنية تجري من تحتها الأنهار وعد الله لا يخلف الله الميعاد

translation: Do you not see that Allah sends down rain from the sky and makes it flow as springs in the earth; then He produces thereby crops of varying colors; then they wither and you see them turn yellow; then He makes them into scattered debris? Indeed in that is a reminder for those of understanding.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the cycle of life and the power of Allah over natural processes. It uses the metaphor of rain and plant growth to remind believers of the transient nature of life and the inevitability of death and decay. The varying colors of crops symbolize diversity and change, while their eventual withering and disintegration serve as a reminder of mortality. This cycle is presented as a lesson for those who possess wisdom and understanding, encouraging reflection on the signs of Allah in nature and the importance of preparing for the afterlife.
orig: ألم تر أن الله أنزل من السماء ماء فسلكه ينابيع في الأرض ثم يخرج به زرعا مختلفا ألوانه ثم يهيج فتراه مصفرا ثم يجعله حطاما إن في ذلك لذكرى لأولي الألباب

translation: Is he whose heart Allah has opened to Islam, so that he is in light from his Lord (equal to one who is hard-hearted)? Woe to those whose hearts are hardened against the remembrance of Allah! They are in manifest error.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual distinction between those who have embraced Islam and those who have not. It suggests that those whose hearts have been opened by Allah to accept Islam are guided by a divine light, indicating a state of enlightenment and closeness to God. Conversely, those who resist this guidance and harden their hearts against the remembrance of Allah are described as being in clear error, emphasizing the dire spiritual consequences of rejecting faith. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of an open and receptive heart in one's spiritual journey.
orig: أفمن شرح الله صدره للإسلام فهو على نور من ربه فويل للقاسية قلوبهم من ذكر الله أولئك في ضلال مبين

translation: Allah has sent down the best narration, a Book consistent in its verses, repeated, whereat shiver the skins of those who fear their Lord; then their skins and their hearts soften to the remembrance of Allah. That is the guidance of Allah by which He guides whom He wills. And one whom Allah sends astray - for him there is no guide.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the profound impact of the Qur'an on the believers. It describes how the Qur'an, being the best form of speech and perfectly coherent, induces a physical and emotional response in those who truly fear Allah. The shivering of the skin signifies an initial reaction of awe and fear, which then transforms into a softening of the heart and skin, symbolizing a deep spiritual connection and humility upon the remembrance of Allah. This transformation is presented as a divine guidance that Allah bestows upon whom He chooses, highlighting the selective nature of spiritual enlightenment and the ultimate authority of Allah in guiding or leading astray.
orig: الله نزل أحسن الحديث كتابا متشابها مثاني تقشعر منه جلود الذين يخشون ربهم ثم تلين جلودهم وقلوبهم إلى ذكر الله ذلك هدى الله يهدي به من يشاء ومن يضلل الله فما له من هاد

translation: Is he who shields himself with his face from the evil of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection [like the one who does not]? And it is said to the wrongdoers, 'Taste what you used to earn.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the stark contrast between the believers and the wrongdoers on the Day of Judgment. It illustrates the desperate act of a wrongdoer trying to shield himself from the severe punishment by using his face, symbolizing the futility and helplessness of their situation. Meanwhile, the command to the wrongdoers to 'taste what you used to earn' underscores the principle of accountability in Islam, where individuals will face the consequences of their actions. This serves as a reminder of the inevitability of divine justice and the importance of living a righteous life.
orig: أفمن يتقي بوجهه سوء العذاب يوم القيامة وقيل للظالمين ذوقوا ما كنتم تكسبون

translation: Those before them denied, so the punishment came upon them from where they did not perceive.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequence of disbelief and rejection of divine messages by previous nations. It serves as a warning that those who deny the truth will face unexpected punishment, emphasizing the inevitability and suddenness of divine retribution for those who follow in the footsteps of past deniers.
orig: كذب الذين من قبلهم فأتاهم العذاب من حيث لا يشعرون

translation: So Allah made them taste disgrace in the life of this world, and certainly the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if they only knew.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequence of disbelief and disobedience to Allah. The disgrace experienced in this worldly life is a direct result of their actions, serving as a precursor to the more severe punishment in the Hereafter. The phrase 'if they only knew' emphasizes the ignorance of the disbelievers regarding the severity of the punishment awaiting them, suggesting that had they been aware, they might have reconsidered their actions. This underscores the importance of knowledge and understanding in guiding one's behavior towards righteousness.
orig: فأذاقهم الله الخزي في الحياة الدنيا ولعذاب الآخرة أكبر لو كانوا يعلمون

translation: And We have certainly presented for the people in this Qur'an from every example that perhaps they will remember.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the comprehensive nature of the Qur'an, indicating that it contains a wide variety of parables and examples intended to serve as reminders and lessons for humanity. The purpose is to encourage reflection and remembrance of God's messages, thereby guiding people towards righteousness and moral conduct.
orig: ولقد ضربنا للناس في هذا القرآن من كل مثل لعلهم يتذكرون

translation: A Qur'an in Arabic, without any crookedness, so that they may become righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the clarity and straightforwardness of the Qur'an, which is revealed in the Arabic language to ensure its message is conveyed without distortion or ambiguity. The purpose of this clear revelation is to guide people towards righteousness and piety, encouraging them to live in accordance with the divine guidance provided.
orig: قرآنا عربيا غير ذي عوج لعلهم يتقون

translation: Allah presents an example: a man having partners in dispute with one another, and a man wholly belonging to another. Are the two equal in comparison? Praise be to Allah; but most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse uses a parable to illustrate the difference between associating partners with Allah (shirk) and pure monotheism (tawheed). The man with partners represents a person who worships multiple deities, leading to internal conflict and division. In contrast, the man wholly belonging to another symbolizes a person devoted solely to Allah, experiencing unity and peace. The rhetorical question emphasizes the clear superiority of tawheed over shirk, highlighting that true gratitude and understanding belong to Allah alone, though many people fail to recognize this truth due to their ignorance.
orig: ضرب الله مثلا رجلا فيه شركاء متشاكسون ورجلا سلما لرجل هل يستويان مثلا الحمد لله بل أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: Indeed, you will die, and indeed, they will die.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of the inevitability of death for all humans, emphasizing that no one, whether the Prophet Muhammad or his contemporaries, is exempt from this universal truth. It underscores the equality of all people before death and encourages a reflection on the transient nature of life, urging believers to focus on their deeds and their afterlife.
orig: إنك ميت وإنهم ميتون

translation: Then indeed you, on the Day of Resurrection, will be disputing before your Lord.
interpretation: This verse underscores the reality of the Day of Judgment where individuals will stand before Allah to argue or dispute over their deeds and actions in life. It highlights the accountability each person will face, emphasizing the importance of living righteously as all disputes will be settled in the presence of the Lord.
orig: ثم إنكم يوم القيامة عند ربكم تختصمون

translation: So who is more unjust than one who lies about Allah and denies the truth when it has come to him? Is there not in Hell a residence for the disbelievers?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity of denying the truth and lying about Allah after receiving clear evidence. It highlights that such actions are the epitome of injustice, as they not only reject the divine message but also mislead others. The rhetorical question at the end underscores the inevitable consequence of such disbelief, which is eternal damnation in Hell, serving as a stark warning and a reminder of the accountability one faces in the afterlife.
orig: فمن أظلم ممن كذب على الله وكذب بالصدق إذ جاءه أليس في جهنم مثوى للكافرين

translation: And he who comes with the truth and believes in it - those are the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of both possessing the truth and having faith in it. The 'righteous' or 'muttaqeen' are those who not only bring forth truthful information or actions but also sincerely believe in the truth they convey. This dual action of truthfulness and belief is what characterizes true righteousness in the eyes of Allah.
orig: والذي جاء بالصدق وصدق به أولئك هم المتقون

translation: They will have whatever they wish with their Lord. That is the reward of the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the promise of divine reward for those who perform good deeds. It suggests that in the afterlife, the righteous will be granted their desires by Allah, indicating a state of ultimate fulfillment and satisfaction as a result of their virtuous actions in this life. The phrase 'with their Lord' highlights the personal and intimate nature of this reward, underscoring the closeness between the believer and Allah.
orig: لهم ما يشاءون عند ربهم ذلك جزاء المحسنين

translation: So that Allah may forgive them their worst deeds and reward them for the best of what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's mercy and justice, indicating that He will overlook the believers' lesser sins and reward them generously based on their good deeds. It emphasizes the concept of divine forgiveness and the importance of striving to do good, as Allah will consider the best of one's actions when determining their reward.
orig: ليكفر الله عنهم أسوأ الذي عملوا ويجزيهم أجرهم بأحسن الذي كانوا يعملون

translation: Is not Allah sufficient for His servant? Yet they frighten you with those besides Him. And whoever Allah sends astray - for him there is no guide.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sufficiency and omnipotence of Allah, reassuring the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that Allah's support is enough against any opposition or threat from others. It highlights the futility of fearing anyone other than Allah, as those who are led astray by Allah cannot find guidance from any other source, underscoring the absolute sovereignty and guidance of Allah alone.
orig: أليس الله بكاف عبده ويخوفونك بالذين من دونه ومن يضلل الله فما له من هاد

translation: And whoever Allah guides - for him there is no misleader. Is not Allah Exalted in Might and Owner of Retribution?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and authority of Allah in guiding individuals. It asserts that once Allah has guided someone, no external force or entity can lead them astray from the path of righteousness. The rhetorical question at the end underscores Allah's might and His capability to exact retribution, reinforcing the notion that His guidance is both a protection and a blessing, while also serving as a reminder of His justice and power.
orig: ومن يهد الله فما له من مضل أليس الله بعزيز ذي انتقام

translation: And if you ask them who created the heavens and the earth, they will surely say, "Allah." Say, "Have you considered what you invoke besides Allah? If Allah intends harm for me, can they remove His harm? Or if He intends mercy for me, can they withhold His mercy?" Say, "Sufficient for me is Allah; upon Him rely the reliant."
interpretation: This verse highlights the fundamental belief in the oneness of God (Tawheed) and His absolute control over all affairs. It challenges the polytheists by questioning the efficacy of their idols or other deities they worship alongside Allah. The verse asserts that only Allah has the power to cause harm or bestow mercy, emphasizing that reliance should be placed solely on Him. This encourages believers to trust completely in Allah's wisdom and providence, reinforcing the concept of tawakkul (reliance on God) as a core aspect of faith.
orig: ولئن سألتهم من خلق السماوات والأرض ليقولن الله قل أفرأيتم ما تدعون من دون الله إن أرادني الله بضر هل هن كاشفات ضره أو أرادني برحمة هل هن ممسكات رحمته قل حسبي الله عليه يتوكل المتوكلون

translation: Say, O my people, work according to your position; indeed, I am working. You will soon know
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of individual accountability and the eventual revelation of the outcomes of one's actions. It encourages steadfastness in faith and good deeds despite opposition or differing paths chosen by others. The Prophet Muhammad is instructed to tell his people to continue on their course, while he will continue on his, with the assurance that the results of their respective actions will become clear in time. This serves as a reminder that everyone is responsible for their own actions and that divine justice will ultimately prevail.
orig: قل يا قوم اعملوا على مكانتكم إني عامل فسوف تعلمون

translation: Whoever it comes to, it will disgrace him with a torment and an abiding punishment will descend upon him.
interpretation: This verse warns of the consequences of disbelief and sin, emphasizing that those who are subjected to divine punishment will face not only immediate disgrace but also a continuous, everlasting torment in the hereafter. It serves as a reminder of the severity of divine retribution and the importance of adhering to the path of righteousness.
orig: من يأتيه عذاب يخزيه ويحل عليه عذاب مقيم

translation: Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book for mankind in truth. So whoever is guided is guided for his own soul, and whoever goes astray, he goes astray only to his own detriment. And you are not over them a manager.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin and purpose of the Qur'an, which is revealed as a guidance for all humanity. It underscores individual responsibility for one's spiritual journey; guidance or misguidance is a personal outcome, reflecting one's own choices and efforts. The Prophet Muhammad is reminded that he is not responsible for enforcing faith upon others, highlighting the principle of free will and personal accountability in Islam.
orig: إنا أنزلنا عليك الكتاب للناس بالحق فمن اهتدى فلنفسه ومن ضل فإنما يضل عليها وما أنت عليهم بوكيل

translation: Allah takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that do not die [He takes] during their sleep. Then He keeps those for which He has decreed death and releases the others for a specified term. Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's absolute control over life and death, illustrating His power to take souls during death or temporarily during sleep. The mention of sleep as a temporary death underscores the ease with which Allah can transition souls between states of life and death. The verse encourages reflection on these divine signs, urging believers to contemplate the deeper meanings of life, death, and the afterlife, thereby strengthening their faith and understanding of Allah's omnipotence.
orig: الله يتوفى الأنفس حين موتها والتي لم تمت في منامها فيمسك التي قضى عليها الموت ويرسل الأخرى إلى أجل مسمى إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يتفكرون

translation: Or have they taken intercessors besides Allah? Say, "Even if they do not possess anything and do not understand?"
interpretation: This verse challenges the concept of intercession by questioning the validity of seeking intercessors other than Allah. It emphasizes the futility of turning to beings who have no power or understanding, thereby reinforcing the Islamic belief in the absolute sovereignty and omniscience of Allah alone.
orig: أم اتخذوا من دون الله شفعاء قل أولو كانوا لا يملكون شيئا ولا يعقلون

translation: Say, "To Allah belongs all intercession." To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. Then to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the exclusive right of Allah to intercede on behalf of His creation. It underscores His supreme authority over all aspects of existence, as He is the sole possessor of the dominion of the heavens and the earth. The verse also reminds believers of the ultimate return to Allah, reinforcing the concept of accountability and the finality of returning to the Creator for judgment.
orig: قل لله الشفاعة جميعا له ملك السماوات والأرض ثم إليه ترجعون

translation: And when Allah alone is mentioned, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter shrink with aversion, but when those besides Him are mentioned, behold, they rejoice.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual condition of those who reject the concept of the Hereafter. When the name of Allah is mentioned in isolation, emphasizing His sole divinity, it causes discomfort and aversion in their hearts because it challenges their worldly attachments and disbelief in accountability after death. Conversely, when other deities or figures are mentioned alongside or instead of Allah, they feel joy and satisfaction, as it aligns with their polytheistic or materialistic inclinations, allowing them to maintain their false sense of security and comfort in this life.
orig: وإذا ذكر الله وحده اشمأزت قلوب الذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة وإذا ذكر الذين من دونه إذا هم يستبشرون

translation: Say, 'O Allah, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, You will judge between Your servants concerning that over which they used to differ.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate authority and omniscience of Allah. It serves as a reminder to believers that all disputes and differences among people will be resolved by Allah's just judgment. The invocation acknowledges Allah's role as the Creator and the All-Knowing, reinforcing the belief that He alone has the complete understanding and the right to arbitrate in matters of disagreement. This verse encourages Muslims to trust in Allah's wisdom and justice, especially in situations where human judgment may falter or differ.
orig: قل اللهم فاطر السماوات والأرض عالم الغيب والشهادة أنت تحكم بين عبادك في ما كانوا فيه يختلفون

translation: And if those who wronged had all that is in the earth entirely and the like of it with it, they would [attempt to] ransom themselves thereby from the worst of punishment on the Day of Resurrection. And there will appear to them from Allah that which they had not taken into account.
interpretation: This verse highlights the severity and inevitability of divine punishment on the Day of Judgment.
