It illustrates that even if the wrongdoers possessed everything in the world, and even more, they would be willing to offer it all to escape the torment they face. Yet, their wealth and possessions would be of no avail. The verse also emphasizes the unexpected nature of divine justice, as wrongdoers will encounter consequences they never anticipated, underscoring the importance of righteousness and the futility of material wealth in the face of divine judgment.
orig: ولو أن للذين ظلموا ما في الأرض جميعا ومثله معه لافتدوا به من سوء العذاب يوم القيامة وبدا لهم من الله ما لم يكونوا يحتسبون

translation: And the evil of what they earned appeared to them, and that which they used to mock at surrounded them.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the moment of realization for those who committed wrongdoings, where the consequences of their actions become visibly apparent and inescapable. It serves as a reminder that the mockery and disbelief they showed towards divine warnings and the truth ultimately encircles them, emphasizing the inevitability of facing the repercussions of one's deeds.
orig: وبدا لهم سيئات ما كسبوا وحاق بهم ما كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: So when adversity touches man, he calls upon Us; then when We bestow on him a favor from Us, he says, "I have only been given it because of [my] knowledge." Rather, it is a trial, but most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to turn to God in times of distress and attribute success to personal merit when blessed. It serves as a reminder that the worldly blessings bestowed upon us are tests from God, meant to assess our gratitude and humility. Most people fail to recognize this, becoming arrogant and attributing their achievements to their own abilities rather than acknowledging divine favor.
orig: فإذا مس الإنسان ضر دعانا ثم إذا خولناه نعمة منا قال إنما أوتيته على علم بل هي فتنة ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: Those before them said it, but what they earned did not avail them.
interpretation: This verse reflects on the futility of relying solely on one's worldly achievements or material gains for salvation. It serves as a reminder that previous generations who uttered similar claims of security or denial of the truth found that their material possessions and deeds did not protect them from the consequences of their disbelief or moral failings. The verse underscores the importance of faith and righteous actions over mere worldly accomplishments.
orig: قد قالها الذين من قبلهم فما أغنى عنهم ما كانوا يكسبون

translation: So the evil (consequences) of what they earned struck them, and those who did wrong from among these (people) will be struck by the evil (consequences) of what they earned, and they will not be able to escape.
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle of divine justice and accountability in Islam. It emphasizes that the negative outcomes individuals experience are a direct result of their own actions ("ما كسبوا"). The verse serves as a warning that those who engage in wrongdoing ("الذين ظلموا") will inevitably face the repercussions of their deeds, reinforcing the concept that no one can evade the consequences of their actions ("وما هم بمعجزين"). This message is intended to encourage moral behavior and the avoidance of sin, highlighting the inescapable nature of divine retribution.
orig: فأصابهم سيئات ما كسبوا والذين ظلموا من هؤلاء سيصيبهم سيئات ما كسبوا وما هم بمعجزين

translation: Do they not know that Allah extends provision for whom He wills and restricts [it]? Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine authority of Allah over the distribution of sustenance. It challenges the believers to recognize that the varying levels of wealth and provision among people are determined by Allah's will, not by human merit or effort alone. The verse serves as a reminder and a test of faith, urging believers to trust in Allah's wisdom and justice in managing the affairs of the world. The signs mentioned are meant to strengthen the faith of those who truly believe, encouraging them to see beyond material disparities and to trust in the overarching plan of Allah.
orig: أولم يعلموا أن الله يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء ويقدر إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يؤمنون

translation: Say, O My servants who have transgressed against themselves [by sinning], do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the boundless mercy and forgiveness of Allah. It serves as a message of hope and encouragement for those who have committed sins, reassuring them that no matter the extent of their transgressions, they should not lose hope in Allah's forgiveness. The verse highlights that Allah's attribute as the Forgiving and the Merciful is central to His nature, urging believers to turn back to Him in repentance, confident in His readiness to forgive all sins.
orig: قل يا عبادي الذين أسرفوا على أنفسهم لا تقنطوا من رحمة الله إن الله يغفر الذنوب جميعا إنه هو الغفور الرحيم

translation: And turn to your Lord and submit to Him before the punishment comes upon you; then you will not be helped.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the urgency of repentance and submission to Allah before the arrival of divine punishment. It serves as a reminder that the opportunity for repentance is available until a certain point, after which it will be too late to seek help or forgiveness. The verse encourages believers to proactively turn back to Allah and embrace Islam fully, highlighting the consequences of delaying this crucial act of faith.
orig: وأنيبوا إلى ربكم وأسلموا له من قبل أن يأتيكم العذاب ثم لا تنصرون

translation: And follow the best of what has been revealed to you from your Lord before the punishment comes upon you suddenly while you do not perceive.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to the divine guidance provided in the Qur'an. It urges believers to actively follow the most excellent teachings and commandments revealed by Allah, highlighting the urgency of doing so before an unexpected punishment arrives. The verse serves as a reminder of the transient nature of life and the suddenness with which divine judgment can come, encouraging a proactive and sincere commitment to righteousness and obedience to God's will.
orig: واتبعوا أحسن ما أنزل إليكم من ربكم من قبل أن يأتيكم العذاب بغتة وأنتم لا تشعرون

translation: That the soul should say, 'Oh, woe to me for what I neglected in the presence of Allah, and I was indeed among those who mocked.'
interpretation: This verse reflects on the regret a person might feel on the Day of Judgment for having neglected their duties towards Allah and for having mocked or taken lightly the signs and commands of Allah during their life. It serves as a warning to believers to be mindful of their actions and to take their religious obligations seriously, as the realization of one's mistakes will come too late after death.
orig: أن تقول نفس يا حسرتا على ما فرطت في جنب الله وإن كنت لمن الساخرين

translation: Or you might say, 'If only Allah had guided me, I would have been among the righteous.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to make excuses for one's lack of faith or righteousness by attributing it to a lack of divine guidance. It serves as a reminder that individuals are responsible for their choices and actions, and cannot solely blame external factors, such as divine intervention, for their spiritual state. The verse encourages self-reflection and accountability in one's journey towards righteousness.
orig: أو تقول لو أن الله هداني لكنت من المتقين

translation: Or he will say, when he sees the punishment, 'If only I had another chance, I would be among the righteous.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the regret and realization that comes too late for some individuals when they witness the consequences of their actions in the afterlife. It underscores the human tendency to wish for a second chance to amend one's ways upon facing divine judgment, emphasizing the importance of living righteously in the present life without delay.
orig: أو تقول حين ترى العذاب لو أن لي كرة فأكون من المحسنين

translation: Yes, indeed, My verses came to you, but you denied them and were arrogant, and you were among the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the accountability of individuals who have been presented with clear signs and evidence of the truth (referred to as "My verses") but have chosen to reject them out of arrogance. It underscores the notion that denial of divine messages is often coupled with pride, leading to disbelief. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of such actions, emphasizing the importance of humility and acceptance in the face of divine guidance.
orig: بلى قد جاءتك آياتي فكذبت بها واستكبرت وكنت من الكافرين

translation: And on the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied against Allah [with] their faces blackened. Is there not in Hell an abode for the arrogant?
interpretation: This verse illustrates the consequence of attributing falsehood to Allah, symbolized by the blackening of the faces of the wrongdoers on the Day of Judgment. It serves as a warning that those who are arrogant and lie about Allah will find their ultimate dwelling in Hell, emphasizing the severe punishment awaiting those who exhibit such behavior.
orig: ويوم القيامة ترى الذين كذبوا على الله وجوههم مسودة أليس في جهنم مثوى للمتكبرين

translation: And Allah will save those who feared Him to their place of success; no evil will touch them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine promise of salvation and protection for those who maintain a state of piety and fear of God. It reassures believers that their adherence to righteousness will lead them to a state of ultimate safety and joy in the hereafter, where they will be shielded from any form of harm or sorrow. This underscores the importance of taqwa (God-consciousness) as a means to achieve eternal peace and security.
orig: وينجي الله الذين اتقوا بمفازتهم لا يمسهم السوء ولا هم يحزنون

translation: Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is the Guardian over all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and sovereignty of Allah. It underscores that He is not only the originator of everything in existence but also maintains control and oversight over all aspects of creation. This highlights the dependence of all things on Allah and His continuous involvement in the sustenance and management of the universe.
orig: الله خالق كل شيء وهو على كل شيء وكيل

translation: To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth. And those who disbelieve in the verses of Allah, it is they who are the losers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's supreme control over the universe, symbolized by the keys of the heavens and the earth. It serves as a reminder of His omnipotence and authority. The latter part of the verse warns that those who reject the signs and revelations of Allah are ultimately the ones who will suffer loss, highlighting the consequences of disbelief and the importance of faith in achieving true success.
orig: له مقاليد السماوات والأرض والذين كفروا بآيات الله أولئك هم الخاسرون

translation: Say, 'Do you order me to worship other than Allah, O ignorant ones?'
interpretation: This verse is a direct challenge to those who suggest worshipping deities other than Allah. It highlights the absurdity of such a suggestion by labeling those who propose it as ignorant, emphasizing the clear and exclusive monotheism that Islam advocates. The verse underscores the Prophet Muhammad's unwavering commitment to the worship of Allah alone, rejecting any form of polytheism or idolatry.
orig: قل أفغير الله تأمروني أعبد أيها الجاهلون

translation: And We have revealed to you and to those before you that if you associate [anything] with Allah, your deeds will surely become worthless, and you will surely be among the losers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental principle of monotheism in Islam, warning that associating partners with Allah (shirk) nullifies all good deeds and leads to ultimate loss in the hereafter. It underscores the gravity of maintaining pure faith and the severe consequences of deviating into polytheism, a message consistently conveyed through divine revelation to prophets across time.
orig: ولقد أوحي إليك وإلى الذين من قبلك لئن أشركت ليحبطن عملك ولتكونن من الخاسرين

translation: Rather, worship Allah and be among the grateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of directing all worship solely to Allah, highlighting monotheism as a core principle of faith. It also encourages believers to cultivate an attitude of gratitude towards Allah, which is seen as a way to enhance one's spiritual connection and contentment with divine will.
orig: بل الله فاعبد وكن من الشاكرين

translation: And they have not appraised Allah with true appraisal, while the earth entirely will be within His grip on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded in His right hand. Exalted is He and high above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence and majesty of Allah, highlighting that humans fail to fully comprehend His greatness. The imagery of the earth being in His grip and the heavens folded in His hand illustrates His absolute control over creation. The verse also serves as a reminder of the Day of Resurrection, urging believers to recognize Allah's supreme power and to avoid associating partners with Him, as He is far above such falsehoods.
orig: وما قدروا الله حق قدره والأرض جميعا قبضته يوم القيامة والسماوات مطويات بيمينه سبحانه وتعالى عما يشركون

translation: And the Trumpet will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall dead, except whom Allah wills. Then it will be blown again, and behold, they will be standing, looking on.
interpretation: This verse describes the events of the Day of Judgment, emphasizing the power of Allah over life and death. The first blowing of the Trumpet signifies the end of life as we know it, causing all beings to die except those Allah chooses to spare. The second blowing of the Trumpet signifies the resurrection, where all beings are brought back to life and stand to face judgment. This illustrates Allah's absolute control over creation and the inevitability of the afterlife, urging believers to prepare for this day.
orig: ونفخ في الصور فصعق من في السماوات ومن في الأرض إلا من شاء الله ثم نفخ فيه أخرى فإذا هم قيام ينظرون

translation: And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord, and the Book will be placed [open], and the prophets and the witnesses will be brought, and it will be judged between them with truth, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Judgment, where the earth will be illuminated by the divine light of Allah, signifying the clarity and truth that will prevail. The Book, representing the record of deeds, will be laid open for all to see, ensuring transparency in judgment. The prophets and witnesses will be present to testify, emphasizing the fairness and justice of the proceedings. The judgment will be based on truth, and no one will be treated unjustly, underscoring the ultimate justice of Allah's court.
orig: وأشرقت الأرض بنور ربها ووضع الكتاب وجيء بالنبيين والشهداء وقضي بينهم بالحق وهم لا يظلمون

translation: And every soul will be paid in full for what it has done, and He is most knowing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of accountability in Islam, where every individual will be recompensed precisely according to their actions. It underscores God's omniscience, indicating that He has complete knowledge of all deeds, whether apparent or hidden. This serves as a reminder for believers to be mindful of their actions, knowing that they will face the consequences in the afterlife.
orig: ووفيت كل نفس ما عملت وهو أعلم بما يفعلون

translation: And those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in groups until, when they reach it, its gates are opened and its keepers will say, 'Did there not come to you messengers from among you, reciting to you the verses of your Lord and warning you of the meeting of this Day of yours?' They will say, 'Yes, but the word of punishment has been justified against the disbelievers.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the accountability of individuals for their choices regarding faith. It illustrates the moment of reckoning for those who rejected the divine messages conveyed through the prophets. The disbelievers are confronted by the guardians of Hell, reminding them of the warnings they received about the Day of Judgment. Their acknowledgment of having received these messages yet choosing disbelief highlights the theme of free will and the consequences of rejecting guidance. The phrase 'the word of punishment has been justified against the disbelievers' emphasizes that their fate is a result of their own actions, affirming the justice of divine retribution.
orig: وسيق الذين كفروا إلى جهنم زمرا حتى إذا جاءوها فتحت أبوابها وقال لهم خزنتها ألم يأتكم رسل منكم يتلون عليكم آيات ربكم وينذرونكم لقاء يومكم هذا قالوا بلى ولكن حقت كلمة العذاب على الكافرين

translation: It will be said, 'Enter the gates of Hell to abide eternally therein, and how wretched is the abode of the arrogant.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the consequence of arrogance and disobedience to God. It illustrates that those who exhibit pride and reject humility will be condemned to Hell, emphasizing that such a fate is fittingly described as a wretched abode. The mention of 'gates of Hell' symbolizes the inescapable and severe punishment awaiting the arrogant, serving as a stern warning against the perils of pride.
orig: قيل ادخلوا أبواب جهنم خالدين فيها فبئس مثوى المتكبرين

translation: And those who feared their Lord will be led to Paradise in groups until, when they reach it while its gates have been opened and its keepers say, 'Peace be upon you; you have become pure; so enter it to abide eternally therein.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the reward for those who have lived in fear and reverence of Allah, illustrating their journey to Paradise. The imagery of being led in groups signifies a communal aspect of entering Paradise, emphasizing unity among the righteous. The opening of the gates and the greeting of peace from the keepers symbolize the welcoming and pure environment of Paradise. The declaration of 'you have become pure' suggests a transformation or purification process that believers undergo, which qualifies them for eternal residence in Paradise. This verse serves as an encouragement for believers to maintain piety and righteousness, promising them a serene and everlasting abode in the afterlife.
orig: وسيق الذين اتقوا ربهم إلى الجنة زمرا حتى إذا جاءوها وفتحت أبوابها وقال لهم خزنتها سلام عليكم طبتم فادخلوها خالدين

translation: And they will say, "Praise to Allah, who has fulfilled His promise to us and has made us inherit the earth [so] we may settle in Paradise wherever we will. And excellent is the reward of [righteous] workers."
interpretation: This verse reflects the gratitude and joy of the believers upon entering Paradise. It underscores the fulfillment of God's promise to the righteous, highlighting the concept of divine justice and reward. The believers' ability to settle in Paradise 'wherever they will' symbolizes the ultimate freedom and satisfaction granted to them as a result of their faith and good deeds. The phrase 'excellent is the reward of [righteous] workers' emphasizes that the rewards in the afterlife are commensurate with one's efforts and righteousness in this world, encouraging believers to strive in their actions.
orig: وقالوا الحمد لله الذي صدقنا وعده وأورثنا الأرض نتبوأ من الجنة حيث نشاء فنعم أجر العاملين

translation: And you will see the angels surrounding the Throne, glorifying the praises of their Lord. And it will be judged between them in truth, and it will be said, 'Praise be to Allah, the Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse depicts a scene from the Day of Judgment where the angels are encircling the Throne of Allah, continuously engaged in glorifying and praising Him. This imagery emphasizes the majesty and reverence of the divine presence. The judgment mentioned signifies the ultimate justice and fairness of Allah's decree on that day. The concluding praise to Allah as the Lord of the worlds reinforces the theme of divine sovereignty and the universal acknowledgment of His greatness and authority.
orig: وترى الملائكة حافين من حول العرش يسبحون بحمد ربهم وقضي بينهم بالحق وقيل الحمد لله رب العالمين

translation: Ha Mim
interpretation: These are among the disjointed letters (muqatta'at) found at the beginning of certain chapters in the Qur'an. Their precise meaning is known only to Allah, but they are believed to hold profound significance and possibly serve as a means of drawing the reader's attention to the divine nature of the text that follows.
orig: حم

translation: The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Exalted in Might, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin of the Qur'an, highlighting that it is a revelation directly from Allah, who possesses ultimate power and complete knowledge. It underscores the authority and reliability of the Qur'an as a source of guidance, stemming from the attributes of Allah as being both mighty and omniscient.
orig: تنزيل الكتاب من الله العزيز العليم

translation: The Forgiver of sin, the Acceptor of repentance, the Severe in punishment, the Bestower (of favors). La ilaha illa Huwa (none has the right to be worshipped but He), to Him is the final return.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the multifaceted nature of Allah's attributes, highlighting His mercy and forgiveness alongside His justice and severity in punishment. It underscores the concept of Tawhid, the oneness of God, affirming that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah, and that all beings will ultimately return to Him. This serves as a reminder of the accountability of one's actions and the importance of seeking forgiveness and repentance, while also acknowledging the ultimate power and sovereignty of Allah.
orig: غافر الذنب وقابل التوب شديد العقاب ذي الطول لا إله إلا هو إليه المصير

translation: None disputes concerning the signs of Allah except those who disbelieve, so let not their going about in the land deceive you.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that only those who have rejected faith engage in arguments against the clear signs of Allah. It warns believers not to be misled by the apparent success or freedom of movement of these disbelievers in the world, as their actions and mobility do not validate their disbelief or negate the truth of Allah's signs.
orig: ما يجادل في آيات الله إلا الذين كفروا فلا يغررك تقلبهم في البلاد

translation: The people of Noah denied before them, and the factions after them. And every nation intended to seize their messenger, and argued falsely to refute the truth. So I seized them, and how [terrible] was My punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the recurring theme of disbelief among various nations throughout history, starting with the people of Noah. It underscores the universal human tendency to reject divine messages and messengers, often resorting to false arguments to deny the truth. The verse serves as a warning that such rejection leads to divine retribution, emphasizing the severity of God's punishment for those who persistently oppose His prophets and the truth they bring. It encourages reflection on the consequences of disbelief and the importance of accepting and following divine guidance.
orig: كذبت قبلهم قوم نوح والأحزاب من بعدهم وهمت كل أمة برسولهم ليأخذوه وجادلوا بالباطل ليدحضوا به الحق فأخذتهم فكيف كان عقاب

translation: And thus the word of your Lord has been justified against those who disbelieved, that they are the companions of the Fire.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability and justice of God's decree. It indicates that those who reject faith and disbelieve in God's messages will face the consequences of their choices, as it is a fulfillment of God's promise that they will be inhabitants of Hell. This serves as a reminder of the accountability and the ultimate reality of the afterlife, emphasizing the importance of belief and righteousness.
orig: وكذلك حقت كلمت ربك على الذين كفروا أنهم أصحاب النار

translation: Those who bear the Throne and those around it glorify the praise of their Lord and believe in Him and ask forgiveness for those who have believed: 'Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge, so forgive those who have repented and followed Your way and protect them from the punishment of the Hellfire.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the intercessory role of the angels who bear the Throne of Allah and those around it. They not only glorify and believe in Allah but also seek forgiveness for the believers on earth. The verse emphasizes Allah's vast mercy and knowledge, which encompasses everything, and it is a plea for forgiveness for those who have repented and followed His path, asking for protection from the torment of Hell. This underscores the importance of repentance and following the divine path, as well as the supportive role of celestial beings in the spiritual journey of humans.
orig: الذين يحملون العرش ومن حوله يسبحون بحمد ربهم ويؤمنون به ويستغفرون للذين آمنوا ربنا وسعت كل شيء رحمة وعلما فاغفر للذين تابوا واتبعوا سبيلك وقهم عذاب الجحيم

translation: Our Lord, and admit them to Gardens of Eden which You have promised them and whoever was righteous among their fathers, their spouses and their offspring. Indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse is a supplication to Allah, asking Him to grant entry into Paradise not only to the believers themselves but also to their righteous family members. It emphasizes the communal aspect of faith and the hope that one's good deeds and faith can benefit their loved ones. The attributes of Allah mentioned, 'the Exalted in Might, the Wise,' underscore His power and wisdom in fulfilling His promises and managing the affairs of the universe.
orig: ربنا وأدخلهم جنات عدن التي وعدتهم ومن صلح من آبائهم وأزواجهم وذرياتهم إنك أنت العزيز الحكيم

translation: And protected them from the evil of that Day, and whoever is protected from the evil of that Day has indeed been shown mercy by Him. And that is the great triumph.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate protection and mercy of Allah on the Day of Judgment. Those who are shielded from the evil and punishment of that Day are recipients of Allah's profound mercy, which is described as the greatest success one can achieve. It underscores the importance of striving for righteousness in this life to attain this divine protection and ultimate victory in the hereafter.
orig: وقهم السيئات ومن تق السيئات يومئذ فقد رحمته وذلك هو الفوز العظيم

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve cry out, "The hatred of Allah for you is greater than your hatred for yourselves when you call to faith and then disbelieve."
interpretation: This verse highlights the self-destructive nature of disbelief. It suggests that when individuals are called to faith but choose to reject it, they are essentially harming themselves more than anyone else could. The phrase "hatred of Allah" indicates the severity of divine displeasure towards those who turn away from faith after being invited to it, emphasizing the gravity of their choice and its consequences.
orig: إن الذين كفروا ينادون لمقت الله أكبر من مقتكم أنفسكم إذ تدعون إلى الإيمان فتكفرون

translation: They will say, 'Our Lord, You made us die twice and gave us life twice, and we confess our sins. So is there any way to get out?'
interpretation: This verse reflects the acknowledgment by the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment of their repeated cycles of life and death, symbolizing their opportunities to recognize and follow the truth. They admit their sins and inquire about the possibility of escaping their punishment, indicating a final realization of their errors and a desperate hope for salvation, which underscores the themes of accountability and the finality of divine judgment.
orig: قالوا ربنا أمتنا اثنتين وأحييتنا اثنتين فاعترفنا بذنوبنا فهل إلى خروج من سبيل

translation: That is because, when Allah alone is called upon, you disbelieve; but if others are associated with Him, you believe. So judgment belongs to Allah, the Most High, the Great.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy and inconsistency in the faith of some people who reject the worship of Allah alone, yet accept the worship of Him alongside other deities. It underscores the principle of tawhid (the oneness of God) and criticizes the practice of shirk (associating partners with Allah). The verse asserts that ultimate judgment and authority belong solely to Allah, emphasizing His supreme status and power over all creation.
orig: ذلكم بأنه إذا دعي الله وحده كفرتم وإن يشرك به تؤمنوا فالحكم لله العلي الكبير

translation: He is the One who shows you His signs and sends down to you from the sky provision. And none will remember except those who turn back [to Allah].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's role as the provider and sustainer of life, illustrating His omnipotence through the natural phenomena and the provision of sustenance from the sky, such as rain. The latter part of the verse highlights the spiritual insight that only those who are inclined to repent and turn back to Allah will truly appreciate and remember these signs, underscoring the importance of a repentant heart in recognizing divine guidance and blessings.
orig: هو الذي يريكم آياته وينزل لكم من السماء رزقا وما يتذكر إلا من ينيب

translation: So call upon Allah, being sincere to Him in religion, even if the disbelievers dislike it.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to worship and call upon Allah with complete sincerity and devotion to the religion, regardless of the opposition or dislike from those who disbelieve. It emphasizes the importance of maintaining steadfastness in faith and practice, highlighting that true devotion to Allah should not be swayed by external pressures or the disapproval of non-believers.
orig: فادعوا الله مخلصين له الدين ولو كره الكافرون

translation: High above all orders (Exalted), the Lord of the Throne sends down the Spirit at His command upon whom He wills of His servants, that he may warn of the Day of Meeting.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the supreme authority and transcendence of Allah, who is described as 'High above all orders' and 'the Lord of the Throne'. The 'Spirit' mentioned here is understood to be a divine revelation or inspiration, which Allah sends to chosen individuals among His servants. This act of sending the Spirit is a manifestation of Allah's sovereign will, as He chooses whom to bestow this honor upon. The purpose of this revelation is to warn humanity about the 'Day of Meeting', which refers to the Day of Judgment, when all individuals will meet Allah and be held accountable for their deeds. Thus, the verse underscores the roles of divine revelation and prophetic warning in preparing humanity for the ultimate accountability before Allah.
orig: رفيع الدرجات ذو العرش يلقي الروح من أمره على من يشاء من عباده لينذر يوم التلاق

translation: The Day when they will appear; nothing about them will be hidden from Allah. To whom belongs the dominion this Day? To Allah, the One, the Subduer.
interpretation: This verse speaks to the Day of Judgment, emphasizing the absolute knowledge and sovereignty of Allah. On this day, all beings will be exposed before Allah, with no aspect of their lives or deeds concealed. The rhetorical question about dominion underscores that ultimate power and authority belong solely to Allah, described here as Al-Wahid (The One) and Al-Qahhar (The Subduer), reinforcing His unique and overwhelming power over all creation.
orig: يوم هم بارزون لا يخفى على الله منهم شيء لمن الملك اليوم لله الواحد القهار

translation: Today every soul will be recompensed for what it has earned. No injustice will there be today. Indeed, Allah is swift in account.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Day of Judgment, where every individual will receive the consequences of their actions with absolute justice. The phrase "no injustice will there be today" underscores that God's judgment will be fair and precise, reflecting the belief that Allah is swift and accurate in His accounting of deeds. This serves as a reminder of the accountability each person has for their actions in life, urging believers to live righteously knowing that their deeds will be meticulously evaluated.
orig: اليوم تجزى كل نفس بما كسبت لا ظلم اليوم إن الله سريع الحساب

translation: And warn them of the Day of the Approaching, when hearts will be at the throats, choking. There will be no close friend and no intercessor for the wrongdoers, who will be obeyed.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder and a warning to believers about the Day of Judgment, which is described as approaching swiftly. The imagery of hearts being at the throats and choking conveys the intense fear and anxiety that people will experience on that day. The verse emphasizes the isolation and helplessness of the wrongdoers, who will find no support or intercession from friends or advocates, underscoring the importance of living righteously and preparing for the accountability that awaits in the hereafter.
orig: وأنذرهم يوم الآزفة إذ القلوب لدى الحناجر كاظمين ما للظالمين من حميم ولا شفيع يطاع

translation: He knows the treachery of the eyes, and what the hearts conceal.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's omniscience, highlighting His complete awareness of even the most subtle forms of betrayal or deceit, such as the fleeting glances of the eyes, and the innermost secrets and intentions hidden within the hearts of individuals.
orig: يعلم خائنة الأعين وما تخفي الصدور

translation: And Allah judges with truth, while those they call upon besides Him do not judge with anything. Indeed, Allah is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute authority and justice of Allah in His judgments, contrasting it with the futility of seeking judgment from any other beings or idols, which have no real power or ability to judge. It reassures believers that Allah is fully aware and observant of all matters, reinforcing the concept of His omnipotence and omniscience.
orig: والله يقضي بالحق والذين يدعون من دونه لا يقضون بشيء إن الله هو السميع البصير

translation: Have they not traveled through the earth and observed how was the end of those before them? They were greater than them in strength and in impact on the earth, but Allah seized them for their sins. And they had no protector against Allah.
interpretation: This verse urges believers to reflect on the historical fate of past civilizations as a lesson. It emphasizes that no matter how powerful or influential a people may be, their ultimate downfall can come as a consequence of their sins if they do not heed divine warnings. The verse serves as a reminder of the transient nature of worldly power and the importance of living righteously under the watchful eyes of Allah, who holds ultimate authority and from whom no one can seek protection if He decides to punish.
orig: أولم يسيروا في الأرض فينظروا كيف كان عاقبة الذين كانوا من قبلهم كانوا هم أشد منهم قوة وآثارا في الأرض فأخذهم الله بذنوبهم وما كان لهم من الله من واق

translation: That is because their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they disbelieved, so Allah seized them. Indeed, He is Powerful and Severe in penalty.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequence of rejecting the clear signs and messages brought by the prophets. It highlights that disbelief in the face of evident truth leads to divine retribution. The mention of Allah being "Powerful and Severe in penalty" serves as a reminder of His omnipotence and the seriousness of the consequences for those who deny His messengers. It underscores the importance of heeding the warnings and guidance provided by the prophets, as failure to do so results in severe punishment.
orig: ذلك بأنهم كانت تأتيهم رسلهم بالبينات فكفروا فأخذهم الله إنه قوي شديد العقاب

translation: And indeed, We sent Moses with Our signs and a clear authority.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine mission of Moses, indicating that he was sent by God with clear miracles and undeniable proof of his prophethood. It highlights the legitimacy and strength of Moses' message, supported by evident signs from God, which served to validate his authority among his people.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا موسى بآياتنا وسلطان مبين

translation: To Pharaoh, Haman, and Qarun; then they said, 'A magician, a liar.'
interpretation: This verse refers to the accusations made by Pharaoh, Haman, and Qarun against Moses, labeling him as a magician and a liar. It highlights the rejection and disbelief of these powerful figures towards the message of truth brought by Moses, illustrating the theme of resistance to divine guidance by those in authority who feel threatened by it.
orig: إلى فرعون وهامان وقارون فقالوا ساحر كذاب

translation: So when he brought them the truth from Us, they said, 'Kill the sons of those who have believed with him and keep their women alive.' But the plot of the disbelievers is nothing but in error.
interpretation: This verse highlights the extreme measures taken by the disbelievers in response to the truth brought by a prophet. It reflects their fear and desperation, leading them to commit heinous acts against innocent believers, specifically targeting the male children to prevent the growth of the new faith. The verse underscores the moral and strategic error of the disbelievers, illustrating that their schemes against the truth are ultimately futile and misguided.
orig: فلما جاءهم بالحق من عندنا قالوا اقتلوا أبناء الذين آمنوا معه واستحيوا نساءهم وما كيد الكافرين إلا في ضلال

translation: And Pharaoh said, 'Leave me to kill Moses and let him call upon his Lord. Indeed, I fear that he will change your religion or that he will cause corruption to appear in the land.'
interpretation: Pharaoh's statement reflects his fear of losing control and authority over his people. He perceives Moses' influence as a threat to the established religious and social order, which he fears might lead to chaos and the undermining of his rule. This verse highlights the resistance of those in power to prophetic messages that challenge the status quo and promote justice and monotheism.
orig: وقال فرعون ذروني أقتل موسى وليدع ربه إني أخاف أن يبدل دينكم أو أن يظهر في الأرض الفساد

translation: And Moses said, "Indeed, I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord from every arrogant one who does not believe in the Day of Account."
interpretation: Moses expresses his reliance on God for protection against the tyranny and disbelief of those who reject the accountability of the Day of Judgment. This verse underscores the theme of seeking divine refuge from the arrogance and injustice of those who deny the afterlife, emphasizing the importance of faith in God's ultimate justice.
orig: وقال موسى إني عذت بربي وربكم من كل متكبر لا يؤمن بيوم الحساب

translation: And a believing man from the family of Pharaoh, who concealed his faith, said, 'Would you kill a man because he says, "My Lord is Allah," while he has brought you clear proofs from your Lord? And if he is a liar, then his lie is upon him; but if he is truthful, some of what he promises you will befall you. Indeed, Allah does not guide one who is a transgressor and a liar.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the courage and moral conviction of a believer within the oppressive environment of Pharaoh's court. It underscores the theme of individual responsibility and the importance of standing for truth, even in the face of overwhelming societal pressure. The believer's argument emphasizes the rationality of faith and the consequences of rejecting a truthful messenger, illustrating that personal accountability for one's actions and beliefs is paramount. It also reflects on the nature of guidance, suggesting that those who are transgressors and liars are not guided by Allah, reinforcing the moral and ethical dimensions of faith.
orig: وقال رجل مؤمن من آل فرعون يكتم إيمانه أتقتلون رجلا أن يقول ربي الله وقد جاءكم بالبينات من ربكم وإن يك كاذبا فعليه كذبه وإن يك صادقا يصبكم بعض الذي يعدكم إن الله لا يهدي من هو مسرف كذاب

translation: O my people, today you have the dominion and are uppermost in the land. But who will help us against the wrath of Allah if it comes upon us? Pharaoh said, 'I do not show you except what I see, and I do not guide you except to the path of right guidance.'
interpretation: This verse reflects a moment of confrontation between a believer from Pharaoh's household and Pharaoh himself. The believer warns his people of their vulnerability despite their current power, emphasizing that no one can protect them from God's punishment if it were to befall them. This highlights the theme of divine omnipotence and the futility of human power against God's will. Pharaoh's response, claiming to guide his people to the right path, underscores his arrogance and denial of truth, illustrating the dangers of self-deception and false leadership.
orig: يا قوم لكم الملك اليوم ظاهرين في الأرض فمن ينصرنا من بأس الله إن جاءنا قال فرعون ما أريكم إلا ما أرى وما أهديكم إلا سبيل الرشاد

translation: And the one who believed said, 'O my people, indeed I fear for you the like of the Day of the Parties.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the concern of a believer for his people, warning them of a potential divine punishment similar to that experienced by previous nations who were destroyed for their disbelief and corruption. The 'Day of the Parties' refers to a historical event where different groups or parties came together, possibly alluding to the Battle of the Confederates (Al-Ahzab) or other instances of collective opposition to God's message. The believer's fear is not just for their physical destruction but also for their spiritual loss, urging them towards repentance and faith.
orig: وقال الذي آمن يا قوم إني أخاف عليكم مثل يوم الأحزاب

translation: The example of the way of the people of Noah and 'Aad and Thamud and those after them is not the same, and Allah does not intend injustice to His servants.
interpretation: This verse highlights that the way of life and the consequences faced by the people of Noah, 'Aad, Thamud, and subsequent nations serve as examples of divine justice. It emphasizes that Allah's actions are not driven by injustice but are a response to the deeds of His servants. The verse reassures believers that any hardship or punishment faced by communities is a result of their own actions and not an arbitrary infliction of harm by Allah.
orig: مثل دأب قوم نوح وعاد وثمود والذين من بعدهم وما الله يريد ظلما للعباد

translation: And O my people, indeed I fear for you the Day of Calling Out.
interpretation: The speaker, likely a prophet, expresses a deep concern for his people, warning them about the Day of Judgment, referred to here as the 'Day of Calling Out.' This day is when people will be called to account for their deeds, and the prophet's fear stems from his knowledge that many of his people may face severe consequences due to their actions. The verse emphasizes the urgency and gravity of turning towards righteousness before it is too late.
orig: ويا قوم إني أخاف عليكم يوم التناد

translation: The Day you will turn your backs and flee; no one will protect you from Allah. And whoever Allah leaves astray, there is no guide for him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability of facing divine judgment on the Day of Resurrection. It highlights that on that day, individuals will be overwhelmed by fear and will attempt to flee, but there will be no refuge or protection from Allah's judgment. The verse also underscores the concept of divine guidance and misguidance, indicating that those whom Allah allows to go astray due to their own choices and actions will find no one to guide them back to the right path, reinforcing the importance of seeking and adhering to divine guidance in this life.
orig: يوم تولون مدبرين ما لكم من الله من عاصم ومن يضلل الله فما له من هاد

translation: And indeed, Yusuf (Joseph) came to you before with clear proofs, but you remained in doubt about that which he brought to you, until when he died, you said, 'No messenger will Allah send after him.' Thus does Allah leave astray him who is a transgressor and a doubter.
interpretation: This verse reflects on the historical disbelief of the people towards Prophet Yusuf, despite the clear signs and proofs he presented. It highlights a pattern of human behavior where doubt persists even in the face of evident truth. The verse also critiques the arrogance of those who, upon the death of a prophet, assert that no further messengers will be sent, thereby limiting Allah's power and wisdom. This attitude of doubt and transgression leads to further misguidance, as Allah allows those who are excessive in their skepticism and doubt to stray from the right path.
orig: ولقد جاءكم يوسف من قبل بالبينات فما زلتم في شك مما جاءكم به حتى إذا هلك قلتم لن يبعث الله من بعده رسولا كذلك يضل الله من هو مسرف مرتاب

translation: Those who argue about the signs of Allah without any authority having come to them - there is great hatred in the sight of Allah and in the sight of those who believe. Thus does Allah seal the heart of every arrogant tyrant.
interpretation: This verse highlights the severe disapproval and disdain from both Allah and the believers towards those who dispute and argue against the clear signs and revelations of Allah without possessing any legitimate evidence or authority. Such behavior stems from arrogance and a refusal to accept the truth, leading to a spiritual sealing of their hearts by Allah. This sealing represents a divine action where the individual's persistent rejection and haughtiness result in their hearts becoming impervious to guidance and truth, further entrenching their tyranny and pride.
orig: الذين يجادلون في آيات الله بغير سلطان أتاهم كبر مقتا عند الله وعند الذين آمنوا كذلك يطبع الله على كل قلب متكبر جبار

translation: And Pharaoh said, "O Haman, build me a tower that I may reach the ways,"
interpretation: Pharaoh's command to Haman to build a tower reflects his arrogance and denial of divine power. He seeks to ascend to the heavens to challenge or disprove the existence of God, symbolizing his attempt to elevate himself to a god-like status and control the natural and spiritual realms.
orig: وقال فرعون يا هامان ابن لي صرحا لعلي أبلغ الأسباب

translation: The ways of the heavens, so that I may look at the God of Moses, and indeed I think he is a liar. And thus was made attractive to Pharaoh the evil of his deed, and he was averted from the path. And the plot of Pharaoh was not but in ruin.
interpretation: This verse highlights Pharaoh's arrogance and disbelief. He demands to see the God of Moses, indicating his challenge to divine authority and his refusal to accept the message of Moses without tangible proof. This reflects his deep-seated denial and his attempt to maintain power by discrediting the prophet. The verse also illustrates how Pharaoh's evil actions were made to seem appealing to him, leading him astray from the right path. Ultimately, it underscores the futility of Pharaoh's schemes, which are doomed to fail, emphasizing the transient nature of worldly power against divine will.
orig: أسباب السماوات فأطلع إلى إله موسى وإني لأظنه كاذبا وكذلك زين لفرعون سوء عمله وصد عن السبيل وما كيد فرعون إلا في تباب

translation: And the one who believed said, 'O my people, follow me, I will guide you to the path of righteousness.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the role of a believer who, out of compassion and guidance, urges his community to follow him towards the right path. It underscores the importance of leadership in faith, where a single individual's conviction can inspire and direct a collective towards moral and spiritual righteousness.
orig: وقال الذي آمن يا قوم اتبعون أهدكم سبيل الرشاد

translation: O my people, this worldly life is only a temporary enjoyment, and indeed the Hereafter is the home of permanence.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the transient nature of worldly life, urging believers to focus on the eternal life of the Hereafter. It serves as a reminder that the pleasures and material gains of this world are fleeting, whereas the Hereafter is where true and lasting settlement lies. The message encourages a shift in priorities from the temporary to the eternal, fostering a mindset that values spiritual growth and preparation for the afterlife over worldly pursuits.
orig: يا قوم إنما هذه الحياة الدنيا متاع وإن الآخرة هي دار القرار

translation: Whoever does an evil deed will not be recompensed except with its equivalent, and whoever does a righteous deed, whether male or female, while being a believer - those will enter Paradise, where they will be provided for without account.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of justice in Islam, where the consequence of an action is proportionate to the action itself. Evil deeds are met with equivalent punishment, reflecting the fairness of divine justice. Conversely, the verse highlights the inclusivity and equality in Islam by stating that righteous deeds performed by any believer, regardless of gender, will be rewarded with entry into Paradise. The promise of provision without account in Paradise underscores the boundless generosity and mercy of Allah towards those who believe and do good, illustrating the ultimate reward for faith and righteousness.
orig: من عمل سيئة فلا يجزى إلا مثلها ومن عمل صالحا من ذكر أو أنثى وهو مؤمن فأولئك يدخلون الجنة يرزقون فيها بغير حساب

translation: And O my people, how is it that I call you to salvation while you call me to the fire?
interpretation: This verse reflects the frustration and disbelief of a prophet or messenger who is trying to guide his people towards righteousness and salvation. He is highlighting the irony and danger of their situation, where he is inviting them to a path that leads to safety and eternal success, while they are, in turn, urging him to follow a path that leads to destruction and hellfire. It underscores the moral and spiritual conflict between the messenger's divine mission and the misguided insistence of his community, emphasizing the urgency of choosing the right path.
orig: ويا قوم ما لي أدعوكم إلى النجاة وتدعونني إلى النار

translation: You invite me to disbelieve in Allah and to associate with Him that of which I have no knowledge, and I invite you to the Almighty, the Most Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between disbelief and faith, emphasizing the futility and ignorance of idolatry versus the wisdom and mercy found in worshipping the one true God. It reflects a call to monotheism, urging people to turn away from associating partners with Allah, which stems from ignorance, and instead embrace the worship of Allah, who is described as both powerful and forgiving. This invitation to the 'Almighty, the Most Forgiving' underscores the attributes of Allah that make Him worthy of worship and the source of ultimate forgiveness and strength.
orig: تدعونني لأكفر بالله وأشرك به ما ليس لي به علم وأنا أدعوكم إلى العزيز الغفار

translation: There is no doubt that what you call me to has no basis in this world or the hereafter, and that our return is to Allah, and that the extravagant are the companions of the fire.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility and falsehood of idolatry and polytheism, asserting that such practices have no merit or validity in either the worldly life or the afterlife. It underscores the inevitability of returning to Allah, the one true God, and warns that those who exceed the bounds of monotheism by associating partners with Allah will ultimately end up in Hellfire. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of straying from the path of true faith and the importance of adhering to monotheism.
orig: لا جرم أنما تدعونني إليه ليس له دعوة في الدنيا ولا في الآخرة وأن مردنا إلى الله وأن المسرفين هم أصحاب النار

translation: So you will remember what I say to you, and I entrust my affair to Allah. Indeed, Allah is Seeing of [His] servants.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of trust in Allah and His omniscience. The speaker, confident in the truth of their message, leaves the outcome of their situation to Allah, knowing that He is fully aware of all His servants' actions and circumstances. It encourages believers to maintain faith and patience, trusting that Allah sees all and will handle matters justly.
orig: فستذكرون ما أقول لكم وأفوض أمري إلى الله إن الله بصير بالعباد

translation: And Allah protected him from the evils of their plot, while the people of Pharaoh were afflicted with the worst punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine protection granted to Prophet Moses against the malicious schemes of Pharaoh and his people. It underscores the theme of God's safeguarding of His messengers, ensuring their safety and success in their mission despite opposition. Conversely, it also illustrates the inevitable and severe consequences faced by those who oppose God's will, as exemplified by the punishment that befell Pharaoh and his followers.
orig: فوقاه الله سيئات ما مكروا وحاق بآل فرعون سوء العذاب

translation: The Fire; they are exposed to it morning and evening. And the Day the Hour appears [it will be said], "Admit the people of Pharaoh into the severest punishment."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the continuous torment faced by the wrongdoers, symbolized here by the people of Pharaoh, who are exposed to the Hellfire twice daily as a forewarning. On the Day of Judgment, they will be subjected to the most intense form of punishment, emphasizing the severity and inevitability of divine retribution for those who persistently oppose God's signs and oppress others.
orig: النار يعرضون عليها غدوا وعشيا ويوم تقوم الساعة أدخلوا آل فرعون أشد العذاب

translation: And [mention] when they will argue in the Fire, and the weak will say to those who were arrogant, 'Indeed, we were your followers, so can you relieve us of a portion of the Fire?'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the accountability and regret that will be experienced in the Hereafter. It shows how those who were misled by the arrogant leaders will confront them in Hell, seeking relief from their punishment. The verse underscores the futility of seeking help from others on the Day of Judgment, emphasizing that each soul is responsible for its own actions. It serves as a warning against blindly following others in matters of faith and morality, highlighting the importance of personal accountability before God.
orig: وإذ يتحاجون في النار فيقول الضعفاء للذين استكبروا إنا كنا لكم تبعا فهل أنتم مغنون عنا نصيبا من النار

translation: Those who were arrogant will say, 'We were all in it. Indeed, Allah has judged between the servants.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the acknowledgment by those who were arrogant in the worldly life that they are now all together in the Hereafter, facing the consequences of their actions. It underscores the theme of divine justice, where Allah, the ultimate judge, has made a final judgment among His servants. This realization comes too late for them, as they now understand that their arrogance and disbelief have led them to the same fate as others in the Hereafter, emphasizing the inevitability and fairness of Allah's judgment.
orig: قال الذين استكبروا إنا كل فيها إن الله قد حكم بين العباد

translation: And those in the Fire will say to the keepers of Hell, "Call upon your Lord to lighten for us the punishment for one day."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the desperation and regret of those who are suffering in Hell. They are so overwhelmed by their torment that they implore the guardians of Hell to intercede on their behalf, asking for even a momentary relief from their punishment. It highlights the severity of the punishment in the afterlife and serves as a warning to believers to avoid actions that could lead them to such a fate.
orig: وقال الذين في النار لخزنة جهنم ادعوا ربكم يخفف عنا يوما من العذاب

translation: They said, 'Did your messengers not come to you with clear proofs?' They said, 'Yes.' They said, 'Then pray [as you will], but the prayer of the disbelievers is nothing but in error.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of the prayers or supplications of those who reject faith after being presented with clear evidence of the truth. It underscores the theme that disbelief, despite receiving divine guidance, leads to a state where one's spiritual efforts are misguided and ineffective. The acknowledgment of receiving the messengers' clear proofs by the disbelievers emphasizes their culpability and the deliberate nature of their rejection, which renders their subsequent prayers devoid of divine acceptance or benefit.
orig: قالوا أولم تك تأتيكم رسلكم بالبينات قالوا بلى قالوا فادعوا وما دعاء الكافرين إلا في ضلال

translation: Indeed, We will support Our messengers and those who believe during their life in this world and on the Day when the witnesses will stand.
interpretation: This verse reassures believers that divine support is promised not only in the afterlife but also in the worldly life. It emphasizes the certainty of God's aid to His messengers and the faithful, highlighting the importance of faith and patience in times of trial. The mention of 'the Day when the witnesses will stand' refers to the Day of Judgment, underscoring the continuity of divine support from this life into the next, reinforcing the believers' trust in God's justice and mercy.
orig: إنا لننصر رسلنا والذين آمنوا في الحياة الدنيا ويوم يقوم الأشهاد

translation: The Day when their excuses will not benefit the wrongdoers, and they will have the curse, and they will have the evil abode.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Day of Judgment, where those who have wronged others will find no benefit in offering excuses for their actions. It underscores the futility of seeking forgiveness or justification at a time when divine judgment has been set. The mention of 'the curse' and 'the evil abode' serves as a warning of the severe consequences awaiting the wrongdoers, highlighting the importance of righteous living and accountability for one's actions in this life.
orig: يوم لا ينفع الظالمين معذرتهم ولهم اللعنة ولهم سوء الدار

translation: And indeed We gave Moses the guidance, and We made the Children of Israel inherit the Book
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine favor bestowed upon Moses with guidance and the subsequent inheritance of the Torah by the Children of Israel. It underscores the continuity of divine revelation and the responsibility placed on the Children of Israel to uphold and follow the teachings contained within the Book.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى الهدى وأورثنا بني إسرائيل الكتاب

translation: Guidance and a reminder for those of understanding.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an serves as both a guide and a reminder specifically for those who possess deep insight and wisdom. It suggests that only those who are thoughtful and reflective can truly benefit from its teachings, highlighting the importance of intellectual and spiritual engagement with the text.
orig: هدى وذكرى لأولي الألباب

translation: So be patient, for the promise of Allah is true. And ask forgiveness for your sin and exalt [Allah] with praise of your Lord in the evening and the morning.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of patience and steadfastness in faith, as the promises made by Allah are certain to be fulfilled. It encourages believers to continuously seek forgiveness for their sins, acknowledging human fallibility, and to engage in regular worship and praise of Allah, specifically during the evening and morning. This practice not only strengthens one's spiritual connection with the Creator but also instills a routine of mindfulness and gratitude.
orig: فاصبر إن وعد الله حق واستغفر لذنبك وسبح بحمد ربك بالعشي والإبكار

translation: Indeed, those who argue about the signs of Allah without any authority having come to them - there is nothing in their hearts except pride. They will never reach it, so seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Seeing.
interpretation: This verse addresses those who engage in disputes over the signs and verses of Allah without possessing any valid evidence or authority. The core issue identified in these individuals is an inherent arrogance or pride within their hearts, which prevents them from truly understanding or accepting the divine messages. The verse suggests that such people are unlikely to attain true faith or comprehension due to their pride. Therefore, the recommendation given is to seek refuge in Allah from such attitudes and behaviors, emphasizing His attributes of being All-Hearing and All-Seeing, which remind believers of His omniscience and omnipresence.
orig: إن الذين يجادلون في آيات الله بغير سلطان أتاهم إن في صدورهم إلا كبر ما هم ببالغيه فاستعذ بالله إنه هو السميع البصير

translation: The creation of the heavens and the earth is indeed greater than the creation of mankind, yet most people do not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the vastness and complexity of the universe, suggesting that the creation of the cosmos is a far greater marvel than the creation of human beings. It highlights the limited understanding and awareness of most people regarding the scale and intricacy of God's creation, pointing to a broader theme of human ignorance about the divine plan and the true nature of existence.
orig: لخلق السماوات والأرض أكبر من خلق الناس ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: And not equal are the blind and the seeing, nor are those who believe and do righteous deeds and the evildoer. Little do you remember.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental differences between various states of human beings in terms of spiritual and moral awareness. It highlights that those who are spiritually blind (ignorant or heedless) cannot be compared to those who possess spiritual insight (the believers who act righteously). Similarly, it draws a clear distinction between the righteous believers and those who commit evil deeds. The phrase 'Little do you remember' serves as a reminder of how often people overlook these significant distinctions and fail to reflect upon their own spiritual condition and actions.
orig: وما يستوي الأعمى والبصير والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات ولا المسيء قليلا ما تتذكرون

translation: Indeed, the Hour is coming - there is no doubt about it, but most of the people do not believe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty of the Day of Judgment, known as the Hour, which is an inevitable event decreed by Allah. Despite its inevitability, the verse points out a common human failing: the majority of people choose not to believe in it. This disbelief can stem from various reasons such as denial, distraction by worldly affairs, or a lack of faith. The verse serves as a reminder and a warning to believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to prepare for the afterlife, highlighting the importance of faith in the unseen and the consequences of neglecting this belief.
orig: إن الساعة لآتية لا ريب فيها ولكن أكثر الناس لا يؤمنون

translation: And your Lord says, "Call upon Me; I will respond to you." Indeed, those who disdain My worship will enter Hell, humiliated.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of supplication and humility before God. It assures believers that God is always ready to respond to their calls, encouraging a personal and direct relationship with Him. Conversely, it serves as a warning against arrogance and neglect of worship, highlighting that such attitudes lead to spiritual loss and humiliation in the afterlife. The promise of response to supplication fosters hope and reliance on God, while the warning about Hell underscores the gravity of turning away from divine guidance.
orig: وقال ربكم ادعوني أستجب لكم إن الذين يستكبرون عن عبادتي سيدخلون جهنم داخرين

translation: Allah is He Who has made for you the night that you may rest therein and the day giving sight. Indeed, Allah is full of bounty to mankind, yet most of mankind give no thanks.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's mercy and provision for humanity by highlighting the natural cycle of night and day, which He has created for our benefit. The night is given as a time for rest and tranquility, allowing us to rejuvenate, while the day is provided with light for us to see and carry out our activities. Despite these clear signs of Allah's favor and generosity towards us, the verse points out that most people fail to recognize and express gratitude for these blessings, underscoring a common human failing of ingratitude.
orig: الله الذي جعل لكم الليل لتسكنوا فيه والنهار مبصرا إن الله لذو فضل على الناس ولكن أكثر الناس لا يشكرون

translation: That is Allah, your Lord, the Creator of all things. There is no god but He. How then are you deluded?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness and supremacy of Allah as the sole Creator of everything. It challenges the reader to reflect on their beliefs and actions, questioning how they can be misled or deluded away from the truth of monotheism despite the clear evidence of Allah's creation and sovereignty.
orig: ذلكم الله ربكم خالق كل شيء لا إله إلا هو فأنى تؤفكون

translation: Thus does Allah let go astray those who were rejecting His signs.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the consequence of disbelief and rejection of Allah's signs. It suggests that those who persistently deny the truth and signs of Allah are led further into error and misguidance as a result of their own choices. The use of 'thus' indicates a pattern or a natural outcome of such behavior, emphasizing that this is a divine law where disbelief leads to increased straying from the right path.
orig: كذلك يؤفك الذين كانوا بآيات الله يجحدون

translation: Allah is He Who made for you the earth a resting place and the sky a canopy, and fashioned you and perfected your forms, and provided you with good things. That is Allah, your Lord; so blessed be Allah, the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the comprehensive care and provision of Allah for humanity. By making the earth a stable place for living and the sky a protective covering, Allah has created an environment conducive to human life. The mention of fashioning and perfecting human forms highlights the divine attention to detail in creation, underscoring the inherent dignity and worth of every individual. The provision of good things further illustrates Allah's ongoing sustenance and generosity. The verse concludes with a declaration of Allah's lordship over all creation, inviting reflection on His majesty and prompting gratitude and praise.
orig: الله الذي جعل لكم الأرض قرارا والسماء بناء وصوركم فأحسن صوركم ورزقكم من الطيبات ذلكم الله ربكم فتبارك الله رب العالمين

translation: He is the Ever-Living; there is no deity except Him, so call upon Him, being sincere to Him in religion. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness and uniqueness of Allah, affirming that He alone is the Ever-Living and the only deity worthy of worship. It encourages believers to direct their prayers and devotion solely to Him with sincerity and purity of intention in their religious practice. The verse concludes with a declaration of gratitude to Allah, acknowledging His sovereignty over all creation.
orig: هو الحي لا إله إلا هو فادعوه مخلصين له الدين الحمد لله رب العالمين

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], "Indeed, I have been forbidden to worship those you invoke besides Allah once the clear proofs have come to me from my Lord, and I have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophet Muhammad's unwavering commitment to monotheism after receiving clear evidence from Allah. It highlights the rejection of polytheism and the obligation to submit to the one true God, reinforcing the core Islamic principle of Tawheed (the oneness of God). The verse serves as a directive for Muslims to follow the Prophet's example in dedicating their worship solely to Allah and submitting to His will.
orig: قل إني نهيت أن أعبد الذين تدعون من دون الله لما جاءني البينات من ربي وأمرت أن أسلم لرب العالمين

translation: He it is Who created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then from a clinging clot; then He brings you out as a child, then [He ordains] that you reach your maturity, then that you become elders, though some among you are taken in death before [that], and that you reach a specified term, and perhaps you will understand.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the stages of human development and life as a manifestation of Allah's power and wisdom. It serves as a reminder of our origin from humble beginnings and our progression through various life stages, culminating in old age or death, all according to a divine plan. The mention of these stages is meant to provoke reflection and understanding of the purpose and temporality of life, encouraging believers to contemplate their existence and the hereafter.
orig: هو الذي خلقكم من تراب ثم من نطفة ثم من علقة ثم يخرجكم طفلا ثم لتبلغوا أشدكم ثم لتكونوا شيوخا ومنكم من يتوفى من قبل ولتبلغوا أجلا مسمى ولعلكم تعقلون

translation: He is the One who gives life and causes death. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, 'Be,' and it is.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and sovereignty of Allah over all creation. It highlights His ability to bring life into existence and to end it, underscoring His control over the cycle of life and death. The phrase 'When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, 'Be,' and it is' illustrates the effortless nature of His command; His will is executed instantly and without any resistance, reflecting His omnipotence and the immediate effect of His divine decree. This serves as a reminder of the submission of all things to His will and the ease with which He can alter the course of events.
orig: هو الذي يحيي ويميت فإذا قضى أمرا فإنما يقول له كن فيكون

translation: Have you not seen those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah? How are they turned away?
interpretation: This verse highlights the phenomenon of people engaging in arguments and disputes over the clear signs and revelations from Allah, indicating a form of denial or rejection of divine guidance. It questions the observer to reflect on how such individuals are misguided and turned away from the truth, emphasizing the consequences of rejecting Allah's signs.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين يجادلون في آيات الله أنى يصرفون

translation: Those who have denied the Book and that with which We sent Our messengers - they are going to know.
interpretation: This verse warns those who reject the Qur'an and the messages brought by the prophets that they will eventually face the consequences of their disbelief. It emphasizes the certainty of divine retribution and serves as a reminder of the accountability that awaits everyone in the hereafter.
orig: الذين كذبوا بالكتاب وبما أرسلنا به رسلنا فسوف يعلمون

translation: When the shackles are around their necks and the chains they are dragged with.
interpretation: This verse depicts the severe punishment and humiliation that awaits the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment. The imagery of shackles around their necks and chains dragging them symbolizes the inescapable and oppressive nature of their punishment, reflecting their bondage to their sins and the consequences thereof.
orig: إذ الأغلال في أعناقهم والسلاسل يسحبون

translation: In scalding water, then in the Fire they will be burned.
interpretation: This verse describes the severe punishment awaiting the disbelievers in the Hereafter. The mention of 'scalding water' followed by 'the Fire' emphasizes the intensity and stages of torment, illustrating the consequences of rejecting faith and the divine warnings. It serves as a stark reminder of the accountability for one's actions and the reality of Hell as a place of suffering.
orig: في الحميم ثم في النار يسجرون

translation: Then it will be said to them, 'Where are those you used to associate [with Allah]?
interpretation: This verse underscores the moment of accountability in the afterlife, where those who worshipped idols or other deities alongside Allah will be confronted with the futility of their beliefs. It highlights the theme of monotheism, emphasizing that on the Day of Judgment, the falsehood of polytheism will be exposed, and individuals will be questioned about the partners they ascribed to Allah, revealing the ultimate truth of His sole divinity.
orig: ثم قيل لهم أين ما كنتم تشركون

translation: Apart from Allah they said, 'They have strayed from us.' Nay, we used to not invoke anything before. Thus does Allah let the disbelievers go astray.
interpretation: This verse highlights the moment of realization among the disbelievers when they see the consequences of their idolatry. They initially attribute their misguidance to the false deities they worshipped, claiming these idols have 'strayed from us.' However, they soon acknowledge the truth that they never truly worshipped any real entity capable of guiding or straying. This admission underscores their self-deception and the futility of their worship. The verse illustrates how Allah allows disbelievers to continue in their misguidance as a consequence of their rejection of the truth, emphasizing divine justice and the natural outcome of disbelief.
orig: من دون الله قالوا ضلوا عنا بل لم نكن ندعو من قبل شيئا كذلك يضل الله الكافرين

translation: That is because you used to rejoice in the earth without right and because you used to be insolent.
interpretation: This verse explains that the punishment or consequences faced by individuals are a direct result of their wrongful actions and arrogance during their life on earth. It highlights the principle of accountability in Islam, where rejoicing in worldly gains without a legitimate right to them, and behaving insolently, leads to divine retribution. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of humility, justice, and the proper use of worldly resources, warning against the dangers of pride and unlawful enjoyment.
orig: ذلكم بما كنتم تفرحون في الأرض بغير الحق وبما كنتم تمرحون

translation: Enter the gates of Hell to dwell therein forever; and how evil is the abode of the arrogant!
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequence of arrogance and pride, highlighting that those who exhibit such traits will be condemned to an eternal stay in Hell. It serves as a stern warning against the sin of haughtiness, illustrating that the ultimate destination for the arrogant is a place of severe punishment and misery, underscoring the importance of humility and obedience to God's commands.
orig: ادخلوا أبواب جهنم خالدين فيها فبئس مثوى المتكبرين

translation: So be patient, indeed, the promise of Allah is truth. And whether We show you some of what We have promised them or We take you in death, it is to Us they will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of patience and steadfastness in faith, reassuring the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that Allah's promise is certain and will be fulfilled. It highlights the inevitability of divine justice, whether it is witnessed in this life or in the hereafter, as all will ultimately return to Allah for judgment.
orig: فاصبر إن وعد الله حق فإما نرينك بعض الذي نعدهم أو نتوفينك فإلينا يرجعون

translation: And We have certainly sent messengers before you. Of them are some whose stories We have related to you, and of them are some whose stories We have not related to you. And it was not for a messenger to come with a sign except by the permission of Allah. So when the command of Allah comes, it is executed in truth, and there the falsifiers will lose.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the continuity and authority of divine revelation across time. It highlights that Allah has sent numerous messengers throughout history, some of whose stories are known to us through the Qur'an, while others remain untold. This serves to remind believers of the vastness of Allah's communication with humanity. The verse also underscores the principle that no messenger can perform a miracle or bring a sign without Allah's explicit permission, reinforcing the idea of divine control over all events. Finally, it asserts that when Allah's decree is issued, it is carried out with absolute justice, leading to the ultimate defeat of those who deny or distort the truth. This interpretation encourages believers to trust in the wisdom and timing of Allah's plans, and to remain steadfast in faith despite the apparent success of falsehood in the world.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا رسلا من قبلك منهم من قصصنا عليك ومنهم من لم نقصص عليك وما كان لرسول أن يأتي بآية إلا بإذن الله فإذا جاء أمر الله قضي بالحق وخسر هنالك المبطلون

translation: Allah is He Who has made for you the cattle, that you may ride on some of them and of some you eat.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's provision for humanity by creating cattle, which serve multiple purposes such as transportation and a source of food. It underscores the dependency of humans on Allah's creation for their sustenance and mobility, reflecting the broader theme of divine providence and the interconnectedness of creation for human benefit.
orig: الله الذي جعل لكم الأنعام لتركبوا منها ومنها تأكلون

translation: And there are benefits for you in them, and that you may reach by their means a need that is in your chests, and upon them and upon ships you are carried.
interpretation: This verse highlights the multifaceted utility of animals, particularly camels, in the lives of humans. It points out that these creatures not only serve practical purposes such as transportation ("upon them and upon ships you are carried") but also fulfill deeper emotional or psychological needs ("a need that is in your chests"). The verse underscores the divine provision of such resources, reminding believers to be grateful for and mindful of the blessings bestowed upon them, which cater to both their material and spiritual well-being.
orig: ولكم فيها منافع ولتبلغوا عليها حاجة في صدوركم وعليها وعلى الفلك تحملون

translation: And He shows you His signs, so which of the signs of Allah do you deny?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the undeniable presence of Allah's signs in the universe, challenging the disbelief of those who witness these signs yet choose to reject them. It serves as a rhetorical question that highlights the clarity and abundance of evidence for Allah's existence and power, urging reflection and acknowledgment of these divine manifestations.
orig: ويريكم آياته فأي آيات الله تنكرون

translation: Have they not traveled through the earth and observed how was the end of those before them? They were greater than them in strength and in impact on the earth, but what they had earned did not avail them.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to reflect on the historical consequences faced by past civilizations that were more powerful and influential than the contemporaries of the Prophet Muhammad.
