It suggests that despite their strength and achievements, these civilizations ultimately declined because their worldly gains could not protect them from divine judgment. The verse serves as a reminder of the transient nature of worldly power and the importance of spiritual and moral integrity over material success.
orig: أفلم يسيروا في الأرض فينظروا كيف كان عاقبة الذين من قبلهم كانوا أكثر منهم وأشد قوة وآثارا في الأرض فما أغنى عنهم ما كانوا يكسبون

translation: So when their messengers came to them with clear proofs, they were exultant in what they had of knowledge, and enveloped them was what they used to ridicule.
interpretation: This verse highlights the irony and consequence of disbelief. When the messengers brought undeniable evidence of the truth, the people, instead of accepting it, took pride in their own limited knowledge and understanding. Their arrogance led them to mock the truth, and ultimately, the very thing they ridiculed came upon them as a punishment or realization, demonstrating the inevitable triumph of divine truth over human folly.
orig: فلما جاءتهم رسلهم بالبينات فرحوا بما عندهم من العلم وحاق بهم ما كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: So when they saw Our punishment, they said, 'We believe in Allah alone and disbelieve in that which we used to associate with Him.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the moment of realization and regret among the disbelievers when they witness the overwhelming power and punishment of Allah. It highlights the futility of their previous idolatry and their last-minute declaration of faith in the oneness of Allah, which comes too late to avert their fate. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of disbelief and the importance of sincere faith before it is too late.
orig: فلما رأوا بأسنا قالوا آمنا بالله وحده وكفرنا بما كنا به مشركين

translation: So their faith was of no use to them when they saw Our punishment. [This is] the way of Allah that has occurred among His servants. And the disbelievers lost there.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of embracing faith only when faced with divine punishment. It underscores a consistent pattern in Allah's dealings with humanity where faith, when adopted out of desperation rather than genuine belief, does not avert the consequences of disbelief. The verse serves as a warning that true faith must be established before the moment of reckoning, as procrastination until the sight of punishment leads to inevitable loss for the disbelievers.
orig: فلم يك ينفعهم إيمانهم لما رأوا بأسنا سنت الله التي قد خلت في عباده وخسر هنالك الكافرون

translation: Ha Mim
interpretation: These are among the disjointed letters (muqatta'at) at the beginning of certain chapters of the Qur'an. Their precise meanings are known only to Allah, but they are believed to hold deep spiritual significance and to serve as a reminder of the Qur'an's divine origin.
orig: حم

translation: A revelation from the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is a divine revelation bestowed upon humanity by Allah, who is described with the attributes of utmost mercy and compassion. It underscores the source of the Qur'an as being from the divine, highlighting its sacredness and the benevolence of its origin.
orig: تنزيل من الرحمن الرحيم

translation: A Book whose verses have been detailed, an Arabic Qur'an for a people who know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the clarity and precision of the Qur'an, indicating that its verses are meticulously explained and structured in the Arabic language, specifically tailored for those who possess understanding and knowledge. It highlights the Qur'an's role as a clear guide and a detailed scripture meant for contemplation and comprehension by those who are willing to learn and reflect upon its teachings.
orig: كتاب فصلت آياته قرآنا عربيا لقوم يعلمون

translation: A bearer of good news and a warner. But most of them turn away, so they do not hear.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the dual role of the Prophet Muhammad as both a bearer of good news (promising rewards for the righteous) and a warner (alerting about the consequences of disbelief and disobedience). The latter part of the verse reflects a common human tendency to ignore divine messages, indicating that despite the clarity and importance of the message, most people choose to disregard it, metaphorically turning a deaf ear to the guidance offered.
orig: بشيرا ونذيرا فأعرض أكثرهم فهم لا يسمعون

translation: And they said, "Our hearts are in coverings from that to which you invite us, and in our ears is deafness, and between us and you is a barrier, so work; indeed, we are working."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the rejection and stubbornness of the disbelievers towards the message of Islam. They metaphorically describe their hearts as being covered, indicating their unwillingness to accept the truth, and their ears as deaf, showing their refusal to listen to the guidance. The mention of a barrier between them and the Prophet Muhammad signifies their psychological and spiritual distance from the message. Their challenge to "work" while asserting that they too are working, reflects a defiant attitude, suggesting a competition in deeds, yet it underscores their persistence in disbelief and opposition to the divine message.
orig: وقالوا قلوبنا في أكنة مما تدعونا إليه وفي آذاننا وقر ومن بيننا وبينك حجاب فاعمل إننا عاملون

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], "I am only a human being like you to whom it has been revealed that your god is one God. So take the straight path to Him and seek His forgiveness. And woe to those who associate others with Allah."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the humanity of the Prophet Muhammad, highlighting that he, like all humans, received divine revelation. It underscores the core Islamic belief in the oneness of God, urging believers to follow the straight path towards Him and to seek His forgiveness. The verse also serves as a warning against polytheism, indicating the severe consequences for those who ascribe partners to God, thereby stressing the importance of maintaining pure monotheistic faith.
orig: قل إنما أنا بشر مثلكم يوحى إلي أنما إلهكم إله واحد فاستقيموا إليه واستغفروه وويل للمشركين

translation: Those who do not give zakat and they, in the Hereafter, are disbelievers
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of zakat, one of the five pillars of Islam, as a fundamental act of worship and social responsibility. Not giving zakat is portrayed as a sign of disbelief in the Hereafter, indicating that such individuals fail to recognize the spiritual and moral obligations that extend beyond this worldly life. The verse suggests that neglecting zakat reflects a deeper spiritual malaise, where one's faith in the afterlife and accountability before God is lacking.
orig: الذين لا يؤتون الزكاة وهم بالآخرة هم كافرون

translation: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them is a reward that will never be cut off.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the eternal nature of the reward promised to those who have faith and perform good deeds. It suggests that the blessings and rewards in the hereafter for such individuals are continuous and uninterrupted, highlighting the enduring value and significance of faith and moral actions in Islam.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لهم أجر غير ممنون

translation: Say, "Do you indeed disbelieve in the One Who created the earth in two days and attribute to Him equals? That is the Lord of the worlds."
interpretation: This verse challenges the disbelief in the Creator, emphasizing the miraculous creation of the earth in just two days as a testament to His power and uniqueness. It critiques the human tendency to associate partners with Allah, reminding believers that He alone is the Lord of all creation, deserving of exclusive worship and recognition.
orig: قل أئنكم لتكفرون بالذي خلق الأرض في يومين وتجعلون له أندادا ذلك رب العالمين

translation: And He placed therein [i.e., the earth] firmly set mountains above it, and He blessed it and determined therein its [creatures'] sustenance in four days, equal for [all] who ask [for it].
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's meticulous creation and management of the earth. The mountains are described as stabilizers that provide balance and structure to the earth. The blessing of the earth signifies its suitability for life, and the determination of sustenance in four days underscores the precise and equitable distribution of resources, available to all who seek them. This reflects Allah's justice and generosity in providing for all His creation equally.
orig: وجعل فيها رواسي من فوقها وبارك فيها وقدر فيها أقواتها في أربعة أيام سواء للسائلين

translation: Then He directed Himself to the heaven while it was smoke and said to it and to the earth, 'Come [into being], willingly or unwillingly.' They said, 'We come willingly.'
interpretation: This verse describes the process of creation where Allah first turns His attention to the heaven, which is described as being in a state of smoke, indicating an early, formless stage of creation. Allah commands both the heaven and the earth to come into existence, giving them the choice to comply willingly or unwillingly. Their response of coming willingly underscores the submission of all creation to Allah's command, highlighting the theme of obedience and the natural order's alignment with divine will.
orig: ثم استوى إلى السماء وهي دخان فقال لها وللأرض ائتيا طوعا أو كرها قالتا أتينا طائعين

translation: So He completed them as seven heavens in two days and inspired in each heaven its command. And We adorned the nearest heaven with lamps and as protection. That is the determination of the Exalted in Might, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse describes the creation of the seven heavens by Allah, emphasizing His power and knowledge in organizing the universe. The mention of 'two days' for the creation of the heavens highlights the swiftness and ease with which Allah accomplishes His will. Each heaven receiving its command signifies the specific roles and functions assigned to different parts of the universe, reflecting divine order and purpose. The 'lamps' in the nearest heaven refer to stars, which not only beautify the sky but also serve as a protective barrier against evil forces, as mentioned elsewhere in the Qur'an. This verse underscores the meticulous planning and execution by 'the Exalted in Might, the Knowing,' reinforcing the belief in Allah's omnipotence and omniscience.
orig: فقضاهن سبع سماوات في يومين وأوحى في كل سماء أمرها وزينا السماء الدنيا بمصابيح وحفظا ذلك تقدير العزيز العليم

translation: And if they turn away, then say, 'I have warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of 'Aad and Thamud.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequence of rejecting the message of the Prophet Muhammad. If the people turn away from the guidance offered, they are warned of a severe punishment similar to that which befell the ancient tribes of 'Aad and Thamud. These tribes were destroyed by a divine thunderbolt due to their arrogance and disbelief. The verse serves as a reminder of the potential consequences of ignoring divine warnings and the inevitability of divine justice.
orig: فإن أعرضوا فقل أنذرتكم صاعقة مثل صاعقة عاد وثمود

translation: When the messengers came to them from before them and from behind them, (saying): "Worship none but Allah," they said: "If our Lord had willed, He would have sent down angels. So indeed we are disbelievers in what you have been sent with."
interpretation: This verse highlights the rejection of divine guidance by a community despite clear warnings from multiple messengers. The messengers approached them from all directions, symbolizing the comprehensive nature of the message to worship only Allah. The people's response reflects their arrogance and disbelief, as they challenge the method of divine communication, suggesting that if God truly wanted them to follow, He would have sent angels instead of human messengers. This indicates their refusal to accept the message based on their own preconceived notions of how divine revelation should occur, ultimately leading to their denial of the messengers' call.
orig: إذ جاءتهم الرسل من بين أيديهم ومن خلفهم ألا تعبدوا إلا الله قالوا لو شاء ربنا لأنزل ملائكة فإنا بما أرسلتم به كافرون

translation: As for 'Aad, they were arrogant in the land without right, and they said, 'Who is mightier than us in strength?' Did they not see that Allah, who created them, is mightier than them in strength? And they used to deny Our signs.
interpretation: This verse reflects on the arrogance and disbelief of the 'Aad people, who boasted about their strength and power, yet failed to recognize the ultimate power of Allah, their Creator. It serves as a reminder of the consequences of denying Allah's signs and the importance of humility and acknowledgment of divine supremacy.
orig: فأما عاد فاستكبروا في الأرض بغير الحق وقالوا من أشد منا قوة أولم يروا أن الله الذي خلقهم هو أشد منهم قوة وكانوا بآياتنا يجحدون

translation: So We sent upon them a screaming wind in days of misfortune to make them taste the punishment of disgrace in the worldly life; and indeed, the punishment of the Hereafter is more disgraceful, and they will not be helped.
interpretation: This verse reflects the divine retribution upon a community that rejected the message of God. The "screaming wind" symbolizes a severe and destructive punishment that was sent as a consequence of their disbelief and arrogance. The "days of misfortune" indicate a period of intense suffering and calamity. The punishment in this life serves as a foretaste of the more severe punishment awaiting them in the Hereafter, emphasizing the concept of accountability and the consequences of one's actions. The mention of them not being helped underscores their isolation and the futility of seeking aid from anyone other than God after having rejected His guidance.
orig: فأرسلنا عليهم ريحا صرصرا في أيام نحسات لنذيقهم عذاب الخزي في الحياة الدنيا ولعذاب الآخرة أخزى وهم لا ينصرون

translation: And as for Thamud, We guided them, but they preferred blindness over guidance; so the thunderbolt of the humiliating punishment seized them for what they used to earn.
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of divine guidance and human responsibility. Thamud, like other nations, was given clear guidance by Allah, yet they chose to reject it, preferring ignorance and disbelief. Their deliberate choice to follow a path away from the truth led to their destruction through a severe punishment, illustrating that the consequences of one's actions are directly linked to their choices. This serves as a reminder and a warning to all people about the importance of heeding divine guidance and the repercussions of willful rejection.
orig: وأما ثمود فهديناهم فاستحبوا العمى على الهدى فأخذتهم صاعقة العذاب الهون بما كانوا يكسبون

translation: And We saved those who believed and used to fear Allah.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine promise of salvation for those who maintain faith and practice righteousness. It underscores the importance of belief coupled with piety as the means to attain God's protection and deliverance from adversity. The verse serves as a reassurance to believers that their faith and fear of Allah will ultimately lead to their rescue and safety in both worldly and spiritual contexts.
orig: ونجينا الذين آمنوا وكانوا يتقون

translation: And the Day when the enemies of Allah will be gathered to the Fire, then they will be arranged in ranks.
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Judgment when those who opposed Allah and His message will be assembled and led to Hell. The phrase 'they will be arranged in ranks' signifies the organized and inevitable nature of their punishment, emphasizing the justice and order in Allah's judgment. It serves as a reminder of the consequences of disbelief and opposition to divine guidance.
orig: ويوم يحشر أعداء الله إلى النار فهم يوزعون

translation: Until, when they reach it, their hearing, their sight, and their skins will testify against them of what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the Day of Judgment, where every part of the human body will bear witness to the deeds committed during one's lifetime. It emphasizes the inescapable accountability for one's actions, highlighting that even the faculties of hearing, sight, and touch will testify against the individual, underscoring the comprehensive nature of divine justice and the impossibility of concealing one's deeds from God.
orig: حتى إذا ما جاءوها شهد عليهم سمعهم وأبصارهم وجلودهم بما كانوا يعملون

translation: And they will say to their skins, 'Why have you testified against us?' They will say, 'Allah has caused us to speak, He who causes all things to speak, and He created you the first time, and to Him you will be returned.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the Day of Judgment when the disbelievers will question their own bodies, specifically their skins, for testifying against them. The skins' response underscores the absolute power of Allah, who can grant speech to anything He wills, emphasizing His omnipotence and control over creation. It also serves as a reminder of the initial creation by Allah and the inevitable return to Him for judgment, highlighting the accountability of every individual for their actions.
orig: وقالوا لجلودهم لم شهدتم علينا قالوا أنطقنا الله الذي أنطق كل شيء وهو خلقكم أول مرة وإليه ترجعون

translation: And you were not covering [yourselves] so that your hearing, your sight, and your skins would testify against you; but you assumed that Allah did not know much of what you were doing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to mistakenly believe that their secret actions or thoughts are hidden from God. It emphasizes that all parts of a person, including their senses and even their skin, will bear witness to their deeds on the Day of Judgment. The verse serves as a reminder of God's all-encompassing knowledge and the futility of trying to conceal sins from Him.
orig: وما كنتم تستترون أن يشهد عليكم سمعكم ولا أبصاركم ولا جلودكم ولكن ظننتم أن الله لا يعلم كثيرا مما تعملون

translation: And that was your assumption which you assumed about your Lord. It has brought you to ruin, and you have become among the losers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of false assumptions about God. It suggests that when people harbor incorrect beliefs or doubts about the nature and justice of God, it leads them astray and ultimately results in their spiritual and moral loss. The verse serves as a warning against underestimating or misunderstanding divine wisdom and justice, emphasizing the importance of correct faith and understanding in avoiding ruin.
orig: وذلكم ظنكم الذي ظننتم بربكم أرداكم فأصبحتم من الخاسرين

translation: So if they are patient, the Fire is their abode, and if they seek to appease, they will not be of those who are allowed to appease.
interpretation: This verse addresses those who reject faith and the message of the Prophet Muhammad. It emphasizes that even if they endure patiently in their disbelief, their ultimate destination will be the Hellfire. Furthermore, if they attempt to seek forgiveness or reconciliation after their persistent rejection, their efforts will be futile because their repentance is not sincere or timely. The verse underscores the importance of accepting faith and the consequences of prolonged disbelief.
orig: فإن يصبروا فالنار مثوى لهم وإن يستعتبوا فما هم من المعتبين

translation: And We have assigned for them companions (in the world), who made fair-seeming to them what was before them and what was behind them. And the Word (of torment) has proved true against them among nations that passed away before them of the jinn and mankind. Truly, they were losers.
interpretation: This verse illustrates how God has allowed certain individuals to be influenced by companions who beautify and justify their wrongdoings, both in their past actions and future intentions. This misguidance leads them astray, resulting in them being counted among the losers, a fate that has befallen previous nations of both jinn and humans. It underscores the concept of divine justice and the consequences of following misleading influences.
orig: وقيضنا لهم قرناء فزينوا لهم ما بين أيديهم وما خلفهم وحق عليهم القول في أمم قد خلت من قبلهم من الجن والإنس إنهم كانوا خاسرين

translation: And those who disbelieve say, 'Do not listen to this Qur'an and make noise during its recitation so that you may overcome.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the active resistance of the disbelievers to the message of the Qur'an. They instruct others to create distractions and noise during its recitation, aiming to prevent its message from being heard and understood, thereby maintaining their influence and control over others. This reflects their fear of the transformative power of the Qur'an's message.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا لا تسمعوا لهذا القرآن والغوا فيه لعلكم تغلبون

translation: So We will surely cause those who disbelieve to taste a severe punishment, and We will surely recompense them for the worst of what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty and inevitability of divine retribution for those who reject faith. It serves as a warning that disbelief and evil deeds will not go unpunished, highlighting God's justice and the accountability of individuals for their actions in the hereafter.
orig: فلنذيقن الذين كفروا عذابا شديدا ولنجزينهم أسوأ الذي كانوا يعملون

translation: That is the recompense of the enemies of Allah - the Fire. For them therein is the eternal home, a recompense for what they used to deny of Our signs.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe consequence for those who actively oppose Allah and reject His signs. The 'enemies of Allah' are those who not only disbelieve but also work against the faith and its teachings. The 'Fire' represents the ultimate punishment in the afterlife, described as an 'eternal home' to signify that there is no escape from this fate for those who persistently deny the truth of Allah's revelations. The mention of 'Our signs' refers to the clear evidences and miracles provided by Allah, which these individuals choose to ignore or reject, leading to their condemnation.
orig: ذلك جزاء أعداء الله النار لهم فيها دار الخلد جزاء بما كانوا بآياتنا يجحدون

translation: And those who disbelieve will say, 'Our Lord, show us those who misled us from among the jinn and men, so we may put them under our feet that they may be among the lowest.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the regret and helplessness of the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment. They will ask to see those who led them astray, both from among the jinn and humans, with the intention of expressing their anger and frustration by symbolically placing them under their feet. This request underscores their desire to hold others accountable for their misguidance, yet it also highlights their own responsibility for following false leaders, as they will still be among the lowest in Hell despite this plea.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا ربنا أرنا اللذين أضلانا من الجن والإنس نجعلهما تحت أقدامنا ليكونا من الأسفلين

translation: Indeed, those who say, 'Our Lord is Allah,' and then remain steadfast, the angels will descend upon them, [saying], 'Do not fear and do not grieve but receive good tidings of Paradise, which you were promised.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the reward for those who sincerely declare their faith in Allah and remain steadfast in their devotion and obedience to Him. The promise of the angels descending to reassure and comfort these believers highlights the divine support and encouragement provided to those who maintain their faith through life's trials. The mention of Paradise as a promised reward serves as a motivation for believers to persevere in their faith and righteousness, illustrating the ultimate goal and blessing awaiting them in the afterlife.
orig: إن الذين قالوا ربنا الله ثم استقاموا تتنزل عليهم الملائكة ألا تخافوا ولا تحزنوا وأبشروا بالجنة التي كنتم توعدون

translation: We are your protectors in the life of this world and in the Hereafter, and you will have therein whatever your souls desire, and you will have therein whatever you ask for.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the comprehensive protection and support that Allah provides to the believers, not only in the worldly life but also in the afterlife. It reassures believers of the fulfillment of their desires and wishes in Paradise, highlighting the boundless generosity and mercy of Allah. The promise of having whatever one's soul desires and whatever one asks for in the Hereafter serves as a motivation for believers to remain steadfast in their faith and obedience to Allah.
orig: نحن أولياؤكم في الحياة الدنيا وفي الآخرة ولكم فيها ما تشتهي أنفسكم ولكم فيها ما تدعون

translation: A provision from the Forgiving, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the sustenance and blessings provided to humanity come directly from Allah, who is characterized by His attributes of forgiveness and mercy. It emphasizes that all provisions, whether material or spiritual, are a gift from a compassionate and forgiving God, highlighting the divine source of all goodness and the benevolent nature of Allah towards His creation.
orig: نزلا من غفور رحيم

translation: And who is better in speech than one who invites to Allah and does righteous deeds and says, 'Indeed, I am of the Muslims.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the excellence of a person who not only calls others to the worship and recognition of Allah but also embodies this call through their actions. By performing righteous deeds and openly declaring their faith as a Muslim, such an individual sets a powerful example of living faith. The verse suggests that the combination of inviting others to Islam, acting righteously, and publicly affirming one's faith is the highest form of speech and conduct in the eyes of Allah.
orig: ومن أحسن قولا ممن دعا إلى الله وعمل صالحا وقال إنني من المسلمين

translation: And not equal are the good deed and the bad. Repel [evil] with that which is better; then the one whom there was enmity between you and him - as though he was a close friend.
interpretation: This verse teaches the principle of responding to negativity or evil with kindness and goodness. By doing so, it suggests that even those who were once enemies can be transformed into close friends. The underlying message is about the power of moral excellence and patience in changing hearts and fostering reconciliation.
orig: ولا تستوي الحسنة ولا السيئة ادفع بالتي هي أحسن فإذا الذي بينك وبينه عداوة كأنه ولي حميم

translation: And none will attain it except those who are patient, and none will attain it except those who have a great share [of good].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that achieving the highest levels of spiritual reward and closeness to Allah is reserved for those who exhibit patience and perseverance in the face of trials and tribulations. It underscores the importance of steadfastness in faith and actions, suggesting that only those who patiently endure hardships and remain committed to their faith will be granted the immense reward and honor from Allah, described here as a 'great share'. This patience is not just about enduring but also about maintaining a strong connection with Allah through consistent worship and good deeds.
orig: وما يلقاها إلا الذين صبروا وما يلقاها إلا ذو حظ عظيم

translation: And if an evil suggestion comes to you from Satan, then seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse instructs believers that when they are tempted or influenced by Satan, they should immediately turn to Allah for protection and guidance. It emphasizes the omnipresence and omniscience of Allah, indicating that He is always aware of our struggles and ready to assist us when we seek His refuge. This act of seeking refuge is not only a means of protection but also a reaffirmation of one's faith and reliance on Allah's mercy and knowledge.
orig: وإما ينزغنك من الشيطان نزغ فاستعذ بالله إنه هو السميع العليم

translation: And of His signs are the night and the day, and the sun and the moon. Do not prostrate to the sun or to the moon, but prostrate to Allah, who created them, if it is Him you worship.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness of God and the rejection of idolatry. It uses the natural phenomena of night, day, sun, and moon as signs of God's creation, reminding believers that these are not to be worshipped. Instead, worship should be directed solely to Allah, the Creator of these phenomena. The verse challenges believers to reflect on their faith and ensure that their worship is directed correctly, reinforcing the core Islamic principle of tawhid (the oneness of God).
orig: ومن آياته الليل والنهار والشمس والقمر لا تسجدوا للشمس ولا للقمر واسجدوا لله الذي خلقهن إن كنتم إياه تعبدون

translation: But if they are arrogant, then those who are with your Lord glorify Him by night and day, and they never tire.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the humility and constant devotion required of believers. It suggests that if some people become arrogant and refuse to worship or acknowledge God, it does not affect the divine order. The angels and other beings in the presence of God continuously praise Him without any fatigue or arrogance. This serves as a reminder to humans to remain humble and persistent in their worship, as their arrogance does not diminish God's glory but only distances them from His favor.
orig: فإن استكبروا فالذين عند ربك يسبحون له بالليل والنهار وهم لا يسأمون

translation: And among His signs is that you see the earth barren; but when We send down rain upon it, it stirs to life and swells. Indeed, He who brings it to life can surely revive the dead. Indeed, He is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse highlights the power and omnipotence of Allah, illustrating His ability to bring life to the seemingly dead earth through rain, symbolizing resurrection and renewal. It serves as a reminder and a proof of Allah's capability to resurrect humans after death, emphasizing His absolute control and power over all aspects of creation.
orig: ومن آياته أنك ترى الأرض خاشعة فإذا أنزلنا عليها الماء اهتزت وربت إن الذي أحياها لمحيي الموتى إنه على كل شيء قدير

translation: Indeed, those who deviate concerning Our verses are not hidden from Us. So, is he who is cast into the Fire better or he who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection? Do whatever you will; indeed, He is Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience of Allah, indicating that those who distort or reject His signs are fully known to Him, and their actions are under His constant surveillance. The rhetorical question posed in the verse serves to highlight the stark contrast between the fate of the disbelievers, who will be thrown into the Fire, and the believers, who will come safely on the Day of Judgment. It underscores the freedom of choice given to humans, urging them to act righteously, as Allah sees all and will judge accordingly.
orig: إن الذين يلحدون في آياتنا لا يخفون علينا أفمن يلقى في النار خير أم من يأتي آمنا يوم القيامة اعملوا ما شئتم إنه بما تعملون بصير

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve in the Reminder when it comes to them... and indeed it is a noble Book.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity of rejecting the Qur'an, referred to as 'the Reminder,' when it is presented. It underscores the divine nature and honor of the Qur'an, described as a 'noble Book,' suggesting that its rejection is not only a denial of guidance but also a dismissal of a highly esteemed and authoritative scripture. The use of 'indeed' twice reinforces the certainty and importance of both the disbelief and the nobility of the Book.
orig: إن الذين كفروا بالذكر لما جاءهم وإنه لكتاب عزيز

translation: Falsehood cannot approach it from before it or from behind it; [it is] a revelation from a Wise and Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the infallibility and divine protection of the Qur'an. It asserts that the Qur'an is safeguarded against any form of falsehood or corruption, whether it attempts to distort its message from the past or the future. This protection is attributed to its origin from Allah, who is described as Wise and Praiseworthy, highlighting the perfection and integrity of the Qur'anic revelation.
orig: لا يأتيه الباطل من بين يديه ولا من خلفه تنزيل من حكيم حميد

translation: Nothing is said to you except what was said to the messengers before you. Indeed, your Lord is the Possessor of forgiveness and the Possessor of painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse reassures the Prophet Muhammad that the opposition and challenges he faces are not unique but are similar to what previous prophets encountered. It emphasizes the dual nature of Allah's attributes: His immense capacity for forgiveness towards those who repent and seek His mercy, and His readiness to impose severe punishment on those who persistently reject His guidance and continue in their wrongdoing. This duality serves as a reminder of the consequences of one's actions and the importance of striving for righteousness.
orig: ما يقال لك إلا ما قد قيل للرسل من قبلك إن ربك لذو مغفرة وذو عقاب أليم

translation: And if We had made it a non-Arabic Qur'an, they would have said, 'Why are its verses not explained? Is it a non-Arabic [Qur'an] and an Arab [messenger]?' Say, 'It is for those who believe a guidance and a cure.' And those who do not believe - in their ears is deafness, and it is upon them blindness. Those are being called from a distant place.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the miraculous nature of the Qur'an being revealed in Arabic, the language of the Prophet Muhammad's people. It suggests that if the Qur'an had been revealed in a foreign language, the disbelievers would still have found reasons to reject it, questioning why its verses were not clear or why an Arab prophet was given a non-Arabic scripture. The verse underscores that the Qur'an's purpose is to guide and heal believers, while those who reject it are described as spiritually deaf and blind, unable to perceive its message, as if they are being called from a distant, unreachable place.
orig: ولو جعلناه قرآنا أعجميا لقالوا لولا فصلت آياته أأعجمي وعربي قل هو للذين آمنوا هدى وشفاء والذين لا يؤمنون في آذانهم وقر وهو عليهم عمى أولئك ينادون من مكان بعيد

translation: And We certainly gave Moses the Scripture, but disputes arose concerning it. And had it not been for a prior decree from your Lord, the matter would have been settled between them. But indeed, they are in suspicious doubt about it.
interpretation: This verse reflects on the divine gift of the Torah to Moses, highlighting the subsequent disagreements among people regarding its interpretation and application. The phrase 'لولا كلمة سبقت من ربك' suggests that God's predetermined plan and mercy delayed a final judgment on these disputes, allowing time for reflection and guidance. The verse underscores the human tendency towards doubt and uncertainty ('شك منه مريب'), which challenges the acceptance and understanding of divine revelations. It serves as a reminder of the importance of faith and the need to overcome skepticism to truly benefit from sacred texts.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى الكتاب فاختلف فيه ولولا كلمة سبقت من ربك لقضي بينهم وإنهم لفي شك منه مريب

translation: Whoever does righteousness, it is for his own soul; and whoever does evil, it is against it. And your Lord is not ever unjust to [His] servants.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes personal accountability and the fairness of God. It teaches that the consequences of one's actions, whether good or bad, are borne by the individual themselves. The righteousness one performs benefits their own soul, enhancing their spiritual state and closeness to God. Conversely, any evil committed harms the perpetrator's own soul. The verse reassures believers of God's justice, stating that He is never unjust to His servants, ensuring that everyone is treated equitably based on their deeds.
orig: من عمل صالحا فلنفسه ومن أساء فعليها وما ربك بظلام للعبيد

translation: To Him is referred the knowledge of the Hour, and no fruit emerges from its sheath, nor does any female become pregnant or give birth except by His knowledge. And on the Day He will call out to them, 'Where are My partners?' they will say, 'We admit to You, none of us can testify to that.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty and omniscience of Allah. It emphasizes that all events, from the monumental (the knowledge of the Hour, or the Day of Judgment) to the seemingly mundane (the emergence of fruit and the processes of pregnancy and birth), are under Allah's complete control and knowledge. The verse also highlights the futility of associating partners with Allah, as on the Day of Judgment, those who did so will have no evidence or witnesses to support their claims, admitting their error in the face of divine truth.
orig: إليه يرد علم الساعة وما تخرج من ثمرات من أكمامها وما تحمل من أنثى ولا تضع إلا بعلمه ويوم يناديهم أين شركائي قالوا آذناك ما منا من شهيد

translation: And lost from them will be those they used to invoke before, and they will be certain that they have no place of escape.
interpretation: This verse highlights the moment of realization for the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment. They will understand that the false deities or idols they worshipped in their earthly life are no longer with them and cannot help them. This realization brings a profound sense of despair as they become certain that there is no way to escape the consequences of their actions. It underscores the theme of accountability and the futility of relying on anything other than the true worship of Allah.
orig: وضل عنهم ما كانوا يدعون من قبل وظنوا ما لهم من محيص

translation: Man does not tire of praying for good, and if evil touches him, he is despairing, hopeless.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to be persistent in seeking good fortune through prayer, yet when faced with adversity, people often quickly fall into despair and lose hope. It reflects on the fragility of human faith and patience, suggesting that one should maintain steadfastness and trust in God's wisdom in all circumstances, not just in times of ease.
orig: لا يسأم الإنسان من دعاء الخير وإن مسه الشر فيئوس قنوط

translation: And if We let him taste mercy from Us after adversity has touched him, he will surely say, 'This is [due] to me, and I do not think the Hour will occur; and [even] if I should be returned to my Lord, indeed, for me there will be with Him the best.' Then We will surely inform those who disbelieved about what they did, and We will surely make them taste a severe punishment.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the human tendency towards ingratitude and denial of divine favor. When a person experiences relief or blessing after hardship, they often attribute it to their own merit rather than acknowledging it as a gift from God. This self-attribution leads to a denial of the Day of Judgment, as they feel secure in their worldly gains and believe they will receive goodness from God regardless of their actions. The verse warns that such attitudes of disbelief and arrogance will be met with accountability and severe punishment in the hereafter, emphasizing the importance of humility, gratitude, and recognition of God's sovereignty over all conditions.
orig: ولئن أذقناه رحمة منا من بعد ضراء مسته ليقولن هذا لي وما أظن الساعة قائمة ولئن رجعت إلى ربي إن لي عنده للحسنى فلننبئن الذين كفروا بما عملوا ولنذيقنهم من عذاب غليظ

translation: And when We bestow favor upon man, he turns away and distances himself; but when evil touches him, he is full of extensive supplication.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to be ungrateful and forgetful of God during times of ease and prosperity. When people receive blessings, they often become arrogant and neglectful of their spiritual duties, turning away from God. However, when they face difficulties or hardships, they quickly turn to God with fervent prayers and supplications, seeking His help and mercy. This behavior reflects a lack of consistent faith and gratitude, as true devotion should remain steadfast in all circumstances.
orig: وإذا أنعمنا على الإنسان أعرض ونأى بجانبه وإذا مسه الشر فذو دعاء عريض

translation: Say, 'Have you considered: if it is from Allah, and you disbelieve in it, who is more astray than one who is in extreme dissension?'
interpretation: This verse challenges the disbelievers to reflect on the consequences of rejecting the Qur'an if it truly comes from Allah. It emphasizes the severity of their error, portraying disbelief as a state of extreme dissension and misguidance, urging them to reconsider their stance in light of the potential truth of the message.
orig: قل أرأيتم إن كان من عند الله ثم كفرتم به من أضل ممن هو في شقاق بعيد

translation: We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth. Is it not sufficient for your Lord that He is a witness over all things?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's omnipotence and His ability to manifest His signs both in the external world (the horizons) and within the human soul. It suggests a gradual revelation of truth that is meant to lead individuals to the undeniable realization of Allah's existence and the veracity of His message. The rhetorical question at the end underscores that Allah's witnessing of all things is a testament to His all-encompassing knowledge and presence, which should be enough to affirm faith in Him.
orig: سنريهم آياتنا في الآفاق وفي أنفسهم حتى يتبين لهم أنه الحق أولم يكف بربك أنه على كل شيء شهيد

translation: Verily, they are in doubt concerning the meeting with their Lord. Verily, He encompasses all things.
interpretation: This verse highlights the skepticism of some people regarding the Day of Judgment and their encounter with Allah. It emphasizes Allah's omnipresence and omniscience, indicating that despite their doubts, Allah is fully aware of and surrounds all aspects of creation, affirming His ultimate control and knowledge over everything.
orig: ألا إنهم في مرية من لقاء ربهم ألا إنه بكل شيء محيط

translation: Ha Mim
interpretation: The letters "Ha" and "Mim" are among the disjointed letters (muqatta'at) found at the beginning of some chapters in the Qur'an. Their precise meaning is known only to Allah, but they serve to emphasize the miraculous nature of the Qur'an and to remind the reader of its divine origin.
orig: حم

translation: Perhaps
interpretation: This word, used in various contexts within the Qur'an, often introduces a possibility or a hypothetical situation, urging reflection on the potential outcomes of actions or events. It serves as a linguistic tool to engage the listener or reader in considering the implications of divine messages.
orig: عسق

translation: Thus does Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise, reveal to you and to those before you.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the continuity and consistency of divine revelation from Allah to His messengers across different times. It highlights that the same Almighty and Wise God who revealed scriptures to previous prophets is also the source of revelation to the Prophet Muhammad. This underscores the unity of the message and the authority of Allah as the ultimate source of guidance, characterized by His attributes of power and wisdom.
orig: كذلك يوحي إليك وإلى الذين من قبلك الله العزيز الحكيم

translation: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And He is the Most High, the Most Great.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and ownership of Allah over all creation, encompassing everything in the heavens and the earth. It highlights His supreme status and greatness, reminding believers of His unmatched power and authority. The attributes 'the Most High' and 'the Most Great' further reinforce His exalted nature and the reverence due to Him.
orig: له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وهو العلي العظيم

translation: The heavens are almost rent asunder from above them, and the angels glorify the praises of their Lord, and they ask forgiveness for those on the earth. Indeed, Allah is the Forgiving, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the immense power and majesty of Allah, suggesting that the heavens themselves are on the brink of splitting due to the awe-inspiring nature of His presence. The angels, in their proximity to Allah, continuously engage in glorifying Him and seeking forgiveness for humanity, highlighting their role as intercessors. The verse concludes by emphasizing Allah's attributes of forgiveness and mercy, reassuring believers of His readiness to forgive and show compassion, despite the overwhelming power He possesses.
orig: تكاد السماوات يتفطرن من فوقهن والملائكة يسبحون بحمد ربهم ويستغفرون لمن في الأرض ألا إن الله هو الغفور الرحيم

translation: And those who take protectors besides Him - Allah is watching over them, and you are not a guardian over them.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of Tawheed, or the oneness of God, by highlighting that those who choose to worship or take protectors other than Allah are under His constant surveillance. It reassures the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and, by extension, all believers, that they are not responsible for guiding or correcting those who stray from the path of monotheism. The ultimate accountability lies with Allah, who is fully aware of everyone's actions and intentions. This serves to relieve the believers of the burden of feeling responsible for others' choices in faith, encouraging them to focus on their own spiritual journey and trust in Allah's divine plan and justice.
orig: والذين اتخذوا من دونه أولياء الله حفيظ عليهم وما أنت عليهم بوكيل

translation: And thus We have revealed to you a Quran in Arabic so that you may warn the Mother of Cities and those around it, and warn of the Day of Assembly, about which there is no doubt. A group will be in Paradise and a group in the Blaze.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the purpose of the Qur'an's revelation in Arabic, which is to serve as a warning to the people of Mecca (referred to as the Mother of Cities) and its surroundings. The warning is twofold: it alerts them to the imminent Day of Judgment, an event that is certain to occur, and it informs them of the ultimate outcomes that await humanity - some will be rewarded with Paradise, while others will face punishment in Hell. This underscores the Qur'an's role as a universal message and a reminder of accountability and the afterlife.
orig: وكذلك أوحينا إليك قرآنا عربيا لتنذر أم القرى ومن حولها وتنذر يوم الجمع لا ريب فيه فريق في الجنة وفريق في السعير

translation: And if Allah had willed, He could have made them one nation, but He admits whom He wills into His mercy. And the wrongdoers will have no protector or helper.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine wisdom and sovereignty of Allah in the diversity of human beliefs and communities. It suggests that the existence of different nations and beliefs is not a result of Allah's inability to unify them, but rather a deliberate choice to test and distinguish between people based on their actions and faith. The phrase "but He admits whom He wills into His mercy" highlights that entry into divine mercy is ultimately determined by Allah's will, emphasizing the importance of faith and righteousness. Conversely, the mention of wrongdoers having no protector or helper serves as a warning that those who engage in injustice or disbelief will face the consequences alone, without any support, in the hereafter.
orig: ولو شاء الله لجعلهم أمة واحدة ولكن يدخل من يشاء في رحمته والظالمون ما لهم من ولي ولا نصير

translation: Or have they taken protectors besides Him? But Allah, He is the Protector, and He gives life to the dead, and He is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of Tawhid, the oneness of Allah, by questioning the practice of taking other beings or entities as protectors or allies besides Allah. It asserts that only Allah is the true Protector and has the power to resurrect the dead, highlighting His omnipotence and sovereignty over all aspects of existence. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to rely solely on Allah and to recognize His ultimate authority and capability in all matters.
orig: أم اتخذوا من دونه أولياء فالله هو الولي وهو يحيي الموتى وهو على كل شيء قدير

translation: And in anything over which you differ, its ruling is with Allah. That is Allah, my Lord; upon Him I rely, and to Him I turn.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate authority of Allah in resolving disputes and making judgments. It instructs believers to refer all matters of disagreement to Allah's guidance and law, reinforcing the concept of tawakkul (reliance on Allah) and tawbah (turning back to Allah). The verse reflects a deep trust in Allah's wisdom and justice, encouraging Muslims to submit to His will and seek His guidance in all aspects of life.
orig: وما اختلفتم فيه من شيء فحكمه إلى الله ذلكم الله ربي عليه توكلت وإليه أنيب

translation: Originator of the heavens and the earth. He has made for you from yourselves mates, and from the cattle mates; He multiplies you thereby. There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the Hearing, the Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's role as the Creator of the universe and highlights His power and uniqueness. By mentioning the creation of mates from humans and cattle, it illustrates how Allah facilitates reproduction and growth among His creations, underscoring His role in sustaining life. The statement 'There is nothing like unto Him' asserts Allah's incomparable nature, reinforcing the concept of tawhid (oneness of God). The attributes of being 'the Hearing, the Seeing' further emphasize Allah's omniscience and omnipresence, indicating that He is fully aware of all that occurs in His creation.
orig: فاطر السماوات والأرض جعل لكم من أنفسكم أزواجا ومن الأنعام أزواجا يذرؤكم فيه ليس كمثله شيء وهو السميع البصير

translation: To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth. He extends provision for whom He wills and restricts [it]. Indeed, He is, of all things, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's complete control and sovereignty over the universe. The 'keys of the heavens and the earth' symbolize His authority to unlock and manage all aspects of creation. The reference to provision indicates that Allah alone decides who receives abundance or scarcity, based on His wisdom and knowledge. This underscores the belief that all sustenance comes from Allah, and He is fully aware of the needs and circumstances of every creature, reflecting His omniscience and omnipotence.
orig: له مقاليد السماوات والأرض يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء ويقدر إنه بكل شيء عليم

translation: He has ordained for you of religion what He enjoined upon Noah and that which We have revealed to you, and what We enjoined upon Abraham and Moses and Jesus - to establish the religion and not be divided therein. Difficult for the polytheists is that to which you call them. Allah chooses for Himself whom He wills and guides to Himself whoever turns back [to Him].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity of the message across different prophets, from Noah to Jesus, indicating that the core of the religion ordained by Allah is singular and consistent. It calls for the establishment of this religion without division, highlighting the challenge this poses to those who associate partners with Allah (polytheists). The verse also underscores Allah's sovereignty in choosing and guiding individuals towards Him, reinforcing the concept of divine selection and guidance in the path of monotheism.
orig: شرع لكم من الدين ما وصى به نوحا والذي أوحينا إليك وما وصينا به إبراهيم وموسى وعيسى أن أقيموا الدين ولا تتفرقوا فيه كبر على المشركين ما تدعوهم إليه الله يجتبي إليه من يشاء ويهدي إليه من ينيب

translation: And they did not become divided until after knowledge had come to them - out of jealous animosity between themselves. And if not for a word that preceded from your Lord for a specified term, it would have been concluded between them. And indeed, those who were granted inheritance of the Scripture after them are in disquieting doubt concerning it.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to diverge from the truth due to envy and rivalry, even after receiving clear knowledge. It reflects on the historical division among the People of the Scripture, suggesting that such division was not due to a lack of knowledge but rather due to selfish motives. The verse also alludes to God's mercy and patience, as He delays judgment until a predetermined time, allowing time for repentance. Furthermore, it points out the uncertainty and doubt that subsequent generations have about the same scriptures, indicating a failure to uphold and understand the divine message properly.
orig: وما تفرقوا إلا من بعد ما جاءهم العلم بغيا بينهم ولولا كلمة سبقت من ربك إلى أجل مسمى لقضي بينهم وإن الذين أورثوا الكتاب من بعدهم لفي شك منه مريب

translation: So invite to that and stand firm as you are commanded and do not follow their desires, but say, 'I believe in what Allah has revealed of the Book, and I am commanded to do justice among you. Allah is our Lord and your Lord. For us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds. There is no argument between us and you. Allah will bring us together, and to Him is the final return.'
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad to steadfastly call people to Islam, adhering firmly to the divine commandments without being swayed by the desires or opinions of others. It emphasizes the importance of belief in the revelations from Allah and the necessity of justice. The verse also highlights the concept of individual accountability for one's actions, acknowledging that while people may have different paths, ultimately, Allah will judge all and bring everyone together on the Day of Judgment. This underscores the unity of humanity under the sovereignty of Allah and the inevitability of returning to Him.
orig: فلذلك فادع واستقم كما أمرت ولا تتبع أهواءهم وقل آمنت بما أنزل الله من كتاب وأمرت لأعدل بينكم الله ربنا وربكم لنا أعمالنا ولكم أعمالكم لا حجة بيننا وبينكم الله يجمع بيننا وإليه المصير

translation: And those who argue concerning Allah after He has been responded to, their argument is invalid before their Lord, and upon them is wrath, and for them is a severe punishment.
interpretation: This verse addresses individuals who continue to dispute and argue about Allah even after the truth has been made clear to them and they have been called to it. Their arguments are considered invalid and futile in the sight of Allah. As a consequence of their persistent rejection and argumentation against the clear signs of Allah, they incur His wrath and are promised a severe punishment in the hereafter. This serves as a warning against the dangers of rejecting the truth out of pride or stubbornness, emphasizing the importance of accepting and submitting to the divine guidance once it has been presented.
orig: والذين يحاجون في الله من بعد ما استجيب له حجتهم داحضة عند ربهم وعليهم غضب ولهم عذاب شديد

translation: Allah is He Who has sent down the Book in truth, and the Balance. And what will make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near!
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin of the Qur'an, stating that it was revealed by Allah with truth and serves as a criterion for judgment. The mention of the Balance (Al-Mizan) symbolizes justice and fairness in divine law. The latter part of the verse serves as a reminder of the unpredictability and imminent possibility of the Day of Judgment, urging believers to remain vigilant and righteous in their actions.
orig: الله الذي أنزل الكتاب بالحق والميزان وما يدريك لعل الساعة قريب

translation: Those who do not believe in it hasten it, while those who believe are fearful of it and know that it is the truth. Indeed, those who dispute concerning the Hour are certainly in extreme error.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrasting attitudes of believers and non-believers towards the Day of Judgment. Non-believers, in their denial, mockingly wish for it to come sooner, not understanding its gravity. In contrast, believers are filled with awe and fear of this event, fully acknowledging its reality and inevitability. The verse also condemns those who argue against the existence or timing of the Hour, labeling their stance as a profound deviation from the truth, emphasizing the certainty and significance of the Day of Judgment in Islamic theology.
orig: يستعجل بها الذين لا يؤمنون بها والذين آمنوا مشفقون منها ويعلمون أنها الحق ألا إن الذين يمارون في الساعة لفي ضلال بعيد

translation: Allah is Subtle with His servants; He provides for whom He wills. And He is the Powerful, the Exalted.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's attribute of subtlety (Lutf), indicating His gentle and precise care for His servants, often in ways that are not immediately apparent. The provision mentioned here is not limited to material sustenance but encompasses guidance, opportunities, and spiritual nourishment. Allah's choice in whom He provides reflects His wisdom and sovereignty. The attributes of being Powerful (Al-Qawi) and Exalted (Al-Aziz) emphasize His absolute capability and majesty, reinforcing the notion that His decisions are beyond human comprehension yet are perfectly just and merciful.
orig: الله لطيف بعباده يرزق من يشاء وهو القوي العزيز

translation: Whoever desires the harvest of the Hereafter, We increase for him in his harvest; and whoever desires the harvest of this world, We give him from it, but he will have no share in the Hereafter.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the choice between prioritizing worldly gains or spiritual rewards. It suggests that God rewards individuals according to their intentions and desires. Those who seek the eternal benefits of the Hereafter will find their efforts multiplied by God, indicating a promise of increased spiritual growth and reward. Conversely, those who focus solely on worldly gains will receive what they seek in this life, but at the cost of having no share in the eternal life of the Hereafter. This teaches the importance of setting one's sights on long-term spiritual goals over short-term material gains.
orig: من كان يريد حرث الآخرة نزد له في حرثه ومن كان يريد حرث الدنيا نؤته منها وما له في الآخرة من نصيب

translation: Or have they partners (with Allah) who have prescribed for them a religion which Allah has not allowed? Had it not been for the decisive word, the matter would have been settled between them. And indeed, the wrongdoers will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse questions whether those who deviate from the true path of Islam are following invented religious practices sanctioned by false deities or partners attributed to Allah. It emphasizes that only Allah has the authority to legislate religious matters. The 'decisive word' refers to Allah's promise to postpone the final judgment until the Day of Resurrection, allowing time for repentance. The verse warns that those who unjustly alter or ignore divine laws will face severe consequences in the hereafter.
orig: أم لهم شركاء شرعوا لهم من الدين ما لم يأذن به الله ولولا كلمة الفصل لقضي بينهم وإن الظالمين لهم عذاب أليم

translation: You see the wrongdoers fearful of what they have earned, and it is about to befall them, while those who have believed and done righteous deeds will be in gardens of Paradise; they will have whatever they wish from their Lord. That is the great bounty.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between the fate of the wrongdoers and the believers. The wrongdoers are depicted as being in a state of fear and anxiety due to the consequences of their actions, which are imminent. In contrast, the believers who have performed righteous deeds are promised a blissful afterlife in Paradise, where they will have everything they desire. This serves as a reminder of the divine justice and the ultimate reward for faith and good deeds, emphasizing the great bounty that awaits the righteous in the hereafter.
orig: ترى الظالمين مشفقين مما كسبوا وهو واقع بهم والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات في روضات الجنات لهم ما يشاءون عند ربهم ذلك هو الفضل الكبير

translation: That is what Allah gives glad tidings to His servants who have believed and done righteous deeds. Say, [O Muhammad], "I do not ask you for it any payment, but only love for the near relatives." And whoever commits a good deed - We will increase for him therein goodness. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Appreciative.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the reward and glad tidings that Allah promises to those who believe and perform good deeds. It highlights that the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) did not seek any worldly compensation for his message, but only asked for love and kindness towards his close relatives, reflecting the importance of family ties in Islam. The verse also assures that any good action performed by an individual will be rewarded by Allah, who will increase the goodness in it, showcasing His attributes of forgiveness and gratitude towards His servants.
orig: ذلك الذي يبشر الله عباده الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات قل لا أسألكم عليه أجرا إلا المودة في القربى ومن يقترف حسنة نزد له فيها حسنا إن الله غفور شكور

translation: Or do they say, 'He has invented a lie about Allah'? But if Allah willed, He could seal over your heart. And Allah eliminates falsehood and establishes the truth by His words. Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse addresses the accusations of those who claim that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) fabricated lies against Allah. It emphasizes that if Allah wished, He could have prevented the Prophet from receiving divine revelation by sealing his heart. However, Allah's wisdom and mercy allow the truth to be revealed through His chosen messenger. The verse underscores Allah's power to obliterate falsehood and affirm the truth through His divine words. It also highlights Allah's omniscience, indicating that He is fully aware of the innermost thoughts and intentions of all beings, reinforcing the notion that nothing is hidden from Him.
orig: أم يقولون افترى على الله كذبا فإن يشإ الله يختم على قلبك ويمح الله الباطل ويحق الحق بكلماته إنه عليم بذات الصدور

translation: And He it is who accepts repentance from His servants and pardons the evil deeds and knows what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's attributes of mercy and forgiveness. It highlights that Allah is always ready to accept the sincere repentance of His servants, no matter the gravity of their sins, as long as they turn back to Him with genuine remorse. Additionally, it reassures believers that Allah is fully aware of all their actions, both good and bad, encouraging them to seek His forgiveness and to strive for righteousness, knowing that He is both forgiving and omniscient.
orig: وهو الذي يقبل التوبة عن عباده ويعفو عن السيئات ويعلم ما تفعلون

translation: And He responds to those who have believed and done righteous deeds and increases them from His bounty. But the disbelievers will have a severe punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the responsiveness of Allah to the believers who not only have faith but also actively perform good deeds. It highlights the concept of divine increase or 'fadl', suggesting that Allah's generosity extends beyond mere response to include additional blessings and favors. Conversely, it serves as a reminder of the consequences faced by those who reject faith, indicating a clear distinction in the outcomes for believers and disbelievers based on their actions and beliefs.
orig: ويستجيب الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات ويزيدهم من فضله والكافرون لهم عذاب شديد

translation: And if Allah were to extend provision to His servants, they would rebel in the earth; but He sends down in due measure what He wills. Indeed, He is, of His servants, Expert and Seeing.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's wisdom in distributing sustenance. It suggests that if Allah were to give unlimited wealth to everyone, it might lead to chaos and corruption on earth, as people might become arrogant and rebellious. Instead, Allah provides in measured amounts according to His knowledge and wisdom, ensuring a balance that tests and guides humanity. The verse emphasizes Allah's complete awareness and oversight of His servants' needs and actions.
orig: ولو بسط الله الرزق لعباده لبغوا في الأرض ولكن ينزل بقدر ما يشاء إنه بعباده خبير بصير

translation: And it is He who sends down the rain after they have despaired and spreads His mercy, and He is the Protector, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's omnipotence and mercy, illustrating how He can bring relief and sustenance in the form of rain even when people have lost all hope. It emphasizes His role as the ultimate Protector and the One worthy of all praise, reinforcing the belief in His continuous care and providence over His creation.
orig: وهو الذي ينزل الغيث من بعد ما قنطوا وينشر رحمته وهو الولي الحميد

translation: And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the creatures He has spread in them. And He is Able to gather them together when He wills.
interpretation: This verse highlights the omnipotence and sovereignty of Allah, illustrating His creative power through the vastness of the universe and the diversity of life within it. The mention of Allah's ability to gather all creatures when He wills underscores His ultimate control over creation and the inevitability of the Day of Judgment, where all beings will be assembled for accountability.
orig: ومن آياته خلق السماوات والأرض وما بث فيهما من دابة وهو على جمعهم إذا يشاء قدير

translation: And whatever misfortune befalls you, it is because of what your hands have earned. And He pardons much.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of personal responsibility in Islam, indicating that the adversities one faces are often a result of one's own actions. However, it also highlights God's mercy, as He forgives many of our shortcomings despite our faults.
orig: وما أصابكم من مصيبة فبما كسبت أيديكم ويعفو عن كثير

translation: And you will not be able to escape (from the power of Allah) on earth, and apart from Allah, you have neither a protector nor a helper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence and omnipresence of Allah, indicating that no one can evade His authority or judgment. It serves as a reminder of human vulnerability and dependence on Allah, underscoring that no other being or entity can provide the protection or assistance that only Allah can offer.
orig: وما أنتم بمعجزين في الأرض وما لكم من دون الله من ولي ولا نصير

translation: And among His signs is that He enables you to sail on the sea in ships like mountains.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine power and mercy of Allah, as He has granted humans the ability to navigate vast oceans using ships, which are likened to mountains due to their size and strength. It serves as a reminder of the intricate balance and design in creation, pointing to the greatness of the Creator who enables such feats of human endeavor and exploration.
orig: ومن آياته الجوار في البحر كالأعلام

translation: If He wills, He can calm the wind, leaving the ships motionless on its surface. Indeed, in that are signs for everyone patient and grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's absolute power over nature, specifically His ability to control the wind and thus the movement of ships. It serves as a reminder of divine omnipotence and the need for humans to recognize and submit to this power with patience and gratitude. The mention of 'patient and grateful' underscores the qualities believers should cultivate in response to God's signs and trials, reflecting a deeper spiritual lesson beyond the physical phenomenon described.
orig: إن يشأ يسكن الريح فيظللن رواكد على ظهره إن في ذلك لآيات لكل صبار شكور

translation: Or He could destroy them for what they have earned, and He pardons much.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's mercy and justice. It indicates that Allah has the power to punish people for their wrongdoings, as they deserve, but He often chooses to forgive them instead, showing His immense mercy. The phrase "and He pardons much" emphasizes that Allah's forgiveness is vast and frequent, encouraging believers to seek repentance and rely on His mercy.
orig: أو يوبقهن بما كسبوا ويعف عن كثير

translation: And those who argue about Our verses will know that they have no escape.
interpretation: This verse warns those who engage in disputing or arguing against the clear signs and verses of Allah that they will eventually realize the futility of their actions. It emphasizes the inevitability of facing the consequences of denying or challenging divine truths, suggesting that on the Day of Judgment, there will be no refuge or escape for them from the accountability of their disbelief and arguments.
orig: ويعلم الذين يجادلون في آياتنا ما لهم من محيص

translation: So whatever you have been given is but a passing enjoyment of this worldly life, but what is with Allah is better and more lasting for those who believe and put their trust in their Lord.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the transient nature of worldly possessions and pleasures, contrasting them with the eternal rewards that await believers in the hereafter. It encourages believers to focus on their faith and trust in Allah, as the ultimate source of lasting goodness and stability, rather than being overly attached to the temporary enjoyments of this life.
orig: فما أوتيتم من شيء فمتاع الحياة الدنيا وما عند الله خير وأبقى للذين آمنوا وعلى ربهم يتوكلون

translation: And those who avoid the major sins and immoralities, and when they are angry, they forgive.
interpretation: This verse highlights the qualities of the righteous believers. It emphasizes their ability to steer clear of grave sins and moral transgressions, showcasing their commitment to a virtuous life. Additionally, it underscores their capacity for forgiveness even in moments of anger, reflecting a high level of spiritual maturity and self-control. This trait of forgiveness in anger is particularly praised as it demonstrates a conscious choice to maintain peace and uphold moral integrity over reacting impulsively.
orig: والذين يجتنبون كبائر الإثم والفواحش وإذا ما غضبوا هم يغفرون

translation: And those who respond to their Lord and establish prayer and their affairs are [determined] by mutual consultation among themselves, and from what We have provided them, they spend.
interpretation: This verse describes the characteristics of believers who are obedient to Allah. It highlights four key actions: responding to the call of their Lord, maintaining regular prayers, making decisions through mutual consultation, and spending in charity from the provisions given by Allah. The emphasis on consultation reflects the importance of collective wisdom and unity in decision-making within the community, promoting a sense of shared responsibility and cooperation. This approach not only strengthens community bonds but also ensures that decisions are made with consideration for the collective good, aligning with Islamic principles of justice and compassion.
orig: والذين استجابوا لربهم وأقاموا الصلاة وأمرهم شورى بينهم ومما رزقناهم ينفقون

translation: And those who, when they are oppressed, they defend themselves.
interpretation: This verse highlights the principle of self-defense in Islam. It indicates that Muslims are permitted to defend themselves when they are wronged or oppressed. This right to self-defense is not only a permission but also an encouragement to stand up against injustice, reflecting the Islamic value of justice and the responsibility to protect oneself and the community from harm.
orig: والذين إذا أصابهم البغي هم ينتصرون

translation: And the recompense of an evil is an evil like it, but whoever pardons and makes reconciliation, then his reward is upon Allah. Indeed, He does not like the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of justice and forgiveness in Islam. It suggests that while it is justifiable to respond to an evil act with a similar act, the higher moral ground is to forgive and seek reconciliation. By doing so, one entrusts their reward to Allah, reflecting a trust in divine justice over personal retribution. The verse also underscores that Allah disapproves of those who persist in wrongdoing, encouraging believers to avoid such behavior and instead opt for forgiveness and peace.
orig: وجزاء سيئة سيئة مثلها فمن عفا وأصلح فأجره على الله إنه لا يحب الظالمين

translation: And whoever avenges himself after having been wronged - those have not upon them any cause [for blame].
interpretation: This verse indicates that if a person takes action to defend themselves or seek justice after being wronged, they are not to be blamed or held accountable for their actions. It emphasizes the permissibility and moral justification of self-defense and seeking retribution within the bounds of justice, highlighting that such actions do not incur sin or liability.
orig: ولمن انتصر بعد ظلمه فأولئك ما عليهم من سبيل

translation: The way (of punishment) is only against those who oppress people and spread corruption in the land without right. Those will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that divine retribution is specifically directed towards individuals who unjustly harm others and cause disorder in society. It highlights the principle of justice in Islam, indicating that punishment is reserved for those who deliberately engage in wrongdoing and tyranny, thereby disrupting the peace and rights of others. The mention of a 'painful punishment' serves as a warning and deterrent against such actions, reinforcing the moral and ethical standards expected within the community.
orig: إنما السبيل على الذين يظلمون الناس ويبغون في الأرض بغير الحق أولئك لهم عذاب أليم

translation: And for those who are patient and forgive, indeed, that is of the matters [requiring] determination.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the virtues of patience and forgiveness, suggesting that these qualities are not only commendable but also indicative of strong resolve and determination. It implies that exercising patience and forgiveness in the face of adversity or wrongdoing requires a firm commitment and strength of character, which are essential for handling significant and challenging situations effectively.
orig: ولمن صبر وغفر إن ذلك لمن عزم الأمور

translation: And whoever Allah leaves astray - for him there is no protector thereafter. And you will see the wrongdoers, when they see the punishment, saying, 'Is there any way to return?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequence of being led astray by Allah, indicating that once someone is misguided by divine decree, they are left without any guidance or protector. It underscores the finality and severity of divine misguidance. The latter part of the verse depicts a scene of realization and regret among the wrongdoers upon witnessing the punishment, where they desperately seek a chance to revert their actions, illustrating the futility of seeking repentance after the moment of judgment has arrived.
orig: ومن يضلل الله فما له من ولي من بعده وترى الظالمين لما رأوا العذاب يقولون هل إلى مرد من سبيل

translation: And you will see them presented before it (the Fire) humbled from disgrace, looking with a furtive glance. And those who believed will say, 'Indeed, the losers are those who lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Beware, indeed, the wrongdoers are in a lasting punishment.'
interpretation: This verse describes the scene on the Day of Judgment where disbelievers are brought before the Hellfire in a state of humiliation and fear, aware of their impending punishment but still trying to look away in shame. The believers, witnessing this, reflect on the true nature of loss, emphasizing that the greatest loss is not material but spiritual—losing one's soul and family due to disbelief. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of wrongdoing and the permanence of the punishment awaiting the unjust, urging believers to remain steadfast in faith and righteousness.
orig: وتراهم يعرضون عليها خاشعين من الذل ينظرون من طرف خفي وقال الذين آمنوا إن الخاسرين الذين خسروا أنفسهم وأهليهم يوم القيامة ألا إن الظالمين في عذاب مقيم

translation: And they will have no allies to help them other than Allah. And whoever Allah sends astray - for him there is no way.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute dependence on Allah and the futility of seeking help from any other source. It highlights that those who are led astray by Allah due to their own actions and disbelief have no recourse or path to salvation, emphasizing the importance of staying on the right path guided by divine will.
orig: وما كان لهم من أولياء ينصرونهم من دون الله ومن يضلل الله فما له من سبيل

translation: Respond to your Lord before a Day comes from Allah when there will be no repelling. You will have no refuge on that Day, nor will there be any denial.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the urgency of responding to Allah's call and guidance in this life before the inevitable Day of Judgment arrives, a day when no one can avert its consequences. It serves as a reminder that on that day, individuals will have no place to seek shelter from the accountability of their actions, nor will they be able to deny or reject the truth they were presented with in their lifetime. The verse underscores the importance of heeding Allah's messages and living righteously while there is still time.
orig: استجيبوا لربكم من قبل أن يأتي يوم لا مرد له من الله ما لكم من ملجإ يومئذ وما لكم من نكير

translation: So if they turn away, then We have not sent you as a guardian over them. Your duty is only to convey (the message). And indeed, when We let man taste mercy from Us, he rejoices in it; but when an evil touches them because of what their hands have sent forth, then indeed, man is ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophet Muhammad's role as a messenger, not as a guardian responsible for people's acceptance of the message. It highlights the human tendency to rejoice in God's blessings but become ungrateful and blameful when faced with adversity, which often results from their own actions. This serves as a reminder of the importance of gratitude and accountability in the face of life's ups and downs.
orig: فإن أعرضوا فما أرسلناك عليهم حفيظا إن عليك إلا البلاغ وإنا إذا أذقنا الإنسان منا رحمة فرح بها وإن تصبهم سيئة بما قدمت أيديهم فإن الإنسان كفور

translation: To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth; He creates what He wills. He bestows female (offspring) to whom He wills, and bestows male (offspring) to whom He wills.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute sovereignty and power over all creation. It highlights that the distribution of offspring, whether male or female, is entirely under Allah's control and discretion, reflecting His wisdom and authority over human affairs. This serves as a reminder to humans to accept and be content with Allah's decrees, recognizing that everything He does is part of a larger divine plan.
