The verse uses the wish for death as a test of the sincerity and truthfulness of their claim, emphasizing the gravity and seriousness of asserting a unique divine alliance.
orig: قل يا أيها الذين هادوا إن زعمتم أنكم أولياء لله من دون الناس فتمنوا الموت إن كنتم صادقين

translation: And they will never wish for it because of what their hands have put forth, and Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse indicates that those who have committed wrongdoings will never truly desire the Day of Judgment due to their fear of facing the consequences of their actions. It underscores the notion that Allah is fully aware of the deeds of the wrongdoers, emphasizing divine omniscience and justice.
orig: ولا يتمنونه أبدا بما قدمت أيديهم والله عليم بالظالمين

translation: Say, "Indeed, the death from which you flee - indeed, it will meet you. Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you about what you used to do."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability of death and the accountability that follows it. It serves as a reminder that no matter how much one tries to avoid or escape death, it is an inescapable reality that every individual will face. After death, individuals will be brought before Allah, who is fully aware of all things hidden and manifest. At that time, each person will be informed of their deeds, highlighting the concept of divine justice and the importance of living a righteous life in preparation for the hereafter.
orig: قل إن الموت الذي تفرون منه فإنه ملاقيكم ثم تردون إلى عالم الغيب والشهادة فينبئكم بما كنتم تعملون

translation: O you who have believed, when [the adhan] is called for the prayer on the day of Jumu'ah [Friday], then proceed to the remembrance of Allah and leave trade. That is better for you, if you only knew.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of prioritizing the Friday prayer over worldly activities such as trade. It instructs believers to hasten towards the mosque for the communal prayer when the call to prayer is made, highlighting that spiritual devotion and the remembrance of Allah are more beneficial for their well-being than material pursuits. The phrase 'if you only knew' suggests that the true value of this act may not be immediately apparent but is significant for spiritual growth and divine reward.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا نودي للصلاة من يوم الجمعة فاسعوا إلى ذكر الله وذروا البيع ذلكم خير لكم إن كنتم تعلمون

translation: So when the prayer is concluded, disperse within the land and seek from the bounty of Allah, and remember Allah much that you may succeed.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to engage actively in worldly affairs after fulfilling their religious obligations, such as prayer. It emphasizes the balance between spiritual devotion and the pursuit of livelihood, suggesting that one should not neglect their duties in this world. The remembrance of Allah is highlighted as a continuous practice that should accompany all actions, reinforcing the idea that success in both worldly and spiritual matters is achieved through a life intertwined with the awareness and gratitude towards Allah.
orig: فإذا قضيت الصلاة فانتشروا في الأرض وابتغوا من فضل الله واذكروا الله كثيرا لعلكم تفلحون

translation: And when they see some merchandise or some amusement, they disperse to it and leave you standing. Say, 'What is with Allah is better than amusement and than merchandise, and Allah is the best of providers.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad's companions who would often leave his side during prayer or sermon to engage in trade or entertainment. It highlights a common human tendency to be distracted by worldly pursuits, even during moments of spiritual significance. The verse serves as a reminder of the superiority of spiritual rewards over material gains, urging believers to prioritize their faith and connection with Allah over temporary pleasures and profits. It also reassures that Allah's provision is the most beneficial and sustaining, encouraging trust in divine providence rather than in fleeting worldly distractions.
orig: وإذا رأوا تجارة أو لهوا انفضوا إليها وتركوك قائما قل ما عند الله خير من اللهو ومن التجارة والله خير الرازقين

translation: When the hypocrites come to you, they say, 'We bear witness that you are indeed the Messenger of Allah.' And Allah knows that you are truly His Messenger, and Allah bears witness that the hypocrites are certainly liars.
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of hypocrisy and divine knowledge. It illustrates how hypocrites outwardly profess faith in the Prophet Muhammad as the Messenger of Allah, yet their hearts are filled with doubt and deceit. The verse emphasizes that while humans may be deceived by outward professions of faith, Allah's knowledge penetrates all facades, affirming the truth of the Prophet's mission and exposing the falsehood of the hypocrites. It serves as a reminder to believers to be wary of hypocrisy and to trust in Allah's ultimate judgment and knowledge.
orig: إذا جاءك المنافقون قالوا نشهد إنك لرسول الله والله يعلم إنك لرسوله والله يشهد إن المنافقين لكاذبون

translation: They have taken their oaths as a screen, so they turn away from the path of Allah. Indeed, evil is what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse criticizes those who use their oaths deceitfully as a means to obstruct others from following the path of Allah. It highlights the moral corruption of such individuals, indicating that their actions are not only wrong but also harmful to the spiritual well-being of the community. The verse serves as a warning against hypocrisy and the misuse of religious commitments for personal gain or to mislead others.
orig: اتخذوا أيمانهم جنة فصدوا عن سبيل الله إنهم ساء ما كانوا يعملون

translation: That is because they believed, then disbelieved, so their hearts were sealed, and thus they do not understand.
interpretation: This verse explains the spiritual consequence of hypocrisy, where individuals initially accept faith but later reject it. The sealing of their hearts is a metaphor for their inability to perceive or understand spiritual truths due to their rejection of faith after initially accepting it. This condition reflects a deliberate choice that leads to a state of spiritual blindness.
orig: ذلك بأنهم آمنوا ثم كفروا فطبع على قلوبهم فهم لا يفقهون

translation: And when you see them, their bodies please you; and if they speak, you listen to their speech. [They are] as if they were pieces of wood propped up. They think every shout is against them. They are the enemy, so beware of them. May Allah destroy them; how are they deluded?
interpretation: This verse describes the hypocrites, who outwardly appear impressive and speak eloquently, yet their hearts are devoid of faith. They are likened to propped-up wooden logs, indicating their lack of genuine substance and inner strength. Their constant fear and paranoia, thinking every shout is directed at them, reveal their inner turmoil and guilt. The verse warns believers to be cautious of such individuals, as they are enemies who can cause harm through their deception and betrayal. The prayer for their destruction reflects the severity of their misguidance and the danger they pose to the community of believers.
orig: وإذا رأيتهم تعجبك أجسامهم وإن يقولوا تسمع لقولهم كأنهم خشب مسندة يحسبون كل صيحة عليهم هم العدو فاحذرهم قاتلهم الله أنى يؤفكون

translation: And when it is said to them, 'Come, the Messenger of Allah will ask forgiveness for you,' they turn aside their heads, and you see them turning away in arrogance.
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and pride of those who refuse to seek forgiveness through the Prophet Muhammad. It illustrates their rejection of divine mercy and guidance, emphasizing their stubbornness and unwillingness to humble themselves before Allah. This attitude is a barrier to spiritual growth and acceptance of faith.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم تعالوا يستغفر لكم رسول الله لووا رءوسهم ورأيتهم يصدون وهم مستكبرون

translation: It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them; Allah will never forgive them. Indeed, Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.
interpretation: This verse suggests that there are individuals whose actions and hearts are so far from the path of righteousness that intercession or prayers for their forgiveness are futile. It underscores the concept that divine guidance and forgiveness are contingent upon one's willingness to follow God's path. Those who persistently choose to defy God's commands, labeled here as 'the defiantly disobedient,' place themselves beyond the reach of divine mercy, not because God is unwilling to forgive, but because they have chosen a path that leads away from His guidance.
orig: سواء عليهم أستغفرت لهم أم لم تستغفر لهم لن يغفر الله لهم إن الله لا يهدي القوم الفاسقين

translation: They are the ones who say, 'Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse.' And to Allah belong the treasures of the heavens and the earth, but the hypocrites do not understand.
interpretation: This verse criticizes the hypocrites who advised against providing financial support to the companions of the Prophet Muhammad, suggesting that they should be left to disperse and abandon the Prophet. The verse highlights the shortsightedness of the hypocrites, as they fail to recognize that Allah is the ultimate provider, possessing the treasures of both the heavens and the earth. The underlying message is a call to trust in Allah's providence and to support the Prophet and his followers, rather than being swayed by the selfish and misguided advice of the hypocrites.
orig: هم الذين يقولون لا تنفقوا على من عند رسول الله حتى ينفضوا ولله خزائن السماوات والأرض ولكن المنافقين لا يفقهون

translation: They say, 'If we return to the city, the more honored [there] will surely expel the more humble.' But honor belongs to Allah and His Messenger and the believers, but the hypocrites do not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the false sense of security and power that the hypocrites felt, believing they could reclaim their status in Medina. It underscores the reality that true honor and power come from Allah, His Messenger, and the believers, not from worldly positions or alliances. The hypocrites' ignorance of this divine truth is emphasized, illustrating their spiritual blindness and misjudgment of what constitutes real strength and honor.
orig: يقولون لئن رجعنا إلى المدينة ليخرجن الأعز منها الأذل ولله العزة ولرسوله وللمؤمنين ولكن المنافقين لا يعلمون

translation: O you who have believed, let not your wealth and your children divert you from remembrance of Allah. And whoever does that - then those are the losers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder to believers that the pursuit of worldly possessions and family responsibilities should not distract them from their primary duty of remembering and worshipping Allah. It emphasizes the importance of maintaining a spiritual focus amidst the distractions of life, warning that those who allow material concerns to overshadow their faith will ultimately be the ones who suffer loss in the hereafter.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تلهكم أموالكم ولا أولادكم عن ذكر الله ومن يفعل ذلك فأولئك هم الخاسرون

translation: And spend from what We have provided you before death approaches one of you and he says, 'My Lord, if only You would delay me for a brief term so I would give in charity and be among the righteous.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of giving charity and spending in the way of Allah from the provisions He has granted us during our lifetime. It serves as a reminder that the opportunity to do good deeds ends with death, and one should not procrastinate in performing acts of righteousness. The verse illustrates the regret one might feel at the moment of death, wishing for a short extension of life to perform good deeds, highlighting the urgency and necessity of acting righteously while one is still alive.
orig: وأنفقوا من ما رزقناكم من قبل أن يأتي أحدكم الموت فيقول رب لولا أخرتني إلى أجل قريب فأصدق وأكن من الصالحين

translation: And Allah will not delay a soul when its time has come, and Allah is All-Aware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability of death and the precise timing determined by Allah for each individual. It reassures believers that no one can postpone their appointed time of death, underscoring the concept of divine decree (Qadar). Additionally, it serves as a reminder that Allah is fully aware of all actions and deeds, encouraging mindfulness and righteousness in one's life.
orig: ولن يؤخر الله نفسا إذا جاء أجلها والله خبير بما تعملون

translation: Whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is on the earth glorifies Allah. His is the dominion, and to Him belong all the praises and thanks, and He is Able to do all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universal glorification of Allah by all creation, both in the heavens and on earth, highlighting His absolute sovereignty and omnipotence. It serves as a reminder of Allah's supreme authority over all existence and His capability to manage all affairs, encouraging believers to recognize and submit to His power and majesty.
orig: يسبح لله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض له الملك وله الحمد وهو على كل شيء قدير

translation: He is the One who created you, and among you are some who disbelieve and among you are some who believe. And Allah is All-Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin of human diversity in faith, indicating that belief and disbelief are part of the human condition as created by Allah. It serves as a reminder that Allah is fully aware of all actions and intentions, encouraging individuals to be mindful of their deeds, as they are under constant divine observation.
orig: هو الذي خلقكم فمنكم كافر ومنكم مؤمن والله بما تعملون بصير

translation: He created the heavens and the earth with truth and formed you, and made your forms good, and to Him is the final return.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's role as the Creator of the universe and humanity. The phrase 'with truth' indicates that the creation is purposeful and not in vain. The mention of forming humans and making their forms good highlights the divine favor and beauty bestowed upon humanity. The final part, 'and to Him is the final return,' reminds believers of the ultimate accountability to Allah, reinforcing the themes of creation, divine purpose, and the afterlife.
orig: خلق السماوات والأرض بالحق وصوركم فأحسن صوركم وإليه المصير

translation: He knows what is in the heavens and the earth, and He knows what you conceal and what you reveal. And Allah is Knowing of that within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience of Allah, highlighting that His knowledge encompasses everything in the universe, both the seen and unseen. It also specifically addresses the human condition, indicating that Allah is aware of our innermost thoughts and feelings, whether we choose to hide them or express them openly. This serves as a reminder to believers of the importance of sincerity and integrity in their actions and intentions, knowing that nothing is hidden from Allah.
orig: يعلم ما في السماوات والأرض ويعلم ما تسرون وما تعلنون والله عليم بذات الصدور

translation: Has there not come to you the news of those who disbelieved before? So they tasted the evil consequence of their affair, and they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder and a warning to the believers about the fate of previous disbelieving nations. It underscores the concept of divine justice, illustrating that those who reject faith and persist in disbelief will ultimately face the consequences of their actions. The 'evil consequence' they tasted refers to the worldly calamities and defeats they suffered, while the 'painful punishment' alludes to the punishment in the Hereafter. This verse encourages reflection on historical examples as a means to understand the outcomes of disbelief and to steer clear of similar fates.
orig: ألم يأتكم نبأ الذين كفروا من قبل فذاقوا وبال أمرهم ولهم عذاب أليم

translation: That is because their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they said, 'Shall human beings guide us?' So they disbelieved and turned away. And Allah is self-sufficient; and Allah is praiseworthy and glorious.
interpretation: This verse highlights the reason for the disbelief of certain communities; despite receiving clear signs and guidance from their messengers, they rejected the message due to their arrogance and unwillingness to be guided by human messengers. Their rejection and subsequent turning away from the truth did not affect Allah's self-sufficiency, emphasizing that Allah remains independent and worthy of all praise regardless of human actions.
orig: ذلك بأنه كانت تأتيهم رسلهم بالبينات فقالوا أبشر يهدوننا فكفروا وتولوا واستغنى الله والله غني حميد

translation: Those who disbelieve claim that they will not be resurrected. Say, 'Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected; then you will be informed of what you did. And that, for Allah, is easy.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the disbelief in the resurrection among some people. It emphasizes the certainty of the resurrection and the Day of Judgment, where individuals will be held accountable for their actions. The phrase 'by my Lord' underscores the absolute truth of this promise, reinforcing the power and capability of Allah to resurrect and judge. The ease with which Allah can accomplish this further highlights His omnipotence and the inevitability of the event, serving as a reminder and warning to believers to be mindful of their deeds.
orig: زعم الذين كفروا أن لن يبعثوا قل بلى وربي لتبعثن ثم لتنبؤن بما عملتم وذلك على الله يسير

translation: So believe in Allah and His Messenger and the light which We have sent down. And Allah is well acquainted with what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of faith in Allah, His Messenger (Muhammad), and the Qur'an, referred to as 'the light'. It serves as a reminder that Allah is fully aware of all actions and deeds, encouraging believers to act righteously knowing that their actions are observed and known by Allah.
orig: فآمنوا بالله ورسوله والنور الذي أنزلنا والله بما تعملون خبير

translation: The Day He will assemble you for the Day of Assembly - that is the Day of Deprivation. And whoever believes in Allah and does righteousness - He will remove from him his misdeeds and admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever. That is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability of the Day of Judgment, referred to as the Day of Assembly and the Day of Deprivation, highlighting its significance and the consequences it holds for individuals. It underscores the importance of faith in Allah combined with righteous actions as the key to salvation. The promise of having one's sins forgiven and being granted entry into Paradise, described as gardens with flowing rivers and eternal residence, serves as a powerful incentive for believers to adhere to their faith and perform good deeds. The ultimate reward mentioned, referred to as the great attainment, signifies the highest level of success and fulfillment in the afterlife, attainable through a life dedicated to belief and virtuous conduct.
orig: يوم يجمعكم ليوم الجمع ذلك يوم التغابن ومن يؤمن بالله ويعمل صالحا يكفر عنه سيئاته ويدخله جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها أبدا ذلك الفوز العظيم

translation: And those who disbelieve and deny Our signs, those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever, and wretched is the destination.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequence of disbelief and rejection of divine signs, indicating that such actions lead to eternal punishment in Hell. It serves as a warning to those who consciously choose to deny the truth revealed by God, highlighting the severity of their ultimate fate and underscoring the importance of faith and acceptance of divine guidance.
orig: والذين كفروا وكذبوا بآياتنا أولئك أصحاب النار خالدين فيها وبئس المصير

translation: No calamity befalls except by the permission of Allah. And whoever believes in Allah, He guides his heart. And Allah is All-Knowing of everything.
interpretation: This verse reassures believers that no misfortune occurs without Allah's permission, emphasizing divine control over all events. It encourages faith in Allah, promising that such faith will lead to spiritual guidance and inner peace. The verse also underscores Allah's omniscience, reminding believers that He is aware of all things, which can provide comfort and trust in His wisdom and plan.
orig: ما أصاب من مصيبة إلا بإذن الله ومن يؤمن بالله يهد قلبه والله بكل شيء عليم

translation: And obey Allah and obey the Messenger; but if you turn away, then upon Our Messenger is only [the duty of] clear notification.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to Allah and His Messenger, Muhammad. It instructs believers to follow the divine commandments and the guidance provided by the Prophet. The phrase "but if you turn away" acknowledges the possibility of human disobedience or rejection of the message. However, it clarifies that the responsibility of the Prophet is solely to convey the message clearly and truthfully, without any obligation to enforce compliance. This underscores the concept of free will in Islam, where individuals are responsible for their choices after receiving the message.
orig: وأطيعوا الله وأطيعوا الرسول فإن توليتم فإنما على رسولنا البلاغ المبين

translation: Allah - there is no deity except Him, and upon Allah let the believers rely.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness of Allah, affirming that He is the only deity worthy of worship. It instructs believers to place their complete trust and reliance on Allah alone, highlighting the importance of tawakkul (trust in Allah) as a fundamental aspect of faith. This reliance on Allah should be unwavering, as it stems from the recognition of His omnipotence and omniscience.
orig: الله لا إله إلا هو وعلى الله فليتوكل المؤمنون

translation: O you who have believed, indeed among your wives and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them. But if you pardon and overlook and forgive - then indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse advises believers to be cautious of their close family members, specifically their wives and children, as they might lead them astray from the path of righteousness due to their influence or demands. However, the verse encourages forgiveness and overlooking their faults, promising that Allah, in turn, will be forgiving and merciful to those who exhibit such qualities. It highlights the importance of maintaining a balance between familial responsibilities and one's faith, urging believers to prioritize their spiritual well-being while still showing compassion and forgiveness towards their family.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إن من أزواجكم وأولادكم عدوا لكم فاحذروهم وإن تعفوا وتصفحوا وتغفروا فإن الله غفور رحيم

translation: Your wealth and your children are but a trial, and Allah has with Him a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that worldly possessions and family, while blessings, can also serve as tests of one's faith and devotion to Allah. They can distract from spiritual growth and the remembrance of Allah. The true and ultimate reward lies with Allah, encouraging believers to focus on earning His pleasure and the hereafter rather than becoming overly attached to material and familial ties.
orig: إنما أموالكم وأولادكم فتنة والله عنده أجر عظيم

translation: So fear Allah as much as you are able and listen and obey and spend in charity; that is best for yourselves. And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul - it is those who will be the successful ones.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fearing Allah to the best of one's ability, which involves being conscious of His presence and commandments in all actions. It encourages obedience to Allah's directives and the Prophet's teachings, as well as engaging in charitable acts, which are described as beneficial for one's own spiritual growth and well-being. The verse also highlights the virtue of overcoming personal greed and selfishness, indicating that those who can master their own stinginess are the ones who will achieve true success in the hereafter.
orig: فاتقوا الله ما استطعتم واسمعوا وأطيعوا وأنفقوا خيرا لأنفسكم ومن يوق شح نفسه فأولئك هم المفلحون

translation: If you loan Allah a goodly loan, He will multiply it for you and forgive you. And Allah is Most Appreciative and Forbearing.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to spend in the way of Allah, which includes acts of charity and good deeds. The 'goodly loan' refers to giving without expecting anything in return, trusting that Allah will reward and multiply the benefits of such actions in this life and the hereafter. The promise of multiplication and forgiveness highlights the immense reward and mercy that follows such acts. Allah's attributes of being 'Most Appreciative' (Shakur) and 'Forbearing' (Halim) emphasize His gratitude towards those who give and His patience in not hastening punishment, encouraging believers to be generous and patient in their giving.
orig: إن تقرضوا الله قرضا حسنا يضاعفه لكم ويغفر لكم والله شكور حليم

translation: Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's omniscience, encompassing both the hidden and the manifest aspects of existence. It highlights His supreme power and wisdom, indicating that He is fully aware of all things, whether they are apparent to humans or not. This attribute of Allah serves as a reminder of His all-encompassing knowledge and authority, encouraging believers to trust in His divine plan and wisdom.
orig: عالم الغيب والشهادة العزيز الحكيم

translation: O Prophet, when you [Muslims] divorce women, divorce them for [the commencement of] their waiting period and keep count of the waiting period, and fear Allah, your Lord. Do not turn them out of their [husbands'] houses, nor should they leave [during that period] unless they are committing a clear immorality. And those are the limits [set by] Allah. And whoever transgresses the limits of Allah has certainly wronged himself. You know not; perhaps Allah will bring about after that a [different] matter.
interpretation: This verse addresses the process of divorce and emphasizes the importance of adhering to the prescribed waiting period (iddah) before the divorce is finalized. It instructs that women should not be expelled from their homes during this period, nor should they leave unless they engage in evident immoral behavior. The verse underscores the sanctity of the boundaries set by Allah, warning that transgressing these limits is a form of self-injury. It also hints at the possibility of reconciliation or a change in circumstances, suggesting that the outcome of the situation might differ from what is initially apparent, encouraging patience and adherence to divine guidance.
orig: يا أيها النبي إذا طلقتم النساء فطلقوهن لعدتهن وأحصوا العدة واتقوا الله ربكم لا تخرجوهن من بيوتهن ولا يخرجن إلا أن يأتين بفاحشة مبينة وتلك حدود الله ومن يتعد حدود الله فقد ظلم نفسه لا تدري لعل الله يحدث بعد ذلك أمرا

translation: So when they have reached their term, either retain them according to acceptable terms or part with them according to acceptable terms. And bring to witness two just men from among you and establish the testimony for Allah. That is instructed to whoever should believe in Allah and the Last Day. And whoever fears Allah - He will make for him a way out.
interpretation: This verse addresses the proper conduct in the context of marriage and divorce, emphasizing justice and righteousness. It instructs that when the waiting period (iddah) of women ends, men should either retain their wives with kindness or let them go with kindness, without causing harm or injustice. The requirement to have two just witnesses underscores the importance of transparency and fairness in these proceedings. The verse connects these actions to faith in Allah and the Last Day, suggesting that adherence to these principles is a reflection of one's belief and piety. It also offers a spiritual reassurance that those who fear Allah and act justly will find solutions and relief from their difficulties, as Allah will provide a way out for them.
orig: فإذا بلغن أجلهن فأمسكوهن بمعروف أو فارقوهن بمعروف وأشهدوا ذوي عدل منكم وأقيموا الشهادة لله ذلكم يوعظ به من كان يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر ومن يتق الله يجعل له مخرجا

translation: And He provides for him from where he does not expect. And whoever relies upon Allah - then He is sufficient for him. Indeed, Allah will accomplish His purpose. Allah has already set for everything a [decreed] extent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of trust in Allah (tawakkul). It reassures believers that Allah will provide for them in ways they might not anticipate, highlighting the boundless nature of divine providence. The verse encourages reliance on Allah alone, promising that such trust will be rewarded as Allah is sufficient for anyone who depends on Him. Additionally, it underscores the concept of divine decree (qadar), affirming that Allah has predetermined measures for all things, which reflects His complete control and wisdom over creation.
orig: ويرزقه من حيث لا يحتسب ومن يتوكل على الله فهو حسبه إن الله بالغ أمره قد جعل الله لكل شيء قدرا

translation: And those who have despaired of menstruation among your women, if you doubt, then their waiting period is three months, and those who have not menstruated and those who are pregnant, their term is until they deliver their burdens. And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out of his difficulties.
interpretation: This verse outlines the waiting periods (iddah) for divorce in different situations for women. It specifies that women who have reached menopause should observe a waiting period of three months if there is any doubt about their status. For women who have not yet menstruated (young girls) and pregnant women, their waiting period extends until they reach puberty or deliver their child, respectively. The verse concludes with a reassurance that those who are mindful of Allah and adhere to His commandments will find ease in their affairs, suggesting that following these guidelines will lead to spiritual and practical facilitation in life's challenges.
orig: واللائي يئسن من المحيض من نسائكم إن ارتبتم فعدتهن ثلاثة أشهر واللائي لم يحضن وأولات الأحمال أجلهن أن يضعن حملهن ومن يتق الله يجعل له من أمره يسرا

translation: That is the commandment of Allah, which He has revealed to you; and whoever fears Allah - He will remove his misdeeds from him and will increase his reward greatly.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to the commandments of Allah as revealed in the Qur'an. It reassures believers that by maintaining a consciousness of Allah (taqwa), not only will their sins be forgiven, but their rewards in the hereafter will also be significantly enhanced. It serves as an encouragement for Muslims to live righteously, with the promise of divine forgiveness and amplified spiritual rewards.
orig: ذلك أمر الله أنزله إليكم ومن يتق الله يكفر عنه سيئاته ويعظم له أجرا

translation: House them where you dwell, according to your means, and do not harm them in order to make life difficult for them. If they are pregnant, spend on them until they deliver their children. And if they nurse your infants, give them their due payment and consult together in a fair manner. But if you make things difficult for each other, then another woman may nurse the child.
interpretation: This verse addresses the rights and responsibilities towards divorced women, particularly emphasizing fairness and support during and after pregnancy. It instructs men to provide adequate housing for their divorced wives, in line with their own living standards, and not to cause them hardship. The verse mandates financial support during pregnancy and after childbirth, and stipulates payment for nursing if the mother chooses to breastfeed. It encourages mutual consultation and agreement on these matters in a just manner. If agreement cannot be reached, it allows for another woman to nurse the child, ensuring the child's welfare is prioritized. This reflects Islam's emphasis on compassion, justice, and the protection of vulnerable groups, particularly women and children during times of familial change.
orig: أسكنوهن من حيث سكنتم من وجدكم ولا تضاروهن لتضيقوا عليهن وإن كن أولات حمل فأنفقوا عليهن حتى يضعن حملهن فإن أرضعن لكم فآتوهن أجورهن وأتمروا بينكم بمعروف وإن تعاسرتم فسترضع له أخرى

translation: Let the man of means spend according to his means, and the man whose resources are restricted, let him spend according to what Allah has given him. Allah puts no burden on any person beyond what He has given him. After hardship, Allah will bring ease.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of spending in accordance with one's financial capacity, reflecting a core Islamic value of moderation and responsibility. It encourages those who are wealthy to be generous, while reassuring those with limited means that they are only expected to contribute from what they can afford, highlighting the fairness and mercy of Allah's commandments. The promise of ease following hardship serves as a reminder of divine justice and hope, encouraging perseverance and faith in Allah's plan.
orig: لينفق ذو سعة من سعته ومن قدر عليه رزقه فلينفق مما آتاه الله لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا ما آتاها سيجعل الله بعد عسر يسرا

translation: And how many a town rebelled against the command of its Lord and His messengers, so We called it to a severe account and punished it with a terrible punishment.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder and warning to communities about the consequences of rejecting the guidance of Allah and His messengers. It underscores the divine justice that holds societies accountable for their actions. The severe accounting and terrible punishment mentioned illustrate the gravity of turning away from divine commandments, emphasizing that such rebellion leads to a downfall that serves as a lesson for others.
orig: وكأين من قرية عتت عن أمر ربها ورسله فحاسبناها حسابا شديدا وعذبناها عذابا نكرا

translation: So she tasted the consequence of her affair, and the outcome of her affair was loss.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the consequences of disbelief and disobedience to God. It refers to the story of the wife of Pharaoh, who, despite her high status, faced a dire end due to her rejection of faith. The phrase "tasted the consequence of her affair" signifies experiencing the negative outcomes of one's actions, while "the outcome of her affair was loss" underscores the ultimate failure and spiritual ruin that results from turning away from God's guidance.
orig: فذاقت وبال أمرها وكان عاقبة أمرها خسرا

translation: Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment, so fear Allah, O you who possess understanding, you who have believed. Allah has sent down to you a reminder.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning and a call to mindfulness. It emphasizes that those who engage in wrongdoing will face a severe punishment from Allah. The address to 'those who possess understanding' and 'those who have believed' highlights the responsibility of the believers to heed this warning and act upon it. The 'reminder' mentioned refers to the Qur'an itself, which serves as guidance and a means to avoid the mentioned punishment. The verse urges believers to fear Allah, not out of mere fear, but as a motivation to adhere to His guidance and live righteously.
orig: أعد الله لهم عذابا شديدا فاتقوا الله يا أولي الألباب الذين آمنوا قد أنزل الله إليكم ذكرا

translation: A messenger who recites to you the clear verses of Allah, so that he may bring out those who believe and do righteous deeds from darknesses into light. And whoever believes in Allah and does righteous deeds, He will admit him into gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever. Allah has indeed provided for him a goodly provision.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of the Prophet Muhammad as a messenger who conveys the clear and unambiguous messages of Allah. The purpose of his message is to guide believers from a state of ignorance and spiritual darkness to enlightenment and righteousness. The verse promises that those who embrace faith and perform good deeds will be rewarded with eternal life in Paradise, described as gardens with flowing rivers, symbolizing abundance and eternal bliss. This promise underscores Allah's generosity and the ultimate reward for a life of faith and moral integrity.
orig: رسولا يتلو عليكم آيات الله مبينات ليخرج الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات من الظلمات إلى النور ومن يؤمن بالله ويعمل صالحا يدخله جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها أبدا قد أحسن الله له رزقا

translation: Allah is He Who created seven heavens and of the earth the like thereof. The command descends between them, that you may know that Allah is Able to do all things, and that Allah indeed encompasses all things in knowledge.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence and omniscience of Allah. By mentioning the creation of seven heavens and an equal number of earths, it highlights the vastness and complexity of Allah's creation. The descent of the command between these layers signifies the orderly and hierarchical nature of the universe, governed by Allah's will. The purpose of this revelation is to affirm the believers' understanding of Allah's absolute power over all things and His complete knowledge that encompasses everything, reinforcing the concept of Tawhid (the oneness of Allah) and the need for humans to recognize and submit to His authority.
orig: الله الذي خلق سبع سماوات ومن الأرض مثلهن يتنزل الأمر بينهن لتعلموا أن الله على كل شيء قدير وأن الله قد أحاط بكل شيء علما

translation: O Prophet, why do you prohibit [yourself] what Allah has made lawful for you, seeking the approval of your wives? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad, reminding him that he should not impose additional restrictions on himself beyond what Allah has legislated, even if his intention is to please his wives. It emphasizes that Allah's laws are sufficient and that the Prophet should adhere to them, trusting in Allah's forgiveness and mercy. The verse highlights the balance between personal desires and divine commandments, urging adherence to the latter.
orig: يا أيها النبي لم تحرم ما أحل الله لك تبتغي مرضات أزواجك والله غفور رحيم

translation: Allah has already ordained for you the absolution of your oaths. And Allah is your Protector, and He is the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah has provided a way for believers to be relieved from the obligations of their oaths under certain conditions, reflecting His mercy and understanding of human circumstances. It reassures believers that Allah is their protector and that His knowledge and wisdom encompass all situations, guiding them towards what is best for them.
orig: قد فرض الله لكم تحلة أيمانكم والله مولاكم وهو العليم الحكيم

translation: And when the Prophet confided a matter to one of his wives, then she disclosed it, and Allah made it known to him, he acquainted her with some of it and avoided some. So when he informed her about it, she said, 'Who told you this?' He said, 'I was informed by the All-Knowing, the All-Aware.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of trust and confidentiality within relationships, particularly in the context of the Prophet Muhammad's household. It serves as a reminder that Allah is fully aware of all actions and secrets, emphasizing divine omniscience and the consequences of betraying trust. The incident underscores the need for integrity and the potential divine revelation of hidden matters, urging believers to be mindful of their actions and words.
orig: وإذ أسر النبي إلى بعض أزواجه حديثا فلما نبأت به وأظهره الله عليه عرف بعضه وأعرض عن بعض فلما نبأها به قالت من أنبأك هذا قال نبأني العليم الخبير

translation: If you two [wives of the Prophet] repent to Allah, [it is best], for your hearts have deviated. But if you conspire against him, then indeed Allah is his protector, and Gabriel and the righteous among the believers and the angels, moreover, are [his] assistants.
interpretation: This verse addresses the wives of the Prophet Muhammad, specifically hinting at Aisha and Hafsa, urging them to repent for their deviation from the right path. It emphasizes the gravity of their actions by stating that their hearts have deviated, suggesting a spiritual misalignment. The verse then reassures the Prophet of the divine and communal support he has, listing Allah, Gabriel, the righteous believers, and the angels as his protectors and assistants. This serves to remind the wives of the Prophet's esteemed position and the consequences of opposing him, while also providing comfort and strength to the Prophet himself amidst personal challenges.
orig: إن تتوبا إلى الله فقد صغت قلوبكما وإن تظاهرا عليه فإن الله هو مولاه وجبريل وصالح المؤمنين والملائكة بعد ذلك ظهير

translation: Perhaps his Lord, if he divorces you, will replace you with wives better than you - submitting, believing, devoutly obedient, repentant, worshipping, and given to fasting - both previously married and virgins.
interpretation: This verse suggests that if the Prophet Muhammad were to divorce his wives, Allah might replace them with women who possess superior qualities in faith and devotion. It emphasizes the importance of spiritual and moral virtues in a marital relationship, highlighting characteristics such as submission to God, belief, obedience, repentance, worship, and fasting. The mention of both widows and virgins indicates that these qualities are valued regardless of marital status, underscoring the universality of these virtues in the eyes of Allah.
orig: عسى ربه إن طلقكن أن يبدله أزواجا خيرا منكن مسلمات مؤمنات قانتات تائبات عابدات سائحات ثيبات وأبكارا

translation: O you who have believed, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is people and stones, over which are [appointed] angels, harsh and severe; they do not disobey Allah in what He commands them but do what they are commanded.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the responsibility of believers to safeguard themselves and their families from the punishment of Hellfire. It highlights the severity of Hell by describing its fuel and the angels appointed over it, who are described as harsh and severe, yet obedient to Allah's commands. The mention of the angels' obedience serves as a reminder of the inevitability of divine justice and the importance of adhering to Allah's commands to avoid such a fate.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا قوا أنفسكم وأهليكم نارا وقودها الناس والحجارة عليها ملائكة غلاظ شداد لا يعصون الله ما أمرهم ويفعلون ما يؤمرون

translation: O you who have disbelieved, make no excuses today. You will only be recompensed for what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse addresses those who have rejected faith, informing them that on the Day of Judgment, their excuses will be futile. It emphasizes the principle of accountability, where individuals will be rewarded or punished solely based on their actions in life, without any opportunity for justification or excuses. This underscores the importance of living a righteous life, as one's deeds are the sole criteria for judgment.
orig: يا أيها الذين كفروا لا تعتذروا اليوم إنما تجزون ما كنتم تعملون

translation: O you who have believed, repent to Allah with sincere repentance. Perhaps your Lord will remove from you your misdeeds and admit you into gardens beneath which rivers flow [on] the Day when Allah will not disgrace the Prophet and those who believed with him. Their light will proceed before them and on their right; they will say, 'Our Lord, perfect for us our light and forgive us. Indeed, You are over all things competent.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sincere repentance (tawbah nasuh) to Allah, highlighting that such repentance can lead to the forgiveness of sins and entry into Paradise. The imagery of light preceding the believers symbolizes guidance and divine favor, reflecting their spiritual purity and closeness to Allah. The plea for the perfection of their light and forgiveness underscores the believers' continuous need for divine mercy and guidance, acknowledging Allah's omnipotence and ability to grant these requests.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا توبوا إلى الله توبة نصوحا عسى ربكم أن يكفر عنكم سيئاتكم ويدخلكم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار يوم لا يخزي الله النبي والذين آمنوا معه نورهم يسعى بين أيديهم وبأيمانهم يقولون ربنا أتمم لنا نورنا واغفر لنا إنك على كل شيء قدير

translation: O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites and be harsh with them. Their abode is Hell, and wretched is the destination.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad to exert effort and be firm in dealing with those who reject faith and those who are hypocritical in their faith. It emphasizes the seriousness of their actions by stating that their ultimate destination will be Hell, highlighting the grave consequences of disbelief and hypocrisy. This serves as a reminder of the importance of sincerity in faith and the need for the Prophet to guide and correct those who stray from the path of righteousness.
orig: يا أيها النبي جاهد الكفار والمنافقين واغلظ عليهم ومأواهم جهنم وبئس المصير

translation: Allah presents an example for those who disbelieve: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot. They were under two of Our righteous servants but betrayed them; so they [the wives] availed them [the husbands] not from Allah at all, and it was said [to them], 'Enter the Fire with those who enter.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates that lineage or association with righteous individuals does not guarantee salvation or divine favor. The wives of Noah and Lot, despite being married to prophets, were punished for their disbelief and betrayal. It underscores the principle that each person is accountable for their own faith and actions, regardless of their proximity to virtuous people. The message is clear: one's personal righteousness and loyalty to faith are what ultimately matter in the eyes of Allah.
orig: ضرب الله مثلا للذين كفروا امرأت نوح وامرأت لوط كانتا تحت عبدين من عبادنا صالحين فخانتاهما فلم يغنيا عنهما من الله شيئا وقيل ادخلا النار مع الداخلين

translation: And Allah presents an example for those who believed: the wife of Pharaoh when she said, 'My Lord, build for me a house near You in Paradise and save me from Pharaoh and his deeds and save me from the wrongdoing people.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the example of Asiya, the wife of Pharaoh, as a model of faith and righteousness for believers. Despite being married to one of the most oppressive rulers in history, she maintained her faith in Allah and sought His protection and closeness. Her prayer reflects a deep spiritual aspiration for a place in Paradise and a desire to be saved from the tyranny and evil around her. This teaches believers the importance of steadfastness in faith, even in the most challenging circumstances, and the power of sincere supplication to Allah.
orig: وضرب الله مثلا للذين آمنوا امرأت فرعون إذ قالت رب ابن لي عندك بيتا في الجنة ونجني من فرعون وعمله ونجني من القوم الظالمين

translation: And [mention] Maryam, the daughter of 'Imran, who guarded her chastity, so We blew into [her garment] through Our angel, and she believed in the words of her Lord and His scriptures, and she was of the devoutly obedient.
interpretation: This verse highlights the exemplary character of Maryam (Mary), emphasizing her purity and devotion to God. Her guarding of her chastity symbolizes her commitment to spiritual and moral integrity. The divine intervention through the blowing of the spirit signifies the miraculous nature of her conception of Jesus, underscoring her unique role in divine plan. Her belief in the words and scriptures of God reflects her deep faith and submission, positioning her as a model of obedience and piety for believers.
orig: ومريم ابنت عمران التي أحصنت فرجها فنفخنا فيه من روحنا وصدقت بكلمات ربها وكتبه وكانت من القانتين

translation: Blessed is He in Whose hand is the dominion, and He is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and omnipotence of Allah. It highlights that all power and authority belong to Him alone, and He has complete control and ability over everything in existence. The term 'Blessed' signifies the perfection and exalted nature of Allah, indicating that His dominion is a source of goodness and blessing for all creation. This verse serves as a reminder of Allah's supreme power and the believer's need to trust in His wisdom and capability in all matters.
orig: تبارك الذي بيده الملك وهو على كل شيء قدير

translation: Who created death and life to test you [as to] which of you is best in deed - and He is the Exalted in Might, the Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the purpose of life and death is a test from Allah to determine who among us performs the best deeds. It highlights the divine attributes of Allah as the Almighty and the Forgiving, indicating that while He tests us, He also possesses the power to forgive our shortcomings. This underscores the importance of striving for excellence in our actions, knowing that our efforts are evaluated by a merciful and powerful Creator.
orig: الذي خلق الموت والحياة ليبلوكم أيكم أحسن عملا وهو العزيز الغفور

translation: He Who created the seven heavens in layers. You will not see in the creation of the Most Merciful any inconsistency. So return [your] vision [to the sky]; do you see any flaw?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the perfection and harmony in the creation of the universe by Allah. The mention of the seven heavens in layers signifies the structured and orderly nature of creation. The challenge to look at the sky and find any flaw underscores the idea that the universe is a testament to Allah's flawless craftsmanship and omnipotence. It invites believers to reflect on the consistency and perfection in creation, reinforcing faith in the Creator's wisdom and power.
orig: الذي خلق سبع سماوات طباقا ما ترى في خلق الرحمن من تفاوت فارجع البصر هل ترى من فطور

translation: Then look again and yet again, your sight will return to you humbled and exhausted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the overwhelming nature of the signs of Allah's creation. When one observes the universe and its intricate details repeatedly, the realization of its vastness and complexity can be so profound that it humbles the observer, leaving them in a state of awe and fatigue, unable to fully comprehend the magnificence of what they have seen.
orig: ثم ارجع البصر كرتين ينقلب إليك البصر خاسئا وهو حسير

translation: And We have certainly beautified the nearest heaven with lamps and made them as missiles for the devils, and We have prepared for them the punishment of the Blaze.
interpretation: This verse highlights the dual purpose of the celestial bodies in the sky. Not only do they serve to beautify the lower heaven, enhancing its aesthetic appeal, but they also function as a means of protection against the devils. The 'lamps' or stars are used metaphorically as missiles to ward off the evil influences of the devils, symbolizing the divine protection that extends to the physical realm. Additionally, the verse underscores the inevitability of divine justice, as it mentions the prepared punishment of the Blaze for the devils, emphasizing the consequences of their actions and the ultimate accountability before God.
orig: ولقد زينا السماء الدنيا بمصابيح وجعلناها رجوما للشياطين وأعتدنا لهم عذاب السعير

translation: And for those who disbelieve in their Lord is the punishment of Hell, and wretched is the destination.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe consequence of disbelief in Allah, highlighting that the ultimate fate for those who reject their Lord is the torment of Hell. It serves as a stark warning about the seriousness of denying the existence or authority of Allah, underscoring the eternal nature of the punishment and the undesirable nature of this outcome.
orig: وللذين كفروا بربهم عذاب جهنم وبئس المصير

translation: When they are cast therein, they will hear its roaring as it boils.
interpretation: This verse describes the moment when the disbelievers are thrown into Hell. The sound of Hell's roaring and boiling signifies the intense and terrifying nature of the punishment awaiting them. It serves as a vivid reminder of the consequences of disbelief and sin, urging believers to heed the warnings and strive for righteousness to avoid such a fate.
orig: إذا ألقوا فيها سمعوا لها شهيقا وهي تفور

translation: It almost bursts with rage. Every time a group is thrown into it, its keepers will ask them, 'Did there not come to you a warner?'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the intense anger and frustration of Hell, personified as if it is about to explode due to its fury. The imagery serves to emphasize the severity of the punishment awaiting those who are cast into it. The question posed by the keepers of Hell to the new arrivals underscores the theme of accountability and the divine justice system, highlighting that every individual was given a chance to heed the warnings of the prophets and messengers sent by God. It reflects the notion that no one enters Hell without having been forewarned, thereby affirming the fairness of God's judgment.
orig: تكاد تميز من الغيظ كلما ألقي فيها فوج سألهم خزنتها ألم يأتكم نذير

translation: They said, 'Yes, a warner has come to us, but we denied him and said, 'Allah has not sent down anything. You are only in great error.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the response of the disbelievers when confronted about the message of the Prophet. It highlights their acknowledgment of receiving the warning but their subsequent rejection of it, attributing their disbelief to a denial of divine revelation. This indicates a deeper issue of arrogance and stubbornness, as they not only reject the messenger but also assert that the concept of divine revelation itself is false, thereby accusing the believers of being misguided. This underscores the psychological and spiritual barriers that prevent acceptance of truth, even when it is clearly presented.
orig: قالوا بلى قد جاءنا نذير فكذبنا وقلنا ما نزل الله من شيء إن أنتم إلا في ضلال كبير

translation: And they will say, 'If we had listened or reasoned, we would not be among the companions of the Blaze.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the regret of those in Hell who acknowledge that their current suffering could have been avoided had they paid attention to the guidance and used their intellect to understand and follow the truth. It underscores the importance of actively listening to divine messages and using reason to discern right from wrong, highlighting the consequences of neglecting these faculties.
orig: وقالوا لو كنا نسمع أو نعقل ما كنا في أصحاب السعير

translation: So they will confess their sin, so away with the companions of the Blaze!
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of sinners acknowledging their wrongdoings in the afterlife. It emphasizes the concept of accountability before God, where no one can deny their sins. The phrase 'so away with the companions of the Blaze' serves as a stern warning and a declaration of the ultimate fate of those who persist in sin, highlighting the severe consequences of disbelief and moral transgression.
orig: فاعترفوا بذنبهم فسحقا لأصحاب السعير

translation: Indeed, those who fear their Lord unseen will have forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of having a deep, intrinsic fear and reverence for Allah, even when one is not in the public eye or under immediate scrutiny. It suggests that such sincere and private devotion to Allah, driven by an awareness of His omnipresence, leads to divine forgiveness and a significant reward in the hereafter. The verse encourages believers to maintain a constant state of mindfulness and piety, regardless of external circumstances.
orig: إن الذين يخشون ربهم بالغيب لهم مغفرة وأجر كبير

translation: And conceal your speech or publicize it; indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omniscience of Allah, indicating that He is fully aware of all human thoughts and intentions, whether they are kept secret or expressed openly. It serves as a reminder to believers to be mindful of their inner thoughts and feelings, as nothing is hidden from Allah.
orig: وأسروا قولكم أو اجهروا به إنه عليم بذات الصدور

translation: Does He not know, He Who created? And He is the Kind, the All-Aware.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's omniscience and His intimate knowledge of His creation. It rhetorically questions whether the Creator, who is described as Al-Lateef (the Kind, the Subtle) and Al-Khabeer (the All-Aware), would not know everything about what He has created. The attributes highlight Allah's kindness and subtlety in His dealings with creation, as well as His complete awareness of all things, underscoring the absurdity of doubting His knowledge.
orig: ألا يعلم من خلق وهو اللطيف الخبير

translation: He is the One Who has made the earth subservient to you, so walk in its paths and eat of His provision, and to Him is the resurrection.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the blessings and provisions that Allah has bestowed upon humanity by making the earth manageable and easy to traverse. The command to 'walk in its paths' suggests that humans should explore and utilize the earth's resources responsibly. The mention of eating from His provision highlights the dependency of all sustenance on Allah, reminding believers to be grateful. The phrase 'and to Him is the resurrection' serves as a reminder of the ultimate return to Allah, underscoring the temporary nature of worldly life and the importance of preparing for the hereafter.
orig: هو الذي جعل لكم الأرض ذلولا فامشوا في مناكبها وكلوا من رزقه وإليه النشور

translation: Do you feel secure that He who is in heaven will not cause the earth to swallow you up when it quakes?
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of God's omnipotence and the unpredictability of His actions. It encourages believers to remain humble and conscious of their dependence on God's mercy, as He has the power to cause natural disasters like earthquakes at any moment, which could engulf them. It underscores the need for constant awareness and gratitude towards God.
orig: أأمنتم من في السماء أن يخسف بكم الأرض فإذا هي تمور

translation: Or do you feel secure that He who is in the heaven will not send against you a storm of stones? Then you would know how [severe] was My warning.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of God's omnipotence and the potential for divine retribution. It challenges the disbelief of those who might feel secure from God's power, suggesting that their security is an illusion. The mention of a "storm of stones" symbolizes a severe punishment that could be unleashed from the heavens, emphasizing the sudden and overwhelming nature of divine intervention. The verse underscores the importance of heeding God's warnings, as ignoring them could lead to dire consequences, thus urging believers to remain vigilant and faithful.
orig: أم أمنتم من في السماء أن يرسل عليكم حاصبا فستعلمون كيف نذير

translation: And indeed, those before them denied, so how was My rejection?
interpretation: This verse reflects on the disbelief of previous nations and emphasizes the severe consequences they faced as a result of rejecting the divine message. It serves as a warning to the current audience of the Qur'an that denial of God's signs leads to inevitable divine retribution, prompting reflection on the historical pattern of divine justice.
orig: ولقد كذب الذين من قبلهم فكيف كان نكير

translation: Do they not see the birds above them, spreading their wings and folding them in? None holds them up except the Most Merciful. Indeed, He is, of all things, Seeing.
interpretation: This verse invites reflection on the natural world as a sign of God's omnipotence and care. The birds, effortlessly gliding and soaring, are upheld not by their own power but by the mercy of Allah. This illustrates the dependency of all creation on God and His all-encompassing knowledge and oversight of every detail in the universe.
orig: أولم يروا إلى الطير فوقهم صافات ويقبضن ما يمسكهن إلا الرحمن إنه بكل شيء بصير

translation: Is this the one who is an army for you to help you against the Most Merciful? The disbelievers are only in delusion.
interpretation: This verse questions the reliance of the disbelievers on anything other than Allah for protection and support. It highlights their delusion in thinking that their false gods or allies can provide them with any real assistance or defense against the power of the Most Merciful. The verse underscores the futility and error of their beliefs, emphasizing that true help and protection come only from Allah.
orig: أمن هذا الذي هو جند لكم ينصركم من دون الرحمن إن الكافرون إلا في غرور

translation: Is He [not best] who provides for you if He withholds His provision? But they have persisted in insolence and aversion.
interpretation: This verse challenges the disbelief of those who doubt God's providence. It questions whether they truly believe in the One who sustains them, suggesting that if God were to withhold His provision, they would be helpless. Yet, despite this clear dependency on God, people often respond with arrogance and rejection of His signs, continuing in their stubbornness and aversion to the truth.
orig: أمن هذا الذي يرزقكم إن أمسك رزقه بل لجوا في عتو ونفور

translation: Is he who walks with his face downcast better guided, or he who walks upright on a straight path?
interpretation: This verse poses a rhetorical question to illustrate the difference between those who are misguided and those who are rightly guided. The one walking with his face downcast symbolizes a person who is lost, confused, or blindly following without understanding, while the one walking upright on a straight path represents someone who is clear-sighted, purposeful, and following the correct guidance of Islam. The verse emphasizes the superiority and clarity of the straight path, which is the path of righteousness and submission to God's will.
orig: أفمن يمشي مكبا على وجهه أهدى أمن يمشي سويا على صراط مستقيم

translation: Say, 'It is He who has created you and made for you hearing, sight, and hearts; little thanks you give.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gratitude humans should have towards Allah for the blessings of creation and the faculties of hearing, sight, and understanding. The use of 'little thanks you give' highlights a common human failing to recognize and appreciate these divine gifts, urging believers to increase their gratitude and mindfulness of Allah's benevolence.
orig: قل هو الذي أنشأكم وجعل لكم السمع والأبصار والأفئدة قليلا ما تشكرون

translation: Say, 'It is He who has scattered you throughout the earth, and to Him you will be gathered.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence of Allah, highlighting His role as the creator who has dispersed humanity across the earth. It also serves as a reminder of the ultimate return to Allah, underscoring the belief in the Day of Judgment where all people will be gathered before Him for accountability.
orig: قل هو الذي ذرأكم في الأرض وإليه تحشرون

translation: And they say, 'When is this promise, if you are truthful?'
interpretation: This verse reflects the skepticism and impatience of those who doubt the prophecies and promises mentioned in the Qur'an. It highlights their challenge to believers, questioning the timing of the promised events, thereby testing the faith and patience of the faithful.
orig: ويقولون متى هذا الوعد إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Say, "Indeed, the knowledge is with Allah, and I am only a clear warner."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the limitation of human knowledge compared to the omniscience of Allah. It instructs the Prophet Muhammad to convey that ultimate knowledge rests solely with Allah, while his role is to clearly warn people of the consequences of their actions, without claiming to possess complete knowledge himself. This highlights the importance of humility and the recognition of divine authority in matters of knowledge and guidance.
orig: قل إنما العلم عند الله وإنما أنا نذير مبين

translation: So when they saw it approaching, the faces of those who disbelieved turned gloomy, and it was said, 'This is what you were calling for.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the moment of realization and despair among the disbelievers when they see the promised event or punishment drawing near. Their gloomy faces reflect their inner fear and regret as they recognize that the very thing they had mocked or denied is now upon them. The statement 'This is what you were calling for' serves as a poignant reminder of their previous disbelief and denial, now confronted with the undeniable truth of the prophecy or divine promise.
orig: فلما رأوه زلفة سيئت وجوه الذين كفروا وقيل هذا الذي كنتم به تدعون

translation: Say, "Have you considered: if Allah should destroy me and those with me or have mercy upon us, who can protect the disbelievers from a painful punishment?"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the powerlessness of disbelievers against the divine will of Allah. It challenges them to consider their fate if Allah chooses to either punish or show mercy to the Prophet Muhammad and his followers. The rhetorical question underscores that no one can save the disbelievers from the painful punishment that awaits them if they continue to reject faith, highlighting the ultimate authority and justice of Allah.
orig: قل أرأيتم إن أهلكني الله ومن معي أو رحمنا فمن يجير الكافرين من عذاب أليم

translation: Say, 'He is the Most Merciful; we have believed in Him, and upon Him we have relied. So you will [come to] know who is in clear error.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the believers' affirmation of faith in Allah, described here as the Most Merciful, and their complete trust in Him. It challenges those who doubt or oppose this faith, promising that the truth will become evident, revealing who is truly misguided. The verse serves as a declaration of confidence in the ultimate vindication of the believers' stance through divine justice.
orig: قل هو الرحمن آمنا به وعليه توكلنا فستعلمون من هو في ضلال مبين

translation: Say, "Have you considered: if your water was to become sunken [into the earth], then who could bring you flowing water?"
interpretation: This verse challenges the reader to reflect on their dependence on God for sustenance. It poses a hypothetical scenario where all available water sinks into the earth, emphasizing that only God can provide the essential resource of water. The verse encourages believers to recognize God's omnipotence and to trust in His provision, highlighting the vulnerability of human existence without divine support.
orig: قل أرأيتم إن أصبح ماؤكم غورا فمن يأتيكم بماء معين

translation: Nun. By the pen and what they write,
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of writing and knowledge, symbolized by the pen, which is a tool for recording and spreading divine revelation. The oath taken by the pen and the act of writing underscores the significance of literacy and the written word in preserving and conveying the message of Islam.
orig: ن والقلم وما يسطرون

translation: You are not, by the grace of your Lord, a madman.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reassurance to Prophet Muhammad from Allah, emphasizing that the divine revelations he receives are not a sign of madness but are a result of Allah's grace and favor. It underscores the authenticity and divine origin of the Qur'an, countering the accusations of his detractors who labeled him as insane due to his prophetic claims.
orig: ما أنت بنعمة ربك بمجنون

translation: And indeed, for you is a reward without end.
interpretation: This verse assures the Prophet Muhammad that he will receive a continuous and unending reward from Allah for his efforts and perseverance in conveying the message of Islam. It emphasizes the eternal nature of the reward, highlighting the divine appreciation and support for his mission.
orig: وإن لك لأجرا غير ممنون

translation: And indeed, you are of a great moral character.
interpretation: This verse highlights the exemplary moral character of Prophet Muhammad, emphasizing his integrity, patience, and compassion as a model for all believers to emulate in their personal conduct.
orig: وإنك لعلى خلق عظيم

translation: So you will see and they will see
interpretation: This verse suggests that on the Day of Judgment, the truth will be revealed to all. Both the believers and the disbelievers will witness the consequences of their actions and beliefs, leading to a clear understanding and realization of the reality of the hereafter.
orig: فستبصر ويبصرون

translation: Which of you is afflicted with madness.
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question posed to the disbelievers, challenging them to reflect on their own state of mind. It suggests that their rejection of the Prophet Muhammad's message is not based on rational thought but rather on a form of spiritual or intellectual madness. The verse invites them to consider the possibility that their disbelief stems from an internal affliction rather than from any fault in the message itself.
orig: بأييكم المفتون

translation: Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who strays from His way, and He is most knowing of the guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's omniscience, highlighting His complete knowledge of those who deviate from the path of righteousness and those who follow it. It serves as a reminder to believers that Allah is fully aware of the choices individuals make, and thus, one should strive to stay on the right path, knowing that their actions are known and judged by Allah.
orig: إن ربك هو أعلم بمن ضل عن سبيله وهو أعلم بالمهتدين

translation: So do not obey the deniers.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) not to be swayed or influenced by those who reject the message of Islam. It emphasizes the importance of steadfastness in faith and mission, despite opposition and denial from others.
orig: فلا تطع المكذبين

translation: They wish that you should compromise so they would compromise.
interpretation: This verse suggests that there are individuals who desire the Prophet Muhammad to make concessions or soften his stance on certain issues, so that they in turn might be willing to make similar compromises. It highlights the pressure faced by the Prophet to dilute the message of Islam in order to appease others, reflecting a test of his resolve and integrity in maintaining the purity of the divine message.
orig: ودوا لو تدهن فيدهنون

translation: And do not obey every contemptible swearer,
interpretation: This verse advises believers not to follow or be influenced by individuals who are known for making false oaths and are of low moral character. It emphasizes the importance of discerning whom to trust and follow, urging one to avoid those whose words and actions lack integrity.
orig: ولا تطع كل حلاف مهين

translation: A slanderer, going about with calumnies
interpretation: This verse describes a person who engages in backbiting and spreading rumors. Such behavior is condemned in Islam as it harms the social fabric and undermines trust within the community. The term 'هماز' refers to someone who constantly slanders others, while 'مشاء بنميم' indicates someone who actively spreads these slanders, moving from one person to another to disseminate false information.
orig: هماز مشاء بنميم

translation: Preventer of good, transgressor, great sinner
interpretation: This verse describes a person who actively blocks or prevents beneficial actions or goodness, and who is characterized by transgression and significant sinfulness. It highlights the moral and ethical failings of such an individual, emphasizing their negative impact on society and their distance from the path of righteousness.
orig: مناع للخير معتد أثيم

translation: Then he followed a course,
interpretation: This verse refers to the journey of Dhul-Qarnayn, a righteous king mentioned in the Qur'an, who traveled to different parts of the world to spread justice and guidance. The phrase "followed a course" indicates his purposeful and directed movement towards another region after his previous endeavors, symbolizing the continuous effort in the path of righteousness and the exploration of new territories to establish justice and faith.
orig: عتل بعد ذلك زنيم

translation: If he had wealth and sons
interpretation: This verse highlights the worldly possessions and familial ties that are often considered as sources of pride and security in human society. It suggests that the mere possession of wealth and children does not necessarily equate to true success or divine favor, as these are temporary and can distract from spiritual priorities.
orig: أن كان ذا مال وبنين

translation: When Our verses are recited to him, he says, 'Myths of the ancients.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the dismissive attitude of some individuals towards the revelations of the Qur'an. When confronted with the divine message, they reject it outright, labeling it as mere legends or stories from the past, thereby refusing to engage with its spiritual and moral teachings. This reaction underscores a deeper resistance to change and an unwillingness to accept the truth that challenges their existing beliefs and lifestyles.
orig: إذا تتلى عليه آياتنا قال أساطير الأولين

translation: We will brand him on the snout.
interpretation: This verse refers to the punishment of those who are arrogant and reject the truth. The imagery of branding on the snout symbolizes a humiliating and painful consequence for such individuals, serving as a metaphor for the severe repercussions of their actions in the hereafter.
orig: سنسمه على الخرطوم

translation: Indeed, We have tried them as We tried the people of the garden, when they swore to pluck its fruits in the morning,
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of divine testing, illustrating that God tests the faith and patience of people in various ways, similar to how He tested the owners of a garden. The owners of the garden swore to harvest their fruits early in the morning, showing their confidence and perhaps their lack of gratitude or acknowledgment of God's provision. This test serves as a reminder to believers to always be mindful of God's role in their lives and to approach their blessings with humility and thankfulness.
orig: إنا بلوناهم كما بلونا أصحاب الجنة إذ أقسموا ليصرمنها مصبحين

translation: And they do not make exception
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of sincerity and complete faith in Allah without making any exceptions or conditions in one's belief. It emphasizes that true believers do not limit their trust or submission to Allah in certain situations but maintain unwavering faith in all circumstances.
orig: ولا يستثنون

translation: So there came upon it a visitation from your Lord while they were asleep.
interpretation: This verse describes a divine intervention or punishment that occurred unexpectedly while the people were asleep, highlighting the suddenness and inevitability of God's decree.
orig: فطاف عليها طائف من ربك وهم نائمون

translation: So it became like a dry, empty field.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the transformation of something once vibrant and lush into a state of desolation and emptiness, symbolizing the consequences of disbelief and the transient nature of worldly life. It serves as a reminder of the ultimate power of Allah to alter conditions and the importance of faith and obedience to avoid spiritual barrenness.
orig: فأصبحت كالصريم

translation: So they called out one another as soon as the morning came,
interpretation: This verse illustrates the urgency and collective action of the people involved, highlighting how they gathered early in the morning to address a pressing matter, reflecting the importance of community and timely response in facing challenges.
orig: فتنادوا مصبحين

translation: Go forth to your tilth if you are going to work hard
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to actively engage in their work or duties, symbolized by 'tilth' or farmland, with diligence and determination. It emphasizes the importance of taking initiative and working hard in one's responsibilities, reflecting a broader Islamic principle of striving in all aspects of life.
orig: أن اغدوا على حرثكم إن كنتم صارمين

translation: So they departed, whispering to each other.
interpretation: This verse describes a scene where individuals are leaving a situation while engaging in secretive or hushed conversations. It highlights a moment of uncertainty or conspiracy among them, reflecting their inner fears or doubts about the path they are taking or the decisions they have made. This can serve as a metaphor for the human tendency to engage in gossip or secretive discussions when faced with challenging or morally ambiguous situations.
orig: فانطلقوا وهم يتخافتون

translation: That no beggar will enter upon you today.
interpretation: This verse suggests a state of exclusivity and isolation, possibly indicating a day of judgment or a significant event where the usual norms of charity and interaction with the less fortunate are suspended, emphasizing the severity and uniqueness of the occasion.
orig: أن لا يدخلنها اليوم عليكم مسكين

translation: And they advanced early, determined upon their purpose.
interpretation: This verse highlights the determination and resolve of the people of 'Ād when they set out to confront the Prophet Hūd. It underscores the theme of human willpower and the lengths to which individuals or groups might go when they are committed to a course of action, even if it leads them to oppose divine guidance. The phrase "غدوا" (they advanced early) signifies their eagerness and urgency, while "على حرد قادرين" (determined upon their purpose) emphasizes their strength and capability in pursuing their misguided intentions.
orig: وغدوا على حرد قادرين

translation: So when they saw it, they said, 'Indeed, we are lost.'
interpretation: This verse reflects a moment of realization and despair among the people of Thamud when they saw the she-camel that was sent as a sign from Allah. Their statement, 'Indeed, we are lost,' signifies their acknowledgment of being astray and their fear of the consequences of rejecting the prophet Saleh's message. It highlights the human tendency to recognize one's errors only when faced with undeniable signs, yet it also underscores the gravity of their situation, as they are now confronted with the reality of divine judgment.
orig: فلما رأوها قالوا إنا لضالون

translation: Rather, we are deprived.
