interpretation: This verse highlights the diversity of belief and action among individuals, even within the same community. It suggests that while some people choose to follow the path of Islam, submitting to the will of Allah and thereby finding guidance, others deviate and act unjustly. The verse emphasizes the importance of choosing submission to Allah as a means to achieve true guidance and righteousness.
orig: وأنا منا المسلمون ومنا القاسطون فمن أسلم فأولئك تحروا رشدا

translation: And as for the wrongdoers, they will be fuel for Hell.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequence of injustice and wrongdoing. Those who deviate from the path of righteousness and fairness, engaging in acts that harm others or disrupt the moral order, are likened to fuel for Hell. This metaphor illustrates the severe punishment awaiting them in the afterlife, underscoring the importance of justice and moral integrity in one's actions and life.
orig: وأما القاسطون فكانوا لجهنم حطبا

translation: And that if they had remained on the right path, We would have given them abundant water to drink.
interpretation: This verse suggests that adherence to the righteous path leads to divine blessings and sustenance. The metaphor of 'abundant water' symbolizes the spiritual and material nourishment that comes from following God's guidance. It emphasizes the conditional nature of divine favor, contingent upon one's commitment to the straight path.
orig: وأن لو استقاموا على الطريقة لأسقيناهم ماء غدقا

translation: We will surely test them therein, and whoever turns away from the remembrance of his Lord, He will impose on him an ever-increasing torment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability of trials and tests in life as a means to distinguish the steadfast from those who turn away from God's guidance. It warns that neglecting the remembrance of Allah and straying from His path will lead to a severe and escalating punishment, underscoring the importance of maintaining a constant connection with the Divine and adhering to His commands.
orig: لنفتنهم فيه ومن يعرض عن ذكر ربه يسلكه عذابا صعدا

translation: And that the mosques are for Allah, so do not invoke with Allah anyone.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sanctity and exclusivity of mosques as places dedicated solely to the worship of Allah. It instructs believers not to associate any other deities or beings with Allah in these sacred spaces, reinforcing the principle of tawhid (the oneness of God) and warning against shirk (polytheism).
orig: وأن المساجد لله فلا تدعوا مع الله أحدا

translation: And that when the servant of Allah stood up calling upon Him, they almost became a compact mass against him.
interpretation: This verse highlights the intense opposition and hostility faced by the Prophet Muhammad when he openly called people to worship Allah. It reflects the unity of his adversaries in their attempt to resist his message, illustrating the challenges and resistance that can accompany the call to faith and the importance of perseverance in the face of such adversity.
orig: وأنه لما قام عبد الله يدعوه كادوا يكونون عليه لبدا

translation: Say, "Indeed, I call upon my Lord and do not associate with Him anyone."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the purity and exclusivity of worship in Islam. It instructs the Prophet Muhammad, and by extension all Muslims, to declare their devotion solely to Allah, rejecting any form of polytheism or association of partners with Him. It underscores the fundamental Islamic principle of Tawheed, the oneness of God, and serves as a reminder to maintain a clear and focused worship directed only towards Allah.
orig: قل إنما أدعو ربي ولا أشرك به أحدا

translation: Say, "Indeed, I do not possess for you [the power of] harm or right guidance."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophet Muhammad's role as a messenger who conveys God's message, but does not possess the power to enforce harm or guide people directly. It highlights the human limitation of the Prophet and the divine authority of God, reminding believers that ultimate power and guidance come from Allah alone.
orig: قل إني لا أملك لكم ضرا ولا رشدا

translation: Say, 'No one can protect me from Allah [if I were to disobey], nor will I find any refuge besides Him.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and authority of Allah, indicating that no one can shield or protect someone from the consequences of disobeying Allah's commands. It also highlights the concept of Tawheed (the oneness of Allah), underscoring that there is no refuge or sanctuary to be found outside of Allah's mercy and protection. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of submitting to Allah alone and seeking His guidance and protection in all matters.
orig: قل إني لن يجيرني من الله أحد ولن أجد من دونه ملتحدا

translation: Except for conveying [the Message] from Allah and His messages. And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger, then indeed, for him is the fire of Hell; they will abide therein forever.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the duty of the Prophet Muhammad to convey the message of Allah and His messages without any alteration. It also serves as a stern warning to those who disobey Allah and His Messenger, indicating that the consequence of such disobedience is eternal damnation in the fire of Hell. The verse underscores the gravity of rejecting divine guidance and the importance of obedience to Allah and His Prophet.
orig: إلا بلاغا من الله ورسالاته ومن يعص الله ورسوله فإن له نار جهنم خالدين فيها أبدا

translation: Until, when they see what they are promised, then they will know who is weaker in helpers and fewer in number.
interpretation: This verse suggests that on the Day of Judgment, those who disbelieved will finally realize the truth of the warnings they were given. They will understand that their supposed allies and supporters were actually weaker and fewer than they had believed, highlighting the futility of relying on anything other than the support of Allah.
orig: حتى إذا رأوا ما يوعدون فسيعلمون من أضعف ناصرا وأقل عددا

translation: Say, 'I do not know whether what you are promised is near or whether my Lord will grant it a longer term.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the humility and submission of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to the divine will of Allah. It highlights that even the Prophet does not have knowledge of the exact timing of the events promised by Allah, such as the Day of Judgment. This serves to remind believers of the importance of patience and trust in Allah's timing and plan, reinforcing the concept that only Allah possesses full knowledge of the unseen and the future.
orig: قل إن أدري أقريب ما توعدون أم يجعل له ربي أمدا

translation: Knower of the unseen, and He does not disclose His unseen to anyone,
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's unique attribute of knowing the unseen (al-ghayb), which includes all things beyond human perception and understanding. The interpretation highlights that Allah alone possesses this knowledge and does not share it with anyone, underscoring His supreme sovereignty and the limitations of all other beings in comparison.
orig: عالم الغيب فلا يظهر على غيبه أحدا

translation: Except for those [messengers] taken by Allah [in death]: for indeed, He is ever, over all things, a Guardian.
interpretation: This verse highlights the special protection and guidance provided by Allah to His messengers. It suggests that while all humans are accountable for their actions, the messengers of Allah are under a unique divine watch, both in front of and behind them, ensuring their path aligns with the divine will. This constant surveillance by Allah serves as a reassurance to the messengers and a testament to their elevated status in the divine scheme.
orig: إلا من ارتضى من رسول فإنه يسلك من بين يديه ومن خلفه رصدا

translation: That He may know that they have conveyed the messages of their Lord; and He has encompassed what is with them, and He has enumerated all things in number.
interpretation: This verse underscores the omniscience of Allah, emphasizing that He is fully aware of whether His messengers have faithfully delivered His messages. It highlights the accountability of the messengers and the all-encompassing knowledge of Allah, who keeps a precise account of everything. This serves as a reminder to all believers of the importance of fulfilling their duties and the certainty that Allah is aware of all actions and will hold everyone accountable.
orig: ليعلم أن قد أبلغوا رسالات ربهم وأحاط بما لديهم وأحصى كل شيء عددا

translation: O you who wraps himself [in clothing]
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad, emphasizing his humility and dedication to prayer. The term 'المزمل' (the one who wraps himself) symbolizes his practice of wrapping himself in his cloak during night prayers, highlighting his devotion and the intimate connection between him and his worship.
orig: يا أيها المزمل

translation: Stand (in prayer) by night, except a little.
interpretation: This verse encourages the believer to engage in night prayer, known as Tahajjud, which is a voluntary act of worship. It emphasizes the importance of dedicating a significant portion of the night to prayer, suggesting that one should not limit their night prayer to just a small amount of time. The act of standing in prayer during the night is seen as a means to draw closer to Allah, to seek His forgiveness, and to strengthen one's faith and spiritual connection.
orig: قم الليل إلا قليلا

translation: Half of it or a little less than that
interpretation: This verse suggests the importance of moderation and balance in one's actions and commitments. It indicates that fulfilling half or slightly less than half of a responsibility or obligation can be considered acceptable, emphasizing flexibility and the human capacity to manage time and duties effectively without being overwhelmed.
orig: نصفه أو انقص منه قليلا

translation: Or add to it and recite the Qur'an in a measured way.
interpretation: This verse encourages the recitation of the Qur'an with careful attention to its rhythm and pacing. It suggests that one should not rush through the recitation but should instead take time to articulate each word clearly and melodiously, allowing the beauty and the message of the Qur'an to be fully appreciated and absorbed. This method of recitation enhances understanding and reflection on the divine words.
orig: أو زد عليه ورتل القرآن ترتيلا

translation: Indeed, We will cast upon you a heavy word.
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah is preparing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to receive a revelation that will be burdensome and significant, challenging him to convey a profound message to his people. It underscores the weight of the prophetic mission and the responsibility placed upon the Prophet.
orig: إنا سنلقي عليك قولا ثقيلا

translation: Indeed, the rising of the night is more effective and more suitable for recitation.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the spiritual and practical benefits of engaging in prayer and recitation during the night. The night's tranquility allows for deeper concentration and a more profound connection with the divine, making it an ideal time for worship and reflection. It suggests that the stillness of the night enhances the quality of one's spiritual practice, fostering a more intimate and focused engagement with the Qur'an.
orig: إن ناشئة الليل هي أشد وطئا وأقوم قيلا

translation: Indeed, for you in the daytime is prolonged occupation.
interpretation: This verse suggests that during the day, one has numerous responsibilities and tasks that require attention and effort. It emphasizes the importance of utilizing the daytime effectively for productive and meaningful activities.
orig: إن لك في النهار سبحا طويلا

translation: And mention the name of your Lord and devote yourself to Him with complete devotion.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of constant remembrance of Allah and dedicating oneself entirely to Him. It encourages believers to focus their lives around worship and obedience to Allah, seeking to purify their hearts and actions through sincere devotion.
orig: واذكر اسم ربك وتبتل إليه تبتيلا

translation: Lord of the East and the West, there is no deity except Him, so take Him as a Disposer of Affairs.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness and omnipotence of Allah, who is the sovereign over all directions and aspects of life. It calls upon believers to entrust their affairs entirely to Allah, recognizing His supreme authority and capability in managing all matters. By taking Allah as a Disposer of Affairs, one acknowledges His ultimate control and seeks His guidance and support in all aspects of life.
orig: رب المشرق والمغرب لا إله إلا هو فاتخذه وكيلا

translation: And be patient with what they say and avoid them with a gracious avoidance.
interpretation: This verse advises believers to maintain patience in the face of criticism or opposition from others. It encourages a response of dignified silence and avoidance, not out of disdain, but with kindness and grace. This approach reflects a higher moral ground, promoting peace and understanding rather than engaging in conflict.
orig: واصبر على ما يقولون واهجرهم هجرا جميلا

translation: And leave Me with [the matter of] the deniers, those of ease and plenty, and give them a little respite.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad to leave the handling of the disbelievers, who are described as being in a state of comfort and luxury, to Allah. It emphasizes patience and trust in divine timing, suggesting that these disbelievers will be given a short period of respite before facing the consequences of their denial. The verse highlights the concept of divine justice and the eventual accountability of all individuals, encouraging believers to maintain faith and patience despite the apparent success of the deniers.
orig: وذرني والمكذبين أولي النعمة ومهلهم قليلا

translation: Indeed, for us are shackles and hellfire.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning about the consequences of disbelief and wrongdoing. It emphasizes the existence of punishment in the afterlife, specifically mentioning 'shackles' as a symbol of restraint and confinement, and 'hellfire' as the ultimate torment for those who have strayed from the path of righteousness. It underscores the reality of divine justice and the accountability of one's actions in the hereafter.
orig: إن لدينا أنكالا وجحيما

translation: And food that chokes, and a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse describes the severe conditions of Hell, where the inhabitants are given food that is difficult to swallow, symbolizing the discomfort and torment they experience. The 'painful punishment' refers to the intense suffering that accompanies their existence in the afterlife, serving as a warning to believers to avoid actions that lead to such a fate.
orig: وطعاما ذا غصة وعذابا أليما

translation: The Day when the earth and the mountains will shake, and the mountains will become a heap of sand pouring down.
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Judgment, emphasizing the immense power and awe-inspiring nature of that day. The shaking of the earth and the transformation of mountains into heaps of sand illustrate the complete upheaval and dissolution of the familiar world, underscoring the overwhelming might of Allah and the reality of the hereafter.
orig: يوم ترجف الأرض والجبال وكانت الجبال كثيبا مهيلا

translation: Indeed, We have sent to you a messenger as a witness over you, just as We sent to Pharaoh a messenger.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the continuity of divine guidance through messengers across different nations and eras. It underscores that the sending of Prophet Muhammad to the people is akin to the sending of a messenger to Pharaoh, illustrating that Allah's method of communicating His message through chosen prophets is consistent and universal. The mention of the messenger as a 'witness' highlights the accountability of people for their actions in the presence of divine guidance.
orig: إنا أرسلنا إليكم رسولا شاهدا عليكم كما أرسلنا إلى فرعون رسولا

translation: So Pharaoh disobeyed the messenger, so We seized him with a severe punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequence of rejecting divine guidance. Pharaoh's disobedience to the messenger, Moses, led to his severe punishment, illustrating that defiance against God's commands results in retribution. It serves as a warning to those who arrogantly reject the truth and the messengers of God, emphasizing the inevitability of divine justice.
orig: فعصى فرعون الرسول فأخذناه أخذا وبيلا

translation: So how will you safeguard yourselves, if you disbelieve, on a Day that will turn the children gray-haired?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity of the Day of Judgment, highlighting that disbelief will lead to such overwhelming fear and distress that even young children will turn gray-haired from the shock and horror of that day. It serves as a warning to believers to remain steadfast in their faith to avoid the dire consequences of disbelief.
orig: فكيف تتقون إن كفرتم يوما يجعل الولدان شيبا

translation: The heaven will be split asunder by it; His promise is to be fulfilled.
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Judgment, emphasizing the immense power of Allah. The splitting of the sky symbolizes the end of the world as we know it, and it serves as a reminder that Allah's promises regarding the hereafter are certain and will undoubtedly come to pass. It underscores the inevitability of divine judgment and the fulfillment of Allah's decrees.
orig: السماء منفطر به كان وعده مفعولا

translation: Indeed, this is a reminder, so whoever wills may take to his Lord a way.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Qur'an's role as a reminder and guidance for humanity. It highlights the freedom of choice given to individuals; anyone who desires can choose to follow the path that leads to their Lord, indicating that the decision to seek and follow divine guidance is a personal one.
orig: إن هذه تذكرة فمن شاء اتخذ إلى ربه سبيلا

translation: Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand [in prayer] almost two-thirds of the night or half of it or a third of it, and [so do] a group of those with you. And Allah determines [the extent of] the night and the day. He has known that you [Muslims] will not be able to keep count of it, so He has turned to you in forgiveness. So recite what is easy [for you] of the Qur'an. He has known that there will be among you those who are ill and others traveling throughout the land seeking [something] of the bounty of Allah and others fighting in the cause of Allah. So recite what is easy from it and establish prayer and give zakah and loan Allah a goodly loan. And whatever good you put forward for yourselves - you will find it with Allah. It is better and greater in reward. And seek forgiveness of Allah. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the flexibility and mercy of Allah in religious obligations, particularly concerning the night prayer (Tahajjud). It acknowledges that not everyone can perform long night prayers due to various reasons such as illness, travel, or engaging in jihad. Allah encourages believers to recite what is easy for them from the Qur'an, indicating that the intention and effort are what truly matter. The verse also underscores the importance of other fundamental acts of worship like prayer, zakah, and charity, promising that any good deed done will be rewarded manifold by Allah. It concludes by urging believers to seek Allah's forgiveness, highlighting His attributes of forgiveness and mercy, which are central to the relationship between the Creator and His servants.
orig: إن ربك يعلم أنك تقوم أدنى من ثلثي الليل ونصفه وثلثه وطائفة من الذين معك والله يقدر الليل والنهار علم أن لن تحصوه فتاب عليكم فاقرءوا ما تيسر من القرآن علم أن سيكون منكم مرضى وآخرون يضربون في الأرض يبتغون من فضل الله وآخرون يقاتلون في سبيل الله فاقرءوا ما تيسر منه وأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة وأقرضوا الله قرضا حسنا وما تقدموا لأنفسكم من خير تجدوه عند الله هو خيرا وأعظم أجرا واستغفروا الله إن الله غفور رحيم

translation: O you who are wrapped up (in garments)!
interpretation: This verse is an address from Allah to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), calling him by a description of his state at the time of receiving revelation, indicating intimacy and the beginning of his mission as a messenger. It signifies the start of a new phase in his prophetic life where he is called to arise and warn his people.
orig: يا أيها المدثر

translation: Arise and warn
interpretation: This verse is a directive from Allah to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), urging him to stand up and actively convey the message of Islam to others. It emphasizes the importance of taking action in spreading the divine message and warning people about the consequences of their actions in the hereafter.
orig: قم فأنذر

translation: And your Lord, so magnify Him
interpretation: This verse instructs believers to exalt and glorify Allah, emphasizing the importance of recognizing His greatness and majesty in all aspects of life. It serves as a reminder to maintain a constant awareness of Allah's supreme power and to express this recognition through acts of worship and reverence.
orig: وربك فكبر

translation: And keep your garments pure
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of purity and cleanliness in one's personal life, extending beyond physical cleanliness to include moral and spiritual purity. It serves as a reminder to maintain a state of cleanliness and purity in all aspects of life, reflecting the overall Islamic principle of cleanliness being half of faith.
orig: وثيابك فطهر

translation: And avoid the filth
interpretation: This verse instructs believers to steer clear of all forms of evil, impurity, and sin. It emphasizes the importance of maintaining spiritual and moral cleanliness by avoiding actions, thoughts, and environments that could lead to corruption or moral decay.
orig: والرجز فاهجر

translation: And do not confer favor to seek more
interpretation: This verse advises against giving charity or doing good deeds with the expectation of receiving something in return or to boast about one's generosity. The act of giving should be purely for the sake of Allah, without any ulterior motives or desire for personal gain.
orig: ولا تمنن تستكثر

translation: And be patient, for the sake of your Lord.
interpretation: This verse encourages steadfastness and patience in the face of adversity and challenges, emphasizing that such endurance should be motivated by devotion to Allah. It underscores the importance of maintaining faith and resilience, trusting in Allah's wisdom and timing, as a means to spiritual growth and ultimate reward.
orig: ولربك فاصبر

translation: Then, when the trumpet is blown with a single blast
interpretation: This verse refers to the event of the Day of Judgment when the trumpet will be blown, signaling the end of the world and the beginning of the resurrection. The sound of the trumpet will be a clear and unmistakable sign that all creation must gather for the final judgment.
orig: فإذا نقر في الناقور

translation: So that Day will be a difficult day,
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity and hardship of the Day of Judgment, indicating that it will be a time of great trial and difficulty for all individuals, underscoring the importance of preparing for it through righteous deeds and faith.
orig: فذلك يومئذ يوم عسير

translation: Upon the disbelievers is a heavy burden
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe consequences and burdens that await those who reject faith. It suggests that disbelief carries with it a significant spiritual and moral weight, which will be felt profoundly by the disbelievers, both in this life and in the hereafter.
orig: على الكافرين غير يسير

translation: Leave Me with the one I created alone
interpretation: This verse is a command from Allah to the Prophet Muhammad, indicating that Allah will deal with a particular individual who has been created alone, possibly referring to someone who is astray or denying the truth. It emphasizes Allah's sovereignty and His direct handling of individuals according to His wisdom.
orig: ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا

translation: And I have granted him extensive wealth.
interpretation: This verse indicates that God has bestowed upon a person not just wealth, but wealth that is abundant and far-reaching. It suggests a divine favor that extends beyond mere sufficiency, into the realm of extravagance, possibly as a test or a means to fulfill certain responsibilities or duties assigned by God.
orig: وجعلت له مالا ممدودا

translation: And sons as witnesses
interpretation: This phrase refers to the righteous offspring that a person may have, who will serve as witnesses to their good deeds and character on the Day of Judgment. These children are a testament to the moral and spiritual guidance provided by their parents.
orig: وبنين شهودا

translation: And I prepared for him a preparation.
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah facilitated and prepared the path for the person mentioned, ensuring that the conditions were set for his success or mission. It reflects the divine support and guidance provided to prophets or chosen individuals to fulfill their roles effectively.
orig: ومهدت له تمهيدا

translation: Then he hopes that I will increase
interpretation: This verse reflects the human tendency to continuously desire more from Allah, even after receiving blessings. It highlights a lack of contentment and gratitude, suggesting that humans often fail to appreciate what they have been given and instead focus on wanting more.
orig: ثم يطمع أن أزيد

translation: Nay, but verily he was stubborn towards Our signs.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the person being referred to was obstinate and refused to accept or be guided by the clear signs and revelations from Allah. It highlights a deliberate rejection of divine guidance, emphasizing the individual's arrogance and resistance to truth.
orig: كلا إنه كان لآياتنا عنيدا

translation: I will surely make him climb
interpretation: This verse reflects a determination to challenge or burden someone with a difficult task or ascent, symbolizing the trials and tests that life or divine will may impose on an individual. It suggests a purposeful intent to push someone towards their limits, possibly for growth or as a form of punishment.
orig: سأرهقه صعودا

translation: Indeed, He has thought and measured.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's meticulous planning and precise calculation in the creation and governance of the universe, highlighting His omniscience and the perfection of His actions.
orig: إنه فكر وقدر

translation: So he planned and he measured.
interpretation: This verse refers to the meticulous planning and precise execution of actions by an individual, highlighting the human capacity for strategic thinking and the consequences that follow from such deliberate actions.
orig: فقتل كيف قدر

translation: Then he considered and how he estimated
interpretation: This verse reflects on the moment when a person, after committing a sin or an act of disbelief, reflects on their actions and calculates the consequences or the perceived benefits. It highlights the human tendency to rationalize wrongdoing after the fact, showing the internal debate and justification process that often follows sinful actions.
orig: ثم قتل كيف قدر

translation: Then he considered
interpretation: This verse reflects a moment of introspection or reflection by an individual, possibly after receiving guidance or witnessing a sign from Allah. It suggests a pause for thought, where the person contemplates their actions, beliefs, or the consequences of their choices in light of divine wisdom.
orig: ثم نظر

translation: Then he frowned and turned away.
interpretation: This verse describes the reaction of a person who, upon being approached or asked for help, shows a negative response by frowning and turning away. It highlights a moment of human weakness where one might react with disdain or impatience, possibly due to feeling inconvenienced or interrupted. This behavior is presented in the Qur'an as an example of improper conduct, especially when it comes to interactions that involve guidance or assistance to others.
orig: ثم عبس وبسر

translation: Then he turned away and was arrogant.
interpretation: This verse describes the behavior of Pharaoh after being confronted with the truth. It highlights his rejection of divine guidance due to his pride and arrogance, which led him to turn away from the path of righteousness. This act of turning away symbolizes not only physical departure but also a spiritual rejection of God's message, illustrating the dangers of arrogance and the consequences of denying the truth out of haughtiness.
orig: ثم أدبر واستكبر

translation: So he said, 'This is nothing but magic that is shown.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the disbelief and denial of the truth by those who are confronted with clear signs and miracles. The speaker, in this case, Pharaoh, dismisses the miracle performed by Moses as mere illusion or magic, refusing to accept it as a divine sign. This highlights the human tendency to reject what challenges their existing beliefs or power, attributing divine acts to trickery or deception.
orig: فقال إن هذا إلا سحر يؤثر

translation: This is nothing but the word of humans
interpretation: This verse suggests that the message or revelation being referred to is dismissed by some as merely human invention, not divine in origin. It highlights the skepticism and disbelief of those who reject the Qur'anic message, attributing it to human authorship rather than accepting it as a revelation from God.
orig: إن هذا إلا قول البشر

translation: I will cast him into Saqar
interpretation: This verse reflects the divine justice and retribution, indicating that those who deny or reject the truth will face severe consequences in the afterlife. 'Saqar' is one of the names of Hell, symbolizing intense punishment and suffering. The use of 'I will cast' emphasizes the certainty and authority of divine action against those who stray from the path of righteousness.
orig: سأصليه سقر

translation: And what will make you know what Saqar is?
interpretation: This rhetorical question emphasizes the severity and horror of Saqar, one of the names of Hell, highlighting that its true nature is beyond human comprehension and serves as a warning of the consequences of disbelief and sinful actions.
orig: وما أدراك ما سقر

translation: Do not leave and do not spare
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the command to be thorough and complete in the task at hand, suggesting that one should not leave any part undone or spare any effort in fulfilling their duty.
orig: لا تبقي ولا تذر

translation: A tablet for mankind
interpretation: This verse refers to the preserved tablet (Al-Lawh Al-Mahfuz) in Islamic theology, which contains the divine decrees and the records of all that has happened and will happen. It symbolizes the ultimate knowledge and plan of Allah for humanity, emphasizing the predetermined nature of events and the comprehensive wisdom of God.
orig: لواحة للبشر

translation: Over it are nineteen
interpretation: This verse refers to the nineteen angels guarding Hell, as mentioned in Surah Al-Muddaththir. The number nineteen is significant as it symbolizes the divine order and the meticulous nature of God's creation and judgment. It serves as a reminder of the precise accountability and the severe punishment awaiting the disbelievers.
orig: عليها تسعة عشر

translation: And We have not made the keepers of the Fire except angels. And We have not made their number except as a trial for those who disbelieve - that those who were given the Scripture will be convinced and those who believe will increase in faith and those who were given the Scripture and the believers will not doubt and that those in whose hearts is disease and the disbelievers will say, 'What does Allah intend by this example?' Thus does Allah leave astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. And none knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him. And it is not but a reminder for humanity.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine wisdom behind the specific details given in the Qur'an, such as the number of the guardians of Hell being angels. This detail serves multiple purposes: it strengthens the faith of believers, reassures those who have received divine scriptures, and acts as a test for disbelievers and those with doubts. The verse illustrates how such revelations can lead to increased faith among the faithful, while causing confusion and disbelief among others, highlighting Allah's ultimate authority over guidance and misguidance. It also emphasizes that the true nature and extent of Allah's forces are known only to Him, serving as a reminder to all of humanity of the limits of our understanding and the necessity of faith.
orig: وما جعلنا أصحاب النار إلا ملائكة وما جعلنا عدتهم إلا فتنة للذين كفروا ليستيقن الذين أوتوا الكتاب ويزداد الذين آمنوا إيمانا ولا يرتاب الذين أوتوا الكتاب والمؤمنون وليقول الذين في قلوبهم مرض والكافرون ماذا أراد الله بهذا مثلا كذلك يضل الله من يشاء ويهدي من يشاء وما يعلم جنود ربك إلا هو وما هي إلا ذكرى للبشر

translation: Nay, by the moon
interpretation: This verse serves as a strong oath, emphasizing the certainty and truth of the message being conveyed. The use of the moon as the object of the oath underscores its significance and visibility, symbolizing the clear and undeniable nature of the truth being affirmed.
orig: كلا والقمر

translation: And [by] the night when it departs
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the cyclical nature of time, highlighting the transition from night to day as a sign of God's creation and control over the universe. It serves as a reminder of the constant change and renewal in life, urging believers to reflect on the passage of time and the opportunities it brings for spiritual growth and gratitude.
orig: والليل إذ أدبر

translation: And [by] the dawn when it breathes
interpretation: This verse refers to the time of dawn when the light begins to spread, symbolizing the clarity and revelation of truth after a period of darkness. It highlights the natural cycle of day and night as a sign of God's creation and a metaphor for spiritual enlightenment.
orig: والصبح إذا أسفر

translation: Indeed, it is one of the greatest [signs].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the magnitude and significance of the event or sign being referred to, indicating that it holds a profound importance within the context of the Qur'an, urging believers to reflect deeply on its implications and to recognize the power and wisdom of Allah manifested through it.
orig: إنها لإحدى الكبر

translation: A warning to mankind
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder that the Qur'an is not just a message of guidance and mercy, but also a stern warning to all of humanity about the consequences of their actions and the importance of heeding the divine message.
orig: نذيرا للبشر

translation: For whoever among you who wishes to go forward or to stay back.
interpretation: This verse highlights the freedom of choice granted to individuals in their spiritual journey. It suggests that each person has the autonomy to decide whether to advance in faith and righteousness or to lag behind, emphasizing personal responsibility in one's actions and decisions.
orig: لمن شاء منكم أن يتقدم أو يتأخر

translation: Every soul is held in pledge for what it has earned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes individual accountability in the eyes of Allah. It means that every person is responsible for their own actions and will be held accountable for them on the Day of Judgment. The concept of being a "pledge" or "hostage" to one's deeds underscores the gravity and inescapability of this accountability, urging believers to be mindful of their actions and strive for righteousness.
orig: كل نفس بما كسبت رهينة

translation: Except the companions of the right hand
interpretation: This verse refers to the righteous believers who will be granted Paradise. The 'companions of the right hand' symbolize those who have been blessed and favored by Allah due to their good deeds and faith. It highlights the distinction and honor bestowed upon them in the afterlife.
orig: إلا أصحاب اليمين

translation: In gardens, they will be questioning one another
interpretation: This verse depicts the scene in Paradise where the righteous will engage in conversations, reflecting a state of peace, contentment, and mutual inquiry about their experiences and blessings, highlighting the social aspect of the afterlife.
orig: في جنات يتساءلون

translation: About the criminals
interpretation: This phrase refers to the state or condition of those who have committed sins or transgressions against the divine law. It suggests a focus on the consequences or the judgment that awaits such individuals in the afterlife, emphasizing the Qur'an's theme of accountability for one's actions.
orig: عن المجرمين

translation: What has caused you to enter Saqar?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question posed to the inhabitants of Hell, asking them what actions or beliefs led them to be condemned to the fire of Saqar. It serves as a reflection point for the damned, emphasizing personal responsibility for one's fate in the afterlife and highlighting the consequences of their choices or lack of faith.
orig: ما سلككم في سقر

translation: They said, 'We were not of those who prayed.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the regret and acknowledgment of those who, on the Day of Judgment, realize that they did not fulfill their religious obligations, specifically the act of prayer, which is a fundamental pillar of Islam. It underscores the importance of regular prayer and the consequences of neglecting it.
orig: قالوا لم نك من المصلين

translation: And we do not feed the poor
interpretation: This verse reflects a statement of denial or neglect by some people regarding their responsibility to help the less fortunate. It highlights a common human failing where individuals might shirk their moral and religious duty to provide for the poor, emphasizing the importance of charity and social responsibility in Islam.
orig: ولم نك نطعم المسكين

translation: And we used to swim with the swimmers
interpretation: This verse reflects on the shared human experience and the inevitability of engaging in life's activities alongside others. It suggests a sense of community and participation in the common struggles and joys of life, emphasizing that no one is isolated in their journey through life.
orig: وكنا نخوض مع الخائضين

translation: And we used to deny the Day of Judgment
interpretation: This verse reflects the mindset of those who rejected the concept of accountability after death, illustrating their disbelief in the divine justice system where deeds are judged. It underscores the human tendency to ignore or reject the notion of a final reckoning, which is a central theme in Islamic eschatology.
orig: وكنا نكذب بيوم الدين

translation: Until the certainty came to us
interpretation: This phrase refers to the moment of death when the truth of the afterlife and the reality of God's existence become undeniably clear to the individual. It signifies the transition from the uncertainty and doubts of worldly life to the absolute certainty of the hereafter.
orig: حتى أتانا اليقين

translation: So the intercession of intercessors will not benefit them.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility of intercession on the Day of Judgment for those who have rejected faith. It underscores that no one, regardless of their status or relationship, can intercede on behalf of the disbelievers to alter their fate. This highlights the absolute justice and sovereignty of Allah, where personal accountability is paramount and no external influence can change the divine decree.
orig: فما تنفعهم شفاعة الشافعين

translation: So what is [the matter] with them that they are, from the reminder, turning away?
interpretation: This verse questions the reason behind people's refusal to heed the divine message. It suggests a sense of bewilderment and disappointment at the human tendency to ignore or reject the guidance and reminders provided by Allah through the Qur'an. The use of 'what is the matter' implies a call for introspection and a challenge to the listeners to consider their actions and the consequences of turning away from the truth.
orig: فما لهم عن التذكرة معرضين

translation: As if they were frightened donkeys
interpretation: This simile illustrates the state of disbelievers on the Day of Judgment, depicting their panic and confusion as akin to that of startled donkeys, emphasizing their fear and lack of direction in the face of divine retribution.
orig: كأنهم حمر مستنفرة

translation: I fled from Qusur
interpretation: This verse refers to a historical event where the speaker had to escape from a place called Qusur due to some compelling circumstances, possibly danger or persecution. It highlights themes of migration and seeking safety, which are recurrent in the Qur'an, emphasizing the human right to seek refuge and the divine protection over those who are forced to flee their homes.
orig: فرت من قسورة

translation: But every man among them desires that he should be given scriptures spread out.
interpretation: This verse suggests that each individual among the disbelievers wishes to receive a personal, clear, and direct revelation from God, tailored specifically to them, as a sign of their importance or as a means to justify their disbelief. It highlights a human tendency to seek personal validation or exceptions in matters of faith.
orig: بل يريد كل امرئ منهم أن يؤتى صحفا منشرة

translation: Nay, but they do not fear the Hereafter.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the reason people engage in disbelief or sinful behavior is not due to a lack of evidence or understanding, but rather because they do not have a genuine fear or concern for the consequences they will face in the afterlife. It emphasizes the importance of having a deep awareness and reverence for the Hereafter as a motivator for righteous conduct.
orig: كلا بل لا يخافون الآخرة

translation: Nay, indeed it is a reminder.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Qur'an's role as a reminder for humanity. It serves as a call to reflect on its message, urging believers to remember and adhere to the guidance it provides, reinforcing its importance and relevance in daily life.
orig: كلا إنه تذكرة

translation: So whoever wills may remember it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the freedom of choice given to individuals in their spiritual journey. It suggests that the message of the Qur'an is available to all, but it is up to each person's free will to engage with it, reflect upon it, and remember its teachings. The verse underscores the personal responsibility one has in seeking and maintaining a connection with the divine guidance.
orig: فمن شاء ذكره

translation: And they will not remember except if Allah wills. He is the One worthy of piety and the One who forgives.
interpretation: This verse underscores the concept of divine guidance and human free will. It suggests that the ability to remember and heed the message of the Qur'an is ultimately dependent on Allah's will. However, this does not negate human responsibility but rather emphasizes that true guidance comes from Allah. The verse also highlights Allah's attributes of being deserving of reverence (taqwa) and being the source of forgiveness, reminding believers of the importance of fearing Allah and seeking His forgiveness.
orig: وما يذكرون إلا أن يشاء الله هو أهل التقوى وأهل المغفرة

translation: I swear by the Day of Judgment
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the solemnity and certainty of the Day of Judgment, highlighting its importance and inevitability in the divine scheme of things. The use of an oath underscores the gravity and truth of the forthcoming statements about the Day of Judgment.
orig: لا أقسم بيوم القيامة

translation: And I swear by the self-reproaching soul
interpretation: This verse refers to the human conscience that constantly self-evaluates and feels remorse for its shortcomings and sins. It highlights the internal struggle and moral awareness within a person, urging them towards self-improvement and righteousness.
orig: ولا أقسم بالنفس اللوامة

translation: Does man think that We shall not assemble his bones?
interpretation: This verse challenges the human notion of disbelief in the resurrection. It questions whether people doubt Allah's power to reassemble their bones after death, emphasizing the certainty and ease with which Allah can bring about the resurrection. It serves as a reminder of Allah's omnipotence and the inevitability of the hereafter.
orig: أيحسب الإنسان ألن نجمع عظامه

translation: Yes, We are able to proportion his fingertips.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine power and precision of Allah, illustrating His capability to recreate even the minutest details of human anatomy, such as fingerprints, which are unique to each individual. It serves as a reminder of the resurrection and the meticulous nature of Allah's creation and re-creation.
orig: بلى قادرين على أن نسوي بنانه

translation: Nay, but man desires to continue in sin before him.
interpretation: This verse suggests that human beings often have a tendency to persist in their sinful behavior, desiring to continue living in a way that they know is wrong, yet they wish to do so without facing the consequences or being held accountable for their actions.
orig: بل يريد الإنسان ليفجر أمامه

translation: He asks, "When will be the Day of Resurrection?"
interpretation: This verse reflects the impatience or curiosity of a disbeliever questioning the timing of the Day of Resurrection, highlighting their skepticism about the hereafter and divine judgment.
orig: يسأل أيان يوم القيامة

translation: So when the sight is dazzled
interpretation: This verse refers to the moment of overwhelming awe and fear that will strike people on the Day of Judgment, when they will be confronted with the reality of their deeds and the majesty of Allah. The 'dazzling of the sight' symbolizes the intensity of this experience, where the enormity of the event causes a sensory overload, rendering people unable to fully comprehend what they are witnessing.
orig: فإذا برق البصر

translation: And the moon is eclipsed.
interpretation: This verse refers to a celestial event where the moon appears to be darkened or obscured, symbolizing a significant sign or event in the cosmic order that serves as a reminder of God's power and the transient nature of worldly phenomena.
orig: وخسف القمر

translation: And the sun and the moon are joined together.
interpretation: This verse refers to a future event on the Day of Judgment when the normal celestial order will be disrupted, symbolizing the end of time and the beginning of a new cosmic reality. The joining of the sun and the moon signifies the collapse of the familiar world and the onset of divine intervention and transformation.
orig: وجمع الشمس والقمر

translation: Man will say on that day, 'Where is the escape?'
interpretation: This verse reflects the human realization and panic on the Day of Judgment, when individuals will desperately seek a way to escape the accountability and consequences of their deeds. It underscores the inevitability of facing one's actions and the futility of seeking an escape from divine judgment.
orig: يقول الإنسان يومئذ أين المفر

translation: Nay, no refuge!
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability of facing the consequences of one's actions on the Day of Judgment. It suggests that there will be no escape or refuge from the accountability that awaits every individual. The word 'Nay' serves to strongly negate any possibility of finding a place to hide or avoid the divine judgment, underscoring the seriousness and inescapability of the event.
orig: كلا لا وزر

translation: To your Lord, that Day, is the [place of] permanence.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate reality that on the Day of Judgment, all things will return to Allah, signifying that He is the final destination and the eternal abode. It underscores the transient nature of worldly life and the permanence of the hereafter, reminding believers of the importance of preparing for that day by living righteously and submitting to Allah's will.
orig: إلى ربك يومئذ المستقر

translation: Man will be informed, that Day, of what he sent ahead and kept back.
interpretation: This verse indicates that on the Day of Judgment, every individual will be made fully aware of all their actions, both those performed in the past and those they postponed or neglected. It underscores the comprehensive accountability humans will face, emphasizing that nothing will be hidden or forgotten on that day.
orig: ينبأ الإنسان يومئذ بما قدم وأخر

translation: But man, against himself, is a clear witness.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of self-awareness and accountability in humans. It suggests that every individual possesses an inherent understanding of their own actions and intentions. This inner witness or consciousness serves as a testament to one's deeds, implying that people are fully aware of their moral and ethical choices, and thus, are responsible for them before God.
orig: بل الإنسان على نفسه بصيرة

translation: And if he had offered his excuses
interpretation: This verse suggests that even if someone were to present justifications or excuses for their actions, it might not change the outcome or the judgment upon them. It emphasizes the importance of sincerity and the potential futility of excuses when one's true intentions or actions are known.
orig: ولو ألقى معاذيره

translation: Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad not to rush in reciting the Qur'an as it is being revealed to him. It emphasizes patience and trust in the divine process of revelation, suggesting that the Prophet should wait for the complete message to be conveyed before he speaks it, rather than trying to memorize or recite it hastily.
orig: لا تحرك به لسانك لتعجل به

translation: Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the responsibility of gathering and preserving the Qur'an lies solely with Allah. It reassures believers that the Qur'an's compilation and its proper recitation are divinely managed, highlighting the divine protection and perfection of the text.
orig: إن علينا جمعه وقرآنه

translation: So when We recite it, then follow its recitation.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to the Qur'an's guidance as it is revealed. It instructs believers to attentively listen and follow the recitation of the Qur'an, indicating that the act of following its teachings is an immediate and ongoing responsibility. This underscores the dynamic relationship between the revelation and the believer's life, urging a continuous alignment with divine guidance.
orig: فإذا قرأناه فاتبع قرآنه

translation: Then upon Us is its explanation.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine responsibility to clarify and elucidate the message of the Qur'an. It reassures believers that Allah will ensure the proper understanding and interpretation of His revelation, emphasizing the completeness and clarity of the guidance provided in the Qur'an.
orig: ثم إن علينا بيانه

translation: Nay, but you prefer the life of this world,
interpretation: This verse critiques the human tendency to prioritize immediate worldly gains and pleasures over spiritual and eternal values. It suggests that people often choose the fleeting benefits of the present life, neglecting the importance of preparing for the hereafter.
orig: كلا بل تحبون العاجلة

translation: And you leave the Hereafter
interpretation: This verse is a critique of those who focus excessively on worldly matters and neglect their spiritual and moral obligations, which are crucial for their afterlife. It emphasizes the importance of preparing for the Hereafter, suggesting that neglecting it is a grave mistake.
orig: وتذرون الآخرة

translation: Faces that Day will be radiant
interpretation: This verse describes the state of the believers on the Day of Judgment, where their faces will be glowing and radiant due to the joy and happiness they experience from being close to Allah and receiving His pleasure and reward.
orig: وجوه يومئذ ناضرة

translation: Looking towards her Lord.
interpretation: This verse describes the state of the soul after death, where it is focused and attentive solely to Allah, its Creator. It signifies a state of complete submission and awareness of the divine presence, indicating the soul's ultimate return and accountability to God.
orig: إلى ربها ناظرة

translation: And [other] faces, that Day, will be radiant,
interpretation: This verse describes the state of the believers on the Day of Judgment. The 'radiant faces' symbolize the joy, happiness, and divine light that will be bestowed upon them as a result of their faith and righteous deeds. It reflects the ultimate reward and the blissful state they will experience in the presence of Allah.
orig: ووجوه يومئذ باسرة

translation: thinking that some calamity will befall it
interpretation: This verse reflects the human tendency to worry excessively about potential misfortunes. It highlights the psychological state of fear and anxiety that can grip individuals when they anticipate negative outcomes, illustrating the need for faith and trust in God's plan to alleviate such concerns.
orig: تظن أن يفعل بها فاقرة

translation: Nay, when the soul reaches the collarbone
interpretation: This verse refers to the moment of death when the soul begins to leave the body, symbolized by reaching the collarbone. It emphasizes the reality and inevitability of death, urging believers to reflect on their deeds and prepare for the afterlife.
orig: كلا إذا بلغت التراقي

translation: And it was said, 'Who is a magician?'
interpretation: This verse refers to a moment of inquiry or challenge within a narrative, likely pointing to a situation where supernatural or miraculous intervention is needed or questioned. It reflects a human tendency to seek out those with extraordinary abilities in times of need or crisis, highlighting themes of reliance on divine or exceptional human intervention.
orig: وقيل من راق

translation: And he thought that he would never part
interpretation: This verse reflects on the human tendency to become attached to worldly life, mistakenly believing that it will last forever. It highlights the importance of remembering the transient nature of life and preparing for the hereafter.
orig: وظن أنه الفراق

translation: And the leg will be intertwined with the leg
interpretation: This verse describes a state of extreme fear and distress on the Day of Judgment, where people will be so overwhelmed that they will lose control of their bodies, leading to their legs intertwining as they tremble in anticipation of their fate.
orig: والتفت الساق بالساق

translation: To your Lord, that Day, is the destination.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate reality that on the Day of Judgment, all beings will return to Allah, their Creator. It underscores the concept of accountability and the finality of returning to God, reminding believers of the importance of their actions in this life, as they will ultimately face their Lord.
orig: إلى ربك يومئذ المساق

translation: So he neither believed nor prayed.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequence of disbelief and neglect of prayer, illustrating a person who did not accept the message of faith nor engaged in the act of worship, which are fundamental aspects of spiritual life in Islam.
orig: فلا صدق ولا صلى

translation: But he denied and turned away.
interpretation: This verse reflects the attitude of someone who rejects the truth and deliberately turns away from guidance. It highlights a common human reaction to deny divine messages out of arrogance or stubbornness, choosing instead to follow their own path despite clear evidence presented to them.
orig: ولكن كذب وتولى

translation: Then he went to his family, walking with a heavy gait.
interpretation: This verse describes the Prophet Jonah (Yunus) after he was saved from the whale and returned to his people. The phrase "walking with a heavy gait" symbolizes his humility and repentance after his ordeal. It reflects the physical and emotional burden he felt, serving as a reminder of the consequences of disobedience to God and the importance of returning to one's community with a renewed sense of purpose and humility.
orig: ثم ذهب إلى أهله يتمطى

translation: Closer to you, so closer
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the proximity and immediacy of divine guidance or support to the individual. It suggests that whatever is beneficial or necessary for the person is made readily available and close at hand, reflecting the idea of God's mercy and care being ever-present and easily accessible.
orig: أولى لك فأولى

translation: Then for you the preference, so prefer.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of giving preference to the Prophet Muhammad in matters of guidance and decision-making. It suggests that since the Prophet has been given the ultimate guidance from Allah, it is incumbent upon the believers to follow his lead and give him precedence in their actions and decisions. The verse serves as a reminder of the Prophet's elevated status and the obligation of the community to adhere to his teachings and example.
orig: ثم أولى لك فأولى

translation: Does man think that he will be left neglected?
interpretation: This verse challenges the human belief that one's life and actions will not be accounted for after death. It emphasizes the concept of accountability in the hereafter, suggesting that every individual will be questioned about their deeds, and thus, should not live carelessly assuming there are no consequences.
orig: أيحسب الإنسان أن يترك سدى

translation: Was he not a drop of sperm emitted?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the humble origins of human beings, reminding us that every person begins as a mere drop of sperm. It serves as a reflection on human creation, highlighting the miraculous journey from such a small and seemingly insignificant beginning to the complex and capable beings that we become. This is meant to instill a sense of humility and gratitude towards the Creator, acknowledging His power and wisdom in the process of human development.
orig: ألم يك نطفة من مني يمنى

translation: Then of a clot; then He created and fashioned.
interpretation: This verse describes the stages of human creation, emphasizing the miraculous process from a mere clot of blood to a fully formed human being. It highlights Allah's power and precision in creation, illustrating how He not only creates but also shapes and perfects the creation, underscoring the divine craftsmanship involved in human development.
orig: ثم كان علقة فخلق فسوى

translation: So He made from it the two mates, the male and the female.
interpretation: This verse refers to the creation of human beings from a single soul, as mentioned in other parts of the Qur'an, and then splitting that soul into two genders, male and female. It highlights the divine origin and purpose of gender diversity, emphasizing the complementary nature of men and women in the human experience.
orig: فجعل منه الزوجين الذكر والأنثى

translation: Is He not able to give life to the dead?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence of Allah, highlighting His ability to resurrect the dead. It serves as a rhetorical question to affirm the belief in Allah's power over life and death, encouraging faith in the resurrection and the afterlife.
orig: أليس ذلك بقادر على أن يحيي الموتى

translation: Has there [not] come upon man a period of time when he was not a thing [even] mentioned?
interpretation: This verse reflects on the humble beginnings of human existence, reminding us that there was a time when each individual did not exist at all, not even as a concept or mention. It serves as a profound reminder of our origins from nothingness, urging humility and gratitude towards the Creator who brought us into being.
orig: هل أتى على الإنسان حين من الدهر لم يكن شيئا مذكورا

translation: Indeed, We created man from a mixture of sperm; We test him, so We made him hearing and seeing.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine origin and purpose of human creation. It highlights that humans are created from humble beginnings ("a mixture of sperm"), yet endowed with the faculties of hearing and sight. These faculties are not just biological attributes but are means through which humans are tested in their life on earth. The verse suggests that the trials humans face are part of a divine plan to assess their use of the senses and their moral and spiritual responses to the world around them.
orig: إنا خلقنا الإنسان من نطفة أمشاج نبتليه فجعلناه سميعا بصيرا

translation: Indeed, We have guided him to the path, be he grateful or be he ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine guidance provided to every individual, indicating that Allah has shown the right path to all humans. It highlights the freedom of choice given to humans, as they can choose to be grateful and follow the guidance or be ungrateful and reject it. The verse underscores the responsibility of individuals in their response to divine guidance.
orig: إنا هديناه السبيل إما شاكرا وإما كفورا

translation: Indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers chains and shackles and a blazing fire.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who reject faith, illustrating the severe consequences awaiting them in the hereafter. The mention of 'chains and shackles' symbolizes the restriction and punishment they will face, while 'a blazing fire' represents the intense suffering and torment of Hell. It underscores the justice of God, emphasizing that disbelief and rejection of divine guidance will not go unpunished.
orig: إنا أعتدنا للكافرين سلاسل وأغلالا وسعيرا

translation: Indeed, the righteous will drink from a cup [of wine] whose mixture is of camphor.
interpretation: This verse describes the reward awaiting the righteous in the afterlife, symbolized by drinking from a special cup. The mention of camphor, known for its cooling and purifying properties, suggests that this drink will provide comfort and purity, reflecting the spiritual state of the righteous in Paradise.
orig: إن الأبرار يشربون من كأس كان مزاجها كافورا

translation: Two springs from which the servants of Allah drink; they will cause them to gush forth.
interpretation: This verse describes the provision of two springs in Paradise, symbolizing the abundant and pure blessings that the righteous servants of Allah will enjoy. The act of causing the springs to gush forth signifies the ease and generosity with which Allah provides for His devoted followers in the afterlife.
orig: عينا يشرب بها عباد الله يفجرونها تفجيرا

translation: They fulfill their vows and fear a Day whose evil will be widespread.
interpretation: This verse highlights the characteristics of the righteous who not only keep their promises and commitments but also maintain a constant awareness of the Day of Judgment. The fear of this day motivates them to uphold their vows, as they are conscious of the severe consequences of failing to do so. The 'Day whose evil will be widespread' refers to the Day of Judgment, emphasizing its universal impact and the intensity of its trials, urging believers to live righteously and fulfill their obligations.
orig: يوفون بالنذر ويخافون يوما كان شره مستطيرا

translation: And they give food, out of love for Him, to the poor, the orphan, and the captive
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of selfless giving and charity motivated purely by the love of Allah. It emphasizes that true believers provide sustenance to the most vulnerable in society—the poor, orphans, and captives—not seeking any worldly reward but solely to please Allah. This act of kindness reflects a deep spiritual connection and commitment to the values of compassion and generosity that are central to Islamic teachings.
orig: ويطعمون الطعام على حبه مسكينا ويتيما وأسيرا

translation: We feed you only for the sake of Allah; we desire from you neither recompense nor thanks.
interpretation: This verse highlights the purity of intention in acts of charity. The believers are expressing that their motivation for providing food to others is solely to seek the pleasure of Allah, without any expectation of reward or gratitude from the recipients. This reflects the Islamic principle of 'ikhlas' or sincerity, where actions are performed purely for the sake of Allah, emphasizing the spiritual over the material or social recognition.
orig: إنما نطعمكم لوجه الله لا نريد منكم جزاء ولا شكورا

translation: Indeed, we fear from our Lord a Day, austere and distressful.
interpretation: This verse expresses a deep sense of fear and reverence towards Allah, highlighting the believers' awareness of the severity of the Day of Judgment. It underscores the importance of being conscious of one's actions in this life, as the Day of Judgment is described as 'austere and distressful,' indicating its overwhelming and inescapable nature. This fear serves as a motivator for righteous behavior and adherence to divine commandments.
orig: إنا نخاف من ربنا يوما عبوسا قمطريرا

translation: Allah will avert from them the evil of that Day, and will make them meet with radiance and joy.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's mercy and protection towards the believers on the Day of Judgment. It signifies that Allah will shield them from the horrors and tribulations of that Day, replacing their fear and anxiety with a state of happiness and contentment. The 'radiance and joy' they encounter is a reflection of the divine favor and the ultimate reward for their faith and righteous deeds.
orig: فوقاهم الله شر ذلك اليوم ولقاهم نضرة وسرورا

translation: And We will reward them for their patience with a Garden and silk.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine promise of reward for those who exhibit patience in their faith and actions. The 'Garden' symbolizes Paradise, a place of eternal bliss and reward, while 'silk' represents the luxurious and pure attire provided to the dwellers of Paradise. The mention of these rewards underscores the value of steadfastness and endurance in the face of life's trials, promising believers that their perseverance will be met with divine generosity and honor in the afterlife.
orig: وجزاهم بما صبروا جنة وحريرا

translation: Reclining therein on couches, they will see neither the sun nor bitter cold.
interpretation: This verse describes the blissful environment of Paradise where the inhabitants enjoy comfort and peace without being affected by extreme weather conditions. The absence of the sun and cold symbolizes a state of perpetual comfort and protection from any form of discomfort or hardship, emphasizing the perfect climate and serene atmosphere of the afterlife.
orig: متكئين فيها على الأرائك لا يرون فيها شمسا ولا زمهريرا

translation: And the shade thereof is close upon them, and the clusters of fruit thereof will be brought low, within reach.
interpretation: This verse describes the bountiful and accessible nature of Paradise. The shade being close suggests a comforting and protective environment, while the fruits being brought low indicates that the blessings of Paradise are easily attainable and abundant, symbolizing the ease and joy with which the inhabitants can enjoy its pleasures.
orig: ودانية عليهم ظلالها وذللت قطوفها تذليلا

translation: And they will be served with vessels of silver and cups of crystal
interpretation: This verse describes the luxurious and pure nature of the rewards in Paradise. The use of silver vessels and crystal cups symbolizes the high quality and clarity of the blessings bestowed upon the righteous, reflecting the purity and perfection of the afterlife.
orig: ويطاف عليهم بآنية من فضة وأكواب كانت قواريرا

translation: Crystal-clear, made of silver: they have determined its measure exactly.
interpretation: This verse describes the cups in Paradise, highlighting their exquisite nature made of silver and perfectly measured, symbolizing the precision and perfection of everything in the afterlife. It underscores the meticulous care and attention to detail in the creation of Paradise, reflecting the ultimate beauty and satisfaction that awaits the believers.
orig: قوارير من فضة قدروها تقديرا

translation: And they will be given to drink a cup [of wine] whose mixture is of ginger.
interpretation: This verse describes the pleasures of Paradise, where the believers will enjoy a special drink. The mention of ginger as a mixture in the drink signifies the unique and refreshing qualities of the beverages in Paradise, symbolizing purity and the enhancement of the drink's taste and health benefits. It reflects the perfection and delight of the heavenly rewards awaiting the righteous.
orig: ويسقون فيها كأسا كان مزاجها زنجبيلا

translation: A spring therein called Salsabil.
interpretation: This verse refers to a specific spring in Paradise named Salsabil, symbolizing the purity and delight of the rewards awaiting the righteous. The mention of Salsabil highlights the detailed and exquisite nature of Paradise, where even the names of elements contribute to the overall sense of peace and satisfaction.
orig: عينا فيها تسمى سلسبيلا

translation: And there will circulate among them young boys made eternal. When you see them, you would think them [as beautiful as] scattered pearls.
interpretation: This verse describes the beauty and purity of the young servants in Paradise, who are likened to scattered pearls, symbolizing their flawless and radiant appearance. This imagery emphasizes the perfection and eternal youth of the inhabitants of Paradise, enhancing the overall picture of a blissful and serene afterlife.
orig: ويطوف عليهم ولدان مخلدون إذا رأيتهم حسبتهم لؤلؤا منثورا

translation: And when you see, then you see a delight and a great dominion
interpretation: This verse describes the experience of witnessing Paradise, where the believer will see immense joy and a magnificent kingdom, symbolizing the ultimate reward and beauty of the afterlife.
orig: وإذا رأيت ثم رأيت نعيما وملكا كبيرا

translation: Upon them will be green garments of fine silk and brocade, and they will be adorned with bracelets of silver, and their Lord will give them a purifying drink.
interpretation: This verse describes the attire and adornments of the inhabitants of Paradise, symbolizing their purity and elevated status. The green garments of fine silk and brocade represent the beauty and luxury bestowed upon them, while the silver bracelets signify honor and dignity. The purifying drink provided by their Lord underscores the spiritual cleansing and eternal bliss they experience in the afterlife.
orig: عاليهم ثياب سندس خضر وإستبرق وحلوا أساور من فضة وسقاهم ربهم شرابا طهورا

translation: Indeed, this is for you a reward, and your effort has been appreciated.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine reward and recognition for the efforts of the believers. It reassures them that their striving in the path of righteousness and their good deeds are not in vain, but are acknowledged and rewarded by Allah. The promise of a reward serves as a motivation for continued perseverance and dedication in faith and good actions.
orig: إن هذا كان لكم جزاء وكان سعيكم مشكورا

translation: Indeed, it is We who have sent down the Qur'an to you in stages.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin of the Qur'an, asserting that it is a revelation directly from Allah to the Prophet Muhammad. The use of 'We' signifies the majesty and plurality of Allah's command. The phrase 'in stages' indicates that the Qur'an was revealed gradually over time, which allowed for the teachings to be absorbed and implemented progressively by the early Muslim community. This method of revelation also served as a continuous guidance and support for the Prophet in his mission.
orig: إنا نحن نزلنا عليك القرآن تنزيلا

translation: So be patient with the decree of your Lord, and do not obey from among them a sinner or a disbeliever.
interpretation: This verse encourages steadfastness and patience in adhering to the divine guidance and rulings of Allah, emphasizing the importance of not being swayed by the influence of those who are morally corrupt or who reject faith. It underscores the need for a believer to maintain their integrity and commitment to Allah's path, even in the face of opposition or temptation from sinners and disbelievers.
orig: فاصبر لحكم ربك ولا تطع منهم آثما أو كفورا

translation: And remember the name of your Lord morning and evening.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining a constant connection with Allah through remembrance (dhikr) throughout the day. By remembering Allah in the morning and evening, it helps believers to start and end their day with mindfulness and gratitude, fostering a continuous awareness of God's presence and blessings in their lives.
orig: واذكر اسم ربك بكرة وأصيلا

translation: And from the night, prostrate to Him and glorify Him a long part of the night.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to dedicate a significant portion of their night to worship and devotion to Allah. It emphasizes the importance of engaging in acts of prostration and glorification during the night, which is a time of tranquility and spiritual connection. This practice is meant to strengthen one's faith and bring them closer to Allah through sincere and prolonged worship.
orig: ومن الليل فاسجد له وسبحه ليلا طويلا

translation: Verily, these people love the fleeting life and leave behind them a heavy Day.
interpretation: This verse critiques those who prioritize the temporary pleasures and material gains of this worldly life over the eternal life to come. It suggests that such individuals are so engrossed in immediate gratification that they neglect to prepare for the Day of Judgment, which is described as a 'heavy Day' due to its seriousness and the accountability it entails. The verse serves as a reminder to focus on the hereafter and not to be distracted by the ephemeral nature of worldly life.
orig: إن هؤلاء يحبون العاجلة ويذرون وراءهم يوما ثقيلا

translation: We created them and strengthened their forms, and when We will, We can change them completely.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's absolute power over creation. It highlights that humans are created by God and their physical forms are under His control. The mention of replacing them with others signifies the transient nature of human life and God's ability to alter or renew creation at His discretion, underscoring the themes of divine omnipotence and the impermanence of worldly existence.
orig: نحن خلقناهم وشددنا أسرهم وإذا شئنا بدلنا أمثالهم تبديلا

translation: Indeed, this is a reminder, so whoever wills may take a path to his Lord.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Qur'an's role as a reminder and an invitation to spiritual guidance. It highlights the freedom of choice given to individuals; anyone who desires can choose to follow the path that leads to closeness with their Lord. The verse underscores the personal responsibility of each person to engage with the divine message and act upon it.
orig: إن هذه تذكرة فمن شاء اتخذ إلى ربه سبيلا

translation: And you do not will except that Allah wills. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse underscores the concept of divine sovereignty and human free will. It suggests that while humans have the capacity to make choices, these choices are ultimately within the framework of Allah's overarching will. The verse emphasizes that Allah's knowledge and wisdom encompass all things, indicating that His will is perfectly aligned with His complete understanding and wise judgment of all situations.
orig: وما تشاءون إلا أن يشاء الله إن الله كان عليما حكيما

translation: He admits into His mercy whom He wills, and for the wrongdoers He has prepared a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine prerogative of Allah to extend His mercy to whomever He chooses, reflecting His infinite wisdom and justice. Conversely, it also serves as a stern reminder that those who engage in wrongdoing will face a severe punishment, emphasizing the consequences of one's actions in the divine order.
orig: يدخل من يشاء في رحمته والظالمين أعد لهم عذابا أليما

translation: And [by] the winds sent forth one after another
interpretation: This verse refers to the divine messengers or angels who are sent forth with specific missions, symbolizing the swift and orderly execution of God's commands. The term 'عرفا' suggests a sequence and continuity, emphasizing the relentless and purposeful nature of these divine agents in carrying out their tasks.
orig: والمرسلات عرفا

translation: Then the 'assaulting' assault.
interpretation: This verse refers to the intense and powerful winds that will accompany the Day of Judgment, symbolizing the overwhelming and inescapable nature of the events that will unfold. It underscores the severity and the suddenness with which the end times will come upon humanity.
orig: فالعاصفات عصفا

translation: And the spreaders spreading
interpretation: This verse refers to the angels who are tasked with spreading the souls of the deceased, dispersing them to their destined places in the afterlife. It highlights the meticulous and organized nature of the divine system governing life and death.
orig: والناشرات نشرا

translation: So the word was justified against them, and We made them as dust scattered.
interpretation: This verse reflects the consequence of disbelief and rejection of divine messages. The term 'fāraqāt' (فَارِقَات) symbolizes the disintegration and scattering, illustrating how those who deny the truth are ultimately dispersed and their influence diminished to nothingness, akin to dust blown away by the wind. This serves as a powerful metaphor for the transient nature of worldly power and the ultimate triumph of divine justice.
orig: فالفارقات فرقا

translation: Then the sperm-drop is cast forth,
interpretation: This verse refers to the moment of conception when the sperm is released, highlighting the miraculous beginning of human life from a mere drop, emphasizing the power and precision of Allah's creation.
orig: فالملقيات ذكرا

translation: Apology or warning
interpretation: This phrase suggests a choice between seeking forgiveness for past actions or issuing a stern warning for future behavior. It emphasizes the dual paths of reconciliation and deterrence, reflecting the Qur'an's guidance on personal accountability and societal order.
orig: عذرا أو نذرا

translation: What you are promised will surely come to pass.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty and inevitability of the events foretold in the Qur'an, such as the Day of Judgment and the afterlife. It serves as a reminder to believers to remain steadfast in their faith and actions, knowing that the promises of Allah are true and will be fulfilled without fail.
