translation: So where are you going?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question posed to the disbelievers, challenging them on the direction and purpose of their lives and beliefs, emphasizing the futility of their path away from the truth and guidance of Islam.
orig: فأين تذهبون

translation: It is but a reminder to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is not just a message for a specific group or time, but a universal reminder and guidance for all humanity and all creation, underscoring its timeless and inclusive nature.
orig: إن هو إلا ذكر للعالمين

translation: For whoever wills among you to take a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of free will in Islam, indicating that the choice to follow the straight path of righteousness is available to every individual. It underscores personal responsibility in one's spiritual journey, suggesting that guidance and success are attainable for those who consciously choose to pursue them.
orig: لمن شاء منكم أن يستقيم

translation: And you do not will except that Allah wills - Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine will and predestination in Islam. It suggests that human free will is ultimately subject to the overarching will of Allah. While humans may desire and choose certain actions, these choices are within the framework of what Allah has willed. The phrase 'Lord of the worlds' underscores Allah's sovereignty and dominion over all creation, reinforcing the idea that His will is supreme and all-encompassing.
orig: وما تشاءون إلا أن يشاء الله رب العالمين

translation: When the sky is split open
interpretation: This verse refers to a significant eschatological event, signaling the onset of the Day of Judgment. The splitting of the sky symbolizes the disruption of the natural order, indicating the transition from the temporal world to the eternal realm where divine justice will be fully manifested.
orig: إذا السماء انفطرت

translation: And when the stars are scattered
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, symbolizing the disintegration and chaos that will occur at the end of the world. The scattering of the stars signifies the breaking apart of the cosmic order, illustrating the immense power and inevitability of God's final decree.
orig: وإذا الكواكب انتثرت

translation: And when the seas are set ablaze
interpretation: This verse refers to a cataclysmic event on the Day of Judgment, symbolizing the complete upheaval and transformation of the world as we know it. The image of the seas being set ablaze underscores the severity and the extraordinary nature of the events that will unfold, serving as a reminder of the power of Allah and the inevitability of the end times.
orig: وإذا البحار فجرت

translation: And when the graves are scattered
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when the graves will be overturned and the dead will be resurrected. It symbolizes the ultimate power of Allah to bring life after death, emphasizing the certainty and inevitability of the resurrection.
orig: وإذا القبور بعثرت

translation: The soul knows what it has brought forward and what it has left behind.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the self-awareness of the soul regarding its actions, both past and future. It suggests that every individual is fully conscious of their deeds and the consequences that follow, highlighting the personal accountability in the eyes of God.
orig: علمت نفس ما قدمت وأخرت

translation: O mankind, what has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question aimed at humanity, urging introspection about their ingratitude and neglect towards Allah, who is described as 'the Generous.' It highlights the human tendency to be distracted by worldly matters and forget the immense generosity and blessings bestowed by their Creator. The term 'Generous' emphasizes Allah's continuous provision and kindness, prompting reflection on why humans fail to recognize and appreciate this generosity.
orig: يا أيها الإنسان ما غرك بربك الكريم

translation: He who created you, then proportioned you, then balanced you.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the meticulous process of human creation by Allah, highlighting three stages: creation, proportioning, and balancing. It underscores the divine wisdom and precision in the formation of every human being, suggesting that each individual is crafted with a specific purpose and design, reflecting the perfection and care of the Creator.
orig: الذي خلقك فسواك فعدلك

translation: In whatever form He willed, He assembled you.
interpretation: This verse highlights the omnipotence and creative power of Allah, emphasizing that He has the ability to create and shape humans in any form He desires. It underscores the idea that human existence and form are a result of divine will and design, reflecting the intricate and purposeful nature of creation.
orig: في أي صورة ما شاء ركبك

translation: Nay! But you deny the Recompense (the Day of Resurrection).
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the human tendency to reject the concept of accountability in the afterlife. It suggests that people often deny the reality of the Day of Resurrection out of fear or disbelief, choosing instead to live as if there will be no consequences for their actions. This denial is portrayed as a fundamental error in judgment, highlighting the importance of faith in the divine system of justice and recompense.
orig: كلا بل تكذبون بالدين

translation: And indeed, over you are guardians
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the presence of divine guardians or angels assigned to watch over and record the deeds of every individual. It serves as a reminder of accountability and the constant supervision by these celestial beings, encouraging believers to be mindful of their actions knowing that they are always observed and their deeds are accounted for.
orig: وإن عليكم لحافظين

translation: Honorable scribes
interpretation: This phrase refers to the angels who record the deeds of humans. They are described as 'honorable' to emphasize their high status and the importance of their task in the divine order. These scribes meticulously document every action, ensuring that justice and accountability are maintained in the afterlife.
orig: كراما كاتبين

translation: They know what you do
interpretation: This verse suggests that the actions of individuals are known and observed by others, possibly referring to the awareness of one's deeds by the community or by divine entities. It emphasizes the concept of accountability and the transparency of one's actions in the eyes of others.
orig: يعلمون ما تفعلون

translation: Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate reward awaiting those who lead a life of righteousness and piety. It assures believers that their steadfastness in faith and good deeds will be met with eternal happiness and comfort in the hereafter. The term 'bliss' here connotes a state of profound joy and satisfaction, far beyond worldly pleasures, indicating the supreme nature of the reward in Paradise.
orig: إن الأبرار لفي نعيم

translation: And indeed, the wicked will be in Hellfire.
interpretation: This verse underscores the Qur'anic teaching on the consequences of moral and spiritual corruption. It serves as a reminder that those who persistently engage in wrongdoing and reject divine guidance will ultimately find themselves in Hellfire, which symbolizes the ultimate state of suffering and separation from God's mercy. This serves as a warning to individuals to reflect on their actions and strive towards righteousness.
orig: وإن الفجار لفي جحيم

translation: They will taste it on the Day of Judgment
interpretation: This verse refers to the experience of the punishment of Hellfire that the disbelievers will endure on the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes the certainty and inevitability of this divine retribution, serving as a warning to heed the message of the Qur'an and to live righteously.
orig: يصلونها يوم الدين

translation: And they are not absent from it.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the disbelievers, despite their denial, are not far from the reality of the Day of Judgment. It emphasizes that they will inevitably face the consequences of their actions, as they are not hidden or exempt from the divine judgment that awaits them.
orig: وما هم عنها بغائبين

translation: And what will make you know what the Day of Judgment is?
interpretation: This rhetorical question emphasizes the profound and mysterious nature of the Day of Judgment, highlighting its significance and the human inability to fully comprehend its reality and magnitude.
orig: وما أدراك ما يوم الدين

translation: Then, what can make you know what is the Day of Recompense?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the profound and mysterious nature of the Day of Judgment, suggesting that its true essence and significance are beyond human comprehension, serving as a rhetorical question to provoke deep reflection on the severity and inevitability of that day.
orig: ثم ما أدراك ما يوم الدين

translation: The Day when no soul will have power [to do] anything for another soul; and the command that Day will be [entirely] with Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and justice of Allah on the Day of Judgment. It highlights that on that day, no individual will be able to intercede or help another, underscoring the personal accountability each soul has before Allah. The command and authority belong solely to Allah, reinforcing the concept that all judgments and decisions on that day are under His exclusive control, ensuring fairness and equity in the divine reckoning.
orig: يوم لا تملك نفس لنفس شيئا والأمر يومئذ لله

translation: Woe to those who give less [than due]
interpretation: This verse condemns those who engage in dishonest practices, specifically in trade and commerce, by cheating others through giving less than what is rightfully due. It highlights the moral and ethical responsibility to be fair and just in all dealings, warning of severe consequences for those who fail to uphold these values.
orig: ويل للمطففين

translation: Those who, when they have to measure out to the people, take full measure
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of honesty and fairness in transactions. It specifically addresses those who are meticulous in ensuring they receive full measure when dealing with others, emphasizing the moral obligation to be just and not to shortchange others in business or any form of exchange.
orig: الذين إذا اكتالوا على الناس يستوفون

translation: And when they measure or weigh for them, they give less than due.
interpretation: This verse highlights the unethical practice of cheating in transactions by giving less than what is rightfully due when measuring or weighing goods. It serves as a critique of dishonesty and exploitation in commercial dealings, emphasizing the importance of integrity and fairness in economic interactions.
orig: وإذا كالوهم أو وزنوهم يخسرون

translation: Do they not think that they will be resurrected?
interpretation: This verse challenges the disbelievers' denial of the afterlife, urging them to reflect on the possibility of resurrection. It emphasizes the Qur'an's call for introspection and belief in the Day of Judgment, highlighting the accountability of one's actions in this life.
orig: ألا يظن أولئك أنهم مبعوثون

translation: For a great day
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, emphasizing its monumental significance and the profound impact it will have on all of creation. It underscores the importance of preparing for this inevitable event by living a righteous life according to the teachings of Islam.
orig: ليوم عظيم

translation: The Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, emphasizing the moment when all of humanity will be resurrected and gathered to stand in front of Allah, the Creator and Sustainer of all existence, to be held accountable for their deeds. It highlights the universal nature of this event, where every individual, regardless of their status or background, will face their Lord.
orig: يوم يقوم الناس لرب العالمين

translation: Nay, indeed, the record of the wicked is in Sijjin.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty and inevitability of the recording of the deeds of the wicked in a specific register called Sijjin, which is a place or record where the evil actions of individuals are documented. It underscores the concept of divine justice and accountability, indicating that no evil deed goes unrecorded or unpunished in the hereafter.
orig: كلا إن كتاب الفجار لفي سجين

translation: And what can make you know what Sijjin is?
interpretation: This rhetorical question emphasizes the mysterious and terrifying nature of Sijjin, a place or record where the deeds of the wicked are kept, highlighting its significance and the gravity of the consequences for those whose records are stored there.
orig: وما أدراك ما سجين

translation: A Book inscribed
interpretation: This refers to the Qur'an, which is described as a book that is meticulously recorded and preserved by Allah. The term 'inscribed' emphasizes the divine origin and the eternal nature of the Qur'an, suggesting that it is a permanent and unalterable record of God's message to humanity.
orig: كتاب مرقوم

translation: Woe, that Day, to the deniers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to those who reject the truth of the Qur'an and the message of Islam. It emphasizes the severity of the consequences that await the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment, highlighting the gravity of their denial and the impending doom they will face.
orig: ويل يومئذ للمكذبين

translation: Those who deny the Day of Judgment
interpretation: This verse refers to individuals who reject the concept of accountability after death, specifically the belief in a final day when all souls will be judged by Allah for their deeds. Denial of this day is considered a grave error, as it undermines the moral and ethical framework that the belief in an afterlife provides, encouraging righteousness and deterring wrongdoing.
orig: الذين يكذبون بيوم الدين

translation: And none denies it except every transgressor, every sinner.
interpretation: This verse suggests that only those who are deeply entrenched in wrongdoing and sin would reject the truth of the Qur'an. It highlights the moral and spiritual state of the deniers, indicating that their rejection stems from their own transgressions and sinful nature rather than from any lack of evidence or clarity in the message itself.
orig: وما يكذب به إلا كل معتد أثيم

translation: When Our verses are recited to him, he says, 'Myths of the ancients.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the dismissive attitude of those who reject the Qur'an, labeling its revelations as mere folklore or legends from the past, indicating their refusal to accept the divine message due to their preconceived notions and biases.
orig: إذا تتلى عليه آياتنا قال أساطير الأولين

translation: Nay, but that which they have earned is rust upon their hearts.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the wrongdoings and sins committed by individuals have a corrosive effect on their hearts, metaphorically described as 'rust'. This rust prevents them from perceiving the truth and accepting guidance, illustrating how one's actions can spiritually blind them and distance them from righteousness.
orig: كلا بل ران على قلوبهم ما كانوا يكسبون

translation: Nay, they will be veiled from their Lord on that Day.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgment, those who denied the truth and turned away from God's guidance will be completely cut off from experiencing the presence and mercy of their Lord. This verse emphasizes the spiritual consequence of their actions, indicating a profound separation and isolation from divine connection due to their rejection of faith.
orig: كلا إنهم عن ربهم يومئذ لمحجوبون

translation: Then indeed, they will [enter and] burn in Hellfire.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the consequence of disbelief and sinful actions, indicating that those who reject faith will ultimately face the punishment of Hellfire. It serves as a stark reminder of the accountability for one's deeds in the afterlife.
orig: ثم إنهم لصالو الجحيم

translation: Then it will be said, 'This is what you used to deny.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of the Day of Judgment when the disbelievers will be confronted with the reality of the afterlife and the truth of the messages they rejected during their earthly lives. It underscores the theme of accountability and the consequences of denying the truth, illustrating how denial in this world leads to a moment of realization and regret in the hereafter.
orig: ثم يقال هذا الذي كنتم به تكذبون

translation: Nay, indeed the record of the righteous is in 'Illiyun.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the exalted status of the righteous in the hereafter. The term 'Illiyun refers to a high place in heaven where the records of the deeds of the righteous are kept, symbolizing their elevated spiritual rank and the honor they receive from Allah. It reassures believers that their good deeds are not only recorded but preserved in a noble and esteemed location, reflecting their closeness to divine favor.
orig: كلا إن كتاب الأبرار لفي عليين

translation: And what will make you know what is 'Illiyun'?
interpretation: This rhetorical question in the Qur'an emphasizes the mysterious and exalted nature of 'Illiyun', a high place in Paradise where the records of the righteous are kept, suggesting that its true essence and significance are beyond human comprehension.
orig: وما أدراك ما عليون

translation: A Book well-guarded
interpretation: This phrase refers to the Qur'an, emphasizing its divine origin and protection from corruption. It underscores the belief that the Qur'an is preserved by Allah and remains unchanged, highlighting its sanctity and reliability as a source of guidance.
orig: كتاب مرقوم

translation: The angels near to Him bear witness to it.
interpretation: This verse refers to the angels who are closest to Allah, indicating their role in affirming and testifying to the truth of Allah's decrees and the reality of His divine presence. Their testimony underscores the certainty and the sacredness of Allah's commands and the events that unfold according to His will.
orig: يشهده المقربون

translation: Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate reward awaiting those who lead a life of righteousness and piety. It assures believers that their steadfastness in faith and good deeds will be met with eternal happiness and comfort in the hereafter, highlighting the concept of divine justice and the promise of paradise for the virtuous.
orig: إن الأبرار لفي نعيم

translation: On thrones, they will be gazing
interpretation: This verse depicts the state of the righteous in Paradise, where they are comfortably seated on thrones, enjoying a position of honor and leisure. The act of gazing suggests a state of contentment and satisfaction, as they observe the blessings and beauty of their eternal abode.
orig: على الأرائك ينظرون

translation: You will recognize in their faces the radiance of bliss.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the believers in Paradise will have a visible glow or radiance on their faces, which is a sign of the immense joy and happiness they experience. This radiance is a physical manifestation of their inner state of bliss and contentment, reflecting the spiritual purity and fulfillment they have attained in the afterlife.
orig: تعرف في وجوههم نضرة النعيم

translation: They will be given to drink of a sealed wine.
interpretation: This verse refers to the pure and delightful drinks that the righteous will enjoy in Paradise. The 'sealed wine' symbolizes the exclusivity and perfection of the pleasures in the afterlife, untouched and preserved for the believers as a reward for their faith and good deeds.
orig: يسقون من رحيق مختوم

translation: Its seal is musk. So for this let the competitors compete.
interpretation: This verse describes the ultimate reward in Paradise, symbolized by musk, which represents purity and luxury. It encourages believers to strive and compete in righteous deeds to attain this sublime reward, highlighting the value of perseverance and effort in one's spiritual journey.
orig: ختامه مسك وفي ذلك فليتنافس المتنافسون

translation: And its mixture is of Tasnim.
interpretation: This verse refers to the drink of the righteous in Paradise, which is mixed with Tasnim, a special fountain in Paradise. The mention of Tasnim highlights the purity and exclusivity of the drink, symbolizing the ultimate reward and pleasure that awaits the believers in the afterlife.
orig: ومزاجه من تسنيم

translation: Two springs from which those brought near [to Allah] drink
interpretation: This verse refers to the two springs in Paradise, which are a reward for those who were closest to Allah in their earthly lives. These springs symbolize the ultimate refreshment and purity that the righteous will enjoy in the afterlife, signifying their elevated status and the special blessings they receive due to their nearness to Allah.
orig: عينا يشرب بها المقربون

translation: Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed.
interpretation: This verse highlights the mockery and derision that believers often face from those who engage in wrongdoing. It points to a common social dynamic where faith and righteousness are ridiculed by those who do not adhere to moral or religious standards. The verse serves as a reminder to believers that such ridicule is a historical and ongoing challenge, encouraging steadfastness in faith despite opposition.
orig: إن الذين أجرموا كانوا من الذين آمنوا يضحكون

translation: And when they pass by them, they wink at each other.
interpretation: This verse highlights the secretive and mocking behavior of some people towards the believers. It suggests that when these individuals encounter the believers, they exchange subtle signals or gestures among themselves, indicating their disdain or ridicule. This behavior reflects their inner hypocrisy and the superficial nature of their interactions, emphasizing the moral contrast between the believers and those who mock them.
orig: وإذا مروا بهم يتغامزون

translation: And when they return to their people, they return jesting.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of certain individuals who mock the teachings of Islam in private after appearing to accept them in public. It points to a deeper issue of insincerity and the lack of true faith, where people might conform outwardly to societal or religious expectations but internally remain detached and even derisive. This behavior not only undermines their own spiritual growth but also spreads doubt and confusion among others.
orig: وإذا انقلبوا إلى أهلهم انقلبوا فكهين

translation: And when they see them, they say, 'Indeed, these are truly astray.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the judgmental attitude of some people towards believers. It reflects how those who are misguided or disbelieving often label the righteous as being lost or astray, showcasing their inability to recognize true guidance. This serves as a reminder to believers to remain steadfast in their faith despite such criticisms.
orig: وإذا رأوهم قالوا إن هؤلاء لضالون

translation: And We did not send guardians over them.
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah did not appoint specific protectors or guardians to watch over the people mentioned, emphasizing human free will and accountability for their actions. It suggests that individuals are responsible for their own choices and the consequences thereof, without divine intermediaries constantly overseeing them.
orig: وما أرسلوا عليهم حافظين

translation: So today those who believed are laughing at the disbelievers
interpretation: This verse illustrates the reversal of fortunes on the Day of Judgment, where the believers, who may have faced ridicule or hardship in worldly life, will find joy and vindication as they witness the disbelievers facing the consequences of their disbelief. It emphasizes the ultimate triumph and happiness of the faithful.
orig: فاليوم الذين آمنوا من الكفار يضحكون

translation: On thrones, they will be looking.
interpretation: This verse describes the scene in Paradise where the believers are seated comfortably on thrones, enjoying a position of honor and ease. The act of looking suggests they are observing the blessings and beauty around them, indicating a state of contentment and fulfillment in the afterlife.
orig: على الأرائك ينظرون

translation: Is then the recompense of the disbelievers anything but what they used to do?
interpretation: This verse suggests that the ultimate consequence or recompense for those who disbelieve will be directly related to their actions during their lifetime. It implies a principle of justice where the outcome for disbelievers is a reflection of their deeds, emphasizing accountability and the natural consequence of one's choices.
orig: هل ثوب الكفار ما كانوا يفعلون

translation: When the sky is split asunder
interpretation: This verse refers to a future event, signaling the onset of the Day of Judgment. The splitting of the sky symbolizes the breaking of the established order, heralding a time of reckoning and transformation, where the unseen realities will become manifest.
orig: إذا السماء انشقت

translation: And she accepted the truth from her Lord and believed.
interpretation: This verse highlights the moment of acceptance and belief in divine truth by a female figure, likely referring to Maryam (Mary), showcasing her submission to God's will and her faith. It underscores the importance of recognizing and embracing the truth as revealed by God, illustrating a model of faith and obedience.
orig: وأذنت لربها وحقت

translation: And when the earth is stretched out
interpretation: This verse refers to the event of the Day of Judgment when the earth will be transformed and expanded, symbolizing the complete alteration of the physical world as we know it, to prepare for the resurrection and gathering of all beings.
orig: وإذا الأرض مدت

translation: And it casts out what is within it and becomes empty
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Judgment when the earth will expel all that is buried within it, including the dead, as a sign of the complete upheaval and transformation of the world. It signifies the resurrection and the accountability of all beings before God.
orig: وألقت ما فيها وتخلت

translation: And she accepted her Lord's command and He made it true
interpretation: This verse refers to Mary, the mother of Jesus, and her acceptance of God's decree. It highlights her submission to God's will and how her faith and obedience led to the fulfillment of God's promise through the miraculous birth of Jesus. This underscores the theme of trust in divine providence and the power of God to bring about what He wills through those who are faithful to Him.
orig: وأذنت لربها وحقت

translation: O mankind, indeed you are laboring toward your Lord with [great] exertion and will meet Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability of meeting God after a lifetime of striving. It serves as a reminder that every human being is constantly working towards their ultimate encounter with their Creator, urging them to reflect on their actions and intentions in light of this meeting.
orig: يا أيها الإنسان إنك كادح إلى ربك كدحا فملاقيه

translation: As for him who is given his record in his right hand,
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when individuals will receive their records of deeds. Receiving the record in the right hand symbolizes success and acceptance by Allah, indicating that the person has lived a righteous life and will be rewarded in the hereafter.
orig: فأما من أوتي كتابه بيمينه

translation: So He will call him to account with an easy reckoning.
interpretation: This verse suggests that for the righteous believers, the accounting on the Day of Judgment will be straightforward and lenient. It implies that their good deeds and faith will make the process of judgment easier, reflecting God's mercy and justice towards those who have lived according to His guidance.
orig: فسوف يحاسب حسابا يسيرا

translation: And he returns to his people joyfully
interpretation: This verse illustrates the happiness and satisfaction one feels upon returning to their community or family after achieving a goal or receiving good news. It emphasizes the joy of reuniting with loved ones and the sense of accomplishment that accompanies such moments.
orig: وينقلب إلى أهله مسرورا

translation: And as for him who is given his record from behind his back,
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when individuals receive their records of deeds. Receiving the record from behind one's back signifies a negative outcome, indicating that the person's deeds were not righteous and they will face the consequences of their actions. It symbolizes failure and disappointment in the afterlife.
orig: وأما من أوتي كتابه وراء ظهره

translation: So he will cry out for destruction,
interpretation: This verse illustrates the intense regret and despair that a person will feel on the Day of Judgment if they have led a life of disbelief or sin. The individual, realizing the gravity of their situation and the impending punishment, will desperately wish for their own destruction as a means to escape the torment they face. It underscores the severity of the consequences of one's actions in the hereafter and serves as a warning to heed the guidance of the Qur'an and live righteously.
orig: فسوف يدعو ثبورا

translation: And he will burn in a blazing fire
interpretation: This verse warns of the severe consequence of disbelief and sinful actions, indicating that those who reject faith and engage in wrongdoing will ultimately face punishment in the hereafter, symbolized by burning in the intense flames of Hell. It serves as a reminder of the accountability one has for their deeds and the importance of adhering to the path of righteousness.
orig: ويصلى سعيرا

translation: Indeed, he was among his people, happy.
interpretation: This verse highlights the state of happiness and contentment that the person experienced while being among his own people, suggesting a sense of belonging and joy in his social environment.
orig: إنه كان في أهله مسرورا

translation: Indeed, he thought that he would never return.
interpretation: This verse reflects the mindset of someone who believed they would not face accountability or return to God after death, highlighting a common human error in underestimating the certainty of the hereafter.
orig: إنه ظن أن لن يحور

translation: Yes, indeed, his Lord was watchful over him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the constant awareness and oversight of Allah over His servant. It conveys the idea that no matter the circumstances, Allah is fully cognizant of the individual's actions, thoughts, and situation, providing a sense of divine protection and guidance.
orig: بلى إن ربه كان به بصيرا

translation: So I swear by the afterglow of sunset
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the solemnity and importance of the message that follows by invoking an oath on the natural phenomenon of the afterglow of sunset, highlighting the beauty and majesty of creation as a testament to the truth of the Qur'anic message.
orig: فلا أقسم بالشفق

translation: By the night and what it envelops,
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the significance of the night as a time of mystery and concealment, symbolizing the hidden aspects of life and the universe that are beyond human comprehension. It invites reflection on the divine power that governs both the seen and the unseen.
orig: والليل وما وسق

translation: And the moon when it is full
interpretation: This verse refers to the moon reaching its full phase, symbolizing the completion and perfection of time cycles. It highlights the divine order and precision in the celestial movements, reminding believers of the power and majesty of Allah in controlling the universe.
orig: والقمر إذا اتسق

translation: You will surely travel from stage to stage.
interpretation: This verse suggests that life is a journey through various stages or phases, each presenting its own challenges and lessons. It emphasizes the transient nature of life and the inevitability of change, encouraging believers to be patient and steadfast as they move through different experiences and trials.
orig: لتركبن طبقا عن طبق

translation: So what is [the matter] with them [that] they do not believe?
interpretation: This verse questions the disbelief of those who reject faith, suggesting a sense of bewilderment or frustration at their refusal to accept the clear signs and truths presented to them. It implies that the evidence for faith is so compelling that their disbelief seems inexplicable or irrational.
orig: فما لهم لا يؤمنون

translation: And when the Qur'an is recited to them, they do not prostrate.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual insensitivity or arrogance of those who do not humble themselves in reverence and submission when the Qur'an is recited. It points to a deeper issue of faith, where the act of prostration symbolizes complete surrender to God's message, which some people fail to acknowledge or accept despite hearing it.
orig: وإذا قرئ عليهم القرآن لا يسجدون

translation: Nay, those who disbelieve (in the Qur'an) deny (it).
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the rejection of the Qur'an by those who disbelieve. It suggests that their denial is not just a simple disagreement but a deliberate act of falsehood against the truth presented in the Qur'an. It highlights the psychological and moral state of the disbelievers, indicating that their disbelief stems from a refusal to accept the evident truth.
orig: بل الذين كفروا يكذبون

translation: And Allah is most knowing of what they keep within themselves.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah has complete knowledge of the innermost thoughts and secrets of individuals. It serves as a reminder to believers that nothing is hidden from Allah, encouraging sincerity and mindfulness in one's actions and intentions.
orig: والله أعلم بما يوعون

translation: So give them tidings of a painful punishment
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who reject faith and engage in wrongdoing. It emphasizes the consequence of their actions, indicating that they will face a severe punishment in the hereafter. The use of 'tidings' or 'give them news' suggests that this outcome is certain and inevitable, serving as a reminder of divine justice and accountability.
orig: فبشرهم بعذاب أليم

translation: Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds; for them is a reward uninterrupted.
interpretation: This verse highlights the exception to a general statement made in the preceding verses, emphasizing that those who have faith in Allah and perform good deeds will receive a continuous and unending reward in the hereafter. It underscores the importance of both belief and righteous actions as prerequisites for attaining eternal reward, suggesting that faith alone without good deeds is insufficient for salvation.
orig: إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لهم أجر غير ممنون

translation: And the heaven with its constellations
interpretation: This verse highlights the magnificence and order of the universe, specifically pointing to the stars and constellations as signs of God's creation. It invites reflection on the vastness and precision of the celestial bodies, encouraging believers to recognize the divine wisdom and power behind their arrangement.
orig: والسماء ذات البروج

translation: And the promised day
interpretation: This phrase refers to the Day of Judgment, which is a central theme in Islamic eschatology. It is the day when all individuals will be resurrected and held accountable for their deeds. The use of 'the promised day' emphasizes the certainty and inevitability of this event, as it has been foretold by Allah and His messengers.
orig: واليوم الموعود

translation: And a witness and what is witnessed
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment where Allah is the ultimate witness to all deeds, and all actions and events of the worldly life are presented as evidence or what is witnessed. It emphasizes the accountability and the comprehensive knowledge of Allah over everything that has occurred.
orig: وشاهد ومشهود

translation: The People of the Ditch were killed
interpretation: This verse refers to a historical event where a group of believers were brutally killed by being thrown into a ditch filled with fire due to their faith. It serves as a reminder of the severe persecution faced by early believers and highlights the theme of steadfastness in faith despite extreme adversity.
orig: قتل أصحاب الأخدود

translation: The fire, the one with fuel
interpretation: This verse refers to the Hellfire, emphasizing its characteristic of being fueled, which signifies its intensity and the continuous nature of its burning. It serves as a reminder of the consequences of disbelief and sinful actions, urging believers to be mindful of their deeds and to seek righteousness.
orig: النار ذات الوقود

translation: When they are seated upon it
interpretation: This verse refers to the moment when people are settled in their positions or places, possibly in the context of the Day of Judgment or a similar significant event, emphasizing the finality and inevitability of their situation.
orig: إذ هم عليها قعود

translation: And they are witnesses over what they do to the believers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the accountability of those who persecute believers, indicating that they are fully aware of their actions and will be held responsible as witnesses to their own deeds against the faithful.
orig: وهم على ما يفعلون بالمؤمنين شهود

translation: And they did not resent them except that they believed in Allah, the Almighty, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse highlights that the believers faced opposition and resentment solely because of their faith in Allah, who is described as Almighty and Praiseworthy. It underscores the purity and sincerity of their belief, which was the only reason for the hostility they encountered. This emphasizes the theme of steadfastness in faith despite persecution, illustrating that true faith in Allah can provoke opposition from those who reject such belief.
orig: وما نقموا منهم إلا أن يؤمنوا بالله العزيز الحميد

translation: He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is Witness over all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty of Allah over the entire universe, highlighting that He has complete control and authority over everything in existence. The phrase 'Allah is Witness over all things' underscores His omniscience and omnipresence, indicating that He is fully aware of and observes every action and event, reinforcing the concept of divine accountability and the ultimate justice that stems from His all-encompassing knowledge.
orig: الذي له ملك السماوات والأرض والله على كل شيء شهيد

translation: Indeed, those who persecuted the believing men and believing women and then did not repent will have the punishment of Hell, and they will have the punishment of the Burning Fire.
interpretation: This verse highlights the severe consequences for those who harm believers without seeking forgiveness. It underscores the importance of repentance and the gravity of actions against the faithful, emphasizing that such transgressions lead to a dire fate in the afterlife, specifically the torment of Hellfire. This serves as a warning and a call to moral accountability within the community.
orig: إن الذين فتنوا المؤمنين والمؤمنات ثم لم يتوبوا فلهم عذاب جهنم ولهم عذاب الحريق

translation: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them are gardens beneath which rivers flow. That is the great triumph.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the reward awaiting believers who not only have faith but also actively engage in good deeds. The 'gardens beneath which rivers flow' symbolize the ultimate bliss and peace in Paradise, indicating a state of eternal happiness and satisfaction. The phrase 'the great triumph' underscores that this reward is the ultimate success and victory in the hereafter, highlighting the significance of faith coupled with righteous actions in achieving divine pleasure and eternal salvation.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لهم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار ذلك الفوز الكبير

translation: Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is severe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severity and inevitability of divine retribution for those who transgress against God's commands. It serves as a reminder of the consequences of disobedience and the importance of adhering to the path of righteousness, highlighting the power and justice of Allah.
orig: إن بطش ربك لشديد

translation: Indeed, it is He who begins and repeats
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and sovereignty of Allah, highlighting His role as the sole initiator and restorer of all creation. It underscores the concept that Allah is the originator of life and the universe, and He has the power to bring things into existence and to renew or repeat them as He wills. This reinforces the belief in the cyclical nature of life and the divine control over all beginnings and endings.
orig: إنه هو يبدئ ويعيد

translation: And He is the Forgiving, the Loving.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes two of Allah's attributes: His forgiveness and His love. It highlights that Allah is ever-ready to forgive the sins of those who sincerely repent, showcasing His mercy. Additionally, it underscores His attribute of love, indicating that Allah's love encompasses all of creation, and He desires good for His servants, encouraging them to draw closer to Him through obedience and repentance.
orig: وهو الغفور الودود

translation: The Possessor of the Majestic Throne
interpretation: This phrase refers to Allah, emphasizing His supreme authority and sovereignty over all creation. The term 'Majestic Throne' symbolizes the grandeur and magnificence of Allah's dominion, highlighting His power and the exalted nature of His rule.
orig: ذو العرش المجيد

translation: Effective in what He intends
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's omnipotence and absolute power over all things. It signifies that whatever Allah wills, He is able to accomplish without any hindrance or delay. It underscores the concept that Allah's will is executed perfectly and efficiently, reflecting His complete control and sovereignty over the universe.
orig: فعال لما يريد

translation: Has the story of the soldiers reached you?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question posed by Allah to the Prophet Muhammad, asking if he has been informed about the story of the soldiers, which refers to the army of elephants led by Abraha that attempted to destroy the Kaaba. The question serves to introduce the narrative of the event known as the 'Year of the Elephant,' highlighting divine intervention and protection of the sacred house.
orig: هل أتاك حديث الجنود

translation: Pharaoh and Thamud
interpretation: This verse refers to two significant examples of communities that rejected the messages of their prophets. Pharaoh symbolizes the rejection of Moses, leading to the oppression and eventual liberation of the Israelites. Thamud represents the people who rejected the prophet Saleh, resulting in their destruction due to their arrogance and disobedience. The mention of these two serves as a reminder of the consequences of denying divine guidance and the inevitability of divine justice.
orig: فرعون وثمود

translation: Nay, those who disbelieve are in denial.
interpretation: This verse highlights the psychological state of the disbelievers, indicating that their rejection of the truth is not merely an intellectual disagreement but a deeper form of denial rooted in their hearts. It suggests that their disbelief is an active choice to reject the evident signs and messages of God, reflecting a stubbornness and unwillingness to accept the truth.
orig: بل الذين كفروا في تكذيب

translation: And Allah is, from behind them, encompassing
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipresence and all-encompassing nature of Allah. It suggests that no matter where one turns or tries to hide, Allah is always surrounding and aware of everything, indicating His complete knowledge and control over all affairs.
orig: والله من ورائهم محيط

translation: Nay, it is a Glorious Qur'an
interpretation: This verse asserts the divine and majestic nature of the Qur'an, emphasizing its honor and high status above any form of falsehood or triviality. It serves as a reaffirmation of the Qur'an's sublime origin and its role as a guide and a source of profound wisdom.
orig: بل هو قرآن مجيد

translation: In a Preserved Tablet
interpretation: This phrase refers to the concept of the 'Preserved Tablet' or 'Al-Lawh Al-Mahfuz,' which in Islamic theology is believed to be a celestial record where all of God's decrees, past, present, and future, are inscribed. It signifies the divine knowledge and predestination of all events, emphasizing the completeness and unchangeable nature of God's plan.
orig: في لوح محفوظ

translation: By the sky and the night-comer
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oath by the sky and the night-comer (often interpreted as a star or a celestial body), highlighting their significance and the divine order of the universe. It serves to draw attention to the majesty and the mysteries of creation, urging reflection on the power and wisdom of the Creator.
orig: والسماء والطارق

translation: And what can make you know what is the piercing star?
interpretation: This rhetorical question emphasizes the mysterious and significant nature of the piercing star, or Al-Tariq, inviting the listener to ponder its deeper meaning and significance in the cosmic order established by Allah.
orig: وما أدراك ما الطارق

translation: The piercing star
interpretation: This phrase refers to the planet Venus, known for its brightness and piercing light in the sky. It symbolizes clarity and guidance, reflecting the Qur'an's role as a source of light and guidance for humanity.
orig: النجم الثاقب

translation: Indeed, every soul has a guardian over it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine accountability and protection, indicating that every individual is constantly watched over by an appointed guardian, likely an angel, who records their deeds. This serves as a reminder of the omnipresence of divine oversight and the importance of being mindful of one's actions, knowing that they are always under surveillance by celestial beings.
orig: إن كل نفس لما عليها حافظ

translation: So let man consider from what he was created.
interpretation: This verse urges humans to reflect upon their origin and creation, emphasizing the miraculous nature of human existence. It encourages contemplation on the fact that humans were created from a simple, humble beginning, which should lead to a sense of humility and gratitude towards the Creator.
orig: فلينظر الإنسان مم خلق

translation: Created from gushing water
interpretation: This verse refers to the miraculous nature of human creation, emphasizing that all humans are created from a simple yet essential element, water. The term 'gushing water' symbolizes the vitality and dynamic force behind creation, highlighting the power and majesty of Allah in initiating life from such a fundamental substance.
orig: خلق من ماء دافق

translation: He emerges from between the backbone and the ribs
interpretation: This verse refers to the origin of human creation, specifically indicating the process of procreation where the human being is formed from the mingling of the male and female reproductive fluids. The 'backbone' symbolizes the male contribution, while the 'ribs' symbolize the female contribution, illustrating the divine design and miracle of human reproduction.
orig: يخرج من بين الصلب والترائب

translation: Indeed, He, over His returning, is Able
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's omnipotence, specifically highlighting His ability to bring about the Day of Resurrection. It reassures believers that Allah has complete power to gather all souls and bring them back to life after death, underscoring the certainty and inevitability of the Hereafter.
orig: إنه على رجعه لقادر

translation: The Day when secrets will be put to the test
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, when all hidden thoughts, intentions, and deeds will be exposed and scrutinized by Allah. It emphasizes the inevitability of accountability for everything one has kept secret in their heart, highlighting the importance of sincerity and righteousness in one's inner self.
orig: يوم تبلى السرائر

translation: So he has no power, nor any helper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate powerlessness and isolation of those who oppose God's will. It underscores the notion that without God's support, individuals lack the strength and assistance needed to prevail, highlighting the dependency of all beings on divine aid.
orig: فما له من قوة ولا ناصر

translation: And the heaven which returns
interpretation: This verse refers to the cyclical nature of the atmosphere, where clouds form, rain falls, and water evaporates to form clouds again, illustrating the continuous cycle of water in the sky.
orig: والسماء ذات الرجع

translation: And the earth with its cracks
interpretation: This verse refers to the physical state of the earth, highlighting its cracked and fissured nature, which can symbolize the transient and fragile state of the world, reminding believers of the impermanence of earthly life and the need to focus on the hereafter.
orig: والأرض ذات الصدع

translation: Indeed, it is a decisive statement
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the clarity and finality of the Qur'anic message, indicating that the words of the Qur'an are clear, precise, and definitive, leaving no room for ambiguity or doubt in its guidance and rulings.
orig: إنه لقول فصل

translation: And it is not a jest
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the seriousness and gravity of the Qur'an, indicating that its message and purpose are profound and should not be taken lightly or considered as mere entertainment or idle talk.
orig: وما هو بالهزل

translation: Indeed, they are planning a plan.
interpretation: This verse highlights the deceptive and secretive plotting of the enemies of the Prophet Muhammad. It underscores their continuous efforts to undermine the message of Islam through various schemes. The verse serves as a reminder to believers of the ongoing opposition they might face and the need for vigilance and reliance on divine guidance.
orig: إنهم يكيدون كيدا

translation: And I will plot a plot
interpretation: This verse reflects the determination and strategic planning of the speaker, often interpreted as Satan, to mislead humanity. It underscores the ongoing spiritual battle and the need for believers to be vigilant and seek divine guidance to counteract such plots.
orig: وأكيد كيدا

translation: So give respite to the disbelievers; give them a little time.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad to be patient with the disbelievers and not to rush their punishment. It suggests that Allah will deal with them in His own time, emphasizing divine patience and the eventual accountability of all individuals.
orig: فمهل الكافرين أمهلهم رويدا

translation: Glorified be the name of your Lord, the Most High.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the supreme greatness and sanctity of Allah, urging believers to recognize and venerate His exalted status above all else. It serves as a reminder of the purity and perfection of Allah's essence, encouraging a state of reverence and humility in the worshipper.
orig: سبح اسم ربك الأعلى

translation: He who created and then proportioned
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power and precision of Allah as the Creator. It highlights that not only did Allah bring everything into existence, but He also meticulously designed and balanced all aspects of creation, reflecting His wisdom and attention to detail in the universe's structure and functionality.
orig: الذي خلق فسوى

translation: And He who has proportioned and guided
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's role as the ultimate creator who not only designs and shapes everything in the universe with precision but also guides all beings towards their purpose and the right path. It highlights the divine wisdom and care in the creation and guidance of life.
orig: والذي قدر فهدى

translation: And He who brings forth the pasture
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's role as the sustainer of life, emphasizing His power to create and nurture vegetation from the earth, which is essential for the survival of all living creatures. It underscores the divine providence and care over the natural world.
orig: والذي أخرج المرعى

translation: So He made it a black, barren land.
interpretation: This verse describes the transformation of a once fertile land into a desolate and barren state as a consequence of the people's disobedience and rejection of divine guidance. It serves as a reminder of the consequences of straying from the path set by Allah, illustrating how blessings can be turned into curses when gratitude and righteousness are forsaken.
orig: فجعله غثاء أحوى

translation: We shall make you recite, so you shall not forget
interpretation: This verse is a divine promise from Allah to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that Allah will ensure he remembers the Qur'an. It highlights the special support and assistance provided by Allah to the Prophet in his mission, ensuring that the revelation is preserved in his memory. This reassurance underscores the importance of the Qur'an and the Prophet's role in conveying it accurately to the community.
orig: سنقرئك فلا تنسى

translation: Except what Allah wills. Indeed, He knows what is declared and what is hidden.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence and omniscience of Allah. It suggests that while humans may have free will, ultimately, everything is subject to Allah's will. The phrase "He knows what is declared and what is hidden" underscores that Allah has complete knowledge of all things, both apparent and secret, reinforcing the idea that nothing escapes His awareness and control.
orig: إلا ما شاء الله إنه يعلم الجهر وما يخفى

translation: And We will ease you toward ease.
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah will facilitate and simplify the path for the Prophet Muhammad towards achieving comfort and ease in his mission. It reflects a promise of divine support and guidance, indicating that despite the challenges faced, the journey will ultimately become smoother and more manageable through Allah's assistance.
orig: ونيسرك لليسرى

translation: So remind, if the reminder should benefit.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of giving reminders or advice, but it is conditional upon the potential benefit to the recipient. It suggests that one should engage in reminding others of their duties, moral values, or religious obligations, but only if there is a likelihood that such reminders will be heeded and lead to positive change. It underscores the wisdom of being selective and mindful in offering guidance, ensuring that it is done in a context where it can be effective and beneficial.
orig: فذكر إن نفعت الذكرى

translation: He will remember who fears.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that only those who possess a sense of fear and reverence for Allah will be reminded and take heed of His messages. It underscores the importance of a heart filled with awe and respect for the divine, as such a heart is more receptive to guidance and admonition.
orig: سيذكر من يخشى

translation: And the wretched will avoid it
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who are spiritually and morally bankrupt will turn away from the path of righteousness and the guidance offered by the Qur'an, leading them to a state of misery and distance from divine mercy.
orig: ويتجنبها الأشقى

translation: The one who will be thrown into the great fire
interpretation: This verse refers to the severe punishment awaiting those who reject faith and commit grave sins. The 'great fire' symbolizes the intensity and eternity of the punishment in Hell, emphasizing the consequences of one's actions in the afterlife.
orig: الذي يصلى النار الكبرى

translation: Then they will neither die therein nor live.
interpretation: This verse describes the state of the disbelievers in Hell, where they will be in a perpetual state of suffering, neither fully dead to escape the torment nor fully alive to experience any joy or relief. It emphasizes the eternal nature of their punishment, highlighting the severity of their fate.
orig: ثم لا يموت فيها ولا يحيى

translation: Indeed, he has succeeded who purifies himself.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of spiritual purification and moral integrity as the path to true success in the eyes of Allah. It suggests that success is not measured by worldly achievements but by one's efforts to cleanse the soul from sins and to develop a pure heart and righteous conduct.
orig: قد أفلح من تزكى

translation: And he mentioned the name of his Lord and prayed.
interpretation: This verse highlights the Prophet Muhammad's devotion and humility. By mentioning the name of his Lord and engaging in prayer, it underscores the importance of regular worship and remembrance of Allah, setting an example for all believers to follow in maintaining a strong spiritual connection with their Creator.
orig: وذكر اسم ربه فصلى

translation: Nay, you prefer the life of this world
interpretation: This verse critiques the human tendency to prioritize worldly life over spiritual and eternal values. It suggests that people often become engrossed in material pursuits and immediate gratifications, neglecting the hereafter and their spiritual duties. The use of "nay" emphasizes a correction or a reminder to shift focus towards what is truly important in the broader scope of existence.
orig: بل تؤثرون الحياة الدنيا

translation: And the Hereafter is better and more lasting.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the superiority and eternal nature of the Hereafter compared to the fleeting pleasures of worldly life. It serves as a reminder for believers to focus on their actions and faith in preparation for the everlasting life to come, which is far more valuable and enduring than any temporary gains in this world.
orig: والآخرة خير وأبقى

translation: Indeed, this is in the former scriptures
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the continuity and consistency of divine revelation across time, affirming that the message being conveyed in the Qur'an is not new but has been mentioned in the earlier scriptures given to previous prophets. It serves to validate the Qur'anic message by connecting it to a long tradition of divine guidance.
orig: إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى

translation: The scriptures of Abraham and Moses
interpretation: This verse refers to the divine revelations and scriptures that were given to the prophets Abraham and Moses. It underscores the continuity and connection of the prophetic messages across different times, affirming the respect and reverence for these earlier scriptures within the Islamic tradition.
orig: صحف إبراهيم وموسى

translation: Has there come to you the news of the overwhelming event?
interpretation: This verse introduces the theme of the Day of Judgment, referred to as 'the overwhelming event,' which will engulf and overpower everything. It prompts the listener to reflect on the inevitability and the overwhelming nature of this event, urging a contemplation of one's readiness and actions in light of this ultimate reality.
orig: هل أتاك حديث الغاشية

translation: Faces, that Day, will be humbled
interpretation: This verse describes the state of some people on the Day of Judgment, where their faces will be lowered in humility and fear due to the overwhelming awe and realization of their accountability before Allah. It reflects the emotional and physical manifestation of their regret and submission to the divine judgment.
orig: وجوه يومئذ خاشعة

translation: Working, ascending
interpretation: This phrase describes the angels who are constantly engaged in their duties, tirelessly working and ascending towards Allah. It signifies their perpetual motion and dedication in carrying out divine commands, reflecting their obedience and closeness to the divine presence.
orig: عاملة ناصبة

translation: They will be roasted in a blazing fire.
interpretation: This verse describes the severe punishment in the afterlife for those who have committed wrongdoing, emphasizing the intense heat and suffering that awaits them in Hell as a consequence of their actions.
orig: تصلى نارا حامية

translation: It is watered by a flowing spring.
interpretation: This verse symbolizes the continuous and abundant provision from Allah, akin to a never-ending spring that sustains and nourishes the righteous, illustrating divine generosity and sustenance in the hereafter.
orig: تسقى من عين آنية

translation: They have no food except from a bitter plant
interpretation: This verse highlights the dire circumstances of the people described, indicating that their sustenance is limited to a plant known as ضريع (dari'), which is bitter and undesirable. It serves as a metaphor for the hardship and suffering they endure, emphasizing the severity of their situation and possibly their punishment or test in the hereafter.
orig: ليس لهم طعام إلا من ضريع

translation: It neither nourishes nor satisfies hunger.
interpretation: This verse metaphorically describes something that is utterly useless and ineffective, offering no real benefit or sustenance, similar to how food that does not nourish or alleviate hunger is of no value.
orig: لا يسمن ولا يغني من جوع

translation: Faces that Day will be radiant
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, where the faces of the righteous will be radiant and joyful, reflecting their inner state of peace and happiness due to their good deeds and faith in Allah.
orig: وجوه يومئذ ناعمة

translation: For its striving, it will be satisfied.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the soul, after enduring the trials and efforts of life, will find contentment and satisfaction in the Hereafter. It emphasizes the reward of perseverance and striving in the path of righteousness, indicating that the soul's efforts will be met with fulfillment and peace in the afterlife.
orig: لسعيها راضية

translation: In a high garden
interpretation: This verse refers to the elevated status of Paradise, symbolizing the spiritual heights and purity that believers will attain. It emphasizes the sublime nature of the reward awaiting the righteous in the hereafter.
orig: في جنة عالية

translation: You will not hear any vain talk therein.
interpretation: This verse suggests that in Paradise, there will be an absence of meaningless or idle chatter, emphasizing the purity and peacefulness of the environment, where only meaningful and beneficial communication exists.
orig: لا تسمع فيها لاغية

translation: In it is a flowing spring.
interpretation: This verse describes the presence of a continuously flowing spring in Paradise, symbolizing the abundance and everlasting nature of the blessings and pleasures that await the righteous. The flowing spring represents purity, life, and the fulfillment of all desires in the hereafter.
orig: فيها عين جارية

translation: In it are couches raised high.
interpretation: This verse describes the luxurious and elevated seating arrangements in Paradise, symbolizing the honor and comfort provided to the righteous. The raised couches signify a place of dignity and relaxation, reflecting the ultimate reward and peace awaiting believers in the afterlife.
orig: فيها سرر مرفوعة

translation: And cups set in place
interpretation: This verse refers to the cups in Paradise that are perfectly arranged and ready for the believers to enjoy, symbolizing the meticulous preparation and the abundance of blessings awaiting them in the afterlife.
orig: وأكواب موضوعة

translation: And ships lined up in rows
interpretation: This verse highlights the organization and beauty of creation, specifically referring to ships arranged in an orderly manner. It reflects on the human ability to harness nature, guided by divine wisdom, to achieve feats like navigation and trade, which are essential for civilization. The imagery of ships in rows also symbolizes unity and cooperation among people, working together towards common goals.
orig: ونمارق مصفوفة

translation: And My servants, the dispersed ones
interpretation: This verse refers to the believers who are spread across the world, indicating that God's mercy and guidance are available to all His servants, regardless of where they are located. It emphasizes the universal nature of Islam and the inclusivity of God's message.
orig: وزرابي مبثوثة

translation: Do they not look at the camels, how they are created?
interpretation: This verse invites reflection on the creation of camels as a sign of God's power and wisdom. The camel, with its unique adaptations to desert life, serves as a clear example of divine design and should prompt humans to ponder the intricacies of creation and recognize the Creator's greatness.
orig: أفلا ينظرون إلى الإبل كيف خلقت

translation: And to the heaven, how it was raised
interpretation: This verse invites contemplation on the creation of the sky, highlighting the marvel and complexity of its structure as a testament to God's power and wisdom in the act of creation.
orig: وإلى السماء كيف رفعت

translation: And to the mountains, how they are set up?
interpretation: This verse invites reflection on the creation and stability of mountains, suggesting that their formation and steadfastness are signs of God's power and wisdom. It encourages believers to contemplate the natural world as a manifestation of divine design and order.
orig: وإلى الجبال كيف نصبت

translation: And to the earth, how it is spread out?
interpretation: This verse invites reflection on the earth's vastness and flatness, encouraging contemplation of God's creation and the suitability of the earth for human life and habitation.
orig: وإلى الأرض كيف سطحت

translation: So remind, for you are only a reminder.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of the Prophet Muhammad as a messenger whose duty is to convey the message of Islam and remind people of their responsibilities towards God. It highlights that the Prophet's task is not to force belief or change hearts by himself, but to deliver the message and leave the ultimate guidance to Allah.
orig: فذكر إنما أنت مذكر

translation: I am not a controller over them
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the limitation of human authority and power. It indicates that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) does not have the ability to force people to believe or to control their actions and choices. It underscores the principle of free will granted to humans by Allah, highlighting that ultimate guidance and control belong to Allah alone.
orig: لست عليهم بمصيطر

translation: Except him who turns away and disbelieves.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the exception to receiving guidance and mercy from Allah is for those who deliberately turn away from the truth and reject faith. It emphasizes personal responsibility in accepting or rejecting divine guidance, highlighting that disbelief is a conscious choice to turn away from the path shown by Allah.
orig: إلا من تولى وكفر

translation: So Allah will punish him with the greatest punishment
interpretation: This verse warns of the severe consequences of disbelief and disobedience to Allah. The "greatest punishment" refers to the eternal torment in Hell, which is the ultimate retribution for those who reject faith and live in opposition to God's commands. It emphasizes the gravity of one's actions and the importance of adhering to the path of righteousness to avoid such a fate.
orig: فيعذبه الله العذاب الأكبر

translation: Indeed, to Us is their return.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability of returning to Allah after death. It serves as a reminder of the accountability that all individuals will face upon their return to the Creator, highlighting the transient nature of worldly life and the eternal reality of the hereafter.
orig: إن إلينا إيابهم

translation: Then upon Us is their account.
interpretation: This verse indicates that after the worldly life, it is Allah's responsibility to take account of the deeds of all individuals. It emphasizes the divine justice and accountability that awaits every soul, reassuring believers that no action, good or bad, will go unnoticed or unjudged by Allah.
orig: ثم إن علينا حسابهم

translation: And the dawn
interpretation: The mention of the dawn in this verse symbolizes the beginning of a new day and new opportunities for spiritual reflection and renewal. It serves as a reminder of God's continuous creation and the cyclical nature of life, urging believers to start their day with remembrance and gratitude towards Allah.
orig: والفجر

translation: And [by] the night when it departs
interpretation: This verse refers to the last ten nights of Ramadan, emphasizing their significance and the spiritual elevation they bring. It highlights the importance of engaging in worship and seeking Laylat al-Qadr during these nights, as they are a time when divine mercy and blessings are particularly abundant.
orig: وليال عشر

translation: And by the even and the odd
interpretation: This verse refers to the oath taken by Allah, emphasizing the balance and harmony in creation. The 'even' and 'odd' symbolize the universal order and the perfection in the diversity and multiplicity of creation, suggesting that everything in the universe is under divine control and perfectly balanced.
orig: والشفع والوتر

translation: And by the night when it departs,
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the cyclical nature of time and the inevitability of change. The night, which is a time of rest and concealment, eventually gives way to the dawn, symbolizing the transition from darkness to light, ignorance to knowledge, and the constant movement towards new beginnings and opportunities for spiritual growth.
orig: والليل إذا يسر

translation: Is there in that an oath for the one who is mindful?
interpretation: This verse poses a rhetorical question aimed at those who are reflective and mindful, urging them to consider the significance of the oath being referenced. It emphasizes the importance of contemplation and understanding the deeper meanings behind divine messages, encouraging believers to engage actively with their faith and the signs provided by Allah.
orig: هل في ذلك قسم لذي حجر

translation: Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with 'Ad?
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder and a warning to the reader about the consequences of arrogance and disbelief. It specifically refers to the historical example of the 'Ad people, who were a powerful and prosperous nation but were destroyed by God due to their rejection of His messages and their corrupt behavior. The rhetorical question 'Have you not seen' is used to engage the reader, urging them to reflect on past events and learn from them, emphasizing that God's justice is inevitable and that no one is beyond His reach.
orig: ألم تر كيف فعل ربك بعاد

translation: Iram, with pillars
interpretation: This verse refers to the ancient city of Iram, known for its towering structures or pillars, symbolizing its grandeur and advanced architecture. The mention of Iram serves as a reminder of the transience of worldly achievements and the ultimate power of God, who can bring down even the mightiest of civilizations.
orig: إرم ذات العماد

translation: The like of which was not created in the lands
interpretation: This verse refers to the unique nature of the Qur'an, suggesting that it is unparalleled and unmatched by any other creation or text in the world. It emphasizes the miraculous aspect of the Qur'an, highlighting its divine origin and the impossibility of humans producing anything similar to it.
orig: التي لم يخلق مثلها في البلاد

translation: And [the tribe of] Thamud, who carved out the rocks in the valley
interpretation: This verse refers to the historical tribe of Thamud, known for their advanced skills in architecture and engineering. They are mentioned as a reminder of the consequences of arrogance and disobedience to divine guidance. By carving out homes in the rocks, they demonstrated their capabilities, yet their rejection of the prophet Salih's message led to their ultimate destruction. The verse serves as a warning to reflect on the transient nature of worldly achievements and the importance of heeding divine warnings.
orig: وثمود الذين جابوا الصخر بالواد

translation: And Pharaoh, the one with the stakes
interpretation: This verse refers to Pharaoh's oppressive rule, symbolized by the 'stakes' or 'pegs,' which represent his use of torture and execution to maintain control and suppress dissent among his people.
orig: وفرعون ذي الأوتاد

translation: Those who have transgressed in the land
interpretation: This verse refers to individuals who have exceeded the bounds of justice and righteousness, causing corruption and oppression within society. It highlights the Qur'an's condemnation of those who abuse their power or position to harm others and disrupt the peace and order established by divine law.
orig: الذين طغوا في البلاد

translation: So they spread corruption in it
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequence of human actions leading to widespread corruption and disorder within society. It serves as a warning about the destructive impact of moral and ethical decay when people deviate from the path of righteousness.
orig: فأكثروا فيها الفساد

translation: So your Lord poured upon them a scourge of torment.
interpretation: This verse refers to the divine punishment that was inflicted upon a community due to their persistent disobedience and rejection of God's messages. It serves as a reminder of the consequences of straying from the path of righteousness and the power of God to enact justice.
orig: فصب عليهم ربك سوط عذاب

translation: Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipresence and vigilance of Allah, indicating that He is always observing and aware of all actions and intentions. It serves as a reminder to believers to be mindful of their deeds, knowing that they are under constant divine surveillance.
orig: إن ربك لبالمرصاد

translation: As for man, when his Lord tries him by honoring him and blessing him, he says, "My Lord has honored me."
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to acknowledge and praise God when experiencing prosperity and blessings. It reflects a moment of gratitude and recognition of divine favor, illustrating how ease and comfort can lead to a positive affirmation of faith and appreciation for God's generosity.
orig: فأما الإنسان إذا ما ابتلاه ربه فأكرمه ونعمه فيقول ربي أكرمن

translation: And when We test him and restrict his provision, he says, 'My Lord has humiliated me!'
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to attribute personal hardships, such as limited provision, directly to divine humiliation. It reflects a lack of patience and understanding of the broader divine wisdom behind trials, suggesting that one's faith is tested through adversity. The response of the individual in the verse indicates a failure to recognize the test as an opportunity for spiritual growth and a closer relationship with God.
orig: وأما إذا ما ابتلاه فقدر عليه رزقه فيقول ربي أهانن

translation: Nay, but you do not honor the orphan.
interpretation: This verse criticizes the societal neglect and lack of compassion towards orphans, emphasizing that one of the reasons for moral decline is the failure to show kindness and respect to those who are vulnerable and in need of care.
orig: كلا بل لا تكرمون اليتيم

translation: And do not urge one another to the food of the poor
interpretation: This verse warns against the practice of some people who would deliberately spoil or waste food intended for the poor, or encourage others to do so, as a means of showing off their wealth or disdain for the less fortunate. It emphasizes the importance of respect and care towards the poor and the proper use of resources.
orig: ولا تحاضون على طعام المسكين

translation: And you devour inheritance all with greed.
interpretation: This verse critiques the excessive and greedy consumption of inheritance, highlighting a moral and ethical concern about how wealth, particularly inherited wealth, should be handled with fairness and responsibility rather than being consumed selfishly.
orig: وتأكلون التراث أكلا لما

translation: And you love wealth with an ardent love
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to excessively desire wealth, often to the point of obsession. It serves as a reminder and a critique of how such love for material possessions can distract individuals from spiritual and moral priorities, urging believers to reflect on their values and priorities in life.
orig: وتحبون المال حبا جما

translation: Nay, when the earth is pounded to powder, pounded to powder,
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability and intensity of the Day of Judgment. The repetition of the word 'daka' (pounded) underscores the complete and utter destruction that will occur, symbolizing the end of the world as we know it and the beginning of the afterlife. It serves as a reminder of the power of Allah and the certainty of the hereafter, urging believers to reflect on their actions and prepare for that day.
orig: كلا إذا دكت الأرض دكا دكا

translation: And your Lord has come and the angels, rank upon rank,
interpretation: This verse describes the majestic arrival of Allah and the angels on the Day of Judgment, emphasizing the grandeur and orderliness of their coming. The phrase "rank upon rank" signifies the disciplined and structured nature of this divine event, highlighting the awe-inspiring power and organization of the celestial beings as they appear before humanity.
orig: وجاء ربك والملك صفا صفا

translation: And Hell will be brought near that Day. On that Day man will remember, but how will the remembrance avail him?
interpretation: This verse underscores the moment of realization and regret that will come upon individuals on the Day of Judgment when they are confronted with the reality of Hell. It highlights the futility of remembering and wishing for a different outcome at that point, as the time for action and repentance will have passed. It serves as a reminder for people to be mindful and take corrective actions in their lives before it is too late.
orig: وجيء يومئذ بجهنم يومئذ يتذكر الإنسان وأنى له الذكرى

translation: He will say, 'Oh, I wish I had sent ahead [some good] for my life.'
